##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Urvashi:) O Pururavas, hero, formerly you embraced me three times a day and gave me pleasure by the striking of the male organ. You gave satisfaction to me, who was without a co-wife. I followed you and came to your house. Then you were my lord and the giver of my pleasure.

##### English translation
Thirce a day, Pururavas, have you embraced me, you have loved me without a rival ; I have followed (you) to your dwelling, you, hero, have been the sovereign of my person.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Urvashi addresses Pururavas himself: त्रिः स्म माह्नः शृथयो वैतसेन (*triḥ sma māhnaḥ śṛthayo vaitasena*)—O Pururavas, when I lived with you formerly, did you not strike me, that is, my yoni region, with your male organ three times a day?
To explain the word वैतस (*vaitasa*) here, Yāska has given an etymology. When listing words of one meaning in pairs (Ni. 3-20), among pairs of words such as प्रपित्वे (*prapitve*)–अभीकॆ (*abhīkè*) and दभ्रं (*dabhraṃ*)–अर्भकं (*arbhakaṃ*), he has given the two words *śepaḥ*–वैतसः (*vaitasaḥ*). These two words have, more or less, one meaning.
शेपो वैतस इति पुंस्रजननस्य । शेषः शपतेः स्पृशतिकर्मणः । वैतसो वितस्तं भवति । यस्यामुशंतः प्रहराम शेषं । त्रिः स्म माह्नः श्नथयो वैतसेन इत्यपि निगमौ भवतः ॥ (*śepo vaitasa iti puṃsrajananasya | śeṣaḥ śapateḥ spṛśatikarmaṇaḥ | vaitaso vitastaṃ bhavati | yasyāmuśaṃtaḥ praharāma śeṣaṃ | triḥ sma māhnaḥ śnathayo vaitasena ityapi nigamau bhavataḥ ‖*)
(Ni. 3-21)

### Printed p. 29

The portion of the male organ that is like a staff (penis) is called शेप (*śepa*) or वैतस (*vaitasa*). The word शेप (*śepa*) is formed from the root शप् (*śap*), "to touch". In sexual union, because the woman's yoni is touched by this male organ, the organ has come to be called शेप (*śepa*). The word वैतस (*vaitasa*) has this meaning in the sense of "being a span long", "being in a weakened state". Because this male member is in a weakened state before touching a woman, it is called वैतस (*vaitasa*). During union with a woman this organ is in an aroused state; at other times it is in the span-long state, that is, in a weakened state. Therefore this staff-like male organ is called वैतस (*vaitasa*); so Yāska has explained the meaning. As examples he has given two Vedic sentences: यस्यामुशंतः प्रहराम शेषं (*yasyāmuśaṃtaḥ praharāma śeṣaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-37) and त्रिः स्म माह्नः श्नथयो वैतसेन (*triḥ sma māhnaḥ śnathayo vaitasena*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-95-5).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुम्मआपिर्या प्रदेचक्षुः । नकारः समुच्छये । ताभिश्चतसृभिरालीभूताभिर्मानिनीभिः
> सहिता ग्रंथिनी ग्रंथनवती संदर्भवती चरण्युश्चरणशीलोर्वश्या जगाम । यद्वा ।
> ग्रंथिनीत्येतत्सखिभूताप्सरोनामधेयं । या सुजूर्णिः सुजवोर्वशी सा ताभिः
> सह जगाम । ता अप्सरसोऽंजय आभरणोपेता अरुणयोऽरुणवर्णा न सस्रुः ।
> पूर्ववन्नगच्छंति । श्रिये श्रयणाय धेनवो नवप्रसूता गावो न गाव इव ।
> आश्रयार्थं यथा गावोऽनवंत शब्दायंते तथा न शब्दयंतीति व्यतिरेके
> दृष्टांतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is Purūravas' speech. She who is सुजूर्णिः (*sujūrṇiḥ*) is a companion of that name (the text reads सुजवैतन्नामिका (*sujavaitannāmikā*))**NOTE**; likewise she who is श्रेणिः (*śreṇiḥ*), she who is सुम्मआपिः (*summaāpiḥ*), she who is प्रदेचक्षुः (*pradecakṣuḥ*). The particle न (*na*) is in the sense of "and". Together with these four proud companions, Granthinī (she who has composition, संदर्भवती (*saṃdarbhavatī*)) and the roving Urvaśī went. Or else: ग्रंथिनी (*graṃthinī*) is likewise the name of a companion apsaras; Urvaśī, who is सुजूर्णिः (*sujūrṇiḥ*) ("swift"), went with them. Those apsarases, adorned with ornaments and red-hued, do not go as before. "For refuge (श्रिये (*śriye*)) they do not sound like (न (*na*)) cows (धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*)), newly calved ones": as cows low for the sake of refuge, so these do not sound; the simile is by way of contrast.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Pururavas:) Urvashi, of excellent roving, has come with all these companions, Sujurni, Shreni, Sumna-api, Pradechakshus and Granthini. All those apsara women, adorned with ornaments and of attractive golden colour, do not run away as before. Like newly calved cows they make sound for refuge.

##### English translation
(Pururavas) Sujurni, Shreni, Sumna-api, Hradechakshus, Granthini and the swift-moving (Urvashi who arrived) they, decorated and purple-tinted did not go first, they lowed like milch-cows for protection.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Sāyaṇa says that what stands in this Ṛk is Pururavas' speech. Here the names of six apsara women are indicated: सुजूर्णिः श्रेणिः सुम्म आपिः प्रदेचक्षुः ग्रंथिनी चरण्णुः (*sujūrṇiḥ śreṇiḥ summa āpiḥ pradecakṣuḥ graṃthinī caraṇṇuḥ*). All of them are adorned with ornaments and shine with a ruddy colour (red). But they do not run away as before. Among these six Urvashi is included, or else these six are together with Urvashi. They do not sound loudly, that is, they do not speak. An illustration is given for this. It is natural for newly calved cows to low for protection; as they do, these do not make sound, that is, they do not cry out loudly but speak softly; this is the purport.
The meaning of this Ṛk is not clear. It is difficult to understand what connection the names of the six apsara women mentioned here have with their going away or making sound, or with the conversation in the sūkta. But the commentator, in his commentary on the next Ṛk, says

### Printed p. 31

अनय्यताभिः सह संसर्गस्तयानुभूत इत्युर्वशी वदति (*anayyatābhiḥ saha saṃsargastayānubhūta ityurvaśī vadati*): in this Ṛk (the second Ṛk) Urvashi tells what kind of relation Pururavas had with these divine women spoken of before. Or else he explains the meaning thus: जायमाने यज्ञार्थं प्रवर्धमाने सति ग्ना देवपत्न्योऽपि समासत समभवन् (*jāyamāne yajñārthaṃ pravardhamāne sati gnā devapatnyo 'pi samāsata samabhavan*), that is, one may also say that these divine women all gathered together here for the sake of the sacrifice.

> जायमाने सति ग्ना अप्सरसो देववेश्या अपि समासत । संगता अभवन् ! अथवा
> जायमाने यज्ञार्थं प्रवर्धमाने सति ग्ना देवपत्योऽपि समासत । समभवन्।
> उतापि चेमेनं पुरूरवसं स्वगूर्ताः स्वयंगामिन्नो नद्यस्तासामाश्रयभूता
> अवर्धयन् ! किंच हे पुरूरवः यद्यस्मात्वा त्वां महे महते रणाय
> रमणीयाय संग्रामाय दस्युहत्याय दस्युहननाय देवास्वामवर्धयन् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Urvaśī says: "A union with these (women) was experienced by you." When this Purūravas was born, the ग्नाः (*gnāḥ*), the apsarases, the courtesans of the gods, gathered together. Or else, when he was growing for the sake of the sacrifice, the wives of the gods also came together. Moreover the self-moving rivers, whose support (he was), made this Purūravas grow. And further, O Purūravas, since the gods made you grow for great, delightful battle, for the slaying of the dasyus (the final clause is cut off at the break of the block in the print order, the sense being "therefore…").

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्मिन् (*asmin*)—this Pururavas
- जायमाने (*jāyamāne*)—as soon as he was born
- ग्नाः (*gnāḥ*)—the divine women
- समासत (*samāsata*)—surrounded him
- उत (*uta*)—and
- ईं (*īṃ*)—him
- स्वगूर्ताः (*svagūrtāḥ*)—self-moving
- नद्यः (*nadyaḥ*)—rivers
- अवर्धन् (*avardhan*)—made grow
- पुरूरवः (*purūravaḥ*)—O Pururavas
- यत् (*yat*)—for the very reason (that)
- महे (*mahe*)—great
- रणाय (*raṇāya*)—for

### Printed p. 32
(Urvaśī:) As soon as he was born, the wives of the gods surrounded him, and the spontaneously flowing rivers nourished him. O Pururavas, for a great battle, and for the destruction of the Dasyus, the gods made you grow strong.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यद्धार्थवागियू (*yaddhārthavāgiyū*)—for the sake of battle
- दस्युहत्याय (*dasyuhatyāya*)—for the destruction of the Dasyus
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- अवर्धन् (*avardhan*)—made you grow strong and thrive

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Urvaśī:) As soon as this Pururavas was born, the wives of the gods surrounded him. The spontaneously flowing rivers nourished him. O Pururavas, for a great battle and for the destruction of the Dasyu people, the gods made you grow strong.

##### English translation
(Urvashi :) As soon as he was born the wives (of the gods) surrounded him, the spontaneously flowing rivers nourished him, for the gods reared you, Pururavas, for a mighty conflict, for the slaughter of the Dasyus.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

As an example of a Ṛk in which the word पुरूरवाः (*purūravāḥ*) is used, Yāska gives an etymology on this Ṛk:
समासतास्मिञ्चायमाने ग्ना गमनादापः । देवपत्न्यो वापि चैनमवर्धयन्नद्यः स्वगूर्ताः स्वयंगामिन्यो वहते च यत्त्वा पुरूरवो रणाय रमणीयाय संग्रामायावर्धयन् दस्युहत्याय च देना देवाः ॥ (*samāsatāsmiñcāyamāne gnā gamanādāpaḥ | devapatnyo vāpi cainamavardhayannadyaḥ svagūrtāḥ svayaṃgāminyo vahate ca yattvā purūravo raṇāya ramaṇīyāya saṃgrāmāyāvardhayan dasyuhatyāya ca denā devāḥ ‖*) (Ni. 10-47)
Here it is said that as soon as this Pururavas was born, all the wives of the gods gathered together at one place and made him grow; or else, since waters have the nature of flowing, ग्ना (*gnā*) is the name for waters (above it was explained as "wives of the gods"); the rivers, full of such waters and flowing of themselves, made this Pururavas grow. In this context the word Pururavas must be explained as the thunderbolt that makes much noise, that is, the middle Agni. The meaning can be given that the rivers, that is, the waters (नदना आपः (*nadanā āpaḥ*)), made this middle Agni grow in the rainy season.
In the latter half too, two kinds of meaning can be given. One meaning: the wives of the gods, the rivers and the gods nourished and reared this newly born Pururavas to fight enemies in delightful battles and to slay the Dasyu people.
Another meaning: taking Pururavas as the thunderbolt or lightning (middle Agni) that makes much noise, the gods made it grow so as to roar and fight with the clouds, and for the slaying of the cloud (Dasyu).

### Printed p. 33
The main purport is this: in this Ṛk the word Pururavas is given two kinds of meaning, the king named Pururavas and the lightning in the atmosphere, or middle Agni. Because this middle Agni (thunderbolt) makes much noise, it is called here by the name Pururavas: puru, "much", rava, "noisy".
In the sense of Pururavas the king: as soon as this king was born, the wives of the gods and the deities presiding over the rivers, all gathering together, nourished and reared him so that, becoming king, he might be able to conquer enemies in battle and slay the Dasyu people.
In the sense of Pururavas as middle Agni: in the rainy season the waters in the form of clouds (ग्नाः (*gnāḥ*) and नद्यः (*nadyaḥ*)) made this middle Agni grow, which roars much and strikes the clouds. That is, the lightning or middle Agni appearing amid the clouds in the rainy season grows, roaring from time to time and striking the clouds (fighting).

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सचा॒ यदा॑सु॒ जह॑ती॒ष्वत्क॒ममा॑नुषेषु॒ मानु॑षो नि॒षेवे॑ ।  
> अप॑ स्म॒ मत्त॒रसं॑ती॒ न भु॒ज्युस्ता अ॑त्रसन्नथ॒स्पृशो॒ नाश्वाः॑ ॥८॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सचा । यत् । आसु । जहतीषु । अत्कं । अमानुषेषु । मानुषः । निसेवे ।  
> अप । स्म । मत् । तरसंती । न । भुज्युः । ताः । अत्रसन् । रथस्पृशः । न । अश्वाः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इदमादित्रीण्यैळवाक्यानि । तत्रादितो द्वाभ्यामुर्वशीमन्याश्च सह स्तौति ।
> यद्यदा सचा सहायभूतः पुरूरवा अत्कं स्वकीयं रूपं । अत्क इति रूपनाम ।
> जहतीषु परित्यजंतीष्वमानुषीषु देवताभूतास्वप्सरःसु मानुषः सन्निषेवे
> अभिमुखं गच्छति तदानीं ता अप्सरसो मन्मत्तोऽपापसृत्यात्रसन् । त्रसतिर्गतिकर्मा।
> 3

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This and the next two Ṛks are the speeches of Aiḷa (Pururavas). Of these, the first two praise Urvaśī and the others together. When Pururavas, as companion, a mortal, comes face to face with these non-human nymphs, divine beings, who are abandoning their own form (अत्क (*atka*) is a name for form), those Apsarases flee away from him. त्रसति (*trasati*) has the sense of going.
### Printed p. 34

> गच्छंति । पलायने दृष्टांतः । तरसंती भुज्युर्न । तरसन्नाम मृगः । तस्य स्त्री
> भुज्युर्भोगसाधनभूता स्त्री मृगी । सा यथा व्याधाद्भीता पलायते । किंच
> रथस्पृशो नाश्वा रथे नियुक्ता अश्वा इव । यथा ते पलायंते तद्वत्पलायंत
> इति । उर्वश्यानेकाभिरस्माभिः सह भोगमनुभुक्तवानसीत्युक्तः प्रत्याचष्टे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

An illustration of the flight is given: like a female तरसन् (*tarasan*), a kind of deer; भुज्युः (*bhujyuḥ*) is the woman who serves for enjoyment, here the doe. As she flees in fear of the hunter, so they flee; and like horses yoked to a chariot, as those run away, so they ran. Being told by Urvaśī, "You have enjoyed pleasure with us, many as we are," he replies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- मानुषः (*mānuṣaḥ*)—Pururavas, in human form
- अत्कं (*atkaṃ*)—their own form
- जहतीषु (*jahatīṣu*)—who had abandoned (it)
- आसु अमानुषेषु (*āsu amānuṣeṣu*)—with these divine women
- सचा (*sacā*)—joining
- निषेवे (*niṣeve*)—became face to face with them; then
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—those divine women
- मत् (*mat*)—leaving me
- तरसंति भुज्युः न (*tarasaṃti bhujyuḥ na*)—like a frightened doe
- रथस्पृशः अश्वाः न (*rathaspṛśaḥ aśvāḥ na*)—like horses harnessed to a chariot
- अप अत्रसन् (*apa atrasan*)—fled in fright

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Pururavas:) When Pururavas, in human form, joined these divine women who had abandoned their bodies and came face to face with them, those divine women left me and fled in fright, like a frightened doe and like horses harnessed to a chariot.

##### English translation
(Pururavas:) When, becoming there companion, (Pururavas) the mortal associated with these immortal (nymphs) who had abandoned their bodies, they fled from me like a timid doe, like horses harnessed to a chariot.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk and the next two are the words of Pururavas, son of Iḷā. In the first two Ṛks (Ṛks 8–9) Pururavas speaks of Urvaśī and the other Apsaras women.
While all those divine women, that is, those born of the gods, who are not human, were together, I, a human (Pururavas), went towards them showing them my own body; then all those Apsaras women moved away from me and fled. How did they flee? As a doe of the kind called तरसत् (*tarasat*), seeing a hunter, flees in fear, or as horses yoked to a chariot (urged by the charioteer) run swiftly, so
### Printed p. 35
these Apsaras women also left me, moved far off and fled. Pururavas says that on seeing me, a human, these Apsaras women, born of divine bodies, quickly ran away from there.
अत्कं (*atkaṃ*)—अत्कं इति रूपनाम । (*atkaṃ iti rūpanāma |*) अत्क (*atka*) means form, shape. Here it means the bodies of the divine women.
आसु जहतीषु अमानुषीषु (*āsu jahatīṣu amānuṣīṣu*)—the purport is that these non-human Apsaras women, seeing the man (Pururavas) coming towards them (मानुषो निषेवे (*mānuṣo niṣeve*)), abandoned the place and went away.
तरसंती न भुज्युः (*tarasaṃtī na bhujyuḥ*)—भुज्युर्भोगसाधनभूता स्त्रीमृगी (*bhujyurbhogasādhanabhūtā strīmṛgī*): भुज्यु (*bhujyu*) means the woman who serves for enjoyment; here, the doe of the kind तरसंती (*tarasaṃtī*). As this doe, on seeing the hunter, runs away in fear that he will kill her, so, the seer describes by illustration, these Apsaras women ran away on seeing the human Pururavas.
रथस्पृशो न अश्वाः (*rathaspṛśo na aśvāḥ*)—a further illustration of running away is given here. As horses yoked to a chariot, urged by the stroke of the charioteer's whip, run swiftly, so these Apsaras women also ran away from Pururavas's presence.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदा॑सु॒ मर्तो॑ अ॒मृता॑सु नि॒स्पृक्सं क्षो॒णीभिः॒ क्रतु॑भि॒र्न  ॒
> प्रंक्ते ।  
> ता आ॒तयो॒ न त॒न्वः॑ शुंभत॒ स्वा अश्वा॑सो॒ न क्री॒ळयो॒ दंद॑शानाः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । आसु । मर्तः । अमृतासु । निस्पृक् । क्षोणीभिः । क्रतुभिः । न । पृंक्ते ।  
> ताः । आतयः । न । तन्वः । शुंभत । स्वाः । अश्वासः । न ! क्रीळयः । दंदशानाः ॥ ९ ॥

### Printed p. 36

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्यदास्वमृतास्वप्सरःसु मर्तो मनुष्यः पुरूरवा निस्पृक् निःशेषेण
> स्पृशन् क्षोणीभिर्वाग्निः क्रतुभिर्न कर्मभिश्च सं पृंक्ते संपर्कं करोति । नकारः
> समुच्चयार्थः । ता अप्सरस आतय आतिभूतास्तदानीं स्वास्तन्व आत्मीयानि रूपाणि न
> शुंभत । न प्रकाशयंति । अश्वासो नाश्वा इव क्रीळयः संक्रीडमाना दंदशाना
> दंदशूका जिह्वाभिरात्मीयाः सृक्वा भक्षयंतः । ते यथा चापल्येन धावंतः
> स्वरूपं न प्रयच्छंति रथिकाय तद्वदिति दुःखाद्ब्रूते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When a mortal, the human Pururavas, in close touch with these immortal Apsarases, comes into contact with them by speech (क्षोणीभिः (*kṣoṇībhiḥ*), taken as *vāgbhiḥ*) and by actions (क्रतुभिः (*kratubhiḥ*)), the particle न (*na*) having the sense of conjunction, then those Apsarases, having become आति (*āti*) birds, do not display their own bodies, their own forms. Like horses playing, दंदशानाः (*daṃdaśānāḥ*), biting, devouring with their tongues, which run in wantonness and do not give their own form to the charioteer, so they do. Thus he speaks out of grief.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अमृतासु (*amṛtāsu*)—who are free from mortality
- आसु (*āsu*)—with these Apsaras women
- मर्तः (*martaḥ*)—the human Pururavas
- निस्पृक् (*nispṛk*)—joining
- क्षोणीभिः (*kṣoṇībhiḥ*)—by words
- ऋतुभिः न (*ṛtubhiḥ na*)—and also by actions
- सं पृंक्ते (*saṃ pṛṃkte*)—comes into contact; then
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—these same Apsaras women
- आतयः (*ātayaḥ*)—in the form of water-fowl
- स्वाः तन्नः (*svāḥ tannaḥ*)—their own bodies
- क्रीळयः (*krīḷayaḥ*)—playing
- दंदशानाः (*daṃdaśānāḥ*)—grazing with grass held in their jaws
- अश्वासो न (*aśvāso na*)—like horses that escape the master's grasp and run away
- न शुंभत (*na śuṃbhata*)—run away without showing their form

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Pururavas:) When the human Pururavas, joining these Apsaras women who are free from mortality, wishes to come into contact with them by words and by his actions, then these same Apsaras women, in the form of water-fowl, hiding their own forms, run away like horses that play, grazing, and escape the master's grasp.

##### English translation
When a mortal mixing with these immortal nymphs has converse with
them with words and actions, they (becoming) ducks do not show their bodies
like playful horses champing (the bit).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Pururavas explains the matter stated in the previous Ṛk in another manner and with another comparison. Here मर्तः (*martaḥ*) means the human Pururavas; अमृतासु (*amṛtāsu*) means the Apsaras women of the divine class, free from death. The human Pururavas, wishing for contact with the deathless Apsaras women
### Printed p. 37
and trying to win them over with words and with actions (gestures), they did not let him see their bodies; that is, not attached to him and not falling into his hands, they took the form of ducks or swans and fled. How did they flee? As thoroughbred horses, of a restless nature, wanting to run off biting the bit, do not act according to the mind of the charioteer but run where they like, so these Apsaras women also ran away. So Pururavas laments, afflicted with grief.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि॒द्युन्न या पतं॑ती॒ दवि॑द्यो॒द्भरं॑ती मे॒ अप्या॒ काम्या॑नि ।  
> जनि॑ष्टो अ॒पो नर्यः॒ सुजा॑तः॒ प्रोर्वशी॑ तिरत दी॒र्घमायुः॑ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विद्युत् । न । या । पतंती । दविद्योत् । भरंती । मे । अप्या । काम्यानि ।  
> जनिष्टो इति । अपः । नर्यः । सुजातः । प्र । उर्वशी । तिरत । दीर्घं । आयुः॥१०॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनयोर्वशीं स्तौति । योर्वशी विद्युन्न विद्युदिव पतंती गच्छंती
> दविद्योत् द्योतते । किं कुर्वती । अप्या । अप इत्यंतरिक्षनाम । तत्संबंधीनि
> व्याप्तानि ना काम्यान्यस्मदभिमतान्युदकानि ना मे मह्यं भरंती संपादयंती ।
> यदागतायास्तस्याः सकाशादपो व्याप्तः कर्मसु नर्यो नरेभ्यो हितः सुजातः
> सुजननः पुत्रो जनिष्टो अजनिष्ट उत्पद्यते तदानीं मनोर्वशी दीर्घमायुः
> प्र तिरत । प्रवर्धयति । प्रजामनु प्रजायसे तदु ते मर्त्यामृतं । तै. ब्रा. १-५-५-६
> इति हि मंत्रः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With these two Ṛks he praises Urvaśī. Urvaśī, falling like lightning (विद्युन्न (*vidyunna*)), shone (दविद्योत् (*davidyot*)). Doing what? अप्या (*apyā*): अप (*apa*) is a name for the atmosphere; bringing (भरंती (*bharaṃtī*)) to me the pervading, desired waters connected with it. When, from her who has come, a son is born, pervading in rites (अपः (*apaḥ*)), beneficial to men (नर्यः (*naryaḥ*)), well-born (सुजातः (*sujātaḥ*)), then Urvaśī prolongs (प्र तिरत (*pra tirata*), प्रवर्धयति (*pravardhayati*)) a long life. He cites the mantra प्रजामनु प्रजायसे तदु ते मर्त्यामृतं । (*prajāmanu prajāyase tadu te martyāmṛtaṃ |*) (Tai. Brā. 1-5-5-6).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- या (*yā*)—the Urvaśī who
- अप्या (*apyā*)—belonging to the atmosphere
- काम्यानि (*kāmyāni*)—and desired waters
- मे (*me*)—to me
- भरंती (*bharaṃtī*)—brings; she; or else, या (*yā*)—the Urvaśī who, अप्या (*apyā*)—desired by me or needed by me, मे (*me*)—my, काम्यानि (*kāmyāni*)—

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विद्युन्न (*vidyunna*)—like lightning
- पतंती (*pataṃtī*)—descending from the heavenly world
- दविद्योत् (*davidyot*)—shines
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—engaged in work
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—beneficial to men
- सुजातः (*sujātaḥ*)—the son of excellent birth
- जनिष्टो (*janiṣṭo*)—when he is born, then
- उर्वशी (*urvaśī*)—Urvaśī
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—my life
- दीर्घं (*dīrghaṃ*)—long
- प्रतीरत (*pratīrata*)—she increases

(The preceding words, up to "…who fulfils my desires, that Urvaśī", stand on the previous page.)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Words of Purūravas) The Urvaśī who brings me the desirable waters of the atmosphere, or who fulfils my desires, comes down like lightning and shines. A son, devoted to work, beneficial to men and of excellent birth, is born of her. Urvaśī lengthens my life.

##### English translation
(Urvashi) who shone like flashing lightning, bringing me the desirable dews (of heaven, has appeared); a son able in act and friendly to man has been born ; Urvashi has prolonged my lengthened existence.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Purūravas addresses Urvaśī alone and praises her. Although the six Apsaras women ran away as soon as they saw him, Urvaśī alone swooped down like lightning from the atmosphere to where he was, stayed with him and shone. She fulfils his desires. In her a good son, devoted to work and a benefactor of people, is born. In this Ṛk Purūravas expresses the assurance that this Urvaśī will grant him long life.

For an example of a Ṛk using the word Urvaśī, Yāska gave an explanation of this Ṛk:
विद्युदिव या पतंत्यद्योतत हरंती मे आप्या काम्यान्युदकान्यंतरिक्षलोकस्य यदा नूनमयं जायेताद्ध्योऽध्यप इति । नर्यो मनुष्यो नृभ्यो हितो नरापत्यमिति वा । सुजातः सुजाततरोऽथोर्वशी प्रवर्धयते दीर्घमायुः ॥ (*vidyudiva yā pataṃtyadyotata haraṃtī me āpyā kāmyānyudakānyaṃtarikṣalokasya yadā nūnamayaṃ jāyetāddhyo 'dhyapa iti | naryo manuṣyo nṛbhyo hito narāpatyamiti vā | sujātaḥ sujātataro 'thorvaśī pravardhayate dīrghamāyuḥ ‖*) (Ni. 11-36)

### Printed p. 39
The explanation (nirvacana) admits two kinds of meaning. One: Purūravas means the lightning and thunder in the atmosphere (puru = much, rava = sound); but here Purūravas is said to be the sound (of thunder) and Urvaśī the lightning. This lightning (Urvaśī), moving again and again in the cloud of the atmosphere, that is, flashing repeatedly, supplies the waters wanted by all in the atmospheric world (हरंती (*haraṃtī*)); rain pours from the cloud-mass accompanied by thunder and lightning. As the fruit of this rain a work beneficial to people, namely growth of plants (the wealth of food and the like), arises. May such an Urvaśī (the cloud with thunder and lightning) increase the life of people by giving food and so on.

The other meaning is the historical view: this Apsaras woman Urvaśī came down from her own abode, the atmosphere (heaven), fulfilled the desires of me, Purūravas, stayed with me and shone. From me a son is born in her, devoted to good works, beneficial to people and of excellent birth. The intention is: may such an Urvaśī give me happiness and joy and long life, that I may live long.

अपः (*apaḥ*) means waters or works.
नर्यः (*naryaḥ*)—मनुष्यो नृभो हितो नरापत्यमिति वा ॥ (*manuṣyo nṛbho hito narāpatyamiti vā ‖*) नरः (*naraḥ*) means a man. नर्यः (*naryaḥ*) means one beneficial to men, or one born of a man.

### Printed p. 40

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इत्थेत्थं गोपीथ्याय । गौः पृथिवी । पीथं पालनं ॥ स्वार्थिकस्तद्धितः ॥
> भूरक्षणाय जज्ञिषे हि । जातोऽसि खलु पुत्ररूपेण । आत्मा वै पुत्रनामेति
> श्रुतेः । पुनर्देव्याह । हे पुरूरवः मे मनोदरे मय्योजोऽपत्योत्पादनसामर्थ्य० दधाथ । मयि निहितवानसि । तत्तथास्तु । अथापि स्थातव्यमिति चेत् तत्राह
> अहं विदुषी भावि कार्यं जानती सस्मिन्नहन् सर्वस्मन्नहनि त्वया कर्तव्यं त्वा
> त्वामशासं । शिक्षितवत्यस्मि । त्वं मे मम वचनं नाशृणोः । न शृणोषि । किं
> त्वमभुगभोक्तापालयिता प्रतिज्ञातार्थमपालयन्नदासि हये जाय इत्यादिकरूपं
> प्रलापं ॥ वदेर्लेट्वयडागमः ! दिवसे त्रिवारं यभस्व एडकबालकमस्माकं पुत्रत्वेन
> परिकल्पय अपत्योत्पादनपर्यंतं वसामि नग्नं त्वां यदाद्राक्षं तदा गच्छामित्येवंरूपो मिथःसमय उर्वशी हाप्सराः पुरूरवसमैळं चकमे तग्ं ह विंदमानोवाच त्रिः स्म माहो वैतसेन दंडेनेत्यादि वाजसनेयकमुदाहृतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

इत्था (*itthā*) is "thus"; गोपीथ्याय (*gopīthyāya*): गौः (*gauḥ*) is the earth, पीथं (*pīthaṃ*) protection (a svārthika taddhita). "You have been born as a son to protect the earth," in accord with the śruti "the self is called son". Again the goddess speaks: "O Purūravas, you have placed in me, in my womb, the power of begetting offspring; so be it. If you ask whether I should still stay—" to that she says: "Knowing what is to come, I instructed you about what you must do on every day. You did not listen to my word. Why do you, a non-protector who has not kept your promise, speak words such as 'Ho wife, stay!'—mere prattle?" वदेर्लेट्वयडागमः (*vaderleṭvayaḍāgamaḥ*) (grammatical note). He then cites the Vājasaneyaka passage on the agreement: "Have intercourse three times a day; regard the ram-lamb as our son; I stay until offspring is born; when I see you naked, I shall go" — such was the mutual pact; "the Apsaras Urvaśī loved Purūravas Aiḷa; finding him, she said, 'Thrice you strike me with a cane of reed'", etc.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरूरवः (*purūravaḥ*)—O Purūravas
- इत्था (*itthā*)—in this way (as a son)
- गोपीथ्याय (*gopīthyāya*)—for the protection of the earth
- जज्जिषे हि (*jajjiṣe hi*)—you have been born
- मे (*me*)—in my womb
- तत् ओजः (*tat ojaḥ*)—that vigour in the form of a son
- दधाध (*dadhādha*)—you have placed
- विदुषी (*viduṣī*)—I, who know the future
- सस्मिन्नहन् (*sasminnahan*)—on all days, what you must do
- त्वा (*tvā*)—to you
- अशासं (*aśāsaṃ*)—have told
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- मे (*me*)—my word
- न अशृणोः (*na aśṛṇoḥ*)—did not hear
- अभुक् (*abhuk*)—having not kept my well-meant word
- किं (*kiṃ*)—why
- वदासि (*vadāsi*)—do you address me and speak?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Words of Urvaśī) O Purūravas, you have been born thus, in the form of a son, to protect the earth. You have placed in my womb vigour in the form of a son. Knowing the future, I told you what you must do on all days. Yet you did not listen to my word. Having not kept my well-meant advice, why do you address me and speak?

##### English translation
(Urvashi :) You have been born thus to protect the earth; you have deposited this vigour in me; knowing (the future) I have instructed you

### Printed p. 41
what to do) every day; you have not listened to me; why do you now address me, neglectful (of my instruction)?

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

विदुषी सस्मिन्नहन् त्वा अशासं (*viduṣī sasminnahan tvā aśāsaṃ*)—अहं भाविकार्यं जानती सर्वस्मिन्नहनि त्वया कर्तव्यं त्वां शिक्षितवत्यस्मि । (*ahaṃ bhāvikāryaṃ jānatī sarvasminnahani tvayā kartavyaṃ tvāṃ śikṣitavatyasmi |*) Since I know what will happen in future, I told you many times before how you should behave towards me.

मे न अशृणोः (*me na aśṛṇoḥ*)—मम वचनं न शृणोषि । (*mama vacanaṃ na śṛṇoṣi |*) You did not listen to my word. What was the word Urvaśī spoke to Purūravas here, and how did he not listen? — अपत्योत्पादनपर्यंतं वसामि । नग्नं त्वां यदाद्राक्षं तदा गच्छामात्येवंरूपो मिथःसमयः । (*apatyotpādanaparyaṃtaṃ vasāmi | nagnaṃ tvāṃ yadādrākṣaṃ tadā gacchāmātyevaṃrūpo mithaḥsamayaḥ |*) Earlier there was an agreement between Purūravas and Urvaśī, and according to it Urvaśī lived with Purūravas like his wife. Then Urvaśī had said at the time of the agreement: "O Purūravas, I shall live with you until a son is born to you in me; but if I get occasion to see you naked, I shall leave you at once and go." Referring to that, she here tells Purūravas that he did not listen to her word. On this matter the commentator cites the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa passage उर्वशी ह्यप्सराः पुरूरवसवमैळं चकमे तग्ं ह विंदमानोवाच त्रिः स्म माहो वैतसेन दंडेन (*urvaśī hyapsarāḥ purūravasavamaiḷaṃ cakame tagṃ ha viṃdamānovāca triḥ sma māho vaitasena daṃḍena*) (Śa. Brā. 11-5-1), etc.

> को दंप॑ती॒ सम॑नसा॒ वि यू॑यो॒दध॒ यद॒ग्निः श्वशु॑रेषु॒  ॑

> कदा । सूनुः । पितरं । जातः । इच्छात् । चक्रन् । न । अश्रु । वर्तयत् । विजानन् ।  
> कः । दंपती इति दंपती । समनसा । वि । यूयोत् । अध । यत् । अग्निः ।  
> श्वशुरेषु । दीदयत् ॥ १२ ॥

### Printed p. 42

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इदं पुरूरवसो वाक्यं । कदा कस्मिन्काले सूनुस्तवोदरजातः सन् पितरं
> मामिच्छात् । इच्छेत् ॥ इषु इच्छायां । लेटि शपीषुगमियमां छ इति छादेशः ।
> लेटोऽडाटावित्यडागमः ॥ कदा वा विजानन्वितरं मामधिगच्छंश्चक्रन् क्रंदमानो
> नाश्रु वर्तयत् । नेति चार्थे । किंच कः किंविधः सन् सूनुः समनसा समनसौ
> समनस्कौ दंपती जायापती त्वां मां च वि यूयोत् । विश्लेषयेत् ॥ यु
> मिश्रणामिश्रणयोः । यौतेश्चांदसः शपः श्लुः । तुजादित्वादभ्यासस्य दीर्घः ॥
> आधाधुनां यद्यदाग्निजव हृदयस्थितस्तेजोरूपो गर्भः श्वशुरेषु दीदयत्
> दीप्यते । दीदयतिर्दिप्तिकर्मेति नैरुक्तो धातुः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is Purūravas' speech. "When will the son, born of your womb, desire me, his father? Or when, knowing me as father, will he cry and shed tears?" इच्छात् (*icchāt*) is from इषु इच्छायां (*iṣu icchāyāṃ*) in the Leṭ; न (*na*) is in the sense of "and". Further: "What kind of son will separate the two of us, husband and wife, of one mind?" यूयोत् (*yūyot*) means "would separate". यदग्निः (*yadagniḥ*): when the fire, the fiery embryo placed in your heart, shines among the parents-in-law. दीदयति (*dīdayati*) is, in the Nairukta, a root meaning shining.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Urvaśī) कदा (*kadā*)—when
- सूनुः (*sūnuḥ*)—the son born in your womb
- पितरं (*pitaraṃ*)—me, his father
- इच्छात् (*icchāt*)—will love
- विजानन् (*vijānan*)—knowing that I am his father
- चक्रन् (*cakran*)—crying out
- न अश्रु वर्तयत् (*na aśru vartayat*)—will shed tears
- आध (*ādha*)—in this situation
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—the embryo in your heart, in the form of fire
- श्वशुरेषु (*śvaśureṣu*)—among your husband's parents
- दीदयत् (*dīdayat*)—shines, at that time
- कः (*kaḥ*)—what kind of son
- समनसा (*samanasā*)—of united minds
- दंपती (*daṃpatī*)—husband and wife, me and you
- वि यूयोत् (*vi yūyot*)—can separate?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Words of Purūravas) O Urvaśī, when will the son born in your womb love me, his father? When, knowing me as his father, will he cry out and shed tears? In this situation, when will the embryo in your heart, in the form of fire, shine among your husband's parents, that is, please the parents? What son can separate us, husband and wife of one mind?

##### English translation
(Pururavas:) When shall a son (born of you) claim me as a father, and, crying, shed a tear on recognizing (me)? What son shall sever husband and wife who are of one mind, now that the fire shines upon your husband's parents?

> अस्मासु निहितं । त्वं परेह्यस्तं । अस्तमिति गृहनाम । स्वगृहं प्रतिगच्छ । हे मूर

> इति भविष्यदर्थे लजि मिष आमादेशः । गुणः । अंत्यलोपश्चांदसः । बहुलवचनादडभावः । आपः । अप्ल व्याप्तौ । लिटि तिजां तिजो भवंतीति थलो णल् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is Urvaśī's speech. "O Purūravas, I shall answer you. Your offspring will shed tears; when the auspicious, desired moment arrives, he will cry, shedding tears." न (*na*) is in the sense of "and". "I send to you that offspring of yours which is placed in me. Go back to your own house (अस्तं (*astaṃ*) is a name for house). O fool, you do not reach me." Grammar notes on हिनव (*hinava*) and आपः (*āpaḥ*) follow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वर्तयते (*vartayate*)—will shed

- चक्रन् (*cakran*)—shedding tears

- यत् ते (*yat te*)—which child of yours
- अस्मे (*asme*)—is placed in me
- तत् (*tat*)—that
- ते (*te*)—to you
- प्र हिनव (*pra hinava*)—I shall send
- अस्तं (*astaṃ*)—to your house
- परेहि (*parehi*)—go back
- मूर (*mūra*)—O fool
- मा (*mā*)—me
- नहि आप्य (*nahi āpya*)—you cannot approach

#### Ṛk 13 (continued)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Urvaśī's words) O Pururavas, I will answer your question. As soon as the proper and auspicious time draws near, your son will come to you shedding tears and addressing you as father. The child lying in my womb I will send to you as soon as he is born. Return to your house. O fool, you cannot approach me.

##### English translation
(Urvashi :) Let me reply. (Your son) will shed tears, crying out and calling aloud when the expected auspicious time arrives; I will send you that (child) which is yours in me, depart to your house, you cannot, simpleton, detain me.

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒दे॒वो अ॒द्य प्र॒पते॒दना॑वृत्परा॒वतं॑ पर॒मां गंत॒वा उ॑ ।  
> अधा॒ शयी॑त॒ निर्ऋ॑तेरु॒पस्थेdधै॑नं॒ वृका॑ रभ॒सासो॑ अ॒द्युः॥१४॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऊं इति ।  
> अध । शयीत । निःऋतेः । उपस्थे । अध । एनं । वृकाः । रभसासः । अद्युः ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथ परिदूनः पुरूरवा उवाच । सुदेवस्त्वया सह सुक्रीडः पतिरद्य
> प्रपतेत् । अत्रैव प्रपततु । अथवानावृदनावृत्तः सन् परमां परावतं दूरादपि
> दूरदेशं गंतवै गंतुं महाप्रस्थानगमनं कुर्यात् । अधाथवा यत्रकुत्रापि
> गंतुं समर्थो निर्ऋतेः पृथिव्या उपस्थे शयीत । शयनं कुर्यात् । यद्वा ।
> निर्ऋतिः पापदेवता । तस्या उपस्थ उत्संगे संनिधौ म्रियतामित्यर्थः । अधाथवैनं
> वृका आरण्याः श्वानो रभसासो वेगवंतोऽद्युः । भक्षयंतु । अत्र वाजसनेयकं ।
> सुदेवोऽद्योद्या बद्धीत प्र ना पतेत्तदेनं वृका वा श्वानो वाद्युरिति हैव
> तदुवाच । शत. ११-५-१-८ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Then Pururavas, distressed, spoke. Let your husband, who sported well with you, fall down right here today; or, never turning back, let him make the great departure to the farthest distance; or, able to go anywhere, let him lie in the lap of the earth (निर्ऋति (*nirṛti*) as the earth). Alternatively, निर्ऋतिः (*nirṛtiḥ*) is the goddess of sin: let him die in her lap, that is, in her presence. Or let wolves, wild dogs, swift and eager, devour him. Sāyaṇa cites the Vājasaneyaka: सुदेवोऽद्योद्या बद्धीत प्र ना पतेत्तदेनं वृका वा श्वानो वाद्युरिति हैव तदुवाच । (*sudevo 'dyodyā baddhīta pra nā patettadenaṃ vṛkā vā śvāno vādyuriti haiva taduvāca |*) Śa. Brā. 11-5-1-8.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुदेवः (*sudevaḥ*)—your husband who sported with you
- अद्य (*adya*)—right now
- प्रपतेत् (*prapatet*)—let him fall down on the ground (or)
- अनावृत् (*anāvṛt*)—without returning
- परमां परावतं (*paramāṃ parāvataṃ*)—to the farthest distant region
- गंत वै (*gaṃta vai*)—let him go out of sight (or let him depart from worldly life)
- अध (*adha*)—or
- निर्ऋतेः (*nirṛteḥ*)—of the goddess of sin named Nirṛti
- उपस्थे (*upasthe*)—on the lap
- शयीत (*śayīta*)—let him lie down
- अथ (*atha*)—or
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—him

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Pururavas's words) O Urvaśī, let your husband who sported with you fall on the ground right now; or let him go, never to return, to the farthest distance (leaving worldly life and vanishing); or let him lie on the lap of the goddess of sin named Nirṛti; or let swift-moving wolves devour him.

##### English translation
(Pururavas :) (Your husband) who sports with you may now depart) never to return (depart) to proceed to a distant region. Either let him sleep upon the lap of Nirriti, or let the swift-moving wolves devour him.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Unable to bear the grief of separation from Urvaśī, Pururavas suggests that it is better to give up life, subjected to manifold afflictions, than to live consumed by sorrow, and he expresses his despair in various laments. This the Ṛk says movingly. Yāska cites this Ṛk as an example of a Ṛk expressing despair or sorrow (Ni. 7-3).
The main sense of the Ṛk: O Urvaśī, how can I, who sported with you till now, live tormented by the pain of separation from you? Should this body of mine not fall lifeless on the ground? Or should I not go to the farthest region, as written earlier? Or lie on a deathbed and be subject to death? Or should wolves not eat me? To Pururavas lamenting thus, Urvaśī in the next Ṛk will reply with words of the same kind and console him.

> १९ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The other (Urvaśī) replied to him. O Pururavas, do not die; do not meet death. Likewise do not fall forth; do not fall right here. Likewise let inauspicious wolves not devour you; the particle उ (*u*) is used in the sense of "indeed". Why do you press upon us so? Do not do so. Then she speaks of the unreliability of such affection: friendships made with women do not exist, they are not lasting. The reason: these friendships are like the hearts of jackals (सालावृकाणां (*sālāvṛkāṇāṃ*)), which kill, as one kills calves and the like that have come to trust. On this the Vājasaneyaka: मैतदादृथा न वै स्रैनग्ं सख्यमस्ति पुनर्गृहानिहीति हैवैनं तदुवाच । (*maitadādṛthā na vai srainagṃ sakhyamasti punargṛhānihīti haivainaṃ taduvāca |*) Śa. Brā. 11-5-19 **NOTE**.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मा मृधाः (*mā mṛdhāḥ*)—do not die
- मा प्र पप्तः (*mā pra paptaḥ*)—do not fall down either
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अशिवासः (*aśivāsaḥ*)—inauspicious
- वृकासः (*vṛkāsaḥ*)—wolves
- मा उक्षन् (*mā ukṣan*)—let them not devour
- सृणानि (*sṛṇāni*)—made with women
- सख्यानि (*sakhyāni*)—friendships
- न वै संति (*na vai saṃti*)—are not lasting
- एता (*etā*)—these
- सालावृकाणां (*sālāvṛkāṇāṃ*)—of the animals called sālāvṛka
- हृदयानि (*hṛdayāni*)—cruel like their hearts (not worthy of trust)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Urvaśī's words) O Pururavas, do not die and do not fall down. Let inauspicious wolves not devour you. Friendship with women is not lasting. These are cruel and unworthy of trust, like the hearts of the animals called sālāvṛka (jackals).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When I, विरूपा (*virūpā*), having left my natural divine form through contact with men, or in various forms suited to my offspring, moved among mortals, men, then I lived four nights-and-autumns (the nights fulfilling), अवसं (*avasaṃ*) = न्यवसं (*nyavasaṃ*); the accusative expresses continuous duration. Then I ate once a day a small drop of ghee; with just that I now move about satisfied.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I, Vasiṣṭha, the one who most causes my companions to dwell well among them, उप शिक्षामि (*upa śikṣāmi*): bring under my control Urvaśī, who fills the atmosphere with her own radiance and is the maker (विमानीं (*vimānīṃ*)) of the colouring रजसः (*rajasaḥ*), water. Let Pururavas, the giver (रातिः (*rātiḥ*)) of good rites, सुकृतस्य (*sukṛtasya*), stand near you. My heart burns; therefore turn back. So the king spoke.

O Aiḷa Pururavas, these gods say this to you: you are मृत्युबंधुः (*mṛtyubaṃdhuḥ*), a binder of death, a kinsman of death, a man who has not come under death's power, as ….

> द्भवसि भविष्यसि प्रजा प्रकर्षेण जायमानस्त्वं ते तव संबंधिनो यष्टव्यान्देवान्नविषा यजासि । यजसि । स्वर्ग उ स्वर्ग एव त्वमपि मादयासे । मादयसेऽस्माभिः
> सह। एवमाहुरित्यर्थः । यस्मादेवं करोषि तस्मादभिलाषं हित्वा सुखी भवेति सेयं
> पुरूरवसं प्रत्युवाच ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(Continuing the verse's explanation.) Aila, the gods say this to you: since you are bound to death, you will be, being born as progeny, one who with oblation worships your related gods who are to be worshipped; and you too will rejoice in heaven with us. This is the meaning: they say so. Because you act in this way, give up your longing and be happy. So she (Urvaśī) replied to Purūravas.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऐळ (*aiḷa*)—O Purūravas, son of Iḷā
- त्वा (*tvā*)—to you
- इमे देवाः (*ime devāḥ*)—these gods
- इति (*iti*)—in this manner
- आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—have said
- यथें (*yatheṃ*)—because
- मृत्युबंधुः (*mṛtyubaṃdhuḥ*)—you, having become subject to death
- भवसि (*bhavasi*)—you are
- एतत् (*etat*)—this is certain
- ते (*te*)—your
- प्रजा (*prajā*)—son (you who are born in the form of a son)
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—with oblation
- यजाति (*yajāti*)—worships (let him worship)
- त्वं अपि (*tvaṃ api*)—you for your part
- स्वर्गे (*svarge*)—in heaven
- मादयासे (*mādayāse*)—you will join us and enjoy delight

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Urvaśī's words) "O Purūravas, (some day) you will become subject to death. This is certain. Your son will worship the gods with oblation. You will join us in heaven and enjoy delight." So the gods have told you.

##### English translation
(Urvashi :) These gods said to you, Aila, since you are indeed subject to death, let your progeny propitiate your gods with oblations, you shall rejoice (with me) in heaven.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Some Western scholars say that nowhere in the Ṛgveda is heaven clearly mentioned, and that it does not explain what connection human beings have with heaven. But in this Ṛk it is clearly said स्वर्ग उ त्वमसि मादयासे (*svarga u tvamasi mādayāse*), "you will enjoy happiness in heaven"; and because भवसि मृत्युबंधुः (*bhavasi mṛtyubaṃdhuḥ*) is said, the matter is clearly stated that a man devoted to good works, having become subject to death and given up this earthly body, then (taking another body) enjoys happiness in heaven.

## Sūkta 96 (Maṇḍala 10)
The ninety-sixth sūkta

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथ प्र ते मह इति त्रयोदशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं । बरुर्नामांगिरस ऋषिः
> इंद्रस्य पुत्रः सर्वहरिर्वा नाम । द्वादशीत्रयोदश्यौत्रिष्टुभौ शिष्टा एकादश जगत्यः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now the sixth sūkta, "Pra te mahe", of thirteen Ṛks. The seer is Baru of the Āṅgirasa line, or else Sarvahari, a son of Indra. The twelfth and thirteenth Ṛks are in the triṣṭubh metre; the remaining eleven are jagatī.

### Printed p. 51

> इंद्रस्याश्व हरी । तयोरत्र स्तूयमानत्वात्तद्देवताकमिदं । तथा चानुक्रांतं ।
> प्र ते सप्तोना बरुः सर्वहरिर्वैंद्रो हरिस्तुतिर्द्वित्रिष्टुबंतं ॥ अतिरात्रे तृतीये
> पर्याये ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन एतत्सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । प्र ते मह ऊती शचीवस्तव
> वीर्येणेति याज्या । आ. ६-४ । इति ॥ षोडशिशस्त्रेऽप्याद्यस्तृचः शंसनीयः । सूत्रितं
> च । प्र ते महे विदथे शंसिषं हरी इति तिस्रो जगत्यः । आ. ६-२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The deity is the two horses (Hari) of Indra; since they are praised here, the sūkta has them as its deity. So the Anukramaṇī says: प्र ते सप्तोना बरुः सर्वहरिर्वैंद्रो हरिस्तुतिर्द्वित्रिष्टुबंतं (*pra te saptonā baruḥ sarvaharirvaiṃdro haristutirdvitriṣṭubaṃtaṃ*). In the Atirātra, in the third paryāya, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin recites this sūkta. It is also given in the sūtra: प्र ते मह ऊती शचीवस्तव वीर्येणेति याज्या (*pra te maha ūtī śacīvastava vīryeṇeti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-4). In the Ṣoḍaśin śastra too the first three Ṛks are to be recited; the sūtra says: प्र ते महे विदथे शंसिषं हरी इति तिस्रो जगत्यः (*pra te mahe vidathe śaṃsiṣaṃ harī iti tisro jagatyaḥ*) (Ā. 6-2).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta "Pra te mahe" is the sixth sūkta in the eighth anuvāka. It has thirteen Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Baru of the Aṅgirasa gotra, or else Sarvahari, a son of Indra. The twelfth and thirteenth Ṛks of this sūkta are in the triṣṭubh metre; the remaining eleven Ṛks are in the jagatī metre. Since the two horses of Indra called Hari are praised in this sūkta, those horses of Indra are its deity. The Anukramaṇī says what has been quoted above. It is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 6-4), which says that in the third paryāya of the sacrifice called Atirātra the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin should recite this sūkta; and (Ā. 6-2) that at the time of reciting the Ṣoḍaśin śastra mantras the first three Ṛks of this sūkta should be recited.

Sūkta 96
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 8; Sūkta 96.
Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 5; Vargas 5, 6, 7.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 13.
Seer: Baru Sarvahari, son of Indra.
Deity: praise of the two Haris.
Metre: 1–11 jagatī; 12, 13 triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र ते॑ म॒हे वि॒दथे॑ शंसिषं॒ हरी॒ प्र ते॑ वन्वे व॒नुषो॑ ॒ ॑
> हर्यतं मदं ।  
> घृ॒तं न यो हरि॑भि॒श्चारु॒ सेच॑त॒ आ त्वा॑ विशंतु॒ हरि॑वर्पसं॒  ॑
> गिरः ॥ १ ॥

> मदु ।  
> धृतं । न । यः । हरिभिः । चारु । सेचते । आ । त्वा । विशंतु । हरिवर्पसं । गिरः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तव हरी अश्वा महे महति विदथे यज्ञे प्र शंसिषं । अशंसिषं।
> अस्ताविषं । तथा वनुषः ॥ वनु हिंसायां ॥ हिंसकस्य ते तव हर्यतं ॥ हर्य
> गतिकांतोः । तस्यौणादिकोऽतच् । चित्स्वरेणांतोदात्तः ॥ कमनीयं मदं प्र
> वन्ने । प्रयाचेऽस्मदभिमतं ॥ वनु याचने ॥ य. इंद्रो हरिभिर्हरितवर्णैरश्वैर्मद्यागं गश्वा चारु चरणीयं धृतं न धृतमिव सुपूतमुदकं सेचते वर्षति
> तं तादृशं हरिवर्पसं । वर्प इति रूपनाम । हरितरूपं त्वा त्वामा विशंतु
> गिरोऽस्मदीयाः स्तुतिवाचस्तव मदाय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, I have praised your two bay horses at the great sacrifice. Further, I ask for your agreeable exhilaration, for you are the destroyer (of foes); the word हर्यतं (*haryataṃ*) means "desirable". I ask, I solicit, what we desire. Indra is he who, with his horses of yellow colour, pours down चारु (*cāru*), graceful, धृतं न (*dhṛtaṃ na*) "like clarified butter", that is, well-purified water. वर्प (*varpa*) is a name for form. Let our praise-words enter you, whose form is yellow, for your exhilaration.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते (*te*)—your
- हरी (*harī*)—horses
- महे (*mahe*)—great
- विदथे (*vidathe*)—at the sacrifice
- प्र शंसिषं (*pra śaṃsiṣaṃ*)—I praise
- वनुषं (*vanuṣaṃ*)—destroyer of foes
- ते (*te*)—from you
- हरतं (*harataṃ*)—attractive
- मदं (*madaṃ*)—delight
- प्रवन्वे (*pravanve*)—I ask
- यः (*yaḥ*)—you who
- हरिभिः (*haribhiḥ*)—with your horses
- चारु (*cāru*)—beneficial
- धृतं न (*dhṛtaṃ na*)—water that is like clarified butter
- सेचते (*secate*)—do you pour down; such a one
- हरिवर्पसं (*harivarpasaṃ*)—having a golden-coloured form
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—our praises
- आ विशंतु (*ā viśaṃtu*)—let them enter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, I praise your horses at the great sacrifice. I ask from you, the destroyer of foes, attractive delight. May our praises enter you, golden-coloured, who together with your horses pour down beneficial water like clarified butter.

##### English translation
I glorified your bay horses, Indra, at the great sacrifice, I solicit the agreeable exhilaration of you, the destroyer of foes. May my praises attain to you, whose form is yellow, who, with your horses, shower (water) like beautiful butter.

### Printed p. 53

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Though here and there a few Ṛks praise Indra's horses, in this sūkta Indra's horses alone are praised throughout. The style is of a high standard. Because the word Hari is used in every pāda of every Ṛk, the recitation of the mantras sounds rhymed and pleasant to hear; this is the distinctive feature of this sūkta.

> हरिं॒ हि योनि॑म॒भि ये स॒मस्व॑रन्हि॒न्वंतो॒ हरी॑ दि॒व्यं यथा॒  ॑
> सदः॑ ।  
> आ यं पृ॒णंति॒ हरि॑भि॒र्न धे॒नव॒ इंद्रा॑य शू॒षं हरि॑वंतमर्चत ॥ २ ॥

> सदः ।  
> आ । यं । पृणंति । हरिभिः । न । धेनवः । इंद्राय । शूषं । हरिवंतं । अर्चत ॥२॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये पूर्वे स्तोतार ऋषयो योनिमिंद्रस्य स्थानभूतं हरिमश्वमभि
> समस्वरन् ॥ स्वृ शब्दोपतापयोः ॥ अभिसंस्तुवंति । किं कुर्वंतः । दिव्यं देवसंबंधि सदो यागगृहं यथा प्रेरयंतींद्रं तथा हरी आश्वा हिन्वंतः प्रेरयंतः।
> सोमेऽभिषुते सति स्वयमेवेंद्रो रथेऽश्वा प्रेरयति अतः स्तोत्यणां
> हरिप्रेरणत्वं । यद्वा । दिव्यं सद इंद्रः प्राप्नुयाद्यथा तथा हरी स्तुतिभिर्हिन्वंतः
> प्रेरयंतः । यमिंद्रं धेनवो नवप्रसूतिका गावो यथा पृणंति क्षीरादिभिः ।
> अत्र पुरस्तादुपचारोऽपि नकार उपमार्थीयः । हरिभिर्हरितवर्णैः सोमैरा
> पृणंति पूरयंति च । तथा यूयमसींद्रायेंद्रस्य हरिवंतं शूषं बलमर्चित ।
> पूजयत हे स्तोतारः स्तुतिभिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ancient praising seers who समस्वरन् (*samasvaran*) (the root स्वृ (*svṛ*) in the sense of sound and heat) praised together the horse Hari, the seat of Indra: doing what? Urging the two horses, as one urges Indra to the divine sacrificial house, the house belonging to the gods. When Soma has been pressed, Indra himself drives the horses on his chariot; hence the praisers are said to urge the horses. Or else: the praisers urge the two horses with praises so that Indra may reach the divine house. The Indra whom, as newly calved cows fill with milk and the like, they fill and satisfy with Soma of yellow colour (here the particle न (*na*) of the preceding clause also has the sense of comparison). So, O praisers, with praises worship the horse-possessing might of that Indra.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The praising seers, urging the horses as if to bring Indra to the venerable sacrificial house, have praised the horse that carries Indra. As cows satisfy with milk and the like, so worship (praise) the horse-possessing might of that Indra whom they fill and satisfy with green-coloured Soma juices.

##### English translation
You, who have praised the horses, the seat of Indra, urging the horses so that (Indra may reach) the divine assembly, do you worship the horse-possessing might of Indra, whom men delight with the golden-tinted Soma juices as milch cows (with their milk.)

> नि मिमिक्षिरे । निषिक्तानि बभूवुः ॥ मिहेः सनंतात्मर्मणि लिटि रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That thunderbolt of this Indra is yellow, and is made of iron, being of the essence of metal; that yellow thunderbolt is निकामः (*nikāmaḥ*), exceedingly desirable. It is a striker (आ हंता (*ā haṃtā*)) of enemies. Such a thunderbolt is in his two hands (गभस्त्योः (*gabhastyoḥ*)); "is" is to be supplied. This Indra is द्युम्ना (*dyumnā*): द्युम्न (*dyumna*) is shining wealth, and he has it. He is सुशिप्रः (*suśipraḥ*), fair-jawed, हरिमन्युसायकः (*harimanyusāyakaḥ*): one whose anger and arrow are slayers of foes and go against them. Or else: one who has anger, the slayer of foes, and the arrow. What more need be said? The forms in Indra are yellow, नि मिमिक्षिरे (*ni mimikṣire*), they were infused; this is the form of the root *mih* in the desiderative-based perfect, middle.

- निकामः (*nikāmaḥ*)—exceedingly attractive
- आयसः (*āyasaḥ*)—made of steel
- सः (*saḥ*)—that thunderbolt
- अस्य (*asya*)—of Indra
- गभस्त्योः (*gabhastyoḥ*)—being in the hands
- आ (हंता) (*ā (haṃtā)*)—is a destroyer of foes
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- द्युम्ना (*dyumnā*)—wealthy
- सुशिप्रः (*suśipraḥ*)—having excellent cheeks
- हरिमन्युसायकः (*harimanyusāyakaḥ*)—having anger and arrows that destroy foes
- हरिता रूपा (*haritā rūpā*)—golden-coloured forms of many kinds
- इंद्रे (*iṃdre*)—in Indra
- नि मिमिक्षिरे (*ni mimikṣire*)—have joined together

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That thunderbolt of Indra which is green in colour, exceedingly attractive and made of steel, being in Indra's hands is a destroyer of foes. Indra is wealthy, has excellent cheeks, and has anger and arrows that destroy foes. Golden-coloured forms of many kinds have joined together in Indra.

##### English translation
That is his thunderbolt, yellow, made of iron, the destroyer (of foes) desirable, it is in his hands; (he is) possessed of riches handsome-jawed, possessed of a shaft and anger which destroys (his foes)-many golden-tinted forms are mixed in Indra.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दि॒वि न के॒तुरधि॑ धायि हर्य॒तो वि॒व्यच॒द्वज्रो॒ हरि॑तो॒ न  ॑
> रंह्या ।  
> तु॒ददहिं॒ हरि॑शिप्रो॒ य आ॑य॒सः स॒हस्र॑शोका अभवद्धरिंभ॒रः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दिवि । न । केतुः । अधि । धायि । हर्यतः । विव्यचत् । वज्रः । हरितः । न । रंह्या ।  
> तुदत् । अहिं । हरिशिप्रः । यः । आयसः । सहस्रशोकाः । अभवत् । हरिंभरः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दिव्यंतरिक्षे केतुः प्रकाशेन सर्वस्य प्रज्ञापक आदित्य इव स यथाधि निहितः
> एवमयमिंद्रोऽधि धायि । अध्यधायि । स्तोतृभिरधि निहितः । किंचेंद्रस्य वज्रो
> हर्यतः स्पृहणीयः सन् विव्यचत्। व्याप्नोति वाप्तव्यं शत्रुसंघं । तत्र दृष्टांतः।
> हरितो न हरितवर्णा अध्वाहर्तारो वाश्वा आदित्यसंबंधिनः । ते यथा रंह्या
> रंहणेन वेगेन व्याप्पुवंति व्याप्तव्यं । योऽस्य वज्र आयसोऽयोविकारोऽहिं
> वृत्रं मेघं वा तुदत् हिनस्ति । योऽयं महानुभावो हरिशिप्रः सोमपानरभसेन हरितवर्णनासिकस्तद्वर्णहनुर्वा हरिंभरो हर्योर्भर्तेंद्रः सहस्रशोका
> अभवत् ॥ शुच दीप्तौ li अपरिमितदीप्तिर्भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Like the sun, which is a केतुः (*ketuḥ*) (a banner), making everything known by its light, set in the sky, so Indra has been set up, placed by his worshippers. Further, Indra's thunderbolt, being desirable (हर्यतः (*haryataḥ*)), pervades, that is, reaches, the host of foes it is to reach. The illustration: as the green-tinted horses that carry the sun along the road traverse by their speed what is to be traversed, so the bolt does. The bolt of iron, a product of iron, strikes Ahi, that is, Vṛtra or the cloud. This great Indra, हरिशिप्रः (*hariśipraḥ*), has either a green-tinted nose from the exhilaration of drinking Soma, or green-tinted jaws; he is हरिंभरः (*hariṃbharaḥ*), the bearer (lord) of the two bay horses, and he became सहस्रशोकाः (*sahasraśokāḥ*): he is of boundless splendour.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवि (*divi*)—in the sky
- केतुः न (*ketuḥ na*)—like the sun, who is a banner
- अधि धायि (*adhi dhāyi*)—Indra too has been established
- रंह्या (*raṃhyā*)—by their speed
- हरितो न (*harito na*)—as the sun's horses reach their goal
- हर्यतः (*haryataḥ*)—attractive
- वज्रः (*vajraḥ*)—the thunderbolt
- विव्यचत् (*vivyacat*)—approaches the host of foes
- यः (*yaḥ*)—of which Indra
- आयसः (*āyasaḥ*)—the thunderbolt made of steel
- अहिं (*ahiṃ*)—the enemy
- तुदत् (*tudat*)—strikes, such
- हरिशिप्रः (*hariśipraḥ*)—having cheeks green from drinking Soma
- हरिंभरः (*hariṃbharaḥ*)—the lord of horses, Indra
- सहस्रशोकाः (*sahasraśokāḥ*)—possessing lustre of many kinds
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—has become

### Printed p. 57

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the sun, the banner-like illuminator of the world, is established in the sky, so Indra too is established. As the sun's horses reach their goal by their speed, the attractive thunderbolt approaches the host of foes. Indra, whose steel thunderbolt strikes the enemy, who has cheeks green from Soma-drinking and is the lord of horses, has become possessed of lustre of many kinds.

##### English translation
He has been placed (by his worshippers) in the sky, like the banner
(of light, the sun). His desirable bolt reaches (the foe) as bay horses (of the
sun reach their aim) through speed. The iron (thunderbolt), of indra with
yellow jaws, which smote Ahi, (he Indra), lord of horses, shone with a
thousand lustres.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वंत्व॑महर्यथा॒ उप॑स्तुतः॒ पूर्वे॑भिरिंद्र हरिकेश॒ यज्ज॑भिः ।  
> त्वं ह॑र्यसि॒ तव॒ विश्व॑मु॒क्क्य१॒॑गमसा॑मि॒ राधो॑ हरिजात  ॒
> हर्यतं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वंत्वं । अहर्यथाः । उपस्तुतः । पूर्वेभिः । इंद्र । हरिजीश । यज्वभिः ।  
> त्वं । हर्यसि । तव । विश्वं । उक्त्यं । असामि । राधः । हरिजात । हर्यतं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र हे हरिकेश हरितरोमवदश्व त्वंत्वं त्वमेव सर्वत्र यज्ञेऽहर्यथाः । अकामयथाः स्तोत्रं हविर्वा । कीदृशस्त्वं । पूर्वभिः पूर्वतनैर्यज्वभिर्यजमानैरुपस्तुतः सन् । हे हरिजात हरितवर्णः सन्प्रादुर्भूत हारकप्रादुर्भाव वा । शत्रुवधार्थं प्रादुर्भूतेत्यर्थः । हे तादृशेंद्र त्वं तव । स्वभूतमिति
> शेषः । विश्वं व्याप्तं सोमचरुपुरोडाशादिरूपं सर्वं ना । यद्वा! यत्र यानि
> यानि हवींषि दीयंते तत्सर्वं वा । तथोक्थ्यं प्रशस्यमसाम्यसाधारणमनमं
> कृत्सं हर्यतं कांतं राधोऽन्नं हविर्लक्षणं हर्यसि । कामयसे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, O हरिकेश (*harikeśa*) (horse with green-tinted hair), you alone, in every sacrifice, have desired the praise-song or the oblation, praised as you are by the ancient sacrificers. O हरिजात (*harijāta*), who have appeared in a green-tinted form, or whose appearance is that of one who carries off (the foe), that is, who have appeared for the slaying of enemies: you desire your own whole offering, pervading all, in the form of Soma, cooked offerings, cakes and the like; or else whatever offerings are given at a sacrifice, all of that. Likewise you desire the praiseworthy, unequalled, undiminished, delightful food (राधः (*rādhaḥ*)), whose nature is the oblation.

O Indra, lord of horses with golden hair, praised by the sacrificers, you alone desire the oblation in every sacrifice. O Indra, who have appeared in a golden form, you desire all the praises that are to be offered to you, and all the unequalled and attractive oblations.

##### English translation
Indra, with horses of yellow locks, when praised by ancient
worshippers, you desired the oblation; you who are manifested of a golden hue
desire your universal praise, your peculiar and delightful (sacrificial) food.

> ता तौ प्रसिद्धौ हर्यता हर्यतौ गंतारौ कांतौ वा हरी हरितवर्णावश्नौ

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those well-known, desirable (going or lovely) two bay horses, green-tinted, carry in the chariot Indra, the rejoicing one, worthy of praise, the wielder of the thunderbolt, for the exhilaration (मदे (*made*)); that is, they bear him and bring our sacrifice to him. For this lovely Indra many libations, the morning and the other ones, and green-tinted Soma-juices are stored up, deposited.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ता (*tā*)—those well-known
- हर्यता (*haryatā*)—attractive
- हरी (*harī*)—green-tinted horses
- मंदिनं (*maṃdinaṃ*)—the joyful
- स्तोम्यं (*stomyaṃ*)—the praiseworthy
- वज्रिणं (*vajriṇaṃ*)—the wielder of the thunderbolt
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- मदे (*made*)—for joy
- रथे (*rathe*)—in the chariot
- वहतः (*vahataḥ*)—bring
- हर ते (*hara te*)—having an attractive form **NOTE**
- अस्मै इंद्राय (*asmai iṃdrāya*)—for this Indra
- पुरूणि (*purūṇi*)—abundant
- हरयः (*harayaḥ*)—green-tinted
- सवनानि (*savanāni*)—fit for the sacrifice
- सोमाः (*somāḥ*)—Soma-juices
- दधन्विरे (*dadhanvire*)—are stored up

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The well-known, attractive, green-tinted horses carry Indra, the joyful, praiseworthy wielder of the thunderbolt, in the chariot for joy. For Indra of attractive form, abundant, green-tinted Soma-juices fit for the sacrifice are stored up.

##### English translation
These two delightful bay horses bring the thunderer, the rejoicing and laudable Indra, in his car to the exhilaration (of the soma); for him the beloved one, many libations of the yellow-tinted Soma-juices are stored up.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हरिवंतं सोमवंतं यज्ञमानशे । व्याप्प्नोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Green-tinted Soma-juices are stored up in plenty for Indra's desire, that is, to satisfy him. Those green-tinted juices urge on the two swift horses for Indra, who is steadfast and does not flee in battle. The chariot that goes with spirited green-tinted horses to the battle, to which brave men resort (जोषं (*joṣaṃ*)), that same chariot reaches Indra's own desirable sacrifice, the one furnished with Soma (हरिवंतं (*harivaṃtaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अरं (*araṃ*)—complete
- कामाय (*kāmāya*)—for (Indra's) satisfaction
- हरयः (*harayaḥ*)—green-tinted Soma-juices
- दधन्विरे (*dadhanvire*)—are stored up
- हरयः (*harayaḥ*)—those same Soma-juices
- स्थिराय (*sthirāya*)—to carry Indra, who stands firm in battle
- तुरा (*turā*)—swift
- हरी (*harī*)—the horses
- हिन्सन् (*hinsan*)—urge on **NOTE**
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whose chariot of Indra
- अर्वद्भिः (*arvadbhiḥ*)—swift
- हरिभिः (*haribhiḥ*)—together with horses
- जोषं (*joṣaṃ*)—to the battle frequented by heroes
- ईयते (*īyate*)—goes
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same chariot
- अस्य (*asya*)—to Indra
- कामं (*kāmaṃ*)—the desired
- हरिवंतं (*harivaṃtaṃ*)—furnished with Soma, sacrifice
- आनशे (*ānaśe*)—enters

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For Indra's complete satisfaction green-tinted Soma-juices are stored up. Those same juices urge the horses to carry Indra, who is steadfast in battle. The chariot of Indra that goes with swift horses to the battle frequented by heroes, that same chariot enters also the sacrifice desired by Indra and furnished with Soma.

##### English translation
Yellow-tinted (Soma-juices) are stored up sufficient for his desire, the yellow-tinted juices urge his two swift bay horses for the stalwart (Indra). His (chariot) which rushes with spirited bay horses to the conflict, has reached his desire (the sacrifice) in which the Soma is presented.

> सोमैर्वा वाजिनीवसुः । वाजिनमन्नं हविर्लक्षणं । तदस्या अस्तित्वि वाजिनी क्रिया ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra has green-tinted beard and green-tinted hair, and a heart of iron, that is, he is the slayer of enemies. This Indra grows strong at the swift drinking (तुरस्सेये (*turasseye*)) of Soma, drinking the green-tinted Soma. He is also वाजिनीवसुः (*vājinīvasuḥ*), through the praisers, the horses or the Soma-juices. *vājinaṃ* is food, the oblation; the action possessing it is वाजिनी (*vājinī*); that is his wealth: his wealth is the sacrifice. Or else *vājinaṃ* itself is वाजिनी (*vājinī*), and that itself is his wealth. Such an Indra, having yoked his two bay horses to the chariot, is to carry us across all our troubles.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, whose heart is hard toward his enemies, who has a golden-brown beard and golden-brown hair, who grows strong while drinking the green-hued Soma at the time of the quickly drunk Soma, and who is rich in wealth in the form of oblations through his swift horses: may that Indra yoke his horses to the chariot and carry us across our paths of sorrow.

##### English translation
The yellow-bearded, the yellow-haired, iron-hearted Indra, the drinker of the yellow (Soma-juice), who has been invigorated by the Soma which has to be quickly quaffed, who is rich in sacrificial food through his swift bay horses, may he drive his two bay horses safe through all difficulties.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains: the two bay (green-hued) horses of Indra "fly forth", that is, they set Indra on the chariot and speed to our sacrifice. Or else: his two green-hued eye-pupils dart toward the Soma. An illustration is given: as the two ladles (sruva), vessels filled with oblation, are poured out for the offering, so his two golden jaws shake for the food, the Soma, the offering made to him.

### Printed p. 63

> सोमलक्षणायान्नाय दविध्वतः कंपयतः पुरतः प्रत्तस्य सोमस्य प्रीत्या चलतः ।
> तथा यद्यदा कृते संस्कृते चमसे वर्तमानं मदस्य मदकरं हर्यतस्य
> कांतमंधसोऽन्नं सोमं पीत्वा हरी अश्नौ प्र मर्मृजत् प्रमार्ष्टि । तदानीं
> स्तुत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The jaws tremble for the food in the form of Soma, moving with pleasure at the Soma offered before him. And when, from the Soma that is in the well-prepared cup, the intoxicating, desirable food, he has drunk, he strokes his two horses. At that time, the meaning is, he is praised.

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- कृते (*kṛte*)—well prepared

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As vessels full of oblation are poured out in haste to offer the oblation, so the green-hued horses of Indra run toward the sacrifice, and his golden jaws tremble to eat the oblation. That Indra, having drunk the food (Soma), which is in the well-prepared camasa cup, intoxicating and attractive, and being satisfied, is praised as he strokes his horses.

##### English translation
He whose bay horses alight (upon the soma) like two ladles, whose yellow jaws tremble (with eagerness) for the sacrificial food. (is praised) when having drunk of the delicious exhilarating beverage in the prepared cup. he rubs down his bay horses.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And the dwelling of the desirable Indra belongs to heaven and earth. That same Indra, owning horses, goes to battle (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)) like a horse. For, Indra, the great praise (धिषणा (*dhiṣaṇā*)) desires you, endowed with might and strength; चित् (*cit*) is a filler. Therefore he goes वाजं (*vājaṃ*) roaring. That being so, you bestow great food on the sacrificer who desires you; here too चित् (*cit*) is a filler.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धिषणा (*dhiṣaṇā*)—praise
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—Indra endowed with strength
- अहर्यत् (*aharyat*)—desires
- (O Indra) हर्यतः (*haryataḥ*)—to the sacrificer, your devotee
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—great
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—food
- आ दधिषे (*ā dadhiṣe*)—you provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The dwelling of Indra of attractive form belongs to both heaven and earth. That same Indra, owning horses, rushes to battle like a horse. Praise full of greatness desires the mighty Indra. O Indra, you provide great food to the sacrificer, your devotee.

##### English translation
The dwelling of the gracious (Indra) is in heaven and earth; exhilarated by the Soma he rushes impetuously as a charger to battle. The earnest prayer desires (Indra endowed) with might; you bestow ample food on the devout (worshippcr).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, desiring, you fill by your greatness the two worlds, heaven and earth ("fill" is to be supplied). You also quickly desire ever newer, pleasing praise worthy of reflection (मन्म (*manma*)). O असुर (*asura*), mighty one: असुः (*asuḥ*) is breath, and the one having it; the affix रः (*raḥ*) is in the sense of possession. Such an Indra: गोः (*goḥ*) is a singular of the class, "of the waters"; make manifest abundantly the desirable dwelling or the place, of the waters possessing the stated qualities, to the sun, the taker of water.

- मन्म (*manma*)—praise
- हरसि (*harasi*)—you desire
- असुर (*asura*)—O mighty Indra
- हरये (*haraye*)—to the water-drinking
- सूर्याय (*sūryāya*)—sun
- गोः (*goḥ*)—of the waters
- हरतं (*harataṃ*)—attractive
- पस्यं (*pasyaṃ*)—dwelling (or place)
- प्र (*pra*)—greatly
- अविष्कृधि (*aviṣkṛdhi*)—make manifest

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you of attractive form fill both heaven and earth by your greatness. You always desire praise that is ever new and beneficial.

### Printed p. 66
O mighty Indra, make manifest to the water-drinking sun the attractive dwelling, or the place, of the waters.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you of green-hued jaws (हरिशिप्रं (*hariśipraṃ*)), desiring the sacrifice: let the horses yoked to the chariot (प्रयुजः (*prayujaḥ*)), having placed you on the chariot, carry you to the sacrificers, the priests and patrons (जनानां (*janānāṃ*)). In the manner in which, desiring the sweet Soma juice collected in the cups and so on, the sacrificial means, prepared by the ten fingers (दशोणिं (*daśoṇiṃ*); *oṇayaḥ* are the fingers), you drink, so let them carry you to the battle (सधमादे (*sadhamāde*)) for victory.

O Indra, you of golden cheeks, desiring the sacrifice: let the horses yoked to the chariot, having seated you on the chariot, bring you to the sacrificers. > कर्मणि षष्ठ्यावेते । अभिषुतान्ना तःसवनिकान्नोमानित्यर्थः । तानपाः । अपिबः । हे
> हरिव इतींद्रसंबोधनं । हरिभ्यामश्वाभ्यां तद्वन् । यद्वा । ऋक्सामात्मकाभ्यां
> हरिभ्यां युक्त । ऋक्सामे वा इंद्रस्य हरी । ऐ- ब्रा. २-२४ । तै. सं. ६-५-९-२
> ताभ्यामेष हरतीति ब्राह्मणं । अथो अपि चेदं माध्यंदिनं सवनं केवलं ते
> तवैनासाधारणं । माध्यंदिनं सवनं केवलं ते । ऋ. ४-३५-७ । इति हि मंत्रांतरं ।
> तस्मिन्सवने हे इंद्र मधुमंतं माधुर्योपेतं सोमं ममद्धि । पिब । आस्वादयेत्यर्थः । मदिरत्रास्वादनकर्मा । पिबंतु मदंतु वियंत्विति च मंत्रः । सत्रा
> वृषन् । सत्राशब्दो भूयिष्ठवचनः । हे भूयिष्ठ वर्षितरिंद्र जठर आ वृषस्व ।
> आसिंचस्व ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is the yājyā of the Ṣoḍaśi-śastra. The sūtra says: एवा हि शक्रो वशी हि शक्र इति जपित्वापः पूर्णेषां हरिवः सुतानामिति यजति (*evā hi śakro vaśī hi śakra iti japitvāpaḥ pūrṇeṣāṃ harivaḥ sutānāmiti yajati*) (Ā. 6-2). "O Indra, of the previous pressed offerings", that is, of the Soma pressed and made ready for the morning pressing (the genitive is in the sense of the object), you drank those. हरिवः (*harivaḥ*) is a vocative of Indra: one who has the two bay horses; or else one yoked with the two bays that are the Ṛk and the Sāman. Ai. Brā. 2-24 and Tai. Saṃ. 6-5-9-2 say: "The Ṛk and the Sāman are Indra's two bays; with them he carries (the offering)", so says the Brāhmaṇa. अथो (*atho*): moreover, this midday pressing is yours alone, not shared. Another mantra is quoted: माध्यंदिनं सवनं केवलं ते (*mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanaṃ kevalaṃ te*) (Ṛ. 4-35-7). At that pressing, O Indra, drink the sweet Soma, the one endowed with sweetness; ममद्धि (*mamaddhi*) means drink, enjoy; the root मदि (*madi*) has the sense of tasting; the mantra says *pibaṃtu madaṃtu viyaṃtu*. सत्रा (*satrā*) means in great abundance. O abundant showerer, Indra, pour (it) into your belly.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हरिवः (*harivaḥ*)—O Indra, who are yoked with horses
- पूर्वेषां (*pūrveṣāṃ*)—formerly, prepared for the morning pressing
- सुतानां (*sutānāṃ*)—of the pressed Soma juices
- अपाः (*apāḥ*)—you have drunk
- अथो (*atho*)—likewise
- इदं सवनं (*idaṃ savanaṃ*)—the juices pressed for this midday pressing also
- केवलं ते (*kevalaṃ te*)—have been pressed with you alone in view
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- मधुमंतं (*madhumaṃtaṃ*)—the tasty
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma juice
- ममद्धि (*mamaddhi*)—drink it and be gladdened
- सत्रा (*satrā*)—in great abundance
- वृषन् (*vṛṣan*)—O Indra, who pour down rain
- जठरे (*jaṭhare*)—in your belly
- आ वृषस्व (*ā vṛṣasva*)—pour this in

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, yoked with horses, you have drunk the pressed Soma juices that were formerly prepared for the morning pressing. Likewise the juices pressed for this midday pressing have been pressed with you alone in view. O Indra, drink the tasty Soma and be gladdened. O Indra, who pour down rain in great abundance, pour this into your belly.

##### English translation
Lord of horses, you drank of previous libations, this sacrifice is for you alone; exhilarate yourself, Indra, with sweet Soma; showerer of copious rain, shower it into your belly.

### Printed p. 69

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That this Ṛk beginning असाः पूर्णेषां (*asāḥ pūrṇeṣāṃ*) **NOTE** is to be recited as the yājyā mantra of the Ṣoḍaśi-śastra is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: एवा हि शक्रो वशी हि शक्र इति जपित्वापः पूर्णेषां हरिवः सुतानामिति यजति (*evā hi śakro vaśī hi śakra iti japitvāpaḥ pūrṇeṣāṃ harivaḥ sutānāmiti yajati*) (Ā. 6-2).

The ninety-seventh sūkta is on the Jīrike (cumin).

In this sūkta are praised the herbs and trees (oṣadhi-vanaspati) used to destroy diseases and the like: that is, small plants, creepers, roots, vines and so on, and also a few large trees such as the aśvattha and the pālāśa. The same sūkta, with some variant readings, is also recited in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 4-2-6). From some Ṛks of this sūkta, and from the mantras of the 145th sūkta of this same maṇḍala beginning इमां खनाम्योषधिं (*imāṃ khanāmyoṣadhiṃ*), it is evident that these herbs were used not only as medicine to cure diseases but also in magical (ābhicārika) rites such as wound-charming, subjugation and harming enemies. The seers believed that the power of these herbs and trees is very great. Soma, or the Soma plant, is said to be the king of these herbs and trees; that is why it is customary to call Soma by the word "king". Although other herbs and trees are described and praised here and there, this is the only sūkta in which these herbs are the main object of praise. The ninth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda is set apart for praising the Soma plant and Soma, its presiding deity; and in many Ṛks of many sūktas, as the context requires, there is praise of the deity Soma as well. In the introduction to the ninth maṇḍala (Ṛ. Saṃ. part 26, pp. 1-98) there is a detailed account of the deity Soma and the Soma plant. In many places in the Ṛks of this sūkta, things regarded as lifeless, that is, creepers and the like that have no power to speak like human beings, are addressed as if they were human beings, and are seen speaking like human beings. But, as the Bhāṣyakāra has said in the Ṛgveda-bhāṣya-bhūmikā, it should be understood that in sentences such as ओषधे त्रायस्यैनं (*oṣadhe trāyasyainaṃ*) ("O herb, protect this man") and in the mantras of the present sūkta, the herbs and trees are not thought of merely as plants but are praised as their presiding deities.

Giving the etymology of the word ओषधि (*oṣadhi*), Yāska says: ओषधयः । ओषद्वयंतीति वा । ओषत्येना भयंतीति वा । दोषं भयंतीति वा (*oṣadhayaḥ | oṣadvayaṃtīti vā | oṣatyenā bhayaṃtīti vā | doṣaṃ bhayaṃtīti vā*) (Ni. 9-27). That is: here the two words ओषत् (*oṣat*) and धयंति (*dhayaṃti*) together make the word ओषधयः (*oṣadhayaḥ*). ओषत् (*oṣat*) is disease pervading the body, such as the heat of fever; धयंति (*dhayaṃti*) means they drink up or destroy. Because it drinks up (destroys) and demolishes the diseases that arise in the body, it gets the name ओषधयः (*oṣadhayaḥ*). Or, because it is drunk by going into the belly, it gets this name. Or, because it destroys the faults (doṣa) in the body, that is, the faults such as vāta and pitta, it gets the name ओषधि (*oṣadhi*). Thus he has given three kinds of meaning.

## Sūkta 97 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> या ओषधीरिति त्रयोविंशत्यृचं सप्तमं सूक्तं । अथर्वणः पुत्रस्य
> भिषग्नाम्न आर्ष० । आनुष्टुभनोषधिदेवताकं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । या ओषधीस्त्र्यधिकाधर्वणो भिषगोषधिस्तुतिरानुष्टुभमिति ॥ दीक्षितानां ज्वराद्युपसंतापे
> संजातेऽनेन सूक्तेन मार्जयेत् । सूत्रितं च । ओषधिसूक्तेन चाप्लाव्यानुम्मृजेत् । आ. ६-९ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seventh sūkta, या ओषधीः (*yā oṣadhīḥ*), of twenty-three Ṛks. Its seer is Bhiṣak, son of Atharvan; its deity is the Oṣadhis; its metre is Anuṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says: या ओषधीस्र्यधिकाधर्वणो भिषगोषधिस्तुतिरानुष्टुभं (*yā oṣadhīsryadhikādharvaṇo bhiṣagoṣadhistutirānuṣṭubhaṃ*). When fever or other affliction has arisen among those consecrated for a rite (dīkṣita), one should sprinkle them with this sūkta. The sūtra says: ओषधिसूक्तेन चाप्लाव्यानुमृजेत् (*oṣadhisūktena cāplāvyānumṛjet*) (Ā. 6-9).

The Anuvāda: this sūkta beginning या ओषधीः (*yā oṣadhīḥ*) is the seventh sūkta in the eighth anuvāka; it has twenty-three Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is the one named Bhiṣak (physician), son of Atharvan; its deity is the herbs; its metre is Anuṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: या ओषधीस्र्यधिकाधर्वणो भिषगोषधिस्तुतिरानुष्टुभं (*yā oṣadhīsryadhikādharvaṇo bhiṣagoṣadhistutirānuṣṭubhaṃ*). If those who have taken the dīkṣā in sacrificial rites are afflicted by fever or other troubles in the middle of the rite, they are to be sprinkled (prokṣaṇa) with the mantras of this sūkta; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, ओषधिसूक्तेन चाप्लाव्यानुमृजेत् (*oṣadhisūktena cāplāvyānumṛjet*) (Ā. 6-9).

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 8; Sūkta 97. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 5; Vargas 8, 9, 10, 11. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 23. Ṛṣi: Bhiṣag Ātharvaṇa. Devatā: praise of the Oṣadhis. Chandas: Anuṣṭubh.
