##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शु॒नम॑ष्ट्रा॒व्य॑चरत्कप॒र्दी व॑र॒त्रायां॒ दार्वा॒नह्य॑मानः ।  
> नृ॒म्मानि॑ कृ॒ण्वन्ब॒हवे॒ जना॑य॒ गाः प॑स्पशा॒नस्तवि॑षीरधत्त ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शुनं । अष्ट्रावी । अचरत् । कपर्दि । वरत्रायां । दारु । आनह्यमानः ।  
> नृम्मानि । कृण्वन् । बहवे । जनाय । गाः । पस्पशानः । तविषीः । अधत्त ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शुनमिति सुखनाम । सुखं यथा भवति तथा । अष्टावी । अष्टा प्रतोदः ।
> तद्वान् ॥ छांदसो विनिः ॥ कपर्दि कपर्दवानचरत् । संचरति । किं कुर्वन् ।
> वरत्रायां वध्र्यां दारु काष्ठं रथांगभूतमानह्यमानः सर्वतो बध्नन् । पुनः
> किं कुर्वन् । बहवे जनाय स्वपुत्रभृत्यादिलक्षणाय नृम्मानि धनानि शत्रुसंबंधीनि
> सुखानि वा कृण्वन् । गाः पस्पशानः स्पृशन् ॥ स्पश बाधनस्पर्शनयोः । छांदसो लिटि
> कानच् ॥ एवं कुर्वंस्तविषीर्बलान्यधत्त । धत्ते । जयं प्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

शुनं (*śunaṃ*) is a name for happiness: "in such a way that there is happiness". अष्ट्रावी (*aṣṭrāvī*) is one who has the goad (aṣṭrā = pratoda), the word being formed in the Veda with the affix vini. कपर्दि (*kapardi*) is one who has braided hair. He moves about (अचरत् (*acarat*)). Doing what? Binding all round the wood, a part of the chariot, with the strap (वरत्रायां (*varatrāyāṃ*)). And again doing what? Making for the many people, that is, for his own sons, servants and the like, नृम्मानि (*nṛmmāni*), namely riches belonging to the enemy, or comforts. पस्पशानः (*paspaśānaḥ*) means touching the cows. Doing thus, he took up (अधत्त (*adhatta*)) powers (तविषीः (*taviṣīḥ*)), that is, he wins victory.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कपर्दि (*kapardi*)—he of beautiful hair (Indra)
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—easily
- अष्टावी (*aṣṭāvī*)—holding the whip
- वरत्रायां दारु (*varatrāyāṃ dāru*)—the (wooden) part of the chariot, with a rope
- आनह्यमानः (*ānahyamānaḥ*)—having bound it tight
- बहवे जनाय (*bahave janāya*)—for many people
- नृम्मानि (*nṛmmāni*)—riches (or happiness)
- कृण्वन् (*kṛṇvan*)—providing
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cows
- पस्पशानः (*paspaśānaḥ*)—touching with affection
- अचरत् (*acarat*)—he moves about everywhere (and)
- तविषीः (*taviṣīḥ*)—his strength and capacity
- अधत्त (*adhatta*)—he bears, that is, he increases them and wins victory

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, with his beautiful braided locks, goes about with a whip in his hand. He binds the loose parts of the chariot tight with a rope. He provides wealth or happiness to many people. He pats the cows with affection. He increases his strength and wins victory.

### Printed p. 185

##### English translation
Wielding the goad (Indra) with the braided hair proceeded happily, fastening the strap to the wood (of the waggon); distributing riches to many people, caressing the oxen he acquired vigour.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मं तं प॑श्य वृष॒भस्य॒ युंजं॒ काष्ठा॑या॒ मध्ये॑ द्रुघ॒णं  ॑
> शयानं ।  
> येन॑ जि॒गाय॑ श॒तव॑त्स॒हस्रं॒ गवां॒ मुद्ग॑लः पृत॒नाज्ये॑षु ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमं । तं । पश्य । वृषभस्य । युंजं । काष्ठायाः । मध्ये । द्रुघनं । शयानं ।  
> येन । जिगाय । शतवत् । सहस्रं । गवां । मुद्गलः । पृतनाज्येषु ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कंचन सखायॆं सेनादिसहायाभावेन जयविषय उपहासं कुर्वाणं प्रति
> ब्रवीति । राजा द्रुघणेन वृषभेण चाजिं जिगायेत्युक्तवान् । पूर्व० वृषभो
> वर्णितः । अत्र द्रुघणो वर्ण्यते । हे सखे तमिमं द्रुघणं पश्य! कीदृशमिममिति
> उच्यते ॥ युजेरसमासे । पा. ७-१-७१ । इति नुम् ॥ युंजं । युज्यत इति
> युक् सखा । वृषभस्य सखिभूतं । वृषभो यावंतमर्थं साधयति तावंतमेव
> साधयंतमित्यर्थः । पुनः कीदृशं । काष्टाया मध्यॆ । आज्यंतोऽपि काष्टोच्यत
> इति निरुक्तं । २-१५ । आज्यंतस्य मध्यॆ । संग्राम इत्यर्थः । तत्र शयानं हंतव्यान्सर्वान्हत्वा सुखेन स्वपंतं निर्व्यापारत्वेन वर्तमानं । ईदृशं द्रुममयं घनं
> पश्येत्यर्थः । येन द्रुघणेन शतवच्छतोपेतं गवां सहस्रं पृतनाज्येषु संग्रामेषु जिगाय अहमजैषं तमिमं पश्येति समन्वयः ॥ जयतेर्लिट् । सन्‌लिटोर्जेरित्यभ्यासादुत्तरस्य कुत्वं । मिपो णल् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Mudgala speaks to a friend who mocks him about victory because he had no army or other help. The king had said that he won the battle with the द्रुघण (*drughaṇa*) (the wooden club) and the bull. Earlier the bull was described; here the club is described. "Friend, look at this club." What is it like? युंजं (*yuṃjaṃ*): that which is yoked (yujyate), a companion; it is the bull's friend, that is, it accomplishes just as much as the bull accomplishes. Again, what is it like? काष्टाया मध्यॆ (*kāṣṭāyā madhyè*): the end of a course is also called kāṣṭhā (Ni. 2-15)**NOTE**; "in the middle of the kāṣṭhā" is the battle. Lying there (शयानं (*śayānaṃ*)): having slain all who were to be slain, sleeping at ease, being without work. "Look at such a club, a solid mass of wood." The construction is: look at this club, with which I won a thousand cows together with a hundred (शतवत् (*śatavat*)) in the battles (पृतनाज्येषु (*pṛtanājyeṣu*)).

### Printed p. 186

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- येन (*yena*)—with which wooden club (O friend)
- गवां शतवत् सहस्रं (*gavāṃ śatavat sahasraṃ*)—hundreds and thousands of cows
- पृतनाज्येषु (*pṛtanājyeṣu*)—in battles
- जिगाय (*jigāya*)—I won and brought
- युंजं (*yuṃjaṃ*)—that which is used as an aid in battle
- वृषभस्य (*vṛṣabhasya*)—that is like a friend of the bull (the ox)
- काष्ठायाः मध्ये (*kāṣṭhāyāḥ madhye*)—in the middle of the battle
- शयानं (*śayānaṃ*)—that lies at ease after destroying enemies
- तं इमं द्रुघणं (*taṃ imaṃ drughaṇaṃ*)—this club of mine (or cudgel)
- पश्य (*paśya*)—look

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Friend, look at this wooden club (cudgel) that I have. With its help I conquered my enemies in battle and won thousands of cows. In battle it is a help to me like a friend. Because it bears the cart together with my bull, it is a companion to the bull too. This club, having beaten down the enemies in the middle of the battle, now lies here as if resting. Look at such a club.

##### English translation
Behold this club, the ally of the bull, resting in the midst of the conflict, with which I, Mudgala, have won hundreds and thousands of cattle in war.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For this ṛk Yāska has given the Nirukta: इमं तं पश्य वृषभस्य सहयुजं काष्ठाया मध्ये द्रुघणं शयानं येन (*imaṃ taṃ paśya vṛṣabhasya sahayujaṃ kāṣṭhāyā madhye drughaṇaṃ śayānaṃ yena*) … भ्रमयोऽस्या अश्वभरणाद्वा (*bhramayo 'syā aśvabharaṇādvā*) **NOTE** (Ni. 9-24)

इमं तं पश्य वृषभस्य सहयुजं काष्ठाया मध्ये द्रुघणं शयानं (*imaṃ taṃ paśya vṛṣabhasya sahayujaṃ kāṣṭhāyā madhye drughaṇaṃ śayānaṃ*)—The sage Mudgala, speaking to his friend about the druhghana, the wooden club or cudgel that he has with him, has praised it: "O friend, behold this club of mine. Since I have only one bull or ox, I have come to the battlefield after yoking the ox on one side of the yoke of the cart and this club on the other side. Therefore this club is called the ox's yoke-fellow (a friend)", वृषभस्य सहयुजं (*vṛṣabhasya sahayujaṃ*). "Since I have used this club freely against the enemies in battle, it has destroyed the enemies and lies in the middle of the battlefield as if resting (as if fallen). Look at this club of mine."

### Printed p. 187
येन जिगाय शतवत् सहस्रं गवां मुद्गलः पृतनाज्येषु (*yena jigāya śatavat sahasraṃ gavāṃ mudgalaḥ pṛtanājyeṣu*)—With the help of this club I, Mudgala, have beaten down the enemies in battles and won hundreds and thousands of cows.

पृतनाज्यमिति संग्रामनाम पृतनानाम जनाद्वा जयनाद्वा (*pṛtanājyamiti saṃgrāmanāma pṛtanānāma janādvā jayanādvā*)—Pṛtanājya means battle. Pṛtanā means people, armies. The place where such armies go together (अजंति गच्छंति (*ajaṃti gacchaṃti*)), that is, meet, is called pṛtanājya, battle. Or else, जयनाद्वा (*jayanādvā*), पृथनाद्वा (*pṛthanādvā*): because armies or people win (jayanāt) in it; since people or armies fight one another here and win, it is called pṛtanājya, that is, battle.

मुद्दलो मुद्दवान्- मुद्दगिलो ना मदनं गिलतीति वा मदंगिलो वा मुदंगिलो वा (*muddalo muddavān- muddagilo nā madanaṃ gilatīti vā madaṃgilo vā mudaṃgilo vā*)**NOTE**—Mudga is the name of a grain, the green gram. Because he has green gram, he is named Mudgala. Or मुद्दलो वा (*muddalo vā*): because he is fond of eating green gram, the name Mudgala came to him. Or मदनं गिलतीति वा (*madanaṃ gilatīti vā*): because he conquers desire (is one who has mastered his senses), he is named Mudgala. Or मदंगिलो वा (*madaṃgilo vā*): he who overcomes excitement or anger, that is, being of peaceful nature, hence the name Mudgala. Or मुदंगिलो वा (*mudaṃgilo vā*): one who has conquered joy, free from pleasure and pain and the like, devoted to the path of withdrawal (nivṛtti). Hence the name Mudgala.

अंसत्रं । अंसत्रमंहसस्त्राणं धनुर्वा कवचं ना । कवचं कु आंचितं भवति कांचितं भवति कायेऽंचितं भवतीति वा ॥ (*aṃsatraṃ | aṃsatramaṃhasastrāṇaṃ dhanurvā kavacaṃ nā | kavacaṃ ku āṃcitaṃ bhavati kāṃcitaṃ bhavati kāye 'ṃcitaṃ bhavatīti vā ‖*) (Ni. 5-26)—Aṃsatra means: अंसरः त्राणं (*aṃsaraḥ trāṇaṃ*)**NOTE**, a bow or a coat of mail that protects from the sin arising from killing people in battle. The armour (the steel armour used in battle) is called kavaca because it is bent crookedly, or bent only slightly, or because it fits the shape of the body and adjusts to it.

Druhghana: द्रुघणो द्रुममयो घनः (*drughaṇo drumamayo ghanaḥ*) (Ni. 9-23)—This word contains two words, dru and ghana. Dru means tree; ghana means solid. Therefore druhghana means a club (cudgel) made of wood and solid.

भार्म्यश्वो भृम्यश्वस्य पुत्रः । भृम्यश्वो भ्रमयोऽस्या अश्वभरणाद्वा (*bhārmyaśvo bhṛmyaśvasya putraḥ | bhṛmyaśvo bhramayo 'syā aśvabharaṇādvā*)—Bhārmyaśva means the son of one called Bhṛmyaśva. As for Bhṛmyaśva: because his horses do not stand in one place but wander everywhere he is named Bhramyaśva; or, because he keeps and nourishes horses, he is named Bhramyaśva.

### Printed p. 188
Kāṣṭhāyāḥ: here the word kāṣṭhā has the sense of battle. Explaining the many meanings of this word, Yāska has given the following explanation (Ni. 9-15):

1. तत्र काष्ठा इत्येतदनेकस्यापि सत्त्वस्य नाम भवति (*tatra kāṣṭhā ityetadanekasyāpi sattvasya nāma bhavati*)—the word kāṣṭhā has many meanings.
2. काष्ठा दिशो भवंति क्रांत्वा स्थिता भवंति (*kāṣṭhā diśo bhavaṃti krāṃtvā sthitā bhavaṃti*)—Kāṣṭhā means the directions. This name is because they extend very far.
3. काष्ठा उपदिशो भवंतीतरेतरं क्रांत्वा स्थिता भवंति (*kāṣṭhā upadiśo bhavaṃtītaretaraṃ krāṃtvā sthitā bhavaṃti*)—The intermediate directions also have the name kāṣṭhā, because they stand as if thrust between two directions.
4. आदित्योऽपि काष्ठोऽच्यते क्रांत्वा स्थितो भवति (*ādityo 'pi kāṣṭho 'cyate krāṃtvā sthito bhavati*)—The sun also has the name kāṣṭha, because the sun crosses over in the sky from one place to another (from east to west).
5. अज्यंतोऽपि काष्ठोऽच्यते क्रांत्वा स्थितो भवति (*ajyaṃto 'pi kāṣṭho 'cyate krāṃtvā sthito bhavati*)—The battlefield also has the name kāṣṭha, because in it the arrows of the warriors cross one another and go from one side to the other.
6. आपोऽपि काष्ठा उच्यंते क्रांत्वा स्थिता भवंतीति स्थावराणां (*āpo 'pi kāṣṭhā ucyaṃte krāṃtvā sthitā bhavaṃtīti sthāvarāṇāṃ*)—Waters also are called kāṣṭhāḥ. Of these there are two kinds, sthāvara and asthāvara. Sthāvara means water that stands in one place without movement in a reservoir (tank, pond) and the like. Asthāvara means water that flows from one place to another (from a height to a hollow). Since these leave one place and flow to another, waters are called kāṣṭhā.

> य आरे समीप एवाघाघानि दुःखानि शत्रुरूपाणि करोति तं को नरो

> स्थापयंति । आरोहयंतीत्यर्थः । अथवा यं रथे युंजंति तमेव प्रहरणार्थमा
> स्थापयंति । उभयविधं कार्यमेकः करोतीत्यर्थः । किंचास्मै तृणं ना भरंति ।
> नाहरंति । तथोदकं नाहरंति ॥ हृग्रहोर्भ इति भत्वं ॥ ईदृशो द्रुघण उत्तरो
> दक्षिणस्य वृषभस्य स्वयमुत्तरः सन् धुरो रथभारस्य रथधुरं वहति प्रदेदिशत्
> प्रकर्षण जयं स्वामिने प्रदिशन् शत्रूणां ना भयं प्रदिशन् वहति ॥ दिश अतिसर्जन
> इत्यस्माद्यज्लुगंताच्छतरि रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa asks who has seen in this way the man who, standing close by, inflicts sufferings that are enemies. He says that the द्रुघण (*drughaṇa*) (the mace) which they yoke on the chariot, that very one they set up (स्थापयंति (*sthāpayaṃti*)), that is, they mount it. Or else, the one they yoke on the chariot they set up for striking. The sense is that one thing does both kinds of work. They bring it neither grass nor water. The mace, standing on the further side of the right-hand bull, itself bears the burden of the chariot, the chariot-pole. It bears it while pointing out (प्रदेदिशत् (*pradediśat*)) victory to its master and no fear to the enemies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- आरे (*āre*)—being near
- अघा (*aghā*)—the man who causes suffering
- कः नरः (*kaḥ naraḥ*)—what man indeed
- नु (*nu*)—now
- इत्था (*itthā*)—in this manner
- ददर्श (*dadarśa*)—sees (looks on)?
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which mace
- युंजंति (*yuṃjaṃti*)—they yoke on the chariot together with the bull
- तमु (*tamu*)—that very mace
- आ स्थापयंति (*ā sthāpayaṃti*)—they set up (use) for slaying the enemy
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—for this mace
- तृणं (*tṛṇaṃ*)—grass (food)
- न आ भरंति (*na ā bharaṃti*)—they do not supply
- न उदकं (*na udakaṃ*)—nor do they give water to drink (even so, this mace)
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—being on the other side of the yoke, the chariot's burden
- वहति (*vahati*)—carries
- प्रदेदिशत् (*pradediśat*)—secures victory (in battle) for its master

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Here the द्रुघण (*drughaṇa*) is praised.) Who, standing near us and seeing the suffering caused by our enemies, would keep quiet? I yoke this mace of mine to the chariot when fighting to slay the enemy. It is natural to yoke two bulls to a chariot or a cart. But since I have only one bull, the bull is yoked to one side of the chariot and this mace to the other. Unlike bulls, this mace needs no grass to be given to it, nor water to be given to drink,

### Printed p. 190

yet it bears the burden of the chariot along with the bull and secures victory in battle for its master.

##### English translation
Who has thus beheld the evils nigh at hand? The (bull) which they yoke, they stop; to him they bring neither fodder nor water. Being above (the bull) he bears the chariot-pole announcing (victory to his lord).

> मंगलवत् सिनवत् । सिनमन्नं । तद्वच्चास्तु । गोरूपान्नवच्च भवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here Mudgalānī, the charioteer, is praised. She is like a woman forsaken (परिवृक्तेव (*parivṛkteva*); root वृजी वर्जने (*vṛjī varjane*)), abandoned by her husband and separated from him. As such a woman reaches (आनट् (*ānaṭ*), which means "pervading") her husband, who is to be obtained, पतिविद्यं (*patividyaṃ*) (*vidyaḥ* meaning *vedyaḥ*, "to be reached"), so Mudgalānī, having come to her husband's side as charioteer, swells and grows (पीप्याना (*pīpyānā*)). Like what? Like one pouring with the कूचक्र (*kūcakra*). कुः (*kuḥ*) is the earth, its circle is कूचक्रः (*kūcakraḥ*); for the sake of that rain-needing earth a cloud pours water. As a cloud, small in the sky, becomes great at the time of raining, so she too, raining streams of arrows in the midst of the enemy, grows. Further, एषः (*eṣaḥ*) is the herd of cows that is to be sought; she who desires it is *eṣaiṣī*. With her, the charioteer, may we win the herd of cows carried off by the enemies. May her gift or share (सातं (*sātaṃ*)) be auspicious (सुमंगलं (*sumaṃgalaṃ*)) and like food (सिनवत् (*sinavat*); सिनमन्नं (*sinamannaṃ*)): may it be like food in the form of cows.

### Printed p. 191

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- परिवृक्ता इव (*parivṛktā iva*)—like a woman forsaken by her husband
- पतिविद्यं (*patividyaṃ*)—the proximity of her husband
- आनट् (*ānaṭ*)—as she reaches it and rejoices, so this charioteer Mudgalānī
- कूचक्रेणेव (*kūcakreṇeva*)—over the circle of the earth
- सिंचन् (*siṃcan*)—as a cloud that rains spreads out large in the sky while raining
- पीप्याना (*pīpyānā*)—grows with joy
- एष्यष्या (*eṣyaṣyā*)—eager in the search for cows
- रथ्या चित् (*rathyā cit*)—by Mudgalānī, the charioteer herself
- जयेम (*jayema*)—we win victory in battle
- सातं (*sātaṃ*)—won (given) by that Mudgalānī
- सुमंगलं (*sumaṃgalaṃ*)—the auspicious herd of cows
- सिनवत् (*sinavat*)—like food, a dear possession to us
- अस्तु (*astu*)—may it be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a wife who has parted from her husband rejoices when she is reunited with him, so this charioteer Mudgalānī grows with joy (swells), as a cloud raining over the earth's disc spreads huge in the sky at the time of raining. Through this Mudgalānī, eager in the search for cows, we win victory in battle. May the auspicious herd of cows given by her, that is, obtained from the enemies in battle, be as dear to us as food.

##### English translation
As a wife who has been abandoned rejoices to find her husband, as cloud expanding when pouring forth rain with the aid of the earth's disc; with her eager (to recover the cattle) for our charioteer, may we win (the prize), may good fortune, together with food, be given to us.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूक्तस्य विकल्पेनैंद्रत्वादादाविंद्रस्य स्तुतत्वादंतेऽपींद्रः स्तूयते । हे
> इंद्र त्वं विश्वस्य सर्वस्य जगतश्चक्षुषश्चक्षुष्मतः पश्यतो ना जगतश्चक्षुरसि । प्रत्येकमुत्पत्तिविशिष्टचक्षुःसद्भावेऽपि सर्वस्य साधारणं चक्षुरसि । त्वया द्रष्टव्यानैहिकामुष्मिकपदार्थान्पश्यंतीत्यर्थः । त्वामेव हि यज्ञादिना लब्ध्वा पुरुषार्थान्साधयंति।
> यद्वा । विश्वस्य जगतो यन्निजं चक्षुरस्ति तस्यापि चक्षुषस्त्वं चक्षुरसि । यद्यस्माद्वृषाभिमतवर्षकस्त्वमाजिं मुद्दलस्य मम संग्रामं वध्रिणा पाशेन युजा
> युजौ युक्तौ वृषणा वृषण् वर्षकावश् रथे योजयित्वा चोदयञ्चतुरुषु
> प्रेरयन् सिषाससि आजिं स्तंभकुमिच्छसि तस्माच्चक्षुरसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Since the sūkta is optionally addressed to Indra, and Indra was praised at the beginning, Indra is praised at the end as well. O Indra, you are the eye of the whole world, of everything that has eyes and sees. Although each being has its own eye, you are the common eye of all: through you they see the things to be seen, of this world and the next, and having obtained you by sacrifice and the like they accomplish the aims of man. Or else: of the world's own eye you are the eye. Because you, the showerer who grants what is wished, desire (सिषाससि (*siṣāsasi*)) the battle of me, Mudgala, urging forward the two showerers yoked to the chariot with the rope, therefore you are the eye. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- विश्वस्य जगतः (*viśvasya jagataḥ*)—of the whole world
- चक्षुषः (*cakṣuṣaḥ*)—that has the power of seeing
- चक्षुषि असि (*cakṣuṣi asi*)—you are of the form of the eye, that is, you hold the first place like the eye **NOTE**
- विश्वस्य जगतः (*viśvasya jagataḥ*)—of the whole world
- चक्षुषिः (*cakṣuṣiḥ*)—to Āditya (the Sun), who is the form of the eye
- चक्षुषि असि (*cakṣuṣi asi*)—you are like an eye
- यत् (*yat*)—for that very reason
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—you who shower the things desired
- आजिं (*ājiṃ*)—the battle I, Mudgala, am conducting, or in the battle
- वध्रिणा (*vadhriṇā*)—with the rope
- वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—your horses
- युजा (*yujā*)—having tied to the chariot
- चोदयन् (*codayan*)—urging the chariot to go through the midst of the enemies
- सिषाससि (*siṣāsasi*)—you wish to win victory for us in battle

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you are the eye of the whole world that has the power of seeing; or else you are like an eye to the Sun, who is the eye of the whole world. Therefore you, so mighty and granting what is wished, in this battle that I, Mudgala, am conducting, wish to win victory for us, yoking your horses to the chariot with a rope and urging it through the midst of the enemies.

##### English translation
You, Indra, are the eye of the eye of the whole world, when, showerer (of benifits), urging on your two vigours steeds, harnessed to the car, you engage in battle.

## Sūkta 103 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Introduction. Concerning this sūkta (आशुः शिशानः (*āśuḥ śiśānaḥ*)) the Ṛgvidhāna says as follows:

सर्वत्र तु परा शांतिर्ज्ञेयोऽप्रतिरथस्त्वृषिः । (*sarvatra tu parā śāṃtirjñeyo 'pratirathastvṛṣiḥ |*)
यमेव देशं गजेत शत्रुं वाप्यनुमंत्रितः ॥ (*yameva deśaṃ gajeta śatruṃ vāpyanumaṃtritaḥ ‖*)
नाजित्वा विनिवर्तेत परं हि ब्रह्मणो बलं । (*nājitvā vinivarteta paraṃ hi brahmaṇo balaṃ |*)
सर्वकामैर्जपेदेतत्सर्वकामसमृद्धये ॥ (*sarvakāmairjapedetatsarvakāmasamṛddhaye ‖*)
संग्राममभ्युद्यताय राज्णे चैतत्पयोजयेत् । (*saṃgrāmamabhyudyatāya rājṇe caitatpayojayet |*)
सर्वान् विजयते शत्रून्न पराजीयतेऽपरैः ॥ (*sarvān vijayate śatrūnna parājīyate 'paraiḥ ‖*)
पथि स्वस्ययनं चैतत्तस्करेभ्यश्चरन् पथि । (*pathi svasyayanaṃ caitattaskarebhyaścaran pathi |*)
भूतोरगपिशाचेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः परिरक्षति ॥ (*bhūtoragapiśācebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ parirakṣati ‖*)
(Ṛgvidhāna, Adhyāya 4, Śloka 6-9)

Apratiratha, the seer of this sūkta, recited it for peace everywhere. A king who is addressed with the mantras of this sūkta, to whatever country he goes to conquer his enemies, does not return without conquering them there; for such is the power and might of this sūkta. Moreover, if this sūkta is muttered, all the desires one wishes for are fulfilled. Above all, if a king setting out to fight his enemies is consecrated with this sūkta, he conquers all his enemies and is not himself defeated. Even when travelling on the road, the muttering of this sūkta removes the fear of thieves and robbers; everything goes off auspiciously. It protects from all fears, from ghosts, serpents, piśācas and the like.

Concerning this sūkta the great sage Śaunaka says as follows in his work called Bṛhaddevatā:

युध्यन् संख्यॆ जयं प्रेप्सुरैंद्रोऽप्रतिरथो जगौ । (*yudhyan saṃkhyè jayaṃ prepsuraiṃdro 'pratiratho jagau |*)
आशुरैंद्रमप्पा देवी अमीषामित्यृचि स्तुता । (*āśuraiṃdramappā devī amīṣāmityṛci stutā |*)
चतुर्थी बार्हस्पत्या स्यान्नाकुले च महानिति ॥ (*caturthī bārhaspatyā syānnākule ca mahāniti ‖*)
द्वृचस्तु मारुतः प्रेतेत्यैंद्री ना ब्रह्म यत्परं ॥ (*dvṛcastu mārutaḥ pretetyaiṃdrī nā brahma yatparaṃ ‖*)
तत्रानिरुक्तसूक्तादावृगेका सूर्यमर्चति ॥ (*tatrāniruktasūktādāvṛgekā sūryamarcati ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. Adhyāya 8, Śloka 13-15)

### Printed p. 194

Apratiratha Aindra recited this sūkta in order to gain victory while fighting. Indra is the deity of this sūkta beginning आशुः शिशानः (*āśuḥ śiśānaḥ*); but in the twelfth Ṛk, beginning अमीषां चित्तं (*amīṣāṃ cittaṃ*), a goddess called अप्पा (*appā*) is praised. The deity of the fourth Ṛk of this sūkta is Bṛhaspati, and in the khila mantras of the seer Nakula, the mantra महान् (*mahān*) also has Bṛhaspati as its deity. In the next two Ṛks beginning प्रेता (*pretā*) (the 13th Ṛk and one Ṛk of the khila mantras) the Maruts are praised, but for the first प्रेता (*pretā*) Ṛk (the 13th) Indra too is an alternative deity. In the first Ṛk of the following khila sūkta, beginning ब्रह्म (*brahma*), the Sun is praised.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आशुः शिशान इति त्रयोदशर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तमिंद्रपुत्रस्याप्रतिरथनाम्न
> आर्षं । त्रयोदश्यनुष्टुप् शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः । बृहस्पते परि दीयेत्यस्या बृहस्पतिर्देवता । अमीषां चित्तमित्यस्या अस्वाख्या देवी देवता । शिष्टा ऐंद्रः ! त्रयोदशी
> विकल्पेन मारुती । तथा चानुक्रांतं । आशुः सप्तोन्नैंद्रोऽप्रतिरथश्चतुर्थि
> बार्हस्पत्योपांत्याष्वादेव्यंत्यानुष्टुम्मारुती वेति ॥ साग्निचिते क्रत् चित्यग्निषु
> प्रणीयमानेषु दक्षिणतो व्रजता ब्रह्मणैत्तूक्तं जप्यं । तथा च सूत्रितं । दक्षिणतश्च
> व्रजञ्चपत्याशुः शिशान इति सूक्तं समाप्य । आ. १-१२ । इति । ब्रह्माप्रतिरथं जपित्वा ।
> आ. ४-८ । इति च ॥ युद्धार्थं राज्यः सन्नहनेऽनेन सूक्तेन राजेक्षितव्यः । सूत्रितं
> च । अथैनमन्वीक्षेताप्रतिरथशाससौपर्णैः । आ- गृ. ३-१२-१३ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta आशुः शिशान (*āśuḥ śiśāna*), of thirteen Ṛks, the fourth, has as its seer Apratiratha, the son of Indra. The thirteenth is anuṣṭubh, the rest triṣṭubh. The deity of बृहस्पते परि दीय (*bṛhaspate pari dīya*) is Bṛhaspati; of अमीषां चित्तं (*amīṣāṃ cittaṃ*) the goddess called अस्वाख्या (*asvākhyā*); the rest are Aindra; the thirteenth is optionally Mārutī. **NOTE** So it is recorded in the Anukramaṇī: आशुः सप्तोन्नैंद्रोऽप्रतिरथश्चतुर्थि बार्हस्पत्योपांत्याष्वादेव्यंत्यानुष्टुम्मारुती वेति ॥ (*āśuḥ saptonnaiṃdro 'pratirathaścaturthi bārhaspatyopāṃtyāṣvādevyaṃtyānuṣṭummārutī veti ‖*). In the agnicayana rite, while the piled fires are being carried forward, the Brahman priest, walking to the south, is to mutter this sūkta; so it is laid down in the sūtra: दक्षिणतश्च व्रजञ्चपत्याशुः शिशान इति सूक्तं समाप्य (*dakṣiṇataśca vrajañcapatyāśuḥ śiśāna iti sūktaṃ samāpya*) (Ā. 1-12), and ब्रह्माप्रतिरथं जपित्वा (*brahmāpratirathaṃ japitvā*) (Ā. 4-8). A king arming for battle is to be looked upon with this sūkta; so it is laid down: अथैनमन्वीक्षेताप्रतिरथशाससौपर्णैः (*athainamanvīkṣetāpratirathaśāsasauparṇaiḥ*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-12-13).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta आशुः शिशानः (*āśuḥ śiśānaḥ*) is the fourth sūkta in the ninth anuvāka. It has thirteen Ṛks. Its seer is Apratiratha, the son of Indra; the thirteenth Ṛk is in the anuṣṭubh metre and the remaining Ṛks in triṣṭubh. The deity of the fourth Ṛk, बृहस्पते परिदीया (*bṛhaspate paridīyā*), is Bṛhaspati; of the twelfth Ṛk, अमीषां चित्तं (*amīṣāṃ cittaṃ*), a goddess named अप्पा (*appā*); the remaining Ṛks are addressed to Indra. For the thirteenth Ṛk the Maruts are an alternative deity. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: आशुः सप्तोनैंद्रोऽप्रतिरथश्चतुर्थि बार्हस्पत्योपांत्यास्वादेव्यंत्यानुष्टुग्मारुती पा (*āśuḥ saptonaiṃdro 'pratirathaścaturthi bārhaspatyopāṃtyāsvādevyaṃtyānuṣṭugmārutī pā*). In the sacrifice with agni-piling, when the piled fires are carried forward, this sūkta is to be muttered by the priest called Brahman as he goes facing south, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra दक्षिणतश्च व्रजन् जपत्याशुः शिशान इति सूक्तं समाप्य (*dakṣiṇataśca vrajan japatyāśuḥ śiśāna iti sūktaṃ samāpya*) (Ā. 1-12); and also by the sūtra ब्रह्माप्रतिरथं जपित्वा (*brahmāpratirathaṃ japitvā*) (Ā. 4-8). That a king who has armed himself and is setting out for battle is to be looked upon with the recitation of this sūkta is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra अथैनवं वीक्षीताप्रतिरथशाससौपर्णॆः (*athainavaṃ vīkṣītāpratirathaśāsasauparṇèḥ*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-12-13).

> व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं ॥ वृषभो न भीमः वृषभो यथा शृंगाभ्यां भयजनकः
> तद्वच्छत्रूणां 'भयजनकश्च । घनाघनो घातकः शत्रूणां हंता ॥ पचाद्यचि
> हंतेर्घश्च । पा. ६-१-१२-७ । इति द्विर्वचनमभ्यासस्याडागमो, घत्वं च धात्वभ्यासयोः ॥ चर्षणीनां । चर्षणयो मनुष्याः । मनुष्याणां द्वेष्याणां क्षोभणः
> क्षोभयिता । संक्रंदनः सम्यक्कंदयिता प्राणिनामाकर्षणेन प्रहारेण वा ।
> अनिमिषश्चक्षुर्निमेषरहितः । सर्वदा स्वयज्ञगमनयुद्धादिकार्येष्ट्वनलस इत्यर्थः ।
> एकवीरः । वीरयत्यमित्रानिति वीरः । एकश्वासौ वीरश्च । अथवा एक एव विक्रांतः ।
> असाहाय्येन कार्यक्षम इत्यर्थः । ईदृशोऽयमिंद्रः शतं सेनाः साकं
> सहैकोद्योगेनैवाजयत् । जयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Indra is swift, quick in action and all-pervading, and sharpened (शिशानः (*śiśānaḥ*)), that is, a cause of fear to his enemies. He is like a bull, formidable (भीमः (*bhīmaḥ*), from "one fears him"): as a bull is fearsome with its sharp horns, so he is. Or else शिशानः (*śiśānaḥ*) means "of sharp mind", the ātmanepada being by vyatyaya. घनाघनः (*ghanāghanaḥ*) is the slayer, the killer of enemies. चर्षणीनां (*carṣaṇīnāṃ*): चर्षणयो (*carṣaṇayo*) are men; he agitates (क्षोभणः (*kṣobhaṇaḥ*)) hated men. संक्रंदनः (*saṃkraṃdanaḥ*) is one who makes creatures cry out, by dragging them off or by striking. अनिमिषः (*animiṣaḥ*) is without winking of the eye; he is never slack in going to his sacrifice, in battle and other deeds. एकवीरः (*ekavīraḥ*): he "heroes" his foes, so he is a hero; he is both one and a hero; or else he alone is valorous, able to act without help. Such an Indra conquered a hundred armies together, by a single effort.

##### English translation

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska, explaining the method of interpreting mantras, says that some mantras are विप्रतिषिद्दार्था भवंति (*vipratiṣiddārthā bhavaṃti*): the meanings stated in mantras are seen to contradict one another. As an example he gives the Śruti passages अशत्रुरिंद्र जज्जिषे । शतं सेना अजयत्साकमिंद्रः (*aśatruriṃdra jajjiṣe | śataṃ senā ajayatsākamiṃdraḥ*) (Ni. 1-15):
त्वं सिंधूरवासृजोऽधराचो अहन्नहिं । अशत्रुरिंद्र जज्जिषे विश्वं पुष्यसि वार्यं तत्वा परिष्वजामहे नभंतामन्यकेषां ज्याका अधि धन्वसु ॥ (*tvaṃ siṃdhūravāsṛjo 'dharāco ahannahiṃ | aśatruriṃdra jajjiṣe viśvaṃ puṣyasi vāryaṃ tatvā pariṣvajāmahe nabhaṃtāmanyakeṣāṃ jyākā adhi dhanvasu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-133-2)
अशुः शिशानो वृषभो न भीमो घनाघनः क्षोभणश्चर्षणीनां । संक्रंदनोऽनिमिष एकवीरः शतं सेना अजयत्साकमिंद्रः ॥ (*aśuḥ śiśāno vṛṣabho na bhīmo ghanāghanaḥ kṣobhaṇaścarṣaṇīnāṃ | saṃkraṃdano 'nimiṣa ekavīraḥ śataṃ senā ajayatsākamiṃdraḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 12-103-1)
The meanings in these two Ṛks are mutually contradictory. In the first Ṛk, अशत्रुरिंद्र जज्जिषे (*aśatruriṃdra jajjiṣe*) — "O Indra, you were born without an enemy" — means that from birth you have had no enemies. In the second Ṛk, एकवीरः शतं सेना अजयत्साकमिंद्रः (*ekavīraḥ śataṃ senā ajayatsākamiṃdraḥ*) — Indra is the sole hero, needs no one else's help, and he alone conquered hundreds of enemy armies. This being so: *yadyaśatruḥ kathaṃ śataṃ senā ajayat | atha śataṃ senā ajayat, kathamaśatruḥ ‖* That is: if Indra has no enemies, how did he conquer a hundred enemy armies? Or if Indra conquers a hundred enemy armies, how is he without enemies? To resolve the differing meanings seen in these passages, the solution must be stated thus: the meanings in these passages are said only to describe Indra's qualities in the highest degree.

> अस्तु नामेंद्र उक्तविधः तथाप्यस्माकं किमिति चेत् आह ! संक्रंदनेनानिमिषेण चोक्तलक्षणेन जिष्णुना जयशीलेन युत्कारेण । योधनं युत् । युद्धकारिणा ॥ कर्मण्यण् ॥ दुश्चवनेनान्यैरविचाल्येन !! च्युज् प्रुज् गतौ । छंदसि
> गत्यर्थेभ्यः । पा- ३-३-१२९ । इति युच् ॥ धृष्णुना धर्षकेण ईदृशेनेंद्रेण
> तद्युद्धं जयत । शत्रुबलं सहध्वं । अभिभवत । हे युधो योद्धारो हे नरो
> नेतारः ॥ विभाषितं विशेषवचने बहुवचनं । पा. ८-१-७४ । इति पूर्वस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वनिषेधादुत्तरं निहन्यते ॥ पुनः कीदृशेनेंद्रेणेति । इषुहस्तेन वृष्णा
> वर्षित्रा च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Granted that Indra is such as described, what is that to us? He answers: with Indra, who has the stated marks of संक्रंदन (*saṃkraṃdana*) and अनिमिष (*animiṣa*), who is victorious (जिष्णुना (*jiṣṇunā*), given to conquering), युत्कारेण (*yutkāreṇa*) (युत् (*yut*) is fighting; one who makes battle), दुश्चवनेन (*duścavanena*) (not to be shaken by others), धृष्णुना (*dhṛṣṇunā*) (bold, overpowering) — with such an Indra win that battle; overcome the enemy force. "O warriors, O leaders" (युधो (*yudho*), नरो (*naro*)). And again, with what kind of Indra? One who has arrows in his hand, a showerer (वृष्णा (*vṛṣṇā*), a rainer).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the previous mantra it was said "conquer with Indra"; here he shows Indra's capacity to bring about victory. That Indra is वशी (*vaśī*), having under his control the warriors with arrows in hand, the Maruts and others; and he is joined with those who have swords (निषंगः (*niṣaṃgaḥ*) is a sword).

### Printed p. 199

> र्युक्तः । निषंगः खड्गः । तद्वद्भर्वशी । स चेंद्रो युधो युध्यमानः सन् ॥
> इगुपथलक्षणः कः ॥ अथवा युधो युद्धहेतोर्गणेन शत्रुसंघेन सह संस्रष्टैकीभवनशीलः । यत एवंविधोऽतः संसृष्टजित् । ये परस्परैकमत्येन युद्धाय
> संसृष्टा भवंति तेषां जीता । तथा सोमपाः सोमस्य पाता । बाहुशर्धि । शर्धो
> बलिं । बाह्योर्बलं बाहुबलं । तद्वान् ॥ मत्वर्थीय इनिः । यद्वा । शृधु
> प्रसहने ! बाहुभ्यां शर्धयत्यभिभवतीति बाहुशर्धि । सुप्यजातौ णिनिस्ताच्छेल्ये ।
> पा. ३-२-७८ । इति णिनिः!! उग्रधन्वोद्यतधन्वा प्रतिहिताभिः शत्रुषु प्रेरिताभिरिषुभिरस्ता
> मारयिता । यत्रेषून्मुंचति तत्र वृथा न भवतीत्यर्थः । ईदृशेनेंद्रेण जयतेति
> संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And that Indra is युधः (*yudhaḥ*), fighting. Or else, for the sake of battle he is given to joining and becoming one with the enemy host (गणेन (*gaṇena*)). Being such, he is संसृष्टजित् (*saṃsṛṣṭajit*), conqueror of those who join one another with a single mind for battle. Likewise सोमपाः (*somapāḥ*), drinker of Soma; बाहुशर्धि (*bāhuśardhi*): *śardhaḥ* is strength, the strength of the arms is बाहुबलं (*bāhubalaṃ*), and he possesses it (the suffix ini in the sense of possession). Or else, from the root शृधु (*śṛdhu*) in the sense of overpowering, he overcomes with the arms, hence बाहुशर्धि (*bāhuśardhi*). उग्रधन्वा (*ugradhanvā*) is one with a raised bow; अस्ता (*astā*) is one who kills with arrows directed at enemies (प्रतिहिताभिः (*pratihitābhiḥ*)); wherever he looses arrows, they are not in vain. The construction is: conquer with such an Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सॆः इंद्रः—आ (*sèḥ iṃdraḥ—ā*)—that Indra
- इषुहस्तैः (*iṣuhastaiḥ*)—is joined with the Maruts holding arrows
- निषंगिभिः (*niṣaṃgibhiḥ*)—is armed with a sword
- वशी (*vaśī*)—brings all under his control
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- युधः (*yudhaḥ*)—while fighting
- गणेन (*gaṇena*)—with the enemy host
- संसृष्टा (*saṃsṛṣṭā*)—joins
- संसृष्टजित् (*saṃsṛṣṭajit*)—conquers the enemies who join him
- सोमपाः (*somapāḥ*)—drinks Soma
- बाहुशर्धी (*bāhuśardhī*)—one possessing strength of arm
- उग्रधन्वा (*ugradhanvā*)—with a raised bow
- प्रतिहिताभिः (*pratihitābhiḥ*)—with arrows directed at enemies
- अस्ता (*astā*)—destroys enemies

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra is joined with the Maruts who hold arrows. He is armed with a sword. He brings all under his control. While fighting he joins the enemy host. He conquers the enemies who join him. He drinks Soma. He possesses strength of arm. With his bow he shoots arrows at the enemies and destroys them.

##### English translation
Indra, with the arrow-bearing (Maruts), armed with swords, the subduer, the warrior, who encounters a multitude (of foes), whod conquers those who encounter him, the drinker of the Soma, the strong-armed, having a powerful bow, who shoots with well aimed arrows (conquer with his help).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Bṛhaspati, protector of the great, O god, go about (परि दीय (*pari dīya*), go round) with your chariot; दीयति (*dīyati*) is a verb of going. Having come, as slayer of Rakṣases (रक्षोहा (*rakṣohā*)), driving away enemies on all sides, destroying them everywhere, and shattering the enemy's armies, प्रमृणः (*pramṛṇaḥ*) crushing them forcefully (root मृण (*mṛṇa*), to injure). With what? युधा (*yudhā*), with battle. Thus, gaining victory everywhere, be you, such as you are, the protector of our chariots.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बृहस्पते (*bṛhaspate*)—O Bṛhaspati
- रथेन (*rathena*)—with your chariot
- परिदीय (*paridīya*)—go about
- युधा (*yudhā*)—by battle
- रक्षोहा (*rakṣohā*)—as slayer of Rākṣasas
- अमित्रान् (*amitrān*)—enemies
- अपबाधमानः (*apabādhamānaḥ*)—harassing
- सेनाः (*senāḥ*)—enemy armies
- प्रभंजन् (*prabhaṃjan*)—destroying
- प्रमृणः (*pramṛṇaḥ*)—injuring
- जयन् (*jayan*)—gaining victory
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—our
- रथानां (*rathānāṃ*)—for the chariots
- अविता (*avitā*)—as protector
- विधि (*vidhi*) be **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Bṛhaspati, go about with your chariot. As slayer of Rākṣasas by battle, harassing enemies, destroying them, gaining victory everywhere, be the protector of our chariots.

### Printed p. 201
Come with your chariot, Brihaspathi, who are the slayer of Rakshasas
discomfiting your enemies, crushing (hostile) hosts and demolishing (them)
victorious in battle, be the defender of our chariots.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ब॒ल॒वि॒ज्ञा॒यः स्थवि॑रः॒ प्रवी॑रः॒ सह॑स्वान्वा॒जी सह॑मान उ॒ग्रः ।  
> अ॒भिवी॑रो अ॒भिस॑त्वा सहो॒जा जैत्र॑मिंद्र॒ रथ॒मा ति॑ष्ठ गो॒वित्॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बलविज्ञायः । स्थविरः । प्रवीरः । सहस्वान् । वाजी । सहमानः । उग्रः ।  
> अभिवीरः । अभिसत्वा । सहजाः । जैत्रं । इंद्र । रथं । आ । तिष्ठ । गोवित् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सर्वस्य भूतस्य बलं विजानातीति बलविज्ञायः । यद्वा । बलं ममायमिति
> सर्वैर्बलत्वेन विज्ञायत इति बलविज्ञायः । सर्वस्य बलभूत इत्यर्थः । स्थविरो
> महान् प्रवीरः प्रकर्षण वीरः सहस्वान् पराभिभवसामर्थ्यवान् वाजी वेजनवान्
> अन्नवान्वा सहमानः शत्रूणामभिभवितोग्र उद्यूर्णबलोऽभिवीरः । अभिगता वीरा
> वीर्यवंतोऽनुचरा यस्यॆ स तथोक्तः । अभिसत्वाभिगतसत्वा सहोजाः सहसो
> बलाज्जातः एवंमहानुभावस्त्वं हे इंद्र जैत्रं जयशीलं रथमा तिष्ठ । अस्मत्सहायार्थमारोढुमर्हसि । त्वं च गोविदुदकस्य स्तुतीर्वा लब्धा वेदिता ना ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains बलविज्ञायः (*balavijñāyaḥ*) as one who knows the strength of every being; or else, as one known by all as "this is my strength", that is, the strength of all. स्थविरः (*sthaviraḥ*) is great. प्रवीरः (*pravīraḥ*) is eminently heroic. सहस्वान् (*sahasvān*) is one with the power to overcome others. वाजी (*vājī*) is one possessed of speed, or of food. सहमानः (*sahamānaḥ*) is one who overcomes enemies. उग्रः (*ugraḥ*) is one of upraised strength. अभिवीरः (*abhivīraḥ*) is one whose followers are heroic and mighty. अभिसत्वा (*abhisatvā*) is one of present, approaching might. सहोजाः (*sahojāḥ*) is born of strength. Being of such majesty, Indra is asked to mount the victorious chariot, to help us. And he is गोवित् (*govit*), the finder of water, or the one who obtains (or knows) our praises.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- बलविज्ञायः (*balavijñāyaḥ*)—one who knows his own greatness through his strength
- स्थविरः (*sthaviraḥ*)—the great one
- प्रवीरः (*pravīraḥ*)—the excellent hero
- सहस्वान् (*sahasvān*)—one who defeats enemies
- वाजी (*vājī*)—the possessor of food
- सहमानः (*sahamānaḥ*)—one who confronts enemies
- उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—the terrible one
- अभिवीरः (*abhivīraḥ*)—one accompanied by heroes
- अभिसत्वा (*abhisatvā*)—one who is of the nature of power
- सहोजाः (*sahojāḥ*)—the son of power
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- जैत्रं (*jaitraṃ*)—that wins victory
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—the chariot
- आ तिष्ठ (*ā tiṣṭha*)—mount and sit
- गोवित् (*govit*)—listen to the praise

### Printed p. 202

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra is one who knows his own greatness through his strength, a great hero (the Kannada has "great Śūdra"), an excellent hero, a defeater of enemies, possessor of food, one who confronts enemies, terrible, accompanied by heroes, the son of power. O Indra, mount the victorious chariot and sit. Listen to our praise. **NOTE**

##### English translation
Known by his strength, mighty, heroic, over-powering, vigorous, enduring, fierce, attendeded by heroes, attended by mighty men, the offspring of strength, the possessor of water, do you, Indra. ascend your triumphant chariot.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> गो॒त्र॒भिदं॑ गो॒विदं॒ वज्र॑बाहुं॒ जयं॑त॒मज्म॑ प्रमृ॒णंत॒मोज॑सा ।  
> इ॒मं स॑जाता॒ अनु॑ वीरयध्व॒मिंद्रं॑ सखायो॒ अनु॒ सं  ॑
> रभध्वं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गोत्रभिदं । गोविदं । वज्रबाहुं । जयंतं । अज्म । प्रमृणंतं । ओजसा ।  
> इमं । सजाताः । अनु । वीरयध्वं । इंद्रं । सखायः । अनु । सं । रभध्वं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गोत्रभिदं । गा उदकानि त्रायंत इति गोत्रा मेघाः । यद्वा! गौर्भूमिः ।
> शां त्रायंत इति गोत्राः पर्वताः । तेषां भेत्तारं गोविदमुदकस्य लब्धारं
> वज्रबाहुं वज्रहस्तं ॥ प्रहरणार्थेभ्यः । पा. २-२-३६-४ । इति परनिपातः ॥ जयंतं
> शत्रुनभिभवंतं जयनशीलमज्म गमनशीलं तत्रुबलमोजसा बलेन जयंतं
> यद्वाज्माजिं जयंतमोजसा बलेन प्रमृणंतं शत्रुनभिभवंतं ईदृशं महानुभावमिममिंद्रं हे सजाताः सहोत्पन्ना योद्धारः यूयमनु वीरयध्वं ।
> एनमग्रतः कृत्वानु पश्चाद्वीरयध्वं । वीरकर्म युद्धं कुरुध्वं ॥ शूर वीर

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

गोत्रभिदं (*gotrabhidaṃ*): the गोत्राः (*gotrāḥ*) are clouds, which protect waters; or else, *gauḥ* is the earth, and the गोत्राः (*gotrāḥ*) are mountains, which protect it. Indra is their breaker, गोविदं (*govidaṃ*) the finder of water, वज्रबाहुं (*vajrabāhuṃ*) the one with the thunderbolt in his hand (the compound has the later member placed first by Pā. 2-2-36 (printed २-२-३६-४ (*2-2-36-4*))). जयंतं (*jayaṃtaṃ*) is one who overcomes enemies, victorious; अज्म (*ajma*) is the moving enemy force, which he conquers by might; or else अज्म (*ajma*) is the battle that he wins. He crushes (प्रमृणंतं (*pramṛṇaṃtaṃ*)) enemies by might. O kindred warriors (सजाताः (*sajātāḥ*)), born together, put him in front and fight behind him, perform heroic deeds. The root is शूर वीर विक्रांतौ (*śūra vīra vikrāṃtau*) (continuing on the next page).

### Printed p. 203

> विक्रांतौ । वीरशब्दात्तत्करोति तदाचष्ट इति णिच् ॥ हे सखायः परस्परं सखिभूताः
> यूयमिमिंद्रं संरभमाणमनु सं रभध्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

From the word वीर (*vīra*) the verb is formed with ṇic, in the sense "he does that" or "he declares that". O friends (सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)), mutually allied, follow this Indra as he sets about (the fight), सं रभध्वं (*saṃ rabhadhvaṃ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सजाताः (*sajātāḥ*)—O warriors, who are kinsmen
- गोत्रभिदं (*gotrabhidaṃ*)—the splitter of clouds
- गोविदं (*govidaṃ*)—the obtainer of water
- वज्रबाहुं (*vajrabāhuṃ*)—the holder of the thunderbolt weapon
- जयंतं (*jayaṃtaṃ*)—the victorious
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—with strength
- अज्म (*ajma*)—who rushes upon the enemy army
- प्रमृणंतं (*pramṛṇaṃtaṃ*)—who destroys the enemy armies
- इमं (*imaṃ*)—this Indra
- अनु वीरयध्वं (*anu vīrayadhvaṃ*)—follow and fight
- सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)—O friends
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- अनु सं रभध्वं (*anu saṃ rabhadhvaṃ*)—follow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O warriors who are kinsmen, follow and fight behind Indra, who splits the clouds, obtains water, holds the thunderbolt, is victorious, and with his strength rushes upon the enemy army and destroys the enemy armies. O friends, follow Indra.

##### English translation
Imitate in heroism, you kindred warriors, follow, friends, in prowess
this Indra, who is the breaker of mountains, the acquirer of water, armed
with the thunderbolt, conquering the swift (foe), destroying (the enemy)
by his might.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि गो॒त्राणि॒ सह॑सा॒ गाह॑मानोद॒यो वी॒रः श॒तम॑न्यु॒रिंद्रः॑।  
> दु॒श्च्य॒व॒नः पृ॑तना॒षाळ॑यु॒ध्यो॒३॒॑ऽस्माकं॒ सेना॑ अवतु॒ प्र यु॒त्सु॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । गोत्राणि । सहसा । गाहमानः । अदयः । वीरः । शतमन्युः । इंद्रः ।  
> दुःच्यवनः । पृतनाषाट् । अयुध्यः । अस्माकं । सेनाः । अवतु । प्र । युत्सु ॥७॥

### Printed p. 204

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमिंद्रो गोत्राण्यभ्राणि मेघान् सहसा बलेनाभि गाहमानः प्रविशन्नरयो निर्दयो वीरो विक्रांतः शतमन्युर्बहुयज्ञो बहुक्रोधो ना दुश्चवनोऽन्यैरचाल्यः ॥ स्वयं पृतनाषाट् शत्रुसेनानामभिभविता ॥ छंदसि सह इति ण्वैः ।
> सहेः साडः स इति मूर्धन्यादेशः ॥ अयुध्यः संप्रहर्तुमशक्यः ॥ युध संप्रहारे।
> छांडसः क्यप् ॥ ईदृगिंद्रोऽस्माकं सेना युत्सु संग्रामेषु प्रावतु । प्रकर्षण
> रक्षतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Indra, entering by force (सहसा (*sahasā*)) the गोत्राणि (*gotrāṇi*), that is the clouds, is अदयः (*adayaḥ*) (pitiless to enemies), वीरः (*vīraḥ*) valiant, शतमन्युः (*śatamanyuḥ*) one of many sacrifices or of much wrath, दुश्च्यवनः (*duścyavanaḥ*) not to be moved by others, himself पृतनाषाट् (*pṛtanāṣāṭ*), the overcomer of enemy armies (the ṣ-substitution is explained by a grammatical rule), अयुध्यः (*ayudhyaḥ*) one with whom none can do battle. Such an Indra, in battles (युत्सु (*yutsu*)), is to protect (प्रावतु (*prāvatu*)) our armies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आदयः (*ādayaḥ*)—pitiless towards enemies **NOTE**
- वीरः (*vīraḥ*)—the valiant
- शतमन्युः (*śatamanyuḥ*)—praiseworthy in many sacrifices
- दुश्च्यवनः (*duścyavanaḥ*)—one not to be moved by others
- पृतनाषाट् (*pṛtanāṣāṭ*)—the defeater of enemy armies
- अयुध्यः (*ayudhyaḥ*)—the unopposed one
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- गोत्राणि (*gotrāṇi*)—the clouds
- सहसा (*sahasā*)—with strength
- अभिगाहमानः (*abhigāhamānaḥ*)—entering
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—our
- सेनाः (*senāḥ*)—armies
- युत्सु (*yutsu*)—in battles
- प्रावतु (*prāvatu*)—may he protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, pitiless towards enemies, valiant, praiseworthy in many kinds of sacrifices, unmoved by others, the defeater of enemy armies, unopposed, entering the clouds with his strength, protect our armies in battles.

##### English translation
May Indra, bursting open the clouds with force; pitiless, heroic, with hundredfold anger, invincible, the overthrower of armies, irresistible, protect our armies in battles.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॑ आसां ने॒ता बृह॒स्पति॒र्दक्षि॑णा य॒ज्ञः पु॒र ए॑तु॒ सोमः॑ ।  
> दे॒व॒से॒नाना॑मभिभंजती॒नां जयं॑तीनां म॒रुतो॑ यं॒त्वग्रं॑ ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 205

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । आसां । नेता । बृहस्पतिः । दक्षिणा । यज्ञः । पुरः । एतु । सोमः ।  
> देवसेनानां । अभिभंजतीनां । जयंतीनां । मरुतः । यंतु । अग्रं ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आसामस्मत्सहायार्थमागतानामयमिंद्रो नेता नायकोऽस्तु । तथा तस्य
> बृहस्पतिः पुर एतु । एवं दक्षिणा यज्ञः सोमश्च पुर एत्विति प्रत्येकं संबंध॥ । तथा
> देवसेनानामभिभजंतीनामस्मदमित्रानाभिमुख्येन मर्दयंतीनां जयंतीनां ॥
> छंदसीति नाम उदात्तत्वं जयंतीनामित्यत्र बहुलवचनान्न भवति । पा. ६-१-१७८ ॥
> तासामग्रं मरुतो यंतु । गच्छंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of these (hosts), who have come to help us, may this Indra be the leader. May Brihaspathi go before him; so also Dakṣiṇā, Yajña and Soma, each separately connected with "go before". Of the divine armies that crush (अभिभंजतीनां (*abhibhaṃjatīnāṃ*)) our enemies by confronting them and are victorious, may the Maruts go in the front. The acute accent on the noun-ending that the rule on the Veda would give does not occur in जयंतीनां (*jayaṃtīnāṃ*), because of the "variously" rule (Pā. 6-1-178).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आसां (*āsāṃ*)—to these armies
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—may Indra
- नेता (*netā*)—be the leader
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Brihaspathi
- पुर एतु (*pura etu*)—let him go in front
- दक्षिणा (*dakṣiṇā*)—Dakshina
- यज्ञः (*yajñaḥ*)—Yajna
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—and Soma (let them go before the army)
- अभिभंजतीनां (*abhibhaṃjatīnāṃ*)—that destroy enemies
- जयंतीनां (*jayaṃtīnāṃ*)—and are victorious
- देवसेनानां (*devasenānāṃ*)—of these armies of the gods
- अग्रं (*agraṃ*)—in front
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Maruts
- यंतु (*yaṃtu*)—let them go

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra be the chief leader of these armies. May Brihaspathi, Dakshina, Yajna and Soma go in the front part of this army. May the Maruts too go as leaders of these armies of the gods, who destroy enemies and are victorious.

##### English translation
May Indra be the leader of these (hosts), may Brihaspathi, Dakshina, Yajna, and Soma go before, let the Maruts march in the van of the destroying and victorious armies of the gods.

> उग्रं ।

> महामनसां भुवनच्यवानां घोषो देवानां जयतामुदस्थात् ॥ ९ ॥

> इंद्रस्य । वृष्णः । वरुणस्य । राज्ञः । आदित्यानां । मरुतां । शर्धः । उग्रं ।  
> महामनसां । भुवनच्यवानां । घोषः । देवानां । जयतां । उत् । अस्थात् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृष्णो वर्षकस्येंद्रस्य राज्यो वरुणस्यादित्यानां मरुतां चोग्रमुद्गूर्णं शर्धो बलमस्माकं भवत्त्विति शेषः । किंच महामनसामुदारमनसां
> भुवनच्यवानां चावयित्यणां देवानां घोषो जयशब्द उदस्थात् । उत्तिष्ठति ॥
> अनूर्ध्वकर्मत्वादात्मनेपदाभावः ॥ पा. १-३-३४ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May the mighty, upraised force (शर्धः (*śardhaḥ*)) of Indra the showerer, of royal Varuṇa, of the Ādityas and of the Maruts be ours (this is the supplied remainder). Moreover, the shout, the cry of victory, of the magnanimous gods, the shakers of the worlds, has arisen (उदस्थात् (*udasthāt*)). Because the verb is not in the sense of upward action, the ātmanepada does not occur (Pā. 1-3-34).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृष्णः (*vṛṣṇaḥ*)—of the bestower of desires
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—Indra
- राज्ञः (*rājñaḥ*)—the lord
- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—of Varuṇa
- आदित्यानां (*ādityānāṃ*)—of the Ādityas
- मरुतां (*marutāṃ*)—of the Maruts
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—the mighty
- शर्धः (*śardhaḥ*)—force (may it be helpful to us)
- महामनसां (*mahāmanasāṃ*)—of the very generous
- भुवनच्यवानां (*bhuvanacyavānāṃ*)—who shake the very world
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—of the gods
- घोषः (*ghoṣaḥ*)—the shout of victory
- उदस्थात् (*udasthāt*)—has risen

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the force of Indra the bestower of desires, and the force of lord Varuṇa, of the Ādityas and of the Maruts be helpful to us. The shout of victory of the very generous gods, who shake the very world, has risen.

##### English translation
(May) the mighty force of the showerer Indra, of the royal Varuna,
of the Adityas and Maruts (be ours). The shout of the magnanimous and
victorious deities, the subverters of worlds, has arisen.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उद्ध॑र्षय मघव॒न्नायु॑धा॒न्युत्सत्व॑नां माम॒कानां॒ मनां॑सि।  
> उद्वृ॑त्रहन्वा॒जिनां॒ वाजि॑ना॒न्युद्रथा॑नां॒ जय॑तां यंतु॒  ॑
> घोषाः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । हर्षय । मघवन् । आयुधानि । उत् । सत्वनां । मामकानां । मनांसि ।  
> उत् । वृत्रेहन् । वाजिनां । वाजिनानि । उत् । रथानां । जयतां । यंतु ।  
> घोषाः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मघवन्निंद्र अस्मदीयान्यायुधान्युद्दर्षय । उत्कृष्टं हर्षय ।
> प्रहरणेषूद्युक्तानि भवंतित्यर्थः । मामकानामस्मदीयानां सत्वनां प्राणिनां
> सेवकानां मनांसि चोद्कर्षय । हे वृत्रहन्निंद्र वाजिनामश्वानां वाजिनानि वेगा
> उद्यंतु । तभा जयतां रथानां घोषा उद्यंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maghavan Indra, rouse up our weapons (उद्धर्षय (*uddharṣaya*)), make them eager in the attacks. Rouse also the minds of my (मामकानां (*māmakānāṃ*)) सत्वनां (*satvanāṃ*), our living beings, our servants. O Vṛtrahan Indra, let the speeds of our horses rise up; and let the sounds of our victorious chariots rise up.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O Indra, the wealthy
- आयुधानि (*āyudhāni*)—our weapons
- उद्धर्षय (*uddharṣaya*)—stimulate
- मामकानां (*māmakānāṃ*)—my
- सत्वानां (*satvānāṃ*)—of the soldiers
- मनांसि (*manāṃsi*)—the minds
- उत् (हर्षय) (*ut (harṣaya)*)—make them full of enthusiasm
- वृत्रहन् (*vṛtrahan*)—O Indra, destroyer of enemies
- वाजिनां (*vājināṃ*)—of our horses
- वाजिनानि (*vājināni*)—the speeds
- उद्यंतु (*udyaṃtu*)—let them appear in abundance
- जयतां (*jayatāṃ*)—victorious
- रथानां (*rathānāṃ*)—of our chariots
- घोषाः (*ghoṣāḥ*)—the sounds
- उत् (*ut*)—let them appear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, stimulate our weapons. Make the minds of our soldiers full of enthusiasm. O Indra, destroyer of enemies, let the speeds of our horses and the sounds of our chariots rise up and appear.

### Printed p. 208

##### English translation
Excite, Maghavan, my weapons, (excite) the spirits of my heroes; slayer of Vritra, let the speed of the horses be accelerated, let the noises of the chariots be increased.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒स्माक॒मिंद्रः॒ समृ॑तेषु ध्व॒जेष्व॒स्माकं॒ या इष॑व॒स्ता ज॑यंतु।  
> अ॒स्माकं॑ वी॒रा उत्त॑रे भवंत्व॒स्मा उ॑ देवा अवता॒ हवे॑षु॥११॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्माकं । इंद्रः । संऋतेषु । ध्वजेषु । अस्माकं । याः । इषवः । ताः । जयंतु ।  
> अस्माकं । वीराः । उत्तरे । भवंतु । अस्मान् । ऊं इति । देवाः । अवत । हवेषु॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्माकं संबंधिष्टेव समृतेषु परसेनां संप्राप्तेषु ध्वजेषु ध्वजवत्सु
> सैनिकेष्ट्विंद्रो रक्षिता भवतु । तथास्माकं या इषवः संति ता एव जयंतु शत्रून् ।
> तथास्माकं । वीरा भटा उत्तर उपरि भवंतु । हे देवाः अस्मा उ अस्मानेवावत रक्षत
> हवेषु संग्रामेषु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May Indra be the protector of our soldiers who carry banners when our banners have met the enemy's army. May the arrows that are ours alone conquer the enemies. May our heroes, our warriors, be uppermost. O gods, protect us alone in the battles.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—our
- ध्वजेषु (*dhvajeṣu*)—with the banners
- संयतेषु (*saṃyateṣu*)—when contact with the enemy's banners has occurred **NOTE**
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra (may he protect us)
- याः (*yāḥ*)—which
- अस्माकं इषवः (*asmākaṃ iṣavaḥ*)—are our arrows
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—those
- जयंतु (*jayaṃtu*)—let them win victory
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—our
- वीराः (*vīrāḥ*)—heroic warriors
- उत्तरे भवंतु (*uttare bhavaṃtu*)—let them be victorious
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods
- हवेषु (*haveṣu*)—in the battles
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us alone
- अवत (*avata*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the banners of our army have met the banners of the enemy armies, may Indra protect us. May the arrows that are ours attain victory. May our heroic warriors win. O gods, protect us alone in the battles.

### Printed p. 209

##### English translation
When the banners are intermingled, may Indra be our (defender), may those arrows which are ours be victorious, may our warriors be triumphant; gods, protect us in battles.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒मीषां॑ चि॒त्तं प्र॑तिलो॒भयं॑ती गृहा॒णांगा॑न्यष्टे॒ परे॑हि ।  
> अ॒भि प्रेहि॒ निर्द॑ह हृ॒त्सु शोकै॑रं॒धेना॒मित्रा॒स्तम॑सा सचंतां॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अमीषां । चित्तं । प्रतिलोभयंती । गृहाण । अंगानि । अष्टे । परा । इहि ।  
> अभि । प्र । इहि । निः । दह । । हृत्सु । शोकैः । अंधेन । अमित्राः । तमसा ।  
> सचंतां ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अष्टे पापाभिमानिनि देवते अमीषां योद्धाणां शत्रूणां चित्तं
> प्रतिलोभयंती विमोहयंत्यंगानि तेषामवयवाञ्चिरअदिकान्गृहाण । स्वीकुरु ।
> अभि प्रेहि । अभिगच्छ । तेषां समीपं गत्वा च हृत्तु हृदयेषु शोकैर्निर्दह ।
> नितरां भस्मीकुरु । तेऽमित्रा अस्मच्छत्रवोऽंधेन तमसा सचंतां । संगच्छंतां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O अष्टे (*aṣṭe*), deity presiding over sin, bewildering the mind of these enemy warriors, seize their limbs, their members beginning with the head **NOTE**; take hold of them. Go against them; having gone near them, burn them with griefs in their hearts, reduce them utterly to ashes. Let these enemies of ours be joined with blinding darkness.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अष्टे (*aṣṭe*)—O deity presiding over sin
- अमीषां (*amīṣāṃ*)—of our enemies
- चित्तं (*cittaṃ*)—the mind
- प्रतिलोभयंती (*pratilobhayaṃtī*)—bewildering
- अंगानि (*aṃgāni*)—their limbs
- गृहाण (*gṛhāṇa*)—seize firmly
- अभि प्रेहि (*abhi prehi*)—go against them
- परेहि (*parehi*)—go far from us
- हृत्सु (*hṛtsu*)—in their hearts
- शोकैः (*śokaiḥ*)—with griefs
- निर्दह (*nirdaha*)—burn
- अमित्राः (*amitrāḥ*)—our enemies
- अंधेन (*aṃdhena*)—sightless
- तमसा (*tamasā*)—with thick darkness
- सचंतां (*sacaṃtāṃ*)—let them be joined

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deity presiding over sin, bewildering the minds of our enemies, seize their limbs firmly. Go against them. Go far from us. Fill their hearts with griefs and burn them. Let our enemies be joined with the sightless, thick darkness.

### Printed p. 210

##### English translation
Bewildering the mind of our foes, Apiva, seize their limbs and depart, proceed against them, burn in their hearts with sorrow, let our enemies be covered with thick darkness.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has given the Nirukta of this Ṛk:
अमीषां चित्तानि प्रज्ञानानि प्रतिलोभयमाना गृहाणांगान्यष्टे परेह्यभिप्रेहि निर्दहैषां हृदयानि शोकैरंधेनामित्रास्तमसा संसेव्यंतां ॥ (*amīṣāṃ cittāni prajñānāni pratilobhayamānā gṛhāṇāṃgānyaṣṭe parehyabhiprehi nirdahaiṣāṃ hṛdayāni śokairaṃdhenāmitrāstamasā saṃsevyaṃtāṃ ‖*) (Ni. 9-33)
O deity of sin named Apvā **NOTE**, bewilder the intellect of our enemies, that is, their power of discrimination. Seize their limbs, that is, hinder their limbs from doing their natural functions. Go to them, and having gone, make their hearts, their minds, be filled with sorrow, grief and the like and burn. Fill their minds with darkness so that those who are in darkness can see nothing to do, that is, destroy their power of discrimination and make them grope in the dark.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रेता॒ जय॑ता नर॒ इंद्रो॑ वः॒ शर्म॑ यच्छतु ।  
> उ॒ग्रा वः॑ संतु बा॒हवो॑ऽनाधृ॒ष्या यथास॑थ ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । इत । जयत । नरः । इंद्रः । वः । शर्म । यच्छतु ।  
> उग्राः । वः । संतु । बाहवः । अनाधृष्याः । यथा । असथ ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे नरो नेतारः संग्रामस्य निर्वोढारो योद्धारः प्रेत । प्रकर्षेण
> गच्छत । गत्वा च जयत तान्प्रतिभटान् ॥ तिजः परत्वात्तिज्ञतिज इति निघाताभावः ॥ वो
> युष्माकमिंद्रः शर्म सुखं यच्छतु । प्रयच्छतु । वो बाहव उग्रा उद्धूर्णबलाः संतु । भवंतु । अनाधृष्या अन्यैरनभिभाव्या यथा यूयमसथ भविष्यथ
> कथोग्राः संतु वो बाहवः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O men, leaders, carriers-through of the battle, warriors, go forth; having gone, conquer those opposing warriors. May Indra grant you happiness. May your arms be fierce, of surging strength, and unassailable by others, as you shall be.

### Printed p. 211

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नरः (*naraḥ*)—O warriors
- प्रेत (*preta*)—advance
- जयत (*jayata*)—win victory
- वे (*ve*)—to you **NOTE**
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- शर्म (*śarma*)—happiness
- यच्छतु (*yacchatu*)—let him give
- यथा (*yathā*)—in the way that
- अनाधृष्याः (*anādhṛṣyāḥ*)—unassailable
- असथ (*asatha*)—you shall be
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- बाहवः (*bāhavaḥ*)—arms
- उग्राः (*ugrāḥ*)—possessed of mighty strength
- संतु (*saṃtu*)—let them be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O warriors, advance. Win victory. May Indra give you happiness. May your arms attain mighty strength, so that you may be unassailable.

##### English translation
Advance, warriors, and conquer; may Indra grant you happiness, may your arms be strong, so that you may be invincible.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The khila mantra to be recited at the end of this sūkta is:
असौ या सेना मरुतः परेषामभ्यैति न ओजसा स्पर्धमाना । तां गूहत तमसापव्रतेन यथामीषामन्यो अन्यं न जानात् ॥ (*asau yā senā marutaḥ pareṣāmabhyaiti na ojasā spardhamānā | tāṃ gūhata tamasāpavratena yathāmīṣāmanyo anyaṃ na jānāt ‖*)
अंधा अमित्रा भवताशीर्षाणा अहय इव । तेषां वो अग्निदग्धनामग्निमूळ्हूनामिंद्रो हंतु वरंवरं ॥ (*aṃdhā amitrā bhavatāśīrṣāṇā ahaya iva | teṣāṃ vo agnidagdhanāmagnimūḷhūnāmiṃdro haṃtu varaṃvaraṃ ‖*)

## Sūkta 104 (Maṇḍala 10)
असावीत्येकादशर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं । वैश्वामित्रस्याष्टकस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । असाव्येकादशाष्टको वैश्वामित्र इति ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ (*asāvītyekādaśarcaṃ paṃcamaṃ sūktaṃ | vaiśvāmitrasyāṣṭakasyārṣaṃ traiṣṭubhamaiṃdraṃ | tathā cānukrāṃtaṃ | asāvyekādaśāṣṭako vaiśvāmitra iti ‖ gataḥ sūktaviniyogaḥ ‖*)
Anuvāda: This sūkta, beginning असावि (*asāvi*), is the fifth sūkta in the ninth anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Aṣṭaka, son of the seer Viśvāmitra; the deity is Indra; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: असाव्येकादशाष्टको वैश्वामित्रः (*asāvyekādaśāṣṭako vaiśvāmitraḥ*). The viniyoga has already been stated earlier.

### Printed p. 212
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 9; Sūkta 104; Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 5; Vargas 24, 25; number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 11. Seer: Aṣṭaka Vaiśvāmitra. Deity: Indra. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> असा॑वि॒ सोमः॑ पुरुहूत॒ तुभ्यं॒ हरि॑भ्यां य॒ज्ञमुप॑ याहि॒  ॑
> तूयं ।  
> तुभ्यं॒ गिरो॒ विप्र॑वीरा इया॒ना द॑धन्व॒र इं॑द्र॒ पिबा॑ सु॒तस्य॑ ॥१॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> असावि । सोमः । पुरुहूत । तुभ्यं । हरिभ्यां । यज्ञं । उप । याहि । तूयं ।  
> तुभ्यं । गिरः । विप्रवीराः । इयानाः । दधन्वरे । इंद्र । पिब । सुतस्य ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पुरुहूत बहुभिः स्तोतृभिराहूत तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं सोमोऽसावि । अभिषुतोऽभूत् ॥ सुञ् अभिषव इत्यस्मात्कर्मणि लुज् ॥ अतो हरिभ्यां हरितवर्णाभ्यामश्वाभ्यां यज्ञमस्मदीयं तूयं तूर्णमुप याहि ॥ उपागच्छ । तुभ्यं
> त्वदर्थं गिरोऽस्मदीयाः स्तुतयो विप्रवीराः । विप्रा मेधाविनो वीरा विशेषेण
> प्रेरयितारः प्रोद्धमयितारो यासां तास्तथोक्ताः । इयाना गमनशीला
> दधन्विरे । गम्यंते । अस्माभिर्युष्मस्त्रीणनाय प्राप्यंत इत्यर्थः ॥ ईज् गतौ ।
> ताच्चीलिकः शानच् । छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् । धविर्गत्यर्थः । इदित्वान्नुम् ।
> कर्मणि च्छांदसो लिट् ॥ यत एवमतः सुतस्याभिषुतस्यांशं सुतं सोमं
> ना पिब !

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, invoked by many singers, Soma has been pressed for you; it has been pressed for your sake. Therefore come quickly to our sacrifice with your two bay (green-hued) horses. For you are our praises, विप्रवीराः (*vipravīrāḥ*), those whose impellers are the wise (विप्रा (*viprā*) are the intelligent, वीराः (*vīrāḥ*) those who especially impel and stir up); इयानाः (*iyānāḥ*), going quickly, दधन्विरे (*dadhanvire*), they are approached by us, that is, they are brought to please you. Since this is so, drink the pressed Soma. **NOTE**

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- असावि (*asāvi*)—has been pressed
- हरिभ्यां (*haribhyāṃ*)—with your horses

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, worthy of the invocation of many, Soma juice has been pressed for you. Come quickly to our sacrifice with your horses. Our praises, recited by the wise and approaching you, are offered to you and reach you. Drink the Soma that has been pressed.

##### English translation
The Soma has been effused for you, (Indra), the invoked of many, come quickly to the sacrifice with your two bay horses; our praises recited by the wise, moving quickly, are addressed to you; drink, Indra, of the libation.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒प्सु धू॒तस्य॑ हरिवः॒ पिबे॒ह नृभिः॑ सु॒तस्य॑ ज॒ठरं॑ पृणस्व ।  
> मि॒मि॒क्षुर्यमद्र॑य इंद्र॒ तुभ्यं॒ तेभि॑र्वर्धस्व॒ मद॑मुक्थवाहः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अप्सु । धूतस्य । हरिवः । पिब । इह । नृभिः । सुतस्य । जठरं । पृणस्व ।  
> मिमिक्षुः । यं । अद्रयः । इंद्र । तुभ्यं । तेभिः । वर्धस्व । मदं । उक्तवाहः ॥ २॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रथमे पर्याये ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिशस्त्रेऽप्सु धूतस्येत्येषा याज्या । सूत्रितं
> च । अप्पु धूतस्य हरिवः पिबेहेति याज्या । आ. ६-४ । इति ॥
> हे हरिवः ऋक्सामे ना इंद्रस्य हरी । ऐ. ब्रा. २-२४ । इति श्रुतेः स्तोत्रशस्त्राधारभूताभ्यामृक्सामाभ्यां हरिभ्यां तद्वन्निंद्र अप्सेकधानादिषूदकेषु धूतस्य

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the first paryāya, in the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's śastra, the Ṛk अप्सु धूतस्य (*apsu dhūtasya*) is the yājyā. It is stated in the sūtra: अप्पु धूतस्य हरिवः पिबेहेति याज्या (*appu dhūtasya harivaḥ pibeheti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-4). Then he addresses Indra as हरिवः (*harivaḥ*), "possessor of bay horses": by the śruti ऋक्सामे ना इंद्रस्य हरी (*ṛksāme nā iṃdrasya harī*) (Ai. Brā. 2-24), the Ṛk and the Sāman are Indra's two bay horses, the supports of stotra and śastra; and he is "having the two" of them. The explanation then begins with the Soma shaken in the waters, in the vessels of water such as the अप्सेकधान (*apsekadhāna*) **NOTE**.

### Printed p. 214

> कंपितस्य । अभिषुतस्येत्यर्थः । तथा नृभिः कर्मनेतृभिः कर्मनिर्वाहकैरध्वय्यादिभिः
> सुतस्याभिषुतस्य ॥ उभयत्र क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानसंज्ञायां
> चतुर्थ्यर्थे बहुलं छंदसीति षष्ठी ॥ ईदृशं सोममिहास्मिन्यज्ञे पिब । पीत्वा च
> जतरं स्वकीयं पृणस्व । पूरय च ॥ चादिलोपे विभाषेति प्रथमा तिज्वभक्तिर्न
> निहन्यते ॥ यं सोममद्रयोऽभिषवग्राणो हे इंद्र तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं मिमिक्षुः
> सेक्तुमभिषोतुमैच्छन् । अभिषवमकुर्वन्नित्यर्थः ॥ मिह सेचन इत्यस्य सनि लिज्युसि
> रूपं ॥ हे उक्तवाह उक्थैः शस्त्रैरुह्यमान तेभिस्तैर्मदं वर्धस्व ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This continues the commentary on the second Ṛk. धूतस्य (*dhūtasya*) means "shaken", that is, pressed. Likewise the Soma is pressed by "men" (नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)), the leaders of the rite, the adhvaryu and the others who carry it out. Sāyaṇa says the verbal action must be taken as understood in both places. The genitive stands for the dative because a "recipient" is implied, by the rule बहुलं छंदसीति (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasīti*). Indra is to drink such Soma here, in this sacrifice, and having drunk it to fill his own belly. The nominative is due to the omission of च (*ca*), and the verb is not accented.

The Soma that the pressing stones desired to sprinkle for Indra, that is, for his sake, means that they performed the pressing. मिमिक्षुः (*mimikṣuḥ*) is the desiderative form of the root मिह (*miha*), "to sprinkle". उक्तवाह (*uktavāha*) addresses Indra as one carried by ukthas, that is, by śastras. With these (the hymns) he is to increase his exhilaration.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हरिवः (*harivaḥ*)—O Indra, carried by horses in the form of the Ṛk and Sāman
- अप्पु (*appu*)—joined with the waters
- धूतस्य (*dhūtasya*)—shaken
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by the priests
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—pressed
- (the Soma,) इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- जठरं (*jaṭharaṃ*)—your belly
- पृणस्व (*pṛṇasva*)—fill
- उक्तवाहः (*uktavāhaḥ*)—carried by śastras (praises)
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Soma
- अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*)—the pressing stones
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you
- मिमिक्षुः (*mimikṣuḥ*)—have pressed
- तेभिः (*tebhiḥ*)—with those
- मदं (*madaṃ*)—delight
- वर्धस्व (*vardhasva*)—increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, carried by horses in the form of the Ṛk and Sāman, drink in this sacrifice the Soma that has been shaken together with the waters and pressed by the priests. Fill your belly. O Indra, carried by the śastra-mantras, drink the Soma that the pressing stones have pressed for you, and increase your delight.

##### English translation
Lord of bay steeds, drink at this ceremony of the juice that has been shaken up with the water, fill your belly with the libation offered by the priests, which the grinding-stones desired to express for you, Indra; do you who are carried by hymns enhance your exhilaration with these (hymns).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the first paryāya, among the śastra-mantras to be recited by the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, this Ṛk beginning अप्पु धूतस्य (*appu dhūtasya*) is to be recited as a yājyā mantra. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, अप्पु धूतस्य हरिवः पिबेहेति याज्या (*appu dhūtasya harivaḥ pibeheti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-4).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रोग्रां प्री॒तिं वृष्ण॑ इयर्मि स॒त्यां प्र॒य्यै सु॒तस्य॑ हर्यश्व॒  ॑
> तुभ्यं ।  
> इंद्र॒ धेना॑भिरि॒ह मा॑दयस्व धी॒भिर्विश्वा॑भिः॒ शच्या॑ गृणा॒नः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । उग्रां । पीतिं । वृष्णे । इयर्मि । सत्यां । प्रय्यै । सुतस्य । हरिअश्व । तुभ्यं।  
> इंद्र । धेनाभिः । इह । मादयस्व । धीभिः । विश्वाभिः । शच्या । गृणानः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्वितीये पर्याये ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः प्रोग्रामित्येषा याज्या । सूत्रितं च ।
> अश्वावति प्रथमः प्रोग्रां पीतिं वृष्ट इयर्मि सत्यामिति याज्या । आ. ६-४ । इति ॥
> हे हर्यश्वेंद्र वृष्णे वर्षकाय तुभ्यमुग्रामुद्गूर्णं सत्यां पीतिं
> सोमपानं प्रेयर्मि । प्रेरयामि । किमर्थं । प्रयै प्रगमनाय । कस्य पीतिं ।
> सुतस्याभिषुतस्य । अतो हे इंद्र शच्या शक्त्या कर्मणा वा युक्तो गृणानः
> स्तूयमानस्त्वं विश्वाभिः सर्वाभिर्धेनाभिः स्तुतिवाग्निर्विश्वाभिर्धीभिः सर्वैः कर्मभिश्चेहास्मिन्यागे मादयस्व । तृप्यस्व ॥ मद तृप्तियोगे । आत्मनेपदं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the second paryāya this is the yājyā of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. It is prescribed in the sūtra अश्वावति प्रथमः प्रोग्रां पीतिं वृष्ट इयर्मि सत्यामिति याज्या । आ. (*aśvāvati prathamaḥ progrāṃ pītiṃ vṛṣṭa iyarmi satyāmiti yājyā | ā.*) (Ā. 6-4).

O Haryaśva Indra, to you the showerer I send forth the fierce, true drinking of Soma (पीतिं (*pītiṃ*)), so that you may come forth (प्रयै (*prayai*), "for going forth"). The Soma is the pressed one. Therefore, O Indra, you who are endowed with power or with action and are praised, be exhilarated, that is, be satisfied, here in this sacrifice. Be satisfied with all the praises (धेनाभिः (*dhenābhiḥ*), meaning praising speech) and with all the rites (धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)). The root मद (*mada*) is used in the sense of satisfaction, and the verb is in the ātmanepada.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हरश्व (*haraśva*)—possessing horses called Hari
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*)—to you who grant desired ends
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you
- उग्रां (*ugrāṃ*)—powerful
- सत्यां (*satyāṃ*)—and excellent
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—of the pressed Soma
- पीतिं (*pītiṃ*)—the drinking
- प्रयै (*prayai*)—for your coming
- प्र इयर्मि (*pra iyarmi*)—I offer
- शच्या (*śacyā*)—endowed with action
- गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)—you who are praised by us
- विश्वाभिः (*viśvābhiḥ*)—all
- धेनाभिः (*dhenābhiḥ*)—with praises
- धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)—and with rites
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- मादयस्व (*mādayasva*)—be satisfied

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, who possess horses called Hari, I offer for your coming a powerful and excellent drink of Soma to you who grant desired ends. You who are endowed with action and are praised by us, be satisfied in this sacrifice with all the praises and with all the rites.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the third paryāya this Ṛk is the yājyā in the śastra of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. It is prescribed in the sūtra ऊती शचीवस्तव वीर्येणेति याज्या (*ūtī śacīvastava vīryeṇeti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-4).

O Śacīvat Indra, the powerful one: by your protection and by your valor, they hold food (वयः (*vayaḥ*)) together with offspring. They are उशिजः (*uśijaḥ*), desiring you alone, and ऋतज्ञाः (*ṛtajñāḥ*), knowing the ṛta, that is, the sacrifice. These are the Aṅgirases. Performing a sattra, they were bewildered in the performance on the sixth day, and were brought across by Nābhānediṣṭha. For that reason they are said to know the ṛta. Such Aṅgirases

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)
