> पूर्व० यथा सोमेन नीतां सोमो ददद्गंधर्वाय । ऋ. १०-८५-४१ । इत्यादिक्रमेण नीतां जुहूं जुहूं यथा लब्धवान् तद्वदिदानीमपि ॥ जुहूं । हु
> दानादनयोः । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यत इति क्विप् । जुहोतेर्द्वै चेति द्विर्वचनं
> दीर्घश्च । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्तुदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते नोज्‌धात्तोरिति
> प्रतिषेध उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यण इति स्वरितत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Juhū speaks indirectly: "My husband obtained me thus." O gods, formerly he, being without a wife, went about as a celibate (ब्रह्मचारी (*brahmacārī*)). Therefore, pervading (वेविषत् (*veviṣat*)) all sacrifices with praises and oblations (विषः (*viṣaḥ*), from *viṣl vyāptau*), he is but one limb of the gods' sacrifice; husband and wife are indeed the two limbs of the sacrifice. By that service of the gods Bṛhaspati found (*anvaviṃdat*) his wife, me, named Juhū. The word न (*na*) is in the sense of comparison: as formerly he obtained Juhū, led away by Soma according to the sequence beginning सोमो ददद्गंधर्वाय (*somo dadadgaṃdharvāya*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-41), so now too. The rest gives the grammar of वेविषत् (*veviṣat*) and जुहूं (*juhūṃ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods
- (सः (*saḥ*)—that Bṛhaspati)
- ब्रह्मचारी (*brahmacārī*)—as a celibate, that is, without a wife
- चरति (*carati*)—went about (therefore)
- विषः (*viṣaḥ*)—the gods who come to all sacrifices
- वेविषत् (*veviṣat*)—although Bṛhaspati worshipped them with praises and oblations, that
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—of the sacrifice that worships the gods
- एकं अंगं (*ekaṃ aṃgaṃ*)—only one limb (part)
- भवति (*bhavati*)—is
- तेन (*tena*)—by that worship of the gods
- सोमेन (*somena*)—by Soma (formerly, that is, at the time of marriage)
- नीतां (*nītāṃ*)—led away
- जुह्वं न (*juhvaṃ na*)—as he obtained me, named Juhū
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Bṛhaspati
- जायां (*jāyāṃ*)—me, named Juhū, his wife
- अनु विंदत् (*anu viṃdat*)—now obtained again

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, Bṛhaspati formerly went about as a celibate, that is, without a wife. Since for performing a sacrifice the sacrificer and his wife are both necessary, the two of them

### Printed p. 319
two principal limbs of a sacrifice. Since Bṛhaspati was without a wife, even though he worshipped the gods in the sacrifices with praises and with oblations, that became only one limb of the sacrifice. Because there was no wife, it was as if the two limbs had not been performed. Therefore, in the sacrifice, with the very purpose that the gods might receive the offering made by Bṛhaspati, Bṛhaspati obtained, as before, his wife whom Soma had brought and handed over.

##### English translation
He leads the life of a Brahmacharin, even adoring all the gods; he becomes a portion of the gods; therefore Brihaspati obtained his wife (formerly) brought him by Soma, as the gods receive an offering.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk Juhū, the wife of Bṛhaspati, addressing the gods, speaks thus: "O gods, after my husband Bṛhaspati abandoned me, he wanders as a brahmacārin, that is, alone, without a wife. In the sacrifices he performs, since he has no wife, the sacrifice is not complete. Husband and wife are the two principal limbs of the sacrificial rite. The sacrifice that Bṛhaspati performs without a wife becomes only one limb and so is not complete. The gods do not accept oblations and the like in that incomplete sacrifice. Therefore, just as at the time of the marriage of me and Bṛhaspati he accepted me, whom Soma had brought and handed over, so now too he has obtained me again, free of fault, handed over by the gods." This is the chief purport.
The commentator here cites the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-41 beginning सोमो ददद्गंधर्वाय (*somo dadadgaṃdharvāya*):
सोमो ददद्गंधर्वाय ऎंब ऋ. सं. १०-८५-४१ ऋक्कन्नु उदाहरिसिद्दारॆ— सोमो ददद्गंधर्वाय गंधर्वो दददग्नये । रयिं च पुत्रांश्चादाग्निर्मह्यमथो इमां ॥ (*somo dadadgaṃdharvāya èṃba ṛ. saṃ. 10-85-41 ṛkkannu udāharisiddārè— somo dadadgaṃdharvāya gaṃdharvo dadadagnaye | rayiṃ ca putrāṃścādāgnirmahyamatho imāṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-4)
**NOTE**
To understand the meaning of this Ṛk one must know the Ṛk before it, stated in the same place:
सोमः प्रथमो विविदे गंधर्वो विविद उत्तरः । तृतीयो अग्निष्टे पतिस्तुरीयस्ते मनुष्यजाः ॥ (*somaḥ prathamo vivide gaṃdharvo vivida uttaraḥ | tṛtīyo agniṣṭe patisturīyaste manuṣyajāḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-40)
Before marriage, while the girl is in childhood, Soma is said to be her husband, that is, her protector; afterwards, in the age of adolescence, the Gandharva is her protector; then, in the stage of maturity, that is, when she has reached marriageable age and is in youth,

### Printed p. 320
Agni is said to be the husband or protector of the girl. Therefore the girl's coming from childhood to adolescence and from there to youth is stated by the Ṛk सोमो ददद्गंधर्वाय (*somo dadadgaṃdharvāya*). Soma gives this girl into the hands of the Gandharva, the Gandharva gives her into the hands of Agni, and Agni hands her over to the human husband, her natural husband; so it is described. In the present Ṛk, "Soma handed Juhū over to Bṛhaspati" means: since at the time of the marriage, in accordance with the rule of the śāstra, the passing in order from Soma to the Gandharva and from the Gandharva to Agni had Soma as its first cause, Soma alone is mentioned here.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पुन॒र्वै दे॒वा अ॑ददुः॒ पुन॑र्मनु॒ष्या॑ उ॒त ।  
> राजा॑नः स॒त्यं कृ॑ण्वा॒ना ब्र॑ह्मजा॒यां पुन॑र्ददुः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुनः । वै । देवाः । अददुः । पुनः । मनुष्याः । उत ।  
> राजानः । सत्यं । कृष्णानाः । ब्रह्मजायां । पुनः । ददुः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> लाभहेतुमाह । देवा ब्रह्मजायां जुहूं बृहस्पतये पुनरददुः । वैशब्दः प्रसिद्धवाची । उताप्यर्थे । मनुष्या अपि पुनरददुः । एवं देवमनुष्यैः कृतं
> दानं सत्यं यथार्थं कृष्णानाः कुर्वाणाः राजानोऽपि पुनस्तस्मै ददुः । एवमव्यवहार्यनिमित्तं पापमपि व्यनाशयन्निति भावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He states the reason for the obtaining. The gods gave back Brahmajāyā, that is Juhū, to Bṛhaspati. The word वै (*vai*) denotes what is well known; उत (*uta*) is in the sense of "also": men too gave her back. Thus, the gift made by gods and men being made true, i.e. real, the kings also gave her back to him. The sense is that in this way they destroyed even the sin that came from her having been unfit for intercourse.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- ब्रह्मजायां (*brahmajāyāṃ*)—Juhū, the wife of Brahma
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- आददुः (*ādaduḥ*)—gave to Bṛhaspati
- मनुष्याः (*manuṣyāḥ*)—men also gave
- सत्यं कृष्णानः (*satyaṃ kṛṣṇānaḥ*)—observing truth
- राजानः (*rājānaḥ*)—kings
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- ददुः (*daduḥ*)—gave

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods gave Juhū, the wife of Brahma, again to Bṛhaspati. Men also gave. The kings who observe truth also gave again. That is, men and kings approved what the gods had given.

### Printed p. 321

##### English translation
The gods gave her back again, men also gave her back, and kings confirming (the gift) gave Brahme's wife back again.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पु॒न॒र्दाय॑ ब्रह्मजा॒यां कृ॒त्वी दे॒वैर्नि॑किल्बि॒षं ।  
> ऊर्जं॑ पृथि॒व्या भ॒क्त्वा यो॑रुगा॒यमुपा॑सते ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुनःदाय । ब्रह्मजायां । कृत्वी । देवैः । निकिल्बिषं ।  
> ऊर्जं । पृथिव्याः । भक्त्याय । उरुगायं । उप । आसते ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवैः ॥ सुपां सुपो भवंतीति जसस्तृतीयादेशः ॥ देवा निकिल्पिषं ॥ अर्थाभावेऽव्ययिभावः । समासस्वरः ॥ तस्याः किल्बिषाभावं कृत्वी ॥ स्नात्वादयश्चेति
> निपातितः ॥ कृत्वा ब्रह्मजायां ब्रह्मणो बृहस्पतेर्भार्यां पुनर्दाय पुनर्दत्वा ॥
> पुनश्चनसोश्चंदसि गतिसंज्ञा वक्तव्येति । पा. १-४-६०-२ । पुनःशब्दस्य गतिसंज्ञायां
> समासल्यप् । न ल्यपि । पा. ६-४-६९ : इतीत्वप्रतिषेधः ! कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥
> पृथिव्याऊर्जं रसभूतमन्नं हवीरूपं भक्त्याय। क्वो यक्! पा. ७-१-४७ । इति
> यगागमः ॥ भक्त्वा विभज्योरुगायं बहुकीर्तिं बहुभिः स्तोतव्यं ना बार्हस्पत्यं
> यज्ञमुपासते । सेवंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

देवैः (*devaiḥ*): the third-case ending is substituted for *jas*. निकिल्पिषं (*nikilpiṣaṃ*): the gods, having made her free of fault, कृत्वी (*kṛtvī*) (the form is irregularly given), having made Brahmajāyā, the wife of Brahma, that is Bṛhaspati, and having given her back again, having divided the sap-like food of the earth, in the form of oblation, they worship, that is serve, the much-renowned one, praised by many, the sacrifice belonging to Bṛhaspati.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवैः (*devaiḥ*)—the gods
- ब्रह्मजायां (*brahmajāyāṃ*)—Juhū, the wife of Brahma
- निकिल्पिषं (*nikilpiṣaṃ*)—as one free of fault
- कृत्वी (*kṛtvī*)—having made
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the earth
- ऊर्जं (*ūrjaṃ*)—the sap-like oblation
- भक्त्याय (*bhaktyāya*)—having divided
- उरुगायं (*urugāyaṃ*)—Bṛhaspati, worthy of praise
- उपासते (*upāsate*)—they serve

##### Grammar

- देवैः — सुपां सुपो भवंतीति जसस्तृतीयादेशः ।
- निकिल्पिषं — अर्थाभावेऽव्ययिभावः । समासस्वरः । तस्याः किल्बिषाभावं कृत्वी ।
- कृत्वी — स्नात्वादयश्चेति निपातितः ।
- पुनर्दाय — पुनश्चनसोश्चंदसि गतिसंज्ञा वक्तव्येति । पा. १-४-६०-२ । पुनःशब्दस्य गतिसंज्ञायां समासल्यप् । न ल्यपि । पा. ६-४-६९ । इतीत्वप्रतिषेधः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ।
- भक्त्याय — क्वो यक् । पा. ७-१-४७ । इति यगागमः ।

### Printed p. 322

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods, having made Juhū, the wife of Brahma, free of fault, and having divided the sap-like oblation of the earth, serve Bṛhaspati, who is worthy of praise.

##### English translation
The gods having given back Brahma's wife, and made her free from sin, having partaken of the food of the earth, sat down to (the sacrifice of) the widely-hymned Brihaspati.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

While Bṛhaspati was without his wife Juhū, the gods were unable to accept the oblations and the like that he offered in the sacrifices he performed. But after Juhū, made free of fault, rejoined Bṛhaspati, the gods were able to accept oblations and the like in the sacrifices that Bṛhaspati performed together with his wife. Therefore this Ṛk says that after handing the wife over to Bṛhaspati the gods began to share the oblation among themselves and partake of it.

## Sūkta 110 (Maṇḍala 10)
Introduction.
In the Saṃhitā of the Ṛgveda there are ten Āprī-sūktas in all. Of these the present sūkta is the last (tenth) Āprī-sūkta. These Āprī-sūktas are as follows:

| 2 | समिद्धो अग्न आ वह (*samiddho agna ā vaha*) | १ (*1*) | १४२ (*142*) | दीर्घतमा औचथ्यः (*dīrghatamā aucathyaḥ*) | ११ (*11*) | | 221 |
| 3 | समिद्धो अद्य राजसि (*samiddho adya rājasi*) | १ (*1*) | १८८ (*188*) | आगस्त्यो मैत्रावरुणिः (*āgastyo maitrāvaruṇiḥ*) | १४ (*14*) | | 216 |
| 4 | समिद्धो अग्निर्निहितः (*samiddho agnirnihitaḥ*) | २ (*2*) | ३ (*3*) | गृत्समदः (*gṛtsamadaḥ*) | १४ (*14*) | | 454 |
| 5 | समित्समित्सुमना (*samitsamitsumanā*) | ३ (*3*) | ४ (*4*) | गाधिनो विश्वामित्रः (*gādhino viśvāmitraḥ*) | १५ (*15*) | | 665 |
| 6 | सुसमिद्धाय शोचिषे (*susamiddhāya śociṣe*) | ५ (*5*) | ५ (*5*) | वसुश्रुत आत्रेयः (*vasuśruta ātreyaḥ*) | १८ (*18*) | | 805 |
| 7 | जुषस्व नः समिधमग्ने (*juṣasva naḥ samidhamagne*) | ७ (*7*) | २ (*2*) | मैत्रावरुणिर्वसिष्ठः (*maitrāvaruṇirvasiṣṭhaḥ*) | २१ (*21*) | | 647 |
| 8 | समिद्धो विश्वतस्पतिः (*samiddho viśvataspatiḥ*) | ९ (*9*) | ५ (*5*) | काश्यपोऽसितोदेव लो वा (*kāśyapo 'sitodeva lo vā*) | २५ (*25*) | | 612 |

### Printed p. 323
Among these there are mantras with the deities इध्वः (*idhvaḥ*) (समिद्भोग्निर्वा (*samidbhognirvā*)), नराशंसः (*narāśaṃsaḥ*), तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*), इळः (*iḷaḥ*), बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*), देवीर्द्वारः (*devīrdvāraḥ*), उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*), दैवौ होतारौ प्रचेतसौ (*daivau hotārau pracetasau*), तिस्रो देव्यः सरस्वतीळाभारत्यः (*tisro devyaḥ sarasvatīḷābhāratyaḥ*), त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*), वनस्पतिः (*vanaspatiḥ*), स्वाहाकृतयः (*svāhākṛtayaḥ*). But as to the deities Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt, in some sūktas the one deity Narāśaṃsa alone is praised, in others the one deity Tanūnapāt alone, and in others both deities Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt. According to this, these Āprī-sūktas are divided in three ways. The Āprī-sūktas composed by the ṛṣis Vasiṣṭha, Atri, Vādhryaśva and Gṛtsamada, that is:
1. जुषस्व नः समिधमग्ने (*juṣasva naḥ samidhamagne*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2 (मैत्रावरुणिर्वसिष्ठः (*maitrāvaruṇirvasiṣṭhaḥ*))
2. सुसमिद्धाय शोचिषे (*susamiddhāya śociṣe*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-5 (वसुश्रुत अत्रेयः (*vasuśruta atreyaḥ*))
3. इमां मे अग्ने समिधं (*imāṃ me agne samidhaṃ*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-70 (सुमित्रो वाध्यश्वः (*sumitro vādhyaśvaḥ*))
4. समिद्धो अग्निर्निहितः (*samiddho agnirnihitaḥ*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3 (गृत्समदः (*gṛtsamadaḥ*))
These four sūktas belong to one group. In them there are single Ṛks with Narāśaṃsa as deity. Therefore these four sūktas are called नराशंसवंति सूक्तानि (*narāśaṃsavaṃti sūktāni*)—Āprī-sūktas that praise only the deity Narāśaṃsa.
1. सुसमिद्दो न आ वह (*susamiddo na ā vaha*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13 (मेधातिथिः काण्वः (*medhātithiḥ kāṇvaḥ*))
2. समिद्धो अग्न आ वह (*samiddho agna ā vaha*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-142 (दीर्घतमा औचथ्यः (*dīrghatamā aucathyaḥ*))
These two Āprī-sūktas belong to the second group. In them there are single Ṛks on behalf of both deities, Narāśaṃsa and Tanūnapāt. Therefore, since both deities are present in these Āprī-sūktas, in sūkta 1-142, leaving out Indra, there come to be twelve homas in place of the eleven Prayāja homas.
1. समिद्धो अद्य राजसि (*samiddho adya rājasi*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-188 (आगस्तो मैत्रावरुणः (*āgasto maitrāvaruṇaḥ*))
2. समित्समित्सुमना (*samitsamitsumanā*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4 (गाधिनो विश्वामित्रः (*gādhino viśvāmitraḥ*))
3. समिद्धो विश्वतस्पतिः (*samiddho viśvataspatiḥ*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-5 (काश्यपेऽसितो देवलो वा (*kāśyape 'sito devalo vā*))
4. समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो (*samiddho adya manuṣo*)—Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110 (जमदग्नि र्भार्गवः (*jamadagni rbhārgavaḥ*))
These sūktas belong to the third group. In them there are only Ṛks with Tanūnapāt as deity (there are no Ṛks with Narāśaṃsa as deity). Therefore they are called तनूनपात्वंति सूक्तानि (*tanūnapātvaṃti sūktāni*), that is, Āprī-sūktas containing mantras with the deity Tanūnapāt.

### Printed p. 324
All matters concerning the Āprī-sūktas we have set out in detail in the introductions and Special Topics of some of the Āprī-sūktas above. Now what is said about these sūktas in the Bṛhaddevatā, and Yāska's Nirukta, will be given. In chapters 2 and 3 of the Bṛhaddevatā it is said thus:
प्रथमायां स्तुतश्चेध्मो द्वितीयायां तनूनपात् । नराशंसस्कृतीयायां चतुर्थ्यां स्तूयते त्विळः ॥ (*prathamāyāṃ stutaścedhmo dvitīyāyāṃ tanūnapāt | narāśaṃsaskṛtīyāyāṃ caturthyāṃ stūyate tviḷaḥ ‖*) (147)
147. In the first Ṛk Idhma (the kindled fire) is praised, in the second the deity Tanūnapāt, in the third the deity Narāśaṃsa, in the fourth the deity Iḷaḥ.
बर्हिरेव तु पंचम्यां द्वारो देव्यस्ततोऽन्यया । नक्तोषासा तु सप्तम्यामष्टम्यां संस्तुतौ सह ॥ (*barhireva tu paṃcamyāṃ dvāro devyastato 'nyayā | naktoṣāsā tu saptamyāmaṣṭamyāṃ saṃstutau saha ‖*) (148)
148. In the fifth Ṛk the deity Barhis (the cut darbha grass), in the next Ṛk the deities Dvāro Devyaḥ, the deities presiding over the doors, in the seventh Ṛk the deities Naktoṣāsā (the deities presiding over night and dawn), in the eighth Ṛk
दैव्याविति तु होतार् नवम्यामृचि संस्तुताः । तिस्रो देव्यो दशम्यां तु ज्ञेयस्त्वष्टैव तु स्तुतः ॥ (*daivyāviti tu hotār navamyāmṛci saṃstutāḥ | tisro devyo daśamyāṃ tu jñeyastvaṣṭaiva tu stutaḥ ‖*) (149)
149. the deities Daivya Hotārau; in the ninth Ṛk the three goddesses Tisro Devyaḥ (Sarasvatī, Iḷā, Bhāratī); in the tenth Ṛk Tvaṣṭā;
एकादश्यां तु सूक्तस्य स्तुतं विद्याद्वनस्पतिं । द्वादश्यां तु स्तुता देवीर्विद्यात्वाहाकृतीरिति ॥ (*ekādaśyāṃ tu sūktasya stutaṃ vidyādvanaspatiṃ | dvādaśyāṃ tu stutā devīrvidyātvāhākṛtīriti ‖*) (150)
150. in the eleventh Ṛk the deity Vanaspati, in the twelfth Ṛk the deity Svāhākṛti are praised.
सूक्तेऽस्मिन्प्रत्यचं यास्तु देवताः परिकीर्तिताः । ता एव सर्वास्वाप्रीषु द्वितीया तु विकल्पते ॥ (*sūkte 'sminpratyacaṃ yāstu devatāḥ parikīrtitāḥ | tā eva sarvāsvāprīṣu dvitīyā tu vikalpate ‖*) (151)
151. Whichever deities are praised in each Ṛk of this sūkta, all of them are praised in this same order in all (ten) Āprī-sūktas. In the matter of the second deity (Tanūnapāt or Narāśaṃsa) there is a slight difference.
प्रैपैः सहाप्रीसूक्तानि तानेकादश संति च । यजूंषि प्रैषसूक्तं वा दशैतानीतराणि तु ॥ (*praipaiḥ sahāprīsūktāni tānekādaśa saṃti ca | yajūṃṣi praiṣasūktaṃ vā daśaitānītarāṇi tu ‖*) (152)

### Printed p. 325

Three groups or varieties of the Āprī hymns.

152. Counting the Praiṣa hymn as well, there are eleven Āprī hymns in all. Since the Praiṣa hymn belongs mainly to the Yajurveda and indicates its mantras, if it is left out there are ten Āprī hymns in all in the Ṛgveda.

> सौत्रामणानि तु त्रीणि प्राजापत्याश्वमेधिके ।
> पुरुषस्य तु यन्मेधे यजुःस्वेव तु तानि षट् ॥ १५३ ॥

153. Besides these, three Āprī hymns belong to the sacrifice called Sautrāmaṇī, and one Āprī hymn each belongs to the sacrifices called Prājāpatya, Aśvamedha and Puruṣamedha. These six Āprī hymns in all belong to the Yajurveda.

> अत्रैव प्रैषसूक्तं स्यान्न यजुःष्वाद्रियेत तत् ।
> तेषां प्रैषगतं सूक्तं यच्च दीर्घतमा जगौ ॥ १५४ ॥

154. Of these six Āprī hymns, only the Praiṣa mantras numbered 29 to 40 in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā of the Śukla Yajurveda need be examined. There is no need to consider the remaining five hymns. The seer named Dīrghatamas recited the 11 mantras of the Praiṣa hymn mentioned above.

> मेधातिथौ यदुक्तं च त्रीण्येवोभयवंति तु ।
> ऋषौ गृत्समदे यच्च वाध्यश्वे च यदुच्यते
> ॥ १५५ ॥

155. Of the above 10 Āprī hymns, in the hymn seen by the seer Medhātithi (hymn 13 of Maṇḍala 1) and in the hymn seen by the seer Dīrghatamas, beginning समिद्धो अग्न आ वह (*samiddho agna ā vaha*) (hymn 142 of Maṇḍala 1), two deities, Tanūnapāt and Narāśaṃsa, stand in the place of the second deity. Therefore these 2 hymns are named "Ubhayavanti hymns" (those having both). There are three more Āprī hymns in which, as in this hymn, Narāśaṃsa is the deity in the place of the second deity. They are: the hymn seen by the seer Gṛtsamada (hymn 3 of Maṇḍala 2), the hymn beginning समिद्धो अग्निर्निहितः (*samiddho agnirnihitaḥ*); the hymn beginning इमां मे अग्ने (*imāṃ me agne*) seen by the seer Vādhryaśva (hymn 70 of Maṇḍala 10); the fifth hymn of the fifth Maṇḍala, beginning सुसमिद्दायॆ (*susamiddāyè*), seen by Vasuśruta Ātreya; and the second hymn of the seventh Maṇḍala, beginning जुषस्व नः (*juṣasva naḥ*), seen by Vasiṣṭha. Since in these four hymns the second deity is Narāśaṃsa, these four Āprī hymns are named "Narāśaṃsavanti hymns".

> नराशंसवदत्रेश्च ददर्श च यदौर्वशः ।
> तनूनपादगस्त्यश्च जमदग्निश्च यज्जगौ
> विश्वामित्र ऋषियर्च जगौ वै काश्यपोऽसितः ।
> मेधातिथेर्यचां यास्तु प्रोक्ता द्वादश देवताः
> ॥ १५६ ॥
> ॥ १५७ ॥

156-157. In the 188th hymn of the first Maṇḍala beginning समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो (*samiddho adya manuṣo*), seen by the seer Agastya; in the 110th hymn of the 10th Maṇḍala beginning समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो (*samiddho adya manuṣo*), seen by the seer Jamadagni; in the fourth hymn of the third Maṇḍala beginning समित्समित्सुमना (*samitsamitsumanā*), seen by the seer Viśvāmitra; and in the 5th hymn of the 9th Maṇḍala beginning समिद्धो विश्वतस्पतिः (*samiddho viśvataspatiḥ*), seen by the seer Asita (or Devala), son of Kaśyapa, Tanūnapāt is the second deity. Therefore these 4 hymns are named "Tanūnapātvanti hymns". In the 13th hymn of the 1st Maṇḍala, seen by the seer Medhātithi, twelve deities in all are praised.

> संपद्यंते यथाग्निं ताः संपदं तां निबोधत ।
> इध्मो यः सर्वमेवाग्निरयं हीध्मः समिध्यते
> ध्मातेर्नैतत्कृतं रूपं ध्मातो हीध्मः समिध्यते
> ॥ १५८ ॥

158. I shall tell how these deities reflect Agni; listen. In all these Āprī hymns the word इध्मः (*idhmaḥ*) in the first Ṛk indicates Agni. For the word समिध्यते (*samidhyate*) means "is kindled and made to blaze", and the word *dhmāti* means "blows (with a blow-pipe) and makes it burn". Since Agni is concerned in these two acts (kindling, and blowing it into flame), the words समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*) and the like found in the first Ṛk indicate Agni himself. Therefore the deity of the first Ṛk of an Āprī hymn is Agni (the blazing one).

Here the second chapter of the work called Bṛhaddevatā ends.

The third chapter

> तनूनपादयं त्वेव नाम्ना यच्छत्यसौ तनुं ।
> नपादिति प्रजामाहुरमुतोऽस्य च संभवं
> ॥ ० ॥

Tanūnapāt, Narāśaṃsa, Iḷā, Barhis — these deities.

1. Tanūnapāt— This Agni has the name Tanūnapāt. "नपात् (*napāt*)" means offspring, progeny. Because the celestial Agni extends his body (tanū), and because the terrestrial Agni arises from it, the terrestrial Agni is named Tanūnapāt.

### Printed p. 327

> नराशंसमिहैके तु यज्ञमाहुरथेतरे ।
> नराः शंसंति सर्वेऽस्मिन्नासीना इति नाध्वरे
> ॥ २ ॥

2. Narāśaṃsaḥ— Some say that this deity Narāśaṃsa is the sacrifice. Or else, because all people (narāḥ) sit in the sacrifice and praise (śaṃsa) this deity, this deity has come by the name Narāśaṃsa.

> एतमेवाहुरन्येग्निं नराशंसोऽध्वरे ह्ययं ।
> नरैः प्रशस्य आसीनैराहुश्चवर्त्विजो नरः ॥ ३ ॥

3. Others again say that this deity (Narāśaṃsa) is Agni. For Agni, this deity, is praised by the men (people) seated in the sacrifice. The officiating priests also say the same.

> इळस्त्वषिकृतं रूपमाडेश्व स्तुतिकर्मणः ।
> इळावांस्तेन वोक्तोऽग्निरिडिना वृद्धि कर्मणा ॥ ४ ॥

4. The seers say that the word इळॆ (*iḷè*) is derived from the root ईळॆ (*īḷè*) stut (to praise). Agni is also named Iḷāvān. This word is derived either from the root īḍ, to praise, or from the root id, to grow.

> बर्हिरेवायमग्निस्तु सर्वं हि परिबृंहितं ।
> अनेन यद्दु तो ना सन्निध्मन परिबृंहितः ॥ ५ ॥

5. Barhiḥ— Agni himself is also called by the name Barhiḥ. For Agni, nourished by food in the form of the oblation, or by the kindling wood, grows (paribṛṃhitaḥ).

> द्वारस्तु देव्यो याः प्रोक्ता विश्वेषां तास्तु पत्नयः ।
> अग्नायामनुर्वंते तथाग्नाय्गिमेव च ॥ ६ ॥

Devīr dvāraḥ and Uṣāsānaktā — these deities.

6. Dvāraḥ devyaḥ— The wives of all the deities (that is, the divine wives) are called by this name. All of them follow the goddess named Agnāyī, the wife of Agni. This Agnāyī follows Agni.

> आग्नौ ध्रुवं स्थितास्तास्तु संस्तूयंतेऽग्निना सह ।
> प्राधान्यं तासु जैवाग्ने स्तुतिष्टेव हविषु च ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 328

7. These deities are firmly established in Agni, and are praised together with Agni. In the praises offered to them and in the oblations, Agni holds the primacy.

> नक्तोषासौ च ये देव्यावाग्नॆयामेव ते स्मृते ।
> श्याव्यााग्नॆयि हि कालस्य तस्यॆवोषाः कलेव तु ॥ ८ ॥

8. Naktoṣāsau or Uṣāsānaktā (that is, the deity Uṣas and the deity presiding over night)— it is said that these two deities too belong to Agni. For since Agni removes darkness, Agni and darkness (Śyāvī) are, as it were, related in a certain way. Uṣas also is said to be one kalā (one part in sixteen) of that night-time.

> तम उच्छत्युषा नक्तानक्तिमां हिमबिंदुभिः ।
> अपि वाव्यक्तवर्णेति नञ्चूर्वाइच्चीरिदं भवेत् ॥ ९ ॥

9. Tamaḥ ucchatīty uṣāḥ— because she drives away darkness, this deity is named Uṣāḥ. Imāṃ (rātriṃ) anakti himabindubhir ati naktā— because she moistens this night-time with drops of frost (dew), night is named Naktā; or the word naktā may be derived from na-añcati. Since in this night-time nothing is seen clearly, she is also named Naktā— Avyaktavarṇā ("of indistinct colour").

> सा हि दोषा भवत्याद् निशीथे सा तमस्वती ।
> नाम्मा भवत्युषाश्चैव सैषा प्रागुदयाद्रवेः ॥ १० ॥

10. This night deity has three kinds of names according to the time. At the beginning of the night she is named Doṣā, at midnight Tamasvatī, and at the end of the night, that is, before sunrise, Uṣā.

> दैव्याविति तु होतारानाग्नी पार्थिवमध्यम् ।
> दिव्यादग्निर्हि जज्ञाते दैव्या तेनेह जन्मना ॥ ११ ॥

Daivyā hotārā, tisro devyaḥ, Tvaṣṭā.

11. Daivyā hotārā means the terrestrial Agni and the middle (atmospheric) Agni. These two forms of Agni have arisen from the celestial Agni (divyād agneḥ); therefore these two forms of Agni are called by the name Daivyā (belonging to heaven).

> तिस्रस्तु देव्यो याः प्रोक्तास्त्रिस्थानैवेह सा तु वाक् !
> त्रिविधेनोच्यते नाम्मा ज्योतिःषु त्रिषु वर्तनी ॥ १२ ॥

### Printed p. 329

12. Tisro devyaḥ— the deities called tisraḥ devyaḥ (three goddesses) reflect Vāk, or the goddess of speech, who is in the three places. Because this goddess of speech is in three places, she is said to have three kinds of forms and is called by three different names.

> अग्निमेवानुगेळा तु मध्यं प्राप्ता सरस्वती ।
> अमुं स्थिताधि लोकं तु भारती भवति ह्यसौ ॥ १३ ॥

13. Following the terrestrial Agni, the goddess of speech in this world is named Iḷā. The Vāk in the middle (atmospheric) world is named Sarasvatī, and the goddess of speech in the heavenly world is named Bhāratī. (One deity has three different names according to difference of place.)

> सैषा शु त्रिविधा वाग्वै दिवि च व्योम्मि चेह च ।
> व्यस्ता चैव समस्ता च भजत्यग्नीमानपि ॥ १४ ॥

14. Though this goddess of speech is one, she exists by three kinds of names in the three places, earth, atmosphere and heaven. Whether in one form or in separate forms, this deity is united with the Agni of the respective place (with the threefold Agni in earth, atmosphere and heaven).

> त्वष्टा तु यस्त्वयमेव पार्थिवोऽग्निरिति स्तुतिः ।
> पार्थिवस्यास्य वर्चसि स्युः कस्याप्यक् चार्तवेषु च ॥ १५ ॥

15. The deity called Tvaṣṭā is praised as the terrestrial Agni itself (or its transformation); or there are Ṛks that praise this deity as a terrestrial deity (belonging to the place of the earth). And among the Ṛks that praise the seasons there is one Ṛk that praises this deity Tvaṣṭā as a transformation of Agni (Kaśyapa).

> त्वषितस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात्तूर्णमश्नुत एव ना ।
> कर्मसूत्तारणो वेति तेन नामृतदश्नुते ॥ १६ ॥

The celestial deity Tvaṣṭā; the story of the seer Dadhīca; the middle-region Tvaṣṭā.

16. Etymology of the word Tvaṣṭā— The word may be derived from the root tviṣ (to shine) or from the root takṣ. Or this god has come by the name Tvaṣṭā because he obtains quickly (tūrṇa), or because he helps in rites.

> यः सहस्रतमो रश्मी रवेश्वंद्रमुपाश्रितः ।
> सोऽपि त्वष्टारमेवाग्निं परं चेह च यन्मधु ॥ १७ ॥

### Printed p. 330

17. The thousandth ray of the sun has taken refuge in the moon. That ray pervades Tvaṣṭā, a transformation of Agni existing in the earth and in the atmosphere, and the Madhu-vidyā (the knowledge that revives the dead), and has taken refuge there.

> प्रादाद्ब्रह्मापि सुप्रीतः सुताय तदथर्वणः ।
> स चाभवदृष्टेन ब्रह्मणा दीप्तिमत्तरः ॥ १८ ॥

18. At one time Indra, pleased with the seer Dadhyañc, the son of Atharvan, taught him the Madhu-vidyā (Brahma-knowledge). By the power of that knowledge the seer Dadhīci shone with exceeding brilliance (varcas).

> तम्मृषिं निषिषेधेंद्रो मैवं वोचः क्वचिन्मधु ।
> न हि प्रोक्ते मधुन्यस्मिज्जीवंतं त्वोत्सजाम्यहं ॥ १९ ॥

19. While teaching this Madhu-vidyā, Indra said to the seer: "You must not teach this (this Madhu-vidyā) to anyone. If, transgressing my word, you tell it to anyone, then I shall not leave you alive."

> तम्मृषिं त्वश्चिन् देवौ निविक्ते मध्वयाचतां ।
> स च ताभ्यां तदाचष्टे यदुवाच शबीपतिः ॥ २० ॥

20. While matters stood so, at one time the Aśvin deities came to the seer Dadhīci and secretly begged him to teach them that Madhu-vidyā. Hearing this, the seer told them what Śacīpati (Indra) had said, that he should not tell this knowledge to anyone.

> तमब्रूतां तु नासत्यावाश्वेन शिरसा भवान् ।
> मध्वाशु ग्राहयत्वानां मेंद्रश्च त्वा वधीत्ततः ॥ २१ ॥

21. Hearing it, the Aśvin deities said: "Then put on the head of a horse, and in that form teach us the Madhu-vidyā. Indra will not kill you."

> आश्वेन शिरसा तौ तु दध्यज्जाह यदश्विन् ।
> तदस्येंद्रोऽहरत्सं तन्न धत्तामस्य यच्चिरः ॥ २२ ॥

22. Thereupon the seer Dadhyañc taught the Aśvin deities that Madhu-vidyā. Enraged at this, Indra cut off the horse's head of the seer Dadhīci. Afterwards the Aśvin deities joined to his body again the head that he had before.

The Kannada translations of verses 23–31 of the Bṛhaddevatā passage on the sūkta's deities follow. The translation of verse 22 stood at the end of the previous page.

1. The horse-head of the sage Dadhīci, cut off by Indra's thunderbolt, fell into the middle of a lake on the mountain called Śaryaṇāvat. **NOTE**

24. The horse-head, which had sunk in the lake water, rises up from time to time, bestows various boons on living beings, and then sinks into that same water again. This work goes on until the end of the yuga.

25. Tvaṣṭā, a deity of the middle region, is the lord of forms and can produce any form he wishes for living beings and others. This deity is praised in many sūktas, here and there, only incidentally. But there is no separate sūkta that praises him.

26. Vanaspati: the deity who is called Vanaspati is only another form of Agni, who is said to be the protector of the forests. Agni is called Vanaspati because he is the guardian of the forests, or because he protects these forests (the trees) so that they are not harmed.

27. The sage Gṛtsamada praised Agni by the word Vanaspati in the third Ṛk (the Ṛk "medyantu te vahnayaḥ") of the sūkta "mandasva hotrād anu" of six Ṛks (Maṇḍala 2, sūkta 37).

28. In the eighth sūkta of the third Maṇḍala, "añjanti tvā", the deity Vanaspati is praised throughout, as occasion arises, as the sacrificial post and as a great tree. (This is the Kannada rendering of verse 28, whose Sanskrit stands at the foot of this page.)

### Printed p. 332

**Vanaspati and Svāhākṛti**

29. Scholars hold many differing views about the deity called Svāhākṛti. But however much they differ, on this point alone all have one opinion: that this deity Svāhākṛti is a particular form of Agni.

30. For Agni is the maker of the svāhākāras (that is, of the oblations offered with the word *svāhā*, or of the mantras). He is both maker and deity of all mantras of this kind. This Agni is the source of origin of all beings (living creatures): all creatures come into being from him. Among all creatures he alone is without destruction; that is, he is imperishable.

**The Āprī sūktas that praise the two deities Tanūnapāt and Narāśaṃsa**

31. Among the Āprī sūktas (the second deity being Tanūnapāt), there are only three in the Ṛgveda that praise the two deities Tanūnapāt and Narāśaṃsa. (Which these are: the 13th sūkta of the 1st Maṇḍala, seen by the sage Medhātithi Kāṇva, and the 142nd sūkta of the 1st Maṇḍala, seen by the sage Dīrghatamas Aucathya. It is said here that there are three such sūktas; but, leaving aside the Praiṣa sūkta, this is wrong. There are only two.)

32. The second mantra belongs to the Āprī sūkta whose deity is Narāśaṃsa. By the use of this Āprī sūkta, the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice obtains the offspring he desires, strength, food, or wealth.

### Printed p. 333

On the Āprī sūktas, the Nirukta of Yāska runs thus:

अथात अप्रियः । अप्रियः कस्मादाप्नोतेः प्रीणातीर्वा । अप्रीभिराप्रीणातीति च ब्राह्मणं ॥ (*athāta apriyaḥ | apriyaḥ kasmādāpnoteḥ prīṇātīrvā | aprībhirāprīṇātīti ca brāhmaṇaṃ ‖*) (Ni. 8-4)

We now explain the matter of the Āprī sūktas. Why did these sūktas get the name "आप्री (*āprī*)"? Because they reach (āpnuvanti) and please (prīṇanti) the deities. When the deities are praised with the Ṛks of these sūktas, these reach those deities or delight them; therefore this sūkta, dear to the deities, is called an Āprī sūkta. Such is the sense.

In explaining the eleven deities found in the Āprī sūktas, Yāska took this very sūkta as his example and gave a separate Nirukta for each of its 11 Ṛks. The Nirukta of each Ṛk is explained under the special topics of that Ṛk.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> समिद्ध इत्येकादशर्चमेकादशं सूक्तं त्रैष्टुभं । भार्गवो जमदग्नि र्यषिः।
> तस्य पुत्रो रामो ना यः परशुराम इति प्रख्यातः । आप्रीसूक्तमिदं । अतः
> समिदाद्याः सतनूनपातो नराशंसवर्जिताः प्रत्यृचं देवताः । तथा चानुक्रांतं
> समिद्ध एकादश जमदग्निस्तत्सुतो वा राम आप्रिय इति ॥ पशौ जामदग्यानामिदमाप्रीसूक्तं यद्वाविशेषेण सर्वेषां । सूत्रितं च । समिद्धो अद्येति सर्वेषां
> यथर्षि वा । आ. ३-२ । इति ॥ अग्निचयनांगभूते प्राजापत्ये पशौ सर्वेषां नित्यमिदमाप्रीसूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । प्राजापत्ये तु जामदग्यः सर्वेषां । आ. ३-२। इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*)": the eleventh sūkta, of eleven Ṛks, in Triṣṭubh metre. The seer is Jamadagni of the Bhṛgu line; his son, known as Rāma, famed as Paraśurāma, is also named. This is an Āprī sūkta, so the deities of its Ṛks are, one to each Ṛk, the Āprī deities beginning with Samit, with Tanūnapāt but without Narāśaṃsa. Sāyaṇa cites the Anukramaṇī: "Samiddha, eleven, Jamadagni or his son Rāma, Āprī". At the animal sacrifice this Āprī sūkta is for the Jāmadagnyas, or, as a general rule, for all. He cites the sūtra (Ā. 3-2) that it is for all, or according to the seer. At the Prājāpatya animal offering, which is part of the building of the fire-altar, it is always for all; and for this he cites the sūtra of Ā. 3-2: for the Prājāpatya animal offering, the Jāmadagnya (sūkta) is for all.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta "समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*)" is the eleventh sūkta in the ninth anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. Its seer is Jamadagni, son of Bhṛgu; the name Rāma or Paraśurāma is famed as that of Jamadagni's son. The metre is Triṣṭubh. This is an Āprī sūkta. Therefore the deities of the 11 Ṛks of this sūkta are those declared for the Āprī sūktas, beginning with Samit, one deity to each Ṛk. But in this sūkta the deity Tanūnapāt is praised, and the deity Narāśaṃsa is not praised here. The Anukramaṇī says: "Samiddha, eleven, Jamadagni, or his son Rāma, Āprī." At the animal sacrifice this Āprī sūkta is prescribed for those of Jamadagni's line, or generally for others also. On this point the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, "samiddho adya, for all, or according to the seer" (Ā. 3-2), gives the direction. That at the Prājāpatya animal offering, which is part of the fire-building, this sūkta is prescribed for all is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, "at the Prājāpatya, the Jāmadagnya for all" (Ā. 3-2).

> आ च॒ वह॑ मित्रमहश्चि॒त्वान्त्वं दू॒तः क॒विर॑सि॒ प्रचे॑ताः ॥ १ ॥

> आ । च । वह । मित्रमहः । चिकित्वान् । त्वं । दूतः । कविः । असि । प्रचेताः ॥ १ ॥

> हे जातवेदो जातप्रज्ञाग्ने देवः स्वतेजसा दीप्यमानस्त्वं मनुषो
> मनुष्यस्य यष्टुर्दुरोणे । गृहनामैतत् । दुरवन आयासेन रक्षितव्ये गृहेऽद्यास्मिन्कर्मणि समिद्धः सम्यक्प्रज्वालितः सन् देवानिंद्रादीन्यजसि । हविर्भिः पूजय ॥
> समिद्धः । इंधी दीप्तौ । कर्मणि क्ले श्विदितो निष्ठायामितीट् प्रतिषेधः । गतिरनंतर
> इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ हे मित्रमहः स्तुत्यस्तोतृलक्षणत्वेन मित्रभूतानां
> स्तोतृणां पूजयितः तैः पूज्यमान वाग्ने चिकित्वांस्तैः कृताः स्तुतीः प्रजानन्
> चेतनावान्वा त्वमस्मदीये यज्ञे देवाना वह च । आप्रापय ॥ वह प्रापणे ।
> लोटि रूपं । चवायोगे प्रथमेति न निघातः ॥ तथा कविः क्रांतप्रज्ञः अत एव
> प्रचेताः प्रकृष्टज्ञानस्त्वं दूतो देवानां हविष्प्रापणेन हितकारी भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Jātavedas, Agni of born wisdom, divine, shining by your own light: you, kindled today in the *duroṇa* of the man, the sacrificer (duroṇa is a word for house, one to be guarded with effort), in this rite, well kindled, sacrifice to the gods, Indra and the rest; that is, honour them with oblations. "Samiddha" is from the root idh, "to shine". O Mitramahas, you who honour the worshippers, who are friends through the relation of praised and praiser, or who are honoured by them, O Agni, knowing (cikitvān) the praises they have made, or being possessed of consciousness, bring the gods to our sacrifice; "vaha" means "cause to arrive". Likewise you are kavi, of far-reaching wisdom, and therefore pracetāḥ, of excellent knowledge: you are the messenger, working good for the gods by conveying the oblation to them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni, who are of the form of Jātavedas
- मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*)—of the sacrificer
- दुरोणे (*duroṇe*)—in the sacrificial house
- अद्य (*adya*)—today
- समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*)—kindled
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—of divine nature, you
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods, Indra and the rest
- यजसि (*yajasi*)—you worship
- मित्रमहः (*mitramahaḥ*)—you who are honoured by the praisers
- चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*)—who know their rite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, who are of the form of Jātavedas, today, kindled in the sacrificer's house and of divine nature, you worship the gods, Indra and the rest. You who are honoured by the praisers and know their rite, bring the gods here. You who are of far-reaching wisdom and of excellent knowledge are the messenger of the gods.

##### English translation
Kindled to-day, Jatavedas, in the dewlling of the wroshipper, you who are divine, sacrifice to the gods. Bear (the oblation), you who respect your friends, who are intelligent; you are the wise, far-seeing messenger (of the gods).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has given an explanation for every Ṛk of this sūkta:

इध्मः । तासामिध्मः प्रथमगामी भवति । इध्मः समिंधनात् । तस्यैषा भवति । समिद्धो अद्य मनुषो दुरोणे देवो देवान्यजसि जातवेदः । आ च वह मित्रमहश्चित्वान्त्वं दूतः कविरसि प्रचेताः ॥ समिद्धो अद्य मनुष्यस्य मनुष्यस्य गृहे देवो देवान्यजसि जातवेद आ च वह मित्रमहश्विकित्वांश्चेतनावांत्वं दूतः कविरसि प्रजेताः प्रवृद्धचेताः ॥यज्ञेध्म इति कात्थक्यः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥ (*idhmaḥ | tāsāmidhmaḥ prathamagāmī bhavati | idhmaḥ samiṃdhanāt | tasyaiṣā bhavati | samiddho adya manuṣo duroṇe devo devānyajasi jātavedaḥ | ā ca vaha mitramahaścitvāntvaṃ dūtaḥ kavirasi pracetāḥ ‖ samiddho adya manuṣyasya manuṣyasya gṛhe devo devānyajasi jātaveda ā ca vaha mitramahaśvikitvāṃścetanāvāṃtvaṃ dūtaḥ kavirasi prajetāḥ pravṛddhacetāḥ ‖yajñedhma iti kātthakyaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*) (Ni. 8-5)

Among the deities praised in the Āprī sūktas, Idhma is the first. The word samiddha is formed from the root idh ("kindle, make blaze") with the prefix sam. Idhma is the samit, the firewood and similar means of kindling, put into the fire so that it burns. The following Ṛk, "samiddho adya", makes clear the meaning of this word idhma.

### Printed p. 336

"समिद्धो अद्य मनुष्यस्य (*samiddho adya manuṣyasya*)": in the house of the man. "दुरोणे (*duroṇe*)" means house, or sacrificial house. "Duravane": in the house to be guarded with effort. The place that protects us from toil, that is, from dangers, is called duravana or duroṇa. O Agni, in the sacrificial house of every man, that is, of the sacrificer, you are kindled and shine; that is, you burn brilliantly.

"देवो देवान् यजसि जातवेदः (*devo devān yajasi jātavedaḥ*)": O Agni of born wisdom, you, divine or shining, worship the gods; that is, you make the oblations and the like which the human sacrificers offer in you (in Agni) as an offering reach their respective deities. *Jātavedas*: the name Jātavedā is given to Agni because as soon as he is produced by friction in the araṇis, everyone sees and knows him, or because he knows all beings that come into being. Because oblations and the like must be offered to the other deities through Agni alone, he is described by the words "देवान् यजसि (*devān yajasi*)" as worshipping them.

"Ā ca vaha mitramaḥ cikitvān cetanāvān tvam": "मित्रमहः (*mitramahaḥ*)" is explained as स्तुत्यस्तोतृलक्षणत्वेन मित्रभूतानां स्तोतृणां पूज्यमानाग्ने (*stutyastotṛlakṣaṇatvena mitrabhūtānāṃ stotṛṇāṃ pūjyamānāgne*): Agni is the one praised, and the people are the praisers. Between them, that is, between the people and Agni, there is the relation of praised and praiser. Through this relation Agni is a friend, that is, one to be honoured, of the people who praise. "चिकित्वान् (*cikitvān*)" means "चेतनावान् (*cetanāvān*)": तैः कृताः स्तुतीः प्रजानन् (*taiḥ kṛtāḥ stutīḥ prajānan*); the sense is that Agni knows the praises the people make.

"त्वं दूतः कविरसि प्रचेताः प्रवृद्धचेताः (*tvaṃ dūtaḥ kavirasi pracetāḥ pravṛddhacetāḥ*)": People offer oblations to the various deities through Agni. Because Agni makes these reach those deities, he is called the messenger between the people and the gods. "Kavi" means of far-reaching wisdom, of excellent knowledge, of knowledge greater than others, of knowledge beyond the senses. This Agni has knowledge that the senses of men cannot grasp. Therefore he is called pracetāḥ or pravṛddhacetāḥ. Hence, O Agni, you are the messenger who carries the oblations and the like between gods and men, of far-reaching wisdom, with knowledge beyond the senses. Such as you are, "आ च वह (*ā ca vaha*)": bring ("आप्रापय (*āprāpaya*)") the gods to this our sacrificial ground; such is the sense.

"यज्ञेध्म इति कात्थक्यः अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः (*yajñedhma iti kātthakyaḥ agniriti śākapūṇiḥ*)": there are differences of opinion about who this deity Idhma is. The opinion of the teacher Kātthakya (son of Katthaka) is that it is the samit called idhma, used in the sacrifice. The opinion of Śākapūṇi is that idhma means Agni.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Tanūnapāt. नपात् (*napāt*) is the name of the immediate offspring. Here the cow is called तनूः (*tanūḥ*), since enjoyable things such as milk are extended in her; milk is born from her, ghee from the milk, and from that Agni. Or else: in the atmosphere the waters are तन्वः (*tanvaḥ*) (extended), from them come plants and the like, and from these Agni. Such is Agni, and the address is to him as Sujihva, "of fair flame"; or *jihvā* is a name of speech, so "of fair speech". He is asked to sweeten the paths of the sacrifice (ṛta), the means of obtaining its fruit, namely the paths called oblations, by making them shine well with the sweet, intoxicating juice, or with the juice produced by speech; स्वदय (*svadaya*) means "make sweet". Further, मन्मानि (*manmāni*) (from the root मन्यते (*manyate*), which belongs to the roots meaning "to worship") are the praises we desire, worthy of reflection; by the धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*), intellects or else rites, he is to make them and the sacrifice, the oblation to be offered, prosperous, and to make our sacrifice (अध्वरं (*adhvaraṃ*)) go to the gods. The affix त्रा (*trā*) after the word देव (*deva*) is in the sense of the locative.
