- तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*)—one named Tanūnapāt
- सुजिह्व (*sujihva*)—O Agni, who have an excellent tongue
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice
- यानान् (*yānān*)—that are the means of obtaining the fruit
- पथः (*pathaḥ*)—the paths
- मध्वा (*madhvā*)—with the intoxicating Soma
- समंजन् (*samaṃjan*)—moistening
- स्वदय (*svadaya*)—make sweet
- मन्मानि (*manmāni*)—our praises, of the nature of meditation
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—and the oblation of our sacrifice
- धीभि॥ (*dhībhi‖*)—by your intelligences
- यंधन् (*yaṃdhan*)—increasing
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- अध्वरं (*adhvaraṃ*)—the sacrifice
- देवत्रा (*devatrā*)—so that it approaches the gods
- कृणुहि (*kṛṇuhi*)—make

### Printed p. 338

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, named Tanūnapāt, who have an excellent tongue, moisten with the intoxicating Soma the paths that lead the sacrifice to its fruit, and make them sweet. Increasing our meditative praises and the oblation of our sacrifice by your intelligences, make our sacrifice reach the gods.

##### English translation
Pure-tongued Tanunapat, flavour the paths of the sacrifice which lead (to success), moistening them with the sweet (Soma-juice); elevating our praises and our rite by understanding. convey our sacrifice to the gods.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

तनूनपात् । तनूनपादाज्यमिति कात्थक्यः । नपादित्यनंतरायाः प्रजाया नामधेयं निर्णततमा भवति । गौरत्र तनूरुच्यते । तता अस्यां भोगाः तस्याः पयो जायते पयस आज्यं जायते ! अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः । अपोऽत्र तन्न उच्यंते । तता अंतरिक्षे ताभ्य ओषधिवनस्पतयो जायंत ओषधिवनस्पतिभ्य एष जायते ॥ तस्यैषापरा भवति । तनूनपात्पथ ऋतस्य यानान्मध्वा समंजन्त्सदया सुजिह्व । मन्मानि धीभिरुत यज्ञमृंधन्देवत्रा च कृणुह्यध्वरं नः ॥ तनूनपात् पथ ऋतस्य यानान् यज्ञस्य यानान् मधुना समंजन् स्वदय कल्याणचिह्वमननानि च नो धीभिर्यज्ञं च समर्धय देवान् नो यज्ञं गमय ॥ (*tanūnapāt | tanūnapādājyamiti kātthakyaḥ | napādityanaṃtarāyāḥ prajāyā nāmadheyaṃ nirṇatatamā bhavati | gauratra tanūrucyate | tatā asyāṃ bhogāḥ tasyāḥ payo jāyate payasa ājyaṃ jāyate ! agniriti śākapūṇiḥ | apo 'tra tanna ucyaṃte | tatā aṃtarikṣe tābhya oṣadhivanaspatayo jāyaṃta oṣadhivanaspatibhya eṣa jāyate ‖ tasyaiṣāparā bhavati | tanūnapātpatha ṛtasya yānānmadhvā samaṃjantsadayā sujihva | manmāni dhībhiruta yajñamṛṃdhandevatrā ca kṛṇuhyadhvaraṃ naḥ ‖ tanūnapāt patha ṛtasya yānān yajñasya yānān madhunā samaṃjan svadaya kalyāṇacihvamananāni ca no dhībhiryajñaṃ ca samardhaya devān no yajñaṃ gamaya ‖*) (Ni. 8-6)

Who is the deity Tanūnapāt praised in this Ṛk? Here too there is a difference of opinion.

तनूपात् । तनूनपादाज्यमिति कात्थक्यः (*tanūpāt | tanūnapādājyamiti kātthakyaḥ*)—according to Kātthakya (son of Katthaka), Tanūnapāt is ghee (ājya). How, will be explained in the next sentence.

नपादित्यनंतरायाः प्रजाया नामधेयं निर्णततमा भवति । गौरत्र तनूरुच्यते । तता अस्यां भोगाः तस्याः पयो जायते पयस आज्यं जायते (*napādityanaṃtarāyāḥ prajāyā nāmadheyaṃ nirṇatatamā bhavati | gauratra tanūrucyate | tatā asyāṃ bhogāḥ tasyāḥ payo jāyate payasa ājyaṃ jāyate*)—नपात् (*napāt*) means the offspring of the offspring, the progeny of the progeny: that is, for a man, the offspring of his son or daughter, i.e. a son's son or daughter's son, a grandson, or possibly a granddaughter. The meaning is a progeny coming after skipping one generation. Now the cow too has the name तनूः (*tanūḥ*). From that cow milk, a means of enjoyment, is produced, and from the milk ghee. So milk is the cow's offspring and ghee the offspring of the milk; ghee is thus the offspring of the cow's offspring. Hence Kātthakya's view that Tanūnapāt is ghee.

**Printed p. 339 content follows below.**
### Printed p. 339
अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः । आपोऽत्र तन्न उच्यंते । तता अंतरिक्षे ताभ्य ओषधिवनस्पतयो जायंत ओषधिवनस्पतिभ्य एष जायते । तस्यैषा भवति ॥ (*agniriti śākapūṇiḥ | āpo 'tra tanna ucyaṃte | tatā aṃtarikṣe tābhya oṣadhivanaspatayo jāyaṃta oṣadhivanaspatibhya eṣa jāyate | tasyaiṣā bhavati ‖*)—Tanūnapāt is Agni, according to the teacher Śākapūṇi. As said before, नपात् (*napāt*) means the offspring of the offspring. तन्नः (*tannaḥ*) are the waters. Those waters, spread in the atmosphere as clouds, bring rain on the earth, and so plants and trees arise. Thus the plants and trees are the offspring of the waters, and from the plants and trees (or from the tree-born fire-sticks) Agni is born; Agni is the offspring of the plants and trees. Hence Agni is the offspring of the waters' offspring, a grandson-like figure. This is what is meant here by Tanūnapāt: Agni, the grandson-like of the waters. The Ṛk in which the word Tanūnapāt occurs is explained here:

तनूनपात् पथ ऋतस्य यानान्मध्वा समंजन्त्सृदया सुजिह्व । मन्मानि धीभिरुत यज्ञमृंधन्देवत्रा च कृणुह्यध्वरं नः ॥ तनूनपात्पथ ऋतस्य यानान् यज्ञस्य यानान्मधुना समंजन् स्वदय कल्याणजिह्वमननानि च नो धीभिर्यज्ञं च समर्थय देवान् नो यज्ञं गमय ॥ (*tanūnapāt patha ṛtasya yānānmadhvā samaṃjantsṛdayā sujihva | manmāni dhībhiruta yajñamṛṃdhandevatrā ca kṛṇuhyadhvaraṃ naḥ ‖ tanūnapātpatha ṛtasya yānān yajñasya yānānmadhunā samaṃjan svadaya kalyāṇajihvamananāni ca no dhībhiryajñaṃ ca samarthaya devān no yajñaṃ gamaya ‖*) (Ni. 8-6)

तनूनपात् पथ ऋतस्य यानान् यज्ञस्य यानान् मधुना समंजन् स्वदय कल्याणजिह्व (*tanūnapāt patha ṛtasya yānān yajñasya yānān madhunā samaṃjan svadaya kalyāṇajihva*)—in this sentence ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*) means "of the sacrifice" and यानान् (*yānān*) means paths, or manner (order). सुजिह्व (*sujihva*) is कल्याणजिह्व (*kalyāṇajihva*), one with an excellent tongue. For Agni the flame is the tongue: as men eat food with their tongue, Agni consumes wood and the like with his flames, or cooks and consumes the oblations such as ghee offered in him. What the tongue is to men, the flame is to Agni; so Agni is addressed here as Sujihva, "of fair flame". The sentence therefore means: O Agni with a tongue of flame, you who are called Tanūnapāt, make the paths of the sacrifice, i.e. its procedures, shine well with your sweet speech-born mantra, or your sweet radiance, or the sweet Soma juice, and make them sweet so that the gods can accept them.

### Printed p. 340
The derivation of the word Tanūnapāt was explained before. पथ ऋतस्य यानान् (*patha ṛtasya yānān*)—the paths of the sacrifice, i.e. its ways, orders and methods: observing correctly the rules as to by which mantras, how and in what order the sacrifice is to proceed. मधुना समंजन् हृदय (*madhunā samaṃjan hṛdaya*)—here the word मधु (*madhu*) may be given many meanings: "smoothly, without any obstacles", or "so as to shine with the sweet radiance of Agni", and so on. समंजन् (*samaṃjan*) means with the anointing of ghee and the like, so that work goes smoothly: as the wheels and other parts of a chariot work easily when smeared with oil or ghee, so carry on the many operations of the sacrifice under a sweet leadership, and make that rite acceptable and pleasing to the gods. Thus Agni is prayed to.

मननानि च नो धीभिर्यज्ञं च समर्थय देवान् नो यज्ञं गमय (*mananāni ca no dhībhiryajñaṃ ca samarthaya devān no yajñaṃ gamaya*)—मन्मानि (*manmāni*) is मननानि (*mananāni*), मननीयानि (*mananīyāni*): mantras fit to be understood in their meaning and fixed in the mind. धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*) means by rites. O Agni, let the praises we recite in this sacrifice, and the sacrifice, proceed in order, by the rites to be done as occasion requires and also by understanding; and bring the gods to this sacrifice we perform. Such is the purport.

The deity Tanūnapāt praised in the second Ṛk of the Āprī-sūkta has thus been explained. In this sūkta Tanūnapāt himself is praised; but in some Āprī-sūktas, along with or instead of Tanūnapāt, the deity Narāśaṃsa is praised. Therefore, in explaining the deities of the Āprī-sūkta, Yāska, though it does not belong to the present context, has explained Narāśaṃsa:

नराशंसः । नराशंसो यज्ञ इति कात्थक्यः । नरा अस्मिन्नासीनाः शंसंति । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः । नरैः प्रशस्यो भवति । तस्यैषा भवति । नराशंसस्य महिमानमेषामुप स्तोषाम यजतस्य यज्ञैः । ये सुक्रतवः शुचयो धियंधाः स्वदंति देवा उभयानि हव्या ॥ (ऋ. सं. ७-२-२) ॥ नराशंसस्य महिमानमेषामुपस्तमो यज्जियस्य यज्ञैर्ये सुकर्माणः शुचयो धियं धारयितारः स्वदयंतु देवा उभयानि हवींषि सोमं चेतराणि चेति वा तांत्रिकाणि चावापिकानि चेति वा ॥ (*narāśaṃsaḥ | narāśaṃso yajña iti kātthakyaḥ | narā asminnāsīnāḥ śaṃsaṃti | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ | naraiḥ praśasyo bhavati | tasyaiṣā bhavati | narāśaṃsasya mahimānameṣāmupa stoṣāma yajatasya yajñaiḥ | ye sukratavaḥ śucayo dhiyaṃdhāḥ svadaṃti devā ubhayāni havyā ‖ (ṛ. saṃ. 7-2-2) ‖ narāśaṃsasya mahimānameṣāmupastamo yajjiyasya yajñairye sukarmāṇaḥ śucayo dhiyaṃ dhārayitāraḥ svadayaṃtu devā ubhayāni havīṃṣi somaṃ cetarāṇi ceti vā tāṃtrikāṇi cāvāpikāni ceti vā ‖*) (Ni. 8-7)

### Printed p. 341
नराशंसो यज्ञ इति कात्थक्यः । नरा अस्मिन्नासीनाः शंसंति (*narāśaṃso yajña iti kātthakyaḥ | narā asminnāsīnāḥ śaṃsaṃti*)—Narāśaṃsa is the sacrifice, according to Kātthakya. Men, i.e. the officiating priests and the patron, sit in this sacrifice (the sacrificial altar) and praise (the gods). Hence Narāśaṃsa is the sacrifice.

अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः । नरैः प्रशस्यो भवति । तस्यैषा भवति (*agniriti śākapūṇiḥ | naraiḥ praśasyo bhavati | tasyaiṣā bhavati*)—Narāśaṃsa is Agni, because Agni is praised by men. This is the view of the teacher Śākapūṇi. The Ṛk in which the word Narāśaṃsa occurs is cited below:

नराशंसस्य महिमानमेषामुप स्तोषाम यजतस्य यज्ञैः । ये सुक्रतवः शुचयो धियंधाः स्वदंति देवा उभयानि हव्या । (*narāśaṃsasya mahimānameṣāmupa stoṣāma yajatasya yajñaiḥ | ye sukratavaḥ śucayo dhiyaṃdhāḥ svadaṃti devā ubhayāni havyā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-2-2)

नराशंसस्य महिमानं एषां उपस्तुमः यजतस्य यज्ञैः (*narāśaṃsasya mahimānaṃ eṣāṃ upastumaḥ yajatasya yajñaiḥ*)—here एषां (*eṣāṃ*) means "for these people engaged in the sacrificial rite". We approach and praise the greatness of this Narāśaṃsa, i.e. of the sacrifice, which gives desired fruits to such people, is worshipped by rites such as sacrifices and is praised by men; or of this deity called Narāśaṃsa (Agni).

ये सुकर्माणः शुचयः धियं धारयितारः स्वदयंतु देवा उभयानि हवींषि सोमं चेतराणि चेति ना तांत्राणि चावापिकानि चेति वा (*ye sukarmāṇaḥ śucayaḥ dhiyaṃ dhārayitāraḥ svadayaṃtu devā ubhayāni havīṃṣi somaṃ cetarāṇi ceti nā tāṃtrāṇi cāvāpikāni ceti vā*)**NOTE**—here सुक्रतवः (*sukratavaḥ*), शुचयः (*śucayaḥ*), धियंधाः (*dhiyaṃdhāḥ*) are epithets of देवाः (*devāḥ*). Since क्रतु (*kratu*) means rite, सुक्रतवः (*sukratavaḥ*) or सुकर्माणः (*sukarmāṇaḥ*) means those who perform good rites of world-protection and favour. शुचयः (*śucayaḥ*) are those free from sin, or radiant. धियंधाः (*dhiyaṃdhāḥ*): धियं (*dhiyaṃ*) is sacrificial rite or intelligence, धाः (*dhāḥ*) those who hold it; that is, those who encourage sacrificial rites and see them completed fully, or those who are wise. उभयानि हव्या (*ubhayāni havyā*) are two kinds of oblations: सोमं चेतराणि च (*somaṃ cetarāṇi ca*), Soma juice and oblations such as cooked cake (caru, puroḍāśa); or तांत्राणि चावापिकानि चेति वा (*tāṃtrāṇi cāvāpikāni ceti vā*), the oblations offered in the Prayāja, Ājyabhāga, Sviṣṭakṛt and similar offerings, and those offered in the principal homas. Let the gods enjoy both kinds of oblations.

The main purport: let those gods who are engaged in good works such as world-protection, sinless, pure or radiant, wise, or helpers of sacrificial rites or givers of their fruit, enjoy

### Printed p. 342
the two kinds of oblations, Soma juice and caru-puroḍāśa, that we offer to them in this sacrifice, or the two kinds of oblations offered in the Prayāja, Ājyabhāga, Sviṣṭakṛt and other homas and in the principal homas.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒जुह्वा॑न॒ ईड्यो॒ वंद्य॒श्च या॑ह्यग्ने॒ वसु॑भिः स॒जोषाः॑ ।  
> त्वं दे॒वाना॑मसि यह्व॒ होता॒ स ए॑नान्यक्षीषि॒तो यजी॑यान् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आजुह्वानः । ईड्यः । वंद्यः । च । आ । याहि । अग्ने । वसुभिः । सजोषाः ।  
> त्वं । देवानां । असि । यह्व । होता । सः । एनान् । यक्षि । इषितः । यजीयान्॥३॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वमस्मत्कर्मण्या याहि । आगच्छ । कीदृशः ! आजुह्वानो देवानांमाह्वाता ॥ हु दानादनयोः चौहोत्यादिकः । अभ्यस्तस्वरः ॥ ईड्यः ॥ ईडिरध्येषणाकर्मा । अध्येष्यः प्रार्थ्यमानः वंद्यः स्तोतव्यः वसुभिर्देवैः सजोषाः सह
> प्रीयमाणः । आगत्य च हे यह्व! महन्नामैतत् । हे महन् स त्वं देव देवानां
> होताह्वातासि । ततो यजीयान् ॥ यष्टृशब्दादीयसुनि तुरिष्ठेमेयःस्थिति
> तृचो लोपः ॥ यष्टृतरः स त्वमिषितोऽस्माभिरध्येषितः प्रार्थितः सन्नेतान्देवान्यक्षि । यज । हविषा पूजय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, come to our rite. How is he? आजुह्वानः (*ājuhvānaḥ*), the caller of the gods; ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*) (the root ईडि (*īḍi*) has the sense of entreaty), one to be entreated, prayed to; वंद्यः (*vaṃdyaḥ*), to be praised; सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*), taking pleasure together with the Vasus, the gods. Having come, O Yahva (a name meaning "great"), O great one, you are the Hotā, the caller of the gods. Hence you are यजीयान् (*yajīyān*), the best sacrificer. Being thus entreated and prayed to by us, you worship these gods (यक्षि (*yakṣi*), यज (*yaja*)): honour them with the oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- आजुह्वानः (*ājuhvānaḥ*)—you who call the gods to the sacrifice
- ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*)—praiseworthy
- वंद्यः (*vaṃdyaḥ*)—worshipful
- वसुभिः (*vasubhiḥ*)—with the gods called Vasus
- सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)—together
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—be gracious and come
- यह्व (*yahva*)—O great-souled Agni
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—of the gods
- होता (*hotā*)—as the caller
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- यजीयान् (*yajīyān*)—most worshipful
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- इषितः (*iṣitaḥ*)—entreated by us
- एतान् यक्षि (*etān yakṣi*)—worship these gods

### Printed p. 343

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who call the gods to the sacrifice, who are worthy of praise and worship: come together with the gods called Vasus. O mighty Agni, you are the invoker of the gods. You, who are most worthy of worship, being solicited by us, worship the gods.

##### English translation
Agni, you are the invoker (of the gods), and are to be solicited and praised; come, being propitated, along with the Vasus ; you, O mighty (Agni), are the invoker of the gods, you, are most entitled to worship solicited by us, offer them adoration.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the deity Iḷa is praised through the use of the word ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*). The Nirukta on this Ṛk is as follows:
ईळः । ईळ ईट्टेः स्तुतिकर्मणः इंथतेर्वा । तस्यैषा भवति ॥ (*īḷaḥ | īḷa īṭṭeḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ iṃthatervā | tasyaiṣā bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 8-8)
The word ईळः (*īḷaḥ*) is derived either from the root ईद् (*īd*), meaning "to praise", or from the root *iṃdha*, meaning "to kindle, to make blaze". ईळः (*īḷaḥ*) is Agni or a particular form of Agni. The Ṛk containing this word is explained here by way of illustration:
अजुह्वान ईड्यो वंद्यश्चायाह्यग्ने वसुभिः सजोषाः । त्वं देवानामसि यह्व होता स एनान्यक्षीषितो यजीयान् । (*ajuhvāna īḍyo vaṃdyaścāyāhyagne vasubhiḥ sajoṣāḥ | tvaṃ devānāmasi yahva hotā sa enānyakṣīṣito yajīyān |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-3)
आहूयमान ईळितव्यो वंदितव्यश्चायाह्यग्ने वसुभिः सहजोषणस्त्वं देवानामसि यह्व होता । यह्व इति महतो नामधेयं यातश्च हूतश्च भवति । स एवान् यक्षेषितो यजीयान् । इषितः प्रेषित इति वाधीष्ट इति वा यजीयान्यष्टृतरः ॥ (*āhūyamāna īḷitavyo vaṃditavyaścāyāhyagne vasubhiḥ sahajoṣaṇastvaṃ devānāmasi yahva hotā | yahva iti mahato nāmadheyaṃ yātaśca hūtaśca bhavati | sa evān yakṣeṣito yajīyān | iṣitaḥ preṣita iti vādhīṣṭa iti vā yajīyānyaṣṭṛtaraḥ ‖*) (Ni. 8-8)
आजुह्वानः (*ājuhvānaḥ*) and ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*): these two words are epithets describing Agni. आहूयमानः (*āhūyamānaḥ*) means one who is called, with prayer, by the priests and the sacrificer at sacrifices and the like. ईळितव्यः (*īḷitavyaḥ*) or वंदितव्यः (*vaṃditavyaḥ*) means one who is honoured with oblations and the like and then praised, or saluted, by all people in the world, or by the priests and the sacrificer.

आ याह्यग्ने वसुभिः सहजोषणः (*ā yāhyagne vasubhiḥ sahajoṣaṇaḥ*): सहजोषणः (*sahajoṣaṇaḥ*) means one of equal affection. That is, whatever affection the other gods have for the priests and the sacrificer engaged in the sacrificial act, Agni has the same affection. The sense is: "O Agni, of equal affection, come to our sacrifice together with the gods called Vasus." The word वसुभिः (*vasubhiḥ*) may mean the eight Vasus, or other gods who give dwelling-places, or wealth and the like.

त्वं देवानां असि यह्व होता (*tvaṃ devānāṃ asi yahva hotā*): यह्व (*yahva*) means great or excessive. होता (*hotā*) is देवानामाह्वाता (*devānāmāhvātā*), one who brings the gods to the sacrificial ground. O Agni, you are great, that is, of great nature, and you are also the one who brings the gods to the sacrificial ground.

यह्व इति महतो नामधेयं यातश्च हूतश्च भवति (*yahva iti mahato nāmadheyaṃ yātaśca hūtaśca bhavati*): यह्व (*yahva*) means great, excessive. In the case of Agni, "great" means *yātaḥ*, one who goes, and *hūtaḥ*, one who is called with prayer. Since Agni, entreated by men, goes to the gods and brings them to the sacrificial ground, he is described here as endowed with greatness. The other gods have no greatness of this kind.

स एनान् यक्षीषितो यजीयान् । इषितः प्रेषित इति वाधीष्ट इति वा यजीयान्यष्टृतम (*sa enān yakṣīṣito yajīyān | iṣitaḥ preṣita iti vādhīṣṭa iti vā yajīyānyaṣṭṛtama*): यजीयान् (*yajīyān*) means यष्टृतमः (*yaṣṭṛtamaḥ*), the best among those who sacrifice and worship the gods. इषितः (*iṣitaḥ*) means impelled; प्रेषितः (*preṣitaḥ*), sent; अधीष्टः (*adhīṣṭaḥ*), entreated. The sense of the sentence is: "O Agni, you, the best among those who invoke and worship the gods, impelled by us, or sent to the gods, or entreated by us, worship the gods and propitiate them."

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रा॒चीनं॑ ब॒र्हिः प्र॒दिशा॑ पथि॒व्या वस्तो॑र॒स्या वृ॑ज्यते॒ अग्रे॒  ॑
> अह्नां ।  
> व्यु॑ प्रथते वित॒रं वरी॑यो दे॒वेभ्यो॒ अदि॑तये स्को॒नं ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 345

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्राचीनं । बर्हिः । प्रदिशा । पृथिव्याः । वस्तोः । अस्याः । वृज्यते । अग्रे । अह्नां ।  
> वि । ऊं इति । प्रथते । वितरं । वरीयः । देवेभ्यः । अदितये । स्कोनं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यदिदं प्राचीनं प्रागंचितं प्राज्मुखं बर्हिरस्ति तदिदं पृथिव्या वेदिलक्षणाया वस्तोः ॥ वस आच्छादने । तुन्द्रत्ययः । चतुर्थ्यर्थे बहुलं छंदसीति षष्ठि ।
> यद्वा। भावलक्षणे तोसुन् द्रष्टव्यः ॥ वसनायाच्छादनार्थमह्नामग्रे पूर्वाह्ने
> प्रदिशा प्रकर्षेण दिश्यमानेन मंत्रेणास्याः प्राच्या दिशो वृज्यते । स्तूयते ।
> आह्रियते । कथा च निगमः । त आ वहंति कवयः पुरस्तादित्यादि । शट्टाहृतं वरीय
> उरुतरं बर्हिनिवितरं विस्तीर्णतरं यथा भवति तथा विप्रथते । विविधमेव वेद्यां
> प्रस्तृतं भवति । तथा देवेभ्योदितये वेदिलक्षणाय्कॆ पृथिव्यै च स्योनं सुखकरं
> भवति । विस्तीर्णे बर्हिषि देवाः सुखं निषीदंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This प्राचीनं (*prācīnaṃ*) barhis (sacrificial grass), laid with its tips to the east, is spread for the earth in the form of the altar, वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*), for covering. The word वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*) comes from the root वस (*vasa*) in the sense of covering; the genitive stands for the dative by the rule that in the Veda the genitive is used variously for the dative. Or else the form is to be understood as a तोसुन् (*tosun*) affix in the sense of the action's occasion. At the beginning of the days, in the forenoon, the barhis is वृज्यते (*vṛjyate*), praised, brought, for this eastern quarter by the mantra that points the way (प्रदिशा (*pradiśā*)). The Veda's own text bears this out: *ta ā vahaṃti kavayaḥ purastāt* and so on. The barhis spreads out वरीयः (*varīyaḥ*), more widely, वितरं (*vitaraṃ*), more expansively; it is spread in many ways over the altar. It is स्योनं (*syonaṃ*), comfortable, for the gods, for Aditi, and for the earth in the form of the altar; on the wide barhis the gods sit at ease.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्राचीनं (*prācīnaṃ*)—facing east
- बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—the seat of darbha grass
- अस्याः पृथिव्याः (*asyāḥ pṛthivyāḥ*)—of this earth in the form of the altar
- वस्तोः (*vastoḥ*)—for covering (to cover the earth)
- अह्नां अग्रे (*ahnāṃ agre*)—at the very time of morning
- प्रदिशा (*pradiśā*)—with the mantra that shows the way
- व्यज्यते (*vyajyate*)—is spread **NOTE**
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—for the gods
- अदितये (*aditaye*)—for Aditi
- स्कोनं (*skonaṃ*)—so as to be comfortable
- वरीयः (*varīyaḥ*)—the broad barhis
- वितरं (*vitaraṃ*)—more widely
- वि प्रथते (*vi prathate*)—is spread out

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The east-facing seat of darbha grass is spread at the very time of morning, with a mantra that shows the way, to cover the earth in the form of the altar. The broad barhis is spread out widely so as to be comfortable for the gods and for Aditi.

##### English translation
In the beginning of the day the sacred grass, pointing eastwards, is strewn with the prescribed (text) as a covering for the earth (of the altar); they spread it out far and wide as a pleasant (seat) for the gods and Aditi.

### Printed p. 346

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

बर्हिः । बर्हिः परिबर्हणात् । तस्यैषा भवति । प्राचीनं बर्हिः प्रदिशा पृथिव्या वस्तोरस्या वृज्यते अग्रे अह्नां । व्यु प्रथते वितरं वरीयो देवेभ्यो अदितये स्कोनं ॥ प्राचीनं बर्हिः प्रदिशा पृथिव्या वसनायास्या प्रवृज्यते अग्रे अह्नां बर्हिः पूर्वाह्ने तद्विप्रथते वितरं विकीर्णतरमिति ना विस्तीर्णतरमिति वा वरीयो वरतरमुरुतरं वा देवोभ्यश्चादितये च स्कोनं । स्कोनमिति सुखनाम स्यतेरवस्यंतेतत् सेवितव्यं भवतीति वा ॥ (*barhiḥ | barhiḥ paribarhaṇāt | tasyaiṣā bhavati | prācīnaṃ barhiḥ pradiśā pṛthivyā vastorasyā vṛjyate agre ahnāṃ | vyu prathate vitaraṃ varīyo devebhyo aditaye skonaṃ ‖ prācīnaṃ barhiḥ pradiśā pṛthivyā vasanāyāsyā pravṛjyate agre ahnāṃ barhiḥ pūrvāhne tadviprathate vitaraṃ vikīrṇataramiti nā vistīrṇataramiti vā varīyo varataramurutaraṃ vā devobhyaścāditaye ca skonaṃ | skonamiti sukhanāma syateravasyaṃtetat sevitavyaṃ bhavatīti vā ‖*) (Ni. 8-9)

बर्हिः परिबर्हणात् । तस्यैषा भवति (*barhiḥ paribarhaṇāt | tasyaiṣā bhavati*): बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*) means darbha grass cut to one even length and spread out as a seat. A seat is prepared on which the gods, entreated and invited to the sacrifice, may come and sit. The seat prepared by spreading darbha grass cut to an even length in three layers, one layer laid upon another so as to be soft to sit on, is called बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*). This seat called बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*) is also used for placing the oblations and the like; oblations are not put on the ground but on the seat spread with darbha. The darbha used for this seat is cut to one measure. The word बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*) has the meaning परिबर्हणात् (*paribarhaṇāt*), परिच्छेदनात् (*paricchedanāt*), "from being cut". This darbha grows very quickly, and the name बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*) has come from that also. A Ṛk containing this word, namely the very Ṛk in hand, is given here as an illustration.

प्राचीनं बर्हिः प्रदिशा पृथिव्या वसनायास्याः प्रवृज्यते (*prācīnaṃ barhiḥ pradiśā pṛthivyā vasanāyāsyāḥ pravṛjyate*): प्राचीनं (*prācīnaṃ*) means toward the east, or with the tips of the darbha toward the east; बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*), darbha grass cut to an even measure; प्रदिशा (*pradiśā*), in the prescribed manner, facing east or north, accompanied by the spreading mantra; पृथिव्या वसनायास्याः प्रवृज्यते (*pṛthivyā vasanāyāsyāḥ pravṛjyate*), it is spread over the earth to cover it. The meaning of the sentence: on the sacrificial altar, so that the gods may come and sit, darbha grass cut to one measure is spread over the ground like a covering, with the tips to the east and with the spreading mantra.

अग्रे अह्नां बर्हिः पूर्वाह्ने तद्विप्रथते (*agre ahnāṃ barhiḥ pūrvāhne tadviprathate*): अग्रे अह्नां (*agre ahnāṃ*) means at the beginning of the day, that is, in the forenoon; the spreading of the darbha takes place in the forenoon (in the morning), widely.

### Printed p. 347
वितरं विकीर्णतरमिति ना विस्तीर्णतरमिति वा वरियो वरतरमुरुतरं वा देवेभ्यश्चादितये स्कोनं (*vitaraṃ vikīrṇataramiti nā vistīrṇataramiti vā variyo varataramurutaraṃ vā devebhyaścāditaye skonaṃ*): वितरं (*vitaraṃ*) means विकीर्णतरं (*vikīrṇataraṃ*), spread out more; or विस्तीर्णतरं (*vistīrṇataraṃ*), spread widely. वरीयः (*varīyaḥ*) means वरतरं (*varataraṃ*) or श्रेष्ठतरं (*śreṣṭhataraṃ*), better than the other parts of the sacrifice; उरुतरं (*urutaraṃ*), more abundant. The meaning is: this abundant and excellent spreading of darbha is made ready, spread widely, so that the gods and Aditi may come and sit in comfort.

स्योनमिति सुखनाम स्यतेरवस्यंत्येतत् सेवितव्यं भवतीति वा (*syonamiti sukhanāma syateravasyaṃtyetat sevitavyaṃ bhavatīti vā*): स्योन (*syona*) is a name for comfort. The word स्योन (*syona*) is derived either from the root स्यति (*syati*), meaning "to find rest", or from the fact that people find rest in it, or from the fact that people resort to it for rest.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> व्यच॑स्वतीरुर्वि॒या वि श्र॑यंतां॒ पति॑भ्यो॒ न जन॑यः॒ शुंभ॑मानाः ।  
> देवी॑र्द्वारो बृहतीर्विश्वमिन्वा दे॒वेभ्यो॑ भवत सुप्राय॒णाः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> व्यचस्वतीः । उर्विया ! वि । श्रयंतां । पतिभ्यः । न । जनयः । शुंभमाः ।  
> देवीः । द्वारः । बृहतीः । विश्वंइन्वाः । देवेभ्यः । भवत । सुप्रअयनाः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> व्यचस्वतीः । व्यचो व्यापनं । तद्वत्यः ॥ ना छंदसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः ॥
> ता द्वारदेवता उर्विया ॥ उरुशब्दात्कृतीयैकवचन इयाडियाजीकाराणामुपसंख्यानं । पा. ७-१-३९-१ । इतीयादेशः ॥ उरुत्वेव वि श्रयंतां । विशेषेणाश्रिता
> भवंतु । तत्र दृष्टांतः । पतिभ्यो न यथा पतीनामर्थाय संभोगकाले शुंभमानाः शोभमाना जनयो जाया विश्रयंति तद्वदस्मिन्कर्मणि विश्रयंतां । हे
> बृहतीर्महत्यो हे विश्वमिन्वाः ॥ इवि प्रीणनार्थः । तस्मात्कर्मण्युपपदेऽण् ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

व्यचस्वतीः (*vyacasvatīḥ*): *vyacaḥ* is pervading, and those that possess it are व्यचस्वतीः (*vyacasvatīḥ*). These are the door-goddesses. They are उर्विया (*urviyā*), by breadth: the instrumental singular of उरु (*uru*) takes the substitute इय (*iya*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39-1, as quoted). With that breadth let them वि श्रयंतां (*vi śrayaṃtāṃ*), be resorted to in a special way, that is, stand open. The illustration: पतिभ्यो न (*patibhyo na*), as wives (जनयः (*janayaḥ*)), adorned and shining at the time of union, open themselves for their husbands' sake, so let the doors open in this rite. बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*), great ones; विश्वमिन्वाः (*viśvaminvāḥ*): the root इवि (*ivi*) has the sense of pleasing, and the affix *aṇ* is added to it when it stands in composition with an object.

### Printed p. 348

> इदित्वान्नुम् । तत्पुरुषे कृति बहुलमित्यत्र बहुलवचनाद्वितीयाया अप्यलुक् ॥
> सर्वस्य प्रीणयित्र्यो हे द्वारो देवीर्द्वाराभिमानिन्नो हे देव्यः यूयं
> देवेभ्यो देवनामर्थाय सुप्रायणाः सुप्रगमनाः सुविवृता भवत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O door-goddesses, you who please all, divine Doors, presiding over the doors: be सुप्रायणाः (*suprāyaṇāḥ*), easy to enter, well opened, for the sake of the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पतिभ्यः (*patibhyaḥ*)—for the joy of their husbands
- शुंभमानाः (*śuṃbhamānāḥ*)—who have adorned themselves
- जनयः न (*janayaḥ na*)—as wives make room
- व्यचस्वतीः (*vyacasvatīḥ*)—the door-goddesses who have ample room
- उर्विया (*urviyā*)—broadly, for the entry of the gods
- वि श्रयंतां (*vi śrayaṃtāṃ*)—let them open the closed door
- बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*)—of great nature
- विश्वमिन्वाः (*viśvaminvāḥ*)—pleasing to all
- द्वारः देवीः (*dvāraḥ devīḥ*)—O door-goddesses
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—for the gods
- सुप्रायणाः (*suprāyaṇāḥ*)—as givers of easy entry
- भवत (*bhavata*)—be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As wives who have adorned themselves for the joy of their husbands make room for their pleasure, so let the broad and great door-goddesses open their closed doors widely for the entry of the gods. O door-goddesses, you who are of great nature and pleasing to all, be givers of easy entry for the gods.

##### English translation
Expanding wide, let the Doors give access as gracefully decorated wives give access to their husbands, divine Doors, spacious and admitting all, be easy of entry for the gods.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The derivation of the word द्वारः (*dvāraḥ*) is explained as follows:
द्वारः । जवतेर्वा द्रवतेर्वा वारयतेर्वा । तासामेषा भवति ॥ व्यचस्वतीरुर्विया विश्रयंतां पतिभ्यो न जनयः शुंभमानाः । देवीर्द्वारो बृहतीविश्वमिन्वा देवेभ्यो भवत सुप्रायणाः ॥ व्यंचनवत्य उरुत्वेन विश्रयंतां पतिभ्य इव जाया ऊरू मैथुने धर्मे शुशोभिषमाणाः वरतममंगमूरू देव्योद्वारो बृहत्यो महत्यो विश्वमिन्वा विश्वमाभिरेति यज्ञे । गृहद्वार इति कात्थक्यः ॥ अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥ (*dvāraḥ | javatervā dravatervā vārayatervā | tāsāmeṣā bhavati ‖ vyacasvatīrurviyā viśrayaṃtāṃ patibhyo na janayaḥ śuṃbhamānāḥ | devīrdvāro bṛhatīviśvaminvā devebhyo bhavata suprāyaṇāḥ ‖ vyaṃcanavatya urutvena viśrayaṃtāṃ patibhya iva jāyā ūrū maithune dharme śuśobhiṣamāṇāḥ varatamamaṃgamūrū devyodvāro bṛhatyo mahatyo viśvaminvā viśvamābhireti yajñe | gṛhadvāra iti kātthakyaḥ ‖ agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*) (Ni. 8-10)

### Printed p. 349
द्वारः जवतेर्वा द्रवतेर्वा वारयतेर्वा । तासामेषा भवति (*dvāraḥ javatervā dravatervā vārayatervā | tāsāmeṣā bhavati*): द्वारः (*dvāraḥ*) means the doors of the sacrificial house. These ordinarily stand only as words ending in the feminine plural. The word द्वारः (*dvāraḥ*) is derived either from the root जु (*ju*), meaning "to go forward or inwards", or from the root द्रु (*dru*), meaning "to run"; or it may be derived from the root वृ (*vṛ*), meaning "to stop, so that one does not go in". Yāska has taken the Ṛk in hand, which contains this word, as an example and has given the Nirukta on it.

व्यचस्वतीरुर्विया विश्रयंतां (*vyacasvatīrurviyā viśrayaṃtāṃ*)—व्यंचनवत्य उरुत्तेन विश्रयंतां (*vyaṃcanavatya uruttena viśrayaṃtāṃ*): let the broad doors of the sacrificial house stand well, or wholly, open. Here an illustration is given about the doors' being open.

पतिभ्यो न जनयः शुंभमानः (*patibhyo na janayaḥ śuṃbhamānaḥ*)—पतिभ्य इव जाया ऊरू मैथुने धर्मे शुशोभिषमाणाः वरतममंगमूरू (*patibhya iva jāyā ūrū maithune dharme śuśobhiṣamāṇāḥ varatamamaṃgamūrū*): as wives at the time of union open and spread their thighs to give joy to their husbands, so let the doors of the sacrificial house be wholly open for the coming of the gods, the priests and the sacrificer, and other people. That is the sense. A woman's thighs are the most attractive of all the other parts of the body.

देवीर्द्वारो बृहतीर्विश्वमिन्वा देवेभ्यो भवत सुप्रायणाः (*devīrdvāro bṛhatīrviśvaminvā devebhyo bhavata suprāyaṇāḥ*)—देव्यो द्वारो बृहत्यो महत्यो विश्वमिन्वा विश्वमाभिरेति यज्ञे । गृहद्वार इति कात्थक्यः ॥ अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥ (*devyo dvāro bṛhatyo mahatyo viśvaminvā viśvamābhireti yajñe | gṛhadvāra iti kātthakyaḥ ‖ agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*) बृहत्यः (*bṛhatyaḥ*) means doors that are great; विश्वमिन्वा (*viśvaminvā*) means विश्वमाभिरेति (*viśvamābhireti*): विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*), all, अभिः (*abhiḥ*), by these doors, एति (*eti*), comes in. That is, great doors fit for all to enter the sacrificial house.

देवेभ्यो भवत सुप्रायणाः (*devebhyo bhavata suprāyaṇāḥ*): सुप्रायणाः (*suprāyaṇāḥ*) means सुप्रगमनाः (*supragamanāḥ*); the sense is "let them be fit for easy entry".

Main purport: just as wives, fully adorned at the time of union, make their attractive thighs broad and wide and stretch them for the enjoyment of their husbands, so let the broad and great doors of the sacrificial house be well open for the easy coming of the gods, the priests and the sacrificer, other people, and the rest. Kātthakya approves the meaning that द्वारः (*dvāraḥ*) here is गृहद्वार (*gṛhadvāra*), the doors of a house. Śākapūṇi's view is that द्वारः (*dvāraḥ*) means Agni, or a particular form of Agni.

### Printed p. 350
On the consecration of the four doors of the sacrificial house, the Taittirīya Saṃhitā gives this account:
प्राचीनवग्ंशं करोति देवमनुष्या दिशो व्यभजंत प्राचीं देवा दक्षिणा पितरः प्रतीचीं मनुष्या उदीचीग्‌० रुद्राः ॥ (*prācīnavagṃśaṃ karoti devamanuṣyā diśo vyabhajaṃta prācīṃ devā dakṣiṇā pitaraḥ pratīcīṃ manuṣyā udīcīg0 rudrāḥ ‖*) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 6-1-1-1)
That is, the eastern door of the sacrificial house was shared by the gods, the southern door by the Pitṛs (the fathers), the western door by men, and the northern door by the (eleven) Rudras.
The names of the doors of this house are as stated at 1-188-5: Virāṭ is the eastern door, Samrāṭ the southern door, Vibhvīḥ the western door, and Prabhvīḥ the northern door. Sāyaṇa has explained the etymological meanings of these words.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ सु॒स्वयं॑ती यज॒ते उपा॑के उ॒षासा॒नक्ता॑ सदतां॒ नि  ॑
> योन् ।  
> दि॒व्ये योष॑णे बृह॒ती सु॑रु॒क्मे अधि॒ श्रियं॑ शुक्र॒पिशं॒ दधा॑ने ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । सुस्वयंती इति । यजते इति । उपाके इति। उषसानक्ता । सदतां । नि । योन् ।  
> दिव्ये इति । योषणे इति । बृहती इति । सुरुक्मे इति सुरुक्मे । अधि । श्रियं । शुक्रपिशं । दधाने इति ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुस्वयंती ॥ अय पय गत् । शतर्युपसर्गस्य सोर्द्विवचनं छांदसं ॥
> सुष्वयंतौ गच्छंतौ । यद्वा ॥ स्वपेण्यंतस्य वर्णलोपः ॥ सुष्वापयंतौ ।
> यजते यष्टव्ये उपाके उपक्रांते उषासानक्कोषश्च नक्तं च ॥ द्वंद्व उषासोषसः । पा. ६-३-३१ । इत्युषासादेशः । देवताद्वंद्वे चेति पूर्वोत्तरपदयो-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सुस्वयंती (*susvayaṃtī*): from the root अय (*aya*) पय (*paya*), "to go". The dual form is Vedic. It means "the two who go". Or, from the causative of *svap* with loss of a letter, "the two who put (people) to sleep". यजते (*yajate*): the two who are to be worshipped. उपाके (*upāke*): the two who have approached. उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*): Uṣas and Night, a dvandva compound; the substitution of उषासा (*uṣāsā*) is by द्वंद्व उषासोषसः । पा. ६-३-३१ (*dvaṃdva uṣāsoṣasaḥ | pā. 6-3-31*).

### Printed p. 351
*Gist (continued):* The two goddesses of Day and Night are to sit down firmly in this place of sacrifice, the womb (योन् (*yon*)). They are of what kind? दिव्ये (*divye*): born in heaven. योषणे (*yoṣaṇe*): gladdening like women; or, योषणे (*yoṣaṇe*) means joined, not separate from each other. बृहती (*bṛhatī*): great in their qualities. सुरुक्मे (*surukme*): beautifully shining; रुक्मं (*rukmaṃ*) is "form". शुक्रपिशं (*śukrapiśaṃ*): they bear beauty of a shining form in abundance.

> र्युगपत्र्कृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ अहोरात्रदेव्यौ योनावस्मिन्यज्ञस्थाने नि नितरां नियमेन
> ना सदतां ! आसीदतां ॥ सदेर्लुजि लृदित्वाच्चेरज् ॥ कीदृश्ये । दिव्ये दिवि भवे
> योषणे योषिताविन प्रीणयित्र्यौ! यद्वा! योषणे समिते परस्परतोऽविविक्ते ।
> बृहतीर्गुणैर्महत्यौ सुरुक्क्षे शोभनदीप्ये ॥ रुक्मं । रोचतेर्मकृत्यये कुत्वे
> च कृते रूपं ॥ शुक्रपिशं शोचमानरूपां श्रियमधि दधाने अधिकं धारयंत्र्यौ ॥

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिव्ये (*divye*)—those born in the heavenly world
- योषणे (*yoṣaṇe*)—those who are united
- बृहती (*bṛhatī*)—those of great form
- सुरुक्मे (*surukme*)—those of abundant radiance
- शुक्रपिशं (*śukrapiśaṃ*)—radiant
- श्रियं (*śriyaṃ*)—beauty
- अधि दधाने (*adhi dadhāne*)—those who possess
- सुस्वयंती (*susvayaṃtī*)—those who give comfort
- यजते (*yajate*)—those worthy of worship
- उपाके (*upāke*)—those who have graciously come together for the sacrifice
- उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*)—the deities of day and night
- योन् (*yon*)—in the place of sacrifice
- नि सदतां (*ni sadatāṃ*)—let them sit

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the deities named Uṣāsānaktā, born in the heavenly world, united together, of great form, of abundant radiance, possessing radiant beauty, givers of comfort, worthy of worship, who have graciously come together for the sacrifice, sit in the place of sacrifice.

##### English translation
May the adorable Day and Night, the givers of sound repose, having approached, sit down in the place (of sacrifice), two divine females, majestic and richly ornamented, bearing beauty of a bright form.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk two deities, Uṣāsānaktā, are described.
उषासानक्ता । उषासानक्कोषाश्च नक्ता चोषा व्याख्याता । नक्तेति रात्रिनामानक्ति भूतान्यवश्यायेनापि ना नक्याव्यक्तवर्णा । तयोरेषा भवति ॥ (*uṣāsānaktā | uṣāsānakkoṣāśca naktā coṣā vyākhyātā | nakteti rātrināmānakti bhūtānyavaśyāyenāpi nā nakyāvyaktavarṇā | tayoreṣā bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 8-11)
The word उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) denotes the very deities that the word नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*) also denotes. In this word are the names of two deities, Naktā and Uṣas. Naktā means night: because it comes without fail every day, and अनक्ति भूतानि (*anakti bhūtāni*) — क्लेदयति भूतानि (*kledayati bhūtāni*) — it troubles all living beings; hence night is called Naktā.

### Printed p. 352
Or, अपि वा नक्ता अव्यक्तवर्णा (*api vā naktā avyaktavarṇā*) (na aktā, anaktā): since in the night there is darkness and no light as by day, no objects can be seen clearly. Therefore night, of indistinct colour, is called Naktā. Uṣas: उषाः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः (*uṣāḥ kasmāducchatīti satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ*) (Ni. 2-18). Because it drives away darkness it is called Uṣas; that is, the last part of the night is called the time of Uṣas. Then all the darkness of the night departs and light gradually becomes visible. After the darkness of the night has gone, the time filled with light before sunrise is called the time of Uṣas. The presiding deity of this time is indicated by the name Uṣas. Naktā and Uṣas are both female deities.
Whether one reads नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*) or उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*), the meaning is the same. The explanation of the word Uṣas has been given earlier. Naktā is a name of night. For, naktā means of indistinct colour; because of the darkness things are not seen well. So night, with its darkness, is called Naktā. And in the night living beings are unable to carry out their activities. अनक्ति क्लेद—यति .भूतानि अवश्यायेन । अपि वानक्ता अव्यक्तवर्णा । यथा अहः सर्वमभिव्यक्तरूपं भवति न तथा रात्रिः ॥ (*anakti kleda—yati .bhūtāni avaśyāyena | api vānaktā avyaktavarṇā | yathā ahaḥ sarvamabhivyaktarūpaṃ bhavati na tathā rātriḥ ‖*) Because the darkness troubles living beings, leaving no room for their activities to go on properly, night with such darkness is called Naktā. Or, because nothing is seen well and all is indistinct, it is called Naktā. By day the forms of all things are seen clearly; in the night they are not. Therefore the time of night is called Naktā; this is the explanation given. (Ni. 8-11)
It was said that the explanation of the word Uṣas was given earlier. That explanation is as follows:
The sixteen words beginning with विभावरी (*vibhāvarī*), सॊनरी (*sònarī*) are names of Uṣas (2-19). And,
उषाः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः ॥ (*uṣāḥ kasmāducchatīti satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ ‖*)
Because it removes the darkness of the night-time it is called Uṣas; that is, it is the later part, the last portion, of the night. To support this meaning an example is given:
इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां जोतिरागाच्चित्रः प्रकेतो अजिनिष्ट विभ्वा । यथा प्रसूता सवितुः सवाय एवा रात्रुषसे योनिमारैक् । (*idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jotirāgāccitraḥ praketo ajiniṣṭa vibhvā | yathā prasūtā savituḥ savāya evā rātruṣase yonimāraik |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1.3-1)

### Printed p. 353
The Nirukta on this Ṛk:
इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां जोतिरागमत् । चित्रं प्रकेतनं प्रज्ञाततममजनिष्ट विभूततमं यथा प्रसूता सवितुः प्रसवाय रात्रिरादित्यस्य । एवं रात्रुषसे योनिमरिचत् स्थानं । स्त्रीयोनिरभियुत एनां गर्भः । (*idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jotirāgamat | citraṃ praketanaṃ prajñātatamamajaniṣṭa vibhūtatamaṃ yathā prasūtā savituḥ prasavāya rātrirādityasya | evaṃ rātruṣase yonimaricat sthānaṃ | strīyonirabhiyuta enāṃ garbhaḥ |*) (Ni. 2-19)
The best and most brilliant light of the sun is rising. The time of Uṣas, which precedes the sun's radiance, appears before the light, like its banner. How? The sun's light shines all day and at sunset becomes the womb, that is the cause, of night; in the same way, at its own end the night becomes the womb, that is the cause, of the time of Uṣas. Yoni means place of birth. The main sense is that night at the end of day, and Uṣas at the end of night, come one after the other by way of alternation. Therefore Uṣas means the radiance, the light, that spreads over all the quarters and appears after night has passed, before sunrise.
The commentator's (Sāyaṇa's) explanation: नक्तशब्द उषश्यब्दश्च लोके कालविशेषवा. चिन् । इह तु तत्कालाभिमानिनिवह्निमूर्तिद्वये प्रयुज्येते ! नक्तोषासा नक्तोषोनामिके वह्निमूर्ति (*naktaśabda uṣaśyabdaśca loke kālaviśeṣavā. cin | iha tu tatkālābhimāninivahnimūrtidvaye prayujyete ! naktoṣāsā naktoṣonāmike vahnimūrti*) — that is, in ordinary usage the two words nakta (night) and uṣas (morning) denote particular times, night and morning. Here, that is in this Ṛk or in the Ṛgveda, these words signify the presiding deities of night and morning. So the words नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*) or उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) are used in the sense of two forms of Agni, the deities presiding over night and the time of Uṣas. The word सुपेशसा (*supeśasā*) (of good form or shape), used in various places, supports this meaning. For night and morning, being divisions of time, have neither form nor shape; if they are taken as presiding deities, form may be assigned to those deities. Since the Ṛk makes such an assignment, it should be understood that it speaks of the presiding deities of those times. The long vowel in नक्तोषासा (*naktoṣāsā*) is lengthened for the convenience of the metre.
The epithet ऋतस्य मातरा (*ṛtasya mātarā*) in Ṛk 1-142-7 is very important.
द्रवंतां त उषसा वाजयंती अग्ने वातस्य पथ्याभिरच्छ । यत्सीमंजंति पूर्व्यं हविर्भिरा वंधुरेव तस्थतुर्दुरोणे ॥ (*dravaṃtāṃ ta uṣasā vājayaṃtī agne vātasya pathyābhiraccha | yatsīmaṃjaṃti pūrvyaṃ havirbhirā vaṃdhureva tasthaturduroṇe ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-14-3)

### Printed p. 354
In this Ṛk the permanent relation between the sacrifice and the two is described. In all the Ṛks that invite them (there are about twenty such Ṛks) they are asked to come with the other deities and sit on the darbha seat. In particular they are very closely related to Agni, who is kindled at the time of Uṣas and in the evening. Therefore it is an ornamental description that they hold Agni between them.
तम उच्छत्युषा नक्तानक्तीमां हिमबिंदुभिः । अपि वाव्यक्तवर्णेति नइद् पूर्वाञ्चीरिदं भवेत् ॥ (*tama ucchatyuṣā naktānaktīmāṃ himabiṃdubhiḥ | api vāvyaktavarṇeti naid pūrvāñcīridaṃ bhavet ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 3-9)
Of these two, Uṣas drives away the darkness; Night makes everyone wet and pervaded with drops of dew. Or, since there is no definite colour, the root अंजन् (*aṃjan*) joins the particle नञ् (*nañ*) and gives the meaning "of indistinct colour".
सा हि दोषा भवत्यादौ निशीथे सा तमस्वती । नाम्मा भवत्युषाश्चैव सैषा प्रागुदयाद्रवेः ॥ (*sā hi doṣā bhavatyādau niśīthe sā tamasvatī | nāmmā bhavatyuṣāścaiva saiṣā prāgudayādraveḥ ‖*)
(Bṛ. De. 3-10)
This deity is called Doṣā at the beginning, Tamasvatī at midnight, and Uṣas before sunrise. Doṣā, Tamasvatī, Śyāvī and Naktā are all names of night, as read in the Nighaṇṭu. (Nighaṇṭu 1-7).
Elsewhere in the Ṛksaṃhitā, by epithets such as तंतुं ततं संवयंती (*taṃtuṃ tataṃ saṃvayaṃtī*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-3-6), the help of Uṣāsānaktā in extending the sacrifice is described.
Yāska's Nirukta on the present Ṛk reads:
आसुष्टयंती यजते उपाके उषासानक्ता सदतां नियोन् । दिव्ये योषणे बृहती सुरुक्मे अधि श्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने ॥ सेस्मीयमाणे इति वा सुष्वापयंत्याविति वा सीदतामिति वा न्यासीदतामिति वा । यज्ञिये उपक्रांते दिव्ये योषणे बृहत्वा महत्वा सुरुक्मे सुरोचने अधिदधाने शुक्रपेशसं श्रियं शुक्रं शोचतेर्ज्वलतिकर्मणः । पेश इति रूपनाम पिंशतेर्विपिशितं भवति ॥ (*āsuṣṭayaṃtī yajate upāke uṣāsānaktā sadatāṃ niyon | divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatī surukme adhi śriyaṃ śukrapiśaṃ dadhāne ‖ sesmīyamāṇe iti vā suṣvāpayaṃtyāviti vā sīdatāmiti vā nyāsīdatāmiti vā | yajñiye upakrāṃte divye yoṣaṇe bṛhatvā mahatvā surukme surocane adhidadhāne śukrapeśasaṃ śriyaṃ śukraṃ śocaterjvalatikarmaṇaḥ | peśa iti rūpanāma piṃśatervipiśitaṃ bhavati ‖*)
(Ni. 8-11)
आसुष्टयंती—सेष्मीयमाणे परस्परं स्मयमाने अथवा सुष्वापयंत्र्यौ सुष्टु जनान् स्थापयंत्यौ ॥ (*āsuṣṭayaṃtī—seṣmīyamāṇe parasparaṃ smayamāne athavā suṣvāpayaṃtryau suṣṭu janān sthāpayaṃtyau ‖*) आसुष्टयंती (*āsuṣṭayaṃtī*) means those who look at each other and smile gently;

### Printed p. 355
or those who make people sleep well; that is, when the time of Uṣas comes people are glad, and in the night they sleep. May these deities Uṣāsānaktā, possessed of such qualities, sit सदतां नियोन् (*sadatāṃ niyon*) in their own place; this is the sense.
यज्ञिये (*yajñiye*)—those worthy of worship in the sacrifice, or those who are helpers in carrying out the sacrificial rite.
उपाके—उपक्रांते । (*upāke—upakrāṃte |*) those who are near.
दिव्ये योषणे (*divye yoṣaṇe*)—those who are not separated from each other in the heavenly world, that is, in the atmosphere. Since the time of Uṣas arrives after night, the sense is that they are joined together.
बृहती सुरुक्मे—महत्यौ सुरोचने । (*bṛhatī surukme—mahatyau surocane |*) those who shine with great brilliance.
अधिश्रियं शुक्रपिशं दधाने—शुक्रपेशसं श्रियं अधिदधाने । (*adhiśriyaṃ śukrapiśaṃ dadhāne—śukrapeśasaṃ śriyaṃ adhidadhāne |*) Those who wear a white-coloured radiance in the upper part of the atmosphere, that is, who shine with abundant splendour.
शुक्रं शोचतेर्ज्वलतिकर्मणः (*śukraṃ śocaterjvalatikarmaṇaḥ*)—the word शुक्र (*śukra*) is derived from the root शुच् (*śuc*), meaning to shine, to blaze. शुक्रं (*śukraṃ*) means shining.
पेश इति रूपनाम पिंशतेर्विपिशितं भवति (*peśa iti rūpanāma piṃśatervipiśitaṃ bhavati*)—पेश (*peśa*) is a name for form. The word पेश (*peśa*) is derived from the root पिश् (*piś*), meaning to adorn. विपिशितं (*vipiśitaṃ*) means well adorned.
The main sense: may the deities of the time of Uṣas and of night, Uṣāsānaktā — smiling gently, or making people sleep; helpers of the sacrificial rite; close at hand; being mingled with each other in the atmosphere; shining with abundant brilliance; wearing a glittering divine radiance of white colour — come to this our sacrificial altar and sit in the place prepared for them.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दैव्या॒ होता॑रा प्रथ॒मा सु॒वाचा॒ मिमा॑ना य॒ज्ञं मनु॑षो॒  ॑
> यजध्यै ।  
> प्र॒चो॒दयं॑ता वि॒दथे॑षु का॒रू प्रा॒चीनं॒ ज्योतिः॑ प्र॒दिशा॑  ॒॑
> दिशंता ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 356
#### Ṛk 7 (continued)

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दैव्या । होतारा । प्रथमा । सुवाचा । मिमाना । यज्ञं । मनुषः । यजध्यै ।  
> प्रचोदयंता । विदथेषु । कारू इति । प्राचीनं । ज्योतिः । प्रदिशा । दिशंता ॥७॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दैव्या ॥ देवाद्यञञाविति यज्ञत्ययः ॥ देवसंबंधिनौ होतारौ होमनिष्पादकौ होतृनामकावग्न्यादित्यावस्थिन्यज्ञ आसीदतां । कीदृशौ । प्रथमा मनुष्यहोतुः पूर्वभाविन्सौ सुवाचा शोभनस्तोत्र मनुषो मनुष्यस्य सर्वस्य यष्टुर्यजध्यै यागनिवृत्तये ॥ यजेस्तुमर्थे शध्यॆन्नृत्ययः ॥ यज्ञं मिमाना
> निर्मिमानावुत्पादयंतौ । विदथेषु । विदंत्यत्रर्त्विजः स्वस्वकर्माणीति विदथा यज्ञाः ।
> तेश्त्वत्वजो यजमानांश्च प्रचोदयंता प्रेरयंतौ कारू स्तुतीनां कर्तारौ
> प्राचीनं पूर्वस्यां दिशि यष्टव्यत्वेन स्थितमाहवनीयाख्यं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा प्रकृष्टेनोपदिष्टमार्गेण यद्वा प्रदिश्यमानेन मंत्रेण दिशंता निर्वहंतौ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

दैव्या (*daivyā*) means "related to the gods." The two Hotṛs, who accomplish the homa and are named Hotṛ, namely Agni and Āditya, are to sit down in this sacrifice. They are described as follows. प्रथमा (*prathamā*): earlier in being than the human Hotṛ. सुवाचा (*suvācā*): possessing fair praise. मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*): of the man, that is, of every sacrificer. यजध्यै (*yajadhyai*): for the accomplishment of the sacrifice. यज्ञं मिमाना (*yajñaṃ mimānā*): fashioning, that is, producing, the sacrifice. विदथेषु (*vidatheṣu*): the priests find (*vidaṃti*) their respective duties in them, so the विदथा (*vidathā*) are sacrifices. प्रचोदयंता (*pracodayaṃtā*): impelling the priests and sacrificers there. कारू (*kārū*): makers of praises. प्राचीनं ज्योतिः (*prācīnaṃ jyotiḥ*): the light called Āhavanīya, which stands in the eastern quarter as the one to be worshipped. प्रदिशा (*pradiśā*): by the excellently taught path, or else by the mantra that is being indicated. दिशंता (*diśaṃtā*): carrying it out.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रथमा (*prathamā*)—the foremost
- सुवाचा (*suvācā*)—those having excellent words of praise
- मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*)—the sacrificer
- यजध्यै (*yajadhyai*)—in order to perform the sacrifice
- यज्ञं मिमाना (*yajñaṃ mimānā*)—those who fashion the sacrifice
- विदथेषु (*vidatheṣu*)—in the sacrifices
- प्रचोदयंता (*pracodayaṃtā*)—those who impel the priests
- कारू (*kārū*)—makers of praise
- प्राचीनं (*prācīnaṃ*)—of the eastern quarter, in the form of the Āhavanīya
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—the fire
- प्रदिशा (*pradiśā*)—with an excellent mantra
- दिशंता (*diśaṃtā*)—those who direct
- दैव्या होतारा (*daivyā hotārā*)—the two Hotṛs related to the gods (Agni and the Ādityas) are to come and sit down in the sacrifice.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the foremost ones, those with excellent words of praise, those who fashion the sacrifice for the sacrificer to perform the sacrifice, those who impel the priests in the sacrifices, the makers of praise, those who direct the fire of the eastern quarter, in the form of the Āhavanīya, with an excellent mantra, the two related to the gods, Agni and Āditya, come and sit down in the sacrifice.

##### English translation
Divine ministers, prior (to those of earth), repeaters of pious praise, instituting the sacrifice at which men are to worship, (sit down) stimulating

### Printed p. 357
(the priests) at the sacrifices, makers (of praises), indicating the eastern fire with the prescribed (text).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दैन्व्या हेतारा दैन्व्या होतारावयं चाग्निरसौ च मध्यमः । तयोरेषाभवति ॥ (*dainvyā hetārā dainvyā hotārāvayaṃ cāgnirasau ca madhyamaḥ | tayoreṣābhavati ‖*) (Ni. 8-12). In this Ṛk two deities, called दैवौ होतार् (*daivau hotār*), are praised. As to who these deities are, Sāyaṇa has said अग्न्यादित्यौ (*agnyādityau*), Agni and Āditya. But Yāska, and following him Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta, say that दैवौ होतार् (*daivau hotār*) means आयं चाग्निरसौ च मध्यमः (*āyaṃ cāgnirasau ca madhyamaḥ*), that is, the terrestrial Agni of this world and Vāyu, the deity of the middle region. As an example of a Ṛk praising these deities, Yāska has given the explanation (nirvacana) for the present Ṛk itself:
दैन्व्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै । प्रचो दयंता विदथेषु कारू प्राचीनं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशंता ॥ (*dainvyā hotārā prathamā suvācā mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai | praco dayaṃtā vidatheṣu kārū prācīnaṃ jyotiḥ pradiśā diśaṃtā ‖*) देव्यौ होतारौ प्रथमौ सुवाचौ निर्मिमाना यज्ञं मनुष्यस्यमनुष्यस्य प्रचोदयमानौ यज्ञेषु कर्तारौ पूर्वस्यां दिशि यष्टव्यमिति प्रदिशंतौ ॥ (*devyau hotārau prathamau suvācau nirmimānā yajñaṃ manuṣyasyamanuṣyasya pracodayamānau yajñeṣu kartārau pūrvasyāṃ diśi yaṣṭavyamiti pradiśaṃtau ‖*) (Ni. 8-12).
दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा (*daivyā hotārā prathamā suvācā*)—दैव्यौ होतार् प्रथमौ सुवाचौ (*daivyau hotār prathamau suvācau*). The two deities named देव्यौ होतार् (*devyau hotār*) are related to the gods and invoke the gods; they are the chief among the gods, possessors of excellent words, or those praised with excellent words.
मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै (*mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai*)—निर्मिमान् यज्ञं मनुष्यस्य मनुष्यस्य यजनाय (*nirmimān yajñaṃ manuṣyasya manuṣyasya yajanāya*). They carry out the proceedings of the sacrifice of every human sacrificer so that they go on in the prescribed manner; that is, they take on the leadership, or the burden of protection, of the sacrifice.
प्रचोदयंता विदथेषु कारू (*pracodayaṃtā vidatheṣu kārū*)—प्रचोदयमानौ यज्ञेषु कर्तारौ (*pracodayamānau yajñeṣu kartārau*). विदथ (*vidatha*) means sacrifice; कारू (*kārū*) means कर्तारौ (*kartārau*), doers. These deities impel the mantras that the priests and others must recite in the sacrifices and the proceedings of the rite; they favour the presiding sacrificers, or they invite the deities who are intended.
प्राचीनं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशंता (*prācīnaṃ jyotiḥ pradiśā diśaṃtā*)—पूर्वस्यां दिशि यष्टव्यमिति प्रदिशंत् (*pūrvasyāṃ diśi yaṣṭavyamiti pradiśaṃt*). प्राचीनं ज्योतिः (*prācīnaṃ jyotiḥ*) means: the fire called Āhavanīya, established on the sacrificial altar in the eastern quarter,

### Printed p. 358
the fire churned in the kindling-sticks, is brought by the mantras that are the injunctions for the carrying forward of the fire, प्राजीमनु प्रदिशं प्रेहि विद्वान् (*prājīmanu pradiśaṃ prehi vidvān*) **NOTE** and so on, to the Āhavanīya fire-pit in the east and established there; the meaning is that they command that the homas be performed in that fire.
The Ṛk means: may the deities देव्य होतारौ (*devya hotārau*), possessed of such qualities (Agni and Āditya, or Vāyu and Agni), come and sit down at the place prepared for them on this our sacrificial altar. Since this Ṛk has no verb, the words सदतां नियोन् (*sadatāṃ niyon*) of the preceding Ṛk are to be supplied here as well.
#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नो॑ य॒ज्ञं भार॑ती॒ तूय॑मे॒त्विळा॑ मनु॒ष्वदि॒ह चे॒तयं॑ती।  
> ति॒स्रो दे॒वीर्ब॒र्हिरेदं स्यो॒नं सर॑स्वती॒ स्वप॑सः सदंतु ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । यज्ञं । भारती । तेयं । एतु । इळा । मनुष्वत् । इह । चेतयंती ।  
> तिस्रः । देवीः । बर्हिः । आ । इदं । स्योनं । सरस्वती । सुऽपसः । सदंतु ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> भारती । भरत आदित्यः । तस्य स्वभूता दीप्तिः ॥ तस्येदमित्यर्थ उत्सादित्वादञ् ।
> पा. ४-१-८६ । टिड्ढाणञ्ति जीप् ॥ नोऽस्मदीयं यज्ञं तूयं क्षिप्रमेतु ।
> आगच्छतु ! तथा मनुष्मन्मनुष्यो यथेवं मया कर्तव्यमिति जानाति तद्वज्जेतयंती
> जानतीळा देवी चेहास्मिन्कर्मण्यागच्छतु ! कथा सरस्वती च । स्वपसः सुकर्माणः ।
> अप इति कर्मनाम ॥ आप्पोतेरसुन्यापः कर्माख्यायां ह्रस्वः । बहुव्रीहानाड्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छंदसीत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ एतास्तिस्रो देवीर्देव्यः स्कोनं सुखकरमिदं बर्हिरिमं यज्ञमा सदंतु । आसीदंतु । प्राप्नुवंतु ॥ सदेर्लोटि
> सीदादेशाभावश्चांदसः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

भारती (*bhāratī*): Bharata is Āditya, and the radiance that is his own is Bhāratī. May she come swiftly to our sacrifice. Further, मनुष्वत् (*manuṣvat*): as a man knows "this is to be done by me," so चेतयंती (*cetayaṃtī*), the knowing goddess Iḷā, is to come here to this rite; and Sarasvatī too. स्वपसः (*svapasaḥ*): those of good works; *apaḥ* is a name for work. These three goddesses are to sit upon, or attain, this comfortable बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*), that is, this sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- भारती (*bhāratī*)—the goddess Bhāratī, the radiance of Āditya
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—to the sacrifice
- शूयं (*śūyaṃ*)—swiftly
- एतु (*etu*)—may she graciously come
- मनुष्वत् (*manuṣvat*)—like human beings
- चेतयंती (*cetayaṃtī*)—

### Printed p. 359
 knowing her duty
- इळा (*iḷā*)—and the goddess Iḷā
- इह (*iha*)—may come to our sacrifice
- सरस्वती च (*sarasvatī ca*)—may Sarasvatī also come
- स्वपसः (*svapasaḥ*)—possessed of excellent work
- तिस्रो देवीः (*tisro devīḥ*)—these three goddesses
- स्योनं (*syonaṃ*)—pleasant
- इदं बर्हिः (*idaṃ barhiḥ*)—on this sacrificial altar
- आ सदंतु (*ā sadaṃtu*)—come and sit down.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the goddess Bhāratī, the radiance of Āditya, come swiftly to our sacrifice. May the goddess Iḷā, who like human beings knows her duty, and Sarasvatī come. May these three goddesses of excellent work come and sit down on this pleasant sacrificial altar.

##### English translation
May Bharati come quickly to our sacrifice, and Ila thinking (of what she has to do), like a human being ; may Saraswati also—the three gracious goddesses, sit down upon this pleasant sacred grass.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk three goddesses, तिस्रो देवीः (*tisro devīḥ*), namely Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī, are praised. Yāska has given the explanation of this Ṛk:
तिस्रो देवीः तिस्रो देव्यः । तासामेषा भवति । आ नो यज्ञं भारती तूयमेत्विळा मनुष्पदिह चेतयंती । तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदं स्योनं सरस्वती स्वपसः सदंतु ॥ ऐतु नो यज्ञं भारती क्षिप्रं । भरत आदित्यस्तस्य भा इळा च मनुष्यवदिह चेतयमाना तिस्रो देव्यो बर्हिरिदं सुखं सरस्वती च सुकर्माण आसीदंतु ॥ (*tisro devīḥ tisro devyaḥ | tāsāmeṣā bhavati | ā no yajñaṃ bhāratī tūyametviḷā manuṣpadiha cetayaṃtī | tisro devīrbarhiredaṃ syonaṃ sarasvatī svapasaḥ sadaṃtu ‖ aitu no yajñaṃ bhāratī kṣipraṃ | bharata ādityastasya bhā iḷā ca manuṣyavadiha cetayamānā tisro devyo barhiridaṃ sukhaṃ sarasvatī ca sukarmāṇa āsīdaṃtu ‖*) (Ni. 8-13).
तिस्रो देवीस्तिस्रो देव्यः । तासामेषा भवति (*tisro devīstisro devyaḥ | tāsāmeṣā bhavati*): तिस्रो देवीः (*tisro devīḥ*) means three goddesses. They are Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī. The explanation of the present Ṛk, which praises them, is set out here.
आ नो यज्ञं भारती तूयं एतु (*ā no yajñaṃ bhāratī tūyaṃ etu*)—ऐतु नो यज्ञं भारती क्षिप्रं । भरत आदित्यस्तस्य भा (*aitu no yajñaṃ bhāratī kṣipraṃ | bharata ādityastasya bhā*). Here Bharata is Āditya. सर्वभूतान्युदकेन बिभर्तिति भरत आदित्यः (*sarvabhūtānyudakena bibhartiti bharata ādityaḥ*): he bears all beings with the water of rain, that is, he nourishes them, and therefore Āditya is called Bharata. तस्य भा (*tasya bhā*): his light, or ray, is called भा (*bhā*). Āditya is a deity of the heavenly region. The meaning of the sentence is: may Bhāratī, such a deity of the heavenly region, come quickly to our sacrifice.

### Printed p. 360
इळा मनुष्यदिह चेतयंती (*iḷā manuṣyadiha cetayaṃtī*)—इळा च मनुष्यवदिह चेतयमाना (*iḷā ca manuṣyavadiha cetayamānā*). चेतयमाः ना (*cetayamāḥ nā*) **NOTE** means one who knows. What does she know? मनुष्यवदिह चेतयमाना (*manuṣyavadiha cetayamānā*): just as human beings come quickly when other human beings invite them to a meal, so this goddess Iḷā knows that in the sacrifice they pray to her and call her to partake of the oblation. May such a goddess Iḷā too come quickly to our sacrifice. This goddess Iḷā is a deity of the terrestrial region.
सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—सरस्वती च (*sarasvatī ca*). May this goddess Sarasvatī too, a deity of the middle region, come quickly to our sacrifice.
तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदं स्योनं स्वपसः सदंतु (*tisro devīrbarhiredaṃ syonaṃ svapasaḥ sadaṃtu*)—तिस्रो देव्यो बर्हिरिदं सुखं सुकर्माण आसीदंतु (*tisro devyo barhiridaṃ sukhaṃ sukarmāṇa āsīdaṃtu*). स्वपसः (*svapasaḥ*) is सु अपसः (*su apasaḥ*): those of excellent work, those who do excellent works. स्योनं (*syonaṃ*) means pleasant. So the meaning of the sentence is: may the three goddesses Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī, of excellent work and established in the three regions, earth, atmosphere and heaven, come and sit on this बर्हि (*barhi*), this seat of darbha grass.
#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य इ॒मे द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी जनि॑त्री रू॒पैरपिं॑श॒द्भव॑नानि॒ विश्वा॑ ।  
> तम॒द्य हो॑तरिषि॒तो यजी॑यान् दे॒वं त्वष्टा॑रमि॒ह य॑श्॒व  
> विद्वान् ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । इमे इति । द्यावापृथिवी इति । जनित्री इति । रूपैः । अपिंशत् । भुवनानि । विश्वा  
> तं । अद्य । होतः । इषितः । यजीयान् । देवं । त्वष्टारं । इह । यक्षि । विद्वान् ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्वाष्टस्य पशोर्वपायां य इमे इत्येषानुवाक्या । सूत्रितं च । य इमॆ
> द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री तन्नस्तुरीपमध पोषयित्सु । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥
> यस्त्वष्टा देवो जनित्री विश्वस्य जनयित्र्याविमे द्यावापृथिवी ॥ द्वंद्वॆ
> दिवो द्यावेति द्यावादेशः । आद्युदात्तः । पृथिवीशब्दो जीषंतत्वेनांतोदात्तः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the vapā-offering of the animal for Tvaṣṭṛ, य इमे (*ya ime*) is the anuvākyā. It is also given in the sūtra: य इमॆ द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री तन्नस्तुरीपमध पोषयित्सु (*ya imè dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī tannasturīpamadha poṣayitsu*) (Ā. 3-8). The god Tvaṣṭṛ who is जनित्री (*janitrī*), the begetter of the world, of these heaven and earth.

### Printed p. 361

> देवताद्वंद्वे चेति पूर्वोत्तरपदयोः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ द्यावापृथिव्य रूपैर्देवतिर्यज्जनुष्या द्याकारैरपिंशत् रूपवत्यावकरोत् ॥ पिश अवयने तौदादिकः । शे
> मुचादीनामिति नुमागमः ॥ तथा विश्वा सर्वाणि भुवनानि भूतजातानि रूपयुक्तान्यकरोत् । हे होतः यजीयान्यष्टृतनो विद्वान् सर्वं जानंस्त्वमिषितोऽस्माभिरध्येषितः प्रार्थितः सन्निह्नास्मिन्कर्मण्यद्यास्मिन्निने तं त्वष्टारं देवं यक्षि ।
> स्तुतिभिर्हविर्भिर्वा यज । पूजय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Heaven and earth, he, Tvaṣṭṛ, made endowed with forms, with the forms that are (their) appearances; अपिंशत् (*apiṃśat*) means that he made them possessed of form. Likewise he made all the worlds, all created things, endowed with form. O Hotṛ, you are यजीयान् (*yajīyān*), the best sacrificer, and विद्वान् (*vidvān*), knowing all; being इषितः (*iṣitaḥ*), requested, that is, prayed to by us, here in this rite today, to that god Tvaṣṭṛ यक्षि (*yakṣi*), offer worship, with praises or with oblations; worship him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- होतः (*hotaḥ*)—O Hotṛ
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Tvaṣṭṛ who
- जनित्री (*janitrī*)—the begetters of the whole world
- इमे द्यावापृथिवी (*ime dyāvāpṛthivī*)—these heaven and earth
- विश्वा भुवनानि (*viśvā bhuvanāni*)—all created things
- रूपैः (*rūpaiḥ*)—with manifold forms
- अपिंशत् (*apiṃśat*)—made endowed with form
- तं (*taṃ*)—that
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—divine
- त्वष्टारं (*tvaṣṭāraṃ*)—god Tvaṣṭṛ
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—you who know all
- यजीयान् (*yajīyān*)—as the best sacrificer
- इह (*iha*)—here
- अद्य (*adya*)—today, on this day of the sacrifice
- इषितः (*iṣitaḥ*)—being prayed to by us
- यक्षि (*yakṣi*)—worship.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Hotṛ, you who know all, as the best sacrificer, worship for us today, at this time of the sacrifice, that divine god Tvaṣṭṛ who made heaven and earth, the begetters of the whole world, and all created things, endowed with form by manifold shapes.

##### English translation
To the divine Twashtri, who decked the parental heaven and earth and all the worlds with living forms, to him, O priest, who are venerable and wise, being solicited by us, offer oblation here to-day-

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra य इमे द्यानापृथिवी जनित्रि तन्न स्तुरीपमध पोषयित्तु (*ya ime dyānāpṛthivī janitri tanna sturīpamadha poṣayittu*) (Ā. 3-8), explains that in the vapā-homa of the animal sacrifice offered to the deity Tvaṣṭṛ this Ṛk, य इमे (*ya ime*), is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra.
In this Ṛk the deity Tvaṣṭṛ is praised. The explanation that Yāska has given for this Ṛk is as follows—

### Printed p. 362

#### Ṛk 8 (Nirukta explanation, continued)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

त्वष्टा तूर्णमश्नुत इति नैरुक्ताः । त्विषेर्वा स्याद्दीप्तिकर्मणस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात्करोतिकर्मणः ॥ तस्यैषा भवति ॥ य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भवनानि विश्वा । तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान्देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् ॥ (*tvaṣṭā tūrṇamaśnuta iti nairuktāḥ | tviṣervā syāddīptikarmaṇastvakṣatervā syātkarotikarmaṇaḥ ‖ tasyaiṣā bhavati ‖ ya ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpairapiṃśadbhavanāni viśvā | tamadya hotariṣito yajīyāndevaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yakṣi vidvān ‖*) (Ni. 8-15)

Two kinds of meaning can be given for the word त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*). Tvaṣṭā is well known as one of the twelve Ādityas. The Nairuktas say he is a deity of the middle region. Śākapūṇi's view is that he is Agni. तूर्णं (*tūrṇaṃ*) means "quickly", अश्नुते (*aśnute*) means "pervades". Because this god quickly pervades all regions with his rays, he has the name Tvaṣṭā. In this sense the god may be Āditya or may be Agni. The word may be derived from the root त्विष् (*tviṣ*), meaning "to shine", or from the root त्वक्स् (*tvaks*), meaning "to fashion, to make". Yāska took the present Ṛk, in which this word occurs, as his example and gave its Nirukta:

य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैः अपिंशत् भुवनानि विश्वा (*ya ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpaiḥ apiṃśat bhuvanāni viśvā*) and य इमे द्यावापृथिव्यौ जनयित्र्य रूपैरकरोत् भूतानि च सर्वाणि (*ya ime dyāvāpṛthivyau janayitrya rūpairakarot bhūtāni ca sarvāṇi*) This god Tvaṣṭā is the maker of heaven and earth; that is, he fashioned (created) them. And he made all the living beings and all moving and unmoving things in heaven and earth to be endowed with various forms and shapes. The meaning is that he produced for each living being or thing the form it ought to have.

तं अद्य होतः इषितः यजीयान् देवं त्वष्टारं इह यक्षिविद्वान् (*taṃ adya hotaḥ iṣitaḥ yajīyān devaṃ tvaṣṭāraṃ iha yakṣividvān*) and तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान् देवं त्वष्टारमिह यज विद्वान्॥ (*tamadya hotariṣito yajīyān devaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yaja vidvān‖*) Here the sacrificer addresses the priest called Hotṛ thus: "O Hotṛ priest, you who are skilled and wise in performing the sacrifice, now, impelled (or requested) by us, invoke and worship (honour) the deity Tvaṣṭṛ, endowed with the qualities described above."

. माध्यमिकस्त्वष्टेत्याहुर्मध्यमे च स्थाने समाम्नातः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः । तस्यैषापरा भवति ॥ (*. mādhyamikastvaṣṭetyāhurmadhyame ca sthāne samāmnātaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ | tasyaiṣāparā bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 8-14)

### Printed p. 363

This deity Tvaṣṭṛ is assigned to the middle (atmospheric) region. Śākapūṇi's view is that this deity is Agni. To make this clear Yāska took the following Ṛk as an example and gave a Nirukta for it also:

आविष्टो वर्धते चारुरासु जिह्मानामूर्ध्वः स्वयशा उपस्थे । उभे त्वष्टुर्बिभ्यतुर्जायमानात्प्रतीची सिंहं प्रतिजोषयेते ॥ (*āviṣṭo vardhate cārurāsu jihmānāmūrdhvaḥ svayaśā upasthe | ubhe tvaṣṭurbibhyaturjāyamānātpratīcī siṃhaṃ pratijoṣayete ‖*) followed by the explanation आविरावेदनात्तत्यो वर्धते चारुरासु । चारु चरतेः जिह्मं जिहीतेः ऊर्ध्व उच्छ्रितो भवति । स्वयशा आत्मयशाः उपस्थ उपस्थाने । उभे त्वष्टुर्बिभ्यतुर्जायमानात्प्रतीची सिंहं प्रति जोषयेते ॥ (*āvirāvedanāttatyo vardhate cārurāsu | cāru carateḥ jihmaṃ jihīteḥ ūrdhva ucchrito bhavati | svayaśā ātmayaśāḥ upastha upasthāne | ubhe tvaṣṭurbibhyaturjāyamānātpratīcī siṃhaṃ prati joṣayete ‖*) (Ni. 8-15)

To show that the Tvaṣṭṛ of the middle region is the lightning-Agni, Yāska gave an explanation of this Ṛk. The Ṛk above contains the words उभे (*ubhe*) and बिभ्यतुः (*bibhyatuḥ*). On who is meant by उभे (*ubhe*) here Yāska says:

द्यावापृथिव्याविति वा । अहोरात्रे इति वा । अरणी इति वा । प्रत्यक्ते सिंहं सहनं प्रत्यासेवेते ॥ (*dyāvāpṛthivyāviti vā | ahorātre iti vā | araṇī iti vā | pratyakte siṃhaṃ sahanaṃ pratyāsevete ‖*) (Ni. 8-15)

Some explain the word उभे (*ubhe*) in this Ṛk as heaven and earth; others say day and night, or the two araṇis (pieces of wood) with which Agni is churned out. Yāska takes the word सिंहं (*siṃhaṃ*) in this Ṛk in the sense "patience" (endurance). So the sentence प्रत्यक्ते सिंहं प्रति जोषयेते (*pratyakte siṃhaṃ prati joṣayete*) means that heaven and earth, fearing the power and might of the lightning-Agni, do not fight against him but wait on him with patience.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒पाव॑सृज॒ त्मन्या॑ समं॒जन्दे॒वानां॒ पाथ॑ ऋतु॒था ह॒वींषि॑ ।  
> वन॒स्पतिः॑ शमि॒ता दे॒वो अ॒ग्निः स्वदं॑तु ह॒व्यं मधु॑ना घृ॒तेन॑ ॥

### Printed p. 364

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उपअवसृज । त्मन्या । संअंजन् । देवानां । पाथः । ऋतुथा । हवींषि ।  
> वनस्पतिः । शमिता । देवः । अग्निः । स्वदंतु । हव्यं । मधुना । धृतेन ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वनस्पते यूप त्मन्या ॥ आत्मशब्दस्य तृतीयैकवचने यादेशः । मंत्रेष्वाज्यादेरात्मन इत्याकारलोपः ॥ आत्मनैवर्तुथर्तावृत् प्राप्ते काले देवानामर्थाय पाथः पशुलक्षणमन्नमन्नानि च हवींषि समंजन् सम्मग्यक्तीकुर्वन्नु पावसृज । उपागम्य प्रयच्छ ॥ गतिर्गतः । पा. ८-१-७० । इति गतेर्निघातः ॥ किंच
> वनस्पतियोऽयं यूपः शमितैतन्नामको देवः यद्वा शामित्रोग्निर्देवो
> दीप्यमान आहवनीयाख्योऽग्निश्चैते त्रयो मधुना मधुरेण धृतेन । यद्वा।
> मधुनोदकेन प्रोक्षणोपनयनादिगतेन धृतेन च । हव्यं हवनयोग्यं स्वदंतु ।
> स्वादं कुर्वंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Addressing the Vanaspati, the sacrificial post (yūpa): त्मन्या (*tmanyā*) is the instrumental of आत्म (*ātma*) with या (*yā*) substituted; the elision of the long ā follows the rule that in the Mantras the ā of *ātman* is dropped. It means "by himself". ऋतुथा (*ṛtuthā*): at the proper season, ऋतावृतौ (*ṛtāvṛtau*). "Make ready (समंजन् (*samaṃjan*), making manifest) the पाथः (*pāthaḥ*), food in the form of the animal, and the other oblation-foods for the gods, and approach and offer them" (उपावसृज (*upāvasṛja*): having come near, give). Further: the Vanaspati, this post; the deity named Śamitṛ, or else the Śāmitra fire; and the shining Agni called Āhavanīya: these three are to sweeten the oblation fit for offering with मधुना (*madhunā*), sweet ghee; or else with water (मधुनोदकेन (*madhunodakena*)) used in sprinkling, bringing near and so on, and with ghee. स्वदंतु (*svadaṃtu*): let them make it sweet.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्मन्या (*tmanyā*)—by his own impulse (addressed: O Vanaspati)
- ऋतुथा (*ṛtuthā*)—in accordance with the time of the sacrifice
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—to the gods
- पाधः (*pādhaḥ*)—food in the form of the animal
- हवींषि (*havīṃṣi*)—the oblations
- समंजन् (*samaṃjan*)—having prepared
- उपावसृज (*upāvasṛja*)—offer
- वनस्पतिः (*vanaspatiḥ*)—the Vanaspati
- शमिता (*śamitā*)—the deity called Śamitṛ
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- मधुना (*madhunā*)—sweet
- घृतेन (*ghṛtena*)—with water
- हव्यं (*havyaṃ*)—the oblation
- स्वदंतु (*svadaṃtu*)—let them make tasty

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vanaspati, in accordance with the time of the sacrifice, prepare and offer, of your own impulse, the food in the form of the animal and the oblations for the gods. Let the Vanaspati, the Śamitṛ and Agni make the oblation tasty with sweet water or with ghee.

##### English translation
Offer of your own will in due season the food (and other) oblations of the gods besmearing it. Let Vanaspati, Shamitri, the divine Agni, sweeten the oblation with honey and butter.

### Printed p. 365

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the deity called Vanaspati this is said:

वनस्पत इत्येनमाहैष हि वनानां पाता वा पालयिता वा । वनं वनोतेः ॥ (*vanaspata ityenamāhaiṣa hi vanānāṃ pātā vā pālayitā vā | vanaṃ vanoteḥ ‖*) (Ni. 8-3)

तत्क्यो वनस्पतिः । यूप इति कात्थक्यः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥ (*tatkyo vanaspatiḥ | yūpa iti kātthakyaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*) (Ni. 8-18)

They call Agni himself Vanaspati, because Agni is the protector or guardian of the forests, that is, of trees. Although Agni lies hidden within a tree he does not burn it, so he is called its protector; or else, because trees or wood are useful for sacrificial implements made of wood and the like, a tree is called वन (*vana*). वनस्पति (*vanaspati*) means king of trees, a great tree. Now which deity is Vanaspati? Kātthakya holds that it is the wooden post (यूप (*yūpa*)) planted in the sacrificial ground for tying the animal in the sacrifice. Śākapūṇi's view is that Vanaspati is Agni. As an example of a Ṛk praising this deity Vanaspati, Yāska took the present Ṛk and gave its Nirukta:

उपावसृजात्मनात्मानं समंजन्देवानामन्नमृतावृतौ हवींषि काले काले वनस्पतिः शमिता देवो अग्निरित्येते त्रयः स्वदयंतु हव्यं मधुना च घृतेन च ॥ (*upāvasṛjātmanātmānaṃ samaṃjandevānāmannamṛtāvṛtau havīṃṣi kāle kāle vanaspatiḥ śamitā devo agnirityete trayaḥ svadayaṃtu havyaṃ madhunā ca ghṛtena ca ‖*) (Ni. 8-17)

On the first half: here उप अवसृज (*upa avasṛja*) means "approach and give" (आश्लिष्य प्रयच्छ (*āśliṣya prayaccha*)). त्मन्या समंजन् (*tmanyā samaṃjan*), that is आत्मनात्मानं समंजन् विशिष्टेन संस्कारेण व्यक्तीकुर्वन् (*ātmanātmānaṃ samaṃjan viśiṣṭena saṃskāreṇa vyaktīkurvan*), means: making himself (Agni) manifest by himself through rites accompanied by mantras. पाथः (*pāthaḥ*) is food; ऋतुथा (*ṛtuthā*) is *ṛtāvṛtau kālekāle*, at the several times; हवींषि (*havīṃṣi*) are the oblations such as ghee. The chief sense: "O deity Vanaspati (Agni), making yourself by yourself, that is, Vanaspati, visible to all by the light of Agni, carry food and oblations such as ghee to the gods at the proper times and give them."

On the second half: the deity Vanaspati, the deity called Śamitṛ and the shining (देव (*deva*)) Agni, these three deities are to make the oblation prepared for the gods in this sacrifice sweet (स्वादु (*svādu*)), with water sprinkled and the like, and with ghee, or with sweet ghee.

### Printed p. 366

Here, to make clear the meaning "post" (यूप (*yūpa*)) for the word वनस्पति (*vanaspati*), Yāska gives the explanation of the Ṛk अंजंति त्वा (*aṃjaṃti tvā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-1); and to make clear the meaning Agni, the explanation of the Ṛks देवेभ्यो वनस्पते (*devebhyo vanaspate*) (Tai. Brā. 3-6-11-2) and वनस्पते रशनया (*vanaspate raśanayā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-70-10). Since they are not needed in the present context, they are not explained here.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒द्यो जा॒तो व्य॑मिमित य॒ज्ञम॒ग्निर्दे॒वाना॑मभवत्सुरो॒गाः ।  
> अ॒स्य होतुः॑ प्र॒दिश्य॒तस्य॑ वा॒चि स्वाहा॑कृतं ह॒विर॑दंतु दे॒वाः ॥

**NOTE**

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सद्यः । जातः । वि । अमिमात । यज्ञं । अग्निः । देवानां । अभवत् । पुरःगाः ।  
> अस्य । होतुः । प्रदिशि । ऋतस्य । वाचि । स्वाहाकृतं । हविः । अदंतु । देवाः ॥११॥
