Indra alone conquered all the enemies equal to the gods Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa (10-89-8, 9). From such statements it is understood that Indra has greater might than all the gods named in them.

### Printed p. 425

Description of the slaying of the Asura**NOTE**
The Asura Vṛtra is of evil nature. His nature is known to no one. He has no good understanding. It is his nature always to lie obstructing the waters. It is described that Indra killed this base-natured Vṛtra with the thunderbolt on the day of the full moon. On this matter the commentators—
quoting a passage of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, have shown that it states that Indra killed Vṛtra on the day of the full moon. Since all the seers have praised Indra's slaying of Vṛtra, it is necessary to give here a detailed account of that slaying. Therefore we set out here the mantra portion of the Yajurveda that gives that account, together with its meaning:—
त्वष्टा हतपुत्रो वींद्रग्ं सोममाहरत्तस्मिन्निंद्र उपहवमैच्छत तं नोपाह्वयत पुत्रं मेवधीरिति स यज्ञवेशसं कृत्वा प्रासहा सोममपिबत्तस्य यदत्यशिष्यश तत्त्वष्टाहवनीयमुप प्रावर्तयत्स्वाहेंद्रशत्रुर्वर्धस्वेति यदवर्तयत्तद्वृत्रस्य वृत्रत्वं यदब्रवीत्स्वाहेंद्रशत्रुर्वर्धस्वेति तस्मादस्येंद्रः शत्रुरभवत्स संभवन्नग्नीषोमावभि समभवत्स इषुमात्रमिषुमात्रं विष्णज्जवर्धत स इमान् लोकानवृणोद्यदिमान् लोकानवृणोत्तद्वृत्रस्य वृत्रत्वं तस्मादिंद्रोऽभिभेत् ॥ (*tvaṣṭā hataputro vīṃdragṃ somamāharattasminniṃdra upahavamaicchata taṃ nopāhvayata putraṃ mevadhīriti sa yajñaveśasaṃ kṛtvā prāsahā somamapibattasya yadatyaśiṣyaśa tattvaṣṭāhavanīyamupa prāvartayatsvāheṃdraśatrurvardhasveti yadavartayattadvṛtrasya vṛtratvaṃ yadabravītsvāheṃdraśatrurvardhasveti tasmādasyeṃdraḥ śatrurabhavatsa saṃbhavannagnīṣomāvabhi samabhavatsa iṣumātramiṣumātraṃ viṣṇajjavardhata sa imān lokānavṛṇodyadimān lokānavṛṇottadvṛtrasya vṛtratvaṃ tasmādiṃdro 'bhibhet ‖*)
(Tai. Saṃ. 2-53-2-1)**NOTE**
In this anuvāka the account of Indra's killing of Vṛtra is given. Behind this story there is another narrative; although we have explained it earlier, it is necessary to explain it briefly here as an introduction to what follows. Formerly Tvaṣṭṛ Prajāpati had a son named Viśvarūpa. He was the priest of the gods; but since he was born of an Asura woman, he had a special fondness for the Asuras. Indra feared that this Viśvarūpa, though priest to the gods, being partial to the Asuras, might watch his opportunity, help the Asuras and plot so that the gods would have no kingdom at all. Therefore Indra killed him by another means. This very matter is stated here by the sentence त्वष्टा हतपुत्रः वींद्रग्० सोममा.. हरत् (*tvaṣṭā hataputraḥ vīṃdrag0 somamā.. harat*). Out of anger that Indra had killed his son, Tvaṣṭṛ, when performing his sacrifice, did not invite Indra to the sacrifice and performed it leaving him out. He did not give him Soma to drink either. Angered by this, Indra came to his sacrifice, obstructed it, and moreover forcibly drank the Soma juice prepared for the sacrifice. Seeing this,

### Printed p. 426

Tvaṣṭṛ resolved to take suitable revenge on Indra, poured the Soma juice left over after Indra's drinking into the Āhavanīya fire, and, praying to Agni with स्वाहेंद्रशत्रुर्वर्धस्व (*svāheṃdraśatrurvardhasva*)—"may a son be born who will conquer Indra and be an enemy to Indra"—offered the remainder of the Soma in the fire. While he offered thus, because of an error of accent in the mantra, instead of a son who would conquer Indra, a son was born who would be conquered by Indra. This son was Vṛtra. This is the manner of his origin. That if an accent is wrongly pronounced when reciting mantras in sacrifices and the like, harm comes to the sacrificer:—
दुष्टः तब्बः स्वरतो वर्णतो ना मिथ्याप्रयुक्तो न तमर्थमाह । स वाग्वज्रो यजमानं हिनस्ति यथेंद्रशत्रुः स्वरतोऽपराधात् ॥ (*duṣṭaḥ tabbaḥ svarato varṇato nā mithyāprayukto na tamarthamāha | sa vāgvajro yajamānaṃ hinasti yatheṃdraśatruḥ svarato 'parādhāt ‖*)
(Pāṇinīya Śikṣā)
The great sage Pāṇini took this very case as his example. Thus, through the error of accent in the mantra, instead of a son who would subdue Indra, as Tvaṣṭṛ wished, a son was born who would be refined**NOTE** by Indra. Even so, that Vṛtra grew in strength by the oblation made in the fire to the deities Agni and Soma. Each day he grew by the measure of an *èllu***NOTE**, became huge in form, and pervaded all these worlds everywhere. Because he was of a nature to pervade all regions, Vṛtra got the name Vṛtra. The word vṛtra is formed from the root वृज् वरणे (*vṛj varaṇe*), meaning to cover, to enclose, to pervade, and indicates the significant name "he who pervades everything." Seeing Vṛtra grow in this way, Indra was afraid.
स प्रजापतिमुपाधावङ्भुत्रुर्मेऽजनीति तस्मै वज्रग्ं सिक्ता प्रायच्छदेतेन जहीति तेनाभ्यायत ॥ (*sa prajāpatimupādhāvaṅbhutrurme 'janīti tasmai vajragṃ siktā prāyacchadetena jahīti tenābhyāyata ‖*)
Then Indra went to Prajāpati and prayed, "O Brahmā, an enemy has been born to me; how is he to be killed?" Prajāpati comforted Indra, telling him not to fear, made his thunderbolt sharp and gave it to him, saying, "With this weapon kill your enemy." Indra took it and came to Vṛtra.
तावब्रूतामग्नीषोमौ मा प्रहारावमंतः स्व इति मम वै युवग् स्थ इत्य ब्रवीन्मामभ्येतमिति तौ भागधेयमैच्छीतां ताभ्यामेतमग्नीषोमीय मेकादशकपालं पूर्णमासे प्रायचत्तावबूतामभि संदष्ट्वै स्नो न तक्कुव ऐतुमिति स इंद्रआत्मनः शीतरूरावजनयत्तच्छीतरूरयोर्जन्मय ऐवग्ं शीतरूरयोर्जन्म वेद नैनग्ं शीतरूरा हतस्ताभ्यामेनमभ्यनयत्तस्माज्जंजभ्यमानादग्नीषोमौ निरक्रामतां ॥ (*tāvabrūtāmagnīṣomau mā prahārāvamaṃtaḥ sva iti mama vai yuvag stha itya bravīnmāmabhyetamiti tau bhāgadheyamaicchītāṃ tābhyāmetamagnīṣomīya mekādaśakapālaṃ pūrṇamāse prāyacattāvabūtāmabhi saṃdaṣṭvai sno na takkuva aitumiti sa iṃdraātmanaḥ śītarūrāvajanayattacchītarūrayorjanmaya aivagṃ śītarūrayorjanma veda nainagṃ śītarūrā hatastābhyāmenamabhyanayattasmājjaṃjabhyamānādagnīṣomau nirakrāmatāṃ ‖*)

### Printed p. 427

Then, when Indra was ready to strike Vṛtra with his weapon, Agni and Soma stopped Indra from striking, saying: "O Indra, do not strike Vṛtra now. We, the deities Agni and Soma, are dwelling in this Vṛtra's mouth." Indra said, "O Agni and Soma, you are our own people. Therefore leave Vṛtra's body and come to me. Then I shall kill Vṛtra." Hearing this, the deities Agni and Soma said: "O Indra, if we do as you say, what favour will you do us? If you arrange a share for us also in the sacrifice, we will do as you say." Indra agreed and arranged for them, in the full-moon sacrifice, a share of the oblation of the purodāśa cake offering called the eleven-potsherd one. Then, although Agni and Soma had thus obtained the boon they wanted, they said to Indra: "O Indra, we cannot now come out of Vṛtra's mouth. We are caught between Vṛtra's teeth and held tightly. Unless he opens his mouth we cannot come out." Then Indra thought of a means for this. From his own body he created cold-fever and the great heat arising from it. This was the first time cold-fever afflicted people in the world. The man who knows this manner of origin of cold-fever is not troubled by this fever. Then Indra took the cold and fever he had created and made them enter the body of the Asura Vṛtra. Then Vṛtra, shivering with cold and exhausted by the heat of fever, opened his mouth wide to sigh from weariness. At once the deities Agni and Soma came out of his mouth.
प्राणापानौ ना एनं तदजहितां प्राणो वै दक्षोऽपानः क्रतुस्तस्माज्जंजभ्यमानो ब्रूयान्मयि दक्षक्रकू इति प्राणापानावेवात्मन्धत्ते सर्वमायुरेति । (*prāṇāpānau nā enaṃ tadajahitāṃ prāṇo vai dakṣo 'pānaḥ kratustasmājjaṃjabhyamāno brūyānmayi dakṣakrakū iti prāṇāpānāvevātmandhatte sarvamāyureti |*)
Thereafter the vital airs called prāṇa and apāna abandoned that Vṛtra; that is, they left his body. The word prāṇa means dakṣa, and the word apāna means kratu. Dakṣa means skill in work, understanding. Kratu means bodily strength for work, capacity. Both of these left that Vṛtra who had opened his mouth. Therefore, while a sacrificial rite is being performed, if one moves the body or yawns and opens the mouth, one must then utter the mantra मयि दक्षक्रतू (*mayi dakṣakratū*). If one does so, prāṇa and apāna do not leave the sacrificer but remain firm. Long life also results.
स देवता वृत्रान्निर्हूय वार्त्र्घ्नग्ं हविः पूर्णमासे निरवपद् घ्नंति ना एनु पूर्णमास अमावास्यायां प्याययंति तत्पद्वार्त्र्घ्निः पूर्णमासेऽनूच्येते वृधन्वति अमावास्यायां ॥ (*sa devatā vṛtrānnirhūya vārtrghnagṃ haviḥ pūrṇamāse niravapad ghnaṃti nā enu pūrṇamāsa amāvāsyāyāṃ pyāyayaṃti tatpadvārtrghniḥ pūrṇamāse 'nūcyete vṛdhanvati amāvāsyāyāṃ ‖*)

### Printed p. 428

Then Indra called out from there all the deities, Agni, Soma and the rest, who were in the mouth of the demon Vṛtra, and on the day of the full moon he prepared the offering, consisting of the ājya portion and the oblation material, as the instrument for Vṛtra's destruction. Even in ordinary life everyone knows that the enemy called darkness, which covers everything everywhere, is destroyed by the bright moonlight of the full moon. On the new-moon day there is no moonlight, so the enemy darkness (Vṛtra) spreads everywhere and grows. Therefore, for the slaying of Vṛtra, on the full-moon day, before the offerings called the Agnīṣomīya ājya portions, the following Ṛks are to be recited as puronuvākyā mantras:

अग्निर्वृत्राणि जंघनद्दृविणस्युर्विपन्यया । समिद्धः शुक्र आहुतः । (*agnirvṛtrāṇi jaṃghanaddṛviṇasyurvipanyayā | samiddhaḥ śukra āhutaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-34)

त्वं सोमासि सत्पतिस्त्वं राजोत वृत्रहा । त्वं भद्रो आसि क्रतुः ॥ (*tvaṃ somāsi satpatistvaṃ rājota vṛtrahā | tvaṃ bhadro āsi kratuḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1.91-5)

Since both these Ṛks use words that indicate the slaying of Vṛtra, they are called the Vārtraghna Ṛks. The reason: Vṛtra was destroyed on the full-moon day, so it is fitting to recite on that day the Ṛks concerned with the slaying of Vṛtra and to make the offering. On the new-moon day darkness has increased; that is, Vṛtra, who pervades everything with darkness, prospers. Therefore on that day the following Ṛks are to be recited, which contain words formed from the root वृधु-वृद्दौ (*vṛdhu-vṛddau*), which denotes increase:

अग्निः प्रश्नेन मन्मना शुंभमानस्तन्वं १ स्वां । कविर्पिप्रेण वावृधे ॥ (*agniḥ praśnena manmanā śuṃbhamānastanvaṃ 1 svāṃ | kavirpipreṇa vāvṛdhe ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-44-12)

सोम गीर्भिष्टा वयं वर्धयामो वचोविदः । सुमृळीको न आ विशः (*soma gīrbhiṣṭā vayaṃ vardhayāmo vacovidaḥ | sumṛḷīko na ā viśaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-91-2)

These Ṛks, which contain words denoting increase, are called the Vṛdhanvatī Ṛks. They are to be recited on the new-moon day, when darkness has increased.

तत्सग्गस्थाप्य वार्त्र्घग्ं हविर्वज्रमादाय पुनरभ्यायत ते अब्रूतां द्यावापृथिवी मा प्रहारावयोर्वै श्रित इति ते अब्रूतं वरं वृणावहै क्षत्रविहिताहमसानीत्यसावब्रवीच्चित्रविहिताहमितीयं कस्मान्नक्षत्रविहितासौ चिद्रविहितेयं य एवं द्यावापृथिवोर्वरं वेद्यनं वरो गच्छति स अभ्यामेव प्रसूत इंद्रो वृत्रमहन् ॥ (*tatsaggasthāpya vārtrghagṃ havirvajramādāya punarabhyāyata te abrūtāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī mā prahārāvayorvai śrita iti te abrūtaṃ varaṃ vṛṇāvahai kṣatravihitāhamasānītyasāvabravīccitravihitāhamitīyaṃ kasmānnakṣatravihitāsau cidravihiteyaṃ ya evaṃ dyāvāpṛthivorvaraṃ vedyanaṃ varo gacchati sa abhyāmeva prasūta iṃdro vṛtramahan ‖*)

### Printed p. 429

Then Indra completely performed the ājya portion and the oblations that cause the slaying of Vṛtra, took the earlier vajra weapon in his hand, and rushed forward facing Vṛtra with the intention of destroying him. Then Heaven and Earth (the earth and the atmosphere) stopped Indra and said: "O Indra, do not kill this Vṛtra. He pervades all the region from the earth up to heaven. He dwells in dependence on us; we cannot give him up." Since Indra did not agree, Heaven and Earth spoke to him again: "O Indra, if we are to give room for the slaying of Vṛtra, you must grant the boon we ask." Indra said, "So be it." Then the heaven (dyau) asked for the boon that it be adorned with stars. The earth asked for the boon that it be filled with wonderful things of many kinds: human beings, animals, trees, mountains, rivers, oceans and the like. Indra granted the boons accordingly. The person who knows this manner in which Heaven and Earth obtained their boons obtains the desired objects he wishes and is happy. Afterwards Indra, having received the consent of Heaven and Earth, struck Vṛtra with the vajra and destroyed him.

ते देवा वृत्रग्ं हत्वाग्नीषोमावब्रुवन् हव्यं नो वहतमिति तावब्रूतामपतेजसौ वै त्र्यौ वृत्रे वै त्र्ययोस्तेज इति तेऽब्रुवन् क इदमच्छैतीति गौरित्यब्रुवन्गौर्वाव सर्वस्य मित्रमिति साब्रवीद्वरं वृण्यै मय्येव सतोभयेन भुनजाध्वा इति तद्गौराहरत्तस्माद्दवि सतोभयेन भुंजत एतद्वा अग्नेस्तेजो यद्धृतमेतत्सोमस्य यत्पयोय एवमग्नीषोमयो स्तेजो वेद तेजस्वीव भवति ॥ (*te devā vṛtragṃ hatvāgnīṣomāvabruvan havyaṃ no vahatamiti tāvabrūtāmapatejasau vai tryau vṛtre vai tryayosteja iti te 'bruvan ka idamacchaitīti gaurityabruvangaurvāva sarvasya mitramiti sābravīdvaraṃ vṛṇyai mayyeva satobhayena bhunajādhvā iti tadgaurāharattasmāddavi satobhayena bhuṃjata etadvā agnestejo yaddhṛtametatsomasya yatpayoya evamagnīṣomayo stejo veda tejasvīva bhavati ‖*)

After the slaying of Vṛtra, all the deities who were near Indra addressed Agni and Soma: "O deities Agni and Soma, you have now come back from Vṛtra's mouth. Henceforth bring the oblations offered for us in sacrifices and the like, and present them to us." Agni and Soma answered the deities: "O deities, we were in Vṛtra's body for a long time and have become devoid of brilliance through his **NOTE**; that is, our strength has shrunk. All our strength, our brilliance, has stayed behind in Vṛtra." **NOTE** Then the deities deliberated among themselves how to bring back the brilliance that Agni and Soma had left behind in Vṛtra's body. They resolved that, since the cow harms no one and behaves with friendliness towards all, they should send her and have the brilliance in Vṛtra brought. Then they called the cow and told her to bring the brilliance that was in Vṛtra. She said, "So be it. But the brilliance that I bring must always remain in me, in the form of milk and ghee. People must receive them from me and carry out their meals and the like. If you grant this boon, I will bring it."

### Printed p. 430

The deities said, "So be it," and gave the boon accordingly. Having received the boon, the cow brought that brilliance. As the result of this granting of the boon, even now the people in the world obtain from cows, from time to time, nourishing food such as milk and ghee, and eat it. Here ghee (ghṛta) is said to be the brilliance of Agni. It is for this reason that in sacrifices and the like people make offerings into the fire with ghṛta, ghee, and make the fire blaze. Milk is said to be the brilliance of Soma. For Soma is liquid like milk, and milk is mixed with it to improve the taste of the Soma juice. This mixture is called gavāśira. By mixing milk in this way the brilliance, or essence (taste), of Soma increases. The man who knows this greatness of the brilliance of Agni and of Soma becomes brilliant.

ब्रह्मवादिनो वदंति किंदेवत्यं पौर्णमासमिति प्राजापत्यमिति ब्रूयात्तेनेंद्रं जेष्ठं पुत्रं निरवासाययदिति तस्राज्येष्ठं पुत्रं धनेन निरवासयंति (*brahmavādino vadaṃti kiṃdevatyaṃ paurṇamāsamiti prājāpatyamiti brūyātteneṃdraṃ jeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ niravāsāyayaditi tasrājyeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ dhanena niravāsayaṃti*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-25-2-1 to 7) **NOTE**

The Brahmavādins ask who is the chief deity of this sacrifice called Paurṇamāsya. The reply is to be given that Prajāpati is the presiding deity of the sacrifice. But in this sacrifice Prajāpati has no share of the oblation; so how is Prajāpati the deity of this sacrifice? The answer: in the beginning Prajāpati created all the sacrifices. This is stated in the Śruti sentence:

प्रजापतिर्यज्ञानसृजताग्निहोत्रं चाग्निष्टोमं च पौर्णमासीं चोक्त्यं चामावास्यां चातिरात्रं च ॥ (*prajāpatiryajñānasṛjatāgnihotraṃ cāgniṣṭomaṃ ca paurṇamāsīṃ coktyaṃ cāmāvāsyāṃ cātirātraṃ ca ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-25-9-1)

That is, it is said here that Prajāpati created all the sacrifices: Agnihotra, Agniṣṭoma, Paurṇamāsī (the sacrifice performed on the full-moon day), Ukthya, Amāvāsyā (the sacrifice performed on the new-moon day), Atirātra and others. The sacrifices created by Prajāpati became his own property. Therefore, as is the custom in ordinary life, that is, as one gives one's property to one's eldest son, Prajāpati entrusted the chief deityship of these sacrifices to his eldest son Indra. This is stated in the very same sentence of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā:

तेनेंद्रं निरवासाययत्तेनेंद्रः परमां काष्ठामगच्छत् (*teneṃdraṃ niravāsāyayatteneṃdraḥ paramāṃ kāṣṭhāmagacchat*)

Therefore it should be understood that all the oblations offered in the Paurṇamāsya sacrifice to the son Indra are offered as it were to the father Prajāpati. For this very reason

### Printed p. 431

this sacrifice called Paurṇamāsya is said to be Prājāpatya, that is, related to Prajāpati. Following this order, even now in ordinary life it is customary for a father to give all his property, wealth and the rest, to his eldest son.

The reason why Prajāpati came to have the name "Ka". **NOTE**

There is a legend on this point:

इंद्रो वैवृत्रं हत्वा सर्वा विजितीर्विजित्याब्रवीत्प्रजापतिमहमेतदसानि यत्त्वमहं महानसानीति स प्रजापतिरब्रवीदथ कोऽहमिति यदैवैतदवोच इत्यब्रवीत्ततो वै को नाम प्रचापतिरभवत्को वै नाम प्रजापतिर्यन्महानिंद्रोऽभवत्तन्महेंद्रस्य महेंद्रत्वं ॥ (*iṃdro vaivṛtraṃ hatvā sarvā vijitīrvijityābravītprajāpatimahametadasāni yattvamahaṃ mahānasānīti sa prajāpatirabravīdatha ko 'hamiti yadaivaitadavoca ityabravīttato vai ko nāma pracāpatirabhavatko vai nāma prajāpatiryanmahāniṃdro 'bhavattanmaheṃdrasya maheṃdratvaṃ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 12-51)

In ancient times, after Indra had destroyed Vṛtra, he conquered all the regions of the earth, and addressing Prajāpati he said: "O Prajāpati, you have now attained a great position and are venerable. From now on I want your great station." Prajāpati asked, "If you take my station, then who (kaḥ) am I? What will be my standing?" Indra replied, "O Prajāpati, as you yourself have just said, your name from now on will be Kaḥ (who); that is, you will be denoted by the word ka." Therefore from that time Prajāpati became denoted by the word ka. This is well known. That is why this matter is stated in the pratigraha mantras, to be recited when accepting any gift: क इदं कस्मा अदादित्याह प्रजापतिर्वै कः । (*ka idaṃ kasmā adādityāha prajāpatirvai kaḥ |*) प्रजापतॆय एव तद्ददाति (*prajāpatèya eva taddadāti*) so runs a Brāhmaṇa sentence of the other Vedas. Since the word ka has the meaning "happiness", in matters and affairs relating to Prajāpati also he is said to be of the nature of happiness. Because Indra thus took on the greatness of Prajāpati, the appellation Mahān came to Indra; that is, Indra became Mahendra. This is stated in the other Vedas: इंद्रो वृत्रमहन्तं देवा अब्रुवन्महान्ना अयमभूद्यो वृत्रमवधीदिति (*iṃdro vṛtramahantaṃ devā abruvanmahānnā ayamabhūdyo vṛtramavadhīditi*) तन्महेंद्रस्य महेंद्रत्वं (*tanmaheṃdrasya maheṃdratvaṃ*). The deities, praising Indra's slaying of Vṛtra, said: "Because this Indra killed Vṛtra he became Mahendra (he obtained great renown)", that is, he became the greatest of all the deities. This, it is said, is the reason why Indra got the name Mahendra.

स महान्युत्वा देवता अब्रवीदुद्धारं म उद्धरतेति यथाप्येतर्हिच्छति (*sa mahānyutvā devatā abravīduddhāraṃ ma uddharateti yathāpyetarhicchati*)

### Printed p. 432

यो वै भवति यः श्रेष्ठतामश्नुते स महान्भवति तं देवा अब्रुवन् स्वयमेव ब्रूष्ट यत्ते भविष्यतीति स एतं माहेंद्रं ग्रहमब्रूत माध्यंदिनं सवनानां निष्केवल्यमुक्थानां तिष्टुभं छंदसां पृष्यं साम्नां तमस्मा उद्धारमुदहरन् उदस्मा उद्धारं हरुति य एवं वेद। (*yo vai bhavati yaḥ śreṣṭhatāmaśnute sa mahānbhavati taṃ devā abruvan svayameva brūṣṭa yatte bhaviṣyatīti sa etaṃ māheṃdraṃ grahamabrūta mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanānāṃ niṣkevalyamukthānāṃ tiṣṭubhaṃ chaṃdasāṃ pṛṣyaṃ sāmnāṃ tamasmā uddhāramudaharan udasmā uddhāraṃ haruti ya evaṃ veda|*)

Then Indra, having obtained the great station as said above, called the deities and spoke thus: "O deities, since I have obtained a great station, arrange on this account, that is, in order to felicitate me, an honouring reception that shows respect." In ordinary life too, when a man obtains boundless prosperity, or distinction in learning and the like, or a royal honour, such a man becomes known as a person of standing among the people, and it is the custom for people to arrange a reception to felicitate him. In the same way Indra put this question to the deities. The deities also approved Indra's word and said: "O Indra, in what manner should this reception be held? How would it please you? You yourself must tell us. We will carry it out accordingly." Indra replied: "Among the grahas (a graha is a special vessel for drinking Soma), the Māhendra graha (the Soma vessel offered to me, Mahendra) must be the best of all the grahas. Likewise, among the three savanas, Prātaḥsavana, Mādhyandinasavana and Tṛtīyasavana, the Mādhyandinasavana; among the śastras (mantras) such as the Āśvina and Marutvatīya, the Niṣkevalya śastra; among the metres such as Gāyatrī, the Triṣṭubh metre; and among the sāman chants, the Bṛhad-rathantara sāman that produces the pṛṣṭha stotra: you must approve these as the best. For they are dear to me. This is the honour you will do me." The deities agreed, "So be it," and approved the pre-eminence of the Māhendra graha and the rest in sacrifices. This is also said in the other Vedas: स एतं माहेंद्रमुदहरत वृत्रं हत्वान्यासु देवतास्वधीति यन्माहेंद्रो गृह्यत उद्धारमेव तं यजमान उद्धरते व प्रजास्वधि (*sa etaṃ māheṃdramudaharata vṛtraṃ hatvānyāsu devatāsvadhīti yanmāheṃdro gṛhyata uddhārameva taṃ yajamāna uddharate va prajāsvadhi*). The sacrificer who knows this obtains pre-eminence and a position of honour among the people.

तं देवा अब्रुवन्सर्वं वा अवोचथा अपि नोऽत्रास्ति स नेत्यब्रवीत्कथं वोऽपि स्यादिति तमब्रुवन्नस्येव नोऽस्तु मघवन्निति तानीक्षतैव ॥ (*taṃ devā abruvansarvaṃ vā avocathā api no 'trāsti sa netyabravītkathaṃ vo 'pi syāditi tamabruvannasyeva no 'stu maghavanniti tānīkṣataiva ‖*) (Pa. Bṛ. 12-9) **NOTE**

Then the deities said to Indra: "O Indra, we have honoured you and offered you in the sacrifice all the essential things you wished. You yourself have taken all the essential things. Give some of them to us also." Indra said, "That cannot be. I myself desired all these essential things. They all came to me. What reason is there to give them to you?" The deities again—"O

### Printed p. 433

Indra, do not refuse our request in this way. Give us also a small share," they prayed, and Indra looked at them with a gracious eye. He said nothing more.

ते देवा अब्रुवन्नियं वा इंद्रस्य प्रिया जाया नावाता प्रासहा नामास्यामेवेच्छामहा इति तथेति तस्यामैच्छंत सैनानब्रवीत्प्रातर्वः प्रतिवक्तास्मीति तस्मात्सित्रयः पत्याविच्छंते तस्मादु स्त्रैनुरात्रं पत्याविच्छते तां प्रातरुपायन्सैतदेव प्रत्यपद्यत । (*te devā abruvanniyaṃ vā iṃdrasya priyā jāyā nāvātā prāsahā nāmāsyāmevecchāmahā iti tatheti tasyāmaicchaṃta sainānabravītprātarvaḥ prativaktāsmīti tasmātsitrayaḥ patyāvicchaṃte tasmādu strainurātraṃ patyāvicchate tāṃ prātarupāyansaitadeva pratyapadyata |*) (Ai. Brā. 12-22)

Since Indra spoke no word, the deities did not understand his intention, so they spoke among themselves thus: "This woman who is now before us is Indra's beloved wife. She is of the middle class. Her name is Vāvātā. Kings have three kinds of wives. Among them it is the custom to call the wife of the highest class Mahiṣī, the wife of the middle class Vāvātā, and the wife of the lowest class Parivṛtti. That is why, in the duties to be performed by the women in the Aśvamedha sacrifice, the Mahiṣī is designated by the word bhūḥ, the wife called Vāvātā by the word bhuvaḥ, and the wife called Parivṛtti by the word suvaḥ. Among these three, the wife of middle class called Vāvātā has the name Prāsahā. For this wife, knowing her husband's wishes and acting accordingly, is able to do all work forcefully, and so she is very dear to the king. Therefore they judged it proper to learn the intention of King Indra through her, and laid their matter before her. Hearing it, Vāvātā said: "O deities, now is not the proper time to inform Indra of your matter and learn his intention. In the world it is the custom for women to tell their husband any important matter in the night, when they are in privacy. In privacy, since there are no obstacles or anxieties, the man listens sympathetically to what the woman says and gives a fitting answer. So tonight, when I am alone with Indra, I will bring up your matter and learn Indra's intention. So if you come tomorrow morning I will tell you Indra's reply." The deities said, "So be it," and coming the next day in the morning asked; and Vāvātā spoke, as her reply, this sentence in the form of a mantra:

यद्वावान पुरुतमं पुराषाळा वृत्रहेंद्रो नामान्यप्राः । अचेति प्रासहस्पतिस्तु विष्मानिति ॥ (*yadvāvāna purutamaṃ purāṣāḷā vṛtraheṃdro nāmānyaprāḥ | aceti prāsahaspatistu viṣmāniti ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-74-6)

Among the men of old, Indra, having slain Vṛtra, and having been victorious in many other battles too, …

### Printed p. 434

…having become victorious, he has won fame throughout the world. Therefore Indra has the name Prāsahaspati. Pra means "excessive", sahaḥ means "of strength", patiḥ means "lord": "the lord of exceeding strength", an utterly mighty one. This name is meaningful in itself. Having won such a name by the great deed of slaying Vṛtra, he has spread abroad throughout the world that the honoured names such as Māhendra-graha and Mādhyandina-savana are most dear to him. This Indra also knows what the gods desire, and he is very powerful. This is the meaning of the first three pādas of this Ṛk. This is what Vāvātā told the gods.

इंद्रो वै प्रासहस्पतिस्तुविष्मान् । यदीमुत्सि कर्तवे करत्तदिति यदेवैतदवोचामाकरत्तदित्येवैनांस्तदब्रवीत् ॥ म (*iṃdro vai prāsahaspatistuviṣmān | yadīmutsi kartave karattaditi yadevaitadavocāmākarattadityevaināṃstadabravīt ‖ ma*)

Having heard the reply that Vāvātā gave through the three pādas of the mantra as described above, the gods spoke among themselves with the fourth pāda, यदीमुष्मसि कर्तवे करत्तत् (*yadīmuṣmasi kartave karattat*). The meaning is: if we gods too have a share in the sacrifice, and if Indra will arrange that sacrificial share for us, then Indra will have fulfilled our wish. Or else, if the sentence of this fourth pāda is taken to be Vāvātā's own reply, then the meaning of the fourth pāda is: "O gods, what you have deliberated on and asked of Indra, Indra does, or will do." This is what is stated plainly here.

ते देवा अब्रुवन्यप्यस्या इहास्तु या नोऽस्मिन्न वै कमविददिति तथेति तस्या अप्यत्राकुर्वन् ॥ (*te devā abruvanyapyasyā ihāstu yā no 'sminna vai kamavidaditi tatheti tasyā apyatrākurvan ‖*)

The gods heard this reply of Vāvātā and thought: "This Vāvātā has done us gods great service. Therefore we must do her a service in return. It is not known whether she has any connection with the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantra or not. Be that as it may, let us arrange a fitting connection for her in the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantra." So they thought, and acted accordingly.

तस्मादेषात्रापि शस्यते यद्वावान पुरुषमं पुराषाळिति । (*tasmādeṣātrāpi śasyate yadvāvāna puruṣamaṃ purāṣāḷiti |*)

Since the gods thus arranged for Vāvātā a connection with this Ṛk (यद्वावान (*yadvāvāna*), Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-74-6) in the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantra, this Ṛk is called the Dhāyyā mantra in the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantra.

सेना वा इंद्रस्य प्रिया जाया नावाता प्रासहा नाम को नाम प्रजापतिः श्वशुरस्तद्यास्य कामे सेना जयेत्तस्या अर्धात्तिष्ठंस्त्रणमुभयुतः (*senā vā iṃdrasya priyā jāyā nāvātā prāsahā nāma ko nāma prajāpatiḥ śvaśurastadyāsya kāme senā jayettasyā ardhāttiṣṭhaṃstraṇamubhayutaḥ*)

### Printed p. 435

परॆच्छिद्येतरां सेनामभ्यस्येत्प्रासहे कस्त्वा पश्यतीति तद्यथैवादः स्नुषा श्वशुराल्लज्जमासा निलीयमानैत्येवमेव सा सेना भज्यमाना निलीयमानैति यत्रैवं विद्वांस्तृणमुभयतः परिच्छिद्येतरां सेनामभ्यस्यति प्रासहे कस्त्वा पश्यतीति । (*parècchidyetarāṃ senāmabhyasyetprāsahe kastvā paśyatīti tadyathaivādaḥ snuṣā śvaśurāllajjamāsā nilīyamānaityevameva sā senā bhajyamānā nilīyamānaiti yatraivaṃ vidvāṃstṛṇamubhayataḥ paricchidyetarāṃ senāmabhyasyati prāsahe kastvā paśyatīti |*) **NOTE**

Here the praise of Vāvātā, Indra's wife, who spoke this Dhāyyā mantra, is told at some length. It was said earlier that Vāvātā is Indra's beloved wife and that her name is Prāsahā. In worldly usage it is said that this Vāvātā or Prāsahā exists in the form of an army made ready for battle, because Indra's wife is the deity presiding over the army. In the Veda too it is said: इंद्राणी वै सेनाय देवता (*iṃdrāṇī vai senāya devatā*). And since she said "kaḥ nāma", "who am I?", it was explained earlier that Prajāpati is what is meant by the word ka. That Prajāpati is the father-in-law of Indra's wife. As to Indra being Prajāpati's son, the Veda itself says: प्रजापतिरिंद्रमसृजतानुजावरं देवानां (*prajāpatiriṃdramasṛjatānujāvaraṃ devānāṃ*).

This being so, if in worldly practice a man eager for battle wishes his army to win, he must perform a rite. At the time of battle, when the two armies stand facing each other to fight, that man goes beyond his own army, that is, a little ahead of the middle of the army, stands on the ground, takes a blade of grass, cuts off its root and its tip, and throws the remaining middle part towards the enemy army (in front of it), as one hurls an arrow. While throwing it he must throw that blade of grass with the mantra प्रासहे कस्त्या पश्यति (*prāsahe kastyā paśyati*): "O wife of Indra, named Prāsahā, Prajāpati, who is denoted by the word ka and is your father-in-law, is looking at you with his eyes." If the blade of grass is thrown in this way with this mantra, the enemy army suffers defeat.

This is made clear by an illustration. In worldly life, in the house of a respectable householder who is devoted to the customs of his forebears, if a young daughter-in-law sees her father-in-law, she out of shyness adjusts the end of her sari, draws in her hands and other limbs, and slips quietly into the inner part of the house. In the same way, through the throwing of the blade of grass with the mantra, the enemy army suffers defeat, retreats across mountains, forests and rivers, and flees to its own country. Having broken off this incidental matter here, he now takes up the matter in hand again:

तानिंद्र उवाचापि वोऽत्मास्त्विति ते देवा अब्रुवन्विराड्याज्यास्तु निष्केवल्यस्य या त्रयस्त्रिंशदक्षरा त्रयस्त्रिंशद्व देवा अष्टौ वसव एकादश रुद्रा द्वाद. (*tāniṃdra uvācāpi vo 'tmāstviti te devā abruvanvirāḍyājyāstu niṣkevalyasya yā trayastriṃśadakṣarā trayastriṃśadva devā aṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvāda.*)

### Printed p. 436

शादित्याः प्रजापतिश्च वषट्कारश्च देवता अक्षरभाजः करोत्यक्षरमक्षरमेव तद्देवता अनु प्रपिबंति देवपात्रेणैव तद्देवतास्तृप्यंति । (*śādityāḥ prajāpatiśca vaṣaṭkāraśca devatā akṣarabhājaḥ karotyakṣaramakṣarameva taddevatā anu prapibaṃti devapātreṇaiva taddevatāstṛpyaṃti |*) **NOTE**

Hearing Vāvātā's word (reply), the gods went to Indra's presence, and Indra said to them: "O gods, as you desire, a share in the sacrifice has been given to you in the Niṣkevalya-śastra of the sacrifice." Hearing this, the gods said: "We (the gods) are thirty-three: eight Vasus, eleven Rudras, twelve Ādityas, together with one Prajāpati and one Vaṣaṭkāra, thirty-three deities in all. Therefore, with a Yājyā mantra of the metre Virāṭ, which has thirty-three syllables, that is, with the Yājyā mantra

पिबा सोममिंद्र मंदतु त्वा यं ते सुषाव हर्यश्वाद्रिः । सोतुर्बाहुभ्यां सुयतो नार्वा । (*pibā somamiṃdra maṃdatu tvā yaṃ te suṣāva haryaśvādriḥ | soturbāhubhyāṃ suyato nārvā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-22-1)

arrange the drinking of Soma." So they prayed to Indra. This Yājyā mantra ought to have thirty-three syllables, but it has only twenty-nine. Nevertheless, by the method of combining syllables, even though syllables are fewer, it must be reckoned as having thirty-three in all. In this way the thirty-three syllables of the Yājyā mantra, one syllable for each deity, satisfy the thirty-three deities. He now explains the harm that comes if, leaving aside this procedure, the Yājyā offering is made with a mantra of another metre:

यं कामयेतानायतवान् स्यादित्यविराजास्य यजेद्गायत्रा वा त्रिष्टुभा वान्येन ना छंदसा वषट्कुर्यादनायतनवंतमेवैनं तत्करोति (*yaṃ kāmayetānāyatavān syādityavirājāsya yajedgāyatrā vā triṣṭubhā vānyena nā chaṃdasā vaṣaṭkuryādanāyatanavaṃtamevainaṃ tatkaroti*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 12-5) **NOTE**

If the Hotṛ wishes that the sacrificing patron lose his house and other possessions, then in the Niṣkevalya-śastra he should perform the homa while reciting mantras of Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh or another metre, and not the Yājyā mantra in the Ṛk of the Virāṭ metre. If he does so, the patron's house and dwellings are destroyed. Therefore, if it is wished that the patron's house-wealth be lasting, the Hotṛ should perform this Yājyā homa with the mantra पिबा सोमविंद्र (*pibā somaviṃdra*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-22-1), a Ṛk of the Virāṭ metre. If he does so, the patron gains abundance of house and dwellings.

### Printed p. 437

**The reason Indra came to be called Marutvān**

The constant companionship of Indra and the Maruts, the relation of king and subjects between them, the offering of oblations in the principal sacrifices to Indra together with the Maruts, and the Maruts' having helped him when he fought the demon Vṛtra are praised in many places in the Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas. **NOTE**

A story of old, telling how Indra was joined with the Maruts and separate from the other gods, is told in the Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa.

आतिथ्येन वै देवा इष्ट्वा । तान्त्समदविंदत्ते चतुर्धाव्यद्रवन्नन्योन्यस्य श्रिया तिष्ठमाना अग्निर्वसुभिः सोमो रुद्रैर्वरुण आदित्यैरिंद्रो मरुद्धिर्भृहस्पतिर्विश्वैर्देवैः ॥ (*ātithyena vai devā iṣṭvā | tāntsamadaviṃdatte caturdhāvyadravannanyonyasya śriyā tiṣṭhamānā agnirvasubhiḥ somo rudrairvaruṇa ādityairiṃdro maruddhirbhṛhaspatirviśvairdevaiḥ ‖*) (Ca. Cā. 3-4-2-1) **NOTE**

Formerly, when the gods performed the rite of hospitality, discord arose among them; unwilling to join one another, they formed four groups and separated. Agni joined the Vasus, Soma the Rudras, Varuṇa the Ādityas, Indra the Maruts, and Bṛhaspati the Viśvedevas, each forming a separate group. This story tells of the close relation that Indra built up with the Maruts through companionship and kept with them.

Moreover, it is said in many places that Indra is the king and the Maruts the subjects. For example, in the same Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa:

क्षत्रं वा इंद्रो विशो मरुतो विशा वै क्षत्रियो बलवान् भवति । (*kṣatraṃ vā iṃdro viśo maruto viśā vai kṣatriyo balavān bhavati |*) (Ka. Brā. 4-3-3-6) **NOTE**

Indra is the king with kṣatra-splendour; the Maruts are his subjects. This indicates that a king becomes powerful through the cooperation of his subjects, and that Indra's prowess grew with the help of the Maruts. Because of such a close relation and companionship, the practice of offering oblations with Indra and the Maruts addressed together is found in the Śrutis. And with Ṛks such as

स नो मरुद्भिवृषभ श्रवो धा उग्र उग्रेभिः स्थविरः सहोदाः । (*sa no marudbhivṛṣabha śravo dhā ugra ugrebhiḥ sthaviraḥ sahodāḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-171-5)

there is invocation and offering of oblations to Indra and the Maruts jointly. Describing this companionship, the Bṛhaddevatā says:

मरुद्भिः सह यत्रेंद्रो मरुत्वांस्तत्र सोऽभवत् (*marudbhiḥ saha yatreṃdro marutvāṃstatra so 'bhavat*) (Bṛ. De. 4-56)

### Printed p. 438

With such sentences the epithet indicating the relation of these deities is explained. But in one sūkta, as a result of a dispute between Indra and the Maruts, their mutual enmity and Indra's anger are indicated. Their dispute, the source of this anger, is told thus:

क्वंस्यावो मरुतः स्वधासीद्यनलोकं समधत्ताहिहेत्ये । अहं ह्युंस्रस्तविषस्तुविष्मान्विश्वस्व शत्रोरनमं ऎण्णलः ॥ (*kvaṃsyāvo marutaḥ svadhāsīdyanalokaṃ samadhattāhihetye | ahaṃ hyuṃsrastaviṣastuviṣmānviśvasva śatroranamaṃ èṇṇalaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-155-6) **NOTE**

"O Maruts, it is false to say that I slew Ahi (Vṛtra) with your help. Where was that strength of yours? Because my own strength is extraordinary, it helped me at the time of the slaying of Vṛtra without needing the help of other strength. I alone am terrible, of wondrous strength, endowed with greatness." Looking at the Maruts with contempt, Indra thus reveals his anger. That anger is indicated here. It is well known that Indra received the help of the Maruts at the time of the slaying of the demon Vṛtra; yet when the Maruts reminded him of this and asked that, in memory of that help, they too be given a share in the oblation due to Indra, Indra declares that no help at all came from the Maruts and that he slew all his enemies by his own strength. The author of the Nirukta, telling the same matter, says:

अगस्त्य इंद्राय हविर्निरुप्य मरुद्भः संप्रदित्सांचकार । स इंद्र एत्य परिदेवयांचक्रे । (*agastya iṃdrāya havirnirupya marudbhaḥ saṃpraditsāṃcakāra | sa iṃdra etya paridevayāṃcakre |*) (Ni. 1-5) **NOTE**

The author of the Nirukta, having given the occasion that when the sage Agastya had prepared an oblation for Indra and wished to offer a share in it to the Maruts too, Indra at once objected, cites the Ṛk that tells this point:

न नूनमस्ति नो श्वः कस्तद्वेद यदद्भुतं । अन्यस्य चित्तमभि संचरेण्यमुताधीतं विनश्यति ॥ (*na nūnamasti no śvaḥ kastadveda yadadbhutaṃ | anyasya cittamabhi saṃcareṇyamutādhītaṃ vinaśyati ‖*) (Ma. Sa. 1-170-1) **NOTE**

Here prayer is addressed to the Maruts, so that the force of that anger may abate and not harm him (the sage), and with the purpose that the share of the oblation rightly due to the Maruts must reach them. After these words of conciliation, Indra's friendship grows as before, and he himself gives the Maruts their share of his oblation. The seer in the eighth Maṇḍala praises him, telling this very matter thus.

### Printed p. 439

वृत्रस्य त्वा श्वसथादीषमाणा विश्वे देवा अजहुर्ये सखायः । मरुद्भरिंद्र सख्यं ते अस्त्वथमा विश्वाः पृतना जयासि ॥ (*vṛtrasya tvā śvasathādīṣamāṇā viśve devā ajahurye sakhāyaḥ | marudbhariṃdra sakhyaṃ te astvathamā viśvāḥ pṛtanā jayāsi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-96-7)

"O Indra, your friendship with the Maruts is well known. Give them too a share in your oblation, and with their help conquer all your enemies": so the prayer goes.

**How Indra slew the demon Namuci**

After first giving a brief account of this Namuci, we shall then explain how Indra slew him.

Namuci's name occurs in the Ṛgveda nine times, and is also found in places such as the Vājasaneya-saṃhitā, the Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa (Tai. Brā. 1-6-1-6, 7) and the Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa (Śa. Brā. 12-3-1-10). He is of demonic nature, and in the Ṛgveda he is called dāsa (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-30-7, 8). In one place (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-57-7) he is described as māyin. It is said in the Ṛgveda that when Indra was defeating Namuci he had the friendship or support of Nami and Sāpya (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-53-7; 6-20-6). **NOTE**

Like the other demons, Namuci too was slain by Indra (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-5; 7-19-5), or was struck down (1-53-7). Indra slew the demons Vṛtra and Namuci and destroyed the hundred forts of the demons (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-19-5). Namuci's head is not cut off as Vṛtra's head is, but he is crushed (ground down) and killed (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-30-8; 6-20-6), or his head is twisted off and he is killed (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-30-7), or he is killed by twisting (wringing) his head with the foam of water (of the sea) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-14-3). In some places it is also said that he cut off the head (Tai. Brā. 1-7-1-6, 7). In one place (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-131-4, 5) Indra sat by Namuci and drank an intoxicating drink; then Sarasvatī, with the help of the Aśvin deities, healed him. All these are the accounts given in the Ṛgveda.

Now we shall explain how the Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa of the Yajurveda tells that Indra destroyed Namuci. नमुचिः । इंद्रेण सह युद्धं न मुंचतीति नमुचिः । (*namuciḥ | iṃdreṇa saha yuddhaṃ na muṃcatīti namuciḥ |*). Some commentators have given this derivation of the word namuci: "he does not leave off fighting Indra, therefore he is Namuci." Because this demon was of great strength, it was very hard for Indra to fight him and conquer him. Therefore Indra had to slay him by a stratagem. On this matter there is an episode in the Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa:

### Printed p. 440

Continuing the episode in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa:

इंद्रो वृत्रग्ं हत्वा । असुरान् पराभाव्य । नमुचिमासुरं नालभत । तग्ं शच्यागृह्णात् । त्वा समलभीतां । सोऽस्मादभिशुनतरोऽभवत् । सोऽब्रवीत् । संधाग्ं संदधावहै । अथ त्वावस्रक्षामि । न मा शुष्केण नार्देण हनः । न दिवा न वक्तमिति । स एतमसां फेनमसिंचत् । न वा एष शुष्को नार्द्रो व्युष्टासीत् । अनुदितः सूर्यः । न वा एतद्दिवा न नक्तं । तस्यैतस्मिन् लोके । असां फेनेन शिर उदवर्तयत् । तदेनमन्ववर्तत । मित्रद्रुगिति । स एतानपामार्गानजनयत् । तानजुहोत् । तैर्वै स रक्षाग् स्यपाहत । यदपमार्गहोमो भवति । रक्षसामपहत्यै ॥ (*iṃdro vṛtragṃ hatvā | asurān parābhāvya | namucimāsuraṃ nālabhata | tagṃ śacyāgṛhṇāt | tvā samalabhītāṃ | so 'smādabhiśunataro 'bhavat | so 'bravīt | saṃdhāgṃ saṃdadhāvahai | atha tvāvasrakṣāmi | na mā śuṣkeṇa nārdeṇa hanaḥ | na divā na vaktamiti | sa etamasāṃ phenamasiṃcat | na vā eṣa śuṣko nārdro vyuṣṭāsīt | anuditaḥ sūryaḥ | na vā etaddivā na naktaṃ | tasyaitasmin loke | asāṃ phenena śira udavartayat | tadenamanvavartata | mitradrugiti | sa etānapāmārgānajanayat | tānajuhot | tairvai sa rakṣāg syapāhata | yadapamārgahomo bhavati | rakṣasāmapahatyai ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 1-7-106, 7)

After Indra had killed the asura Vṛtra, he also killed other asuras. But he could not conquer the asura named Namuci. This Namuci was very strong, and no kind of weapon could make him yield. Therefore Indra wished to defeat him by the strength of his own body alone and began a wrestling bout with him. Yet the more they fought, the more Namuci's strength grew. Indra could not escape his hold. Then Indra asked Namuci to release him. The asura said to Indra: "O Indra, if I am to release you, you must do as I say. Let us now make a pact with each other. You may again wish to fight me by some stratagem and kill me. In that case the weapon you use to kill me must be neither wet nor dry; you must not kill me by day, and you must not kill me by night. If you agree to these conditions I will release you." Indra agreed, saying "So be it", freed himself from his hold, and began to think how he might conquer him. After some time Indra thought of a means. While walking along the seashore, the foam of the sea fell within his sight. This foam is neither wet nor dry. "So I will make this my weapon and kill Namuci. When night has passed and dawn has begun, it is fully light before the sun rises. That time is not night, since there is no darkness, and not day, since the sun has not risen. If I fight Namuci at such a time and kill him with a weapon made of the water's foam, I shall not have broken my word." Having resolved thus, he fought Namuci accordingly and cut off his head with that foam. Yet the asura did not die; he chased Indra in order to kill him. "O Indra, betrayer of a friend, stop, stop! You gave your word earlier that you would not kill me, and now you have done this treacherous deed. Even now I will not leave you unkilled," he said. Then Indra, frightened, created the apāmārga, a particular kind of plant, and offered its sticks as an oblation in the fire to increase his vigour.

### Printed p. 441

Through that, Indra's strength increased, and he killed Namuci. Therefore those who wish to be free from the affliction of the rākṣasas should offer apāmārga sticks in the fire for the increase of vigour. By that offering their strength grows and they become able to conquer the rākṣasas. Such is the episode. This asura Namuci is mentioned in the Ṛgveda in the following Ṛks:

नम्या यदिंद्र सख्या परावति निबर्हयो नमुचिं नाम मायिनं ॥ (*namyā yadiṃdra sakhyā parāvati nibarhayo namuciṃ nāma māyinaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-53-7)

यः पिप्रुं नमुचिं यो रुधिकां तस्मा इंद्रायांधसो जुहोत ॥ (*yaḥ pipruṃ namuciṃ yo rudhikāṃ tasmā iṃdrāyāṃdhaso juhota ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-5)

निवेशने शततमाविवेषीरहज्ज वृत्रं नमुचिमुताहन् (*niveśane śatatamāviveṣīrahajja vṛtraṃ namucimutāhan*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-19-5)

त्वं जघंथ नमुचिं मखस्युं दासं कृष्णान ऋषये विमायं ॥ (*tvaṃ jaghaṃtha namuciṃ makhasyuṃ dāsaṃ kṛṣṇāna ṛṣaye vimāyaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-23-7)

आत्रा दासस्य नमुचेः शिरो यदवर्तयो मनवे गातुमिच्छन् ॥ (*ātrā dāsasya namuceḥ śiro yadavartayo manave gātumicchan ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-30-7)

युजं हि मामकृथा आदिदिंद्र शिरो दासस्य नमुचेर्मथायन् ॥ (*yujaṃ hi māmakṛthā ādidiṃdra śiro dāsasya namucermathāyan ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-30-8)

प्र शैनो न मदिरमंशुमस्मै शिरो दासस्य नमुचेर्मथायन् ॥ (*pra śaino na madiramaṃśumasmai śiro dāsasya namucermathāyan ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-20-6)

अपां फेनेन नमुचेः शिर इंद्रोदवर्तयः (*apāṃ phenena namuceḥ śira iṃdrodavartayaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-14-13)

युवं सुराममश्विना नमुचावासुरे सचा (*yuvaṃ surāmamaśvinā namucāvāsure sacā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-131-4 **NOTE**)

These Ṛks exist; there are none elsewhere.

**The reason Indra is called Yajiṣī**

**NOTE**

Ṛjiṣī: Yāska has given the following explanation of this word:

ख जिषी सोमो यत्सोमस्य पूयमानस्यातिरिच्यते तदृजीषमपार्जितं भवति तेनर्जिषी सोमः । अथाप्यैंद्रो निगमो भवति ऋजिषी वज्री इति ॥ (*kha jiṣī somo yatsomasya pūyamānasyātiricyate tadṛjīṣamapārjitaṃ bhavati tenarjiṣī somaḥ | athāpyaiṃdro nigamo bhavati ṛjiṣī vajrī iti ‖*) (Ni. 5-12)

**NOTE**

### Printed p. 442

After the soma plant has been crushed with stones and the juice taken out, the juiceless, husk-like material that remains is called ṛjīṣa. This ṛjīṣa is thrown away as useless. On some occasions that ṛjīṣa is soaked in water and a little more juice is squeezed out. Such soma juice is called "ऋजीषः सोमः (*ṛjīṣaḥ somaḥ*)". At the third pressing, āśira substances such as flour are mixed with this ṛjīṣa soma and it is offered to Indra. Because Indra drinks this ṛjīṣa soma, it has become customary to call Indra by the very word ṛjīṣī. Moreover, Indra's horses, the Haris, are well known to eat the husks of these soma plants called ṛjīṣa. As an example in this matter Yāska has cited the Vedic sentence बद्धां ते हरीधाना उप ऋजीषं जिघ्रतां (*baddhāṃ te harīdhānā upa ṛjīṣaṃ jighratāṃ*). The meaning of that sentence is: "O Indra, let your horses eat grain and then sniff this ṛjīṣa."

What is ṛjīṣa? Why does it have this name? What is its use in the sacrifice? These and similar matters, as stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, we shall examine here in brief:

सोमो वै राजमुष्मिंल्लोक आसीत्तं देवाश्च ऋषयश्चाभ्यध्यायन् कथमयमस्मात्सोमो राजागच्छेदिति तेऽब्रुवंश्वंदांसि यूयं न इमं सोमं राजानमाहरतेति तथेति ते सुपर्णा भूत्वोदपतन् (*somo vai rājamuṣmiṃlloka āsīttaṃ devāśca ṛṣayaścābhyadhyāyan kathamayamasmātsomo rājāgacchediti te 'bruvaṃśvaṃdāṃsi yūyaṃ na imaṃ somaṃ rājānamāharateti tatheti te suparṇā bhūtvodapatan*) (I. Citra. 13-25)

**NOTE**

In the beginning King Soma (the soma plant; it is the custom to call the soma plant "King Soma" out of respect) was in the world of heaven, not in this world. Knowing this, the gods and the ṛṣis considered how this soma might be brought here. Then, deliberating on the matter, they concluded that the metres had the power to bring soma from heaven to earth, and they addressed the metres: "O metres, for us, that is, for use in our sacrifice, bring the soma that is in heaven down to earth." They begged them thus. Accepting their request, the metres took the forms of certain birds well known in the world and flew off to the world of heaven. First the metre Jagatī, taking the form of a bird, flew towards heaven. But before it had gone far it grew tired, could not reach heaven, and turned back. Then the metre Triṣṭubh said that it would bring the soma and leapt into the atmosphere. But before it had gone a little beyond half the way it was exhausted with fatigue and turned back. When the gods saw that Jagatī and Triṣṭubh had come back unable to bring the soma, they went to the metre Gāyatrī and begged: "O Gāyatrī, you must bring soma from heaven for us."

### Printed p. 443

Gāyatrī agreed, saying "So be it", took the form of a śyena bird, flew to heaven, frightened the guardians of the soma there, Sthāna, Bhrāja and others, carried the soma off, and brought it to earth. Because she brought the soma plant, Gāyatrī obtained the most excellent place among the metres.

सा यद्धक्षिणेन पदा समगृभ्वात्तत्मा तःसवनमभवत्तद्गायत्री स्वमायतनमकुरुत तस्मात्तत्समृद्धतमं मन्यंते सर्वॆषां सवनानामग्रियो मुख्यो भवति श्रेष्ठतामश्नुते य एवं वेदाथ यत्सव्येन पदा समगृभ्वात्तन्माध्यंदिनं सवनमभवत्तद्विस्रंसत तद्विस्त्रस्तं नान्वप्पोत्तूर्वं सवनं ते देवाः प्राजिज्ञासंत तस्मिंस्त्रिष्टुभं छंदसामदधुरिंद्रं देवतानां तेन तत्समावद्वीर्यमभवत्तूर्वेण सवनेनोभाभ्यां सवनाभ्यां समावद्वीर्याभ्यां समावज्जामिभ्यां राध्योति य एवं वेदाथ यन्मुखेन समगृभ्वात्तृतीयसवनमभवत् (*sā yaddhakṣiṇena padā samagṛbhvāttatmā taḥsavanamabhavattadgāyatrī svamāyatanamakuruta tasmāttatsamṛddhatamaṃ manyaṃte sarvèṣāṃ savanānāmagriyo mukhyo bhavati śreṣṭhatāmaśnute ya evaṃ vedātha yatsavyena padā samagṛbhvāttanmādhyaṃdinaṃ savanamabhavattadvisraṃsata tadvistrastaṃ nānvappottūrvaṃ savanaṃ te devāḥ prājijñāsaṃta tasmiṃstriṣṭubhaṃ chaṃdasāmadadhuriṃdraṃ devatānāṃ tena tatsamāvadvīryamabhavattūrveṇa savanenobhābhyāṃ savanābhyāṃ samāvadvīryābhyāṃ samāvajjāmibhyāṃ rādhyoti ya evaṃ vedātha yanmukhena samagṛbhvāttṛtīyasavanamabhavat*) (I. Citra. 13-26)

**NOTE**

While bringing the soma plants, the śyena bird carried them gripped in both its feet and in its beak. The soma (or soma plant) that the bird seized with its right foot and brought became the morning pressing. Gāyatrī made that, the morning pressing, her own abode. Therefore, among all the pressings, the morning pressing is held by the ritualists to be the best of all. In that morning-pressing rite the use of mantras and the like is also special. Therefore the man who knows this well is regarded as becoming the best and the chief among those equal to him. When Gāyatrī brought the soma plant gripped in her left foot, the left foot did not have as much strength as the right, so those plants kept slipping a little from the foot from time to time. For this reason this midday pressing did not become equal to the morning pressing in strength and capacity. Seeing this, the gods deliberated and established for the metres used in the midday-pressing rite the metre Triṣṭubh and Indra, the best of the gods. Through the company of Indra, the best among the gods, and of Triṣṭubh, the metre dear to him, the midday pressing obtained a position equal to the morning pressing in strength, capacity and excellence. The man who knows this equality of the morning and midday pressings, and their strength, capacity and excellence, obtains prosperity in wealth and the like, and well-being, and lives happily. Then the portion of soma that Gāyatrī, in śyena form, bit and brought with her beak became famous as the third pressing.

### Printed p. 444

तस्य पतंती रसमधयत्तद्वीतरसं नान्वाप्पोत्पूर्वे सवने ते देवाः प्राजिज्ञासंत तत्सशुष्पपत्यंस्तद्यदाशिरमवनयंत्याज्येन पशुना चरंति तेन तत्समावद्वीर्यमभवत्पूर्वाभ्यां सवनाभ्यां सर्वैः सवनैः समावद्वी. र्यैः समावज्जा मिभी राध्योति य एवं वेद ॥ (*tasya pataṃtī rasamadhayattadvītarasaṃ nānvāppotpūrve savane te devāḥ prājijñāsaṃta tatsaśuṣpapatyaṃstadyadāśiramavanayaṃtyājyena paśunā caraṃti tena tatsamāvadvīryamabhavatpūrvābhyāṃ savanābhyāṃ sarvaiḥ savanaiḥ samāvadvī. ryaiḥ samāvajjā mibhī rādhyoti ya evaṃ veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 13-27)

While Gāyatrī (the śyena) was coming, carrying the soma plant in her beak, she drank the juice in the plant little by little, sucking it. Therefore, that is, because the soma plants brought in the beak had little juice rather than much, this third pressing did not become equal to the morning and midday pressings in strength, capacity and so on. The gods, seeing this, deliberated and found that the suitable means lay in animals. From animals one obtains milk, curds and the offering substances such as ājya (ghee) obtained from them. If milk is mixed into the soma juice, which is scanty in the plants, that juice becomes strong. If oblations and the like are made with ājya and with the limbs of the animals, the pressing rite becomes complete. Therefore those who know the sacrificial rite add milk and other āśira substances to the juice of the ṛjīṣa used at the third pressing (the husks of the soma plant that remain after the juice has been taken at the morning and midday pressings are called ṛjīṣa), and make oblations with the ājya obtained from animals and with the heart and other organs of animals; knowing that by this the third-pressing rite becomes equal to the morning and midday pressings in strength, capacity and so on, they perform it accordingly. This matter is stated in another śākhā as follows:

ब्रह्मवादिनो वदंति कस्मात्सत्याद्यायत्री कनिष्ठा छंदसाग्ं सती यज्ञमुखं षरियायेति यदेवादः सोममाहरत्तस्माद्यज्ञमुखं पर्यैत्तस्मात्तेजस्वीनीतमा पद्भ्यां द्वे सवने समगृह्णान्मुखेनैकं यन्मुखेन समगृह्णात्तदधयत्तस्माद्वे सवने शुक्रवती प्रातःसवनं च माध्यंदिनं च तस्मात्तृतियसवन ऋजीषमभिषुण्वंति धीतनिव हि मन्यंते आशिरमवनयति सशुक्रत्वाय ॥ (*brahmavādino vadaṃti kasmātsatyādyāyatrī kaniṣṭhā chaṃdasāgṃ satī yajñamukhaṃ ṣariyāyeti yadevādaḥ somamāharattasmādyajñamukhaṃ paryaittasmāttejasvīnītamā padbhyāṃ dve savane samagṛhṇānmukhenaikaṃ yanmukhena samagṛhṇāttadadhayattasmādve savane śukravatī prātaḥsavanaṃ ca mādhyaṃdinaṃ ca tasmāttṛtiyasavana ṛjīṣamabhiṣuṇvaṃti dhītaniva hi manyaṃte āśiramavanayati saśukratvāya ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6.1.6-4)

Thus the same idea is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. The man who knows this matter, namely that the three pressings, the morning, midday and third, have obtained an equal position in strength, capacity and excellence, will enjoy happiness endowed with all prosperity.

### Printed p. 445

**The question how Indra and Vāyu obtained the first drinking of soma**

In the Ṛk अग्रं पिब मधूनां (*agraṃ piba madhūnāṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-46-1) it is said that Vāyu, before Indra and the other gods, is entitled to drink soma first. In support of this, the Ṛk

आ नायो भूष शुचिपा उप नः सहस्रं ते नियुतो विश्ववार । उपो ते अंधो मद्यमयामि यस्य देव दधिषे पूर्वपेयं ॥ (*ā nāyo bhūṣa śucipā upa naḥ sahasraṃ te niyuto viśvavāra | upo te aṃdho madyamayāmi yasya deva dadhiṣe pūrvapeyaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-92-1)

is cited, and it is pointed out there that the seer prays that Vāyu drink soma first. On how Vāyu obtained the foremost place among the gods in the drinking of soma, there is an ancient story in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. We set it out here:

देवा वै सोमस्य राज्योऽग्रपेये न समपादयन्नहं प्रथमः पिबीयमहं प्रथमः पिबीयमित्येवाकामयंत ते संपादयंतोऽब्रुवन् हंताजिमयाम स यो न उज्जॆष्यति स प्रथमः सोमस्य पाश्यतीति तथेति त आजिमयुस्तेषामाजिं यतामभिसृष्टानां वायुर्मुखं प्रथमः प्रत्यपद्यताथेंद्रोऽथ मित्रावरुणावथाश्विन् । (*devā vai somasya rājyo 'grapeye na samapādayannahaṃ prathamaḥ pibīyamahaṃ prathamaḥ pibīyamityevākāmayaṃta te saṃpādayaṃto 'bruvan haṃtājimayāma sa yo na ujjèṣyati sa prathamaḥ somasya pāśyatīti tatheti ta ājimayusteṣāmājiṃ yatāmabhisṛṣṭānāṃ vāyurmukhaṃ prathamaḥ pratyapadyatātheṃdro 'tha mitrāvaruṇāvathāśvin |*) (Ai. Brā. 9-25)

In the past all the gods together wished to drink soma, and a dispute arose as to which of them should drink first; each began to argue that he should drink first. Since the matter could not be settled in any way, they all conferred together and came to an agreement: "Let us all together arrange a contest. Whoever wins in it will be entitled to drink soma first." When all consented, the contest was fixed thus: they were to run from one place to another place far off, and whoever first reached a rock or a tree there was to be regarded as the winner. When all agreed to the pact that the winner, victorious among them, should drink soma first, all the gods began to run at the same moment. Among all the gods who were running, Vāyu reached the appointed place ahead of all. Indra came right behind Vāyu and was second. Then, behind Indra, Mitra and Varuṇa, and behind them the Aśvins, ran up and reached the appointed place. Therefore among these gods Vāyu ran ahead of all and was the winner.

सोऽवेदिंद्रो वायुमुद्वै जयतीति तमनु परापतत्सह नावथोज्जयावेति स नेत्यब्रवीदहमेवोर्ज्जेष्यामीति तृतीयं मेऽथोज्जयावेति (*so 'vediṃdro vāyumudvai jayatīti tamanu parāpatatsaha nāvathojjayāveti sa netyabravīdahamevorjjeṣyāmīti tṛtīyaṃ me 'thojjayāveti*)

### Printed p. 446

सेति हैवाब्रवीदहमेवोज्जॆष्यामीशि तुरीयं मेऽथोज्ययावेति तथेशि तं तुरीयेऽत्यार्जत शत्रुरीयभागिंद्रोऽभवत्ति भाग्वायु: (*seti haivābravīdahamevojjèṣyāmīśi turīyaṃ me 'thojyayāveti tatheśi taṃ turīye 'tyārjata śatrurīyabhāgiṃdro 'bhavatti bhāgvāyu:*)

Indra saw Vāyu running swiftly ahead of him and decided: "This Vāyu will run ahead of everyone and win. Somehow I too must run along with him and win." He used all his strength and ran close to Vāyu. Yet no sign appeared that he would leave Vāyu behind and go ahead. Then Indra said to Vāyu: "O Vāyu, the two of us are ahead of everyone. So let us regard ourselves both as having won, and let us share the first Soma-drinking between us: half for me, half for you. Thus let us work together and secure the victory." Hearing this, Vāyu said: "O Indra, I am at least a little ahead of you. So I alone will be the winner. The whole of the first Soma-drinking must come to me. I cannot give you half." Then Indra said: "Very well. Then I do not want half. Take two of the three parts, and give me only one part." Vāyu did not agree even to that, and said: "Whatever happens, I shall win. All of it will come to me; I am not willing to give you one part in three." Then Indra again entreated Vāyu: "I do not want even one part in three. Still less will do: if you give me one part in four, that is enough. Please agree to that." Vāyu said, "So be it," and agreed. Therefore in the Aindravāyava-graha (that is, when Indra and Vāyu drink Soma together) it was arranged that Indra should have one part and Vāyu three parts.

शौ सहैवेंद्रवायू उदजयतां सह मित्रावरुण् सहार्श्विनौ त विषामेशे यथोज्जितं भक्त्वा इंद्रवाय्योः प्रथमोऽत मित्रामरुणयोरथाश्विषो॥ (*śau sahaiveṃdravāyū udajayatāṃ saha mitrāvaruṇ sahārśvinau ta viṣāmeśe yathojjitaṃ bhaktvā iṃdravāyyoḥ prathamo 'ta mitrāmaruṇayorathāśviṣo‖*)
स एष इंद्रतुरियो ग्रहो गृह्यते यद्यंद्रवायवः ॥ (*sa eṣa iṃdraturiyo graho gṛhyate yadyaṃdravāyavaḥ ‖*)

In this way Indra and Vāyu, working together, won the contest and were the first to reach the appointed place. Behind them Mitra and Varuṇa came and arrived. Behind them came the Aśvin deities. Therefore, among these deities, they became entitled to the Soma-drinking in the order of the places each obtained in the contest: first Indra and Vāyu, after them Mitra and Varuṇa, after them the Aśvins. Thus the order in which the deities drink Soma together came into use. Therefore in the Aindravāyava-graha Indra has only one part in four of the Soma-drinking.

### Printed p. 447

तदेतदृषिः पश्यन्नभ्यनूनाच नियुत्वा इंद्रसारथिरिति (*tadetadṛṣiḥ paśyannabhyanūnāca niyutvā iṃdrasārathiriti*)

The seer, knowing by divine vision that Indra has one part in four in the Aindravāyava-graha, expressed this matter in the following Ṛk, that is in शतेना नो अभिष्टिभिर्नियुत्वा इंद्रसारथिः (*śatenā no abhiṣṭibhirniyutvā iṃdrasārathiḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4.46-2), by the sentence नियुत्वा इंद्रसारथिः (*niyutvā iṃdrasārathiḥ*). Here, as in the Nirukta statement नियुतो वायोः (*niyuto vāyoḥ*) (Ni. 2-28), the horses called niyuta are well known as the vehicle of the god Vāyu. Therefore the word niyutvat points to a connection with Vāyu. In the Ṛk above, the word नियुत्वान् (*niyutvān*) indicates Indra together with Vāyu. Mantras such as अधा न युं नियुतः सश्चितस्वाः (*adhā na yuṃ niyutaḥ saścitasvāḥ*) (Tai. Brā. 2-8.1-1) support this. The word इंद्रसारथिः (*iṃdrasārathiḥ*) means Indra, who is the charioteer of Vāyu. From Indra's standing in the place of Vāyu's charioteer, it is indicated that Indra has only a fourth part in the first Soma-drinking.

तस्माद्दाप्येतर्हि भरताः सत्वनां वित्तिं प्रयंति तुरिये हैव संग्रहीतारो वदंतेऽमुनैवानूकाशेन यदद इंद्रः सारथिरिव भूत्वो दजयत् ॥ (*tasmāddāpyetarhi bharatāḥ satvanāṃ vittiṃ prayaṃti turiye haiva saṃgrahītāro vadaṃte 'munaivānūkāśena yadada iṃdraḥ sārathiriva bhūtvo dajayat ‖*) (I. Bo, 9-25) **NOTE**

The matter stated above is made clear by an example from worldly practice. Warriors in battle sit in chariots, win with the help of their charioteers, and seize the wealth and the like of their enemies. When they have seized it, they give one part of that wealth, that is, one part in four, to the charioteers who helped them. This practice is current in worldly dealings. In the same way, in this contest arranged by the deities, Indra was Vāyu's charioteer and Vāyu was the winner; so a fourth part of the first Soma-drinking obtained in the contest became Indra's share. The chief point is that Indra earned his fourth part as Vāyu's charioteer.

**Indra's slaying of the Asura Varāha**

There is an account that there was an Asura named Varāha and that Indra killed him. Viṣṇu also has a part in it. The history told in the Caraka-brāhmaṇa on this matter is set out here.

विष्णुयज्ञः । स देवेभ्य आत्मानमंतरधात् । तमन्यदेवता नाविंदन्निंद्रस्ववेत् । स इंद्रमब्रवीत्को भवानिति । तमिंद्रः प्रत्यब्रवीदह (*viṣṇuyajñaḥ | sa devebhya ātmānamaṃtaradhāt | tamanyadevatā nāviṃdanniṃdrasvavet | sa iṃdramabravītko bhavāniti | tamiṃdraḥ pratyabravīdaha*)

### Printed p. 448

दुर्गाणामसुराणां च हंता भवांस्तु क इति । सोऽब्रवीदहं दुर्गादाहर्ता त्वं तु यदि दुर्गाणामसुराणां हंता ततोऽयं वराहोवाममुष एकविंश्याः पुरां पारेऽत्ममयानां वसति ततस्मिन्नसुराणां वसु वाममस्ति तमिमं जहीति ॥ तस्येंद्रस्ताः पुरो भित्वा हृदयमविध्यत् अधि तत्र यदासीत्तद्विष्णुराहरदिति । सोऽयमितिहासः ॥ (*durgāṇāmasurāṇāṃ ca haṃtā bhavāṃstu ka iti | so 'bravīdahaṃ durgādāhartā tvaṃ tu yadi durgāṇāmasurāṇāṃ haṃtā tato 'yaṃ varāhovāmamuṣa ekaviṃśyāḥ purāṃ pāre 'tmamayānāṃ vasati tatasminnasurāṇāṃ vasu vāmamasti tamimaṃ jahīti ‖ tasyeṃdrastāḥ puro bhitvā hṛdayamavidhyat adhi tatra yadāsīttadviṣṇurāharaditi | so 'yamitihāsaḥ ‖*)

The chief sense of this is as follows. Viṣṇu is the sacrifice. That Viṣṇu, in the form of the sacrifice, once left the deities and stayed in a hidden place. The other deities did not know this; only Indra knew. When Indra went to the place where Viṣṇu was, Viṣṇu asked Indra who he was. In answer Indra said: "I am the destroyer of strongholds and of Asuras. But who are you?" Viṣṇu said: "I am the one who carries off from strongholds the wealth and the like belonging to the Asuras. Who are you? What work do you do?" he asked again, and then Viṣṇu said: "If you are, as you say, the destroyer of the strongholds and the Asuras, then there is an Asura named Varāha who has carried off wealth and the like and hidden it in himself. He lives beyond twenty-one forts, in a fort firmly built of stones. The Asuras have much wealth with him. So kill that Asura." Hearing this, Indra destroyed those cities of the Asuras and pierced the heart of the Asura Varāha. Then Viṣṇu brought from there all the wealth that the Asura had. This is the chief sense of this history. The commentator says that this matter is stated in the Ṛk mentioned above and also in the Ṛk

अस्येदु मातुः सवनेषु सद्यो महः पितुं पपिवाञ्चार्वन्ना । मुषायद्विष्णुः पचतं सहीयान्विध्यद्वराहं तिरो अद्रिमस्ता (*asyedu mātuḥ savaneṣu sadyo mahaḥ pituṃ papivāñcārvannā | muṣāyadviṣṇuḥ pacataṃ sahīyānvidhyadvarāhaṃ tiro adrimastā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1.6.7-2),

and he explains the meaning by fitting the words of the present Ṛk, and of the quoted words, to the history above.

अस्येदु मातुः इत्यत्र विष्णुना हे इंद्र त्वं दुर्गाणां हंतेत्यात्मानंकथॆयसि तर्हि वाममुषं वराहमसुरं जहीत्युक्तार्थो विध्यद्वराहुं इति पादेन प्रतिपादितः ॥ (*asyedu mātuḥ ityatra viṣṇunā he iṃdra tvaṃ durgāṇāṃ haṃtetyātmānaṃkathèyasi tarhi vāmamuṣaṃ varāhamasuraṃ jahītyuktārtho vidhyadvarāhuṃ iti pādena pratipāditaḥ ‖*)

The statement made by Viṣṇu in the history above — "O Indra, you claim to be the destroyer of strongholds and of Asuras. Then kill the Asura named Varāha, who has carried off wealth and the like and hidden it in himself" — is stated in the last pāda of the Ṛk quoted above, अस्येदु मातुः (*asyedu mātuḥ*), in the words विद्यद्वराहं शिरो अद्रिमस्ता (*vidyadvarāhaṃ śiro adrimastā*).

### Printed p. 449

इंद्रेण च विष्णो त्वं दुर्गादाहर्तेति ब्रूषे मया पुराणि जितान्यसुरश्च घातितस्तस्य वामं वस्वानयेत्युक्तो विष्णुमूर्तिस्तस्य वराहासुरस्य धनं मुमोष । सोऽर्थं मुषायुद्विष्णुः पचतं सहीयान् इति पादेन सूचितं ॥ (*iṃdreṇa ca viṣṇo tvaṃ durgādāharteti brūṣe mayā purāṇi jitānyasuraśca ghātitastasya vāmaṃ vasvānayetyukto viṣṇumūrtistasya varāhāsurasya dhanaṃ mumoṣa | so 'rthaṃ muṣāyudviṣṇuḥ pacataṃ sahīyān iti pādena sūcitaṃ ‖*)

And Indra said to Viṣṇu: "O Viṣṇu, you claimed to be the one who brings the wealth and the like of the Asuras from their strongholds. Now I have conquered many enemy cities and killed the Asura. Bring the wealth that is with that Asura." Viṣṇu agreed to this and carried off and brought the wealth that was with the Asura Varāha. This account is made plain by the pāda of the quoted Ṛk, मुषायुद्विष्णुः पचतं सहीयान् (*muṣāyudviṣṇuḥ pacataṃ sahīyān*).

स किं पुनर्मुषितवानिति तदत्रोच्यते । विश्वेत्ता इति । हे इंद्र त्वेषितस्त्वया प्रेरितो विष्णुर्यज्ञरूपी । त्वेषितस्त्वं दुर्गादाहार्ता किल तर्हि त्वं तस्य धनान्याहरेति त्वया प्रेरितः सन्नुरुक्रमो भूत्वा विश्वेत्ता यानि च तत्र स्थितानि तानि सर्वाण्याभरत् । अभरत् । कानि तानीति । शतं महिषानपरिमितान् प्रशस्तान् पदार्थान् तेषां वाहनरूपान् महिषान्वा क्षीरपाक मोदनं च पक्वमात्रमेवौदनं चाभरत् ॥ (*sa kiṃ punarmuṣitavāniti tadatrocyate | viśvettā iti | he iṃdra tveṣitastvayā prerito viṣṇuryajñarūpī | tveṣitastvaṃ durgādāhārtā kila tarhi tvaṃ tasya dhanānyāhareti tvayā preritaḥ sannurukramo bhūtvā viśvettā yāni ca tatra sthitāni tāni sarvāṇyābharat | abharat | kāni tānīti | śataṃ mahiṣānaparimitān praśastān padārthān teṣāṃ vāhanarūpān mahiṣānvā kṣīrapāka modanaṃ ca pakvamātramevaudanaṃ cābharat ‖*)

It has been said that Viṣṇu again carried off many more things. The details of this are set out fully in the present Ṛk, विश्वेत्ता (*viśvettā*). O Indra, you said to Viṣṇu, who is the sacrifice: "O Viṣṇu, you claimed to be the one who carries off wealth and the like from the strongholds of the Asuras. Then bring the wealth and the like that is with this Asura Varāha." As soon as he was urged by you (Indra), Viṣṇu agreed, "So be it," went quickly to the city of the Asura, and carried off and brought all the wealth and the like that was with the Asura, that is, whatever things he had been told to bring. What were those things that Viṣṇu brought? The most excellent and countless things such as wealth, the buffaloes and other animals that carry them, and cooked foods such as rice boiled in milk: all of these he carried off and brought, as Indra had said. This detail is clearly indicated in the present Ṛk.

विध्यद्वराहं इत्यत्रोक्तोऽर्थश्च चरमपादेनोच्यते । इंद्रस्तु वराहारं स्वीकृतासुरसर्वस्वं वराहरूपिणं वैमुषमेमुषनामानमथवैमुषं धनानामामोषकं वराहमसुरं हृदयेऽविध्यदिति शेषः ॥ (*vidhyadvarāhaṃ ityatrokto 'rthaśca caramapādenocyate | iṃdrastu varāhāraṃ svīkṛtāsurasarvasvaṃ varāharūpiṇaṃ vaimuṣamemuṣanāmānamathavaimuṣaṃ dhanānāmāmoṣakaṃ varāhamasuraṃ hṛdaye 'vidhyaditi śeṣaḥ ‖*)

### Printed p. 450

Now he explains the meaning of the last pāda of the present Ṛk, विध्यद्वराहमिंद्र एमुषं (*vidhyadvarāhamiṃdra emuṣaṃ*). This Asura named Varāha, being in the form of a varāha (boar), had carried off and kept much wealth from many. So it is customary to call him एमुषं (*emuṣaṃ*), that is धनानामामोषकं (*dhanānāmāmoṣakaṃ*), "the one who carries off wealth." Indra, with his own power and might, pierced the chest of such an Asura, Ēmuṣa in the form of a boar, and killed him. This is the sense set out in the last pāda of the present Ṛk.

The account of this matter is given in the same way in the Taittirīya-saṃhitā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda:

यज्ञो देवेभ्यो निलायत विष्णू रूपं कृत्वा स पृथिवीं प्राविशत्तं देवा हस्तान्त्सग्ं रभ्यैच्छन्तमिंद्र उपर्युपर्यत्य क्रामत्सोऽब्रवीत्कोमायमुपर्युपर्यत्यक्रमादित्यहं दुर्गे हंतेत्यथ कस्य मित्यहं दुर्गादाहर्तेति सोऽब्रवीद्दुर्गे वै हंतावोचथावरादोऽयं नाममोषः सप्तानां गिरीणां परस्ताद्वित्तं वेद्यमसुराणां बिभर्ति तं जहि यदि दुर्गे हंतासीति सदर्भपुंजीलमुदृह्य सप्तगिरीन् भित्वा तमहन्सोऽब्रवीद्दुर्गाद्वा आहर्ता वोचथा एतमाहरेति तमेभ्यो यज्ञ एव यज्ञमाहरदत्तद्वित्तं वेध्यमसुराणामविदंत तदेकं वेद्यै वेदित्वं ॥ (*yajño devebhyo nilāyata viṣṇū rūpaṃ kṛtvā sa pṛthivīṃ prāviśattaṃ devā hastāntsagṃ rabhyaicchantamiṃdra uparyuparyatya krāmatso 'bravītkomāyamuparyuparyatyakramādityahaṃ durge haṃtetyatha kasya mityahaṃ durgādāharteti so 'bravīddurge vai haṃtāvocathāvarādo 'yaṃ nāmamoṣaḥ saptānāṃ girīṇāṃ parastādvittaṃ vedyamasurāṇāṃ bibharti taṃ jahi yadi durge haṃtāsīti sadarbhapuṃjīlamudṛhya saptagirīn bhitvā tamahanso 'bravīddurgādvā āhartā vocathā etamāhareti tamebhyo yajña eva yajñamāharadattadvittaṃ vedhyamasurāṇāmavidaṃta tadekaṃ vedyai veditvaṃ ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-4,23)

A history is told in the Yajurveda to explain how the sacrificial altar came to be called vedi.

In former times, for some reason, the sacrifice took the form of Viṣṇu, left the deities and went away. Then that Viṣṇu, in the form of the sacrifice, entered the earth and hid himself so that no one knew. The deities, not seeing him, held one another's hands and searched everywhere, but did not find the place where Viṣṇu was. Then Indra was passing over the region where Viṣṇu was hidden, and Viṣṇu below said: "Who is it that passes over this place where I am?" Hearing this, Indra asked: "I am the hero who strikes and destroys the strongholds of the Asuras. But who are you?" To this Viṣṇu replied: "I am the one who brings the wealth and the like that is there, after the strongholds and so on of the Asuras are destroyed." And addressing Indra, he said: "O man, if you are, as you claim, the destroyer of enemy cities,

### Printed p. 451

then from here, beyond seven mountains, there is an Asura named Varāha. He has carried off the wealth and the like of the Asuras and keeps it inside his strong fort. If you have, as you claim, the power to destroy the strongholds of the Asuras, strike and destroy that Asura Varāha. Only then will your power be known." Hearing this, Indra took a bunch of darbha grass that was near, made it his weapon, split the seven impenetrable mountains, and struck and killed the Asura Varāha. Then he said to Viṣṇu: "O man, as you said, I have split the seven mountains and killed the Asura who was there. By this my strength and capacity have become clear. You said that you are the one who brings the wealth and the like from the strongholds of the Asuras destroyed before. Now, as you claimed, bring the wealth and the things that are there; then your power will be manifest." Viṣṇu said, "So be it," and in the very form of the sacrifice carried off the wealth and the things that were with that Asura and brought them near the deities. Because in this way the deities obtained the Asuras' wealth through the sacrifice, the place where the sacrifice is performed came to be named vedi. This is the chief sense of this history.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मनीषिण इति दशर्चं द्वादशं सूक्तं वैरूपस्याष्ट्रादंष्ट्रस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । तथा चानुक्रम्यते । मनीषिणो दशाष्ट्रादंष्ट्र इति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that the sūkta मनीषिणः (*manīṣiṇaḥ*) is a twelfth sūkta of ten Ṛks. Its seer is Aṣṭrādaṃṣṭra of the Vairūpa lineage, its deity is Indra, and its metre is Triṣṭubh. He cites the Anukramaṇī: मनीषिणो दशाष्ट्रादंष्ट्र इति (*manīṣiṇo daśāṣṭrādaṃṣṭra iti*). The viniyoga has already been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta मनीषिणः (*manīṣiṇaḥ*) is the twelfth sūkta in the ninth anuvāka. It has ten Ṛks. Its seer is Aṣṭrādaṃṣṭra of the lineage of the sage Virūpa; the deity is Indra; the metre is Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says मनीषिणो दशाष्ट्रादंष्ट्रः (*manīṣiṇo daśāṣṭrādaṃṣṭraḥ*). The viniyoga has already been stated.

Sūkta 111. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 9; Sūkta 111. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 6; Vargas 10, 11. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Seer: Aṣṭādaṃṣṭra. Deity: Indra. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मनी॑षिणः॒ प्र भ॑रध्वं मनी॒षां यथा॑यथा म॒तयः॒ संति॑  ॒
> नृणां ।

### Printed p. 452

> इंद्रं सत्यैरेरयामा कृतेभिः स हि वीरो गिर्वणस्युर्विदानः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मनीषिणः । प्र । भरध्वं । मनीषां । यथायथा । मतयः । संति । नृणां ।  
> इंद्रं । सत्यैः । आ । ईरयाम । कृतेभिः । सः । हि । वीरः । गिर्वणस्युः । विदानः ॥१॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मनीषिणः स्तोतारः मनीषां मनस ईशित्रीं स्तुतिमिंद्राय प्र भरध्वं ।
> कुरुत । नृणां कर्मनेतृणां युष्माकं यथायथा मतयः संति भवंति तथा
> बुद्ध्यनुसारेण स्तुतिं कुरुध्वं । वयं च कृतेभिः कृतैः सत्यैर्यथार्थभूतैः
> स्तोत्रैरिंद्रमेरयाम । यज्ञं प्रत्यागमयाम ॥ ईर गत् । ण्यंतस्य लोट् ॥
> हि यतो विदानो जानानः समर्थः स इंद्रो गिर्वणस्युः गीर्भिर्वनंति संभजंत
> इति गीर्वणसः स्तोतारः ॥ वनतेरसुनि रूपं । उपपदस्य दीर्घाभावश्चांदसः ।
> तदंतात्क्यप् । क्याच्छंदसीत्युप्रत्ययः ॥ स्तोत्कन्यामयमानः खलु । अतस्तमभिष्टुत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O wise worshippers, offer to Indra the मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*), praise that governs the mind. As the thoughts of you, the leaders of the rite, are, so make your praise, according to your understanding. We too, with true, genuine hymns that have been made, shall bring Indra (एरयाम (*erayāma*)) to the sacrifice. Since he is knowing (विदानः (*vidānaḥ*)), that is, capable, that Indra is गिर्वणस्युः (*girvaṇasyuḥ*): worshippers serve him with songs. Sāyaṇa adds that the stem takes the suffix kyap and the u-suffix after it. Because he desires praise, they praise him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मनीषिणः (*manīṣiṇaḥ*)—O wise worshippers
- नृणां (*nṛṇāṃ*)—to you, the leaders of the rite
- यथायथा (*yathāyathā*)—in whatever manner
- मतयः (*matayaḥ*)—powers of intellect
- संति (*saṃti*)—are; accordingly
- मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)—praise addressed to Indra
- प्र भरध्वं (*pra bharadhvaṃ*)—procure
- वीरः सः (*vīraḥ saḥ*)—that heroic Indra
- हि (*hi*)—by whose power
- विदानः (*vidānaḥ*)—knowing our wishes and capable of supplying them
- गिर्वणस्युः (*girvaṇasyuḥ*)—since he desires the praises of worshippers
- सत्यैः (*satyaiḥ*)—true
- कृतेभिः (*kṛtebhiḥ*)—by your praises
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- एरयाम (*erayāma*)—let us urge on, to come to the sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wise worshippers, leaders of the rite, make praise addressed to Indra in whatever manner your intellectual powers permit. The heroic Indra, by his power knowing our wishes and capable of supplying them, desires the praises of the worshippers; therefore let us urge Indra to come to the sacrifice with your true praises.

### Printed p. 453

##### English translation
Offer, worshipper, to Indra praise agreeable to the thoughts of men ; let us incite Indra hither with sincere adoration, for he, the hero, capable (of granting our wishes, is) desirous of laudation.
#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋ॒तस्य॒ हि सद॑सो धी॒तिरद्यौ॒त्सं गा॑र्ष्टे॒यो वृ॑ष॒भो गोभि॑रानट् ।  
> उद॑तिष्ठत्तवि॒षेणा॒ रवे॑ण म॒हांति॑ चि॒त्सं वि॑व्याचा॒ रजां॑सि ॥२॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऋतस्य । हि । सदसः । धीतिः । अद्यात् । सं । गार्ष्टेयः । वृषभः । गोभिः । आनट् ।  
> उत् । अतिष्ठत् । तविषेण । रवेण । महांति । चित् । सं । विव्याच । रजांसि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋतस्योदकस्य सदसः स्थानस्यांतरिक्षस्य धीतिर्धारकः स इंद्रोऽद्यात् ।
> द्योतते । प्रकाशते । हि प्रसिद्धौ ॥ द्युत दीप्तौ । लुज' द्युद्भो लुजीति परस्मैपदं । चेर्लुक् छांदसः । हलंतलक्षणा वृद्धिरिसि ॥ यद्वा! अद्यात् । तादृश इंद्रो
> यज्ञमभिगच्छति ॥ द्यु अभिगमे आदादिकः । लज् । उतो वृद्धिर्लुकि हलीति वृद्धिः ॥
> गार्ष्टेयः । सकृत्पसूता धेनुर्गृष्टिः । तस्या अपत्यं वृषभो गोभिः समानट् ।
> संव्याप्नोति । तथैषोऽपि सर्वं स्वमहिम्मा व्याप्नोति । तथा तविषेण । महन्नामैतत् । महता रवेण शब्देनोदतिष्ठत् । उच्च्रित उन्नतोऽभवत् । अत एव महांति
> चिन्महांत्यपि रजांस्युदकानि भुवनानि वा सं विव्याच । संव्याप्नोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sustainer (धीतिः (*dhītiḥ*)) of the water's abode, the atmosphere, that Indra shines (अद्यात् (*adyāt*)); हि (*hi*) marks something well known. Alternatively, अद्यात् (*adyāt*) means that such an Indra approaches the sacrifice. गार्ष्टेयः (*gārṣṭeyaḥ*): a cow that has calved once is गृष्टिः (*gṛṣṭiḥ*); her offspring is the bull, which pervades (आनट् (*ānaṭ*)) with the cows. So Indra too pervades all by his own greatness. तविषेण (*taviṣeṇa*) is a name for "great": with a great roar he rose up, became exalted. Hence he pervades (सं विव्याच (*saṃ vivyāca*)) even the great रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*), waters or worlds.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of water
- सदसः (*sadasaḥ*)—of the atmosphere, its abode
- धीतिः (*dhītiḥ*)—Indra, the sustainer
- अद्यात् (*adyāt*)—shines
- गार्षेयः (*gārṣeyaḥ*)—born of a cow
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—the bull

### Printed p. 454
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with the cows
- समानट् (*samānaṭ*)—as one who joins them and shines, displaying his power; (Indra likewise)
- तविषेण (*taviṣeṇa*)—with exceeding
- रवेण (*raveṇa*)—roar
- उदतिष्लत् (*udatiṣlat*)—manifested himself
- महांति चित् (*mahāṃti cit*)—exceedingly great
- रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*)—worlds
- सं विव्याच (*saṃ vivyāca*)—has pervaded

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the sustainer of the atmosphere, the abode of water, shines. As a bull, born as the first calf of a cow, shines among the cows displaying his power, so Indra too, manifesting himself with an exceeding roar, has pervaded all the exceedingly great worlds.

##### English translation
Sustainer of the abode of the water, (the firmament), he shone brightly; the bull, the offspring of a cow which has only borne once, met the cows, with a loud roar he sprang up, he pervaded the vast worlds.
#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः॒ किल॒ श्रुत्या॑ अ॒स्य वे॑द॒ सहि जि॒ष्णुः प॑थि॒कृत्सूर्या॑य ।  
> आन्मेनां॑ कृ॒ण्वन्न च्यु॑तो॒ भुव॒द्दोः पति॑र्दि॒वः स॑न॒जा अप्र॑तीतः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । किल । श्रुत्यै । अस्य । वेद । सः । हि । जिष्णुः । पथिकृत् । सूर्याय ।  
> आत् । मेनां । कृण्वन् । अच्युतः । भुवत् । गोः । पतिः । दिवः । सनजाः । अप्रतिइतः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्यास्मदीयस्य स्तोत्रस्य श्रुत्यै श्रवणायेंद्रः किलेंद्र एव वेद । जानाति ।
> स हि स एव जिष्णु ! शत्रुणां जयशीलः सूर्याय पथिकृन्मार्गकर्ता भवति । किंचाच्युतः शत्रुभिरगंतव्यो वृषणश्वस्य मेनामात्मानं कृण्वन् कुर्वन् इंद्र आत् ।
> आगच्छत्यस्मदीयं यज्ञं ! मेनाभवो वृषणश्वस्य सुक्रतो ! य. १-५१-१३ । इति
> मंत्रांतरं ॥ अस गतिदीप्त्यादानेषु भौवादिकः । ............ ॥ दिवो द्युलोकस्य च
> पतिर्भुवत् । अभूत् ॥ भवतेर्लॆट् । वाक्यभेदादनिघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra alone knows how to hear (श्रुत्यै (*śrutyai*)) this hymn of ours. He, victorious over enemies, is the maker of a path (पथिकृत् (*pathikṛt*)) for the sun. Moreover, unshakable (अच्युतः (*acyutaḥ*)), not to be approached by enemies, making himself (मेनां (*menāṃ*)) the Mena of Vṛṣaṇaśva, Indra comes (आत् (*āt*)) to our sacrifice. Sāyaṇa cites another mantra: मेनाभवो वृषणश्वस्य सुक्रतो (*menābhavo vṛṣaṇaśvasya sukrato*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-51-13). He is also lord of heaven (दिवः (*divaḥ*)) and became (भुवत् (*bhuvat*)) so.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्य (*asya*)—our praises
- श्रुत्यै (*śrutyai*)—capable of hearing
- इंद्रः किल (*iṃdraḥ kila*)—Indra himself
- वेद (*veda*)—knows our wishes
- जिष्णुः (*jiṣṇuḥ*)—victorious
- स हि (*sa hi*)—he
- सूर्याय (*sūryāya*)—for the sun's movement
- पथिकृत् (*pathikṛt*)—has built a path
- अच्युतः (*acyutaḥ*)—the imperishable Indra
- मेनां (*menāṃ*)—Mena
- कृण्वन् (*kṛṇvan*)—making his own
- आत् (*āt*)—comes to the sacrifice
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of heaven
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—lord
- गोः (*goḥ*)—lord of cattle
- सनजाः (*sanajāḥ*)—eternal
- अप्रतीतः (*apratītaḥ*)—unassailed
- भुवत् (*bhuvat*)—becomes

### Printed p. 455
