##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who is able to hear our praises, knows our wishes. He, the victorious, has built a path for the sun's movement. The imperishable Indra, making Mena his own, comes to the sacrifice. He is lord of cattle, lord of heaven, eternal and unassailed.

##### English translation
On hearing our praise Indra knows our wishes; victorious, he opens a path for the sun ; making himself Mena, he came (to the sacrifice), he was unassailable, the lord of cattle, (the lord) of heaven, eternal, unsurpassed.
#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रो॑ म॒ह्ना म॑ह॒तो अ॑र्ण॒वस्य॑ व्र॒तामि॑ना॒दंगि॑रोभिर्ग्णा॒नः ।  
> पु॒रूणि॑ चि॒न्नि त॑ताना॒ रजां॑सि द॒धार॒ यो ध॒रुणं॑ स॒त्यता॑ता॥४॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । मह्ना । महतः । अर्णवस्य । व्रता । अमिनात् । अंगिरभिः । गृणान ।  
> पुरूणि । चित् । नि । ततान । रजांसि । दाधार । यः । धरुणं । सत्यताता ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 456

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रोऽंगिरोभिर्यषिभिर्गृणानः स्तूयमानः सन् महतोऽर्णवस्य ॥
> अर्णसः सलोपश्च । का. ५-२-१०९-३ । इति वप्रत्ययः ॥ उदकवतो मेघस्य व्रता
> व्रतानि कर्माणि मह्ना स्वमहिम्मॆनाविनात् । अहिंसीत् ॥ मीज् हिंसायां । लजि
> मीनातेर्निगम इति ह्रस्वः ॥ ततः पुरूणि चिद्बहुन्येव रजांस्युदकानि नि ततान ।
> नीचीनान्यकरोत् । य इंद्रः सत्यताता सत्यैर्देवैस्तते । यद्वा । सत्यशब्दादपि
> स्वार्थिकस्तातिल् द्रष्टव्यः । सत्ये । द्युलोके धरुणं धारकं बलं दाधार आधारयत्॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, praised by the Aṅgirases, has by his own greatness injured (अमिनात् (*amināt*)) the functions (व्रता (*vratā*)), the works, of the great अर्णवस्य (*arṇavasya*), the water-bearing cloud. Then he made many रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*), waters, spread downward (नि ततान (*ni tatāna*)): he who is सत्यताता (*satyatātā*), extended by the true gods. Alternatively, the affix tāti is to be seen as added to the word सत्य (*satya*) without change of sense; in the true heaven he upheld (दाधार (*dādhāra*)) the supporting (धरुणं (*dharuṇaṃ*)) strength.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अंगिरभिः (*aṃgirabhiḥ*)—by the Aṅgirases
- गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)—praised
- महतः (*mahataḥ*)—great
- अर्णवस्य (*arṇavasya*)—of the cloud
- व्रता (*vratā*)—functions
- मह्ना (*mahnā*)—by his own greatness
- अमिनात् (*amināt*)—has injured
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- सत्यताता (*satyatātā*)—in the true heaven
- धरुणं (*dharuṇaṃ*)—his world-supporting power
- दाधार (*dādhāra*)—has upheld; that Indra
- पुरूणि चित् (*purūṇi cit*)—abundant
- रजांसि (*rajāṃsi*)—waters
- नि ततान (*ni tatāna*)—has poured down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, praised by the Aṅgirases, has by his own greatness injured the functions of the great clouds. The Indra who has upheld his world-supporting power in the true heaven has poured down abundant waters.

##### English translation
Praised by the Angirasas, Indra has by his might injured the functions of the mighty cloud; he has sent down abundant rains, he who (at other times) has supported the supporting (cloud) in heaven.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रो॑ दि॒वः प्र॑ति॒मानं॑ पृथि॒व्या पिश्वा॑ वेद॒ सव॑ना॒ हंति॒ शुष्णं॑।  
> म॒हीं चि॒द्ध्यामात॑नो॒त्सूर्ये॑ण चा॒स्कंभ॑ चि॒त्कंभ॑नेन॒  ॑
> स्तभीयान् ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 457

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । दिवः । प्रतिमानं । पृथिव्याः । विश्वा । वेद । सवना । हंति । शुष्णं ।  
> महीं । चित् । द्यां । आ । अतनोत् । सूर्येण । चास्कंभ । चित् । स्कंभनेन ।  
> स्कभीयान् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दिवो द्युलोकस्य पृथिव्याश्च प्रतिमानं महत्त्वेन प्रतिनिधिरिंद्रो विश्वा
> सर्वाणि सवना सवनानि वेद । सोमपानार्थं जानाति । शुष्णं सर्वस्य शोषकमेतन्नामानमसुरं हंति ॥ वाक्यभेदादनिघातः ॥ अपि च महीं चिन्महतीमपि द्यां
> सूर्येणातनोत् । सर्वत्र प्रकाशयुक्तामकरोत् । स्कभीयान् स्कंभयित्यणां
> मध्यॆ श्रेष्ठः स स्कंभनेन चिन्निरोधनसाधनेन सामर्थ्येनैव चास्कंभ । द्युलोकमवरुद्धमकरोत् ॥ स्कंभिः सौत्रो धातुः । लटि तुजादीनामिति दीर्घः । चित्कंभनेनेत्यत्र संहितायां सलोपः । उत्पूर्वस्य स्कंभेरुदः स्थास्त्रंभोः । पा. ८-४-६१ ।
> इति सलोप उक्तः । चित्तूर्वस्य स्कंभेरपि भवति च्छंदोविषयत्वात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, the counterpart (प्रतिमानं (*pratimānaṃ*)) of heaven and earth in greatness, knows all (विश्वा (*viśvā*)) सवना (*savanā*), the soma-pressings, for the drinking of soma. He slays the asura named Śuṣṇa, the desiccator of all. Moreover, he spread even the great heaven (महीं चित् द्यां (*mahīṃ cit dyāṃ*)) with the sun, making it full of light everywhere. स्कभीयान् (*skabhīyān*), the best of proppers, propped (चास्कंभ (*cāskaṃbha*)) heaven with prop (स्कंभनेन (*skaṃbhanena*)), a means of restraint, namely his power, and held heaven fast.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of heaven
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of earth
- प्रतिमानं (*pratimānaṃ*)—the counterpart
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- सवना (*savanā*)—sacrificial rites
- वेद (*veda*)—has known
- शुष्णं (*śuṣṇaṃ*)—the desiccating Śuṣṇa asuras
- हंति (*haṃti*)—has slain
- महीं चित् (*mahīṃ cit*)—great
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—heaven
- सूर्येण (*sūryeṇa*)—with the help of the sun
- आतनोत् (*ātanot*)—made extended
- स्कभियान् (*skabhiyān*)—Indra, the best of those who give support
- स्कंभनेन चित् (*skaṃbhanena cit*)—by his power fit to support all
- चास्कंभ (*cāskaṃbha*)—became the support of heaven

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the counterpart of heaven and earth, has known all sacrificial rites. He has slain the desiccating Śuṣṇa asuras. He made the great heaven extended with the help of the sun. Indra, best in giving support, became the support of heaven by his power fit to support all.

##### English translation
Indra, the counterpart of heaven and earth, is cognizant of all sacrifices he is the slayer of Shushna; he spread out the spacious heaven with the sun (to light it up); best of proppers, he propped up (the heaven) with a prop.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वज्रे॑ण॒ हि वृ॑त्र॒हा वृ॒त्रमस्त॒रदे॑वस्य॒ शूशु॑वानस्य मा॒याः ।  
> विधृ॑ष्णो॒ अत्र॑ दृष॒ता जं॑घं॒थाथा॑भवो मघवन्ना॒ह्वो॑जाः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वज्रेण । हि । वृत्रहा । वृत्रं । अस्तः । आदेवस्य । शूशुवानस्य । मायाः ।  
> वि । धृष्टो इति । अत्र । धृषता । जघंथ । अथ । अभवः । मघवन् । बाहुओजाः ॥६॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वृत्रहा वृत्रस्य हंता वज्रेण वृत्रमस्तः । अस्त्रणाः । अवधीः ॥
> स्त्वणातेर्लज' बहुलं !छंदसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । सिपि गुणः । हियोगादनिघातः ॥
> अनंतरं हे धृष्णो धर्षणशील त्वमदेवस्याद्योतमानस्य शूशुवानस्य स्वबलेन
> वर्धमानस्य तस्य माया धृषता समर्थेन वज्रेणात्रास्मिन्काल एव वि जघंथ ।
> विनाशितवानसि ॥ हंतेर्लिटि थल्यभ्यासाच्चेति कुत्वं ॥ अथ हे मघवन्मनवन्निंद्र
> बाह्वोजा भुजबलवानभवः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, you have struck down Vṛtra with the thunderbolt." Next, "O bold one, who are of daring nature, you have destroyed at this very time the deceits of that godless (अदेवस्य (*adevasya*), non-shining) Vṛtra, who grows by his own strength (शूशुवानस्य (*śūśuvānasya*)), with the capable thunderbolt." Then, "O Maghavan, possessor of wealth, Indra, you became strong-armed."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—you, the slayer of enemies (O Indra)
- वज्रेण (*vajreṇa*)—with the thunderbolt
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—Vṛtra the Asura
- अस्तः (*astaḥ*)—have slain
- धृष्टो (*dhṛṣṭo*)—you, the assailant of enemies
- अदेवस्य (*adevasya*)—of the one who is not a worshipper of the gods
- शूशुवानस्य (*śūśuvānasya*)—and who was growing by his own strength, of that Vṛtra
- मायाः (*māyāḥ*)—the deceitful powers
- धृषता (*dhṛṣatā*)—with the powerful thunderbolt
- वि जघंथ (*vi jaghaṃtha*)—have destroyed
- अथ (*atha*)—thereafter
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O Indra, possessor of wealth
- बाह्वोजाः (*bāhvojāḥ*)—possessed of exceedingly great strength of arm
- अभवः (*abhavaḥ*)—have become

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you, the slayer of enemies, have slain Vṛtra the Asura with the thunderbolt. You, the assailant of enemies, have destroyed with your powerful thunderbolt the deceitful powers of that Asura, who is not a worshipper of the gods and who was growing by his own strength. Thereafter, O wealthy Indra, you became possessed of exceedingly great strength of arm.

### Printed p. 459

##### English translation
The slayer of Vritra, you have laid him low with the thunderbolt ; resolute Indra, you have now overcome by your powerful (bolt), the devices of the impious (Asura). confiding in his own strength ; you, Maghavan, wast strong-armed.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सचं॑त॒ यदु॒षसः॒ सूर्ये॑ण चि॒त्राम॑स्य के॒तवो॒ राम॑विंदन् ।  
> आ यन्नक्ष॑त्रं॒ ददृ॑शे दि॒वो न पुन॑र्य॒तो नकि॑र॒द्धा नु वे॑द ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सचंत । यत् । उषसः । सूर्येण । चित्रां । अस्य । केतवः । रां । अविंदन् ।  
> आ । यत् । नक्षत्रं । वदृशे । दिवः । न । पुनः । यतः । नकिः । अद्या । नु । वेद ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्यदोषस उषःकालाः सूर्येण सूर्यात्मकेनेंद्रेण सचंत संगच्छंते ॥ सच समवाये भौवादिकः ॥ तदानीमस्य स्वभूताः केतवः सर्वस्य प्रज्ञापका
> रश्मयश्चित्रां नानावर्णां रां रायं श्रियमविंदन् । अलभंत । पुनरुदयानंतरं
> यद्यदा दिवो नक्षत्रं न ददृशे न दृश्यते ॥ दृशेः कर्मणि लिट् । यद्योगादनिघातः ॥ तदानीं यतः ॥ इणः शत्रंतस्य शसि शतुरनुनो नद्यजादी इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥ सर्वत्र गच्छतोऽस्य रश्मीन्नकिर्न कश्चिन्नु वेद । जानाति । एतदद्धा सत्यमेव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the dawns (the times of dawn) unite with the sun, that is, with Indra in the form of the sun, then his own rays (केतवः (*ketavaḥ*), the makers of knowledge of all things) obtain variegated, many-coloured splendour (रां (*rāṃ*), wealth). Again, after the rising, when the star of heaven is not seen, then no one knows these rays of his as he goes everywhere. This is indeed true (अद्धा (*addhā*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—the parts of the goddess Uṣas
- सूर्येण (*sūryeṇa*)—with the sun

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heaven
- नक्षत्रं (*nakṣatraṃ*)—the star
- न ददृशे (*na dadṛśe*)—is not seen, then

### Printed p. 460

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

At the time of sunrise, when the parts of the goddess Uṣas unite with the sun, the sun's rays obtain the wealth of beauty of many colours. After the rising, when the star of heaven is not seen, no one can know the rays of this sun, which moves everywhere. This is true.

##### English translation
When the dawns are associated with the sun, his rays acquire wonderful beauty ; but when the constellation of heaven is not seen, no one really knows (his rays) as he moves.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दू॒रं किल॑ प्रथ॒मा ज॑ग्मुरासा॒मिंद्र॑स्य॒ याः प्र॑स॒वे स॒सुरापः॑ ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आसामपां मध्ये प्रथमाः प्रथमगामिन्यस्ता आपो दूरं किल जग्मुः ।
> दूरमेव गताः । या अप इंद्रस्य प्रसवे प्रेरणे ॥ षू प्रेरणे । जवसन् चेति
> वक्तव्यं । पा. ३-३-५६-४ । इत्यबपवादेऽच् । थाथघञ्काजबित्रकाणामितुक्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं ॥ तस्याज्ञायां सस्रुः । सरंति । गच्छंति खलु । अथ प्रत्यक्षकृतः ।
> हे आपः आसां युष्माकमग्रं क्व स्वित् । कुत्र वर्तते । बुध्नो मूलं च क्व । तथा
> वो युष्माकं मध्यं च क्व नूनमिदानीं युष्माकमंतोऽवसानं च क्व । सर्वगतश्वादनिर्ज्ञायमानगमना आसन्नित्यर्थः ॥ क्व । किंशद्वात् सप्तम्यर्थे किमोऽदित्यप्रत्ययः । क्वातीति क्वादेशः । तित्स्वरितः । अंतः । अमेर्गत्यर्थस्यासिहसीत्यादिना
> तत्पत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Among these waters, those that go first went very far indeed: the waters that flow at Indra's impulsion (प्रसवे (*prasave*), in sending). He derives प्रसवे (*prasave*) from the root षू (*ṣū*) in the sense of impelling, and says सस्रुः (*sasruḥ*) means they flow, they go. Then, addressing them as if before his eyes: "O waters, where is your front? Where is your root (बुध्नः (*budhnaḥ*))? Where is your middle? Where now is your end?" The meaning is that, being all-pervading, their going was not known. He also remarks on क्व (*kva*) (the ending in the sense of the locative) and on अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*).

- सस्रुः (*sasruḥ*)—flow
- आसां (*āsāṃ*)—among those streams of water
- प्रथमाः (*prathamāḥ*)—the first streams
- दूरं किल (*dūraṃ kila*)—very far
- जग्मुः (*jagmuḥ*)—go
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—O waters
- आसां (*āsāṃ*)—your
- अग्रं (*agraṃ*)—beginning
- क्व स्वित् (*kva svit*)—where is it
- बुध्नः (*budhnaḥ*)—root
- क्व (*kva*)—where
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- मध्यं (*madhyaṃ*)—middle part
- क्व (*kva*)—where
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—end
- क्व (*kva*)—where is it

### Printed p. 461

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Of the streams of water that flow at Indra's impulsion, the first streams go very far. O waters, what is your beginning, what your root? What is your middle? What is your end?

##### English translation
The first of those waters, which issued forth at Indra's sending, went very far. Where, waters, is your beginning, where your root, where is your centre, where indeed is your termination ?

> मुमु॑क्षमाणा उ॒त या मु॑मु॒च्रेऽधेदे॒ता न र॑मंते॒  ॑

> मुमुक्षमाणाः । उते । याः । मुमुच्रॆ । अध । इत् । एताः । न । रमंते । नितिक्ताः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अहिनाहंतव्येन वृत्रेण मेघेन वा जग्रसानान् ॥ ग्रस अदने ।
> अनुदात्तेत् । छंदसि लिटः कानच् ॥ ग्रस्ताः सिंधून् स्यंदमाना अपः सृजः । असृजः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, you have released the streams (सिंधून् (*siṃdhūn*)), the flowing waters, that had been swallowed (जग्रसानान् (*jagrasānān*), from the root ग्रस (*grasa*) in the sense of eating) by Ahi, that is, by Vṛtra who was to be slain, or by the cloud."

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(continued in the next block)

### Printed p. 462

> निरगमयः । आदित् । इदवधारणे ! अनंतरमेवैता आपो जवेन वेगेन प्र विविज्रे ।
> सर्वत्रात्यंतं चलिता बभूवुः ॥ ओविजी भयचलनयोः । उदात्तेत् । लिटीरयो
> रे । पा. ६-४-७६ । इतीरयो रेआदेशः ॥ उतापि च मुमुक्षमाणा इंद्रेण
> मोचयितुमिष्यमाणा या आपो मुमुचे इंद्रेण मोचिता अभूवन् ॥ मुचे
> कर्मणि लिट् ॥ अधेदनंतरमेव नितिक्ता नितरां शुद्धा आपो न रमंते । एकत्र न
> क्रीडंते । किंतु सर्वत्र गमनशीला इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

आदित् (*ādit*): इत् (*it*) is in the sense of restriction; immediately afterwards these waters rushed forth with speed, becoming greatly agitated everywhere (from the root ओविजी (*ovijī*) in the sense of fear and moving). Further, the waters that desired to be released by Indra were released by Indra (मुमुच्रॆ (*mumucrè*), perfect passive of *muclṛ*). Immediately afterwards, नितिक्ताः (*nitiktāḥ*), the thoroughly pure waters, do not delight (न रमंते (*na ramaṃte*)) in one place: they do not sport in one place, but are given to going everywhere.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अहिना (*ahinā*)—by Vṛtra in the form of a cloud (O Indra)
- जग्रसानान् (*jagrasānān*)—swallowed
- सिंधून् (*siṃdhūn*)—the streams of water
- सृजः (*sṛjaḥ*)—you have released
- आदित् (*ādit*)—immediately upon that
- एताः (*etāḥ*)—these waters
- जवेन (*javena*)—with speed
- प्र विविज्रे (*pra vivijre*)—have rushed forward and flowed
- उत (*uta*)—and
- मुमुक्षमाणाः (*mumukṣamāṇāḥ*)—possessed of the desire to be released by Indra
- याः (*yāḥ*)—which waters
- मुमुच्रॆ (*mumucrè*)—were released from the Asura
- अधेत् (*adhet*)—right after that
- नितिक्ताः (*nitiktāḥ*)—the thoroughly pure waters
- न रमंते (*na ramaṃte*)—do not sport in one place (they flow everywhere)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you have released the streams of water swallowed by Vṛtra in the form of a cloud. Immediately upon that, these waters have rushed forward and flowed with speed. The waters, possessed of the desire to be released by Indra, that were released from the Asura, being thoroughly pure, do not stay in one place but flow everywhere.

##### English translation
Yon have set at liberty the streams which had been swallowed by Ahi ; they rushed forth with rapidity ; the waters which longed to be liberated were set free, and now the pure (streams) never stop.

> कामयमानाः स्त्रियः स्वपतिमभिगच्छंति तद्वत् । जारः शत्रूणां जारयिता पूर्भिदिंद्रः सॆनाच्चिरादेवासामपामारितः प्रेरकत्वेन स्वामी भवति । हे इंद्र अस्मे
> अस्माकं स्वभूतानि पार्थिवा पार्थिवानि वसूनि धनवस्त्रीणयित्यणि हवींषि पूर्विर्बह्व्यः सून्यता वाचः स्तुतिलक्षणाश्च ते त्वदीयमस्तं गृहमा जग्मुः । आगच्छंतु ।
> यद्वा! अस्मदीयाः स्तुतयस्ते गृहं गच्छंतु । अस्माकं गृहं त्वदीयानि पार्थिवानि
> धनान्यभिगच्छंतु ॥ गमेश्वंदसि सार्वकालिको लिट् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सध्रीचीः (*sadhrīcīḥ*) (the form is explained by the substitution of सध्रि (*sadhri*) for सह (*saha*) and by the addition of the affix जीप् (*jīp*)): the waters, going together, came to the ocean (सिंधुं (*siṃdhuṃ*)), their lord. The illustration: as women who are full of desire go to their own husband, so do they. जारः (*jāraḥ*) is the destroyer of enemies; Indra, the breaker of cities (पूभित् (*pūbhit*)), has from long ago (सनात् (*sanāt*)) been lord of these waters as their impeller (आरितः (*āritaḥ*)). "O Indra, our earthly (पार्थिवा (*pārthivā*)) possessions (वसूनि (*vasūni*)), the oblations, and many true words (सूनृताः (*sūnṛtāḥ*)) in the form of praise, let them come to your house (अस्तं (*astaṃ*))." Or else: let our praises go to your house; and let your earthly riches come to our house. जग्मुः (*jagmuḥ*) is the perfect used in the sense of all times in the Veda.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उशतीरिव (*uśatīriva*)—as women who long for union with their husband go to their husband and join him
- सध्रीचीः (*sadhrīcīḥ*)—the rivers that flow joined together
- सिंधुं (*siṃdhuṃ*)—the ocean
- आयन् (*āyan*)—go and join
- जारः (*jāraḥ*)—the destroyer of enemies
- पूर्वित् (*pūrvit*)—and the splitter of enemy cities, Indra
- सनात् (*sanāt*)—from long ago
- आसां (*āsāṃ*)—of these waters
- आरितः (*āritaḥ*)—has been the lord, the impeller
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अस्मे (*asme*)—our
- पार्थिवा (*pārthivā*)—earth-born
- वसूनि (*vasūni*)—riches in the form of oblations
- पूर्विः (*pūrviḥ*)—abundant
- सूनृताः (*sūnṛtāḥ*)—praises
- ते (*te*)—your
- अस्तं (*astaṃ*)—house
- आजग्मुः (*ājagmuḥ*)—let them go and reach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As women who long for union with their husband go to their husband and join him, the rivers, flowing joined together, go and join the ocean. Indra, the destroyer of enemies and the splitter of enemy cities, has from long ago been the lord and impeller of these waters. O Indra, let our earth-born riches in the form of oblations, and our abundant praises, go and reach your house (go to you).

##### English translation
They hasten associated together to the ocean, like loving wives (to a husband); (Indra), the witherer of foes, the demolisher of cities, is their

## Sūkta 112 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्र पिबेति दशर्चं त्रयोदशं सूक्तं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं नभःप्रभेदनो
> नाम विरूपगोत्र ऋषिः । तथा चानुक्रम्यते । इंद्र पिब नभःप्रभेदेन इति ॥
> गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning इंद्र पिब (*iṃdra piba*) has ten Ṛks (the thirteenth sūkta), is in the Triṣṭubh metre, and is addressed to Indra. Its seer is Nabhaḥprabhedana, of the Virūpa gotra. The Anukramaṇī says: इंद्र पिब नभःप्रभेदेन इति (*iṃdra piba nabhaḥprabhedena iti*). The viniyoga (ritual use) has already been stated.

The Kannada Anuvāda says: This sūkta, Indra pibā, is the thirteenth sūkta in the ninth anuvāka and has ten Ṛks. Its seer is Nabhaḥprabhedana of the Virūpa gotra; the deity is Indra; the metre is Triṣṭup. The Anukramaṇī says "Indra piba nabhaḥprabhedanaḥ". The viniyoga was stated earlier.

Maṇḍala 10, Anuvāka 9, Sūkta 112. Aṣṭaka 8, Adhyāya 6, Vargas 12, 13. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Seer: Nabhaḥprabhedana Vairūpa. Deity: Indra. Metre: Triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हर्ष॑स्व॒ हंत॑वे शूर॒ शत्रू॑नु॒क्छेभि॑ष्टे वी॒र्या॒३॒॑३प्र ब्र॑वाम ॥१॥

> हर्षस्व । हंतवे । शूर । शत्रून् । उक्षेभिः । ते । वीर्या । प्र । ब्रवाम ॥ १ ॥

> हे इंद्र त्वं प्रतिकामं ये ये कामास्तांस्तान्नृति ॥ अव्ययीभावसमासः ।
> तस्य स्वरः ॥ यथेच्छं सुतस्याभिषुतस्य यो भागस्तुभ्यं दातव्यस्तं पिब ॥ आमंत्रित.

> सोमस्तव हि । तृतीयार्थे षष्ठि । त्वयैव पूर्वपीतिः प्रथमत एव पातव्यः ।
> यद्वा । प्रातःसावः । सप्तम्याः सुः । प्रातःसवने तनैव प्रथमपानं खलु । ऐंद्रवायवग्रहे ह्यादित एवेंद्रः पिबति ॥ तत्पुरुषे दासीभारादित्वात्तूर्वपदांतोदात्तत्वं । यद्वा। बहुव्रीहिः ॥ ततो हे शूर समर्थ त्वं शत्रोन्हंतवे हंतुं हर्षस्व ।
> हृष्टो भव । अथ ते त्वदीयानि वीर्या वृत्रहननादिलक्षणानि वीर्याणुक्थॆभिरुक्थैः
> शस्त्रैः प्र ब्रवाम । प्रकर्षण वदाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, drink, at will, the share of the pressed Soma that is to be given to you." प्रतिकामं (*pratikāmaṃ*) is an avyayībhāva compound meaning "each desire, whatever the desires". The Soma pressed at the morning pressing is yours; the genitive तव (*tava*) is used in the sense of the instrumental, so it is to be drunk first, by you alone (पूर्वपीतिः (*pūrvapītiḥ*)). Alternatively प्रातःसावः (*prātaḥsāvaḥ*) has the locative ending dropped: at the morning pressing yours is the first drinking, for in the Aindravāyava graha Indra drinks first. Then, "O hero, capable one, rejoice to slay your foes, be glad. And we shall proclaim your heroic deeds, such as the slaying of Vṛtra, with the uktha-hymns, the recitations (śastras)."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- प्रतिकामं (*pratikāmaṃ*)—as much as you desire
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—of the pressed Soma
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- प्रातःसावः (*prātaḥsāvaḥ*)—the Soma pressed at the morning pressing
- तव हि (*tava hi*)—by you indeed
- पूर्वपीतिः (*pūrvapītiḥ*)—to be drunk first
- शूर (*śūra*)—O capable Indra
- शत्रून् (*śatrūn*)—foes
- हंतवे (*haṃtave*)—to slay
- हर्षस्व (*harṣasva*)—be encouraged
- ते (*te*)—your
- वीर्या (*vīryā*)—heroic deeds
- उक्षेभिः (*ukṣebhiḥ*)—with the śastra-mantras
- प्र ब्रवाम (*pra bravāma*)—we praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, drink as much as you wish of the Soma pressed here. The Soma pressed at the morning pressing is to be drunk first by you. O capable Indra, take the encouragement fit for slaying foes. We praise your heroic deeds with the śastra-mantras.

##### English translation
Drink, Indra, at will of the effused libation, for it is poured out at the morning sacrifice, and is first drunk by you; exult, hero, in slaying your foes, we will glorify your heroic exploits with hymns.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र मनसोऽपि जवीयानतिशयेन गंता ते त्वदीयो यो रथोऽस्ति
> तेन रथेन सोमपेयायास्मदीयं सोमं पातुमा याहि । आगच्छ ॥ पा पाने ।
> भावेऽचो यत् । ईद्यतीतीत्वं । अर्धधातुकलक्षणो गुणः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ तथा ते त्वदीया हरयो रथे संयुक्ता अश्वास्तूयं क्षिप्रमाभिमुख्येन
> प्र द्रवंतु । प्रगच्छंतु । वृषभिः सेक्तृभिर्यॆभिर्यैरश्वैर्मंदमानो नोदमानः
> सन् यासि गच्छसि । हरी इंद्रस्येति वचनादिंद्रस्य द्वानेवाश्वाविति न चोदनीयं आ
> त्वा सहस्रमा शतमित्यादिनिगमांतरे दर्शनात् । ऋ. ८-१-२४ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, come with that chariot of yours, swifter even than the mind, to drink our Soma." May your horses (हरयः (*harayaḥ*)) yoked to the chariot run swiftly towards us, the vigorous (showering) steeds with which you come rejoicing. Because the text says "the two bays of Indra", one need not object that Indra has only two horses, since other passages show otherwise: *ā tvā sahasramā śataṃ* etc. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-1-24).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- मनसः (*manasaḥ*)—than the mind
- जवीयान् (*javīyān*)—swifter
- ते (*te*)—your
- यः रथः (*yaḥ rathaḥ*)—the chariot which is
- तेन (*tena*)—with it
- सोमपेयाय (*somapeyāya*)—for drinking Soma
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—deign to come
- वृषभिः (*vṛṣabhiḥ*)—powerful
- येभिः (*yebhiḥ*)—with which steeds
- मंदमानः (*maṃdamānaḥ*)—rejoicing
- यासि (*yāsi*)—you come
- ते हरयः (*te harayaḥ*)—your horses
- तूयं (*tūyaṃ*)—swiftly
- आ प्र द्रवंतु (*ā pra dravaṃtu*)—let them run hither

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, with your chariot that is swifter than the mind, deign to come for the drinking of Soma. May those powerful horses of yours, with which you come rejoicing, run hither swiftly.

##### English translation
Come, Indra, to the Soma-drinking with your chariot, which is swifter than thought; let you bays, the vigorous steeds with which you go along rejoicing quickly, hasten hither.

> हरि॑त्वता॒ वर्च॑सा॒ सूर्य॑स्य॒ श्रेष्ठै॑ रू॒पैस्त॒न्वं॑ स्पर्शयस्व ।  
> अ॒स्माभि॑रिंद्र॒ सखि॑भिर्हुवा॒नः स॑ध्रीची॒नो मा॑दयस्वा नि॒षद्य॑ ॥

> सूर्यस्यॆ वर्चसा तेजसा तत्सदृशैः श्रेष्ठैः प्रशस्य तम्मिरात्मीयै रूपैस्तन्वमात्मीयं

> निषण्णो भूत्वा मादयस्व । सोमपानेन हृष्टो भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, with the golden-hued radiance (हरित्वता (*haritvatā*)) of the sun, and with excellent forms like it, make your body touch (be adorned)." Alternatively *tanūḥ* is the sacrifice (from तायत (*tāyata*)): make it radiant. Further, सध्रीचीनः (*sadhrīcīnaḥ*): being accompanied by the Maruts, invoked by us who are your friends, sit down in the sacrifice and be exhilarated; be glad with the drinking of Soma.**NOTE**

- स्पर्शयस्व (*sparśayasva*)—adorn
- सखिभिः (*sakhibhiḥ*)—your friends
- अस्माभिः (*asmābhiḥ*)—by us
- हुवानः (*huvānaḥ*)—one who is called
- सध्रीचीनः (*sadhrīcīnaḥ*)—you, who are joined with the Maruts
- निषद्य (*niṣadya*)—sitting in the sacrifice
- मादयस्व (*mādayasva*)—rejoice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, adorn your body with excellent forms equal to the golden radiance of the sun. Called by us, your friends, and accompanied by the Maruts, sit in the sacrifice and rejoice.

### Printed p. 468

Decorate your person with most beautiful forms with the golden radiance of the sun; invoked by us your friends, Indra, sit down and be exhilarated, accompanied by the Maruts.

> दीयं यज्ञसदनमा याहि । आगच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, these two great ones, heaven and earth, do not separate (नाविविक्तां (*nāviviktāṃ*)) the greatness of you, which arose in the exhilarations produced by Soma-drinking, but remain within your greatness." With your most dear bay horses yoked to the chariot, come towards the pleasing food, namely Soma, to our sacrificial dwelling (तदोकः (*tadokaḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यस्य ते (*yasya te*)—of you, produced by Soma-drinking

- त्यत् महिमानं (*tyat mahimānaṃ*)—that famous greatness
- मही (*mahī*)—of great nature
- इमे रोदसी (*ime rodasī*)—these heaven and earth
- न अविविक्तां (*na aviviktāṃ*)—do not separate

- युक्तैः (*yuktaiḥ*)—yoked to the chariot
- प्रियेभिः (*priyebhiḥ*)—dear to you
- हरिभिः (*haribhiḥ*)—with horses
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—gladdening
- अन्नं अच्छ (*annaṃ accha*)—towards our oblation in the form of Soma
- तदोकः (*tadokaḥ*)—to our sacrificial house
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—deign to come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the great heaven and earth do not separate the famous greatness you manifested in the exhilaration arising from your Soma-drinking. With your beloved horses yoked to the chariot, deign to come to our sacrificial house, towards our gladdening oblation of Soma.

##### English translation
You whose greatness (manifested) in your exhilarations the vast heaven and earth, do not seperate; come, Indra, with your beloved bay horses harnessed to your chariot, come to our dwelling to (partake of) the (sacri-ficial) food that is agreeable to you.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, having drunk (पपिवान् (*papivān*)) the Soma, you have slain for whichever sacrificer the foes, continually, with a weapon fit for battle (रण्या (*raṇyā*)), one that needs no repetition (अननुकृत्या (*ananukṛtyā*)), able to kill the foe with a single blow."

### Printed p. 470

> निघाते लित्स्वरः ॥ स यष्टा ते त्वदर्थं तविषीं महतीं पुरंधिं बह्वीं स्तुतिमियर्ति । प्रेरयति ॥ ऋ गतौ जौहोत्यादिकः । अर्तिपिपर्त्योरित्यभ्यासस्यॆत्वं । अभ्यासस्यासवर्ण इतीयज् ॥ हे इंद्र सुतोऽभिषुतः स सोमस्ते मदाय समर्थो
> भवति । यद्वा । स यष्टा सुतः सोमः । सुब्व्यत्ययः । अभिषुतं सोमं त्वन्मदाय
> प्रेरयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues the previous verse. The sacrificer who has been aided in destroying his enemies offers to Indra a mighty, abundant hymn of praise: इयर्ति (*iyarti*) means "he sends forth" (root ऋ (*ṛ*) in the sense of going, of the Hautyādika class). Addressing Indra, he adds that the pressed Soma is capable of bringing Indra exhilaration. Alternatively, the sacrificer is himself the pressed Soma (by a change in the case-ending), and sends forth the pressed Soma for Indra's exhilaration.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- पपिवान् (*papivān*)—you who have drunk Soma
- अनानुकृत्या (*anānukṛtyā*)—by the weapon free of imitation (incomparable)
- रण्या (*raṇyā*)—with the weapon
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which sacrificer
- शत्रुन् (*śatrun*)—the enemies
- शश्वत् (*śaśvat*)—many times
- चकर्थ (*cakartha*)—you have destroyed
- सः (*saḥ*)—that sacrificer
- ते (*te*)—addressing you
- तविषीं (*taviṣīṃ*)—powerful
- पुरंधिं (*puraṃdhiṃ*)—the hymn of praise
- इयर्ति (*iyarti*)—offers
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—pressed
- सः सोमः (*saḥ somaḥ*)—that very Soma, offered by the sacrificer
- ते (*te*)—your
- मदाय (*madāya*)—is for delight

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who have drunk Soma, the sacrificer whose enemies you have destroyed many times with your incomparable weapon offers to you a powerful hymn of praise. O Indra, the Soma that has been pressed and offered by that same sacrificer is for your delight.

##### English translation
That Soma, drinking constantly of which, Indra, you have destroyed the enemies (of the worshipper) with an inimitable weapon,—that Soma prompts your powerful, abundant (laudation), it is effused, Indra, for your exhilaration.

### Printed p. 471

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इदं । ते । पात्रं । सनवित्तं । इंद्र । पिब । सोमं । एना । शतक्रतो इति शतक्रतो।  
> पूर्णः । आहावः । मदिरस्य । मध्यः । यं । विश्वे । इत् । अभिहर्यंति । देवाः॥६॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते त्ववर्धं पात्रं चमसादिकं सनवित्तं । अस्माभिश्शिरादेव लब्धं ॥
> विद्ल लाभे ! कर्मणि निष्ठा ॥ हे शतक्रतो बहुकर्मन्निंद्रॆनैतेन पात्रेण सोमं
> पिब । यतो मदिरस्य मदकरस्य मध्यो मधुनः सोमस्याहावः पानस्थानीयपात्रविशेषः पूर्णः पूरितोऽभूत् ॥ ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां । निपानमाहावः । पा. ३-३-
> ७४ । इति निपातितः । स्तुतिभिराहूयमाना देवा अत्र सोमं पिबंतीति । थाथादिस्वरः ॥
> यमिद्यमाहावमेव विश्वे सर्वॆ देवा अभिहर्यंति । अभिकामयंते ॥ हर्य
> गतिकांत्योः भौवादिकः । यद्योगात्तिजो निघाताभावे तिजि चोदात्तवतीति
> गतेर्निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, your vessel, the cup (चमस (*camasa*)) and the like, has been obtained by us long ago." O Shatakratu (of many deeds), drink Soma from this vessel, for the आहावः (*āhāvaḥ*), the special vessel serving as drinking-place of the sweet, intoxicating Soma, is full. आहावः (*āhāvaḥ*) is derived from the root ह्वेञ् (*hveñ*) (to call) and is irregularly formed by (Pā. Sū. 3-3-74 **NOTE**); the gods, invoked by hymns, drink Soma here. All the gods desire this very आहावः (*āhāvaḥ*) (root हर्य (*harya*), in the sense of going and desiring, Bhauvādika).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—for you
- पात्रं (*pātraṃ*)—the cup-vessel
- सनवित्तं (*sanavittaṃ*)—has been obtained long ago
- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O Indra, performer of many deeds
- एना (*enā*)—with this vessel
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- मदिरस्य (*madirasya*)—intoxicating
- मध्यः (*madhyaḥ*)—of the Soma
- आहावः (*āhāvaḥ*)—the vessel
- पूर्णः (*pūrṇaḥ*)—is full
- यं इत् (*yaṃ it*)—that very vessel filled with Soma
- विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*)—all the gods
- अभिहर्यंति (*abhiharyaṃti*)—desire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the cup-vessel has been obtained for you long ago. O Indra, performer of many deeds, drink Soma from this vessel. The vessel of the intoxicating Soma is filled with Soma juice. All the gods desire that very Soma-filled vessel.

##### English translation
This your cup, Indra, has been long since provided by us, drink the Soma from it, Shatakratu; the goblet is full of the sweet Soma-juice, which all the gods desire.

> वि हि त्वामिं॑द्र पुरु॒धा जना॑सो हि॒तप्र॑यसो वृषभ॒  ॑
> ह्वयंते ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । हि । त्वां । इंद्रः । पुरुधा । जनासः । हितप्रयसः । वृषभ । ह्वयंते ।  
> अस्माकं । ते । मधुमत्त्कतमानि । इमा । भुवन् । सवना । तेषु । हर्य॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वृषभ कामानां वर्षक हितप्रयसः । प्रय इत्यन्न नाम प्रीणनकारित्वात् । संभृतहनिष्का जनासो जनाः पुरुधा बहुधा । हिरवधारणे । त्वामेव वि
> ह्वयंते । विविधमाह्वयंति ॥ हैञ् स्पर्धायां । निसमुपविभ्यो ह्व इत्यात्मनेपदं ॥ अस्माकं स्वभूतानीमेमानि सवना सवनानि ते त्वदर्थं मधुमत्तमान्यतिशयेन सोमवंति भुवन् । अभवन् । तस्मात्त्वं तेषु सवनेषु हर्य । सोमान्कामयस्व ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, showerer of desires, people holding acceptable sacrificial food (प्रय (*praya*) is a name for food, because it gratifies) invoke you in many ways, you alone (हि (*hi*) is emphatic); the root is ह्वेञ् (*hveñ*), and the middle voice follows from the rule on ह्व (*hva*) with ni, sam, upa, vi. These sacrifices (सवना (*savanā*)) of ours have become exceedingly rich in Soma for you; therefore, take pleasure in (desire the Soma at) those sacrifices.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)—bestower of desires
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- हितप्रयसः (*hitaprayasaḥ*)—provided with beneficial oblation
- जनासः (*janāsaḥ*)—people
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- पुरुधा (*purudhā*)—in many ways
- विह्वयंते (*vihvayaṃte*)—invoke
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—offered by us
- इमं सवना (*imaṃ savanā*)—these sacrifices
- ते (*te*)—for you
- मधुमत्तमानि (*madhumattamāni*)—the sweet Soma
- भुवन् (*bhuvan*)—prepare
- तेषु (*teṣu*)—in those sacrifices
- हर्य (*harya*)—desire the Soma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, bestower of desires, people provided with beneficial oblation invoke you in many ways. These sacrifices offered by us present sweet Soma to you. Desire the Soma in those sacrifices.

##### English translation

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र त॑ इंद्र पू॒र्व्याणि॒ प्र नू॒नं वी॒र्या॑ वोचं प्रथ॒मा  ॒॑
> कृतानि ।  
> स॒ती॒नम॑न्युरश्रथायो॒ अद्रिं॑ सुवेद॒नाम॑कृणो॒ ब्रह्म॑णे॒  
> गां ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । ते । इंद्र । पूर्व्याणि । प्र । नूनं । वीर्या । वोचं । प्रथमा । कृतानि ।  
> सतीनमन्युः । अश्रथयः । अद्रिं । सुवेदनां । अकृणोः । ब्रह्मणे । गां ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते त्वदीयानि प्रथमादितः कृतानि पूर्व्याणि पुरातनानि च वीर्या
> वीर्याणि नूनमिदानीं प्र वोचं । प्रकर्षण वदामि । एकः प्रशब्दः पूरणः ॥
> वोचं । लुजि ब्रुवो वचिः । क्लेरज् ॥ कानि तानि । सतीनमन्युः । सतीनमित्युदकनाम । उदकाभिवर्षणबुद्धियुक्तस्त्वमिंद्रं मेघमश्रथयः । वज्रेणाहिंसीः ।
> ब्रह्मणे बृहस्पतये गां पणिभिरपहृतां सुवेदनां सुष्टु ज्ञापनीयामकृणोः ।
> अकरोरित्यादीनि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, I now proclaim your ancient exploits, done first of all (प्र (*pra*) is merely a filler; वोचं (*vocaṃ*) is an aorist of *brū* with the substitute वचि (*vaci*)). Which ones? सतीनमन्युः (*satīnamanyuḥ*): सतीन (*satīna*) is a name for water; you, intent on sending down water, अश्रथयः (*aśrathayaḥ*) ("pierced") the cloud (अद्रि (*adri*)) with the thunderbolt. You made the cow, carried off by the Paṇis, easily recognizable (सुवेदनां (*suvedanāṃ*)) for ब्रह्मणे (*brahmaṇe*), Bṛhaspati; अकृणोः (*akṛṇoḥ*) is the same as *akaroḥ*.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- प्रथमा (*prathamā*)—principal
- पूर्व्याणि (*pūrvyāṇi*)—from most ancient times
- कृतानि (*kṛtāni*)—done
- वीर्या (*vīryā*)—heroic deeds
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—now
- प्र वोचे (*pra voce*)—I praise exceedingly
- सतीनमन्युः (*satīnamanyuḥ*)—intent on sending rain
- अद्रिं (*adriṃ*)—the cloud
- अश्रथयः (*aśrathayaḥ*)—you split with the thunderbolt
- गां (*gāṃ*)—the cows carried off by the Paṇis
- ब्रह्मणे (*brahmaṇe*)—for Bṛhaspati
- सुवेदनां (*suvedanāṃ*)—so as to be easily known
- अकृणोः (*akṛṇoḥ*)—you made

### Printed p. 474

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, I now praise exceedingly your principal and most ancient heroic deeds. Intent on sending rain, you split the cloud with your thunderbolt. You made the cows carried off by the Paṇis easy for Bṛhaspati to find.

##### English translation
I will proclaim now, Indra, your ancient first-achieved exploits; resolved to send rain, you cleft the cloud, you made the cow easily discoverable for the Brahman.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नि षु सी॑द गणपते ग॒णेषु॒ त्वामा॑हु॒र्विप्र॑तमं कवी॒नां ।  
> न ऋ॒ते त्वत्क्रि॑यते॒ किं च॒नारे म॒हाम॒र्कं म॑घवञ्चि॒त्रम॑र्च ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नि । सु । सीद । गणपते । गणेषु । त्वां । आहुः । विप्रतमं । कवीनां ।  
> न । ऋते । त्वत् । क्रियते । किं । चन । आरे । महां । अर्कं । मघवन् । चित्रं ।  
> अर्च ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे गणपते त्वं गणेषु स्तोतृगणेषु सु सुष्टु नि षीद । स्तुतिश्रवणार्थं
> निषण्णो भव । यतः कवीनां क्रांतप्रज्ञानां मध्यॆ त्वा त्वां विप्रतममतिशयेन
> मेधाविनमित्याहुः । किंच त्वदृते ॥ अन्यारादितरर्तॆ । पा. २-३-२९ । इति पंचमी ॥
> त्वां वर्जयित्वा किं चन कर्मारे दूरे समीपे वा न क्रियते । तस्मान्निषीद । ततो
> हे मघवन्छनवन्निंद्र महां महांतमर्कमर्चनीयमस्मदीयं त्रिवृत्पंचदशादिलक्षणं स्तोमं चित्रं नानारूपं कृत्वार्च । पूजय । विधेहि ॥ अर्च पूजायां
> भौवादिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O lord of the hosts (गणपते (*gaṇapate*)), sit well among the hosts of worshippers, to hear their praise; for among the wise (कवीनां (*kavīnāṃ*), those of far-reaching understanding) they call you the most sagacious. Moreover, without you no rite is done, far or near; the fifth case is by (Pā. Sū. 2-3-29). Therefore sit down. Then, O Maghavan, wealthy Indra, make our great, venerable hymn (अर्कं (*arkaṃ*)), of the Trivṛt, Pañcadaśa and similar forms, varied in many forms, and honour it. अर्च (*arca*) is of the root meaning worship, Bhauvādika.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गणपते (*gaṇapate*)—O Indra, lord of the Marut host
- गणेषु (*gaṇeṣu*)—among your worshippers
- सु नि षीद (*su ni ṣīda*)—sit in an excellent manner
- कवीनां (*kavīnāṃ*)—among the wise and discerning
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- विप्रतमं (*vipratamaṃ*)—as the most sagacious
- आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—the knowing say
- त्वदृते (*tvadṛte*)—without you
- किं चन (*kiṃ cana*)—any rite whatever
- आरे (*āre*)—whether far or near
- न क्रियते (*na kriyate*)—is not accomplished
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- महां (*mahāṃ*)—of great form
- अर्कं (*arkaṃ*)—our venerable hymn
- चित्रं (*citraṃ*)—in various forms
- अर्च (*arca*)—honour

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, lord of the Marut host, sit in an excellent manner among your worshippers. Among the wise and discerning, the knowing say that you are the most sagacious. Without you no rite is accomplished, far or near. O wealthy Indra, honour our great and venerable hymn in its various forms.

##### English translation
Lord of the companies (of the Maruts), sit down among the companies (of the worshippers), they call you the most sage of sages; without you nothing is done in the distance; have in honour, Maghavan, our great and various adoration.

### Printed p. 476

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मघवन्थनवन्निंद्र नाधमानान्॥ नाध्य नाध्य याच्छोपतापैश्वर्याशीषु
> भौवादिकः । अनुदात्तेत्॥ याचमानानोऽस्मानभिख्याभिख्यापनेन तेजसा युक्तान्
> कुरु । प्रसिद्धान्वा कुरु ! हे सखे धनदानेन हे वसुपते वसूनां स्वामिन् त्वं
> सखीनां स्तोतृत्वेन सखिभूतानामस्माकं स्वभूतानि स्तोत्राणि बोधि । बुध्यस्व ॥
> बुध अवगमने । भौवादिकः । लोटि च्छांदसः शपो लुक् । छंदस्युभयथेति
> हेरार्धधातुकत्वेनाजित्वादजितश्चेति हेर्धिभावः । अत एव गुणः । सार्वधातुकत्वेन
> जित्वादंतोदात्तत्वं । वर्णलोपश्चांदसः ॥ हे रणकृच्छतुभिः सह युद्धकर्तः
> अत एव हे सत्यशुष्म यथार्थबलोपेत त्वं रणं कृधि । कुरु । शत्रूञ्छहि ॥ करोतेर्लोटि श्रुशृणुष्यकृवृभ्यश्चंदसीति हेर्धिः ॥ किंचाभक्ते चिदसंभजनीये
> स्थानेऽप्यस्मान्राये धनाया भजा । भागिनः कुरु ॥ व्यचोतस्तिज इति संहितायां
> दीर्घः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa glosses the verse. "Maghavan" is the wealthy Indra. The root नाध (*nādha*) (nādh) is in the sense of asking, afflicting, lordship and blessing. Indra is asked to make us, who are suppliants, endowed with lustre by अभिख्या (*abhikhyā*) (making known), or to make us renowned. "O friend" is addressed through his gift of wealth; "O lord of wealth" means lord of riches. As we are his friends by being his praisers, he is asked to take notice of our hymns बोधि (*bodhi*) ("know"). "O battle-maker" means one who fights with enemies; therefore "O you of true strength", possessing real power, "make battle", that is, "slay the enemies". Further, even in a place that is not to be shared अभक्ते चित् (*abhakte cit*), he is asked to make us sharers राये (*rāye*) in wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O Indra, endowed with wealth
- नाधमानान् (*nādhamānān*)—those who are petitioning you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अभिख्या (*abhikhyā*)—make us endowed with lustre
- सखे (*sakhe*)—O Indra, our friend
- वसुपते (*vasupate*)—and lord of riches
- सखीनां (*sakhīnāṃ*)—the wishes of us, your friends
- बोधि (*bodhi*)—know
- रणकृत् (*raṇakṛt*)—O skilled in battle
- सत्यशुष्म (*satyaśuṣma*)—O you who have true power
- रणं (*raṇaṃ*)—battle
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make
- अभक्ते चित् (*abhakte cit*)—even in a place where we have no share
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- राये (*rāye*)—in wealth
- आ भज (*ā bhaja*)—make us sharers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, make us, who petition you, endowed with lustre. O Indra, our friend and lord of riches, know the wishes of us, your friends. O Indra, skilled in battle and possessed of true strength, make war. Even in a place where we have no share, make us sharers in wealth.

##### English translation
Render us, Maghavan, who are you suitors, illustrious; comprehend, friendly (Indra), who are the lord wealth, (the wishes of) your friends ; make war (for us), you warrior endowed with real strength, give us a share in the undivided riches.

## Sūkta 113 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दशमेऽनुवाके षोडश सूक्तानि । तत्र तमस्येति दशर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तमैंद्रं । शतप्रभेदनो नाम वैरूप ऋषिः । अंत्या त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टा जगत्यः । तथा
> चानुक्रांतं । तमस्य शतप्रभेदनस्त्रिष्टुबंतमिति ॥ दशरात्रस्याष्टमेऽहनि मरुत्वतीय
> एतत्तूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । तमस्य द्यावापृथिवी महा इंद्रो नृवदिति मरुत्वतीयं ।
> आ. ८-७ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the tenth anuvāka there are sixteen sūktas. Of these, the first, "tam asya", is a ten-verse hymn to Indra. Its seer is Śataprabhedana Vairūpa; the last verse is Triṣṭubh, the rest Jagatī. So the Anukramaṇī: तमस्य शतप्रभेदनस्त्रिष्टुबंतमिति (*tamasya śataprabhedanastriṣṭubaṃtamiti*). On the eighth day of the Daśarātra it is used in the Marutvatīya (śastra). It is prescribed in the sūtra तमस्य द्यावापृथिवी महा इंद्रो नृवदिति मरुत्वतीयं (*tamasya dyāvāpṛthivī mahā iṃdro nṛvaditi marutvatīyaṃ*), Ā. 8-7.

##### Anuvāda

In the tenth anuvāka of the tenth maṇḍala there are sixteen sūktas. Of them this sūkta beginning "tamasya" is the first; it has ten Ṛks. Its seer is Śataprabhedana Vairūpa; the deity is Indra; the last Ṛk is in Triṣṭubh metre, the others in Jagatī. The Anukramaṇī says "tamasya Śataprabhedanas triṣṭubantam". Its use is in the Marutvatīya śastra mantras on the eighth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, as set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, "tamasya dyāvāpṛthivī mahā indro nṛvad iti marutvatīyam" (Ā. 8-7).

Sūkta 113. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 10; Sūkta 113. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 6; Varga 14, 15. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Seer: Śataprabhedana Vairūpa. Deity: Indra. Metre: 1-9 Jagatī, 10 Triṣṭubh.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"सचेतसा (*sacetasā*)": heaven and earth, which are aware together, with all the gods, protect this Indra's शुष्मं (*śuṣmaṃ*), his strength that dries up enemies (*pā. sū. 2-4-32* is cited on the substitution after an anvādeśa). The sense: may his strength protect us first, and afterwards may these two also protect. "कृण्वानः (*kṛṇvānaḥ*)": performing the slaying of Vṛtra and the like, when he attained ऐत् (*ait*) his greatness and sufficient prowess, then, possessing ritual works, having drunk Soma, he grew. The Grammar part covers the dative sense in the genitive and the form पीत्वी (*pītvī*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- *(iṃdraḥ)*—Indra
- कृष्णानः (*kṛṣṇānaḥ*)—performing the slaying of Vṛtra and other deeds
- महिमानं (*mahimānaṃ*)—his greatness
- इंद्रियं (*iṃdriyaṃ*)—his prowess
- ऐत् (*ait*)—he obtained (then)
- सचेतसा (*sacetasā*)—united together
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth
- विश्वेभिः देवैः (*viśvebhiḥ devaiḥ*)—with all the gods
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra
- तं शुष्मं (*taṃ śuṣmaṃ*)—that famous strength
- अन्वावतां (*anvāvatāṃ*)—may they protect
- क्रतुमान् (*kratumān*)—Indra, possessed of ritual works
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—Soma
- पीत्वी (*pītvī*)—having drunk
- अवर्धत (*avardhata*)—grew

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

While Indra, accomplishing the slaying of Vṛtra and other deeds, attains his greatness and prowess, may heaven and earth, joined together with all the gods, protect this famous strength of Indra. Indra, the possessor of ritual works, drank Soma and grew.

##### English translation
May the concurring heaven and earth, together with all the gods, preserve that strength of Indra, whereby achieving (great deeds) he obtained

the greatness that is appropriate to him, and having drunk the Soma, he, eminent for his prowess, increased (in strength).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viṣṇu is so named, or "the pervading one" is the sacrifice. Impelling दधन्वान् (*dadhanvān*) the shoot, the stalk of the intoxicating sweet Soma, by his own vigour he extols वि रष्यते (*vi raṣyate*) (makes resound variously, praises) this greatness of Indra, born of that vigour. Maghavan is the wealthy one; सयावभिः (*sayāvabhiḥ*) means those who go together: with the gods, the Maruts, having slain Vṛtra, Indra became वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*), to be chosen by all, to be resorted to.

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*)—worthy of worship
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—became

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Viṣṇu presses the stalk of the sweet Soma into juice and by his lustre makes the famous greatness of Indra still greater. Indra, wealthy, who with all the gods that follow him destroyed the Asura Vṛtra, became worthy of worship.

##### English translation
Vishnu offering the portion of the Soma, glorifies by his own vigour that greatness of his. Indra, the lord of wealth, with the associated gods having slain Vritra, became deserving of honour.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

You, Indra, bearing weapons such as the thunderbolt for battle, when you came together समस्थिथाः (*samasthithāḥ*) with Vṛtra, the unslayable अहिना (*ahinā*): then, to make known your prowess in slaying Vṛtra and the rest, I praise शंसं (*śaṃsaṃ*) with hymns (śastras). Further, O fierce one, of mighty strength, at this very time all the Maruts of their own accord magnified your greatness and prowess; for the Maruts are Indra's strength. (The grammatical details of the forms are omitted.)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra of exceeding strength, when you, bearing weapons for battle, met Vṛtra who cannot be slain, I praise you to know your duty of slaying him. At this very time all the Maruts, of their own accord, increased your greatness and strength.

##### English translation
When you encountered the indestructible Vritra, wielding your weapons for combat, you acquired renown; all the associated Maruts of their own accord magnified your great might appropriate to Indra.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa takes the pāda "that Indra, just born". As soon as he was born he struck down his rivals (स्पृधः (*spṛdhaḥ*), enemies), oppressing them exceedingly. Being a hero, that is, capable, he looked to the battle and clearly saw his own manly strength, knowing "such is his might". He split the cloud, cutting it so that rain might fall. Then he sent the streaming waters downward, making them flow out. Wishing to do a good work, he propped up the vast heaven (नाकं (*nākaṃ*), the world of heaven), holding it fast. Sāyaṇa adds that स्तंभिः (*staṃbhiḥ*) is a sautra root.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- जज्ञान एव (*jajñāna eva*)—at the very moment of being born
- स्पृधः (*spṛdhaḥ*)—the enemies
- व्य बाधत (*vya bādhata*)—harmed and destroyed
- वीरः (*vīraḥ*)—Indra, the capable
- रणं (*raṇaṃ*)—the battle, setting it forward
- पौंस्यं (*pauṃsyaṃ*)—his own strength
- प्रापश्यत् (*prāpaśyat*)—perceived
- अद्रिं (*adriṃ*)—the cloud
- अवृश्चत् (*avṛścat*)—split, for the sake of rain
- सस्यदः (*sasyadaḥ*)—the flowing waters
- अव सृजत् (*ava sṛjat*)—made them flow downward
- स्वपस्यया (*svapasyayā*)—wishing to do a good work
- पृथुं (*pṛthuṃ*)—the vast
- नाकं (*nākaṃ*)—the world of heaven
- अस्तभ्नात् (*astabhnāt*)—lifted up and held

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As soon as he was born, Indra harmed and destroyed his enemies. Indra, the capable, set the battle before him and perceived his own strength. He split the cloud for the sake of rain. He made the flowing waters run downward, and, wishing to do a good work, lifted up and set firm the vast heaven.

##### English translation
As soon as born he discomfited his assailants; the hero contemplated his own manly prowess in war; he divided the cloud, sent forth the flowing waters, and with the determination to do a good deed, upheld the vast heaven.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आदिंद्रः॑ स॒त्रा तवि॑षीरपत्यत॒ वरी॑यो॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी अ॑बाधत ।  
> अवा॑भरद्धृषि॒तो वज्र॑माय॒सं शेवं॑ मि॒त्राय॒ वरु॑णाय  ॒॑
> दाशुषे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आत् । इंद्रः । सत्रा । तविषीः । अपत्यत । वरीयः । द्यावापृथिवी इति । अबाधत ।  
> अव । अभरत् । धृषितः । वज्रं । आयसं । शेवं । मित्राय । वरुणाय । दाशुषे ॥५॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आदपि च स इंद्रस्तविषीर्महतीः सेनाः सत्रा सहैवापत्यत । अगच्छत् ॥ पद गतौ
> दैवादिकः । वर्णव्यत्ययः ॥ यद्वा। पत्यत इत्यैश्वर्यकर्मा । सेनानामिष्टे । तासामीश्वरोऽभवदित्यर्थः । स एव द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यौ वरीयः ॥ तृतीयायाः
> सुः ॥ उरुतरेण महिम्माबाधत । तयोरंतस्थिताण्त्यूनवधीदित्यर्थः । धृषितः
> शत्रुवधे प्रगल्भः सन्नायसमयोमयं वज्रमवाभरत् । आधारयत् । किमर्थं ।
> मित्राय वरुणाय दाशुषे हनिर्दत्तवते यज्वने च शेवं सुखं कर्तु० ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Then too that Indra went together with the great armies (तविषीः (*taviṣīḥ*)). Alternatively, पत्यत (*patyata*) means lordship: he became the lord of the armies. He, with surpassing greatness, overcame heaven and earth, that is, he slew the enemies standing between the two. Bold in killing foes, he wielded the iron thunderbolt, made of iron. For what purpose? To bring comfort (शेवं (*śevaṃ*)) to Mitra, to Varuṇa, and to the sacrificer who has given the oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आत् (*āt*)—immediately
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- तविषीः सत्रा (*taviṣīḥ satrā*)—together with great armies
- अपत्यत (*apatyata*)—set out
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—all the enemies stationed between heaven and earth
- वरीयः (*varīyaḥ*)—by his exceedingly great strength
- अबाधतॆ (*abādhatè*)—harmed and destroyed
- धृषितः (*dhṛṣitaḥ*)—Indra of firm strength
- मित्राय (*mitrāya*)—for Mitra
- वरुणाय (*varuṇāya*)—for Varuṇa
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—for the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- शेवं (*śevaṃ*)—to produce comfort
- आयसं (*āyasaṃ*)—made of iron
- वज्रं (*vajraṃ*)—the thunderbolt weapon
- अवाभरत् (*avābharat*)—lifted and held

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As soon as the battle began, Indra set out with great armies. With his exceedingly great strength he harmed and destroyed all the enemies standing between heaven and earth. Indra, of firm strength, lifted up and held the iron thunderbolt, in order to bring comfort to the god Mitra, to Varuṇa, and to the sacrificer who offers the oblation.

### Printed p. 484

##### English translation
Indra advanced with vast (armies); he overcame with his might (his foes stationed between) heaven and earth; confident, he wielded his iron thunderbolt (to do) good to Mitra, Varuna, and the donor (of the oblation).

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॒स्यात्र॒ तवि॑षीभ्यो विर॒प्सिन॑ ऋघाय॒तो अ॑रंहयंत  ॒॑
> मन्यवे ।  
> वृ॒त्रं यदु॒ग्रो व्यवृ॑श्च॒दोज॑सा॒पो बिभ्र॑तं॒ तम॑सा॒ परी॑वृतं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रस्य । अत्र । तविषीभ्यः । विरप्सिनः । ऋघायतः । अरंहयंत । मन्यवे ।  
> वृत्रं । यत् । उग्रः । वि । अवृश्चत् । ओजसा । अपः । बिभ्रतं । तमसा । परिवृतं॥६॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्रास्मिन्काल एव विरष्यिनो महतो विविधं शब्दायमानस्य वर्धायतः शत्रुन्हिंसत इंद्रस्य तविषीभ्यः । षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी । बलानां मन्यवे प्रख्यापनायारंहयंत । आपो निरगच्छन् । रहिर्गत्यर्थः । उग्र उद्धूर्ण सोऽप उदकानि
> बिभ्रतं धारयंतं तमसा परीवृतं परितो वेष्टितं ॥ वृणोतेः कर्मणि क्तः ।
> गतिरनंतर इति स्वरः । संहितायामुपसर्गस्य घञ् । पा. ६-३-१२२ । इति दीर्घः ॥
> तं वृत्रं यद्यस्मिन्काल ओजसा स्ववीर्येण व्यवृश्चत् अत्यर्थमवधीत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At this very time, for the proclaiming of the powers (तविषीभ्यः (*taviṣībhyaḥ*), the dative standing in the sense of the genitive) of Indra, who is great, roaring in many ways, growing, and smiting his enemies, the waters flowed forth; रहि (*rahi*) has the sense of motion. Fierce Indra, when he cut Vṛtra to pieces with his own vigour, utterly slew him: Vṛtra who was holding the waters and was wrapped on all sides in darkness.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—Indra of exceedingly great strength
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- बिभ्रतं (*bibhrataṃ*)—holding
- तमसा (*tamasā*)—by pitch darkness
- परीवृतं (*parīvṛtaṃ*)—enveloped
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—Vṛtra
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—by his strength
- व्यवृश्चत् (*vyavṛścat*)—destroyed
- अत्र (*atra*)—at that time
- विरप्सनः (*virapsanaḥ*)—one who makes much noise
- ऋघायतः (*ṛghāyataḥ*)—the destroyer of enemies
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- तविषीभ्यः (*taviṣībhyaḥ*)—of the powers
- मन्यवे (*manyave*)—for the manifesting
- अरंहयंत (*araṃhayaṃta*)—the waters flowed
**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When Indra of exceedingly great strength destroyed with his strength Vṛtra, who held back the waters and was surrounded by pitch darkness, then, to proclaim the powers of Indra, who makes loud noise and destroys his enemies, the waters flowed.

##### English translation
Then (the waters) rushed forth to proclaim the might of Indra, shouting loudly, and crushing (his foes), when fierce he cut Vritra to pieces by his strength—Vritra who) obstructed the waters, and was encompassed by darkness.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> या वी॒र्या॑णि प्रथ॒मानि॒ कर्त्वा॑ महि॒त्वेभि॒र्यत॑मानौ समी॒यतुः॑ ।  
> ध्वां॒तं तमोऽव॑ दध्वसे ह॒त इंद्रो॑ म॒ह्ना पू॒र्वहू॑तावपत्यत ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> या । वीर्याणि । प्रथमानि । कर्त्वा । महित्वेभिः । यतमानौ । संईयतुः ।  
> ध्वांतं । तमः । अव । दध्वसे । हते । इंद्रः । मह्ना । पूर्वहूतौ । अपत्यत ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महित्वेभिर्मंहनीयैः स्वबलैर्यतमानौ युद्धाय प्रयत्नं कुर्वंताविंद्रवृत्तौ प्रथमानि पूर्वभावीनि कर्त्वा ॥ कृत्यार्थे त्वन्प्रत्ययः ॥ कर्तव्यानि यानि
> वीर्याणि समीयतुः संयोजयामासतुः ॥ इण् गतौ । लिटि दीर्घ इणः कितीति
> दीर्घः ॥ तयोर्मध्य इंद्रेण वृत्रे हते सति ध्वांतमतिनिबिडं तमोऽव दध्वसे ।
> अवध्वस्तं विनष्टमभूत् ॥ ध्वंसेर्लिट् । कित्वान्नलोपः ॥ इंद्रस्तु मह्णा स्वमहिम्मा पूर्वहूतौ प्रथमाह्वानेऽपत्यत । अगच्छत् । शूराणां मध्येऽयमेव
> प्रथममाहूयमानोऽभवदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra and Vṛtra, each striving for battle with his own praiseworthy powers, joined the first, that is, the preliminary, heroic deeds that were to be done. When Vṛtra was slain by Indra in the midst of these, the very thick darkness was destroyed. Indra, by his own greatness, went at the first summons (पूर्वहूतौ (*pūrvahūtau*)): among the heroes he alone was the one called first.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महित्वेभिः (*mahitvebhiḥ*)—by their prowess
- यतमानौ (*yatamānau*)—Indra and Vṛtra, who strove for battle
- प्रथमानि कर्त्वा (*prathamāni kartvā*)—to be done beforehand
- या वीर्याणि (*yā vīryāṇi*)—which heroic deeds
- समियतुः (*samiyatuḥ*)—they carried out, and among them
- हते (*hate*)—when Vṛtra was slain
- ध्वांतं तमः (*dhvāṃtaṃ tamaḥ*)—the very thick darkness
- अव दध्वसे (*ava dadhvase*)—was dispersed
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- मह्ना (*mahnā*)—by his greatness
- पूर्वहूत् (*pūrvahūt*)—being called first among the mighty
- अपत्यत (*apatyata*)—set out

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

After Indra and Vṛtra, who strove for battle with their prowess, had displayed their heroic deeds, Vṛtra was slain. Immediately the very thick darkness dispersed. Indra, by his greatness called first among the mighty, went forward.

##### English translation
(In the midst of) the first exploits to be performed by them which (Indra and Vritra) achieved striving with their utmost might, Vritra being slain, the thick darkness was destroyed, and Indra in his might came at the first challenge.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, after the slaying of Vṛtra all the gods, that is, the priests, with Soma-bearing speech (वचस्यया (*vacasyayā*), the wish to praise) increased your powers. Vṛtra the serpent, the cloud that obstructs the waters, struck down by Indra's weapon of killing, the thunderbolt, was quickly eaten as food (आवयत् (*āvayat*), "ate"; आवयति (*āvayati*) has the sense of eating): that is, people ate the food produced by the water that came from it. The illustration: just as Agni eats food with his own teeth (जंभैः (*jaṃbhaiḥ*)), so it is here.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृष्ण्यानि (*vṛṣṇyāni*)—powers
- अवर्धयन् (*avardhayan*)—increased
- जंभैः (*jaṃbhaiḥ*)—with its flames
- अग्निर्न (*agnirna*)—as Agni devours the oblations
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- हन्मना (*hanmanā*)—by the thunderbolt weapon, the instrument of killing
- रद्धं (*raddhaṃ*)—struck
- अहिं (*ahiṃ*)—the enemy
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—Vṛtra (the cloud that covered the water)
- तृषु (*tṛṣu*)—quickly
- अन्नं (*annaṃ*)—in the form of food
- आवयत् (*āvayat*)—(people) ate
**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, immediately after the slaying of Vṛtra, all the priests increased your powers with praises accompanied by Soma. As Agni devours the oblations with its flames, people ate in the form of food the enemy Vṛtra, that is, the cloud that had covered the water, struck by Indra's thunderbolt (they drank the water).

##### English translation
Then all the gods magnified your exploits with praise, accompanied with libations of Soma ; (and people) quickly devoured Vritra, the obstructer of water, wounded by Indra's slaughtering (weapon). as Agni devours food with his teeth.

> हे स्तोतारः दक्षेभिर्वर्धनहेतुभिर्यक्वभिः ॥ छंदसीवनिपावितिवनिप्रत्ययः ।
> अयस्मयादित्वेन भत्वाज्जश्वाभावः । पदत्वात्कुत्वं । का. १-४-२० ॥ मंत्रयुक्तैः
> सख्येभिः ॥ तदर्हतीत्यर्थे छंदसि चेति यत्पत्ययः ॥ सख्युरिंद्रस्य योग्यैर्वचनेभिर्वचनैः स्तोत्रैः सख्यानि स्तुत्यस्तोतृलक्षणान्यभिलक्ष्य भूरि बहुवारमिंद्रं प्र
> वोचत । प्रब्रूत । अभिष्टुत । इंद्रस्तु दभीतय एतन्नामकाय राजर्षये धुनिं
> च चुमुरिं चैतन्नामकौ द्वावसुरौ दंभयन् हिंसञ्चुद्धामनस्या ॥ मनःशब्दात्कृच् ॥ श्रद्धायुक्तया मनस इच्छया शृणुते । युष्माभिः कृतानि स्तोत्राणि
> शृणोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the praisers: "O praisers, with praises (वचनैः (*vacanaiḥ*)) that promote growth (दक्षेभिः (*dakṣebhiḥ*)), that are joined with mantras (यक्वभिः (*yakvabhiḥ*)) and that are fitting for Indra the friend (सख्येभिः (*sakhyebhiḥ*)), praise Indra many times (भूरि (*bhūri*)), keeping in view the friendship that is characterised by the relation of the praised and the praisers." Indra, for the royal seer named Dabhīti, harms the two asuras named Dhuni and Chumuri, and with a mind full of faith, that is, with desire, he hears the praises you have made.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दक्षेभिः (*dakṣebhiḥ*)—capable of promoting growth
- ऋक्वभिः (*ṛkvabhiḥ*)—joined with mantras
- सख्येभिः (*sakhyebhiḥ*)—fitting for Indra the friend
- वचनेभिः (*vacanebhiḥ*)—with praises
- सख्यानि (*sakhyāni*)—in a fitting manner
- भूरि (*bhūri*)—abundantly
- प्र वोचत (*pra vocata*)—praise Indra
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- दभीतये (*dabhītaye*)—for the royal seer Dabhīti
- धुनिं च (*dhuniṃ ca*)—the demon Dhuni
- चुमुरिं च (*cumuriṃ ca*)—and Chumuri
- दंभयन् (*daṃbhayan*)—destroying
- श्रद्धामनस्या (*śraddhāmanasyā*)—with an affectionate mind
- शृणुते (*śṛṇute*)—hears the praises of the praisers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praisers, praise Indra abundantly and in a fitting manner with praises that are joined with mantras capable of promoting Indra's growth and that are fitting for Indra the friend. Indra, destroying for the royal seer Dabhīti the demon Dhuni and Chumuri, hears the praises of the praisers with an affectionate mind.

##### English translation
Celebrate the numerous benevolent (acts of Indra) with clever affectionate praises, together with texts; Indra subduing (the Asuras) Dhuni, and

### Printed p. 489
Chumuri for (the Rishi) Dabhiti beares the praises made to him with a desire for adoration.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं पु॒रूण्या भ॑रा॒ स्वश्वा॒ येभि॒र्मंसै॑ नि॒वच॑नानि॒ शंस॑न् ।  
> सु॒गेभि॒र्विश्वा॑ दुरि॒ता त॑रेम वि॒दो षु ण॑ उर्वि॒या गा॒धम॒द्य ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । पुरूणि । आ । भर । सुअश्वा । येभिः । मंसै । निवचनानि । शंसन् ।  
> सुगेभिः । विश्वा । दुःइता । तरेम । विदो इति । सु । नः । उर्विया । गाधं । आद्य ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं स्वश्वा स्वश्वानि शोभनाश्वयुक्तानि पुरूणि बहूनि धनानि मह्यमा भर । आहर ! प्रयच्छ । निवचनानि नितरां वक्तव्यानि स्तोत्राणि शंसन्नहं येभिर्धनैर्मंसै । मन्यतिरर्चतिकर्मा । देवान्पूजयानि तानि देहि ॥ मन्यतेर्लेटि
> बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । सिप्यडागमः । सिपः पित्वेनानुदात्तत्वाद्धातुस्वरः ॥
> सुगेभिः सुष्टु गंतव्यस्मैर्धनैः स्तोत्रैर्वा विश्वा सर्वाणि दुरिता दुरितानि पापानि
> तरेम । हे इंद्र अद्यास्मिन्कर्मणि गाधं ग्रथ्यमानं क्रियमाणं नोऽस्मदीयं
> स्तोत्रमुर्वियोरुत्वेन बहुमानेन सु सुष्टु विदो । विद उ । जानीह्येव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, bring to me, that is, give, many riches (पुरूणि (*purūṇi*)) endowed with good horses (स्वश्वा (*svaśvā*)). Uttering praises that are to be spoken constantly (निवचनानि (*nivacanāni*)), I would honour the gods (मंसै (*maṃsai*); the root मन्यति (*manyati*) is a word of worship) with those riches; give them." With riches or praises that are easy to travel by (सुगेभिः (*sugebhiḥ*)), may we cross all evils (दुरिता (*duritā*)), that is, sins. "O Indra, today, in this rite, our praise (गाधं (*gādhaṃ*)), which is being composed and performed, know well (सु विदो (*su vido*)) with great regard (उर्विया (*urviyā*))." विद उ (*vida u*) is explained as जानीह्येव (*jānīhyeva*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- निवचनानि (*nivacanāni*)—excellent praises
- शंसन् (*śaṃsan*)—reciting
- येभिः (*yebhiḥ*)—with whichever riches
- मंसै (*maṃsai*)—I shall worship you
- स्वश्वा (*svaśvā*)—riches accompanied by excellent horses
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- पुरूणि (*purūṇi*)—in great abundance
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—give to me
- सुगेभिः (*sugebhiḥ*)—with those riches that are fit for a good life
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- दुरिता (*duritā*)—hardships
- तरेम (*tarema*)—may we cross over
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this time of the rite
- गाधं (*gādhaṃ*)—being composed
- नः (*naḥ*)—our praise
- उर्विया (*urviyā*)—with great regard
- सु विदो (*su vido*)—knowing, accept

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, give me abundantly those riches, endowed with excellent horses, with which I shall worship you while reciting excellent praises. With those riches that are fit for a good life, may we cross over all hardships. Knowing it, accept with great regard our praise that is composed at this time of the rite.

##### English translation
Do you, Indra, grant me ample riches and excellent horses with which I may honour (the gods) proffering praises; with well-acquired (riches) let us cross over all iniquity, accept our praise to day with the might.

## Sūkta 114 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> घर्मेति दशर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तं । सध्रिर्नाम वैरूप ऋषिः । तपसः पुत्रो
> घर्मो वा । चतुर्थी जगती । शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । घर्मा सध्रिस्तापसो वा घर्मो वैश्वदेवं चतुर्थी जगतीति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The second sūkta, beginning घर्मेति (*gharmeti*), has ten Ṛks. Its seer is Sadhri Vairūpa, or Gharma, the son of Tapas. The fourth Ṛk is in jagatī, the rest in triṣṭubh. Sāyaṇa quotes the Anukramaṇī: घर्मा सध्रिस्तापसो वा घर्मो वैश्वदेवं चतुर्थी जगतीति (*gharmā sadhristāpaso vā gharmo vaiśvadevaṃ caturthī jagatīti*). The viniyoga has already been given.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, beginning घर्मा (*gharmā*), is the second sūkta in the tenth anuvāka. It has ten Ṛks. Its seer is one named Sadhri Vairūpa, or Gharma, the son of Tapas; its deity is the Viśvedevas; the fourth Ṛk of this sūkta is in jagatī metre and the remaining Ṛks are in triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says: घर्मा सध्रिस्तापसो वा घर्मो वैश्वदेवं चतुर्थि जगती (*gharmā sadhristāpaso vā gharmo vaiśvadevaṃ caturthi jagatī*); the viniyoga was stated earlier.
**NOTE**

Particulars: Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 10; Sūkta 114. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 6; Vargas 16, 17. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Seer: Sadhri Vairūpa, or Gharma Tāpasa. Deity: the Viśvedevas. Metre: Ṛks 1–3 and 5–10 triṣṭubh; Ṛk 4 jagatī.

> जगाम ।  
> दि॒वस्पयो॒ दिधि॑षाणा अनेषन्नि॒दुर्दे॒वाः स॒हसा॑मानम॒र्कं ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> घर्मा । संअंता । त्रिवृतं । वि । आपतुः । तयोः । जुष्टिं । मातरिश्वा । जगाम ।  
> दिवः । पयः । दिधिषाणाः । अवेषन् । विदुः । देवाः । सहसामानं । अर्क० ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> समंता समंतौ संव्याप्तदिगंतौ घर्मा ॥ घर्मा
> दीप्यमानावग्न्यादित्यौ त्रिवृतं । त्रयो ना इमे त्रिवृतो नोकाः । ऐ. आ. १-१-२ ।
> इत्याम्नानात् । त्रैलोक्यं व्यापतुः । स्वतेजोभिर्व्याप्तवंतौ । मातरिश्वांतरिक्षे
> वर्तमानो वायुस्तयोरग्न्यादित्त योर्जुष्टिं प्रीतिं जगाम । गतवान् । यदा
> सहसामानं । सामशब्द उपलक्षकः । वेदत्रयतेजसहितं । सर्वं तेजः सामरूपं
> ह शश्वदित्याम्नानात् । ईदृशमर्कमर्चनीयं सूर्यं देवा दीप्यमानाः स्वरश्मयो
> विदुः विविदुः लेभिरे प्रापुः तदा दिधिषाणा लोकधारणशीलास्ते दिवो म्युलोकस्य
> संबंधि पय उदकमवेशन् । व्याप्तवंतः । ववर्षुरित्यर्थः ॥ दिवस्वय इत्यत्र
> षष्ठ्याः पतिपुत्रेऽसत्वं । दिधिषाणाः । धिष धारणे । चानश् । शपः श्लुः । यद्वा । धि
> धारणे । सनंतस्य जानश् । अज्जनगमां सनीति दीर्घाभावश्चांदसः ॥ यद्वा । समंतौ
> संगतौ घर्मौ स्वयं दीप्यमान् जीवेश्वरौ त्रिवृतं सत्त्वरजस्तमोगुणात्मिकां
> मायां व्यापतुः । नियंतृनियंतव्यभावेन मातरिश्वा परमात्मा तयोर्जुष्टिं
> संभोक्तव्यपदार्थैः संजातां प्रीतिं जगाम । गतवान् । तं परमात्मानं वेदमयमिमं सूर्यमिति देवा जानंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

समंता (*samaṃtā*) means those two whose ends reach the quarters; घर्मा (*gharmā*) means the two shining ones, Agni and Āditya. They pervaded the threefold (त्रिवृतं (*trivṛtaṃ*)), the three worlds, with their own radiance, as the tradition has it: त्रयो ना इमे त्रिवृतो नोकाः (*trayo nā ime trivṛto nokāḥ*) (Ai. Ā. 1-1-2). Mātariśvā, the wind that dwells in the atmosphere, attained (जगाम (*jagāma*)) the pleasure (जुष्टिं (*juṣṭiṃ*)) of those two. Or else: when the shining gods, that is, the rays, found, reached, the adorable sun (अर्कं (*arkaṃ*)) together with the Sāman (सहसामानं (*sahasāmānaṃ*); the word Sāman stands for the whole, so "with the radiance of the three Vedas"; the tradition says *sarvaṃ tejaḥ sāmarūpaṃ ha śaśvaditi*), then those world-sustaining ones (दिधिषाणाः (*didhiṣāṇāḥ*)) poured down (अवेषन् (*aveṣan*)) the water (पयः (*payaḥ*)) belonging to the heavenly world.
Another explanation: the two Gharmas, समंतौ (*samaṃtau*), the self-luminous individual self and the Lord, pervaded the threefold Māyā, whose nature is the three guṇas, sattva, rajas and tamas. Mātariśvā, the Supreme Self, as controller of what is to be controlled, attained the pleasure born of the objects to be enjoyed. The gods know him, the Supreme Self, as this Vedic sun.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समंता (*samaṃtā*)—those that pervade all the quarters
- घर्मा (*gharmā*)—the shining Agni and Ādityas
- त्रिवृतं (*trivṛtaṃ*)—the three worlds
- व्यापतुः (*vyāpatuḥ*)—have pervaded
- मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*)—the wind
- तयोः (*tayoḥ*)—for Agni and Āditya
- जुष्टिं (*juṣṭiṃ*)—pleasure
- जगाम (*jagāma*)—has produced

### Printed p. 492
- सहसामानं (*sahasāmānaṃ*) (when)—one endowed with radiance in the form of the three Vedas
- अर्कं (*arkaṃ*)—the adorable sun
- दिधिषाणाः (*didhiṣāṇāḥ*)—having the power to sustain the worlds
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the shining rays
- विदुः (*viduḥ*)—approached; then
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—belonging to the heavenly world
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—the waters
- अवेषन् (*aveṣan*)—rained down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni and Āditya, who pervade all the quarters and are shining, have pervaded the three worlds. The wind has produced pleasure for Agni and Āditya. When the shining rays, which have the power to sustain the worlds, approached the sun, who is adorable and endowed with radiance in the form of the three Vedas, then the waters belonging to the heavenly world rained down.

##### English translation
The two sources of heat (Agni and Aditya) spreading to the limit (of the horizon), have pervaded the threefold (universe); Matariswan has come to give them pleasure; (when) the shining (rays) reached the adorable (sun), having the brilliancy of the Saman, sustaining (the universe), they attained the water of heaven.

> वोढारस्ता न जानंति । कवयः क्रांतदर्शिनस्तु तासां सृष्ट्यादीनामुग्न्यादीनां वा
> निदानं मूलकारणं परमात्मानं नि चिक्क्युः । नितरां चिन्वंति जानंति । परेषूत्कृष्टेषु ना गुह्येषु ना गोप्तव्येषु कर्मसु यमनियमादिषु व्रतेषु याः
> प्रवृत्तयः संति तासां निदानं नि चिक्क्युः । जानंति ॥ चिञ् चयने । लिटि विभाषांचेरित्यभ्यासामुत्तरस्य कवर्णादेशः ! यद्वा। चायतेर्लिटि चायः की । पा. ६-१-३५ ।
> इतिच्छंदसि कीत्यादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

निर्ऋतीः (*nirṛtīḥ*) is a name of the earth; by it the other worlds are also meant. The three deities, Agni and the others, stationed there are worshipped by the sacrificers (उपासते (*upāsate*)) so that they may give (देष्ट्राय (*deṣṭrāya*)) oblations. Then these deities, far-famed (दीर्घश्रुतः (*dīrghaśrutaḥ*)) and carriers (वह्नयः (*vahnayaḥ*)) who bring the world to its goal, know the worship done by these; they do acknowledge it.
Or else: निर्ऋतिः (*nirṛtiḥ*) are those that go (ऋ (*ṛ*)) completely. The three, creation, preservation and dissolution, are served to give the self the fruit of its action. Those who hear for long (दीर्घश्रुतः (*dīrghaśrutaḥ*)) in the round of rebirth know only the thing to be thought of and seen; they do not know what the vision of the mantra and the like is. Hence the carriers (वह्नयः (*vahnayaḥ*)) of saṃsāra do not know them. But the seers (कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)), who see beyond, know thoroughly (नि चिक्क्युः (*ni cikkyuḥ*)) the origin (निदानं (*nidānaṃ*)), the root cause, the Supreme Self, of those, creation and the rest, or of Agni and the others. They know the origin of those activities that exist in the highest (परेषु (*pareṣu*)), secret (गुह्येषु (*guhyeṣu*)) works, that is, those to be guarded, and in the vows (व्रतेषु (*vrateṣu*)) such as the yamas and niyamas. Sāyaṇa then explains नि चिक्क्युः (*ni cikkyuḥ*) from the root चिञ् (*ciñ*) "to gather", with an alternative derivation from *cāyateḥ* (Pā. 6-1-35).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- निर्ऋतीः (*nirṛtīḥ*)—resting on the three worlds
- तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*)—the deities Agni, Vāyu and Āditya
- देष्ट्राय (*deṣṭrāya*)—to offer oblations
- उपासते (*upāsate*)—the sacrificers worship
- दीर्घश्रुताः (*dīrghaśrutāḥ*)—those of great fame
- वह्नयः (*vahnayaḥ*)—these deities, who bear the worlds
- वि जानंति (*vi jānaṃti*)—know their worship
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—the wise (knowers of reality)
- परेषु (*pareṣu*)—in the highest
- गुह्येषु (*guhyeṣu*)—and secret
- व्रतेषु (*vrateṣu*)—works
- याः (*yāḥ*)—those deities who are engaged in them
- तासां (*tāsāṃ*)—of these deities
- निदानं (*nidānaṃ*)—the root cause (the Supreme Self)
- नि चिक्युः (*ni cikyuḥ*)—have fully known
**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificers worship, by offering oblations, the deities Agni, Vāyu and Āditya, who rest on the three worlds. These deities, who are of great fame and bear the worlds, know their worship. The wise fully know the root cause of those deities who are engaged in the highest and secret works.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> चतु॑ष्कपर्दा युव॒तिः सु॒पेशा॑ घृ॒तप्र॑तीका व॒युना॑नि वस्ते ।  
> तस्यां॑ सुप॒र्णा वृष॑णा॒ नि षे॑दतु॒र्यत्र॑ दे॒वा द॑धि॒रे भा॑ग॒धेयं॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तस्यां । सुपर्णा । वृषणा । नि । सेदतुः । यत्र । देवाः । दधिरे । भागधेयं ॥३॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चतुष्कपर्दा चतुष्कोणा युवतिः स्त्रीरूपा सुपेशाः शोभनालंकारा धृतप्रतीका धृतप्रमुखहविश्कृतादृशी वेदिर्वयुनानि ज्ञातव्यानि पदार्थजातानि कर्माणि
> स्तोत्राणि वा वस्ते । आच्छादयति । तस्यां वेद्यां वृषणा वृषण् हविषां वर्षितारौ
> सुपर्णा सुपर्णौ सुपतन् जायापती यजमानब्रह्माण् ना निषेदतुः । निषण्ण
> भवतः । यत्र यस्यां वेद्यां देवा अग्न्यादयो भागधेयं । स्वार्थिको धेयप्रत्ययः । स्वस्वभागं हविर्दधिरे । धारयंति ॥ यद्वा! चतुष्कपर्दा नामाख्यातोपसर्गनिपाताश्चत्वारः कपर्दस्थानीया यस्याः सा युवतिस्तरुणी नित्या धृतप्रतीका
> दीप्यमानवर्णावयवैषपनिषदी वाग्वयुनानि ज्ञानानि वस्ते । आच्छादयति । तस्यां
> वाचि सुपर्णा सुपर्णौ जीवपरमात्मान् निषण्ण भवतः । यत्र ॥ इतराभ्योऽपि
> दृश्यंत इति तृतीयार्थे त्रल्पत्ययः ॥ यया वाचा देवा भागं धारयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

चतुष्कपर्दा (*catuṣkapardā*) is "four-cornered"; युवतिः (*yuvatiḥ*) is "of woman's form"; सुपेशाः (*supeśāḥ*) is "well adorned"; धृतप्रतीका (*dhṛtapratīkā*) is the altar (vedi) marked with ghee and the oblations that come first.**NOTE** वयुनानि (*vayunāni*) are things to be known, rites or praises; वस्ते (*vaste*) means "covers". On that altar the two वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*), showerers of oblations, the two सुपर्णा (*suparṇā*), who fly well, husband and wife, the sacrificer and … **NOTE**, sit down. यत्र (*yatra*) means "on which altar" the gods, Agni and the rest, hold their own share of the oblation; भागधेयं (*bhāgadheyaṃ*) has the redundant suffix dheya.

Alternatively: the "four hair-knots" are the four classes of words, noun, verb, preposition and particle. She is the young, ever-youthful Speech (Vāc), bright with shining letters, of Upaniṣadic character. वयुनानि (*vayunāni*) are forms of knowledge that she covers. In that Speech the two सुपर्णा (*suparṇā*), the individual self and the supreme self, are seated. The suffix tral in यत्र (*yatra*) is in the sense of the instrumental ("by which Speech the gods hold their share").

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चशुष्कपर्दा (*caśuṣkapardā*)—that which has four corners
- युवतिः (*yuvatiḥ*)—that which has a woman's form
- सुपेशा (*supeśā*)—that which is finely adorned
- धृतप्रतीका (*dhṛtapratīkā*)—that which shines with ghee; the sacrificial altar
- वयुनानि (*vayunāni*)—by excellent rites
- वस्ते (*vaste*)—is thickly covered**NOTE**
- यत्र (*yatra*)—on which altar
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods, Agni and the others
- भागधेयं (*bhāgadheyaṃ*)—their respective shares of the sacrifice
- दधिरे (*dadhire*)—they hold

### Printed p. 495
- तस्यां (*tasyāṃ*)—on that same sacrificial altar
- वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)—the two bestowers of desired objects
- सुपर्णा (*suparṇā*)—the sacrificer and his wife, of excellent going
- नि षेदतुः (*ni ṣedatuḥ*)—sit down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificial altar, which is four-cornered, of woman's form, finely adorned and shining with ghee, is pervaded by excellent rites. On that altar where Agni and the other gods receive their respective shares of the sacrifice, the sacrificer and his wife, bestowers of desired objects and, like birds, of excellent going, sit down.

ablations, clothes herself in pious rites; the two birds, the showerers of
oblations, have sat down thereon where the gods receive their share.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

एकः (*ekaḥ*): alone, without help in all works. सुपर्णः (*suparṇaḥ*): the well-flying deity of the middle region. He enters समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*), the atmosphere (antarikṣa). Having entered, he surveys all this world, all that is born, looking on it so as to favour it. I saw him, this deity, near at hand with a ripe mind. Further, माता (*mātā*) is the maker of the waters, the middle-region Speech; she licks, that is, tastes him. Only sustenance is meant here. And he too licks Mother Speech, that is, he lives by her alone. (The text continues on the next page.)

### Printed p. 496

> रेळ्हि । आस्वादयति । उपजीवनमात्रमत्र लक्ष्यते । स उ स खुलु मातरं वाचं रेळ्हि
> लेढि । तामेवोपजीवति ॥ लिह आस्वादने ॥ यद्वा । सुपर्णः पक्षवान्निराधारसंचार्येकः प्राणवायुः परमात्मा ना समुद्रं । समुद्रवंत्यापोऽस्मादिति समुद्रमंतरिक्षं । यद्वा । समुद्रवं सर्वतो गमनं । तच्छीलं प्रपंचजातमाविष्टवान्।
> सृष्ट्वा तदेवानुप्राविशत् । त्वै. आ. ८-६ । इति श्रुतेः । वायुपक्षे वाय्वादिरूपेणाविवेश । स इदं विश्वं सर्व० लोकं वि चष्टे । विशेषेण ख्यापयति । सति हि प्राणे
> परमात्मनि वा जीवंतः पुरुषा लोकं विख्यातं कुर्वंति । तं देवमुपासकोऽहं
> पाकेन परिपक्वज्ञानेन मनसांतितः ॥ अंतिकशब्दात्तसिः । अंतिकस्य तसि कादिलोपो
> भवत्याद्युदात्तत्वं च ॥ पा. ६-४-१४९-८ । इति कादिलोपः ॥ अंतिके समीपे स्वहृदयेऽपश्यं । तं प्राणं माता नाग्रेळ्ळि । नाक् प्राणेऽंतर्भवतीत्यर्थः । स्वापे हि
> वाग्व्यापारो न दृश्यते प्राणव्यापारस्तु दृश्यत इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Root लिह (*liha*) is in the sense of tasting. Alternatively: सुपर्णः (*suparṇaḥ*) is the winged one, moving without support, the one prāṇa-vāyu or the supreme self. समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*) is the atmosphere, from which the waters flow; or else the going everywhere, the creation whose nature it is to go. He has entered it, as the śruti says: सृष्ट्वा तदेवानुप्राविशत् (*sṛṣṭvā tadevānuprāviśat*) (Tai. Ā. 8-6).**NOTE** On the wind interpretation he entered in the form of wind and the rest. He वि चष्टे (*vi caṣṭe*), makes known especially this whole world: when prāṇa or the supreme self is present, living persons make the world known. I, the worshipper, saw that deity near, in my own heart, with ripened knowledge. माता (*mātā*) is Speech; she licks that prāṇa, meaning that Speech is contained within prāṇa. For in sleep the activity of speech is not seen, but the activity of prāṇa is seen.
