### Printed p. 497

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The deity called Suparṇa, who does all works without any help and can move everywhere, enters the atmosphere and moves about there, and looks on the whole class of beings with a mind to favour them. I saw such a deity close at hand with a ripened (that is, devout) mind. The goddess Speech, maker of the waters and a deity of the middle region, and that Suparṇa deity dwell in the atmosphere, each resting on the other.

Or else: the prāṇa-vāyu or the supreme self, unsupported and given to moving, that is, pervading everywhere, enters in the form of wind the atmosphere or the class of beings whose nature is to move (prāṇa). After entering the bodies of beings, that supreme self makes this whole world, that is, all the classes of beings, endowed with consciousness. I saw that supreme self, so described, very near, that is, abiding within my own heart, with a pure and ripened mind, that is, with the help of the mind. Speech, the power of speaking, remains in a living being as long as there is prāṇa. The activity of prāṇa too always remains mingled with the activity of speech; as long as prāṇa lasts, speech co-operates with the body. In the time of sleep there is no activity of speech; only the activity of prāṇa is seen.

##### English translation
One of the birds has entered the firmament; he contemplates this whole world : with mind mature I beheld him nigh at hand ; him the mother licks, he licks the mother.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On this Ṛk Yāska has given the Nirukta: एकः सुपर्णः स समुद्रमाविशति स इमानि सर्वाणि भूतान्यभिविपश्यति तं पाकेन मनसापश्यमंतित इत्यृषेर्दृष्टार्थस्य प्रीतिर्भवत्याख्यानसंयुक्ता तं माता रेढि वागेषा माध्यमिका स उ मातरं रेढि ॥ (*ekaḥ suparṇaḥ sa samudramāviśati sa imāni sarvāṇi bhūtānyabhivipaśyati taṃ pākena manasāpaśyamaṃtita ityṛṣerdṛṣṭārthasya prītirbhavatyākhyānasaṃyuktā taṃ mātā reḍhi vāgeṣā mādhyamikā sa u mātaraṃ reḍhi ‖*) (Ni. 10-46).

Here एकः (*ekaḥ*) means the unequalled one: there is none with power like his; it means one of extraordinary strength and ability. सुपर्णः (*suparṇaḥ*) is one of excellent going, always moving by nature; there is no other so given to going as he. (Continued on the next page.)

### Printed p. 498
This wind (or prāṇa-vāyu, or the supreme self) enters the atmosphere or the class of beings. After entering he sees those beings, or makes them see, that is, he makes them endowed with consciousness and impels them to their respective activities. This deity, distinguished by such qualities, I saw with a ripe mind full of knowledge, near me, in the space of my heart (so the seer says to another person beside him). The main sense is that this wind or supreme self, pervading the atmosphere, acts together with the classes of beings it has entered, in mutual dependence.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒प॒र्णं विप्रा॑ क॒वयो॒ वचो॑भि॒रेकं॒ संतं॑ बहु॒धा क॑ल्पयंति ।  
> छंदां॑सि च॒ दध॑तो अध्व॒रेषु॒ ग्रहा॒न्सोम॑स्य मिमते॒द्वाद॑श ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुपर्णं । विप्राः । कवयः । वचभिः । एकं । संतं । बहुधा । कल्पयंति ।  
> छंदांसि । च । दधतः । अध्वरेषु । ग्रहान् । सोमस्य । मिमते । द्वादश ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विप्रा मेधाविनः कवयः क्रांतप्रज्ञा मनुष्याः सुपर्णं सुपतनमेकं संतं
> परमात्मानं वचोभिः स्तुतिलक्षणैर्वचनैर्बहुधा बहुप्रकारं कल्पयंति । कुर्वंति ।
> किंच त एव कवयोऽध्वरेषु यज्ञेषु च्छंदांसि गायत्र्यादीनि सप्त च्छंदांसि दधतः
> स्तोत्रशस्त्रादिना धारयंतो द्वादशसंख्याकान्सोमस्य ग्रहान् ग्रहणसाधनानि
> पात्राण्युपांश्वंतर्यामादीनि मिमते । निर्मिमते ॥ ग्रहान्! गृह्यत एभिरिति ग्रहाः ।
> ग्रहवृदृनिश्चिगमश्चेति करणेऽप्पत्ययः । सोमस्येति कर्मणि षष्ठि । द्वादशेत्यत्र
> संख्या । पा. ६-२-३५ । इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The विप्राः (*viprāḥ*) (the intelligent) and कवयः (*kavayaḥ*) (men of far-reaching wisdom) fashion, कल्पयंति (*kalpayaṃti*), the one सुपर्णं (*suparṇaṃ*), the supreme self, in many ways by words of praise. Further, those same seers, at the sacrifices, hold the seven metres beginning with Gāyatrī by means of stotra, śastra and the rest, and मिमते (*mimate*), make, the twelve Soma ग्रहान् (*grahān*), the vessels for taking up (the Soma), the upāṃśu, antaryāma and the others. ग्रहाः (*grahāḥ*) are "that by which (Soma) is taken up"; the affix ap is in the instrumental sense. सोमस्य (*somasya*) is a genitive of the object. In द्वादश (*dvādaśa*) the accent is that of the first member.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—the intelligent
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—the seers of far-reaching wisdom
- सुपर्णं (*suparṇaṃ*)—the supreme self
- एकं संतं (*ekaṃ saṃtaṃ*)—though he is one only
- वजोभिः (*vajobhiḥ*)—by their praises
- बहुधा (*bahudhā*)—in many ways
- कल्पयंति (*kalpayaṃti*)—they describe (the same seers)
- अध्वरेषु (*adhvareṣu*)—at the sacrifices
- छंदांसि (*chaṃdāṃsi*)—the metres such as Gāyatrī
- दधतः (*dadhataḥ*)—possessing (reciting)
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—of Soma
- द्वादश ग्रहान् (*dvādaśa grahān*)—the twelve vessels, antaryāma and the rest
- मिमते (*mimate*)—they make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Though the supreme self is one, the intelligent seers of far-reaching wisdom describe him in many ways by their praises, as having different forms. The same seers, reciting the metres such as Gāyatrī at the sacrifices, have made the twelve vessels of Soma, antaryāma and the rest. (They prepare the twelve graha vessels.)

##### English translation
The wise seers through their praise make into many forms the bird which is only one; and holding the (seven) metres at the sacrifices, they measure twelve bowls of Soma.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

छंदासि च दधतः आध्वरेषु- यज्ञेषु गायत्र्यादीनि सप्त छंदांसि स्तोत्रशस्त्रादिना धारयंतः । (*chaṃdāsi ca dadhataḥ ādhvareṣu- yajñeṣu gāyatryādīni sapta chaṃdāṃsi stotraśastrādinā dhārayaṃtaḥ |*). Here "metres" means the seven chief kinds, Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh, Jagatī and the rest. Although metres are of many kinds, it is the custom in the Prātaranuvāka and in the śastra mantras to recite only certain mantras composed in the seven metres beginning with Gāyatrī. The meaning is "reciting the mantras of such metres".

ग्रहान् सोमस्य मिमते द्वादश-ग्रहणसाधनानि पात्राण्युपांश्वंतर्यामादीनि निर्मिमाते । (*grahān somasya mimate dvādaśa-grahaṇasādhanāni pātrāṇyupāṃśvaṃtaryāmādīni nirmimāte |*). गृह्यत विभिरिति ग्रहाः (*gṛhyata vibhiriti grahāḥ*).**NOTE** "Graha" means the vessel from which the gods drink Soma; because that vessel is held in the hand at the time of drinking Soma (गृह्यते (*gṛhyate*), it is held), the Soma-drinking vessel is called graha. These have various names, the upāṃśu vessel, the antaryāma vessel and so on. This Ṛk says that twelve such vessels are filled with Soma juice, consecrated and made ready for the drinking of the gods.

> ष॒ट्त्रिं॒शांश्च॑ च॒तुरः॑ क॒ल्पयं॑त॒श्चंदां॑सि च॒ दध॑त आद्वाद॒शं ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूर्वं सामान्येन यज्ञग्रहानुक्त्येदानीं सर्वग्रहादिपूर्वको यज्ञोऽभिधीयते । षट्त्रिंशान् । द्वावुपांश्वंतर्याम् । ऐंद्रवायनादयस्त्रयो

> आदित्यसावित्र्द्वै । वैश्वदेवः पात्मीवतो हारियोजन इति त्रयो ग्रहाः । एवं

> षोडशीति चेति चत्वारः । एतांश्चत्वारिंशत्संख्याकान्गहान्कल्पयंतः सोमेन
> पूरयंतः । किंचाद्वादशं ॥ आङ्मर्यादाभिविध्योः । सा. २-१-१३ । इत्यव्ययाभावसमासः । तस्य स्वरः ॥ द्वादशसंख्याकप्रउगादिशस्त्रसमाप्ति पर्यंतं छंदांसि गायत्यादीनि दधतः संतः शस्त्रादिरूपेण धारयंतः कवयो मनीषा ॥ तृतीयाया
> आकारः ॥ मनीषया बुद्धैवं यज्ञं विमाय निर्माय रथं । रमंत्यत्रेति
> रथो यज्ञः । तं रथं यज्ञमृक्सामाभ्यां प्रवर्तयंति । प्रकर्षेण संपादयंति ॥
> चतुर इत्यत्र चतुरः शसीत्यंतोदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that the sacrificial cups were mentioned earlier only in general terms, and that the rite is now described as one that begins with all the cups. "Thirty-six" is made up as follows. The Upāṃśu and the Antaryāma are two. The three cups beginning with the Aindravāyava belong to two deities each. The Śukra and the Manthin are two. The Āgrayaṇa, the Ukthya and the Dhruva are three. The Ṛtugrahas are twelve. The Aindrāgna and the Vaiśvadeva are two. The Marutvatīya cups are three. The Māhendra is one. The Āditya and the Sāvitra are two. The Vaiśvadeva, the Pātnīvata and the Hāriyojana are three. In this way the cups come to thirty-six. In the Atyagniṣṭoma the earlier thirty-six cups are joined by the two Aṃśu-Adābhya cups, the Dadhigraha and the Ṣoḍaśin, which makes four more. Thus "arranging" (kalpayantaḥ) means filling forty cups with Soma. Next, आद्वादशं (*ādvādaśaṃ*) is an avyayībhāva compound, formed by the rule आङ्मर्यादाभिविध्योः (*āṅmaryādābhividhyoḥ*), and it means "up to the number twelve". The wise (kavayaḥ), holding the metres, Gāyatrī and the rest, in the form of the śastras (recitations), that is, bearing them, from the Prauga-śastra onward until the twelve śastras are complete, by their intelligence (manīṣā; the instrumental ending is lengthened) thus measure out and construct the sacrifice. The "chariot" (ratha) is the sacrifice, because people delight in it (ramanti). They carry that chariot-sacrifice forward with the Ṛc and the Sāman, that is, they accomplish it in a superior manner. In चतुरः (*caturaḥ*) the final syllable has the high accent by the rule on the accusative plural ending शस् (*śas*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- षट्त्रिंशांश्च चतुरः (*ṣaṭtriṃśāṃśca caturaḥ*)—forty (36+4) cups (sacrificial vessels)
- कल्पयंतः (*kalpayaṃtaḥ*)—filling with Soma juice
- आद्वादशं (*ādvādaśaṃ*)—the Prauga and other śastra mantras, extending up to the number twelve

### Printed p. 501
- छंदांसि (*chaṃdāṃsi*)—with mantras accompanied by the bhuvas and so on (the Gāyatrī and other metres)
- दधतः (*dadhataḥ*)—reciting
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—the wise seers
- मनीषा (*manīṣā*)—by their own intelligence
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the sacrifice
- विमाय (*vimāya*)—having constructed (and carried forward)
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—that same sacrifice
- ऋक्सामाभ्यां (*ṛksāmābhyāṃ*)—with the mantras of the Ṛgveda and the Sāmaveda
- प्र वर्तयंति (*pra vartayaṃti*)—they adorn it exceedingly and make it go forward

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wise seers, so that the gods may drink Soma at the sacrifice, fill forty sacrificial cups with Soma juice. They recite twelve śastra mantras in the seven kinds of metre beginning with the Gāyatrī. By their intelligence they construct the sacrifice, and they make that same sacrifice proceed, adorned with Ṛks and with Sāmans.

##### English translation
Filling thirty six and four vessels, and holding the metres as for as twelve, measuring out the rite by their by their intelligence, the sages complete the sacrifice with the Ric and the Saman.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The previous Ṛk spoke of twelve Soma vessels. Now, in this Ṛk, the commentator explains still further vessels, and which gods drink Soma from which vessels. The names of forty vessels in all are given here. They are as follows.
The vessels called Upāṃśu and Antaryāma—2.
The Aindravāya cups and others, from which two deities together, such as Indra and Vāyu, drink—2×3=6.
The vessels called Śukra and Manthī—2.
The vessels called Āgrayaṇa, Ukthya and Dhruva—3.
The Ṛtugraha vessels—12.
The Aindrāgna and Vaiśvadeva vessels—2.
The Marutvatīya vessels—3.
The Māhendra-graha vessel—1.
The Āditya and Savitṛ vessels—2.

### Printed p. 502
The Vaiśvadeva, Pātnīvata and Hāriyojana vessels—3.
All these together make 36 cup-vessels. Besides these, in the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice there are four other cups: Aṃśu, Adābhya, Dadhigraha and Ṣoḍaśī. All together they come to 40 cup-vessels. These are what is called here षट्त्रिंशाश्च चतुरः (*ṣaṭtriṃśāśca caturaḥ*), "thirty-six and four".
The main purport is as follows.
The wise and learned priests fill forty kinds of cup-vessels with Soma juice so that the gods may drink Soma at the sacrifice. They carry out the sacrificial work reciting twelve kinds of śastra mantras, beginning with the Prauga and composed in the seven kinds of metre beginning with the Gāyatrī. For the śastra mantras at the sacrifice they recite Ṛks and hymns of the Ṛgveda. For the recitation of praise-songs (stotra) they sing Sāmaveda mantras. In this way, with various kinds of proceedings, they complete the sacrifice in all its parts. This is the main purport of the Ṛk.

> समर्थं चात्वोलोत्करमध्यदेशमिहास्मिन्यज्ञे कः प्र वोचत् । को व्यक्ति । न

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

There are fourteen other greatnesses (mahimānaḥ), that is, manifestations, of this supreme Self who is in the form of the sacrifice. Seven wise ones, the Hotṛ priests and the rest, lead him forth (praṇayanti, "carry on") by speech in the form of śastra. आप्नानं (*āpnānaṃ*) is from the root आप्ल (*āpla*) in the sense of pervading, and the vikaraṇa is altered irregularly. It means "pervasive". Sāyaṇa takes तीर्थं (*tīrthaṃ*) to be the sacred place at the Cātvāla and Utkara, able to remove sin. "Who here, at this sacrifice, could declare it?" The sense is that no one can.

### Printed p. 503

> कोऽपीत्यर्थः । येन पथा येन यज्ञमार्गेण सुतस्याभिषुतं सोमं प्रपिबंते
> देवा अतिशयेन पिबंति ॥ पा पाने । पाघ्रेत्यादिना पिबादेशः । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । उपसर्गेण समासः । यद्योगादनिघाते तिजि चोदात्तवतीति गतेर्निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"By which path", that is, by which sacrificial way, the gods drink the pressed Soma (प्रपिबंते (*prapibaṃte*), "drink abundantly"). The root is पा (*pā*) in the sense of drinking, and the substitute पिब (*piba*) is made by the rule पाघ्रेत्यादिना (*pāghretyādinā*). The ātmanepada is irregular. The verb is compounded with the preverb. Because of the connection with येन (*yena*) the verb is unaccented, and the preverb is likewise unaccented by the rule on a verb whose ending has the high accent.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्य (*asya*)—to Prajāpati, who is of the form of the sacrifice
- चतुर्दश (*caturdaśa*)—fourteen in number
- अन्ये महिमानः (*anye mahimānaḥ*)—there are other special manifestations
- तं (*taṃ*)—him
- सप्त धीराः (*sapta dhīrāḥ*)—the seven wise Hotṛ priests
- वाचा (*vācā*)—by speech (mantra) in the form of śastra
- प्रणयंति (*praṇayaṃti*)—they carry forward
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- येन पथा (*yena pathā*)—by which sacrificial path
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—of the pressed Soma
- प्रपिबंते (*prapibaṃte*)—the gods drink
- आप्नानं (*āpnānaṃ*)—extended
- तीर्थं (*tīrthaṃ*)—(and) sin-destroying sacrificial place
- कः (*kaḥ*)—who indeed
- प्रवोचत् (*pravocat*)—could describe it?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Prajāpati, who is of the form of the sacrifice, has fourteen other special manifestations. The wise seven Hotṛ priests praise him through speech in the form of śastra (mantra). By the prescribed path of this sacrifice the gods drink the pressed Soma. Who could describe such an extensive, venerable sacrificial place, such as the Cātvāla, which is able to carry one across sin?

##### English translation
There are fourteen other great developments of him; seven sages conduct him by prayer.  Who may declare the expanded place of sanctity at this (rite), the path by which they drink of the libation.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सहस्रधा सहस्रसंख्याकेषु ब्रह्मादिस्तंबपर्यंतेषु देहेषु पंचदशानि
> चक्षुः श्रोत्रं मनो वाक् प्राण इत्येतानि पंच । तदाधारत्वेन मातापितृः
> सकाशादागतानि पृथिव्यप्तेजोवाय्वाकाशरूपाणि भूतानि मिलितानि दश । एवं पंचदशसंख्याकान्युक्थान्युत्कृष्टान्यंगानि विद्यंते प्राणिदेहेषु जातेषु ! द्यावापृथिवी ॥
> षष्ठिद्विवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगिति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः ॥ द्यावापृथिव्योर्यावद्यत्परिमाणमस्ति तावदित्तत्परिमाणमेवात्माधिष्ठितं प्राणिदेहजातं भवति ॥ यावत्तावच्छब्दयोर्यत्तदेतेभ्यः परिमाणे वतुपि । पा. ५-२-३९ ! आ सर्वनाम्नः । पा. ६-३-९१।
> इति दीर्घः ॥ किंच सहस्रधा सहस्रसंख्याकेषु सहस्रं महिमानः सहस्रसंख्याका
> महांतो व्यवहारविशेषा भवंति । प्रतिविषयं प्रतिलक्षणं दर्शनश्रवणादिव्यवहारनिष्पत्तेः ॥ सहस्रधेत्यत्र विधार्थे धाप्रत्ययः ॥ ब्रह्म जगत्कारणं वस्तु यावन्नानाविधप्राणिदेहरूपेण यावत्परिमाणं भूत्वा निष्ठितं विशेषेण स्थितं वाक् तावती
> तत्परिमाणा भवति । एकैकस्याभिधेयार्थस्यैकैकनामापेक्षणात् । अन्यत्रापि श्रूयते ।
> सर्वाणि रूपाणि विचिंत्य धीरो नामानि कृत्वाभिवदन्यदास्त इति । सहस्रधा पंचदशान्युक्थॆति पंच हि दशतो भवंतीत्यादिकमारण्य कमत्रानुसंधेयं । ऐ. आ. १-३-८ !

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"In a thousand ways" means in a thousand bodies, from Brahmā down to a blade of grass. In them are fifteen: eye, ear, mind, speech and breath, which are five. As their support come the elements, earth, water, fire, air and space, which derive from the mother and father and are joined together as ten. Thus fifteen excellent limbs are found in the bodies of living beings once born. Next, द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*): the ending is the dual, and the long vowel arises as the homogeneous long. Whatever the measure of heaven and earth, just that measure is the body-product of living beings, presided over by the self. The words यावत् (*yāvat*) and तावत् (*tāvat*) take the affix वतु (*vatu*) in the sense of measure (Pā. Sū. 5-2-39), and the long vowel is made by Pā. Sū. 6-3-91. Further, in a thousand ways, in a thousand, there are a thousand greatnesses, that is, a thousand great kinds of activity, since seeing, hearing and the like are accomplished with respect to each object and each mark. In सहस्रधा (*sahasradhā*) the affix धा (*dhā*) is used in the sense of kind. Brahman, the cause of the world, having become of whatever measure in the form of the bodies of the various living beings, stands specially established; speech is of that very measure, because each single thing signified requires its own name. It is heard elsewhere too: "Having considered all forms, the wise one, making the names, speaks of them as he sits." Sāyaṇa adds that the Āraṇyaka passage beginning "In a thousand ways, fifteen are the uktha; for five become ten" and so on should be brought to bear here (Ai. Ā. 1-3-8).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहस्रधा (*sahasradhā*)—in this body of the Supreme Self, which has many divisions from Brahmā down to a blade of grass
- पंचदशानि उक्ता (*paṃcadaśāni uktā*)—fifteen chief limbs are established
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth
- यावत् (*yāvat*)—of whatever measure they are
- तावदित् (*tāvadit*)—of just that measure
- तत् (*tat*)—that body exists
- सहस्रधा (*sahasradhā*)—in thousands of places
- सहस्रं महिमानः (*sahasraṃ mahimānaḥ*)—thousands of greatnesses are manifested
- यावत् (*yāvat*)—of whatever measure
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—Brahman, the cause of the world
- विष्ठितं (*viṣṭhitaṃ*)—is established
- तावती (*tāvatī*)—of just that measure
- वाक् (*vāk*)—speech is pervaded

### Printed p. 505

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In this body of the Supreme Self, which has many divisions from Brahmā down to a blade of grass, fifteen chief limbs are established. This body exists as being of just the measure that heaven and earth have. Thousands of greatnesses are manifested in thousands of places. Of just the measure of Brahman, the cause of the world, as established, the principle of speech too is pervasive.

##### English translation
The fifteenen chief forms (are found) in a thousand places; as heaven
heaven and earth are, so verily is that; the thousand great (functions) are in
a thousand places; as Brahma is variably developed, so is speech.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सहस्रधा— सहस्रसंख्याकेषु ब्रह्मादिस्तंबपर्यतेषु देहेषु । (*sahasradhā— sahasrasaṃkhyākeṣu brahmādistaṃbaparyateṣu deheṣu |*) Here "thousand" is not only the number one thousand; it means in the bodies of many, or manifold, kinds of living beings.
पंचदशानि—चक्षुःश्रोत्रं मनो वाक् प्राण इत्येतानि पंच । तदाधारत्तेन मातापितोः सकाशादागतानि पृथिव्यप्तेजोवाय्वाकाशरूपाणि भूतानि मिलितानि दश । (*paṃcadaśāni—cakṣuḥśrotraṃ mano vāk prāṇa ityetāni paṃca | tadādhārattena mātāpitoḥ sakāśādāgatāni pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśarūpāṇi bhūtāni militāni daśa |*) "Fifteen" means bodies made up of fifteen parts or portions. They are as follows. In the body of every living being there are five organs of knowledge: eye, ear, mind, speech (the power of speaking or making sound) and breath. There are also outer limbs that serve as their support. That is to say, although acts such as seeing belong to the organs of knowledge, there are also the outer organs that are the means of producing such knowledge. To see and know an object, the eye, an outer limb, and the mind, an inner organ, are the chief means. The other limbs are likewise. The inner organs, mind and the rest, follow the past and present condition of the particular living being. The outer limbs alone follow the bodily constitution of the father and mother, who are the cause of the origin of that being's body. If the parents are strong in body, the children too will be strong like them. Therefore the five elements, earth, water, fire, air and space, which are the cause of the outer body (the bodies formed of the five elements), arise from the bodily constitution of the parents. So the five elements connected with the father and the five connected with the mother together make ten kinds of substance, and with the five organs, eye and the rest, mentioned before, the body of every living being is made up of fifteen kinds of substance in all. That is the purport.

### Printed p. 506
"Just as the heaven and earth, so far as they extend, are made of the manifold substances composed of the subtle and gross five elements, this body too is constructed in just that way." That is, the things or substances seen in heaven and earth are present also in the bodies of living beings; this is the sense.

[[b-note-none]]

The Kannada explains: "A thousand-fold is the greatness; as far as a thousand the Brahman is spread out, so far extends speech" (the Sanskrit is quoted in the Kannada as: सहस्रधा महिमानः सहस्रं यावत् ब्रह्म विस्थितं तावती वाक् (*sahasradhā mahimānaḥ sahasraṃ yāvat brahma visthitaṃ tāvatī vāk*)). Here too the word "thousand" means many, manifold, countless. The Brahman, the root of all and the cause of the world, takes on the bodies of countless and manifold living beings and is dealt with under manifold forms and shapes. Likewise speech is dealt with by just as many designations by name. How? Every living being and thing in the world is a transformation of the Brahman-substance. As they have forms, so every thing has a name. As many things as there are, so many names. Hence it is described here that speech (names) corresponds in measure to things. To support this the commentator cites the following passages of the Taittirīya and Aitareya Āraṇyakas, whose purport is the same as explained above:

सर्वाणि रूपाणि विचिंत्य धीरो नामानि कृत्वाभिवदन्यदास्ते ॥ (*sarvāṇi rūpāṇi viciṃtya dhīro nāmāni kṛtvābhivadanyadāste ‖*) (Tai. Ā. 3-12-7)

सहस्रधा पंचदशान्न्युक्थेति पंच हि दशतो भवंति ॥ (*sahasradhā paṃcadaśānnyuktheti paṃca hi daśato bhavaṃti ‖*) (Ai. Ā. 1-3-8) **NOTE**

> कश्चंद॑सां॒ योग॒मा वे॑द॒ धीरः॒ को धिष्ण्यां॒ प्रति॒ वाचं॑

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धीरो धीमान् को मानुषश्चंदसां गायत्र्यादीनां योगं स्तुतशस्त्रात्मना नियोगमा वेद । आजानाति । को ना धिष्ण्यां । धिष्ण्यानि होत्रादीनां सप्त
> स्थानानि । तदर्हां वाचं प्रति पपाद । प्रतिपादयति । करोति । किंचर्त्विजां होत्रादीनां सप्ता नामष्टममष्टसंख्यापूरकं शूरं स्वतंत्रं कमाहुः । वदंति । कः स्मित्
> कः खल्विंद्रस्य हरी ऋक्सामरूपौ द्वावश्वा । ऋक्सामे ना इंद्रस्य हरी इत्याम्नायते । तादृशौ हरी नि चिकाय । नितरां पूजयति । जानाति । वेदिता प्रतिपादयिताष्टसंख्यापूरकस्य देवस्य ज्ञाता ना परमात्मनोऽन्यो नास्तीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Who among men, wise (dhīra), knows the application (yoga) of the metres Gāyatrī and the rest, i.e. their assignment as stuta and śastra? Who sets forth the speech fitting the dhiṣṇyas, the seven stations of the Hotṛ and the other priests? Further, whom do they call the eighth of the seven priests, the Hotṛ and the rest — the one who completes the number eight, the independent (śūra)? Who, indeed, has honoured (ni cikāya: worships, knows) the two bay horses of Indra, the Ṛk and the Sāman? It is traditionally said ऋक्सामे ना इंद्रस्य हरी (*ṛksāme nā iṃdrasya harī*). The sense: no one other than the Supreme Self is knower and expounder of the god who completes the number eight.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कः धीरः (*kaḥ dhīraḥ*)—which wise man
- छंदसां (*chaṃdasāṃ*)—of the metres Gāyatrī etc.
- योगं (*yogaṃ*)—the application
- आ वेद (*ā veda*)—knows
- धिष्ण्यां (*dhiṣṇyāṃ*)—the seven stations of the Hotṛ etc.
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—in the form of praise
- कः (*kaḥ*)—who indeed
- प्रति पपाद (*prati papāda*)—explains and describes
- ऋत्विजां (*ṛtvijāṃ*)—among the priests
- अष्टमं (*aṣṭamaṃ*)—the eighth
- शूरं (*śūraṃ*)—the independent
- कं (*kaṃ*)—whom
- आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—they describe
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- हरी (*harī*)—the Ṛk and Sāman mantras, famed as horses
- कः स्मित् (*kaḥ smit*)—who indeed
- नि चिकाय (*ni cikāya*)—can know?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Which wise man knows the application of the metres Gāyatrī and the rest? Who indeed explains and describes, in the form of praise, the seven stations of the Hotṛ and the others? Whom do they describe as the eighth among the priests, the independent one? Who indeed can know the horses of Indra (the Ṛk and Sāman mantras)?

##### English translation
What grave person knows the application of the metres? Who utters the words appropriate to the functions (of the) different priests? Whom do

### Printed p. 508

##### English translation
they call the eighth of the priests, the independent ? Who has done honour to the two bay horses of Indra ?

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the seer asks who is the wise man who can know the greatness of the metres such as Gāyatrī used in sacrifices, of the seven Hotṛs, of the mantras they recite, of the god set forth in those mantras, and of the Ṛk and Sāman mantras famed as Indra's horses.

कः छंदसां योगं आ वेद धीरः (*kaḥ chaṃdasāṃ yogaṃ ā veda dhīraḥ*) etc.: Among the metres there are many kinds, Gāyatrī and others. There is a rule that particular rites are to be done only with mantras of particular metres. Even in reciting the Prātaranuvāka and similar mantras there is a rule that separate mantras of the seven metres, Gāyatrī and others, are to be recited. Therefore, which man, however wise, can know the use of the metres as occasion requires in reciting the śastra mantras (Ṛgveda mantras) and in singing the stotra mantras (Sāmaveda mantras), and their greatness? (The sense: no one is able to know it fully.)

कः धिष्ण्यां प्रति वाचं पपाद (*kaḥ dhiṣṇyāṃ prati vācaṃ papāda*): Dhiṣṇyā means station, rank. The dhiṣṇyā of the Hotṛ means the position and standing of the priest called Hotṛ, the mantras he must recite in the sacrifice, the duties he must perform, and so on. Likewise the other priests have their positions. Which man can fully know the positions of the Hotṛ and the rest in sacrifices, their duties and the mantras they must recite?

कं ऋत्विजां अष्टमं शूरं आहुः (*kaṃ ṛtvijāṃ aṣṭamaṃ śūraṃ āhuḥ*): In the sacrifice there are seven chief priests, the seven Hotṛs. But who is the eighth? No one is able to say this. The eighth is the very god worshipped in the sacrifice. Who is he, what is his nature, what his greatness? Only the omniscient Supreme Self can know and tell this; no one else can know. This is the sense.

हरी इंद्रस्य नि चिकाय कः स्वित् (*harī iṃdrasya ni cikāya kaḥ svit*): Who indeed honours, knows, Indra's Ṛk and Sāman horses? The Ṛk and Sāman mantras famed as Indra's horses, and their true

### Printed p. 509
meaning — what man can know them rightly? Except the all-powerful Supreme Self there is no one else who knows this; this is the sense.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भूम्या॒ अंतं॒ पर्येके॑ चरंति॒ रथ॑स्य धू॒र्षु यु॒क्तासो॑  
> अस्थुः ।  
> श्रम॑स्य दा॒यं वि भ॑जंत्येभ्यो य॒दा य॒मो भव॑ति ह॒र्म्ये  ॒
> हितः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भूम्याः । अंतं । परि । एके । चरंति । रथस्य । धूःऽसु । युक्तासः । अस्तुः ।  
> श्रमस्य । दायं । वि । भजंति । एभ्यः । यदा । यमः । भवति । हर्म्ये । हितः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एके केचनाश्वा भूम्याः पृथिव्याः । अनेन द्युलोकोऽप्युपलक्ष्यते ।
> द्युलोकस्य चांतं पर्यंतं परि चरंति । तदानीं सर्वत आगच्छंति । तदा च
> तेऽश्वा रथस्य धूर्षु युगादिभारेषु युक्तासो युक्ताः संतोऽस्थुः । तिष्ठंति ।
> विभ्योऽश्वेभ्यः श्रमस्य दायं ॥ दो अवखंडने । घञ् । कर्षात्वत इत्यंतोदात्तत्वं ॥ श्रमस्य नाशकं घासादिकं वि भजंति । देवाः प्रयच्छंति । यदा यस्मिन्काले
> यमो नियंता सूर्यो हर्म्यॆ हर्म्यस्थानीये रथे हितो निहितो भवति ।
> तदैते भजंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Some horses, from the earth (and by this the heaven is also indicated), range to the end of heaven; then they come from all sides, and at that time stand harnessed to the yoke-loads of the chariot. The gods apportion (vi bhajanti) to these horses the share of fatigue-relief (śramasya dāya), fodder and the like. When the Yama, the controller, i.e. Sūrya, is placed in the chariot, which stands for the हर्म्य (*harmya*) (mansion), then they apportion it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एके (*eke*)—some horses, i.e. the seven horses of Sūrya
- भूम्याः (*bhūmyāḥ*)—of the earth
- अंतं (*aṃtaṃ*)—in the farthest regions
- परि चरंति (*pari caraṃti*)—range about (at that time those same horses)
- रथस्य (*rathasya*)—of the chariot
- धूर्षु (*dhūrṣu*)—at the yokes
- युक्तासः (*yuktāsaḥ*)—harnessed
- अस्थुः (*asthuḥ*)—stand
- यदा (*yadā*)—when
- यमः (*yamaḥ*)—Sūrya, who controls these seven horses
- हर्म्ये (*harmye*)—in his chariot
- हितः (*hitaḥ*)—placed

### Printed p. 510
- भवति (*bhavati*)—becomes, then
- विभ्यः (*vibhyaḥ*)—to these horses
- श्रमस्य दायं (*śramasya dāyaṃ*)—food materials such as grass that remove fatigue
- वि भजंति (*vi bhajaṃti*)—the gods give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Some horses (Sūrya's seven horses) range right to the extremities of heaven and earth. Then those same horses stand harnessed at the yokes of the chariot. When Sūrya, who controls these seven horses, seats himself in his chariot, the gods give these horses fatigue-removing food such as grass, and tend them.

##### English translation
Some (horses) proceed to the limit of the earth; they stand still harnessed to the yoke of the chariot; (the gods) apportion among them the alleviation of fatigue, when the charioteer is placed (ready to drive them) to their dwelling.

## Sūkta 115 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चित्र इति नवर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तमाग्नेयं । उपस्तुतो नाम वृष्टिहव्यपुत्र
> ऋषिः । अष्टमी त्रिष्टुप् । नवमी शक्वरी । आदितः सप्त जगत्यः । तथा चानुक्रांतं ।
> चित्र इन्नव वार्ष्टिहव्य उपस्तुत आग्नेयं जागतं त्रिष्टुप्यक्वर्यंतमिति ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्जागते छंदसीदं सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । चित्र इच्छिशोर्वसुं न
> चित्रमहसमिति जागतं । आ. ४-१३ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The third sūkta, चित्र इति (*citra iti*), of nine Ṛks, is addressed to Agni. The seer is Upastuta, son of Vṛṣṭihavya. The eighth Ṛk is Triṣṭubh, the ninth Śakvarī, the first seven Jagatī. The Anukramaṇī says: चित्र इन्नव वार्ष्टिहव्य उपस्तुत आग्नेयं जागतं त्रिष्टुप्यक्वर्यंतमिति (*citra innava vārṣṭihavya upastuta āgneyaṃ jāgataṃ triṣṭupyakvaryaṃtamiti*). The sūkta is used in the Prātaranuvāka and in the Aśvina-śastra for the Jagatī metre; it is prescribed by the sūtra चित्र इच्छिशोर्वसुं न चित्रमहसमिति जागतं (*citra icchiśorvasuṃ na citramahasamiti jāgataṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 4-13).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, चित्रः (*citraḥ*), is the third sūkta in the tenth anuvāka. It has nine Ṛks. Its seer is Upastuta, son of Vṛṣṭihavya; the deity is Agni; its eighth Ṛk is in Triṣṭubh, the ninth in Śakvarī, the first seven in Jagatī. The Anukramaṇī states: चित्र इन्नव वार्षिहव्य उपस्तुत आग्नेयं जागतं त्रिष्टुप्‌शक्वर्यंतं (*citra innava vārṣihavya upastuta āgneyaṃ jāgataṃ triṣṭupśakvaryaṃtaṃ*). When the Aśvina-śastra mantras are recited at the time of the Prātaranuvāka, this sūkta is applied for the Ṛks in Jagatī metre, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, चित्र इच्छिशोर्वसुं न चित्रमहसमिति जागतं (*citra icchiśorvasuṃ na citramahasamiti jāgataṃ*) (Ā. 4-13).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The carrying of the oblation (हनिर्वहनं (*hanirvahanaṃ*)) by the child, the young, new Agni is indeed a wonder (चित्रः । इत् (*citraḥ | it*)): he who is born does not go to his two parents — the makers of all, i.e. heaven and earth as mother and father, or the two kindling-sticks — to drink. Here धातवे (*dhātave*) is from the root धेट् (*dheṭ*) in the sense of drinking; he does not go even to drink. अनूधाः (*anūdhāḥ*): if this world and that world, being without udders, bore Agni, it would be proper that he not go to suck; that is not so; rather, heaven and earth are indeed the wish-fulfilling cows of all, yet he does not go. Therefore his carrying of the oblation is a wonder; and after birth ….

### Printed p. 512

> मेव नृद्यास्मिन्निने सद्यस्तदानीमेव शीघ्रं महि महद्दूत्यं ॥ दूतस्य भागकर्मणी
> इति कर्मणि यत्कृत्ययः ॥ दूतकर्म चरन् ववक्ष । देवान्प्रति हवींषि वहति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues his gloss of the last words of the verse. In this passage the text is damaged and begins in the middle of a sentence: the Agni, once born, on that very day and at that very moment, swiftly performs the great office of messenger. He explains दूत्यं (*dūtyaṃ*) (office of the messenger) with the rule दूतस्य भागकर्मणी (*dūtasya bhāgakarmaṇī*) (the affix yat in the sense of the action). Performing the messenger's work, ववक्ष (*vavakṣa*): he carries the oblations to the gods. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Agni
- मातरौ (*mātarau*)—to Heaven and Earth, the makers of the world, who stand in the place of mother and father
- धातवे (*dhātave*)—for suckling
- न अस्येति (*na asyeti*)—does not go
- शिशोः (*śiśoḥ*)—who is of the form of an infant
- तरुणस्य (*taruṇasya*)—and a youth, of Agni
- वक्षथः (*vakṣathaḥ*)—the work of carrying the oblation
- चित्रइत् (*citrait*)—is indeed wonderful
- अनूधाः (*anūdhāḥ*)—the mother who has no udder
- यदि (*yadi*)—by what greatness
- जीजनत् (*jījanat*)—she gave birth to Agni (therefore he has no suckling)
- अध च (*adha ca*)—as soon as he is born
- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—swiftly
- महि (*mahi*)—great
- दूत्यं (*dūtyaṃ*)—the work of the gods' messenger
- चरन् (*caran*)—performing
- ववक्ष (*vavakṣa*)—he carries the oblation to the gods

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The work of carrying the oblation, performed by that Agni who is an infant and a youth, and who does not go for suckling to Heaven and Earth, the makers of the world, who stand in the place of mother and father, is indeed wonderful. The mother who has no udder gave birth to Agni by her greatness; therefore he has no suckling. As soon as he is born, swiftly performing the great work of the gods' messenger, Agni carries the oblation to the gods.

##### English translation
Wonderful is the conveyance of (the oblation by) the tender infant, who does not come to his parents to drink, although the underless (world) gave him birth : he immediately bears (the oblation to the gods) fulfilling the important office of their messenger.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यः धातये मातरौ न अस्येति (तस्य) शिशोः तरुणस्य वक्षथः चित्र इत् (*yaḥ dhātaye mātarau na asyeti (tasya) śiśoḥ taruṇasya vakṣathaḥ citra it*)—Heaven and Earth are not merely the makers of the world; they are the mother and father of all in the world. For all living beings are born within the space between Heaven and Earth, and from a portion of Heaven and Earth (that is, from the five elements). Therefore Heaven and Earth are the mother and father of Agni too. In worldly practice a newborn child, for some time, relies on its mother for suckling. But Agni does not rely, for suckling, on his mother and father Heaven and Earth, or on the fire-sticks (araṇi), the place of his birth.

### Printed p. 513

अनूधाः यदि जीजनत् ऊधो रहितोऽयं लोकश्चैनमग्निं यदि अजनयत् तर्हि स्तनपानाय न गच्छतीति युक्तं । तथा न भवति । किंतु द्यावापृथिव्यौ सर्वेषां कामदुघे खलु । तथापि न याति । तस्मादस्य हविवहनं चित्रं ॥ (*anūdhāḥ yadi jījanat ūdho rahito 'yaṃ lokaścainamagniṃ yadi ajanayat tarhi stanapānāya na gacchatīti yuktaṃ | tathā na bhavati | kiṃtu dyāvāpṛthivyau sarveṣāṃ kāmadughe khalu | tathāpi na yāti | tasmādasya havivahanaṃ citraṃ ‖*) It has been said that the Heaven and Earth spoken of above stand in the place of father and mother to Agni. As in worldly practice, a mother naturally ought to have breasts for the suckling of her children. If it is said that Agni did not rely on them for suckling because Heaven and Earth have no such breasts, that is not right. For it is well known that Heaven and Earth nourish all beings, supplying to each the food and the like that is dear to him. Even so Agni did not rely on Heaven and Earth for suckling, that is, for his nourishment. Yet that this Agni is capable in the work of carrying the oblation is wonderful indeed, so the seer describes.
अथ च नु ववक्ष सद्यः महि दूत्यं चरन्—उत्पत्त्यनंतरमेव अस्मिन् दिने तदानीमेव शीघ्रं महद्दूत्यकर्म चरन् देवान् प्रति हवींषि वहति ॥ (*atha ca nu vavakṣa sadyaḥ mahi dūtyaṃ caran—utpattyanaṃtarameva asmin dine tadānīmeva śīghraṃ mahaddūtyakarma caran devān prati havīṃṣi vahati ‖*) As soon as this Agni is born (in the fire-sticks), immediately and swiftly he undertakes the messenger's work, which is great in nature and hard to accomplish, and carries the oblations to the gods.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Apastamaḥ: because the word अपः (*apaḥ*) has final acute accent, it is known that the matvartha affix is dropped (otherwise, by the rule on *apaḥ karmākhyāyāṃ*, the affix asun would give an initial acute). Meaning: Agni, "the one most full of action (karma)"; the instrumental ending is dropped. नाम्ना (*nāmnā*): by the bowing, that is by the oblation, or by praise. धायि (*dhāyi*): he is indeed held (nourished) by the sacrificers, since दन् (*dan*) he is the giver of wealth to those who sacrifice (root डुदाञ् (*ḍudāñ*), to give). The Agni who, with भस्मना (*bhasmanā*), that is with shining, illuminating splendour, and with दता (*datā*) (tooth), joins वना (*vanā*), the forests, that is burns them completely. Further, अभिप्रमुरा (*abhipramurā*): with the ladle called juhū, raised on all sides or else enveloped on all sides with oblations; स्वध्वरः (*svadhvaraḥ*), Agni of the good sacrifice, moves in the oblation fit for offering (the verb is to be supplied). The illustration: like a इनः (*inaḥ*), a capable, प्रोथमानः (*prothamānaḥ*), sufficient, strong-limbed bull, as a bull moves in grass and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Agni
- भस्मना (*bhasmanā*)—by his shining splendour
- दता (*datā*)—and by his teeth of the form of flames
- वना (*vanā*)—the forests (trees)
- संयुवते (*saṃyuvate*)—who burns together
- अपस्तमति (*apastamati*)—who is intent on the best action
- दन् (*dan*)—giver of wealth to the sacrificers
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- नाम (*nāma*)—by the oblation
- धायि (*dhāyi*)—is held (is nourished)
- इनः (*inaḥ*)—capable
- प्रोथमानः (*prothamānaḥ*)—having strong limbs
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—a bull
- यवसे न (*yavase na*)—as it feeds and is satisfied in the pasture
- अभिप्रमुरा (*abhipramurā*)—with a full supply of oblation
- जुह्वा (*juhvā*)—with the ladle
- स्वध्वरः (*svadhvaraḥ*)—Agni who has received the good sacrificial offering (is satisfied in the sacrificial place)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Agni who burns the forests together with his shining splendour and his teeth of flame, who is intent on the best action and a giver of wealth to the sacrificers, is nourished with the oblation. As a capable, strong-limbed bull feeds and is satisfied in the pasture, so Agni, receiving the good sacrificial offering from the ladle full of oblation, is satisfied in the sacrificial place.

> हे स्तोतारः वो यूयं तमग्निमभिष्टुत । कीदृशं । विं न दक्षिणमिव
> द्रुषदं । द्रुवृक्षः । अरणिलक्षणे वृक्षे सीदंतं देवं द्योतमानं अंधस इंदुं
> स्तोतृणामन्नस्य क्लेदयितारं प्रापयितारं ॥ उंदेरिच्चादेः । उ. १-१३ । इत्युप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेराद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ प्रोथंतं शब्दायमानं प्रवपंतमत्यर्थं
> वनानां दाहकं अर्णवं ॥ अर्णसः सलोपश्चति मत्त्वर्थीयो वः ॥ अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिरित्यादिक्रमेणोदकवं० आसा ॥ आस्यॆशब्दस्य पद्दन्नित्यादिनासन्नादेशः । वर्णलोपश्कांदसः ॥ आसैन वह्निं हविषां वोढारं । यद्वा । आसा । अंतिकनामैतत् ।
> देवानां समीपे हविषां प्रापकं । वहने दृष्टांतः । वह्निं न । वह्निर्वा अनड्वान् ।
> तै. ब्रा. १-८-२-५ । इति श्रवणादनड्वाहमिव वहने समर्थं शोचिषा स्वदीप्ता
> विरप्पिनं । महन्नामैतत् । महांतं महिव्रतं न महाकर्माणमादित्यमिनाध्वनः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praisers, praise that Agni. What is he like? विं न (*viṃ na*), like a bird; द्रुषदं (*druṣadaṃ*): dru is a tree, one sitting in the tree that is the fire-stick; देवं (*devaṃ*), shining; अंधस इंदुं (*aṃdhasa iṃduṃ*), the one who moistens, who brings forward, the food of the praisers (the affix u by Uṇ. Sū. 1-13, with initial acute). प्रोथंतं (*prothaṃtaṃ*), sounding; प्रवपंतं (*pravapaṃtaṃ*), greatly burning the forests; अर्णवं (*arṇavaṃ*), possessing water, in the order beginning "the offering cast into the fire …". आसा (*āsā*): by the mouth, the carrier of oblations. Or else आसा (*āsā*) is a word for "near": he brings oblations near the gods. The illustration for carrying: वह्निं न (*vahniṃ na*), since it is heard in वह्निर्वा अनड्वान् (*vahnirvā anaḍvān*) (Tai. Brā. 1-8-2-5), he is capable of carrying like an ox. शोचिषा (*śociṣā*), by his own light, विरप्पिनं (*virappinaṃ*) (virapśin: "mahat" is the meaning), great; like Āditya, of great action (महिव्रतं न (*mahivrataṃ na*)), *adhvanaḥ sarajaṃtaṃ* (continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 516

> सरजंतं । मार्गान्सह युगपदेव रंजयंतं । एवंगुणमग्निमभिष्टुत ॥ सरजंतं ।
> रन्ज रागे । रंजेः शतरि रंजेश्च । पा. ६-४-२६ । इति नलोपे सहस्य सभावे च कृते
> रूपं ॥ यद्वा । सरतीति सरः । सरस्कोदकस्य जनयितारं ॥ जनेस्तप्रत्यये कृते
> रूपमिति वा । व्युत्पत्त्यनवधारणादनवग्रहः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He colours the paths at once together: praise Agni of such qualities. Sarajantam: from the root रन्ज (*ranja*) (to colour), by the rule रंजेः शतरि रंजेश्च (*raṃjeḥ śatari raṃjeśca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-26) the nasal is dropped and सह (*saha*) becomes स (*sa*). Or else, sara is "that which moves", that is water, so "the producer of water"; the form arises from the root जन (*jana*) with the affix ta. The derivation not being fixed, there is no determination.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वः (*vaḥ*)—you (O praises)
- विं न (*viṃ na*)—as birds sit on a tree
- द्रुसदं (*drusadaṃ*)—who is in the fire-sticks made of wood (having been born there)
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—shining
- अंधसः इंदुं (*aṃdhasaḥ iṃduṃ*)—who carries to the gods the oblations and the like offered by the praisers
- प्रोथंतं (*prothaṃtaṃ*)—with sound, that is making a crackling sound
- प्रवपंतं (*pravapaṃtaṃ*)—who burns the forest trees
- अर्णवं (*arṇavaṃ*)—who is the cause of the rain water
- आसा वह्निं (*āsā vahniṃ*)—who carries the oblation near to the gods; or else: वह्निं न (*vahniṃ na*)—like a bull (ox) bearing a burden; आसा (*āsā*)—with his mouth, that is with his flame, carrying the oblation to the gods
- शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)—with his radiance
- विरष्यिनं न (*viraṣyinaṃ na*)—like Āditya of great majesty
- अध्वनः (*adhvanaḥ*)—the paths
- सरजंतं (*sarajaṃtaṃ*)—who shines, or who sheds rain
- तं (*taṃ*)—that famous Agni (praise him)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praisers, praise that Agni: who, as birds sit on trees, is in the fire-sticks made of wood; who is shining; who carries to the gods the oblations of the praisers; who with a crackling sound burns the forest trees; who is the cause of the rain water; who like an ox bearing a burden carries the oblation to the gods with his flames; and who, like the sun shining with great majesty by his radiance, lights up the paths.

##### English translation
(Glorify) him, (worshippers), the divine, like a bird seated upon a tree, demanding sacrificial food, clamorous, wood-consuming, water shedding, like one bearing (the obation) in his mouth, mighty with radiance, simultaneously illuminating the paths, like the great functionary (the sun).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नि यस्य॑ ते ज्रयसा॒नस्या॑जर॒ धक्षो॒र्न वाताः॒ परि॒ संत्यच्यु॑ताः।

### Printed p. 517

> आ रण्वासो युयुधयो न सत्वनं त्रितं नशंत प्र शिषंत  
> इष्टये ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । यस्य । ते । ज्रयसानस्य । अजर । धक्षोः । न । वातः । परि । संति । अच्युताः ।  
> आ । रण्वासः । युयुधयः । न । सत्वनं । त्रितं । नशंत । प्र । शिषंतः । इष्टये ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अजर जरारहिताग्ने ज्रयसानस्य ॥ ज्रयतिर्गत्यर्थः । बाहुलकादस्मादप्यसानच् प्रत्ययः ॥ गमनशीलस्य धक्षोः ॥ दहेः सन् । द्विर्वचनप्रकरणे छंदसि वेति
> वक्तव्यं । का. ६-१-८-१ । इति द्विर्वचनाभावः । तदंतादुप्रत्ययः । अरण्यदहनेच्छोर्यस्य ते तव स्वभूता अच्युताः शत्रुभिरच्यवनीयाः प्रभावा वाता न वायुव
> इव वि परि संति सर्वतो विशेषेण वर्तंते ॥ संति । अस्तेर्लट् । यद्योगादनिघातः ॥ युयुधयो न ॥ युधेः किन्मत्तयः ॥ योद्धार इव रण्वासः शीघ्रं
> गंतारः शब्दायमाना वर्त्विज इष्टये यागाय प्र शिषंतः प्रकर्षेण सिषंतः
> सिषासंतः संभक्तुमिच्छंतः सत्वनं बलवंतं त्रितं त्रिष्वाहवनीयादिषु स्थानेषु
> ततं विस्तृतं त्वामा नशंत । स्तुतिभिर्हविर्भिश्च व्याप्नुवंति । आज् पूर्वो नशिर्व्याप्तिकर्मा । आक्षण आनडिति व्याप्तिकर्मसु पाठात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O ageless Agni, who art without old age: ज्रयसानस्य (*jrayasānasya*), of one inclined to going (the root ज्रय (*jraya*) has the sense of going; the affix asāna is added to it through variety of usage); धक्षोः (*dhakṣoḥ*), of one desiring to burn (from दह (*daha*) with san; the doubling is absent by the rule cited, द्विर्वचनप्रकरणे छंदसि वेति वक्तव्यं (*dvirvacanaprakaraṇe chaṃdasi veti vaktavyaṃ*), and the affix u follows). Of thee who desirest to burn the forest, thy own unfailing powers, which enemies cannot dislodge, वाता न (*vātā na*) like winds, spread round on every side, वि परि संति (*vi pari saṃti*). युयुधयो न (*yuyudhayo na*): like warriors, the रण्वासः (*raṇvāsaḥ*), quick-going, sounding priests, desiring प्र शिषंतः (*pra śiṣaṃtaḥ*) (siṣāsantaḥ: wishing to attain) for the sacrifice (इष्टये (*iṣṭaye*)), pervade thee, mighty and spread in the three places such as the Āhavanīya (त्रितं (*tritaṃ*)), आ नशंत (*ā naśaṃta*), with praises and with oblations. The root *naś* preceded by आज् (*āj*) has the sense of pervading, as it is read among roots of the sense of pervading in the list beginning आक्षण आनडिति (*ākṣaṇa ānaḍiti*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अजर (*ajara*)—O Agni, free from old age, that is ever young
- जयसानस्य (*jayasānasya*)—of one inclined to going
- धक्षोः (*dhakṣoḥ*)—of one who burns the forest
- यस्य ते (*yasya te*)—of thee, whose
- अच्युताः (*acyutāḥ*)—powers not obstructed by enemies
- वाता न (*vātā na*)—like the wind
- वि परि संति (*vi pari saṃti*)—surround thee on all sides
- युयुधो न (*yuyudho na*)—like warriors
- रण्वासः (*raṇvāsaḥ*)—priests who move swiftly or who make the sound of reciting mantras
- इष्टये (*iṣṭaye*)—the sacrifice
- प्र शिषंतः (*pra śiṣaṃtaḥ*)—desiring to carry it out
- सत्वनं (*satvanaṃ*)—possessed of strength
- त्रितं (*tritaṃ*)—who dwellest in the three places such as the Āhavanīya
- आ नशंत (*ā naśaṃta*)—approach thee with praises and the like and with the oblation

### Printed p. 518

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O ageless Agni, your unobstructed powers (you who are swift-moving and burn the forest trees) surround you on every side like the wind. Like warriors, the priests, running to and fro and making a sound (the chanting of mantras), desire to carry out the sacrifice. They approach you, who are mighty and established in the three places beginning with the Āhavanīya, with oblations and with hymns of praise.

##### English translation
O imperishable Agni, the invincible winds spread around you (who are) rapid in movement, and desirous of consuming (the forest); like comba-tants (the priests) calling aloud. anxious to bestow (the oblation) glorify you, the mighty, stationed in the three (altars).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स इद॒ग्निः कण्व॑तमः॒ कण्व॑सखा॒र्यः पर॒स्यांत॑रस्य॒ तरु॑षः ।  
> अ॒ग्निः पा॑तु गृण॒तो अ॒ग्निः सू॒रीन॒ग्निर्द॑दातु॒ तेषा॒मवो॑ नः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । इत् । अग्निः । कण्वतमः । कण्वसखा । अर्यः । परस्य । अंतरस्य । तरुषः ।  
> अग्निः । पातु । गृणतः । अग्निः । सूरीन् । अग्निः । ददातु । तेषां । अवः । नः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कण्वतमः ॥ कणतेः शब्दार्थादशिपुषीत्यादिना क्वन्मत्तयः ॥ अतिशयेन स्तोता
> अत एव कण्वसखा ॥ बहुव्रीहित्वात्समासांतोदात्ताभावः ॥ कण्वाः स्तोतारः सखायो
> यस्य स तादृशोऽर्यः ॥ स्वामिन्यंतोदात्तत्वं वक्तव्यं । पा. ३-१-१०३-१ । इत्यंदोदात्तत्वं ॥ स्वामी सर्वस्येश्वरः स इत् स एवाग्निः परस्य च प्रकृष्टस्य च बाह्यस्यांतरस्याव्यवहितस्य समीपे वर्तमानस्य शत्रोस्तरुषस्तारयिता विनाशयिता भवति ।
> सोऽग्निर्गृणतः स्तोत्थानस्मान्पातु । रक्षतु ॥ ग्य शब्दे क्रादिकः । शतुरनुमो नद्य-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

कण्वतमः (*kaṇvatamaḥ*) is formed from the root कण (*kaṇa*) in the sense of sound; it means one who praises in the highest degree. For that very reason he is कण्वसखा (*kaṇvasakhā*): the Kaṇvas, the praisers, are his friends. अर्यः (*aryaḥ*) is the lord, the master of all. That same Agni is the destroyer (तरुषः (*taruṣaḥ*)) of the enemy, whether far off (outside) or inward, that is, near at hand and unseparated. That Agni protects us who praise him. Likewise सूरीन् (*sūrīn*), from the root षू (*ṣū*) in the sense of impelling: may he protect us, who send forth oblations.

> जादी इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥ तथा सूरीन् ॥ षू प्रेरणे ॥ हविषां प्रेरयित्कानस्मानक्षतु । किंच तेषामेषां नोऽस्माकमवो रक्षणमन्नं वाग्निर्ददाशु ।
> प्रयच्छतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May he protect those who impel the oblations. Further, may Agni give to us, these people, protection (अवः (*avaḥ*)) or food.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कण्वतमः (*kaṇvatamaḥ*)—one who praises (the gods) (and therefore)
- कण्वसखा (*kaṇvasakhā*)—friend of the people who praise
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—lord of all
- सः इत् अग्निः (*saḥ it agniḥ*)—that very Agni
- परस्य (*parasya*)—of the one who is far off, that is, outside
- अंतरस्य (*aṃtarasya*)—of the enemy who is near
- तरुषः (*taruṣaḥ*)—is the destroyer
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- गृणतः (*gṛṇataḥ*)—us who praise him
- पातु (*pātu*)—may he protect
- सूरीन् (*sūrīn*)—and may he protect us also, who offer oblations
- तेषां नः (*teṣāṃ naḥ*)—to us, such as we are
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—protection or food
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- ददातु (*dadātu*)—may he give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That Agni, who himself praises the gods, and therefore is a friend to the people who praise, and is lord of all, destroys the enemy, whether far off or near. May Agni protect us who praise him and offer oblations. May Agni give us protection or food.

##### English translation
Agni, the most earnest of eulogists, the friends of those who praise him, the lord, the destroyer of enemies, whether far off or nigh, may Agni protect those who adore him, may, Agni (protect) those who offer oblations, may Agni give to us:both these protection.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सुपित्र्य । पितुरागतः पित्र्यः ॥ पितुर्यच्च । पा. ४-३-७९ । इति यत्पत्ययः ॥
> शोभनपित्र्य हे अग्ने वाजिंतमायातिशयेनान्नवतेऽत्यंतं बलवते ना ॥ नाद्भस्यॆति
> नुडागमः ॥ सह्यसे सहीयसे शत्रूणामतिशयेनाभिभवित्रॆ जातवेदसे जातप्रज्ञाय
> तुभ्यं त्वां स्तोतुं तृषु क्षिप्रमनु च्यवानः स्तुतिभिरनुगत उद्युक्तोऽस्मि ॥ क्रियार्थोपपदस्य च कर्मणीति जातवेदःशब्दस्य चतुर्थी । सह्यसे । सहस्विञ्चादीयसुनि
> विन्मतोर्लुगितीयसुन ईकारलोपश्चांदसः ॥ अनुद्रे चिदुदकवर्जिते स्थाने ।
> आपदीत्यर्थः । शत्रुभिः संजातायामापदि धृषता शत्रुधर्षणसमर्थेन धन्वनेदात्मीयेन धनुसैवाविष्यते पालकाय सते भूष्णवे ॥ शतुरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥ मंहितमाय पूज्यतमाय दातृतमाय वा ईदृशायाग्नये योऽहं
> वरं वरणीयं हविः प्रयच्छामि सोऽहं स्तुतिमपि तस्मै करोमीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सुपित्र्य (*supitrya*): one who has come from the father is पित्र्यः (*pitryaḥ*); hence "O Agni of good paternal descent." He addresses Agni as वाजिंतमाय (*vājiṃtamāya*), most abounding in food, exceedingly strong, and सह्यसे (*sahyase*), the greatest overcomer of enemies, and जातवेदसे (*jātavedase*), one whose knowledge is born. To praise you I have set out, following with hymns, quickly (तृषु (*tṛṣu*)). The dative for जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*) is by the rule on the object of a word subordinate to an action. अनुद्रे चित् (*anudre cit*) means in a place devoid of water, that is, in distress. When distress arises from enemies, he is the protector (अविष्यते (*aviṣyate*)), the one who is (सते (*sate*)), with his own bow (धन्वना (*dhanvanā*)) that is able to overcome enemies. मंहितमाय (*maṃhitamāya*) means most worthy of worship or most generous. To such an Agni I, who offer the choice (वरं (*varaṃ*)) oblation, also make praise for him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुपित्र्य (*supitrya*)—O Agni, who have excellent parents
- वाजिंतमाय (*vājiṃtamāya*)—exceedingly strong
- सह्यसे (*sahyase*)—who defeat enemies
- जातवेदसे (*jātavedase*)—who know everything; in order to praise you
- तृषु (*tṛṣu*)—quickly
- अनु च्यवानः (*anu cyavānaḥ*)—I am ready, having approached, to praise
- अनुद्रे चित् (*anudre cit*)—in a waterless region or in time of distress
- धृषता (*dhṛṣatā*)—that overcomes enemies
- धन्वना इत् (*dhanvanā it*)—with your bow alone
- अविष्यते सते (*aviṣyate sate*)—who are protecting us
- महिंतमाय (*mahiṃtamāya*)—to Agni, most worshipful or a generous giver
- यः (*yaḥ*)—(the) I who
- वरं (*varaṃ*)—offer the best oblation or hymn

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, who have excellent parents, I have come quickly to your presence and am ready to praise you, who are exceedingly strong, who defeat enemies, and who know everything. In a waterless region, that is, in our time of hardship, to you, most glorious, who protect us with your bow that overcomes enemies,

### Printed p. 521
I offer the best oblation or hymn.

##### English translation
O Agni you have fair ancestors, (I have) arrived quickly to (praise) you, the most bountiful bestower of food, the overcomer (of foes) the Jathavedas, (I who offer) the best to you, the most mighty being, the protector in calamity, with your capable (bow).

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वाग्निर्मर्त्यैः॑ स॒ह सू॒रिभि॒र्वसु॑ ष्टवे॒ सह॑सः सू॒नरो॒ नृभिः॑ ।  
> मि॒त्रासो॒ न ये सुधि॑ता ऋता॒यवो॒ द्यावो॒ न द्यु॒म्मॆर॒भि  
> संति॒ मानु॑षान् ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । अग्निः । मर्त्यैः । सह । सूरिभिः । वसुः । स्तवे । सहसः । सूनरः । नृभिः ।  
> मित्रासः । न । ये । सुधिताः । ऋतयवः । द्यावः । न । द्युम्नैः । अभि । संति ।  
> ।  
> मानुषान् ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सहसो बलस्य सूनरः सुष्टु प्रेरकः । यद्वा । सूनुरित्यस्य वर्णव्यत्ययः ।
> सूनरः सूनुः । बलेन मध्यमानत्वात्तस्य पुत्रः । अग्निर्नृभिः कर्मनेतृभिर्मर्तैर्मनुष्यैः सह सूरिभिर्विद्वद्भिरस्माभिर्वसु धनमभिलक्ष्यनैवं स्तवे । स्तूयते ॥
> वसुष्टव इत्यत्र संहितायां पूर्वपदादिति षत्वं ॥ मित्रासो न सुहृद इव सुधिताः
> सुहितास्त्रप्ताः ॥ दधातेर्निष्ठायां सुधितवसुधितेति निपातितः । सुधितार्थास्त्वर्था
> इति काशिकायामुक्तं ॥ ऋतायवो यज्ञं कामयमानाः ॥ न च्छंदस्य पुत्रस्येति

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सूनरः (*sūnaraḥ*) of सहसः (*sahasaḥ*) (strength) means a good impeller of strength; or else सूनरः (*sūnaraḥ*) is a transposition of letters for सूनुः (*sūnuḥ*), the son, since he is born of the strength of the churning. Agni is praised thus (स्तवे (*stave*)) by us, the wise, together with mortal men, the leaders of the rite, aiming at wealth (वसु (*vasu*)). मित्रासो न (*mitrāso na*) means like friends; सुधिताः (*sudhitāḥ*) means well satisfied, as the Kāśikā says. ऋतायवः (*ṛtāyavaḥ*) means those desiring the sacrifice.

> दीर्घत्वयोः प्रतिषेधः ॥ ईदृशा ये सूरयो द्यावो न द्योतमाना इव
> द्युम्नैः । द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो वान्नं वा । नि. ५-५ । इति यास्कः । अग्निप्रदत्रैर्बलरात्मीय्यैर्यशोभिर्वा मानुषाञ्यात्रवाञ्जनानभि संति अभिभवंति ॥
> यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those wise men who are like shining ones (द्यावो न (*dyāvo na*)) overcome (अभि संति (*abhi saṃti*)) men, the enemy people, by the glories (द्युम्नैः (*dyumnaiḥ*)), the strength or fame given by Agni. On द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*): "द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो वान्नं वा (*dyumnaṃ dyotateryaśo vānnaṃ vā*)" (Ni. 5-5), says Yāska.

### Printed p. 522

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहसः (*sahasaḥ*)—of strength
- सूनरः (*sūnaraḥ*)—the son
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—the leaders of the rite
- मर्त्यैः सह (*martyaiḥ saha*)—together with men
- सूरिभिः (*sūribhiḥ*)—by us, the discerning
- वसु (*vasu*)—for the attainment of wealth
- एव (*eva*)—in this manner
- स्तवे (*stave*)—is praised
- मित्रासो न (*mitrāso na*)—like friends
- सुधिताः (*sudhitāḥ*)—satisfied
- ऋतायवः (*ṛtāyavaḥ*)—desiring the sacrificial rite
- ये सूरयः (*ye sūrayaḥ*)—the wise who are such
- द्यावो न (*dyāvo na*)—being like shining ones
- द्युम्नैः (*dyumnaiḥ*)—by the fame or strength obtained from Agni
- मानुषान् (*mānuṣān*)—enemy people
- अभि संति (*abhi saṃti*)—they defeat

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, born of the application of strength, is praised in this way for wealth by men (by us) who are leaders of the rite and discerning. The wise, that is, the discerning, who are satisfied like friends, who desire to perform the sacrificial rite, and who are shining, defeat enemies by the food (strength) or fame obtained from Agni.

##### English translation
In this manner, Agni, the son of strength, is glorified by (us his) wor-shippers, together with pious mortals, for the sake of wealth—(his worshippers) who, like delighted friends, desiring the sacrifice, like shining (ones), over-come (hostile) men through his might.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऊर्जो॑ नपात्सहसाव॒न्नि ति॑ त्वोपस्तु॒तस्य॑ वंदते॒ वृषा॒ वाक् ।  
> त्वां स्तो॑षाम॒ त्वया॑ सु॒वीरा॒ द्राघी॑य॒ आयुः॑ प्रत॒रं  ॑
> दधानाः ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 523

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऊर्जः । नपात् । सहसावन् । इति । त्वा । उपस्तुतस्य । वंदते । वृषा । वाक् ।  
> त्वां । स्तोषाम । त्वया । सुवीराः । द्राघीयः । आयुः । प्रततरं । दधानाः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऊर्जो नपात् । नपादित्यपत्यनाम । अन्नस्य पुत्र । अन्नं वा आज्यमिति
> श्रवणात्तेन प्रवृद्ध्यमानत्वात् । बलस्य ना पुत्र ॥ सुबामंत्रिते परांगवत्सर इत्यूर्ज
> इत्यस्यॆ परांगवद्भावेनामंत्रितत्व आमंत्रितस्य चेति षाष्ठिकमाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ हे
> सहसावन् सहस्विन्नग्ने त्वा त्वामित्येवमुपस्तुतस्यैतन्नामकस्यर्षेर्मम वृषा
> हविषां वर्षदित्री तैः सहिता वाक् स्तुतिर्वंदते । स्तोति ॥ वृषा । इगुपधज्ञेति कः ।
> अजाद्यतष्टाप् ॥ किंच वयं त्वां स्तोषाम । स्तवाम ॥ स्तौतेर्लॆट्यडागमः ॥
> ततस्त्वया सुवीराः शोभनपुत्राः स्याम । द्राघीयो दीर्घतममायुर्जीवनं
> प्रतरमत्यर्थं दधाना धारयंतो भवेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ऊर्जो नपात् (*ūrjo napāt*): नपात् (*napāt*) is a name for offspring; so, son of food, since he grows by it, in accordance with the statement "the ghee is food"; or else son of strength. The vocative ऊर्जः (*ūrjaḥ*) takes the accent on its first syllable by the rule on a vocative. O सहसावन् (*sahasāvan*), mighty Agni: thus the speech (वाक् (*vāk*)), the praise of me, the seer named Upastuta, joined with the oblations that rain down (वृषा (*vṛṣā*)), praises (वंदते (*vaṃdate*)) you. Further, we praise you (स्तोषाम (*stoṣāma*)). Then through you may we be blessed with good sons (सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*)), and may we hold (दधानाः (*dadhānāḥ*)) a very long life (द्राघीयः आयुः (*drāghīyaḥ āyuḥ*)) in the highest degree (प्रतरं (*prataraṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऊर्जोनपात् (*ūrjonapāt*)—who grow by the oblation in the form of food, or son of strength
- सहसावन् (*sahasāvan*)—O Agni, of exceeding strength
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- इति (*iti*)—in this manner
- उपस्तुतस्य (*upastutasya*)—of me, named Upastuta
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—accompanied by the oblation
- वाक् (*vāk*)—the speech in the form of praise
- वंदते (*vaṃdate*)—praises you (and we)
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- स्तोषाम (*stoṣāma*)—praise
- त्वया (*tvayā*)—through you, that is, by your grace (we)
- सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*)—may we become possessed of excellent sons
- द्राघीयः (*drāghīyaḥ*)—for a long time
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—life
- प्रतरं (*prataraṃ*)—exceedingly
- दधानाः (*dadhānāḥ*)—may we sustain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who grow by the oblation, or are the son of strength, and are exceedingly mighty: the speech of me, named Upastuta, in the form of praise, praises you in this way. We too praise you. May we by your grace obtain excellent sons, and may we live an exceedingly good life for a long time.

### Printed p. 524
"Offspring of food! vigorous (Agni)," thus the praise of Upastuta, showering forth oblations, glorifies you. "Let us praise you; through you let us obtain excellent male progeny, enjoing long protracted life."

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इति॑ त्वाग्ने वृष्टि॒हव्य॑स्य पु॒त्रा उ॑पस्तु॒तास॒ ऋष॑योऽवोचन् ।  
> तांश्च॑ पा॒हि गृ॑ण॒तश्च॑ सू॒रीन्व ष॒ड्वष॒ळितू॒र्ध्वासो॑ अनक्ष॒न्न मो॒  
> नम॒ इत्युद्॒ध्वासो॑ अनक्षन् ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इति । त्वा । अग्ने । वृष्टिहव्यस्य । पुत्राः । उपस्तुतासः । ऋषयः । अवोचन् ।  
> तान् । च । पाहि । गृणतः । च । सूरीन् । वषट् । वषट् । इति । ऊर्ध्वासः । अनक्षन् ।  
> नमः । नमः । इति । ऊर्ध्वासः । अनक्षन् ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वा त्वामित्येवमुक्तप्रकारेण वृष्टिहव्यस्यैतन्नामकस्यर्षः पुत्रा
> उपस्तुतास उपस्तुता एतदभिधाना ऋषयः सूक्तद्रष्टारोऽवोचन् । अभ्यष्टुवन् ।
> शानृषींश्च त्वं पाहि । रक्ष ॥ चवायोगे प्रथमेति न निघातः ॥ तथा गृणतः स्तोत्र्यन्
> सूरीन्विदुषश्च पाहि । वषड्वषडिति मंत्रेणोर्ध्वासो हविष्ट्रदानार्थमूर्ध्वमुख.
> हस्ताः संतोऽनक्षन् । व्याप्प्नुवन् । नक्षतिर्व्याप्तिकर्मा । नमो नम इत्येवमूर्ध्वासः स्तोशुमुद्युक्ता अनक्षन् । य उक्तगुणास्तानुभयविधान्यष्टन् स्तोत्र्यन्पालय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, in the manner stated, the sons of the ṛṣi named Vṛṣṭihavya, the ṛṣis named Upastuta, the seers of the sūkta, have praised you. Protect those ṛṣis (the particle च (*ca*) means no accent-lowering occurs on पाहि (*pāhi*)). Protect also the praisers, the learned. With the mantra वषट् वषट् (*vaṣaṭ vaṣaṭ*) they, with faces and hands raised in order to give the oblation, have reached you; नक्षति (*nakṣati*) is a root of pervading. Likewise, with faces raised, ready to praise, saying नमो नम (*namo nama*), they have reached you. Protect the praisers of both kinds who have these qualities.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- इति (*iti*)—in this manner
- वृष्टिहव्यस्य (*vṛṣṭihavyasya*)—of the ṛṣi named Vṛṣṭihavya
- पुत्राः (*putrāḥ*)—the sons
- उपस्तुतासः (*upastutāsaḥ*)—famed by the name Upastuta
- ऋषयः (*ṛṣayaḥ*)—the ṛṣis, seers of the sūkta
- अवोचन् (*avocan*)—have praised
- त्वं च (*tvaṃ ca*)—you also

- तान् (*tān*)—those ṛṣis
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—protect
- गृणतः (*gṛṇataḥ*)—who are praising
- सूरीन् च (*sūrīn ca*)—protect the wise also
- वषट् वषट् (*vaṣaṭ vaṣaṭ*)—uttering the vaṣaṭ-cries "वषट् वषट् (*vaṣaṭ vaṣaṭ*)"
- ऊर्ध्वासः (*ūrdhvāsaḥ*)—the priests holding up their ghee-filled ladles for the offering
- अनक्षन् (*anakṣan*)—have approached you
- ऊर्ध्वासः (*ūrdhvāsaḥ*)—the praisers with faces raised
- नमः नमः (*namaḥ namaḥ*)—saying "namo namaḥ", bowing
- अनक्षन् (*anakṣan*)—have come to you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the ṛṣis, seers of the sūkta, sons of the ṛṣi Vṛṣṭihavya and named Upastuta, have thus praised you. Protect those ṛṣis who are praising. O Agni, the priests, holding up ladles filled with ghee for the offering and uttering the vaṣaṭ-cry, approach you. Likewise the people who praise you have come to you, bowing with "namo namaḥ".

##### English translation
Thus, Agni, the Rishis, the Upastutas, the sons of Vrishtihavya cele-
brated you, and do you protect them and the pious worshippers. With
uplifted faces, calling out vashat! vashat! they reached you; with uplifted
faces they reached you, calling out namas! namas!

## Sūkta 116 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पिबेति नवर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । स्थूरनाम्नः पुत्रोऽग्नियुताख्य ऋषिरग्नियूपाख्यो वा । तथा चानुक्रम्यते । पिब स्थौरोऽग्नियुतोऽग्नियूपो वेति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta पिब (*piba*) has nine ṛks, is the fourth sūkta, in Triṣṭubh metre, addressed to Indra. Its ṛṣi is Agniyuta, son of Sthūra, or Agniyūpa. So the Anukramaṇī says: पिब स्थौरोऽग्नियुतोऽग्नियूपो वेति (*piba sthauro 'gniyuto 'gniyūpo veti*). The viniyoga has been stated already.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning पिब (*piba*) is the fourth sūkta in the tenth anuvāka. It has nine ṛks. Its ṛṣi is Agniyuta or Agniyūpa, son of the ṛṣi named Sthūra; the deity is Indra; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: पिब स्थौरोऽग्नियुतोऽग्नियूपो वा (*piba sthauro 'gniyuto 'gniyūpo vā*). The viniyoga was stated earlier.

### Printed p. 526
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 10; Sūkta 116. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 6; Varga 20, 21. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 9. Ṛṣi: Agniyuta Sthāra, or Agniyūpa Sthāra. Deity: Indra. Metre: Triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पिबा॒ सोमं॑ मह॒त इं॑द्रि॒याय॒ पिबा॑ वृ॒त्राय॒ हंत॑वे  
> शविष्ठ ।  
> पिब॑ रा॒ये शव॑से हू॒यमा॑नः॒ पिब॒ मध्व॑स्त्र॒पदिं॒द्रा वृ॑षस्व ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पिब । सोमं । महते । इंद्रियाय । पिब । वृत्राय । हंतने । शविष्ठ ।  
> पिब । राये । शवसे । हूयमानः । पिब । मध्वः । तृपत् । इंद्र । आ । वृषस्व ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं महते प्रभूतायेंद्रियायेंद्रस्यात्मनो जुष्टाय
> वीर्याय सोममस्माभिर्दीयमानं पिब ॥ इंद्रियमिंद्रलिंगेत्यादिनेंद्रियशब्दो यजंतत्वेन निपातितः ॥ हे शविष्ठातिशयेन प्रवृद्ध वृत्राय हंतने वृत्रं
> हंतुं सोमं पिब ॥ क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति वृत्रस्य संप्रदानत्वं ॥ तथा हूयमानोऽस्माभिराहूयमानस्त्वं राये धनाय ॥ ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥ शवसेन्नाय । धनान्नयोः प्रदानाय सोमं पिब । मध्वो मदकरान्सर्वान्नोमान्पिब ॥ वा छंदसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घाभावः । अनंतरं हे इंद्र
> तृपत्तृपोभवन्ना वृषस्व । अस्मदभिलषितान्यासिंच । ददस्व ॥ तृपत् । तृप्ति
> तौदादिकः । अनित्यमागमशासनमिति नुमभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, drink the Soma offered by us for your great इंद्रिय (*iṃdriya*), the vigour dear to you, Indra. O most mighty one, drink the Soma in order to slay Vṛtra (Vṛtra stands as the recipient of the action). Likewise, being invoked by us, drink for riches and for strength, that is, for the giving of wealth and food. Drink all the intoxicating (honeyed) Somas. Then, O Indra, being satisfied, shower down: pour out what we desire, give it.

### Printed p. 527

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra, you) महते (*mahate*)—for great
- इंद्रियाय (*iṃdriyāya*)—valour, that is, for power and capacity
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice offered by us
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- शविष्ठ (*śaviṣṭha*)—O Indra, exceedingly growing
- वृत्राय हंतवे (*vṛtrāya haṃtave*)—for slaying Vṛtra
- पिब (*piba*)—drink the Soma
- हूयमानः (*hūyamānaḥ*)—you, invoked with prayer by us
- राये (*rāye*)—for giving us wealth
- शवसे (*śavase*)—and for giving food
- पिब (*piba*)—drink the Soma
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—sweet, that is, tasty Soma
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- तृपत् (*tṛpat*)—satisfied by drinking Soma
- आ वृषस्व (*ā vṛṣasva*)—fulfil our wishes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, drink this Soma juice offered by us for the attainment of exceeding strength and capacity, or valour. O growing Indra, drink Soma also in order to slay Vṛtra. Invoked by us with prayer, drink this sweet and tasty Soma juice so as to give us wealth and food. O Indra, satisfied by the Soma, fulfil our requests.

##### English translation
Drink (Indra) the Soma for the invigoration of your organs, drink most mighty one, for the death of Vritra; drink when invoked for wealth, for strength; drink of the exhilarating beverage, and being satisfied, Indra, shower down (blessings).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒स्य पि॑ब क्षु॒मतः॒ प्रस्थि॑त॒स्येंद्र॒ सोम॑स्य॒ वर॒मा सु॒तस्य॑ ।  
> स्व॒स्ति॒दा मन॑सा मादयस्वार्वाची॒नो रे॒वते॒ सौभ॑गाय ॥२॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्य । पिब । क्षुमतः । प्रस्थितस्य । इंद्र । सोमस्य । वरं । आ । सुतस्य ।

### Printed p. 528

> स्वस्तिदाः । मनसा । मादयस्व । अर्वाचीनः । रेवते । सौभगाय ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र क्षुमतः स्तुतियुक्तस्य यद्वा हवीरूपान्नवतः प्रस्थितस्य हविर्धानादुत्तरवेदिं प्रति प्रस्थापितस्य सुतस्याभिषुतस्य सोमस्य वरं वरणीयं त्वदीयं
> भागमाभिमुख्येन पिब ॥ प्रस्थितस्य । तिष्ठतेः कर्मणि निष्ठा । गतिरनंतर इति गतेः
> प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ ततः स्वस्तिदाः कल्याणस्य दाता त्वं मनसांतःकरणेन मादयस्व ।
> हृष्टो भव । यद्वा । अस्मानपि हृष्टान्कुरु । तदेवोच्यते । रेवते धनवते सौभगाय
> सौभाग्याय तदस्मभ्यं दातुमर्वाचीनोऽभिमुखांचनो भव ॥ विभाषांचेरदिक्ष्त्रियामिति खः । रयिशब्दान्मतुपश्यंदसीर इति वत्वं । रयेर्मत् बहुलमिति
> संप्रसारणं । पूर्वरूपत्वे गुणः । सौभगाय । उद्धात्रादिषु सुभग मंत्र इति
> पठ्यते। तस्योत्तरपदस्य हृद्भगेति वृद्धिर्नॆष्यते सर्वविधीनां छंदसि विकल्पितत्वात् ।
> इत्त्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, drink your choice share of the Soma that is क्षुमतः (*kṣumataḥ*), accompanied by praise, or else furnished with food in the form of oblation; प्रस्थित (*prasthita*), sent forth from the oblation-holder to the Uttaravedi; and pressed. Then, giver of welfare, be delighted in mind; or else make us delighted. For this is said: be turned towards us to give us wealth and good fortune.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- क्षुमतः (*kṣumataḥ*)—that is accompanied by praise, or in the form of oblation
- प्रस्थितस्य (*prasthitasya*)—placed on the Uttaravedi
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—of which the Soma plants have been pounded and pressed
- अस्य सोमस्य (*asya somasya*)—of this Soma juice
- वरं (*varaṃ*)—the share due to you
- आ (*ā*)—seated before us
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- स्वस्तिदाः (*svastidāḥ*)—you who bring welfare
- मनसा (*manasā*)—wholeheartedly
- मादयस्व (*mādayasva*)—be delighted, or make us delighted
- रेवते (*revate*)—to make us wealthy
- सौभगाय (*saubhagāya*)—and to bring good fortune
- अर्वाचीनः (*arvācīnaḥ*)—be turned towards us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, drink the share due to you of this Soma juice in the form of oblation, which is placed on the Uttaravedi, consecrated by mantras, and pressed from the pounded Soma plants. You who give what is best, be delighted by the Soma, or make us delighted. Sit facing us, in order to give us wealth and bring auspiciousness.

##### English translation
Drink, Indra, your excellent portion of this renowned Soma effused and poured forth ; the giver of prosperity, be delighted in your mind, (be) turned towards us to bestow riches and happiness.
