##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्र पादशब्दो भागवचनः । एकपादेकभागधनः पुरुषो द्विपदो द्विगुणधनस्य मार्गं भूयः ॥ तृतीयायाः सुः ॥ भूयसा कालेन वि चक्रमे । विविधं
> गच्छति ॥ वेः पादविहरणे । पा. १-३-४१ । इत्यात्मनेपदं ॥ तथा द्विपात्पुरुषस्त्रिपादं
> त्रिभागधनं पुरुषं पश्चादभ्येति । अभिगच्छति । चतुष्पाच्चतुर्भागधनस्तु द्विपदां ।
> बहुवचनादेकपादादय उपलक्ष्यंते । एकपादधनादीनां पंक्तीरभिस्वरेऽभिगमने
> संपश्यन् सम्यगीक्षमाणः सन्नुपतिष्ठमान एति । गच्छमानो भवति । अन्नोन्यापेक्षया
> सर्व उत्तमाधमाः । तस्मात्त्वमहमेव धनवानिति न मन्ये किंत्वतिथिभ्यो धनानि
> ददस्वेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here the word पाद (*pāda*) means "part". A man who has one part of wealth takes a longer time to cover the path of the man who has a two-fold wealth, and moves along it in various ways. In the same way the man of two parts comes up after the man who has three parts of wealth, and the man of four parts of wealth goes towards those who have fewer. By the plural in द्विपदां (*dvipadāṃ*) those with one foot and so on are also indicated. At the approach he goes on, looking properly at the ranks of those who have one part of wealth and so on, and proceeding to them. All are higher or lower in relation to one another. Therefore one should not think "I alone am wealthy", but should give wealth to guests. That is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एकपात् (*ekapāt*)—one who has only one foot
- द्विपदः (*dvipadaḥ*)—than a man who has two feet (in covering a road, that is, when walking)
- भूयः (*bhūyaḥ*)—a longer time
- वि चक्रमे (*vi cakrame*)—he walks (and likewise)
- द्विपात् (*dvipāt*)—one who has two feet
- त्रिपादं (*tripādaṃ*)—one who has three feet
- पश्चात् (*paścāt*)—afterwards, that is, still more slowly
- अभि एति (*abhi eti*)—approaches
- चतुष्पात् (*catuṣpāt*)—one who has four feet
- अभिस्वरे (*abhisvare*)—at the time of travelling
- द्विपदां (*dvipadāṃ*)—also those who have one and two feet
- संपश्यन् (*saṃpaśyan*)—looking, that is, drawing near
- उपतिष्ठमानः (*upatiṣṭhamānaḥ*)—overtaking them
- एति (*eti*)—goes ahead

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In covering a road, that is, in walking, one who has only one foot cannot keep pace with one who has two feet, and needs more time to reach a given place. In the same way one who has two feet needs more time than one who has three. But one who has four feet leaves behind those who have one, two or three feet, and goes ahead of everyone in travelling.

##### English translation
He who has but one foot takes a longer time on a journey than he who has two ; he who has two feet comes after him who has three; he who has four feet comes up overtaking two-footed (and three-fooied), beholding their traces as he passes by.

### Printed p. 567

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk and in the next, as in the previous Ṛk, the seer describes through illustrations the difference between the giver and the miser. Here Sāyaṇa explains the word पाद (*pāda*) as "part". Accordingly, one who has two shares of wealth is superior to one who has one share; or one who gives two parts in gift is superior to a man who gives one part. In the same way one who gives three parts is superior to one who gives two parts. One who gives four shares goes ahead of all these, that is, he is superior to all. That is the meaning.

> स॒मौ चि॒द्धस्तौ॒ न स॒मं वि॑विष्टः संमा॒तरा॑ चि॒न्नस॒मं दु॑हाते ।  
> य॒मयो॑श्चि॒न्न स॒मा वी॒र्या॑णि ज्ञा॒ती चि॒त्संतौ॒ न स॒मं  ॑
> पृणीतः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> समौ । चित् । हस्तौ । न । समं । विविष्टः । संमातरा । चित् । न । समं । दुहाते इति ।  
> यमयोः । चित् । न । समा । वीर्याणि । ज्ञाती इति । चित् । संतौ । न । समं ।  
> पृणीतः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अतिथिभ्यो धनमप्रयच्छन्नपि मम भ्राता दास्यतीति चेत् तत्र हेतुमाह ।
> समौ चिद्दस्तौ समावपि समं समानं न विविष्टः । कार्यं न व्याप्नुतः ॥ विष्णु
> व्याप्तौ जौहोत्यादिकः । संज्ञापूर्वकस्य विधेरनित्यत्वादभ्यासस्य गुणाभावः ॥ तथा
> संमातरा वत्सस्य मातर्ौ धेनू समे अपि समं समानं पयो न दुहाते । यम.
> योश्चित् सहजातयोः पुत्रयोरपि समा समानि वीर्याणि न संति । तस्माज्जाती
> चिदेकस्मिन्कुले संतौ जातावपि समं न पृणीतः । न प्रयच्छतः । तस्माद्यस्य धनमस्ति
> स एव दद्यादित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Suppose one says: "Even if I give no wealth to guests, my brother will give." Sāyaṇa gives the reason against this. The two hands, though equal, do not accomplish equal work. Two cows that are mothers of calves, though alike, do not yield equal milk. Of twins, born together, the powers are not equal. Therefore two kinsmen born in one family do not give equally. So only the man who has wealth should give. That is the meaning.

### Printed p. 568

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हस्तौ (*hastau*)—the two hands
- समौ चित् (*samau cit*)—though alike (in shape and form)
- समं (*samaṃ*)—equal work
- न विविष्टः (*na viviṣṭaḥ*)—do not perform
- सं मातरा चित् (*saṃ mātarā cit*)—though two cows, mothers of calves, are of one kind
- समं (*samaṃ*)—equally
- न दुहाते (*na duhāte*)—do not yield milk
- यमयोश्चित् (*yamayościt*)—even in twin children born of one mother at one time
- समा (*samā*)—equal
- वीर्याणि (न) (*vīryāṇi (na)*)—there are no equal strength and capacity (likewise)
- ज्ञाती चित् संतौ (*jñātī cit saṃtau*)—kinsmen or brothers born in one family, that is, in one house, or of the same father and mother
- समं (*samaṃ*)—equally
- न पृणीतः (*na pṛṇītaḥ*)—do not give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Though the two hands are alike, their works are not alike; cows that have calved, though alike, do not both yield milk equally; twin children do not have the same kind of strength and capacity; kinsmen or those born in one family are not equal in giving.

##### English translation
The two hands are alike, but they do not perform the same work; two cows calving at the same time do not yield the same milk; two twins have not the same strength; two persons of the same family do not display equal liberality.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

A man has two hands. To look at, they are alike in shape and form. But in work they do not have equal strength. The strength that the right hand has, the left hand does not have.

Two cows of like shape and like age do not give milk equally. One cow gives much milk, the other gives only a little. Though no difference is seen to the eye, cows give milk according to their nature.

Twin children born of one mother are alike to look at, with no difference in shape or form. But a difference is seen in their strength, capacity and intelligence.

### Printed p. 569

In the same way, among sons born to the same father and mother in one house, and among other relatives, the same kind of quality is not found. So too among brothers. One is a generous giver, another is a miser and covetous.

In the work called Ṛgvidhāna, said to have been composed by the great sage Śaunaka, the use (viniyoga) of this sūkta is stated thus:

न वा उ देवा इत्येतज्जपेत नियतव्रतः । अन्नं विंदति सर्वत्र यत्र यत्रोपतिष्ठति ॥ पाप्मोपहतमात्मानं यो मन्येत विचक्षणः । स जपेन्नियतो भूत्वा लघु मन्येत पाप्मना । वाचं प्रपद्येद्याक्कामो जुह्वदाशु जपन्निमाः । (*na vā u devā ityetajjapeta niyatavrataḥ | annaṃ viṃdati sarvatra yatra yatropatiṣṭhati ‖ pāpmopahatamātmānaṃ yo manyeta vicakṣaṇaḥ | sa japenniyato bhūtvā laghu manyeta pāpmanā | vācaṃ prapadyedyākkāmo juhvadāśu japannimāḥ |*) (Ṛgvidhāna, Adhyāya 4, Śloka 16-18)

If a man tormented by hunger, having become pure, mutters this sūkta beginning न वा उ देवाः (*na vā u devāḥ*), he obtains food and other nourishment in all places. A man who doubts that he has committed some sin, if he mutters this sūkta with restraint, becomes free from sin. A man who desires wealth of speech, if he recites the mantras of this sūkta and offers oblations in the fire, quickly obtains success.

## Sūkta 118 (Maṇḍala 10)

**Introduction**
The deity of this sūkta is Rakṣohā Agni. Though the matter of Rakṣohā Agni occurs here and there in many Ṛks, the sūktas that praise this deity chiefly are three: कृणुष्पपाजः (*kṛṇuṣpapājaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-4), रक्षोहणं वाजिनं (*rakṣohaṇaṃ vājinaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-87) and अग्ने हंसि न्यगत्रिणं (*agne haṃsi nyagatriṇaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-118). For these three sūktas Rakṣohā Agni is the deity. It is the custom to recite the sūktas that praise Rakṣohā Agni, so that the molestation of the hosts of Rākṣasas may not occur in sacrifices and the like. The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, in the context of the churning of fire, says that if at the time of churning fire is not produced from the araṇis, one should consider the molestation of the Rākṣasa hosts to be the cause, and should recite the Rākṣasa-destroying sūkta अग्ने हंसि (*agne haṃsi*), which is in the Gāyatrī metre. We have said this in describing the rite of fire-churning.

In Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-124, Indra, Soma and others are called destroyers of Rākṣasas, and that sūkta too is called a Rākṣasa-destroying sūkta. The epithet रक्षोहाः (*rakṣohāḥ*) sometimes applies also to Soma, as in रक्षोहा विश्वचर्षणिः (*rakṣohā viśvacarṣaṇiḥ*) (9-1-2) and the like. In the present sūkta

### Printed p. 570

there are matters concerning Jātavedas in the form of Agni, Rakṣohā Agni, the Rākṣasa hosts, bhūtas, piśācas and yātudhānas; hence a fuller account of them is necessary.

Jātavedas: The Nirukta-writers have explained this word thus: जातानि वेद, जातानि नैनं विदुः जाते जाते विद्यत इति वा, जातविद्यो जातधनः जातविद्यो जातप्रज्ञानः यत्तज्जातः पशूनविंदतेति तज्जातवेदसो जातवेदस्त्वं (*jātāni veda, jātāni nainaṃ viduḥ jāte jāte vidyata iti vā, jātavidyo jātadhanaḥ jātavidyo jātaprajñānaḥ yattajjātaḥ paśūnaviṃdateti tajjātavedaso jātavedastvaṃ*) इति ब्राह्मणं (*iti brāhmaṇaṃ*).
The nature of Jātavedas is stated in the Bṛhaddevatā thus:

इहाग्निभूतस्तृषिभिर्लोके स्तुतिभिरीळितः। जातवेदाः स्तुतो मध्यॆ स्तुतो वैश्वानरो दिवि ॥ (*ihāgnibhūtastṛṣibhirloke stutibhirīḷitaḥ| jātavedāḥ stuto madhyè stuto vaiśvānaro divi ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 1-67)

This verse says that the seers call the Agni that is on the earth Jātavedas, and the Agni that is in the heavenly world Vaiśvānara. Continuing the same explanation:

वैश्वानरं श्रितोह्यग्निरग्निं वैश्वानरः श्रितः । अनयोर्जातवेदास्तु तथैते जातवेदसि ॥ (*vaiśvānaraṃ śritohyagniragniṃ vaiśvānaraḥ śritaḥ | anayorjātavedāstu tathaite jātavedasi ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 1-97)

It is explained that Agni is contained in Vaiśvānara and Vaiśvānara in Agni, and Jātavedas is contained in both these forms; and that these two forms are different parts of Jātavedas. Having thus stated the places of Jātavedas in the first chapter, the Bṛhaddevatā in the second chapter gives the derivation of the nature of Jātavedas thus:

भूतानि वेद यज्ञातो जातवेदाथ कथ्यते । यच्चैष जातविद्योs भूत् वित्तं जातोऽधिवेत्ति वा ॥ (*bhūtāni veda yajñāto jātavedātha kathyate | yaccaiṣa jātavidyos bhūt vittaṃ jāto 'dhivetti vā ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 2-30)
विद्यते सर्वभूतैर्हि यद्वा जातः पुनःपुनः । तेन्नैष मध्यभागेंद्रो जातवेदा इति स्तुतः ॥ (*vidyate sarvabhūtairhi yadvā jātaḥ punaḥpunaḥ | tennaiṣa madhyabhāgeṃdro jātavedā iti stutaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 2-31)

The Bṛhaddevatā derives it thus: Agni is praised as Jātavedas, like Indra who dwells in the middle world, because he knows everything at the moment he is born; or because knowledge arose in him; or because at the moment of birth he knows and possesses all wealth; or because, each time he is born again, he is known by all beings. In accordance with this, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa too explains the nature of this Agni thus:

### Printed p. 571

यः संवत्सरं जातः स्यात्पाणो वा अग्निस्तमेतद्विभर्त्यथ ह वै रेतः सिक्तं प्राणोऽन्ववरोहति तद्विंदते तद्यज्जातं जातं विंदते तस्माज्जातवेदाः ॥ (*yaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ jātaḥ syātpāṇo vā agnistametadvibhartyatha ha vai retaḥ siktaṃ prāṇo 'nvavarohati tadviṃdate tadyajjātaṃ jātaṃ viṃdate tasmājjātavedāḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 9-5-16-8)

It says that Agni, in the form of the vital breath, pervades by his power all the beings that are born, and therefore is called Jātavedas. The Upaniṣads describe this Jātavedas, who is to be worshipped in the sacrificial house, as Brahman, the Self of the universe:

विश्वरूपं हरिणं जातवेदसं परायणं ज्योतिरेकं तपंतं (*viśvarūpaṃ hariṇaṃ jātavedasaṃ parāyaṇaṃ jyotirekaṃ tapaṃtaṃ*) (Pra. U. 1-8) **NOTE**

The Praśna Upaniṣad says that the sun rises, he who has the form of the universe, has a thousand rays, is all-knowing, is the refuge of the whole world, is known by the wise, and is the inner self of all beings. And:

अरण्योर्निहितो जातवेदा गर्भ इव सुभृतो गर्भिणीभिः । दिवे दिव ईड्यो जागृवद्भिर्हविष्मद्भिर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः । (*araṇyornihito jātavedā garbha iva subhṛto garbhiṇībhiḥ | dive diva īḍyo jāgṛvadbhirhaviṣmadbhirmanuṣyebhiragniḥ |*) (Ka. U. 1-4-8) **NOTE**

The Kaṭha Upaniṣad describes that Jātavedas who, abiding between the araṇis at the adhiyajña, enjoys all oblations; whom yogis, as pregnant women with affection nourish and rear their unborn child, hold in their hearts and meditate upon as the Supreme Person; and towards whom, as the worshipful Agni, sacrificers offer oblations, as Parabrahman, the Self of the universe. In the same sequence, the Kaṭha text states the very matter described in Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-29-2. Thus all the śrutis praise him as being called Jātavedas because he is all-knowing, all-pervading, the support of all and the most excellent of all.

The deity of this sūkta is Agni Rakṣohā; that is, Agni who destroys the hosts of Rākṣasas, who obstruct sacrifices, such as bhūtas and piśācas. Yāska, explaining the word रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*), has given the derivation:

रक्षो रक्षितव्यमस्मात् । रहसि क्षणोतीति वा । रात्रौ नक्षत इति ना ॥ (*rakṣo rakṣitavyamasmāt | rahasi kṣaṇotīti vā | rātrau nakṣata iti nā ‖*) (Ni. 4-18)

That is: the host of beings called Rakṣas devours men; our body must be protected from it, and because it must be protected it is called रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*). Or, because it harms men in a lonely place where no one is, or in the dark, it is called रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*). Or, because it moves about at night, it is called रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*). Thus three kinds

### Printed p. 572
…a threefold explanation has been given. The word *rakṣas* differs from the word *rākṣasa*. Rākṣasas are particular beings, of human form or of some other terrible form that can be seen by the eye. They are of evil nature, always inflicting harm on good people and obstructing good rites. The word *rakṣas* denotes beings that cannot be seen by the eye: ghosts, spirits, goblins and the like (Demons, evil spirits &c). Their nature is to harm men and to obstruct good rites such as sacrifices. It is customary, in sacrifices and in other rites, to pray to Agni to remove their molestation and protect us. The Agni who removes this kind of molestation is called Rakṣohā-Agni.

The goblins or ghosts that dwell on earth are the enemies of men. The class-name that denotes them is *rakṣas*. This word occurs more than fifty times, in the singular and the plural. In general it occurs together with some deity, either as a prayer or as praise. In the hymns 7-104 and 10-87 they are the very subject. The words *rakṣasaḥ*, *yātu*, *yātudhāna* and the like indicate them here. Since *rakṣasaḥ* is the name of deities (?) and goblins and all of these, it may be taken as the class-name, and *yātu* as a sub-class name.

These goblins or ghosts have the forms of dogs, vultures, owls and other birds (7-104-20 to 22). In the form of birds they fly about at night (7-104-8). Taking the form of a brother, husband or lover, they approach women and wish to destroy their children (10-162-5). In the form of a dog or an ape they lie in wait to fall upon women (A. Ve. 4-37-11)**NOTE**. Therefore pregnant women and children are exposed to harm from them (A. Ve. 8-6). At the time of marriage they move about around the bride, and shoot small arrows into the air to pierce their eyes (Mā. Gṛ. Sū. 1-10)**NOTE**. Their form and so on are described in the Atharvaveda itself. They mostly take on human form, and their limbs such as head, eyes and heart are mentioned; but some deformity is always there: three heads, two mouths, four eyes, five feet, no fingers, feet turned backwards, or horns on the hands, and so on (A. Ve. 8-6; Hi. Gṛ. Sū. 23-7)**NOTE**. Blue, yellow and green goblins are also mentioned (A. Ve. 19-22-4, 5). Among them too there are males and females, families and kings (A. Ve. 5-22-12; Hi. Gṛ. Sū. 2-3-7); they too are mortal (A. Ve. 6-3-2-2; etc.).

### Printed p. 573
The Yātudhānas eat the flesh of men and horses and drink cow's milk (10-86-16, 17). To satisfy their craving for blood and flesh they attack men; this attack is generally by entering into them. There is a prayer to Agni to keep the rākṣasas from entering those who support (the sacrifice) (8-48-20). A goblin presiding over disease, flying hither and thither, enters men (A. Ve. 7-76-4). These ghosts and spirits generally enter us through our mouth when we eat or drink (A. Ve. 5-29-6 to 8); they also enter by other doors (A. Ve. 8-6-3). No sooner have they entered than they tear and eat the man's flesh and cause disease (A. Ve. 5-29-5, 10). They cause madness and destroy the power of speech (A. Ve. 6-101-3 **NOTE**; Hi. Gṛ. Sū. 1-15-5). They invade the dwellings of men (Kau. Sū. 13-5-9)**NOTE**. Some ghosts, in the evening, dance around houses, braying like asses, or roam in forests, or laugh loudly or drink from skulls (A. Ve. 8-6-10, 11, 14; Hi. Gṛ. Sū. 2-3-3). Their time of roaming is night or evening (7-104-8). In the east their sport does not go on; the rising sun drives them away there (Tai. Saṃ. 1-6-6-3). A falling meteor is thought to be the form of a ghost (Kau. Sū. 125-9). As the pitch-dark of the new-moon night is suited to the roaming of the spirits of the dead, so it is also the favourable time for goblins (A. Ve. 1-161; 4-36-3).

Nothing endangers sacrifices as they do. In sacrifices fit for the gods the goblins cause defects and omissions, and the Yātudhānas scatter the offered oblations about (7-104-21 **NOTE**). They cannot bear the sight of a hymn of praise (10-182-3). There is a prayer to Agni to burn the ghosts and others so that no curse may touch the sacrifice (1-76-3). There is a mantra by which, through the magic of the Yātudhānas and of the troops of rākṣasas, an enemy's sacrifice is made to flourish (A. Ve. 7-70-2). In the form of departed spirits they come as obstacles to the food and water offered to the dead (A. Ve. 18-2-28; compare Vā. Saṃ. 1-29). In the Purāṇas it is common that these troops of rakṣas (treated as rākṣasas) trouble yogins.

Agni, who removes darkness and is the master of the sacrifice, is bound in enmity with them. One prays to Agni himself: burn them, drive them off, or destroy them (10-87-3, 6 etc.). From this very work the name "रक्षोहा (*rakṣohā*)" has come to Agni and to some other deities.

### Printed p. 574
These ghosts are harmful not only by their own nature; they also cause harm when impelled by others. The word *rakṣoyujaḥ* (those who impel rākṣasas) is found (6-62-9), and here and there are the ghosts and Yātus of sorcerers (7-104-23; 8-60-20). One troubled by a ghost sent by an enemy may drive them away by making an offering to Yaviṣṭha Agni (Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-3-2); and the ghosts themselves are commanded to swallow the very one who sent them (A. Ve. 2-2-4).

In the sense of ghosts the word *rakṣas* is used in both masculine and feminine. In the neuter it also means danger. It may be from the root *rakṣ* (to trouble) (*ṛkṣā*, dangerous), but this use is very rare. It may also be from the ordinary *rakṣ*, to protect; in that case *rakṣas* means "that which is to be guarded against".

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्ने हंसीति नवर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तममहीयुगोत्रस्योरुक्षयस्यार्षं
> गायत्रं । रक्षोहाग्निर्देवता । तथा चानुक्रम्यते । अग्ने हंस्युरुक्षय आमहीयव
> आग्नेयं राक्षोघ्नं गायत्रं त्विति ॥ मध्यमानेऽग्नावजायमान इदमनुवक्तव्यं ।
> सूत्रितं च । अजायमाने त्वेतस्मिन्नेवावसानेऽग्ने हंसि न्यत्रिणामिति सूक्तमावपेत ।
> आ. २-१६ । इति ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोरपि गायत्रे छंदसीदं सूक्तं । सूत्रितं
> च । अग्ने हंस्यग्निं हिन्वंतु नः । आ. ४-१३ । इति ॥ दशमेऽहनि धिष्ण्यांगाराभिविहरण
> आद्या जप्या । सूत्रितं च । परि त्वाग्ने पुरं वयमित्येतस्याः स्थानेऽग्ने हंसि
> न्यत्रिणं । आ. ८-१२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This sūkta, beginning अग्ने हंसि (*agne haṃsi*), has nine Ṛks; its seer is Urukṣaya of the Āmahīya (gotra)**NOTE**, the metre is Gāyatrī, the deity Rakṣohā Agni. He quotes the Anukramaṇī: अग्ने हंस्युरुक्षय आमहीयव आग्नेयं राक्षोघ्नं गायत्रं त्विति ॥ (*agne haṃsyurukṣaya āmahīyava āgneyaṃ rākṣoghnaṃ gāyatraṃ tviti ‖*). Uses: when Agni, though churned, is not born, this sūkta is to be recited, according to the sūtra अजायमाने त्वेतस्मिन्नेवावसानेऽग्ने हंसि न्यत्रिणामिति सूक्तमावपेत । (*ajāyamāne tvetasminnevāvasāne 'gne haṃsi nyatriṇāmiti sūktamāvapeta |*) (Ā. 2-16). It is also used in the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra, among the verses in Gāyatrī metre, according to अग्ने हंस्यग्निं हिन्वंतु नः (*agne haṃsyagniṃ hinvaṃtu naḥ*) (Ā. 4-13). On the tenth day, at the scattering of coals at the dhiṣṇyas, its first Ṛk is to be muttered, according to परि त्वाग्ने पुरं वयमित्येतस्याः स्थानेऽग्ने हंसि न्यत्रिणं । (*pari tvāgne puraṃ vayamityetasyāḥ sthāne 'gne haṃsi nyatriṇaṃ |*) (Ā. 8-12).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, "अग्ने हंसि (*agne haṃsi*)", is the sixth sūkta in the tenth anuvāka. It contains nine Ṛks. Its seer is Urukṣaya of the Ahīyu gotra; the deity is Rakṣohā Agni; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated: अग्ने हंस्युरुक्षय आमहीयव आग्नेयं राक्षोघ्नं गायत्रं तु (*agne haṃsyurukṣaya āmahīyava āgneyaṃ rākṣoghnaṃ gāyatraṃ tu*). If at the time of churning the fire, however much one churns, Agni is not produced, this sūkta is to be recited; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra अजायमाने त्वेतस्मिन्नेवावसानेऽग्ने हंसि न्यत्रिणमिति सूक्तमावपेत (*ajāyamāne tvetasminnevāvasāne 'gne haṃsi nyatriṇamiti sūktamāvapeta*) (Adhyāya 2-16). The use of this sūkta for the Ṛks in Gāyatrī metre in the recitation of the Prātaranuvāka and of the Āśvina-śastra is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra अग्ने हंस्यग्निं हिन्वंतु नः (*agne haṃsyagniṃ hinvaṃtu naḥ*) (Ā. 4-13). On the tenth

### Printed p. 575
day of the sacrifice, when the coals are scattered at the dhiṣṇyas, the first Ṛk of this sūkta is to be muttered; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra परि त्वाग्ने पुरं वयमित्येतस्याः स्थानेऽग्ने हंसि न्यत्रिणं (*pari tvāgne puraṃ vayamityetasyāḥ sthāne 'gne haṃsi nyatriṇaṃ*) (Ā. 8-12).

Maṇḍala 10 · Anuvāka 10 · Sūkta 118
Aṣṭaka 8 · Adhyāya 6 · Vargas 24, 25
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 9
Ṛṣi: Urukṣaya Āmahīyava
Devatā: Agni Rakṣohā
Chandas: Gāyatrī

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॒ हंसि॒ न्य१॒॑त्रिणं॒ दीद्य॒न्मत्ये॒ष्वा ।  
> स्वे क्षये॑ शुचिव्रत ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । हंसि । नि । अत्रिणं । दीद्यत् । मर्त्येषु । आ ।  
> स्वे । क्षये । शुचिव्रते । ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शुचिव्रत पूतकर्मन् दीप्यमानतेजस्क हे अग्ने अत्रिणमत्तारं शत्रुं
> तमोरूपं नितरां हंसि । विनाशय ॥ आमंत्रितस्याविद्यमानत्वेन पादादित्पादनिघातः ॥
> किं कुर्वन् । मर्त्येषु मनुष्येषु यजमानेष्वाभिमुख्येन दीद्यत् कर्मसिद्ध्यर्थं
> प्रकाशमानः । दीदितिर्दिप्ति कर्मा । तथा स्व आत्मीये क्षये निवासभूत आहवनीयादिस्थाने दीप्यमानः ॥ क्षयो निवासे । पा. ६-१-२०१ । इत्याद्यु दात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, whose rites (vrata) are pure and whose splendour blazes, you thoroughly slay (destroy) the devourer (attrin), the enemy in the form of darkness. How? Shining forth among mortals, that is, among men, the sacrificers, to accomplish the rite; दीदितिर्दिप्ति कर्मा (*dīditirdipti karmā*) (dīditi is a verb of shining). Likewise shining in your own dwelling (kṣaya), the abode in places such as the Āhavanīya. क्षयो निवासे (*kṣayo nivāse*) (Pā. 6-1-201) is cited for the accent.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुचिव्रत (*śucivrata*)—one with pure rites, or one who shines with radiant splendour
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- मर्त्येषु (*martyeṣu*)—among men, that is, among the sacrificing sacrificers (in the sacrificial houses of the sacrificers)

### Printed p. 576
- स्वे क्षये (*sve kṣaye*)—in your own dwelling-places, the fire-pits such as the Āhavanīya
- आ दीद्यन् (*ā dīdyan*)—shining well for the performance of the rite
- अत्रिणं (*atriṇaṃ*)—the destructive enemy in the form of darkness, that is, the darkness
- नि हंसि (*ni haṃsi*)—destroy thoroughly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, of pure rites, or shining with radiant splendour: shining well, for the performance of the sacrificial rite, in the houses of men, that is of the sacrificers, and in your own places, the fire-pits such as the Āhavanīya, destroy utterly the enemy in the form of darkness, that is, the darkness.

##### English translation
Agni, observer of purity, you destroy the devouring (gloom), shining, amongst men in your own dwelling.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उत्ति॑ष्ठसि॒ स्वा॑हुतो घृ॒तानि॒ प्रति॑ मोदसे ।  
> यत्ना॒ स्रुचः॑ स॒मस्थि॑रन् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । तिष्ठसि । सुआहुतः । घृतानि । प्रति । मोदसे ।  
> यत् । त्वा । स्रुचः । संअस्थिरन् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने स्वाहुतोऽस्माभिः सुष्ठाहूयमानः सन्नुत्तिष्ठसि । अरणीभ्यामुद्गतो भव ॥ ऊर्ध्वकर्मत्वादात्मनेपदाभावः । पा. १-३-२४ ॥ उद्गत्य च घृतानि
> घृतेन सहितान्यस्माभिर्दीयमानानि हवींषि प्रति मोदसे । हृष्टो भव ॥ मुद
> हर्षॆ भौवादिकः । अनुदात्तेत् ॥ यद्यदा त्वा त्वां स्ट्रुचो जुह्लादीनि पात्राणि
> समस्थिरन् संगतान्यभवन् ॥ समवप्रविभ्यः स्थ इति लुज्यात्मनेपदं । स्थाघ्वोरिच्छेति
> सिचः कित्त्वमिकारश्चांतादेशः । प्रस्वादंगादिति सिचो लोपः । व्यत्ययेन झस्य रन् ।
> तिजि चोदात्तवतीति गतेर्निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, well invoked (svāhuta) by us, you rise up: be risen from the two aranis. Having risen, rejoice in the oblations accompanied by ghee that we give; be gladdened (मुद हर्षॆ (*muda harṣè*), a root of the first class). *Yat* means "when": when the ladles (sruc), the vessels such as the juhū, have come together, that is, approached you.

### Printed p. 577

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वाहुतः (*svāhutaḥ*)—specially prayed to by us
- उत्तिष्ठसि (*uttiṣṭhasi*)—you appear in the aranis
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- स्रुचः (*srucaḥ*)—the ladles of oblation, the juhū and others
- समस्थिरन् (*samasthiran*)—approach for the oblation; then
- धृतानि (*dhṛtāni*)—the oblations accompanied by ghee offered by us (accepting them)**NOTE**
- प्रति मोदसे (*prati modase*)—be delighted

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, prayed to specially by us and invoked, you are produced in the aranis. When the ladles (spoons), the juhū and other vessels filled with ghee, approach you for the oblation, accept the oblations accompanied by ghee that we offer, and be delighted.

##### English translation
You spring up when piously invoked, you delight in the oblation when the ladles are brought near you.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स आहु॑तो॒ वि रो॑चते॒ऽग्नि री॒ळेन्यो॑ गि॒रा ।  
> स्रु॒चा प्रती॑कमज्यते ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । आहुतः । वि । रोचते । अग्निः । ईळेन्यः । गिरा ।  
> सुप्रा । प्रतीकं । अज्यते ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आहुत अभिमुख्येन हुतः ॥ गतिरनंतर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरः ॥ गिरा स्तुतिलक्ष
> णया वाचेळेन्यः स्तोतव्यः सोऽग्निर्वि रोचते । अत्यर्थं दीप्यते । तथा प्रतीकं
> सर्वेषां देवानां पूर्वमेव स्रुचा धृतसहितयाज्यते । सिच्यते ॥
> 36

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

*Āhuta* means offered facing (him). By speech (gir), that is, by the voice that consists of praise, he who is to be praised (īḷenya), Agni, shines forth: he blazes exceedingly. Likewise his front (pratīka), the foremost of all the gods, is anointed (ajyate), that is, sprinkled, by the ladle with ghee.

### Printed p. 578

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आहुतः (*āhutaḥ*)—he who is offered oblations facing him
- गिरा (*girā*)—by speech in the form of praise
- ईळेन्यः (*īḷenyaḥ*)—he who is praised
- सः अग्निः (*saḥ agniḥ*)—that Agni
- वि रोचते (*vi rocate*)—shines exceedingly
- प्रतीकं (*pratīkaṃ*)—(before all the gods) in the first place
- स्रुचा (*srucā*)—with the ladle filled with ghee
- अज्यते (*ajyate*)—is sprinkled

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, to whom the oblation is offered facing him, and who is praised with speech in the form of praise, is sprinkled for the homa with the ladle filled with ghee before all the gods.

##### English translation
Agni, who is to be glorified with the voice (of praise), blazes up when invoked, he is sprinkled with the ladle before (the other goods).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In performing homa, the offering is made to Agni first, before all the other deities, with the ladle filled with ghee. Only after the homa with ghee has been made to Agni are the oblations offered to the other deities, through Agni himself.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> घृ॒तेना॒ग्निः सम॑ज्यते॒ मधु॑प्रतीक॒ आहु॑तः ।  
> रोच॑मानो वि॒भाव॑सुः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> घृतेन । अग्निः । सं । अज्यते । मधुप्रतीकः । आहुतः ।  
> रोचमानः । विभावसुः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निर्घृतेन हविषा समज्यते । सम्यक् सिक्तो भवति । कीदृशः । मधुप्रतीको
> घृतप्रयुक्तावयवः आहुतः स्तुतिभिर्हविर्भिर्वा रोचमानो दीप्यमानः विभावसुः
> स्वदीप्त्या सर्वमाच्छादयन् । यद्वा । दीप्तिरेव धनं यस्य सः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is well sprinkled with ghee, the oblation. He is मधुप्रतीकः (*madhupratīkaḥ*), one whose limbs are charged with ghee; आहुतः (*āhutaḥ*), invoked with praises or with oblations; रोचमानः (*rocamānaḥ*), shining; विभावसुः (*vibhāvasuḥ*), covering everything with his own radiance. Or else, he whose wealth is radiance itself.

### Printed p. 579

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मधुप्रतीकः (*madhupratīkaḥ*)—he whose limbs are drenched with ghee
- आहुतः (*āhutaḥ*)—he who is called by prayer with praises and oblations
- रोचमानः (*rocamānaḥ*)—he who shines with brilliance
- विभावसुः (*vibhāvasuḥ*)—he who covers everything with his own light, or he whose wealth is radiance
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- धृतेन (*dhṛtena*)—with ghee (clarified butter)
- सं अज्यते (*saṃ ajyate*)—is well sprinkled

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, whose limbs are drenched with ghee, who is called with praises and oblations, who shines with divine brilliance and covers everything with his own light, is well sprinkled with ghee.

##### English translation
Agni is anointed with butter, having a face of honey, invoked, radiant irradiating all.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Since homa is made in Agni with ghee, the limbs of Agni, that is, Agni, are drenched with ghee. As the ghee offered in the fire falls and most of Agni is drenched, he is here called one whose limbs are drenched with ghee. विभावसुः (*vibhāvasuḥ*) means one who covers everything with his own light; or, since radiance is the chief quality of Agni, he is here described by the epithet विभावसुः (*vibhāvasuḥ*), one whose wealth is radiance. धृतेन समज्यते (*dhṛtena samajyate*) means that at the time of homa much ghee is poured into Agni as an oblation and Agni is drenched with ghee.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> जर॑माणः॒ समि॑ध्यसे दे॒वेभ्यो॑ हव्यवाहन ।  
> तं त्वा॑ हवंत॒ मर्त्याः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> जरमाणः । सं । इध्यसे । देवेभ्यः । हव्यवाहन ।  
> तं । त्वा । हवंत । मर्त्याः ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 580

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अप्पोर्यामे होतुरतिरिक्तोक्ष्ये जरमाणः समिध्यस इत्यनुरूपस्तृचः ।
> सूत्रितं च । जराबोध तद्विविद्धि जरमाणः समिध्यसे । अ. ९-११ । इति ॥
> हे हव्यवाहन हव्यानां प्रापयितः ॥ हव्येऽनंतः पादं । पा. ३-२-६६ । इति
> इ्युट् ॥ जरमाणः स्तोतृभिः स्तूयमानः । जरतिः स्तुतिकर्मा । स त्वं देवेभ्यो
> देवार्थं समिध्यसे । हविर्भिः सम्यग्गीप्यसे । तं तादृशं त्वा त्वां मर्त्या मनुष्येषु साधवो यजमाना हवंत । आह्वयंति ॥ ह्वयतेर्लजि बहुलं छंदसीति
> संप्रसारणं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Āprī-type recitation (अप्पोर्यामे (*apporyāme*)) the verse जरमाणः समिध्यसे (*jaramāṇaḥ samidhyase*) is the anurūpa of a triplet, in the Hotṛ's supplementary recitation; and it is prescribed in the sūtra: जराबोध तद्विविद्धि जरमाणः समिध्यसे । अ. ९-११ । (*jarābodha tadvividdhi jaramāṇaḥ samidhyase | a. 9-11 |*) (Ā. Sū. 9-11).
O Havyavāhana, conveyer of oblations! Praised by the worshippers (जरतिः (*jaratiḥ*) is a root meaning praise), you are kindled for the gods, that is, for their sake; you are well lit with oblations. Such as you, the mortals, the pious sacrificers among men, invoke.
**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हव्यवाहन (*havyavāhana*)—O Agni, bearer of oblations (to the gods)
- जरमाणः (*jaramāṇaḥ*)—you who are praised by the worshippers
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—for the gods (for divine rites)
- सं इध्यसे (*saṃ idhyase*)—you are well kindled with oblations and the like
- तं (*taṃ*)—you, endowed with such qualities
- मर्त्याः (*martyāḥ*)—mortals, that is, the sacrificers who perform sacrifice
- हवंत (*havaṃta*)—call by prayer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, who carry the oblation to the gods, you who are praised by the worshippers are made to blaze with oblations and the like for the gods, that is, for the sake of divine rites (made to burn fiercely). Such as you, men, that is, the sacrificers, call by prayer.

##### English translation
Bearer of oblations, glorified by the worshippers, you are kindled for the gods; as such mortals invoke you.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

It is explained that in the Aptoryāma sacrifice, in the supplementary (atiriktokta) mantra recited by the Hotṛ, three Ṛks beginning जरमाणः समिध्यसे (*jaramāṇaḥ samidhyase*) (Ṛks 5–7 of this sūkta) are to be recited, according to the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra जराबोध तद्विविड्डि जरमाणः समिध्यसे (*jarābodha tadviviḍḍi jaramāṇaḥ samidhyase*) (Ā. 9-11).

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं म॑र्ता॒ अम॑ूर्त्यं घृ॒तेना॒ग्निं स॑पर्यत ।  
> अदा॑भ्यं गृ॒हप॑तिं ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 581

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । मर्ताः । अमर्त्यं । धृतेन । अग्निं । सपर्यश ।  
> ।  
> अदाभ्यं । गृहपतिं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मर्ता ऋत्विजः अमत्यर्त्यं मनुष्यधर्मरहितमग्निं धृतेन हविषा
> सपर्य्यत । परिचरत ॥ सपरशब्दः कंड्वादिः ॥ कीदृशं । अदाभ्यं कैश्चिदप्यहिंस्यं ॥
> दभेश्चेति वक्तव्यं । पा. ३-१-१२४-३ । इति ण्यत् ॥ गृहपतिं गृहस्य स्वामिनं
> यजमानरूपं ॥ पत्यावैश्वर्य इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O mortals, priests! Serve Agni, free of human nature, with ghee, the oblation. सपर्य्यत (*saparyyata*) means "attend upon". What sort of Agni? अदाभ्यं (*adābhyaṃ*), one who cannot be harmed by anyone; गृहपतिं (*gṛhapatiṃ*), the master of the house, in the form of the sacrificer.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मर्ताः (*martāḥ*)—O priests who are men
- अमर्त्यं (*amartyaṃ*)—him who is free of human nature (deathless)
- अदाभ्यं (*adābhyaṃ*)—him who cannot be harmed by anyone
- गृहपतिं (*gṛhapatiṃ*)—him who is the master of the house
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- धृतेन (*dhṛtena*)—with ghee (oblation)
- सपर्यत (*saparyata*)—serve

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests, who are men, serve with oblation mixed with ghee Agni, who is free of mortality, whom no hindrance affects, and who is lord of the house like a master.

##### English translation
Mortals, worship with ghi the immortal agni, the indestructible, the master of the mansion.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गोपाः । ऋतस्य । दीदिहि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वमादाभ्येनाहिंस्येन शोचिषा तेजसा रक्षः । जातावेकवचनं ।
> सर्वान्नाक्षसान्दह । विनाशय । किंचर्तस्य यज्ञस्य गोपा गोपायिता सन् दीदिहि ।
> दीप्यस्व ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, with your unharmable flame, your brilliance, burn the रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*) (a singular used in the generic sense), all the rākṣasas; destroy them. And as the guardian of the sacrifice (ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)), shine.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- अदाभ्येन (*adābhyena*)—with unobstructed
- शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)—(your) brilliance
- रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*)—all the rākṣasas
- दह (*daha*)—burn to ashes
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice
- गोपाः (*gopāḥ*)—as protector
- दीदिहि (*dīdihi*)—shine exceedingly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, with your unobstructed brilliance, that is, brilliance that none can endure, burn all hosts of rākṣasas; shine as the protector of the sacrifice.

##### English translation
Wito your indestructible flame, agni, consume the rakshasas; shine, the defender of the sacrifice.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स त्वम॑ग्ने॒ प्रती॑केन॒ प्रत्यो॑ष यातुधा॒न्यः॑ ।  
> उ॒रु॒क्षये॑षु॒ दीद्य॑त् ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सॆः । त्वं । अग्ने । प्रतीकेन । प्रति । ओष । यातुऽधान्यः ।  
> उरुक्षयेषु । दीद्यत् ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने स त्वं प्रतीकेन त्वदवयवभूतेन तेजसा यातुधानो यातुधानी
> राक्षसीः प्रत्योष । प्रतिकूलं दह ॥ उष दाहे भौवादिकः । लोटि हेर्लुक् ।
> जातेरस्त्रीविषयात् । पा. ४-१-६३ । इति यातुधानशब्दस्य जीष् । उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यण इति स्वरितत्वं ॥ किं कुर्वन् । उरुक्षयेषु विस्तीर्णेषु निवासेष्वाहवनीयादिषु दीद्यद्दीप्यमानः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, such as you, with your प्रतीकेन (*pratīkena*), the brilliance that is part of your body, burn up प्रत्योष (*pratyoṣa*) the यातुधानी (*yātudhānī*), the female rākṣasas, hostilely. What are you doing? Shining दीद्यत् (*dīdyat*) in the उरुक्षयेषु (*urukṣayeṣu*), the wide dwellings, the Āhavanīya and other fires.

### Printed p. 583

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- सः त्वं (*saḥ tvaṃ*)—such as you
- प्रतीकेन (*pratīkena*)—with your brilliance, which is part of your body
- उरुक्षयेषु (*urukṣayeṣu*)—in the wide (or many) fire-pits, Āhavanīya and others
- दीद्यत् (*dīdyat*)—shining
- यातुधान्यः (*yātudhānyaḥ*)—the hosts of female rākṣasas called Yātudhānīs
- प्रति ओष (*prati oṣa*)—burn so that they are reduced to ashes
**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, shining brilliantly in the wide sacrificial pits such as the Āhavanīya, with your brilliance which is like your limb, burn well the female rākṣasas called Yātudhānīs.

##### English translation
Do you, Agni with your brightness, consume the female fiends, shining in your outspread dwellings.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The matter of the Yātudhānas and Yātudhānīs is explained in the introduction to this sūkta.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं त्वा॑ गी॒र्भिरु॑रु॒क्षया॑ हव्य॒वाहं॒ समा॑धिरे ।  
> यजि॑ष्ठं॒ मानु॑षे॒ जने॑ ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । त्वा । गीःभिः । उरुक्षयाः । हव्यवाहं । सं । ईधिरे ।  
> यजिष्ठं । मानुषे । जने ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने उरुक्षया बहुनिवासा यजमाना हव्यवाहं हविषां वोढारं
> मानुषे मनुष्यसंबंधिनि जने जनमध्ये यजिष्ठं यष्टृतमं तं त्वा त्वां गीर्भिः
> स्तुतिभिस्तत्सहितैर्हविर्भिः समाधिरे । सम्यगदीदिपन् ॥ इंथेर्लिटींधिभवतिभ्यां चेति
> कित्वे नलोपः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, the sacrificers, उरुक्षया (*urukṣayā*), having many dwellings, have kindled you well, with praises and with the oblations that go with them: you, bearer of oblations, यजिष्ठं (*yajiṣṭhaṃ*), the best sacrificer, among the people connected with men.

- (O Agni) उरुक्षयाः (*urukṣayāḥ*)—the sacrificers who dwell in many houses
- हव्यवाहं (*havyavāhaṃ*)—the one who carries the oblation to the gods
- मानुषे जने (*mānuṣe jane*)—among human beings
- यजिष्ठं (*yajiṣṭhaṃ*)—the one most worthy of worship
- तं त्वा (*taṃ tvā*)—you
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—with praises and with oblations and the like
- समीधिरे (*samīdhire*)—kindle exceedingly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The many sacrificers who dwell in various houses, in their sacrificial houses, cause you to blaze exceedingly with words of praise and with oblations and the like. You carry the oblation to the gods, and among human beings you are the most worthy of worship, that is, the one who is honoured.

##### English translation
The masters of many mansions have, by their praises, kindled you,
Agni, the bearer of oblations, who are most adorable among human beings.

## Sūkta 119 (Maṇḍala 10)

**Pīṭhike**
The seer of this sūkta is Laba. Once, in the hermitage of the seer Laba, Indra took on the form of the seer Laba and drank Soma. The other seers saw it. Then Indra, being in Laba's form, praised himself with this sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इति वा इति त्रयोदशर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तं गायत्रं । इंद्रो लबरूपमास्थाय सोमपानं कुर्वन् तदानीमृषिभिः दृष्टः सन् स्वात्मानमनेन सूक्तेनास्तावीत् । अतो लबरूपापन्न इंद्र ऋषिः । स एव देवता । तथा चानुक्रम्यते । इति वै
> सप्तोनैंद्रो लब आत्मानं तुष्टावेति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the seventh sūkta of the tenth anuvāka, beginning इति वा (*iti vā*), of thirteen Ṛks, in the Gāyatra metre. Indra, having taken on the form of Laba and drinking Soma, was then seen by the seers and praised himself with this sūkta. Therefore Indra, who has assumed Laba's form, is the seer, and he himself is the deity. So the Anukramaṇī says इति वै सप्तोनैंद्रो लब आत्मानं तुष्टावेति (*iti vai saptonaiṃdro laba ātmānaṃ tuṣṭāveti*). The viniyoga has already been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, इति वै (*iti vai*), is the seventh sūkta in the tenth anuvāka. It has thirteen Ṛks. Once Indra, in the form of the seer Laba, was drinking Soma, and the other seers saw it. Then Indra praised himself in that same form.

### Printed p. 585

Therefore the seer of this sūkta is Indra himself, wearing Laba's form; he is also the deity; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: इति वै सप्तोन्यैंद्रो लब आत्मानं तुष्टाव (*iti vai saptonyaiṃdro laba ātmānaṃ tuṣṭāva*). The viniyoga has been stated earlier.

Sūkta—109 **NOTE**
Maṇḍala—10. Anuvāka—10. Sūkta—119.
Aṣṭaka—8. Adhyāya—6. Varga—26, 27.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta—13.
Ṛṣi: Laba Aindra.
Devatā: Ātmastuti (self-praise).
Chandas: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इति॒ वा इति॑ मे॒ मनो॒ गामश्वं॑ सनुया॒मिति॑ ।  
> कु॒वित्सोम॒स्यापा॒मिति॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इति । वै । इति । मे । मनः । गां । अश्वं । सनुयां । इति ॥  
> कुवित् । सोमस्य । अपां । इति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इति वा इति खल्वित्येवं प्रकारेण मे मदीयं मनो वर्तते । तं प्रकारं
> दर्शयति । गामश्वं च सनुयां स्तोतृभ्यः प्रयच्छामाति ॥ षणु दाने तानादिकः ॥
> इति शब्दो हेत् । यस्मात् कुविद्बहुवारं सोमस्य सोममपां पीतवानस्मि ॥
> क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति सोमस्य संप्रदानसंज्ञा । चतुर्थ्यर्थे बहुलमिति षष्ठी ।
> पा पाने । लुजि गातिस्थेति सिचो लुक् । कुविद्योगादनिघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says: "thus indeed" — in this way my mind is disposed. He shows that manner: "I shall give a cow and a horse to the praisers." सनुयां (*sanuyāṃ*) is from the root ṣaṇu, in the sense of giving, of the tānādi class. The word इति (*iti*) has the sense of a reason: because I have drunk Soma many times (कुवित् (*kuvit*), "often"). Soma takes the designation of recipient (sampradāna), and the genitive stands in place of the dative. The root pā means "to drink"; the form अपां (*apāṃ*) is an aorist, and the accent is not lowered owing to the connection with कुवित् (*kuvit*).

### Printed p. 586

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इति वै (*iti vai*)—just so
- इति (*iti*)—in this manner
- (I to the praising people) गां (*gāṃ*)—a cow
- अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*)—a horse
- सनुयां (*sanuyāṃ*)—will give
- इति (*iti*)—thus
- मे (*me*)—my
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—the mind is so (because I)
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—many times
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—Soma juice
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—have drunk

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I have drunk Soma many times. Delighted by it, I shall give a cow and a horse in this way to the people who praise me. It is in my mind that I should give thus.

##### English translation
Thus, indeed, thus my mind (resolved) : " I will give cows and horses
(to my worshippers), " for I have often drunk of the Soma.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र वाता॑ इव॒ दोध॑त॒ उन्मा॑ पी॒ता अ॑यंसत ।  
> कु॒वित्सोम॒स्यापा॒मिति॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । वाताः इव । दोधतः । उत् । मा । पीताः । अयंसत ।  
> कुवित् । सोमस्यॆ । अपां । इति ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दोधतो भृशं कंपयमाना वाता इव वायवो यथा वृक्षादीनुद्यच्छंते
> तद्वृत्तीताः सोमा मा मां प्रकर्षणोदयंसत । उद्यच्छंते ॥ यमेर्लुजि
> समुदाज्यो यमोऽग्रंथे । पा. १-३-७५ । इत्यात्मनेपदं ॥ यस्माद्बहुवारं
> सोममपां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Just as winds (वाता इव (*vātā iva*)) that violently shake (दोधतः (*dodhataḥ*)) lift up trees and the like, so the Soma draughts that have been drunk lift me up vigorously (*udayaṃsata*, "they raise"). The verb takes the ātmanepada by Pā. 1-3-75. The reason: because I have drunk Soma many times.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्र दोधतः (*pra dodhataḥ*)—violently shaking (blowing) trees and the like
- वात इव (*vāta iva*)—like a storm
- पीताः (*pītāḥ*)—the Soma juices drunk by me
- मा (*mā*)—me
- उत् (*ut*)—up

### Printed p. 587

- अयंसत (*ayaṃsata*)—lift up and make full of enthusiasm
- इति (*iti*)—because (I)
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—many times (or greatly)
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—Soma
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—have drunk

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Like storms that make trees and the like shake violently, the Soma juices that I have drunk lift me up and fill me with enthusiasm, because I have drunk Soma greatly.

##### English translation
Like the winds violently shaking (the trees), the draughts (of Soma) have lifted me up, for I have often drunk of the Soma).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उन्मा॑ पी॒ता अ॑यंसत॒ रथ॒मश्वा॑ इवा॒शवः॑ ।  
> कु॒वित्सोम॒स्यापा॒मिति॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । मा । पीताः । अयंसत । रथं । अश्वाः इव । आशवः ।  
> कुवित् । सोमस्य । अपां । इति ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पीताः सोमा मामुदयंसत । उद्यच्छंते । तत्र दृष्टांतः । रथमश्वा इव
> यथाशवः क्षिप्रगामिनो गमनेन व्याप्ता वाश्वा रथमुद्गमयंति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Soma draughts that have been drunk lift me up. The illustration: as swift horses (आशवः (*āśavaḥ*)), going fast and pervading the way by their going, make the chariot move up and onward, so do the Soma draughts me.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आशवः (*āśavaḥ*)—swift-going
- अश्वा इव (*aśvā iva*)—like horses
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—as they carry the chariot, throwing it up
- पीताः (*pītāḥ*)—the Soma juices drunk by me
- मा (*mā*)—me
- उत् (*ut*)—up
- अयंसत (*ayaṃsata*)—make full of enthusiasm
- इति (*iti*)—because (I)
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—greatly
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—Soma
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—have drunk

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As swift-running horses, when drawing a chariot, lift it up by their quick going, so the Soma juices that I have drunk lift me up and fill me with enthusiasm, because I have drunk Soma greatly.

### Printed p. 588

##### English translation
The draughts (of Soma) have lifted me up like swift horses (drawing)
a chariot, for I have often drunk of the Soma.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उप॑ मा म॒तिर॑स्थित वा॒श्रा पु॒त्रमि॑व प्रि॒यं ।  
> कु॒वित्सोम॒स्यापा॒मिति॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उप । मा । मतिः । अस्थित । वाश्रा । पुत्रं इव । प्रियं ।  
> कुवित् । सोमस्य । अपां । इति ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मतिः स्तोतृभिः क्रियमाणा स्तुतिकर्मा मामुपास्थित । संयोजयति ॥
> उपाद्देवपूजासंगतिकरणेत्यात्मनेपदं ॥ कथमिव । वाश्रा पुत्रमिव यथ वाश्रा
> शब्दायमाना धेनुः प्रियं पुत्रं वत्सं संगच्छति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The praise (मतिः (*matiḥ*)), the act of praise made by the singers, has approached me (*upāsthita*, "joins"); the ātmanepada is from the rule on worship of gods, association, and the like. How? As a lowing cow (वाश्रा (*vāśrā*), "making a sound") goes to her dear son, her calf, so does the praise come to me.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाश्राः (*vāśrāḥ*)—lowing cows
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—dear to her
- पुत्रमिव (*putramiva*)—as they go to their calf
- मतिः (*matiḥ*)—the praise that the praising people recite (loudly)
- मा (*mā*)—me
- उप अस्थित (*upa asthita*)—comes close and joins
- इति (*iti*)—because (I)
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—greatly
- सोमस्यॆ (*somasyè*)—Soma
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—have drunk

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As cows go lowing to their dear calves, the praise that the praising people recite comes to me and joins me, because I have drunk Soma greatly.

##### English translation
The praise (of the pious) has come to me like a lowing cow to her
beloved calf for I have often drunk of the Soma,

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒हं तप्पे॑व वं॒धुरं॒ पर्य॑चामि हृ॒दा म॒तिं ।  
> कु॒वित्सोम॒स्यापा॒मिति॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अहं । तप्पा इव । वंधुरं । परि । अचामि । हृदा । मतिं ।  
> कुवित् । सोमस्य । अपां । इति ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तष्टेव तक्षा यथा वंधुरं सारथिनिवासस्थानं । तद्वान्वोपलक्ष्यते तत्स्थानं
> रथं वा साधुकरोति तद्वदहं मतिं स्तुतिं हृदात्मीयेन मनसा पर्यचरामि ।
> साधुकरणाय परिगच्छामि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As a carpenter (तक्षा (*takṣā*)) puts in good order the vandhura, the charioteer's seat — or the place is meant, or the chariot that has it — so I (पर्यचरामि (*paryacarāmi*), "go about") attend upon the praise (मतिं (*matiṃ*)) with my heart, that is, with my own mind; I go about it in order to put it in good order.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कष्टेव (*kaṣṭeva*)—like a carpenter (or craftsman) **NOTE**
- वंधुरं (*vaṃdhuraṃ*)—as he builds well the place in the chariot where the charioteer sits (the front seat)
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- मतिं (*matiṃ*)—the praise
- हृदा (*hṛdā*)—with the heart, that is, wholeheartedly
- परि अचामि (*pari acāmi*)—take up
- इति (*iti*)—because (I)
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—greatly
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—Soma
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—have drunk

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a carpenter carefully makes well the place in the chariot where the charioteer sits, so I accept wholeheartedly the praise that the praising people make, because I have drunk Soma greatly.

##### English translation
I revolve the song of praise in my heart as a carpenter (making) a
charioteer's seat, for I have often drunk of the Soma.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न॒हि मे॑ अक्षि॒पच्च॒नाच्छां॑त्सुः॒ पंच॑ कृ॒ष्टयः॑ ।  
> कु॒वित्सोम॒स्यापा॒मिति॑ ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 590

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नहि । मे । अक्षिपत् । चन । अच्छांत्सुः । पंच । कृष्टयः ।  
> कुवित् । सोमस्य । अपां । इति ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चनेति निपातसमुदायोऽप्यर्थे । पंच कृस्टयोऽपि निषादपंचमाश्चत्वारो
> वर्णाः पंच जनाः । यद्वा । देवमनुष्यादयः । मे मदीयमक्षिपच्चक्षुःपतनं
> दृष्टिसंचारं नह्यच्छांत्सुः । न ह्यपवृण्वंति । न हि द्रष्टुर्दृष्टेर्विपरिलोपो विद्यत
> इति हि श्रुतेः । शत. १४-७-१-२३ ॥ छदि अपवारणे । चुरादीनामिति वा ण्यंतत्वादत्र
> ण्यभावे लुजि हलंतलक्षणा वृद्धिः । पा. ७-२-३ ॥ यस्माद्बहुवारं सोममपां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

चन (*cana*) is a combination of particles, and here it has the sense "even". The "five tribes" (पंच । कृष्टयः (*paṃca | kṛṣṭayaḥ*)) are the four castes with the Niṣāda as the fifth, that is, five groups of people. Or else they are gods, men and the rest. "My अक्षिपत् (*akṣipat*)", that is, the falling of my eye, the movement of my glance, they do not elude (न ह्यपवृण्वंति (*na hyapavṛṇvaṃti*)). He cites the śruti: न हि द्रष्टुर्दृष्टेर्विपरिलोपो विद्यत (*na hi draṣṭurdṛṣṭerviparilopo vidyata*) (Śa. 14-7-1-23). The reason is that I have drunk Soma many times.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चन (*cana*)—and
- पंच कृष्णयः (*paṃca kṛṣṇayaḥ*)—the people of the five groups beginning with the Brāhmaṇas, together with the Niṣādas, or the five kinds of people, gods, men and others
- मे (*me*)—my
- अक्षिपत् (*akṣipat*)—falling in the sight
- नहि अच्छान्सुः (*nahi acchānsuḥ*)—cannot escape
- इति (*iti*)—because (I)
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—much
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—Soma
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—have drunk

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Moreover, the people of the five groups, Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras and Niṣādas, or the five kinds of people such as gods and men, cannot escape falling within my sight (all will certainly fall within my sight), because I have drunk much Soma.

##### English translation
The five castes have not eluded the glance of my eye, for I have often drunk of the Soma.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न॒हि मे॒ रोद॑सी उ॒भे अ॒न्यं प॒क्षं च॒न प्रति॑ ।  
> कु॒वित्सोम॒स्यापा॒मिति॑ ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 591

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नहि । मे । रोदसी इति । उभे इति । अन्यं । पक्षं । चन । प्रति ।  
> कुवित् । सोमस्य । अपां । इति ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उभे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्य मे मदीयमन्यं पक्षं चन पक्षमपि प्रति
> समाने न भवतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Both heaven and earth are not equal to any other side (half) of me.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—even both heaven and earth together
- मे (*me*)—my (in power, capacity and so on)
- अन्यं पक्षं चन (*anyaṃ pakṣaṃ cana*)—even half
- प्रति नहि (*prati nahi*)—are not equal
- इति (*iti*)—because (I)
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—much
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—Soma
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—have drunk

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Even heaven and earth together cannot match even half of me in power and capacity, because I have drunk much Soma.

##### English translation
Both heaven and earth (are) not equal to one half of me, for I have often drunk of tne Soma.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि द्यां म॑हि॒ना भु॑वम॒भी॒३॒॑३मां पृ॑थि॒वीं म॒हीं ।  
> कु॒वित्सोम॒स्यापा॒मिति॑ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । द्यां । महिना । भुवं । अभि । इमां । पृथिवीं । महीं ।  
> कुवित् । सोमस्य । अपां । इति ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 592

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उक्तमर्थं प्रतिपादयति । महिना महिम्नात्मीयेन द्यां द्युलोकमभि
> भुवं । अभिभवामि । तथा महीं महतीमिमां पृथिवीं स्वमहिम्नाभि भवामि ॥ भवतेर्लजि च्छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् । भूसुवोस्तिजीति गुणे प्रतिषिद्द उवजादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He sets forth the matter already stated. "By my own greatness (महिना (*mahinā*)) I overcome (अभि भुवं (*abhi bhuvaṃ*)) the sky (द्यां (*dyāṃ*)), the world of heaven; likewise I overcome this great earth by my own greatness."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महिना (*mahinā*)—I, by my own power or greatness
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the world of Dyu (heaven)
- अभि भुवं (*abhi bhuvaṃ*)—have defeated (likewise)
- महीं (*mahīṃ*)—vast
- इमां पृथिवीं (*imāṃ pṛthivīṃ*)—this earth also
- अभि (*abhi*)—have defeated
- इति (*iti*)—because (I)
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—much
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—Soma
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—have drunk

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

By my greatness I have overcome the world of heaven and also this vast earth, because I have drunk much Soma.

##### English translation
I excel the sky in greatness, (I excel) this great earth; for I have often drunk of the Soma.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कु॒वित्सोम॒स्यापा॒मिति॑ ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हंत । अहं । पृथिवीं । इमां । नि । दधानि । इह । वा । इह । वा ।  
> कुवित् । सोमस्य । अपां । इति ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हंतेति संभावनायामनुज्ञायां वा । संभावयाम्येतदनुजानामि वा ।
> किं तत् । अहमिमां पृथिवीमिह वांतरिक्षे नि दधानि । इह वा द्युलोक इति हस्तेन
> निर्दिशति ॥ दधातेर्लोटि मेर्निः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

हंत (*haṃta*) is used in the sense of supposition or of permission: "I suppose this" or "I permit this". What is it? "I shall set down (नि दधानि (*ni dadhāni*)) this earth here, or in the atmosphere; or here, in the world of heaven", and he points with the hand.

### Printed p. 593

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हंत (*haṃta*)—lo
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- इमां पृथिवीं (*imāṃ pṛthivīṃ*)—this globe of the earth
- इह वा (*iha vā*)—right here, if I wish
- इह वा (*iha vā*)—or in the atmosphere, if I wish
- नि दधानि (*ni dadhāni*)—I can place
- इति (*iti*)—because (I)
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—much
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—Soma
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—have drunk

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Lo! I can set this globe of the earth here, if I wish, or in the atmosphere, because I have drunk much Soma.

##### English translation
Lo! I will place this earth (where I will), either here or there; for I have often drunk of the Soma.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska, explaining the meaning and use of the word वा (*vā*), says: वेति विचारणार्थे । हंताहं पृथिवीमिमां नि दधानीह वेह वा । अथापि समुच्चयार्थे भवति । वायुर्वा त्वा मनुर्वा त्वा । (*veti vicāraṇārthe | haṃtāhaṃ pṛthivīmimāṃ ni dadhānīha veha vā | athāpi samuccayārthe bhavati | vāyurvā tvā manurvā tvā |*) (Ni. 1-4 **NOTE**). The word वा (*vā*) is used when considering a weighty or profound matter. In the above example हंताहं पृथिवीमिमां नि दधानीह वेह वा (*haṃtāhaṃ pṛthivīmimāṃ ni dadhānīha veha vā*) the thought is expressed: "Ah! I can place this earth right here, or I can place it in the atmosphere." The word is also used in the sense of conjunction, that is, "and". In the example वायुर्वा त्वा मनुर्वा त्वा (*vāyurvā tvā manurvā tvā*), वा (*vā*) has the sense "and": "Vāyu and Manu".

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the earth
- ओषं (*oṣaṃ*)—the sun shining with his own brilliance
- इह वा (*iha vā*)—in the atmosphere

### Printed p. 595

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मे मदीयोऽन्यः पक्षो दिवि द्युलोके स्थापितः । अधः ॥ पूर्वाधरावराणामसीत्यादिनासिप्रत्ययः । प्रकृतेरधादेशश्च ॥ अधस्तात्पृथिव्यामन्यं पक्षमचीकृषं । अकार्षं ॥ कृष विलेखने । ण्यंतस्य लुजि चज नित्यं छंदसि । पा. ७-४-८ ।
> इत्यकारादेशः ॥ विलेखनं नामोत्पादनं । उदपादयं । आस्थापयमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

One wing of mine is set in the sky, in the world of heaven. Below (अधः (*adhaḥ*)), that is, beneath on the earth, I have made (आचीकृषं (*ācīkṛṣaṃ*), "I made") the other wing. कृष (*kṛṣa*) here has the sense of विलेखन (*vilekhana*), which means producing: "I produced", "I established".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मे (*me*)—my
- अन्यः पक्षः (*anyaḥ pakṣaḥ*)—one wing
- दिवि (*divi*)—is set in heaven
- अन्यं (*anyaṃ*)—the other wing
- अधः (*adhaḥ*)—to the earth below
- आचीकृषं (*ācīkṛṣaṃ*)—he has drawn and cast down
- इति (*iti*)—because (I)
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—much
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—Soma
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—have drunk

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

One of my wings is set in heaven and the other on earth, because I have drunk much Soma.

##### English translation
One of my wings is in the sky; the other I dragged below; for I have often drunk of the Soma.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कु॒वित्सोम॒स्यापा॒मिति॑ ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अहं । अस्मि । महामहः । अभिनभ्यं । उत्ईषितः ।  
> कुवित् । सोमस्य । अपां । इति ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अभिनभ्यं नाभौ मध्यस्थाने भवं नभ्यमंतरिक्षं ॥ उगवादिभ्यो यत् ।
> पा. ५-१-२ । इति यत्पत्ययः । तत्रैव पाठान्नभादेशश्च । लक्षणेनाभिप्रती अभिमुख्ये ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अभिनभ्यं (*abhinabhyaṃ*): नभ्यं (*nabhyaṃ*) is what is in the navel, the middle region, that is, the atmosphere. The suffix यत् (*yat*) is added by उगवादिभ्यो यत् (*ugavādibhyo yat*) (Pā. 5-1-2), and नभ (*nabha*) is substituted because the word is read in that very list. Figuratively अभि (*abhi*) and प्रति (*prati*) have the sense of facing. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 596

> पा. २-१-१४ । इत्यव्ययाभावसमासस्वरः ॥ अंतरिक्षमभ्युदीषित उद्धतः सूर्यात्माहं महामहोऽस्मि । महतामपि महानस्मि । यद्वा । महत्प्रभूतं महस्तेजो
> यस्य । प्रभूततेजस्कोऽस्मि ॥ आन्महत इत्यात्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes the explanation of the preceding Ṛk: the one who has been raised up into the middle region (the sky) is the sun-natured "I", great among the great (महामहः (*mahāmahaḥ*)). Or else, one whose splendour (महः (*mahaḥ*)) is great, that is, one of abundant radiance. The lengthening of the vowel is explained by the rule आन्महत (*ānmahata*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- अभिनभ्यं (*abhinabhyaṃ*)—in the sky, the navel-place
- उदीषितः (*udīṣitaḥ*)—established
- महामहः (*mahāmahaḥ*)—as Āditya, of great glory or shining with great radiance
- अस्मि (*asmi*)—I am
- इति (*iti*)—because (I)
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—abundantly
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—Soma
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—have drunk

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I am Āditya, the sun, established in the sky, the navel-place of the universe, of great glory, or shining with great radiance. For I have drunk Soma abundantly.

##### English translation
I am (the sun), the great, raised to the firmament; for I have often drunk of the Soma.

> कु॒वित्सोम॒स्यापा॒मिति॑ ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गृहः । यामि । अरंकृतः । देवेभ्यः । हव्यवाहनः ।  
> कुवित् । सोमस्य । असां । इति ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गृहो हविषां ग्रहीतारंकृतो यजमानैरलंकृतोऽहं देवेभ्य इंद्रादिभ्यो हव्यवाहनो हविषां वोढा प्रापयिताग्न्यात्मा सन्यामि । हवींषि प्रापयामि ॥ या प्रापणे । लट् । हव्येऽनंतःपादमिति वहेञ्युट् । इत्ताद्वाद्यु-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"I" am गृहः (*gṛhaḥ*), the receiver of oblations, and अरंकृतः (*araṃkṛtaḥ*), adorned by the sacrificers. In the form of Agni, the bearer of oblations (हव्यवाहनः (*havyavāhanaḥ*)) to the gods, Indra and the others, I go (यामि (*yāmi*)), that is, I convey the oblations. The root is या (*yā*) in the sense of conveying.

### Printed p. 597

> दात्तः । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥ इति यस्मात्कुविद्बहुवारं सोमस्य
> सोममपां पीतवानस्मि । तस्मादेतान्यकार्षमितींद्रः स्वात्मानमेवास्तावीत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Because I have drunk the Soma (*somaṃ apāṃ*) many times, therefore I have done these things; thus Indra praised his own self.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गृहः (*gṛhaḥ*)—the one who holds the oblation
- अरंकृतः (*araṃkṛtaḥ*)—adorned by the sacrificing worshippers
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—to the gods, Indra and the rest
- हव्यवाहनः (*havyavāhanaḥ*)—as Agni, who bears the oblation
- यामि (*yāmi*)—I carry the oblation to the gods
- इति (*iti*)—because (I)
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—abundantly
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—Soma juice
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—have drunk

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Prepared and adorned at the sacrificial altar by the sacrificing worshippers, bearing the oblation to the gods, and for that purpose holding the oblation, I, as Agni, carry the oblation to the gods. For I have drunk Soma abundantly.

##### English translation
Receiving the offering I go, graced (by the worshippers), bearing the oblation to the gods; for I have often drunk of the Soma.

Here the sixth adhyāya of the eighth aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, with Sāyaṇa's commentary and a Kannada translation, comes to its end.

## Sūkta 120 (Maṇḍala 10)
Eighth aṣṭaka, seventh adhyāya; tenth maṇḍala, hundred and twentieth sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तत्राष्टमाष्टके षष्ठाध्यायं व्याख्याय सप्तमाध्याय आरभ्यते । दशममंडलस्य दशमेऽनुवाके सूक्तसप्तकं व्याख्यातं । तदिदिति नवर्चमष्टमं सूक्तमथर्वणः पुत्रस्य बृहद्दिवस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । तदिन्नवाधर्वणो
> बृहद्दिव इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि निष्केवल्य इदं सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । तदिदासेति च

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Having explained the sixth adhyāya of the eighth aṣṭaka, the seventh is begun. In the tenth anuvāka of the tenth maṇḍala seven sūktas have been explained. The eighth sūkta, तदित् (*tadit*), has nine Ṛks; its seer is Bṛhaddiva, son of Atharvan; metre Triṣṭubh; deity Indra. The Anukramaṇī says: तदिन्नवाधर्वणो बृहद्दिव (*tadinnavādharvaṇo bṛhaddiva*). On the Cāturviṃśika day this sūkta belongs to the Niṣkevalya.

### Printed p. 600

> पुरस्तात्तूक्तस्य शंसेत् । आ. ७-३. । इति ॥ व्योमविश्वदेवस्तुत्पंचशारदीयेष्टप्येकाहेष्टिदमेव निष्केवल्यनिविद्वानं । सूत्रितं च । एतेषां त्रयाणां कया शुभा
> तदिदासेति मध्यंदिनः । आ. ९-८ । इति ॥ राशिमरायाख्ययोरेकाहयोरपीदं
> निष्केवल्यनिविद्वानं । सूत्रितं च । राशिमराययोश्च कयाशुभीयतदिदासीये ।
> आ. ९-८ । इति ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्येऽप्येतत्तूक्तं । तथैव पंचमारण्यके शौनकेन
> सूत्रितं । तदिदास भवनेषु ज्येष्ठं तां सु ते कीर्तिं मघवन्महित्वा । ऐ. आ. ५-१-
> ६ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Sūtra says तदिदासेति च पुरस्तात्तूक्तस्य शंसेत् (*tadidāseti ca purastāttūktasya śaṃset*) (Ā. 7-3). In the Vyoma, Viśvadevastut and Pañcaśāradīya Ekāhas, this very sūkta is the Niṣkevalya nivid-sūkta: एतेषां त्रयाणां कया शुभा तदिदासेति मध्यंदिनः । (*eteṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ kayā śubhā tadidāseti madhyaṃdinaḥ |*) (Ā. 9-8). In the Rāśimarāya Ekāhas as well: राशिमराययोश्च कयाशुभीयतदिदासीये । (*rāśimarāyayośca kayāśubhīyatadidāsīye |*) (Ā. 9-8). In the Mahāvrata Niṣkevalya also this sūkta is used; Śaunaka so prescribes in the fifth Āraṇyaka: तदिदास भवनेषु ज्येष्ठं तां सु ते कीर्तिं मघवन्महित्वा । (*tadidāsa bhavaneṣu jyeṣṭhaṃ tāṃ su te kīrtiṃ maghavanmahitvā |*) (Ai. Ā. 5-1-6).

Anuvāda: The sūktas of the seventh adhyāya in the eighth aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā are now to be explained. The first seven sūktas of the tenth anuvāka of the tenth maṇḍala were explained in the previous adhyāya. In this anuvāka the sūkta beginning तदित् (*tadit*) is the eighth. It has nine Ṛks. Its seer is Bṛhaddiva, son of the sage Atharvan; the deity is Indra; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: तदिन्नवाधर्वणो बृहद्दिवः (*tadinnavādharvaṇo bṛhaddivaḥ*). It is stated, by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra तदिदासेति च पुरस्तात्तूक्तस्य शंसेत् (*tadidāseti ca purastāttūktasya śaṃset*) (Ā. 7-3), that this sūkta is to be recited for the Niṣkevala-śastra mantras on the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika. And that in the iṣṭis called Vyoma, Viśvedevastut, Pañcaśāradīya and Ekāha, this sūkta is to be included and recited as the nivit-sūkta in the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras, is stated by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra एतेषां त्रयाणां कया शुभा तदिदासेति मध्यंदिनः (*eteṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ kayā śubhā tadidāseti madhyaṃdinaḥ*) (Ā. 9-8). In the Ekāha-iṣṭis called Rāśimarāya also, it is to be recited in the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras as the nivid sūkta, as stated by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra राशिमराययोश्च कया शुभीय तदिदासीये (*rāśimarāyayośca kayā śubhīya tadidāsīye*) (Ā. 9-8). That this sūkta is used when the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras are recited in the Mahāvrata-iṣṭi is declared by the sage Śaunaka in the fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya-Āraṇyaka. In this matter the Sūtra is तदिदास भुवनेषु ज्येष्ठं तां सु ते कीर्तिं मघवन् महित्वा (*tadidāsa bhuvaneṣu jyeṣṭhaṃ tāṃ su te kīrtiṃ maghavan mahitvā*) (Ai. Ā. 5-1-6).

Sūkta 120; Maṇḍala 10, Anuvāka 10, Sūkta 12; Aṣṭaka 8, Adhyāya 7, Vargas 1, 2. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 309 **NOTE**. Seer: Bṛhadvipa Ātharvaṇa **NOTE**. Deity: Indra. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

तत् (*tat*) is that which is known in all Vedānta as the cause of the world; इत् (*it*) is for emphasis. Among the worlds (भुवनेषु (*bhuvaneṣu*)), Brahman alone, the cause of the world, was the most excellent (ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*)), since it is the highest reality and everything other than it is only of practical (empirical) standing. Or else, ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*) means the oldest, the origin of all as cause of the world. Or else that Brahman shone (आस (*āsa*)) by its own light. From it as the material source (यतः (*yataḥ*)) was born Indra, fierce (उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)), of blazing strength (त्वेषनृम्मः (*tveṣanṛmmaḥ*)), of sun-nature. It is heard: चक्षोः सूर्यो अजायत (*cakṣoḥ sūryo ajāyata*) (Ṛ. 11-90-13) and सूर्याचंद्रमसौ धाता यथापूर्वमकल्पयत् (*sūryācaṃdramasau dhātā yathāpūrvamakalpayat*) (Ṛ. 10-190-3). As soon as born (जज्ञानः (*jajñānaḥ*)) he quickly destroys (नि रिणाति (*ni riṇāti*)) the enemies, the Mandeha and other Rākṣasas; or he destroys the sin-like enemies of his worshippers. So the Brāhmaṇa: सद्यो हैष जातः पाप्मानमपाहत (*sadyo haiṣa jātaḥ pāpmānamapāhata*) (Ai. Ā. 1-3-4). ऊमाः (*ūmāḥ*) are living beings, those who protect (अवंति (*avaṃti*)); all beings rejoice (मदंति (*madaṃti*)) looking up to that sun-natured Indra as he rises, thinking "he has risen for me, for me". So the Brāhmaṇa: भूतानि वै विश्व ऊमास्त एनमनुमदंत्युदगादुदगादिति (*bhūtāni vai viśva ūmāsta enamanumadaṃtyudagādudagāditi*) (Ai. Ā. 1-3-4), and the Taittirīya: तस्मात्सर्व एव मन्यंते मां प्रत्युदगादिति (*tasmātsarva eva manyaṃte māṃ pratyudagāditi*). Or else, all beings, after him who is gladdened by praise and the like, obtain their desires and rejoice. The construction: that Indra was born.
