> हर्षे । व्यत्ययेन शप् ॥ तथा च ब्राह्मणं । भूतानि वै विश्व ऊमास्त एनमनुमदंत्युदगादुदगादिति । ऐ- आ. १-३-४ । इति । तैत्तिरीयकं च । तस्मात्सर्व एव मन्यंते
> मां प्रत्युदगादिति । यद्वा । यं स्तुत्यादिभिर्माद्यंतमनु पश्चात्सर्वे प्राणिनोऽभीष्टप्राप्ता हृष्यंति ॥ अनुर्लक्षणे । पा. १-४-८४ । इत्यनोः कर्मप्रवचनीयत्वात्कर्मप्रवचनीययुक्त इति द्वितीया ॥ स इंद्रो जज्ञ इत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(continuation) मदी हर्षे (*madī harṣe*), with शप् (*śap*) by variation. Then the Brāhmaṇa and Taittirīya quotations and the alternative explanation as in the preceding block; the word अनु (*anu*) is a karmapravacanīya, hence the accusative; the construction is that Indra was born.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- भुवनेषु (*bhuvaneṣu*)—among the worlds, earth and the rest, the cause of the world
- तत् इत् (*tat it*)—Brahman itself, taught in all Vedānta
- ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*)—before all (in the beginning)
- आस (*āsa*)—was
- यतः (*yataḥ*)—from that Brahman, the cause of all
- उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)—the powerful
- तेषनृम्मः (*teṣanṛmmaḥ*)—one whose strength is radiance, that is, who shines with his own light; Indra of sun-nature
- जज्ञे (*jajñe*)—was born
- जज्ञानः (*jajñānaḥ*)—that sun-natured Indra, as soon as born
- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—at once
- शत्रून् (*śatrūn*)—the Rākṣasas, Mandeha, Aruṇa and the rest
- नि रिणाति (*ni riṇāti*)—destroys
- विश्वे ऊमाः (*viśve ūmāḥ*)—all living beings
- यं (*yaṃ*)—whom, the sun-natured Indra
- अनु (*anu*)—looking up to, seeing
- मदंति (*madaṃti*)—rejoice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Among all the worlds, earth and the rest, Brahman (Parabrahman) alone, taught in all Vedānta as the cause of the world, was in the beginning of all. From that Brahman was born Indra, exceedingly powerful, shining with exceeding brilliance, of sun-nature. As soon as born, that Indra became the destroyer of enemies, and all living beings, seeing him, rejoiced.

##### English translation
That was the chiefest in all worlds, from whence the fierce one, the rich in radiance, was born; as soon as born, he destroys the foes, he in whom all living beings delight.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk it is said that before everything, that is, before creation, only the Parabrahman taught in all Vedānta existed in the beginning, and from it Indra, of sun-nature, was born. That Indra's power is immeasurable; as soon as he was born he subdued the enemies.

### Printed p. 603
Seeing such an Indra, all beings are described as showing joy. The four pādas of this Ṛk describe four separate matters, and it is necessary to explain each separately.

तत् इत् आस भुवनेषु ज्येष्ठं (*tat it āsa bhuvaneṣu jyeṣṭhaṃ*)—तत् (*tat*) means that thing. Which thing? The thing called Parabrahman, famed as the cause of the world and examined in the darśanas such as all Vedānta. The word तत् (*tat*) in the great saying तत्त्वमसि (*tattvamasi*) (tat + tvam + asi) also points to this same meaning. Since Parabrahman has no distinctions of gender, female or male, it is indicated by neuter words such as तत् (*tat*) and Brahman. For the word ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*) several meanings are given here. ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*) means प्रशस्ततमं (*praśastatamaṃ*): the most excellent, most praiseworthy. Or परमार्थत्वात् तद्व्यतिरिक्तानां व्यावहारिकत्वाच्च (*paramārthatvāt tadvyatiriktānāṃ vyāvahārikatvācca*): this is different from all the things in the world. Other things are subject to destruction; Brahman is not. Therefore, from the standpoint of practical life, it is wholly different from the other things of the world. Its nature resembles nothing. Or ज्येष्ठं वृद्धतमं जगत्कारणत्वेन सर्वेषामादिभूतं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ vṛddhatamaṃ jagatkāraṇatvena sarveṣāmādibhūtaṃ*): this Brahman is the cause of the world, that is, all worlds arose from it; therefore it is the beginning and root of all. There is nothing that existed before it; it is the first of all. Such Parabrahman, in the beginning of all creation, was alone, shining by itself with its own light; this is the meaning of the sentence.

Passages describing the nature of Brahman are especially numerous in the various Upaniṣads and Vedānta works.

ब्रह्म देवानजनयत् । ब्रह्म विश्वमिदं जगत् । ब्रह्मणः क्षत्रं निर्मितं । ब्रह्म ब्राह्मण आत्मना । अंतरस्मिन्निमे लोकाः । अंतर्विश्वमिदं जगत् । ब्रह्मैव भूतानां ज्येष्ठं । तेन कोऽर्हति स्पर्धितुं । ब्रह्मदेवास्त्रयस्त्रिग्ंशत् । ब्रह्मन्निंद्रप्रजापती । ब्रह्मन् ह विश्वा भूतानि । नावीवान्तः समाहिता ॥ (*brahma devānajanayat | brahma viśvamidaṃ jagat | brahmaṇaḥ kṣatraṃ nirmitaṃ | brahma brāhmaṇa ātmanā | aṃtarasminnime lokāḥ | aṃtarviśvamidaṃ jagat | brahmaiva bhūtānāṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ | tena ko 'rhati spardhituṃ | brahmadevāstrayastrigṃśat | brahmanniṃdraprajāpatī | brahman ha viśvā bhūtāni | nāvīvāntaḥ samāhitā ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 2-8-8-9, 10).

Brahman, that is Parabrahman, produced the gods. Not only that: this whole universe is itself of the nature of Brahman. The Kṣatriya class was created by Brahman. The Brāhmaṇa is himself of the nature of Brahman. In this Brahman all the worlds, this whole world, are contained. This Brahman is the chief, the most praiseworthy, the beginning, of the five great elements beginning with earth and of all living beings. Who is able to compete with such a Brahman in power and ability? As is said in the Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad, न तत्समश्चाभ्यधिकश्च दृश्यते (*na tatsamaścābhyadhikaśca dṛśyate*): none is seen equal to or greater than this Brahman. This Brahman

### Printed p. 604

…in that very Brahman the thirty-three gods are hidden. Indra and Prajāpati too are contained within Brahman. All beings likewise dwell in this Brahman, as people gathered in one place in a boat when crossing a river.

In the Taittirīya Upaniṣad:

यतो वा इमानि भूतानि जायंते । येन जातानि जीवंति । यत्प्रयंत्यभिसंविशंति । तद्विजिज्ञासस्व । तद्ब्रह्मेति ॥ (*yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyaṃte | yena jātāni jīvaṃti | yatprayaṃtyabhisaṃviśaṃti | tadvijijñāsasva | tadbrahmeti ‖*) (Tai. U. 3-1)

That supreme-of-the-supreme reality from which all these beings are born, by whose power the born beings live, and into which at the end they merge and perish: that is Brahman. In the sentence यो देवानां प्रथमं पुरस्तात् (*yo devānāṃ prathamaṃ purastāt*) (Tai. U. 4-12-3) it is said that this Brahman is the foremost and the first of all the gods. In another place of the same Upaniṣad:

यतो वाचो निवर्तंते । अप्राप्य मनसा सह। आनंदं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान् । न बिभेति कदाचनेति ॥ (*yato vāco nivartaṃte | aprāpya manasā saha| ānaṃdaṃ brahmaṇo vidvān | na bibheti kadācaneti ‖*) (Tai. U. 2-4)

This Supreme Brahman cannot be described in words, nor contemplated by the mind; it lies beyond speech and mind. The discerning person who obtains the bliss that arises from knowing this nature of Brahman has no fear, affliction or sorrow of any kind. So it is said.

And in the Kena Upaniṣad**NOTE**:

केनेषितं पतति प्रेषितं मनः केन प्राणः प्रथमः प्रैति युक्तः । केनेषितां वाचमिमां वदंति चक्षुः श्रोत्रं क उ देवो युनक्ति ॥ (*keneṣitaṃ patati preṣitaṃ manaḥ kena prāṇaḥ prathamaḥ praiti yuktaḥ | keneṣitāṃ vācamimāṃ vadaṃti cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ ka u devo yunakti ‖*) (Kena. U. 1-1)

By whose wish, by whose impulsion does this mind engage in its object? By whose command does the breath first begin its work? By whose wish do people speak? Who is the deity that commands the eyes and ears? The answer to these questions is given there itself:

शोत्रस्य शोत्रं मनसो मनो यद्वाचो ह वाचं स उ प्राणस्य प्राणश्चक्षुषश्चक्षुरतिमुच्य धीराः प्रेत्यास्माल्लोकादमृता भवंति ॥ (*śotrasya śotraṃ manaso mano yadvāco ha vācaṃ sa u prāṇasya prāṇaścakṣuṣaścakṣuratimucya dhīrāḥ pretyāsmāllokādamṛtā bhavaṃti ‖*) (Kesa. U. 1-2)**NOTE**

That which is the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind, the speech of speech, is the breath of the breath and the eye of the eye. The wise go beyond these, that is, pass beyond these organs; and after departing from this world they attain the state of immortality (the deathless state of liberation).

### Printed p. 605

न तत्र चक्षुर्गच्छति न वाग्गच्छति नो मनो न विद्यो न विजानीमो यथैतदनुशिष्यादन्यदेव तद्विदितादधो अविदितादधि । इति शुश्रुम पूर्वेषां ये नस्तद्वाचक्षिरे ॥ (*na tatra cakṣurgacchati na vāggacchati no mano na vidyo na vijānīmo yathaitadanuśiṣyādanyadeva tadviditādadho aviditādadhi | iti śuśruma pūrveṣāṃ ye nastadvācakṣire ‖*) (Kesa. U. 1-3)

Our sight cannot go to where That, that is, that Brahman, is. Our power of speech cannot reach it. Our mind cannot go and touch it that far. We do not know it. We do not know it so completely that we could instruct disciples and make it known to them. It is beyond what is known and what is not known. Thus we have heard from the forebears who taught us that knowledge.

यद्वाचानभ्युदितं येनवागभ्युद्यते । तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥ यन्मनसा न मनुते येनाहुर्मनो मतं । तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते । यच्चक्षुषा न पश्यति येन चक्षूंषि पश्यति । तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥ यच्छोत्रेण न शृणोति येन श्रोत्रमिदं श्रुतं । तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥ यत्प्राणेन न प्राणिति येन प्राणः प्रणीयते । तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥ (*yadvācānabhyuditaṃ yenavāgabhyudyate | tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ‖ yanmanasā na manute yenāhurmano mataṃ | tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate | yaccakṣuṣā na paśyati yena cakṣūṃṣi paśyati | tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ‖ yacchotreṇa na śṛṇoti yena śrotramidaṃ śrutaṃ | tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ‖ yatprāṇena na prāṇiti yena prāṇaḥ praṇīyate | tadeva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yadidamupāsate ‖*) (Kena. U. 1-4-8)

Know that to be Brahman which cannot be described by the power of speech, by whose power speech (the power of speaking) is manifested. What people worship as Brahman is not Brahman. Know that to be Brahman which cannot be reasoned about with the help of the mind, but of which the mind itself is the object of reflection. Know that to be Brahman which cannot be seen with the eyes (cannot be seen), but which can see the eyes themselves. Know that to be Brahman which cannot be heard and known by the ears, but which hears the ears themselves. Know that to be Brahman which does not breathe by the help of breath, but which makes the vital breath itself breathe. What people are worshipping as Brahman is not Brahman.

In the Taittirīya Upaniṣad:

सत्यं ज्ञानमनंतं ब्रह्म । यो वेद निहितं गुहायां परमे व्योमन् सोऽश्नुते सर्वान्कामान् सह । ब्रह्मणा विपश्चितेति ॥ (*satyaṃ jñānamanaṃtaṃ brahma | yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ parame vyoman so 'śnute sarvānkāmān saha | brahmaṇā vipaściteti ‖*) (Tai. U. 2-1)

### Printed p. 606

What is Brahman? Brahman is of the nature of truth. Merely because it is subtle and not perceptible to the outer eye, one cannot say that it does not exist or that its existence is not true. That it exists is certain; because our power of sight has a limit, we cannot see it with our eyes. ज्ञानं (*jñānaṃ*) means understanding, consciousness. Granting that Brahman exists, though in a subtle state, what power has it? Is it not an inert thing like a mountain? No: it is endowed with consciousness and has the power of knowing everything. Not only that; it is the source of all the consciousness and knowledge in the universe. From it, as its parts, come the consciousness and knowledge of all beings. Now what is the meaning of the word अनंतं (*anaṃtaṃ*)? Does that Brahman, which through the two qualities just stated (being always existent, and consisting of consciousness or knowledge) exists only somewhere in one place? No. It is pervasive everywhere; it has neither end nor beginning. There is no place, time or thing where it is not. अंत (*aṃta*) means end; अनंत (*anaṃta*) means that which has no end. One cannot say, "The Brahman-reality ends here; this is its end; beyond this it is not." It has neither end nor beginning; it has no limitation of place, time or thing; it was in the past, it is now, it will be in the future. In all times, in all regions, in all things, it is pervasive. The main sense is this: the person who knows this Brahman, of the nature of being-consciousness-bliss and infinite, to be established in the most secret region, his heart, and worships it, becomes one with that omniscient Brahman, obtains all his desires, and experiences unsurpassed bliss.

In another place of the Taittirīya Upaniṣad (Tai. U. 4-1) the nature of this Supreme Brahman is described at length and very well. Only its essence is set out here:

अंभस्य पारे भुवनस्य मध्यॆ नाकस्य पृष्ठे महतो महीयान् । शुक्रेण ज्योतीग्ंषि समनुप्रविष्टः प्रजापतिश्चरति गर्भे अंतः । (*aṃbhasya pāre bhuvanasya madhyè nākasya pṛṣṭhe mahato mahīyān | śukreṇa jyotīgṃṣi samanupraviṣṭaḥ prajāpatiścarati garbhe aṃtaḥ |*) (Tai. U. 4-1)

This Brahman is greater than all the great things there are in the Lokāloka regions at the farthest end of the many oceans, in the middle region of the worlds beginning with the earth, and on the upper part of heaven. With its shining divine light it enters the heart-lights of all beings, and, being in those beings in the form of the soul (in the form of consciousness), governs their movements.

यस्मिन्निदग्ं सं च वि चैति सर्वं यस्मिन्देवा अधि विश्वे निषेदुः । तदेव भूतं तदु भव्यमा इदं तदक्षरे परमे व्योमन् ॥ (*yasminnidagṃ saṃ ca vi caiti sarvaṃ yasmindevā adhi viśve niṣeduḥ | tadeva bhūtaṃ tadu bhavyamā idaṃ tadakṣare parame vyoman ‖*)

### Printed p. 607

In that Supreme Brahman the whole world is contained; that is, at the time of creation it appears in manifest form; at the time of dissolution, unmanifest (in subtle form), it is absorbed and contained in Brahman itself. In that Brahman all the gods are contained. From that Brahman of unmanifest nature the origin of all the gods took place. At the end they all become one in Brahman. That Brahman itself is the support of the whole world that was, is, and will be created. In this imperishable Supreme Brahman, which like the sky is in the unmanifest state in subtle form, the whole universe is contained.

येनावृतं खं च दिवं महीं च येनादित्यस्तपति तेजसा भ्राजसा च । यमंतःसमुद्रे कवयो वयंति तदक्षरे परमे प्रजाः ॥ (*yenāvṛtaṃ khaṃ ca divaṃ mahīṃ ca yenādityastapati tejasā bhrājasā ca | yamaṃtaḥsamudre kavayo vayaṃti tadakṣare parame prajāḥ ‖*)

The sky, heaven and this vast earth are all enveloped by this Brahman; that is, Brahman pervades these worlds within and without. The shining sun too, by the power of this Brahman, is able to spread his rays and shine. Whatever moving and unmoving things and beings the poets (seers) have described in this whole world together with its seas, all of them are contained in this imperishable Supreme Brahman.

यतः प्रसूता जगतः प्रसूती तोयेन जीवान्वचसर्ज भूम्यां । यदोषधीभिः पुरुषान्पशूग्‌श्च विवेश भूतानि चराचराणि ॥ (*yataḥ prasūtā jagataḥ prasūtī toyena jīvānvacasarja bhūmyāṃ | yadoṣadhībhiḥ puruṣānpaśūgśca viveśa bhūtāni carācarāṇi ‖*)

From Brahman the creation of this world came about; and from the five elements beginning with water the beings on earth came into being. Through food (nourishment) produced by plants and trees (vegetation), that Brahman entered human beings and other beings and nourished them. Nourishing by water and the like the moving and unmoving things such as trees, and being within them, he made them grow.

अतःपरं नान्यदणीयसग्ं हि परात्परं यन्महतो महांतं । यदेकमव्यक्तमनंतरूपं विश्वं पुराणं तमसः परस्तात् ॥ (*ataḥparaṃ nānyadaṇīyasagṃ hi parātparaṃ yanmahato mahāṃtaṃ | yadekamavyaktamanaṃtarūpaṃ viśvaṃ purāṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt ‖*)

There is no thing more excellent or greater than this Supreme Brahman. There is nothing smaller or subtler than this, nor anything larger than this. This Brahman shines of itself, without a second, that is, with nothing equal to it. It is in the unmanifest (subtle) state, imperceptible to the senses. It is infinite, without limitation by place, time or thing. It comprises the whole universe. It shines luminous, distinct from tamas, that is, darkness or ignorance. It is also beginningless.

### Printed p. 608

तदेवर्तं तदु सत्यमाहुस्तदेव ब्रह्म परमं कवीनां । इष्टापूर्तं बहुधा जातं जायमानं विश्वं बिभर्ति भुवनस्य नाभिः ॥ (*tadevartaṃ tadu satyamāhustadeva brahma paramaṃ kavīnāṃ | iṣṭāpūrtaṃ bahudhā jātaṃ jāyamānaṃ viśvaṃ bibharti bhuvanasya nābhiḥ ‖*)

Whether contemplated in the mind or described in words, that Brahman-reality is truth itself, say those who know. The poets have called this the supreme Brahman. The sacrifice-form too is this Brahman. All the worlds created in former kalpas and all the worlds now created are this Brahman. This Brahman, which is like the navel of the world, that is, which has entered the worlds in the form of consciousness and dwells there, upholds and nourishes the whole world by its power.

तदेवाग्निस्तद्वायुस्तत्सूर्यस्तदु चंद्रमाः । तदेव शुक्रममृतं तद्ब्रह्म तदासः स प्रजापतिः ॥ (*tadevāgnistadvāyustatsūryastadu caṃdramāḥ | tadeva śukramamṛtaṃ tadbrahma tadāsaḥ sa prajāpatiḥ ‖*)

Agni too is of the nature of that Brahman. Likewise the wind, the sun and the moon, the shining starry sphere, the five elements beginning with water, and Prajāpati in the form of Virāṭ: all these are that Brahman itself.

सर्वे निमेषा जज्जिरे विद्युतः पुरुषादधि । कला मुहूर्ताः काष्ठाश्च होरात्राश्च सर्वशः ॥ अर्धमासा मासा ऋतवः संवत्सरश्च कल्पंतां । स आपः प्रदुघे उभे इमे अंतरिक्षमथो सवः ॥ (*sarve nimeṣā jajjire vidyutaḥ puruṣādadhi | kalā muhūrtāḥ kāṣṭhāśca horātrāśca sarvaśaḥ ‖ ardhamāsā māsā ṛtavaḥ saṃvatsaraśca kalpaṃtāṃ | sa āpaḥ pradughe ubhe ime aṃtarikṣamatho savaḥ ‖*)

From that self-luminous Brahman the divisions of time arose, that is, nimeṣa (the time of closing and opening the eyelid), kāṣṭhā, kalā, muhūrta, day, night, fortnight (fifteen days, or half-month), month, seasons, year; all these divisions of time, having come into being, are of the nature of this Supreme Brahman. This Brahman, who is of the nature of time, created the earth together with the five elements beginning with water, the atmosphere and heaven.

नैनमूर्ध्वं न तिर्यंचं न मध्ये परिजग्रभत् । न तस्येशे कश्चन तस्य नाम महद्यशः । (*nainamūrdhvaṃ na tiryaṃcaṃ na madhye parijagrabhat | na tasyeśe kaścana tasya nāma mahadyaśaḥ |*)

Since this Brahman is all-pervading, it has none of the divisions called upper part, lower part, breadth, length, height, middle. It is not under anyone's control; that is, there is no one who exercises authority over it. Because it is thus entirely independent, its glory, that is, its greatness, is immeasurable.

न संदृशे तिष्ठति रूपमस्य न चक्षुषा पश्यति कश्चनैनं । हृदा मनीषा मनसाभिक्ल्प्नो य एनं विदुरमृतास्ते भवंति ॥ (*na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpamasya na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścanainaṃ | hṛdā manīṣā manasābhiklpno ya enaṃ viduramṛtāste bhavaṃti ‖*)

### Printed p. 609

This Brahman is not a thing that is visible to anyone. No person is able to see its form with the eye. Those who, meditating with the mind on this Supreme Brahman dwelling in the lotus of the heart, realise and know it, become deathless and obtain the eternal supreme state. (Trai. U. 4-1)**NOTE**

Besides these, there are many mantras and sentences in the Vedas and Upaniṣads that try to convey the nature of Brahman. Since explaining this Supreme Brahman in one way or another is the purpose of all the Upaniṣads, it is not possible to set out all of them here. Therefore this account is stopped here and the explanation of the present Ṛk will be continued.

यतो जज्ञ उग्र स्वेषनृष्णः (*yato jajña ugra sveṣanṛṣṇaḥ*)—from which Brahman Indra, उद्धूर्णः (*uddhūrṇaḥ*) (of kindled strength), of the nature of the sun, was born. From this Supreme Brahman Indra came into being, most brilliant, powerful and of the nature of the sun. In the mantras quoted above it is said that Agni, Indra and the Sun arose from Brahman. Besides, in the mantra चक्षोः सूर्यो अजायत्त (*cakṣoḥ sūryo ajāyatta*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-90-13) it is said that the sun was born from the eye of this Brahman, that is, of the Supreme Person. And in the mantra सूर्याचंद्रमसौ धाता यथा पूर्वमकल्पयत् (*sūryācaṃdramasau dhātā yathā pūrvamakalpayat*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-190-3)**NOTE**, it is said that this Brahman created the sun and moon in this kalpa too, as in the former kalpa. Here identity of the sun and Indra is stated. Indra and the Sun are both parts of that Brahman. And in many places they are described as lords of the world and as themselves of the nature of Brahman. The Śruti sentence असावादित्यो ब्रह्मेति (*asāvādityo brahmeti*) (this Āditya who is visible to our eyes is none other than Brahman) supports this.

सद्यः जज्ञानः नि रिणाति शत्रून् (*sadyaḥ jajñānaḥ ni riṇāti śatrūn*)—as soon as he was born, this Indra destroyed his enemies. Other people become able to fight enemies and kill them only many years after birth, that is, after passing childhood and boyhood and reaching youth. But the case of Indra is not so. As soon as he was born, he was able to slay enemies with his extraordinary strength and power. In the case of the Sun too, as soon as the Sun is born he destroys the enemies of the form of darkness and makes light for the whole world; that is, as soon as the Sun rises the darkness goes and light arises. Or else, in accordance with the Aitareya Āraṇyaka sentence सद्यो ह्येष जातः पाप्मानमपाहत (*sadyo hyeṣa jātaḥ pāpmānamapāhata*) (Ai. Ā. 1-3-4), as soon as the Sun rises he removes the sins of the people who worship him, or destroys the Mandeha and other Rākṣasas. On this subject a legend is told in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka—

### Printed p. 610
(This passage, with the itihāsa announced at the end of the previous page, is quoted from Sāyaṇa's Taittirīya Āraṇyaka citation, Tai. Ā. 2-2.) Ṛ. Saṃ. Mandala 10, Sūkta 120.

Once, in the earlier anuvāka, the demons practised severe austerity. Prajāpati the god appeared before them and asked what boon they wished for. They begged: "Grant us the power and the opportunity to fight with the Sun." Prajāpati consented: "So be it." For this reason the demons, as soon as the Sun rises, begin to fight him and go on fighting until his setting. But they can be driven away by water (the arghya water) sanctified by the recitation of the Gāyatrī. Therefore the Brahmavādins, at the morning and evening twilights, recite the Gāyatrī mantra and offer arghya with the water so purified. These drops of water offered as arghya turn into a thunderbolt and hurl the demons who are fighting the Sun into the island called Mandeha-Aruṇa. After that the Brahmavādins, by the twilight worship with circumambulation and obeisance, shake off their sin. The Brahmin who knows this truth (the knower of Brahman), reciting the Gāyatrī at sunrise and sunset and offering arghya, worships Āditya thereby, and obtains every kind of welfare. Āditya is the Supreme Brahman. The person who worships, knowing that Āditya, the object of Gāyatrī worship, is Brahman, attains union with Brahman, becomes Brahman and is merged in Brahman. So it is said.

"All the beings rejoice (ūmāḥ) after him": in the last pada of this Ṛk it is said that all creatures rejoice on seeing the Sun rise. At night, because of darkness, creatures have trouble in moving about and in getting their food, and there is the possibility of other afflictions such as enemies; therefore all creatures (men too)

### Printed p. 611
await the Sun's arrival and welcome his rising with joy. On this point the commentator has cited the Aitareya Āraṇyaka sentence भूतानि वै विश्व ऊमास्त एनमनुमदंत्युदगादुदगादिति (*bhūtāni vai viśva ūmāsta enamanumadaṃtyudagādudagāditi*) (Ai. Ā. 1-3-4) and the Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentence तस्मात्सर्व एव मन्यते मां प्रत्युदगादिति (*tasmātsarva eva manyate māṃ pratyudagāditi*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-5-4-2). The origin of Indra, being of the nature of the Sun, is also stated here: "such an Indra was born."

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वा॒वृ॒धा॒नः शव॑सा॒ भूर्यो॑जाः॒ शत्रु॑र्दा॒साय॑ भि॒यसं॑ दधाति।  
> अव्य॑नच्च व्य॒नच्च॒ सस्नि॒ सं ते॑ नवंत॒ प्रभृ॑ता॒ मदे॑षु ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ववृधानः । शवसा । भूरिऽओजाः । शत्रुः । दासाय । भियसं । दधाति ।  
> अविऽअनत् । च । विऽअनत् । च । सस्नि । सं । ते । नवंत । प्रभृता । मदेषु ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शवसा बलेन ववृधानो वर्धमानः अत एव भूर्योजा बहुबलः शत्रुः
> शातयितेंद्रो दासायोपक्षयकारिणे शत्रवे भयसं भीतिं दधाति । विदधाति ।
> करोति । अव्यनत् । विविधमनिति श्वसितीति व्यनत् प्राणवज्जंगमं । तद्विलक्षणमव्यनत्
> स्थावरं । तदुभयमपि सस्नि संस्नातमिंद्रेण सम्यक्कोधितं भवति ॥ स्नातेरादृगमहन
> इत्ति । व्यत्ययेन कर्मणि किन्प्रत्ययः ॥ यद्वा ॥ अंतर्णीतण्यर्थात्कर्तर्येव किन् ॥
> वृष्ट्यादिना सम्यक् स्थापयिता शोधयिता भवति ॥ न लोकाव्ययेति कर्मणि षष्ठ्याः
> प्रतिषेधः ॥ शिष्टः पादः प्रत्यक्षकृतः । हे इंद्र ते तव मदेषु हर्षेषु हविषा
> स्तुत्या च जातेषु सत्तु प्रभृता प्रभृतानि प्रकर्षण धृतानि पोषितानि ना सर्वाणि
> भूतजातानि संनवंत। संगच्छंते। स्तोतुं हवींषि च दातुं समूहीभवंतीत्यर्थः ।
> नवतिर्गतिकर्मा ॥ प्रभृता । बिभर्तॆः कर्मणि निष्ठा । शेश्पंदसि बहुलमिति शेर्लोपः ।
> गतिरनंतर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, growing by strength and therefore of great might, is the destroyer (śatru) of the foe; he puts fear into the Dāsa, the harmful enemy. Avyanat is the immovable (the unbreathing), vyanat the moving (the breathing, living); both are purified (sasni) by Indra, i.e. made properly clean. Alternative: the form is active in sense, since the suffix is used by interchange; Indra is the one who by rain and the like duly establishes and cleanses. The genitive with the object is not prohibited here by the rule on lokāvyaya. The remaining pada is plain: O Indra, when joys arise in you through oblation and praise, all creatures, nourished (prabhṛtā) by you, come together (saṃ navanta) to praise and to give oblations; navati is a verb of motion.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शवसा (*śavasā*)—by strength
- ववृधानः (*vavṛdhānaḥ*)—growing (and therefore)
- भूर्योजाः (*bhūryojāḥ*)—of much power and capacity
- शत्रुः (*śatruḥ*)—destroyer of enemies, or the enemy of demons etc., that Indra
### Printed p. 612
- दासाय (*dāsāya*)—to the harmful Dasyu people
- भियसं (*bhiyasaṃ*)—fear
- दधाति (*dadhāti*)—produces (that Indra)
- व्यनत् च (*vyanat ca*)—the world of breathing creatures
- अव्यनत् च (*avyanat ca*)—the immovable fixed things
- सस्नि (*sasni*)—he makes pure by rain etc.
- ते (*te*)—to you (O Indra)
- मदेषु (*madeṣu*)—when joy arises through the oblation and praise offered by people
- प्रभृता (*prabhṛtā*)—all creatures
- सं नवंत (*saṃ navaṃta*)—gather together in one place to praise you and offer you oblations

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, growing in strength day by day and of exceeding power and capacity, causes fear to the Dasyus, the enemies of good people; that is, seeing his great power the Dasyus are terrified. He nourishes all creatures, both fixed and moving, with rain and the like. For Indra's delight all creatures, that is, people, gather together in one place to offer him oblation and praise; that is, at the sacrificial altar all people, the priests, the sacrificers and the rest, assemble and praise Indra.

##### English translation
Waxing in strength, the very powerful, destructive (Indra), implants fear in the Dasa ; both the inanimate and the animate (world) is purified by him. Nourished in your exhilaration (all creatures) are assembled.

> सु सुष्पभि योधीः । अभियोधय । अभितः क्रीडय ॥ धातूनामनेकार्थत्वाद्युध्यतिरत्र क्रीडार्थ वर्तते ॥ मिथुनं वै स्वादु प्रजा स्वादु । ऐ. आ. १-३-४ । इत्यादि
> ब्राह्मणमत्रानुसंधेयं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, in you all sacrificers complete (vṛñjanti) the rite to be performed. The word api signifies the inclusion of all beings and all minds mentioned in the Brāhmaṇa: all elements, earth and the rest, the minds of all creatures and all sacrifices are completed by the sacrificers in you who are all-pervading. So the Brāhmaṇa: त्वयिमानि सर्वाणि भूतानि सर्वाणि मनांसि सर्वॆ क्रतवोऽपि वृंजंतीत्येव तद (*tvayimāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni sarvāṇi manāṃsi sarvè kratavo 'pi vṛṃjaṃtītyeva tada*) (Ai. Ā. 1-3-4). Since these ūmāḥ (satisfiers; the word derived from the root av in the sense of satisfying with an Uṇādi suffix) sacrificers, first single, are afterwards born twice as woman and man, and again thrice with offspring: one self is born as woman and man, by the śruti that the wife is half of oneself; the son is also the self, by the śruti आत्मा वै पुत्रनामासि (*ātmā vai putranāmāsi*) (Śa. 14-9-26). Since they thus prosper, it is understood that they complete in you all the rite performed. So the Brāhmaṇa: द्वै वै संतौ मिथुनौ प्रजायेते प्रजात्यै (*dvai vai saṃtau mithunau prajāyete prajātyai*) (Ai. Ā. 1-3-4). O Indra, unite us with a child sweeter than the sweet, dearer than home and wealth, with the sweet pair of mother and father. Or: unite also the offspring born of the sweet state. That offspring is honey; with another honey, the pair that causes joy, or the grandson, "fight" (yodhīḥ), i.e. sport around; for roots have many meanings, yudh here has the sense of play. The Brāhmaṇa मिथुनं वै स्वादु प्रजा स्वादु (*mithunaṃ vai svādu prajā svādu*) (Ai. Ā. 1-3-4) etc. is to be borne in mind here.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्वे (*tve*)—in you (O Indra)
- विश्वे अपि (*viśve api*)—all the sacrificers
- क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*)—the sacrificial rite they perform
- वृंजंति (*vṛṃjaṃti*)—offer and bring to completion
- यत् (*yat*)—because
- एते ऊमाः (*ete ūmāḥ*)—these sacrificers (single before the sacrifice, afterwards)
- द्विः (*dviḥ*)—two, as husband and wife (then)
- त्रिः (*triḥ*)—three, joined by a son along with husband and wife
- स्वादोः (*svādoḥ*)—than house, wealth and the like, dear to us
- स्वादीयः (*svādīyaḥ*)—you are exceedingly dear (and)
- स्वादुना (*svādunā*)—with our dear offspring
- सं सृज (*saṃ sṛja*)—unite us (and further)
- मधु (*madhu*)—dear to us
- अदः (*adaḥ*)—that offspring of ours, the son etc.
- मधुना (*madhunā*)—with the delightful grandson-line
- अभि योधीः (*abhi yodhīḥ*)—make them sport
### Printed p. 614

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, all sacrificers offer to you the rites such as sacrifice that they perform and have them completed in you. For before sacrificing these sacrificers, being without wives, were single; but since wives are necessary in sacrificing, they joined them and became two, husband and wife. Then, by your grace, may we, accompanied by husband and wife, obtain a son-line dear to us, and through that son-line a delightful grandson-line, and sport with them.

##### English translation
To you all (worshippers) offer adoration, whether those propitiators be two or three. Combine that which is sweeter than the sweet with sweet-ness, unite that honey with honey.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The meaning of this Ṛk is somewhat difficult; other words must be supplied here and there to fit the sense.

क्रतुं अपि वृंजंति विश्वे (*kratuṃ api vṛṃjaṃti viśve*)—for the word api Sāyaṇa says अपिशब्दो ब्राह्मणोक्त सर्वभूतानां सर्वमनसां समुच्चयार्थः (*apiśabdo brāhmaṇokta sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvamanasāṃ samuccayārthaḥ*): it denotes the sense of "and", that is, all creatures stated in the Brāhmaṇa śruti sentence and their minds. In the Aitareya Āraṇyaka it is said त्वयिमानि सर्वाणि भूतानि सर्वाणि मनांसि सर्वॆ क्रतवोऽपि वृंजंतीत्येव तदाह (*tvayimāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni sarvāṇi manāṃsi sarvè kratavo 'pi vṛṃjaṃtītyeva tadāha*) (Ai. Ā. 1-3-4). Its meaning is सर्वाणि पृथिव्यादीनि भूतानि सर्वेषां प्राणिनां मनांसि सर्वॆ यज्ञ क्रतवश्च व्याप्ते त्वय्येव यजमानैः परिसमाप्यंत इत्यर्थः । (*sarvāṇi pṛthivyādīni bhūtāni sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ manāṃsi sarvè yajña kratavaśca vyāpte tvayyeva yajamānaiḥ parisamāpyaṃta ityarthaḥ |*): O Indra, the worlds such as earth, all creatures in them, their minds, all sacrificial rites are completed in you, the all-pervading; and so all sacrificers offer the rites they perform to you. That is: from Indra, who is of the nature of the Sun, arise the worlds such as earth, all creatures, their minds, that is their activities, and sacrificial rites; therefore in the end they are merged, that is completed, in Indra; with this firm conviction the sacrificers offer all the rites they perform to you alone.

द्विः यत् एते त्रिः भवंति ऊमाः (*dviḥ yat ete triḥ bhavaṃti ūmāḥ*)—the word ūmāḥ, according to the sūtra अवतेस्तर्पणार्थादौणादिको मन् प्रत्ययः (*avatestarpaṇārthādauṇādiko man pratyayaḥ*), means "those who give satisfaction"; that is, sacrificers who satisfy the gods by offering oblations and the like. While in the brahmacarya stage these sacrificers are alone, single (without a wife).
### Printed p. 615
A wife is necessary to perform a sacrifice; since the wife has her part in the rite, the sacrificer must have a wife; a man without a wife cannot sacrifice. Therefore द्विः भवंति (*dviḥ bhavaṃti*): the sacrificers, single in that stage, marry and become of two forms, husband and wife. In the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa: अथो अर्थो वा एष आत्मनः । यत्पत्नि ॥ (*atho artho vā eṣa ātmanaḥ | yatpatni ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 3-3-3-5): the wife is half of the man. Husband and wife must sacrifice together, for अयज्ञो वा एषः । योऽपत्निकः ॥ (*ayajño vā eṣaḥ | yo 'patnikaḥ ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 3-3-3-1): the sacrifice of one without a wife does not count as a sacrifice, it is said there. So in sacrificing for Indra's pleasure the sacrificer and his wife, two, are needed; this is what द्विः भवंति (*dviḥ bhavaṃti*) says here.

एते त्रिः भवंति (*ete triḥ bhavaṃti*)—here triḥ is three: the sacrificer, his wife and their offspring (son or daughter). By the fruit of performing the sacrifice the sacrificer obtains offspring, and they become three. By the śruti आत्मा वै पुत्रनामासि (*ātmā vai putranāmāsi*) the son too is a part of the man, so the man has become three: himself, his wife, his son; this is the main sense.

स्वादोः स्वादीयः स्वादुना संसृज (*svādoḥ svādīyaḥ svādunā saṃsṛja*)—svādu means sweet, dear. O Indra, you are dearer to us than a dear thing. Such as you, unite us with a dear son; that is, grant a son: this is the sense of the sentence.

अदु मधु मधुना सु योधीः (*adu madhu madhunā su yodhīḥ*)—And, O Indra, it is not enough that you grant us a son; cause a dear grandson also to be born from the son you grant. That is, give us sons, grandsons and the rest, and let us live in happiness and joy, sporting with them. The seer prays that our line may prosper through offspring of sons and grandsons.

> इति चिद्येवमेव खलु हे इंद्र मदे मदे सोमपानजन्ये हर्षे सति धना
> शत्रुधनानि जयंतं जयेन प्राप्नुवंतं त्वामनु पश्चात् ॥ लक्षणेऽनोः कर्मप्रवचनीयत्वं ॥ विप्रा मेधाविनः स्तोतारो मदंति हृष्यंति यद्वा त्वामनुवदंति
> अनुक्रमेण स्तुवंति । मदतिः स्तुतिकर्मा ॥ हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥ हे दृष्टो
> शत्रुवाणां धर्षयितरिंद्र ॥ त्रसिगृधिधृषिक्षिपेः क्नुः ॥ ओजीयः ॥ ओजस्विशब्दादीयसुनि
> विन्मत्तोर्लुगिति विनो लुक् । टेरिति टिलोपः ॥ बलवत्तरं अत एव स्थिरं दृढं
> धनमा तनुष्ट । अभितोऽस्मदर्थं विस्तारय । त्वा त्वां च मा दभन् मा हिंसंतु
> दुरेवा दुर्गतयो यातुधाना राक्षसाः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Iti cid" means "thus indeed": O Indra, whenever there is exhilaration (mada) arising from drinking Soma, the wise (vipra) praisers rejoice after you, who win by conquest the wealth of your enemies. Here अनु (*anu*) is a karmapravacanīya in the sense of "after". Or else, they praise you in succession, since the root mada has the sense of praising. The non-accentuation (nighāta) is prevented by हि च (*hi ca*). "O bold one (dhṛṣṭo)" is addressed to Indra, the subduer of enemies. ओजीयः (*ojīyaḥ*) means stronger. Therefore, spread out for our sake wealth that is firm and secure, in every direction. May the evil-going Yātudhānas, the Rākṣasas, not harm you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इति चिद्दि (*iti ciddi*)—in this very manner
- मदेमदे (*mademade*)—when joy arises in you from drinking Soma
- धना (*dhanā*)—the wealth that is with the enemies
- जयंतं (*jayaṃtaṃ*)—you who conquer and bring it
- अनु (*anu*)—with reference to
- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—wise praisers
- मदंति (*madaṃti*)—delight you by praising
- दृष्टो (*dṛṣṭo*)—O Indra, defeater of enemies
- ओजीयः (*ojīyaḥ*)—of exceeding strength
- स्थिरं (*sthiraṃ*)—and firm wealth
- आ । तनुष्ट (*ā | tanuṣṭa*)—bring to us
- दुरेवाः (*durevāḥ*)—of evil going
- यातुधानाः (*yātudhānāḥ*)—the Rākṣasas called Yātudhānas
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- मा दभन् (*mā dabhan*)—let them not harm

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, thus, when joy arises in you from drinking Soma, wise praisers praise and delight you, who conquer the enemies and bring their wealth. O Indra, the subduer of enemies, supply us with abundant and lasting wealth. May the Yātudhānas, who roam in evil places, not harm you.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, favoured by you we शाशद्महे (*śāśadmahe*) in battles, that is, we greatly destroy our enemies (root शत्रु शातने (*śatru śātane*)). Doing what? Seeing clearly (prapaśyantaḥ) the many, abundant things that are fit for fighting (युधेन्यानि (*yudhenyāni*), with the sense of fitness). Moreover, I urge your weapons, the instruments of fighting such as the vajra, with words, that is, with praises; I incite them against the enemies. For you I prepare (सं शिशामि (*saṃ śiśāmi*)) the oblation-foods, the vayāṃsi (a name for food), together with the sacred verse (brahman) in the form of praise: I perfect them, that is, I consecrate them.

- शापद्महे (*śāpadmahe*)—we destroy the enemies

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, by your favour we, knowing well the strengths and weaknesses of the enemies in battle, destroy them. I praise your weapons, the vajra and others, with hymns and urge you to use them on the enemies. And, addressing you, I consecrate with mantras and the like the foods in the form of oblation and offer them.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

स्तुषेय्यं (*stuṣeyyaṃ*) means "to be praised" (an Uṇādi formation, Uṇ. Sū. 3-99). Many-formed (पुरुवर्पसं (*puruvarpasaṃ*)), shining widely, most lordly (इनतमं (*inatamaṃ*)), the one to be attained among those to be attained: such an Indra "I praise" (this is the word to be supplied). That Indra, with might (śavas), tears apart (आ दर्षते (*ā darṣate*)) the seven Dānavas, Vṛtra, Namuci, Kuyava and the rest.

> पदं । लेटोऽडाटावित्यडागमः । सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् ॥ तथा प्रतिमानान्यसुराणां
> प्रतिरूपाणि भूरि भूरीणि बहून्यसुरबलानि प्र साक्षते य इंद्रः प्रसहते । यद्वा ।
> बहूनि प्रतिमानान्यसुराणां स्थानानि प्र साक्षते प्राप्नोति । साक्षतिराप्नोतिकर्मेति
> यास्कः । नि. ११-१२ ॥ षह अभिभवे । लेट्यडागमः । सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् । टत्वकत्वषत्वानि । छांदसो दीर्घः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Likewise he overcomes (प्र साक्षते (*pra sākṣate*)) the many counterparts (pratimānāni) of the asuras, that is, the many asura forces. Or else he reaches the many places of the asuras. Yāska: साक्षतिराप्नोतिकर्मेति यास्कः । नि. ११-१२ (*sākṣatirāpnotikarmeti yāskaḥ | ni. 11-12*) (Ni. 11-12).

- य इंद्रः (*ya iṃdraḥ*)—the Indra who

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Indra who by his power tore apart seven chief Dānavas such as Vṛtra, Namuci and Kuyava, or the clouds; who can endure the excessive strength of the enemies, or can storm and seize their impregnable places: such an Indra, worthy of praise, able to assume many forms, exceedingly resplendent, lord of all, and among the gods to be invoked with prayer the most greatly prayed to, I praise.

##### English translation
I praise (Indra) who is worthy of praise, multiform, vast, supreme, most accessible of the accessible: he assails with might the seven Danavas, he overpowers many opposing hosts.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In explaining the word आप्त्यानां (*āptyānāṃ*) in this Ṛk, Yāska gives a nirvacana for the Ṛk:
आप्त्याः । आप्त्या अप्नोतेः । तेषामेष निपातो भवत्रैंद्रामृचि ॥ स्तुषेय्यं पुरुवर्पसमृभ्वमिनतमाप्त्यमाप्त्यानां ॥ आ दर्षते शवसा सप्तदानून्प्रसाक्षते प्रतिमानानि भूरि ॥ (*āptyāḥ | āptyā apnoteḥ | teṣāmeṣa nipāto bhavatraiṃdrāmṛci ‖ stuṣeyyaṃ puruvarpasamṛbhvaminatamāptyamāptyānāṃ ‖ ā darṣate śavasā saptadānūnprasākṣate pratimānāni bhūri ‖*) स्तोतव्यं बहुरूपमुरुभूतमीश्वरतममाप्तव्यमाप्तव्यानामादृणाति यः शवसा बलेन सप्तॆ दात्यनिति ना सप्तॆ दानवानिति ना प्रसाक्षते प्रतिमानानि बहूनि ॥ (*stotavyaṃ bahurūpamurubhūtamīśvaratamamāptavyamāptavyānāmādṛṇāti yaḥ śavasā balena saptè dātyaniti nā saptè dānavāniti nā prasākṣate pratimānāni bahūni ‖*) (Ni. 11-2-1)

### Printed p. 620
The word आप्त्या (*āptyā*) is derived from the root आप्ल व्याप्तौ (*āpla vyāptau*). It is used in this Indra-Ṛk by way of context.
स्तुषेय्यं पुरुवर्पसमृभ्वं (*stuṣeyyaṃ puruvarpasamṛbhvaṃ*)—स्तोतव्यं बहुरूपमुरुभूतमीश्वरतमं ॥ (*stotavyaṃ bahurūpamurubhūtamīśvaratamaṃ ‖*) The words in this pāda and in the next are epithets describing Indra's qualities. Indra is worthy of being praised; being a god of great glory, all people praise him. Indra can assume many forms. As the Śruti sentence इंद्रो मायाभि पुरुरूप एति (*iṃdro māyābhi pururūpa eti*) says, Indra by his power or glory is able to take whatever forms he wishes. ऋभ्वं (*ṛbhvaṃ*) is said to mean उरुभूतं (*urubhūtaṃ*): one of large form, or of excellent glory.
इनतमं आप्तं आप्त्यानां (*inatamaṃ āptaṃ āptyānāṃ*)—ईश्वरतमं आप्तव्यं आप्तव्यानां ॥ (*īśvaratamaṃ āptavyaṃ āptavyānāṃ ‖*) इन (*ina*) means master, lord, sovereign. इनतम (*inatama*) means the supreme or most excellent lord, the master of all. आप्त (*āpta*) means one worthy of being attained: people desire that they may attain him, that he may be obtained by them, or that he may come near them. Among gods endowed with such qualities, Indra is आप्तव्यं (*āptavyaṃ*), the one most desired to be near: people wish that Indra, being near, may hear their hymns and grant their desired ends. Hence people desire Indra more than all other gods; this is the main intention.
आ दर्षते शवसा सप्त दानून् (*ā darṣate śavasā sapta dānūn*)—आ दृणाति यः शवसा बलेन सप्त दात्यनिति वा सप्त दानवानिति वा॥ (*ā dṛṇāti yaḥ śavasā balena sapta dātyaniti vā sapta dānavāniti vā‖*) Two meanings are given here for the word दानवान् (*dānavān*). सप्त दात्यन्सप्तसर्पणशीलान् वृष्टुदकप्रदात्यन् मेघान्। (*sapta dātyansaptasarpaṇaśīlān vṛṣṭudakapradātyan meghān|*) One meaning: the clouds that move in the sky and give, that is, pour down, rain-water. Or else दानवानिति वा (*dānavāniti vā*): the Dānavas, the sons born of Danu, one of the wives of the sage Kaśyapa, are called Dānavas. Since they are of evil nature, it is customary to say that they belong to the group of asuras. Hence the sense of this sentence is: Indra by his strength and power tears apart the moving clouds, or the asuras called Dānavas.

### Printed p. 621
प्र साक्षते प्रतिमानानि भूरि (*pra sākṣate pratimānāni bhūri*)—प्र साक्षते प्रतिमानानि बहूनि ॥ (*pra sākṣate pratimānāni bahūni ‖*) Since it is said here that साक्षतिराप्पोति कर्मा (*sākṣatirāppoti karmā*) (sākṣati is a verb of reaching), प्रसाक्षते (*prasākṣate*) means he approaches, that is, approaches and defeats. The intention is: Indra overcomes the strength and power of many asuras, or approaches the places of the asuras and conquers them.

> आ । मातरा । स्थापयसे । जिगत्तू इति । अतः । इनोषि । कर्वरा । पुरूणि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तत्तस्मिन्यजमानस्य गृहेवरमल्पं भौमं धनं परमुत्कृष्टं दिवि भवं धनं
> च हे इंद्र त्वं नि दधिषे । निदधासि । निक्षिपसि । यस्मिन्नुरोणे गृहेवसा । अन्ननामैतत् । तर्पकेणान्नेन हविर्लक्षणेनाविथ अवसि तृप्यसि ॥ अवतेस्तृप्त्यर्थाच्छंदसि
> लुज्लज्लिट इति सार्वकालिको लिट् । आत आदेरित्यभ्यासस्यात्वं । यद्वृत्तानित्यमिति
> निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥ अपि च मातरा सकलस्य भूतजातस्य निर्मात्र्य द्यावापृथिव्यौ
> जिगत्तू गमनशीले इतस्ततः प्रचलंत्यावा स्थापयसे । स्वकीये स्थानेऽवस्थापयसि ।
> नैश्चल्येन यथावतिष्ठेते तथा करोषीत्यर्थः । विश्वक्तस्तंभ पृथिवीमुत द्यामिति
> निगमांतरं । ऋ. १०-८९-४ । हे इंद्र अतः कारणात्पुरूणि बहूनि कर्वरा । कर्मनामैतत् । कर्वराणि ॥ शेश्चंदसि बहुलमिति शेर्लोपः ॥ कर्माणि लौकिकानि
> वैदिकानि चेनोषि । प्राप्नोषि ॥ इण् गतौ । व्यत्ययेन श्नुः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you नि दधिषे (*ni dadhiṣe*), that is, deposit, in the house of the sacrificer the lesser wealth of the earth (avara) and the superior wealth born in heaven (para), in that house where you are gratified (अविथ (*avitha*)) with the satisfying food (avasā; a name for food) in the form of oblation. Moreover you set (स्थापयसे (*sthāpayase*)) the two mothers, heaven and earth, makers of all beings, which are moving, shifting this way and that, in their own place; you make them stand firm. Another Nigama: विश्वक्तस्तंभ पृथिवीमुत द्यामिति (*viśvaktastaṃbha pṛthivīmuta dyāmiti*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-89-4). For this reason, O Indra, you accomplish (इनोषि (*inoṣi*), obtain) many deeds (कर्वरा (*karvarā*), a name for karma), both worldly and Vedic.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्मिन् दुरोणे (*yasmin duroṇe*)—in whose house, the sacrificer's
- अवसा (*avasā*)—with food in the form of oblation
- आविध (*āvidha*)—you are gratified
- तत् (*tat*)—in that sacrificer's house
- अवरं (*avaraṃ*)—the lesser wealth relating to the earth
- परं च (*paraṃ ca*)—and the superior, of the heavenly world

### Printed p. 622
(The Pratipadārtha of the previous Ṛk continues:) …the greater wealth of the supreme heaven. नि दधिषे (*ni dadhiṣe*)—you set it down, provide it. जिगत्नू (*jigatnū*)—the trembling ones. मातरा (*mātarā*)—heaven and earth, the birthplace of all beings. आ स्थापयसे (*ā sthāpayase*)—you establish them firmly in their places (O Indra). अतः (*ataḥ*)—therefore. पुरूणि (*purūṇi*)—manifold. कर्वरा (*karvarā*)—worldly and Vedic rites. इनोषि (*inoṣi*)—you obtain.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, in the house of the sacrificer with whose food in the form of the oblation he offers you are pleased, you provide and keep, in that sacrificer's house, the lesser wealth that belongs to the earth and the greater wealth of the heavenly world, wealth and the like. You have firmly established heaven and earth, the birthplace of all beings, which do not stand still but tremble, so that they do not move. Therefore, O Indra, you are worshipped in all kinds of Vedic and worldly rites.

##### English translation
You deposit the lesser and the greater wealth in the mansion in which you are satisfied with food; you fix the two wandering mothers, you accomplish many works.

> इ॒मा ब्रह्म॑ बृ॒हद्दि॑वो विव॒क्तींद्रा॑य शू॒षम॑ग्रि॒यः स्व॒र्षाः ।

> महः । गोत्रस्य । क्षयति । स्वऽराजः । दुरः । च । विश्वाः । अवृणोत् । अप । स्वाः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बृहद्दिव ऋषिरिमेमानि ब्रह्म ब्रह्माणींद्राय शूषं सुखं यथा भवति तथा
> विवक्ति । प्रब्रवीतीत्यात्मन एव परोक्षनिर्देशः ॥ वच परिभाषणे आदादिकः । छांदसः
> शपः श्लुः । बहुलं छंदसीत्यभ्यासस्यॆत्वं ॥ ऋषिर्विशेष्यते । अग्रियोऽग्रे भवः ।
> ऋषीणां प्रमुखः श्रेष्ठ इत्यर्थः ॥ घच्छौ च । पा. ४-४-११७ । इत्यग्रशब्दाद्भवार्थे

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer Bṛhaddiva says: "these prayers (brahma) he recites for Indra, so that it is pleasing (śūṣa, happiness)". The statement about himself is made in the third person (parokṣa). The verb विवक्ति (*vivakti*) is from the root vac, "to speak". The seer is qualified: अग्रियः (*agriyaḥ*) is "born first"; he is foremost and best among seers.

### Printed p. 623

> घच् ॥ स्वर्षाः स्वर्गस्य संभक्ता । यद्वा । स्वरादित्य इंद्रः । असौ वा आदित्य इंद्र इति
> श्रुत्यंतरात् । तस्य संभक्ता सेवक इत्यर्थः ॥ वन षण संभक्तौ । जनसनखनक्रमगमो
> विट् । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यादित्वात्वं । सनोतेरन इति षत्वं ॥ य इंद्रो महो
> महतो गोत्रस्य पर्वतस्य वलेनासुरेण गवां विधानार्थं निहितस्य स्वराजः स्वयमेव राजमानस्य ॥ क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुथ्यर्थे
> षष्ठी ॥ ईदृशं पर्वतं क्षयति अपगमयति ॥ क्षि क्षये भौवादिकः ॥ यद्वा ॥
> गोशब्दात्समूहार्थ इनित्रकट्यचश्च । पा. ४-२-५१ । इति प्रप्रत्ययः ॥ गोत्रस्य
> गोसमूहस्य महो महतः स्वराजः स्वयमेव राजमानस्य य इंद्रः क्षयति
> ईष्टे । क्षयतिरैश्वर्यकर्मा ॥ स्वशब्दोपपदाद्राजतेः सत्तूद्विषेति क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ दुरश्च बिलद्वाराणि च विश्वाः सर्वाः स्वा वलासुरस्य स्वभूता
> अपावृणोत् । अपगतावरणा अकरोत् । उद्घाटितवानित्यर्थः । यद्वा । दुरश्चापावृणोत् विश्वाः सर्वाः स्वाः स्वभूता गा बिलमध्यॆ वर्तमाना अलभतेति शेषः ।
> एवंभूतो य इंद्रस्तस्मा इंद्राय विवक्तित्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

स्वर्षाः (*svarṣāḥ*) is the one who shares in heaven. Or else svar means the sun, Indra, on the authority of another śruti: "that sun is Indra"; the seer is his devotee or servant. The Indra who "rules" (kṣayati) the great mountain (gotra), in which the asura Vala had hidden the cattle to keep them, and which shines of itself (svarāj): the genitive stands for the dative, because the action must take its object as recipient. Such a mountain he makes go away (kṣayati, from kṣi in the sense of "to destroy"). Or else: with the word go and the suffix of collection (Pā. Sū. 4-2-51) गोत्रस्य (*gotrasya*) means "of the herd of cattle"; the great, self-shining herd is ruled (īṣṭe) by Indra; kṣayati has the sense of lordship. दुरश्च (*duraśca*): the doors, the openings of the cave; विश्वाः सर्वाः (*viśvāḥ sarvāḥ*): all of Vala's own possessions. He opened them (uncovered, unlocked). Or else: he opened the doors and obtained all the cows, his own, that were within the cave (the verb "obtained" is to be supplied). The construction: to this Indra he recites (विवक्ति (*vivakti*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बृहद्दिवः (*bṛhaddivaḥ*)—the seer of this sūkta, called Bṛhaddiva
- अग्रियः (*agriyaḥ*)—the chief of all
- स्वर्षाः (*svarṣāḥ*)—the one who is of the sun's nature, which Indra
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great
- स्वराजः (*svarājaḥ*)—shining
- गोत्रस्य (*gotrasya*)—the mountain (the mountain cave)
- क्षयति (*kṣayati*)—approached and advanced on
- दुरः च (*duraḥ ca*)—and the closed doors of that cave
- अप अवृणोत् (*apa avṛṇot*)—opened
- विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)—all (hidden in the cave)
- स्वाः (*svāḥ*)—his own cows
- अलभत (*alabhata*)—obtained and brought; for such
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for the sake of Indra
- इमा ब्रह्माणि (*imā brahmāṇi*)—these hymns
- शूषं (*śūṣaṃ*)—so that it is pleasing (to Indra)
- विवक्ति (*vivakti*)—he recites

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Indra who is the leader of all and of the sun's nature approached the cave of the great mountain, opened its doors and released all the cows of the gods hidden there. For the sake of that Indra, the seer of this sūkta, Bṛhaddiva, recites these hymns and offers them, so that they are beneficial to Indra.

##### English translation
Brihaddiva, the chief (of Rishis), the servant of the sun, repeats these prayers to gratify Indra. (Indra) rules over the great self-ruling herd of cattle, and he opened all his doors.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्वसा॑रो मात॒रिभ्य॑रीररि॒प्रा हि॒न्वंति॑ च॒ शव॑सा व॒र्धयं॑ति च ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । महान् । बृहत्ऽदिवः । अथर्वा । अवोचत् । स्वां । तन्वं । इंद्रं । एव ।  
> स्वसारः । मातरिभ्वरीः । अरिप्राः । हिन्वंति । च । शवसा । वर्धयंति । च ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महान्गुणैरधिकोऽथर्वा । उपचाराज्जन्ये जनकशब्दः । अथवर्णः पुत्रो
> बृहद्दिवाख्य ऋषिर्देवेषु मध्य इंद्रमेव प्रति स्वामात्मीयां तन्वं विस्तृतां
> स्तुतिमेवमवोचत् । प्रोक्तवान् ॥ वचेर्लुङ्ज्यस्यतिवक्तित्यादिना चेरणादेशः ।
> वच उमित्युमागमः । पादादित्वान्न निहन्यते ॥ अपि चैनमेवेंद्रं मारिभ्वरीर्मातरि
> सकलस्य भूतजातस्य निर्मात्र्यां भूमौ भवंत्यो वर्तमानाः ॥ भवतेरन्येभ्योऽपि
> दृश्यंत इति वनिप् । वनो र चेति जीब्रेफौ । जसि वा छंदसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः ।
> पृषोदरादित्वाद्दर्णलोपः ॥ अरिप्रा अपापाः स्वसारः स्वयमेव सरंत्यः परस्परं
> भगिन्यो ना गंगाद्या नद्यो हिन्वंति । यागसाधनत्वेन प्रीणयंति ॥ हिविः प्रीणनार्थः । भौवादिकः । व्यत्ययेन शः । इदित्वान्नुम् । यद्वा । हि गतौ वृद्धौ च ।
> स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः ॥ वृष्ट्यर्थं तमिंद्रमुपगच्छंति । गत्वा च शवसा यागजन्येन बलेन
> तं वर्धयंति च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

महान् (*mahān*) means "eminent in qualities". अथर्वा (*atharvā*): by transference the word for the father is used for the son: the son of Atharvan, the seer called Bṛhaddiva, among the gods spoke thus to Indra alone his own "body" (tanū), that is his extended praise. अवोचत् (*avocat*): he declared. (The rest of the sentence gives the grammar.) Moreover, the rivers: मातरिभ्वरीः (*mātaribhvarīḥ*) are those that exist on the earth, the mother, the maker of all beings. अरिप्राः (*ariprāḥ*) are the sinless; स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*) are those that flow of themselves, or are sisters to one another: the Gaṅgā and other rivers. हिन्वंति (*hinvaṃti*): they please him by being the means of the sacrifice. The root hi is for pleasing; or else hi in the sense of motion and growth. For rain they go to Indra, and having gone they make him grow with the strength (śavas) produced by the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महान् (*mahān*)—one endowed with great qualities
- अथर्वा (*atharvā*)—the son of Atharvan
- बृहद्दिवः (*bṛhaddivaḥ*)—the seer called Bṛhaddiva
- इंद्रमेव (*iṃdrameva*)—addressing Indra alone
- स्वां (*svāṃ*)—composed by himself
- तन्वं (*tanvaṃ*)—this extended hymn
- अवोचत् (*avocat*)—has recited
- मातरिभ्वरीः (*mātaribhvarīḥ*)—those that flow on the earth, the birthplace of all beings
- अरिप्राः (*ariprāḥ*)—the sinless
- स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*)—those that flow of their own impulse, or are like sisters to one another, the rivers Gaṅgā and others
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- हिन्वंति (*hinvaṃti*)—they delight (with the means of the sacrifice)

### Printed p. 625
- शवसा (*śavasā*)—with strength connected with the sacrifice
- वर्धयंति च (*vardhayaṃti ca*)—and they also make him grow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Bṛhaddiva, the seer of this sūkta, eminent in qualities and son of the seer Atharvan, among all the gods addressed Indra alone, reciting and offering this extended praise composed by himself. The rivers such as the Gaṅgā, which flow on this earth, the cause of the birth of all beings, which destroy sin, flow of their own impulse or are like sisters to each other, delight Indra (with the sacrificial materials such as darbha grass and soma creeper that grow on their banks). By the rites performed in the sacrifice and by hymns and the like, they increase Indra's power and capacity.

##### English translation
Thus the great Brihaddiva, son of Atharvan, repeated his diffiused (praise) to Indra. The unsullied sister (streams) abiding in the mother (earth), go to Indra, and augment him with strength.

## Sūkta 121 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
For this sūkta the deity is stated to be कशब्दाभिधेयः प्रजापतिर्देवता (*kaśabdābhidheyaḥ prajāpatirdevatā*), that is, Prajāpati, known by the name Ka. As to why Prajāpati got the name Kaḥ, there is a story in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 12-21):
इंद्रो वृत्रं हत्वा सर्वा विजितीर्विजित्याब्रवीत्प्रजापतिमहमेतदसानि यत्त्वमहं महानसानीति स प्रजापतिरब्रवीदथ कोs हमिति यदैवैतद वोच इत्यब्रवीत्ततो वै को नाम प्रजापतिरभवक्को वै नाम प्रजापतिर्यन्महानिंद्रोऽभवत्तन्महेंद्रस्य महेंद्रत्वं ॥ (*iṃdro vṛtraṃ hatvā sarvā vijitīrvijityābravītprajāpatimahametadasāni yattvamahaṃ mahānasānīti sa prajāpatirabravīdatha kos hamiti yadaivaitada voca ityabravīttato vai ko nāma prajāpatirabhavakko vai nāma prajāpatiryanmahāniṃdro 'bhavattanmaheṃdrasya maheṃdratvaṃ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 12-21)
Formerly, after Indra killed Vṛtra, he conquered all the regions of the earth, and said to Prajāpati: "O Prajāpati, you have now gained a great station and are honoured. Henceforth I want your great position." To that Prajāpati

### Printed p. 626
said: "If you take my position, then I, having lost it, who (kaḥ) shall I be? What will be my standing?" Indra replied: "O Prajāpati, as you have just said, your name will henceforth be Kaḥ (Who), that is, you will be denoted by the word ka." Therefore from that time Prajāpati became denoted by the word ka; that is, the name Ka became established for Prajāpati. For that reason this matter is stated in the pratigraha mantras that are recited when one accepts any gift, namely: क इदं कस्मा अदादित्याह । प्रजापतिर्वै कः । प्रजापतॆय एव तद्ददाति (*ka idaṃ kasmā adādityāha | prajāpatirvai kaḥ | prajāpatèya eva taddadāti*) — a Brāhmaṇa sentence of other Vedas. Since the word ka also means happiness, in matters and affairs connected with Prajāpati he is said to be of the nature of happiness. Because Indra accepted the greatness of Prajāpati in this way, the designation Mahān came to Indra; that is, Indra became Mahendra. This is also stated in other Vedas: इंद्रो वृत्रमहन्तं देवा अब्रुवन्महान्वा आयमभूद्यो वृत्रमवधीदिति तन्महेंद्रस्य महेंद्रत्वं (*iṃdro vṛtramahantaṃ devā abruvanmahānvā āyamabhūdyo vṛtramavadhīditi tanmaheṃdrasya maheṃdratvaṃ*) — the gods praised him thus: since Indra killed Vṛtra he became Mahendra (gained the position of greatness); that is, Indra became the best of all the gods. This is said to be the reason why Indra got the name Mahendra.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हिरण्यगर्भ इति दशर्चं नवमं सूक्तं प्रजापतिपुत्रस्य हिरण्यगर्भाख्यस्यार्षं
> त्रैष्टुभं । कशब्दाभिधेयः प्रजापतिर्देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । हिरण्यगर्भो दश
> हिरण्यगर्भः प्राजापत्यः कायमिति ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ प्राजापत्यस्य पशोर्वपापुरोडाशहविषां क्रमेणादितस्तिस्रोऽनुवाक्यास्ततिस्तिस्रो याज्याः । सूत्रितं च ।
> हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्र इति षट् प्राजापत्याः । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥ वरुणप्रघासेषु
> कायस्य हविषो हिरण्यगर्भ इत्येषा याज्या । सूत्रितं च । कयानश्चित्र आ भुवद्धिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्र इति प्रतिप्रस्थाता वाजिने तृतीयः । आ. २-१७ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta हिरण्यगर्भ (*hiraṇyagarbha*) is of ten Ṛks, the ninth sūkta; its seer is Hiraṇyagarbha, son of Prajāpati; metre triṣṭubh; the deity is Prajāpati, denoted by the word ka. So the Anukramaṇī: हिरण्यगर्भो दश हिरण्यगर्भः प्राजापत्यः कायमिति (*hiraṇyagarbho daśa hiraṇyagarbhaḥ prājāpatyaḥ kāyamiti*). Use of the sūkta: in the animal sacrifice to Prajāpati, for the oblations of vapā, puroḍāśa and havis, the first three Ṛks are anuvākyās in order, and the next three are yājyās. It is stated in the sūtra: हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्र इति षट् प्राजापत्याः (*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgra iti ṣaṭ prājāpatyāḥ*) (Ā. 3-8). In the Varuṇapraghāsa offerings, for the oblation to Ka, the verse हिरण्यगर्भ (*hiraṇyagarbha*) is the yājyā. It is stated in the sūtra: कयानश्चित्र आ भुवद्धिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्र इति प्रतिप्रस्थाता वाजिने तृतीयः (*kayānaścitra ā bhuvaddhiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgra iti pratiprasthātā vājine tṛtīyaḥ*) (Ā. 2-17).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, हिरण्यगर्भः (*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ*), is the ninth sūkta in the tenth anuvāka. It has ten Ṛks. Its seer is Hiraṇyagarbha, son of Prajāpati; its deity is Prajāpati, known by the name Ka; the metre is triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated: हिरण्यगर्भो दश हिरण्यगर्भः प्राजापत्यः कायं (*hiraṇyagarbho daśa hiraṇyagarbhaḥ prājāpatyaḥ kāyaṃ*). In the animal sacrifice made to the deity Prajāpati, when vapā, puroḍāśa and havis are offered, the first three Ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited as anuvākyā mantras in order (that is, the first Ṛk for the vapā offering, the second for the puroḍāśa offering, the third for the havis offering), and the next three, the fourth to the sixth, in the same way as yājyā mantras; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्र इति षट् प्राजापत्याः (*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgra iti ṣaṭ prājāpatyāḥ*) (Ā. 3-8). And in the Varuṇapraghāsa sacrifices, in the havis offering made to Prajāpati called Ka, the first Ṛk of this sūkta, हिरण्यगर्भः (*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ*), is to be recited as a yājyā mantra;

### Printed p. 627
this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra कया नश्चित्र आ भुवद्धिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्र इति प्रतिप्रस्थाता वाजिने तृतीयः (*kayā naścitra ā bhuvaddhiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgra iti pratiprasthātā vājine tṛtīyaḥ*) (Ā. 2-17).

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 10; Sūkta 121. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 7; Vargas 3, 4. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 10. Seer: Hiraṇyagarbha Prājāpatya. Deity: Ka. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Hiraṇyagarbha is Prajāpati, the one who is the embryo (garbha) of the golden egg. So the Taittirīya: प्रजापतिर्वै हिरण्यगर्भः प्रजापतेरनुरूपत्वाय (*prajāpatirvai hiraṇyagarbhaḥ prajāpateranurūpatvāya*) (Tai. Saṃ. 5-5-1-2). Or else: the golden egg is within whose belly as an embryo, that sūtrātman is called Hiraṇyagarbha. अग्रे (*agre*): before the origination of the manifold world he came into being; he was born from the Supreme Self, who presides over māyā and desires to create. Although the Supreme Self himself is Hiraṇyagarbha, yet…

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Because the subtle elements (ether and the rest) that serve as the limiting adjunct of Brahman arise, the one conditioned by them is also said to have arisen. Born, he was at the very moment of birth the sole lord, without a second, of all that has come into being: the whole world of transformations, beginning with the Brahmāṇḍa. Nor was he only its lord: that Hiraṇyagarbha upheld the broad earth, heaven, and also this earth that lies before us and is seen by us. Or else, "earth" is a name of the atmosphere, and he upholds the atmosphere, heaven and earth. कस्मै (*kasmai*): here the word किं (*kiṃ*) stands for Prajāpati because his nature is not determined. Or else, he is कः (*kaḥ*) because he desired (कामयत (*kāmayata*)) for the sake of creation. Or else कं (*kaṃ*) is happiness, and being of that nature he is called कः (*kaḥ*). Or else, questioned by Indra, Prajāpati bestowed his greatness on him and said, "What (कः (*kaḥ*)) would I be?" Indra answered, "What you say, 'What would I be?', that very thing be you." For this reason Prajāpati is called Ka. The Brāhmaṇa beginning "Indra, having slain Vṛtra and won all victories, said…" is to be recalled here (Ai. Brā. 3-21). When किं (*kiṃ*) is a pronoun, the form with स्मै (*smai*) is established; when it is a yaugika (derived) word, it is to be understood by vyatyaya. The dative arises because the object is the recipient. "To Ka, the god, the one endowed with qualities such as generosity, we would minister (विधेम (*vidhema*)) with the oblation": the oblation is either the fat (vapā) of the Prājāpatya animal or a one-potsherd cake (puroḍāśa). "We" means the priests, who would serve him. विधति (*vidhati*) is a verb of serving.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हिरण्यगर्भः (*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ*)—Prajāpati, famed by the name Hiraṇyagarbha
- अग्रे (*agre*)—before the origin of the world
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—without a second (no other)
- सं आवर्तत (*saṃ āvartata*)—he alone existed
- जातः (*jātaḥ*)—as soon as born
- भूतस्य (*bhūtasya*)—of the whole world, the Brahmāṇḍa and the rest, produced from his own part
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—as lord
- आसीत् (*āsīt*)—he was
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Hiraṇyagarbha
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the broad
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the world of Dyu (heaven)
- उत (*uta*)—and
- इमां (*imāṃ*)—this earth visible to our eyes, or the atmosphere and the earth also
- दाधार (*dādhāra*)—he upholds
- देवाय (*devāya*)—to the one endowed with generosity and other qualities
- कस्मै (*kasmai*)—to Prajāpati, whose nature is happiness
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—with an oblation such as the puroḍāśa
- विधेम (*vidhema*)—let us serve

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Prajāpati, who bears the name Hiraṇyagarbha, existed alone, by himself, before the creation of the world. Then, as soon as he came into being, he was the one sole lord of the whole world, Brahmāṇḍa and the rest, created from his own part

### Printed p. 629
of everything. That Hiraṇyagarbha, by his own power, upholds the broad heaven, this earth and the atmosphere; that is, the worlds beginning with earth are established through his support. Let us serve with the oblations of vapā and puroḍāśa that very Prajāpati, endowed with generosity and other qualities.

##### English translation
Hiranyagarbhaa was present at the begining; when born, he was the sole lord of created beings; he upheld this earth and heaven.—let us offer worship with an oblation to the divine Ka.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

हिरण्यगर्भः सं अवर्तत अग्रे (*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ saṃ avartata agre*)—The commentator gives two or three kinds of meaning for the word Hiraṇyagarbha. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 5-5-1-2) it is said that Hiraṇyagarbha is Prajāpati: प्रजापतिर्वै हिरण्यगर्भः (*prajāpatirvai hiraṇyagarbhaḥ*). हिरण्यगर्भः (*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ*) means हिरण्मयस्यांडस्यगर्भभूतः प्रजापतिर्हिरण्यगर्भः (*hiraṇmayasyāṃḍasyagarbhabhūtaḥ prajāpatirhiraṇyagarbhaḥ*): before creation the whole universe was in the form of an egg (the shape of a hen's egg), contained within Prajāpati's belly. That egg shone brilliantly like gold. It is the custom to call Prajāpati, who holds such a golden egg in the middle of his belly, Hiraṇyagarbha. Besides this: before creation, when the Supreme Self was in the unmanifest (subtle) state, none of this visible world existed. When the wish to create the world arose in the Supreme Self, the unmanifest form took on a manifest form. This is what the Upaniṣadic text sets forth:
सो 5 कामयत । बहु स्यां प्रजायेयेति । स तपोऽतप्यत । स तपस्त्वप्त्वा इदग्ं सर्वमसृजत । यदिदं किंच । तत्सृष्ट्वा । तदेनानु प्राविशत् । तदनु प्रविश्य । सच्च त्यच्चाभवत् ॥ (*so 5 kāmayata | bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti | sa tapo 'tapyata | sa tapastvaptvā idagṃ sarvamasṛjata | yadidaṃ kiṃca | tatsṛṣṭvā | tadenānu prāviśat | tadanu praviśya | sacca tyaccābhavat ‖*) (Tai. U. 9-6)
When that Supreme Brahman (the Supreme Self) took on manifest form, the world and the rest that had been absorbed in him in subtle form are said here to have existed in the form of an egg. Something that lies within the middle of another thing is called its "womb" (garbha). Therefore the world and the rest, absorbed in the Supreme Self in unmanifest (subtle) form, are called here the egg or womb. It is described as shining like gold (hiraṇya), and this Supreme Self or Prajāpati, who holds such a golden egg in his womb (middle), is praised as Hiraṇyagarbha. Such a Hiraṇyagarbha (or Prajāpati)

### Printed p. 630
was alone before creation. Since there was no creation, no one other than this Prajāpati existed then.
भूतस्य जातः पतिः एकः आसीत् (*bhūtasya jātaḥ patiḥ ekaḥ āsīt*)—It has been said that before creation this Hiraṇyagarbha was alone, so that no other moving or unmoving things existed then. How, then, is he भूतस्य पतिः (*bhūtasya patiḥ*), lord of all beings, creatures? When there were no creatures, is it not impossible to call him lord of creatures? The answer: all those beings, that is, the universe containing all the Brahmāṇḍas, arose from this Hiraṇyagarbha himself. Thus, as soon as the whole world (and the creatures in it) came into being, this Hiraṇyagarbha or Prajāpati was the one sole lord of them all. There was no other lord apart from him. The meaning is that everything was subject to his command.
सः दाधार पृथिवीं द्यां उत इमां (*saḥ dādhāra pṛthivīṃ dyāṃ uta imāṃ*)—He is the support of the worlds of earth, atmosphere and heaven, which arose from a part of this Prajāpati, and by his surpassing power and capacity he is the cause of their continuance. It is by his power and capacity that the worlds beginning with earth, established in their appointed places, are able to perform their own duties.
कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम (*kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema*)—Two or three meanings can be given for the word कः (*kaḥ*). The word किं (*kiṃ*) has the sense "what", of undetermined nature. When one asks "what, which?", its nature is not known. Likewise, saying कस्मै (*kasmai*), one may say that the nature or power of this Prajāpati is not known to ordinary people, that is, one may give the meaning "of a nature that cannot be fully known by anyone". Or कं (*kaṃ*) is happiness; कस्मै (*kasmai*) may also be taken to mean "to the one whose nature is happiness". As in the Śruti text आनंदो ब्रह्मेति व्यजानात् (*ānaṃdo brahmeti vyajānāt*), Brahman (or Prajāpati) is of the nature of bliss or happiness. Or, as in the story told in the introduction to this sūkta, Prajāpati acquired the name Ka for another reason. In the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa too it is said that Prajāpati has the name Ka: प्रजापतिर्वै कः (*prajāpatirvai kaḥ*) (Tai. Brā. 2-5-5). The chief purport of this Ṛk is: let us serve and worship such a Hiraṇyagarbha or Prajāpati, of the nature of happiness, with oblations such as caru and puroḍāśa. Explaining the word कः (*kaḥ*) in this Ṛk, Yāska has given a Nirukta on it:
कः । कः कमनो वा क्रमणो ना सुखो ना । तस्यैषा भवति ॥ (*kaḥ | kaḥ kamano vā kramaṇo nā sukho nā | tasyaiṣā bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 10-22)
कः (*kaḥ*) means कमनो वा (*kamano vā*). The word कः (*kaḥ*) is derived from the root कम् (*kam*) "to love": one who loves, that is, one who loves all the creatures he has created; or कः (*kaḥ*) means क्रमणो वा (*kramaṇo vā*), one who surpasses: one who surpasses everything by his power and capacity, the one greater than all;

### Printed p. 631
or कः सुखो वा (*kaḥ sukho vā*): कं (*kaṃ*) is happiness, so it also means one whose nature is happiness. The Ṛk in which this word is used is cited here:
हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्रे भूतस्य जातः पतिरेक आसीत् । स दाधार पृथिवीं द्यामुतेमां कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥ (*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgre bhūtasya jātaḥ patireka āsīt | sa dādhāra pṛthivīṃ dyāmutemāṃ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ‖*)
हिरण्यगर्भो हिरण्मयो गर्भो हिरण्यमयो गर्भोऽस्येति वा । गर्भो गृभेर्गृणात्यर्थे, गिरत्यनर्थानिति वा ॥ यदा हि स्त्री गुणान् गृह्णाति गुणाश्चास्या गृह्यंतेऽथ गर्भो भवति समभवदग्रे भूतस्य जातः पतिरेको बभूव स धारयति पृथिवीं च दिवं च कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेमेति व्याख्यातं । विधतिर्दानकर्मा ॥ (*hiraṇyagarbho hiraṇmayo garbho hiraṇyamayo garbho 'syeti vā | garbho gṛbhergṛṇātyarthe, giratyanarthāniti vā ‖ yadā hi strī guṇān gṛhṇāti guṇāścāsyā gṛhyaṃte 'tha garbho bhavati samabhavadagre bhūtasya jātaḥ patireko babhūva sa dhārayati pṛthivīṃ ca divaṃ ca kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhemeti vyākhyātaṃ | vidhatirdānakarmā ‖*) (Ni. 10-23)
हिरण्यगर्भः हिरण्मयो गर्भो हिरण्यमयो गर्भोऽस्येति वा (*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ hiraṇmayo garbho hiraṇyamayo garbho 'syeti vā*)—Hiraṇyagarbha is one whose womb is full of gold (hiraṇya), like gold or made of gold. That is, his womb (the world and the rest in his interior) shines like gold. He who holds such a womb in the middle of his body is called Hiraṇyagarbha.
गर्भो गृभेर्गृणात्यर्थे, गिरत्यनर्थानिति वा (*garbho gṛbhergṛṇātyarthe, giratyanarthāniti vā*)—The word गर्भ (*garbha*) is derived from the root गृभ् (*gṛbh*), which means to praise, to extol: all praise it. Or it may be derived from the root गिरति (*girati*), meaning to destroy: गिरत्यनर्थान् (*giratyanarthān*), since it destroys all useless things it is called garbha. Thus two kinds of meaning are given for the word garbha.
यदा हि स्त्री गुणान् गृह्णाति गुणाश्चास्या गृह्यंतेऽथ गर्भो भवति (*yadā hi strī guṇān gṛhṇāti guṇāścāsyā gṛhyaṃte 'tha garbho bhavati*)—How the womb (embryo) comes about is explained here. At the time of union the woman receives through her yoni the qualities in the man's seed (semen). And the qualities in the blood-state of the woman's limbs, such as bone, sinew (nerve) and marrow, are absorbed by the man's semen. Hence the qualities in the man's semen and the qualities of the blood in the woman's limbs, that is, the blood and semen (the woman's blood and the man's semen, both), unite and the embryo arises in the woman's body. Or: when a woman and a man, attracted by each other's qualities, love one another, both feel pleasure, and from their union the embryo arises; this is what is explained here. The scholar Lakṣmaṇasarūp has explained it as follows.

### Printed p. 632
Durga describes the process of fertilization as follows—
When a woman receives from a man the life-germs, i e, the essence of the marrow of his bones &c in the form of seminal fluid and brings them (i. e. spermatozoa) in contact with her own life-germs, i. e. the essence of her flesh and blood in the form of her germinating fluid, then by the mutual contact of the male and fcmale fluid in the interior of the uterus which is capable of receiving them, fertilization of a woman takes place. Or when a woman admires the qualities of a man, on account of her love for him, and a man a woman, the result of their mutual admiration is passion, and passionate intercourse produces ferlization.
समभवदग्रे भूतस्य जातः पतिरेको बभूव (*samabhavadagre bhūtasya jātaḥ patireko babhūva*)—That Hiraṇyagarbha was alone before creation, and afterwards was the one sole lord of the whole world and the creatures produced from himself.
स धारयति पृथीवीं च दिवं च (*sa dhārayati pṛthīvīṃ ca divaṃ ca*)—That Hiraṇyagarbha (or Prajāpati) pervades within and without this earth, the atmosphere and heaven, nourishes them with the rain and other things they need, and upholds and protects them. It is by his power and capacity that the upholding, nourishing and protecting of the world and the rest take place.
कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम (*kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema*)—The chief purport is: let us offer oblations such as caru and puroḍāśa to such a Hiraṇyagarbha or Prajāpati, endowed with all qualities (or of the nature of happiness).
विधतिर्दानकर्मा (*vidhatirdānakarmā*)—The root विधति (*vidhati*) means to give, to offer. Therefore the word विधेम (*vidhema*) here means "let us offer", or "let us serve and worship with oblations and the like".

> समानं पूर्वेण हविषा पुरोडाशात्मनेति तु विशेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

यः (*yaḥ*), the Prajāpati who is आत्मदाः (*ātmadāḥ*), giver of selves: all selves arise from that Supreme Self, as sparks arise from fire. Or else, the purifier of selves (root दैप् (*daip*), to purify). बलदा (*baladā*): giver, or purifier, of strength. प्रशिषं (*praśiṣaṃ*) is his excellent command; all (विश्वे (*viśve*)) creatures उपासते (*upāsate*), that is, pray for or serve it. Likewise the gods also attend upon his command. Also अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*), immortality (the statement is bhāva-pradhāna). Or else अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*) is nectar, since in it there is no death. That too is his, Prajāpati's, छाया (*chāyā*): it is as his shadow. मृत्युः (*mṛtyuḥ*), Yama, the taker of life, is also as his shadow. The rest, "to that Ka, the god", and so on, is the same as the preceding, except that the oblation here is the puroḍāśa.

- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which Prajāpati
- प्रशिषं (*praśiṣaṃ*)—the excellent command

- छाया (*chāyā*)—follows like a shadow
- मृत्युः (*mṛtyuḥ*)—death also

- देवाय (*devāya*)—to the god called Prajāpati

### Printed p. 634

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let us offer oblations and the like to the divine Prajāpati, the blissful one. He gives life-breath to all beings and to the world, or gives them the self that is a part of himself. He is the giver of strength. All beings, and even the gods, obey his supreme command. Death and deathlessness follow him constantly and inseparably, like a shadow.

##### English translation
(To him) who is the giver of soul, the giver of strength, whose commands all (beings), even the gods obey, whose shadow is immortality, whose shadow is death,—let us offer worship with an oblation to divine Ka.

> ईश ऐश्वर्ये आदादिकोऽनुदात्तेत् । लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्टिति तलोपः । अनुदा-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that the one who is Hiraṇyagarbha is meant. प्राणतः (*prāṇataḥ*) means "of one who breathes" (root अन (*ana*), in the sense of breathing). निमिषतः (*nimiṣataḥ*) means "of one who moves the eyelids", and the case-ending is accented as in the previous word. जगतः (*jagataḥ*) means "of the moving world, the class of living beings". महित्वा (*mahitvā*) means "by greatness", the instrumental ending being replaced by ā. By his majesty he, being the one and without a second, became king, that is, he is lord. Sāyaṇa then begins on the next clause: of this visible two-footed creature (man and others) and four-footed creature (cows, horses and others), the Prajāpati who rules over them ईशे (*īśe*) (root ईश (*īśa*), "to have lordship").

### Printed p. 635
#### Ṛk 3 (continued)

> तेत्वाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । अस्य! ऊडिदमितीदमो विभक्तिरुदात्ता।
> द्वौ पादौ यस्य स द्विपात् । संख्यासुपूर्वस्यॆति पादशब्द स्यांत्यलोपः समासांतः ।
> भसंज्ञायां पादः पदिति पद्भावः । द्वित्रिभ्यां पादन्नित्येकादेशविकृतस्यानन्यत्वादुत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं । स्वरवर्जमेषैव चतुष्पद इत्यत्रापि प्रक्रिया । बहुव्रीहौ
> प्रकृत्येति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । पूर्वपदं नृः संख्यायाः । फि. २-५ । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । इदुदुपधस्य चाप्रत्ययस्यॆति विसर्जनीयस्य षत्वं ॥ ईदृशो यः प्रजापतिस्तस्मै कस्मा इत्यादि सुबोभं हविषा हृदयाद्यात्मनेत्ययमत्र विशेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The remainder of this block is almost entirely grammatical (the accent of ईशे (*īśe*), अस्य (*asya*), द्विपदः (*dvipadaḥ*) and चतुष्पदः (*catuṣpadaḥ*), the formation of the compound as a bahuvrīhi with a numeral as first member, and the change of visarga). Of the sense, Sāyaṇa adds that द्विपदः (*dvipadaḥ*) means "having two feet", and चतुष्पदः (*catuṣpadaḥ*) is treated in the same way. He ends by saying that for such a Prajāpati the words कस्मै (*kasmai*) and the rest are to be understood as before. The only difference here is that the oblation (हविषा (*haviṣā*)) is the heart and the like, offered as the self.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जगतः (*jagataḥ*)—to the moving class of living beings
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—by his greatness
- एक इत् (*eka it*)—without a second
- राजा (*rājā*)—as lord
- बभूव (*babhūva*)—who has been
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the god who
- अस्यॆ (*asyè*)—visible to our eyes
- द्विपदः (*dvipadaḥ*)—to men and others having two feet
- चतुष्पदः (*catuṣpadaḥ*)—to cows and other animals having four feet
- ईशे (*īśe*)—who is the master of these
- कस्मै देवाय (*kasmai devāya*)—to the god named Prajāpati, the blissful one
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—with oblations and the like
- विधेम (*vidhema*)—let us serve

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let us offer oblations and the like to the god Prajāpati, the blissful one. By his greatness he is the unrivalled lord of the whole class of living beings that breathe and move the eyelids, that is, that are alive. He is the master of the visible two-footed beings such as men and of the four-footed animals such as cows.

##### English translation
(To him) who, by his greatness has verily become the sole king of the breathing and seeing world, who rules over this aggregate of two-footed and four-footed beings,—let us offer worship with an oblation to the divine Ka.
