##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हिमा अस्मिन्संतीति हिमवान् । तेन बहुवचनांतेन सर्वॆ पर्वता लक्ष्यंते ।
> यथा छत्रिणो गच्छंतीति । हिमवंतो हिमवदुपलक्षिता इमे दृश्यमानाः सर्वॆ
> पर्वता यस्य प्रजापतेर्महित्वा महत्त्वं माहात्ममैश्वर्यमित्याहुः । तेन सृष्टत्वात्तद्रूपेणावस्थानाद्वा ! तथा रसया ! रसो जलं ! तद्वती रसा नदी ॥ अर्शअदित्वादच् ॥ जातानेकवचनं । रसाभिर्नदीभिः सह समुद्रं । पूर्ववदे कवचनं । सर्वान्समुद्रान्यस्य महाभाग्यमित्याहुः कथयंति सृष्ट्यभिज्ञाः । यस्य चेमाः प्रदिशः
> प्राच्यारंभा आग्नेयाद्याः कोणदिश ईशानांता ना । तथा बाहू । वचनव्यत्ययः ।
> बाहवो भुजाः । भुजवत्पाधान्ययुक्ताः प्रदिशश्च यस्य स्वभूताः । तस्मै कस्मा
> इत्यादि समानं पूर्वेण ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

A "himavat" is that in which there is snow. By this word, in the plural, all mountains are indicated, as in "the men with umbrellas are going". These visible mountains, marked by snow, are what they call the greatness, majesty and lordship of this Prajāpati, either because they were created by him or because he abides in that form. Likewise रसया (*rasayā*): रस (*rasa*) is water, and रसा (*rasā*) is a river possessing it. The singular stands for a class, so "with the rivers". As before, the singular समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*) stands for all oceans. Those who know creation say that this is his great fortune. His also are these directions, beginning with the east, and the intermediate directions from the south-east to the north-east. Likewise बाहू (*bāhū*) shows a change of number: it means arms (*bāhavaḥ*). The directions, which are as prominent as arms, are his own. The rest, from तस्मै कस्मा (*tasmai kasmā*) onward, is the same as in the previous verse.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हिमवंतः (*himavaṃtaḥ*)—the Himalaya, covered with snow, and all the other mountains
- इमे (*ime*)—these
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which god
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—as greatness or lordship
- आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—they say
- रसया (*rasayā*)—with the rivers
- सह (*saha*)—together
- समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*)—all the oceans
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which god, as a special glory
- आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—(those who know the order of creation) say
- इमाः (*imāḥ*)—these directions, the east and the others
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which god
- बाहू (*bāhū*)—which are the arms
- प्रदिशः (*pradiśaḥ*)—the four intermediate directions also
- यस्यॆ (*yasyè*)—which are like the arms of which god
- कस्मै (*kasmai*)—to the blissful
- देवाय (*devāya*)—Prajāpati
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—oblations and the like
- विधेम (*vidhema*)—let us offer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let us offer oblations and the like to the blissful Prajāpati. All the mountains, beginning with the snow-covered (that is, very high) Himalaya, are called his lordship. The oceans together with the rivers are called his great fortune. The eastern and other directions, and the south-eastern and other intermediate directions, are called his arms.

### Printed p. 637

##### English translation
Through whose greatness these snow-clad (mountains exist), whose property men call the ocean with the rivers, whose are these quarters of space, whose are the two arms,—let us offer worship with an oblation to the divine Ka.

> यः । अंतरिक्षे । रजसः । विमानः । कस्मै । देवाय । हविषा । विधेम ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> येन प्रजापतिना द्यौरंतरिक्षमुग्रोद्गूर्णं विशेषागहनरूपं वा । पृथिवी
> भूमिश्च दृळ्ता येन स्थिरीकृता । स्वः स्वर्गश्च येन स्तभितं स्तब्धं कृतं । यथाधो
> न पतति तथोपर्यवस्थापितमित्यर्थः ॥ ग्रसितस्कभितस्तभितेति निपात्यते ॥ तथा नाक
> आदित्यश्च येनांतरिक्षे स्तभितः । यश्चांतरिक्षे रजस उदकस्यॆ विमानो निर्माता ।
> तस्मै कस्मा इत्यादि गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By which Prajāpati the sky (द्यौः (*dyauḥ*), the atmosphere) was made उग्रा (*ugrā*), that is, lofty, or exceedingly dense; and the earth was made firm; and by whom heaven (स्वः (*svaḥ*)) was स्तभितं (*stabhitaṃ*), made rigid, that is, placed above so that it does not fall downward. Sāyaṇa says the form स्तभित (*stabhita*) is irregularly derived. Likewise by him the sun (नाकः (*nākaḥ*)) was fixed in the atmosphere. He is the one who is विमानः (*vimānaḥ*), the maker, of the रजसः (*rajasaḥ*), the water, in the atmosphere. The rest, from तस्मै कस्मा (*tasmai kasmā*) onward, has been explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- येन (*yena*)—by which Prajāpati
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—the sky
- उग्रा (*ugrā*)—was made exceedingly dense
- पृथिवी च (*pṛthivī ca*)—and the earth
- दृळ्हा (*dṛḷhā*)—was firmly established
- येन (*yena*)—by which god
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—the heavenly world also
- स्तभितं (*stabhitaṃ*)—was established firmly, so that it does not fall downward
- येन (*yena*)—by which god
- नाकः (*nākaḥ*)—the sun also was established in the sky so that he does not fall
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the god who
- अंतरिक्षे (*aṃtarikṣe*)—in the atmosphere
- रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)—of the water (of the cloud)

### Printed p. 638
- विमानः (*vimānaḥ*)—is the maker
- कस्मै (*kasmai*)—to the blissful
- देवाय (*devāya*)—god Prajāpati
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—oblations and the like
- विधेम (*vidhema*)—let us offer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let us offer oblations and the like to the blissful Prajāpati. By him the atmosphere was made exceedingly dense. By him the earth was firmly established so that it does not shake. By him the heavenly world was held and made to stand in the atmosphere so that it does not fall down. By him the sun was established. He is the maker, in the sky, of the clouds full of water.

##### English translation
By whom the sky was made profound and the earth solid, by whom heaven and the solar sphere were fixed, who was the measure of the water in firmament,—let us offer worship with an oblation to the divine Ka.

> दर्शने । लज्यडादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ कीदृशौ द्यानापृथिव्यौ । रेजमाने राजमाने
> दीप्यमाने ॥ आकारस्य व्यत्ययेनैत्वं ॥ अदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे धातु-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

क्रंदसी (*kraṃdasī*) means heaven and earth, because Prajāpati cried out (क्रंदितवान् (*kraṃditavān*)) or impelled in them. For it is heard: यदरोदीत्तदनयो रोदस्त्वं (*yadarodīttadanayo rodastvaṃ*) (Tai. Brā. 2-2-9-4). Those two, तस्तभाने (*tastabhāne*), were created by Prajāpati and so received stability, for the protection of the world, with protection (अवसा (*avasā*)) as the cause. They looked upon (अभ्यैक्षेतां (*abhyaikṣetāṃ*)) Prajāpati with the mind, perceiving "our greatness is through him". The root is ईक्ष (*īkṣa*), "to see". The two are described as रेजमाने (*rejamāne*), shining, radiant.

### Printed p. 639

> स्वरः । यद्वा । लिटः कानच् । फणां च सप्तानां । पा. ६-४-१२५ । इत्येत्वाभ्यासलोपौ।
> छंदस्युभयथेति सार्वधातुकत्वाच्छप् । अभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ यत्राधि
> यस्मिन्नाधारभूते प्रजापतौ सूरः सूर्य उदित उदयं प्राप्तः सन् विभाति
> प्रकाशते ॥ उत्सूर्वादेतेः कर्मणि निष्ठा । गतिरनंतर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ।
> तस्मैकस्मा इत्यादि सुज्ञानं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa gives two derivations for रेजमाने (*rejamāne*), which belong to grammar. Of the sense he adds: यत्राधि (*yatrādhi*) means "in which Prajāpati, the support", the sun (सूरः (*sūraḥ*)) having risen (उदितः (*uditaḥ*)), having attained its rising, shines forth (विभाति (*vibhāti*)). For तस्मै कस्मा (*tasmai kasmā*) and the rest he says the meaning is easy to understand.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रेजमाने (*rejamāne*)—shining
- अवसा (*avasā*)—for the protection of the world
- तस्तभाने (*tastabhāne*)—created and established by Prajāpati
- क्रंदसी (*kraṃdasī*)—heaven and earth
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Prajāpati
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with a mind full of gratitude
- अभि ऐक्षेतां (*abhi aikṣetāṃ*)—looked at
- यत्र अधि (*yatra adhi*)—in which Prajāpati, the support of everything (by the greatness of Prajāpati)
- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—the sun
- उदितः (*uditaḥ*)—having risen
- विभाति (*vibhāti*)—shines
- कस्मै (*kasmai*)—to the blissful
- देवाय (*devāya*)—Prajāpati
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—with oblations and the like
- विधेम (*vidhema*)—let us offer and worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Heaven and earth are radiant and were created and established by Prajāpati for the protection of the world. They looked with a mind of gratitude towards that Prajāpati. By the greatness of that Prajāpati, the support of the whole universe, the sun rises and shines. Let us offer oblations and the like to that blissful Prajāpati.

##### English translation
Whom heaven and earth established by his protection, and, shining brightly, regarded with their mind, in whom the risen sun shines forth,— let us offer worship with an oblation to the divine Ka.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आपः । ह । यत् । बृहतीः । विश्वं । आयन् । गर्भं । दधानाः । जनयंतीः । अग्निं ।  
> ततः । देवानां । सं । अवर्तत । असुः । एकः । कस्मै । देवाय । हविषा । विधेम ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बृहतीर्बृहत्यो महत्यः ॥ जसि वा छंदसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः । बृहन्महतोरुपसंख्यानमिति जीप उदात्तत्वं ॥ अग्निं । उपलक्षणमेतत् । अग्न्युपलक्षितं
> सर्वं वियदादिभूतजातं । जनयंतीर्जनयंत्यः तदर्थं गर्भं हिरण्मयांडस्य
> गर्भभूतं प्रजापतिं दधाना धारयंत्य आपो हाप एव । विश्वमायन् सर्वं
> जगद्वाप्नुवन् यद्यस्मात् ततस्तस्माद्भेतोर्देवानां देवादीनां सर्वेषां
> प्राणिनामसुः प्राणभूत एकः प्रजापतिः समवर्तक । समजायत । यद्वा । यद्यं
> गर्भं दधाना आपो विश्वात्मनावस्थिताः ततो गर्भभूतात्पजापतेर्देवादीनां
> प्राणात्मको वायुरजायत । अथवा । यत् ॥ लिंगवचनयोर्व्यत्ययः ॥ उक्तलक्षणा
> या आपो विश्वमावृत्य स्थिताः ततस्ताभ्योऽद्भ्यः सकाशादेकोऽद्वितीयोऽसुः
> प्राणात्मकः प्रजापतिः समवर्तक । निश्चक्राम । तस्मै कस्मा इत्यादि गतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*) means "great, vast waters". अग्निं (*agniṃ*) is only an indication: it stands for the whole class of created things beginning with fire and the ether. The waters give birth to these. For that purpose they hold the "germ", namely Prajāpati, who is the embryo of the golden egg. Those waters pervaded the whole world. Therefore from them one Prajāpati, who is the life-breath of all beings, gods and others, came into being (समवर्तक (*samavartaka*) is glossed "was born"). Alternatively: from Prajāpati, the embryo held by the waters that stood as the universe, the wind, whose nature is breath (of the gods and the rest), was born. Or else: यत् (*yat*) is taken with a change of gender and number, so that it refers to those waters which, as described, stood covering the universe. From those waters the one, second-less Prajāpati, whose nature is breath, came forth (निश्चक्राम (*niścakrāma*)). The refrain कस्मै (*kasmai*) and the rest has been explained already.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*)—those that pervade widely (abundantly)
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—the five elements beginning with fire
- जनयंतीः (*janayaṃtīḥ*)—those that produce (for the very purpose of producing)
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—the germ, of golden form and containing Prajāpati
- दधानाः (*dadhānāḥ*)—holding
- यत् (*yat*)—which
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—waters
- विश्वं ह (*viśvaṃ ha*)—the entire universe
- आयन् (*āyan*)—pervaded
- ततः (*tataḥ*)—from such waters
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—for the gods
- असुः एकः (*asuḥ ekaḥ*)—Prajāpati, who is the life-breath
- सं अवर्तत (*saṃ avartata*)—was born
- कस्मै (*kasmai*)—to him who is of the nature of happiness
- देवाय (*devāya*)—addressing Prajāpati
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—with oblations and other materials
- विधेम (*vidhema*)—let us offer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The waters were vast and spread everywhere. They held the golden germ for the very purpose of producing the five great elements beginning with fire, and they covered the whole universe. From those waters Prajāpati, the life-breath of all the gods, came into being. Let us offer oblations and other materials to that Prajāpati, who is of the nature of happiness.

### Printed p. 641

##### English translation
When the vast waters overspread the universe containiug the germ and giving birth to Agni, then was produced the one breath of the gods,—let us offer worship with an oblation to the devine Ka.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk and in the next, the following point is set out: before creation there was only water, pervading everything, and the whole creation proceeded from that water. Moreover, the Taittirīya Saṃhitā gives this account of creation: before creation everything consisted of water, and creation, beginning with the world, went forward from that water (see Part 29, pp. 247-252).

> पा. ७-३-९६ । इतीडागमः ॥ तस्मै कस्मा इत्यादि गतं ॥
> 41

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*) stands for the whole class of products indicated by the sacrifice. The waters give birth to them. For that purpose the waters hold within themselves दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*), Prajāpati, who grows into the form of the universe. The waters so described are in the nominative by a change of case. अपः (*apaḥ*) means the waters of the time of dissolution. महिना (*mahinā*) means "by greatness". Prajāpati beheld them on every side by his own majesty. Among the gods he was the god, the lord even of them, and was the one, second-less. आसीत् (*āsīt*) here is "is". The refrain कस्मै (*kasmai*) and the rest has been explained already.

- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the derived creation beginning with the sacrifice
- जनयंतीः (*janayaṃtīḥ*)—those that produce (for that very purpose)
- दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*)—Prajāpati, who becomes manifest as the universe (within themselves)
- दधानाः (*dadhānāḥ*)—those that hold (pervading everywhere)
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- यः चित् (*yaḥ cit*)—the Prajāpati who
- महिना (*mahinā*)—by his majesty
- पर्यपश्यत् (*paryapaśyat*)—beheld
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Prajāpati who
- देवेषु अधि (*deveṣu adhi*)—among the gods

- विधेम (*vidhema*)—let us serve

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Prajāpati by his majesty beheld the all-pervading waters, which are the cause of creation beginning with the sacrifice and which hold Prajāpati himself in their womb. He is also a god among the gods, that is, the god of gods. Let us offer oblations and other materials to that Prajāpati, who is of the nature of happiness.

##### English translation
He who by his might beheld the waters all around containing the creative power and giving birth to sacrifice, he who among the gods was the one supreme god,—let us offer worship with an oblation to the devine Ka.

> यश्चा॒पश्चं॒द्रा बृ॑ह॒तीर्ज॒जान॒ कस्मै॑ दे॒वाय॑ ह॒विषा॑ विधेम॥

> मा । नः । हिंसीत् । जनिता । यः । पृथिव्याः । यः । वा । दिवं । सत्यधर्मा । जजान ।  
> यः । च । अपः । चंद्राः । बृहतीः । जजान । कस्मै । देवाय । हविषा । विधेम ॥९॥

### Printed p. 643

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स प्रजापतिर्नोऽस्मान्मा हिंसीत् । मा बाधतां । यः पृथिव्या भूमेर्जनिता
> जनयिता स्रष्टा ॥ जनिता मंत्र इति णिलोपो निपात्यते । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्नादिति पृथिवीशब्दाद्विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥ यो वा यश्च सत्यधर्मा सत्यमवितथं
> धर्म जगतो धारणं यस्य स तादृशः प्रजापतिर्दिवमंतरिक्षोपलक्षितान्सवाल्लोकाञ्चजान जनयामास ॥ जनी प्रादुर्भावे । णिचि वृद्धौ जनीज्यष्कसुरंजः ।
> धा. १९-६३-६७ । इति मित्वान्मितां ह्रस्व इति ह्रस्वत्वं। ततो लिट्यमंत्रे। पा. ३-१-३५ ।
> इति निषेधादाम्रत्ययाभावे तिपो णलि वृद्धौ लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्कोदात्तत्वं ॥
> यश्च बृहतीर्महतीश्चंद्रा आह्लादिनीरप उदकानि जजान जनयामास ॥ ऊडिदमित्यादिनाप्यब्दादुत्तरस्य शस उदात्तत्वं ॥ तस्मै कस्मा इत्यादिगतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May that Prajāpati not harm us, that is, not oppress us. He is जनिता (*janitā*), the begetter and creator, of the earth. He is सत्यधर्मा (*satyadharmā*): सत्य (*satya*) is the unfailing, and धर्म (*dharma*) is the upholding of the world, which is his. Such a Prajāpati begot दिवं (*divaṃ*), that is, all the worlds indicated by the heaven and the middle region. जजान (*jajāna*) means "caused to be born". He also begot the बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*), the great, and चंद्राः (*caṃdrāḥ*), the delightful, अपः (*apaḥ*), the waters. The refrain कस्मै (*kasmai*) and the rest has been explained already.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (that Prajāpati) नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मा हिंसीत् (*mā hiṃsīt*)—may he not harm
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Prajāpati who
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the earth
- जनिता (*janitā*)—is the creator
- सत्यधर्मा (*satyadharmā*)—who carries out true works such as upholding the world
- यः वा (*yaḥ vā*)—the Prajāpati who
- दिवं (*divaṃ*)—all the worlds beginning with the middle region
- जजान (*jajāna*)—produced
- य च (*ya ca*)—the Prajāpati who
- बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*)—great
- चंद्राः (*caṃdrāḥ*)—and delightful
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—waters
- जजान (*jajāna*)—produced; to such
- कस्मै (*kasmai*)—who is of the nature of happiness
- देवाय (*devāya*)—to Prajāpati
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—oblations and other materials
- विधेम (*vidhema*)—let us offer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May that Prajāpati not harm us. He created this earth, he created the upper worlds beginning with the middle region, and he produced the great and delightful waters. Let us offer oblations and other materials to that Prajāpati, who is of the nature of happiness.

##### English translation
May he do us no harm who is the parent of the earth or who the unerring support (of the world) begat the heaven, and who generated the vast and delightful waters,—let us offer worship with an oblation to the divine Ka.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रजा॑पते॒ न त्वदे॒तान्य॒न्यू विश्वा॑ जा॒तानि॒ परि॒ ता ब॑भूव ।

> रयीणां ॥ १० ॥

> प्रजापते न त्वदेतान्यन्यो विश्वा जातानि परि ता बभूव ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इळादधाख्य इष्ट्ययने प्राजापत्यस्य हविषः प्रजापत इत्येषानुवाक्या ।
> सूत्रितं च । प्राजापत्य इळादधः प्रजापते न त्वदेतान्यन्यः। आ. २-१४ । इति !! केशनखकीटादिभिर्दुष्टानि हवींष्यनय्यॆनाप्सु प्रक्षिपेत् । सूत्रितं च । अपोऽभ्यवहरेयुः
> प्रजापते न त्वदेतान्यन्यः । आ. ३-१० । इति ॥ चौलादिकर्मस्वप्येषा होमार्था ।
> सूत्रितं च । तेषां पुरस्ताच्चतस्र आज्याहुतीर्जुहुयादग्न आयूंषि पवस इति
> तिसृभिः प्रजापते न त्वदेतान्यन्य इति च । आ. गृ. १-४-४ । इति ॥
> हे प्रजापते त्वत् त्वत्तोऽन्यः कश्चिदेतानीदानीं वर्तमानानि विश्वा विश्वानि
> सर्वाणि ॥ शेश्चंदसि बहुलमिति शेर्लोपः ॥ जातानि प्रथमविकारभांजि ता तानि
> सर्वाणि भूतजातानि न परि बभूव । न परिगृह्णाति । न व्याप्प्नोति । त्वमेवैतानि परिगृह्य
> स्रष्टुं शक्षोषीति भावः ॥ परिपूर्वो भवतिः परिग्रहार्थः । वयं च यत्कामा
> यत्पलं कामयमानास्ते तुभ्यं जुहुमः हवींषि प्रयच्छामः तत्पलं नोऽस्माकमस्तु । भवतु । तथा वयं च रयाणां धनानां पतॆय ईश्वराः स्याम । भवेम ॥
> नामन्यतरस्यामिति नाम उदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Iḷādadha sacrifice (iṣṭi) this Ṛk, प्रजापते (*prajāpate*), is the anuvākyā for the oblation to Prajāpati. The sūtra says: प्राजापत्य इळादधः प्रजापते न त्वदेतान्यन्यः (*prājāpatya iḷādadhaḥ prajāpate na tvadetānyanyaḥ*) (Ā. 2-14). Where oblations are spoiled by hair, nails, insects and the like, they are to be thrown into water with this Ṛk. The sūtra says: अपोऽभ्यवहरेयुः प्रजापते न त्वदेतान्यन्यः (*apo 'bhyavahareyuḥ prajāpate na tvadetānyanyaḥ*) (Ā. 3-10). This Ṛk is also used for the homa in rites such as the tonsure (caula). The sūtra says: तेषां पुरस्ताच्चतस्र आज्याहुतीर्जुहुयादग्न आयूंषि पवस इति तिसृभिः प्रजापते न त्वदेतान्यन्य इति च (*teṣāṃ purastāccatasra ājyāhutīrjuhuyādagna āyūṃṣi pavasa iti tisṛbhiḥ prajāpate na tvadetānyanya iti ca*) (Ā. Gṛ. 1-4-4).
Meaning: O Prajāpati, no one other than you has encompassed all these existing things, the products of the first transformation. The sense is that you alone, having encompassed them, are able to create them; the root भू (*bhū*) with परि (*pari*) has the sense of encompassing. And we, desiring whatever fruit we offer oblations to you for, may that fruit be ours; and may we be the lords of riches.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रजापते (*prajāpate*)—O Prajāpati

- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—anyone else

- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- जातानि (*jātāni*)—the products of the first creation, whichever there are

- न परि बभूव (*na pari babhūva*)—is not able to undertake to create

- ते (*te*)—to you
- जुहुमः (*juhumaḥ*)—we offer oblations and other materials, and perform homa
- तत् (*tat*)—that fruit in the form of the wish
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- अस्तु (*astu*)—may it come
- वयं च (*vayaṃ ca*)—and we also
- रयीणां (*rayīṇāṃ*)—of riches
- पतयः (*patayaḥ*)—as lords
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we become

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Prajāpati, apart from you there is no one else who sets about creating all that now exists, the first creation, the five great elements and the rest. May we obtain the fruit of the wish for whose fulfilment we offer you oblations. May we also become lords of riches.

##### English translation
No other than you. Prajapathi has given existance to all these beings may that object of our desires for which we sacrifice to you be ours, may we be the possessors of riches.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the iṣṭi called Iḷādadha, in the oblation-homa made to the deity Prajāpati, this Ṛk प्रजापते (*prajāpate*) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra. This is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra in the sūtra प्राजापत्य इळादधः प्रजापते न त्वदेतान्यन्यः (*prājāpatya iḷādadhaḥ prajāpate na tvadetānyanyaḥ*) (Ā. 2-14). If among the oblation materials offered by homa to the gods there are mixed impure things such as hair, nails, worms and insects, those oblations are to be put in water with the recitation of this Ṛk प्रजापते (*prajāpate*). This is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra in the sūtra अपोऽभ्यवहरेयुः प्रजापते न त्वदेतान्यन्यः (*apo 'bhyavahareyuḥ prajāpate na tvadetānyanyaḥ*) (Ā. 3-10). And this Ṛk is also employed for the homa in domestic rites such as the tonsure. This is set out by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtra in the sūtra तेषां पुरस्ताच्चतस्र आज्याहुतीर्जुहुयादग्न अयूंषि पवस इति तिसृभिः प्रजापते न त्वदेतान्यन्य इति च (*teṣāṃ purastāccatasra ājyāhutīrjuhuyādagna ayūṃṣi pavasa iti tisṛbhiḥ prajāpate na tvadetānyanya iti ca*) (Ā. Gṛ. 1-4-8).**NOTE**
In explaining the word Prajāpati, Yāska has given an etymology that bears on this Ṛk: प्रजापतिः प्रजानां पाता वा पालयिता वा ॥ तस्यैषा भवति ॥ (*prajāpatiḥ prajānāṃ pātā vā pālayitā vā ‖ tasyaiṣā bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 10-42). The word Prajāpati means the protector of creatures, the one who looks after creatures. The following Ṛk concerns Prajāpati: प्रजापते न त्वदेतान्यन्नो विश्वा जातानि परि ता बभूव । यत्कामास्ते जुहु मस्तन्नो अस्तु वयं स्याम पतयो रयीणां ॥ (*prajāpate na tvadetānyanno viśvā jātāni pari tā babhūva | yatkāmāste juhu mastanno astu vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇāṃ ‖*)

### Printed p. 646
Addressed to Prajāpati: "O Prajāpati, none other than you has encompassed all these things that have been born. May that for which we desire and offer you oblations be ours; may we be lords of riches." This is the Nirukta's explanation:

प्रजापते न हि त्वदेतान्यन्यः सर्वाणि जातानि तानि परि बभूव यत्कामास्ते जुहुमस्तॆन्नो अस्तु वयं स्याम पतयो रयीणामित्याशीः ॥ (*prajāpate na hi tvadetānyanyaḥ sarvāṇi jātāni tāni pari babhūva yatkāmāste juhumastènno astu vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇāmityāśīḥ ‖*) (Ni. 10-43)

O Prajāpati, apart from you there is no one else who pervades, within and without, these masses of created things and the divine forms. May all those wishes for whose fulfilment we offer oblations to you be accomplished for us. May we become lords of abundant wealth. This is the main purport of the explanation. Yāska has said that this Ṛk is in the form of a blessing.

## Sūkta 122 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वसुं नेत्यष्टर्चं दशमं सूक्तं वसिष्ठपुत्रस्य चित्रमहस आर्षमाग्नेयं
> आद्यापंचमी त्रिष्टुभौ शिष्टा जगत्यः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । वसुं नाष्टौ चित्रमहा
> वासिष्ठ आग्नेयं जागतमाद्यां पंचमीं चर्त इति ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोराग्नेये क्रत्वा जागते छंदसीदं सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । वसुं न चित्रमहसमिति
> जागतं । अ. ४-१३ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning वसुं न (*vasuṃ na*) has eight Ṛks and is the tenth sūkta of its anuvāka. Its seer is Citramahas, son of Vasiṣṭha; its deity is Agni. The first and fifth Ṛks are in Triṣṭubh, the rest in Jagatī. Sāyaṇa cites the Anukramaṇī: वसुं नाष्टौ चित्रमहा वासिष्ठ आग्नेयं जागतमाद्यां पंचमीं चर्त इति ॥ (*vasuṃ nāṣṭau citramahā vāsiṣṭha āgneyaṃ jāgatamādyāṃ paṃcamīṃ carta iti ‖*). The sūkta is used in the Prātaranuvāka and in the Āśvina śastra, among the Jagatī-metre verses belonging to the Āgneya kratu. He cites the sūtra: वसुं न चित्रमहसमिति जागतं (*vasuṃ na citramahasamiti jāgataṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 4-13).

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning "वसुं न (*vasuṃ na*)" is the tenth sūkta in the tenth anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. Its seer is Citramahas, son of the sage Vasiṣṭha; its deity is Agni. In this sūkta the first and fifth Ṛks are in Triṣṭup metre; the remaining Ṛks are in Jagatī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: "Vasuṃ na … Citramahas Vāsiṣṭha, Āgneya, Jāgata, the first and fifth …". Its use, for the Jagatī-metre Ṛks connected with the Āgneya kratu in the recitation of the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina śastra mantras, is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra "वसुं न चित्रमहसमिति जागतं (*vasuṃ na citramahasamiti jāgataṃ*)" (Ā. 4-13).

Sūkta 122. Maṇḍala 10. Anuvāka 10. Sūkta 122. Aṣṭaka 8. Adhyāya 7. Vargas 5, 6. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8. Seer: Citramahas Vāsiṣṭha. Deity: Agni. Metre: 1–5 Triṣṭubh; 2–4, 6–8 Jagatī.

> तवैकेनिति केन्यप्रत्ययः । नञा बहुव्रीहौ नञ्च्यामित्युत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं ॥
> सोऽग्निः शुरुधः शोकस्य रोधयित्रीर्निवारयित्रीर्विश्वधायसः क्षीरप्रदानादिना
> विश्वं सर्वं जगद्धारयंतीर्गाः सुवीर्यं शोभनवीर्यं च रासते । यजमानेभ्यो ददाति ॥ रा दाने । आस्माल्लेट् । लेट्यडागमः । सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । विश्वशब्दोपधाद्दधातेर्वहिहाधाइ इत्यसुन् । णिदित्यनुवृत्तेरातो युक्‌चिणिति युक् मरुद्वधादित्वात्पूर्वपदांतोदात्तत्वं ॥ कीदृशोऽग्निः ।
> होता देवानामाह्वाता होमनिष्पादको ना गृहपतिर्यजमानगृहाणामीश्वरः ॥
> गेहे कः । पा. ३-१-१४४ । इति ग्रहेः कप्रत्ययः । ग्रहिज्येत्यादिना संप्रसारणं ।
> पत्यावैश्वर्य इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । शोभनं वीर्यं यस्येति बहुव्रीहौ
> वीरवीयौ चेत्युत्तरपदाद्यु दात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"I praise Agni" — the one who gives dwelling, like the sun (वसुं न (*vasuṃ na*)), of wonderful (चित्रमहसं (*citramahasaṃ*)) radiance. The verb गृणीषे (*gṛṇīṣe*) is from the root गृ (*gṛ*) (Kryādi class), with an exchange of person. Alternatively, चित्रमहसं (*citramahasaṃ*) stands for the nominative (the accusative used in the sense of the first case) and न (*na*) has the sense of "now": "now I, Citramahas, praise Agni who gives dwelling." Of what kind is he? वामं (*vāmaṃ*): lovely, to be desired; शेवं (*śevaṃ*): the giver of happiness; अतिथिं (*atithiṃ*): to be honoured like a guest, or else one who goes constantly to carry the oblations; अद्विषेण्यं (*adviṣeṇyaṃ*): free from hatred. That Agni gives to the sacrificers the cows that are शुरुधः (*śurudhaḥ*) (they check and remove sorrow) and विश्वधायसः (*viśvadhāyasaḥ*) (they sustain the whole world by giving milk and so on), and also excellent vigour (सुवीर्यं (*suvīryaṃ*)); रासते (*rāsate*) means "gives". What kind of Agni? He is the Hotā, the invoker of the gods and accomplisher of the homa; the गृहपतिः (*gṛhapatiḥ*), lord of the sacrificers' houses; the one whose vigour is excellent.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वामं (*vāmaṃ*)—one desired by all
- शेवं (*śevaṃ*)—the giver of happiness
- अतिथिं (*atithiṃ*)—worthy of worship like a guest, or one who always comes to us to carry the oblation
- अद्विषेण्यं (*adviṣeṇyaṃ*)—free of enemies
- वसुं न (*vasuṃ na*)—like the sun
- चित्रमहसं (*citramahasaṃ*)—possessed of wonderful radiance; Agni, such as this

### Printed p. 648
- गृणीषे (*gṛṇīṣe*)—I praise [or: वासकं (*vāsakaṃ*)—Agni, the giver of dwelling; न (*na*)—now; चित्रमहसं (*citramahasaṃ*)—I, named Citramahas; गृणीषे (*gṛṇīṣe*)—I praise]
- होता (*hotā*)—the invoker of the gods
- गृहपतिः (*gṛhapatiḥ*)—lord, or protector, of the houses of the sacrificers
- स आग्निः (*sa āgniḥ*)—that Agni
- शुरुधः (*śurudhaḥ*)—the removers of sorrow
- विश्वधायसः (*viśvadhāyasaḥ*)—those that protect all by giving milk (the cows)
- सुवीर्यं (*suvīryaṃ*)—excellent valour
- रासते (*rāsate*)—gives to the sacrificers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, named Citramahas, praise Agni, who is desired by all, the giver of happiness, worthy of worship like a guest, free of enemies, endowed like the sun with wonderful radiance, the giver of dwelling. That Agni, the invoker of the gods and protector of the sacrificers' houses, gives to the sacrificers cows that remove sorrow and protect all by giving milk and the like, and also excellent strength and capacity.

##### English translation
I glorify him who is of wonderful radiance like the sun, the desirable, the giver of happiness, the guest (of man). the benevolent. He bestows vigour (upon the worshippers); Agni, the remover of sorrow, the sustainer of all, the invoker (of the gods), the lord of the mansion.

#### Ṛk 2

> जु॒षा॒णो अ॑ग्ने॒ प्रति॑ हर्य मे॒ वचो॒ विश्वा॑नि वि॒द्वान्व॒युना॑नि सुक्रतो ।  
> घृत॑निर्णि॒ग्ब्रह्म॑णे गा॒तुमेर॑य॒ तव॑ दे॒वा अ॑जनय॒न्ननु॑  ॒
> व्रतं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> जुषाणः । अग्ने । प्रति । हर्य । मे । वचः । विश्वानि । विद्वान् । वयुनानि । सुक्रतो  
> इति सुक्रतो ।

### Printed p. 649

> धृतनिर्निक् । ब्रह्मणे । गातुं ' आ । ईरय । तव । देवाः । अजनयन् । अनु ।  
> व्रतं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने जुषाणः प्रीयमाणस्त्वं मे मम वचो वचनं स्तोत्रं प्रति
> हर्य । कामयस्व ॥ हर्य गतिकांत्योः ॥ तथा हे सुक्रतो शोभनकर्मन्
> शोभनप्रज्ञ वा त्वं विश्वानि सर्वाणि वयुनानि । ज्ञाननामैतत् इह ज्ञातव्ये वर्तते।
> ज्ञातव्यान्यर्थजातानि विद्वाञ्ज्ञानन्वर्तसे ॥ हेत् शतृप्रत्ययः ॥ यतो जानासि
> ततो हेतोर्मद्वचनं कामयस्वेत्यर्थः हे घृतनिर्णिगृतेनाज्येन निर्णिज्यमान
> पुष्यमाणशरीर ॥ णिजिर् शौचपोषणयोः ॥ यद्वा । निर्णिगिति रूपनाम । दीप्तरूपाग्ने ब्रह्मणे ब्राह्मणाय यजमानाय गातुं गातव्यं ज्ञातव्यं वा यज्ञमेरय।
> आगमय । तव व्रतं त्वदीयं यज्ञकर्मानु पश्चाद्देवा इंद्रादयः सर्वॆऽजनयन् । यजमानाय फलानि जनयंति । अतस्त्वदीयं यज्ञं यजमानाय प्रापयेत्यर्थः ॥ लक्षणेऽनोः कर्मप्रवचनीयत्वं व्रतमिति कर्मप्रवचनीययुक्त
> इति द्वितीया । जनेर्ण्यंताच्छांदसो लज् । जनीज्यस्क्नसुरंजोऽमंताश्चेति
> मित्वान्मितां ह्रस्व इति ह्रस्वत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, being pleased (जुषाणः (*juṣāṇaḥ*)), desire (हर्य (*harya*), from the root meaning 'to go' and 'to desire'; कामयस्व (*kāmayasva*)) my speech, my praise." And "O सुक्रतो (*sukrato*), of good works or of good understanding, you are knowing (विद्वान् (*vidvān*)) all (विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)) वयुनानि (*vayunāni*)." वयुन (*vayuna*) is a name for knowledge and here stands for the knowable: you know all things to be known. Since you know, therefore desire my speech. "O *ghṛtanirṇik*, you whose body is washed and nourished with ghee (the root णिजिर् (*ṇijir*) means purifying and nourishing)." Or else निर्णिक् (*nirṇik*) is a name for form: Agni of radiant form. "For the Brahmin, the sacrificer, send (*eraya*; bring) the गातुं (*gātuṃ*), the thing to be gone to or known, the sacrifice. After (अनु (*anu*)) your rite (व्रतं (*vrataṃ*)) the gods, Indra and the rest, all produce (अजनयन् (*ajanayan*)) fruits for the sacrificer. Therefore bring your sacrifice to the sacrificer." अनु (*anu*) is a karmapravacanīya, hence the accusative of व्रतं (*vrataṃ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- जुषाणः (*juṣāṇaḥ*)—with a pleased mind
- मे (*me*)—my
- वचः (*vacaḥ*)—speech in the form of praise
- प्रति हर्य (*prati harya*)—desire
- सुक्रतो (*sukrato*)—O Agni, of good works or excellent knower
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- वयुनानि (*vayunāni*)—things to be known
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—you are one who knows
- धृतनिर्णिक् (*dhṛtanirṇik*)—O Agni, whose body is soaked with ghee, or of radiant form
- ब्रह्मणे (*brahmaṇe*)—for the sacrificer who is a Brahmin
- गातुं (*gātuṃ*)—the sacrifice that he should know
- आ ईरय (*ā īraya*)—impel
- तव (*tava*)—relating to you
- व्रतं (*vrataṃ*)—sacrificial rite
- अनु (*anu*)—in accordance with
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- अजनयन् (*ajanayan*)—give the fruit to the sacrificer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, listen with regard to the praise I make, satisfied. O Agni, of excellent works, you know all that is to be known. O Agni, whose body is sprinkled with ghee, or whose form is radiant, impel and bring to completion the sacrificial rite for the Brahmin sacrificer. In this rite of yours the gods give the sacrificers the fruits of the sacrifice.

### Printed p. 650

##### English translation
Accept, Agni, being well pleased, my praise; author of great deeds, (you are) cognizant of all objects of knowledge; anointed with butter, stimulate the movements of the Brahmana; the gods produce (rewards) after your worship.

> सु॒वीरे॑ण र॒याणा॑ग्ने स्वा॒भुवा॒ यस्त॒ आन॑ट् स॒मिधा॒ तं  ॑
> जुषस्व ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सप्त । धामानि । परियन् । अमर्त्यः । दाशत् । दाशुषे । सुकृते । ममहस्व ।  
> सुवीरेण । रयिणा । अग्ने । सुअभुवा । यः । ते । आनट् । संइधा । तं ।  
> जुषस्व ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने सप्त सप्तसंख्याकानि धामानि स्थानानि पृथिव्यादिलोकात्मकानि परियन्
> परितो गच्छन्नमर्त्यो मरणधर्मरहितस्त्वं यो यजमानः पुरोडाशादीनि
> हवींषि दाशत् प्रयच्छति तस्मै दाशुषे दत्तवते सुकृते सुष्टु यागं कृतवते
> मामहस्व । अपेक्षितं धनं ददस्व । महतिर्दानकर्मा ॥ सुकर्मसापेत्यादिना सुपूवात्कृञ्चो भूते काले क्विप् ॥ यश्च यजमानः समिधा समिंधनसाधनेनेध्मेन हे
> अग्ने ते त्वामानट् प्राप्नोति ॥ नशतिर्गतिकर्मा । अस्माच्चांदसो लज् । बहुलं
> छंदसीति शपो लुक् । छंदस्यपि दृश्यत इत्याडागमः । अश्नोतेर्वा व्यत्ययेन
> श्नम् ॥ तं यजमानं सुवीरेण । शोभनवीराः पुत्रा यस्य ॥ वीरवीर्यौ चेत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ तादृशेन स्वाभुवा सुष्वा समंताद्दूष्णुना वर्धिष्णुना
> रयिणा धनेन दाशव्येन सार्धं जुषस्व ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, moving round the seven (सप्त (*sapta*)) abodes (धामानि (*dhāmāni*)), that is, the places consisting of the worlds beginning with the earth, you the immortal — to that sacrificer who gives (दाशत् (*dāśat*)) oblations such as the purodāśa, to the giver (दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)), to the one who has well performed the sacrifice (सुकृते (*sukṛte*)), give (मामहस्व (*māmahasva*)) the wealth he desires." महति (*mahati*) is a verb of giving. "And the sacrificer who approaches (आनट् (*ānaṭ*)) you, O Agni, with kindling-wood (समिधा (*samidhā*)), the instrument of kindling — him, together with wealth (रयिणा (*rayiṇā*)) that is सुवीरेण (*suvīreṇa*) (his sons being good heroes) and स्वाभुवा (*svābhuvā*) (growing well, increasing), and fit to be given, favour (जुषस्व (*juṣasva*))." The root नश (*naśa*) is a verb of going; alternatively आनट् (*ānaṭ*) is from *aśnoti*.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Agni) सप्त धामानि (*sapta dhāmāni*)—the seven places, the worlds beginning with the earth
- परियन् (*pariyan*)—moving round
- अमर्त्यः (*amartyaḥ*)—you who are free from death
- दाशत् (*dāśat*)—whichever sacrificer offers you purodāśa and the like

- सुकृते (*sukṛte*)—to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice well
- मामहस्व (*māmahasva*)—give the wealth that he desires
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which sacrificer
- समिधा (*samidhā*)—with kindling-wood such as fuel
- ते (*te*)—you
- आनट् (*ānaṭ*)—approaches (to serve)
- तं (*taṃ*)—that sacrificer
- सुवीरेण (*suvīreṇa*)—with valorous sons
- स्वाभुवा (*svābhuvā*)—growing well
- रयिणा (*rayiṇā*)—with wealth
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—serve, that is, satisfy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who can move in the seven places beginning with the earth, and are free from death: give the wealth he needs to the sacrificer who offers you oblations and the like and performs the sacrifice well. O Agni, to the sacrificer who approaches to serve you with kindling-wood and other materials, give valorous sons and increasing wealth, and satisfy him.

##### English translation
Traversing the seven regions (of the universe), immortal Agni, bestow wealth, giving liberally to the pious liberal giver. Gratify with easily obtainable riches, together with fair offspring, him who feeds you with fuel.

> प्रीणने तौदादिकः। शतुरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति
> कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्च तुर्थी ॥ हविर्भिः प्रीणयंतं यजमानं धनैः प्रीणयंतं।
> यद्वा । पृणतिर्दानकर्मा । हवींषि ददते यजमानाय पृणंतं धनानि प्रयच्छतं । सुवीर्यं शोभनवीर्योपेतं देवं द्योतमानं दानादिगुणयुक्तं वा
> एवंगुणविशिष्टमग्निं हविष्मंतो हविर्भियुक्ताः सप्त होतृप्रमुखा वषट्कर्तार
> ईळते । स्तुवंति ॥ ईड स्तुतौ आदादिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Of the sacrifice" means of the yāga; Agni is its "banner" (केतुं (*ketuṃ*)), that is, its indicator. He is "first" (प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)): chief among all the gods, or holding the first place. He is "purohita": one who does good in front. Alternatively, he is placed in front, in the eastern quarter, in the form of the Āhavanīya fire. Sāyaṇa explains the formation of पुरोहितं (*purohitaṃ*): the affix asi after the word for "east", the substitution of पुर (*pura*), the designation as an indeclinable and as gati. वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*) is "mighty" or "possessed of food". शृण्वंतं (*śṛṇvaṃtaṃ*) is one who hears our praises with his ear. धृतपृष्टं (*dhṛtapṛṣṭaṃ*) is one whose back (body) is shining. उक्षणं (*ukṣaṇaṃ*) is one who, through the sacrifice, distributes rain, or one who is able to sprinkle, a youth. पृणते (*pṛṇate*) means for the sacrificer who gratifies him with oblations. पृणंतं (*pṛṇaṃtaṃ*) means gratifying the sacrificer with oblations, or, alternatively, since the root pṛṇ means giving, giving wealth to the sacrificer who offers oblations. सुवीर्यं (*suvīryaṃ*) is endowed with excellent valour. देवं (*devaṃ*) is shining, or possessed of qualities such as generosity. The seven vaṣaṭkartṛs, the hotṛ and the others, bearing oblations, praise Agni so qualified (ईळते (*īḷate*), root īḍ, to praise).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—of the sacrifice
- केतुं (*ketuṃ*)—the indicator
- प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—the one who is chief among all the gods, or who holds the first place
- पुरोहितं (*purohitaṃ*)—the one established in the form of Āhavanīya in the eastern part of the sacrificial altar
- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—the mighty, or the possessor of food
- शृण्वंतं (*śṛṇvaṃtaṃ*)—the one who hears and understands our praises
- धृतपृष्टं (*dhṛtapṛṣṭaṃ*)—the one with a shining body
- उक्षणं (*ukṣaṇaṃ*)—the one who pours rain through the conduct of the sacrifice, or the youthful one
- पृणते (*pṛṇate*)—to the sacrificer who offers oblations and satisfies him
- पृणंतं (*pṛṇaṃtaṃ*)—the one who gives wealth and the like
- सुवीर्यं (*suvīryaṃ*)—the one of excellent capacity
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—the radiant one
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- हविष्मंतः (*haviṣmaṃtaḥ*)—those who have prepared the oblation
- सप्त (*sapta*)—seven priests beginning with the hotṛ, that is, the seven hotṛs who are vaṣaṭ-makers
- ईळते (*īḷate*)—praise
### Printed p. 653

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The seven hotṛs, bearing oblations, praise Agni: the indicator of the sacrifice, or one like its banner; the chief of all the gods; established in the form of Āhavanīya in the eastern part of the sacrificial altar; possessed of strength or food; who listens to and hears our praises; whose body is shining; the sprinkler of rain; who gives wealth and the like to the sacrificer who offers oblations; who has excellent strength and capacity; the radiant one.

##### English translation
The seven (priests) bearing oblations worship Agni, the emblem of sacrifice, the first of the gods, the family priest, the possessor of food, the hearer (of our prayers), the anointed with butter, the shedder of moisture propitiating the worshipper who propitiates him, divine, endowed with excellent might.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you are the messenger, appointed to the messenger's office of the gods; you are "first", chief or renowned, and "to be chosen", worthy of being resorted to. Being invoked by us for immortality, that is, for the sake of freedom from death, and being gratified with the oblation, "be exhilarated" (मत्स्य (*matsya*), root mad, to rejoice; the vikaraṇa is dropped in the Veda). Moreover, the Maruts, the groups of gods of that place, decorate you who abide in the middle region in the form of lightning.
### Printed p. 654

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मानं मरुतस्तत्रत्या देवगणा मर्जयन् । मार्जयंति । अलंकुर्वंति । तथा
> दाशुषो हवींषि दत्तवतो यजमानस्यगृहे स्तोमेभिः स्तोमैः स्तोत्रैर्भृगवो
> भृगुगोत्रा ऋषयस्त्वां वि रुरुचुः । विशेषेण दीपयंति ॥ भृगुशब्दादुत्तरस्यॆ
> तद्धितस्यात्रिभृगुकुत्सेत्यादिना । पा. २-४-६५ । बहुषु लुक् । रुरुचुः । रुच दीप्तौ ।
> अस्माच्छांदसो लिट् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(continued) The Maruts "adorn" (मर्जयन् (*marjayan*)) you. Likewise, in the house of the sacrificer who has given oblations, the Bhṛgus, the seers of the Bhṛgu lineage, make you shine forth specially with stomas, that is, with hymns of praise (रुरुचुः (*rurucuḥ*), root ruc, to shine, in the Vedic liṭ). Sāyaṇa cites Pā. Sū. 2-4-65 for the dropping of the taddhita affix after the word *Bhṛgu* in the plural.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Agni) त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- दूतः (*dūtaḥ*)—are the messenger who carries the oblation to the gods
- प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—the chief among all the gods
- वरेण्यः (*vareṇyaḥ*)—the one desired by all
- सः(त्वं) (*saḥ(tvaṃ)*)—that you
- अमृताय (*amṛtāya*)—for the deathless state (heaven)
- हूयमानः (*hūyamānaḥ*)—being prayed to and called by us
- मत्स्य (*matsya*)—be satisfied (attain delight)
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you who are in the atmosphere in the form of lightning
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Marut deities there
- मर्जयन् (*marjayan*)—adorn
- दाशुषः (*dāśuṣaḥ*)—of the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- गृहे (*gṛhe*)—in the house
- भृगवः (*bhṛgavaḥ*)—the seers of the Bhṛgu lineage
- स्तोमेभिः (*stomebhiḥ*)—with stomas and praises
- वि रुरुचुः (*vi rurucuḥ*)—make you shine especially

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who are called messenger because you carry the oblation to the gods, and who are desired by all: being prayed to and called by us for the attainment of the deathless heaven and the like, be glad at heart. The Maruts there adorn you, who are in the atmosphere in the form of lightning-fire. In the house of the sacrificer who offers oblations, the seers born in the Bhṛgu lineage kindle you with hymns and the like and make you shine.

##### English translation
You are the chief and most excellent messenger; do you, invoked by us to partake of the ambrosia, become, exhilarated; the Maruts decorated you in the dwelling of the donor of the oblation: the Bhrigus have glorified you with hymns.

> हे सुक्रतो सुकर्मन् शोभनप्रज्ञ वागे यज्ञप्रिये यज्ञैर्हविर्भिर्देवा
> स्त्रीणयित्रे यजमानाय विश्वधायसं विश्वस्य सर्वस्य धारयित्रिं सुदुघां दोग्धुं
> सुशक्यां यज्ञरूपिणीं गामिषमिष्यमाणं यागफलरूपं पयो दुहन् क्षारयन्
> तथा घृतस्नुर्फृतेनाज्येन प्रस्नातः ॥ स्नातेरौणादिकः कुप्रत्ययः ॥ यद्वा । घृतो

> मांस्पृत्नामुपसंख्यानं । पा. ६-१-६३-१ । इति सानुशब्दस्य स्नुभावः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ ईदृशस्त्वं त्रिस्तिवारमावृत्तान्यतानि सत्यभूतानि
> पृथिव्यादीनि त्रीणि स्थानानि यद्वा गार्हपत्यादीनि स्थानानि दीद्यद्दीपयन्वर्तिः सर्वं
> यज्ञगृहं सर्वमनुष्ठीयमानं यागं च परियन् परितो गच्छन् तत्तद्यज्ञगृहं
> तं तं यज्ञं च प्राप्नुवन् सुक्रतूयसे । शोभनं क्रतुं यज्ञमात्मन इच्छिसि ।
> यद्वा । शोभनः क्रतुर्यस्यासौ सुक्रतुर्यजमानः । स इवाचरसि । स यथा
> सम्यगनुष्ठाने प्रवर्तते एवं त्वमपि स्वयमेव यागस्य सम्यग्निष्पत्यर्थं प्रवर्तस
> इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Sukratu (doer of good deeds, of good wisdom), Agni: for the sacrificer who pleases with sacrifices, that is, who gratifies the gods with oblations, you milk the desired milk, the fruit of the sacrifice, from the cow in the form of the sacrifice, which sustains all and is easily milked. You are "anointed with ghee" (घृतस्नुः (*ghṛtasnuḥ*), with the Uṇādi affix ku after the root snā). Alternatively, one whose ridge (स्नु (*snu*), for सानु (*sānu*)), the mass of flames, is lit and risen high. You make the three true places shine, the earth and the others, or the places of the Gārhapatya and the other fires, and go around the entire house of sacrifice and the sacrifice being performed, reaching each house and each sacrifice. सुक्रतूयसे (*sukratūyase*): you desire a good sacrifice for yourself. Alternatively, as a sacrificer who has a good sacrifice acts, so you too yourself proceed for the proper completion of the sacrifice. For the sāna-to-snu substitution Sāyaṇa cites Pā. 6-1-63-1.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुक्रतो (*sukrato*)—O one endowed with excellent works
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यज्ञप्रिये (*yajñapriye*)—to the one who pleases the gods by sacrificial rites
- यजमानाय (*yajamānāya*)—for the sacrificer
- विश्वधायसं (*viśvadhāyasaṃ*)—who sustains and nourishes all
- सुदुघां (*sudughāṃ*)—the cow in the form of the sacrifice, who yields the milk of desired objects
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—the milk that is the fruit of the sacrifice
- दुहन् (*duhan*)—milking
- घृतस्नुः (*ghṛtasnuḥ*)—you, who are sprinkled with ghee, or have flames kindled by ghee
- त्रिः ऋतानि (*triḥ ṛtāni*)—the three true places, the earth and the others, or the three fire-places such as the Gārhapatya
### Printed p. 656
- दीद्यन् (*dīdyan*)—making shine
- वर्तिः (*vartiḥ*)—around the house of sacrifice and the sacrifice
- परियन् (*pariyan*)—moving about
- सुक्रतुयसे (*sukratuyase*)—you perfect the sacrificer's sacrifice well, or you behave like a sacrificer who performs a sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, endowed with excellent works or wisdom: you milk, for the sacrificer who gratifies the gods with the sacrificial rite, that is, with oblations and the like, the milk that is the fruit of the sacrifice, from the cow in the form of the sacrifice, which sustains and nourishes all and yields the milk of desired objects. Your body is sprinkled with ghee, or you are of blazing splendour. Making the three true places, the earth and the others, or the three fire-pits such as the Gārhapatya, shine, you go around the sacrifice and the house of sacrifice and perfect the sacrificer's sacrifice well.

##### English translation
Milking the easily milked cow (of sacrifice) of her all-sustaining food, for the benefit of the pious institutor of the rite, O Agni, doer of good deeds, anointed with butter, illumining the three regions, presiding (over the hall of sacrifice). going round the sacrifice. you accomplish each holy rite.

> अस्या इदानीं दृश्यमानाया उषसो व्युष्टिषु विवासनेषु प्रभातेषु सत्वु
> हे अग्ने त्वामित्तामेव देवानां दूतं कृष्णानाः कुर्वाणा मानुषा मनुष्या
> अयजंत । यजंति । सर्वदेवात्मकं त्वामेव यजंतीत्यर्थः । तथा देवा अपि त्वां
> महयाय्याय पूजायै ॥ मह पूजायां । आस्मादौणादिको भाव आय्यप्रत्ययः॥
> आत्मनः पूजार्थं नावृधुः । वर्धयंति । किं कुर्वंतः । अध्वरे । ध्वरो हिंसानिमित्तः प्रत्यवायः । तद्रहिते याग आज्यं । उपलक्षणमेतत् । आज्योपलक्षतं सर्वं
> हविर्निमृजंतस्त्वयि निमार्जयंतः । प्रक्षिपंत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the dawnings (व्युष्टिषु (*vyuṣṭiṣu*): the lighting up, the break of day) of this dawn now seen, O Agni, men worship you alone, making you the messenger of the gods; that is, they worship you, who are of the nature of all the gods. Likewise the gods too magnify you for adoration (महयाय्याय (*mahayāyyāya*), root mah, to worship, with the Uṇādi affix āyya, in the sense of the noun of action) of themselves. How? In the ādhvara, the sacrifice free of injury (ध्वर (*dhvara*) being the harm or fault arising from injury), sprinkling ghee on you, which stands for all oblations marked by ghee, that is, casting it into you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अस्याः (*asyāḥ*)—of this now seen
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—dawn
- व्युष्टिषु (*vyuṣṭiṣu*)—at the time of its appearance
- त्वां इत् (*tvāṃ it*)—you alone
- दूतं (*dūtaṃ*)—as the messenger who carries the oblation to the gods
- कृष्णानाः (*kṛṣṇānāḥ*)—having made
- मानुषा (*mānuṣā*)—men
- आयजंत (*āyajaṃta*)—worship you alone (likewise)
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods also
- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—in the sacrifice
- आज्यं (*ājyaṃ*)—ghee, or the oblation together with ghee
- निम्मजंतः (*nimmajaṃtaḥ*)—offering (placing)
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- महय्याय (*mahayyāya*)—for the sake of worship
- नावृधुः (*nāvṛdhuḥ*)—praise with hymns and the like and make you grow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, at the appearance of the dawn that is seen just now, men who have made you the messenger who carries the oblation to the gods worship you alone. The gods too, offering ghee in the sacrifice, praise you with hymns for the sake of worship and make you grow.

##### English translation
Men worshipped you, Agni, at the opening of the present dawn, appointing you their messenger to the gods; the gods have magnified you for their adoration, sprinkling butter upon you at the sacrifice.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, at the विदथेषु (*vidatheṣu*)": a विदथ (*vidatha*) is a sacrifice, since in it one finds the gods who are to be worshipped. At these, the sons of Vasiṣṭha, the seers, who ordain the rites and sing praise, invoked you, who are वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*), that is, possessed of food and strength; न्यह्वंत (*nyahvaṃta*) means they called you down intensely, or they praised you. You, in us the sacrificers, establish रायः पोषं (*rāyaḥ poṣaṃ*), the nourishment, the increase, of wealth. The plural in "you protect" is for honour, although Agni is only one.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- विदथेषु (*vidatheṣu*)—at the sacrifices

- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—you, who possess food or strength
- नि अह्वंत (*ni ahvaṃta*)—call you down specially
- (त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you)
- यजमानेषु (*yajamāneṣu*)—among us who perform the sacrifice
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—of wealth
- पोषं (*poṣaṃ*)—the nourishment, that is, the increase
- धारय (*dhāraya*)—establish (O gods)
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the sons of Vasiṣṭha, who are engaged in rites and are praising you, specially entreat and praise you, who possess food. Establish abundance of wealth among the sacrificers, or bestow wealth and nourishment on the sacrificers. O gods, protect us always with blessings.

##### English translation
The pious Vasishthas invoked you, Agni, at the sacrificial meetings, praising you, the mighty one; continue the sustenance of riches amongst the institutors of the rite, and do you (gods) ever cherish us with blessings.

## Sūkta 123 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction.** The seer and the deity of this sūkta are said to be Vena. There are differing opinions about who this Vena is. Yāska says: वेनो वेनतेः कांतिकर्मणः (*veno venateḥ kāṃtikarmaṇaḥ*) (Ni. 10-38). The word Vena is formed from the root वेनति (*venati*), meaning "to wish, to desire". He has explained the sense that this deity is a deity of the middle region who illumines all the worlds, and since he benefits all, everyone desires him.

In Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-83-5 it is said:
यज्ञैरथर्वा प्रथमः पथस्तते ततः सूर्यो व्रतसा वेन आजनि । आ गा आजदुशना काव्यः सचा यमस्य जातममृतं यजामहे ॥ (*yajñairatharvā prathamaḥ pathastate tataḥ sūryo vratasā vena ājani | ā gā ājaduśanā kāvyaḥ sacā yamasya jātamamṛtaṃ yajāmahe ‖*)
For the word वेनः (*venaḥ*) in this Ṛk Sāyaṇa explains: वेनः कांतः सूर्यः सूर्यरूप इंद्र: (*venaḥ kāṃtaḥ sūryaḥ sūryarūpa iṃdra:*)—the shining sun, or Indra in the form of the sun. Moreover, this Ṛk also mentions the sage Bhṛgu, the father of the seer of this sūkta. Therefore the word Vena has the sense "lovely, shining, desired by all". Who is the deity endowed with this quality? Ordinarily one would have to say the Sun. In his bhāṣya on the present Ṛk Sāyaṇa explains: वेनः कांत एतत्संज्ञो मध्यमस्थानो देवः (*venaḥ kāṃta etatsaṃjño madhyamasthāno devaḥ*)—a shining deity of the middle (atmospheric) region named Vena. The qualities mentioned above, being shining and desired by all, apply also to many other deities, and chiefly to the Supreme Brahman,

### Printed p. 660
so one may say that Vena means Brahman. Since in the present sūkta this deity is praised as a deity of the middle region and as the cause of rain and the like, he may also be the deity Indra or Parjanya. In the Taittirīyopaniṣad of the Yajurveda:
वेनस्तत्पश्यन्विश्वा भुवनानि विद्वान्यत्र विश्वं भवत्येकनीळं । यस्मिन्निदग्ं सं च वि चैकग्ं स ओतः प्रोतश्च विभु प्रजासु ॥ प्र तद्वोचे अमृतं नु विद्वान्गंधर्वो नाम निहितं गुहासु । त्रीणि पदा निहिता गुहासु यस्तद्वेद सवितुः पिता सत् ॥ (*venastatpaśyanviśvā bhuvanāni vidvānyatra viśvaṃ bhavatyekanīḷaṃ | yasminnidagṃ saṃ ca vi caikagṃ sa otaḥ protaśca vibhu prajāsu ‖ pra tadvoce amṛtaṃ nu vidvāngaṃdharvo nāma nihitaṃ guhāsu | trīṇi padā nihitā guhāsu yastadveda savituḥ pitā sat ‖*) (Tai. U. 4-1)
For the word वेनः (*venaḥ*) in these mantras Sāyaṇa explains: वेनो नाम गंधर्वः (*veno nāma gaṃdharvaḥ*)—a Gandharva named Vena. But for the word गंधर्व (*gaṃdharva*) in the 4th Ṛk of this sūkta Sāyaṇa explains: गवामुदकानां धर्ता (*gavāmudakānāṃ dhartā*)—one who holds and cherishes the waters. And in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1 139-10; 8-3-18; 8-63-1 and the like, the word Vena is used only in the general sense of "desired by all" or "radiant". This is the only sūkta in the Ṛgveda that praises this deity; there is no other.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं वेन इत्यष्टर्चमेकादशं सूक्तं भार्गवस्य वेनस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं ।
> वेनो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । अयं वेनो वैन्यमिति ॥ प्रवर्ग्येऽभिप्तव
> आद्यानुवक्तव्या । सूत्रितं । स्रक्वे द्रप्सस्यायं वेनश्चोदयत्पृश्निगर्भाः । आ. ४-६ ।
> इति ॥ वैश्वदेवशस्त्रेऽप्येषा धाय्या! सूत्रितं च । तक्षन्रथमयं वेनश्चोदयत्पृश्निगर्भाः । आ- ५-१८ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta अयं वेन (*ayaṃ vena*) has eight Ṛks and is the eleventh sūkta. Its seer is Vena of the Bhṛgu line, its metre is Triṣṭubh, and its deity is Vena. So the Anukramaṇī: अयं वेनो वैन्यमिति (*ayaṃ veno vainyamiti*). In the Pravargya, at the Abhiplava, the first Ṛk is to be recited afterwards; it is stated in the sūtra: स्रक्वे द्रप्सस्यायं वेनश्चोदयत्पृश्निगर्भाः । आ. ४-६ । (*srakve drapsasyāyaṃ venaścodayatpṛśnigarbhāḥ | ā. 4-6 |*) This Ṛk is also the Dhāyyā in the Vaiśvadeva śastra, and it is stated: तक्षन्रथमयं वेनश्चोदयत्पृश्निगर्भाः । आ- ५-१८ । (*takṣanrathamayaṃ venaścodayatpṛśnigarbhāḥ | ā- 5-18 |*)

**Anuvāda.** This sūkta अयं वेनः (*ayaṃ venaḥ*) is the eleventh sūkta in the tenth anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. Its seer is Vena of the Bhṛgu gotra; its deity is the deity of the middle region called Vena; its metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated: अयं वेनो वैन्यं (*ayaṃ veno vainyaṃ*). That the first Ṛk of this sūkta is to be recited in the Pravargya is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra स्रक्वे द्रप्पस्यायं वेनश्चोदयत्पृश्निगर्भाः (*srakve drappasyāyaṃ venaścodayatpṛśnigarbhāḥ*) (Ā. 4-6). That the first Ṛk of this sūkta is to be recited as a Dhāyyā mantra among the mantras of the Vaiśvadeva śastra is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra तक्षन्रथमयं वेनश्चोदयत्पृश्निगर्भाः (*takṣanrathamayaṃ venaścodayatpṛśnigarbhāḥ*) (Ā. 5-18).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं वे॒नश्चो॑दय॒त्पृश्नि॑गर्भा॒ ज्योति॑र्जरायू॒ रज॑सो  ॒॑
> विमाने ।  
> इ॒मम॒पां सं॑ग॒मे सूर्य॑स्य॒ शिशुं॒ न विप्रा॑ म॒तिभी॑ रिहंति ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । वेनः । चोदयत् । पृश्निगर्भाः । ज्योतिर्जरायुः । रजसः । विमाने ॥  
> इमं । अपां । सॆरगमे । सूर्यस्य । शिशुं । न । विप्राः । मतिभीः । रिहंति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वेनः कांत एतत्संज्ञो मध्यस्थानो देवो ज्योतिर्जरायुः । ज्योतिर्द्योतमानो मेघो जरायुः । उदरे गर्भो येन वेष्टितोऽवतिष्ठते तज्जरायु । तदिव वेष्टको यस्य स तथोक्तः । मेघमध्यॆ गर्भवदवस्थित इत्यर्थः ।
> विमाने । विमायंते निर्मियंतेऽस्मिन्नाप इति विमानमंतरिक्षं । रजस उदकस्य
> निर्मातर्यंतरिक्षे स्थितः सन्नयं वेनः पृश्निगर्भाः । पृश्निरादित्यः तस्य गर्भभूताः ।
> यद्वा पृश्नयः सप्तोज्वलवर्णाः सूर्यरश्मयः । तेषां गर्भभूताः अंतरिक्षस्था
> अपश्चोदयत् । पृथिवीं प्रति प्रेरयति । अपामुदकानामांतरिक्षाणां सूर्यस्य च
> संगमे संगमने०तरिक्षे स्थितमिमं वेनं विप्रा मेधाविनः स्तोतारो मतिभिः
> स्तुतिभी रिहंति । रिहतिरर्चतिकर्मा । अर्चंति । पूजयंति ! स्तुवंतीत्यर्थः । शिशुं न ।
> यथा बालं पुत्रं मातापित्राद्या बांधवाः स्तुतिपदैरुपलालयंति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वेनः (*venaḥ*) is the lovely deity of that name, of the middle region. He is ज्योतिर्जरायुः (*jyotirjarāyuḥ*): ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*) is the shining cloud; जरायु (*jarāyu*) is that by which the embryo in the womb is enveloped and stays; one who has such an envelope is so called, that is, he stays in the midst of the cloud like an embryo. विमाने (*vimāne*): विमान (*vimāna*) is the atmosphere, since in it the waters are measured out, created. Standing in the atmosphere, the maker of रजसः (*rajasaḥ*) (water), this Vena is पृश्निगर्भाः (*pṛśnigarbhāḥ*): पृश्नि (*pṛśni*) is Āditya, and those that are his embryos. Or else पृश्नयः (*pṛśnayaḥ*) are the seven brightly coloured rays of the sun, and the waters in the atmosphere that are their embryos he चोदयत् (*codayat*) impels, sends towards the earth. At the संगमे (*saṃgame*), the meeting, of the waters of the atmosphere and the sun, in the atmosphere, the विप्राः (*viprāḥ*), the wise praisers, रिहंति (*rihaṃti*) this Vena with मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*), praises; रिहति (*rihati*) is a verb of worship: they worship, they praise. शिशुं न (*śiśuṃ na*): as a mother, father and other kinsmen fondle a little child with words of praise, so.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ज्योतिर्जरायुः (*jyotirjarāyuḥ*)—hidden like an embryo in the midst of shining clouds
- अयं वेनः (*ayaṃ venaḥ*)—this deity named Vena
- रजसः विमाने (*rajasaḥ vimāne*)—
### Printed p. 662
being in the atmosphere, the place where waters are created
- पृश्निगर्भाः (*pṛśnigarbhāḥ*)—the waters of the atmosphere, that are embryos of the sun's rays
- चोदयत् (*codayat*)—impels to fall on the earth in the form of rain
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—of the waters, and
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of the sun
- संगमे (*saṃgame*)—in the atmosphere, the meeting place (where he is)
- इमं (*imaṃ*)—this deity Vena
- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—wise praisers
- शिशुं न (*śiśuṃ na*)—as parents fondle a small child
- मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*)—with praises
- रिहंति (*rihaṃti*)—worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This deity named Vena, hidden shining in the midst of the cloud, stays in the atmosphere and impels the waters there (those that are embryos of the sun's rays, that is, in the midst of the cloud) to fall on the earth in the form of rain. The wise praisers worship this deity, who is in the atmosphere between the waters and the sun, with their praises, as parents tenderly fondle their child.

##### English translation
This Vena, enfolded in the membrance of light, urges on (the waters) the germs of the sun in the firmament of the water; the sages cherish him at the confluence of the waters, and the sun with endearments like a child.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

ज्योतिर्जरायुः (*jyotirjarāyuḥ*)—The shining cloud is the जरायु (*jarāyu*), that is, उदरे गर्भो येन वेष्टितोऽवतिष्ठते तज्ञरायु (*udare garbho yena veṣṭito 'vatiṣṭhate tajñarāyu*). That which holds in its belly some object like an embryo, that is, as something inside, is called जरायु (*jarāyu*). Here, because the cloud holds water in its midst (in its belly) as in a womb, this cloud is called जरायु (*jarāyu*). In the present context, for the word ज्योतिर्जरायुः (*jyotirjarāyuḥ*) the meaning is: as the water lies as an embryo in the midst of the cloud, so this shining deity Vena is in the midst of the cloud.

विमाने (*vimāne*)—विमायंते निर्मायंते अस्मिन्नाप इति विमानमंतरिक्षं (*vimāyaṃte nirmāyaṃte asminnāpa iti vimānamaṃtarikṣaṃ*). With the help of the sun's rays, the water of the sea and other reservoirs is drawn up in the form of vapour, and there, in the atmosphere, that vapour is transformed (created) into clouds filled with water; hence the atmosphere is called विमान (*vimāna*).

पृश्निगर्भाः (*pṛśnigarbhāḥ*)—पृश्निरादित्यः तस्य गर्भभूताः (*pṛśnirādityaḥ tasya garbhabhūtāḥ*). पृश्नि (*pṛśni*) means Āditya (?). It is said that the waters that are his embryos, that is, produced by his action, are the embryos of Pṛśni or Āditya. Or else, *pṛśnayaḥ saptojjvalavarṇāḥ sūryaraśmayaḥ teṣāṃ garbhabhūta

### Printed p. 663
aṃtarikṣasthā apaḥ*. The sun's rays of various kinds, that is, of seven kinds, are spread in the atmosphere. The waters that are in the midst of them in the form of cloud are called पृश्निगर्भाः (*pṛśnigarbhāḥ*).

शिशुं न विप्रा मतिभिः रिहंति (*śiśuṃ na viprā matibhiḥ rihaṃti*)—Two kinds of meaning can be given for the word रिहंति (*rihaṃti*). Since the use of the letter r in place of l is a special feature of the Ṛgveda (as the word अरंकृतः (*araṃkṛtaḥ*) stands for आलंकृतः (*ālaṃkṛtaḥ*)), रिहंति (*rihaṃti*) here means लिहंति (*lihaṃti*). According to the sense of the root लिह—आस्वादने (*liha—āsvādane*), लिहंति (*lihaṃti*) means "they lick, they caress". As mothers and fathers or kinsmen fondle and cherish their child with love and trust, so the wise praisers worship this Vena with the utmost regard. Or, according to the Nirukta statement रिहतिरर्चतिकर्मा (*rihatirarcatikarmā*), the meaning "they worship" can be given.

Yāska has given the Nirukta on this Ṛk:
अयं वेनश्चोदयत्पृश्निगर्भा प्राष्टवर्णगर्भा आप इति वा ज्योतिर्वरायुर्ज्योतिरस्य जरायुस्थानीयं भवति । जरायुर्जरया गर्भस्य जरया यूयत इति वेममपां च संगमने सूर्यस्य च शिशुमिव विप्रा मतिभी रिहंति लिहंति स्तुवंति वर्धयंति पूजयंतीति वा ॥ शिशुः शंसनीयो भवति। शिशीतेर्वा स्याद्दानकर्मणः । चिरलब्धो गर्भो भवति ॥ (*ayaṃ venaścodayatpṛśnigarbhā prāṣṭavarṇagarbhā āpa iti vā jyotirvarāyurjyotirasya jarāyusthānīyaṃ bhavati | jarāyurjarayā garbhasya jarayā yūyata iti vemamapāṃ ca saṃgamane sūryasya ca śiśumiva viprā matibhī rihaṃti lihaṃti stuvaṃti vardhayaṃti pūjayaṃtīti vā ‖ śiśuḥ śaṃsanīyo bhavati| śiśītervā syāddānakarmaṇaḥ | ciralabdho garbho bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 10—39)

अयं वेनश्चोदयत् पृश्निगर्भाः प्रास्टवर्णगर्भा आप इति वा (*ayaṃ venaścodayat pṛśnigarbhāḥ prāsṭavarṇagarbhā āpa iti vā*)—पृश्नि (*pṛśni*) means Āditya. The meaning of the word पृश्निगर्भाः (*pṛśnigarbhāḥ*) is: waters drawn up (आष्टः (*āṣṭaḥ*), obtained) by the excellent colour or rays of this sun. रश्म्यंतर्गताः परिपक्वाः आपो मासाष्टकेन संभृताः ताः वेनश्चोदयति प्रावृषि वर्षभावेन प्रेरयति (*raśmyaṃtargatāḥ paripakvāḥ āpo māsāṣṭakena saṃbhṛtāḥ tāḥ venaścodayati prāvṛṣi varṣabhāvena prerayati*)—The waters of reservoirs and the like, drawn up by the sun's rays, are carried to the atmosphere in the form of vapour; there, for eight months, they ripen, that is, are transformed into the form of cloud; and Vena impels those waters in the rainy season to fall on the earth as rain. This is the purport of the sentence.

ज्योतिर्जरायुज्योतिरस्य जरायुस्थानीयं भवति । जरायुर्जरया गर्भस्य जरया यूयते इति वा (*jyotirjarāyujyotirasya jarāyusthānīyaṃ bhavati | jarāyurjarayā garbhasya jarayā yūyate iti vā*)—ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*) means the light called lightning (the flash). Vena is one who holds such light in the form of an embryo. What is a जरायु (*jarāyu*) here? जरया गर्भस्य (*jarayā garbhasya*)—that which, while the embryo is at first small, grows gradually, they call जरायु (*jarāyu*). Or else: प्रसूताया गोः स्त्रिया ना पश्चात् पतति सा जरॆत्युच्यते । तया च यायते मिश्रते तज्जराय्वित्युच्यते (*prasūtāyā goḥ striyā nā paścāt patati sā jarètyucyate | tayā ca yāyate miśrate tajjarāyvityucyate*)—what falls afterwards from the belly of a cow or a woman at the time of delivery is called जरा (*jarā*), that is, the afterbirth. The thing (the creature) that is joined with that afterbirth **NOTE**

### Printed p. 664
the name jarāyu; the creature that is joined with the womb is called jarāyu. In the present Ṛk the light itself (the lightning) is in the form of the cloud's embryo. That is, Vena, who is luminous in nature and has the form of lightning, is in the form of the embryo of the clouds. This is the meaning.

इममपां च संगमने सूर्यस्य शिशुमिव विप्रा मतिभी रिहंति लिहंति स्तुवंति वर्धयंति पूजयंतीति (*imamapāṃ ca saṃgamane sūryasya śiśumiva viprā matibhī rihaṃti lihaṃti stuvaṃti vardhayaṃti pūjayaṃtīti*) (Ni.)—here "at the meeting-place of the waters and of the sun" means: at the place where the waters in the form of vapour and the sun meet, that is, in the region where these two (water and sun) come together, that is, in the atmosphere. "Like a child they caress (rihanti)" means: just as people fondle, cherish and praise a small child with good words. The intended sense is this: the wise people praise, extol, make grow, or worship, with their words of praise, this god Vena, who dwells as light in the midst of the cloud in the atmosphere, the meeting-place of the sun and the waters, as people caress, cherish and praise children.

शिशुः शंसनीयो भवति । शिशीतेर्वा स्याद्दानकर्मणः । चिरलब्धो गर्भो भवति (*śiśuḥ śaṃsanīyo bhavati | śiśītervā syāddānakarmaṇaḥ | ciralabdho garbho bhavati*)—a child is called śiśu because it is praised with good words or soothed. Or else the root śiś has the sense "give"; दीयते हि स पुरुषेण स्त्रियै धारणाय (*dīyate hi sa puruṣeṇa striyai dhāraṇāya*)—since the child is given by the man to the woman to bear in her womb, it is called śiśu. The Nirukta's meaning is that the embryo, long retained in the womb, comes out.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒मु॒द्रादू॒र्मिमुदि॑यर्ति वे॒नो न॑भो॒जाः पृ॒ष्ठं ह॑र्य॒तस्य॑ दर्शि ।  
> ऋ॒तस्य॒ साना॒वधि॑ वि॒ष्टपि॒ भ्राट् स॑मा॒नं योनि॑म॒भ्य॑नूषत॒ व्राः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> समुद्रात् । ऊर्मिं । उत् । इयर्ति । वेनः । नभःजाः । पृष्ठं । हर्यतस्य । दर्शि ।  
> ऋतस्य । सान् । अधि । विष्टपि । भ्राट् । समानं । योनिं । अभि । अनूषत । व्राः ॥२॥

### Printed p. 665

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तस्मिन्नेवाभीष्टवे समुद्रादूर्मिमित्येषा । सूत्र्यते हि । समुद्रादूर्मिमुदियर्ति वेनो द्रप्सः समद्रमभि यज्जिगाति । आ. ४-७ । इति ॥
> समुद्रवंत्यस्मादाप इति समुद्रमंतरिक्षं । तस्मादूर्मिं जलसमूहमयं
> वेन उदियर्ति । उद्गमयति । अधः पातयतीत्यर्थः । कीदृशः । नभोजाः । नभस्याकाशे............ । इमं वेनमभि शब्दायंते ॥ नु स्तुत् । कुटादिः । छांदसो लज् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In that same Abhiṣṭava (the Pravargya hymn of praise), this Ṛk "Samudrād ūrmim" is used. The sūtra says: समुद्रादूर्मिमुदियर्ति वेनो द्रप्सः समद्रमभि यज्जिगाति । (*samudrādūrmimudiyarti veno drapsaḥ samadramabhi yajjigāti |*) (Ā. 4-7). **NOTE**
Sāyaṇa explains: from this the waters flow, therefore samudra is the atmosphere (antarikṣa). From it Vena sends up (udiyarti) the wave, the mass of water; that is, he makes it come out and fall down. What kind of being is he? Nabhojāḥ, "born in the sky (nabhas)…" The text then breaks off in dots. Of what follows only fragments stand: "they sound towards this Vena", and "nu, praise", "कुटादिः (*kuṭādiḥ*)", "Vedic laj". **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नभोजाः (*nabhojāḥ*)—born in the middle of the sky (in the clouds)
- वेनः (*venaḥ*)—this god Vena
- समुद्रात् (*samudrāt*)—from the atmosphere
- ऊर्मिं (*ūrmiṃ*)—the mass of water
- उत् इयर्ति (*ut iyarti*)—impels it to fall on the earth in the form of rain; (afterwards)
- हर्यतस्य (*haryatasya*)—of heaven
- पृष्ठं (*pṛṣṭhaṃ*)—the lower part
- दर्शि (*darśi*)—is seen
- विष्टपि (*viṣṭapi*)—in heaven (that is, in the atmosphere)
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of water
- सानौ अधि (*sānau adhi*)—on the upper part
- भ्राट् (*bhrāṭ*)—this Vena shines
- समानं योनिं (*samānaṃ yoniṃ*)—in the atmosphere, their common place
- व्राः (*vrāḥ*)—the Marut troops (or the clouds)
- अभि अनूषत (*abhi anūṣata*)—praise this Vena, sounding loudly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This god Vena, born in the middle of the sky, in the cloud-region, impels water from the atmosphere to fall on the earth as rain. After the rain has fallen, the lower part of the sky, that is, the sky, is seen clear (without clouds). On the high region of the atmosphere, above the water (the cloud), this god shines. In the atmosphere, which is the common place of Vena and of the Maruts or clouds, the Marut troops or clouds praise this Vena with their sound.

##### English translation
The cloud-born Vena sends the water from the firmament ; the back of the azure (sky) is beheld. He shone on the summit of the water in heaven the troops praised their common abode.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Pravargya-abhiṣṭava mentioned above, this Ṛk "Samudrād ūrmim" is to be recited; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra समुद्रादूर्मिमुदियर्ति वेनो द्रप्सः समुद्रमभि यज्जिगाति (*samudrādūrmimudiyarti veno drapsaḥ samudramabhi yajjigāti*) (Ā. 4-7).
A loss of text is seen in the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of this Ṛk.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒मा॒नं पू॒र्वीर॒भि वा॑वशा॒नास्तिष्ठ॑न्व॒त्सस्य॑ मा॒तरः॒ सनी॑ळाः ।  
> ऋ॒तस्य॒ साना॒वधि॑ चक्रमा॒णा रि॒हंति॒ मध्वो॑ अ॒मृत॑स्य॒ वाणीः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> समानं । पूर्विः । अभि । वावशानाः । तिष्ठन् । वत्सस्य । मातरः । सनीळाः ।  
> ऋतस्य । सान् । अधि । चक्रमाणाः । रिहंति । मध्वः । अमृतस्य । वाणीः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूर्वीर्बह्वः समानं वेनस्यात्मनश्च साधारणं स्थानं प्राप्याभि वावशाना
> अभितः शब्दायमानाः । यद्वा । तमेव वेनमभिकामयमानाः । वत्सस्य वत्सस्थानीयस्य वैद्युताग्नेर्मातरो मातृभूताः सनीळाः समाननिलयाः एवंविधा आंतरिक्ष्या
> आपस्तिष्ठन् । तिष्ठंति । अपि चर्तस्योदकस्य सानावधि सान् गमुच्छ्रितेऽंतरिक्षस्थाने
> चक्रमाणाः प्रवर्तमाना मध्वो मधुरस्यामृतस्योदकस्य वाणीर्वाण्यः शब्दा
> रिहंति । इमं वेनमर्चंति । अलंकुर्वंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The many (pūrvīḥ) waters, having reached the common place shared by Vena and themselves, "clamour all round" (vāvaśānāḥ), sounding on every side; or else, desiring that very Vena. They are the mothers of the "calf", the calf here standing for the lightning fire (vaidyutāgni); being mothers and sharing one abode (sanīḷāḥ), these aerial waters stay (tiṣṭhan). Moreover, moving on the elevated part (sāna) of the water (ṛta), in the lofty atmosphere, the sounds of the sweet, ambrosial water "lick" (rihanti) this Vena, that is, they worship or adorn him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूर्विः (*pūrviḥ*)—many
- समानं (*samānaṃ*)—being in the atmosphere, the common place of themselves and of Vena
- अभि (*abhi*)—all around
- वावशानाः (*vāvaśānāḥ*)—sounding, or desiring Vena
- वत्सस्य (*vatsasya*)—of the lightning fire that stands in the place of the calf (child)
- मातरः (*mātaraḥ*)—being its mothers
- सनीळाः (*sanīḷāḥ*)—and dwelling in the atmosphere, the common place; the waters (of the cloud)
- तिष्ठन् (*tiṣṭhan*)—remain (there); (and)
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the water (of the cloud)
- सान् (*sān*)—on the upper part, that is, in the lofty atmosphere
- चक्रमाणाः (*cakramāṇāḥ*)—moving
- मध्वः उदकस्य (*madhvaḥ udakasya*)—of the sweet water
- वाणीः (*vāṇīḥ*)—the sounds
- रिहंति (*rihaṃti*)—praise this god Vena

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The waters, that is, the clouds, which are of great extent, which stay in the atmosphere, the common place, and sound all round (thunder and rumble), and which are mothers of the child-like lightning fire, remain in the atmosphere, the common dwelling of themselves and Vena. And the roarings of the clouds, with their sweet waters, moving on the upper part of the lofty atmosphere, also praise this Vena (they seem to praise him).

### Printed p. 667

##### English translation
The many waters occupy a common station, clamouring arround like the assembled mothers of the calf ; wandering above the summit of the water they utter the praises of the sweet-flavoured ambrosia.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> जा॒नंतो॑ रू॒पम॑कृपंत॒ विप्रा॑ मृ॒गस्य॒ घोषं॑ महि॒षस्य॒ हि  
> ग्मन् ।  
> ऋ॒तेन॒ यंतो॒ अधि॒ सिंधु॑मस्थुर्वि॒दद्गं॑ध॒र्वो अ॒मृता॑नि॒  ॑
> नाम ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> जानंतः । रूपं । अकृपंत । विप्राः । मृगस्य । घोषं । महिषस्य । हि । ग्मन् ।  
> ऋतेन । यंतः । अधि । सिंधुं । अस्थुः । विदत् । गंधर्वः । अमृतानि । नाम ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विप्रा मेधाविनः स्तोतारोऽस्य वेनस्य रूपं जानंतीत्यर्थः । स्तुवंति ।
> कृपतिः स्तुतिकर्मा । कथमस्य रूपं जानंतीत्यत आह । मृगस्यान्वेषणीयस्य महिषस्य । महन्नामैतत् । महतो वेनस्य घोषं गर्जितलक्षणं मेघस्थं शब्दं हि
> यस्माद्मन् अभिगच्छंति आतस्तदीयं रूपं जानंतीत्यर्थः ॥ गमेश्वांदसे लज्
> बहुलं छंदसीति शपो लुक् । गमहनेत्युपधालोपः । बहुलं छंदस्यमाज्योगेऽपीत्यडभावः ॥ अपि चर्तेन सत्यभूतेन स्तोत्रेण यज्ञेन वा यंतस्तं वेनं
> गच्छंतः प्राप्नुवंतो जनाः सिंधुं स्यंदनशीलं जलसमूहमध्यस्तुः । अधितिष्ठंति ।
> तेषां सॆ वेनो वृष्टिं करोतीत्यर्थः । तत्र किं कारणमिति चेत् यतोऽयं
> गंधर्वो गवामुदकानां धर्ता वेनोऽमृतान्यमरणहेतुभूतानि नाम । उदकनामैतत् । नमनशीलान्युदकानि विदत् वेद जानाति । तस्य वशे वर्तंत इत्यर्थः ।
> आतस्तद्भक्तानां वृष्टिः सुलभा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The viprāḥ, the wise praisers, know the form of this Vena; kṛpati has the sense of praising. How do they know his form? Sāyaṇa says: of the mṛga, "the one to be sought", the mahiṣa (महन्नामैतत् (*mahannāmaitat*), mahat being a name), the great Vena, they approach (gman) the ghoṣa, the sound located in the cloud, marked by thundering; therefore they know his form. Further, men who approach that Vena with ṛta, true praise or the sacrifice, reach the sindhu, the flowing mass of water, and take their stand upon it (adhi asthuḥ); that is, Vena makes rain for them. If it is asked why, the reason is that this Vena is the gandharva, the bearer of the waters (gavām); he knows (vidat) the amṛtāni nāma, "waters" (a name of water), which are deathless, the cause of not dying, being of bending nature. That is, they are under his control; therefore rain is easy for his devotees.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—the wise praisers
- मृगस्य (*mṛgasya*)—who is sought
- महिषस्य (*mahiṣasya*)—of this Vena, who is of great form
- घोषं (*ghoṣaṃ*)—the sound in the form of thunder
- हि (*hi*)—for which reason

### Printed p. 668
- ग्मन् (*gman*)—approaching (hearing) they know, for that very reason
- रूपं (*rūpaṃ*)—the form of this god Vena
- जानंतः (*jānaṃtaḥ*)—knowing
- अकृपंत (*akṛpaṃta*)—they praise him
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—by true praise or by the sacrifice
- यंतः (*yaṃtaḥ*)—the people who approach this Vena
- सिंधुं (*siṃdhuṃ*)—the mass of water of flowing nature
- अधि अस्तुः (*adhi astuḥ*)—obtain in the form of rain (because)
- गंधर्वः (*gaṃdharvaḥ*)—this Vena, who bears the waters
- अमृतानि (*amṛtāni*)—deathless, that is, ambrosia-like
- नाम (*nāma*)—water
- विदत् (*vidat*)—knows (that is, the water indispensable for nourishing the body, so that it does not fall to death, is in this Vena's control)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

These wise praisers, learning from the roar (thunder) that he makes where he is, the form of this Vena of great nature whom they are seeking, praise him. The people who worship him with praises and the like, or with sacrifice, obtain flowing water in the form of rain; that is, by his grace the water of the Pṛṣṭhya is obtained, and the water indispensable for nourishing the body, so that it does not fall to death, is in this Vena's control. This Vena bestows it in the form of rain on the people who praise him.

##### English translation
The pious, knowing his form, praised him, for they followed the cry of the great deer; approaching him with sacrifice, they reached the flowing (water) for the sustainer of the waters knows the amb osial (fluids).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अप्परा अपां सारयित्र्यप्पु क्रीडार्थं सरंती वोपसिष्मियाणा कांतसमीपमुपगत्येषद्ध संती ॥ स्मिज् ईषद्धसने । छांदसो लिट् । तस्य लिटः कानज्वेति कानच्॥
> ईदृशी योषा स्त्री विद्युद्रूपा जारमपां जारयितारं । यद्वा! जार उपपतिः । स
> इव प्रियं । इमं वेनं परम उत्कृष्टे व्योमन् व्योमन्यंतरिक्षे बिभर्ति ।
> पोषयति । धारयति वा । यथा काचिद्रूपवती योषिज्जारमुपगम्येषद्ध संती तं
> निर्जने स्थले पुष्णाति तद्वदनेन वेनेन विद्युद्रमत इत्यर्थः । प्रियस्यास्य वेनस्य
> योनिषु स्थानेषु चरत् । विद्युद्रूपा योषिच्चरति गच्छति । अभिसारिकावृत्ता स्वयमेव गच्छति । स च वेनः प्रियोऽस्या अनुकूलतमः सन् हिरण्यये हिरण्मये
> हिरण्मयवद्भास्वरे हितरमणीयरूपे ना पक्ष आत्मनः पक्षभूते मेघे सीदत् ।
> सीदति । तया सहोपविशति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Apsarā is she who moves in the waters (apām), either to sport in the waters or as one who, approaching her beloved, smiles slightly (upasiṣmiyāṇā). Such a woman (yoṣā), in the form of lightning, holds the jāra of the waters, the one who makes them old (jārayitṛ). Or else, jāra is the paramour (upapati); as such a dear one she bears this Vena in the highest vyoman, the atmosphere; she nourishes or supports him. Just as some beautiful woman, approaching her lover and smiling slightly, nourishes him in a lonely place, so the lightning sports with this Vena. In the places (yoniṣu) of this dear Vena the lightning-woman moves (carat), going of herself like an abhisārikā. And Vena, dear to her and most favourable, sits (sīdat) in his golden wing (pakṣa), radiant like gold and of lovely form, that is, in the cloud which is as a wing to him; he sits down with her.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- योषा (*yoṣā*)—a young woman
- उपसिष्मियाणा (*upasiṣmiyāṇā*)—smiling gently with a faint smile
- जारं (*jāraṃ*)—as one approaches her paramour or beloved
- अप्सराः (*apsarāḥ*)—moving in the mass of water in the atmosphere
- योषा (*yoṣā*)—the woman in the form of lightning
- जारं (*jāraṃ*)—this Vena, who is dear to her
- परमे व्योमन् (*parame vyoman*)—in the upper part of the atmosphere
- बिभर्ति (*bibharti*)—nourishes
- प्रियस्य (*priyasya*)—of this beloved Vena
- योनिषु (*yoniṣu*)—in his own place, the atmosphere
- चरत् (*carat*)—this woman in the form of lightning moves
- सः वेनः (*saḥ venaḥ*)—that Vena
- प्रियः (*priyaḥ*)—being dear to this lightning-woman
- हिरण्यये (*hiraṇyaye*)—shining like gold, or lovely
- पक्षे (*pakṣe*)—in the cloud that is a wing to him, that is, that is around him
- सीदत् (*sīdat*)—sits

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a smiling woman approaches her beloved and sports with him, the woman called vidyut (lightning), moving among the clouds in the atmosphere, sports with her beloved Vena in the atmosphere; and this lightning-woman moves in the atmosphere, the own place of this beloved Vena (that is, lightning moves in the clouds). This Vena too, being dear to this lightning-woman, sits with her on the cloud-region, which shines like gold or is lovely, and roams about.

##### English translation
The Apsaras, smiling affectionately like a wife at her lover, cherishes him in the highest heaven : she wanders in the abodes of her beloved ; he, Vena, being loved, sits down on his golden wing.

### Printed p. 670

*(Special Topics, continued from Ṛk 5)*

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk, in describing that the god named Vena dwells in the midst of clouds accompanied by lightning, the description is compared to a young woman approaching her beloved with a gentle smile. Just as a young woman approaches the man dear to her with a gentle smile and sports with him, so the woman called Vidyut (lightning), who appears from time to time in the midst of the cloud-mass, joins this Vena in the upper part of the atmosphere and cherishes him. Here the young woman's smiling is compared with the shining lightning. Further, अप्सराः (*apsarāḥ*) means a beautiful woman who shines with beauty and charm like an Apsaras. From the standpoint of Vena, अप्सराः (*apsarāḥ*) means आपांसारयित्र्यप्पु क्रीडार्थं सरंतीति वा (*āpāṃsārayitryappu krīḍārthaṃ saraṃtīti vā*), that is, she who is the essence of water, or she who moves about in the water for sport. The lightning (vidyut) that appears from time to time in the midst of the water-laden cloud-masses is here designated by the words अप्सराः (*apsarāḥ*) and योषा (*yoṣā*). And just as a young woman and her beloved meet in a secluded, private place, so Vena and his beloved Vidyut are described as meeting in the upper part of the atmosphere (परमे व्योमन् (*parame vyoman*)). Moreover, just as a young woman moves about in the region where her beloved is and sits near him and sports, so this woman Vidyut, ranging from time to time through the atmosphere, sits with Vena in the shining cloud-mass (that is, remains hidden in the cloud-mass) and sports; this is the sense of the simile stated here.

In sum: Vena dwells in the cloud in the atmosphere. In that very cloud the vidyut, the lightning, appears from time to time. The seer has described just this by comparing it with a smiling young woman approaching her beloved and sporting with him. This simile is very apt both in the likeness of the things and in the presentation of the subject.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हिर॑ण्यपक्षं॒ वरु॑णस्य दू॒तं य॒मस्य॒ योन्॑शकु॒नं भु॑र॒ण्युं॥
