> हिरण्यपक्षं । वरुणस्य । दूतं । यमस्य । योन्शकुनं । भुरण्युं ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 671

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अभिष्टवे नाके सुपर्णमित्येषा । सूत्रितं च । नाके सुपर्णमुप यत्पतंतमिति समाप्य प्रणवेनोपविशेत् । आ. ४-७ । इति ॥
> हे वेन त्वा त्वां हृदा हृदयेन मनसा वेनंतः कामयमानाः स्तोतारो
> नाके०तरिक्षे यद्यदाभ्यचक्षत अभिपश्यंति तदानीं त्वमुप आगच्छसीति शेषः । कथंभूतं । सुपर्णं शोभनपतनं पतंतमंतरिक्षे गच्छंतं हिरण्यपक्षं हिरण्मयाभ्यां
> पक्षाभ्यामुपेतं वरुणस्य जलाभिमानिनो देवस्य दूतं चारं यमस्य नियामकस्य
> वैद्युताग्नेर्योन् स्थाने०तरिक्षे शकुनं पक्षिरूपेण वर्तमानं भुरण्यं भर्तारं ।
> यद्वा। वृष्टिप्रदानादिना सर्वस्य जगतः पोषकं ॥ भुरण धारणपोषणयोः ।
> कंड्वादिः । अस्मादौणादिक उप्रत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk नाके सुपर्णं (*nāke suparṇaṃ*) is used in the Abhiṣṭava. The sūtra says: नाके सुपर्णमुप यत्पतंतमिति समाप्य प्रणवेनोपविशेत् (*nāke suparṇamupa yatpataṃtamiti samāpya praṇavenopaviśet*) (Ā. 4-7). "O Vena, when the praisers, desiring you (वेनंतः (*venaṃtaḥ*) = कामयमानाः (*kāmayamānāḥ*)) with the heart, i.e. with the mind, behold you in the नाके (*nāke*), the atmosphere, then you come near" — "you come" is to be supplied. What kind of one? सुपर्णं (*suparṇaṃ*): one of fine flight, moving through the atmosphere; हिरण्यपक्षं (*hiraṇyapakṣaṃ*): endowed with two golden wings; दूतं (*dūtaṃ*): the messenger, the agent, of Varuṇa, the god presiding over water; शकुनं (*śakunaṃ*): existing in the form of a bird in the योन् (*yon*), the place, the atmosphere, of Yama, the regulator, i.e. the lightning-fire; भुरण्युं (*bhuraṇyuṃ*): the bearer; or else, the nourisher of the whole world by granting rain and so on.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुपर्णं (*suparṇaṃ*)—one who rains well **NOTE**
- पतंतं (*pataṃtaṃ*)—one who moves in the atmosphere
- हिरण्यपक्षं (*hiraṇyapakṣaṃ*)—one endowed with golden wings
- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—of Varuṇa, the god presiding over water
- दूतं (*dūtaṃ*)—the messenger
- यमस्य (*yamasya*)—of the lightning-fire, the regulator of rain
- योन् (*yon*)—in the place, the atmosphere
- शकुनं (*śakunaṃ*)—one who is like a bird
- भुरण्युं (*bhuraṇyuṃ*)—one who proclaims the whole world by granting rain and so on **NOTE**
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- हृदा (*hṛdā*)—with the mind
- वेनंतः (*venaṃtaḥ*)—the desiring praisers
- नाके (*nāke*)—in the atmosphere
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अभि अचक्षत (*abhi acakṣata*)—behold
- उप (*upa*) (आगच्छसि (*āgacchasi*))—you come near

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Vena, when the praisers who wish with all their heart for your coming behold you in the atmosphere—you who bestow rain, move through the atmosphere, are endowed with golden wings, are the messenger of Varuṇa the god presiding over water, are like a bird in the atmosphere, the place of the lightning-fire that regulates rain, and nourish the whole world by granting rain and so on—then you come near them. That is, you approach them in the form of rain-water (you pour down rain).

##### English translation
Those desiring you in their hearts contemplated you travelling as a strong-winged bird in the sky, the golden-winged messenger of Varuna, the bird which nourishes (the world) in Yama's dwelling.

### Printed p. 672

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That the Ṛk नाके सुपर्णं (*nāke suparṇaṃ*) is to be recited in the Abhiṣṭava is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra: नाके सुपर्णमुपयत्पतंतमिति समास्य प्रणवेनोसविशेत् (*nāke suparṇamupayatpataṃtamiti samāsya praṇavenosaviśet*) (Ā. 4-7). **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऊ॒र्ध्वो गं॑ध॒र्वो अधि॒ नाके॑ अस्थात्प्र॒त्यज् चि॒त्रा बिभ्र॑द॒स्यायु॑धानि ।  
> वसा॑नो॒ अत्कं॑ सुर॒भिं दृ॒शे कं स्व१॒॑ १ र्ण नाम॑ जनत प्रि॒याणि॑॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऊर्ध्वः । गंधर्वः । अधि । नाके । अस्थात् । प्रत्यज् । चित्रा । बिभ्रत् । अस्य । आयुधानि।  
> वसानः । अत्कं । सुरभिं । दृशे । कं । स्वः । न । नाम । जनत । प्रियाणि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऊर्ध्व उपरिदेशे वर्तमानो गंधर्वो गवामुदकानां धर्ता । गवि गन्
> धृइतो व इति गोशब्दोपपदाद्दृञ् धारण इत्यस्माद्वप्रत्यय उपपदस्य गन्भावश्च ॥
> ईदृशो वेनः प्रत्यङ्जस्मत्प्रत्यंचनोऽभिमुखः सन्नाकेऽध्यंतरिक्षेऽस्थात् । तिष्ठति । किं
> कुर्वन्। अस्यात्मनः स्वभूतानि चित्रा चित्राणि चायनीयान्याश्चर्यभूतानि वायुधानि
> बिभ्रद्दारयन् ॥ बिभर्तेः शतरि भृञामिदित्यभ्यासस्यॆत्वं । नाभ्यस्ताच्छतुरिति नुम्मतिषेधः । अभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ तथा सुरभिं शोभनमत्कमात्मीयं व्याप्तं
> रूपं वसानः सर्वत्राच्छादयन् । किमर्थं । दृशे दर्शनार्थं ॥ दृशे विख्ये चेति
> केप्रत्ययांतो निपात्यते ॥ कमिति पूरणः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । स्वर्ण । स्वः शोभनारण
> आदित्यः । स यथात्मीयं रूपं दर्शनाय सर्वत्राच्छादयति तद्वत् । तदनंतरं
> नाम नामानि नमनशीलान्युदकानि प्रियाणि सर्वेषामनुकूलानि जनत । जनयति ।
> वृष्टिमुत्पादयतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ऊर्ध्वः (*ūrdhvaḥ*) is one stationed in the upper region; गंधर्वः (*gaṃdharvaḥ*) is the bearer of *gavāṃ*, of waters (गवि गन् धृइतो व इति (*gavi gan dhṛito va iti*): from the word गो (*go*) as the preceding member, the root *dhṛñ* in the sense of holding, with the affix व (*va*), and गन् (*gan*) as substitute of the preceding member). Such a Vena, प्रत्यङ् (*pratyaṅ*), facing us, stands नाके अधि (*nāke adhi*) in the atmosphere. Doing what? Bearing (बिभ्रत् (*bibhrat*)) his own wonderful (चित्रा (*citrā*)) weapons, which are worthy of being gathered, marvellous. Likewise, वसानः (*vasānaḥ*), covering everywhere his own beautiful, pervading form (*surabhiṃ atkaṃ*). For what purpose? दृशे (*dṛśe*), for being seen; कं (*kaṃ*) is a filler. The example is स्वः न (*svaḥ na*): स्वः (*svaḥ*) is the Sun, of beautiful rays; as he covers his own form everywhere for being seen, so does Vena. Thereafter he जनत (*janata*), generates, नाम (*nāma*), the waters, bending down in their nature, प्रियाणि (*priyāṇi*), agreeable to all; the meaning is that he produces rain.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऊर्ध्वः (*ūrdhvaḥ*)—one who is in the lofty region of the atmosphere
- गंधर्वः (*gaṃdharvaḥ*)—one who bears the waters, that is, the support of the waters; this Vena
- प्रत्यज् (*pratyaj*)—facing us

- नाकेअधि (*nākeadhi*)—in the region of the atmosphere
- अस्थात् (*asthāt*)—he stays
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Vena
- अस्य (*asya*)—his own
- चित्रा (*citrā*)—of many kinds
- आयुधानि (*āyudhāni*)—weapons
- बिभ्रत् (*bibhrat*)—bearing
- सुरभिं (*surabhiṃ*)—beautiful
- अत्कं (*atkaṃ*)—with his form
- स्वः न (*svaḥ na*)—like the Sun
- वसानः (*vasānaḥ*)—covering everywhere
- प्रियाणि (*priyāṇi*)—dear to all
- नाम (*nāma*)—the waters
- जनत (*janata*)—he produces

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This god Vena, who is in the lofty region of the atmosphere and is the support of the waters, stays in the region of the atmosphere facing us. Bearing his wonderful weapons, and covering everything with his excellent form like the Sun, that Vena produces the rain-water that is dear to all; that is, he pours down rain.

##### English translation
The Gandharva stood erect upon the firmament, brandishing towards us his wonderful weapons, investing ali) in his beautiful diffusive (form), to make them visible, like the sun he generated the precious (rains). **NOTE**

> भानुः । शुक्रेण । शोचिषा । चकानः । तृतीये । चक्रे । रजसि । प्रियाणि ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रवर्गैऽभिष्टवे द्रप्सः समुद्रमित्येषा । सूत्रितं च । द्रप्सः समुद्रमभि
> यज्जिगाति सखे सखायमभ्या ववृत्स्व । आ. ४-७ । इति ॥
> विधर्मान्विधर्मणि विधारकेंतरिक्षे स्थितो द्रप्सो द्रवणशीलः । यद्वा । द्रप्सा
> 43

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Pravargya Abhiṣṭava the Ṛk द्रप्सः समुद्रं (*drapsaḥ samudraṃ*) is used. The sūtra says: द्रप्सः समुद्रमभि यज्जिगाति सखे सखायमभ्या ववृत्स्व (*drapsaḥ samudramabhi yajjigāti sakhe sakhāyamabhyā vavṛtsva*) (Ā. 4-7). विधर्मन् (*vidharman*) is विधर्मणि (*vidharmaṇi*), in the sustaining atmosphere; stationed there, he is द्रप्सः (*drapsaḥ*), of flowing nature; or else, द्रप्सा (*drapsā*) are drops of water, and he is possessed of them.

### Printed p. 674

> उदकबिंदवः । तद्वान् ॥ अर्श आदित्वादच्॥ गृध्रस्य गृधो रसानभिकांक्षतः सूर्यस्य
> चक्षसा तेजसा पश्यन् प्रकाशमानो वेनो यद्यदा समुद्रं समुंदनशीलं मेघमभि जिगाति अभिगच्छति तदानीं भानुः सूर्यः शुक्रेण शुभ्रेण शोचिषा तेजसा
> तृतीये रजसि लोके चकानो दीप्यमानः प्रियाणि सर्वेषामभीष्टान्न्युदकानि
> चक्रे । करोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

गृध्रस्य (*gṛdhrasya*) means of the Sun, who is eager for the juices (रसानभिकांक्षतः (*rasānabhikāṃkṣataḥ*)). Looking चक्षसा (*cakṣasā*), with the brilliance, i.e. shining, Vena, when he goes towards the समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*), the cloud, of flowing nature, then भानुः (*bhānuḥ*), the Sun, with bright (शुक्रेण (*śukreṇa*)) radiance, shining in the third sphere (तृतीये रजसि (*tṛtīye rajasi*)), the world, makes (चक्रे (*cakre*) = करोति (*karoti*)) the waters प्रियाणि (*priyāṇi*), desired by all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विधर्मन् (*vidharman*)—one who is in the atmosphere
- द्रप्सः (*drapsaḥ*)—one possessed of liquid drops of water
- गृध्रस्य (*gṛdhrasya*)—of the Sun
- चक्षसा (*cakṣasā*)—with the brilliance
- पश्यन् (*paśyan*)—Vena, who is shining
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*)—the cloud
- अभि (*abhi*)—aiming at, that is, facing the cloud
- जिगाति (*jigāti*)—goes, then
- भानुः (*bhānuḥ*)—the Sun
- शुक्रेण (*śukreṇa*)—with bright or shining
- शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)—radiance
- तृतीये रजसि (*tṛtīye rajasi*)—in the heaven-world (in the atmosphere)
- चकानः (*cakānaḥ*)—shining
- प्रियाणि (*priyāṇi*)—the waters dear to all
- चक्रे (*cakre*)—he produces

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When this god Vena, who is in the atmosphere in the form of liquid drops of water and shines with the Sun's brilliance, goes towards the cloud, then the Sun, with his bright radiance shining in the third world, heaven (the atmosphere), produces the rain-waters beneficial to all.

##### English translation
When (Vena as) the drop of rain approaches the firmament, contemplating (all things) with the eye of the hawk in the supporting (firmament), then the sun shining with brilliant radiance, makes the precious (showers) in the third sphere.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That the Ṛk द्रप्सः समुद्रं (*drapsaḥ samudraṃ*) is to be recited in the Pravargya Abhiṣṭava is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra: द्रप्सः समुद्रमभि यज्जिगाति सखे सखायमभ्या ववृत्स्व (*drapsaḥ samudramabhi yajjigāti sakhe sakhāyamabhyā vavṛtsva*) (Ā. 4-7).

### Printed p. 675

## Sūkta 124 (Maṇḍala 10)

Formerly Agni had three elder brothers. They undertook the work of carrying the oblations to the gods and conducted the sacrificial rites. While so engaged, they died from the thunderbolt-blow of the vaṣaṭ-oblations offered in the sacrifices. Seeing this, Agni was afraid that the same fate might befall him, and out of fear fled without telling anyone and hid in the water and in the plants and trees. As a result, with no one to carry the oblation to the gods in sacrifices, the gods were in difficulty and there arose the danger that the performance of sacrifice would stop. Therefore the gods Soma, Varuṇa and others, searching for Agni, came to the water where he lay hidden and prayed that Agni should rise from the water, carry the oblations to them as before, and help in the sacrificial rites. This prayer is what is stated in this sūkta. This matter is explained at length in the 51st sūkta of this same tenth Maṇḍala, beginning महत्तदुल्बं (*mahattadulbaṃ*) (see Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 28, pp. 250-257).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमं नो अग्न इति नवर्चं द्वादशं सूक्तं । द्वितीयाद्याभिस्ति सृभिरग्नि र्यषिर्भूत्वा स्वात्मानं देवतारूपिणमस्तौत् । आतस्तासां स एवर्षिर्देवता च । शिष्टाभिरग्निवरुणसोमा अस्तुवन् । अतस्तासां षण्णां ते ऋषयः । आद्याग्नेयी । नवमींद्रदेवत्या । शिष्टासु चतसृषु लिंगोक्तदेवता । सप्तमी जगती शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः । तथा
> चानुक्रांतं । इमं नो नव्यंद्र्युत्तमा निहवोऽग्निवरुणसोमानामाद्याग्नेयी
> तिस्रश्चाग्नेरात्मस्तवः शिष्टा यथानिपातं सप्तमी जगतीति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta इमं नो अग्न (*imaṃ no agna*) has nine Ṛks and is the twelfth sūkta. With the three Ṛks beginning from the second Agni, having become the seer, praised himself in the form of the deity; so for these he is both seer and deity. With the remaining Ṛks, Agni, Varuṇa and Soma praised; therefore they are the seers of those six. The first is addressed to Agni; the ninth has Indra as deity; in the remaining four the deity is the one indicated by the text. The seventh is Jagatī, the rest Triṣṭubh. So the Anukramaṇī says: इमं नो नव्यंद्र्युत्तमा निहवोऽग्निवरुणसोमानामाद्याग्नेयी तिस्रश्चाग्नेरात्मस्तवः शिष्टा यथानिपातं सप्तमी जगतीति ॥ (*imaṃ no navyaṃdryuttamā nihavo 'gnivaruṇasomānāmādyāgneyī tisraścāgnerātmastavaḥ śiṣṭā yathānipātaṃ saptamī jagatīti ‖*). The viniyoga has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta इमं नो अग्ने (*imaṃ no agne*) is the twelfth sūkta in the tenth anuvāka. It has nine Ṛks. In this sūkta, from the second Ṛk to the following three Ṛks, that is, up to Ṛks 2-4, Agni himself as seer has praised himself. Therefore for those three Ṛks Agni is both seer and deity. Of the remaining Ṛks, for the 1st Ṛk Agni is the seer. For Ṛks 5-9 Agni, Varuṇa and Soma are the seers; for the first Ṛk Agni is the deity. For the ninth Ṛk Indra is the deity; for the remaining four Ṛks, that is Ṛks 5-8, those who are praised in them are the deities. The seventh Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Jagatī metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: इमं नो नव्येंद्रुत्तमा निहवोS ग्निवरुणसोमानामाद्याग्नेया तिस्रश्चाग्नेरात्मस्तवः शिष्टा यथानिपातं सप्तमी जगती (*imaṃ no navyeṃdruttamā nihavoS gnivaruṇasomānāmādyāgneyā tisraścāgnerātmastavaḥ śiṣṭā yathānipātaṃ saptamī jagatī*). The viniyoga has been stated earlier. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 676
Maṇḍala 10, Anuvāka 10, Sūkta 124. Aṣṭaka 8, Adhyāya 7, Vargas 9, 10. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 9.

Ṛṣi: Ṛks 1, 5–9, Agni-Varuṇa-Somānāṃ Nihavaḥ; Ṛks 2–4, Agni. Devatā: Ṛks 1–4, Agni; Ṛks 5–8, as each occurs (yathānipātam); Ṛk 9, Indra. Chandas: Ṛks 1–6, 8, 9, Triṣṭubh; Ṛk 7, Jagatī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मं नो॑ अग्न॒ उप॑ य॒ज्ञमेहि॒ पंच॑यामं त्रि॒वृतं॑ स॒प्ततं॑तुं ।  
> असो॑ हव्य॒वाळु॒त नः॑ पुरो॒गा ज्योगे॒व दी॒र्घं तम॒ आश॑यिष्ठाः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमं । नः । अग्ने । उप । यज्ञं । आ । इहि । पंचयामं । त्रिवृतं । सप्ततंतुं ।  
> असः । हव्यवाट् । उत । नः । पुरःगाः । ज्योक् । एव । दीर्घं । तमः । आ ।  
> अशयिष्ठाः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> भ्रातैषु हविर्वहनेषु मृतेषु मरणभीत्या कृतपलायनं गुहायां निगूढमग्निमग्न्याद्याः सूक्तद्रष्टार ऋषयोऽनयाह्वयन् । हे अग्ने नोस्माकमिमं
> यज्ञमुपेहि । उपागच्छ । प्राप्पुहि । मा पलायिष्ठाः ! कीदृशं । पंचयामं
> यजमानपंचमैऋत्विग्निर्नियमितं । यद्वा! धानाकरंभादिभिः पंचभिर्हविर्भिः
> पंचभिः प्रयाजैर्वा प्राप्तं । त्रिवृतं पाकयज्ञहविर्यज्ञसोमयज्ञभेदेन
> सवनत्रयात्मना वा त्रिगुणं सप्ततंतुं सप्त तंतनस्तनितारः कर्मणां विस्तारयितारो
> होत्राद्याः सप्त वषट्कर्तारो यस्य! यद्वा। अग्निष्टोमोऽत्यग्निष्टोम उक्त्यः
> षोळशी वाजपेयोऽतिरात्रोऽप्रोर्याम इति सप्तधा विस्तीयमाणं । ईदृशं
> यज्ञमुपगत्य चानंतरं नोऽस्माकं हव्यवाड्धव्यानां हविषां वोढासः ! भव ॥
> अस्तेर्लेट्यडागमः ॥ उतापि च नोऽस्माकं पुरोगाः पुरतो गंता भव ॥ जनसन-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk the seers of the sūkta, Agni's brothers (Agni and the rest), call Agni. His fellow oblation-bearers had died, and out of fear of death he had fled and hidden himself in a cave. "O Agni, come to this sacrifice of ours; do not flee." The sacrifice is described as पंचयामं (*paṃcayāmaṃ*): governed by five, the sacrificer as fifth together with the priests; or else reached through five oblations such as dhānā and karambha, or through the five prayājas. It is त्रिवृतं (*trivṛtaṃ*): threefold, by the division into the pākayajña, the haviryajña and the somayajña, or as consisting of the three savanas. It is सप्ततंतुं (*saptataṃtuṃ*): its vaṣaṭ-makers are seven, the hotṛ and the others, who spread out the rites; or else it is spread out in seven forms: the agniṣṭoma, atyagniṣṭoma, ukthya, ṣoḍaśī, vājapeya, atirātra and aptoryāma. "Having come to such a sacrifice, be the bearer of our oblations; and also be our leader, going before us." Sāyaṇa explains असः (*asaḥ*) as the root as with the augment aṭ in the leṭ form, and पुरोगाः (*purogāḥ*) as formed with viṭ.

> खनक्रमगमो विट् । विड्वरोरनुनासिकस्यादित्यात्वं ॥ ज्योक् चिरकालमेवास्मान्परित्यज्य दीर्घं तमो महदंधकारं गुहायामाशयिष्ठाः । आस्थाय शयनमकार्षिः।
> इत ऊर्ध्व० तस्मात्स्थानादस्मानागच्छेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues: "For a long time you have forsaken us and lain in the cave, in long, great darkness. Rise from that place and come to us" is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- पंचयामं (*paṃcayāmaṃ*)—performed by five persons, the four priests beginning with the hotṛ together with the sacrificer
- त्रिवृतं (*trivṛtaṃ*)—consisting of the three savanas
- सप्ततंतुं (*saptataṃtuṃ*)—accompanied by the seven vaṣaṭ-makers
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- इमं यज्ञं (*imaṃ yajñaṃ*)—this sacrifice, with reference to it
- उप आ इहि (*upa ā ihi*)—deign to come
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- हव्यवाट् (*havyavāṭ*)—as the bearer of the oblation
- असः (*asaḥ*)—be
- उत (*uta*)—and
- *(naḥ)*—(for us)
- पुरोगाः (*purogāḥ*)—be also the leader in front
- ज्योक् एव (*jyok eva*)—for a long time (leaving us)
- दीर्घं तमः (*dīrghaṃ tamaḥ*)—in great darkness
- आ अशयिष्ठाः (*ā aśayiṣṭhāḥ*)—you have lain (therefore rise and come quickly)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Words of the gods.) O Agni, you have long forsaken us and lain in deep darkness. Therefore leave that region enveloped in darkness (the region in the midst of the water), come to this sacrifice of ours, which is performed by the four priests beginning with the hotṛ and by the sacrificer, which consists of the three savanas and is accompanied by the seven vaṣaṭ-makers, and be in front of us as the bearer of our oblations.

##### English translation
Come, Agni, to this our sacrifice, which has five oblations, three-fold, spread out by seven (priests); be the bearer of our oblations, be our proceder, you have long been sleeping in profound darkness.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The second pāda of this Ṛk, पंचयामं त्रिवृतं सप्ततंतुं (*paṃcayāmaṃ trivṛtaṃ saptataṃtuṃ*), is also read as the fourth pāda of Ṛk 4 of Sūkta 52 of this same maṇḍala, विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*). The three words in this pāda are all qualifying words for the word yajña. Sāyaṇa explains them as follows.

### Printed p. 677
पंचयामं (*paṃcayāmaṃ*)—यजमानपंचमैर्यत्विग्निर्नियमितं । यद्वा । धानाकरंभादिभिः पंचभिः हविर्भिः पंचभिः प्रयाज्यर्वा प्राप्तं ॥ (*yajamānapaṃcamairyatvignirniyamitaṃ | yadvā | dhānākaraṃbhādibhiḥ paṃcabhiḥ havirbhiḥ paṃcabhiḥ prayājyarvā prāptaṃ ‖*). Pañcayāma means the sacrifice performed jointly by these five: the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice, and the four priests called hotṛ, adhvaryu, udgātṛ and brahman; or the sacrifice in which the offering is made with five kinds of oblations, dhānā, karambha and the rest; or the sacrifice performed with the five kinds of prayāja offerings.

### Printed p. 678
त्रिवृतं (*trivṛtaṃ*)—पाकयज्ञ हविर्यज्ञ सोमयज्ञ भेदेन सवनत्रयात्मना वा त्रिगुणं (*pākayajña haviryajña somayajña bhedena savanatrayātmanā vā triguṇaṃ*). Among sacrifices there are three groups: pākayajñas, haviryajñas and somayajñas. Or else, when Soma juice is pressed in a sacrifice, it is pressed and prepared at three times of the day: morning, midday and evening. These three rites are called in order the morning savana, the midday savana and the third savana. The meaning is: the sacrifice that is made up of these three kinds of savana.

सप्ततंतुं (*saptataṃtuṃ*)—सप्ततंतवस्तनितारः कर्मणां विस्तारयितारो होत्राद्याः सप्तवर्षट्कर्तारो यस्य तं । यद्वा अग्निष्टोमोऽत्यग्निष्टोम उक्त्यः षोळशी वाजपेयोऽपोर्याम इति सप्तधा विस्तीर्यमाणं ॥ (*saptataṃtavastanitāraḥ karmaṇāṃ vistārayitāro hotrādyāḥ saptavarṣaṭkartāro yasya taṃ | yadvā agniṣṭomo 'tyagniṣṭoma uktyaḥ ṣoḷaśī vājapeyo 'poryāma iti saptadhā vistīryamāṇaṃ ‖*). In a sacrifice there are seven priests, the hotṛ and others, appointed to offer the vaṣaṭkāra and other oblations. They are called the seven hotṛs. Who are they? The seven priests hotṛ, maitrāvaruṇa, brāhmaṇācchaṃsī, potṛ, neṣṭṛ, acchāvāka and āgnīdhra. The meaning is: the sacrifice carried out by them. Or else the meaning is: the sacrifice that is one of the seven forms (saṃsthā) called agniṣṭoma, atyagniṣṭoma, ukthya, ṣoḍaśī, vājapeya, atirātra and aptoryāma.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अदे॑वाद्दे॒वः प्र॒चता॒ गुहा॒ यन्प्र॒पश्य॑मानो अमृत॒त्वमे॑मि ।  
> शि॒वं यत्संत॒मशि॑वो॒ जहा॑मि॒ स्वात्स॒ख्यादर॑णीं॒ नाभि॑मेमि ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अदेवात् । देवः । प्रचता । गुहा । यन् । प्रपश्यमानः । अमृतत्वं । एमि ।  
> शिवं । यत् । संतं अशिवः । जहामि । स्वात् । सख्यात् । अरणीं । नाभिं । एमि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अदेवाददेवनशीलाद्गुहा गुहायां वर्तमानात् ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या
> लुक् ॥ प्रचता देवानां प्रयाचनेन हेतुना यन् निर्गच्छन् देवो देवनशी-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अदेवात् (*adevāt*) means from one who has the nature of a deva, a god; गुहा (*guhā*) means in the cave. Sāyaṇa notes that the locative ending is dropped (luk) by the rule सुपां सुलुगिति (*supāṃ sulugiti*). प्रचता (*pracatā*) means by the entreaty of the gods, as the cause. यन् (*yan*) means coming out; the deva, whose nature is to shine, ...

### Printed p. 679

> लोहं प्रपश्यमानो देवैर्मदर्थं कल्पितं प्रयाजानुयाजादिलक्षणं हविर्भागं
> प्रपश्यमानो निरीक्षमाणः सन्नमृतत्वमेमि । मरणधर्मराहित्यं देवत्वं
> प्राप्नोमि ॥ दृशेर्व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं ॥ हनिर्वहनाध्भीतः पलायितोऽबादिसु
> स्थानेषु निगूढः पुनर्देवैर्हनिर्वहनाय प्रार्थ्यमानस्मैर्दत्तेन हविषाहं
> देवत्वं प्राप्तवानस्मीत्यर्थः । यद्यस्यहं गुहातो निर्गत्य प्रकाशमानः सञ्ज्योभनं यज्ञं निर्वर्तयामि तथापि शिवं शोभनं संतं भवंतं यज्ञमशिवोऽशोभनरूपोऽप्रकाशमानः सन् यद्यस्मिन्समाप्ति काले जहामि परित्यजामि तदानीं नाभिं
> नहनशीलां बंधनशीलामरणीमश्वत्थमेव स्वात्सख्यादात्मीयात्सखित्वाच्चिरकालमश्वरूपोऽहं तत्र न्यवात्समिति स्नेहवशादेमि । प्राप्नोमि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

... seeing the share of oblations, marked by the prayājas, anuyājas and the like, which the gods have arranged for me, I attain immortality, that is, freedom from the nature of dying, godhood. The verb प्रपश्यमानः (*prapaśyamānaḥ*) takes the ātmanepada by vyatyaya. The meaning: afraid of carrying the oblations, I fled and hid in places such as the waters; when the gods again entreated me to carry oblations, I have gained godhood by the oblation they gave me. "If I come out of the cave, shine, and carry out a good sacrifice, yet when it is complete I, becoming inauspicious and not shining, abandon the auspicious sacrifice; then, through my own friendship, I go, I reach, the अरणीं (*araṇīṃ*), the aśvattha, which is of a binding nature (नाभिं (*nābhiṃ*)), out of affection, thinking: 'I, in the form of a horse, dwelt there for a long time.'"

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अदेवात् (*adevāt*)—having come, leaving the form of the gods or the work of carrying oblations
- गुहा (*guhā*)—the one hidden in a secret place (in the water)
- प्रचता (*pracatā*)—by the entreaty made by the gods
- यन् (*yan*)—the one who has come out (of the water)
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—I, who am shining
- प्रपश्यमानः (*prapaśyamānaḥ*)—looking at the shares of the oblation, marked by prayājas and the like, arranged for me by the gods
- अमृतत्वं (*amṛtatvaṃ*)—godhood, free from the nature of dying
- एमि (*emi*)—I obtain
- शिवं (*śivaṃ*)—auspicious
- संतं (*saṃtaṃ*)—your sacrifice
- यत् अशिवः (*yat aśivaḥ*)—when it is not auspicious
- जहामि (*jahāmi*)—I abandon it, and
- नाभिं (*nābhiṃ*)—of the nature of a bond (my dwelling place)
- अरणीं (*araṇīṃ*)—the araṇi made of aśvattha
- स्वात् सख्यात् (*svāt sakhyāt*)—from my own affection
- एमि (*emi*)—I reach (I go and join it)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Words of Agni.) O gods, I had left the duty of the gods, that is, the work of carrying oblations, and stayed in the water, a secret place. Entreated by you, the gods, and looking at the prayāja and other oblations arranged for me, I come back to you and obtain immortality. When your sacrifice is no longer auspicious, that is, when the sacrifice comes to its completion, I abandon it and go and join my own place, the araṇi, through the former friendship.

##### English translation
(Agni speaks :) From being no divinity I issue a divinity from the cave at the solication (of the gods). and being manifest I attain immortality ; when being inauspicious, I abandon the sacrifice as it becomes auspicious. through my (old) friendship I come to the binding touch-wood,

### Printed p. 680

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Agni speaks thus: Fearing that the work of carrying oblations was very dangerous, I ran away and hid in the water, a secret place, where no one would know. Then the gods searched for me and came there, and when they entreated me to undertake again the carrying of oblations for them, I accepted from them the boons they granted, namely the prayāja and other oblations, and gained godhood. Therefore I rise up out of the secret place where I was hidden, shine as before, and carry out the excellent work of the sacrifice. And after the sacrifice is completed, since that sacrifice is no longer auspicious, I then abandon it and, as a result of the former friendship between me and the araṇi, my dwelling place, I go back and join the araṇi itself. This is the main sense of the Ṛk.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पश्य॑न्न॒न्यस्या॒ अति॑थिं व॒याया॑ ऋ॒तस्य॒ धाम॒ वि मि॑मे पु॒रूणि॑ ।  
> शंसा॑मि पि॒त्रे असु॑राय॒ शेव॑मयज्जि॒याद्य॒ज्ञॆयं॑ भा॒गमे॑मि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पश्यन् । अन्यस्याः । अतिथिं । वयायाः । ऋतस्य । धाम । वि । मिमे । पुरूणि ।  
> शंसामि । पित्रे । असुराय । शेवं । अयज्ञियात् । यज्ञियं । भागं । एमि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मम स्थानभूता या पृथिवी ततोऽन्यस्या वयाया गंतव्याया दिवः संबंधिनमतिथिं सततगामिनं सूर्यं पश्यञ्जनन् सूर्यस्य गतिमनुसृत्य वसंतादिकाल ऋतस्य
> यज्ञस्य धाम धामानि शरीराणि पुरूणि बहूनि वि मिमे । निर्ममे ! निष्पादयामि ।
> ततः पित्रे पितृभूताय द्युलोकवर्तिने देवजनायासुराय शत्रुक्षेपणकुशलाय
> शेवं सुखमुद्दिश्य होता भूत्साहमुक्थानि शंसामि । यत एवं तस्मात्कारणादयज्ञियाद्यज्ञानर्हात्पदेशान्निर्गत्य यज्जियं यज्ञार्हं वेदिलक्षणं भूभागं
> हविर्लक्षणं वैमि । प्राप्नोमि ॥ यज्ञशब्दादर्हार्थे यज्ञर्त्वग्भां घखञाविति
> घप्रत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Beholding the guest, the ever-moving Sun, belonging to the heaven that is to be gone to, which is other than the earth that is my place, that is, following the Sun's course, I create many abodes, bodies, of the sacrifice, at the seasons such as spring. Then, for the father, the asura, the company of gods dwelling in the sky, skilled in casting off enemies, I become hotṛ and recite the ukthas for their happiness. Therefore, leaving the place unfit for sacrifice, I go to the sacrificial portion of earth, the altar, and obtain the oblation." Sāyaṇa adds that यज्ञियं (*yajñiyaṃ*) is formed from the word yajña in the sense "fit for", with the affix gha.

### Printed p. 681

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अन्यस्याः (*anyasyāḥ*)—other than the earth, my own place
- वयायाः (*vayāyāḥ*)—different, that is, belonging to heaven
- अतिथिं (*atithiṃ*)—the Sun, who is always moving
- पश्यन् (*paśyan*)—looking, that is, following his course
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of the sacrifice
- पुरूणि (*purūṇi*)—of many kinds
- धाम (*dhāma*)—bodies, that is, forms
- वि ममे (*vi mame*)—I create
- असुराय (*asurāya*)—skilled in subduing enemies
- पित्रे (*pitre*)—to the company of gods in heaven who are as fathers
- शेवं (*śevaṃ*)—in order to bring happiness, as hotṛ priest
- शंसामि (*śaṃsāmi*)—I recite the ukthas
- अयज्ञियात् (*ayajñiyāt*)—leaving the region unfit for sacrifice
- यज्जियं (*yajjiyaṃ*)—to the region of earth fit for sacrifice, the altar
- एमि (*emi*)—I go

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Words of Agni.) O gods, leaving this earth, my own place, and following the course of the Sun, who moves always in another place, heaven, I create manifold institutions of sacrifice (many kinds of sacrifices). To bring happiness to the company of gods who dwell in the sky and are skilled in subduing enemies, I take the part of hotṛ and recite the ukthas; abandoning the evil regions unfit for sacrifice, I go to the sacrificial altar fit for sacrifice.

##### English translation
Beholding the guest of another family, I have created the manifold
abodes of sacrifice; I repeat praises, (wishing) good luck to the paternal foe-
destroying (race of deites), I pass from a place unfit for sacrifice to a place
where sacrifice can be offered.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ब॒ह्वीः समा॑ अकरमं॒तर॑स्मि॒न्निंद्रं॑ वृणा॒नः पि॒तरं॑ जहामि ।  
> अ॒ग्निः सोमो॒ वरु॑ण॒स्ते च्य॑वंते प॒र्याव॑र्द्रा॒ष्टं तद॑वाम्या॒यन् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बह्वीः । समाः । आकरं । अंतः । अस्मिन् । इंद्रं । वृणानः । पितरं । जहामि ।

> अग्निः । सोमः । वरुणः । ते । च्यवंते । परिआवर्त् । राष्ट्रं । तत् । अवामि ।
> आयन् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्मिन्वेदिलक्षणस्थाने बह्वीः समाः संवत्सरानकरं । अकार्ष० । चिरकालं
> न्यवात्सं । तत्रेंद्रं वृणानः संभजमानः पितरमुत्पादकमरण्यात्मकं जहामि । परित्यजामि । यदा त्वहं देवेभ्यो निर्गत्य गुहायां निगूढः तदा ते देवा अग्निः
> सोमो वरुणश्च च्यवंते । राष्ट्रात्प्रच्युता अभवन् । एकस्याप्यग्निर्हविर्वोढृत्वरूपेण देवतात्मना च पृथक्त्वात्परोक्षनिर्दॆशः । आयन् पुनरागच्छन्नहं यद्राष्ट्रमसुरैरपहृतं पर्यावर्त् पर्यावर्तमानं मदभिमुखं पुनरावर्तमानं
> तद्राष्ट्रं राज्यं यज्ञभूमिमवामि । असुरेभ्यो रक्षामि । पर्यावर्त् ॥ उपसृष्टाद्वृतेरन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यंत इति विच् । रात्सस्यॆति नियमात्संगांतस्यॆति
> लोपाभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In this place of the altar I have spent many years, and have stayed for a long time. There, choosing Indra, I abandon my begetter, the fire-stick (araṇi). When I had gone away from the gods and was hidden in a cave, those gods, Agni, Soma and Varuna, fell, that is, were dislodged from their kingdom. Although Agni is one, the third-person reference is made because he is distinct as the bearer of the oblation and as a deity. Coming back, I protect from the Asuras that kingdom, the sacrificial ground, which they had seized and which is turning back toward me. पर्यावर्त् (*paryāvart*) is explained by a grammatical note on the affix vic and on the absence of elision.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्मिन् (*asmin*)—in this sacrificial place called the vedi
- बह्वीः (*bahvīḥ*)—many
- समाः (*samāḥ*)—years
- अकरं (*akaraṃ*)—I have spent (living there). But!
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—to Indra
- वृणानः (*vṛṇānaḥ*)—in order to go
- पितरं (*pitaraṃ*)—the araṇi, which is like a father, having produced me
- जहामि (*jahāmi*)—I abandon (when I had left the gods and was hidden in a secret place)
- ते (*te*)—those gods, namely
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—and Varuna as well
- च्यवंते (*cyavaṃte*)—are driven out of their kingdom or place (for lack of a share of the oblation)
- आयन् (*āyan*)—I, coming again from the secret place
- पर्यावर्त् (*paryāvart*)—returning, again obtained
- तत् राष्ट्रं (*tat rāṣṭraṃ*)—that realm of mine, the sacrificial ground
- अवामि (*avāmi*)—I protect from the Asuras

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Agni's speech.) O gods, I have spent many years living in this sacrificial place, the vedi. In order to go to Indra, that is, when conducting the sacrifice for Indra's pleasure, I leave behind the araṇi, my own place, which is like a father to me. When I had run away from the gods and hidden in a secret place, gods such as Agni, Soma and Varuna, lacking a share of the oblation in the sacrifice (because I was absent), were fallen from their places. But I rise from my secret place, come back, settle as before in the sacrificial ground that is my realm, conduct the sacrifice, bear the oblation to the gods, and protect the sacrifice from the Asuras.

### Printed p. 683

##### English translation
I spent many years within this (altar); preferring Indra, I abandon the progenitor; Agni, Soma, Varuna, fall (from their power); returning, I protect that kingdom which awaits me

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> निर्मा॑या उ॒ तै असु॑रा अभूव॒न्त्वं च॑ मा वरुण का॒मया॑से ।  
> ऋ॒तेन॑ राज॒न्न नृ॑तं विविं॒चन्मम॑ रा॒ष्ट्रस्याधि॑पत्य॒मेहि॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> निःसमायाः । ऊं इति । तै । असुराः । अभूवन् । त्वं । च । मा । वरुण । कामयासे ।  
> ऋतेन । राजन् । अनृतं । विविंचन् । मम । राष्ट्रस्य । अधिपत्यं । आ । इहि ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्ये तेऽसुरा मय्यग्नानागते सति निर्माया मायारहिता अभूवन् ।
> आसुर्यः सर्वा माया मया दग्धा आसन्नित्यर्थः । हे वरुण त्वं च ॥ अयं चशब्दश्चेदर्थे वर्तमानश्चणिति निपातांतरं । अनेन युक्तत्वात्कामयास इति तिङ्विभक्तेर्निपातैय्यद्यदिहंतेति निघातप्रतिषेथः । पा. ८-१-३० ॥ हे वरुण त्वं चेन्मा कामयासे
> मां कामयेथाः तर्हि हे राजन्नीश्वर ऋतेन सत्येनास्यदीयेन कर्मणानृतमसत्यभूतं मायामयमासुरं चरित्रं विविंचन् पृथक्कुर्वन्नपसारयन् मम राष्ट्रस्य
> मया यत्साधितं राज्यं तस्याधिपत्यमधिपतित्वमीश्वरत्वमेहि । प्राप्पुहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those Asuras, when I, Agni, have come, become free of magic: all the Asura illusions have been burnt by me. "And you, Varuna": the word च (*ca*) here has the sense of "if", and is another particle; because of its connection with it, the verb कामयासे (*kāmayāse*) is not accented (Pā. Sū. 8-1-30). O Varuna, if you desire me, then, O king, lord, by the truth, my own act, separating and driving away the untrue, illusory Asura conduct, obtain sovereignty and lordship over my realm, the kingdom I have accomplished.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्ये असुरा (*tye asurā*)—those Asuras (if they come near me, Agni)
- निर्मायाः (*nirmāyāḥ*)—free of magic
- अभूवन् (*abhūvan*)—become
- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuna
- त्वं च (*tvaṃ ca*)—you also
- मा (*mā*)—me
- कामयासे (*kāmayāse*)—if you desire
- राजन् (*rājan*)—as lord of all
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—

### Printed p. 684

- (ऋतेन (*ṛtena*) continued)—by my true act
- अनृतं (*anṛtaṃ*)—the untrue magic of the Asuras
- विविंचन् (*viviṃcan*)—separating
- मम (*mama*)—my
- राष्ट्रस्य (*rāṣṭrasya*)—of the realm
- अधिपत्यं (*adhipatyaṃ*)—lordship
- एहि (*ehi*)—you obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Agni's speech.) If those Asuras come near me, Agni, all their magic is burnt and destroyed by me. O Varuna, if you too desire me, then, as lord of all, separating the untrue from the true, you will obtain sovereignty over my realm.

##### English translation
These Asuras were deprived of their magical power; if you, Varuna, desire me, (then), O king, separating truth from falsehood come and enjoy sovereignty over my realm.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इदं । स्वः । इदं । इत् । आस । वामं । अयं । प्रकाशः । उरु । अंतरिक्षं ।  
> हनाव । वृत्रं । निःएहि । सोम । हविः । त्वा । संतं । हविषा । यजाम ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इयमृगग्नेर्वरुणस्य वा वाक्यं । हे सोम इदं स्वरयं द्युलोकः
> यद्वायं शोभनारणः सूर्य इदमिदिदमेव वामं वननीयमास । बभूव ।
> इदंशब्देन प्रकृतं स्वः परामृश्यते । अयं च प्रकाशः प्रकाशस्याधारभूत उरु
> विस्तीर्णमिदमंतरिक्षं हे सोम एतत्सर्वं पश्य । आत एवास्मिन्समय आवां वृत्रं
> हनाव ! हिनसाव ! तदर्थं निरेहि । निष्क्रम्यागच्छ । हविः संतं लतारूपेण
> हविर्भवंतं देवतात्मानं त्वां हविषा चरुपुरोडाशादिना वयं यजाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is the speech of Agni or of Varuna. O Soma, this is heaven, the sky; or else this is the beautiful-rayed sun; just this is what is desirable. The word "this" refers to the heaven under discussion. And this light, and this broad firmament, the support of the light: O Soma, see all this. Therefore, at this time, let us two slay Vṛtra; for that come forth. You who are the oblation, being in the form of the plant and the deity, we worship with the oblation, the cooked rice-cake and so on.

### Printed p. 685

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Soma) इदं स्वः (*idaṃ svaḥ*)—this is the heaven (or the sun)
- इदमित् (*idamit*)—this (heaven)
- वामं (*vāmaṃ*)—desired by all
- आस (*āsa*)—is
- आयं (*āyaṃ*)—this sun
- प्रकाशः (*prakāśaḥ*)—the support of the light
- उरु (*uru*)—broad
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the firmament (see all this; therefore now we)
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—Vṛtra
- हनाव (*hanāva*)—let us slay (for that)
- निरेहि (*nirehi*)—come forth and be ready
- हविः संतं (*haviḥ saṃtaṃ*)—you who, being in the form of the plant, become the oblation (with cooked rice-cake and other substances)
- यजाम (*yajāma*)—we worship

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(The speech of Agni and Varuna addressed to Soma.) O Soma, this is the world of heaven. It is desired by all. This sun is the support of the light. This is the broad firmament. See all this; now let us set out to slay Vṛtra. Be ready for it. O Soma, you who are in the form of the plant and become the juice, you are yourself the oblation. Such as you, we worship.

##### English translation
(Agni or Varuna speaks :) This, O Soma, is heaven ; this verily was beautiful, this (was) the light, the broad firmament; let us two slay Vritra ; come forth ; we worship with an oblation you who are yourself the oblation

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कविः क्रांतदर्शि मित्रः कवित्वा कवित्वेन ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयाया आकारः॥
> क्रांतदर्शनेन दिवि द्युलोके रूपमात्मियं तेज आसजत् । आसक्तं करोति ॥ षन्व
> संगे । आस्माल्लज शपि दंशसंजष्टंजां शपि । पा. ६-४-२५ । इति नलोपः ॥ अप्रभूत्यप्रभूत्या ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयायाः पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः ॥ अप्रभूष्णुनाल्वेनैव
> यत्नेन वरुणो मेघादपो निः सृजत् । निरगमयत् । वरुणेन विसृष्टास्ता आपः
> सिंधवः स्कंदनशीला नद्यो भूत्वा जनयो न जाया इव यथा जायाः पत्युः
> क्षेमकारिण्यो भवंति तथा क्षेमं कुर्वाणा जगतो रक्षणं कुर्वाणाः शुचयः
> शुद्धा दीप्यमाना वास्यॆ वरुणस्य वर्णं शुक्लं भास्वररूपं भरिभ्रति । भृशं बिभ्रति
> धारयंति ॥ वाधर्त्यादिसूत्रे भरिभ्रदिति निपातनाद्बिभर्तेय्‌ज्लुक्यभ्यासस्य
> जश्वाभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer Mitra, by his far-seeing wisdom, fixed his own form, his radiance, in heaven. Varuna, with but little effort, sent forth the waters out of the cloud. The waters sent forth by Varuna became flowing rivers and, like wives who bring welfare to a husband, bring welfare and protect the world; pure and shining, they bear strongly the white, bright colour of this Varuna. Grammatical remarks are given on the ending of कवित्वा (*kavitvā*), the loss of the nasal in आसजत् (*āsajat*), the lengthening in अप्रभूती (*aprabhūtī*) and the form भरिभ्रति (*bharibhrati*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—Mitra, the far-seeing
- कवित्वा (*kavitvā*)—by his far-reaching wisdom
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the heavenly world (in the firmament)
- रूपं (*rūpaṃ*)—his form (the radiance that is his form)
- आ असजत् (*ā asajat*)—has fixed firmly
- अप्रभूती (*aprabhūtī*)—by little effort alone
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuna
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters in the clouds
- निःसृजत् (*niḥsṛjat*)—sends forth (makes them fall); those waters
- सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—as flowing rivers
- जनयोन (*janayona*)—as wives bring benefit to their husbands
- क्षेमं (*kṣemaṃ*)—welfare to the world
- कृष्णानाः (*kṛṣṇānāḥ*)—producing
- शुचयः (*śucayaḥ*)—pure, or shining
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Varuna
- वर्णं (*varṇaṃ*)—the white colour that is radiance
- भरिभ्रति (*bharibhrati*)—cast all around (cause to shine)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Mitra (the sun), the far-seeing, by his boundless far-reaching wisdom has fixed his divine form firmly in heaven (the firmament). Varuna, with his slight effort alone, makes the waters in the clouds fall upon the earth as rain. Those waters become flowing rivers, filled with pure water, and, as wives do good to their husbands, doing good to the world, they make shine for the world the white form (or greatness) of this Varuna.

##### English translation
The sage (Mitra) by his wisdom fixed his body in the sky ; Varuna with but a slight effort let loose the waters, conferring happiness, like wives, the pure rivers assume his (white) tint.

> ताः । अस्य । ज्येष्ठं । इंद्रियं । सचंते । ताः । ईं । आ । क्षेति । स्वधया । मदंतीः ।  
> ताः । ईं । विशः । न । राजानं । वृणानाः । बीभत्सुवः । अप । वृत्रान् । अतिष्ठन् ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ताः पूर्वोक्ता वृष्टा आपोऽस्य वरुणस्य ज्येष्ठं वृद्धतमिंद्रियं वीर्यं
> सचंते । समवयंति । संभजंते । धारयंतीत्यर्थः । आपो वरुणस्य पत्न आसन्निति
> श्रुतेः । स्वधया । अन्ननामैतत् । हनिर्लक्षणेनान्नेन मदंतीर्माद्यंतीः । यद्वा ।
> व्रीह्याद्युत्पादनद्वारेण हविषा मादयंतीः । ता अप ईमयं वरुण आक्षेति ।
> अभिगच्छति ॥ क्षि निवासगत्योः । छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् ॥ ताश्चमेनं वरुणं विशो
> न एशः प्रजा यथा राजानं स्वामिनं संभजंते तथा वृणानाः संभजमाना बीभत्सुवो भयेन कंपमानाः । यद्वा बद्धा वृत्रेणावृताः सत्यः । तस्मिन्हते सति तस्माद्वृत्तादपातिष्ठन् । अपक्रम्य तत्र तत्रावतिष्ठंते ॥ बध बंधन इत्यस्माद्द्धातोर्मान्बधदान्यान्भ्यः । पा. ३-१-६ । इति सन् अभ्यासस्य च दीर्घः । सनाशंसभिक्ष उरित्युप्रत्ययः । जसि च्चांदस उवजादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those rains mentioned before follow, that is, partake of and bear, the foremost, greatest vigour of this Varuna, according to the Śruti "the waters were the wives of Varuna". स्वधया (*svadhayā*) is a name for food; they rejoice with food in the form of the oblation. Or else they gladden with the oblation by way of producing rice and the like. This Varuna approaches those waters. As subjects join their king and lord, so the waters, choosing him, trembling with fear; or else bound, enclosed by Vṛtra, when he was slain they moved away from that enclosure and stood in their several places. Grammar: the desiderative formation from the root meaning "to bind" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-6), the lengthening of the reduplication, the affix u, and the substitution uv before the plural ending.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ताः (*tāḥ*)—the rain-waters spoken of before
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Varuna
- ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*)—the greatest
- इंद्रियं (*iṃdriyaṃ*)—vigour
- सचंते (*sacaṃte*)—obtain (bear)
- स्वधया (*svadhayā*)—with food in the form of the oblation
- मदंतीः (*madaṃtīḥ*)—who rejoice
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—those waters
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this Varuna
- आ क्षेति (*ā kṣeti*)—approaches
- विशः (*viśaḥ*)—subjects
- राजानं न (*rājānaṃ na*)—as they approach their lord the king with fear and devotion
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—these waters
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this Varuna, their husband.

### Printed p. 688
Pratipadārtha (continued from the previous page):
- वृणानाः (*vṛṇānāḥ*)—approaching
- बीभत्सवः (*bībhatsavaḥ*)—trembling with fear, or, being enveloped by Vṛtra, terrified
- वृत्रात् (*vṛtrāt*)—from Vṛtra
- अप अतिष्ठन् (*apa atiṣṭhan*)—went away, fled far off

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The rain-waters spoken of before (being also his wives) sustain the most excellent energy of this Varuṇa. Varuṇa approaches those waters, which are gratified with the food that is the oblation. Those waters too, as subjects approach their lord the king with fear and devotion, approach Varuṇa their husband, and trembling with fear they flee far from Vṛtra, who envelops them.

##### English translation
They sustain his most excellent energy, he approaches them delighting him with (sacrificial) food; like subjects choosing a king, they smitten with fear, fled from Vritra.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अनुस्तुभं । अनु । चर्चूर्यमाणं । इंद्रं । नि । चिक्कुः । कवयः । मनीषा ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बीभत्सूनां कंपमानावयवानां यद्वा मेघेन बद्धानां । हंति गच्छतीति
> हंसः सूर्यः । तं सयुजं सखायमाहुः । ब्रह्मवादिनः कथयंति । एतदेवाह ।
> दिव्यानां दिवि भवानामांतरिक्षाणामपां सख्ये सखित्वे चरंतं वर्तमानं । अनुष्टुभमनुष्टोभनीयं स्तोतव्यं । यद्वा । अनुष्टुप्यब्बेन तत्संबद्धो यागः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains बीभत्सूनां (*bībhatsūnāṃ*) as "of those whose limbs tremble", or "of those bound by the cloud". हंसः (*haṃsaḥ*) is the sun, because he goes (हंति गच्छतीति (*haṃti gacchatīti*)). The Brahmavādins call him the friend (सयुजं (*sayujaṃ*)). He explains: the sun abides in friendship with the waters of heaven, i.e. those of the atmosphere. अनुष्टुभं (*anuṣṭubhaṃ*) means "to be praised". Or else the word अनुष्टुप् (*anuṣṭup*) signifies the sacrifice connected with it, or praise.

### Printed p. 689

> स्तुतिर्वा लक्ष्यते । अनुष्टुप्संबद्धं यागमनुष्टुप्संदसा युक्तं स्तुतिविशेषं वा ।
> अनुलक्ष्य, चर्चूर्यमाणं पुनःपुनश्चरंतं गच्छंतं ॥ चरतेर्यज्युत्परस्यातः ।
> पा. ७-४-८८ । इत्यभ्यासादुत्तरस्याकारस्योत्वं । चरफलोश्च । पा. ७-४-८७ । इति नुकि
> प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेनाभ्यासस्य रुगागमः ॥ एवंगुणविशिष्टमिंद्रं कवयः क्रांतदर्शिन
> ऋषयो मनीषा मनीषया स्तुत्या नि चिक्क्युः । पूजयंति । यद्वा । मनीषा
> बुद्धा नि चिक्क्युः । जानंति ॥ मनीषाशब्दात्तृतीयायाः सुपां सुलुगिति लुक् ।
> चायै पूजानिशामनयोरित्यस्माच्चांदसे लिटि चायः की । पा. ६-१-३५ । इति
> प्रकृतेः कीभावः । एरनेकाच इति यण् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(continuing) अनुष्टुभं (*anuṣṭubhaṃ*) also means the sacrifice connected with the Anuṣṭubh, or a special praise in Anuṣṭubh metre. चर्चूर्यमाणं (*carcūryamāṇaṃ*) means moving about again and again. Indra, endowed with these qualities, is honoured by the Kavis, the far-seeing seers, with praise (मनीषा (*manīṣā*)); or else they know him by understanding (बुद्धा (*buddhā*)). The rest of the block is grammatical.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बीभत्सूनां (*bībhatsūnāṃ*)—of those trembling with fear
- हंसं (*haṃsaṃ*)—the sun
- सयुजं (*sayujaṃ*)—as a friend
- आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—(the Brahmavādins) say
- दिव्यानां (*divyānāṃ*)—in the atmosphere (in the form of cloud)
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—of the waters
- सख्यॆ (*sakhyè*)—in friendship
- चरंतं (*caraṃtaṃ*)—who abides
- अनुष्टुभं (*anuṣṭubhaṃ*)—worthy of praise, or praised by mantras in Anuṣṭubh metre
- अनु (*anu*)—having regard to the praise
- चर्चूर्यमाणं (*carcūryamāṇaṃ*)—who moves about again and again
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- कवयिः (*kavayiḥ*)—the seers of far-reaching wisdom
- मनीषा (*manīṣā*)—by praise (by understanding)
- नि चिक्कुः (*ni cikkuḥ*)—know

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Brahmavādins say that the sun is the friend of those who tremble with fear. Indra, who abides in friendship with the waters of the atmosphere (of the cloud), who is praised by all, or praised by mantras in Anuṣṭubh metre, and who, having regard to the praise, comes again and again to the worshippers, is known by the seers of far-reaching wisdom through their understanding (or praise).

##### English translation
The sages called the sun the ally of those who are affrighted, abiding in the friendship of the waters of heaven ; the wise have honoured with their praise Indra, who ceaselessly moves after the Anushtubh.

## Sūkta 125 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
Formerly there was a great seer named Ambhṛṇa. He had a daughter named Vāk, accomplished in the knowledge of Brahman. Worshipping the supreme Brahman, who is of the nature of being, consciousness and bliss and pervades all things in the form of the whole world, she came to think herself united (identical) with him, and in this hymn praises herself.

### Printed p. 690
That is, with the sense of identity that she is the all-pervading Supreme Self of the nature of being, consciousness and bliss, she expresses the idea that she herself can perform the immense deeds which the Supreme Self of infinite power can perform, and in this hymn describes herself, that is the Supreme Self, as capable of any work.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अहमित्यष्टर्चं त्रयोदशं सूक्तं । अंभृणस्य महर्षेर्दुहिता वाज्ञामिन्
> ब्रह्मविदुषी स्वात्मानमस्तौत् । अतः सर्षिः । सच्चित्सुखात्मकः सर्वगतः परमात्मा
> देवता । तेन ह्येषा तादात्म्यमनुभवंती सर्वजगद्रूपेण सर्वस्याधिष्ठानत्वेन
> चाहमेव सर्वं भवामीति स्वात्मानं स्तौति । द्वितीया जगती शिष्टाः सप्त त्रिष्टुभः ।
> तथा चानुक्रांतं । अहमष्टौ वागांभृणी तुष्टावात्मानं द्वितीया जगतीति ॥
> गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn अहं (*ahaṃ*) has eight Ṛks and is the thirteenth sūkta. Vāk, daughter of the great seer Ambhṛṇa, knower of Brahman, praised her own Self; therefore she is the seer. The deity is the all-pervading Supreme Self of the nature of being, consciousness and bliss. Experiencing identity with him, she praises herself as the form of the whole world and as the substrate of all: "I alone become everything." The second verse is Jagatī, the other seven Triṣṭubh. So the Anukramaṇī says: अहमष्टौ वागांभृणी तुष्टावात्मानं द्वितीया जगती (*ahamaṣṭau vāgāṃbhṛṇī tuṣṭāvātmānaṃ dvitīyā jagatī*). The application has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This hymn अहं (*ahaṃ*) is the thirteenth sūkta in the tenth anuvāka, with eight Ṛks. In it Vāk, the Brahman-knower, daughter of the seer Ambhṛṇa, praises herself. She is therefore the seer; the deity is the Supreme Self, all-pervading, of the nature of being, consciousness and bliss. Experiencing identity with him, the seer's daughter thinks herself, in the form of the whole world, the doer of all deeds, and praises herself in this hymn. The second Ṛk is in Jagatī metre; the remaining Ṛks are Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says: अहमष्टौ वागांभृणी तुष्टावात्मानं द्वितीया जगती (*ahamaṣṭau vāgāṃbhṛṇī tuṣṭāvātmānaṃ dvitīyā jagatī*). The application has been stated earlier.

##### Particulars

Sūkta 125. Maṇḍala 10, Anuvāka 10, Sūkta 125. Aṣṭaka 8, Adhyāya 7, Vargas 11, 12. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8. Seer: Vāgāmbhṛṇī. Deity: Vāgāmbhṛṇī. Metre: 1, 3–8 Triṣṭubh; 2 Jagatī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒हं रु॒द्रेभि॒र्वसु॑भिश्चराम्य॒हमा॑दि॒त्यैरु॒त वि॒श्वेदे॑वैः ।  
> अ॒हं मि॒त्रावरु॑णो॒भा बि॑भर्म्य॒हमिं॑द्रा॒ग्नी अ॒हम॒श्विनो॒भा॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अहं । रुद्रेभिः । वसुभिः । चरामि । अहं । आदित्यैः । उत । विश्वदेवैः ।  
> अहं । मित्रावरुणा । उभा । बिभर्मि । अहं । इंद्राग्नी इति । अहं । अश्विना । उभा ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अहं सूक्तस्य द्रष्ट्री वागांभृणी यद्ब्रह्म जगत्कारणं तद्रूपा भवंती
> रुद्रेभी रुद्रैरेकादशभिः । इत्थंभावे तृतीया । तदात्मना चरामि । एवं वसुभिरित्यादौ तत्तदात्मना चरामिति योज्यं । तथा मित्रावरुणा मित्रं च वरुणं च ॥
> सुपां सुलुगिति द्वितीयाया आकारः ॥ उभोभावहमेव ब्रह्मीभूता बिभर्मि ।
> धारयामि । इंद्राग्नी अप्यहमेव धारयामि । उभोभावश्विनाश्विनावप्यहमेव
> धारयामि । मयि हि सर्वं जगच्चुक्तौ रजतमिवाध्यस्तं सद्दृश्यते । माया च
> जगदाकारेण विवर्तते । तादृश्या मायया आधारत्वेनासंगस्यापि ब्रह्मण उक्तस्य
> सर्वस्योत्पत्तिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I, Vāk Āmbhṛṇī, the seer of the hymn, being of the form of Brahman, the cause of the world, move (चरामि (*carāmi*)) with the eleven Rudras (रुद्रेभिः (*rudrebhiḥ*), instrumental of state). Likewise with the Vasus and the rest: "I move as each of them." Mitra and Varuṇa, both, I, become Brahman, bear (बिभर्मि (*bibharmi*)); Indra and Agni I bear; the two Aśvins I bear. In me the whole world appears superimposed, like silver on mother-of-pearl, and Māyā evolves in the form of the world; by such Māyā the origin of all is stated even of Brahman, who is unattached, as the support.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I, the seer of this hymn, daughter of Ambhṛṇa, of the form of the supreme Brahman, cause of the world
- रुद्रेभिः (*rudrebhiḥ*)—in the form of the eleven Rudras
- चरामि (*carāmi*)—I move
- वसुभिः (*vasubhiḥ*)—with the eight Vasus
- आदित्यैः (*ādityaiḥ*)—with the twelve Ādityas
- विश्वदेवैः (*viśvadevaiḥ*)—with the forms of all the gods
- (चरामि (*carāmi*)—I move)
- उभौ मित्रा वरुणा (*ubhau mitrā varuṇā*)—the two gods Mitra and Varuṇa
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I myself
- बिभर्मि (*bibharmi*)—bear
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—the two gods Indra and Agni
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I myself bear
- उभौ (*ubhau*)—both
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—the Aśvin gods
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I myself bear and nourish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, the seer of this hymn, daughter of the seer Ambhṛṇa, who have attained identity with the supreme Brahman of the nature of being, consciousness and bliss, move in the form of the eleven Rudras, the eight Vasus, the twelve

### Printed p. 692
Ādityas and of all the other gods. That is, being in the form of these gods, I myself carry out their proper duties. Moreover I myself bear and nourish the paired gods Mitra and Varuṇa, Indra and Agni, and the Aśvins. By my support all these gods, relying on me, become able to perform their duties.

##### English translation
I proceed with the Rudras, with the Vasns, with the Adityas, and with Vishwadevas; I support both Mitra and Varuna, Agni and Indra, and the two Ashwins.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒हं सोम॑माह॒नसं॑ बिभम्य॒हं त्वष्टा॑रमु॒त पू॒षणं॒  ॑
> भगं ।  
> अ॒हं द॑धामि॒ द्रवि॑णं ह॒विष्म॑ते सुप्रा॒व्ये॒३॒॑ ३ यज॑मानाय  ॒
> सुन्वते ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अहं । सोमं । अहनसं । बिभर्मि । अहं । त्वष्टारं । उत । पूषणं । भगं ।  
> अहं । दधामि । द्रविणं । हविष्मते । सुप्र अव्ये । यजमानाय । सुन्वते ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आहनसमाहंतव्यमभिषोतव्यं सोमं यद्वा शत्रूणामाहंतारं दिवि
> वर्तमानं देवतात्मानं सोममहमेव बिभर्मि । तथा तृष्णारमुतापि च पूषणं
> भगं चाहमेव बिभर्मि । तथा हविष्मते हविर्भियुक्ताय सुप्ताव्ये शोभनं
> हनिर्दॆवानां प्रापयित्रे तर्पयित्रे ॥ अवतेस्तर्पणार्थादवित्यस्तंत्रिभ्य ईः ।
> उ. ३-१५८ । इतीकारप्रत्ययः । चतुर्थैकवचने यण्युदात्तस्वॆरितयोर्यणः
> स्वरितोऽनुदात्तस्यॆति सुपः स्वरितत्वं ॥ सुन्वते सोमाभिषवं कुर्वते ॥ शतुरनुम
> इति चतुर्थ्या उदःतत्वं ॥ ईदृशाय यजमानाय द्रविणं धनं यागफलरूपमहमेव धारयामि । एतच्च ब्रह्मणः फलदातृत्वं फलमत उपपत्तेः । ३-२-३८ । इत्यधिकरणे भगवता भाष्यकारेण समर्थितं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

आहनसं (*āhanasaṃ*) is Soma who is to be struck (pressed), or the striker of enemies, existing in heaven as a deity; I alone bear him. Likewise I alone bear Tvaṣṭṛ, and Pūṣan and Bhaga. Likewise to the sacrificer हविष्मते (*haviṣmate*), furnished with oblations, सुप्राव्ये (*suprāvye*), who conveys good oblation to the gods and satisfies them, सुन्वते (*sunvate*), who presses Soma: to such a sacrificer I alone bear (give) wealth (द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*)), the fruit of the sacrifice. That Brahman is the giver of fruit is established by the revered Bhāṣyakāra in the adhikaraṇa फलमत उपपत्तेः । ३-२-३८ (*phalamata upapatteḥ | 3-2-38*). The rest is grammatical.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आहनसं (*āhanasaṃ*)—who, existing in the form of the creeper, is struck with stones and pressed for his juice; or the slayer of enemies
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma, the deity existing in heaven
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I myself
- बिभर्मि (*bibharmi*)—bear and nourish
- त्वष्टारं (*tvaṣṭāraṃ*)—the god Tvaṣṭṛ
- उत (*uta*)—and
- पूषणं (*pūṣaṇaṃ*)—the deity Pūṣan
- भगं (*bhagaṃ*)—the deity Bhaga
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I myself bear and nourish
- हविष्मते (*haviṣmate*)—who has prepared the oblation to offer to the gods
- सुप्राव्ये (*suprāvye*)—who offers the oblation to the gods
- सुन्वते (*sunvate*)—who has pressed the Soma juice for the gods
- यजमानाय (*yajamānāya*)—for the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice
- द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*)—wealth
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- दधामि (*dadhāmi*)—bear, that is, give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I myself bear and nourish Soma, who is pressed after being beaten in the form of the creeper, or Soma who is the slayer of enemies, in heaven, of divine nature. Likewise I myself bear and nourish the gods Tvaṣṭṛ, Pūṣan and Bhaga. And to the sacrificer who prepares the oblation and offers it to the gods, and who presses and offers Soma juice to please the gods, I myself give wealth.

##### English translation
I support the foe-destroying Soma, Twashtri, Pushan and Bhaga; I bestow wealth upon the institutor of the rite offering the oblation, deserving of careful protection, pouring forth the libation.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अहं । राष्ट्री । संगमनी । वसूनां । चिकितुषी । प्रथमा । यज्ञियानां ।  
> तां । मा । देवाः । वि । अदधुः । पुरुत्रा । भूरिस्थात्रां । भूरि । आवेशयंती ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अहं राष्ट्री । ईश्वरनामैतत्। सर्वस्य जगत ईश्वरी । तथा वसूनां धनानां
> संगमनी संगमयित्युपासकानां प्रापयित्री । चिकितुषी यत्साक्षात्कर्तव्यं परं
> ब्रह्म तञ्ञातवती स्वात्मतया साक्षात्कृतवती । अत एव यज्ञियानां यज्ञार्हाणां
> प्रथमा मुख्या । यैवंगुणविशिष्टाहं तां मां भूरिस्थात्रां बहुभावेन प्रपंचात्मनावतिष्ठमानां भूरि भूरीणि बहूनि भूतजातान्यावेशयंती जीवभावेनात्मानं
> प्रवेशयंतीं ईदृशीं मां पुरुत्रा बहुषु देशेषु व्यदधुः । देवा विदधति ।
> कुर्वंति । उक्तप्रकारेण वैश्वरूप्येणावस्थानात् । यद्यत्कुर्वंति तत्सर्वं मामेव
> कुर्वंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"I am the sovereign (राष्ट्री (*rāṣṭrī*))": this is a name for a ruler, so I am the mistress of the whole world. I am also the one who brings together the treasures and gives them to my worshippers. I am the knower (चिकितुषी (*cikituṣī*)): I know the Supreme Brahman, which is to be realised, and have realised it as my own Self. For that reason I am the first, the chief, of those worthy of sacrifice. The gods set me, who am so endowed, in many places. I abide as many things, in the form of the universe, and I cause many beings to enter, taking the form of the individual soul, so that I enter into them. Because I abide in this manifold form, whatever the gods do, they do for me alone.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- राष्ट्री (*rāṣṭrī*)—I am the lord of the whole world
- वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)—of the treasures to be given to the people who worship me
- संगमनी (*saṃgamanī*)—I am the place of their gathering (that is, all the treasures to be given to them are gathered together in me)
- चिकितुषी (*cikituṣī*)—I have known the Supreme Brahman well and realised it
- यज्ञॆयानां (*yajñèyānāṃ*)—among the gods worthy of sacrifice
- प्रथमा (*prathamā*)—I am the chief
- तां (*tāṃ*)—such a one, endowed with these qualities
- भूरिस्थात्रां (*bhūristhātrāṃ*)—existing in the form of the universe through manifold being
- भूरि (*bhūri*)—in manifold beings
- आवेशयंती (*āveśayaṃtī*)—who has entered and dwells
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- पुरुत्रा (*purutrā*)—in many places
- व्यदधुः (*vyadadhuḥ*)—they establish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I am the lord of all people. All the wealth that is to be given to everyone is gathered in me alone. I have known the Supreme Brahman well and have realised him. Among the gods worthy of sacrifice I alone am the chief. I exist in the form of the many things of the world, and I dwell as consciousness in the bodies of beings of many kinds. The gods establish me, such as I am, in many places; that is, they invoke me in many places and worship me.

##### English translation
I am the sovereign queen, the collectress of treasures. cognizant (of the Supreme Being), the chief of objects of worship; as such the gods have

### Printed p. 695
put me in many places, abiding in manifold conditions, entering into numerous (forms).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> योऽन्नमत्ति स भोक्तृशक्तिरूपया मयैवान्नमत्ति । यश्च विपश्यति । आलोकयतीत्यर्थः । यश्च प्राणिति श्वासोच्योस्वादिव्यापारं करोति सोऽपि मय्यव ।
> यश्चोक्तं शृणोति ॥ श्रु श्रवणे । श्रुवः शृ चेति श्रुधातोः शृभावः ॥ य ईदृशीमंतर्यामिरूपेण स्थितां मां न जानंति तेऽमंतवोऽमन्यमाना अजानंत उप
> क्षियंति । उपक्षीणाः संसारेण हीना भवंति ॥ मनेरौणादिकस्तु प्रत्ययः । नञ्चमासे
> व्यत्ययेनांतोदात्तत्वं । यद्वा। भावे तुप्रत्ययः । ततो बहुव्रीहौ नञ्चभ्यामित्युत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं माममंतवो मद्विषयज्ञानरहिता इत्यर्थः ॥ हे श्रुत
> निश्रुत सखे श्रुधि । मया वक्ष्यमाणं शृणु ॥ छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् । श्रुशृणुपृकृवृभ्य इति हेर्धिभावः ॥ किं तच्चोतव्यं । त्रद्विवं । श्रद्धिः श्रद्धा । तया युक्तं ।
> श्रद्धायत्नेन लभ्यमित्यर्थः । श्रदंतरोरुपसर्गवद्वृत्तिरिष्यते । पा. १-४-५७-२ । इति
> श्रच्छब्दस्योपसर्गवद्वर्तमानत्वादुपसर्गे घोः किरिति किप्रत्ययः । मत्त्वर्थीयो
> पः ॥ ईदृशं ब्रह्मात्मकं वस्तु ते शुभ्यं वदामि । उपदिशामि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Whoever eats food eats it through me alone, in the form of the power of the enjoyer. Whoever sees (looks), and whoever breathes, performing the acts of in-breath and out-breath, does so in me alone. Whoever hears what is spoken does so in me too. Those who do not know me, who stand thus as the inner controller, are अमंतवः (*amaṃtavaḥ*), those who do not think or know. They उप क्षियंति (*upa kṣiyaṃti*): they are wasted, and become bereft by saṃsāra. The word अमंतवः (*amaṃtavaḥ*) is formed with an Uṇādi suffix from the root man. Or else the suffix tu is used in the sense of the abstract state; then, in a bahuvrīhi, the final syllable of the second member is acute. The sense is "those devoid of knowledge about me". "O Śruta, O renowned friend, listen: hear what I shall say." What is it that is to be heard? It is श्रद्धिवं (*śraddhivaṃ*), endowed with śraddhi, which is faith; the sense is that it is attained by faithful effort. A thing of this kind, whose nature is Brahman, I tell to you; I instruct you.

- अन्नं (*annaṃ*)—food, or nourishment
- अत्ति (*atti*)—eats
- मया (*mayā*)—that is done through me alone (by my power); likewise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

A man's eating food and other nourishment, seeing with the eye, breathing in and out, and hearing with the ear what another has said: all these activities go on through me alone, that is, by my agency. Those who do not know me, who am present in all beings as the inner controller, meet a downfall. O friend, hear with faith the word that I speak to you.

##### English translation
He who eats food (eats) through me; he who sees, who breathes, who hears what is spoken, does so through me; those who are ignorant of me perish; hear you who has hearing, I tell you that which is deserving of belief.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I myself declare this thing, whose nature is Brahman. It is served by the gods, Indra and the others, and also by human beings. I, being of the nature of this thing, make exalted (उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)), superior to all, whichever man I wish to protect. That same man I make a Brahmā, a creator. I make him a seer (ṛṣi), one who perceives what lies beyond the senses. I make him also सुमेधां (*sumedhāṃ*), of excellent wisdom.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I myself declare that I am that thing whose nature is the Supreme Brahman. That Brahman is served and worshipped by all the gods and by human beings. Moreover, whichever man I wish to protect, I can make him superior to all. I can make him a Brahmā, a creator, a ṛṣi who knows what lies beyond the senses, and a man of excellent wisdom (a sage).

##### English translation
I verily of myself declare this which is approved of by both gods and men ; whomsoever I will. I render formidable. I make him a Bramhan, a Rishi, or a sage.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Formerly, at the time of the conquest of the Three Cities (Tripura), I stretch the bow of Rudra, that is, of Mahādeva (the dative रुद्राय (*rudrāya*) stands in the sense of the genitive); I make it taut with the string. For what purpose? To slay the hater of Brahmins (ब्रह्मद्विषे (*brahmadviṣe*)), the शरवे (*śarave*), the violent one, the asura dwelling in the Three Cities. The particle उ (*u*) is a filler. I alone make समदं (*samadaṃ*): समत् (*samat*) is battle, in which people rejoice together. For the sake of the praising people I alone make battle with their enemies. So too I have entered heaven and earth, as the inner controller.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शरवे (*śarave*)—the violent asura (dweller in the Three Cities)
- हंतवै उ (*haṃtavai u*)—in order to destroy
- रुद्राय (*rudrāya*)—of Rudra
- धनुः (*dhanuḥ*)—the bow
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- आ तनोमि (*ā tanomi*)—I bend (I have bent)
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- जनाय (*janāya*)—for the praising people
- समदं (*samadaṃ*)—battle
- कृणोमि (*kṛṇomi*)—I make
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth (as the inner controller)
- आ विवेश (*ā viveśa*)—I have entered

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

At the time of the destruction of the Three Cities, when Rudra was set on slaying the violent asura who hated Brahmins, I myself bent his bow and made it ready, to be used against the enemies. For the people who praise me, I myself make war. And I have entered heaven and earth (the whole world) as the inner controller.

##### English translation
I bend the bow of Rudra, to slay the destructive enemy of the Brahmanas, I wage war with (hostile) men, I pervade heaven and earth,

> सर्वाणि भुवनानि व्याप्नोमि । अन्यत्समानं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By the śruti "Heaven is the father" the father is heaven. I bring forth (सुवे (*suve*)), I generate, the father, heaven; for the śruti says आत्मन आकाशः संभूतः । तै. आ. ८-१ । इति श्रुतेः । (*ātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ | tai. ā. 8-1 | iti śruteḥ |*) (Tai. Ā. 8-1). Where? "On the head of this Supreme Self": above. In him, who is the cause, the whole body of effects, heaven and the rest, abides like cloth in threads. My source (योनिः (*yoniḥ*)), my cause, is in the ocean (समुद्रे (*samudre*)). The Supreme Self is the ocean, since all beings flow forth from him. In him, within the waters, the pervasive modifications of the mind, is the Brahman-consciousness, and that is my cause. Since I am such, I stand pervading variously, entering all (विश्वा (*viśvā*)) the worlds, the created things. The ātmanepada form is by the rule on sthā with sam, ava, pra, vi. And I touch also that yonder heaven (द्यां (*dyāṃ*)), the world of svarga situated in a remote region. This is indicative: the whole body of modifications so indicated I touch with my own body (वर्ष्णणा (*varṣṇaṇā*)), which is the cause and is made of māyā. Alternatively: above (on the head of) this earth-world I bring forth the father, the ākāśa. In the ocean, the watery expanse, among the waters within, my source, the ṛṣi named Ambhṛṇa, who is the cause, abides. Or else: in the ocean, the atmosphere, in divine bodies made of water, the Brahman-consciousness that is my cause abides. Therefore I, being of the nature of the cause, pervade all the worlds. The rest is the same.

- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Supreme Self
- मूर्धन् (*mūrdhan*)—on the head, that is, in the upper part
- सुवे (*suve*)—I bring forth
- मम (*mama*)—my

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- योनिः (*yoniḥ*)—the place that is the cause
- समुद्रे (*samudre*)—connected with the Supreme Self
- अप्पुअंतः (*appuaṃtaḥ*)—what lies within the workings of the intellect
- ततः (*tataḥ*)—from that cause

- भुवना (*bhuvanā*)—the classes of beings, that is, living creatures

- उप स्पृशामि (*upa spṛśāmi*)—I touch

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I have brought forth heaven in the highest part. Its cause, that is its root, lies hidden in the workings of the Supreme Self's intellect. That is, the intellect of the Supreme Self is itself the cause of this creation. Therefore, entering all creatures as the inner controller, I appear in many kinds of forms. And I touch with my body of māyā even the worlds such as heaven that stand in very lofty regions.

##### English translation
I bring forth the paternal (heaven) upon the brow of this (Supreme Being), my birthplace is in the midst of the waters; from thence I spread through all beings, and touch this heaven with my body.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The meaning of this Ṛk is somewhat difficult, so it is necessary to explain each of its pādas.

अहं सुवे पितरं अस्य मूर्धनि (*ahaṃ suve pitaraṃ asya mūrdhani*)—Here the word पितरं (*pitaraṃ*) has been explained as the world of heaven. On this point the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa says द्यौः पिता ! पृथिवी माता (*dyauḥ pitā ! pṛthivī mātā*) (Tai. Brā. 3-7-5-4): the heavenly world is the father and the earth the mother. For all creatures heaven and earth are like father and mother. "On the head of Brahman": the head is the highest part of the body. Likewise the world of heaven is higher than the earth and other worlds. So the sense of this sentence is: I have created this world of heaven as standing in a very lofty region.

मम योनिः अप्पु अंतः समुद्रे (*mama yoniḥ appu aṃtaḥ samudre*)—योनिः (*yoniḥ*) means place, or that which is the cause. Since the meaning "action" is stated for the word अपः (*apaḥ*) (Ni. 3-9), अप्पु (*appu*) means "in actions". The word समुद्र (*samudra*) has various meanings. Besides the meanings atmosphere and mass of water, the bhāṣyakāra here says समुद्ध्र वंत्यस्माद्भूतजातानीति समुद्रः परमात्मा (*samuddhra vaṃtyasmādbhūtajātānīti samudraḥ paramātmā*): since all classes of beings (creatures) arise from this Supreme Self, the word samudra can bear the meaning "the Supreme Self".

### Printed p. 701
He says so. The sense is that the cause of the creation of the world and the rest lies in the midst of the workings of such a Supreme Self's intellect; that is, the working of the Supreme Self's intellect is itself the cause of the creation of the world and the rest.

Besides, he says: समुद्रे जलधावप्पूदकेष्टंतर्मध्यॆ मम योनिः कारणभूतः अंभृणाख्यऋषिर्वर्तते (*samudre jaladhāvappūdakeṣṭaṃtarmadhyè mama yoniḥ kāraṇabhūtaḥ aṃbhṛṇākhyaṛṣirvartate*)—in the midst of the waters of the sea, the sage named Ambhṛṇa, the cause of my origin, came into being. From Śruti sentences such as आपो वा इदमग्रे सलिलमासन् (*āpo vā idamagre salilamāsan*) it is said that the earth and other worlds and all creatures arose from the waters that existed before creation. So the seeress (Ambhṛṇī) may have said that the middle of the sea, filled with water, is the place of origin for her father and for herself.

Or else: समुद्रेs नरिक्षेऽप्सम्मयेषु देवशरीरेषु मम कारणभूतं ब्रह्म चैतन्यं वर्तते । ततोऽहं कारणात्मिका सती सर्वाणि भुवनानि व्याप्नोमि (*samudres narikṣe 'psammayeṣu devaśarīreṣu mama kāraṇabhūtaṃ brahma caitanyaṃ vartate | tato 'haṃ kāraṇātmikā satī sarvāṇi bhuvanāni vyāpnomi*)—Samudra means the atmosphere; in the atmosphere, in the bodies of the gods whose bodies are made of water, Brahman, the cause of all, exists in the form of consciousness. Therefore that form of consciousness is in me also. The sense of this sentence can be stated thus: I, endowed with such consciousness and being of the nature of the cause, pervade all the worlds.

ततः वि तिष्ठे भुवना अनु विश्वा (*tataḥ vi tiṣṭhe bhuvanā anu viśvā*)—It has been said that the Supreme Brahman is the cause of all. Therefore I, who am of the very nature of the Supreme Brahman, enter all worlds and the classes of creatures in them as inner controller, and appear in many kinds of forms. Like the Śruti sentence अंतः प्रविष्टः शास्ता जनानाग्ं सर्वात्मा (*aṃtaḥ praviṣṭaḥ śāstā janānāgṃ sarvātmā*) (Tai. Ā. 3-11-1) and the Śruti sentence तत्सृष्ट्वा । तदेवानु प्राविशत् (*tatsṛṣṭvā | tadevānu prāviśat*) (Tai. U. 2-6), after creating, the Supreme Self dwells as inner controller, that is in the form of consciousness, in all the things and creatures he has created. Though creatures and things are of many kinds in shape and form, the Supreme Self who is the inner controller in them is one only. Therefore in this sentence it is said वि तिष्ठे (*vi tiṣṭhe*): I appear in many kinds of forms.

उत अमूं द्यां वर्षणा उप स्पृशामि (*uta amūṃ dyāṃ varṣaṇā upa spṛśāmi*)—Here it is said that I can touch this world of heaven. Ordinary men cannot touch with their hands the tops of things higher than themselves. The heavenly world is very high; no one can touch it. But the power and capacity of the Supreme Self are wonderful. However high it be, the Supreme Self can touch it with his power of māyā, that is, with his surpassing power and capacity. For to the Supreme Self, who pervades everything, there is no difference of distance, height and the like, and nothing is impossible. This is the sense.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒हमे॒व वात॑ इव॒ प्र वा॑म्या॒रभ॑माणा॒ भुव॑नानि॒ विश्वा॑ ।  
> प॒रो दि॒वा प॒र ए॒ना पृ॑थि॒व्यैताव॑ती महि॒ना सं ब॑भूव ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अहं । एव । वातः इव । प्र । वामि । अरभमाणा । भुवनानि । विश्वा ।  
> परः । दिवा । परः । एना । पृथिव्या । एतावती । महिना । सं । बभूव ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वा विश्वानि सर्वाणि भुवनानि भूतजातानि कार्याण्यारभमाणा कारणरूपेणोत्पादयंत्यहमेव परेणानधिष्ठिता स्वयमेव प्र वामि । प्रवर्ते । वात इव
> यथा वातः परेणाप्रेरितः सन् स्वेच्छयैव प्रवाति तद्वत् । उक्तं सर्वं निगमयति ।
> परो दिवा । पर इति सकारांतं परस्तादित्यर्थे वर्तते यथाध इत्यधस्तादर्थे ।
> तद्योगे च तृतीया सर्वत्र दृश्यते । दिव आकाशस्य परस्तात्! एना पृथिव्या!! द्वितीयाटौस्वेन इतीदम एनादेशः ॥ अस्याः पृथिव्याः परः परस्तात् । द्यावापृथिव्योरुपादा
> नमुपलक्षणं । एतदुपलक्षितात्सर्वाद्विकारजातात्परस्ताद्वर्तमानासंगोदासीनकूटस्थब्रह्मचैतन्यरूपाहं महिना महिम्मृतावती सं बभूव । एतच्छब्देनोक्तं सर्वं
> परामृश्यते । एत्परिमाणमस्याः ॥ यत्तदेतेभ्यः परिमाणे । पा. ५-२-३९ । इति
> वतुप् । आ सर्वनाम्न इत्यात्वं ॥ सर्वजगदात्मनाहं संभूतास्मि ॥ महच्छब्दादिमनिचि
> टेरिति टलोपः । ततः तृतीयायामुदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण तस्या उदात्तत्वं । छांदसो
> मलोपः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

विश्वा (*viśvā*) means all; I alone, undirected by another, begin and produce all the beings, the created things, in their causal form, and I move of my own accord, like the wind which, unimpelled by another, blows by its own will. He then sums up all that was said. परो दिवा (*paro divā*): पर (*para*) ending in s has the sense "beyond", as अध (*adha*) has the sense "below"; in connection with it the instrumental is seen everywhere. Beyond the sky; एना पृथिव्या (*enā pṛthivyā*)—एन (*ena*) is the substitute for *idam* (in the rule द्वितीयाटौस्वेन (*dvitīyāṭausvena*)). Beyond this earth. The mention of heaven and earth is indicative: I, who am the unattached, indifferent, immutable Brahman-consciousness, existing beyond all this modification-world that they indicate, have come to be so vast महिना (*mahinā*), by greatness. The word एत (*eta*) refers back to everything stated; एतावती (*etāvatī*) means "of this measure". I have come into being as the self of the whole world. (The rest of the block is grammatical.)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाक इव (*vāka iva*)—like the wind that blows of its own will, without another's impulse
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- भुवनानि (*bhuvanāni*)—the worlds and the creatures in them
- आरभमाणा (*ārabhamāṇā*)—producing
- अहमेव (*ahameva*)—I alone, without others' help
- प्र वामि (*pra vāmi*)—I remain steady
- दिवा (*divā*)—from the sky or from the world of heaven
- परः (*paraḥ*)—beyond
- एना पृथिव्याः (*enā pṛthivyāḥ*)—from this vast earth
- परः (*paraḥ*)—beyond
- महिना (*mahinā*)—pervading by my greatness
- एतावती (*etāvatī*)—I who am thus
- संबभूव (*saṃbabhūva*)—I exist everywhere and at all times

### Printed p. 703

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the wind blows of its own will without another's impulse, so I too, without any impulse or control, by my own impulse alone, producing all the worlds and all the creatures in them, remain steady alone, without the help of others. Pervading by my greatness beyond the sky or the heavenly world, and beyond this vast earth (both within and without), I, who am thus, exist at all times and in all regions.

##### English translation
I breathe forth like the wind, giving form to all created worlds; beyond the heaven, beyond this earth (am I), so vast am I in greatness.

## Sūkta 126 (Maṇḍala 10)
Introduction.
Although it is said that in this sūkta the Viśvedevas are praised, three deities in particular are chiefly praised: Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman. Since we have described Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 14, pp. 119-129, there is no need to describe them again here.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> न तमित्यष्टर्चं चतुर्दशं सूक्तं शिलूषपुत्रस्य कुल्मलबर्हिषस्यार्षं
> वामदेवपुत्रस्यांहोमुज्ञान्नो वा । वैश्वदेवं । अष्टमी त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टा उपरिष्वादृहत्यः । त्र्यष्टकद्वादशकवत्युपरिष्वादृहती । अनु. ७-४ । इति हि तल्लक्षणं ।
> तथा चानुक्रांतं । न तं शैलूषः कुल्मलबर्हिषो वामदेव्यो वांहोमुगैश्वदेवमुपरिष्वादार्हतमंत्या त्रिष्टुबिति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta न तं (*na taṃ*) of eight Ṛks is the fourteenth sūkta. Its seer is Kulmalabarhiṣa, son of Śilūṣa, or Aṃhomuc, son of Vāmadeva. The deity is the Viśvedevas. The eighth is triṣṭubh; the rest are upariṣṭādbṛhatī, for which he cites the definition त्र्यष्टकद्वादशकवत्युपरिष्वादृहती (*tryaṣṭakadvādaśakavatyupariṣvādṛhatī*) (Anu. 7-4). He also quotes the Anukramaṇī: न तं शैलूषः कुल्मलबर्हिषो वामदेव्यो वांहोमुगैश्वदेवमुपरिष्वादार्हतमंत्या त्रिष्टुबिति (*na taṃ śailūṣaḥ kulmalabarhiṣo vāmadevyo vāṃhomugaiśvadevamupariṣvādārhatamaṃtyā triṣṭubiti*). The viniyoga has been given already.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta न तं (*na taṃ*) is the fourteenth sūkta in the tenth anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. Its seer is Kulmalabarhiṣa, son of Śilūṣa, or Aṃhomuc, son of the seer Vāmadeva, may be the seer. The deity is the Viśvedevas. The eighth Ṛk of this sūkta is in triṣṭubh metre. The other Ṛks are in the metre called upariṣṭādbṛhatī. In the Ṛks of this metre there are four pādas, the first three having eight syllables each and the

### Printed p. 704
fourth twelve syllables. In the Chandonukramaṇikā it is said: अंत्यश्चेदुपरिष्टाद्वहती (*aṃtyaścedupariṣṭādvahatī*) (Anu. 7-4). In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: न तं शैलूषः कुल्मलबर्हिषो वामदेवो वा०होमुग्वैश्वदेवमुपरिष्टाद्बार्हतमंत्या त्रिष्टुप् (*na taṃ śailūṣaḥ kulmalabarhiṣo vāmadevo vā0homugvaiśvadevamupariṣṭādbārhatamaṃtyā triṣṭup*). The viniyoga was stated earlier.

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 10; Sūkta 126. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 7; Varga 13. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8.
Seer: Kulmalabarhiṣa Śailūṣi, or Aṃhomuc Vāmadevya. Deity: Viśvedevas. Metre: 1-7 upariṣṭādbṛhatī; 8 triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न त मंहो॒ न दु॑रि॒तं देवा॑सो अष्ट॒ मर्त्यं॑ ।  
> स॒जोष॑सो॒ यम॑र्य॒मा मि॒त्रो नयं॑ति॒ वरु॑णो॒ अति॒  ॑
> द्विषः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । तं । अंहः । न । दुःइतं । देवासः । अष्ट । मर्त्य० ।  
> सजोषसः । यं । अर्यमा । मित्रः । नयंति । वरुणः । अति । द्विषः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवासो देवाः ॥ अज्जसेरसुक् ॥ तं मर्त्यं मनुष्यमंहः पापं
> दुरितं तत्फलरूपं दुर्गमनं च नाष्ट । न प्राप्नोति ॥ अशेश्चांदसे लुजि झलो
> झलीति सिचो लोपः । अडभावश्चांदसः ॥ अरीन्नियच्छतीत्यर्यमा प्रमीतेस्रा
> यको देवो मित्रः पापानां निवारयिता देवो वरुणः । एते त्रयो देवाः
> सजोषसः संगताः समानं प्रीयमाणा वा भवंतो द्विषो द्वेष्यञ्चितूनतिक्रम्य
> यं स्तोतारं नयंत्यभिमतं देशं प्रापयंति तं नाष्टेत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O gods! That mortal man, sin (अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)) and its fruit, evil going (दुरितं (*duritaṃ*)), do not reach. अर्यमा (*aryamā*) is the god who restrains enemies, the saviour from death; मित्रः (*mitraḥ*) is the god who removes sins; वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*) is the god who wards off evils. These three gods, united or equally pleased, pass beyond the haters (द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)) and lead the praiser to the desired place. The construction is: sin does not reach him. (The rest is grammatical.)

### Printed p. 705

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—O gods
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—the god Aryaman (who protects from the fear of death)
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—the god Mitra (who removes sin)
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—the god Varuṇa; these three
- सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*)—united, with equal love
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—enemies
- अति (*ati*)—passing beyond, that is, removing
- यं (*yaṃ*)—whichever man
- नयंति (*nayaṃti*)—to the desired place, that is a safe place
- नयंति (*nayaṃti*)—they lead
- तं मर्त्यं (*taṃ martyaṃ*)—that man
- अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)—sin
- दुरितं (*duritaṃ*)—sorrow
- न आष्ट (*na āṣṭa*)—does not obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, these three gods, Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa, united and with equal love, protect from enemies whatever man they lead to his desired place; to that man neither sin nor sorrow comes.

##### English translation
Neither sin nor sorrow, O gods, affect the man whom Aryaman Mitra, and Varuna, being alike pleased by him, conduct beyond (the reach) of) his enemies.
