##### Gist of the bhāṣya

हि (*hi*) is for emphasis: that very protection we choose, we pray for. (The rest of)

### Printed p. 706

> अर्यमन् येन रक्षणेन मर्त्यं स्तोतारमंहसः पापाद्यूयं निः पाथ निशेषेण रक्षथ ॥ पा रक्षणॆ आदादिकः । यद्वृत्तान्नित्यमिति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥ येन
> च रक्षणेन मर्त्यं मनुष्यं स्तोतारं द्विषोऽति नेथ अतीत्य नयथ अभीष्टं प्रापयथ तद्वृणीमह इत्यन्वयः ॥ नयतेश्छांदसः शपो लुक् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes the previous verse: "O Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, by whatever protection you wholly guard the mortal, your worshipper, from sin (अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)), and by which protection you lead him beyond his enemies and bring him what he desires, that very protection we ask for." पा (*pā*) is the root for protecting, of the ādādika class. The यद्वृत्तान्नित्यमिति (*yadvṛttānnityamiti*) rule prevents nighāta (loss of accent). नयतेश्छांदसः शपो लुक् (*nayateśchāṃdasaḥ śapo luk*) is added as a grammatical note on नेथ (*netha*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa
- मित्र (*mitra*)—Mitra
- अर्यमन् (*aryaman*)—Aryaman
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- येन (*yena*)—by which protection of yours
- मर्त्यं (*martyaṃ*)—the human being who praises
- अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)—from sin
- निः पाथ (*niḥ pātha*)—you protect completely
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—his enemies
- अति नेथ (*ati netha*)—you drive away from him
- तत् हि (*tat hi*)—that very protection
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- वृणीमहे (*vṛṇīmahe*)—we pray for

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, by whatever protection of yours you protect from sin the man who praises you, and drive his enemies far away from him, that very protection we ask of you.

##### English translation
We implore that (protection) of yours Varuna, Mitra, andAryaman whereby you preserve a man from sin, and lead him beyond (the reach of) his enemies.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते नू॒नं नो॒ऽयमू॒तये॒ वरु॑णो मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा ।  
> नयि॑ष्ठा उ नो ने॒षणि॒ पर्षि॑ष्ठा उ नः प॒र्षण्यति॒ द्विषः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । नूनं । नः । अयं । ऊतये । वरुणः । मित्रः । अर्यमा ।  
> नयिष्ठाः । ऊं इति । नः । नेषणि । पर्षिष्ठाः । ऊं इति । नः । पर्षणि । अति । द्विषः॥

### Printed p. 707

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं वरुणो मित्रश्चार्यमा च देवा नोऽस्माकमूतये रक्षणाय
> नूनमवश्यं भवंतु । नेषणि नेतव्ये विषये हे वरुणादयः यूयं नोऽस्मान्नयिष्ठाः । नयत ॥ वचनव्यत्ययः । यद्वा । प्रत्येकाभिप्रायेणैकवचनं । छांदसो
> लुज् ॥ उशब्दः समुच्चये पदपूरणार्थो वा । पर्षणि पारयितव्ये विषये
> नोऽस्मान्द्विषोऽति पर्षिष्ठाः । अतिपारयथ ॥ नयिष्ठा इतिवत्प्रक्रिया ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May this Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman surely be for our protection (ऊतये (*ūtaye*)). In the matter to which we are to be led (नेषणि (*neṣaṇi*)), O Varuṇa and the rest, lead us (नयिष्ठाः (*nayiṣṭhāḥ*) = नयत (*nayata*)); the number is altered, or else the singular is used with each deity separately in view; the lun-type aorist is Vedic. The word उ (*u*) is for combining, or is a filler. In the matter to be crossed over (पर्षणि (*parṣaṇi*)), take us across, beyond our enemies (पर्षिष्ठाः (*parṣiṣṭhāḥ*) = अतिपारयथ (*atipārayatha*)). The derivation is like that of नयिष्ठा (*nayiṣṭhā*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अयं वरुणः (*ayaṃ varuṇaḥ*)—this Varuṇa
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- आर्यमा (*āryamā*)—Aryaman
- ते (*te*)—these three
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—let them be surely (O Varuṇa and the rest) you
- नेषणि (*neṣaṇi*)—to the region we must go and reach
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- नयिष्ठाः (*nayiṣṭhāḥ*)—lead
- उ (*u*)—and
- पर्षणि (*parṣaṇi*)—to the region we must cross over to
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- द्विषः अति (*dviṣaḥ ati*)—far from enemies
- पर्पिष्ठाः (*parpiṣṭhāḥ*)—carry across

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May these three deities, Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman, be for our protection. O Varuṇa and the rest, lead us to the region we must go and reach, and take us across to the region we must cross over to, carrying us so that we are far from our enemies.

##### English translation
May this Varuna and Mitra and Aryaman be our protection, may they lead us to the spot to which we should be led, and make us cross over to the spot to which we should cross over beyond (the reach of) our enemies.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यू॒यं विश्वं॒ परि॑ पाथ॒ वरु॑णो मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा ।  
> यु॒ष्माकं॒ शर्म॑णि प्रि॒ये स्याम॑ सुप्रणीत॒योऽति॒ द्विषः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यूयं । विश्वं । परि । पाथ । वरुणः । मित्रः । अर्यमा ।  
> युष्माकं । शर्मणि । प्रिये । स्याम । सुप्रनीतयः । अति । द्विषः ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 708

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवा वरुणादयः यूयं विश्वं सर्वं जगत्परि पाथ । परितो रक्षथ । हे
> सुप्रणीतयः शोभनप्रणयना मित्रादयः युष्माकं युष्मदीये युष्माभिर्दत्ते प्रियेऽनुकूले वेद्ये शर्मणि सुखे वयं स्याम । भवेम । द्विषो
> द्वेष्टांश्चाति क्रामेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O gods, Varuṇa and the rest, you protect the whole world (विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)) on all sides. O सुप्रणीतयः (*supraṇītayaḥ*), Mitra and the rest, excellent leaders, may we be (स्याम (*syāma*)) in your dear, favourable, ordained happiness, given by you; and may we overcome those who hate us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Varuṇa and the other gods) यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—the whole world
- परि (*pari*)—all around
- पाथ (*pātha*)—protect
- सुप्रणीतयः (*supraṇītayaḥ*)—O Mitra and the rest, excellent guides
- युष्माकं (*yuṣmākaṃ*)—your, or to you
- प्रिये (*priye*)—favourable
- शर्मणि (*śarmaṇi*)—in happiness
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we be
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—hating enemies
- अति (*ati*)—may we overcome (subdue)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa and the other gods, protect the whole world well on every side. O Mitra and the rest, excellent guides, may we be in the happiness that is dear to you; that is, by your grace may we be happy, and may we subdue the enemies who hate us.

##### English translation
You, Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman, protect the universe; may we abide in your blessed felicity, O excellent leaders, beyond (the reach of) our enemies.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒दि॒त्यासो॒ अति॒ स्त्रिधो॒ वरु॑णो मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा ।  
> उ॒ग्रं म॒रुद्भी॑ रु॒द्रं हु॑वे॒मेंद्र॑म॒ग्निं स्व॒स्तयेऽति॒ द्विषः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आदित्यासः । अति । स्रिधः । वरुणः । मित्रः । अर्यमा ।  
> उग्रं । मरुत्भिः । रुद्रं । हुवेम । इंद्रं । अग्निं । स्वस्तये । अति । द्विषः ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 709

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आदित्यासोऽदितेः पुत्रा वरुणादयो देवाः स्त्रिधो हिंसकाञ्त्यत्रूनस्मानति
> नयंतु । मरुद्भिः पुत्रैः सहितमुग्रमुद्दूर्णतेजसं रुद्रमिंद्रमग्निं च स्वस्तये
> क्षेमाय हुवेम । आह्वयेमहि ॥ ह्वयतेराशीर्लिजि बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणं।
> लिज्याशिष्यज् ॥ आहूतास्तेऽस्मान्द्विषो, द्वेष्ट नति नयंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May the Ādityas, sons of Aditi, the gods Varuṇa and the rest, lead us beyond (अति (*ati*)) our hostile foes (स्त्रिधः (*stridhaḥ*)). For our welfare (स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)) we invoke (हुवेम (*huvema*) = आह्वयेमहि (*āhvayemahi*)) the fierce (उग्रं (*ugraṃ*), of raised-up splendour) Rudra, together with the Maruts, his sons, and Indra and Agni. Having been invoked, may they lead us beyond our enemies. The remaining sentences give the grammar of हुवेम (*huvema*) (samprasāraṇa in the benedictive lin, and so on).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आदित्यासः (*ādityāsaḥ*)—the sons of Aditi
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—Aryaman, these three
- स्त्रिधः (*stridhaḥ*)—hostile enemies
- अति (*ati*)—passing beyond (far from them) (नयंतु (*nayaṃtu*)—let them carry us)
- मरुद्भिः (*marudbhiḥ*)—accompanied by the Maruts, his sons
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—of great splendour
- रुद्रं (*rudraṃ*)—Rudra
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for our welfare
- हुवेम (*huvema*)—we pray and call
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—our enemies
- अति (*ati*)—passing beyond (नयंतु (*nayaṃtu*)—let them carry us)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May these gods, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, sons of Aditi, carry us far away so that we do not fall into the hands of our enemies. We pray and call, for our welfare, Rudra, who is accompanied by the Maruts, his sons, and endowed with exceeding splendour, and also Indra and Agni. May they carry us far from our enemies.

##### English translation
May the Adityas, Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman, (lead us) beyond (the reach of) the malignant; let us invoke the fierce Rudra with the Maruts, and Indra and Agni for our welfare, that they may place us) beyond (the reach of) our enemies.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नेता॑र ऊ॒ षु ण॑स्ति॒रो वरु॑णो मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा ।  
> अति॒ विश्वा॑नि दुरि॒ता राजा॑नश्चर्यणी॒नामति॒ द्विषः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 710

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नेतारः । ऊं इति । सु । नः । तिरः । वरुणः । मित्रः । आर्यमा ।  
> अति । विश्वानि । दुःइता । राजानः । चर्षणीनां । अति । द्विषः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नेतारो नयनकुशलाः ॥ नयतेः साधुकारिणि तृन् ॥ वरुणादयो देवा
> नोऽस्माकं पापानि सु सुष्टु तिरस्तिरोधानमदर्शनं नयंतु । उ इति पूरणः ।
> चर्षणीनां मनुष्याणां राजानः स्वामिनो वरुणादयो देवा विश्वानि सर्वाणि
> दुरिता दुरितानि दुर्गमनानि पापफलरूपाण्यस्मानति नयंतु । द्विषो द्वेष्टात्रूंश्चाति नयंतु ॥ नामन्यतरस्यामिति चर्षणिशब्दात्परस्यॆ नाम उदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

नेतारः (*netāraḥ*) are those skilled in leading. May the gods Varuṇa and the rest lead our sins (पापानि (*pāpāni*)) well (सु (*su*)) into disappearance (तिरः (*tiraḥ*)), out of sight; उ (*u*) is a filler. May Varuṇa and the rest, the gods who are lords (राजानः (*rājānaḥ*)) of men (चर्षणीनां (*carṣaṇīnāṃ*)), lead us beyond all (विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)) hardships (दुरिता (*duritā*)), that is, the difficult-to-traverse results of sin, and lead us beyond our enemies. The last sentence is an accent note.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नेतारः (*netāraḥ*)—good guides
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—Aryaman
- नः (*naḥ*)—our sins
- सु (*su*)—well
- तिरः (*tiraḥ*)—let them remove out of sight
- उ (*u*)—and
- चर्षणीनां (*carṣaṇīnāṃ*)—for humans
- राजानः (*rājānaḥ*)—the gods Varuṇa and the rest, who are lords
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- दुरितानि (*duritāni*)—sorrows
- अति (*ati*)—let them drive away
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—enemies
- अति (*ati*)—let them drive far away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May these gods Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman, who lead humans on the good path, remove our sins completely; may these gods, Varuṇa and the rest, lords of humans, remove all our sorrows and drive our enemies far away.

##### English translation
May the leaders Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman, (lead) us apart (from wickedness), may the kings of men lead us beyond all calamities, beyond (the reach of) of our enemies.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शु॒नम॒स्मभ्य॑मू॒तये॒ वरु॑णो मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा ।  
> शर्म॑ यच्छंतु स॒प्रथ॑ आदि॒त्यासो॒ यदीम॑हे॒ अति॒ द्विषः॑ ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शुनं । अस्मभ्यं । ऊतये । वरुणः । मित्रः । आर्यमा ।  
> शर्म । यच्छंतु । सप्रथः । आदित्यासः । यत् । ईमहे । अति । द्विषः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वरुणादयो देवा ऊतये रक्षायै शुनं सुखमस्मभ्यं स्तोतृभ्यः
> प्रयच्छंतु । तथादित्यासोऽदितेः पुत्रास्ते सप्रथः सर्वतः पृथु विस्तीर्णं शर्म
> सुखं च यच्छंतु । अस्मभ्यं ददतु । यच्छर्म वयमीमहे याचामहे । द्विषश्चाति नयंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May Varuṇa and the other gods give happiness (शुनं (*śunaṃ*)) to us, the worshippers, for our protection (ऊतये (*ūtaye*)). Likewise may the Ādityas, sons of Aditi, give widely extended (सप्रथः (*saprathaḥ*)) happiness (शर्म (*śarma*)), the happiness that we ask for (ईमहे (*īmahe*)); and may they lead us beyond our enemies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—Mitra
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—Aryaman, these three
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for our protection
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—happiness
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—let them give to us who are praising
- आदित्यासः (*ādityāsaḥ*)—these Varuṇa and the rest, sons of Aditi
- सप्रथः (*saprathaḥ*)—in all the extended regions
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever happiness
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we ask for, such
- शर्म (*śarma*)—happiness
- यच्छंतु (*yacchaṃtu*)—let them give us
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—our enemies
- अति (*ati*)—let them drive far away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May these gods Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman give happiness to us who praise them, for our protection. May these Varuṇa and the rest, sons of Aditi, give us, in all these extended regions, whatever kind of happiness we ask for. May they drive our enemies far away.

##### English translation
May Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman (bestow) upon us felicity for our protection; may the Adityas grant us that adundant happiness which we solicit, (and lead us) beyond (the reach of) our enemies.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यथा॑ ह॒ त्यद्व॑सवो गौ॒र्यं॑ चित्प॒दि षि॒ताममुं॑चता यजत्राः ।

### Printed p. 712

> एवो ष्वग्‌स्मन्मुंचता व्यंहः प्रतार्यग्ने प्रतरं न आयुः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यथा । ह । त्यत् । वसवः । गौर्यं । चित् । पदि । सितां । अमुंचत । यजत्राः ।  
> एवो इति । सु । अस्मत् । मुंचत । वि । अंहः । प्र । तारि । अग्ने । प्रतरं । नः ।  
> आयुः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वसवो वासका हे यजत्रा यागार्हा मित्रादयो देवाः ॥ अमिनक्षीत्यादिना । उ. ३-१०५ । यजेरत्रन्प्रत्ययः ॥ त्यत् ते प्रसिद्धा यूयं ॥ सुपां
> सुलुगिति विभक्तेर्लुक् ॥ यथा ह यथा खलु पदि पादे सितां बद्धां ॥ पद्दन्नित्यादिना
> पादशब्दस्य पदादेशः । ऊडिदंपदादीत्यादिना सप्तम्या उदात्तत्वं । षिञ् बंधन
> इत्यस्मान्निष्ठा ॥ ईदृशीं गौर्यं गौरीं गौरवर्णां सोमक्रयणीं गां ॥ षिङ् रादिभ्यश्चति जीष् । अमि पूर्व इत्यत्र वा छंदसीत्यनुवर्तनात्पूर्वरूपस्य पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घस्य चाभावे यण् । उदाद्तस्वरितयोर्यण इति परस्यानुदात्तस्य स्वरितत्वं ॥
> ईदृशीं गाममुंचत यथा खलु यूयं विश्वावसोर्गंधर्वान्मोचितवंतः एवो
> एवमेवास्मदस्मैत्तोऽहः पापं सुष्टु वि मुंचत । विश्लेषयत । हे अग्ने नोऽस्माकमायुर्जीवनं प्रतरं प्र तारि । प्रकर्षण त्वया प्रवर्धतां । प्रपूर्वस्तिरतिर्वर्धनार्थः ॥ प्रशब्दात्तरष्यमु च च्छंदसीत्यमुप्रत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the Vasus, the "dwellers" or "those who cause dwelling", and the Yajatras, the deities Mitra and the rest, who are worthy of sacrifice; यजेरत्रन्प्रत्ययः (*yajeratranpratyayaḥ*). त्यत् (*tyat*) means "you who are well known". यथा ह (*yathā ha*) means "just as indeed", and पदि सितां (*padi sitāṃ*) means "bound by the foot". The cow is गौर्यं (*gauryaṃ*), a cow of pale (gaura) colour, the one used for buying Soma. "As you released such a cow from the Gandharva Viśvāvasu, even so (एवो (*evo*)) release the sin (अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)) from us well." He then says: O Agni, let our life be greatly prolonged by you; the verb प्र तारि (*pra tāri*) has the sense of increase.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसवः (*vasavaḥ*)—(you) who give dwelling, or who dwell everywhere
- यजत्राः (*yajatrāḥ*)—worthy of sacrifice; O Mitra and the other deities
- त्यत् (*tyat*)—you, the well known
- पदि (*padi*)—by the foot
- सितां (*sitāṃ*)—bound (with a rope)
- गौर्यं चित् (*gauryaṃ cit*)—the cow of pale colour
- यथा ह (*yathā ha*)—in which manner
- अमुंचत (*amuṃcata*)—you released
- एवो (*evo*)—in that same manner
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—from us
- अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)—our sins
- सु (*su*)—well
- वि मुंचत (*vi muṃcata*)—release (remove)
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—life (the time of living)
- प्रतरं (*prataraṃ*)—extended, for a long time
- प्रतारि (*pratāri*)—let it be increased by you

### Printed p. 713

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and the other deities, givers of dwelling or all-pervading, worthy of sacrifice: as you, the well known, released the pale cow whose foot was bound with a rope, even so remove our sins from us. O Agni, increase the measure of our life so that we may live long.

##### English translation
As you, adorable Vasus, set free the cow fastened by her foot, even so remove sin away from us, and prolong, Agni, our protracted life.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Formerly, when Soma was in heaven, the gods prayed to the metres in order to fetch it, and of them the Gāyatrī metre, in the form of a falcon, brought the Soma plants to earth. While it was bringing them, a Gandharva named Viśvāvasu snatched the Soma plants on the way. Then the gods gave a pale cow to Viśvāvasu and got the Soma plants back from him by purchase. The Gandharva had kept the cow he had received in exchange for the Soma plant bound, with a rope tied to its foot. There is an ancient story that, at the cow's prayer, the Viśvedevas Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman loosed the cow's bond and freed it. This is what is indicated here by the sentence गौर्यं चित्पदि षिताममुंचत (*gauryaṃ citpadi ṣitāmamuṃcata*).

## Sūkta 127 (Maṇḍala 10)
In this sūkta Night is praised. Although verses praising Night occur here and there in other sūktas, apart from this there is no complete sūkta praising Night. This sūkta has eight Ṛks. Some khila mantras (supplementary mantras) to be recited at the end of this sūkta also praise Night. Some of these khila mantras appear to be very ancient, because, when explaining the meaning of the word rātri, Yāska cites one of these khila mantras as an example and gives its Nirukta. Therefore

### Printed p. 714
these khila mantras can be said to have been in use in very early times, that is, in Yāska's time. Even now it is customary to recite this sūkta together with some khila mantras belonging to it as the Rātrisūkta. Yāska explains the etymology of the word rātri thus:
रात्रिः कस्मात् प्ररमयति भूतानि नक्तंचारीण्युपरमयतीतराणि ध्रुवीकरोति । रातेर्वा स्याद्दानकर्मणः प्रदेयंतेऽस्यामवश्यायाः ॥ (*rātriḥ kasmāt praramayati bhūtāni naktaṃcārīṇyuparamayatītarāṇi dhruvīkaroti | rātervā syāddānakarmaṇaḥ pradeyaṃte 'syāmavaśyāyāḥ ‖*) (Ni. 2-18)
What is rātri, and how did the word arise?
प्ररमयति भूतानि नक्तं चारीणि (*praramayati bhūtāni naktaṃ cārīṇi*)—When this Night arrives, it gladdens certain creatures, namely forest wild beasts, piśācas and the like, and the asuras that roam at night. Since their roaming and sporting take place only at night, these beings naturally rejoice when day has passed and night has come. Therefore it is said here that Night delights certain beings and the creatures that move about at night.
उपरमयतीतराणि ध्रुवीकरोति (*uparamayatītarāṇi dhruvīkaroti*)—Likewise, as soon as night arrives it makes the other creatures, that is, human beings and the like, stop their own work and rest. Since at night there is no light, seeing with the eye is not possible; therefore human beings and others do nothing at that time but stay fixed in one place, that is, they sleep. The meaning is that they do not move about and so on.
रातेर्वा स्याद्दानकर्मणः प्रदीयंतेऽस्यामवश्यायाः (*rātervā syāddānakarmaṇaḥ pradīyaṃte 'syāmavaśyāyāḥ*)—This word rātri is derived from the root rā-dāne, meaning "to give". What is given? At night, because there is no heat of the sun, dew falls from the atmosphere. Because there is a giving or production of this dew, which of necessity falls, it is called rātri; this is the purport of the etymology.
तस्यैषा भवति । आ रात्रि पार्थिवं रजः पितुरः प्रायि धामभिः । दिवः सदांसि बृहती वि तिष्ठस आ त्वेषं वर्तते तमः ॥ (*tasyaiṣā bhavati | ā rātri pārthivaṃ rajaḥ pituraḥ prāyi dhāmabhiḥ | divaḥ sadāṃsi bṛhatī vi tiṣṭhasa ā tveṣaṃ vartate tamaḥ ‖*) आ पूपुरस्त्वं रात्रि पार्थिवं रजः—स्थानैर्मध्यमस्य दिवः सदांसि बृहती महती वितिष्ठस आवर्तते त्वेषं तमोरजः ॥ (*ā pūpurastvaṃ rātri pārthivaṃ rajaḥ—sthānairmadhyamasya divaḥ sadāṃsi bṛhatī mahatī vitiṣṭhasa āvartate tveṣaṃ tamorajaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 9-29)
This Ṛk, which contains the word rātri and praises Night, is given here as an example. This mantra beginning आ रात्रि (*ā rātri*) is not in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā. It is stated in the khila mantras that belong, as it were, to the 127th sūkta of the 10th maṇḍala which praises Night (the first mantra of the 26th khila sūkta).

### Printed p. 715
आपूपुरस्त्वं रात्रि पार्थिवं रजः (*āpūpurastvaṃ rātri pārthivaṃ rajaḥ*)—O Night, you (with your darkness) have filled the world of the earth, and स्थानैर्मध्यमस्य दिवः सदांसि (*sthānairmadhyamasya divaḥ sadāṃsi*) the places of the atmosphere and of heaven. O Night of great majesty, the fearful darkness, covering all regions, draws everything to your vicinity; this is the purport of the etymology.
Concerning the greatness and the use of the Rātrisūkta, the great sage Śaunaka says in his work Ṛgvidhāna:
रात्रीं प्रपद्येत सदा शुचिश्चीर्णव्रतो निशि ॥ २० ॥ (*rātrīṃ prapadyeta sadā śuciścīrṇavrato niśi ‖ 20 ‖*)
यः कामयेत न पुनर्जायेयमिति योनिषु । (*yaḥ kāmayeta na punarjāyeyamiti yoniṣu |*)
सहस्रकृत्तो मनसा जपेद्रातीति रात्रिषु ॥ २१ ॥ (*sahasrakṛtto manasā japedrātīti rātriṣu ‖ 21 ‖*)
स्थालीपाकेन रात्रीं च यजीताहरहर्निशि । (*sthālīpākena rātrīṃ ca yajītāharaharniśi |*)
तन्नना निशि चासीनस्तिष्ठेदहनि धार्मिकः ॥ २२ ॥ (*tannanā niśi cāsīnastiṣṭhedahani dhārmikaḥ ‖ 22 ‖*)
ऊर्ध्वं संवत्सराच्चैव चरुं पयसि संस्कृतं । (*ūrdhvaṃ saṃvatsarāccaiva caruṃ payasi saṃskṛtaṃ |*)
सहस्रकृत्वस्वतेन दिवा होमो विधीयते ॥ २३ ॥ (*sahasrakṛtvasvatena divā homo vidhīyate ‖ 23 ‖*)
जुहुयान्निशि पूर्वस्मिन् रात्रिभागे समाहितः । (*juhuyānniśi pūrvasmin rātribhāge samāhitaḥ |*)
दिवा चावश्यकं कार्यं छायायामंशुतेजसा ॥ २४ ॥ (*divā cāvaśyakaṃ kāryaṃ chāyāyāmaṃśutejasā ‖ 24 ‖*)
इति प्रयत आत्मावान्नूक्तं तु मनसा जपेत् । (*iti prayata ātmāvānnūktaṃ tu manasā japet |*)
संवत्सरे तृतीये तु सर्पिषा साधयेच्चरुं ॥ २५ ॥ (*saṃvatsare tṛtīye tu sarpiṣā sādhayeccaruṃ ‖ 25 ‖*)
अथास्य वरदा देवी रात्रिर्भवति शर्वरी । (*athāsya varadā devī rātrirbhavati śarvarī |*)
विज्ञापयीत तां देवीं वरदां स्वयमागतां ॥ २६ ॥ (*vijñāpayīta tāṃ devīṃ varadāṃ svayamāgatāṃ ‖ 26 ‖*)
संवत्सर ऋतौ मासि दिवसेऽस्मिन् क्षणेऽपि वा । (*saṃvatsara ṛtau māsi divase 'smin kṣaṇe 'pi vā |*)
प्रयाणकालो भविता तव वत्सेति वत्सला ॥ २७ ॥ (*prayāṇakālo bhavitā tava vatseti vatsalā ‖ 27 ‖*)
रात्रीसूक्तं जपन्नेव तं कालं प्रतिपद्यते । (*rātrīsūktaṃ japanneva taṃ kālaṃ pratipadyate |*)
न योनिं पुनरायाति सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥ २८ ॥ (*na yoniṃ punarāyāti sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ‖ 28 ‖*)
(Ṛgvidhāna, Adhyāya 4, Ślokas 20-28)
To recite this Rātrīsūkta, one must always be purified, wearing a clean (washed) garment, and recite it at night. A man who desires, "May I not be born again in the wombs of various creatures; may I attain liberation without return",

### Printed p. 716
should recite this Rātrīsūkta mentally a thousand times at night. Every day, at night, he should make a homa with the mantras of this Rātrīsūkta in the established fire by the sthālīpāka procedure; at night and by day he should always keep meditating on the goddess Night in his mind. Having done this for one year, he should then prepare a milk-mixed caru and perform a thousand homas in the daytime. While performing the homa he should do it in the first part of the night, that is, while there is still a little sunlight, and he should keep reciting the sūkta mentally during the homa. Having done so in the second year, then in the third year he should perform the homa with the caru mixed with ghee. If he does so, the goddess Night appears before that practitioner and becomes ready to grant a boon. Then the practitioner should pray thus to the goddess who has come to bestow a boon on him: "O goddess, if from here onward, whether within a year, or a season, or a month, or a day, or even at this very moment, my time of departure (the time of death) should arrive, do you in compassion avert it. I am a son dear to you." By praying thus and reciting the Rātrīsūkta he becomes able to ward off the calamity (that time of death) that might befall him. And a man who dies while reciting the Rātrīsūkta is freed from all sins and is not born again in a womb. Such is the account.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रात्रित्यष्टर्चं प चदतं सूक्तं सोभरिपुत्रस्य कुशिकस्यार्षं । यद्वा । भारद्वाजस्य सुता रात्र्याख्यास्य सूक्तस्यर्षिका । गायत्रं रात्रि देवताकं । कथा चानुक्रांतं । रात्रि कुशिकः सौभरो रात्रिर्वा भारद्वाजी रात्रिस्तवं गायत्रमिति ॥ दुःस्वप्नदर्शन उपोषितेन कर्त्रा पायसेन होतव्यं । तत्रैतत्तूक्तं करणत्वेन विनियुक्तं ।
> तथा चारण्यके श्रूयते । स यद्येतेषां किंचित्पश्येदुपोष्य पायसं स्थालीपाकं
> श्रपयित्वा रात्रिसूक्तेन प्रत्यृचं हुत्वा । ऐ. आ. ३-२-४ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta रात्रित्यष्टर्चं (*rātrityaṣṭarcaṃ*) has eight Ṛks and is the fifteenth sūkta of the anuvāka. Its seer is Kuśika, son of Sobhari; or else the seer is Rātri, daughter of Bharadvāja. The deity is Rātri and the metre Gāyatrī. The Anukramaṇī says: रात्रि कुशिकः सौभरो रात्रिर्वा भारद्वाजी रात्रिस्तवं गायत्रं (*rātri kuśikaḥ saubharo rātrirvā bhāradvājī rātristavaṃ gāyatraṃ*). Use: on seeing a bad dream, the performer, having fasted, is to make an offering of pāyasa; this sūkta is applied as the instrument. So it is heard in the Āraṇyaka: स यद्येतेषां किंचित्पश्येदुपोष्य पायसं स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वा रात्रिसूक्तेन प्रत्यृचं हुत्वा । (*sa yadyeteṣāṃ kiṃcitpaśyedupoṣya pāyasaṃ sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā rātrisūktena pratyṛcaṃ hutvā |*) (Ai. Ā. 3-2-4).

Anuvāda: this sūkta Rātrī is the fifteenth sūkta in the tenth anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. Its seer is Kuśika, son of Sobhari; or the woman named Rātri, daughter of the sage Bharadvāja, may be the seer of this sūkta. Its deity is Rātri; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: रात्रि कुशिकः सौभरो रात्रिर्वा भारद्वाजी रात्रिस्तवं गायत्रं (*rātri kuśikaḥ saubharo rātrirvā bhāradvājī rātristavaṃ gāyatraṃ*). Bad dreams: on seeing them, one who has fasted

### Printed p. 717
is to make a homa in the fire with pāyasa. That the mantras of this sūkta are to be recited for the homa is stated in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka: स यद्यतेषां किंचित्पश्येदुपोष्य पायसं स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वा रात्रीसूक्तेन प्रत्यृचं हुत्वा (*sa yadyateṣāṃ kiṃcitpaśyedupoṣya pāyasaṃ sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā rātrīsūktena pratyṛcaṃ hutvā*) (Ā. Ai. 3-2-4).
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 10; Sūkta 127; Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 7; Varga 14. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8. Ṛṣi: Kuśika Saubhara, or Rātri Bhāradvājī. Deity: Rātristava. Metre: Gāyatrī.
#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> रात्री॒ व्य॑ख्यदाय॒ती पु॑रु॒त्रा दे॒व्य१॒॑ १ क्षभिः॑ ।  
> विश्वा॒ अधि॒ श्रीयो॑ऽधित ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> रात्री । वि । अख्यत् । आयती । पुरुत्रा । देवी । अक्षभिः ।  
> विश्वाः । अधि । श्रियः । अधित ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आयत्यागच्छंती ॥ आज्पूर्वादेतेः शतर्यदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । इणो यण्णिति
> यणादेशः । उगितश्चति जीप् । शतुरनुम इति नद्या उदात्तत्वं ॥ अक्षभिरक्षिस्थानीयैः
> प्रकाशमानैनर्नक्षत्रैः ॥ छंदस्यपि दृश्यत इत्यक्षिशब्दस्यानजादेशः ॥ यद्वा। अक्षभिरंजकैस्तेजोभिः । पुरुत्रा बहुषु देशेषु देवी देवनशीला ॥ देवमनुष्यपुरुषपुरुमर्त्येभ्य इत्यादिना पुरुषब्दात्सप्तम्यर्थे त्राप्रत्ययः ॥ रात्रीयं रात्रिदेवता
> व्यख्यत् । विचष्टे । विशेषेण पश्यति ॥ रात्रेश्चाजसाविति जीप् । ख्यातेश्चांदसे
> लुज्यस्यतिवक्तीत्यादिना चेरजादेशः ॥ अपि चैषा विश्वाः सर्वाः श्रियः शोभा अध्यधित ।
> अधिधारयति ॥ दधातेर्लुजि स्थाघ्वोरिच्छेतीत्वं । सिचः कित्वं । ह्रस्वादंगादिति
> सिचो लोपः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

आयती (*āyatī*) is "coming", from ā + the root i with śatṛ; the sūtras on the lopa of śap, the yaṇ substitution and the nadī accent are given. अक्षभिः (*akṣabhiḥ*) means by the stars, shining like eyes in place (of the eyes); the word akṣi takes the substitute aja. Or else अक्षभिः (*akṣabhiḥ*) means by colouring lights. पुरुत्रा (*purutrā*) means in many places; देवी (*devī*) is "of shining nature"; the affix trā is added to puru in the locative sense. This Night-deity व्यख्यत् (*vyakhyat*), looks about, sees in particular. Moreover she अध्यधित (*adhyadhita*), puts on, all (विश्वाः (*viśvāḥ*)) splendours (श्रियः (*śriyaḥ*)); the verb is from dhā in the luṅ aorist.

### Printed p. 718

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आयती (*āyatī*)—the approaching
- रात्रि देवी (*rātri devī*)—the goddess Night
- पुरुत्रा (*purutrā*)—in many regions
- अक्षभिः (*akṣabhiḥ*)—with her eyes, the shining stars
- व्यख्यत् (*vyakhyat*)—she looks about in particular
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- श्रियः (*śriyaḥ*)—excesses of beauty
- अधि अधित (*adhi adhita*)—she wears

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The goddess Night, who has just now come, looks about in many regions with her eyes, the shining stars. She shines with all her splendour and other adornments.

##### English translation
The divine Night approaching looked upon many places with her eyes,
she has assumed all beauties.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ओर्व॑प्रा॒ अम॑त्या नि॒वतो॑ दे॒व्यु१॒॑ १ द्वतः॑ ।  
> ज्योति॑षा बाधते॒ तमः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । उरु । अप्राः । अमत्यार् । निवतः । देवी । उत्वतः ।  
> ज्योतिषा । बाधते । तमः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अमर्त्या मरणरहिता देवी देवनशीला रात्रिरुरु विस्तीर्णमंतरिक्षमाप्राः ।
> प्रथमतस्तमसापूरयति ॥ प्रा पूरणे आदादिकः । लजं व्यत्ययेन मध्यमः ॥ तथा
> निवतो नीचीनाल्लतागुल्मादीनुद्वत उत्थितान्वृक्षादींश्च स्वकीयेन तेजसावृणोति ।
> तदनंतरं तत्तमोऽंधकारं ज्योतिषा ग्रहनक्षत्रादिरूपेण तेजसा बाधते। पीडयति॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The immortal goddess Night, whose nature is to shine, fills the vast firmament (उरु (*uru*) is "wide", *āprāḥ* is from the root प्रा (*prā*), "to fill"): first she fills it with darkness. Likewise she covers with her own brilliance the low creepers, shrubs and the like (निवतः (*nivataḥ*)) and the risen trees and the like (द्वतः (*dvataḥ*)). After that she afflicts (बाधते (*bādhate*)) that darkness with light, that is, with the brilliance in the form of planets, stars and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अमर्त्या (*amartyā*)—the deathless
- देवी (*devī*)—the goddess Night
- उरु (*uru*)—the vast firmament
- आ अप्राः (*ā aprāḥ*)—has filled (and)
- निवतः (*nivataḥ*)—the creepers and the like that grow and spread below (on the earth)

### Printed p. 719
- उद्वत (*udvata*)—she covers also the trees grown tall with her brilliance (the darkness); (then)
- तमः (*tamaḥ*)—the darkness
- ज्योतिषा (*jyotiṣā*)—with the light in the form of planets, stars and the like
- बाधते (*bādhate*)—she afflicts

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The deathless goddess Night has filled the whole vast firmament with darkness. She covers with darkness the small plants, herbs and creepers that grow on the ground and the trees that grow tall. Then she afflicts the darkness with the brilliance in the form of planets and stars.

##### English translation
The immortal goddess has filled the expanded (firmament), the low places and the high places, she fights the darkness with lustre.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When night comes after sunset the whole sky is filled with darkness. Small plants and large trees alike remain in the darkness. Then the stars and the like, which appear as if to dispel that darkness, become visible and lend beauty to the night. This is the main sense.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> निरु॒ स्वसा॑रमस्कृतो॒षसं॑ दे॒व्या॑य॒ती ।  
> अपेदु॑ हासते॒ तमः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> निः । ऊं इति । स्वसारं । अकृत । उषसं । देवी । आयती ।  
> अप । इत् । ऊं इति । हासते । तमः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आयत्यागच्छंती देवी देवनशीला रात्रिः स्वसारं भगिनीमुषसं निरकृत ।
> निष्करोति । प्रकाशेन संस्करोति । निवर्तयतीत्यर्थः । तस्यामुषसि जातायां नैशं
> तमोऽपेद्धासते । अपैव गच्छति ॥ ओहाज् गत् । लेट्यडागमः । सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The goddess Night, coming (आयती (*āyatī*)), "makes out" (निरकृत (*nirakṛta*)) her sister Dawn: that is, she sets her in order with light, she turns herself back. When Dawn has been born, the darkness of night goes away (*apeddhāsate* means it just departs).

### Printed p. 720

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आयती (*āyatī*)—coming, pervading everywhere
- देवी (*devī*)—the goddess Night
- स्वसारं (*svasāraṃ*)—her own sister
- उषसं (*uṣasaṃ*)—to Dawn (the dawn time)
- निः अकृत (*niḥ akṛta*)—she makes room (then)
- तमः (*tamaḥ*)—the darkness
- अप इत् हासते (*apa it hāsate*)—goes away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The goddess Night, who comes pervading everywhere, after some time, that is at the end of the night, goes away herself and makes room (a path) for the coming of her sister Dawn (for the arrival of the dawn time); and after the dawn time the darkness goes away.

##### English translation
The advancing goddess prepared (the way for) her sister Dawn, and then the darkness departs.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सा नो॑ अ॒द्य यस्या॑ व॒यं नि ते॒ याम॒न्न वि॑क्ष्महि ।  
> वृ॒क्षे न व॑स॒तिं वयः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सा । नः । अद्य । यस्याः । वयं । नि । ते । यामन् । अविष्महि ।  
> वृक्षे । न । वसतिं । वया ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अद्यास्मिन्काले नोऽस्माकं सा रात्रिदेवता प्रसीदतु यस्या रात्रेर्यामन्यामनि प्राप्तौ सत्यां वयं न्यविक्ष्महि निविशामहे सुखेन गृह आस्महे ॥ निशेर्लजति
> नेर्विशः । पा. १-३-१७ । इत्यात्मनेपदं । छांदसः शपॊं लुक् ॥ तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> वयः दक्षिणो वृक्षे न यथा वृक्षे नीडाश्रये वसतिं रात् निवासं कुर्वंति तथा
> निवसाम इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May that deity Night be gracious to us today, at this time, upon whose arrival (यामन् (*yāman*)) we settle down (न्यविक्ष्महि (*nyavikṣmahi*)), that is, we rest in our houses in comfort. The example is: as birds (वयः (*vayaḥ*), "winged ones") make their night's dwelling in a tree, in their nest as their shelter, so do we dwell.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्याः (*yasyāḥ*)—of which night
- यामन् (*yāman*)—at the time of coming
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—birds
- वृक्षे (*vṛkṣe*)—in a tree
- वसतिं न (*vasatiṃ na*)—as they dwell
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- नि अविष्महि (*ni aviṣmahi*)—dwell in comfort in the house; such
- अद्य (*adya*)—at this night time
- सा (*sā*)—that deity Night
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us; may she be gracious

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As birds dwell at night in their nests in the trees, we shall dwell in comfort in our houses. May such a goddess Night be gracious to us now.

##### English translation
May she be favourable to us to-day upon whose approach we re-enter (our dwellings), as birds (re-enter) their nest upon the tree.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नि ग्रामा॑सो अविक्षत॒ नि प॒द्वंतो॒ नि प॒क्षिणः॑ ।  
> नि श्वे॒नास॑च्चिद॒र्थिनः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नि । ग्रामासः । अविक्षतॆ । नि । पत्ववंतः । नि । दक्षिणः ।  
> नि । श्वेनासः । चित् । अर्थिनः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ग्रामासो ग्रामाः । अत्र गामशब्दो जनसमूहे वर्तते यथा ग्राम आगत
> इति । सर्वे जना न्यविक्षत । तस्यां रात्रावागतायां निविशंते । शेरते ॥ निपूर्वाद्विशतेश्चांदसे लुजि पूर्ववदात्मनेपदं । शल इगुपधादनिटः क्सः । पा. ३-१४-५ ।
> क्सस्याचि । पा. ७-३-२२ । इत्याकारलोपः ॥ तथा पद्वंतः पादयुक्ता गवाश्वादयश्च
> निविशंते । तथा दक्षिणः पक्षोपेताश्च निविशंते । अर्थिनः । अर्तॆरर्थो गमनं ।
> शीघ्रगमनयुक्ताः श्येनासश्चिच्छेना अपि तस्यां रात्र्यां निविशंते । एषा रात्रिः
> सर्वाणि भूतजातान्यहनि संचारेण श्रांतानि स्वयमागत्य सुखयतीत्यर्थः ॥
> 46

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ग्रामासः (*grāmāsaḥ*) means villages; here the word "village" denotes a company of people, as in "the village has come". All people settle down (न्यविक्षत (*nyavikṣata*)) when that night has arrived, that is, they lie down. So also the footed creatures (पद्वंतः (*padvaṃtaḥ*)), cattle, horses and the like, settle; so also the winged ones (पक्षिणः (*pakṣiṇaḥ*)). As to अर्थिनः (*arthinaḥ*): the root *arti* has the sense of going, so even the hawks (श्येनासः (*śyenāsaḥ*)), endowed with swift flight, settle in that night. The sense is: this Night, coming of her own accord, gives comfort to all beings wearied by their movements during the day.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ग्रामासः (*grāmāsaḥ*)—all the people who live in a village, as soon as night falls
- नि अविक्षत (*ni avikṣata*)—come to their own houses and stay; likewise
- पक्षिणः नि (*pakṣiṇaḥ ni*)—the birds also betake themselves to their nests
- पद्वंतः नि (*padvaṃtaḥ ni*)—footed beasts such as cattle also betake themselves to their stalls
- अर्थिनः (*arthinaḥ*)—swiftly moving
- श्येनासः च (*śyenāsaḥ ca*)—the hawks also
- नि (*ni*)—betake themselves to their nests

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As soon as night falls all people come to their houses. Birds go to their nests. Cattle, horses and other beasts go to their stalls. The swiftly moving hawks also betake themselves to their nests.

##### English translation
Men have re-entered (their dwelling), and beasts and birds and the
swift hawks.

> अथा॑ नः सु॒तरा॑ भव ॥ ६ ॥

> अथ । नः । सुतरा । भव ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऊर्म्म्ये । रात्रिनामैतत् । रात्रे वृक्यं वृकस्य स्त्रियं वृकं चास्मान्हिंसंतं यवय । अस्मत्तः पृथक्कुरु । अस्मान्बाधितुं यथा न प्राप्नोति तथा । स्तेनं
> - रं च यवय । अस्मैत्तो वियो जरु । अथानंतरं नोऽस्माकं सुतरा सुखीन
> शरणीया क्षेमकरी भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Ūrmyā", which is a name of Night: O Night, keep away from us (यवय (*yavaya*), "make separate from us") the she-wolf (वृक्यं (*vṛkyaṃ*), the female of the wolf) and the wolf (वृकं (*vṛkaṃ*)) that would harm us, so that it may not reach to hurt us. Keep away also the thief (स्तेनं (*stenaṃ*)). Then (अथ (*atha*)) be for us सुतरा (*sutarā*), easy to cross, a giver of safety. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऊर्मॆ (*ūrmè*)—O Night
- वृक्यं (*vṛkyaṃ*)—the she-wolf
- वृकं (*vṛkaṃ*)—the wolf
- यवय (*yavaya*)—make them not come near us; likewise
- स्तेनं (*stenaṃ*)—make the thief not come
- अथ (*atha*)—then (the night time)
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- सुतरा (*sutarā*)—so as to pass comfortably
- भव (*bhava*)—be (let it be)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Night, while we sleep at night, let neither the she-wolf nor the wolf (nor other beasts of prey) nor thieves come near us. May we pass the night in comfort without any trouble.

Keep off, O Urmya, the she-wolf, keep off the wolf and the robber,
and be safely passed by us.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उप॑ मा॒ पेपि॑श॒त्तमः॑ कृ॒ष्णं व्य॑क्तमस्थित ।  
> उष॑ ऋ॒णेव॑ यातय ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उप । मा । पेपिशत् । तमः । कृष्णं । विअक्तं । अस्थित ॥  
> उषः । ऋणाइव । यातॆय ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पेपिशद्भृशं पिंशत् सर्ववस्तुष्वाश्लिष्टं तमोऽंधकारं कृष्णं कृष्णवर्णं
> व्यक्तं विशेषेण स्वभासा सर्वस्यांजकं स्पष्टरूपं वा ईदृशं नैशं तमो मामुपास्थित । उपागच्छत् ॥ संगतकरण आत्मनेपदं ॥ हे उष उषोदेवते त्वमृणेवर्णानीव तत्तमो यातय । अपगमय । स्तोत्थाणामृणानि यथा धनप्रदानेनापाकरोषि तथा तमोऽप्यपसारयेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The darkness of night, पेपिशत् (*pepiśat*) (greatly crushing, clinging to all things), black in colour (कृष्णं (*kṛṣṇaṃ*)), व्यक्तं (*vyaktaṃ*) (variously making all things coloured by its own light, or of distinct form), has come up to me (*upāsthita*; the middle voice is used in the sense of "joining"). "O Ushas, goddess Dawn, drive away that darkness like debts (ऋणेव (*ṛṇeva*))": as you remove the debts of those who praise you by giving wealth, so drive off the darkness too. This is the sense.

### Printed p. 724
*Pratipadārtha and the rest of Ṛk 7*

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मा (*mā*)—me
- पेपिशत् (*pepiśat*)—pervading
- कृष्णं (*kṛṣṇaṃ*)—black
- व्यक्तं (*vyaktaṃ*)—manifest
- तमः (*tamaḥ*)—the pitch darkness
- उप अस्थित (*upa asthita*)—has set out, has gone away
- उषः (*uṣaḥ*)—O Ushas, you
- ऋणेव (*ṛṇeva*)—as one pays off a debt
- यातय (*yātaya*)—drive that darkness away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The manifest pitch darkness (dense gloom) that spreads all around me has gone away. O Goddess Ushas (the dawn time), as one pays off a debt, drive the pitch darkness away.

##### English translation
The all-embracing black diffused darkness has approached me, discharge it, Ushas, as if it were a debt.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पेपिशत्—सर्ववस्तुष्वाश्लिष्टं (*pepiśat—sarvavastuṣvāśliṣṭaṃ*): the darkness that fills all things and covers them.

व्यक्तं—विशेषेण स्वभासा सर्वस्यांजकं स्पष्टरूपं वा (*vyaktaṃ—viśeṣeṇa svabhāsā sarvasyāṃjakaṃ spaṣṭarūpaṃ vā*): that which, by its own nature, enters into and covers everything, or that which is black so as to be visible to the eye; thick, dense darkness (Thick black darkness).

ऋणेव (*ṛṇeva*)—ṛṇa means debt. A man who has contracted a debt is in a kind of anxiety until he repays it; his mind has no peace. Tormented by the creditor's pressure, he wishes his debt would be cleared quickly so that he may be free of care. In the same way darkness too gives people a kind of torment. In darkness there is trouble from wicked beasts and thieves. In darkness nothing can be seen clearly with the eye, and no work can be done. It is natural to wish that such darkness would quickly go and become light, pleasant to all. Therefore the seer here prays to Ushas, the goddess of morning time, to remove quickly this darkness, which, like the burden of a debt, nobody wants.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उप॑ ते॒ गा इ॒वाक॑रं वृणी॒ष्व दु॑हितर्दिवः ।  
> रात्रि॒ स्तोमं॒ न जि॒ग्न्युषे॑ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उप । ते । गाःइव । आ । अकरं । वृणिष्व । दुहितः । दिवः ।  
> रात्रि । स्तोमं । न । जिग्युषे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे रात्रि रात्रिदेवते ते त्वां गा इव पयसो दोग्निर्धेनूरिवोपेत्याकरं।
> स्तुतिभिरभिमुखीकरोमि ॥ करोतेश्चांदसे लुजि कृमृद्यरुहिभ्य इति चेरजादेशः ॥
> दिवो दुहितर्द्योतमानस्य सूर्यस्य पुत्रि यद्वा दिवसस्य तनये ॥ परमपि चृंदसि ।
> पा. २-१-२-६ । इति परस्य षष्ठ्यंतस्य पूर्वामंत्रितांगवद्भावात्पदद्वयसमुदायस्याष्टमिकं सर्वानुदात्तत्वं ॥ त्वत्प्रसादाज्जिग्युषे शत्रूइज्जिग्युषो मम स्तोमं न
> स्तोत्रमिव हविरपि वृणीष्ट । त्वं भजस्व ॥ जयतेर्लिटः क्वसुः । सन्‌लिटोर्जेरित्यभ्यासादुत्तरस्य जकारस्य कुत्वं । षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थि वक्तव्येति चतुर्थि । वसोः
> संप्रसारणमिति संप्रसारणं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Rātri, goddess of Night, I come up to you like cows, like a milch cow, and bring you to face me with praises; *ākaraṃ* is "I make". He gives the Vedic aorist form of the root kṛ, with the substitution *ir*. *divo duhitaḥ*: daughter of the shining Sun, or alternatively daughter of the day. The accentual remark is that the two words together are wholly anudātta. By your grace, for me who am victorious over enemies, accept (वृणीष्व (*vṛṇīṣva*)) also the oblation, as a hymn of praise; "you, partake". जिग्युषे (*jigyuṣe*) is from the root ji in the perfect with the affix kvasu; the dative stands for the genitive.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रात्रि (*rātri*)—O goddess of Night
- गा इव (*gā iva*)—like a cow that gives milk, coming to you
- ते (*te*)—to you
- आ अकरं (*ā akaraṃ*)—I have offered praise
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the Sun
- दुहितः (*duhitaḥ*)—O Night, daughter
- जिग्युषे (*jigyuṣe*)—of me who conquer enemies
- स्तोमं न (*stomaṃ na*)—like a hymn (the oblation that I offer)
- वृणीष्ट्वा (*vṛṇīṣṭvā*)—accept with favour

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess of Night, coming to you as one comes to a milch cow, I have offered this praise to you. O Night, daughter of the Sun, accept the pleasing oblation as you would the hymn of me who wish to conquer enemies.

### Printed p. 726

##### English translation
I have brought (these verses) before you like milch cows; accept, O Night, daughter of the sky, (my oblation) as the eulogy of one about to conquer.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

गा इव ते (*gā iva te*)—As people go joyfully to a milch cow to draw milk, so I come to you (Night), giver of desired things, and offer praise: this is the meaning.

दिवः दुहितः (*divaḥ duhitaḥ*)—द्योतमानस्य सूर्यस्य पुत्रि यद्वा दिवसस्य तनये (*dyotamānasya sūryasya putri yadvā divasasya tanaye*): daughter of the shining Sun, or daughter of the day. Day and night arise from the Sun; since day arises when the Sun rises and night when he sets, day and night may be called daughters of the Sun. Likewise, since night comes when day has ended, night may be thought of as born of day. It is the custom to say that when one thing exists first and another arises from it, the second is the daughter of the first. In the hymns describing Ushas, day is described as born from night and night from day. Since night arises after the day has passed, it is natural to call night the daughter of day.

Supplementary (khila) mantras to be recited at the end of this sūkta:

आ रात्रि पार्थिवं रजः पितरः प्रायु धामभिः । दिवः सदांसि बृहती वि तिष्ठस आ त्वेषं वर्तते तमः ॥ १ ॥ (*ā rātri pārthivaṃ rajaḥ pitaraḥ prāyu dhāmabhiḥ | divaḥ sadāṃsi bṛhatī vi tiṣṭhasa ā tveṣaṃ vartate tamaḥ ‖ 1 ‖*)
ये ते रात्रि नृचक्षसो युक्तासो नवतिर्नव । अशीतिः संत्वष्टा उतो ते सप्त सप्ततीः ॥ २ ॥ (*ye te rātri nṛcakṣaso yuktāso navatirnava | aśītiḥ saṃtvaṣṭā uto te sapta saptatīḥ ‖ 2 ‖*)
रात्रीं प्रपद्ये जननीं सर्वभूतनिवेशनीं । भद्रां भगवतीं कृष्णां विश्वस्य जगतो निशां ॥ ३ ॥ (*rātrīṃ prapadye jananīṃ sarvabhūtaniveśanīṃ | bhadrāṃ bhagavatīṃ kṛṣṇāṃ viśvasya jagato niśāṃ ‖ 3 ‖*)
संवेशिनीं संयमिनीं ग्रहनक्षत्रमालिनीं । प्रपन्नोऽहं शिवां रात्रीं भद्रे पारमशीमहि (*saṃveśinīṃ saṃyaminīṃ grahanakṣatramālinīṃ | prapanno 'haṃ śivāṃ rātrīṃ bhadre pāramaśīmahi*) (भद्रॆ पारमशीमहोऽहं नमः ॥ ४ ॥ (*bhadrè pāramaśīmaho 'haṃ namaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*))
स्तोष्यामि प्रयतो देवीं शरण्यां बह्वृचप्रियां । सहस्रसंमितां दुर्गां जातवेदसे सुनवाम सोमं ॥ ५ ॥ (*stoṣyāmi prayato devīṃ śaraṇyāṃ bahvṛcapriyāṃ | sahasrasaṃmitāṃ durgāṃ jātavedase sunavāma somaṃ ‖ 5 ‖*)
५ ॥ शांत्यर्थं तद्विजातीनामृषिभिः सोमपाश्रिताः । ऋग्वेदे त्वं समुत्पन्नारातीयतो नि दहाति वेदः ॥ ६ ॥ (*5 ‖ śāṃtyarthaṃ tadvijātīnāmṛṣibhiḥ somapāśritāḥ | ṛgvede tvaṃ samutpannārātīyato ni dahāti vedaḥ ‖ 6 ‖*)

### Printed p. 727
ये त्वां देवि प्र पद्यंति ब्राह्मणा हव्यवाहनीं । अविद्या बहुविद्या वा स नः पर्षदति दुर्गाणि विश्वा ॥ ७ ॥ (*ye tvāṃ devi pra padyaṃti brāhmaṇā havyavāhanīṃ | avidyā bahuvidyā vā sa naḥ parṣadati durgāṇi viśvā ‖ 7 ‖*)
ये अग्निवर्णां शुभां सौम्यां कीर्तयिष्यंति ये द्विजाः । तांस्तारयति दुर्गाणि नावेव सिंधुं दुरितात्यग्निः ॥ ८ ॥ (*ye agnivarṇāṃ śubhāṃ saumyāṃ kīrtayiṣyaṃti ye dvijāḥ | tāṃstārayati durgāṇi nāveva siṃdhuṃ duritātyagniḥ ‖ 8 ‖*)
दुर्गॆषु विषमे घोरे संग्रामे रिपुसंकटे । अग्निचोरनिपातेषु दुष्टग्रहनिवारिणि ॥ ९ ॥ (*durgèṣu viṣame ghore saṃgrāme ripusaṃkaṭe | agnicoranipāteṣu duṣṭagrahanivāriṇi ‖ 9 ‖*)
दुर्गेषु विषमेषु त्वं संग्रामेषु वनेषु च । मोहयित्वा प्र पद्यंते तेषां मे अभयं कुरु (*durgeṣu viṣameṣu tvaṃ saṃgrāmeṣu vaneṣu ca | mohayitvā pra padyaṃte teṣāṃ me abhayaṃ kuru*) (तेषां मे अभयं कुर्वों नमः (*teṣāṃ me abhayaṃ kurvoṃ namaḥ*)) ॥ १० (*10*) ॥
केशिनीं सर्वभूतानां पंचमीति च नाम च । सा मां समा निशा देवी सर्वतः परिरक्षतु (*keśinīṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ paṃcamīti ca nāma ca | sā māṃ samā niśā devī sarvataḥ parirakṣatu*) (सर्वतः परि रक्षत्वो नमः (*sarvataḥ pari rakṣatvo namaḥ*)) ॥ ११ (*11*) ॥
तामग्निवर्णां तपसा ज्वलंतीं वैरोचनीं कर्मपलेषु जुष्टां । दुर्गां देवीं शरणमहं प्र पद्ये सुतरसि तरसे नमः ॥ १२ ॥ (*tāmagnivarṇāṃ tapasā jvalaṃtīṃ vairocanīṃ karmapaleṣu juṣṭāṃ | durgāṃ devīṃ śaraṇamahaṃ pra padye sutarasi tarase namaḥ ‖ 12 ‖*)
दुर्गा दुर्गेषु स्थानेषु शं नो देवीरभिष्टये । य इमं दुर्गास्तवं पुण्यं रात्रौ रात्रौ सदा पठेत् ॥ १३ ॥ (*durgā durgeṣu sthāneṣu śaṃ no devīrabhiṣṭaye | ya imaṃ durgāstavaṃ puṇyaṃ rātrau rātrau sadā paṭhet ‖ 13 ‖*)
रात्रिः कुशिकः सोभरो रात्रिर्ना भारद्वाजो रात्रिस्तवो गायत्री ॥ (*rātriḥ kuśikaḥ sobharo rātrirnā bhāradvājo rātristavo gāyatrī ‖*)
रात्रीसूक्तं जपेन्नित्यं तत्कालमुपपद्यते । न योनिं पुनरायाति सर्वपाष्टैः प्रमुच्यते ॥ १४ ॥ (*rātrīsūktaṃ japennityaṃ tatkālamupapadyate | na yoniṃ punarāyāti sarvapāṣṭaiḥ pramucyate ‖ 14 ‖*)
क्षीरेण स्नापिता दुर्गा चंदनेन विलेपिता । बिल्वपत्रकृतापीडा नमो दुर्गॆ नमो नमः ॥ १५ ॥ (*kṣīreṇa snāpitā durgā caṃdanena vilepitā | bilvapatrakṛtāpīḍā namo durgè namo namaḥ ‖ 15 ‖*)
सर्वभूतपिशाचेभ्यः सर्वसर्पसरीसृपैः । दैनेभ्यो मानुषेभ्यश्च उभयोभ्योऽभिरक्ष मां ॥ १६ ॥ (*sarvabhūtapiśācebhyaḥ sarvasarpasarīsṛpaiḥ | dainebhyo mānuṣebhyaśca ubhayobhyo 'bhirakṣa māṃ ‖ 16 ‖*)
या ऋग्वेदे स्तुता देवी काश्यपेन उदाहृता । जातवेदप्रभा गौरी जातवेदसे सुनवाम सोमं ॥ १७ ॥ (*yā ṛgvede stutā devī kāśyapena udāhṛtā | jātavedaprabhā gaurī jātavedase sunavāma somaṃ ‖ 17 ‖*)
सुरासुरैर्द्विजवरैः पिशाचोरगराक्षसैः । अरातिभय उत्पन्ने अरातीयतो नि दहाति वेदः ॥ १८ ॥ (*surāsurairdvijavaraiḥ piśācoragarākṣasaiḥ | arātibhaya utpanne arātīyato ni dahāti vedaḥ ‖ 18 ‖*)

### Printed p. 728
गजद्वारेऽपथे घोरे संग्रामेषु च गौतमी । सर्वं रक्षतु दुरितं स नः पर्षदति दुर्गाणि विश्वा ॥ १९ ॥ (*gajadvāre 'pathe ghore saṃgrāmeṣu ca gautamī | sarvaṃ rakṣatu duritaṃ sa naḥ parṣadati durgāṇi viśvā ‖ 19 ‖*)
महाभये समुत्पन्ने स्मरंति च जपंति च । सर्वं तारयते दुर्गा नावेव सिंधुं दुरितात्यग्निः ॥ २० ॥ (*mahābhaye samutpanne smaraṃti ca japaṃti ca | sarvaṃ tārayate durgā nāveva siṃdhuṃ duritātyagniḥ ‖ 20 ‖*)
य इमं दुर्गास्तवं पुण्यं शृण्वंति च जपंति च । त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातं त्रिषु लोकेषु पूजितं ॥ २१ ॥ (*ya imaṃ durgāstavaṃ puṇyaṃ śṛṇvaṃti ca japaṃti ca | triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātaṃ triṣu lokeṣu pūjitaṃ ‖ 21 ‖*)
अपुत्रो लभते पुत्रान् धनहीनो धनं लभेत् । अचक्षुर्लभते चक्षुर्बद्धो मुच्येत बंधनात् ॥ २२ ॥ (*aputro labhate putrān dhanahīno dhanaṃ labhet | acakṣurlabhate cakṣurbaddho mucyeta baṃdhanāt ‖ 22 ‖*)
२ ॥ व्याधितो मुच्यते रोगादरोगी श्रियमाप्नुयात् । ददाति कामितं सर्वं कात्यायनि नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ २३ ॥ (*2 ‖ vyādhito mucyate rogādarogī śriyamāpnuyāt | dadāti kāmitaṃ sarvaṃ kātyāyani namo 'stu te ‖ 23 ‖*)
उलूकयातुं शुशुलूकयातुं जहि श्वयातुमुत कोकयातुं । सुपर्णयातुमुत गृध्रयातुं दृषदेव प्र मृण रक्ष इंद्र ॥ (*ulūkayātuṃ śuśulūkayātuṃ jahi śvayātumuta kokayātuṃ | suparṇayātumuta gṛdhrayātuṃ dṛṣadeva pra mṛṇa rakṣa iṃdra ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-104-22.)
पिशंगभृष्टिमंभृणं पिशाचिमिंद्र सं मृण । सर्वं रक्षो नि बर्हय ॥ (*piśaṃgabhṛṣṭimaṃbhṛṇaṃ piśācimiṃdra saṃ mṛṇa | sarvaṃ rakṣo ni barhaya ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-133-5.)

## Sūkta 128 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
In this sūkta the Viśvedevas are praised. As in other sūktas addressed to the Viśvedevas, besides the praise of various deities, the seer describes the request that these deities protect and keep the worshippers in every way, protect sacrifices and the like, and fulfil wishes such as wealth and good sons. In a way this sūkta is a blessing for those who wish to obtain the favour of the gods. On the use of this sūkta, the great sage Śaunaka, in the fourth chapter of his work Ṛgvidhāna, says:

ममाग्ने वर्च इत्येतत्सर्वकामैर्जपेद्विजः । जुह्स्वदाज्यमनेनैव सर्वान्नामानवाप्नुयात् ॥ २९ ॥ (*mamāgne varca ityetatsarvakāmairjapedvijaḥ | juhsvadājyamanenaiva sarvānnāmānavāpnuyāt ‖ 29 ‖*)

### Printed p. 729
A man who wishes all his desires fulfilled should mutter this sūkta beginning ममाग्ने वर्चः (*mamāgne varcaḥ*), and if he offers ghee in the established fire while reciting the mantras of this sūkta, he will obtain all his desires.

यां कल्पयंतीति सदा जपेत नियतव्रतः । नैनं कृत्या निहिंसंति क्रुद्धाभिचरितानि च ॥ ॥ ३० ॥ (*yāṃ kalpayaṃtīti sadā japeta niyatavrataḥ | nainaṃ kṛtyā nihiṃsaṃti kruddhābhicaritāni ca ‖ ‖ 30 ‖*)
For a man who, always with discipline, mutters the sūkta यां कल्पंति (*yāṃ kalpaṃti*) (a khila sūkta belonging to the sūkta ममाग्ने वर्चः (*mamāgne varcaḥ*); it is explained in the special topics of the last Ṛk of this sūkta), the hostile rites (magic, sorcery and the like) performed by others in anger do not touch him; that is, those rites do not harm him.

यमंगिरसकल्पैस्तु तद्विदोऽभिचरंति सः । प्रत्यंगिरसकल्पेन सर्वांस्तान् प्रतिबाधते ॥ ३० ॥ (*yamaṃgirasakalpaistu tadvido 'bhicaraṃti saḥ | pratyaṃgirasakalpena sarvāṃstān pratibādhate ‖ 30 ‖*)
If, according to the Āṅgirasa-kalpa (as stated in the Atharvaveda), those who know hostile rites perform them against a man with intent to harm him, that man, by acting in return according to the procedure stated in the Pratyaṅgirasa-kalpa, does not suffer from those rites but becomes able to harm his own rivals in return.

प्रत्यंगिरसविद्वांस्तु न रिष्येत कदाचन । नैनं कृत्या निहिंसंति ज्ञाताज्ञातानि यानि च ॥ ३२ ॥ (*pratyaṃgirasavidvāṃstu na riṣyeta kadācana | nainaṃ kṛtyā nihiṃsaṃti jñātājñātāni yāni ca ‖ 32 ‖*)
अजानता जानता वा क्रुद्धेनामर्षितेन वा आक्रुष्टं वा दुरुक्तंवा नैनो लिंपति तद्विदं ॥ ३३ ॥ (*ajānatā jānatā vā kruddhenāmarṣitena vā ākruṣṭaṃ vā duruktaṃvā naino liṃpati tadvidaṃ ‖ 33 ‖*)
A scholar who knows the Pratyaṅgirasa mantras and the manner of using them is never troubled by hostile rites. No mantra-rites, whether done deliberately or unknowingly, can harm him; the mantra-rites done in anger or envy, knowingly or unknowingly, subjugation, cursing and similar practices can do nothing to this scholar.

एतमेव जपेन्नित्यमृषिं स्वस्त्ययनाय वै । सर्वप्रायश्चित्तमेतदभाषत ऋषिः स्वयं (*etameva japennityamṛṣiṃ svastyayanāya vai | sarvaprāyaścittametadabhāṣata ṛṣiḥ svayaṃ*)
For well-being and prosperity this sūkta should be muttered every day; and the seer of this sūkta himself has said that it is an expiation for all faults of omission.

स्थावरणां निवेशे तु नगराणां तथैव च । ग्रामाणां च गृहाणां च जपेदिममृषिं सदा ॥ ८५ ॥ (*sthāvaraṇāṃ niveśe tu nagarāṇāṃ tathaiva ca | grāmāṇāṃ ca gṛhāṇāṃ ca japedimamṛṣiṃ sadā ‖ 85 ‖*)

### Printed p. 730
In mountain regions, cities, villages, houses and other places, at convenient spots, this very sūkta should always be recited.

जातरूपमयं विद्वान्कारयेत्त्रिवृतं मणिं । (*jātarūpamayaṃ vidvānkārayettrivṛtaṃ maṇiṃ |*)
सहस्रसंपातहुतमृषिणा तेन तं ततः ॥ (*sahasrasaṃpātahutamṛṣiṇā tena taṃ tataḥ ‖*) (36)
प्रतिमुंचेत शिरसि ग्रीनायामथवोरसि । (*pratimuṃceta śirasi grīnāyāmathavorasi |*)
नैनं कृत्या निहिंसंति ज्ञाताज्ञातानि यानि च ॥ (*nainaṃ kṛtyā nihiṃsaṃti jñātājñātāni yāni ca ‖*) (37)

A discerning practitioner should make beads from the tree called jātarūpa, string a thousand such beads into a three-stranded necklace, and wear it on his head, at his throat or on his chest. Then magic, sorcery and other hostile rites (ābhicāraka) can do him nothing.

अनेनैव तु सूक्तेन राज्ञां च समलोहितं । (*anenaiva tu sūktena rājñāṃ ca samalohitaṃ |*)
कारयेत मणिं विद्वांस्तावदेवानुमंत्रणं ॥ (*kārayeta maṇiṃ vidvāṃstāvadevānumaṃtraṇaṃ ‖*) (38)
संग्रामेषु ध्वजाग्राणि वादित्राण्यनुमंत्रयेत् । (*saṃgrāmeṣu dhvajāgrāṇi vāditrāṇyanumaṃtrayet |*)
आसनानि च शय्याश्च यानानि विविधानि च ॥ (*āsanāni ca śayyāśca yānāni vividhāni ca ‖*) (39)
तस्याभिचरतः साक्षादंगिरसोऽप्युषेः स्वयं । (*tasyābhicarataḥ sākṣādaṃgiraso 'pyuṣeḥ svayaṃ |*)
प्रत्यंगिरसकल्पेन सर्वं तत्पतिबाधते ॥ (*pratyaṃgirasakalpena sarvaṃ tatpatibādhate ‖*) (40)

Having made the beads as described above and consecrated them with the mantras of this sūkta, kings should tie them to the tops of the banners used in battle and the like. Likewise, if the beads are tied to the various drums such as the nagārī and other instruments, to seats, beds and other articles, then even if the sage Aṅgiras himself, who is skilled in magical arts, were to direct hostile rites against them, all of these can be warded off by the procedure of the Pratyaṅgirasa-kalpa.

अमानुषीरभिचरेत् कृत्यासूक्तं जपन्निदं । (*amānuṣīrabhicaret kṛtyāsūktaṃ japannidaṃ |*)
मुच्यते सर्वतोऽनिष्टात् किंपुनर्मानुषाद्भयं (*mucyate sarvato 'niṣṭāt kiṃpunarmānuṣādbhayaṃ*) (printed number 40)**NOTE**

Sitting in a secluded place without human traffic and reciting this Kṛtyā-sūkta, all kinds of misfortune, fear and the like will be destroyed. What can fears and terrors arising from human beings do in front of the recitation of this mantra?

तपस्वी नियतो दांतः प्रयोक्ता चेद्भवेदृषिं । (*tapasvī niyato dāṃtaḥ prayoktā cedbhavedṛṣiṃ |*)
सर्वं तरति शांतात्मा तपो हि सुमहद्बलं (*sarvaṃ tarati śāṃtātmā tapo hi sumahadbalaṃ*) (42)

### Printed p. 731
आयुष्यमायुर्वर्चस्यं सूक्तं दाक्षायणं महत् । (*āyuṣyamāyurvarcasyaṃ sūktaṃ dākṣāyaṇaṃ mahat |*)
अलंकारं हिरण्यं ना प्राप्य दाक्षायणं जपेत् । (*alaṃkāraṃ hiraṇyaṃ nā prāpya dākṣāyaṇaṃ japet |*)
प्रायश्च श्रियमादत्ते बहु चान्नं समश्नुते (*prāyaśca śriyamādatte bahu cānnaṃ samaśnute*) (43)

If an ascetic man, with discipline and a calm mind, recites this sūkta and performs the rites accordingly, he removes by the power of his austerity all misfortunes and fears and lives happily. If this great sūkta is recited at the auspicious time of the dakṣiṇāyana, long life, splendour, adornment, gold and other prosperity, wealth, and abundance of riches and grain will all be obtained.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ममाग्न इति नवर्चं षोडशं सूक्तमांगिरसस्य विहव्यस्यार्षं वैश्वदेवं ।
> अंत्या जगती शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः । अनुक्रम्यते हि । ममाग्ने नव विहवो वैश्वदेवं
> जगत्यंतमिति ॥ संसवे निमित्तभूते वैश्वदेवसूक्तस्य पुरस्तादेतच्छंस्यं । सूत्रितं
> च । ममाग्ने वर्च इति वैश्वदेवसूक्तस्यापि वैतेष्वेव निविदो दध्यात् । आ. ६-६ ।
> इति ॥ समावर्तनेऽनेन सूक्तेन सिष्णासुना प्रत्यृचं समिधाधातव्या । सूत्रितं च ।
> ममाग्ने वर्च इति प्रत्यृचं समिधोऽभ्यादध्यात् । आ. गृ. ३-९-२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the sixteenth sūkta, of nine ṛks, beginning ममाग्न (*mamāgna*). Its seer is Vihavya of the Āṅgirasa line, its deity the Viśvedevas; the last ṛk is Jagatī and the rest are Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says: ममाग्ने नव विहवो वैश्वदेवं जगत्यंतमिति (*mamāgne nava vihavo vaiśvadevaṃ jagatyaṃtamiti*). In the saṃsava, which is the occasion, this sūkta is to be recited before the Vaiśvadeva sūkta. It is prescribed by the sūtra ममाग्ने वर्च इति वैश्वदेवसूक्तस्यापि वैतेष्वेव निविदो दध्यात् (*mamāgne varca iti vaiśvadevasūktasyāpi vaiteṣveva nivido dadhyāt*) (Ā. 6-6). In the samāvartana the one who wishes to bathe should place a fuel-stick with each ṛk of this sūkta; the sūtra reads ममाग्ने वर्च इति प्रत्यृचं समिधोऽभ्यादध्यात् (*mamāgne varca iti pratyṛcaṃ samidho 'bhyādadhyāt*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-9-2).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning ममाग्ने (*mamāgne*) is the sixteenth sūkta in the tenth anuvāka. It contains nine ṛks. Its seer is Vihavya of the Aṅgirasa gotra; its deity is the Viśvedevas; the last ṛk of the sūkta is in the Jagatī metre; the remaining ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated: ममाग्ने नव विहवो वैश्वदेवं जगत्तंतं (*mamāgne nava vihavo vaiśvadevaṃ jagattaṃtaṃ*). In the saṃsava, when the Vaiśvadeva sūkta is recited, this sūkta is to be recited beforehand; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana-śrautasūtra ममाग्ने वर्च इति वैश्वदेवसूक्तस्यापि वैतेष्टेव निविदो दध्यात् (*mamāgne varca iti vaiśvadevasūktasyāpi vaiteṣṭeva nivido dadhyāt*) (Ā. 6-6). In the samāvartana rite also, a fuel-stick is to be put into the fire with each ṛk of this sūkta; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana-gṛhyasūtra ममाग्ने वर्च इति प्रत्यृचं समिधोऽभ्यादध्यात् (*mamāgne varca iti pratyṛcaṃ samidho 'bhyādadhyāt*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-9-2).

Sūkta 128. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 10; Sūkta 128. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 7; Vargas 15, 16. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 9. Seer: Vihavya. Deity: Viśvedevas. Metre: 1–8 Triṣṭubh; 9 Jagatī.

### Printed p. 732
#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ममा॑ग्ने॒ वर्चो॑ विह॒वेष्व॑स्तु व॒यं त्वेंधा॑नास्त॒न्वं॑ पुषेम ।  
> मह्यं॑ नमंतां प्र॒दिश॒श्चत॑स्र॒स्य याध्य॑क्षेण॒ पृत॑ना जयेम ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मम । अग्ने । वर्चः । विहवेषु । अस्तु । वयं । त्वा । इंधानाः । तन्वं । पुषेम ।  
> मह्यं । नमंतां । प्रदिशः । चतस्रः । त्वया । अधिअक्षेण । पृतनाः । जयेम ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने । विविधमाहूयंते येषु शूरा इति विहवाः संग्रामाः । यद्वा ।
> विविधं यागार्थं देवा आहूयंत एष्विति विहवा यज्ञाः ॥ ह्वः संप्रसारणं च
> न्यभ्युपविषु । पा. ३-३-७२ । इत्यधिकरणेऽप् संप्रसारणं च । थाथादिनोत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं ॥ संग्रामेषु यज्ञेषु वा वर्चो दीप्तिस्त्वदनुग्रहान्ममास्तु । भवतु ।
> वयं च त्वा त्वामिंधानाः समिद्धिर्दिपयंतस्तन्वं तव शरीरं पुषेम । हविर्भिर्व.
> र्धयेम ॥ इंथेः शानचि श्नसोरल्लोप उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण शानच आद्युदात्तत्वे
> प्राप्ते विभाषा वेण्विंदानयोः । पा. ६-१-२१५ । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ तन्नं पुषेम ॥
> पुषेर्लिजि लिज्याशिष्यज् ॥ अपि च मह्यं मदर्थं ॥ जयि चेत्यस्मद आद्युदात्तत्वं ॥
> चतस्रः प्रदिशः प्रकृष्टा दिशः । तद्वासिनो जना इत्यर्थः । नमंतां । स्वतः एव प्रह्वीभवंतु ॥ नमतेः कर्मकर्तरि लोटि न दुहस्सु नमामिशि यक्रतिषेधः ॥ त्वयास्माभिर्हविर्भिः प्रवर्धितेनाध्यक्षणेश्वरेण सता पृतनाः शत्रुसेना जयेम। अभिभवेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni." विहवाः (*vihavāḥ*) are battles, in which heroes are called in various ways; or else विहवाः (*vihavāḥ*) are sacrifices, in which the gods are called in various ways for the sake of the offering. In battles or sacrifices may radiance (वर्चः (*varcaḥ*)) be mine through your favour. And we, kindling you (इंधानाः (*iṃdhānāḥ*)) with fuel-sticks, would nourish (पुषेम (*puṣema*)) your body (तन्वं (*tanvaṃ*)), that is, make it grow with oblations. Further, may the four प्रदिशः (*pradiśaḥ*), the principal quarters, that is, the people living there, bow (नमंतां (*namaṃtāṃ*)) of themselves for me. With you, made strong by us through oblations and being our overlord (अध्यक्षेण (*adhyakṣeṇa*)), may we conquer the पृतनाः (*pṛtanāḥ*), the enemy armies, that is, overcome them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni (by your grace)
- विहवेषु (*vihaveṣu*)—in sacrifices or in battles
- वर्चः (*varcaḥ*)—radiance, that is, capacity
- मम (*mama*)—to me
- अस्तु (*astu*)—let there be
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- इंधानाः (*iṃdhānāḥ*)—having kindled with fuel-sticks and the like
- तन्वं (*tanvaṃ*)—your body
- पुषेम (*puṣema*)—we nourish and make grow with oblations and the like
- चतस्रः प्रदिशः (*catasraḥ pradiśaḥ*)—the four quarters, that is, the people in the four quarters
- मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*)—towards me
- नमंतां (*namaṃtāṃ*)—let them bow
- अध्यक्षेण (*adhyakṣeṇa*)—who are the lord
- त्वया (*tvayā*)—by you, that is, with your help
- पृतनाः (*pṛtanāḥ*)—enemy armies
- जयेम (*jayema*)—may we conquer

### Printed p. 733

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, by your grace, in sacrifices or in battles may strength and capacity arise in me. Having kindled you with fuel-sticks and the like, we nourish and make grow your body with oblations and the like. May the people in the four quarters bow to me, that is, be subject to my command. With your help, you who are lord of all, may we conquer the enemy armies.

##### English translation
May glory, Agni, be mine in battle, may we, kindling you, cherish your person, may the (inhabitants of the) four quarters bow down before me, may we with you for our leader overcome (hostile) armies.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मनु॑ दे॒वा वि॑ह॒वे सं॑तु॒ सर्व॒ इंद्र॑वन्नो म॒रुतो॒ विष्णु॑र॒ग्निः ।  
> ममां॒तरि॑क्षमु॒रुलो॑कमस्तु॒ मह्यं॒ वातः॑ पवतां॒ कामे॑  ॒
> अस्मिन् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मम । देवाः । विहवे । संतु । सर्वे । इंद्रवनः । मरुतः । विष्णुः । अग्निः ।  
> मम । अंतरिक्षं । उरुलोकं । अस्तु । मह्यं । वातः । पवतां । कामे । अस्मिन् ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सर्वे देवा विहने संग्रामे यज्ञे ना मम संतु । ममैव साधका भवंतु।
> के पुनस्ते । इंद्रवंत इंद्रेण युक्ता मरुतो विष्णुरग्निश्च । तथांतरिक्षं मनोरुलोकं विस्तीर्णप्रकाशकमस्तु ॥ लोकृ दर्शने । भावे घञ् । लोक आलोकः
> प्रकाशः । उरुर्लोको यस्यॆति बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ अपि चास्मिन्मामे कामयितव्ये फले निमित्तभूते सति वातो वायुः पवतां । अनुगुणं
> प्रवातु ॥ पूज् पवने भौवादिकः । ऊडिदमित्यादिनेदमः सप्तम्या उदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May all the gods be mine in battle or sacrifice, that is, be my accomplishers. Who are they? The इंद्रवंतः (*iṃdravaṃtaḥ*), the Maruts accompanied by Indra, and Viṣṇu and Agni. Likewise may the antarikṣa be उरुलोकं (*urulokaṃ*), widely luminous: the root लोकृ (*lokṛ*) means "to see", and लोक (*loka*) is the view, light; उरुर्लोको यस्य (*ururloko yasya*) is a bahuvrīhi. And in this कामे (*kāme*), this desired fruit being the occasion, may Vāta, the wind, blow (पवतां (*pavatāṃ*)), that is, blow favourably.

### Printed p. 734

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रवंतः (*iṃdravaṃtaḥ*)—accompanied by Indra
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Marut deities
- विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*)—Viṣṇu
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—and Agni; all these and others
- सर्वे देवाः (*sarve devāḥ*)—all the gods
- विहवे (*vihave*)—in battle or in sacrifice
- मम (*mama*)—mine, that is, as helpers to me
- संतु (*saṃtu*)—let them be (and likewise)
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the atmospheric world
- मम (*mama*)—in respect of me
- उरुलोकं (*urulokaṃ*)—possessing wide light
- अस्तु (*astu*)—let it be
- मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*)—for me
- कामे (*kāme*)—desiring the fruit
- आस्मिन् (*āsmin*)—in me
- वातः (*vātaḥ*)—the wind
- प्रवतां (*pravatāṃ*)—let it blow pleasantly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May all the gods, Indra, the Maruts, Viṣṇu, Agni and the rest, be my helpers in battle or sacrifice. In my case may the atmosphere also shine brightly. For me, who desire the fruit, may the wind blow beneficially.

##### English translation
May all the gods be on my side in battle, the Maruts with Indra, Vishnu and Agni ; may the expanded firmament be mine, may the wind blow (propitiously) to this my desire.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मयि॑ दे॒वा द्रवि॑ण॒मा य॑जंतां॒ मय्या॒तीर॑स्तु॒ मयि॑ दे॒वहू॑तिः ।  
> दैव्या॒ होता॑रो वनुषंत॒ पूर्वेरि॑ष्टाः स्याम त॒न्वा॑ सु॒वीराः॑॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मयि । देवाः । द्रविणं । आ । यजंतां । मयि । आशीः । अस्तु । मयि । देवहूतिः।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May all the gods offer (यजंतां (*yajaṃtāṃ*)) wealth (द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*)) to me, the praiser, that is, cause it to come, give it to me. So too may the आशीः (*āśīḥ*), the sacrificial fruit to be desired, be mine alone. (The explanation of देवहूतिः (*devahūtiḥ*) begins at the end of this block and continues in the next.)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

देवहूतिः (*devahūtiḥ*) is the sacrifice, in which there is an invoking of the gods; may that be in me. Further, those priests who are दैव्याः (*daivyāḥ*), belonging to the gods, who accomplish the good homa, my own priests, being earlier (पूर्वे (*pūrve*)) than the priests of others, may they worship (वनुषंत (*vanuṣaṃta*)) the gods, that is, serve them. And we, अरिष्टाः (*ariṣṭāḥ*), unharmed in body (तन्वा (*tanvā*)), and सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*), having good sons, may we be.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—all the gods
- मयि (*mayi*)—in me, the praiser, or to me
- द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*)—wealth
- आ यजंतां (*ā yajaṃtāṃ*)—let them provide and give
- आशीः (*āśīḥ*)—the sacrificial fruit in the form of a blessing
- मयि अस्तु (*mayi astu*)—let it come to me
- देवहूतिः (*devahūtiḥ*)—the sacrifice also
- मयि (*mayi*)—let it be conducted by me
- दैन्व्याः (*dainvyāḥ*)—belonging to the gods, our
- होतारः (*hotāraḥ*)—priests
- पूर्वे (*pūrve*)—even earlier than others
- वनुषंत (*vanuṣaṃta*)—let them worship the gods
- तन्वा (*tanvā*)—by our body
- अरिष्टाः (*ariṣṭāḥ*)—let us be unharmed
- सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*)—sons possessing vigour
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May all the gods provide wealth to me, the praiser. By their grace may the sacrifice in the form of a blessing, and its fruit, come to me. May our priests, who invoke the gods, pray to the gods and worship them before everyone else. May we live happily, without disease or other afflictions in our bodies, and may we obtain vigorous sons.

##### English translation
May the gods bestow wealth upon me, may (their) blessing be upon
me, may sacrifice in which the gods are invoked be (beneficial) to me, may
my invokers of the gods be the first to propitiate them; may we be unharmed
in body and blessed with male offspring.

> ब्रूत ॥ वक्तेर्लोटि व्यत्ययेनाट् । वच उमित्युमागमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*) means "for me": let the priests worship the gods with oblations. Alternatively the dative stands for the genitive, so that "mine" means my priests. हव्या (*havyā*) are the oblations that belong to me, such as the caru and the puroḍāśa; the priests are to offer with these. May the resolve (ākūti) of my mind, that is, its formed intention and the prayer for what is desired, be true, that is, come to fulfilment. And may I not go to any sin at all. मा नि गां (*mā ni gāṃ*) means "may I not go down or to anything lowly", that is, "may I not commit sin". Further, "O all gods (विश्वे देवासः (*viśve devāsaḥ*)), speak for us (अधि वोचत— (*adhi vocata—*))", that is, speak with partiality for us in disputes.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मम (*mama*)—my
- यानि हव्यानि (*yāni havyāni*)—whatever oblations there are, caru, puroḍāśa and so on
- मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*)—for me, or my priests
- यजंतु (*yajaṃtu*)—let them offer to the gods
- मे (*me*)—my
- मनसः (*manasaḥ*)—of the mind
- आकूतिः (*ākūtiḥ*)—the prayer for what is desired
- सत्या (*satyā*)—truly
- अस्तु (*astu*)—be fulfilled
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- कतमच्चन (*katamaccana*)—of whatever kind
- एनः (*enaḥ*)—sin
- मा नि गां (*mā ni gāṃ*)—may I not incur
- विश्वे देवासः (*viśve devāsaḥ*)—O all gods
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- अधि वोचत (*adhi vocata*)—speak so that it may be well, that is, bless us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May my priests offer to the gods, for me, these oblations that I have prepared. May the wish in my mind be fulfilled. May no sin of any kind befall me. O all gods, bless us that it may be well with us.

### Printed p. 737

##### English translation

> हे षडुर्विः षट्संख्याका उव्यः । एताश्चान्यत्राम्नायंते । षण्मोर्विरंहसः पांतु द्यौश्च पृथिवी चाहश्च रात्रिश्चापश्चौषधयश्चति । ईदृश्यो हे देवीर्देव्यः ॥ जसि वा छंदसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः । नामंत्रिते समानाधिकरणे सामान्यवचनमित्यस्याविद्यमानत्वनिषेधेन षळुर्विरित्यनयोरामंत्रितयोः पदात्परत्वादाष्टमिकमामंत्रितानुदात्तत्वं ॥ ता यूयमुरु विस्तीर्णं धनं नोऽसाक्कं
> कृणोत । कुरुत ॥ कृवि हिंसाकरणयोः । धिन्विकृण्वोरच्चेत्युप्रत्ययः । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चति तस्य तबादेशः ॥ हे विश्वे सर्वॆ देवासो देवाः यूयं चेहास्मिन्धने
> प्राप्तव्ये विषये वीरयध्वं । विक्रामयत । तथा वयं तद्धनं लभेमहि ।
> तथा वीर्यवंतो यूयं प्रयच्छध्वमित्यर्थः ॥ वीर विक्रांतौ !! अपि च प्रजया
> पुत्रादिरूपया मा हास्महि । वयं मा परित्यज्येमहि । मा च तनूभिः शरीरैस्त्यज्येमहि । आस्मान्कदाचिदपि पुत्रादयः शरीराणि च मा परित्याक्षुरित्यर्थः ॥ ओ
> हाक् त्यागे । आस्मात्मर्मणि लुजि चिण्णद्भावाभावे रूपमेतत् ॥ तथा हे राजन्राजमान यद्वास्माकं स्वामिन् हे सोम द्विषतेऽप्रीतिं कुर्वते ॥ द्विषेः शतर्या-
> 47

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O six wide ones": six in number, the wide ones (*urvyaḥ*). They are recited elsewhere: षण्मोर्विरंहसः पांतु द्यौश्च पृथिवी चाहश्च रात्रिश्चापश्चौषधयश्चति । (*ṣaṇmorviraṃhasaḥ pāṃtu dyauśca pṛthivī cāhaśca rātriścāpaścauṣadhayaścati |*). Being such, O goddesses (देवीः (*devīḥ*)), you, make for us (नः कृणोत (*naḥ kṛṇota*)) wide, that is, ample wealth (उरु (*uru*)). "O all gods (विश्वे देवासः (*viśve devāsaḥ*)), exert your prowess (वीरयध्वं (*vīrayadhvaṃ*)) here (इह (*iha*)), in this matter of the wealth to be obtained", that is, show valour, so that we may obtain that wealth. The sense is: "grant it, being so valiant". Further, may we not be deserted (मा हास्महि (*mā hāsmahi*)) by offspring, sons and the like, nor deserted by our bodies; that is, may sons and the rest, and our bodies, never forsake us. Then, "O king (राजन् (*rājan*)), shining one, or else our lord, O Soma, may we not रधाम (*radhāma*) to the one who hates (द्विषते (*dviṣate*)), who acts without love", where the dative stands for the genitive; the sense is "may we not fall into the power of the hating enemy, so act". Yāska says रध्यति (*radhyati*) means "going into subjection" (Ni. 6-32 is not cited here; the text of this block continues on p. 738).

### Printed p. 738

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दादित्वाच्चपो लुक् । शतुरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी वक्तव्येति
> चतुर्थी ॥ द्विषतः शत्रोर्मा रधाम । मा वशं प्राप्नुयाम! तथा त्वं कुर्वित्यर्थः।
> रध्यतिर्वशगमन इति यास्कः । नि. ६-३२ । यद्वा । द्विषते शत्रवे तदर्थं मा रधाम ।
> परिपक्वा हननार्हा मा भूम । रथ हिंसासंराध्योः । संराध्धिः पाक इति तद्वृत्तिः ।
> माजि लुजि पुषादित्वाच्चेरजादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The block gives the Nirukta citation रध्यतिर्वशगमन इति यास्कः । नि. ६-३२ (*radhyatirvaśagamana iti yāskaḥ | ni. 6-32*) (Ni. 6-32): to "fall into the power of the enemy". Alternatively: for the hater, the enemy, may we not be रधाम (*radhāma*), that is, may we not become ripened, fit to be slain for him. The root रथ (*ratha*) is in the senses of killing and of perfecting (saṃrādhi), and "saṃrādhi is cooking" is the gloss on the latter sense.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- षट् उर्वीः (*ṣaṭ urvīḥ*)—six in number and of great majesty
- देवीः (*devīḥ*)—O goddesses, you
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- उरु (*uru*)—abundant wealth
- कृणोत (*kṛṇota*)—provide
- इह (*iha*)—in this matter of obtaining wealth
- विश्वे देवासः (*viśve devāsaḥ*)—O Viśvedevas, you
- वीरयध्वं (*vīrayadhvaṃ*)—make effort (and we)
- प्रजया (*prajayā*)—by sons and the like
- मा हास्महि (*mā hāsmahi*)—may we not be left without them
- तनूभिः (*tanūbhiḥ*)—by bodies also
- मा (*mā*)—may we not be forsaken
- राजन् (*rājan*)—lord, or shining one
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- द्विषते (*dviṣate*)—to the enemies who hate us
- मा रथाम (*mā rathāma*)—may we not fall into their power

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O six goddesses of great majesty, provide us with abundant wealth. In this matter let the Viśvedevas also strive to help us. May we not be without sons, that is, may we not lack sons and the rest, and may separation from the body, that is, death, not befall us. O Soma, our lord, may we not be put under the power of the enemies who hate us and be destroyed.

##### English translation
You, six mighty goddesses, bestow upon us ample (wealth); universal gods, display prowess here; let us not be bereft of our offspring, or be harmed in our bodies, may we not become subject to our enemy, royal Soma.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Here, by "six wide goddesses" the Bhāṣyakāra means the six goddesses who are the presiding deities of heaven (dyau), earth, the days, the night, the waters, and the herbs and trees, and he has cited in that connection the above śruti passage षण्मोर्वी रंहसः पांतु द्यौश्च पृथिवी चाहश्च रात्रिश्चापश्चौषधयश्च (*ṣaṇmorvī raṃhasaḥ pāṃtu dyauśca pṛthivī cāhaśca rātriścāpaścauṣadhayaśca*).

> हे अग्ने परेषां शत्रूणां मन्युं क्रोधं प्रतिनुदन् प्रतिमुखं प्रेरयंस्तिरस्कुर्वनदब्धः केनाप्यहिंसितो गोपा गोपायिता ॥ गुपू रक्षण इत्यस्मादायप्रत्ययांतात्किपि वेरपृक्तस्य लोपात्पूर्वं वलि लोपे रूपमेतत् ॥ ईदृशस्त्वं
> नोऽस्मान्परि पाहि । परितः सर्वतो रक्ष । ते शत्रवः प्रत्यंचः प्रत्यंचंतः प्रतिनिवर्तमाना निगुतः ॥ गुज् अव्यक्ते शब्दे । आस्मात्किपि तुक् ॥ भयेन गद्गदरूपमव्यक्तं
> शब्दं नितरां कुर्वंतः पुनर्यंतु । स्वकीयं स्थानं पुनर्गच्छंतु । अपि च प्रबुधां
> प्रबुध्यमानानामेतेषां शत्रूणां चित्तं ज्ञानसाधनं मनोऽमा सह युगपदेव
> वि नेशत् । विनश्यतु ॥ प्रत्येकाभिप्रायेणैकवचनं । णश आदर्शन इत्यस्माच्चांदसो
> लुज् । पुषादित्वाच्चॆरजादेशः । नशिमन्योरलिट्यत्वं वक्तव्यं । सा. ६-४-१२०-५ ॥
> इत्यकारस्यॆत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, driving back (प्रतिनुदन् (*pratinudan*)) the wrath of the enemies, that is, repelling it face to face and putting it down; unharmed (अदब्धः (*adabdhaḥ*)) by anyone; protector (गोपाः (*gopāḥ*)), guardian: such as you are, protect us on all sides (परि पाहि (*pari pāhi*)). May those enemies of yours turn back (प्रत्यंचः (*pratyaṃcaḥ*)), retreating, and, from fear, making a faltering, indistinct sound (निगुतः (*nigutaḥ*)), go again (पुनर्यंतु (*punaryaṃtu*)) to their own place. Further, may the mind (चित्तं (*cittaṃ*)), the instrument of knowing, of these enemies who are awake (प्रबुधां (*prabudhāṃ*)), perish (वि नेशत् (*vi neśat*)) at the same moment (अमा (*amā*)); the singular is used with reference to each one.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- परेषां (*pareṣāṃ*)—of the enemies
- मन्युं (*manyuṃ*)—the wrath
- प्रतिनुदन् (*pratinudan*)—who spurns
- अदब्धः (*adabdhaḥ*)—who is subject to no one's harm
- गोपाः (*gopāḥ*)—who protects the singers of praise
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- परि (*pari*)—all round
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—protect
- प्रत्यंचः (*pratyaṃcaḥ*)—returning defeated
- ते (*te*)—your enemies
- निगुतः (*nigutaḥ*)—muttering from fear
- पुनः यंतु (*punaḥ yaṃtu*)—let them go back again to their own places

### Printed p. 740
- प्रबुधां (*prabudhāṃ*)—who are alert
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of these enemies
- चित्तं (*cittaṃ*)—the mind (or discriminating knowledge)
- अमा (*amā*)—at once
- वि नेशत् (*vi neśat*)—let it perish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who spurn the anger of the enemies without regard, and who are subject to no one's harm, protect us everywhere. May the enemies who return defeated go back to their places muttering from fear, or speaking in stammering words. May the mind, that is, the power of discernment, of these enemies who are ever on the alert be destroyed at once.

##### English translation
Agni you are an invincible protector, defend us, baffling the wrath of our enemies ; let them return grumbling to their homes, may the intelligence of those watchful (foes) be at once destroyed.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> धा॒ता धा॑तृ॒णां भुव॑नस्य॒ यस्पति॑र्दे॒वं त्रा॒तार॑मभिमातिषा॒हं ।

> न्यर्थात् ॥ ७ ॥

> धाता । धातृणां । भुवनस्य । यः । पतिः । देवं । त्रातारं । अभिमातिसहं ।  
> इमं । यज्ञं । अश्विना । उभा । बृहस्पतिः । देवाः । पांतु । यजमानं । निअर्थात् ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धातृणां स्रष्टाणामपि धाता स्रष्टा भुवनस्य कृत्स्नस्य भूतजातस्य य इंद्रः
> सविता वा पतिः पालयिता तं देवं देवनशीलं त्रातारं सर्वेभ्यो भयेभ्यः पालयितारमभिमातिषाहमभिमातीनां शत्रोणां सोढारमभिभवितारं एवंगुणविशिष्टमिंद्रं सवितारं वा स्तौमीति शेषः ॥ षह अभिभवे । छंदसि सह इति णिप्रत्ययः ।
> छांदसं विभक्तुदात्तत्वं ॥ उभोभावश्विन् बृहस्पतिश्चैतत्पमुखाः सर्वे देवा इमं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He who, as the creator (धाता (*dhātā*)) even of creators (धातृणां (*dhātṛṇāṃ*)), is the lord (पतिः (*patiḥ*)), the protector, of the whole universe (भुवनस्य (*bhuvanasya*)), that is, Indra or Savitṛ: that god (देवं (*devaṃ*)), of shining nature, the saviour (त्रातारं (*trātāraṃ*)) who guards from all fears, the vanquisher (अभिमातिषाहं (*abhimātiṣāhaṃ*)) who overcomes hostile enemies, Indra or Savitṛ, endowed with such qualities, I praise; "I praise" is to be supplied. Both Aśvins, Bṛhaspati, and all the gods headed by them protect this sacrifice that is being performed, and the sacrificer, from न्यर्थात् (*nyarthāt*).

### Printed p. 741

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यज्ञमनुष्ठीयुमानं यजमानं च न्यर्थान्निकृष्णादर्थात्पापात् । यद्वा । अर्थस्य
> प्रयोजनस्याभावो न्यर्थं । तस्मात्पांतु । रक्षंतु । सफलं कुर्वंतित्यर्थः ॥ नेरनिधाने । पा ६-२-१९२ । इत्युत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

न्यर्थात् (*nyarthāt*) means from a low or mean object, that is, from sin. Or else: न्यर्थं (*nyarthaṃ*) is the absence of an object (artha), of purpose; from that let them protect, that is, make it fruitful. For न्यर्थात् (*nyarthāt*) the accent is on the final of the latter member, by Pā. 6-2-192.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the god who
- धातृणां (*dhātṛṇāṃ*)—of creators
- धाता (*dhātā*)—is the creator
- भुवनस्य (*bhuvanasya*)—of the whole world of living beings
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—who is the protector: such
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—shining
- त्रातारं (*trātāraṃ*)—who saves from fears
- अभिमातिषाहं (*abhimātiṣāhaṃ*)—who conquers enemies: Indra or the god Savitṛ I praise
- उभा अश्विनौ (*ubhā aśvinau*)—both Aśvins
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Bṛhaspati
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—all the gods headed by them
- इमं यज्ञं (*imaṃ yajñaṃ*)—this sacrifice that is going on
- यजमानं (*yajamānaṃ*)—this sacrificer who sacrifices
- न्यर्थात् (*nyarthāt*)—from sin
- पांतु (*pāṃtu*)—let them protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise Indra or the god Savitṛ, who is the creator even of the gods who are creators, who is the protector of the whole world of living beings, who is shining, who saves from all kinds of fear, and who defeats enemies. May the two Aśvins, Bṛhaspati and all the gods headed by them protect this sacrifice now going on, and the sacrificer, so that no sin befalls.

##### English translation
The creator of creators, he who is the protector of the universe, (him I praise), the divine defender, the destroyer of enemies; may the two Ashwins, Brihaspathi, and the gods, protect this sacrifice from disappoint- ment.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the first half of this Ṛk the Bhāṣyakāra gives the meaning "I praise Indra or the god Savitṛ, endowed with the qualities beginning with धाता धातृणां (*dhātā dhātṛṇāṃ*)". Although this meaning is appropriate, the same sūkta, with slight changes, is recited in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 4-7-14), and there the word सवितारं (*savitāraṃ*) is used in place of त्रातारं (*trātāraṃ*) in this Ṛk. It therefore appears that the deity intended here may be Savitṛ.
