> रश्मीन् ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सहस्तोमाः । सहछंदसः । आवृतः । सहप्रमाः । ऋषयः । सप्त ! दैन्व्याः ।  
> पूर्वॆषां । पंथां । अनुदृश्य । धीराः । अनुआलेभिरे । रथ्यः । न । रश्मीन् ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्तोमैः त्रिवृत्पंचदशादिभिः सह वर्तमानाः सहस्तोमाः सहच्छंदसो
> गायत्र्यादिभिश्चंदोभिः सह वर्तमाना आवृत आवर्तमानाः सहप्रमाः । प्रमितिः
> प्रमा यज्ञस्येयत्तापरिज्ञानं । तेन सह वर्तमाना दैव्या देवस्य प्रजापतेः
> संबंधिनः यद्वा देवानां यष्टव्यानां संबंधिन ऋषयो द्रष्टारः सप्तसंख्याकाः
> शीर्षण्याः । यद्वा । मरीचिप्रमुखाः सप्तर्षयो होत्रादयः सप्त वषट्कर्तारो
> ना । एवंविधा एते पूर्वेषां पूर्वपुरुषाणामंगिरःप्रभृतीनां विश्वसृजां
> देवानां ना पंथां पंणानमनुष्ठानमार्गमनुदृश्य क्रमेण ज्ञात्वा धीरा धीमंतः
> संतोऽन्वालेभिरे । अनुक्रमेणारब्धवंतः । यागानुष्ठाने प्रवृत्ता इत्यर्थः ।
> रथ्यो न यथा रथिनो रथेन युक्ता रथस्य नेतारः सूता रश्मीनश्वनियोजनार्थान्प्रग्रहान् सम्यग्रथस्य नयनाय हस्तेनान्सारभंते अन्वारभ्य च सम्यक् तं रथं
> प्रवर्तयंति एवमेतेऽप्यनुष्ठानमार्गं श्रुतितोऽवगम्य सम्यगन्वतिष्ठन्नित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सहस्तोमाः (*sahastomāḥ*): those who are with stomas such as the Trivṛt and Pañcadaśa. सहच्छंदसः (*sahacchaṃdasaḥ*): those who are with metres such as Gāyatrī. आवृतः (*āvṛtaḥ*): those who go on reciting. सहप्रमाः (*sahapramāḥ*): प्रमितिः प्रमा (*pramitiḥ pramā*), that is, knowledge of the extent of the sacrifice; those who are with that. दैव्याः (*daivyāḥ*): belonging to the god Prajāpati, or else belonging to the gods who are to be worshipped. The seers, the "seers" (drastāraḥ), seven in number, are शीर्षण्याः (*śīrṣaṇyāḥ*) (chief). Or else they are the seven seers headed by Marīci, or the seven vaṣaṭkartṛs (those who utter the vaṣaṭ), the Hotṛ and the others. Such as these, having in due order come to know the path, the way of performance, of the forefathers, the world-creating gods beginning with Aṅgiras, and being wise, अन्वालेभिरे (*anvālebhire*): began in order; that is, engaged in performing the sacrifice. रथ्यो न (*rathyo na*): just as charioteers, yoked to the chariot and leading it, take in the hand the reins, the straps for guiding the horses, in order to drive the chariot well, and having taken them up make it go properly, so these too, having learned the way of performance from the revealed text, performed it properly: this is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहस्तोमाः (*sahastomāḥ*)—those accompanied by the recitation of stomas such as Trivṛt and Pañcadaśa
- सहच्छंदसः (*sahacchaṃdasaḥ*)—those who recite mantras of the seven metres beginning with Gāyatrī
- आवृतः (*āvṛtaḥ*)—those who recite the mantras
- सहप्रमाः (*sahapramāḥ*)—those possessed of knowledge of the performance of the sacrifice
- दैन्व्याः (*dainvyāḥ*)—belonging to the god Prajāpati, or belonging to the gods
- सप्त ऋषयः (*sapta ṛṣayaḥ*)—the seven seers beginning with Marīci, or

### Printed p. 801

the Hotṛ and the other vaṣaṭ-performers
- पूर्वॆषां (*pūrvèṣāṃ*)—of the forefathers, Aṅgiras and the others, or of the world-creating gods
- पंथां (*paṃthāṃ*)—the path of performance of the sacrifice
- अनुदृश्य (*anudṛśya*)—having understood in order
- धीराः (*dhīrāḥ*)—being wise
- रथ्यः (*rathyaḥ*)—the charioteer who drives the chariot
- रश्मीन्‌न (*raśmīnna*)—as he takes the reins of the horses
- अन्वालेभिरॆ (*anvālebhirè*)—began the performance of the sacrifice in order, that is, engaged in it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The seven seers beginning with Marīci, belonging to the gods, or the seven vaṣaṭ-performers, reciting the stoma mantras such as Trivṛt and Pañcadaśa and the mantras of the seven metres beginning with Gāyatrī, and possessed of knowledge of the performance of the sacrifice, having learned the way of performing the sacrifice of the earlier world-creating gods or of Aṅgiras and the others, became wise, and engaged in performing the sacrifice, as a charioteer who drives a chariot takes the reins of the horses and drives it.

##### English translation
Associated with praises, accompanied by metres invested, having authority, the seven divine Rishis, bold, and observing the path of their predecessors like charioteers, took up the reins.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सहस्तोमाः (*sahastomāḥ*)—Among stomas there are nine kinds: the Trivṛt stoma, Pañcadaśa stoma, Saptadaśa stoma, Ekaviṃśa stoma, Triṇava stoma, Trayastriṃśa stoma, Caturviṃśa stoma, and Catuścatvāriṃśa stoma. We have explained these, and the varieties of stuti found in them, at length with examples in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 2, pp. 137-150. The meaning is: those who recite such various stoma mantras. **NOTE**

सहच्छंदसः (*sahacchaṃdasaḥ*)—Although there are many kinds of metres, in sacrifices and the like, in the morning-recitation (prātaranuvāka) mantras, the Śastra mantras and so on, it is chiefly mantras in seven kinds of metre that are recited: Gāyatrī, Triṣṭup, Jagatī, Anuṣṭup, Paṅkti, Uṣṇik and Bṛhatī. There is a rule that such and such mantras must be in such and such a metre. The meaning is: those who recite mantras accompanied by the seven kinds of metre beginning with Gāyatrī.

सहप्रमाः (*sahapramāḥ*)—यज्ञस्येयत्तापरिज्ञानं (*yajñasyeyattāparijñānaṃ*). The intention is: the seers who knew that such a sacrifice must be performed for so many days, and who knew the order of performing the sacrifice.

### Printed p. 802
daivyāḥ—the Sādhyas, the earlier gods who are the vital breath of Prajāpati, the god of gods. Or else:

ṛṣayaḥ sapta—Bharadvāja, Kaśyapa, Gotama, Atri, Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni and Vasiṣṭha are called the seven ṛṣis. Or else they are the priests, the Hotṛ and the others, who perform the seven vaṣaṭkāras.

rathyo na raśmīn—as a charioteer who drives a chariot takes the reins of the horses in his hand in order to drive it, and sets about driving the chariot, so the seven ṛṣis followed the very path of sacrificial performance that the earlier gods or the Aṅgirasa ṛṣis had followed, and themselves set about performing sacrifices. This is the main purport.

## Sūkta 131 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अप प्राच इति सप्तर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं कक्षीवतः पुत्रस्य सुकीर्तरार्षं ।
> चतुर्थ्यनुष्टुप् शिष्टाः षट् त्रिष्टुभः । चतुर्थीपंचम्यावश्विदेवत्ये शिष्टा ऐंद्रः ।
> तथा चानुक्रांतं । अप प्राचः सुकीर्तिः काक्षीवतो मध्यॆऽनुष्टुप्पोत्तरा चाश्विन्याविति ॥ षष्ठेऽहनि ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन उक्धशस्त्र एतत्तूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । सुकीर्तिं
> ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी वृषाकपिं च पंक्तिशंसं । आ. ८-४ । इति ॥ चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिने
> सवने मैत्रावरुणस्याप प्राच इत्येषारंभणीया कद्वत्पगाथानंतरं शंसनीया ।
> सूत्रितं च । कद्वंतः प्रगाथा अप प्राच इंद्र विश्वा अमित्रान् । आ. ७-४ । इति ॥
> अहर्गणेष्टपि द्वितीयादिष्टहःसु तस्यैव तस्मिन्नेव शस्त्र आरंभणीया । सूत्रितं च ।
> आरंभणीयाः पर्यासान्कद्वतोऽहरहः शस्यानीति होत्रका द्वितीयादिष्टेव ।
> आ. ७-१ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the third sūkta of the series, of seven ṛks, seen by Sukīrti, son of Kakṣīvat. The fourth ṛk is in anuṣṭubh and the remaining six are in triṣṭubh. The fourth and fifth ṛks have the Aśvins as deity, and the rest are addressed to Indra. Sāyaṇa quotes the Anukramaṇī: अप प्राचः सुकीर्तिः काक्षीवतो मध्यॆऽनुष्टुप्पोत्तरा चाश्विन्याविति॥ (*apa prācaḥ sukīrtiḥ kākṣīvato madhyè 'nuṣṭuppottarā cāśvinyāviti‖*) Use: on the sixth day, in the ukthya śastra of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, this sūkta is recited. The sūtra says सुकीर्तिं ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी वृषाकपिं च पंक्तिशंसं । आ. ८-४ । इति॥ (*sukīrtiṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsī vṛṣākapiṃ ca paṃktiśaṃsaṃ | ā. 8-4 | iti‖*) (Ā. 8-4). On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, the verse अप प्राच (*apa prāca*) is the ārambhaṇīyā of the Maitrāvaruṇa, to be recited after the Kadvat pragāthas. The sūtra says कद्वंतः प्रगाथा अप प्राच इंद्र विश्वा अमित्रान् । आ. ७-४ । इति॥ (*kadvaṃtaḥ pragāthā apa prāca iṃdra viśvā amitrān | ā. 7-4 | iti‖*) (Ā. 7-4). In the ahargaṇa rites too, from the second day onward, it is the ārambhaṇīyā in that same śastra. The sūtra says आरंभणीयाः पर्यासान्कद्वतोऽहरहः शस्यानीति होत्रका द्वितीयादिष्टेव । आ. ७-१ । इति॥ (*āraṃbhaṇīyāḥ paryāsānkadvato 'harahaḥ śasyānīti hotrakā dvitīyādiṣṭeva | ā. 7-1 | iti‖*) (Ā. 7-1).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, अप प्राच (*apa prāca*), is the third sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka. It has seven ṛks. Its ṛṣi is Sukīrti, son of the ṛṣi Kakṣīvān. In this sūkta the fourth ṛk is in the anuṣṭubh metre. The other six ṛks are in the triṣṭubh metre. The deities of the fourth and fifth ṛks are the Aśvins; the other ṛks have Indra as deity. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: अप प्राचः सुकीर्तिः काक्षीवतो मध्यॆऽनुष्टुप्पोत्तरा चाश्विन् (*apa prācaḥ sukīrtiḥ kākṣīvato madhyè 'nuṣṭuppottarā cāśvin*). On the sixth day of the sacrifice this sūkta is used as ukthaśastra mantras to be recited by the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, सुकीर्तिं ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी वृषाकपिं च पंक्तिशंसं (*sukīrtiṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsī vṛṣākapiṃ ca paṃktiśaṃsaṃ*)

### Printed p. 803
(Ā. 8-4). At the midday pressing on the day called Cāturviṃśika, the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa is to recite this ṛk अप प्राचः (*apa prācaḥ*) after the Kadvat pragāthas; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, कद्वंतः प्रगाथा अप प्राच इंद्र विश्वा अमित्रान् (*kadvaṃtaḥ pragāthā apa prāca iṃdra viśvā amitrān*) (Ā. 7-8). **NOTE** In the ahargaṇa rites also, on the second day and the following days, the Maitrāvaruṇa is to recite it as the opening ṛk among the śastra mantras at the midday pressing; this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, आरंभणीयाः पर्यासान् कद्वतोs हरहः शस्यानीति होत्रका द्वितीयादिष्टेव (*āraṃbhaṇīyāḥ paryāsān kadvatos harahaḥ śasyānīti hotrakā dvitīyādiṣṭeva*) (Ā. 7-1).

Sūkta 131. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 131. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 7; Varga 19. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Ṛṣi: Sukīrti Kākṣīvata. Deity: 1–3, 6, 7 Indra; 4, 5 the Aśvins. Metre: 1–3, 5–7 triṣṭubh; 4 anuṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अप॒ प्राच॑ इंद्र॒ विश्वा॑ अ॒मित्रा॒नपापा॑चो अभिभूते नुदस्व ।  
> अपोदे॑चो॒ अप॑ शूराध॒राच॑ उ॒रौ यथा॒ तव॒ शर्म॒न्मदे॑म॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अप । प्राचः । इंद्र । विश्वान् । अमित्रान् । अप । अपाचः । अभिभूते । नुदस्व ।  
> अप । उदीचः । अप । शूर । अधराचः । उर् । यथा । तव । शर्मन् । मदेम ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र प्राचः प्रमुखमंचतः प्राग्देशे वर्तमानान्। अस्मत्तः पूर्वभागे
> वर्तमानानित्यर्थः ॥ प्रपूर्वादंचतेर्युत्विगित्यादिना क्विन् । अनिदितामित्विनलोपः ।
> शस्य च इत्यकारलोपे चाविति दीर्घत्वं । अनिगंतोऽंचतौ वप्रत्यये । पा. ६-२-५२।
> इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ तादृशान्विश्वान्सर्वानमित्रा ञ्यत्रूनप नुदस्व । अस्मत्तोऽपगमय। तथा हे अभिभूते शत्रूणामभिभवितरिंद्र अपाचोऽपमुखमंचतः पृष्ठभागे

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, drive away from us all the enemies who are प्राचः (*prācaḥ*)", that is, who dwell in the eastern region, in the part before us. Likewise, O Indra, vanquisher of enemies (अभिभूते (*abhibhūte*)), drive away all the enemies who are अपाचः (*apācaḥ*), that is, who face away and are placed at the back.

### Printed p. 804

> वर्तमानान्सर्वाञ्त्यूनप नुदस्व । अपि चोदीच ऊर्ध्वमंचत उपरिवर्तमानान् ॥
> उत्तूर्वादंचतेः पूर्ववत्क्विन्युद ईदित्यंचतेरकारस्येकारः । पूर्ववत्स्वरः ॥ तथाविधानपि शत्रूनप नुदस्व । तथा हे शूर शौर्यवन्निंद्र अधराचोऽधरदेशमधोभागमंचतश्चाधस्तनानपि शत्रूनप नुदस्व ॥ अधरशब्दोपपदादंचतेः शसि पूर्ववत्प्रक्रिया । चानिति पूर्वपदस्यांतोदात्तः ॥ उरौ विस्तीर्णे तव संबंधिनि त्वया दत्ते
> शर्मञ्त्यर्माणि गृहे सुखे वा यथा वयं मदेम निरुपद्रवाः संतो हृष्येम
> तथा त्वं सर्वत्र वर्तमानानस्मदीयाञ्त्यून्विनाशयेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Also drive away the enemies who are उदीचः (*udīcaḥ*), those dwelling above, in the upper direction. Drive away such enemies too. Likewise, O heroic Indra (शूर (*śūra*)), drive away the enemies who are अधराचः (*adharācaḥ*), those dwelling in the lower region, below. उरौ (*urau*) means "wide"; "in your wide शर्मन् (*śarman*)", that is, in the house or happiness given by you. The sense is: destroy our enemies wherever they are, so that, free from danger, we may rejoice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- प्राचः (*prācaḥ*)—those who are in the eastern direction (who are in front of us)
- विश्वान् (*viśvān*)—all
- अमित्रान् (*amitrān*)—enemies
- अप नुदस्व (*apa nudasva*)—drive away from us
- अभिभूते (*abhibhūte*)—O Indra, who overcomes the enemies
- अपाचः (*apācaḥ*)—all the enemies who are behind us
- अप नुदस्व (*apa nudasva*)—drive away
- उदीचः (*udīcaḥ*)—the enemies who are in the upper part
- अप (*apa*)—drive away
- शूर (*śūra*)—O heroic Indra
- अधराचः (*adharācaḥ*)—the enemies who are in the lower part
- अप (*apa*)—drive away
- तव (*tava*)—your
- उरौ (*urau*)—wide
- शर्मन् (*śarman*)—in the house or in happiness
- यथा (*yathā*)—in the way that
- मदेम (*madema*)—we may be joyful; in that way drive away all our enemies

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, so that we may live happily in the house granted by your favour, strike and drive away all the enemies there may be in front of us, behind us, above and below.

##### English translation
Victorious Indra, drive off all our foes, those who dwell in the east, and those who dwell in the west, (drive) off, O hero, those who dwell in the north, those who dwell in the south, that we may rejoice in your exceeding felicity.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कु॒विदं॒ग यव॑मंतो॒ यवं॑ चि॒द्यथा॒ दांत्य॑नुपू॒र्वं  ॒॑
> वियूय ।

### Printed p. 805

> इहेहैषां कृणुहि भोजनानि ये बर्हिषो नमोवृक्तिं न  
> जग्मुः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कुवित् । अंग । यवमंतः । यवं । चित् । यथा । दांति । अनुपूर्वं । वियूय ।  
> इहइह । एषां । कृणुहि । भोजनानि । ये । बर्हिषः । नमःवृक्तिं । न । जग्मुः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अंग हे इंद्र यवमंतो यवादिधान्ययुक्ताः कर्षका यवं चित् ।
> उपलक्षणमेतत् । यवगोधूमादीननुपूर्वं यो यो धान्यविशेषः प्रथमं
> पच्यते तेनानुपूर्व्येण विययू पृथक्कृत्य यथा कुविद्दहुलं दांति लुनंति ॥
> दाप् लवने आदादिकः । विपूर्वाद्यौतेर्ल्यपि युप्लु वोर्दिर्घश्चंदसि । पा. ६-४-५८ ।
> इति दीर्घः ॥ एवमिहेहास्मिन्नस्मिन्देशे सर्वस्मिन्नेषां यजमानानां भोजनानि ।
> धननामैतत् । भोगसाधनानि धनानि कृणुहि । कुरु । यस्मिन्यस्मिन्देशे यद्ध नमपेक्षितं
> तदनुगुणं प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः ॥ उतश्च प्रत्ययाच्छंदसि वावचनं । पा. ६-४-१०६-१ ।
> इति हेर्लुगभावः ॥ एषामित्युक्तं के पुनरिम इत्यत आह । ये यजमाना बर्हिषो
> यज्ञस्य नमोवृक्तिं नमसो हविर्लक्षणस्यान्नस्य नमस्कारात्मकस्य स्तोत्रस्य वा
> वर्जनमकरणं न जग्मुः न प्राप्पुवंति किंतु सर्वदा हविर्भिर्यजंति स्तुतिभिः स्तुवंति
> च । एषां कृणुहीत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Dear Indra (अंग (*aṃga*)), as farmers (यवमंतः (*yavamaṃtaḥ*)) who possess barley and other grains cut (दांति (*dāṃti*)) the barley in abundance (कुवित् (*kuvit*)), separating it in due order, grain by grain as each ripens first; and यवं चित् (*yavaṃ cit*) is only an illustration, standing for barley, wheat and the rest, so here and there, in every place, make (कृणुहि (*kṛṇuhi*)) means of enjoyment (भोजनानि (*bhojanāni*)) for these sacrificers." भोजनानि (*bhojanāni*) is a name for wealth: wealth that is the means of enjoyment. The sense is: in whatever place whatever is wanted, give accordingly. Asked who "these" are, he answers: the sacrificers who have not come (न जग्मुः (*na jagmuḥ*)) to the neglect or non-performance of the बर्हिषः (*barhiṣaḥ*), the sacrifice, of the नमः (*namaḥ*), that is, food in the form of oblation, or praise consisting of homage; rather, they always sacrifice with oblations and praise with hymns. The construction is "make for these".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अंग (*aṃga*)—O Indra
- यवमंतः (*yavamaṃtaḥ*)—farmers who grow barley and other grains
- यवं चित् (*yavaṃ cit*)—barley and other grains
- अनुपूर्वं (*anupūrvaṃ*)—as they grow strong and ripen
- वियूय (*viyūya*)—separating them
- यथा (*yathā*)—in the way that
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—abundantly
- दांति (*dāṃti*)—separate from the crop and cut, in the way that
- ये (*ye*)—those sacrificers who perform the sacrifice
- बर्हिषः (*barhiṣaḥ*)—to be offered in the sacrifice
- नमोवृक्तिं (*namovṛktiṃ*)—the oblation or the hymn
- न जग्मुः (*na jagmuḥ*)—do not abandon
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—for such sacrificers
- इहेह (*iheha*)—in the several places where they perform the sacrifice
- भोजनानि (*bhojanāni*)—wealth that is the means of enjoyment
- कृणुहि (*kṛṇuhi*)—provide

### Printed p. 806

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as farmers who grow grains separate the grains that have ripened and are ready for cutting, and cut them from the crop, so you provide wealth, the means of enjoyment, to the sacrificers who do not forget the oblation or the hymn to be offered in the sacrifice, wherever they may be.

##### English translation
As the growers of barley often cut the barley, separating it in due order, so do you, (O Indra), bestow here and there nourishment upon those who have not neglected the performance of the sacrifice.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न॒हि स्फूर्यृ॑तु॒था या॒तमस्ति॒ नोत श्रवो॑ विविदे संग॒मेषु॑।  
> ग॒व्यंत॒ इंद्रं॑ स॒ख्याय॒ विप्रा॑ अश्वा॒यंतो॒ वृष॑णं वा॒जयं॑तः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नहि । स्थूरि । ऋतुथा । यातं । अस्ति । न । उत । श्रवः । विविदे । संगमेषु ।  
> गव्यंतः । इंद्रं । सख्याय । विप्राः । अश्वयंतः । वृषणं । वाजयंतः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एकेन धुर्येण युक्तमनः स्फूरीत्युच्यते । ऋतुथर्त् यद्यस्मिन्काले
> प्राप्तव्यं तद्योग्यकाले स्फूर्यनो यातं तं देशं प्राप्तं नह्यस्ति । न हि भवति ।
> एकेन धुर्येण युक्तः शकटः शीघ्रं गंतव्यं न प्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः । उतापि च
> संगमेषु संप्रामेषु श्रवोऽन्नं यशो वा न विविदे । न लभते । इंद्रस्तूक्तविलक्षणः । वृषणं वर्षितारं तमिंद्रं गव्यंतो गा इच्छंतो विप्रा मेधाविनो
> वयं सख्याय सखिकर्मण आह्वयाम इति शेषः कथं भूताः । अश्वायंतोऽश्वानप्यात्मन इच्छंतः वाजयंतोऽन्नकामा बलकामाश्च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

A cart yoked with a single draught animal is called स्फूरी (*sphūrī*). What is to be reached at a particular time is not reached by it in due season: it does not reach that place. **NOTE** A cart yoked to a single beast of burden does not reach where it must go quickly. And in संगमेषु (*saṃgameṣu*) one does not obtain (न विविदे (*na vivide*)) श्रवः (*śravaḥ*), food or fame. Indra is different from what has been said. We, the wise (विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)), desiring cattle (गव्यंतः (*gavyaṃtaḥ*)), call upon that showerer (वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)) Indra for friendship (सख्याय (*sakhyāya*)); the verb "we call" is understood. How are we? Desiring horses for ourselves (अश्वायंतः (*aśvāyaṃtaḥ*)), and desiring food and strength (वाजयंतः (*vājayaṃtaḥ*)).

### Printed p. 807

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतुधा (*ṛtudhā*)—that should come in the right season
- स्थूरि (*sthūri*)—a single-yoke cart
- यातं (*yātaṃ*)—to the place where it must go
- नहि अस्ति (*nahi asti*)—does not go and arrive
- उत (*uta*)—and
- संगमेषु (*saṃgameṣu*)—in battles
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—food or fame
- न विविदे (*na vivide*)—does not obtain (but)
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—who bestows what is desired
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- गव्यंतः (*gavyaṃtaḥ*)—desiring to worship
- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—we, the wise
- अश्वायंतः (*aśvāyaṃtaḥ*)—desiring horses
- वाजंयंतः (*vājaṃyaṃtaḥ*)—desiring food or strength
- सख्याय (*sakhyāya*)—for Indra's friendship; we pray to him and call him

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

A cart with only a single yoke, that is, a cart drawn by one ox, does not quickly reach the place where it must go; and with the help of such a cart one cannot win victory in battle and obtain food and the like. But Indra, who bestows what is desired, is one alone, and we, the wise, desiring horses, food and the like and wishing to worship him, seek Indra's friendship and call him with prayer.

##### English translation
The cart has not arrived in due season, nor does he acquire fame in battles; (let us), the sages, desiring cattle, desiring horses, desiring food, (solicit) Indra, the showerer, for his friendship.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यु॒वं सु॒राम॑मश्विना॒ नमु॑चावासु॒रे सचा॑ ।  
> वि॒पि॒पा॒ना शु॑भस्पती॒ इंद्रं॒ कर्म॑स्वावतं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युवं । सुरामं । अश्विना । नमुचौ । आसुरे । सचा ।  
> विपिपाना । शुभः । पती इति । इंद्रं । कर्मऽसु । आवतं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सौत्रामण्यां सुराग्रहाणां पुरोनुवाक्या युवमित्येषा । सूत्रितं च ।
> युवं सुराममश्विनेति ग्रहाणां पुरोनुवाक्या । आ. ३-९ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Sautrāmaṇī, the verse युवं (*yuvaṃ*) is the puronuvākyā for the surā-grahas. The sūtra says: युवं सुराममश्विनेति ग्रहाणां पुरोनुवाक्या । आ. ३-९ । इति॥ (*yuvaṃ surāmamaśvineti grahāṇāṃ puronuvākyā | ā. 3-9 | iti‖*) (Ā. 3-9).

### Printed p. 808

> हे अश्विनाश्विन् हे शुभस्पती उदकस्य शोभनालंकारस्य वा पती पालयितारौ
> सुरामं सुष्टु रमणसाधनमिदं हविर्विपिपाना विशेषेण पीतवंतौ युवं युवां
> सचा संतौ संगतावासुरेऽसुरपुत्रे नमुचावेतत्संज्ञेऽसुरे हंतव्ये सति कर्मसु
> योधनकर्मस्त्विंद्रमावतं । अरक्षतं ॥ विपिपाना । पा पान इत्यस्माल्लिटः कानच् ।
> बहुलं छंदसीत्यभ्यासस्यॆत्वं । शुभस्पती इति सुबामंत्रित इति षष्ठ्यंतस्य परांगवद्भावात्पष्ट्यामंत्रितसमुदायस्याष्टमिकं सर्वानुदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, lords of the waters or of fair adornment, having drunk the pleasing offering (सुरामं (*surāmaṃ*), the means of delight), you two together protected Indra in the battles when the Asura Namuci, the Asura's son, was to be slain. Sāyaṇa glosses *āvataṃ* as "you protected".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुभस्पती (*śubhaspatī*)—those who are guardians of the waters, or those endowed with fair adornment
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- सुरामं (*surāmaṃ*)—this delightful offering
- *epipānā*—having drunk especially
- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you
- सचा (*sacā*)—being together
- आसुरे (*āsure*)—the Asura's son
- नमुचौ (*namucau*)—the Asura named Namuci (who was to be slain)
- कर्मसु (*karmasu*)—in the acts of battle (in which he was engaged)
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- अवतं (*avataṃ*)—you protected

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, guardians of the waters and endowed with fair adornment, after you drank this delightful offering, or Soma, together, you protected Indra while he was fighting the Asura Namuci.

##### English translation
You, O Ashwins, lords of light, having drunk the grateful (libation), jointly preserved Indra in battle against the Asura Namuchi.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

We have described in detail how Indra slew the Asura Namuci in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 19, p. 193.
In the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice, when the cups of surā are taken, this Ṛk beginning युवं (*yuvaṃ*) is to be recited as the Puronuvākyā. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, युवं सुराममश्विनेति ग्रहाणां पुरोनुवाक्या (*yuvaṃ surāmamaśvineti grahāṇāṃ puronuvākyā*) (Ā. 3-9).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पु॒त्रमि॑व पि॒तरा॑व॒श्विनो॒भेंद्रा॒वथुः॒ काव्य॑र्दं॒सना॑भिः ।

### Printed p. 809

> यत्सुरामं व्यपिबः शचीभिः सरस्वती त्वा मघवन्न भिष्णक् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुत्रं इव । पितरौ । अश्विना । उभा । इंद्र । अवधुः । काव्यैः । दंसनाभिः ।  
> यत् । सुरामं । वि । अपिबः । शचीभिः । सरस्वती । त्वा । मघवन् । अभिष्णक् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पूर्वोक्तानामेव ग्रहाणां पुत्रमिवेति याज्या । सूत्रितं च । पुत्रमिव
> पितरावश्विनोभेति याज्या । आ. ३-९ । इति ॥
> हे इंद्र त्वां पितरौ मातापितरौ पुत्रमिव ॥ पिता मात्रा । पा. १-२-७० । इति
> पितुः शेषः ॥ उभोभावश्विन् काव्यैः प्रशस्यॆर्दंसनाभिरात्मीयैः कर्मभिरावथुः ॥
> मध्यमो व्यत्ययेन ॥ आवतुः । ररक्षतुः । त्वं च सुरामं सुखेन रमणसाधनं
> हविर्यद्यदा शचीभिः शक्तिभिः सार्धं व्यपिबः विशेषेण पीतवानसि तदा हे मघवन्थनवन्निंद्र सरस्वती देवी त्वा त्वामभिष्णक् । उपासेवत ॥ भिष्णक् उपसेवायां ।
> कंड्वादिः । छांदसो यगभावः । लजि बहुलं छंदसीति शपो लुक् । हल्ज्याब्ब
> इति लोपः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the Yājyā for the same cups mentioned before (in the Sautrāmaṇī); he cites the sūtra पुत्रमिव पितरावश्विनोभेति याज्या (*putramiva pitarāvaśvinobheti yājyā*) (Ā. 3-9). O Indra, the two Aśvins protected you with their own praiseworthy deeds, as the two parents (mother and father) protect a son. Here the father alone remains, by Pā. 1-2-70, as the printed text cites it. आवथुः (*āvathuḥ*) is the middle person used by a change and means "they protected". And when you drank the pleasing offering, the easy means of delight, together with your powers (शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)), then, O wealthy Indra, the goddess Sarasvatī served you; अभिष्णक् (*abhiṣṇak*) means "she attended on you".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- पितरौ (*pitarau*)—mother and father
- पुत्रमिव (*putramiva*)—as they protect their sons
- उभा अश्विना (*ubhā aśvinā*)—both the Aśvin deities
- काव्यैः (*kāvyaiḥ*)—praiseworthy
- दंसनाभिः (*daṃsanābhiḥ*)—by their daring deeds
- आवथुः (*āvathuḥ*)—protected you
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—you, O wealthy Indra
- सुरामं (*surāmaṃ*)—the delight-giving offering
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—with your powers
- वि अपिबः (*vi apibaḥ*)—you drank
- सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)—the goddess Sarasvatī
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अभिष्णक् (*abhiṣṇak*)—came near

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as parents protect their sons, the two Aśvin deities protected you with their praiseworthy daring deeds. O wealthy Indra, when you drank the delight-giving offering for the increase of your valour, the goddess Sarasvatī came to you and served you.

### Printed p. 810

##### English translation
Both the Ashwins defended (thee), Indra, like two fathers (defending) a son with glorious exploits; when (triumphing) through the deeds of valour, you drank the grateful libation, Saraswati approached you, O Maghavat.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Sautrāmaṇī cup-taking described earlier, this Ṛk beginning पुत्रमिव (*putramiva*) is to be recited as the Yājyā mantra. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, पुत्रमिव पितरावश्विनोभेति याज्या (*putramiva pitarāvaśvinobheti yājyā*) (Ā. 3-9).

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः॑ सु॒त्रामा॒ स्ववा॒ अवो॑भिः सुमृळी॒को भ॑वतु वि॒श्ववे॑दाः ।  
> बाध॑तां॒ द्वेषो॒ अभ॑यं कृणोतु सु॒वीर्य॑स्य॒ पत॑यः  
> स्याम ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । सुत्रामा । स्ववान् । अवभिः । सुमृळीकः । भवतु । विश्ववेदाः ।  
> बाधतां । द्वेषः । आभयं । कृणोतु । सुवीर्यस्य । पतयः । स्याम ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुत्रामा सुष्टु त्राता स्ववान्थनवान् स इंद्रोऽवोभी रक्षणैः सुमृळीकः
> सुष्टु सुखयिता भवतु । तथा च विश्ववेदाः सर्वधनः सर्वविद्वान्वा स इंद्रो
> द्वेषो द्वेष्टन् शत्र्यान् बाधतां । हिनस्तु । अभयं भयरहितं चास्माकं
> कृणोतु । करोतु । वयं च तत्पसादात्सुवीर्यस्य शोभनवीर्यस्य पतयः
> स्याम । भवेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May that Indra, the good protector and wealthy one (स्ववान् (*svavān*)), be a good bestower of happiness through his protections. And may he, the all-possessing or all-knowing (विश्ववेदाः (*viśvavedāḥ*)), strike down our hating enemies and make us free from fear. May we, by his grace, become lords of fair valour (सुवीर्यस्य (*suvīryasya*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुत्रामा (*sutrāmā*)—the one who protects exceedingly
- स्ववान् (*svavān*)—the wealthy one
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अवोभिः (*avobhiḥ*)—with his protections
- सुमृळीकः (*sumṛḷīkaḥ*)—as one who gives excellent happiness

### Printed p. 811
- भवतु (*bhavatu*)—let him be
- विश्ववेदाः (*viśvavedāḥ*)—Indra, who knows everything
- द्वेषः (*dveṣaḥ*)—the enemies who hate us
- बाधतां (*bādhatāṃ*)—let him strike down
- आभयं (*ābhayaṃ*)—freedom from fear for us
- कृणोतु (*kṛṇotu*)—let him bring about
- सुवीरस्य (*suvīrasya*)—of all wealth that is excellent and powerful
- पतयः (*patayaḥ*)—as lords
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may he favour us so that we become

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, who protects exceedingly and is wealthy, give excellent happiness with his protections. May Indra, who knows everything, strike down the enemies who hate us. May he make us free from fear. May we become lords of all wealth that is excellent and powerful.

##### English translation
May Indra, the protector, the possessor of great wealth, the all-knowing, be favourable (to us) with his protections; may he confound our enemies, may he make us free from fear, may we be the parents of excellent male offspring.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May we be within the fair, gracious mind (सुमतौ (*sumatau*)) of the sacrifice-worthy Indra, that is, become objects of it; and in his auspicious good-will (सौमनसे (*saumanase*))

> भवेमेति ॥ सप्तम्यास्तु । तस्य यज्ञार्हस्येंद्रस्यानुग्रहबुद्धौ भजनीये सौमनस्ये
> च वयं विषयभूता भवेम । सुष्टु त्राता धनवान् स इंद्रोऽस्मत्तो दूरदेशे
> द्वेष्टानंतर्धानं योजयत्विति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

we also, may we be. The sense is: may that Indra produce in us a gracious mind and good-will. May the same Indra, the good protector and wealthy one, keep the hating enemies (द्वेषः (*dveṣaḥ*)) far away from us, hidden (सनुतः (*sanutaḥ*) means "concealed"), and separate them (युयोतु (*yuyotu*)). Sāyaṇa says the passage *trātāramiṃdraṃ* in 4-7-32 has been explained already in this section. The word-by-word sense is: may Indra, the good protector, wealthy and knower of all, be a good giver of happiness through his protections, strike down enemies and give us freedom from fear; therefore may we become lords of wealth endowed with fair valour. As for the seventh-case construction (सप्तम्यास्तु (*saptamyāstu*)): may we become objects in the gracious mind of that sacrifice-worthy Indra and in his adorable good-will; and may that good protector, the wealthy Indra, bring about the concealment of the hater far from us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तस्य यज्ञियस्य (*tasya yajñiyasya*)—of that Indra, worthy of worship
- सुमत् (*sumat*)—to the gracious mind, as its objects
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we be
- भद्रे (*bhadre*)—auspicious
- सौमनसे अपि (*saumanase api*)—may we also be objects of his affection
- सुत्रामा (*sutrāmā*)—the one who protects exceedingly
- स्ववान् (*svavān*)—the wealthy one
- स इंद्रः (*sa iṃdraḥ*)—that same Indra
- द्वेषः (*dveṣaḥ*)—the enemies who hate us
- अस्मे (*asme*)—than ourselves
- आराच्चित् (*ārāccit*)—in a place extremely far away
- सनुतः (*sanutaḥ*)—out of sight
- युयोतु (*yuyotu*)—let him keep them apart, not joined with us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May we be objects of the gracious mind of that same Indra, who is worthy of worship. May we also be objects of his auspicious affection. May that same Indra, who protects exceedingly and is wealthy, keep the enemies who hate us in a place extremely far from us, out of our sight and not joined with us.

##### English translation
May we be ever in (the enjoyment of) the favour of that adorable divinity (retained) in his favourable thoughts, and may the protecting and opulent Indra drive away far off from us those who hate us

## Sūkta 132 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ईजानमिति सप्तर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं नृमेधपुत्रस्य शकपूतस्यार्षं मित्रावरुणदेवताकं । आद्या तु लिंगोक्तद्युभूम्यश्विदेवताका न्यंकुसारिणी द्वितीयद्वादशकत्र्यष्टकवती । द्वितीयाषष्ठौ प्रस्तारपंक्ति द्विद्वादशकद्व्यष्टकवती । सप्तमी
> महासतो बृहती त्र्यष्टकद्विद्वादशकवती । शिष्वासिस्तिस्रो विराडूपा एकादशिनस्त्रयोऽष्टकश्चेति लक्षणलक्षिताः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । ईजानं शकपूतो नार्मेधो मैत्रावरुणं न्यंकुसारिण्यद्या लिंगोक्तदेवतांत्या महासतोबृहत्युपाद्योपांत्ये
> प्रस्तारपंक्ति शेषा विराडूपा इति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning ईजानं (*ījānaṃ*) has seven Ṛks and is the fourth sūkta (of the anuvāka). Its seer is Śakapūta, son of Nṛmedha, and its deity Mitrāvaruṇa. The first Ṛk has as its deities those named by the gender-marks in it: heaven, earth and the Aśvins. It is a Nyaṅkusāriṇī, with a second pāda of twelve syllables and three of eight. The second and sixth are Prastārapaṅktis with two twelves and two eights. The seventh is a Mahāsatobṛhatī, with two twelves and three eights. The remaining three are Virāḍrūpās, with three elevens and an eight. He cites the Anukramaṇī: ईजानं शकपूतो नार्मेधो मैत्रावरुणं न्यंकुसारिण्यद्या लिंगोक्तदेवतांत्या महासतोबृहत्युपाद्योपांत्ये प्रस्तारपंक्ति शेषा विराडूपा इति ॥ (*ījānaṃ śakapūto nārmedho maitrāvaruṇaṃ nyaṃkusāriṇyadyā liṃgoktadevatāṃtyā mahāsatobṛhatyupādyopāṃtye prastārapaṃkti śeṣā virāḍūpā iti ‖*). He then says the viniyoga has been given.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning ईजानं (*ījānaṃ*) is the fourth sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. Its seer is Śakapūta, son of Nṛmedha; its deities are Mitra and Varuṇa. For the first Ṛk of this sūkta the deities indicated by the gender-marks (Heaven, Earth and the Aśvin deities) are the deities; for the remaining Ṛks 2-7 Mitra and Varuṇa are the deities. The first Ṛk of this sūkta is in the metre named Nyūṅkusāriṇī. A Ṛk in this metre has four pādas, of which the second has 12 syllables and the other three have eight each. The second and sixth Ṛks are in the metre named Prastārapaṅkti. A Ṛk in this metre has four pādas, of which the first two have twelve syllables each and the last two have eight each. The seventh Ṛk is in the metre named Mahāsatobṛhatī. A Ṛk in this metre has five pādas, of which the first two have twelve syllables each and the last three have eight each. The remaining three Ṛks are in the metre named Virāḍrūpā. A Ṛk in this metre has eleven syllables in each of the first three pādas and eight syllables in the last pāda. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: ईजानं शाकपूतो नार्मेधो मैत्रावरुणं न्यूकुसारिण्याद्या लिंगोक्तदेवतांत्या महासतोबृहत्युपाद्योपांत्ये प्रस्तारपंक्ति शेषा विराड्रूपाः (*ījānaṃ śākapūto nārmedho maitrāvaruṇaṃ nyūkusāriṇyādyā liṃgoktadevatāṃtyā mahāsatobṛhatyupādyopāṃtye prastārapaṃkti śeṣā virāḍrūpāḥ*). The viniyoga has been stated earlier.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ई॒जा॒नमिद्यौगू॒र्ताव॑सुरीजा॒नं भूमि॑र॒भि प्र॑भू॒षणि॑ ।  
> ई॒जा॒नं दे॒वाव॒श्विना॑व॒भि सु॒म्मैर॑वर्धतां ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ईजानं । इत् । द्यौः । गूर्तवसुः । ईजानं । भूमिः । अभि । प्रभूषणि ।  
> ईजानं । देवौ । आत्विनौ । अभि । सुम्नैः । अवर्धतां ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गूर्तवसुः । गूर्तमुद्यतं स्तोतृभ्यो दानाय हस्ते धृतं वसु धनं
> यस्याः सा तथोक्ता ॥ गुरी उद्यमने । निष्ठा । श्विदितो निष्ठायामितीट्टतिषेधः ।
> नसत्तनिषत्तेत्यादिना निपातनान्निस्थानत्वाभावः । अन्वेषामपीति सांहितिको दीर्घः ।
> बहुहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ ईदृशी द्यौर्म्यलोकाभिमानिनी देवतेजानमिद्यज्ञैरिष्टवंतमेव पुरुषमभवर्धयति ॥ यजेर्लिटः कानच् । वचिस्वॆपीति
> संप्रसारणे द्विर्वचनं ॥ तथा भूमिश्च प्रभूषणि प्रभवने यद्वा प्रकृष्टभूषणेऽलंकारे निमित्तभूते सतीजानमभिवर्धयति । आपि च देवौ दानादिगुणयुक्तावश्विनावीजानमिष्टवंतं पुरुषं सुम्मैर्धनैरभ्यवर्धतां । अभिवर्धयतः ॥ वृधेरंतर्भावितण्यर्थाच्छांदसो लज् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

गूर्तवसुः (*gūrtavasuḥ*) is one whose wealth is "raised" (*gūrtaṃ*), that is, held up in the hand for giving to the singers. Such a Heaven, the deity presiding over the heavenly world, advances only the man who has sacrificed, the ईजानं (*ījānaṃ*), by means of sacrifices. Likewise the Earth advances him when there is प्रभूषणि (*prabhūṣaṇi*), either "in prospering" or, alternatively, "when excellent adornment is the cause". The two divine Aśvins, endowed with qualities such as generosity, also advance the sacrificer with सुम्नैः (*sumnaiḥ*), that is, with riches; अवर्धतां (*avardhatāṃ*) means "they advance".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गूर्तवसुः (*gūrtavasuḥ*)—holding wealth raised in the hand in order to give it
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—the deity presiding over the heavenly world
- ईजानं इत् (*ījānaṃ it*)—advances the very man who sacrifices, the sacrificer, with wealth and the like

### Printed p. 815
- प्रभूषणि (*prabhūṣaṇi*)—shining with special adornments
- भूमिः (*bhūmiḥ*)—the Earth goddess
- ईजानं (*ījānaṃ*)—the sacrificer
- अभि (*abhi*)—advances
- देवौ (*devau*)—endowed with qualities such as generosity
- अश्विनौ (*aśvinau*)—the Aśvin deities
- ईजानं (*ījānaṃ*)—the sacrificer
- सुम्नैः (*sumnaiḥ*)—with riches
- अभि अवर्धतां (*abhi avardhatāṃ*)—cause to prosper

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The deity presiding over the heavenly world, who holds wealth raised in her hand for the very purpose of giving it, gives wealth to the man who sacrifices. The Earth goddess, resplendent with the adornment of plants, gives the sacrificer grain and other riches and makes him prosper. The Aśvin deities, endowed with generosity and other qualities, give the sacrificer riches and make him prosper.

##### English translation
The Heaven liberal of treasure (prospers) the sacrificer, the Earth (prospers) the sacrificer because of the ornament, the divine Ashwins prospered the sacrificer with blessings.
#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ता वां॑ मित्रावरुणा धार॒यत्क्र॑ी सुषु॒म्नेषि॑त॒त्वता॑ यजामसि ।  
> यु॒वोः क्रा॒णाय॑ स॒ख्यैर॒भि ष्या॑म र॒क्षसः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ता । वां । मित्रावरुणा । धारयत्क्री इति धारयत्क्षिती । सुसुम्ना । इषितत्वता ।  
> यजामसि ।  
> युवोः । क्राणाय । सख्यैः । अभि । ष्याम । रक्षसः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणौ धारायत्कृष्टी ध्रियमाणभूमिकौ । यद्वा । क्षितिरिति मनुष्यनाम । हवींषि धारयंतः क्षितयो मनुष्या ययोः स्वभूतास्तथाविधौ ।
> सुषुम्ना सुषुम्नौ सुधन् सुसुखौ ना ता तौ नां युवामिषितत्वतेषितत्वेन ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Mitra and Varuṇa, धारायत्कृष्टी (*dhārāyatkṛṣṭī*)", those who bear the earth. Alternatively, *kṣitiḥ* is a word for "man": the two to whom belong men who bear oblations. सुषुम्ना (*suṣumnā*) means "you two, givers of good wealth, of good happiness"; इषितत्वता (*iṣitatvatā*) is a form with an inserted ṭ-sound in the instrumental singular, a Vedic usage. Alternatively, a bhāva-affix is added again after one that already ends in a bhāva-affix.

### Printed p. 816

> तृतीयैकवचने छांदसस्तकारोपजनः । यद्वा । भावप्रत्ययांतात्पुनरपि भावप्र।
> त्ययो विकरणद्वयवत् ॥ इषितव्यत्वेन प्राप्तव्यत्वेन । हेतौ तृतीया । यतो युवांदेवेषु मध्ये प्राप्तव्य् ततो हेतोर्यजामसि । हविर्भिर्यजामः ॥ इदंतो
> मसीति मस इकारागमः । एवं च युवोर्युवयोः सख्यैः सखित्वैः ॥ सख्युर्यः॥
> क्राणाय कुर्वते यजमानाय ॥ करोतेः शानचि च्छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् ।
> तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी ॥ यजमानार्थ० रक्षसो यज्ञस्य बाधकान्नाक्षसानभि ष्याम ।
> अभिभवेम ॥ उपसर्गप्रादुर्भ्या० ।, पा. ८-३-८७ । इत्यस्तेः सकारस्य षत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

इषितव्यत्वेन (*iṣitavyatvena*) means "because you are to be reached"; the instrumental is of cause. Because you are to be reached among the gods, therefore यजामसि (*yajāmasi*): we worship with oblations. *yuvoḥ sakhyaiḥ* means "by your friendships". क्राणाय (*krāṇāya*) means "for the sacrificer who performs"; the dative is of purpose. For the sacrificer's sake, may we overcome the Rākṣasas, the obstructors of the sacrifice; अभि ष्याम (*abhi ṣyāma*) means "may we overcome".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa (you)
- धारयत्किती (*dhārayatkitī*)—you who bear and nourish this earth
- सुसुम्ना (*susumnā*)—givers of wealth or happiness
- इषितत्वता (*iṣitatvatā*)—you who are invoked among the gods
- ता वां (*tā vāṃ*)—such as you
- यजामसि (*yajāmasi*)—we worship with oblations
- युवोः (*yuvoḥ*)—of you two
- सख्यैः (*sakhyaiḥ*)—by favours in the form of friendship
- क्राणाय (*krāṇāya*)—for the sake of the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice
- रक्षसः (*rakṣasaḥ*)—the Rākṣasas who cause obstacles to the sacrifice
- अभि स्याम (*abhi syāma*)—let us defeat and drive away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you bear and nourish this earth, that is, you are the support of this earth. Or else men offer oblations for you. You give wealth or happiness. Among the gods people long for you alone and call you with prayer. Such as you, we worship with oblations. By your favour in the form of friendship, may we defeat and drive away the Rākṣasas who cause obstacles to the sacrificer's sacrifice.

##### English translation
Mitra and Varuna, who sustain the earth, we worship you, the givers of felicity, for the sake of attaining our desires: may we, through your favour for the perfomer (of the sacrifice), overcome the Rakshasas.
#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अधा॑ चि॒न्नु यद्दिधि॑षामहे वाम॒भि प्रि॒यं रेक्ञः॒ सत्य॑मानाः ।  
> द॒द्वा वा॒ यत्पुष्य॑ति॒ रेक्ञः॒ सम्वा॑र॒न्न कि॑रस्य म॒घानि॑ ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 817

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध । चित् । नु । यत् । दिधिषामहे । नां । अभि । प्रियं । रेक्णः । पत्यमानाः ।  
> दद्वान् । वा । यत् । प्रष्यति । रेक्णः । सं । ऊं इति । आरन् । नकिः । अस्य । मघानि ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुण् नां युवाभ्यां युवयोरर्थं यद्यदा दिधिषामहे
> हवींषि धारयामः । यद्वा । धिष शब्दे ॥ नां युवां स्तुमहे । अधा चिदनंतरमेव नु क्षिप्रं प्रियमभीष्टं रेक्ष्णः । धननामैतत् । धनमभि सत्यमाना अभिपतंतोऽभिप्राप्नुवंतो भवामः । दद्वान् ददिवान् ॥ ददातेर्लिटः क्वसुः । छंदस्युभयथेति वसोः सार्वधातुकत्वाच्छाभ्यस्तयोरात इत्यकारलोपः । आत एवेडभावश्च ।
> संहितायां नकारस्य दीर्घादटि समानपाद इति रुत्वं । आतोTटि नित्यमिति सानुनासिक आकारः ॥ वाशब्दश्चार्थे । हवींषि दत्तवांश्च यद्यो यजमानो रेक्ष्णो धनं
> पुष्यति वर्धयति अस्य दत्तवतो यजमानस्य मघानि धनानि नकिः समारन् । नैवापगच्छंति । किंतु तमेव सर्वदा भजंते । समित्येदपेत्येतस्यार्थे । उ इति पूरणः ॥
> आर्तेश्चांदसे लुजि सर्तिशास्त्रृतिभ्यश्चेति चेरजादेशः । ऋदृशोऽजि गुणः ।
> पा. ७-४-१६ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Mitra and Varuṇa, whenever we दिधिषामहे (*didhiṣāmahe*) for you", that is, we bear oblations; or alternatively, from the root धिष (*dhiṣa*) in the sense of sound, we praise you. Then, immediately and quickly, may we come to attain the desired wealth; रेक्ष्णः (*rekṣṇaḥ*) is a word for wealth, and सत्यमानाः (*satyamānāḥ*) means "moving towards, reaching". दद्वान् (*dadvān*) means "one who has given"; वा (*vā*) is in the sense of "and". The sacrificer who has given oblations and fosters his wealth: the riches of this giving sacrificer do not go away, but always serve him alone. सम् (*sam*) has the sense of एत (*eta*) and *apeta* ("they go" and "they depart"); उ (*u*) is a filler particle.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Mitra and Varuṇa) वां (*vāṃ*)—with you in view
- यत् (*yat*)—whenever (we)
- दिधिषामहे (*didhiṣāmahe*)—bear and offer oblations, or praise
- अध चित् (*adha cit*)—right afterwards
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—desired
- रेक्ष्णः (*rekṣṇaḥ*)—wealth
- अभि पत्यमानाः (*abhi patyamānāḥ*)—may we obtain
- दद्वान् वा (*dadvān vā*)—who offers oblations to you
- यत् (*yat*)—whichever sacrificer
- रेक्ष्णः (*rekṣṇaḥ*)—his own wealth
- पुष्यति (*puṣyati*)—makes grow
- अस्य (*asya*)—of such a sacrificer
- मघानि (*maghāni*)—the riches
- नकिः सं आरन् (*nakiḥ saṃ āran*)—may no one carry them off

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, as soon as we offer oblations or praise with you in view, may we obtain the wealth we desire. May no one snatch away the riches, which bring growth, of the sacrificer who offers oblations to you.

### Printed p. 818

##### English translation
May we, when we present to you (oblations), quickly alight upon desirable wealth, and the generous man who fosters his wealth, may his riches not depart from him.
#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒साव॒न्नो अ॑सुर सूयत॒ द्यौस्त्वं विश्वे॑षां वरुणासि॒ राजा॑ ।  
> मू॒र्धा रथ॑स्य चाक॒न्नॆताव॒तैन॑सांतक॒ध्रुक् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> असौ । अन्यः । असुर । सूयत । द्यौः । त्वं । विश्वेषां । वरुण । असि । राजा ॥  
> मूर्धा । रथस्य । चाकन् । न । एतावता । एनसा । अंतकध्रुक् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे असुर तमसः क्षेपक । यद्वा । असवः प्राणाः । तान्नदाति मनुष्येभ्यः
> स्वोदयेन प्रयच्छतीत्यसुरः । ईदृश हे मित्र द्यौर्द्युलोको देवनशीलादितिर्वान्यः ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति द्वितीयायाः स्वादेशः ॥ वरुणापेक्षयान्यमसावसुं
> नभसि दृश्यमानं त्वां सूयत । असूत ॥ षूज् प्राणिप्रसवे । छांदसोऽडभावः ॥
> हे वरुण त्वं च विश्वेषां सर्वॆषां प्राणिनां राजासि । ईश्वरो भवसि । तादृशयोर्युवयो रथस्य मूर्धा शिरश्चाकन् । अस्मद्यज्ञं कामयते । यद्वा । रथस्य
> रंहणशीलस्य यज्ञस्य मूर्धा न मूर्धेव प्रधानः सोमश्चाकन् । युवां कामयते ॥ कन दीप्ति कांतिगतिषु । अस्माद्यज्लुगंताच्चांदसो लज् ॥ यत एवमतः
> कारणादंतकध्रुगंतकस्य हननशीलस्य राक्षसादेर्यमस्यॆव ना द्रोग्धा ॥ द्रुह
> जिघांसायां । सत्तूद्विषेत्यादिना क्विप् । वा द्रुहमुहष्णु हष्टिहां । पा. ८-२-३३ ।
> इति घत्वं । भष्भावः ॥ ईदृशः स यज्ञ एतावतैनसेयत्परिमाणेनापि पापलेशेनापि
> न युज्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O असुर (*asura*)", one who casts away darkness; or alternatively, the असवः (*asavaḥ*) are the vital breaths, and he who gives them to men by his own rising is असुर (*asura*). O Mitra, such a one: द्यौः (*dyauḥ*) is the heavenly world, or else Aditi, the one who plays. In relation to Varuṇa, "the other", you, this one seen in the sky, सूयत (*sūyata*), she bore; the root is षूज् (*ṣūj*) in the sense of the birth of beings. "And you, O Varuṇa, are king, lord, of all beings. Of you two, such as you, the head of the chariot, चाकन् (*cākan*), desires our sacrifice." Alternatively: Soma, who is chief like a head of the swift sacrifice, desires you two; the root is कन (*kana*) in the senses of shining, desire and going. Since this is so, this sacrifice, the "destroyer-deceiver" (अंतकध्रुक् (*aṃtakadhruk*)), that is, the one that is hostile, as Yama is, to the slaying Rākṣasas and the like, is not touched by sin to this extent, not even by the least trace of sin.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- असुर (*asura*)—O Mitra, remover of darkness or giver of life
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—the heavenly world
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—one of Mitra and Varuṇa
- आसौ (*āsau*)—you, this one shining in the sky
- सूयत (*sūyata*)—

### Printed p. 819
  brought forth
- वरुण (*varuṇa*)—O Varuṇa
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- विश्वेषां (*viśveṣāṃ*)—of all beings
- राजा असि (*rājā asi*)—are the lord
- रथस्य (*rathasya*)—of the sacrifice
- मूर्धा (*mūrdhā*)—Soma, the chief
- चाकन् (*cākan*)—desires you
- अंतकध्रुक् (*aṃtakadhruk*)—this sacrifice that destroys Rākṣasas and the like
- एतावता एनसा (*etāvatā enasā*)—even by a little sin
- न (*na*)—is not stained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra, remover of darkness, the heavenly world brought you forth, one of Mitra and Varuṇa. O Varuṇa, you are lord of all beings. The Soma and other oblations, chief in this sacrifice, desire you, Mitra and Varuṇa. This sacrifice, which is the cause of the destruction of Rākṣasas and the like, is not joined with even a little sin.

##### English translation
(Mitra), scatterer of darkness, the Heaven gave birth to you the other; you, Varuna, are sovereign over all. The head of (your) chariot desired (this sacrifice); opposing the destroyer, (the rite)is not (vitiated) by the smallest defect.

> आवोः । वा । यत् । धात् । तनूषु । अवः । प्रियासु । यज्ञियासु । अर्वा ॥ ५ ॥

> पापकरमायुधं ना मित्रे देवे हिते हिताचरणपरेऽनुकॊले सति निगतान्निगंतव्याह्मननार्थं नियमेन प्राप्तव्यान्वीराञ्चत्रोः पुत्रादीन् सु सुष्टु हंति । हिनस्ति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ṛṣi named Śākapūta says: the sin (एनः (*enaḥ*)) that stands in this Śākapūta, the weapon that is the sinful instrument against enemies, when Mitra the god is kindly disposed and intent on doing good, strikes down well the heroes of the enemy, his sons and others, who are certain to go down to be killed. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 820

> दुःखं जनयतीत्यर्थः ॥ निगतान् । निपूर्दाद्गमेः कर्मणि निष्ठा । गतिरनंतर इति
> गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ कदेत्यत आह । अवोर्हविर्भिस्तर्पयितुः ॥ अवतेर्‌णादिक
> उप्रत्ययः ॥ तस्य यजमानस्य यज्ञियासु यज्ञार्हासु क्रियासु तनूषु शरीरेष्टर्वाभिगंता मित्रो वरुणो वा यद्यदावो रक्षणं धात् दधाति निडधाति स्थापयति।
> यद्वा । यदार्वाभिगंता स ऋषिरवितू रक्षितुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्य वा यागार्हासु
> प्रियासु तनूषु शरीरेष्टवो हविर्लक्षणमन्नं धात् धारयति । तदानीं मित्रे
> वरुणे चानुकूले सति तदेनो वीरान्हंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The verse is the sixth in a sequence on Mitra and Varuṇa; this block completes the bhāṣya on Ṛk 5. Sāyaṇa says that this sin, the weapon that works harm for enemies, lodged in this Śakapūta, causes suffering. He glosses निगतान् (*nigatān*) as the verbal participle of नि (*ni*) with the root *gam* in the passive sense. To the question "when?" he answers that it is when the approaching one, Mitra or Varuṇa, establishes protection, अवः (*avaḥ*), in the bodies, तनूषु (*tanūṣu*), that is, the sacrificial actions of the sacrificer who gratifies them with oblations. Alternatively, when the approaching ṛṣi sets down food in the form of oblation in the dear sacrificial bodies of the protector, Mitra or Varuṇa, then, with Mitra and Varuṇa favourable, this weapon kills the heroes.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अवोः (*avoḥ*)—of the sacrificer who offers oblations
- यज्ञियासु (*yajñiyāsu*)—in those fit for sacrifice
- प्रियासु तनूषु (*priyāsu tanūṣu*)—in the auspicious rites
- अर्वा (*arvā*)—Mitra or Varuṇa, who comes to the sacrifice
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—protection
- धात् (*dhāt*)—he establishes. Or else: अर्वा (*arvā*)—the sacrificing seer Śakapūta; अवोः (*avoḥ*)—to Mitra or Varuṇa, the protector; प्रियासु (*priyāsu*)—dear; यज्ञियासु तनूषु (*yajñiyāsu tanūṣu*)—in the sacrificial rites; अवः (*avaḥ*)—the food in the form of oblation; धात् (*dhāt*)—he holds, that is, prepares and offers it; then
- मित्रे (*mitre*)—the god Mitra
- हिते (*hite*)—being favourable to Śakapūta, the seer of this hymn
- अस्मिन् शकपूते (*asmin śakapūte*)—in this seer Śakapūta
- एतत् (*etat*)—this
- एनः (*enaḥ*)—the weapon that harms enemies
- निगतान् (*nigatān*)—who rush forward
- वीरान् (*vīrān*)—the enemy heroes or their sons
- सु (*su*)—well
- हंति (*haṃti*)—kills

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When, in the pleasing sacrificial rites that the sacrificer performs for Mitra and Varuṇa, Mitra and Varuṇa grant him protection; or when, in the rites dear to Mitra and Varuṇa, the seer Śakapūta offers them oblations, Mitra, being gracious toward that seer, the weapon in him kills the enemy heroes.

##### English translation
This iniquity (found) in this Shakaputha, when Mitra is propitious, destroys opposing heroes, when the approaching (Rishi) places food in the dear adorable bodies of the protector (Mitra).

> न क्रियते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, of distinguished knowledge, your mother is Aditi, the undiminished and unbreakable, who is none other than the earth; the Śruti says इयं वा अदितिरिति (*iyaṃ vā aditiriti*). As the heaven purifies the whole world with its water, the rain, so this earth, with her own sap transformed into oblation, is the cause of purifying the sacrificers and cleansing their sin. Addressing the two, he says: bring to us dear goods; दिदिष्णन (*didiṣṇana*) means "direct them toward us, give". Also cleanse or nourish us with the sun's rays, निनिक्त (*ninikta*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विचेतसा (*vicetasā*)—O Mitra and Varuṇa, endowed with distinguished knowledge
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—the heaven (the atmosphere)
- पयसा न (*payasā na*)—as it purifies the whole world with rain-water
- युवोः हि (*yuvoḥ hi*)—your
- माता (*mātā*)—mother
- अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)—the undiminished (unbroken)
- भूमिः (*bhūmiḥ*)—the earth goddess
- पयसा (*payasā*)—with oblations and the like
- पुपूतनि (*pupūtani*)—removes the sins of the sacrificers and makes them pure
- प्रिया (*priyā*)—dear wealth
- अव दिदिष्टन (*ava didiṣṭana*)—bring and give before us
- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—of the sun
- रश्मिभिः (*raśmibhiḥ*)—with the rays
- निनिक्त (*ninikta*)—make us pure

### Printed p. 822

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O all-knowing Mitra and Varuṇa, as the atmosphere purifies the whole world with its rain-water, so this unbroken earth, with the oblations obtained from the herbs and trees born in her, removes the sins of the sacrificers and makes them wholly pure. O Mitra and Varuṇa, bring us dear wealth, and purify us with the rays of the sun.

##### English translation
O (Mitra and Varuna), endowed with various wisdom, your mother Aditi, the earth, (is) for the purification (of all things) by its libation, as the heaven (purifies by its rain); you display before us precious (treasures), and wash us with the sun's rays.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you, shining through your work (अप्प (*appa*) is a name for work, such as sending rain and giving light), sat down, that is, sit in your own place. The two are made to desire a shout, a clamour, in order to overcome those well-known enemy peoples who clamour. संप्रति (*saṃprati*): now, the chariot…

> बभूव ॥ त्रैज् पालन इत्यस्मात्मर्मणि लिट् । यद्वा । उपचाराज्जन्ये जनकशब्दः ।
> नृमेधस्य पुत्रः शकपूतोऽहं पापाद्युवाभ्यां तत्रे । रक्षितोऽस्मि । सुमेधोऽन्नोऽपि सुयज्ञो यजमानोऽ०हसः पापात्तत्रे । युवाभ्यामेवारक्ष्यत ॥
> भीत्रार्थानां । पा. १-४-२५ । इत्यंहसोऽपादानसंज्ञा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

…तिष्ठत् (*tiṣṭhat*): "let each mount the chariot". What kind of chariot? धूर्षदं (*dhūrṣadaṃ*): sitting at the place of the yoke-horses' draught; वनर्षदं (*vanarṣadaṃ*): sitting in the groves, for sport. Or else, वन (*vana*) is a name of water: Varuṇa dwells in the middle of the sea, so it means sitting in the sea-water. O Mitra and Varuṇa, by you my father Nṛmedha was protected from sin, तत्रे (*tatre*) meaning "was guarded". Or else, "father" is used figuratively of a descendant: I, Śakapūta, son of Nṛmedha, am protected from sin by you. Sumedha too, the good sacrificer, was protected from sin by you alone. Sin takes the ablative designation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- युवं हि (*yuvaṃ hi*)—you (O Mitra and Varuṇa)
- अप्प राजौ (*appa rājau*)—shining through the work of rain and light
- असीदतं (*asīdataṃ*)—sit in your own place
- कणूकयंतीः (*kaṇūkayaṃtīḥ*)—who make an uproar for battle
- ताः नः (*tāḥ naḥ*)—our enemy peoples, to defeat them
- न (*na*)—now
- धूर्षदं (*dhūrṣadaṃ*)—with horses yoked to the yoke
- वनर्षदं (*vanarṣadaṃ*)—standing in the forest or the sea
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—your chariot
- तिष्ठत् (*tiṣṭhat*)—mount and sit
- नृमेधः (*nṛmedhaḥ*)—our father, the ṛṣi Nṛmedha
- अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)—from sin
- तत्रे (*tatre*)—was protected by you
- सुमेधः (*sumedhaḥ*)—the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice (I too)
- अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)—from sin
- तत्रे (*tatre*)—was protected

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you sit in your own place, performing your works of rain and light. To defeat our enemies, who raise an uproar for battle, mount now your chariot, with its horses yoked to the yoke and standing in the forest or amid the sea-water. Our father the ṛṣi Nṛmedha was freed from sin by your grace. The sacrificer who performs the sacrifice (I too) was protected from sin.

##### English translation
For you, brilliant through your functions, have sat down; now mount (each of you, his) chariot, which rests on the yoke, which abides in the forests, (to overcome) those (people) who clamour against us; Nrimedha was preserved (by you) from sin, the pious worshipper was preserved from sin.

## Sūkta 133 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रो ष्विति सप्तर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं पिजवनपुत्रस्य सुदास आर्षमैंद्रं ।
> आद्यस्तृचः शाक्वरः । षट्पंचाशदक्षरी शक्वरी । द्वितीयस्तृचो महापांक्तः ।
> षळष्टका महापंक्तिः । सप्तमी त्रिष्टुप् । तथा चानुक्रांतं । प्रो షు सुदाः पैजवनः
> शाक्वरमहापांक्तावाद्यौ तृचावंत्या त्रिष्टुबिति ॥ षोळशिशस्त्र आद्यस्तृचः शंसनीयः ।
> सूत्रितं च । त्रिकद्रुकेषु महिषो यवाशिरं प्रो ष्वस्मै पुरोरथमिति तृचावातिच्छंदसौ । आ. ६-२ । इति ॥ महाव्रते माध्यंदिनसवने ब्रह्मशस्त्रेऽनुरूपतृचस्य प्रो
> ष्वस्मा इत्येका । तथैव पंचमारण्यके सूत्रितं च । प्रो ष्वस्मै पुरोरथमित्यतोऽनुरूपः । ऐ. आ. ५-१-१ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

प्रो षु (*pro ṣu*) is the fifth hymn of seven Ṛks, with Sudās, son of Pijavana, as seer and Indra as deity. The first triplet is Śākvara, शक्वरी (*śakvarī*) of fifty-six syllables; the second triplet is Mahāpāṅkta, महापंक्ति (*mahāpaṃkti*) of six octosyllabic pādas; the seventh is Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī is quoted: प्रो षु सुदाः (*pro ṣu sudāḥ*) … त्रिष्टुबिति (*triṣṭubiti*) **NOTE**. In the Ṣoḍaśin śastra the first triplet is to be recited. The sūtra is quoted: त्रिकद्रुकेषु महिषो यवाशिरं प्रो ष्वस्मै पुरोरथमिति तृचावातिच्छंदसौ । (*trikadrukeṣu mahiṣo yavāśiraṃ pro ṣvasmai purorathamiti tṛcāvāticchaṃdasau |*) (Ā. Sū. 6-2). In the Mahāvrata, at the midday pressing, in the Brahmaśastra, one Ṛk, प्रो ष्वस्मा (*pro ṣvasmā*), serves for the Anurūpa triplet. In the Fifth Āraṇyaka likewise: प्रो ष्वस्मै पुरोरथमित्यतोऽनुरूपः (*pro ṣvasmai purorathamityato 'nurūpaḥ*) (Ai. Ā. 5-1-1).

##### Anuvāda

This hymn प्रो षु (*pro ṣu*) is the fifth hymn in the eleventh Anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. The seer of this hymn is Sudās, son of Pijavana; the deity is Indra. The first three Ṛks of the hymn are in the Śakvarī metre; the Śakvarī Ṛk has fifty-six syllables. The three Ṛks from the fourth to the sixth are in the Mahāpaṅkti metre, whose Ṛk has six pādas of eight syllables each. The seventh Ṛk is in Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: प्रो षु सुदाः पैजवनः शाक्वरमहापांक्तानाद्यौ तृचावंत्या त्रिष्टुप् (*pro ṣu sudāḥ paijavanaḥ śākvaramahāpāṃktānādyau tṛcāvaṃtyā triṣṭup*). In the sacrifice called Ṣoḍaśin the first three Ṛks are to be recited for the śastra mantras, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: त्रिकद्रुकेषु महिषो यवाशिरं प्रो ष्टस्मै पुरोरथमिति तृचावातिच्छंदसौ (*trikadrukeṣu mahiṣo yavāśiraṃ pro ṣṭasmai purorathamiti tṛcāvāticchaṃdasau*) (Ā. 9-2). In the Mahāvrata rite, at the midday pressing, among the śastra mantras to be recited by the priest called Brahman, one Ṛk, प्रो ष्टस्मै (*pro ṣṭasmai*), is employed for the Anurūpa triplet, as indicated in the Fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka by प्रो ष्टस्मै पुरोरथमित्यतोऽनुरूपः (*pro ṣṭasmai purorathamityato 'nurūpaḥ*) (Ai. Ā. 5-1-1).

Sūkta 133. Maṇḍala 10, Anuvāka 11, Sūkta 133. Aṣṭaka 8, Adhyāya 7, Varga 21. Number of Ṛks in the hymn: 7. Seer: Sudās Paijavana. Deity: Indra. Metre: 1-3 Śakvarī; 4-6 Mahāpaṅkti; 7 Triṣṭubh.

> अ॒भीके॑ चिदु लोक॒कृत्सं॒गे स॒मत्तु॑ वृत्र॒हास्माकं॑ बोधि  
> चोदि॒ता नभं॑तामन्य॒केषां॑ ज्या॒का अधि॒ धन्व॑सु ॥ १ ॥

> प्रो इति । सु । अस्मै । पुरःरथं । इंद्राय । शूषं । अर्चत ।  
> अभीके । चित् । ऊं इति । लोककृत् । संगे । समत्सु । वृत्रहा । अस्माकं।  
> बोधि । चोदिता । नभंतां । अन्यकेषां । ज्याकाः । अधि । धन्वसु ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्मा इंद्राय । षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी । अस्येंद्रस्य पुरोरथं रथस्य पुरः
> पुरतः ॥ पुरोऽव्ययमिति गतित्वाद्दतिसमासः ॥ रथस्याग्रतो वर्तमानं शूषं बलं
> सु प्रो अर्चत । हे स्तोतारः सुष्टु प्रपूजयत । प्र उ इति निपातसमुदायः
> प्रो इति ॥ ओदिति प्रगृह्य संज्ञं ॥ इंद्रो विशेष्यते । समत्तु । समानं माद्यंत्यत्रेति
> समदः संग्रामाः ॥ औणादिकोऽधिकरणे क्विप् । समानस्य च्छंदसीति सभावः ॥ समत्तु
> संग्रामेषु संगे संगमनीये शत्रुबले ॥ डोऽन्यत्रापि दृश्यते । पा- ३-२-४८ ।
> इति गमेर्डः ॥ अभीके चिदभ्यर्ण्येऽपि निकटं प्राप्तेऽपि केशाकेश्यवस्थायामपि
> लोककृत्स्थितिकृन्न पलायिता स्थित्वा वृत्रहा वृत्राणामावरकाणां हंता एवंविधः स
> इंद्रोऽस्माकं स्तोतृणां चोदिता धनानां प्रेरिता सन्मोधि । अस्माभिः कृतानि
> परिचरणानि बुध्यतां ॥ बुधेश्पांदसे लुजि दीपजनबुधेत्यादिना कर्तरि चेश्चिणादेशः।
> बहुलं छंदस्यमाज्योगेऽपीत्यडभावः ॥ अपि चान्यकेषां कुत्सितानामन्येषां
> शत्रूणामधि धन्वसु धनुःष्टधिरोपिता ज्याकाः कुत्सिता ज्या नभंतां । हिंस्यंतां ।
> नश्यंतु ॥ ज्याशब्दात्कुत्सायां प्रागिवात्कः । पा. ५-३-७०-७४ । नभ तुभ हिंसायां
> क्रैयादिकः । व्यत्ययेन शप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अस्मा इंद्राय (*asmā iṃdrāya*): the dative stands for the genitive, "of this Indra". पुरोरथं (*purorathaṃ*) is "in front of the chariot"; the compound arises because पुरः (*puraḥ*) is an indeclinable. O praisers, worship well the strength, शूषं (*śūṣaṃ*), that goes before the chariot; प्रो (*pro*) is a combination of the particles प्र (*pra*) and उ (*u*). Indra is further qualified: समत्सु (*samatsu*), in battles, where men rejoice together; संगे (*saṃge*), in the enemy force to be encountered. Even when the enemy is close, even at grappling, he is लोककृत् (*lokakṛt*), one who makes a stand and does not flee, the slayer of the Vṛtras, the obstructers. Such an Indra, becoming the impeller of wealth for us his praisers, बोधि (*bodhi*), let him take note of the services done by us. Also, let the bowstrings, ज्याकाः (*jyākāḥ*), bad ones, strung on the bows of other, contemptible enemies, be destroyed: नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*) means "let them be harmed, let them perish".

### Printed p. 826

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्मै इंद्राय (*asmai iṃdrāya*)—(O worshippers) of this Indra
- पुरोरथं (*purorathaṃ*)—the one who stands in front of the chariot
- शूषं (*śūṣaṃ*)—the might
- सु प्रो अर्चत (*su pro arcata*)—worship well
- समत्सु (*samatsu*)—in battles
- संगे (*saṃge*)—when the enemy forces have gathered together
- अभीके चित् (*abhīke cit*)—even when they have come near
- लोककृत् (*lokakṛt*)—who stands firm in battle without fleeing
- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—Indra, the slayer of enemies
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—for us
- चोदिता (*coditā*)—as the impeller (the one who urges us on)
- बोधि (*bodhi*)—may he know the service-rite we perform
- अन्यकेषां (*anyakeṣāṃ*)—of the wretched enemies
- अधि धन्वसु (*adhi dhanvasu*)—fixed upon the bows
- ज्याकाः (*jyākāḥ*)—the bowstrings
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—may they meet destruction

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O worshippers, worship well the might that goes before this Indra's chariot. In the hand-to-hand fights that take place when the enemies gather and clash in battles, Indra, the slayer of enemies, is able to keep the battle-position from being spoilt. May he be our impeller, that is, urging us on in battles, and may he take note of the service-rites we perform. May the well-strung bowstrings on the bows of the wretched enemies be destroyed.

##### English translation
Adore fervently the might of that Indra which goes before his chariot; he who makes room for us in the hand to hand conflict, who slays the Vritra in the hostile army in battles, he who is our simulator, may he know (the adoration paid by us); may the bowstrings on the bows of our enemies be destroyed.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For the words अभीके चित् (*abhīke cit*) in this Ṛk the Bhāṣyakāra explains अभ्यर्णॆऽपि निकटं प्राप्तेपि केशाकेश्यवस्थायामपि (*abhyarṇè 'pi nikaṭaṃ prāptepi keśākeśyavasthāyāmapi*): (enemies) who have come very close and, seizing one another by the topknots, are striking each other. Yāska, giving the etymology of the word अभीके (*abhīke*), says—
प्रपित्वेऽभीक इत्यासन्नस्य । प्रपित्वे प्राप्ते । अभीके अभ्यक्ते । आपित्वे नः प्रपित्वे तूयमागहि । अभीके चिदुलोककृत् । इत्यपि निगमौ भवतः ॥ (*prapitve 'bhīka ityāsannasya | prapitve prāpte | abhīke abhyakte | āpitve naḥ prapitve tūyamāgahi | abhīke cidulokakṛt | ityapi nigamau bhavataḥ ‖*) (Ni. 3-20)
Among the twenty-six words beginning प्रपित्वे (*prapitve*), अभीके (*abhīke*), etc., the words go in pairs, that is, the two words प्रपित्वे (*prapitve*) and अभीके (*abhīke*)
### Printed p. 827
(and likewise the two words दभ्रं (*dabhraṃ*) and अर्भकं (*arbhakaṃ*)) indicate one and the same meaning. प्रपित्वे (*prapitve*) means "come near"; अभीके (*abhīke*) means अभ्यक्ते (*abhyakte*), facing, that is, standing near, in front. In this matter it is indicated that the Vedic sentence आपित्वे नः प्रपित्वे तूयमागहि (*āpitve naḥ prapitve tūyamāgahi*) is the example of a sentence where the word प्रपित्वे (*prapitve*) is used, and the Vedic sentence अभीके चिदुलोककृत् (*abhīke cidulokakṛt*) is the example of a sentence where the word अभीके (*abhīke*) is used.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं सिंधू॒रवा॑सृजोऽध॒राचो॒ अह॒न्नहिं॑ ॥  
> अ॒श॒त्रुरिं॑द जज्ञिषे॒ विश्वं॑ पुष्यसि॒ वार्यं॒ तं त्वा॒परि॑ ष्वजामहे॒  
> नभं॑तामन्य॒केषां॑ ज्या॒का अधि॒ धन्व॑सु॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । सिंधून् । अव । असृजः । अधराचः । अहन् । अहिं ।  
> अशत्रुः । इंद्र । जज्जिषे । विश्वं । पुष्यसि । वार्यं । तं । त्वा । परि । स्वजामहे ।  
> नभंतां । अन्यकेषां । ज्याकाः । अधि । धन्वसु ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र सिंधून् स्यंदनशीलाञ्चलपूरानधराचोऽधरमधोमुखमंचतो गंत्कानवासृजः । मेघान्निरगमयः । यतस्त्वमहिमंतरिक्षे गतं मेघमहन्
> हतवानसि । यद्वा । अहिमागत्य हंतारं सर्वस्य जगत आवरकं वृत्रमसुरमहन्
> हतवानसि ! अतो हे इंद्र त्वमशत्रुः शत्रुरहितो जज्जिषे । जायसे ॥ न संति
> शत्रवोऽस्येति बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं । जनेर्लिटि गमहनेत्यादिनोपधालोपः । द्विर्वचनेऽचीति स्थानिवद्भावाद्विर्वचनं ॥ तथा विश्वं सर्वं
> वार्यं वरणीयं संभजनीयं धनं पुष्यसि । वर्धयसि ॥ वृज् संभक्तौ । ऋहलोर्ण्यत् । ईडवंदवृशंसदुहां ण्यत इत्याद्युदात्त त्वं ॥ तादृशं त्वां परि
> ष्वजामहे । हविर्भिः स्तुतिभिश्चालिंगनं कुर्मः । वशीकुर्म इत्यर्थः ॥ ष्टन्व परिष्वंगे ।
> दंशसंजष्टंजां शपि ! पा. ६-४-२५ । इत्यनुनासिकलोपः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you have sent forth the rivers, the swiftly flowing floods, the clouds that go moving downward (अधराचः (*adharācaḥ*): going with face turned down); for you struck Ahi, the cloud in the atmosphere. Or else: coming to Ahi, you slew Vṛtra the Asura, the slayer, who covers the whole world. Therefore, Indra, you are born without an enemy; you have no enemies. And you increase all the desirable, shareable wealth. Such as you are, we embrace you with oblations and praises, that is, we bring you under our sway. The remainder of the sentence about the bowstrings is not explained further here; the rest, he says, is established.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you slew the Asura Vṛtra who enveloped the cloud, and you made the rain-waters he had held back, flowing by nature, fall on the earth and run as rivers in the low-lying regions. O Indra, you were born without an enemy; you increase the wealth all desire. Such as you are, we serve you with oblations and embrace you, that is, we bring you under our control. May the bowstrings of our enemies' bows be destroyed.

##### English translation
You have sent the rivers away downwards, you have slain Ahi ; you are born, Indra. without an enemy, you grant all that is desirable. as such we embrace you, may the bowstrings on the bows of our enemies be destroyed.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Citing sentences of mutually contradictory meaning, Yāska here explains the sentence अशत्रुरिंद्र जज्जिषे (*aśatruriṃdra jajjiṣe*)—
अथापि विप्रतिषिद्दार्था भवंति । एक एव रुद्रो ऽवतस्थॆ न द्वितीयः । असंख्याताः सहस्राणि ये रुद्रा अधि भूम्यां ॥ अशत्रुरिंद्र जज्जिषे । शतं सेना अजयत्साकमिंद्रः ॥ (*athāpi vipratiṣiddārthā bhavaṃti | eka eva rudro 'vatasthè na dvitīyaḥ | asaṃkhyātāḥ sahasrāṇi ye rudrā adhi bhūmyāṃ ‖ aśatruriṃdra jajjiṣe | śataṃ senā ajayatsākamiṃdraḥ ‖*) (Ni. 1-15)
Here two sentences indicating mutually contradictory meanings are cited: एक एव रुद्रोऽवतस्थे न द्वितीयः (*eka eva rudro 'vatasthe na dvitīyaḥ*) and असंख्याता सहस्राणि ये रुद्रा अधि भूम्यां (*asaṃkhyātā sahasrāṇi ye rudrā adhi bhūmyāṃ*) (Vā. Saṃ. 16-5).
### Printed p. 829
These two Vedic sentences contain mutually opposed views. In the first sentence the meaning is that Rudra is one alone, there is no other equal to him. In the second sentence it is said that the number of Rudras on earth is countless. These two meanings contradict each other. Likewise, in अशत्रुरिंद्र जज्जिषे (*aśatruriṃdra jajjiṣe*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-133-2) the meaning is that Indra was born without an enemy, while in शतं सेना अजयत्साकमिंद्रः (*śataṃ senā ajayatsākamiṃdraḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-103-1) it is said that Indra conquered hundreds of enemy armies. If Indra was without enemies at birth, that is, when he had no enemies at all, is it not contradictory to say that he conquered hundreds of enemy armies? To say that one without an enemy conquered enemies means that he had enemies; once enemies existed, how was he without an enemy? The purport of these two sentences is mutually contradictory.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May all our enemy-folk, the non-givers and assailants (अर्यः (*aryaḥ*): those who come against us), be utterly destroyed. O Indra, may our praises and rites, the धियः (*dhiyaḥ*), be directed to you. O Indra, whoever wishes to slay us, against that enemy you are the hurler of the weapon (वधं (*vadhaṃ*)), the instrument of slaying; अस्तासि (*astāsi*) means you are the thrower. Your रातिः (*rātiḥ*) (the bestowing of wealth; in the next block its cause, the hand) …
### Printed p. 830

> तुर्हस्तः ॥ रा दाने । करणे क्तिन् । मंत्रे वृषेषपचमनविदभूवीरा उदात्त
> इति क्तिन उदात्तत्वं ॥ सा रार्तिर्वसु धनं ददिः । अस्मभ्यं दाता भवतु ॥ आद्यगमहन
> इति ददातेः किप्रत्ययः । न लोकाव्ययेति वसुशब्दात्पश्यभावः ॥ सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

… that gift of yours, रातिः (*rātiḥ*) (from रा दाने (*rā dāne*)), may it be the giver of wealth, वसु (*vasu*), to us. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सु वि नशंश (*su vi naśaṃśa*)—may they be well destroyed

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whichever enemy
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- जिघांसति (*jighāṃsati*)—wishes to kill
- शत्रवे (*śatrave*)—in order to kill that enemy
- वधं (*vadhaṃ*)—your thunderbolt, the instrument of slaying
- अस्ता असि (*astā asi*)—you hurl at him
- ते (*te*)—your
- या रातिः (*yā rātiḥ*)—that hand of yours that gives us wealth
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth
- ददिः (*dadiḥ*)—may it give us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May all our enemies who rush upon us be destroyed. May the work of slaying enemies go forward. O Indra, against whatever enemy wishes to kill us, may your thunderbolt be hurled for his destruction. May your wealth-giving hand give us wealth. May the strung bowstrings on the enemies' bows be destroyed.

##### English translation
May all our assailants, who make no offerings, puickly perish, may our praises (be successful); you, Indra, hurl the weapon at the foe who seeks to slay us, may that liberal (hand) of yours be the giver of wealth (to us); may the bowstrings on the bows of our enemies be destroyed.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र यो जनो वृकायुः । वृको हिंसकोऽरण्यश्वा स्तेनो वा ।
> स इवाचरन्नोऽस्मानभितः सर्वत आदिदेशति अभिलक्ष्यायुधान्यतिसृजति ॥ दिशतेर्लेट्यडागमः । छांदसः शपः श्लुः । नाभ्यस्तस्याचि पितीत्यत्र बहुलं छंदसीति वक्तव्यमिति वचनात्पतिषेधाभावे लघूपधगुणः । अभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वं ॥
> तमीं तमिमं जनमधस्पदं पादस्याधस्ताद्वर्तमानं कृधि । कुरु ॥ करोतेश्छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् श्रुशृणुष्यकृवृभ्य इति हेर्धिः ॥ यतस्त्वं विबाधो
> विशेषेण बाधिता शत्रूणां सासहिरभिभविता चासि । सिद्धः शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, the man who is वृकायुः (*vṛkāyuḥ*)—वृक (*vṛka*) being the destructive forest dog (wolf) or a thief—behaving like that, aims at us on every side and hurls weapons at us (आदिदेशति (*ādideśati*)). Make that man अधस्पदं (*adhaspadaṃ*), lying beneath the foot; कृधि (*kṛdhi*) means "do". For you are विबाधः (*vibādhaḥ*), one who specially afflicts enemies, and सासहिः (*sāsahiḥ*), an overcomer. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वृकायुः (*vṛkāyuḥ*)—who, like a wolf or a thief, does us harm
- यः जनः (*yaḥ janaḥ*)—whichever enemy
- नः अभितः (*naḥ abhitaḥ*)—around us
- आदिदेशति (*ādideśati*)—swings and hurls his weapon
- तं ईं (*taṃ īṃ*)—that enemy
- अधस्पदं (*adhaspadaṃ*)—so that he falls beneath our feet
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make (you, O Indra)
- विबाधः (*vibādhaḥ*)—though specially harassed by enemies
- सासहिः असि (*sāsahiḥ asi*)—you defeat them
- अन्यकेषां (*anyakeṣāṃ*)—of the enemies
- अधि धन्वसु (*adhi dhanvasu*)—fixed upon the bows
- ज्याकाः (*jyākāḥ*)—the bowstrings
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—may they meet destruction

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, whatever enemy, harming us like a wolf or a thief, swings and hurls his weapon around us, make that enemy fall beneath our feet. O Indra, even when the enemies afflict you greatly, you defeat them. May the well-strung bowstrings on the enemies' bows be destroyed.

##### English translation
The man who, like a wolf, prowls around us, O Indra, cast him beneath our feet, for you are the resister, the overcomer (of foes); may the bowstrings on the bows of our enemies be destroyed.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, the enemy who is सनाभिः (*sanābhiḥ*), of the same birth as ourselves, and assails (अभिदासति (*abhidāsati*), "harms") us, and the one who is निष्ट्यः (*niṣṭyaḥ*), of lower birth and harms us: the word निष्ट्यः (*niṣṭyaḥ*) is formed from the indeclinable निः (*niḥ*) denoting the inferior, with the affix in the sense of "born". Of that enemy, break the strength, which is vast like the great heaven (महीव द्यौः (*mahīva dyauḥ*)), yourself (त्मना (*tmanā*) = त्मना (*tmanā*), with loss of the long ā in mantras). अव तिर (*ava tira*) means "slay"; the root तिर (*tira*) has the sense of killing. The rest is already explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which
- सनाभिः (*sanābhiḥ*)—enemy belonging to our own kin
- यश्च (*yaśca*)—and which
- निष्पृः (*niṣpṛḥ*)—enemy born in a family lower than ours
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अभिदासति (*abhidāsati*)—troubles
- महीव द्यौः (*mahīva dyauḥ*)—great like the wide atmosphere
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of that enemy
- बलं (*balaṃ*)—strength
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—you yourself
- अव तिर (*ava tira*)—destroy
- अन्यकेषां (*anyakeṣāṃ*)—of the enemy folk
- अधि धन्वसु (*adhi dhanvasu*)—on the bows, tied tight
- ज्याकाः (*jyākāḥ*)—bowstrings (cords)
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—may they be destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, whether the enemy who troubles us is of our own kin or of low birth, reduce and destroy, yourself, the strength of that enemy, which is great like the wide atmosphere. May the well-fitted bowstrings on the bows of the enemy folk be destroyed.

### Printed p. 833

##### English translation
He who assails us, Indra, whether he be of the same caste or of degraded caste—scatter of yourself his host; (though it be vast) as the wide heaven ; may the bowstrings on the bows of our enemies be destroyed.

> हे इंद्र त्वायवस्त्वामात्मन इच्छंतो वयं सखित्वं सखिकर्म यज्ञात्मकमा रभामहे । उपक्रमामहे । ऋतस्य सत्यस्य यज्ञस्य पथा मार्गेण ॥ भस्य
> टीर्लोपः उदात्तनिवृत्ति स्वरेण तृतीयाया उदात्तत्वं ॥ विश्वानि सर्वाणि दुरिता
> दुरितानि दुर्गमनानि पापानि तत्पलानि च नोऽस्मानति नय । अतिपारय । गतमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, we who desire you (त्वायवः (*tvāyavaḥ*), wishing you for ourselves) undertake (आ रभामहे (*ā rabhāmahe*), "begin") the work of friendship, the sacrificial act that makes you our friend. By the path (पथा (*pathā*)) of ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*), of truth or of sacrifice, lead us across all evils (दुरिता (*duritā*)), that is, hard-to-traverse sins and their fruits. अति नय (*ati naya*) means "carry us across". The rest is already explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वायवः (*tvāyavaḥ*)—desiring you
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- सखित्वं (*sakhitvaṃ*)—the sacrificial act that is the means to your friendship
- आ रभामहे (*ā rabhāmahe*)—we begin
- ऋतस्य पदा (*ṛtasya padā*)—by the path of truth, or by means of sacrifice
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- नः दुरिता (*naḥ duritā*)—our sins or troubles (having removed them)
- अति नय (*ati naya*)—carry us across
- अन्यकेषां (*anyakeṣāṃ*)—of our enemies
- अधि धन्वसु (*adhi dhanvasu*)—on the bows, fitted
- ज्याकाः (*jyākāḥ*)—bowstrings
- नभंतां (*nabhaṃtāṃ*)—may they be destroyed

### Printed p. 834

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, desiring you, we begin the sacrificial act that is the means of your friendship. By the path of truth, or by means of sacrifice, remove all our sins or troubles and carry us also across them. May the bowstrings on the bows of our enemies be destroyed.

##### English translation
Devoted to you, Indra, we strive after your friendship; lead us by the path of sacrifice beyond all evils; may the bowstrings on the bows of our enemies be destroyed.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒स्मभ्यं॒ सु त्वमिं॑द्र॒ तां शि॑क्ष॒ या दोह॑ते॒ प्रति॒ वरं॑ जरि॒त्रे ।  
> अच्छि॑द्रोध्नी पी॒पय॒द्यथा॑ नः स॒हस्र॑धारा॒ पय॑सा म॒ही गौः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्मभ्यं । सु । त्वं । इंद्र । तां । शिक्ष । या । दोहते । प्रति । वरं । जरित्रे ।  
> अच्चिद्रऊध्नी । पीपयत् । यथा । नः । सहस्रधारा । पयसा । मही । गौः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं तां गामस्मभ्यं स्तोतृभ्यः सु शिक्ष । प्रदेहि । शिक्षतिर्दानकर्मा ।
> या गौर्जरित्रे स्तोत्रे वरं वरणीयं पयः प्रति दोहते प्रतिदिनं नैरंतर्येण
> दुग्धे ॥ दुहेर्बहुलं छंदसीति शपो लुगभावः। अदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे
> शपः पित्वादनुदात्तत्वं । धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । वरं । वृञ् वरण इत्यस्मादृहवृद्धनिश्चिगमश्चेति कर्मण्यण् ॥ सा प्रत्या गौरच्चिद्रोद्धी निविडोधस्का अत एव सहस्रधारा
> बहुभिः क्षिरधाराभिरुपेता मही महती सती यथा नोऽस्मान्वयसा क्षीरेण पीपयत्
> प्रवर्धयेत् तथा तां कुर्विति शेषः ॥ ओप्यायी वृद्दौ । ण्यंताच्छांदसो लुज् ।
> व्यत्ययेन धातोः पीभावः । अडभावश्चांदसः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, give (शिक्ष (*śikṣa*); the root शिक्ष (*śikṣa*) means giving) to us, your praisers, that cow which daily and without break yields choice (वरं (*varaṃ*), desirable) milk to the praiser (जरित्रे (*jaritre*)). वरं (*varaṃ*) is from the root वृञ् (*vṛñ*) in the sense of choosing, with the affix *aṇ* in the object sense. That cow has an unbroken, compact udder, and therefore is सहस्रधारा (*sahasradhārā*), furnished with many streams of milk, and great (मही (*mahī*)). Do so that she may nourish us with milk (पीपयत् (*pīpayat*), "may make grow"); "do thus" is to be supplied. The root ओप्यायी (*opyāyī*) is used in the sense of growth. The Vedic aorist after the causative, the replacement of the root by पी (*pī*), and absence of the augment *aṭ* are mentioned.
