##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- या (*yā*)—which cow
- जरित्रे (*jaritre*)—to the one who praises
- वरं (*varaṃ*)—excellent milk, or as much as is desired
- प्रति (*prati*)—every day
- दोहते (*dohate*)—yields
- तां (*tāṃ*)—such a cow
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- सुशिक्ष (*suśikṣa*)—give
- गौः (*gauḥ*)—the cow you thus give us
- मही (*mahī*)—abundant
- सहस्रधारा (*sahasradhārā*)—with many streams of milk
- अच्छिद्रोद्ध्नी (*acchidroddhnī*)—always yielding milk without break (every day)
- यथा (*yathā*)—in the way in which
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- पयसा (*payasā*)—with milk
- पीपयत् (*pīpayat*)—she may fill
- (so) do

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, give us that cow which every day yields to the praiser as much milk as he desires. Make that cow which you give us, with many streams of milk, yielding abundant milk without break, fill us with milk.

##### English translation
Give to us, Indra (the cow) which gives milk to the worshipper according to his desire, so that the mighty cow possessed of an unfailing udder, the shedder of a thousand streams, may supply us plentifully with milk.

## Sūkta 134 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उभे यदिति सप्तर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं । युवनाश्वपुत्रस्य मांधातुरार्षं ।
> पूर्वेणेत्यर्धर्चसहितायाः सप्तम्यास्तु गोधा नाम ब्रह्मवादिन्यृषिः । सप्तमी
> पंक्तिः । शिष्टाः षळष्टका महापंक्तयः । इंद्रो देवता । तथा चानुक्रातं । उभे
> यन्मांधाता यौवनाश्वो महापांक्तं पंक्तिरंत्या तामध्यर्धां गोधापश्यदिः ॥
> गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनेच्छावाकस्याद्यश्चो
> वैकल्पिकः स्तोत्रियः । सूत्रितं च । उभे यदिंद्र रोदसी अव यत्त्वं शतक्रतो ।
> आ. ७-४ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta उभे यत् (*ubhe yat*) has seven Ṛks and is the sixth sūkta. Its seer is Māndhātā, son of Yuvanāśva. The seer of the seventh Ṛk, together with the half-Ṛk of the sixth beginning पूर्वेण (*pūrveṇa*), is Godhā, a woman brahmavādin. The seventh is in Paṅkti metre; the remaining six are Mahāpaṅktis. The deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇī is quoted: उभे यन्मांधाता यौवनाश्वो महापांक्तं पंक्तिरंत्या तामध्यर्धां गोधापश्यदिः (*ubhe yanmāṃdhātā yauvanāśvo mahāpāṃktaṃ paṃktiraṃtyā tāmadhyardhāṃ godhāpaśyadiḥ*). The general use of the sūkta has been stated. On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, the first Ṛk of the sūkta is an optional Stotriya of the Acchāvāka. It is prescribed in the sūtra उभे यदिंद्र रोदसी अव यत्त्वं शतक्रतो (*ubhe yadiṃdra rodasī ava yattvaṃ śatakrato*) (Ā. 7-4).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning उभे यत् (*ubhe yat*) is the sixth sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Māndhātā, son of Yuvanāśva.

### Printed p. 836

The seer of the latter half of the sixth Ṛk of this sūkta, beginning with पूर्वेण (*pūrveṇa*), and of the seventh Ṛk, is Godhā; the seventh Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Paṅkti metre; the remaining six Ṛks are in the metre called Mahāpaṅkti. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: उभे यन्मांधाता यौवनाश्वो महापांक्तं पंक्तिरंत्या तामध्यर्धां गोधापश्यत् (*ubhe yanmāṃdhātā yauvanāśvo mahāpāṃktaṃ paṃktiraṃtyā tāmadhyardhāṃ godhāpaśyat*). The use of the sūkta has been stated before. On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the midday pressing, the priest called Acchāvāka may optionally recite the first three Ṛks of this sūkta for the Stotriya triplet; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta sūtra उभे यदिंद्र रोदसी अव यत्त्वं शतक्रतो (*ubhe yadiṃdra rodasī ava yattvaṃ śatakrato*) (Ā. 7-4).

Sūkta 134. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 134. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 7; Varga 22. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Seer: 1–5 and the first half of 6, Māndhātā Yauvanāśva; the latter half of 6 and 7, Godhā. Deity: Indra. Metre: 1–6 Mahāpaṅkti; 7 Paṅkti.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒भे यदिं॑द्र॒ रोद॑सी आप॒प्राथो॒षा इ॑व ।  
> म॒हांतं॑ त्वा म॒हीनां॑ स॒म्राजं॑ चर्षणी॒नां दे॒वी जनि॑त्र्यजीजनद्भ॒द्रा जनि॑त्र्यजीजनत् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उभे इति । यत् । इंद्र । रोदसी इति । आपप्राथ । उषाः इव ।  
> महांतं । त्वा । महीनां । संराजं । चर्षणीनां । देवी । जनित्री । अजीजनत् ।  
> भद्रा । जनित्री । अजीजनत् ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 837

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र उभे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ यद्यस्त्वमापप्राथ तेजसाप्रथयसि
> आपूरयसि ॥ प्रा पूरणे आदादिकः । छांदसो लिट् ॥ उषा इव यथोषाः स्वभासा
> सर्वं जगदापूरयति तद्वत् । तं महीनां महतां देवानामपि महांतमधिकं
> चर्षणीनां मनुष्याणामपि सम्राजमीश्वरमिंद्रं त्वा त्वां देवी देवनशीला
> जनित्र्यदितिरजीजनत् । अजनयत् ॥ जनेर्न्यंताल्लुजि चजि रूपमेतत् ॥ यस्मादेषा
> जनित्रीदृशं पुत्रमजीजनत् अतः कारणात्सा भद्रा कल्याणी प्रशस्ता जाता ॥ जनेर्न्यंतात्साधुकारिणि तृन् । जनिता मंत्र इतीडाद् णिलोपो निपात्यते । ऋन्नेभ्य
> इति जिप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, since you fill (आपप्राथ (*āpaprātha*), "make full") both heaven and earth with your splendour, like the dawn (उषा इव (*uṣā iva*)) that fills the whole world with its light, — you, great (महांतं (*mahāṃtaṃ*)) even among the great gods (महीनां (*mahīnāṃ*)), and lord (सम्राजं (*samrājaṃ*)) even of men (चर्षणीनां (*carṣaṇīnāṃ*)) — Aditi, the divine (देवी (*devī*)) progenitress (जनित्री (*janitrī*)), gave birth to (अजीजनत् (*ajījanat*)). Because she bore such a son, therefore she became भद्रा (*bhadrā*), auspicious and praised. The root प्रा (*prā*) is in the sense of filling; the verb form is a Vedic perfect.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—you who
- उषा इव (*uṣā iva*)—as the dawn fills the whole world with its radiance
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- आपप्राथ (*āpaprātha*)—you fill with your splendour
- (तं (*taṃ*)—such)
- महीनां (*mahīnāṃ*)—among the great gods
- महांतं (*mahāṃtaṃ*)—the greater one
- चर्षणीनां (*carṣaṇīnāṃ*)—of all men
- सम्राजं (*samrājaṃ*)—the lord
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- देवी (*devī*)—the divine one
- जनित्री (*janitrī*)—she who bears good sons, Aditi
- अजीजनत् (*ajījanat*)—gave birth to
- जनित्री (*janitrī*)—Indra, the good son
- अजीजनत् (*ajījanat*)—for which reason she bore him, for that reason Aditi
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—became worthy of praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as the dawn fills the whole world with its radiance, you fill both heaven and earth with your splendour (your own power). You, who are greater than all the gods and lord even of men — the divine Aditi bore you. For this very reason, because she bore you, Aditi became worthy of praise.

##### English translation
You, Indra, who fill both heaven and earth (with light) like the dawn—the devine progenitress has given birth to you, the mighty of the mighty (gods), the sovereign of men; auspicious progenitress has given you birth.

> अ॒ध॒स्प॒दं तमिां॑ कृधि॒ यो अ॒स्मा आ॒दिदे॑शति दे॒वी जनि॑त्रजीजनद्भ॒द्रा जनि॑त्रजीजनत् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अव । स्म । दुःहनायतः । मर्तस्य । तनुहि । स्थिरं ।  
> अधॆःपदं । तं । ईं । कृधि । यः । अस्मान् । आदिदेशति । देवी । जनित्री । अजीजनत् ।  
> भद्रा । जनित्री । अजीजनत् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दुर्हणायतो दुःखप्रदं हननमाचरतो मर्तस्य मनुष्यस्य शत्रोः स्थिरं
> दृढं बलमव तनुहि । अवततं नीचीनं कुरु । स्मेति पूरकः । तं शत्रुमीमेनमधस्पदं पादयोरधस्ताद्वर्तमानं कृधि । कुरु । यः शत्रुरस्मानादिदेशति जिघांसति ।
> समानमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of the mortal, that is, the enemy, who practises painful killing, break down the firm, steady strength; make it bent down. स्म (*sma*) is a mere filler. Make that enemy lie beneath the feet. The enemy who wishes to strike us down: do this to him. The rest is as before.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दुर्हणायतः (*durhaṇāyataḥ*)—of one set upon the painful act of killing
- मर्तस्य (*martasya*)—of the enemy
- स्थिरं (*sthiraṃ*)—the firm strength, or steadiness
- अव तनुहि स्म (*ava tanuhi sma*)—destroy
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which enemy
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- आदिदेशति (*ādideśati*)—wishes to kill
- तं एनं (*taṃ enaṃ*)—that enemy
- अधस्पदं (*adhaspadaṃ*)—as though fallen beneath our feet
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make
- देवी (*devī*)—the divine
- जनित्री (*janitrī*)—your mother Aditi
- अजीजनत् (*ajījanat*)—gave birth to you
- जनित्री अजीजनत् (*janitrī ajījanat*)—your mother, who bore such a good son
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—worthy of praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, destroy the steadiness of the enemy who strives only to kill others. Make the enemy who wishes to kill us fall beneath our feet. Because the divine Aditi bore you, such a good son, she has become worthy of praise.

### Printed p. 839

##### English translation
Enfeeble the strength of malicious man, cast under foot him who tries to kill us; the devine progenitress has given you birth, the auspicious progenitress has given you birth.

> अव॒ त्या बृ॑ह॒तीरिषो॑ वि॒श्वश्चं॑द्रा अमित्रहन् ।  
> शची॑भिः शक्र धूनु॒हींद्र॒ विश्वा॑भिरू॒तिभि॑र्दे॒वी जनि॑त्र्यजीजनद्भ॒द्रा जनि॑त्र्यजीजनत् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अव । त्याः । बृहतीः । इषः । विश्वचंद्राः । अमित्रहन् ।  
> शचीभिः । शक्र । धूनुहि । इंद्र । विश्वाभिः । ऊतिभिः । देवी । जनित्री । अजीजनत् ।  
> भद्रा । जनित्री । अजीजनत् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अमित्रहन्नमित्राणां शत्रुणां हंतर्हे शक्रेंद्र शचीभिरात्मीयाभिः
> शक्तिभिरात्मीयैः कर्मभिर्वा त्यास्ताः प्रसिद्धा बृहतीर्महतीः ॥ बृहन्महतोरुपसंख्यानमिति जीप उदात्तत्वं ॥ विश्वश्चंद्राः । विश्वानि सर्वाणि चंद्राणि हिरण्यानि यासां
> तादृशीः ॥ ह्रस्वाच्चंद्रोत्तरपदे मंत्र इति सुडागमः । बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायामिति पूर्वपदांतोदात्तत्वं ॥ एवंभूता इषोऽन्नानि विश्वाभिः सर्वाभिरूतिभी
> रक्षाभिः सार्थमव धूनुहि । आस्मास्ववाज्मुखं कंपय । अस्मदभिमुखं गमयेत्यर्थः । गतमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, slayer of foes, शक्र (*śakra*), with your own powers or deeds, shake down upon us those well-known great इषः (*iṣaḥ*) (foods), "all-shining", that is, having all gold. He cites the rule on *bṛhanmahatoḥ* for the accent of बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*) (Jīp) and the rule on the augment suṭ for विश्वश्चंद्राः (*viśvaścaṃdrāḥ*) and its accent. Shake them down together with all your protections: make them come toward us. The rest has been explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अमित्रहन् (*amitrahan*)—destroyer of enemies
- शक्र इंद्र (*śakra iṃdra*)—O Indra, endowed with power
- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—by your own powers
- त्याः (*tyāḥ*)—those well-known
- बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*)—abundant
- विश्वश्चंद्राः (*viśvaścaṃdrāḥ*)—all riches
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—foods and the like
- विश्वाभिः (*viśvābhiḥ*)—all
- ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*)—together with your protections
- अव धूनुहि (*ava dhūnuhi*)—make them come and fall near us
- देवी (*devī*)—the divine

### Printed p. 840
- जनित्री (*janitrī*)—your mother Aditi
- अजीजनत् (*ajījanat*)—gave birth to you
- जनित्री अजीजनत् (*janitrī ajījanat*)—for having borne such a good son, your mother
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—became worthy of praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, destroyer of enemies and endowed with power, by your own powers make the well-known abundant wealth of gold and the like, and food, come and fall near us together with all your protections. Because the divine Aditi bore a good son like you, she has become worthy of praise.

##### English translation
Destroyer of enemies, Indra, Shakra, shake down upon us by your exploits those abundant, all-shining viands, (accompanied) with all your protections; the divine progentress has given you birth, the avspicious progentress has given you birth.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अव॒ यत्त्वं श॑तक्रत॒विंद्र॒ विश्वा॑नि धूनु॒षे ।  
> र॒यिं न सु॑न्व॒ते सचा॑ सह॒स्रिणी॑भिरू॒तिभि॑र्दे॒वी जनि॑त्र्यजीजनधृ॒द्रा जनि॑त्र्यजीजनत् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अव । यत् । त्वं । शतक्रतो इति शतक्रतो । इंद्र । विश्वानि । धूनुषे ।  
> रयिं । न । सुन्वते । सचा । सहस्रिणीभिः । ऊतिभिः । देवी । जनित्री । अजीजनत् ।  
> भद्रा । जनित्री । अजीजनत् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनेऽच्छावाकस्याव यत्त्वमिति तृचो वैकल्पिकोऽनुरूपः । सूत्रं तु सूक्तादावुदाहृतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, the triplet अव यत्त्वं (*ava yattvaṃ*) is an optional anurūpa for the Acchāvāka. The sūtra was quoted at the beginning of the sūkta.

### Printed p. 841

> हे शतक्रतो बहुकर्मन् बहुप्रज्ञ वेंद्र सुन्वते सोमाभिषवं कुर्वते ॥
> सुनोतेर्लटः शतृ । हुश्नुवोः सार्वधातुक इति यण् । शतुरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥ ईदृशाय यजमानाय यद्यदा त्वं विश्वानि व्याप्तान्यन्नानि वाव
> धूनुषे अभिगमयसि । ददासीत्यर्थः । तदा रयिं न रयिं च पुत्ररूपं धनं च
> सहस्रिणीभिः सहस्रसंख्यायुक्ताभिरूतिभी रक्षाभिः सचा सह प्रदेहि । गतमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Śatakratu, of many deeds or of much wisdom, Indra, to the one who presses Soma: when you "shake down" to such a sacrificer all pervading foods, that is, give them, then give also wealth in the form of a son, together with protections numbering a thousand. He notes the सुन्वते (*sunvate*) formation (present participle, yaṇ) and the accent of the ending. The rest has been explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—one who has done many daring deeds, or of much wisdom
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सुन्वते (*sunvate*)—to the sacrificer who presses and offers Soma juice
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all riches or foods
- अव धूनुषे (*ava dhūnuṣe*)—you provide and give, then
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth in the form of a son
- सहस्रिणीभिः (*sahasriṇībhiḥ*)—in thousands
- ऊतिभिः सचा (*ūtibhiḥ sacā*)—provide together with your protections
- देवी (*devī*)—the divine
- जनित्रि (*janitri*)—your mother Aditi
- अजीजनत् (*ajījanat*)—gave birth to you
- अजीजनत् (*ajījanat*)—because she gave birth to you
- जनित्रि (*janitri*)—your mother
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—worthy of praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, of many daring deeds or of much wisdom, when you provide all wealth or food to the sacrificer who presses and offers Soma juice for you, then along with it provide also a son and your protections in thousands. Because your mother Aditi bore you, a good son, she has become worthy of praise.

##### English translation
When you, Indra, Shatakrathu, shake down (upon us) all blessings, (then bestow) upon the offerer of the libation wealth also, together with your thousandfold protections; the divine progenitress has given you birth, the auspicious progenitress has given you birth.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अव॒ स्वेदा॑ इवा॒भितो॒ विश्व॑क्षतंतु दि॒द्यवः॑ ।

> दूर्वाया इव तंतवो व्यगस्मदेतु दुर्मतिर्देवी जनित्र्यजीजनद्भद्रा जनित्र जीजनत् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अव । स्वेदाःऽइव । अभितः । विष्णक् । पतंतु । दिद्यवः ।  
> दूर्वायाःऽइव । तंतवः । वि । अस्मत् । एतु । दुःऽमतिः । देवी । जनित्री । अजीजनत् । भद्रा । जनित्री । अजीजनत् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्वेदा इव गात्रात्वेदविंदव इवाभितः सर्वतो दिद्यवो द्योतमानान्यायुधानींद्रस्य दीप्तयो वा विष्णग्नानामुखा अव पतंतु । निपतंतु । दूर्वाया
> इव तंतवः । यथा दूर्वाकांडा बहुशः प्ररोहंति एवं बहुशो विस्त्रता
> दृश्यंते । दुर्मतिर्दुष्टाभिसंधिः शत्रुरस्मदस्मत्तो व्येतु । वियता गच्छतु ।
> गतमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Like drops of sweat from the body, may Indra's blazing weapons, or his flashes, fall all around, in many directions. Like the shoots of dūrvā grass, which spring up in many places, they are seen spread out in many ways. May the enemy of evil intent go away from us. The rest has been explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वेदा इव (*svedā iva*)—as drops of sweat drip from the body
- दिद्यवः (*didyavaḥ*)—the shining weapons of Indra
- अभितः (*abhitaḥ*)—all around
- विष्णक् (*viṣṇak*)—in many directions
- अव पतंतु (*ava pataṃtu*)—let them fall upon the enemies
- दूर्वाया इव तंतवः (*dūrvāyā iva taṃtavaḥ*)—as blades of the grass called dūrvā grow quickly
- दुर्मतिः (*durmatiḥ*)—the ill-minded enemy
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—from us
- वि एतु (*vi etu*)—let him quickly depart
- देवी (*devī*)—the divine
- जनित्री (*janitrī*)—your mother Aditi
- अजीजनत् (*ajījanat*)—gave birth to you
- अजीजनत् (*ajījanat*)—because she gave birth to you
- जनित्री (*janitrī*)—your mother
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—became worthy of praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As drops of sweat drip from the body, let Indra's shining weapons fall all around, in many directions, upon the enemies; as dūrvā grass grows quickly, let the ill-minded enemy quickly go away from us. Because the divine Aditi bore you, she has become worthy of praise.

### Printed p. 843

##### English translation
Let your radiant (weapons) fall down everywhere round about like drops of perspiration; let the enemy depart from us like the stems of the durva grass; the divine progentress has given you birth, the auspicios progentress has given you birth.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दी॒र्घं ह्यं॑कु॒शं य॑था॒ शक्तिं॒ बिभ॑र्षि मंतुमः ।  
> पूर्वे॑ण मघवन्प॒दाजो व॒यां यथा॑ यमो दे॒वी जनि॑त्रैजीजनद्भ॒द्रा जनि॑त्रैजीजनत् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दीर्घं । हि । अंकुशं । यथा । शक्तिं । बिभर्षि । मंतुमः ।  
> पूर्वेण । मघवन् । पदा । अजः । वयां । यथा । यमः । देवी । जनित्री ।  
> अजीजनत् । भद्रा । जनित्री । अजीजनत् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दीर्घमायतमंकुशं सृणिं यथा बिभर्षि एवमायतां शक्तिं हे मंतुमः।
> मंतुज्ञानं । तद्वन् ॥ मतुवसो रुरिति संबुद्धौ नकारस्य रुत्वं ॥ ईदृकेंद्र
> बिभर्षि । धारयसि ॥ डुभृञ् धारणपोषणयोः जौहोत्यादिकः । श्ला भृञामिदित्यभ्यासस्यॆत्वं ॥ हे मघवनधनवन्निंद्र यथा पूर्णेण देहस्य पूर्वभागे वर्तमानेन पदा पादेनाजश्चागो वयां शाखामाकर्षति तथा पूर्वोक्तया शक्त्याकृष्य
> यमः । शत्रून्नियच्छसि ॥ यमेर्लॆट्व्यडागमः । बहुलं छंदसीति शपो लुक् ॥
> गतमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As you bear a long अंकुशं (*aṃkuśaṃ*) (hook), so, O मंतुमः (*maṃtumaḥ*) (possessor of knowledge), you bear an extended शक्तिं (*śaktiṃ*) (spear). He explains मंतुमः (*maṃtumaḥ*) as possessing मंतु (*maṃtu*), knowledge (with the vocative rule for the final n), and बिभर्षि (*bibharṣi*) as "you hold" (root भृञ् (*bhṛñ*), Hu class, with reduplication). O Maghavan, wealthy Indra, as a goat pulls a branch with the forward foot, the one in the front part of its body, so you, drawing by the aforesaid spear, restrain enemies, यमः (*yamaḥ*). The rest has been explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दीर्घं (*dīrghaṃ*)—long
- अंकुशं (*aṃkuśaṃ*)—a hooked staff (a pole)
- मंतुमः (*maṃtumaḥ*)—the wise one
- यथा (*yathā*)—as he takes it and uses it, so you

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शक्तिं (*śaktiṃ*)—your power
- बिभर्षि (*bibharṣi*)—you bear
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- अजः (*ajaḥ*)—a goat
- पूर्वेण पदा (*pūrveṇa padā*)—with its fore-foot
- वयां (*vayāṃ*)—a branch of a tree; as it bends it, so you
- यमः (*yamaḥ*)—you bend (subdue) the enemies
- देवी (*devī*)—divine in nature (your)
- जनित्री (*janitrī*)—mother Aditi
- अजीजनत् (*ajījanat*)—bore you
- अजीजनत् (*ajījanat*)—precisely because she bore you
- जनित्री (*janitrī*)—your mother
- भद्रा (*bhadrā*)—is worthy of praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as a wise man takes a long hooked pole in his hand and uses it, so you use your power. O wealthy Indra, as a goat bends the branch of a tree with its fore-foot, so you bend (defeat) your enemies. Because Aditi, your mother, divine in nature, bore you, she has become worthy of praise.

##### English translation
For you, sapient (Indra), wield your might like a long hook; you drag (your foes), Maghavan, as a goat with its fore-foot (drags) a branch; the divine pragenitress has given you birth, the auspicious progenitress has givee you birth.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नकि॑र्देवा मिनीमसि॒ नकि॒रा यो॑पयामसि मंत्र॒श्रुत्यं॑  
> चरामसि ।  
> प॒क्षेभि॑रपिक॒क्षेभि॒रत्रा॒भि सं र॑भामहे ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नकिः । देवाः । मिनीमसि । नकिः । आ । योपयामसि । मंत्रश्रुत्यं । चरामसि ।  
> पक्षेभिः । अपि कक्षेभिः । अत्र । अभि । सं । रभामहे ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवा इंद्रादयः युष्मद्विषये नकिर्मिनीमसि । न किमपि हिंस्मः ॥
> मीज् हिंसायां क्रैयादिकः ॥ मीनातेर्निगम इति ह्रस्वः । इदंतो मसिः ॥ आकारः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O gods, Indra and the rest, in regard to you we do not injure (नकिर्मिनीमसि (*nakirminīmasi*)): we harm you in nothing." The root is "to injure", of the Kryādi class.

### Printed p. 845

> समुच्चये । नकिर्न किंच योपयामसि । योपयामः । अननुष्ठानेन विमोहयामः ॥ युप विमोहने ॥ किं तर्हि मंत्रश्रुत्यं मंत्रेण स्मार्यं श्रुत्
> विधिवाक्ये प्रतिपाद्यं युष्मद्विषयं कर्म तच्चरामसि । आचरामः । अनुतिष्ठामः ।
> अपि च पक्षेभिः पक्षैः पक्षस्थानीयैः स्तुतशस्त्रैरपिकक्षेभिः । अपिकक्षो नाम बाह्वोर्मध्यभागः । यज्ञस्यापिकक्षभूतैर्हविर्भिरत्रास्मिन्यज्ञेऽभितः सर्वतो युष्मान्सं
> रभामहे । सम्यगवलंबामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The particle ā is for conjunction. "Nor do we bewilder you (योपयामः (*yopayāmaḥ*)) by failing to perform; what, then? The rite relating to you, which is to be recalled by the mantra and is taught in the injunctive text (मंत्रश्रुत्यं (*maṃtraśrutyaṃ*)), that we perform and carry out." Further, with the पक्षेभिः (*pakṣebhiḥ*), the praise-recitations that stand in the place of wings, and with the अपिकक्षेभिः (*apikakṣebhiḥ*): apikakṣa means the middle part of the arms; with oblations which are as it were the arm-hollows of the sacrifice, here in this sacrifice, on all sides, we take hold of you, we rely on you fully.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods, Indra and the others (in regard to you we)
- नकिः मिनीमसि (*nakiḥ minīmasi*)—do not injure in the least
- नकिः आ योपयामसि (*nakiḥ ā yopayāmasi*)—do not trouble you by neglecting the rites; (but)
- मंत्रश्रुत्यं (*maṃtraśrutyaṃ*)—as stated in the Vedic mantras
- चरामसि (*carāmasi*)—we perform the sacrificial rites, and
- पक्षेभिः (*pakṣebhiḥ*)—with the śastra-mantras that stand in the place of wings
- अपिकक्षेभिः (*apikakṣebhiḥ*)—and with oblations and the like offered with the arms
- अत्र (*atra*)—in this sacrifice
- अभि (*abhi*)—in all places, you
- सं रभामहे (*saṃ rabhāmahe*)—we resort to

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and the other gods, in regard to you we do no act that causes injury, and we give you no kind of trouble. But as ordained in the Vedic texts, we perform sacrificial rites directed to you. In this sacrifice, with śastra-mantras and with oblations, we attend upon you especially and take refuge in you.

##### English translation
O gods, we never injure (you), we never inflict annoyance (on you), we follow the teaching of the mantra ; we take hold of you at this (sacrifice) with wings and arms.

## Sūkta 135 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Introduction. There is a narrative in the Kaṭha Upaniṣad. The sage Vājaśravas had a son named Naciketas. While he was still a boy, that is, of tender age, his father performed a sacrifice and gave away to brahmins the lean cows he had. Seeing this, Naciketas thought: "Why is my father doing this? What use will those brahmins have from these lean cows?" and said to his father: "Father, what merit comes to you by giving such cows? Give good things." When the father said, "Except you, Naciketas, nothing is left with me," Naciketas said, "Give me to someone." The father paid no heed to his childish speech and kept silent. Naciketas did not leave it at that and went on pressing his father: "To whom will you give me?" The father grew angry, and in the rush of anger, not knowing what to say, said: "Boy, I have given you to Death (Yama)."

### Printed p. 846
Believing that to be true, Naciketas went to Yama. Yama was not at home, so he fasted for three days until Yama should come, waiting there for his arrival. After three days Yama came home and, seeing at his door the boy fasting and awaiting him, was greatly moved and said: "Boy, you, a brahmin and a brahmacārin, have come as a guest to my house and been fasting for three days. This is not right; great harm will come to me from it. What sin may befall me who have not honoured a guest!" Greatly repentant, he said: "Boy, to atone for your three days' fast in my house I give you three boons of your choice; take them and return happy." Naciketas accordingly asked for three boons. Two he asked for: that his father's affection for him remain, and that his father's poverty perish and wealth and prosperity be gained. For the third boon he asked that Yama explain what becomes of men after they are subject to death, that is, what their state and nature are after death, and other matters touching the truths of the self. Yama tried in many ways to appease him, urging him to ask another boon and saying that even the gods cannot know this, but Naciketas would not agree. He prayed again that this very matter be made known to him. So Yama finally explained, as he desired, the nature of death. Then Naciketas, having obtained Yama's leave, came to his father. This account is set out in the Kaṭha Upaniṣad. The commentator says that this matter is alluded to in the Ṛks of this sūkta. We have explained the summary of this Kaṭha Upaniṣad and the conversation between Naciketas and Yama at length in Ṛ. Saṃ. part 27, pp. 582-594.

Regarding the conversation between Naciketas and Yama, the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, third kāṇḍa, 11th prapāṭhaka, 8th anuvāka, says:

### Printed p. 847
उशन् ह वै (*uśan ha vai*) … य उ चैनमेवं वेद ॥ (*ya u cainamevaṃ veda ‖*) **NOTE** (Tai. Brā. 3-11-8-1, 2, 3, 4, 5)

In former times there was a sage named Vājaśravas of the Gautama gotra. He had a son named Uddālaka. Once Uddālaka set about performing a special sacrifice called Viśvajit. The peculiarity of this sacrifice is giving away all one possesses to the officiating priests and other brahmins. So the sage Uddālaka, desiring that the full fruit of his sacrifice be his, gave all his wealth and other things to brahmins. At that time Naciketas, Uddālaka's son, a boy who was watching all this, felt a special effect in his mind. The boy had not yet had his initiation. In him too a special faith in giving arose. Thinking that he, the son, was a possession belonging to his father, the boy said to his father: "Father, you have given away all you had.

### Printed p. 848
"I, your son, am I not a possession of yours? Why did you not give me? To whom do you mean to give me?" Hearing his son's words, the father thought: "He is still a boy who knows nothing. His question is not proper. Why should I answer it?" and, ignoring his words, gave no reply. But the boy did not leave it at that and asked the same question a second time, a third time, again and again. At this the father grew angry and, thinking, "I took him for a boy who knows nothing, but he is an obstinate, utter fool," said: "I give you to Death." Then, as the son was ready to go to Death on hearing his father's word, a bodiless voice spoke thus: "Boy of the Gotama line (Naciketas), your father has said that he gives you to Death. So now set out to the house of Death (Yama). When you go to Yama's house he will have gone abroad on a journey. He will not come for three days. Even so, go there and stay in his house fasting until he comes, until three nights have passed. Eat nothing, whatever is offered. Afterwards, when Yama has come, he will ask you: 'Boy, how many days is it since you came?' You must say: 'Three nights have passed since I came.' Again, if he asks, 'What did you eat on the first day (or night)?', say: 'I ate your offspring'; if 'What did you eat on the second night?', say: 'I ate your cattle and other wealth'; if 'What did you eat on the third night?', say: 'I ate the good deeds you have done.'" Thus the goddess of speech gave Naciketas beneficial counsel and sent him off.

[A little explanation is needed here. If a guest who comes to a householder's house on an errand is not honoured and not satisfied with food and the like, great sin comes to that householder. That is, if the guest fasts one night (one day) in his house, the householder's progeny, sons and the rest, perish; if he fasts a second day too, the householder's cattle, wealth, grain and other possessions perish; if he fasts a third day too, all the merit of the sacrifices and good rites the householder has performed up to then perishes. This, as stated in the Dharmaśāstra, is explained here. It is shown here that the goddess of speech advised Naciketas what answer to give to these questions of Yama.]

Keeping the goddess of speech's counsel in mind, Naciketas came to Yama's abode. Yama had gone on a journey. After three days he came home and, seeing the boy sitting there fasting for three days, said: "Boy, how many days is it since you came here"

### Printed p. 849
and, when asked, Naciketas said three nights had passed. Then, asked what he ate the first night, he said: "I ate your progeny." Then, asked what he ate the second day, he said: "Cattle and other wealth." Asked what he ate the third day, he said: "The fruits of the good deeds you have performed." Hearing all this Yama was greatly distressed at heart and said: "Revered one, homage to you. You have fasted and wasted away three days in my house; great sin has befallen me thereby. To atone for that sin I will give three boons, one for each of the three days you fasted; ask." Naciketas asked for the three boons he wanted thus: "O Yama, if you give me boons, let me go to my father as I now am, without falling under death." Yama granted the boon, "So be it," and said, "Ask the second boon." Naciketas said: "Tell me the method by which śrauta and smārta rites yield imperishable fruits." Yama accordingly explained to him the method of piling the fire-altar and said that this piling of the fire should be famous by the name Naciketas (Nāciketa fire). Granting the second boon — that the man who performs the Nāciketa fire-piling gains exceeding fruit for the śrauta and smārta rites he performs — he then said, "Ask the third boon." Naciketas said: "O Yama, a man through his actions takes many births and falls under death many times. Therefore tell me the means of conquering death, so as to be freed from saṃsāra. This is the third boon I ask." Yama then explained to Naciketas at length the means of conquering death and the nature of the Supreme Brahman, it is said.

The commentator says that this sūkta can be explained in two ways, and accordingly explains one meaning with reference to Yama and another with reference to Āditya. Yāska also approves this Āditya-related meaning and gives the etymology of the first Ṛk of the sūkta accordingly. Following this, we too have explained the Ṛks of this sūkta in two ways, with reference to Yama and to Āditya.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यस्मिन्निति सप्तर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तं यमगोत्रस्य कुमारस्यार्षं । आनुष्टुभं
> यमदेवत्यं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । यस्मिन्कुमारो यामायनो याममानु_
> ष्टुभं त्विति ॥
> 54

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seventh sūkta, of seven Ṛks, beginning यस्मिन् (*yasmin*), has as its seer Kumāra of the Yama gotra; its metre is Anuṣṭubh and its deity Yama. So the Anukramaṇī says: यस्मिन्कुमारो यामायनो याममानु_ष्टुभं त्विति ॥ (*yasminkumāro yāmāyano yāmamānu_ṣṭubhaṃ tviti ‖*)

### Printed p. 850
*Anuvāda.* This sūkta, "Yasmin", is the seventh sūkta in the eleventh Anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Kumāra of the Yama gotra; the deity is Yama; the metre is Anuṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: यस्मिन् कुमारो यामायनो याममानुष्टुभं तु (*yasmin kumāro yāmāyano yāmamānuṣṭubhaṃ tu*).

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 135. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 7; Varga 23. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Seer: Kumāra Yāmāyana. Deity: Yama. Metre: Anuṣṭup.

> यस्मि॑न्वृ॒क्षे सु॑पला॒शे दे॒वैः सं॒पिब॑ते य॒मः ।  
> अत्रा॑ नो वि॒श्वतिः॑ पि॒ता पु॑रा॒णा अनु॑ वेनति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अत्र । नः । विश्वतिः । पिता । पुराणान् । अनु । वेनति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृक्षे । लुप्रोपममेतत् । वृक्षवत्सुपलाशे शोभनपलाशोपेते शोभनोद्यानसहिते । यद्वा । शोभनपर्णोपेते वृक्षे । तादृशस्य वृक्षस्य मूलं यथाष्ट्यजनितश्रमापनोदनेन सुखकरं भवति तद्वत्सुखकरे यस्मिन्स्थाने देवैः परिजनभूतैर्यमो नियंता वैवस्वतः संपिबते सह भुंक्ते । पिबतीत्यर्थः । विश्वतिर्विशां
> प्रजानामधिपतिः पिता नः ॥ व्यत्ययेन बहुवचनं ॥ मम नचिकेतसो जनको वाजश्रवसोऽत्रास्मिन्यमस्य स्थाने पुराणान्नुरातनानत्र चिरकालं निवसतः पित्यननु तेषां
> पश्चात्तत्समीपे निवसत्वयमिति वेनति । मां कामयते । नचिकेता नाम कुमारो
> वाजश्रवसेन पित्रा यमलोकं प्रस्थापितः सन् यमं दृष्ट्वा प्रसाद्य पुनरपीमं
> लोकमाजगाम । अयमर्थ इदमादिकैर्मंत्रैः प्रतिपाद्यते । यद्वा । कुमारो

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वृक्षे (*vṛkṣe*) is an elliptical comparison (lupta-upamā): "in a place that is like a tree with good leaves", that is, one with a good garden. Or else it means a tree with good foliage. As the foot of such a tree gives comfort by removing the fatigue produced by the sun's heat, so in the place that gives comfort Yama, the Vaivasvata, the controller, drinks (that is, enjoys) together with the gods, his retinue. विश्वतिः (*viśvatiḥ*) is the lord of the people; "father" is नः (*naḥ*), the plural being by vyatyaya. It is I, Naciketas, the son of Vājaśravas, who speak: my father desires me to dwell here, in Yama's place, after the ancient fathers who have long lived here, near them. The story: a boy named Naciketas, sent by his father Vājaśravas to Yama's world, saw Yama, propitiated him and came back to this world. This meaning is set forth by the mantras beginning with this one. Or else Kumāra is some other seer, different from Naciketas.

> नाम नचीकेतसोऽन्यः कश्चिदृषिः । यच्छतीति यम आदित्यः । तमनेन सूक्तेन

> पालयिता प्राणात्मना सर्वेषां जनकः स आदित्यः पुराणांश्चिरंतनान् स्तोत्यन्नोऽस्मानपि वेनति । अनुग्राह्यत्वेन कामयते । यद्वा । अत्र स्थाने स्थितान्नोऽस्माकं
> पुराणान्पूर्वपुरुषाननु वेनति । अनुक्रमेण कामयते ॥
> ॥ प्रतिपदार्थ— यमनपरवागि ॥
> सुपलाशे—उत्तमवाद ऎलॆगळिंद निबिडवाद । वृक्षे—वृक्षद नॆरळिनंतॆ सुखकरवाद ।
> यस्मिन्—याव स्थानदल्लि । यमः—विवस्वंतन पुत्रनाद यमनु । देवैः—तन्न परिजन
> रिंद सहितनागि । संपिबते—पानमाडुत्तानॆयो ऎंदरॆ भोगवन्नु अनुभविसुत्तानॆयो ।
> अत्र—अंतह यमन स्थानदल्लि । पुराणान् अनु—बहुकालदिंद अल्लिये वासमाडुत्तिरुव
> पितृगळ समीपदल्लि नानु वासमाडबेकॆंदु । विश्वतिः—प्रजॆगळल्लि ऎंदरॆ जनरल्लि श्रेष्ठनाद ।
> नः पिता—नन्न तंदॆयु । वेनति—आपेक्षिसुत्तानॆ.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

यम (*yama*) means "he who restrains": the Āditya. The seer praised him with this sūkta. Like a tree with good leaves, in a pleasant place Yama, the Āditya, unites with the gods, that is, the shining rays; पिबति (*pibati*) here has the sense of "go", because of the preverb, and the ātmanepada is by vyatyaya. Standing in this place, the Āditya, protector of the people by shining and raining, father of all as their breath, desires us also, the praisers of old, as those to be favoured. Or else: he desires in succession us who stand here, the ancient forefathers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

*(on Yama)*
- सुपलाशे (*supalāśe*)—dense with excellent leaves
- वृक्षे (*vṛkṣe*)—comfortable like the shade of a tree
- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in which place
- यमः (*yamaḥ*)—Yama, son of Vivasvat
- देवैः (*devaiḥ*)—together with his retinue
- संपिबते (*saṃpibate*)—drinks, that is, enjoys pleasure
- अत्र (*atra*)—in that place of Yama
- पुराणान् अनु (*purāṇān anu*)—near the fathers who have long dwelt there, "that I should dwell"
- विश्वतिः (*viśvatiḥ*)—the best among the people, that is, among men
- नः पिता (*naḥ pitā*)—my father
- वेनति (*venati*)—desires

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the shade of a tree densely covered with excellent leaves is comfortable for rest, so in Yama's place (Yama's world), which is comfortable like it, Yama, son of Vivasvat, dwells happily with his retinue. In this world of Yama my father, the best among men, desires that I too should dwell near the fathers who have lived here for a long time.

##### English translation
In that leafy tree where Yama drinks with the gods, there the progenitor, the lord of the house, invites us to join the men of old.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Formerly a seer named Vājaśravas had a son named Naciketas. Once, for some reason, he displeased his father, and the father in a fit of anger told his son to go to Yama's world. Naciketas took his father's word as true, went accordingly to Yama's world, conversed there with Yama and, by his favour, came back to this earth. This matter is told in this Ṛk and in the following Ṛks of this sūkta.

### Printed p. 852
यस्मिन् वृक्षे सुपलाशे (*yasmin vṛkṣe supalāśe*)—as the foot of a tree with good leaves gives comfort by removing the fatigue produced by heat, so in the place that gives comfort. Here the word "tree" is used as an illustration. When a man walking in the sun is wearied by the toil of the road, it is natural for him to sit at the foot of a tree dense with leaves, that is, in its shade, to remove his weariness, that is, to rest. So the foot of a tree dense with leaves is pleasant to sit in; Yama's place is likewise pleasant, and so it is described by comparison with a tree.

देवैः संपिबते यमः (*devaiḥ saṃpibate yamaḥ*)—Yama, the controller, the Vaivasvata, enjoys together with his retinue. The meaning is that Yama, son of Vivasvat, dwells happily in his own place, Yama's world, with his retinue, that is, with the fathers.

अत्र नः विश्वतिः पिता पुराणान् अनु वेनति (*atra naḥ viśvatiḥ pitā purāṇān anu venati*)—पुराणान् (*purāṇān*) means the fathers who have long dwelt here, in this world of Yama. Naciketas says: "My father desires that I should dwell, that is, be, near such fathers; that is, I have come here according to my father's word."

**The meaning on the side of the Āditya**
When the word Kumāra in Ṛks 3, 4 and 5 of this sūkta is explained on the side of Yama, it must be taken as Naciketas, son of Viśravas (Vājaśravas); when explained on the side of the Āditya, it must be taken as another seer named Kumāra, not Naciketas. This seer Kumāra praised the Āditya in this sūkta.

- सुपलाशे (*supalāśe*)—dense with excellent leaves
- वृक्षे (*vṛkṣe*)—comfortable like the foot of a tree
- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in which atmosphere or heavenly place
- यमः (*yamaḥ*)—the Āditya
- देवैः (*devaiḥ*)—together with his shining rays
- संपिबते (*saṃpibate*)—moves about
- अत्र (*atra*)—in such a place
- विश्वतिः (*viśvatiḥ*)—protector of the people by rain, light and so on
- पिता नः (*pitā naḥ*)—the Āditya, the breath and the begetter of all
- पुराणान् (*purāṇān*)—the ancient praisers
- नः (*naḥ*)—us also
- अनु वेनति (*anu venati*)—desires, with the intention to favour

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In heaven (the atmosphere), pleasant like the shade of a tree dense with excellent leaves, the Āditya shines with his bright rays. That Āditya, who nourishes the people by giving rain, light and so on, and is the breath and begetter of all, desires to favour the earlier praisers and us.

### Printed p. 853

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In explaining the word Yama, Yāska has given a Nirukta for this Ṛk: यमः । यमो यच्छतीति सतः । तस्यैषा भवति ॥ (*yamaḥ | yamo yacchatīti sataḥ | tasyaiṣā bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 10-19). यच्छति (*yacchati*) means he brings to an end the life of living beings; hence the name Yama. Here the word Yama is taken to mean the Āditya. The explanation of the Ṛk in which this word occurs is given here:

यस्मिन् वृक्षे सुपलाशे स्थाने वृतक्षये वासि वोपमार्थे स्यात् वृक्ष इव सुपलाश इति वृक्षो व्रश्चनात्पलाशं पलाशनाद्देवैः संगच्छते यमो रश्मिभिरादित्यस्तत्र नः सर्वस्य पाता ना पालयिता ना पुराणाननुकामयेत ॥ (*yasmin vṛkṣe supalāśe sthāne vṛtakṣaye vāsi vopamārthe syāt vṛkṣa iva supalāśa iti vṛkṣo vraścanātpalāśaṃ palāśanāddevaiḥ saṃgacchate yamo raśmibhirādityastatra naḥ sarvasya pātā nā pālayitā nā purāṇānanukāmayeta ‖*) (Ni. 12-29)

यस्मिन् वृक्षे सुपलाशे स्थाने वृतक्षये वापि वोपमार्थे स्यात् वृक्ष इव सुपलाश इति (*yasmin vṛkṣe supalāśe sthāne vṛtakṣaye vāpi vopamārthe syāt vṛkṣa iva supalāśa iti*)—in a tree with good leaves, that is, in a charming and pleasant place of trees. Or वृतक्षये (*vṛtakṣaye*): in the place where people who have done good deeds dwell, that is, in the better world. Or the word "tree" is used here as a comparison: it must be understood that the word is used to describe a place beneficial like the shade of a tree.

वृक्षो वृश्चनात्पलाशं पलाशनात् (*vṛkṣo vṛścanātpalāśaṃ palāśanāt*)—the plant is called "tree" because people cut it (व्रश्चन (*vraścana*)) for timber and the like. The leaves are called पलाश (*palāśa*) because they fall (पलाशनात् (*palāśanāt*)) down.

देवैः संगच्छते यमो रश्मिभिरादित्यः (*devaiḥ saṃgacchate yamo raśmibhirādityaḥ*)—देवैः (*devaiḥ*) means with the shining rays; यमः (*yamaḥ*) the Āditya. संपिबते (*saṃpibate*) means संगच्छते (*saṃgacchate*), he moves about or sets. The meaning is that the Āditya moves in the atmosphere shining with his bright rays, or sets (sinks) together with the rays.

तत्र नः सर्वस्य पाता वा पालयिता ना पुराणाननुकामयेत (*tatra naḥ sarvasya pātā vā pālayitā nā purāṇānanukāmayeta*)—तत्र (*tatra*): in the heavenly place where the sun shines; विश्वतिः (*viśvatiḥ*) means the protector of all, the guardian. The words पतिः (*patiḥ*) and पिता (*pitā*) are explained as one who protects or guards. The Nirukta's meaning is that such an Āditya gladdens the people who have long lived in heaven (or on earth).

> अपेक्षिसुत्तिरुववनू । अमुया— ई विधवाद । पापया— कॆट्ट बुद्धियिंद । चरंतं—

> युक्तनागि । अभि आचाकशं— नोडिदॆनु । पुनः—आनंतर । तस्मै—पितुराज्ञॆगॆ ऒळपट्टु
> आ मृत्युविन बळिगॆ होगबेकॆंदु । अस्पृहयं—बयसिदॆनु.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Naciketas speaks. My father Vājaśravas desired me to follow the ancient fathers and was going about with this base thought. Being filled with mental anguish ("he has told me, who live happily, 'Go near death'"), I first looked on him with असूयन् (*asūyan*); *abhyacākaśaṃ* is from the root meaning "see". Afterwards I longed for him: at my father's command I wished to reach that death. The word तस्मै (*tasmai*) is dative because स्पृह (*spṛha*) gives the sense of recipient (sampradāna).

Or else (of the Āditya): I looked, with a base understanding unable to praise, and with *asūyā* (the bringing out of faults in qualities), at him who desires in succession the ancient forefathers, the praisers, and who moves in the sky by rising and setting; showing faults in another's qualities, I saw him as "he too is somebody", as an ordinary being. Now, knowing the greatness of that Āditya, I longed for him: I wished to reach that very Āditya by praises and by acts of service.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

*(Meaning on the side of Yama)*
- पुराणान् (*purāṇān*)—the ancient fathers
- अनुवेनंतं (*anuvenaṃtaṃ*)—him who desires that I should follow and go
- अमुया (*amuyā*)—of this kind
- पापया (*pāpayā*)—with a bad understanding
- चरंतं (*caraṃtaṃ*)—my father Vājaśravas, who is so (first)
- असूयन् (*asūyan*)—filled with agitation of mind
- अभि आचाकशं (*abhi ācākaśaṃ*)—I looked
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—afterwards
- तस्मै (*tasmai*)—submitting to my father's command, to go to that death
- अस्पृहयं (*aspṛhayaṃ*)—I wished

### Printed p. 855

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Words of Naciketas) My father Vājaśravas, who with an evil mind wished me to follow the ancient fathers, I first looked at with agitation of mind (anger). Afterwards, from the duty of obeying my father's command, I was willing to go to death.

##### English translation
(At first) I beheld him with anguish inviting me to join the men of olden time, and walking with that fell design; but afterwards I longed for him.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The words of this Ṛk were spoken by Naciketas: "My father Vājaśravas has wished, in his evil mind, that I should dwell near the fathers. Hearing this, at first great distress and anger arose in my mind. Does a father send his own son to death? Why has this evil mind come to him? Such resentment arose in my mind. Afterwards, thinking thus, I understood that obeying the father's command is the son's duty, and resolved in my mind that I would go to death." This is the main sense of the Ṛk.

**The meaning on the side of the Āditya**
- पुराणान् (*purāṇān*)—the ancient praisers, that is, the seers of former times, or the fathers of former times
- अनुवेनंतं (*anuvenaṃtaṃ*)—him who desires
- चरंतं (*caraṃtaṃ*)—the Āditya who moves in the atmosphere between rising and setting
- पापया (*pāpayā*)—unable or unwilling to praise
- बुद्ध्या (*buddhyā*)—with a base mind
- असूयन् (*asūyan*)—filled with envy (first)
- अभि आचाकशं (*abhi ācākaśaṃ*)—I looked
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—but now (knowing the Āditya's greatness)
- तस्मै (*tasmai*)—the Āditya, by praises and acts of service
- अस्पृहयं (*aspṛhayaṃ*)—I wished to obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Words of the seer Kumāra) The Āditya desires to favour the ancient seers or fathers who have praised him from of old, and moves in the atmosphere from sunrise to sunset. Unable to praise him, I, filled with evil thought and envy, thought "What is this sun, so great? What is seen in the world …"

### Printed p. 856
*(continuing from the previous page)*

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

He looked on this Sun with envy, thinking: "He is only one among the things seen in the world." Afterwards, having learned the greatness of this Āditya, he gave up that evil thought of his and wished to win Āditya's favour with hymns and acts of service.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The above statement was spoken by the seer called Kumāra. Because he did not at first know Āditya's greatness, he says that he first looked on him with disregard and ill will. Later, when knowledge had dawned and he understood Āditya's glory, he wished to praise him with hymns and the like and to obtain his grace.

> एकईषं । विश्वतः । प्रांचं । अपश्यन् । अधि । तिष्ठसि ॥ ३ ॥

> नचिकेतःसंज्ञं कुमारं यमोऽनयोत्तरया च प्रलोभयति । हे
> कुमार नवमभिनवमितः पूर्वमदृष्टं । अभिनवत्वमेव व्यनक्ति । अचक्रं चक्ररहितं

> गच्छंतं यं रथं मनसाकृणोर्मत्समीपं प्रतिगमनायाध्यवसायात्मकमीदृशं
> यं रथमकरोः कृत्वा चापश्यन् कर्तव्याकर्तव्यविभागमजानन्नधि तिष्ठसि । रथमारोहसि । यद्वा । स्तोतारं कुमाराख्यमृषिमादित्यः प्रत्यक्षः सन् देहात्मनोर्विनेकं
> बोधयति । हे कुमारर्षे चक्ररहितमेकेषं । एकः प्राण ईषास्थानीयो यस्य ।
> ईदृशमभिनवं सर्वतो गच्छंतं शरीरात्मकं यं रथं मनसांतःकरणेनाकृणोः
> अकरोः । संकल्पात्मकेन मनसा हि कामो जायते । सत्यां हि कामनायां पुण्यापुण्यात्मकं कर्म क्रियते! तेन च भोगप्रदानायेदं शरीरमारभ्यत इति परंपरया

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Yama tempts the boy called Naciketas with this verse and the next. "O Kumāra, new" means not seen before; he makes the newness plain. "Wheelless": without wheels; "single-poled": one that has a single pole (एकेष (*ekeṣa*)). Yet it goes everywhere, forward. Yama says: this chariot, which you made in your mind for coming to me, and having made it you mount it without seeing, not knowing what is to be done and what not.

Or else: Āditya, appearing in person, teaches the seer Kumāra, who praises him, the discrimination between body and self. "O seer Kumāra, the wheelless one with a single pole," meaning one whose single pole is the vital breath. This new body, going everywhere, which you made with the mind, the inner organ. Desire arises from the mind consisting of resolve; when desire exists, action of merit and demerit is done, and for the yielding of its fruit this body is begun. Thus, indirectly, the mind produces the body. Not seeing, i.e. not knowing, that body-chariot, you mount it, from not knowing my nature; you accept it as an abode of enjoyment.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The block continues as above: अपश्यन् (*apaśyan*) has the affix śatṛ in the sense of cause (Pā. Sū. 3-2-126), "because you do not know my nature you mount it, you accept it as an abode of enjoyment."

**Pratipadārtha** (Yama's sense)
- कुमार (*kumāra*)—O boy Naciketas
- अपश्यन् (*apaśyan*)—lacking the power of discrimination
- नवं (*navaṃ*)—new, that is, not seen till now
- अचक्रं (*acakraṃ*)—wheelless
- एकेषं (*ekeṣaṃ*)—having a single axle-pole
- विश्वतः (*viśvataḥ*)—in all regions
- प्रांचं (*prāṃcaṃ*)—able to travel well
- यं रथं (*yaṃ rathaṃ*)—the chariot you mounted
- मनसा (*manasā*)—in the mind, "I must come to me"
- अकृणोः (*akṛṇoḥ*)—you resolved
- अधि तिष्ठसि (*adhi tiṣṭhasi*)—you sit mounted

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Yama's words) O boy Naciketas, thinking in your mind that you must come to me, you have imagined in your mind a new chariot for that purpose. Its form is most wondrous: it must be new, seen by no one ever; it has no wheels and one axle-pole; yet it must be able to travel in every region. Imagining such a chariot in your mind, you sit mounted on it. That is, without considering whether it is right to come to me (Death), with a firm mind that you must set out you sit on that chariot; that is, you have resolved in your mind to come to me.

##### English translation
The new chariot, wheeless, single-poled, but turning everywhere,
which you, my child, has mentally formed-you stand thereon though you
see it not.

**Āditya's sense**
Addressing the seer Kumāra who praises him, Āditya appears before him, explains the difference between body and self, and teaches discriminating knowledge.
- कुमार (*kumāra*)—O seer Kumāra
- अचक्रं (*acakraṃ*)—without wheels
- नवं (*navaṃ*)—new
- एकेषं (*ekeṣaṃ*)—endowed with breath
- विश्वतः प्रांचं (*viśvataḥ prāṃcaṃ*)—able to travel everywhere
- यं रथं (*yaṃ rathaṃ*)—this chariot called the body
- मनसा (*manasā*)—by the inner organ (resolve)
- अकृणोः (*akṛṇoḥ*)—you have built for yourself
- अपश्यन् (*apaśyan*)—not knowing my nature
- अधि तिष्ठसि (*adhi tiṣṭhasi*)—you sit mounted

### Printed p. 858

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Āditya speaks thus to the seer Kumāra: O seer Kumāra, this body is like a chariot. It has no wheel, only a single axle-pole; that is, as the axle-pole is the support of a chariot, so the breath is the support of the body. This body can travel everywhere with the help of the feet. Listen, I shall tell how it came to you. From the resolve born in the mind arises desire (longing) to do an act. When desire arises, acts of merit and demerit are done. To experience those acts the body is obtained. Thus by the power of the mind's resolve a living being obtains a body. You built this body by the resolve of your own mind, and, not knowing my nature as the Supreme Brahman, you sit in that chariot of the body. That is, without gaining knowledge of Brahman and without liberation, you remain in the body and toil in the ocean of worldly life. The sense is that Āditya thus teaches Kumāra the discrimination of body and self; this meaning is suggested in the Ṛk.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यं कु॑मार॒ प्राव॑र्तयो॒ रथं॒ विप्रे॑भ्य॒स्परि॑ ।  
> तं सामानु॒ प्राव॑र्तत॒ समि॒तो ना॒व्याहि॑तं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यं । कुमार । प्र । अवर्तयः । रथं । विप्रेभ्यः । परि ।  
> तं । साम । अनु । प्र । अवर्तत । सं । इतः । नावि । आहितं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे कुमार नचिकेतः यं पूर्वोक्तमधिष्ठितं रथं प्रावर्तयः मत्समीपं
> प्रत्यगमयो विप्रेभ्यो मेधाविभ्यः पर्युपरि भूलोके वर्तमानानां मेधाविनां बांधवानामुपरिष्कात् । अंतरिक्ष इत्यर्थः ॥ पंचम्याः परावध्यर्थ इति
> विसर्जनीयस्य सत्वं ॥ तं रथं साम पित्रा कृतं सांत्वनं यमसमीपं गत्वैवमेव
> त्वया वक्तव्यमिति प्रत्यागमनकारणमुपायोपदेशनमनु प्रावर्तत । इतोऽस्माल्लोकादन्वगच्छत् । कथंभूतं । नावि नौवत्तरणसाधनायां बुद्धौ समाहितं सम्य-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O boy Naciketas, the chariot mentioned and mounted, which you drove" (प्रावर्तयः (*prāvartayaḥ*)): you made it come to my vicinity, "from the sages," i.e. above (परि (*pari*) = upari) the wise kinsmen living on the earth, that is, in the atmosphere. The visarga takes sattva because the sense of परि (*pari*) is that of "above" in construction with the ablative. "That chariot, the साम (*sāma*)": the consolation given by your father, "Go to Yama and speak to him just so," being the counsel of the means for returning, "followed" (अनु प्र अवर्तत (*anu pra avartata*)) from this world. How is it? "On the ship" (नावि (*nāvi*)): placed, firmly held, in the intellect which is the means of crossing like a boat, सम्य- (*samya-*)

### Printed p. 859

> गृतं । यद्वा । हे कुमारर्षे यं शरीरात्मकं रथमधिष्ठितं प्रावर्तयः संसारे
> प्रवर्तितवानसि मेधाविनां मध्यॆ तं रथमनु साम । उपलक्षणमेतत् । ऋक्सामादिसाध्यं स्तोत्रं नावि नौवत्तायित्र्यां वाचि वेदात्मिकायां समाहितं सम्यकृतिपाद्यत्वेन हितं कर्म चेतोऽस्माल्लोकात्पावर्तत । प्रवृत्तमभूत् । इत्थमात्मस्वरूपापरिज्ञानेन शरीरबंधनं तेन कर्तव्यं व्यवहारजातं चोक्तं । अथ तु सत्यज्ञानादिस्वरूपमकर्तारं परमात्मानं यदि स्वात्मतया साक्षात्करोति तदोक्तं न संभवतीत्यभिप्रायः॥
> यमन परवाद अर्थ
> कुमार—ऎलै नचिकेतकुमारने । यं रथं—नन्न बळिगॆ बरुवदक्कागि नीनु हत्ति
> कुळितिद्द याव रथवन्नु हत्ति । विप्रेभ्यः—भूलोकदल्लिरुव मेधाविजनर । परि—मेलुभाग
> दल्लि ऎंदरॆ अंतरिक्षदल्लि । प्र अवर्तयः—नन्न समीपक्कॆ बंदॆयो । तं—अंतह रथवन्नु ।
> नावि सं आहितं—निन्न तंदॆयिंद निनगॆ हितोपदेशरूपवागि माडिद । साम—यमन
> समीपक्कॆ होगि अवनॊडनॆ ई रीति मातनाडु ऎंब सांत्ववचनवु । इतः—ई भूलोकदिंद ।
> अनु प्र अवर्तत—अनुसरिसि बंदितु.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

...held well. Or else: O seer Kumāra, the body-chariot you mounted, you have set rolling in worldly life among the wise; साम (*sāma*) here is an indication of the whole: the hymn to be accomplished with Ṛk, Sāman and the like, and the act well placed (as properly to be performed) in the speech made of the Veda, which is like a boat, followed from this world. Thus bondage to the body through ignorance of the nature of the self, and the activities to be performed by it, are stated. But if one directly realises as one's own self the Supreme Self, of the nature of truth and knowledge, a non-doer, then what has been said is not possible: this is the intention.

**Pratipadārtha** (Yama's sense)
- कुमार (*kumāra*)—O boy Naciketas
- यं रथं (*yaṃ rathaṃ*)—the chariot you mounted in order to come to me
- विप्रेभ्यः (*viprebhyaḥ*)—of the wise people on earth
- परि (*pari*)—above, that is, in the atmosphere
- प्र अवर्तयः (*pra avartayaḥ*)—you came near me
- तं (*taṃ*)—that chariot
- नावि सं आहितं (*nāvi saṃ āhitaṃ*)—made by your father to you as wholesome counsel
- साम (*sāma*)—the conciliatory speech "Go near Yama and speak to him thus"
- इतः (*itaḥ*)—from this earth
- अनु प्र अवर्तत (*anu pra avartata*)—followed and came

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Yama's words) O Kumāra, to come to me you mounted a chariot, and with its help you passed through the atmosphere over the intelligent people of the earth and have come near me. At that time the conciliatory counsel, the wholesome advice made by your father, followed you together with that chariot. That is, your father's wholesome advice was remembered by you.

##### English translation
The chariot which you, my child, has driven down to me from the sages above, the Saman has driven it back again from hence placed on a ship.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

"Which chariot, Kumāra, you drove, from the sages above": what the words विप्रेभ्यः परि (*viprebhyaḥ pari*) are used for here is not clear. It is commonly held that the world of the Fathers (Yama's world) and heaven lie in a high region. So to go to the lofty world of Yama one must pass over humans and others on the earth. Moreover the word विप्र (*vipra*) means the wise, the intelligent. However intelligent, men cannot go to the upper part of the atmosphere (another world) without some means of help.

### Printed p. 860
So even if intelligent, people remain below on the earth. The seer has used the words विप्रेभ्यः परि (*viprebhyaḥ pari*) to show that Naciketas, going to Yama's world, left behind the mountains, animals, men and so on of the earth and went above.

"That Sāman followed from here, placed on the ship": some words in this sentence need explanation. The seer's intention cannot be known, so the commentator's explanation must be followed here. For the word साम (*sāma*) he explains पित्रा कृतं सांत्वनं, यमसमीपं गत्वा, एवमेव त्वया वक्तव्यमिति प्रत्यागमनकारणमुपायोपदेशं (*pitrā kṛtaṃ sāṃtvanaṃ, yamasamīpaṃ gatvā, evameva tvayā vaktavyamiti pratyāgamanakāraṇamupāyopadeśaṃ*); that is, साम (*sāma*) means conciliatory speech, appeasement: "O son, go to Yama and speak to him obediently; tell him in good words that you have come to him at my command, and win his favour," and the like; such is the counsel. नावि (*nāvi*)—नौवत्तरणसाधनायां बुद्धौ (*nauvattaraṇasādhanāyāṃ buddhau*): नावि (*nāvi*) means "in a boat." Here the word is used purely in the sense of a means: as a boat is needed to cross the sea or a river, and with its help we cross the river easily, so in times of trouble with the help of our intellect we cross, that is, remove, our troubles. The boat is the means of crossing the river, the intellect the means of crossing troubles. आहितं (*āhitaṃ*)—सम्यग्धृतं (*samyagdhṛtaṃ*): placed, that is, placed in the intellect or mind, remembered in the mind. The wholesome advice the father gave his son Naciketas as he went to Yama's world followed him when he sat in the chariot; that is, Naciketas kept his father's advice in his mind and did not forget it.

**Āditya's sense**
- कुमार (*kumāra*)—O seer called Kumāra, you
- यं रथं (*yaṃ rathaṃ*)—having mounted the chariot called the body (becoming embodied)
- विप्रेभ्यः परि (*viprebhyaḥ pari*)—among wise people
- प्र अवर्तयः (*pra avartayaḥ*)—you have become engaged in worldly life
- तं (*taṃ*)—remaining in that body
- साम (*sāma*)—which is accomplished with Ṛk, Sāman and other mantras
- नावि समाहितं (*nāvi samāhitaṃ*)—which is contained in Vedic sentences, that sacrificial act
- अनु (*anu*)—performing following it
- इतः (*itaḥ*)—from this world
- प्र अवर्तत (*pra avartata*)—you go to the Supreme Self

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Āditya's words) O seer called Kumāra, mounted on the chariot of the body, that is, as an embodied man, you are engaged among wise people in worldly acts, and

### Printed p. 861
you perform sacrificial acts which are contained in the Vedic sentences and accomplished with Ṛk and Sāman mantras. Having performed these acts, then as their fruit you realise by your pure intellect the Supreme Self, of the nature of truth and knowledge and so on, unattached, and you join the Supreme Self: this is the sense.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the first half of this Ṛk the embodied man's engagement in worldly life is described, and in the second half his release from it, his realisation of the Supreme Self by the path of withdrawal, and his attainment of the good goal.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कः पुरुष इमं कुमारमजनयत् । अधिक्षेपे किंशब्दः । ईदृशं बालं
> यमसमीपं प्रहिण्वन् कथं पिता समीचीनः स्यात् । तत्तावदास्तां । को ना
> पुरुषोऽस्य बालस्य यमसमीपं प्रतिगमनाय तं रथं निरवर्तयत् । निर्वर्तितवान् । सोऽपि मूर्ख इत्यर्थः । यथा येन प्रकारेणायं कुमारोऽनुदेय्यनुदातव्योऽभवत् भवति तत्तदनुगुणं वचनमुपायकथनमद्यास्मिन्काले नोऽस्माकं कः स्वित् को नाम ब्रूयात् । अभिदध्यात् । प्रथमं यमसमीपं गत्वा
> पश्चात्ततो निर्गमनोपायं ब्रुवन्नपि न प्राज्ञ इत्यर्थः । अथवा । कुमाराख्य
> ऋषिरात्मनः सर्वात्म्यमवगच्छन् स्वव्यतिरिक्तस्यान्यस्यासंभवं किंशब्देनाक्षेपवाचिना
> दर्शयति । कुमारं मां कः पिताजनयत् । न कोऽपि । अजो नित्यः शाश्वतः ।
> क. उ. २-१८ । इति श्रुत्युक्तरूपोऽहं भवामि । कश्च शरीरात्मकं रथं निरवर्तयत् ।
> निर्वर्तयति । मद्व्यतिरिक्तस्य निर्वर्तयितुरभावात् तथा निर्वर्त्यस्यान्यस्यासंभवाच्च

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Who" (कः (*kaḥ*)) begot this boy? The word "who" is used in reproach: how could a father be sound who sends such a child to Yama? Let that be. What man made that chariot go forth for this child's going to Yama? He too is a fool. In whatever way this boy would be one to be consoled, which fitting speech, which means-telling, would anyone now speak to us? One who, having first gone to Yama, afterwards tells the way of getting out of there, is not wise either.

Or else: the seer called Kumāra, realising his identity with all, shows with the word "who," which conveys rejection, that anything other than himself is impossible. "Who, a father, begot me, Kumāra?" No one. I am of the form stated by the Śruti: अजो नित्यः शाश्वतः (*ajo nityaḥ śāśvataḥ*) (Ka. U. 2-18). And who makes the body-chariot go forth? None, since there is no maker other than I, and likewise no other thing to be made. ()

### Printed p. 862

> अद्यास्मिन्नाले सर्वात्म्यानुभवदशायां तं तं प्रकारं कः स्वित्को नाम नोऽस्माकं
> ब्रूयात् यथा येन प्रकारेणानुदेय्यनुदातव्या मद्व्यतिरिक्तान्यपदार्थसत्ताभवत् भवति । स प्रकारोऽपि दुर्वचन इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes the sentence. In this present state of experiencing everything as the Self, who, what person indeed, would tell us the manner in which (यथा (*yathā*)) the existence of anything other than myself, the अनुदेय्य (*anudeyya*), comes to be? That manner too is hard to state.

**Pratipadārtha** (Yama version)
- कः (*kaḥ*)—which man
- कुमारं (*kumāraṃ*)—this boy (in order to send him to Yama)
- अजनयत् (*ajanayat*)—begets
- कः (*kaḥ*)—which man (in order to send the boy to Yama's presence)
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—a chariot
- निः अवर्तयत् (*niḥ avartayat*)—prepares
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- अनुदेयिा (*anudeyiā*)—the boy, as one to be handed over to Yama
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—becomes (and afterwards, to come back from there)
- तत् (*tat*)—the corresponding means
- अद्य (*adya*)—now
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- कः स्वित् (*kaḥ svit*)—which man, pray
- ब्रूयात् (*brūyāt*)—would tell

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the affairs of the world, what man would beget a son in order to hand him over to the power of death? What man would seat the son he has begotten in a chariot and send him to Yama's presence? And after sending him to Yama, what man would teach him the means by which his son may come back?

##### English translation
Who has begotton the youth? Who has driven the chariot of? Who can tell us how restitution was made ?

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Is there in the world a man who hands over to the power of death his own son, whom he himself has begotten? Is there in the world a father who himself tells his son to go to Yama's house, prepares a chariot for his going, teaches him the means of returning from there, and so sends him to Yama? If there were one, he would be a pure fool. A man who acts against justice and the practice of the world is not wise but a pure fool; this is the purport.

(Āditya version) The seer named Kumāra, knowing that he is a part of the Supreme Self, that he is identical with the Supreme Self, that nothing else exists apart from the Supreme Self, and that everything is the Supreme Self's own, refutes in this Ṛk the view opposed to that.

### Printed p. 863
**Pratipadārtha** (Āditya version)
- कुमारं (*kumāraṃ*)—me, bearing the name Kumāra
- कः (*kaḥ*)—which father
- अजनयत् (*ajanayat*)—begot (none did)
- कः (*kaḥ*)—who
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—as if placed in the chariot that is the body
- निरवर्तयत् (*niravartayat*)—makes
- अद्य (*adya*)—now
- यधा (*yadhā*)—in what manner
- अनुदेयिा (*anudeyiā*)—a thing other than me (the Self)
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—exists
- कः स्वित् (*kaḥ svit*)—which man
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- ब्रूयात् (*brūyāt*)—would tell
- तत् (*tat*)—that statement is a false statement indeed (for apart from the Self there is no other thing)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Which father begot me, who am called Kumāra? Since the world, the things in the world, all men and living beings, everything, are of the nature of the Supreme Self and nothing exists apart from the Supreme Self, who is the son and who the father? What is it, then, for a father to beget a son? All this is mere delusion. Our body is a chariot; in it I (the seer Kumāra), a part of the Supreme Self, dwell. Who has made it to be so? None other than the Supreme Self. What man says that in the world there is a thing apart from the Self (the Supreme Self)? One who says so is a fool, and his statement is utterly false, because apart from the Self there is no other thing. This is the main purport.

#### Ṛk 6

> पु॒रस्ता॑द्बु॒द्न आत॑तः प॒श्चान्नि॒रय॑णं कृ॒तं ॥ ६ ॥

> पुरस्तात् । बुध्नः । आततः । पश्चात् । निःऽअयनं । कृतं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यमेन दत्तोऽभवत् भवति तथा ततस्तस्माद्वाजश्रवसात्पितुरग्रं यमसमीपं गच्छेति
> वचनस्याग्रतो वर्तमानं नचिकेतसा यमेन सह वदितव्यं तं वै प्रवसंतं गंतासीति

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अनुदेय्य (*anudeyya*) means "to be given back". In the manner in which this boy, following his father, comes to be given by Yama, so from that father, Vājaśravasa, there stood in front (अग्रं (*agraṃ*)) of the command "Go to Yama's presence" a matter on which Naciketas was to speak with Yama. The Brāhmaṇa text, तं वै प्रवसंतं गंतासीति होवाचेत्यादिकं । (*taṃ vai pravasaṃtaṃ gaṃtāsīti hovācetyādikaṃ |*) (Tai. Brā. 3-11-8-2), is cited at the page's end (continued in the next block).

> भवति तदनुगुणं ततस्तस्मान्मायाविशिष्टादात्मनोऽग्रं स्रष्टव्यस्य विकारजातस्याद्यं
> मनस्तत्त्वं सिसृक्षाकारणमजायत। उदपद्यत। पुरस्तात्सृष्टेः प्रागवस्थायां बुध्नो
> मूलमव्याकृतं मायात्मकं कारणमेवाततः । आ समंतात्ततं विस्तृतमासीत् ।
> पश्चात्तमस उत्पत्यनंतरं निरयणं तद्दतानां कार्याणां तस्मात्कारणान्निर्गमनं
> घटपटादिभेदेन स्वरूपालंभनं कृतं । ब्रह्मणा निर्मितं । तथा मृद्विकारो घटादिर्मृदोऽन्नो न भवति । आदित्यानुग्रहाद्ब्रह्मभावं प्राप्तस्य मम विकारः प्रपंचो
> मदन्यो न भवतीति व्यतिरिक्तस्य पित्रादेराक्षेपः पूर्वोक्तः समर्थितः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That is what the other Brāhmaṇa says. अजायत (*ajāyata*) means "appeared": the father gave the instruction. पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*): before that, बुद्ध (*buddha*) (the printed form of बुध्नः (*budhnaḥ*)), the root of the stated अग्र (*agra*), that is, the command "Go to Yama's house", was आततः (*ātataḥ*), very widely spread. Since it could not be undone, afterwards the father, giving up his anger, made निरयणं (*nirayaṇaṃ*), a means of going out from Yama, done by the father.

Alternatively (Āditya): अनुदेय्य (*anudeyya*) is the thought of the existence of things other than the nature of the Self, which is to be given after the Self. In whatever manner that comes to be, accordingly from the Self endowed with māyā, first of all, the foremost principle of what was to be created, the mind-principle, the cause of the desire to create, arose. Before creation, in the state prior to it, the root (बुध्नः (*budhnaḥ*)), the unmanifest māyā-natured cause alone, was spread out everywhere. Afterwards, after the arising out of darkness, निरयणं (*nirayaṇaṃ*), the going out of the effects contained in it from that cause, the taking on of their own form as pot, cloth and so on, was made by Brahman. Just as a pot and the like, a modification of clay, is not other than the clay, so for me, who by the grace of Āditya have attained the state of Brahman, the world, my modification, is not other than me. Thus the earlier-stated rejection of something separate, such as a father, is justified.

**Pratipadārtha** (Yama version)
- अनुदेयि (*anudeyi*)—this boy (Naciketas), one who is to be sent back by Yama to his father
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—he comes to be, in that manner
- ततः (*tataḥ*)—from Vājaśravas, Naciketas's father
- अग्रं (*agraṃ*)—beforehand, that is, before saying "Go to Yama"
- अजायत (*ajāyata*)—the thought arose in the mind
- पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*)—before that
- बुध्नः (*budhnaḥ*)—the root-like sentence "Go to Yama's house"
- आततः (*ātataḥ*)—was spread in the mind (was fixed)
- पश्चात् (*paścāt*)—afterwards (when the anger had been given up)
- निरयणं (*nirayaṇaṃ*)—the means of coming back again from Yama's house
- कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)—was decided upon by the father

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Before the father Vājaśravas told his son Naciketas to go to Yama's house, the means for Naciketas to come back from Yama's house had occurred to his mind. Therefore, before telling him to go to Yama's house, the father had settled the means of the son's return.

##### English translation
How restitution was made appeared from the (command given) at first; before that the depth was outstretched, afterwards a means of returning (from Yama) was provided.

### Printed p. 865

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The father told his son Naciketas to go to Yama's house. But before saying so, he had thought out the means by which the son should come back from there to him, and only then spoke. Though in a surge of anger he said "Go to Yama's house", afterwards he gave up his anger and with a calm mind made the suitable means for his son to come back from Yama's house. This is the main purport.

(Āditya version)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अनुदेयि (*anudeyi*)—the false notion that there is a thing other than the nature of the Self
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—it arises
- ततः (*tataḥ*)—prior to that intellect endowed with māyā
- अग्रं (*agraṃ*)—first
- अजायत (*ajāyata*)—the mind-principle was created
- पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*)—in the state existing before creation
- बुद्धिः (*buddhiḥ*)—the māyā-natured cause that was in the unmanifest state
- आततः (*ātataḥ*)—was spread everywhere
- पश्चात् (*paścāt*)—afterwards, that is, after the cause had begun to take the form of effect
- निरयणं (*nirayaṇaṃ*)—so that from the unmanifest, of the nature of cause, the manifest, of the nature of effect, that is, the world and the rest, should appear
- कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)—was made (was created)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

It merely appears in the minds of ordinary men that a thing other than the Self exists in this world. Before such a false notion arose in the mind, the mind-principle (that is, the mind of living beings) was created. Only after the mind is created do the mind's activities go on. Therefore the mind-principle was created first. Afterwards the mind's activity of thinking, that is, the false notion that things other than the Self exist, arose. Before creation, when Brahman was in the unmanifest state, the world and the rest existed in that unmanifest state in the form of cause. Afterwards, when the unmanifest came into the manifest state, the world and the rest (pots, cloths and other things) passed from the causal state to the state of effect. All this is Brahman's creation. For example, things that are modifications of clay, such as the pot, though they appear in many shapes such as pot and tile, have one and the same original substance, clay. In the same way, though the things seen in this world are of many kinds, Brahman alone is the original cause of them all. Therefore the seer describes that I, who by Āditya's grace have attained the state of Brahman, have come to the knowledge that no thing other than myself exists in this world.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्वा । देवानां रश्मीनां निर्माणसाधनमिति गीयते । अस्य यमस्य प्रीणनायेयं नाळीर्वाद्यविशेषो वेणुर्धम्यते । वाद्यते । यद्वा । नाळीति वाज्ञाम । इयं
> स्तुतिरूपा वागस्य प्रीणनाय धम्यते । उच्चार्यते । एवं सत्ययं यमो गीर्भिः
> स्तुतिभिः परिष्कृतः । अलंकृतोऽभूत् ॥ संपर्युपेभ्य इति सुडागमः । परिनिविभ्य
> इति षत्वं । गतिरनंतर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the सदनं (*sadanaṃ*), the place, of Yama, the controller, or of Āditya Vaivasvata; that dwelling which is said (उच्यते (*ucyate*)), spoken of everywhere, to be देवमानं (*devamānaṃ*), made by the gods. Or else it is sung of as the means of making the rays of the gods. To please this Yama this नाळीः (*nāḷīḥ*), a particular instrument, the flute, is blown (धम्यते (*dhamyate*), played). Or else नाळी (*nāḷī*) is a name of speech: this speech in the form of praise is uttered (धम्यते (*dhamyate*)) to please him. This being so, this Yama is adorned (परिष्कृतः (*pariṣkṛtaḥ*)) by praises (गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)).

**Pratipadārtha** (Yama version)

- उच्यते (*ucyate*)—is said, such
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—this world of Yama
- यमस्य (*yamasya*)—of Yama
- सदनं (*sadanaṃ*)—is the abode
- अस्य (*asya*)—for the pleasure of this Yama
- इयं नाळीः (*iyaṃ nāḷīḥ*)—this particular instrument called the flute
- धम्यते (*dhamyate*)—is blown
- आयं (*āyaṃ*)—this Yama

- परिष्कृतः (*pariṣkṛtaḥ*)—is adorned (is praised)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This (Yama's) world, made by the gods, is renowned as Yama's dwelling-place. For the pleasure of this Yama they blow the instrument called the flute, and this Yama is praised with words in the form of praise.

##### English translation
This is the dwelling of Yama, which is called the fabric of the gods; this pipe is sounded for his (gratification) he is propitiated by hymns.

The place that has been made by the gods or by shining rays is renowned as the orb of Āditya. That orb of Āditya is Āditya's place. For the pleasure of this Āditya, people praise him, reciting words in the form of praise, with hymns and the like.

## Sūkta 136 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
The deities of this sūkta are the Keśins. Yāska, explaining the meaning of the word Keśin, says:
केशी केशा रश्मयस्तैस्तद्वान् भवति । काशनाद्वा प्रकाशनद्वा ॥ (*keśī keśā raśmayastaistadvān bhavati | kāśanādvā prakāśanadvā ‖*) (Ni. 12-25)
Keśāḥ means hairs, body-hair. Keśa is also a name for rays, because hairs are fine and long; since rays are like them, it is customary to call rays keśāḥ too. One who has such hairs or rays is called Keśin. One who has rays may be the sun, fire or wind. Therefore it is said that the deities of this sūkta are Agni, Sūrya and Vāyu. Chiefly the deity of this sūkta is Sūrya. The word keśa is derived from the root kāś, "to shine"; keśāḥ means shining or radiant rays. In the Bṛhaddevatā the meaning of the word Keśin is explained thus:
कृत्वा सायं पृथग्याति भूतेभ्यस्तमसोऽत्यये । प्रकाशं किरणैः कुर्वंस्तेनैनं केशिनं विदुः ॥ (*kṛtvā sāyaṃ pṛthagyāti bhūtebhyastamaso 'tyaye | prakāśaṃ kiraṇaiḥ kurvaṃstenainaṃ keśinaṃ viduḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 2-65)
Explanation of the word Keśin: in the evening he sets and darkness comes; when in due course that darkness has passed and it is light, he makes light with his rays for the benefit of all living beings; therefore they call this god (the sun) Keśin.

### Printed p. 868

Further, in the 44th Ṛk of the 164th sūkta of the first maṇḍala it is said: त्रयः केशिनः (*trayaḥ keśinaḥ*), "the three Keśins, possessed of excellent rays that stand in the place of hair". The word केशिनः (*keśinaḥ*) applies to the three deities Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya, as having excellent rays in place of hair. The Bṛhaddevatā describes the same thing and states the particular nature of Agni, Vāyu and Āditya:

अर्चिभिः केश्ययं त्वग्निर्विद्युद्भिश्चैव मध्यमः । निपातमात्रे कथ्यंते तथाग्नेयानि कानिचित् ॥ (*arcibhiḥ keśyayaṃ tvagnirvidyudbhiścaiva madhyamaḥ | nipātamātre kathyaṃte tathāgneyāni kānicit ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 1-94)

The flame of the earthly Agni is like hair, so Agni is named Keśin. Vāyu, who dwells in the atmosphere, is Keśin through his lightning-like radiances, and Āditya, who dwells in the heavenly world, through his rays. Each is so called through his own … **NOTE**.

एतेषां तु पृथक्त्वेन त्रयाणां केशिनामिह । संलक्ष्यंते प्रक्रियासु त्रयः केशिन इत्यैचि ॥ (*eteṣāṃ tu pṛthaktvena trayāṇāṃ keśināmiha | saṃlakṣyaṃte prakriyāsu trayaḥ keśina ityaici ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 1-95)

Since the natures of these three kinds of Keśins are different, their actions too are different; this is what is said in the Ṛk त्रयः केशिनः (*trayaḥ keśinaḥ*) (1-164-44). But it is not possible to divide up their actions and their extent and to say exactly that this is so and not otherwise. Since all are all-pervading, a division of places is also not possible.

न चैवैषां प्रसूतिर्वा विभूतिस्थानजन्म वा । निर्वक्तुं शक्यमेतैर्हि कृत्स्नं व्याप्तमिदं जगत् ॥ (*na caivaiṣāṃ prasūtirvā vibhūtisthānajanma vā | nirvaktuṃ śakyametairhi kṛtsnaṃ vyāptamidaṃ jagat ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 1-96)

It is not possible to say separately of these their origin, their power or their place. The whole world is pervaded by them. Their power and their actions are limited neither by place nor by time.

It must be examined whether these three deities—who under the names Agni, Vāyu and Āditya carry out their duties in the three worlds in three ways, according to time—are of different natures, or are three different forms of one principle. In the 164th sūkta, from its beginning, it is seen that the main aim is the teaching of the one principle that pervades the whole universe. In some Ṛks it is described as the Supreme Brahman, in other places as the Supreme Person, golden in form, who dwells within Āditya. Although the present Ṛk seems to describe deities of different natures, it is described in many places that the basic principle of all of them is one, and that all of them are different forms of that basic principle. In some places that basic principle is called Āditya, in others Agni.

### Printed p. 869

भवद्भूतस्य भव्यस्य जंगमस्थावरस्य च । अस्यैके सूर्यमेवैकं प्रभवं प्रलयं विदुः ॥ (*bhavadbhūtasya bhavyasya jaṃgamasthāvarasya ca | asyaike sūryamevaikaṃ prabhavaṃ pralayaṃ viduḥ ‖*)

असतत्त्व सतश्चैव योनिरेषा प्रजापतिः । यदक्षरं च वाच्यं च यथैतद्ब्रह्म शाश्वतं ॥ (*asatattva sataścaiva yonireṣā prajāpatiḥ | yadakṣaraṃ ca vācyaṃ ca yathaitadbrahma śāśvataṃ ‖*)

कृत्वैष हि त्रिधात्मानं एष लोकेषु तिष्ठति । देवान्यथायथं सर्वान् निवेश्य स्वेषु रश्मिषु ॥ (*kṛtvaiṣa hi tridhātmānaṃ eṣa lokeṣu tiṣṭhati | devānyathāyathaṃ sarvān niveśya sveṣu raśmiṣu ‖*)

एतद्भूतेषु लोकेषु अग्निभूतं स्थितं त्रिधा । ऋषयो गीर्भिरर्चंति होत्रायां व्यक्तबर्हिषः ॥ (*etadbhūteṣu lokeṣu agnibhūtaṃ sthitaṃ tridhā | ṛṣayo gīrbhirarcaṃti hotrāyāṃ vyaktabarhiṣaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 1-61 to 64)

For the continuance and the dissolution (destruction) of the whole moving and unmoving world in the present, past and future, Sūrya (Prajāpati) alone is the chief cause. Prajāpati is the source of the principles (states) called asat and sat, which have an unmanifest and a manifest nature; that is, the manifest and unmanifest forms come into being from Prajāpati himself. This Prajāpati is the one denoted by the word Parabrahman, imperishable and eternal. This Prajāpati, or Sūrya, having divided his own nature into three parts, stands established in this world. He has placed all the deities in his rays, that is, in the bond of his own power. This Prajāpati or Sūrya himself is established in these worlds in three ways: he shines in three ways, like Agni on earth, like lightning in the atmosphere, and like Sūrya in heaven. The seers praise and worship him with Vedic words and with Sāman chants. He is the basic principle of the three deities described in the present Ṛk in the three forms Agni, Vāyu and Āditya; all of them are his different forms.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> केशीति सप्तर्चमष्टमं सूक्तमग्निसूर्यवायुदेवताकं । वातरशनपुता
> जूतिवातजूतिप्रभृतयः प्रत्यृचं क्रमेणर्षयः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । केशी
> मुनयो वातरशना जूतिर्वातजूतिर्विप्रजूतिर्वृषाणकः करिक्रत एतश ऋष्यशृंगश्चैकर्चाः कैशिनमिति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The eighth sūkta, beginning केशी (*keśī*), has seven Ṛks, and its deities are Agni, Sūrya and Vāyu. The seers, one for each Ṛk in order, are the sons of Vātarasana: Jūti, Vātajūti, and so on. He quotes the Anukramaṇī: केशी मुनयो वातरशना जूतिर्वातजूतिर्विप्रजूतिर्वृषाणकः करिक्रत एतश ऋष्यशृंगश्चैकर्चाः कैशिनमिति (*keśī munayo vātaraśanā jūtirvātajūtirviprajūtirvṛṣāṇakaḥ karikrata etaśa ṛṣyaśṛṃgaścaikarcāḥ kaiśinamiti*). The ritual use (viniyoga) has been stated already.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, केशी (*keśī*), is the eighth sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. Its deities are Agni, Sūrya and Vāyu; seven seers, sons of the seer Vātarasana—Jūti, Vātajūti, Viprajūti, Vṛṣāṇaka, Karikrata, Etaśa and Ṛṣyaśṛṅga—are the seers of its Ṛks, one for each Ṛk in order. In the Anukramaṇī: *keśī munayo

### Printed p. 870

vātaraśanā jūtirvātajūtirviprajūtirvṛṣāṇakaḥ karikrata etèśa ṛṣyaśṛṃgaścaikarcāḥ kaiśinaṃ* is what is said. The viniyoga has been stated before.

Sūkta 136
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 136; Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 7; Varga 24.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 7.
Seers: the Munis, sons of Vātarasana: 1. Jūti; 2. Vātajūti; 3. Viprajūti; 4. Vṛṣāṇaka; 5. Karikrata; 6. Etaśa; 7. Ṛṣyaśṛṅga.
Deity: the Keśins.
Metre: Anuṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> के॒श्य१॒॑ग्निं के॒शी वि॒षं के॒शी बि॑भर्ति॒ रोद॑सी ।  
> के॒शी विश्वं॒ स्व॑र्दृ॒शे के॒शीदं ज्योति॑रुच्यते ॥ १ ॥
