> केशी । विश्वं । स्वः । दृशे । केशी । इदं । ज्योतिः । उच्यते ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> केशाः केशस्थानीया रश्मयः । तद्वंतः केशिनोऽग्निर्वायुः सूर्यश्च । एते
> त्रयः स्तूयंते । केशी रश्मिभिर्युक्तः प्रकाशमानो ना सूर्योऽग्निं बिभर्ति ।
> हविर्भिः पोषयति । धारयति वा । कालविशेषे ह्यग्नेः पोषणाय होमः । स च
> कालविशेषः सूर्यगत्यधीन इति सूर्य एव बिभर्तित्युच्यते । तथा विषं । उदकनामैतत् । उदकं रश्मिभिर्घर्मसमय आह्ृतमयमेव केशी बिभर्ति विस्रष्टुं । तथा
> रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावश्ययमेव बिभर्ति । आपि च विश्वं व्याप्तं स्वः सर्वं जगद्दृशे
> दर्शनायायमेव केशी करोति । प्रकाशयतीत्यर्थः । इत्थंमहानुभावः केशी को
> नामेत्यत अह । इदं दृश्यमानं मंडलस्थं यज्योतिरिदमेव केशीत्युच्यते ।
> नान्य इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

केशाः (*keśāḥ*) are the rays standing in the place of hair; those who possess them are केशिनः (*keśinaḥ*): Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya. These three are praised. The radiant Keśin, Sūrya, joined with rays, "bears" Agni: he nourishes him with oblations, or he sustains him. For the homa that nourishes Agni takes place at a particular time, and that particular time depends on the course of Sūrya; therefore it is said that Sūrya alone bears him. Likewise विषं (*viṣaṃ*) is a name for water; the Keśin bears the water drawn up by his rays in the hot season, in order to release it. Likewise he bears heaven and earth (रोदसी (*rodasī*)) necessarily. Moreover the Keśin makes the whole pervaded world visible, for seeing; that is, he illumines it. Who then is this Keśin of such greatness? He answers: this visible light in the orb, this alone is called the Keśin, and no other.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- केशी (*keśī*)—Sūrya, joined with rays or radiant
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- बिभर्ति (*bibharti*)—nourishes (with oblations)
- केशी (*keśī*)—Sūrya
- विषं (*viṣaṃ*)—bears the water
- केशी (*keśī*)—Sūrya
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- बिभर्ति (*bibharti*)—bears
- केशी (*keśī*)—Sūrya
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—pervaded
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—the heavenly world
- दृशे (*dṛśe*)—makes visible to all
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—this visible
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—the radiant orb of the sun
- केशी (*keśī*)—as Sūrya
- उच्यते (*ucyate*)—is called

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The radiant Sūrya, joined with rays, nourishes Agni with oblations. The same Sūrya draws up water and bears it; he bears heaven and earth. He makes the heavenly world shine so that all can see it. This orb of light that we see with our eyes is Sūrya.

##### English translation
The radiant (Sun supports) Agni, the radiant one (supports) water, the
the radiant one supports the heaven and earth, the radiant one is for the
visibility of the whole diffused (universe)—the light is called the radiant one.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

केशी अग्निं केशी विषं (बिभर्ति) (*keśī agniṃ keśī viṣaṃ (bibharti)*)—केशः (*keśaḥ*) means rays. Those who possess those rays are called केशिनः (*keśinaḥ*). In the present Ṛk Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya are called केशिनः (*keśinaḥ*). In this sentence it is said that Sūrya bears Agni. Whether one has to make an offering in Agni or to perform sacrifices and the like, one does so at certain fixed times. When performing sacrifices one must take account of divisions of time: month, fortnight, lunar day, constellation, full moon, new moon, morning, midday, evening, night, and so on. There is a rule that such rites are to be done at such times. Since these divisions of time arise from the course of Sūrya, and since he is their lord, the help of Sūrya is needed for the homas and the like performed at those times. Therefore, since Agni is nourished by the homas and the like carried out with the help of Sūrya, it is said here that Sūrya nourishes and bears Agni.

The word विषं (*viṣaṃ*) is read among the names of water. In the hot season Sūrya draws up with his rays the water in seas and other reservoirs, and causes it to be changed, in the form of vapour, into clouds in the rainy season. Therefore it is said here that Sūrya bears the water for the sake of rain.

### Printed p. 872

केशी बिभर्ति रोदसी (*keśī bibharti rodasī*)—Sūrya bears and nourishes heaven and earth. He lights up earth and atmosphere with his radiance, and by his rays draws up water and makes that water fall on the earth as rain, and thereby makes plants and the like grow on the earth. Since he thus supplies light, rain-water and plants and the like as food, it is said that Sūrya bears and nourishes heaven and earth.

केशी विश्वं स्वः दृशे केशी इदं ज्योतिः उच्यते (*keśī viśvaṃ svaḥ dṛśe keśī idaṃ jyotiḥ ucyate*)—Sūrya sheds his light everywhere so that all the people in the world can see other things with their eyes. Without the light of Sūrya no creature could see anything or do any work. The light of Sūrya is indispensable to all. This orb of light that appears before our eyes is Sūrya.

Yāska has given a derivation for this Ṛk:

केश्यग्निं च विषं च । विषमित्युदकनाम। विष्णातेर्विपूर्वस्य स्नातेः शुद्ध्यर्थस्य विपूर्वस्य वा सचतेः । द्यावापृथिव्यौ च धारयति केशीदं सर्वमिदमभिविपश्यति, केशीदं ज्योतिरुच्यत इत्यादित्यमाह ॥ अथाप्येते इतरे ज्योतिषी केशिनी उच्येते । धूमेनाग्नी रजसा च मध्यमः ॥ (*keśyagniṃ ca viṣaṃ ca | viṣamityudakanāma| viṣṇātervipūrvasya snāteḥ śuddhyarthasya vipūrvasya vā sacateḥ | dyāvāpṛthivyau ca dhārayati keśīdaṃ sarvamidamabhivipaśyati, keśīdaṃ jyotirucyata ityādityamāha ‖ athāpyete itare jyotiṣī keśinī ucyete | dhūmenāgnī rajasā ca madhyamaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 1-36)

This Keśin (Āditya) bears Agni and water. विषं (*viṣaṃ*) is a name for water. The word विषं (*viṣaṃ*) is derived from the root स्ना (*snā*) with the prefix वि (*vi*), in the sense of purifying; or the word विष (*viṣa*) may be derived from the root सच् (*sac*), in the sense of following or being together. This Keśin (Āditya) bears and nourishes heaven and earth, and looks upon this whole world (pervades it with his rays); "this orb of light that we see is Āditya", they say. Moreover there are two other kinds of lights; they too are called Keśin. These are the well-known Agni on earth, whose smoke is like hair, so that Agni too is called Keśin; and Vāyu, the deity of the middle region, who is joined with lightning fire. In the atmosphere Vāyu is joined with mist, and this mist is hair-like; therefore Vāyu too may be called Keśin. There is another Ṛk praising these deities named केशिनः (*keśinaḥ*):

त्रयः केशिन ऋतुथा वि चक्षते संवत्सरे वपत एक एषां । विश्वमेको अभि चष्टे शचीभिर्ध्र्राजिरेकस्य ददृशे न रूपं ॥ (*trayaḥ keśina ṛtuthā vi cakṣate saṃvatsare vapata eka eṣāṃ | viśvameko abhi caṣṭe śacībhirdhrrājirekasya dadṛśe na rūpaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-44)

### Printed p. 873

त्रयः केशिन ऋतुथा विचक्षते कालेकालेऽभिविपश्यंति संवत्सरे वपत एक एषामित्यग्निः पृथिवीं दहति सर्वमेकोऽभिविपश्यति कर्मभिरादित्यो गतिरेकस्य दृश्यते न रूपं मध्यमस्य ॥ (*trayaḥ keśina ṛtuthā vicakṣate kālekāle 'bhivipaśyaṃti saṃvatsare vapata eka eṣāmityagniḥ pṛthivīṃ dahati sarvameko 'bhivipaśyati karmabhirādityo gatirekasya dṛśyate na rūpaṃ madhyamasya ‖*) (Ni. 12-27)

The three deities (Agni, Sūrya, Vāyu) who are called by the name केशिनः (*keśinaḥ*) perform their tasks at their respective times. Of them one burns on earth; this is Agni. Another looks upon the whole world with a mind of grace, by his actions such as rain and illumination; this is Āditya. Of another only the movement is seen, the form is not seen; this is Vāyu. That is, we can know that the wind blows, but cannot see its form with the eye. This is the intention of the derivation.

> आच्छादयंति ॥ वसॆ आच्छादने आदादिकः ॥ ईदृशास्ते यद्यदा देवासो देवास्तपसो
> महिम्ना दीप्यमानाः संतोऽविकृत देवतास्वरूपं प्राविशन् ॥ विशेर्लुजि शल
> इगुपधादनिटः क्सः । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं ॥ तदा ते वातस्य वायोर्ध्राजिं गतिमनु
> यंति । अनुगच्छंति । प्राणोपासनया प्राणरूपिणो वायुभावं प्रपन्ना इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sons of Vātarasana, the Munis who see things beyond the senses, Jūti, Vātajūti and the others, wear (वसते (*vasate*) means "cover") garments that are tawny (पिशंगा (*piśaṃgā*), of tawny colour) and dirty (मला (*malā*), soiled), of the nature of bark. When such as they, shining by the greatness of their austerity, entered the divine nature, then they follow the course (ध्राजिं (*dhrājiṃ*)) of Vāta, that is, of Vāyu: by meditation on Prāṇa they have attained the state of Vāyu, taking the form of Prāṇa. The verbal forms are explained by grammatical remarks, which are left out here.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वातरशनाः (*vātaraśanāḥ*)—sons of the seer called Vātarasana
- मुनयः (*munayaḥ*)—the seers Jūti, Vātajūti and others, who see things beyond the senses
- पिशंगाः (*piśaṃgāḥ*)—of tawny colour

### Printed p. 874
#### Ṛk 2 (continued)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- …soiled, that is dirty, garments
- वसते (*vasate*)—they wear (these sages)
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—shining by their austerity and their greatness
- अविक्षत (*avikṣata*)—when they enter the divine nature
- वातस्यॆ (*vātasyè*)—of the wind
- ध्राजिं (*dhrājiṃ*)—the course
- अनुयंति (*anuyaṃti*)—they follow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sages Jūti and the others, who see beyond the senses and are sons of the sage Vātaraśana, wear dirty bark garments of a dull yellowish colour. But when, through the greatness of their austerity, they attain the divine nature, they follow the course of the wind.

##### English translation
The Munis, the sons of Vatarashana, wear the yellow dirty (vestments of bark), they follow the course of the wind, when they have assumed the (power of) gods.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Jūti and the other sages, sons of the sage Vātaraśana, who saw this sūkta, live in their hermitage in the forest. They therefore cannot wear clean and costly garments like townspeople, and so wear only dull-coloured bark cloths. In earlier times, in places where cloth was not to be had, forest people used to pound the barks of certain trees, make them supple, and use them as clothing. Even now forest people in many countries use such tree-bark, or certain kinds of grass, instead of cloth. But the greatness of the austerity of Jūti and the other sages is unfathomable. By their austerity they have mastered the vital breath through prāṇāyāma and the like and have obtained the wind-state, that is, a subtle divine form. That they follow the course of the wind means that the course of the wind, which is invisible to other ordinary men, becomes visible to them. The meaning is that what others cannot do becomes possible for them, who possess a divine form.

> उन्मत्तवदाचरंतः । यद्वा । उत्कृष्टं मदं हर्षं प्राप्ताः । वयं वातान्वायूनस्माभिरुपास्यमानाना तस्थिम । आस्थितवंतः । हे मर्तासो मनुष्याः अस्माकं

> वायुना सायुज्यं प्राप्ताः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"By the mauneya", that is, by the state of a sage, by giving up all worldly dealings, they are उन्मदिता (*unmaditā*), "maddened", behaving like madmen; or else they have attained excellent joy (mada). "We have mounted the winds", the winds that are worshipped by us. "O mortals, men, you look only at our bodies, not at us", because we have attained union (sāyujya) with the formless wind.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मौनेयेन (*mauneyena*)—having given up worldly dealings, in the state of a sage
- उन्मदिताः (*unmaditāḥ*)—like madmen, or experiencing excellent joy
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- वातान् (*vātān*)—the winds (which we worship)
- आ तस्थिम (*ā tasthima*)—have mounted and are seated
- मर्तासः (*martāsaḥ*)—O men
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—our
- शरीरा इत् (*śarīrā it*)—bodies
- यूयं (*yūyaṃ*)—you
- पश्यथ (*paśyatha*)—behold

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Having given up worldly dealings, living in the state of a sage and cheerful in mind, we are seated mounted upon the wind which we worship. O men, behold our bodies.

##### English translation
Exhilarated by the sanctity of the Muni we have mounted upon the winds ; behold, mortals, (in them) our forms !

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

उन्मदिताः-उन्मत्ता उन्मत्तवदाचरंतः यद्वा उत्कृष्टं मदं हर्षं प्राप्ताः । (*unmaditāḥ-unmattā unmattavadācaraṃtaḥ yadvā utkṛṣṭaṃ madaṃ harṣaṃ prāptāḥ |*) — Those who look like madmen (lunatics) because of the dirty garments they wear; or, mada means joy: those who are cheerful in mind.
वातान् आ तस्थिम वयं (*vātān ā tasthima vayaṃ*)—What is meant by being seated mounted upon the wind? The meaning is that these sages, worshipping the wind, have obtained the wind-nature and have become inwardly merged in the wind in a subtle form. By the greatness of his austerity an ascetic can assume a form however subtle. These sages, by the greatness of their austerity, have assumed forms as subtle as the wind. That is perhaps what is described here as being seated upon the wind.

> सर्वाणि रूपाणि रूप्यमाणानि पदार्थजातान्यवचाकशदभिपश्यन् स्वतेजसा दर्शयन् ।
> तथा देवस्यदेवस्य ॥ नित्यवीप्सयोरिति द्विर्वचनं । अनुदात्तं चेति परस्याम्रेडितस्यानुदात्तत्वं ॥ सर्वस्यापि देवस्य सखा सखिभूतः अत एव सौकृत्याय । सुष्टु देवानु -
> द्दिश्य क्रियमाणं यागात्मकं कर्म सुकृतं । तस्य भावाय सम्यगनुष्ठापनाय
> हितः । सहितः स्थापितो भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The muni, the seer of this ṛk, the sage Vṛṣāṇaka, having attained the nature of the wind and of the sun by worship of each, moves through the antarikṣa, the sky. Doing what? Looking at all forms, that is, all things that can be perceived, or showing them by his own radiance. Likewise "of every god" (देवस्यदेवस्य (*devasyadevasya*)), the doubling being made by rule. He is the friend of every god, and for that very reason is placed (hita), set in position, for सौकृत्याय (*saukṛtyāya*), for the good performance of the sacrificial rite that is well done (sukṛta) when directed to the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मुनिः (*muniḥ*)—the sage Vṛṣāṇaka, the seer of this ṛk (having become one with the wind or the sun)
- विशः (*viśaḥ*)—all **NOTE**
- रूपा (*rūpā*)—things possessing forms
- अवचाकशन् (*avacākaśan*)—looking at
- अंतरिक्षेण (*aṃtarikṣeṇa*)—along the path of the sky
- पतति (*patati*)—moves about
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—of every single deity (word repeated)
- सखा (*sakhā*)—as friend
- सौकृत्याय (*saukṛtyāya*)—for the carrying out of good rites such as sacrifices
- हितः (*hitaḥ*)—is established

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sage Vṛṣāṇaka, the seer of this ṛk, by the power of his worship attains identity with the sun or the wind, and moves along the path of the sky, looking at the forms of all things.

### Printed p. 877
Likewise he behaves with friendliness towards every deity, and is appointed for the carrying out of sacrifices and other rites.

##### English translation
The Muni flies through the firmament, illumining all objects, the friend of each deity, appointed for pious works.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वात॒स्याश्वो॑ वा॒योः सखाथो॑ दे॒वेषि॑तो॒ मुनिः॑ ।  
> उ॒भौ स॑मु॒द्रावा क्षे॑ति॒ यश्च॒ पूर्व॑ उ॒ताप॑रः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वातस्य । अश्वः । वायोः । सखा । अथो इति । देव इषितः । मुनिः ।  
> उभौ । समुद्रौ । आ । क्षेति । यः । च । पूर्वः । उत । अपरः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वातस्य वायोर्गतिरिवाश्च व्याप्तः । यद्वा । वायोरशिता भोक्ता।
> वायुरेव तस्याहार इत्यर्थः । अत एव वायोः सखा मित्रभूतः अथो अपि च देवेषितो देवेन द्योतमानेन वायुना सूर्योण वेषितः प्राप्तः ॥ तृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ ईदृशो मुनिः करिक्रताख्य ऋषिरुक्तप्रकारेण वायुरूपः सूर्यरूपो वा सन्नुभौ समुद्रावुदधी आ क्षेति । अभिगच्छति॥ क्षि निवासगत्योः।
> छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् ॥ कौ तौ समुद्रौ। यश्च पूर्वः समुद्रः । उतशब्दश्चार्थे ।
> यत्थापरः समुद्रः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वातस्याश्वो (*vātasyāśvo*): he is pervasive (aśva), like the course of the wind; or else he is an eater, an enjoyer, of the wind: the wind itself is his food. For that reason he is the friend of the wind, and also (अथो (*atho*)) देवेषितः (*deveṣitaḥ*), reached (iṣita) by the shining deity, the wind or the sun. Such a muni, the sage called Karikrata, being in the form of the wind or of the sun as stated, goes to both oceans (आ क्षेति (*ā kṣeti*) = approaches). Which are those two oceans? The one that is the eastern ocean, and (उत (*uta*) is in the sense of "and") the one that is the western ocean.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वातस्य (*vātasya*)—like the course of the wind
- अश्वः (*aśvaḥ*)—all-pervading; (or) [of the wind itself—having as food] therefore
- वायोः (*vāyoḥ*)—to the wind
- सखा (*sakhā*)—friend
- अथो (*atho*)—and
- देवेषितः (*deveṣitaḥ*)—come from the shining sun or from the wind
- मुनिः (*muniḥ*)—the muni Karikrata, the seer of this ṛk
- यः च पूर्वः (*yaḥ ca pūrvaḥ*)—the ocean that lies in the eastern direction
- उत (*uta*)—and
- अपरः (*aparaḥ*)—in the other direction, that is, in the western direction
- उभौ समुद्रौ (*ubhau samudrau*)—these two oceans
- आ क्षेति (*ā kṣeti*)—approaches and goes

### Printed p. 878

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sage Karikrata, the seer of this ṛk, who is all-pervading like the wind, or has the wind itself as his food, who is a friend of the wind, and who has attained identity with the shining sun or with the wind, goes to both oceans, the eastern and the western.

##### English translation
The steed of the wind, the friend of Vayu, the Muui, who is instigated by the deity, repairs to both oceans, the eastern and the western.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒प्स॒रसां॑ गंध॒र्वाणां॑ मृ॒गाणां॒ चर॑णे॒ चर॑न् ।  
> के॒शी केत॑स्य वि॒द्वान्त्सखा॑ स्वा॒दुर्म॒दिंत॑मः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अप्सरसां । गंधर्वाणां । मृगाणां । चरणे । चरः ।  
> केशी । केतस्य । विद्वान् । सखा । स्वादुः । मदिन्तमः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अप्सरसां देवस्त्रीणां गंधर्वाणां चरणे संचारभूते दिव्यंतरिक्षे च तथा
> मृगाणां सिंहादीनां संचारस्थले पृथिव्यां चरन् व्याप्य संचरन्नेश्यग्निर्वायुः
> सूर्यो वा केतस्य ज्ञातव्यस्य सर्वस्यार्थजातस्य विद्वान् यद्वा ज्ञातव्यस्यास्यर्षेरेतशस्य सखा विद्वानविशेषात्सर्वं जानन् स्वादुः स्वादयिता रसयिता सर्वस्य रसस्कोत्पादकः अत एव मदिंतमो मादयितृतमो भवति ॥ नाद्भस्यॆति नुडागमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Of the Apsarases", the divine women, "and of the Gandharvas", in their चरणे (*caraṇe*), their place of roaming, that is, the divine sky; and likewise in the roaming-place of beasts (mṛga) such as lions, the earth: moving, that is, pervading and ranging, is Keśī, Agni, Vāyu or Sūrya. He is knower of केतस्य (*ketasya*), of everything that is to be known, all the things that exist; or else he is the friend of this sage Etaśa, who is to be known, and knows all without exception. He is स्वादुः (*svāduḥ*), one who gives savour, the producer of the savour of everything; for that very reason he is मदिंतमः (*madiṃtamaḥ*), the greatest gladdener. The augment nuṭ is by rule.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अप्सरसां (*apsarasāṃ*)—of the Apsara women, and
- गंधर्वाणां (*gaṃdharvāṇāṃ*)—of the Gandharvas
- चरणे (*caraṇe*)—in the sky, their region of roaming
- मृगाणां (*mṛgāṇāṃ*)—on the earth where beasts such as lions roam
- चरन् (*caran*)—pervading and roaming
- केतस्य (*ketasya*)—all matters that are to be known
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—one who knows
- सखा (*sakhā*)—and friend of the sage Etaśa, the seer of this ṛk
- केशी (*keśī*)—Agni, Vāyu or Sūrya

### Printed p. 879
- स्वादुः (*svāduḥ*)—producing all sweet savours
- मदिंतमः (*madiṃtamaḥ*)—becomes the one who causes joy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, Vāyu or the Sun, who pervades and roams both the sky where the Apsara women and the Gandharvas move and the regions of the earth where beasts such as lions roam, who knows everything, and who is a friend of the sage Etaśa, the seer of this ṛk, is a beneficial friend of this sage Etaśa and a friend who produces delight.

##### English translation
Wandering in the track of the Apsarasas and the Ghanharvas, and the wild beasts, the radiant (Sun), cognizant of all that is knowable, (is my) sweet and most delightful friend.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वा॒युर॑स्मा॒ उपा॑मंथत्नि॒नष्टि॑ स्मा कुनंन॒मा ।  
> के॒शी वि॒षस्य॒ पात्रे॑ण॒ यद्रु॒द्रेणापि॑बत्स॒ह ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वायुः । अस्मै । उप । अमंथत् । पिनष्टि । स्म । कुनंनमा ।  
> केशी । विषस्य । पात्रेण । यत् । रुद्रेण । अपिबत् । सह ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> केशी रश्मिभिर्युक्तः सूर्यो रुद्रेण रुद्रपुत्रेण मरुद्धणेन । यद्वा ।
> रुद्रो वा एष यदग्निः । तै. सं. ५-४-३-१ । इति श्रवणाद्रुद्रो वैद्युताग्निः । तेन
> सह वर्तमानो विषस्य । उदकनामैतत् ॥ क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः
> संप्रदानत्वाच्च तुर्थर्थ्यर्थ्य षष्ठि ॥ विषमुदकं पात्रेण पानसाधनेन रश्मिजालेन यद्यदापिबत् पिबति तदास्कै केशिने वायुरूपामंथत् । भूगतं सर्वं रसमुपमथ्याति ।
> यद्वा । यदापिबत् पीतवान्भवति तदा सूर्यमंडले घनीभूतमस्य तदुदकं
> वायुरुपमथ्याति । मंथनेन वैद्युताग्निनालोडयति । तथा कुनंनमा कुत्सितमपि
> भृशं नमयित्रि स्वयं नमयितुमशक्या स्वतंत्रा माध्यमिका वाक् पिनष्टि स्म ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Keśī, the sun endowed with rays, is with Rudra, a son of Rudra, the host of the Maruts. Or else, from the text रुद्रो वा एष यदग्निः (*rudro vā eṣa yadagniḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 5-4-3-1), Rudra is the lightning fire; being together with him, विषस्य (*viṣasya*) (viṣa is a name for water; the genitive stands for the accusative, by the rule that a verb is to be supplied and that the object has the sense of recipient) — when he drinks the water with the पात्रेण (*pātreṇa*), the vessel, the means of drinking, that is the net of rays, then the wind churns (उपामंथत् (*upāmaṃthat*)) for this Keśī: it churns up all the sap that is in the earth. Or else, when he has drunk, the wind churns that water, condensed in the solar orb, and stirs it with the churning lightning fire. Likewise कुनंनमा (*kunaṃnamā*): the one who bends greatly even what is crooked, and who herself cannot be made to bend, the independent speech of the middle region, grinds (पिनष्टि स्म (*pinaṣṭi sma*)).

### Printed p. 880

> यथाधस्तात्स्रवति तथा चूर्णीकरोति । स्मेति प्रसिद्धौ ॥ कुपूर्वान्नमयतेः
> पचाद्यचि यजोऽचि चेति यजो लुक् । थाथादिनोत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues the explanation of the previous Ṛk. The wind pulverises the water so that it flows downward. स्म (*sma*) is two well-known particles. He then gives the derivation of the word kunaṃnamā (from कुपूर्वान्नमयतेः (*kupūrvānnamayateḥ*)), which is grammatical.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- केशी (*keśī*)—the Sun, endowed with rays
- रुद्रेण (*rudreṇa*)—with the Maruts, the sons of Rudra, or with the lightning-fire of the atmosphere
- सह (*saha*)—together with
- विषस्य (*viṣasya*)—the water
- पात्रेण (*pātreṇa*)—by means of his rays, which serve as the instrument of drinking, that is, of sucking up
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अपिबत् (*apibat*)—he drinks, that is, draws up; then
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—for the help of this Sun
- वायुः (*vāyuḥ*)—the wind
- उप अमंथत् (*upa amaṃthat*)—churns the water of the oceans and other reservoirs on the earth (stirring it into turmoil) and dries it up; or, when the water drawn up by the Sun is in the form of clouds, the wind scatters it, or the lightning-fire stirs it up
- कुनंनमा (*kunaṃnamā*)—the divine Vāk of the middle region, who bends the base, yet herself is subject to no one's control
- पिनष्टि स्म (*pinaṣṭi sma*)—grinds the cloud-water to powder, that is, makes the rain-water fall on the earth drop by drop

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the radiant Sun, together with the Maruts, the divine sons of Rudra (the wind), draws up the water of the oceans and other reservoirs, the wind, for the Sun's help, churns the water into turmoil, or scatters the water that is in the form of clouds so that it spreads all around. That Vāk-goddess of the atmosphere (the lightning?), who holds everyone under her control while herself remaining under nobody's, makes the rain-water in the clouds fall on the earth in tiny drops.

##### English translation
Vayu churned for him, the inflexible (thunder) ground it when the radiant (Sun), along with Rudra, drink the water with his cup.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the seer explains how the Sun, with the help of wind and fire, becomes the cause of rain. First, the Sun's fierce rays fall on the oceans and other reservoirs and draw up their water as vapour. The vapour so drawn up is transformed into clouds by the help of the wind in the atmosphere and remains there. And that same wind scatters the clouds so that they do not stay in one place but move about; that is, as the wind blows, the clouds move onward. In such a mass of clouds the lightning-fire (lightning) appears and helps in the work of rain. The Vāk of the middle region, which is the very form of this lightning-fire, is not subject to anyone's control, that is, to anyone's authority; but she alone has the power to hold everyone under her authority. With the help of this Vāk-goddess the water in the clouds falls on the earth drop by drop: this is the main purport.

### Printed p. 881
## Sūkta 137 (Maṇḍala 10)
This sūkta prays to the deities to cure those afflicted by disease and the like. It is therefore said that this sūkta has the power of curing disease. The sage Śaunaka says of this sūkta in his work called Ṛgvidhāna:

उत देवा इति जपेदामयावी यतव्रतः (*uta devā iti japedāmayāvī yatavrataḥ*) (46)
घृतकुंभं निधायाथ जुहुयाज्ञातवेदसि (*ghṛtakuṃbhaṃ nidhāyātha juhuyājñātavedasi*) ।
कुंभात्संपातमन्यस्मिन् कांस्ये पात्रे निधापयेत् (*kuṃbhātsaṃpātamanyasmin kāṃsye pātre nidhāpayet*) (47)
यन्न पानं न चान्यं स्यात्स इदं संप्रकल्पयेत् (*yanna pānaṃ na cānyaṃ syātsa idaṃ saṃprakalpayet*) ।
तेनाज्येनांगमभ्यज्य शनकैरन्नभाग्भवेत् (*tenājyenāṃgamabhyajya śanakairannabhāgbhavet*) (48)
रोगार्तस्याप्यनेनैव गात्रमंक्त्वा जपेदिदं (*rogārtasyāpyanenaiva gātramaṃktvā japedidaṃ*) ।
अजीर्णान्नोऽप्यंजयीत सुखं भवति तेन ह (*ajīrṇānno 'pyaṃjayīta sukhaṃ bhavati tena ha*) (49)
(Ṛgvidhāna, Adhyāya 4, verses 46–49)

A man suffering from disease and the like should recite this sūkta with self-discipline. Filling a vessel with pure ghee and consecrating it, he should make an offering with the mantras of this sūkta in the established fire. While offering, the ghee that spills out of the vessel should be collected and put in another copper vessel. If the body of a man who, owing to the severity of his illness, cannot take food and drink is rubbed with this ghee, food and the like will gradually become palatable to him. Also, for the cure of the disease, the body of the sick man should be anointed with this ghee and the mantras of this sūkta recited. One should do so even in indigestion. By this the disease is cured and happiness results.

### Printed p. 882

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उत देवा इति सप्तर्चं नवमं सूक्तमानुष्टुभं वैश्वदेवं भरद्वाजकश्यपगोतमात्रिविश्वामित्रजमदग्निवसिष्ठा इति क्रमेण प्रत्यृचमृषयः । तथा चानुक्रांतं।
> उत देवाः सप्तर्षय एकर्चा वैश्वदेवमिति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This ninth sūkta of the eleventh anuvāka, beginning उत देवा (*uta devā*), has seven Ṛks, in Anuṣṭubh metre, addressed to the Viśvedevas. The seers, one per Ṛk in order, are Bharadvāja, Kaśyapa, Gotama, Atri, Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni and Vasiṣṭha. The Anukramaṇī says: उत देवाः सप्तर्षय एकर्चा वैश्वदेवमिति (*uta devāḥ saptarṣaya ekarcā vaiśvadevamiti*). The viniyoga has been stated already.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning उत देवाः (*uta devāḥ*) is the ninth sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. In this sūkta each of the seven sages Bharadvāja, Kaśyapa, Gotama, Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni and Vasiṣṭha (with Atri) is the seer of one Ṛk; the Viśvedevas are the deity. The metre is Anuṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: उत देवाः सप्तर्षय एकर्चा वैश्वदेवं (*uta devāḥ saptarṣaya ekarcā vaiśvadevaṃ*). The viniyoga has been stated before.

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 137; Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 7; Varga 25.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 7.
Seers: seven sages, one Ṛk each: 1. Bharadvāja; 2. Kaśyapa; 3. Gotama; 4. Atri; 5. Viśvāmitra; 6. Jamadagni; 7. Vasiṣṭha.
Deity: Viśvedevas.
Metre: Anuṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त दे॑वा॒ अव॑हितं॒ देवा॒ उन्न॑यथा॒ पुनः॑ ।  
> उ॒ताग॑श्च॒क्रुषं॑ देवा॒ देवा॑ जी॒वय॑था॒ पुनः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । देवाः । अव्यहितं । देवाः । उत् । नयथ । पुनरिति ।  
> उत । आगः । चक्रुषं । देवाः । देवाः । जीवयथ । पुनरिति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च हे देवाः अवहितमुन्नयथ । उतापि च हे देवाः आगोऽपराधं
> चक्रुषं कृतवंतं मां तस्मादागसो रक्षत । हे देवाः रक्षित्वा च पुनः पश्चाज्जीवयथ । चिरजीविनं कुरुत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"And, O gods, you raise up the one who has fallen low; and, O gods, protect me who have committed an offence, from that offence; and having protected me, afterwards make me live long."

### Printed p. 883

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods
- अवहितं (*avahitaṃ*)—the man who lies unable to rise, afflicted by disease and the like
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again, that is, as before
- उन्नयथ (*unnayatha*)—(giving strength) make him rise
- उत (*uta*)—and
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods
- आगः (*āgaḥ*)—sin or offence
- चक्रुषं (*cakruṣaṃ*)—me, who am committing it: protect
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—afterwards
- जीवयथ (*jīvayatha*)—favour me so that I live long

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, raise up again, that is, as before, by giving strength, the man who lies unable to rise, afflicted by disease and the like. O gods, forgive and protect me from the sin or offence that I am committing or have committed. Afterwards, O gods, grant that I may live long.

##### English translation
O gods, raise again the man, O gods, who has sunk ; O gods, give life again to the man, O gods, who has committed sin.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> द्वावि॒मौ वात्॑ वात॒ आ सिंधो॒रा प॑रा॒वतः॑ ।  
> दक्षं॑ ते अ॒न्य आ वा॑तु॒ परा॒न्वो वा॑तु॒ यद्रपः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> द्वौ । इमौ । वात् । वाशः । अ । सिंधोः । आ । परावतः ।  
> दक्षं । ते । अन्यः । आ । वातु । परा । अन्यः । वातु । यत् । रपः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमौ दृश्यमानौ द्वौ वात् पुरोवातः पश्चाद्वातश्चा सिंधोरा समुद्रात् ।
> मर्यादायामाकारः । यद्वा । परावतः समुद्रादपि यो दूरदेशस्तं देशमवधीकृत्य वातः । गच्छतः ॥ वा गतिगंधनयोः आदादिकः ॥ तयोर्वातयोरन्न एको
> हे स्तोतः ते तव दक्षं बलमा वातु । आगमयतु । अन्यश्च त्वदीयं यद्रपः पापं
> तत्परा वातु । परागमयतु ॥
> அன்புடைமை ஆன்ற குடிப்பிறத்தல் இவ்விரண்டும்

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These two winds that are seen, the east wind and the west wind, blow from the sea (आ (*ā*) marks the limit); or, taking the limit as परावतः (*parāvataḥ*), they blow up to a place even farther than the sea. वा (*vā*) is the root meaning "to go" and "to smell", of the Adādi class. Of those two winds, let one, O worshipper, bring you strength (दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*)); let the other drive away that sin (रपः (*rapaḥ*)) of yours.

**Pratipadārtha** and **Bhāvārtha** follow on the next page.

### Printed p. 884

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इमौ (*imau*)—these, seen here
- द्वौ वात् (*dvau vāt*)—the two kinds of wind blowing eastward and westward
- सिंधोः (*siṃdhoḥ*)—up to the shore of the sea
- आ परावतः (*ā parāvataḥ*)—up to a region farther than the sea
- वातः (*vātaḥ*)—blow
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—one of those winds
- ते (*te*)—to you
- दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*)—strength
- आ वातु (*ā vātu*)—let it bring
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—the other
- यत् रपः (*yat rapaḥ*)—whatever sin of yours there is
- परा वातु (*parā vātu*)—let it drive far away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

These two winds, blowing eastward and westward, blow as far as the sea or even to regions farther than that. Of them, let one wind bring you strength; let the other drive your sin far away.

##### English translation
These two winds blow to the regions which are far beyond the ocean; may the one bring you vigour, may the other blow away all evil.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ वा॑त वाहि भेष॒जं वि वा॑त वाहि॒ यद्रपः॑ ।  
> त्वं हि वि॒श्वभे॑षजो दे॒वानां॑ दू॒त ईय॑से ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । वात । वाहि । भेषजं । ए । वात । वाहि । यत् । रपः ।  
> त्वं । हि । विश्वभेषजः । देवानां । दूतः । ईयसे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वात भेषजं सुखं व्याध्युपशमनमौषधं ना वाहि । आगमय । हे वात
> यद्रपोऽस्मदीयं पापं तद्वि वाहि ! विगमय ! अस्मत्तो विश्लेषय । त्वं हि खलु
> देवानां दूतो विश्वभेषजः । विश्वानि भेषजानि यस्मिन् ॥ बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं
> संज्ञायामिति पूर्वपदांतोदात्तत्वं ॥ ईदृशश्च सन्नीयसे । सततं गच्छसि ॥ ईज्

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Wind, bring a remedy (भेषजं (*bheṣajaṃ*)), an easeful medicine that allays disease. O Wind, carry away (वि वाहि (*vi vāhi*)) our sin (रपः (*rapaḥ*)); remove it from us. For you are the messenger of the gods and विश्वभेषजः (*viśvabheṣajaḥ*), he in whom are all remedies; being such, you constantly go about (ईयसे (*īyase*))." The remainder of the block gives the accent rules for the compound and the verb.

### Printed p. 885

> गत् दैवादिकः । श्यनो नित्यात् इत्यादिर्नित्यमित्याद्युदात्तत्वं । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The root ईज् (*īj*) "to go", of the Daivādika class, with its accent rule, and the prohibition of nighāta after हि (*hi*): grammatical matter only.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वात (*vāta*)—O Wind
- भेषजं (*bheṣajaṃ*)—the medicine that allays disease and gives comfort
- आ वाहि (*ā vāhi*)—bring it near to us
- वात (*vāta*)—O Wind
- यत् रपः (*yat rapaḥ*)—whatever sin of ours there is
- वि वाहि (*vi vāhi*)—drive it back
- त्वं हि (*tvaṃ hi*)—you
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—for the gods
- दूतः (*dūtaḥ*)—as messenger
- विश्वभेषजः (*viśvabheṣajaḥ*)—as the provider of all comforts or medicines
- ईयसे (*īyase*)—you move about

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Wind, bring to us the medicine that can allay disease. O Wind, drive our sin back so that it does not come to us. You move about as messenger of the gods and as provider of all comforts or medicines.

##### English translation
Breathe, wind, medicinal balm; blow away, wind, all evil; for you are the universal medicine, you move as the messenger of the gods.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ त्वा॑गमं॒ शंता॑तिभि॒रथो॑ अरि॒ष्टता॑तिभिः ।  
> दक्षं॑ ते भ॒द्रमाभा॑ष्यं॒ परा॒ यक्ष्यं॑ सुवामि ते ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । त्वा । आगमं । शंतातिभिः । अथो इति । अरिष्टतातिभिः ।  
> दक्षं । ते । भद्रं । आ । अभार्षं । परा । यक्ष्यं । सुवामि । ते ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे स्तोतः त्वा त्वां शंतातिभिः सुखकरैरथो अपि चारिष्टतातिभिरहिंसाकरैश्च
> रक्षणैरागमं । आगतवानस्मि ॥ शिवशमरिष्टस्य करे । पा. ४-४-१४३ । इत्युभयत्र तातिल्पत्ययः । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वं ॥ अपि च भद्रं कल्याणं ते तव दक्षं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O worshipper, I have come to you with protections that bring happiness (शंतातिभिः (*śaṃtātibhiḥ*)) and also with protections that bring no harm (अरिष्टतातिभिः (*ariṣṭatātibhiḥ*)). The affix tāti is added in both words by Pā. 4-4-143. The accent falls on the syllable before the affix. Moreover, auspicious (भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)) … your strength (दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*))…"

### Printed p. 886

> बलमाभार्षं । आहार्षं । वायुसकाशादानैषं । तथा ते तव यक्ष्मं रोगं च
> परा सुनामि । विनाशयामि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes the gloss: "I have brought" (आहार्षं (*āhārṣaṃ*)) means "I have fetched" (आहार्षं (*āhārṣaṃ*)), I have brought it from the wind's neighbourhood. Likewise I drive away your यक्ष्मं (*yakṣmaṃ*), your disease, I destroy it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्वा (*tvā*)—you (O worshipper)
- शंतातिभिः (*śaṃtātibhiḥ*)—with pleasure-giving (protections)
- अथो (*atho*)—and
- अरिष्टतातिभिः (*ariṣṭatātibhiḥ*)—with protections that do no harm
- आ अगमं (*ā agamaṃ*)—I am approaching (and)
- ते (*te*)—for you
- भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)—welfare
- दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*)—and strength
- अभार्षं (*abhārṣaṃ*)—I have borne and brought (likewise)
- ते (*te*)—your
- यक्ष्मं (*yakṣmaṃ*)—disease
- परा सुवामि (*parā suvāmi*)—I destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(The wind's words:) O worshipper, I am coming to you with protections that give pleasure and do no harm. I have brought you welfare and strength. Likewise I destroy your disease.

##### English translation
(The wind speaks:) I have come to you with pleasures and with protections; I have brought you fortunate vigour, I drive away your disease.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्रायं॑तामि॒ह दे॒वास्त्राय॑तां म॒रुतां॑ ग॒णः ।  
> त्रायं॑तां॒ विश्वा॑ भू॒तानि॒ यथा॒यम॑र॒पा अस॑त् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्रायंतां । इह । देवाः । त्रायतां । मरुतां । गणः ।  
> त्रायंतां । विश्वा । भूतानि । यथा । अयं । अरपाः । असत् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इहास्मिन्देशे सर्वे देवास्त्रायंतां । अस्मान्पालयंतां । तथा मरुतां गणः
> संघः स त्रायतां । विश्वानि सर्वाण्यन्यानि च भूतानि भूतजातानि त्रायंतां । अस्मानृक्षंतु । यथायमस्मदीयः शरीरादिररपा असत् पापरहितो भवति तथेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Let all the gods in this place protect us, look after us. Let the company of the Maruts protect us. Let all other beings too protect us, guard us, so that this body of ours (or this person) may be free from sin.

### Printed p. 887

> रप इति पापनाम । नञा बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं । अस्तेर्लेट्यडागमः । यावद्यथाभ्यां । पा- ८-१-३६ । इति निघाताभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

रप (*rapa*) is a name for sin. With the negative prefix in a bahuvrīhi compound, the final of the last member takes the udātta. The root अस् (*as*) takes the augment aṭ in the leṭ. By Pā. Sū. 8-1-36 (यावद्यथाभ्यां (*yāvadyathābhyāṃ*)) there is no nighāta.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इह (*iha*)—in this place
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—all the gods
- त्रायंतां (*trāyaṃtāṃ*)—let them protect us; and
- मरुतां (*marutāṃ*)—of the Maruts
- गणः (*gaṇaḥ*)—the company
- त्रायतां (*trāyatāṃ*)—let it protect us
- यथा (*yathā*)—in which way
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this body (or this person)
- अरपाः (*arapāḥ*)—free from sin
- असत् (*asat*)—may become, so
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- भूतानि (*bhūtāni*)—all classes of beings, gods, humans and others
- त्रायंतां (*trāyaṃtāṃ*)—let them protect us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May all the gods and the hosts of Maruts look after us in this place. As this body becomes free from sin (that is, so that sin does not come), so may all beings, gods, humans and others, protect us.

##### English translation
May the gods give (us) protection in this world, may the company of the Maruts protect us, may all beings grant protection so that this (person) may be free from sin.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आप॒ इद्वा उ॑ भेष॒जीरापो॑ अमीव॒चात॑नीः ।  
> आपः॒ सर्व॑स्य भेष॒जीस्तास्ते॑ कृण्वंतु भेष॒जं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आपः । इत् । वै । ऊं इति । भेषजीः । आपः । अमीवचातनीः ।  
> आपः । सर्वस्य । भेषजीः । ताः । ते । कृण्वंतु । भेषजं ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आप इद्वा आप एव खलु भेषजीर्भेषजभूताः । स्नानपानादिना सुखहेतवः ।
> यद्वा। ओषधिरूपेण परिणता रोगोपशमनहेतवो भवंति ॥ केवलमामकेत्यादिना।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Waters alone are medicinal, medicine-like: by bathing, drinking and the like they cause happiness. Or else, transformed into the form of herbs, they become causes of the allaying of disease. (The grammatical remark begins with केवलमामकेत्यादिना (*kevalamāmaketyādinā*) and continues on the next page.)

### Printed p. 888

> पा. ४-१-३० । भेषजशब्दाद्वीप् । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण जीप उदात्तत्वं । जसि वा
> छंदसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घत्वं ॥ य एवमतः कारणादापोऽमीवचातनीरमीवचातन्यो रोगाणां नाशयित्र्यो भवंति । चातयतिर्वधकर्मा । किंचापः सर्वस्य
> प्राणिजातस्य भेषजीर्भेषजभूता भवंति न कतिपयस्य । तास्त्रथाविधा आपस्ते तव
> भेषजं कृण्वंतु । कुर्वंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Therefore the waters are destroyers of diseases; चातयति (*cātayati*) is a verb of killing. Further, the waters are medicine for every class of living beings, not for a few. Such waters, let them make medicine for you, let them do it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आप इत् वै (*āpa it vai*)—those very waters
- भेषजीः उ (*bheṣajīḥ u*)—are in the form of medicine, and by bathing, drinking and the like give us happiness
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—waters
- अमीवचातनीः (*amīvacātanīḥ*)—are destroyers of diseases
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—waters
- सर्वस्य (*sarvasya*)—for all classes of beings
- भेषजीः (*bheṣajīḥ*)—are medicinal
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—such waters, of this quality
- ते (*te*)—for you
- भेषजं (*bheṣajaṃ*)—the happiness that comes of allaying sickness
- कृण्वंतु (*kṛṇvaṃtu*)—let them bring about

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those waters are a means of bathing, drinking and so on, and give us happiness; and they destroy our diseases. These waters are medicine for all classes of beings. May such waters allay your sickness and bring you happiness.

##### English translation
Waters verily are medicinal; waters are the dissipators of disease; waters are the medicines for everything ; may they act as medicine to you-

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ना॒म॒यि॒त्नुभ्यां॑ त्वा॒ ताभ्यां॒ त्वोप॑ स्पृशामसि ॥ ७ ॥

> अनामयित्नुभ्यां । त्वा । ताभ्यां । त्वा । उप । स्पृशामसि ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दशशाखाभ्यां । दशांगुलयः शाखाभूता ययोः तादृशाभ्यां प्रजापतेर्हस्ताभ्यां सृज्यमाना जिह्वा रसना वाचः शब्दस्य पुरोगवी पुरतो गंत्रि जाता । यत्र

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The tongue, created by the two hands of Prajāpati, of which the ten fingers are the branches (दशशाखाभ्यां (*daśaśākhābhyāṃ*)), became the forerunner of speech (वाचः (*vācaḥ*)): wherever there is speech, it moves forward first for the utterance of that word.

### Printed p. 889

> यत्र शब्दस्तत्र सर्वत्र तस्य शब्दस्योच्चारणाय पुरतो व्याप्रियत इत्यर्थः । अनामयित्नुभ्यां सम्यगारोग्यहेतुभ्यां ताभ्यां हस्ताभ्यां हे स्तोतः त्वामुप स्पृशामसि । उपस्पृशामः ॥ इदंतो मसिः । त्वैति पुनरुक्तिः पारपूरणार्था ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That is the meaning. With those two hands, which are causes of perfect health, O worshipper, we touch you. The ending मसि (*masi*) has *idaṃtaḥ*. The second त्वा (*tvā*) is a repetition to fill out the verse-quarter.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाचः (*vācaḥ*)—for the utterance of words
- पुरोगवी (*purogavī*)—moving in advance
- जिह्वा (*jihvā*)—the tongue
- दशशाखाभ्यां (*daśaśākhābhyāṃ*)—provided with ten fingers
- हस्ताभ्यां (*hastābhyāṃ*)—has been created by the two hands of Prajāpati
- अनामयित्नुभ्यां (*anāmayitnubhyāṃ*)—which are the cause of health
- ताभ्यां (*tābhyāṃ*)—with those hands (हे स्तोतः (*he stotaḥ*), O worshipper)
- त्वा त्वा (*tvā tvā*)—you
- उपस्पृशामसि (*upaspṛśāmasi*)—we touch

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The tongue moves before the utterance of words; that is, utterance of words comes about by the movement of the tongue. That tongue has been fashioned by the two hands of Prajāpati, with their ten fingers. O worshipper, with those hands of Prajāpati, which are causes of health, we touch you so that you may be happy.

##### English translation
The tongue (being cleansed) by the ten-branched hands (of Prajapathi is) the forerunner of speach; with those (hands) the removers of disease we touch you.

## Sūkta 138 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तव त्य इति षडृचं दशमं सूक्तमुरुनाम्नः पुत्रस्यांगाख्यस्यार्षं जागतमैंद्रं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । तव त्ये षळंग औरवो जागतमिति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥
> आनुवादवु—तव तै ऎंब ई सूक्तवु हन्नॊंदनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि हत्तनॆय सूक्तवु.
> इदरल्लि आरु ऋक्कुगळिरुवुवु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ उरु ऎंब ऋषिय पुत्रनाद अंग ऎंबुवनु ऋषियु,
> इंद्रनु देवतॆयु; जगती छंदस्सु. अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि-तव तै षळंग औरवो जागतं ऎंदु
> हेळिरुवुदु. विनियोगवन्नु हिंदॆये हेळलागिदॆ.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The tenth sūkta, तव त्य (*tava tya*), of six Ṛks. Its seer is Aṅga, son of Uru; the deity is Indra; the metre Jagatī. The Anukramaṇī says: तव त्ये षळंग औरवो जागतमिति (*tava tye ṣaḷaṃga auravo jāgatamiti*). The viniyoga has been stated already.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta तव त्य (*tava tya*) is the tenth sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Its seer is Aṅga, son of the ṛṣi Uru; the deity is Indra; the metre is Jagatī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: *tava tye ṣaḷaṃga auravo jāgataṃ*. The viniyoga was stated earlier.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तव॒ त्य इं॑द्र स॒ख्येषु॒ वह्न॑य ऋ॒तं म॑न्वा॒ना व्य॑दर्दिरुर्व॒लं ।  
> यत्रा॑ दश॒स्यन्नु॒षसो॑ रि॒णन्न॒पः कुत्सा॑य॒ मन्म॑न्न॒ह्य॑श्च  ॒॑
> दंसयः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तव । त्ये । इंद्र । सख्येषु । वह्नयः । ऋतं । मन्वाना । वि । अदर्दिरुः । वलं ।  
> यत्र । दशस्यन् । उषसः । रिणन् । अपः । कुत्साय । मन्मन् । अह्यः । च । दंसयः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र तव सख्येषु सखित्वेषु सत्तु त्ये ते प्रसिद्धा वह्नयो वोढारो
> हविषां स्तुतीनां वा अत एवर्तं यज्ञं मन्वाना अवबुध्यमाना अंगिरसो वलं
> गवामपहर्तारमेतत्संज्ञकमसुरं व्यवर्दिरुः । अत्यर्थं व्यदारयन् ॥ दृ विदारणे । अस्माद्यज् लुगांताल्लुज् । सिजभ्यस्तेति झॆर्जुः । जुसि चेति गुणः । व्यत्ययेनेत्वं ॥ आपि च यत्र यस्मिन्काले मन्मन् मन्मनि स्तोत्रे सति कुत्साय महर्षय
> उषस उषःकालान्वृत्तेणावृतत्वात्तूर्वमसत्प्रायांस्तदपनोदनेन दशस्यन्वयच्छन्
> तथापो वृत्रेणावृतान्युदकानि च रिणंस्तस्मान्निर्गमयन्वर्तसे ॥ री गतिरेषणयोः ।
> क्रैयादिकः । प्वादीनां ह्रस्वत्वं ॥ तदानीमहोऽहेर्वृत्रस्य च दंसयः कर्माणि
> वितथान्यासन्नित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, while those well-known bearers (वह्नयः (*vahnayaḥ*)) of oblations or of praises were in your friendship, therefore, understanding the sacrifice (ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)), the Aṅgirases tore asunder Vala, the demon of that name who carried off the cows. The verb दृ (*dṛ*) means splitting. And further, at the time when, praise (मन्मन् (*manman*)) being offered, you were giving (दशस्यन् (*daśasyan*)) to the great seer Kutsa the dawns, which, being covered by darkness, had been almost non-existent, by removing that darkness, and were releasing (रिणन् (*riṇan*)) the waters covered by Vṛtra, taking them out from it: री (*rī*) is a root of going and moving, of the kryādi class. Then the deeds (दंसयः (*daṃsayaḥ*)) of Ahi, Vṛtra, were rendered vain; that is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- तव (*tava*)—your
- सख्येषु (*sakhyeṣu*)—friendship being present
- त्ये (*tye*)—those well-known
- वह्नयः (*vahnayaḥ*)—bearers of praise or oblation, who offer it to the gods
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—the order of performing the sacrifice
- मन्वानाः (*manvānāḥ*)—the Aṅgirasa seers who knew it
- वलं (*valaṃ*)—the king Vala (who had carried off the gods' cows)
- वि अदर्दिराः (*vi adardirāḥ*)—tore apart (and)
- यत्र (*yatra*)—when
- मन्मन् (*manman*)—you are praised, then (you)
- कुत्साय (*kutsāya*)—for the great seer Kutsa
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—the dawns (light)
- दशस्यन् (*daśasyan*)—producing
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters covered by Vṛtra
- रिणन् (*riṇan*)—freed from there and sent out
- अह्यः च (*ahyaḥ ca*)—and of Ahi
- दंसयः (*daṃsayaḥ*)—the deeds that obstruct the waters were also in vain

### Printed p. 891

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, while your friendship was there, those Aṅgirasa seers, who offer praises and oblations to the gods and know the performance of sacrifice, tore apart the asura Vala who had carried off the gods' cows. When Kutsa praised you, you made the dawns for him, that is, made light, and freed the waters that were covered by Vṛtra, sending them out from there; and all the deeds of the demon Vṛtra that obstruct the waters were rendered vain.

##### English translation
The bearers of oblations (the Angirasas), Indra honouring the sacrifice, have through your friendship torn Vala to pieces, when praise (being offered) desiring to give the dawns to Kutsa 'you were engaged in) freeing the waters, and Ahi's expolits (were foiled).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the word दंसयः (*daṃsayaḥ*) in this Ṛk, Yāska says: दंसयः कर्माणि दंसयंत एतानि । कुत्साय मन्मन्नह्यश्च दंसयः । इत्यपि निगमो भवति । (*daṃsayaḥ karmāṇi daṃsayaṃta etāni | kutsāya manmannahyaśca daṃsayaḥ | ityapi nigamo bhavati |*) (Ni. 4-25). दंसयः (*daṃsayaḥ*) means works; because these are done and finished, works are called दंसयः (*daṃsayaḥ*). Ordinarily the works done by servants (śūdras, farmers, cultivators) are called दंसयः (*daṃsayaḥ*).
The explanation Sāyaṇa gives of this Ṛk differs from that of Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta. For the word वोढारः (*voḍhāraḥ*) Sāyaṇa takes the Aṅgirasa seers who bear oblation or praise. Durgācārya takes this word to mean Indra's horses that carry Indra's chariot, and explains the Ṛk accordingly: O Indra, the horses that carry you, for your pleasure, split the cloud (Vala) to release the water that is in the clouds, and you, for the farmer (cultivator)

### Printed p. 892
…who were Aṅgiras sages bearing the oblation or the praise. Durgācārya, however, explains this word as Indra's horses that draw Indra's chariot, and has explained the Ṛk accordingly: "O Indra, the horses that bear you split open the cloud (Vala) to release the waters held in the clouds, for your pleasure. And you, to make the farmer's (the cultivator's) tasks easy, brought about the dawn-time, split the cloud that had held back the waters necessary for farming, and sent them out hither. The waters of the cloud, sent out by the clouds, fell upon the earth in the form of rain and helped the farmer in his farming." This is the main purport.

> अवा॑सृजः प्र॒स्वः॑ श्वं॒चयो॑ गि॒रीनुदा॑ज उ॒स्रा अपि॑बो॒ मधु॑  ॒

> अवर्धयः। वनिनः । अस्य । दंससा । शुशोच । सूर्यः । ऋतजातया । गिरा ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र प्रस्वः । प्रसूतिर्जन्म । तद्धेतुभूता अपोऽवासृजः । आवारकान्मेघादधः पातितवानसि । तथा गिरीन्पर्वतान्नलेन गोमतो बिलस्य विधानाय निहिताइंचयः । अभैत्सीरित्यर्थः ॥ श्वचि गत् । अस्माण्णंताल्लजि बहुलं छंदस्यमाज्योगेऽपीत्यडभावः । समानवाक्यॆ निघातयुष्मदस्मदादेशा वक्तव्याः। सा. ८-१ १८-५।
> इति वचनात्पूर्वपदस्यासमानवाक्यगतत्वेनास्य तिज्ञतिज इति निघाताभावः ॥ तथा
> वलासुरेण बिले निहिता उस्रा गाः पर्वतभेदानानंतरमुदाजः । उदगमयः । ततः
> पयोदध्याज्यादिकं प्रियमनुकूलं मधु मधुरं हविरपिबः । पीतवानसि । यद्वा !
> श्रयणसाधनासु तासु गोष्टागतासु यजमानैः प्रियमभीष्टं मधु सोमात्मकमपिबः । पिबसि । तथा वनिनो वनसंबद्धान्वृक्षान् । यद्वा । वनमित्युदकनाम । तद्युक्तान्समुद्रान् अवर्धयः । वृष्टिप्रदानेन वर्धयसि । ऋजताजया । ऋतं यज्ञं ।
> तदर्थं जातं जन्म यस्याः तया गिरा वेदात्मिकया वाचा स्सूयमानस्यास्येंद्रस्य
> दंससा कर्मणावृण्वतो वृत्रादेरपि नोदनात्मकेन सूर्यः शुशोच । नभसि

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, you sent down the waters, which are the cause of birth (प्रसूतिर्जन्म (*prasūtirjanma*)), from the covering cloud, causing them to fall. Likewise you split the mountains (गिरीन् (*girīn*)), which had been set to make the opening of the cave holding the cows" — this is the meaning of श्वंचयः (*śvaṃcayaḥ*) (the sense: "you split"). After the mountains were broken you led out (उदाजः (*udājaḥ*), "made to go up") the cows (उस्राः (*usrāḥ*)) that the Asura Vala had hidden in the cave. Then you drank the dear, favourable, sweet oblation: milk, curds, ghee and the like. Or else: when those cows, which are the means of nourishment, had come to the cow-pen, you drink the dear, desired honey of the nature of Soma offered by the sacrificers. Likewise you made grow the trees connected with the forest (वनिनः (*vaninaḥ*)); or else, since *vanaṃ* is a name for water, the oceans possessing it, by giving rain. ऋतजातया गिरा (*ṛtajātayā girā*): ṛta is the sacrifice; the speech whose birth is for its sake, the speech of the Veda; by the deed of this Indra, who is praised with it, a deed that even drives away such as Vṛtra who ward him off (वृण्वतो वृत्रादेरपि (*vṛṇvato vṛtrāderapi*)), the sun shone, blazed forth in the sky.

> वाचा प्रदीप्यत इत्यर्थः ऋग्भिः पूर्वाह्ने दिवि देव ईयत इत्यादिकं तैत्तिरीयकमत्रानुसंधेयं । तै. ब्रा. ३-१२-९-१ ॥ शुशोचेत्यस्य पदात्परत्वेऽपि पादादित्वादपादादाविति पर्युदासस्यानुवृत्तेर्निघाताभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Or else, "by speech born of the ṛta" is an epithet of the sun alone: he is lit up by speech having the form of the triple Veda. The Taittirīya passage beginning ऋग्भिः पूर्वाह्ने दिवि देव ईयत (*ṛgbhiḥ pūrvāhne divi deva īyata*) and so on is to be recalled here (Tai. Brā. 3-12-9-1).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रस्वः (*prasvaḥ*)—(O Indra) the waters gathered in the clouds
- अवासृजः (*avāsṛjaḥ*)—you have made fall downward upon the earth
- गिरीन् (*girīn*)—the mountains that hid the cows
- श्वंचयः (*śvaṃcayaḥ*)—you approached (after the splitting of the mountains)
- उस्राः (*usrāḥ*)—the cows hidden by Vala
- उदाजः (*udājaḥ*)—released and drove out of the cave (afterwards)
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—beneficial
- मधु (*madhu*)—the sweet oblation
- अपिबः (*apibaḥ*)—you drank
- वनिनः (*vaninaḥ*)—the trees, or the oceans full of water
- अवर्धयः (*avardhayaḥ*)—you have made to grow by giving rain
- ऋतजातया (*ṛtajātayā*)—composed for the sacrifice
- गिरा (*girā*)—praised by the Vedic speech
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra
- दसंसा (*dasaṃsā*)—by the deed of slaying Vṛtra and others
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—the sun
- शुशोच (*śuśoca*)—shone, blazing in the sky; or else:
- [ऋतजातया (*ṛtajātayā*)—created for the sacrifice by the Supreme Self
- गिरा (*girā*)—by the speech of praise consisting of Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—the sun
- शुशोच (*śuśoca*)—shone in the sky.]

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you made the waters gathered in the clouds fall on the earth in the form of rain. You approached the mountains in which Vala had hidden the cows of the gods, released the cows that were in them and drove them out. Afterwards you drank the sweet oblation offered to you in the sacrifice. By giving rain you made flourish the trees that are in the forest, or the oceans full of water. By your deed of slaying Vṛtra and the like — you who are praised by the Vedic speech created for the sacrifice by the Supreme Lord — or by the Vedic speech consisting of Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman, the sun blazed forth in the sky.

##### English translation
You has sent forth the generative (waters), you have cleft the mountains you have fetched forth the cows, you have quaffed the delicacies Soma, you have caused the trees of the forest to grow; through his expolits by means of the voice produced for the sacrifice the sun has shone bright.

### Printed p. 894

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Regarding the statement that the sun shines in the sky through speech in the form of the Veda, the commentator has cited passages of the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa:
ऋचां प्राची महती दिगुच्यते । (*ṛcāṃ prācī mahatī digucyate |*) (Tai. Brā. 3-12-9-1).
The east is dear to the deities presiding over the Ṛgveda; likewise the south to the deities presiding over the Yajus, the west to the deities presiding over the Atharvaveda, and the north to the deities presiding over the Sāmaveda.
ऋग्भिः पूर्वाह्ने दिवि देव ईयते । यजुर्वेदे तिष्ठति मध्यॆ अह्नः । सामवेदेनास्तमये महीयते । वेद्यरशून्यस्त्रिभिरीति सूर्यः ॥ (*ṛgbhiḥ pūrvāhne divi deva īyate | yajurvede tiṣṭhati madhyè ahnaḥ | sāmavedenāstamaye mahīyate | vedyaraśūnyastribhirīti sūryaḥ ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 3-12-9-1).
The sun, shining in the sky, moves in the forenoon with the deities presiding over the Ṛk; at midday he is near the deities presiding over the Yajus; at sunset he is worshipped by the deity presiding over the Sāmaveda. Thus the sun, joined with the three Vedas, moves at all times.
ऋग्भो जाताग्ं सर्वशो मूर्तिमाहुः । सर्वा गतिर्याजुषी हैव शश्वत् ॥ सर्वं तेजः सामरूप्यग्ं ह शश्वत् । सर्वग्ं हेदं ब्रह्मणा हैव सृष्टं ॥ (*ṛgbho jātāgṃ sarvaśo mūrtimāhuḥ | sarvā gatiryājuṣī haiva śaśvat ‖ sarvaṃ tejaḥ sāmarūpyagṃ ha śaśvat | sarvagṃ hedaṃ brahmaṇā haiva sṛṣṭaṃ ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 3-12-9-1, 2).
Whatever forms the Āditya or other deities have, the wise say that all of them are produced from the Ṛk mantras. The movements and the like of the deities are obtained from the Yajus mantras. The splendour that is in the deities is established by the power of the Sāmaveda. Thus everything has been created by Brahman alone. And so on.

> दृढानि स्थिराणि पुराणि बलानि वर्जिश्वना राजर्षिणा चक्रवान् सख्यं कुर्वन्निंद्रो
> व्यास्यत् । व्यक्षिपत् । विविधमाक्षिप्तवान् । व्यनीनशदित्यर्थः ॥ असु क्षेपणे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the middle of the heavenly world the sun, Āditya, unyoked his chariot for setting out (व्यमुचत् (*vyamucat*), "released"). When, it is asked? When the knowing Indra (आर्यः (*āryaḥ*)) learns (विदत् (*vidat*)) the requital, the counter-action (प्रतिमानं (*pratimānaṃ*)), against the Dāsa, the destroyer, Vṛtra and the like; he finds or obtains it.**NOTE**. And the Asura is māyin, possessed of illusion. Indra, making friendship with the royal sage Ṛjiśvan (printed वर्जिश्वना (*varjiśvanā*), चक्रवान् (*cakravān*)), cast down (व्यास्यत् (*vyāsyat*)) — scattered, destroyed — the firm, stable strongholds and forces of the Asura named Pipru. The verb is from the root meaning "to throw".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आर्यः (*āryaḥ*)—the knowing Indra
- दासाय (*dāsāya*)—in regard to the destroying enemy, Vṛtra and the like
- प्रतिमानं (*pratimānaṃ*)—retaliation
- विदत् (*vidat*)—when he knew it should be done (resolved)
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heavenly world (the sky)
- मध्यॆ (*madhyè*)—in the middle
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—Āditya
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—his chariot (unyoking its horses)
- वि अमुंचत् (*vi amuṃcat*)—left and stopped (and)
- मायिनः (*māyinaḥ*)—of the illusionist
- पिप्रोः (*piproḥ*)—named Pipru
- असुरस्य (*asurasya*)—of the Asura
- दृळ्हानि (*dṛḷhāni*)—the firm towns or armies
- ऋजिश्वना (*ṛjiśvanā*)—with the royal sage named Ṛjiśvan
- चकृवान् (*cakṛvān*)—having made friendship
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- वि अस्यत् (*vi asyat*)—destroyed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the knowing Indra resolved to requite his enemies, Vṛtra and others, Āditya in the middle of the sky unyoked the horses of his chariot and halted it. Indra, making friendship with the royal sage Ṛjiśvan, destroyed the towns, furnished with strong forts, of the illusionist Asura named Pipru, or his strong armies.

> मा॒सेव॒ सूर्यो॒ वसु॒ पुर्य॒मा द॑दे गृणा॒नः शत्रू॑रशृणाद्वि॒रुक्त॑ता ॥ ४ ॥

> मासाइव । सूर्यः । वसु । पुर्यं । आ । ददे । गृणानः । शत्रून् । अशृणात् ।  
> विरुक्तता ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धृषितः शत्रूणां धर्षयिता प्रगल्भ इंद्रोऽनाधृष्टानीतः पूर्वं शत्रुभिरप्रधृष्टान्यबाधितान्यसुरबलानि व्यास्यत् । व्याक्षिप्तवान् । तथायास्योऽयासनीयश्चालयितुमशक्यः । यद्वा । आयास्योऽंगिराः । स्तोतृवाचिना शब्देन स्तुत्यो
> लक्ष्यते । अयास्येनर्षिणा स्तुत्य इंद्रो निधीनसुरैर्निहितान्थनसमूहान् यद्वा
> निधातृन्नि तरां बलानां धारयित्कनदेवान्देवविरोधिनोऽसुरानमृणत् । अहिंसीत्॥
> मृण हिंसायां । तौदादिकः ॥ अपि च सूर्यो मासेव मासेनेव ॥ पवन्नित्यादिना
> मासशब्दस्य मास्भावः । स यथा मासविशेषेण भौमान्रसानादत्ते तथा पुर्यमसुराणां पुरि भवं ॥ भवे छंदसीति यत् ! हलि चेति दीर्घस्य न भकुर्भुरां ।
> पा. ८-२-७९ । इति प्रतिषेधः । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ ईदृशं वसु धनमाददे । आदत्ते स्म ॥ आजो दोऽनास्यविहरण इत्यात्मनेपदं ॥ तथा गृणानः स्तोतृभिः स्तूयमानः सन् ॥ व्यत्ययेन कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः ॥ शत्रूञ्चितयित्कनसुरान्विरुक्तता विरोचमानेन वज्रेणाशृणात् । अहिंसीत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, the bold (धृषितः (*dhṛṣitaḥ*)), the assailer of enemies, cast down (व्यास्यत् (*vyāsyat*)) the forces of the Asuras that till then had been unassailed (अनाधृष्टानि (*anādhṛṣṭāni*)), unhindered by enemies. Likewise he is अयास्यः (*ayāsyaḥ*), one who cannot be moved. Or else, अयास्यः (*ayāsyaḥ*) is Aṅgiras: by a word denoting the praiser, the one praised is indicated; Indra, praised by the sage Ayāsya, struck down the Asuras — the treasures (निधीन् (*nidhīn*)) laid up by them, the hoards of wealth; or else the "holders" who firmly hold the forces — the god-opposing (अदेवान् (*adevān*)) Asuras: अमृणत् (*amṛṇat*), he injured them. Further, "like the sun with the month" (मासेव (*māseva*)): as the sun by the course of the month draws earthly juices, so he took पुर्यं (*puryaṃ*), what is in the cities of the Asuras — wealth of such a kind (वसु (*vasu*)); he took it (आददे (*ādade*)). Likewise, being praised (गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)) by the praisers, he destroyed the enemies, the Asuras, with the shining (विरुक्तता (*viruktatā*)) thunderbolt (अशृणात् (*aśṛṇāt*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धृषितः (*dhṛṣitaḥ*)—Indra, the strong, who crushes enemies
- अनाधृष्टानि (*anādhṛṣṭāni*)—the enemy armies not defeated until now
- वि आस्यत् (*vi āsyat*)—destroyed (likewise)
- अयास्यः (*ayāsyaḥ*)—Indra, who is unable to be shaken, or Indra praised by the sage Aṅgiras
- निधीन् (*nidhīn*)—the wealth of the Asuras, or the exceedingly powerful
- अदेवान् (*adevān*)—Asuras who are enemies of the gods
- अमृणत् (*amṛṇat*)—injured (killed)
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—the sun
- मासेव (*māseva*)—as in the summer month he draws and absorbs the juices of the earth, so Indra
- पुर्यं (*puryaṃ*)—that was in the cities of the Asuras
- वसु (*vasu*)—the wealth
- आ ददे स्म (*ā dade sma*)—plundered
- गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)—being praised by the praisers
- शत्रून् (*śatrūn*)—the Asuras who were enemies
- विरुक्मता (*virukmatā*)—with his shining thunderbolt
- अश्वणात् (*aśvaṇāt*)—killed, injuring them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the heroic crusher of enemies, defeated and destroyed the enemy armies that had been defeated by no one till then. Indra, whom no one could shake, seized and carried off the wealth of the Asuras. He injured and killed the Asuras who were enemies of the gods. As the sun in summer draws and absorbs the juices, the waters, lying on the earth, so Indra plundered the wealth that was in the enemy cities. Indra, praised by the praisers, injured the enemy Asuras with his thunderbolt gleaming brightly.

##### English translation
Bold (Indra) has annihilated the (hitherto) unbaffled (hosts of the Asura), the objeet of Ayasya's adoration has despoiled the impious of their treasurers; the sun as if with the (aid of the) moon has seized upon the wealth of the cities (of the Asuras), glorified (by his worshippers,) he has demolished the foe with his blaziug (thunderbolt).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विभ्वा विभुना व्याप्तेन विभिंदता विदारयता एवंविधेनापि परकीयबलेनायुद्धसेनोऽप्रहृतसेनः । यद्वा । विभ्वा विभुव्याप्तो विभिंदता शत्रुबलानि विदारयता वज्रेण । वृत्रहा वृत्रं हतवान् एवंविधॆ इंद्रो दाशत् । दाशति । स्तोतृभ्यो

> त्यागे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

विभ्वा (*vibhvā*) means "by the pervading" and विभिंदता (*vibhiṃdatā*) "by the rending". Even against an enemy force of such a kind, Indra's army is अयुद्धसेनः (*ayuddhasenaḥ*), one whose army is not struck. Alternatively, विभ्वा (*vibhvā*) is the pervading thunderbolt and विभिंदता (*vibhiṃdatā*) the thunderbolt that splits the enemy hosts. Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, दाशत् (*dāśat*): he gives wealth to his praisers (root दाश्य (*dāśya*), to give). तुज्यानि (*tujyāni*) are the hostile enemy forces rushing forward, and तेजते (*tejate*) means he makes them slight and reduces them (root तिज (*tija*), to sharpen). Or else: he sharpens, makes keen, the weapons directed against the enemies. All the enemy host was afraid of the thunderbolt of such an Indra, which injures on every side. When the Asuras had thus been cast down by Indra, शुंध्यूः (*śuṃdhyūḥ*), the purifier, the Sun, set out to illuminate the world. Uṣas, the deity of dawn, also left her own cart (अनः (*anaḥ*)), her chariot; she gave it up in order to depart.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विभ्वा (*vibhvā*)—all-pervading
- विभिंदता (*vibhiṃdatā*)—with the thunderbolt that cleaves the enemy armies
- अयुद्धसेनः (*ayuddhasenaḥ*)—possessing an irresistible force
- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—the slayer of Vṛtra, Indra
- दाशत् (*dāśat*)—gives wealth to the praising people
- तुज्यानि (*tujyāni*)—the enemy armies rushing forward with zeal
- तेजते (*tejate*)—makes them dwindle; or [तुज्यानि (*tujyāni*)—his weapons to be used against enemies; तेजते (*tejate*)—he sharpens them]
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of such an Indra
- अभिश्नथः (*abhiśnathaḥ*)—enemy-destroying
- वज्रात् (*vajrāt*)—from the thunderbolt
- अबिभेत् (*abibhet*)—caused fear to the enemies (afterwards)
- शुंध्यूः (*śuṃdhyūḥ*)—the Āditya (Sun) who purifies everything with his light
- प्र अक्रामत् (*pra akrāmat*)—began to shine
- उषाः (*uṣāḥ*)—the deity Uṣas also
- अनः (*anaḥ*)—her cart, that is, her chariot
- अजहात् (*ajahāt*)—abandoned and departed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, of irresistible prowess and slayer of Vṛtra, with his all-pervading thunderbolt that can split the enemy armies, kills and thins the enemy armies that rush upon him with zeal,

### Printed p. 899
or he sharpens his weapons for use against the enemies, and gives wealth to the people who praise him. With his enemy-destroying thunderbolt he strikes fear into the enemies. After Indra had thus destroyed the enemies, the goddess Uṣas abandoned her chariot and departed; that is, the time of dawn passed, and the Sun, the purifier, rose and lit the whole world with his radiance.

##### English translation
(Indra), leading an irresistible army, slaying Vritra with the perva-
ding piercing (bolt), gives (wealth to his worshippers), thins the (hosts of the
Asuras) which have to be attacked ; (the whole host of the enemy) was afraid
of Indra's wide-destroying thunderbolt. the purifying (Sun) came forth,
Ushas left her waggon.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ता त्या ते॒ श्रुत्या॑नि॒ केव॑ला॒ यदेक॒ एक॒मकृ॑णोरय॒ज्ञं ।

> पिता ॥ ६ ॥

> मासां । विधानं । अदधाः । अधि । द्यवि । त्वया । विभिन्नं । भरति । प्रधिं । पिशा ॥६॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्या तानि ते तव त्वदीयानि वीर्यकर्माण्येतैतान्येव केवला
> केवलानि श्रुत्यानि शोतव्यानि स्तुत्यर्हाणि । नान्यदीयानि । कानि पुनस्तानि । एकोऽसहायस्त्वमेकं प्रधानभूतमयज्ञं यज्ञरहितमसुरमकृणोः अहिंसीरिति यदेशदेकं कर्म ॥ कृवि हिंसाकरणयोः । अत्र हिंसार्थः । इदित्वान्नुम् । धिन्विकृण्वोरच्चेत्युप्रत्ययोऽकारांतादेशश्च । तस्य लोपे सति स्थानिवद्भावाल्लघपधगुणाभावः ॥
> तथा मासां मासानां ॥ पद्दन्नित्यादिना मासशब्दस्य मास्भावः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, only these deeds of valour of yours are श्रुत्यानि (*śrutyāni*), worthy to be heard and praised; they are not another's. Which are they? The one deed: that you, alone and unaided, अकृणोः (*akṛṇoḥ*), injured the one chief Asura, who was without sacrifice (अयज्ञं (*ayajñaṃ*)). The root is कृवि (*kṛvi*), in the sense of injuring here. Next: मासां (*māsāṃ*) is "of the months", the word मास (*māsa*) becoming मास् (*mās*) by the rule beginning पद्दन् (*paddan*), and the case-ending taking the udātta by the rule beginning *ūḍidaṃ* (continued on the next page).

### Printed p. 900

> विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥ मासानां विधानं विधातारं कर्तारं सूर्यमधि द्यवि द्युलोक
> उपर्यदधाः । आधारयः ॥ विपूर्वाद्दधातेः कृत्यल्युटो बहुलमिति कर्तरि ल्युट् ॥
> इदमपरं कर्म। तथा पिता पालको द्युलोको विभिन्नं विदारितं वृत्राद्विभक्तं प्रधिं
> रथचक्रस्य पार्श्वं । पार्श्वफलके प्रधी इत्युच्येते । ईदृशं सूर्यरथसंबंधिनं
> प्रधिमन्वैर्धारयितुमशक्त्यं त्वय्येव भरति । धारयति । इदमपरं कर्म । एतत्प्रभृतीनि
> त्वया कृतानि कर्माणि परेषामसाधारणानि सर्वदाम्ना तव्यानीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

You placed the maker of the months, the Sun, above in the heaven-world (अधि द्यवि (*adhi dyavi*)); अदधाः (*adadhāḥ*) means "you set up". This is another deed. Likewise पिता (*pitā*), the protector, the heaven-world, bears in you (त्वय्येव भरति (*tvayyeva bharati*)) the प्रधि (*pradhi*), the rim of the chariot wheel of the Sun, which had been split and separated from Vṛtra; the felly of a wheel is called प्रधि (*pradhi*). Others are unable to support this rim belonging to the Sun's chariot. This too is a deed. The sense: the deeds done by you, beginning with these, are not shared by others and are to be extolled always.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) त्या (*tyā*)—famous
- ते (*te*)—your
- एता (*etā*)—deeds of daring
- केवला (*kevalā*)—chiefly (impossible for others to do)
- श्रुत्यानि (*śrutyāni*)—those that deserve to be praised
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—you, the valiant one without helper
- एकं (*ekaṃ*)—the chief
- अयज्ञं (*ayajñaṃ*)—the Asura who does not perform sacrifice
- अकृणोः (*akṛṇoḥ*)—that you injured and killed; that very deed is worthy of praise
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever there is
- मासां (*māsāṃ*)—of the divisions of time such as months
- विधानं (*vidhānaṃ*)—the maker, the Sun
- अधि द्यवि (*adhi dyavi*)—in the upper part of heaven
- अदधाः (*adadhāḥ*)—you have established
- पिता (*pitā*)—the heaven-world that protects all
- विभिन्नं (*vibhinnaṃ*)—split by Vṛtra
- प्रधिं (*pradhiṃ*)—the rim of the Sun's chariot wheel
- त्वया (*tvayā*)—with your help
- भरति (*bharati*)—bears

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, these famous deeds of daring of yours no one else can do; you alone can. Such acts are worthy of praise. The deed of killing, alone and without the help of others, the Asuras who were hostile to sacrifice is likewise praiseworthy. You have established the Sun, the maker of the divisions of time such as months, in the upper part of the heaven-world. The heaven-world, which protects all by giving rain and the like, holds up with your help alone the rim of the Sun's chariot wheel, split by Vṛtra.

##### English translation
These wondrous exploits are yours alone, in that you unaided has
injured the chief neglector of sacrifice; you have placed in the sky the regu-
lator of the months, through your aid the paternal (heaven) upholds the
circumference of the wheel (of the Sun' s car) which had been shattered
(by Vritra).

## Sūkta 139 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूर्यरश्मिरिति षडृचमेकादशं सूक्तं त्रैष्टुभं । विश्वावसुर्नाम गंधर्व
> ऋषिः । स च पूर्वेण तृचेन सवितारं स्तुतवान् उत्तरेण स्वात्मानं । अतः प्रथमतृचस्य सविता देवता द्वितीयस्य गंधर्वः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । सूर्यरश्मिर्देवगंधर्वो विश्वावसुरात्मानमस्तौत्पूर्वार्धे सवितारमिति । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The eleventh sūkta, beginning सूर्यरश्मिः (*sūryaraśmiḥ*), has six Ṛks and is in the Triṣṭubh metre. The seer is the Gandharva named Viśvāvasu. With the first triplet he praised Savitṛ, and with the latter one himself. Hence the deity of the first triplet is Savitṛ, and of the second the Gandharva. So the Anukramaṇī says: सूर्यरश्मिर्देवगंधर्वो विश्वावसुरात्मानमस्तौत्पूर्वार्धे सवितारमिति । (*sūryaraśmirdevagaṃdharvo viśvāvasurātmānamastautpūrvārdhe savitāramiti |*). The application (viniyoga) has already been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, "सूर्यरश्मि (*sūryaraśmi*)", is the eleventh sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka. It contains six Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is the Gandharva named Viśvāvasu. With the first three Ṛks of this sūkta that Gandharva praised the deity Savitṛ, and with the last three Ṛks he praised himself. Therefore the deity of the first three Ṛks is Savitṛ and of the last three the Gandharva; the metre is Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says: सूर्यरश्निर्देवगंधर्वो विश्वासुरात्मानमस्तौत् पूर्वार्धे सवितारं (*sūryaraśnirdevagaṃdharvo viśvāsurātmānamastaut pūrvārdhe savitāraṃ*). The application has been stated before.

Sūkta 139. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 139; Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 7; Varga 27. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6. Seer: Viśvāvasu, the divine Gandharva. Deity: 1–3 Savitṛ; 4–6 Viśvāvasu. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तस्य॑ पू॒षा प्र॑स॒वेया॑ति वि॒द्वान्सं॒पश्य॒न्विश्वा॒ भुव॑नानि गो॒पाः॥

### Printed p. 902

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूर्यरश्मिः । उषसः प्रादुर्भानानंतरं सूर्यस्योदयात्पूर्वं यः
> कालस्तस्य कालस्याभिमानी देवः सवितेत्युच्यते ! सूर्यरश्मिः सूर्यस्य सर्वस्य
> प्रेरकस्यादित्यस्य रश्मिरेव रश्मियस्य स तथोक्तः हरिकेशः हरयो हरणशीला
> हरितवर्णा वा केशाः केशस्थानीयाः प्रकाशमाना वा दीप्तयो यस्य ईदृशः सविता
> सर्वस्य प्रेरको देवः पुरस्तात्पूर्वस्यां दिश्यजस्रमनवरतं ज्योतिस्तेज उदयान् ।
> उद्याति । उद्दमयति ॥ यातेरंतर्भावितण्यर्थाच्छंदसो लज् । व्यत्ययेन बहुवचनं । संहितायां दीर्घादटि समानपाद इति नकारस्य रुत्वं । आतोऽट नित्यमिति
> सानुनासिक आकारः॥ तस्य सवितुः प्रसने प्रेरणेऽनुज्ञायां सत्यां विद्वाञ्ज्ञानन्नोपा
> गोपायिता रक्षिता पूषा पोषको देव आदित्यो याति । नभसि गच्छति । किं कुर्वन्।
> विश्वा विश्वानि सर्वाणि भुवनानि भूतजातानि संपश्यन् । सम्यक् प्रकाशयन् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सूर्यरश्मिः (*sūryaraśmiḥ*): the deity who presides over the time that lies after the appearance of Uṣas and before the rising of the Sun is called Savitṛ. He is called सूर्यरश्मिः (*sūryaraśmiḥ*) because the rays of the Sun, the impeller of all, are his own rays. हरिकेशः (*harikeśaḥ*): he whose "hairs", that is, shining radiances like hairs, are हरि (*hari*), either capturing or tawny. Such a Savitṛ, the impelling deity of all, उदयान् (*udayān*) sends up unceasingly ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*), light, in the eastern quarter (the form is from या (*yā*) with the causative sense implied, with change of number). At the impulsion, that is, the permission, of that Savitṛ, Pūṣan, the nourishing deity, the Āditya, who is विद्वान् (*vidvān*) (knowing) and गोपाः (*gopāḥ*) (protector), moves in the sky, looking upon all beings, that is, illuminating them well.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूर्यरश्मि (*sūryaraśmi*)—he who is endowed with the rays of the Sun
- हरिकेशः (*harikeśaḥ*)—he who has radiances like tawny hair
- सविता (*savitā*)—the god Savitṛ
- पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*)—in the eastern quarter
- अजस्रं (*ajasraṃ*)—at all times, that is, every morning
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—his radiance
- उदयान् (*udayān*)—sends forth
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of that god Savitṛ
- प्रसवे (*prasave*)—by the impulsion
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—the one who knows everything
- गोपाः (*gopāḥ*)—the protector
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the Āditya who nourishes all
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- भुवनानि (*bhuvanāni*)—creatures or worlds
- संपश्यन् (*saṃpaśyan*)—looking at (pervading with rays)
- याति (*yāti*)—travels in the sky

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The god Savitṛ, accompanied by the rays of the Sun and shining with his tawny (golden) radiance like hair, rises every day in the east after the time of dawn and spreads his light. By the impulsion of this very Savitṛ, the Āditya, who knows all and nourishes all, moves in the sky looking at all the worlds and the creatures in them.

##### English translation
Savitri, the solar-rayed, the yellow-haired, sent up the undying light
from the east; at his command the sage Pushan, the preserver, follows,
looking upon all creatures.

### Printed p. 903

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The difference between Savitṛ and Sūrya or Āditya is this: उषसः प्रादुर्भावानंतरं सूर्यस्योदयात्पूर्वं यः कालः तस्याभिमानी देवः सवितेत्युच्यते (*uṣasaḥ prādurbhāvānaṃtaraṃ sūryasyodayātpūrvaṃ yaḥ kālaḥ tasyābhimānī devaḥ savitetyucyate*). When night has passed and the time of dawn has come, the Sun that is just then rising at the end of that dawn is called Savitṛ. Afterwards, when he has risen fully and shines in the sky, he is called Sūrya or Āditya. Because at the beginning of sunrise the rays have a slight tinge of red and yellow, Savitṛ is here described as हरिकेशः (*harikeśaḥ*), one with golden hair. After the end of night dawn appears; the darkness of night departs and it becomes light. But the Sun has not yet risen. This time, filled only with light without the rays of the Sun, is called the time of dawn. After the dawn, golden rays are seen little by little in the east. The Sun, rising slowly in this way, is called Savitṛ only at that time; after he has fully risen he is spoken of as Sūrya. The seer Hiraṇyastūpa described the same matter, in order, as follows:

ह्वयाम्यग्निं प्रथमं स्वस्तये ह्वयामि मित्रावरुणाविहावसे । ह्वयामि रात्रीं जगतो निवेशनीं ह्वयामि देवं सवितारमूतये ॥ (*hvayāmyagniṃ prathamaṃ svastaye hvayāmi mitrāvaruṇāvihāvase | hvayāmi rātrīṃ jagato niveśanīṃ hvayāmi devaṃ savitāramūtaye ‖*)
आ कृष्णेन रजसा वर्तमानो निवेशयन्नमृतं मर्त्यं च । हिरण्ययेन सविता रथेना देवो याति भुवनानि पश्यन् ॥ (*ā kṛṣṇena rajasā vartamāno niveśayannamṛtaṃ martyaṃ ca | hiraṇyayena savitā rathenā devo yāti bhuvanāni paśyan ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-35-1, 2)

Here first the Agni that shines at night is praised; then Mitra and Varuṇa, the presiding deities of day and night; then Night; then the god Savitṛ, in order. It says that this god Savitṛ rises, dispels the darkness of night with his radiance, and comes, rising on a chariot shining with golden lustre (in the present Ṛk the rays of Savitṛ are described as golden hair), looking at all the worlds. The sequence is: first night; then, when night has passed, dawn; then the appearance of Savitṛ; then sunrise; then day and again night. Thus these divisions of time follow one another without interruption. Here the usage is to call the Sun that is just rising after dawn the god Savitṛ.
