> नृचक्षा नृन्मनुष्यान्पश्यन् यद्वा नृभिर्नेतृभी रश्मिभिः प्रकाशमान एष
> सविता दिवो म्युलोकस्य मध्य आस्ते । निषीदति । किं कुर्वन् । रोदसी द्यावापृथि
> व्यावंतरिक्षं चापप्रिवान् स्वतेजसापूरयन् ॥ प्रा पूरणे । अस्माच्छांदसो लिट् ।
> क्वसुश्चति तस्य क्वसुरादेशः । वस्वेकाजाद्भसामितीडागमः ॥ स देवो विश्वाचीर्विश्वमंचंतीः सर्वव्यापिनीः प्राच्यादिमहादिशोऽभि चष्टे । प्रकाशयति । तथा धृताचीर्घृतं दीप्तं रूपमंचंतीराग्नेय्यादिविदिशश्च प्रकाशयति ॥ अंचतेः क्विनंतादंचतेश्चोपसंख्यानमिति जीप् । ततो भसंज्ञायामच इत्याकारलॊपे चाविति
> दीर्घत्वं । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण जीप उदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते चाविति पूर्वस्याच उदात्तत्वं ।' तथा पूर्व० पूर्वभागं केतुं प्रज्ञापनीयपरं सृष्टभागं चांतरांतरालं चाभि चष्टे । प्रकाशयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

नृचक्षा (*nṛcakṣā*) means one who looks upon men; or else, one shining with the "men", that is the leading rays. This Savitṛ sits in the middle of the heavenly world. What is he doing? He fills (अपप्रिवान् (*apaprivān*)) heaven and earth and the firmament with his own radiance. The root is प्रा (*prā*) in the sense of filling. This god illumines all the all-pervading (विश्वाचीः (*viśvācīḥ*)) great quarters, the east and the rest. Likewise he illumines the धृताचीः (*dhṛtācīḥ*), the intermediate quarters such as the south-east, which bear a bright (घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*)) form. He also illumines the "front part", the केतुं (*ketuṃ*) (the distinguishing mark, to be made known), the "hind part" that is created, and the interval between.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नृचक्षाः (*nṛcakṣāḥ*)—beholding men, or shining with rays
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—this Savitṛ god
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the firmament
- अपप्रिवान् (*apaprivān*)—filling (lighting) with his radiance
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heavenly world (the sky)
- मध्यॆ (*madhyè*)—in the middle
- आस्ते (*āste*)—sits
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Savitṛ god
- विश्वाचीः (*viśvācīḥ*)—the quarters, east and the rest, pervading all regions
- अभि चष्टे (*abhi caṣṭe*)—illumines
- धृताचीः (*dhṛtācīḥ*)—he also lights the intermediate quarters, south-east and the rest
- केतुं (*ketuṃ*)—standing in the place of a banner
- पूर्वं (*pūrvaṃ*)—the front part (the region lying ahead)
- अपरं च (*aparaṃ ca*)—and the hind part
- अंतरा (*aṃtarā*)—the middle part between these also
- (अभि चष्टे (*abhi caṣṭe*)—illumines)

### Printed p. 905

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This god Savitṛ, shining with rays or watching men, sits in the middle of the sky, filling heaven, earth and the firmament with his radiance. That Savitṛ lights with his brightness all the quarters, east and the rest, the intermediate quarters such as the south-east, the front part, the hind part, and the region between them.

##### English translation
Beholding mankind he sits in the midst of the sky, filling (with light) the heaven and earth and the firmament; he illumines the all-pervading (quarters of space) the bright-pervading (intermediate points), and the mid-most, the foremost, and the hindmost mark.
#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> रा॒यो बु॒ध्नः सं॒गम॑नो॒ वसू॑नां॒ विश्वा॑ रू॒पाभि च॑ष्टे॒  ॑
> शचीभिः ।  
> दे॒व इ॑व सवि॒ता स॒त्यध॒र्मेंद्रो॒ न त॑स्थौ सम॒रे धना॑नां ॥३॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> रायः । बुध्नः । संगमनः । वसूनां । विश्वा । रूपा । अभि । चष्टे । शचीभिः ।  
> देवः इव । सविता । सत्यधर्मा । इंद्रः । न । तस्थौ । संअरे । धनानां ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रायो धनस्य बुध्नो बंधको मूलभूतो ना ॥ ऊडिदमित्यादिना रैशब्दाद्विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥ तथा वसूनां धनानां संगमनः संगमयिता प्रापयिता ईदृशः
> सविता शचीभिर्दिप्तिभिर्विश्वा रूपा सर्वाणि रूपाणि निरूपणीयानि पदार्थजातान्यभि
> चष्टे । अभिपश्यति । प्रकाशयति । अपि च देव इवायं सविता सावको देवः सत्यधर्मा
> सत्यमवितथं धर्म धारणं धारणहेतुभूतं कर्म वा यस्य तादृशो भवति
> तथेंद्रो नेंद्र इव धनानां समरे संग्रामे सम्यक्प्रापणे तस्थौ । अयं
> सवितोद्युक्तः संस्थिष्ठति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

रायः (*rāyaḥ*) is wealth; बुध्नः (*budhnaḥ*) is its binder, its root-source. Such a Savitṛ, the one who brings together (संगमनः (*saṃgamanaḥ*)) and gets for us the treasures (वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)), with his powers (शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*), lights) looks upon and illumines all forms, all things that can be described. Moreover, like a god, this Savitṛ, the impeller, is one whose धर्म (*dharma*) (support, or the act that is the ground of support) is truth, unfailing. Like Indra, तस्थौ (*tasthau*): in the contest for riches, in battle, in good attainment, this Savitṛ stands ready, exerting himself.

### Printed p. 906

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—to wealth
- बुद्धः (*buddhaḥ*)—being its root, that is, its support
- वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)—of various kinds of wealth
- संगमनः (*saṃgamanaḥ*)—the Savitṛ god who provides them
- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—with his radiances
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- रूपा (*rūpā*)—these forms, that is, things that can be seen by the eye
- अभि चष्टे (*abhi caṣṭe*)—looks all around (or illumines)
- देव इव (*deva iva*)—like a god
- सविता (*savitā*)—this Savitṛ
- सत्यधर्मा (*satyadharmā*)—he whose nature or act is truth
- धनानां (*dhanānāṃ*)—made for the gaining of wealth
- समरे (*samare*)—in battle
- इंद्रः न (*iṃdraḥ na*)—like Indra
- तस्थौ (*tasthau*)—stands firm

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This god Savitṛ, the support of wealth and provider of various kinds of wealth, illumines all kinds of things with his radiances. Like the god of dharma, this Savitṛ stands firm like Indra in the battle fought for gaining wealth.

##### English translation
The root of riches, the aquirer of treasure illumines by his functions all (visible) forms); Savitri, like a god, whose attribute is truth, stands like Indra in the battle for riches.
#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि॒श्वाव॑सुं सोम गंध॒र्वमापो॑ ददृ॒शुषी॒स्तदृ॒तेना॒ व्या॑यन् ।  
> तद॒न्ववै॒दिंद्रो॑ रारहा॒ण आ॑सां॒ परि॒ सूर्य॑स्य परि॒धीर॑पश्यत् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विश्ववसुं । सोम । गंधर्वं । आपः । ददृशुषीः । तत् । ऋतेन । वि । आयन् ।  
> तत् । अनुअवैत् । इंद्रः । ररहाणः । आसां । परि । सूर्यस्य । परिधीन् ।  
> अपश्यत् ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 907

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वया सहितं गंधर्वं गीतरूपां गां शब्दं धारयंतं विश्वावसुमेतत्संज्ञं मां ॥ उत्तरत्र तच्छब्दश्रुतेर्यच्छब्दाध्याहारः ॥ यदापो वसतीवर्याख्या ददृशुषीर्दृष्टवत्यः ॥ दृशेर्लिटः क्वसुः । उगितश्चति जीप् । वसोः
> संप्रसारणमिति संप्रसारणं । जसि वा छंदसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः ॥ तत्तदानीम्ृतेन
> यज्ञेन हेतुना व्यायन् । विविधमगच्छन्यष्टृजनाः । तद्गमनमासामपां
> ररहाणो गमयितेंद्रोऽन्ववैत् । अस्वबुध्यत । बुद्ध्वा च कुत्र यज्ञः प्रवृत्त
> इति सूर्यस्य परिधीन्परितो धीयमानानाच्यादिदिग्वभागान्पर्यपश्यत् । परितो
> दृष्टवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Soma, me, called Viśvāvasu, the Gandharva, the one who bears गां (*gāṃ*) (speech, sound) in the form of song, together with you." A यत् (*yat*) is to be supplied, since तत् (*tat*) follows later: "when the waters called Vasatīvarī saw (ददृशुषीः (*dadṛśuṣīḥ*)) …". Then (तत् (*tat*)), by reason of the ऋत (*ṛta*), the sacrifice, the officiating priests went (व्यायन् (*vyāyan*)) in various directions. Indra, the impeller (ररहाणः (*rarahāṇaḥ*)) of these waters, became aware (अन्ववैत् (*anvavait*)) of their going. Having awakened, and wondering where the sacrifice was proceeding, he looked all around (पर्यपश्यत् (*paryapaśyat*)) at the परिधीन् (*paridhīn*) of the sun, the quarters, east and the rest, that surround it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O god Soma
- गंधर्वं (*gaṃdharvaṃ*)—singing (accompanied by you)
- विश्वावसुं (*viśvāvasuṃ*)—me, named Viśvāvasu
- (यत् (*yat*)—when)
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters called Vasatīvarī
- ददृशुषीः (*dadṛśuṣīḥ*)—saw
- तत् (*tat*)—then
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—for the sacrifice
- व्यायन् (*vyāyan*)—various people came there
- तत् (*tat*)—their coming
- आसां (*āsāṃ*)—of the waters
- ररहाणः (*rarahāṇaḥ*)—who sends them forth
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अन्ववैत् (*anvavait*)—understood (then, to learn where the sacrifice was proceeding)
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of the sun
- परिधीन् (*paridhīn*)—the quarters, east and the rest, around
- परि (*pari*)—all around
- अपश्यत् (*apaśyat*)—looked

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(Words of the Gandharva Viśvāvasu.) O god Soma, when the waters Vasatīvarī and the people who had come for the sacrifice saw me, who am with you, Indra, the impeller of the rain-waters, understood that a sacrifice was going on, and, to learn where it was proceeding, searched and looked all around in the quarters, east and the rest, surrounding the sun.

##### English translation
Beholding Soma, the Gandharva Viswavasu, the waters have come forth by means of the sacrifice; Indra impelling them knew of this (their approach), and looked round the rims of the sun.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि॒श्वाव॑सुर॒भि तन्नो॑ गृणातु दि॒व्यो गं॑ध॒र्वो रज॑सो  ॒॑
> वि॒मानः॑ ।

### Printed p. 908

> यद्वा घा सत्यमुत यन्न विद्म धियो हिन्वानो धिय  
> इन्नो अव्याः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विश्ववसुः । अभि । तत् । नः । गृणातु । दिव्यः । गंधर्वः । रजसः । विमानः ।  
> यत् । वा । घ । सत्यं । उत । यत् । न । विद्म । धियः । हिन्वानः । धियः । इत् ।  
> नः । अव्याः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विश्वावसुर्गंधर्वो नोऽस्माकं तदभि गृणातु । अभिमुखं ब्रवीतु ॥ ग्य
> शब्दे । क्रैयादिकः । प्वादित्वाद्रस्वः ॥ कीदृशः । दिव्यो दिवि भवः तथा रजस उदकस्य
> विमानो निर्माता । किं पुनस्तत् । यद्वा घ यच्च खलु सत्यमवितथं यथार्थफलं कर्मजातं । उतशब्दश्चार्थे । यच्च न विद्मन जानीमः तदुभयं ब्रवीत्वित्यर्थः॥
> ऋचि तुनुघेत्यादिना घशब्दस्य साहितिको दीर्घः ॥ शिष्टः पादः प्रत्यक्षकृतः । हे
> विश्वावसो धियः कर्माणि हिन्वानः सोमेन प्रवर्धयन् ॥ हि गतौ वृदौ च ॥
> यद्वा । धियः स्तुतीर्हिन्वानः प्राप्नुवन्नोऽस्माकं धिय इत्कर्माण्येव बुद्धीरेव
> नाव्याः । रक्ष ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May the Gandharva Viśvāvasu declare (अभि गृणातु (*abhi gṛṇātu*)) that to us, speaking toward us. What kind is he? दिव्यः (*divyaḥ*), born in heaven, and the विमानः (*vimānaḥ*), the maker, of रजसः (*rajasaḥ*), water. And what is "that"? Whatever is truly (सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)) the unfailing set of rites yielding their due fruit, and whatever we do not know: let him declare both. Sāyaṇa notes that the particle घ (*gha*) has a lengthening in the saṃhitā. The remaining quarter-verse is evident. O Viśvāvasu, धियः (*dhiyaḥ*), our rites, you who advance (हिन्वानः (*hinvānaḥ*)) them with Soma (the root हि (*hi*) in the sense of going and increase). Or else, you who gain our praises (धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)): protect (अव्याः (*avyāḥ*)) indeed our rites and understandings.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वासुः गंधर्वः (*viśvāsuḥ gaṃdharvaḥ*)—the Gandharva Viśvāvasu
- दिव्यः (*divyaḥ*)—dwelling in heaven (the firmament)
- रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)—of the water
- विमानः (*vimānaḥ*)—the maker, and he
- सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)—certainly
- यत्वा घ (*yatvā gha*)—what it is
- उत (*uta*)—and
- यत् (*yat*)—what
- न विद्म (*na vidma*)—we cannot know
- तत् (*tat*)—that
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- अभिगृणातु (*abhigṛṇātu*)—let him declare toward us (O Viśvāvasu)
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—praises
- हिन्वानः (*hinvānaḥ*)—increasing with Soma
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- धिय इत् (*dhiya it*)—sacrificial and other rites
- अव्याः (*avyāḥ*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let the Gandharva Viśvāvasu tell us who is the maker of the waters in heaven, that is, in the firmament, and what we do not know. O Viśvāvasu, you who are with Soma, increase our praises and sacrificial rites and protect them.

### Printed p. 909

##### English translation
May the celestial Gandharva Viswavasu, the measurer of the water, declare to us that which is the truth, and that which we do not know; accepting our praises, (Viswavasu), protect our sacrifices.

> प्र । आसां । गंधर्वः । अमृतानि । वोचत् । इंद्रः । दक्षं । परि । जानात् ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सस्निमद्भिः संस्कृतं प्रकर्षेण सर्वस्य जगतः स्थापयितारं मेघं ॥ स्ना
> शौचे । आद्यगमहन इति किन्नत्ययः । लिड्डद्भावाद्विर्वचनं ॥ नदीनां शब्दकारिणीनामपां चरणे संचरणस्थानेऽंतरिक्षेऽविंदत् । इंद्रोऽलभत । लब्ध्वा चात्मव्रजानां ।
> अश्मा व्यापो मेघः तत्र व्रजंतीनां । यद्वा । मेघो व्रजो गोष्ठं निवासस्थानं यासां तादृशीनां अपां । दुरो द्वाराणि मेघान्निर्गमनप्रदेशानपावृणोत् । आपावृतवान् । यद्वा । अश्मसु शिलासु व्रजंतीनां गच्छंतीनां व्याप्तगमनानां वा
> नदीनां गंगायमुनादीनां चरणे संचरणे प्रवहणननिमित्तभूते सति तदर्थमिंद्रः
> सस्निं मेघमविंदत् । अलभत । लब्ध्वा चात्मर्गतानामपां निर्गमनसाधनानि मेघस्य
> दुरो द्वाराण्यपावृणोत् । अपावृतवान् । तथासां नदीनाममृतान्यमरणसाधकान्युदकानि गंधर्वो गोर्वज्रस्य धर्ता विश्वाससरूपेण वर्तमान इंद्रः
> प्र वोचत् । प्रब्रवीति । प्रवोढुमनुजानाति । तथा दक्षं । दक्षत्युदकं प्रयच्छतीति

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सस्निं (*sasniṃ*) is the cloud, purified by waters, the one who firmly establishes the whole world (root स्ना (*snā*) in the sense of purity). Indra found (अविंदत् (*aviṃdat*)) it in the चरणे (*caraṇe*), the place of movement, the firmament, of the sounding waters, the rivers (नदीनां (*nadīnāṃ*)). Having found it, he opened (अवृणोत् (*avṛṇot*)) the doors (दुरः (*duraḥ*)), the places of exit from the cloud, of the waters that go there: अश्वव्रजानां (*aśvavrajānāṃ*) is explained as "of those that move in the अश्मा (*aśmā*), the cloud", or else "of waters whose व्रज (*vraja*), stall or dwelling, is the cloud". Another explanation: while the rivers such as the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, going over stones (अश्मसु (*aśmasu*)) or moving far-reaching, are in motion for flowing, Indra for that purpose found the cloud and opened the doors of the cloud, the means of exit of the waters in it. Further, Indra, existing in the form of the Gandharva, the bearer of the गो (*go*) and vajra, declares (प्र वोचत् (*pra vocat*)) the immortal waters of these rivers, those that cause deathlessness; he permits them to flow forth. Likewise दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*) ….

### Printed p. 910

> दक्षो वर्षणसमर्थो मेघः । तादृशं मेघमहीनां मेघानां मध्यॆ परि
> जानात् । परितः सर्वतो जानाति ॥ ज्ञा अवबोधने । लेट्यडागमः । ज्ञाजनोर्जेति जादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues the gloss. *dakṣaḥ* is the cloud able to cause rain. Indra knows such a cloud completely among the clouds (अहीनां (*ahīnāṃ*)). परि जानात् (*pari jānāt*) means "knows on every side"; it comes from the root ज्ञा (*jñā*) in the sense of knowing.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सस्निं (*sasniṃ*)—the cloud that drenches everything with streams of water (the cloud)
- नदीनां (*nadīnāṃ*)—of the sounding waters
- चरणे (*caraṇe*)—what is in the atmosphere, the place of their movement
- अविंदत् (*aviṃdat*)—Indra found (came to know)
- अश्वव्रजानां (*aśvavrajānāṃ*)—of the waters in the multitudes of clouds
- दुरः (*duraḥ*)—the doors through which they come out
- अप अवृणोत् (*apa avṛṇot*)—he unfastened and opened
- आसां (*āsāṃ*)—of these rivers
- अमृतानि (*amṛtāni*)—the waters like ambrosia
- गंधर्वः (*gaṃdharvaḥ*)—in the form of the Gandharva Viśvāvasu
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- प्र वोचत् (*pra vocat*)—he has known how to bring them flowing
- अहीनां (*ahīnāṃ*)—among the clouds
- दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*)—which cloud can pour rain
- परि जानात् (*pari jānāt*)—Indra knows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Among the waters that make sounds such as lightning and thunder and move in the atmosphere, Indra found the cloud able to pour rain and drench everything. He opened doors so that the waters in those clouds might come down. Indra, in the form of the Gandharva Viśvāvasu, has known how to make these ambrosial rain-waters flow as rivers. He has known which cloud, among the many clouds in the atmosphere, is full of water and able to pour rain.

##### English translation
(Indra) discovered the cloud in the region of the rivers, he set open the portals of (the waters) whose dwelling is in the clouds; Indra, (in the form of) the Gandharva (Viswavasu), proclaimed the ambrosial (waters), he knew the strength of the dragons.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the phrase in this Ṛk, सस्निमविंदच्चरणे नदीनां (*sasnimaviṃdaccaraṇe nadīnāṃ*), Yāska gives the Nirukta: सस्निमविंदच्चरणे नदीनां । सस्निं संस्नातं मेघं (*sasnimaviṃdaccaraṇe nadīnāṃ | sasniṃ saṃsnātaṃ meghaṃ*) (Ni. 5-1). The word सस्नि (*sasni*) means "bathed, drenched" with waters. Or the cloud is called सस्नि (*sasni*) because it can drench everything with streams of water. That power of drenching belongs also to reservoirs such as rivers. But here प्रकरणसामर्थ्याच्छब्दोऽप्यर्थांतरं भजते (*prakaraṇasāmarthyācchabdo 'pyarthāṃtaraṃ bhajate*): according to context a word can be given many kinds of meaning. Therefore सस्नि (*sasni*) is here explained as the cloud.

### Printed p. 911
In सस्निं अंविदत् चरणे नदीनां (*sasniṃ aṃvidat caraṇe nadīnāṃ*) the commentator says that the word नदीनां (*nadīnāṃ*) is derived from the root नद (*nada*) (to sound). The waters in the atmosphere in the form of clouds make sounds called lightning and thunder, so "sounding waters" is said here. सस्नि (*sasni*) means having the power to drench, that is, full of water. Though there are many cloud-masses in the atmosphere, not all can pour rain; only some, full of water (looking dark), have the power of pouring rain. The chief sense of the sentence is that Indra knows which cloud has that power.

In अपावृणोत् दुरो अश्वव्रजानां (*apāvṛṇot duro aśvavrajānāṃ*) the words अश्व (*aśva*) and व्रज (*vraja*) are read among the names of the cloud. So अश्व (*aśva*) may be taken as cloud and व्रज (*vraja*) as multitude: "of the multitudes of clouds". The waters in clouds do not always fall as rain; they may stay in the clouds a long time. So Indra made an opening in the lower part of the clouds, and opened it wide, so that the waters might fall downward on the earth.

In प्र आसां गंधर्वो अमृतानि वोचत् (*pra āsāṃ gaṃdharvo amṛtāni vocat*) the word गंधर्व (*gaṃdharva*) is explained as Indra, or Indra in the form of a Gandharva. इंद्रो गंधर्वः तस्य मरुतोऽप्सरसः (*iṃdro gaṃdharvaḥ tasya maruto 'psarasaḥ*): it is well known that Gandharvas are always accompanied by Apsarases. Here, if Indra is a Gandharva, the Marut deities are with him, so they are taken as the Apsarases, and Indra is described by the word गंधर्व (*gaṃdharva*). The word अमृत (*amṛta*) means waters, sweet waters like ambrosia; अमृत (*amṛta*) is also read among the names of water. प्र वोचत् (*pra vocat*), "Indra said", means: आसां प्रजानां जीवध्वमेभिरुदुकैरस्सद्दत्तैरिति (*āsāṃ prajānāṃ jīvadhvamebhirudukairassaddattairiti*), "O creatures, live by these waters given through our (Indra's) grace."

In इंद्रो दक्षं परि जानादहीनां (*iṃdro dakṣaṃ pari jānādahīnāṃ*): of the clouds in the atmosphere some cannot pour rain, some full of water can. So the sense of this sentence is that Indra can know which cloud among the many can pour rain. The word दक्ष (*dakṣa*) means the cloud having the power of pouring rain.

### Printed p. 912
## Sūkta 140 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्ने तवेति षड्यचं द्वादशं सूक्तं । पावकगुणविशिष्टोऽग्नि र्यषिः । शुद्धाग्निर्देवता। आद्या विष्णारपंक्तिरष्टकद्विद्वादशाष्टकवती । अथ तिस्रः सतोबृहत्योऽयुजौ
> जागत् । अनु ८-४ । इति लक्षणोपेताः । पंचम्युपरिष्वाज्योतिः । षष्ठि त्रिष्टुप् ।
> तथा चानुक्रांतं । अग्ने तवाग्नि । पावक अग्नेयं विष्णारपंक्तिस्तिस्त्रः सतोबृहत्य उपरिष्टाज्योतिरिति ॥ महाव्रत आग्निमारुतशस्त्र इदं सूक्तं स्तोत्रियानुरूपार्थं ।
> तथैव पंचमारण्यके सूत्रितं ॥ ऐ. आ. ५-३-२ ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This sūkta, अग्ने तव (*agne tava*), has six Ṛks and is the twelfth sūkta. The seer is Agni, endowed with the quality of purifying (पावक (*pāvaka*)); the deity is Agni, the pure fire. The first Ṛk is विष्णारपंक्ति (*viṣṇārapaṃkti*) with the pattern 8, 12, 12, 8. The next three are सतोबृहती (*satobṛhatī*), defined by अयुजौ जागत् (*ayujau jāgat*) (Anu. 8-4). The fifth is उपरिष्टाज्योतिः (*upariṣṭājyotiḥ*); the sixth is त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*). He cites the Anukramaṇī. Use: in the Mahāvrata, in the Āgnimāruta śastra, for the स्तोत्रियानुरूप (*stotriyānurūpa*) verses, as laid down in the fifth Āraṇyaka (Ai. Ā. 5-3-2).

**Printed Kannada Anuvāda**
This sūkta अग्ने तव (*agne tava*) is the twelfth sūkta in the eleventh Anuvāka, with six Ṛks. Its seer is Agni, the purifier. The deity is Agni. The first Ṛk is in the metre विष्टारपंक्ति (*viṣṭārapaṃkti*): four pāda-s, the first of eight syllables, the second and third of twelve each, the last of eight. The next three Ṛks, 2–4, are सतोबृहती (*satobṛhatī*), whose rule is अयुजौ जागत् (*ayujau jāgat*) (Anu. 8-4): the odd pādas (1 and 3) are like the jagatī. The fifth is उपरिष्टाज्योतिः (*upariṣṭājyotiḥ*), the sixth त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*). The Anukramaṇī says: अग्ने तवाग्निः पावकआग्नेयं विष्टारपंक्ति स्त्रिसः सतोबृहत्य उपरिष्टाज्योतिः (*agne tavāgniḥ pāvakaāgneyaṃ viṣṭārapaṃkti strisaḥ satobṛhatya upariṣṭājyotiḥ*). In the Mahāvrata rite, at the recitation of the Āgnimāruta śastra, this sūkta is used for the स्तोत्रियानुरूप (*stotriyānurūpa*) mantras, as indicated in the fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka (Ai. Ā. 5-3-2).

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 140; Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 7; Varga 28. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6. Ṛṣi: Agni Pāvaka. Deity: Agni. Metre: 1 Viṣṭārapaṅkti; 2–4 Satobṛhatī; 5 Upariṣṭājjyotiḥ; 6 Triṣṭup.

### Printed p. 913
#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॒ तव॒ श्रवो॒ वयो॒ महि॑ भ्राजंते अ॒र्चयो॑ विभावसो ।  
> बृह॑द्भानो॒ शव॑सा॒ वाज॑मु॒क्थं१॒॑ १ दधा॑सि दा॒शुषे॑ कवे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । तव । श्रवः । वयः । महि । भ्राजंते । अर्चयः । विभावसो इति विभावसो ।  
> बृहद्भानो इति बृहत् ऽभानो । शवसा । वाजं । उक्ष्यं । दधासि । दाशुषे । कवे ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे आग्ने तव वयोऽन्नं श्रवः श्रवणीयं प्रशस्यं । हविरात्मकस्य तस्य मंत्रसंस्कृतत्वेन प्रशस्तत्वात् । अन्नेषु मध्यॆ तवैवान्नं श्रेष्ठमित्यर्थः । हे विभावसो ।
> विशिष्टा दीप्तिर्विभा । सैव वसुर्धनं यस्य तादृशाग्ने अर्चयो दीप्तयो महि
> महद्बहुलं भ्राजंते ! दीप्यंते ॥ भाज्य दीप्तौ । अनुदात्तेत् । भौवादिकः ॥ हे
> बृहद्भानो प्रौढदीप्ते कवे क्रांतदर्शिन्नग्ने एवं महानुभावस्त्वं शवसा
> बलेनोपेतमुक्थ्यं प्रशस्यं । यद्वा । उक्थो यज्ञः । तद्योग्यं वाजमन्नं
> दाशुषे हवींषि दत्तवते यजमानाय दधासि । ददासि । प्रयच्छसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, your food (वयः (*vayaḥ*)) is श्रवः (*śravaḥ*), praiseworthy, since the oblation, being consecrated by mantra, is praised; of all foods yours is the best. O विभावसो (*vibhāvaso*), whose wealth is special radiance (विभा (*vibhā*)), your flames blaze greatly (महि (*mahi*)); भ्राजंते (*bhrājaṃte*) means "shine", from भाज्य दीप्तौ (*bhājya dīptau*), first class. O बृहद्भानो (*bṛhadbhāno*) of mature radiance, O कवे (*kave*) far-seeing Agni, being so great you give (दधासि (*dadhāsi*) = ददासि (*dadāsi*), प्रयच्छसि (*prayacchasi*)) to the sacrificer (दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)) who has given oblations food (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)) endowed with strength (शवसा (*śavasā*)) and praiseworthy (उक्ष्यं (*ukṣyaṃ*)). Or else उक्थ (*uktha*) is sacrifice, and the food is fit for it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- तव (*tava*)—your (the oblation-food offered to you)
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—food
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—praiseworthy
- विभावसो (*vibhāvaso*)—O Agni whose wealth is radiance
- अर्चयः (*arcayaḥ*)—your flames
- महि (*mahi*)—greatly
- भ्राजंते (*bhrājaṃte*)—shine
- बृहद्भानो (*bṛhadbhāno*)—you who shine with surpassing brilliance
- कवे (*kave*)—O far-seeing Agni, you
- शवसा (*śavasā*)—endowed with strength (nourishing)
- उक्ष्यं (*ukṣyaṃ*)—and praiseworthy
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who offers oblation to you
- दधासि (*dadhāsi*)—you give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, the oblation-food offered to you is praiseworthy. O Agni whose wealth is radiance, your flames shine abundantly. O Agni, shining with surpassing brilliance and far-seeing, you give nourishing and praiseworthy food (or sacrifice) to the sacrificer who offers oblation to you.

### Printed p. 914

##### English translation
Yours, Agni, is the most excellent sacrificial food; your flames, O opulent in radiance, blaze fiercely; wise and widely luminous (Agni), you bestow upon the donor (of the oblation) the choicest food with strength.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पा॒व॒कव॑र्चाः शु॒क्रव॑र्चा॒ अनू॑नवर्चा॒ उदि॑यर्षिभा॒नुना॑ ।  
> पु॒त्रो मा॒तरा॑ वि॒चर॒न्नु पा॑वसि पृ॒णक्षि॒ रोद॑सी उ॒भे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पावकवर्चाः । शुक्रवर्चाः । अनूनवर्चाः । उत् । इयर्षि । भानुना ।  
> पुत्रः । मातरा । विचरन् । उप । अवसि । पृणक्षि । रोदसी इति । उभे इति ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पावकवर्चाः शोधकदीप्तिः शुक्रवर्चा निर्मलतेजस्कोऽनूनवर्चाः संपूर्णतेजस्कः । हे अग्ने ईदृशस्त्वं भानुना तेजसोदियर्षि । उद्धच्छसि ॥ ऋ सृ गतौ
> जौहोत्यादिकः । अर्तिपिपर्त्योश्चेत्यभ्यासस्यॆत्वं ॥ स त्वं पुत्रः सन् मातरा मातृभूते अरण्य विचरन् यागावसाने विशेषेण प्राप्पुवन्नु पावसि । उपगतान्यजमानान्रक्षसि । तथोभे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ पृणक्षि । संयोजयसि । हविषा
> द्युलोकं वृष्ट्येमं लोकं च पूरयसीत्यर्थः ॥ पृची संपर्के । रौधादिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

पावकवर्चाः (*pāvakavarcāḥ*) has purifying lustre, शुक्रवर्चाः (*śukravarcāḥ*) spotless lustre, अनूनवर्चाः (*anūnavarcāḥ*) full lustre. O Agni, being such, you rise up (उदियर्षि (*udiyarṣi*), "you go up", from ऋ सृ गतौ (*ṛ sṛ gatau*), juhotyādi) with splendour (भानुना (*bhānunā*)). As a son, ranging between your two mothers, the forest-born fire-sticks, at the end of the sacrifice you reach them specially and protect (अवसि (*avasi*)) the sacrificers who have come near. Also you fill (पृणक्षि (*pṛṇakṣi*), "unite", from पृची संपर्के (*pṛcī saṃparke*), rudhādi) both heaven and earth (रोदसी (*rodasī*)): the world of heaven with the oblation, this world with rain.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पावकवर्चाः (*pāvakavarcāḥ*)—having purifying radiance
- शुक्रवर्चाः (*śukravarcāḥ*)—shining with spotless brilliance
- अनूनवर्चाः (*anūnavarcāḥ*)—shining with full (undiminished) light; O Agni, you
- भानुना (*bhānunā*)—together with splendour
- उदियर्षि (*udiyarṣi*)—you become manifest (rise from the fire-sticks)
- पुत्रः (*putraḥ*)—you, in the place of a son
- मातरा (*mātarā*)—in the fire-sticks that are like mothers to you
- विचरन् (*vicaran*)—going (at the end of the sacrifice) and joining
- उप अवसि (*upa avasi*)—you protect the sacrificers near you, and
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- पृणक्षि (*pṛṇakṣi*)—you fill the world of heaven with oblation, and the earth with rain

### Printed p. 915

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, of purifying radiance, shining with spotless brilliance and full light, you are born from the fire-sticks together with your splendour. You, who are in the place of a son to the fire-sticks, at the end of the sacrifice go and join them, your mothers, and protect the sacrificer. You fill both heaven and earth: you unite and nourish the world of heaven (the gods) with oblation and the earth with rain.

##### English translation
Agni you are of purifying radiance, of unsoiled Instre, of full brightness, you issue forth with splendour; visiting your parents (like) a son, you protect (the worshippers). you unite both heaven and earth.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऊर्जो॑ नपाज्जातवेदः सुश॒स्तिभि॒र्मंद॑स्व धी॒तिभि॑र्हि॒तः ।  
> त्वे इषः॒ सं द॑धु॒र्भूरि॑वर्पसश्चि॒त्रोत॑यो वा॒मजा॑ताः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऊर्जः । नपात् । जातवेदः । सुशस्तिभिः । मंदस्व । धीतिभिः । हितः ।  
> त्वे इति । इषः । सं । दधुः । भूरिवर्पसः । चित्रऊतयः । वामजाताः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऊर्जो नपादूर्जोऽन्नस्य पार्थिवस्यारण्यादेः पुत्र हे जातवेदो
> जातानां वेदितरग्ने सुशस्तिभिरस्माभिः क्रियमाणैर्मंदस्व । मोदस्व । तथा धीतिभिः
> कर्मभिरस्माभिः क्रियमाणैरग्निहोत्रादिभिः कर्मभिर्हितः सुहितस्तृप्तो भव । अपि च
> भूरिवर्पसः । वर्ष इति रूपनाम । बहुविधरूपाश्चित्रोतयः चित्रा विचित्रोतिस्तृप्तिर्यासां तास्त्रथोक्ता वामजाताः वामं वननीयं जातं जन्म यासां
> तादृशीरिषोऽन्नानि हविर्लक्षणानि त्वे त्वय्येव सं दधुः । संदधति । सम्यग्हुश्वति
> यजमानाः । यद्वा । भूरिवर्पस इत्यादिकं कर्तृविशेषणं । तदानीं चित्रोतय
> इत्यस्य विचित्ररक्षा इति योज्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O ऊर्जः । नपात् (*ūrjaḥ | napāt*), son of earthly food (ऊर्जः (*ūrjaḥ*)) such as the forest wood, O जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*), knower of all born things, Agni: rejoice (मंदस्व (*maṃdasva*) = मोदस्व (*modasva*)) in the praises (सुशस्तिभिः (*suśastibhiḥ*)) we make, and be well pleased and satisfied (हितः (*hitaḥ*)) with the rites (धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*)) such as the Agnihotra performed by us. Moreover the foods (इषः (*iṣaḥ*)) in the form of oblations, which are of many forms (भूरिवर्पसः (*bhūrivarpasaḥ*); वर्ष (*varṣa*) is a name for form), of wonderful satisfaction (चित्रोतयः (*citrotayaḥ*)), and of lovely birth (वामजाताः (*vāmajātāḥ*)), the sacrificers place together in you alone (त्वे (*tve*) = *tvayi*; सं दधुः (*saṃ dadhuḥ*) = संदधति (*saṃdadhati*)). Or else भूरिवर्पसः (*bhūrivarpasaḥ*) and so on is an epithet of the agent, and then चित्रोतयः (*citrotayaḥ*) is to be construed as "of wonderful protection".

#### Ṛk 3 (continued)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऊर्जः (*ūrjaḥ*)—of food, or of the araṇi (the tree) that grows on the earth
- नपात् (*napāt*)—O son
- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni, who know all things that have come into being
- सुशस्तिभिः (*suśastibhiḥ*)—with the praises offered by us
- मंदस्व (*maṃdasva*)—be gladdened (and likewise)
- धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*)—with the rites such as Agnihotra that we perform
- हितः (*hitaḥ*)—be satisfied (and)
- भूरिवर्पसः (*bhūrivarpasaḥ*)—those that shine with many kinds of forms
- चित्रोतयः (*citrotayaḥ*)—those that bring satisfaction in diverse (many) ways
- *�vāmajātāḥ*—those that are excellently prepared
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—the foods that have the character of oblations
- त्वे (*tve*)—in you alone
- सं दधुः (*saṃ dadhuḥ*)—the sacrificers offer them by performing the homa

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, son of food (of strength) or of the araṇi, knower of all that is born, be gladdened by the praises we offer and be satisfied by the rites such as Agnihotra that we perform. The sacrificers offer into you alone, by homa, foods that have the character of oblations, that are of many forms, that bring satisfaction in many ways, and that are well prepared.

##### English translation
Son of strength, Jatavedas, rejoice in our adorations, (be) satisfied by our offerings; (the worshippers) have placed before you viands of many sorts of wonderful efficacy, of excellent origin.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒र॒ज्यन्न॑ग्ने प्रथयस्व जं॒तुभि॑र॒स्मे रायो॑ अमर्त्य ।  
> स द॑र्श॒तस्य॒ वपु॑षो॒ वि रा॑जसि पृ॒णक्षि॑ सान॒सिं क्रतुं॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इरज्यन् । अग्ने । प्रथयस्व । जंतुभिः । अस्मे इति । रायः । अमर्त्य ।  
> सः । दर्शतस्य । वपुषः । वि । राजसि । पृणक्षि । सानसिं । क्रतुं ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 917

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने जंतुभिर्जातैः शत्रुभिः सहेरज्यन्नीर्ष्यन् स्पर्धां कुर्वन् ॥
> इरज् ईर्ष्यायां । कंड्वादिः ॥ यद्वा! इरज्यतिरैश्वर्यकर्मा । जंतुभिर्जायमानैरात्मीयैस्तेजोभिरिरज्यन्नीश्वरो भवन् । हे अमर्त्य मरणरहिताग्ने आस्मे
> अस्माकं ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति षष्ठ्याः शेआदेशः ॥ रायो धनानि प्रथयस्व । विस्तारय ॥
> रयिशब्दाच्छसः स्थाने व्यत्ययेन जस् । शसो वा व्यत्ययेनोडिदमिति विभक्तुदात्तत्वं न क्रियते ॥ स त्वं दर्शतस्य दर्शनीयस्य वपुषस्तेजोमयस्य शरीरस्य वि
> राजसि । तृतीयार्थे षष्ठि ना । ईदृशेन शरीरेण विशेषेण दीप्यसे । यद्वा ।
> राजतिरैश्वर्यकर्मा वपुरिति च रूपनाम । दर्शनीयेन रूपेण वि राजसि । विशेषेणेशिषे । अत एव सानसिं संभजनीयं क्रतुं कर्म पृणक्षि । अस्माभिः संपर्कयसि ।
> फलेन वा संयोजयसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, इरज्यन् (*irajyan*)": being jealous, rivalling, with जंतुभिः (*jaṃtubhiḥ*), that is, with born enemies. Or else: इरज्यति (*irajyati*) is a verb of lordship; becoming lord by his own splendours that are being born. "O immortal Agni", free from death, "अस्मे (*asme*)", for us, "रायः (*rāyaḥ*)", riches, "प्रथयस्व (*prathayasva*)", spread them out. "That you", with a "दर्शतस्य (*darśatasya*)", beautiful, "वपुषः (*vapuṣaḥ*)", luminous body, "वि राजसि (*vi rājasi*)": you shine specially with such a body (the genitive is in the sense of the instrumental). Or else: राजति (*rājati*) is a verb of lordship and वपुषः (*vapuṣaḥ*) is a name for form; you rule specially with a beautiful form. Therefore you पृणक्षि (*pṛṇakṣi*) the सानसिं क्रतुं (*sānasiṃ kratuṃ*), the rite that is to be shared: you join it with us, or you unite it with its fruit.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जंतुभिः (*jaṃtubhiḥ*)—with enemies
- इरज्यन् (*irajyan*)—one who fights
- अमर्त्य (*amartya*)—one free from death
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अस्मे (*asme*)—to us
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—wealth
- प्रथयस्व (*prathayasva*)—give abundantly (or: increase the wealth that is with us)
- सः (त्वं) (*saḥ (tvaṃ)*)—such as you are
- दर्शतस्य (*darśatasya*)—attractive
- वपुषः (*vapuṣaḥ*)—with your luminous body
- विराजसि (*virājasi*)—you shine specially [or: दर्शतस्य वपुषः (*darśatasya vapuṣaḥ*)—with your attractive form; वि राजसि (*vi rājasi*)—you are lord of all] (therefore)
- सानसिं (*sānasiṃ*)—that is to be obtained
- क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*)—the fruit of the rite
- पृणक्षि (*pṛṇakṣi*)—you cause it to reach us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, who fight with enemies and are free from death, give us wealth in abundance, or spread out, that is, increase, the wealth that is with us. You, whose form is attractive, shine specially with the radiance of your luminous body; or you are lord of all by your attractive form. Therefore unite with us the fruits of the sacrifice that are to be obtained by us (make them reach us).

##### English translation
Contending with enemies, bestow upon us, immortal Agni, riches; you shine with a graceful person, you fulfill (the purpose of) the enjoyable rite.

### Printed p. 918
#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒ष्क॒र्तार॑मध्व॒रस्य॒ प्रचे॑तसं॒ क्षयं॑तं॒ राध॑सो म॒हः ।  
> रा॒तिं वा॒मस्य॑ सु॒भगां॑ म॒हीमिषं॒ दधा॑सि सान॒सिं र॒यिं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इष्कर्तारं । अध्वरस्य । प्रचेतसं । क्षयंतं । राधसः । महः ।  
> रातिं । वामस्य । सुभगां । महीं । इषं । दधासि । सानसिं । रयिं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इष्कर्तारं निष्कर्तारं ॥ छांदसो वर्णलोपः ॥ अध्वरस्य यज्ञस्य निष्कर्तारं
> संस्कर्तारं प्रचेतसं प्रकृष्टज्ञानं महोमहतो राधसो धनस्य क्षयंतमीश्वरं ।
> क्षयतिरैश्वर्यकर्मा । नामस्य वननीयस्य धनस्य रातिं दातारं ॥ रातेः कर्तरि
> क्तिच् ॥ ईदृशं त्वां स्तुम इति शेषः । स त्वं सुभगां सौभाग्योपेतां महीं
> महतीमिषमन्नं सानसिं संभक्तव्यं रयिं धनं च दधासि । स्तोतृभ्यो ददासि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

इष्कर्तारं (*iṣkartāraṃ*) is निष्कर्तारं (*niṣkartāraṃ*) (the Vedic dropping of a letter). The one who perfects, prepares, the अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*), the sacrifice; प्रचेतसं (*pracetasaṃ*), of excellent knowledge; क्षयंतं (*kṣayaṃtaṃ*), the lord of महः (*mahaḥ*), great राधसः (*rādhasaḥ*), wealth (क्षयति (*kṣayati*) is a verb of lordship); रातिं (*rātiṃ*), the giver, of वामस्य (*vāmasya*), desirable wealth. The words "we praise you who are such" are to be supplied. Such as you are, you bestow सुभगां (*subhagāṃ*), fortunate, महीं (*mahīṃ*), great, इषं (*iṣaṃ*), food, and सानसिं (*sānasiṃ*), shareable रयिं (*rayiṃ*), wealth; you give them to the praisers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Agni) अध्वरस्य (*adhvarasya*)—of the sacrifice
- इष्कर्तारं (*iṣkartāraṃ*)—the perfecter (one who makes it proceed well)
- प्रचेतसं (*pracetasaṃ*)—one endowed with excellent knowledge
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great
- राधसः (*rādhasaḥ*)—of wealth
- क्षयंतं (*kṣayaṃtaṃ*)—the lord
- वामस्य (*vāmasya*)—of the wealth desired by all
- रातिं (*rātiṃ*)—the giver (one who gives); we praise you who are such (such as you are)
- सुभगां (*subhagāṃ*)—fortunate
- महीं (*mahīṃ*)—abundant
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- सानसिं (*sānasiṃ*)—that we are to obtain
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- दधासि (*dadhāsi*)—you give to the people who praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, we praise you, who perfect the sacrifice so that it proceeds well, who have excellent understanding, who are the owner of abundant wealth, and who give to each the wealth that all desire. Such as you are, you give to us who praise you auspicious and abundant food and the wealth that we are to obtain.

### Printed p. 919

##### English translation
(We praise you), the perfector of the sacrifice, the sage, the lord of great wealth, the giver of what is desirable; you bestow auspicious and abundant food, and enjoyable riches.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋ॒तावा॑नं महि॒षं वि॒श्वद॑र्शतम॒ग्निं सु॒म्नाय॑ दधिरे पु॒रो  ॑
> जनाः ।  
> श्रुत्क॑र्णं स॒प्रथ॑स्तमं त्वा गि॒रा दैव्यं॒ मानु॑षा यु॒गा ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऋतवानं । महिषं । विश्वदर्शतं । अग्निं । सुम्नाय । दधिरे । पुरः । जनाः ।  
> श्रुत्कर्णं । सप्रथस्तमं त्वा । गिरा । दैव्यं । मानुषा । युगा ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋतावानं सत्यवंतं यज्ञवंतं वा ॥ छंदसीवनिपाविति मत्त्वर्थीयो वनिप् ॥
> महिषं महांतं पूज्यं वा विश्वदर्शतं विश्वैः सर्वैर्दर्शनीयं । यद्वा । विश्वं
> दर्शनं यस्य॥ बहव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायामिति पूर्वपदांतोदात्तत्वं ॥ ईदृशमग्निं
> सुम्माय सुखार्थं जना ऋत्विग्यजमानरूपाः पुरो दधिरे । पुरो दधते । सर्वकर्मभ्यः पुरस्ताद्दारयंति । यद्वा । पुरः पुरस्तात्पूर्वस्यां दिश्याहवनीयरूपेण
> धारयंति । परोऽर्धर्चः प्रत्यक्षकृतः । अपि च हे अग्ने श्रुत्कर्णं श्रुत् स्तुतीः
> सम्यक् शृण्वन्कर्णः श्रोत्रेंद्रियं यस्य तादृशं सप्रथस्तममतिशयेन प्रख्यातं
> यद्वा सर्वतो विस्तार्यमाणं दैव्यं देवानां हनिर्वोढृत्वेन संबंधिनं ईदृशं
> त्वा त्वां मानुषा मानुषाणि मनोरपत्यानि युगा युगानि युगलानि पत्नीयजमानरूपाणि गिरा स्तुत्या स्तुवंतीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ऋतावानं (*ṛtāvānaṃ*): one who has truth, or who has sacrifice (the affix vanip in the sense of "possessing" under the rule छंदसीवनिपाविति (*chaṃdasīvanipāviti*)). महिषं (*mahiṣaṃ*): great or worshipful. विश्वदर्शतं (*viśvadarśataṃ*): to be seen by all; or else, one whose appearance is all. Such an Agni the जनाः (*janāḥ*), the people in the form of ṛtvijs and sacrificers, पुरो दधिरे (*puro dadhire*) place in front for the sake of happiness (सुम्नाय (*sumnāya*)): they set him in front of all rites; or else, पुरः (*puraḥ*) means "in front, in the eastern direction", and they hold him there in the form of the Āhavanīya. The second half of the ṛk is addressed directly (परोऽर्धर्चः प्रत्यक्षकृतः (*paro 'rdharcaḥ pratyakṣakṛtaḥ*)). Further, O Agni, श्रुत्कर्णं (*śrutkarṇaṃ*): one whose ear listens well to praises; सप्रथस्तमं (*saprathastamaṃ*): most renowned, or spread out on all sides; दैव्यं (*daivyaṃ*): connected with the gods as the bearer of oblations to them. You, so described, मानुषा युगा (*mānuṣā yugā*), the human pairs, the descendants of Manu, in the form of the sacrificer and his wife, praise गिरा (*girā*) with praise (the verb "praise" is to be supplied).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतावानं (*ṛtāvānaṃ*)—one who is truthful, or worthy of sacrifice
- महिषं (*mahiṣaṃ*)—the worshipful
- विश्वदर्शतं (*viśvadarśataṃ*)—one fit to be seen by all
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- सुम्माय (*summāya*)—that there may be happiness for all
- जनाः (*janāḥ*)—the ṛtvijs and sacrificers
- पुरः (*puraḥ*)—at the beginning of all rites also

### Printed p. 920
- दधिरे (*dadhire*)—they establish [or: पुरः (*puraḥ*)—in the Āhavanīya fire that is in the eastern direction; दधिरे (*dadhire*)—they establish] (O Agni)
- श्रुत्कर्णं (*śrutkarṇaṃ*)—one who listens with your ears to praises
- सप्रथस्तमं (*saprathastamaṃ*)—the well renowned, or one who spreads everywhere
- दैव्यं (*daivyaṃ*)—one connected with the gods, since he carries oblations to the gods
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- मानुषा (*mānuṣā*)—human
- युगा (*yugā*)—the two, the sacrificer and his wife
- गिरा (*girā*)—with words in the form of praise—they praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the happiness of all, the ṛtvijs and sacrificers establish Agni, who is truthful or worthy of sacrifice, worshipful, and fit to be seen by all, at the beginning of all rites, in the Āhavanīya fire-pit in the eastern direction. O Agni, you who listen with your ears to praise, who are well renowned or who quickly pervade and spread, and who belong to the gods, are praised with hymns and the like by the human couple, the sacrificer and his wife.

##### English translation
Men for the sake of happiness place before them Agni, the speaker of truth, the mighty, the contemplator of all; the posterity of Manu in pairs (propitiate) with praises you, whose ears are open (to their praises), who are most renowned, and the (minister) of the gods.

## Sūkta 141 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The sage Śaunaka has praised this sūkta in this way in his work called Ṛgvidhāna:
अग्ने अच्छा वदेत्येतद्धनकामः प्रयोजयेत् । नियतः सर्पिषा हुत्वा जपेदयुतशः पुनः ॥ ५० ॥ (*agne acchā vadetyetaddhanakāmaḥ prayojayet | niyataḥ sarpiṣā hutvā japedayutaśaḥ punaḥ ‖ 50 ‖*)
खादिरीणां हि समिधां जुहुयाद्दशतीर्दश । दशकृत्वः सदारेण रायस्पोषेण पुष्यति ॥ ५१ ॥ (*khādirīṇāṃ hi samidhāṃ juhuyāddaśatīrdaśa | daśakṛtvaḥ sadāreṇa rāyaspoṣeṇa puṣyati ‖ 51 ‖*)
१ ॥ बिल्वोदुंबरपालाशीस्तथा रौहितकीश्च याः । जुहुयाद्दनकामस्तु रायस्पोषेण पुष्यति ॥ ५२ ॥ (*1 ‖ bilvoduṃbarapālāśīstathā rauhitakīśca yāḥ | juhuyāddanakāmastu rāyaspoṣeṇa puṣyati ‖ 52 ‖*)

### Printed p. 921
२ ॥ वैभीदकेध्मो बैल्वकीर्जुहुयादर्धमासभुक् । द्विषद्द्वेषेण तस्यांते सूक्तमेतत्प्रयोजयेत् ॥ ५३ ॥ (*2 ‖ vaibhīdakedhmo bailvakīrjuhuyādardhamāsabhuk | dviṣaddveṣeṇa tasyāṃte sūktametatprayojayet ‖ 53 ‖*)
द्विषंतं धनिनं हत्वा द्विषतो विंदते धनं । अथवा जप्यमेव स्याद्रायस्पोषधनार्थिः (*dviṣaṃtaṃ dhaninaṃ hatvā dviṣato viṃdate dhanaṃ | athavā japyameva syādrāyaspoṣadhanārthiḥ*) **NOTE**
(Ṛgvidhāna, adhyāya 4, verses 51-54.)
One who desires wealth should employ the mantras of this sūkta beginning "अग्ने अच्छा (*agne acchā*)", and, with a purified mind, offer homa in the fire and also mutter the sūkta ten thousand times. While performing the homa he should, together with his wife, offer a thousand khādira sticks. He should also offer homa with sticks of the bilva, udumbara, muttuga (palāśa) and other trees. If he offers homa thus, wealth and prosperity are obtained. For the removal of enemies who hate him, the practitioner should perform homa with sticks of the vaibhedaka tree and of the bilva tree for fifteen days, taking one meal a day. After the homa he should mutter this sūkta. If he does so, even if his enemy is wealthy, the enemy is destroyed and the practitioner obtains all his wealth; and so on.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्न इति षडृचं त्रयोदशं सूक्तं । तापसगुणविशिष्टस्याग्नेरार्षं वैश्वदेवमानुष्टुभं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । अग्नेऽच्छाग्निस्तापसो वैश्वदेवमानुष्टुभं हीति ॥
> गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This sūkta beginning अग्न (*agna*) is the thirteenth sūkta, of six ṛks. Its seer is Agni endowed with the quality of austerity (tāpasa); its deity the Viśvedevas; its metre Anuṣṭubh. So the Anukramaṇī has it: अग्नेऽच्छाग्निस्तापसो वैश्वदेवमानुष्टुभं हीति (*agne 'cchāgnistāpaso vaiśvadevamānuṣṭubhaṃ hīti*). The viniyoga has been given already (गतो विनियोगः (*gato viniyogaḥ*)).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "Agne" is the thirteenth sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka. It has six ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Agni endowed with the quality of austerity; the deity is the Viśvedevas; the metre is Anuṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: अग्नेच्छाग्निस्तापसो वैश्वदेवमानुष्टुभं हि (*agnecchāgnistāpaso vaiśvadevamānuṣṭubhaṃ hi*). The use of the sūkta has been stated earlier.

##### Particulars

- Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 141
- Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 7; Varga 29
- Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 6
- Ṛṣi: Agni Tāpasa
- Devatā: Viśvedevas
- Chandas: Anuṣṭubh

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॒ अच्छा॑ वदे॒ह नः॑ प्र॒त्यज्ञः॑ सु॒मना॑ भव ।  
> प्र नो॑ यच्छ विशस्पते धन॒दा अ॑सि न॒स्यं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । अच्छ । वद । इह । नः । प्रत्यज् । नः । सुमनाः । भव ।  
> प्र । नः । यच्छ । विशः । पते । धनदाः । असि । नः । त्वं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने इहास्मिन्देशे नोऽस्मानच्छ वद । अभिमुख्येन प्रियं ब्रूहि ! तथा
> प्रत्यज्योऽस्मान्प्रत्यंचन् सुमनाः शोभनमनस्को भव । हे विशस्पते यजमानलक्षणायाः प्रजायाः पालयितः नोऽस्मभ्यं प्र यच्च धनानि प्रदेहि यतस्त्वं
> नोऽस्माकं धनदा असि धनानां दाता भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, speak to us here in this place, facing us, a pleasing word; and, turning towards us, be well-disposed (सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*), "of good mind"). O lord of the people (विशस्पते (*viśaspate*)), protector of the folk who are the sacrificer, bestow wealth upon us, since you are our giver of wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- इह (*iha*)—in this place
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- अच्छ वद (*accha vada*)—speak words beneficial to us; likewise
- प्रत्यज् नः (*pratyaj naḥ*)—in our matter
- सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*)—having a mind of favour
- भव (*bhava*)—be
- विशस्पते (*viśaspate*)—O Agni, protector of the people, the sacrificer and others
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- प्रयच्छ (*prayaccha*)—give wealth and the like
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- धनदाः असि (*dhanadāḥ asi*)—are a giver of wealth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, being in this place, gladden us with loving words. Be favourably disposed towards us. O protector of the people, give us wealth and the like, for you are our giver of wealth.

##### English translation
Agni, speak out to us hero, be favourably disposed towards us; bestow upon us (riches), lord of men, for you are the giver of wealth to us.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र । देवाः । प्र । उत । सूनृता । रायः । देवी । ददातु । नः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अर्यमारीणां नियंतार्याणां निर्माता वैतत्संज्ञो देवो नोऽस्मभ्यं
> प्र यच्छतु धनं । तथा भग एत्संज्ञको देवश्च प्रयच्छतु । बृहस्पतिश्च प्रयच्छतु ।
> सर्वॆ देवाश्च प्रयच्छंतु । उतापि च सूनृता प्रियसत्यवाग्रूपा देवी देवनशीला
> सरस्वती रायो धनानि नोऽस्मभ्यं प्र ददातु ॥ ऊडिदमित्यादिना रायो विभक्तिरुदात्ता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Aryaman, the god so named, controller of enemies and maker of nobles, is to give us wealth; so too the god named Bhaga, and Bṛhaspati, and all the gods. And Sūnṛtā, the goddess (देवी (*devī*), "of shining nature"), Sarasvatī in the form of speech both pleasant and true, is to give us wealth (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)). The case-ending of रायः (*rāyaḥ*) is acute-accented.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—the god Aryaman
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- प्र यच्छतु (*pra yacchatu*)—let him give wealth
- भगः (*bhagaḥ*)—the god named Bhaga
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—and Bṛhaspati
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—all the gods
- उत (*uta*)—and
- सूनृता (*sūnṛtā*)—who is the form of pleasant and true speech
- देवी (*devī*)—the goddess Sarasvatī
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—wealth
- प्र ददातु (*pra dadātu*)—let her give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Aryaman, Bhaga, Bṛhaspati, all the gods, and the goddess Sarasvatī, who always speaks pleasant and true words, give us wealth.

##### English translation
May Aryaman, may Bhaga, may Brihaspati, may the gods give liberally to us; may the truth-speaking goddess (Saraswati) bestow riches upon us.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सोमं । राजानं । अवसे । अग्निं । गीःभि । हवामहे ।  
> आदित्यान् । विष्णुं । सूर्यं । ब्रह्माणं । च । बृहस्पतिं ॥ ३ ॥

> हवामहे । आह्वयामहे । तथादित्यानदितेः पुत्रान् मित्रादीन् विष्णुं सूर्यं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We call upon Soma, who is shining or is lord (राजानं (*rājānaṃ*)), and Agni, with praises (गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)), for protection. Likewise we call, for protection, the Ādityas, sons of Aditi, Mitra and the others, and Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Brahmā (Prajāpati) and Bṛhaspati.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राजानं (*rājānaṃ*)—the shining one, or lord of all
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—with praises
- अवसे (*avase*)—for protection
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we pray and call; likewise
- आदित्यान् (*ādityān*)—the gods Mitra and others, sons of Aditi
- विष्णुं (*viṣṇuṃ*)—Viṣṇu
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—Sūrya
- ब्रह्माणं (*brahmāṇaṃ*)—Prajāpati
- बृहस्पतिं च (*bṛhaspatiṃ ca*)—and Bṛhaspati too; we pray and call them for protection

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We pray and call, with praises, for protection, Soma, who is shining or lord of all, and Agni. Likewise we pray and call for our protection the gods Mitra and others, sons of Aditi, and the gods Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Prajāpati and Bṛhaspati.

##### English translation
We invoke for our protection the royal Soma. (we invoke) Agni with praises (we invoke) the Adityas, Vishnu, Surya, Brahma and Brihaspati.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इं॒द्र॒वा॒यू बृह॒स्पतिं॑ सु॒हवे॒ह ह॑वामहे ।  
> यथा॑ नः॒ सर्व॒ इज्जनः॒ संग॑त्यां सु॒मना॒ अस॑त् ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 925

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रवायू इति । बृहस्पतिं । सुहवा । इह । हवामहे ।  
> यथा । नः । सर्वः । इत् । जनः । संगत्यां । सुमनाः । असत् । ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रश्च वायुश्चेंद्रवायू ॥ उभयत्र वायोः प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः ।
> पा ६-३-२६-१ । इत्यानजः प्रतिषेधः । नोत्तरपदेऽनुदात्तादाविति देवताद्वंद्वे
> चेति प्राप्तस्योभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरस्य निषेधः । समासस्येत्यंतोदात्तत्वं ॥ बृहस्पतिं
> बृहतां देवानां पालकं !! तद्बृहतोः करपत्योः । पा. ६-१-५७ । इति सुट्तलोपौ ! वनस्पत्यादित्वादुभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ सुहवा सुहवौ सुह्वानाविंद्रवायू बृहस्पतिं चेहास्मिन्कर्मणि हवामहे । आह्वयामहे ! यथा नोऽस्माकं
> सर्व इत् सर्व एव जनः संगत्यां संगमने धनस्य प्राप्ता सुमना असत्
> शोभनमनस्को भवेत् तथाह्वयामह इत्यर्थः ॥ अस्तेर्लेट्यडागमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

इंद्रवायू (*iṃdravāyū*) is Indra and Vāyu (a dvandva). Sāyaṇa explains the accent of the compound, with the exclusion of the accent of both members in a divinity-dvandva, and its final acute. बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*) is the protector of the great gods. Well-invoked (सुहवा (*suhavā*)) Indra and Vāyu, and Bṛhaspati, we call here, in this rite. We call them so that all our people, in the meeting (संगत्यां (*saṃgatyāṃ*)) for the obtaining of wealth, may be well-disposed (सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*)) towards us. असत् (*asat*) is a subjunctive of *asti* with the augment *aṭ*.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यथा (*yathā*)—in such manner as
- सर्व इत् (*sarva it*)—all
- जनः (*janaḥ*)—the people
- संगत्यां (*saṃgatyāṃ*)—gathering together in one place for our obtaining of wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—in our matter
- सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*)—of good mind
- असत् (*asat*)—may become, so
- इह (*iha*)—in this rite
- सुहवा (*suhavā*)—worthy of excellent invocation
- इंद्रवायू (*iṃdravāyū*)—the gods Indra and Vāyu
- बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—Bṛhaspati
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we pray and call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

So that all the people may gather together for our obtaining of wealth and become favourably disposed towards us, we pray and call in this rite Indra and Vāyu, worthy of excellent invocation, and Bṛhaspati.

##### English translation
We invoke the adorable Indra and Vayu and Brihaspati on this occasion, that all our race may be favourably inclined to us in the aquisition (of wealth).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praiser, urge by praise Aryaman and the other gods to the giving (दानाय (*dānāya*)) of wealth. Likewise urge to giving Vāta (Vāyu), Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, and Savitṛ, who is endowed with food and strength (वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- O praiser
- अर्यमणं (*aryamaṇaṃ*)—Aryaman
- बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*)—Bṛhaspati
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- वातं (*vātaṃ*)—Vāyu
- विष्णुं (*viṣṇuṃ*)—Viṣṇu
- सरस्वतीं (*sarasvatīṃ*)—the goddess Sarasvatī
- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—endowed with strength, or giver of food
- सवितारं च (*savitāraṃ ca*)—the god Savitṛ too
- दानाय (*dānāya*)—so that they give us wealth and the like
- चोदय (*codaya*)—urge with praises

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, in order that they give us wealth and the like, urge with praises these gods: Aryaman, Bṛhaspati, Indra, Vāyu, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, and Savitṛ the giver of food.

##### English translation
Stimulate to liberality Aryaman. Brihaspathi, Indra, Vata, Vishnu, Saraswati, and the food-bestowing Savitri.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं नो॑ अग्ने अ॒ग्निभि॒र्ब्रह्म॑ य॒ज्ञं च॑ वर्धय ।

### Printed p. 927

> त्वं नो देवतातये रायो दानाय चोदय ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । नः । अग्ने । अग्निभिः । ब्रह्म । यज्ञं । च । वर्धय ।  
> त्वं । नः । देवतातये । रायः । दानाय । चोदय ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वमग्निभिस्तद्विभूतिभूतैरन्यैरग्निभिः सार्धं नोऽस्माकं ब्रह्म
> स्तोत्रं यज्ञं च वर्धय । तथा त्वं नोऽस्माकं देवतातये । यज्ञनामैतत् ।
> यागार्थं रायो धनस्य दानाय प्रदानाय चोदय । दात्यन्रेरय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, together with the other fires, which are manifestations of you, increase our prayer (ब्रह्म (*brahma*), hymn of praise) and our sacrifice. Likewise, for the sacrifice (देवतातये (*devatātaye*), which is a name for sacrifice), urge on the giving (दानाय (*dānāya*)) of wealth; impel the givers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- अग्निभिः (*agnibhiḥ*)—together with other fires, particular manifestations of you (forms of Agni)
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—prayer
- यज्ञं च (*yajñaṃ ca*)—and sacrifice
- वर्धय (*vardhaya*)—increase (cause to be completed fully)
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- देवतातये (*devatātaye*)—for the sacrifice
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—of wealth
- दानाय (*dānāya*)—for the giving
- चोदय (*codaya*)—urge the givers

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, together with the other fires which are your special manifestations, that is, your other forms (the lightning fire, Vaiśvānara fire, Pāvaka fire, etc.), advance and bring to completion the prayer and the sacrifice that we perform. Urge the givers to help our sacrifice with wealth.

##### English translation
Augment our prayer and sacrifice, Agni, with your fires; do you at our sacrifice stimulate (the gods) to give us wealth.

## Sūkta 142 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमग्न इत्यष्टर्चं चतुर्दशं सूक्तमाग्नेयं । शार्ङ्ग इति पक्षिविशेषस्याख्या । शार्ङ्गजातयो जरितृप्रभृतयश्च त्वारश्च तुर्णां दृचानां क्रमेण

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn अयमग्न (*ayamagna*) has eight Ṛks; it is the fourteenth sūkta and addressed to Agni. शार्ङ्ग (*śārṅga*) is the name of a particular bird. The Śārṅgas, Jaritṛ and the others, four (seers), have the dṛcās in order. ()

### Printed p. 928

> द्रष्टारः । आदितो द्वे जगत्यौ । अथ चतस्रस्त्रिष्टुभः । ततो द्वे अनुष्टुभौ । तथा
> चानुक्रांतं । अयमष्टौ द्वृचाः शार्ङ्गा जरिता द्रोणः सारिसृक्वः स्तंबमित्रश्चाग्नेयमाद्ये जगत्यौ चतस्रश्च त्रिष्टुभ इति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues his introduction to the sūkta. The seers are Jaritṛ and three others, of the Śārṅga clan, one for each pair of ṛks in order. The first two ṛks are Jagatī, the next four are Triṣṭubh, and the last two are Anuṣṭubh. He cites the Anukramaṇī: अयमष्टौ द्वृचाः शार्ङ्गा जरिता द्रोणः सारिसृक्वः स्तंबमित्रश्चाग्नेयमाद्ये जगत्यौ चतस्रश्च त्रिष्टुभ इति ॥ (*ayamaṣṭau dvṛcāḥ śārṅgā jaritā droṇaḥ sārisṛkvaḥ staṃbamitraścāgneyamādye jagatyau catasraśca triṣṭubha iti ‖*). He then says that the viniyoga has already been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "ayam agne" is the fourteenth sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka. It has eight ṛks. The seers of this sūkta are four persons of the Śārṅga clan, Jaritṛ and the others, one for each pair of ṛks in order. Śārṅga means the name of a bird. Agni is the deity. The first two ṛks of this sūkta are in the Jagatī metre. The next four ṛks (3–6) are in the Triṣṭubh metre. The next two ṛks (7–8) are in the Anuṣṭubh metre. The Anukramaṇī says: अयमष्टाद्वृचाः शार्ङ्गा जरिता द्रोणः सारिसृक्वः स्तंबमित्रश्चाग्नेयमाद्ये जगत्यौ चतस्रश्च त्रिष्टुभः (*ayamaṣṭādvṛcāḥ śārṅgā jaritā droṇaḥ sārisṛkvaḥ staṃbamitraścāgneyamādye jagatyau catasraśca triṣṭubhaḥ*). The viniyoga has already been stated earlier.

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 142. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 7; Varga 30. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 8.
Ṛṣi: Śārṅgas — ṛks 1–2, जरिता (*jaritā*); 3–4, द्रोणः (*droṇaḥ*); 5–6, सारिस्कृत्वः (*sāriskṛtvaḥ*); 7–8, स्तंबमित्रः (*staṃbamitraḥ*).
Devatā: Agni.
Chandas: 1–2 Jagatī; 3–6 Triṣṭubh; 7–8 Anuṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यम॑ग्ने जरि॒ता त्वे अ॑भू॒दपि॒ सह॑सः सूनो न॒ह्य१॒॑ १ नृदस्त्याप्यं॑ ।  
> भ॒द्रं हि शर्म॑ त्रि॒वरू॑थ॒मस्ति॑ त आ॒रे हिंसा॑ना॒मप॑ दि॒द्युमा  ॑
> कृधि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । अग्ने । जरिता । त्वे इति । अभूत् । आपि । सहसः । सूनो इति । नहि । अन्यत् ।  
> अस्ति । अप्यं ।

### Printed p. 929

> भद्रं । हि । शर्म । त्रिवरूथं । अस्ति । ते । आरे । हिंसानां । अप । दिद्युं । आ । कृधि ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वे त्वयि ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्याः शेआदेशः ॥ आयमृषिर्जरिता
> स्तोताभूदपि । अपिशब्दः संभावनायां । इदानीं स्तोतृत्वेन संभाव्यते । तत्र
> कारणमाह । हे सहसः सूनो बलस्य पुत्र त्वत्तोऽन्यदाप्यमाप्तव्यं न ह्यस्ति । न
> खलु विद्यते । अतः प्राप्तव्यं त्वामेव स्तुत्या प्राप्नोमि । भद्रं कल्याणं त्रिवरूथं
> दुःखत्रयस्य निवारकं शर्म सुखं हि यस्मात्ते तनास्ति विद्यते । अथवा शोभनं
> त्रिवरूथं त्रिभूमिकं गृहं तनास्ति हि । अतो हिंसानां हिंस्यमानानाममस्माकमारे
> दूरे दिद्युं दीप्यमानामात्मीयां ज्वालामपा कृधि । अपाकुरु । निवारय ॥
> करोतेश्चांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् । श्रुशृणुष्यकृवृभ्य इति हेर्धिभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, त्वे (*tve*) means 'in you'. This seer Jaritā, the praiser, has become yours; the word अपि (*api*) is used in the sense of likelihood: he is now thought of as a praiser." Sāyaṇa gives the reason: "O son of strength, there is nothing else to be attained apart from you. So by praise I attain you alone, who are to be attained. Auspicious happiness, a warder-off of the three sorrows (त्रिवरूथं (*trivarūthaṃ*)), is with you." Or else: "a fine three-storeyed house is with you." Therefore: "Remove far from us, who are being harmed, your blazing flame. Drive it away, ward it off."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- त्वे (*tve*)—in you (yourself) **NOTE**
- आयं (*āyaṃ*)—this seer (this seer called Jaritṛ)
- जरिता (*jaritā*)—the praiser
- अभूदपि (*abhūdapi*)—has become
- सहसः (*sahasaḥ*)—of strength
- सूनो (*sūno*)—O Agni, the son
- अन्यत् (*anyat*)—other than you
- आप्यं (*āpyaṃ*)—a thing to be obtained
- नहि अस्ति (*nahi asti*)—there is none at all
- भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)—auspicious
- त्रिवरूथं (*trivarūthaṃ*)—removing the three kinds of sorrow
- शर्म (*śarma*)—happiness
- हि (*hi*)—for which reason
- ते (*te*)—with you
- अस्ति (*asti*)—there is; therefore
- हिंसानां (*hiṃsānāṃ*)—harmful to us **NOTE**
- आरे (*āre*)—far away
- दिद्युं (*didyuṃ*)—your flame, shining brightly
- अप आ कृधि (*apa ā kṛdhi*)—ward off

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, this seer called Jaritṛ, the seer of the mantra, praises you alone. O son of strength, apart from you there is nothing else for us to obtain. The happiness that is auspicious and that removes the three kinds of sorrow — ādhyātmika, ādhidaivika and ādhibhautika — is with you. Therefore ward off your fierce flame, which shines brightly far off and is harmful to us, so that it does not come near us.

##### English translation
This person, Agni, was your praiser, for there is nothing else attainable, O son of strength; holy is the happiness derived from you, a triple

### Printed p. 930

defence; remove far from us, who are susceptible of harm, your scorching flame.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the first six ṛks of this sūkta the forest fire is described in a manner that touches the heart. In the last two ṛks Agni is prayed that the forest fire may cause no harm to the poets or their houses, and that the regions all round their houses may be rich in water, grass and wood and so be safe from the danger of fire.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र॒वत्ते॑ अग्ने॒ जनि॑मा पितूय॒तः सा॒चीव॒ विश्वा॒ भुव॑ना॒  ॑
> न्यृंजसे ।  
> प्र सप्त॑यः॒ प्र स॑निषंत नो॒ धियः॑ पु॒रश्व॑रंति पशु॒पा इ॑व॒  ॑
> त्मना ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रवत् । ते । अग्ने । जनिम । पितुयतः । साचीइव । विश्वा । भुवना । नि । ऋंजसे ।  
> प्र । सप्तयः । प्र । सनिषंत । नः । धियः । पुरः । चरंति । पशुपाइव । त्मना ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने पितूयतः पितुमन्नं भक्ष्यमिच्छतस्ते तव जनिम जन्म प्रामर्भावं
> प्रवत्प्रकृष्टमुत्कृष्टं भवति ॥ उपसर्गाच्छंदसि धात्वर्थ इति वतिः ॥ स त्वं साजीव
> सचिव इव विश्वा विश्वानि व्याप्तानि भुवनानि भूतजातानि न्यृंजसे । प्रसाधयसि । वशीकरोषीत्यर्थः । सप्लयः सर्पणशीला नोऽस्माकं धियः स्तुतयस्तादृशं त्वां प्र
> सनिषंत । प्रकर्षण संभजंते । एकः प्रशब्दः पूरकः । यद्वा । सप्लयः । लुप्तोपममेतत् । सर्पणशीला अश्वा यथाजं प्रकर्षण संभजंते तथास्मदीया धिय
> इत्यर्थः । अनंतरं पुरस्तव पुरस्तात् त्मनात्मना स्वयमेव चरंति । व्याप्य वर्तंते ।
> पशुपा इव । यथा पशूनां पालका गोपालाः पालयितव्यानां पुरस्तात्संचरंति
> तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Agni, you who desire food (पितूयतः (*pitūyataḥ*): the food that is to be eaten), your birth, your manifestation, is excellent (प्रवत् (*pravat*)). Such as you are, you, like a minister (साजीव (*sājīva*) = सचिव (*saciva*)), bring all the beings that pervade the world under control (न्यृंजसे (*nyṛṃjase*): you accomplish, you subdue). Our praises, which move quickly (सप्लयः (*saplayaḥ*): of a moving nature), attain you eagerly (प्र सनिषंत (*pra saniṣaṃta*)); one प्र (*pra*) is a mere filler." Or else, सप्लयः (*saplayaḥ*) is a simile with its particle dropped: as swift horses are set forward eagerly, so are our praises. Then: "They go of their own accord (त्मना (*tmanā*)) before you, pervading, as herdsmen, the guardians of cattle, go ahead of those they must guard."

### Printed p. 931

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- पितूयतः (*pitūyataḥ*)—who desire food in the form of the oblation
- ते (*te*)—your
- जनिम (*janima*)—birth (manifestation)
- प्रवत् (*pravat*)—is excellent (such as you are)
- साजीव (*sājīva*)—like a minister
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all the classes of beings
- नृंजसे (*nṛṃjase*)—you bring under control
- सप्तयः (*saptayaḥ*)—going near you
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—praises
- प्र सनिषंत (*pra saniṣaṃta*)—come to you and join you
- सप्तयः (*saptayaḥ*) (alternative)—horses eager to rush forward
- प्र सनिषंत (*pra saniṣaṃta*) (alternative)—as they go and join the battlefield, our praises join you
- those praises, पुरः (*puraḥ*)—in front of his herd
- पशुपा इव (*paśupā iva*)—as a herdsman goes
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—of their own accord
- चरंति (*caraṃti*)—go and join Agni

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, your birth, you who desire food in the form of the oblation, is excellent. Like a minister you bring all beings under your control. Like horses eager to rush into the battlefield, our praises join you. And as a herdsman goes in front of his herd, our praises of their own accord come to you and join you.

##### English translation
Exalted is the birth of you, Agni, who are desirous of (sacrificial) food; you preside like a councillor over all created beings; our praises flowing smoothly proceed to you, as herdsmen of their own will (go slowly) before (their flocks).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त वा उ॒ परि॑ वृणक्षि॒ बप्स॑द्ब॒होर॑ग्न॒ उल॑पस्य स्वधावः ।  
> उ॒त खि॒ल्या उ॒र्वरा॑णां भवंति॒ मा ते॑ हे॒तिं तवि॑षीं चुक्रुधाम ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । वै । ऊं इति । परि । वृणक्षि । बप्सत् । बहोः । अग्ने । उलपस्य । स्वधावः ।  
> उत । खिल्याः । उर्वराणां । भवंति । मा । ते । हेतिं । तविषीं । चुक्रुधाम ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे स्वधावो दीप्तिमन्नग्ने बप्पद्दहन् ॥ भस भर्त्सनदीप्योः । चौहोत्यादिकः ।
> शतरि घसभसोहलि च । पा. ६-४-१०० । इत्युपधालोपः । नाभ्यस्ताच्छतुरिति नुमः
> प्रतिषेधः ॥ बहोर्बहुलस्कोलपस्य तृणजातस्य ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठि ॥ सर्वं वनमुत
> वा अपि खलु परि वृणक्षि । परिवर्जयसि । विनाशयसि । उ इति पूरकः । उतापि
> चोर्वराणां । सस्याढ्या भूमय उर्वराः । तासां संबंधिनः प्रदेशाः खिल्याः
> खिलाः प्राणिभिर्गंतुं योग्या भवंति । त्वया दग्ना इति शेषः । तविषीं महतीं ते तव
> हेतिं हननहेतुभूतां ज्वालां मा चुक्रुदाम । मा क्रोधयाम । अपि तु स्तुतिभिः
> प्रसाधयाम ॥ ऊतियूतीत्यादिना हंतेः क्तिनि हेतिरित्यंतोदात्तो निपात्यते ।
> चुक्रुदामेति क्रुदेर्ण्यंताल्लुजि चजि रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O blazing Agni (स्वधावः (*svadhāvaḥ*)), burning (बप्पद्दहन् (*bappaddahan*) — the root भस (*bhasa*) in the senses of threatening and shining), you destroy much grass (उलपस्य (*ulapasya*), a kind of grass; the genitive stands for the object): the whole forest. The particle उ (*u*) is a filler. And the regions belonging to the fertile, crop-rich lands (उर्वराणां (*urvarāṇāṃ*)) become खिल्याः (*khilyāḥ*), waste land, fit for beings to walk on; understand 'burnt by you'. We must not anger (मा चुक्रुदाम (*mā cukrudāma*)) your mighty flame, the cause of destruction; rather we appease it with praises."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वधावः (*svadhāvaḥ*)—shining
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni, you
- बहोः (*bahoḥ*)—abundant
- उलपस्य (*ulapasya*)—mass of grass
- उत वै (*uta vai*)—everything
- बप्सत् (*bapsat*)—devouring, that is, burning
- परि वृणक्षि (*pari vṛṇakṣi*)—you destroy
- उ (*u*)—certainty
- उत (*uta*)—and
- उर्वराणां (*urvarāṇāṃ*)—of the regions dense with crops and the like
- खिल्याः (*khilyāḥ*)—(burnt by you) they become open waste regions
- भवंति (*bhavaṃti*)—become (O Agni)
- ते (*te*)—your
- तविषीं (*taviṣīṃ*)—great
- हेतिं (*hetiṃ*)—flame, the cause of destruction
- मा चुक्रुधाम (*mā cukrudhāma*)—we shall not make it angry, that is, we shall quiet it with praises

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O shining Agni, you burn and destroy a great mass of grass. Regions that have grown dense with shrubs and trees, after being burnt by you, become open ground fit for creatures to move about in. O Agni, we shall not make your flame, which is able to destroy everything, angry.

##### English translation
Blazing Agni, you destroy many a shrub, as you burn; and (the sites) of the tilled fields are laid waste, many we never rouse to anger your terrible flame. **NOTE**

> य॒दा ते॒ वातो॑ अनु॒वाति॑ शो॒चिर्वप्ते॑व॒ श्मश्रु॑ वपसि॒ प्र  ॑
> भूम ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । उत् ऽवतः । निवतः । यासि । बप्सत् । पृथक् । एषि । प्रगर्थिनीऽइव । सेना ।  
> यदा । ते । वाशः । अनुवाति । शोचिः । वप्ताऽइव । श्मश्रु । वपसि । प्र । भूम ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्यदोद्वत उद्धतानुच्छ्रितान् निवतो नीचीनांस्तरुगुल्मादीन् हे अग्ने
> बप्सद्दहन्यासि प्राप्पोषि तदानीं बह्वीभिर्ज्वालाभिः पृथग्विभिन्नः सन्नेषि । गच्छसि ।
> तत्र दृष्टांतः । प्रगर्धिनीव सेना ॥ गृधु अभिकांक्षायां ॥ परराष्ट्रं गच्छतो
> राज्ञः सेना तत्रत्यं धनजातमभिकांक्षमाणेतस्ततः संघशो गच्छति तद्वत् । वातो
> वायुश्च ते तव शोचिः दीप्तिं यदा यस्मिन्कालेऽनुवाति अनुगुणं प्रवर्तते तदा
> श्मश्रु । श्म शरीरं । तत्र श्रितं स्थितं केशरोमादिकं वस्तेव यथा वप्ता नापितो
> वपति मुंडयति तथा भूम भूमिं प्र वपसि । प्रकर्षण मुंडयसि ! सर्वं वनं
> निःशेषेण दहसीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"When, O Agni, you go burning (बप्सत् (*bapsat*) = दहन् (*dahan*)) the trees and shrubs that are tall (उद्वतः (*udvataḥ*)) and low (निवतः (*nivataḥ*)), then you move divided (पृथक् (*pṛthak*)) in many flames." The illustration is प्रगर्धिनीव सेना (*pragardhinīva senā*): the army of a king marching into an enemy's country, eager for the wealth there, goes in bands this way and that. "When the wind follows your flame, then you shave the earth, as a barber (वप्ता (*vaptā*)) shaves (वपति (*vapati*)) the hair that stands on the body (श्म (*śma*) means body); you shave it clean (प्र वपसि (*pra vapasi*)). The meaning is that you burn the whole forest without remainder."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Agni) यत् (*yat*)—when
- उद्वतः (*udvataḥ*)—the trees and the like grown tall
- निवतः (*nivataḥ*)—the small bushes and creepers growing below
- बप्सत् (*bapsat*)—(devouring) burning
- यासि (*yāsi*)—you go forward; then
- प्रगर्धिनीव (*pragardhinīva*)—destroying everything that meets it
- सेना (*senā*)—like an army
- पृथक् (*pṛthak*)—separately (in many parts)
- एषि (*eṣi*)—you go and burn
- यदा (*yadā*)—when
- वातः (*vātaḥ*)—the wind
- ते (*te*)—your
- शोचिः (*śociḥ*)—radiance
- अनुवाति (*anuvāti*)—blows following; then
- श्मश्रु (*śmaśru*)—the hairs on the face
- वप्तेव (*vapteva*)—as a barber shaves
- भूम (*bhūma*)—the earth
- प्र वपसि (*pra vapasi*)—you burn everything and make it clean

### Printed p. 934
#### Ṛk 4 (continued)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, when you burn a forest, you go forward burning the trees that have grown tall and touch the clouds, and also the low plants and creepers that grow on the ground. Just as a king's army, after destroying its enemies, splits into many bands and plunders and ruins everything it meets, so you (Agni) advance burning the trees and shrubs that stand here and there, in many divisions. While you are burning the forest, if the wind also comes to your help (that is, if the wind blows), then, as a barber shaves the beard and moustache on the face perfectly smooth, you (Agni) burn all the trees and other growth on the earth completely and make it a bare open tract with nothing left.

##### English translation
When you move burning above and burning below, you scatter yourself like a devastating host; when the wind fans your flame. you shave the earth as a barber shaves a beard.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The rows of flames of this burning Agni are seen (प्रति ददृश्रे (*prati dadṛśre*), "are seen"). The passage that follows is abridged in print (dots) and part of it is not available; then "तव्वत् (*tavvat*)" ("like that"). Here, from the sense, a comparison is understood. O Agni, बाहू (*bāhū*) stands in the instrumental sense: you "cleanse" the whole forest with your arms, that is, with masses of flame that take the place of arms.**NOTE**

> मृजञ्ज्योधयन् । दहन्नित्यर्थः । न्यज् न्यंचन् प्रह्वीभवन्नुत्तानामूर्ध्वाभिमुखां भूमिं यद्यदान्नेषि अनुगच्छसि तदानीमस्य श्रेणयो ददृश्र इत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

मृजञ्ज्योधयन् (*mṛjañjyodhayan*): "cleansing" means burning. न्यज् (*nyaj*) means bending down, becoming low. When, Agni, you go along the earth that faces upward (उत्तानां (*uttānāṃ*)), then the rows of flames of this Agni are seen. Such is the construction.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni; you
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- बाहू (*bāhū*)—with your flames that are like arms
- अनुमर्मृज्यमानः (*anumarmṛjyamānaḥ*)—cleansing the forest, that is, burning it
- उत्तानां (*uttānāṃ*)—the earth furnished with tall trees and the like
- भूमिं (*bhūmiṃ*)—the earth
- न्यज् (*nyaj*)—making it level (by burning the trees and the rest)
- अन्वेषि (*anveṣi*)—you advance; then
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Agni
- श्रेणयः (*śreṇayaḥ*)—the burning rows of flames
- बहवः (*bahavaḥ*)—many
- रथासः (*rathāsaḥ*)—provided with chariots
- एकं नियानं (*ekaṃ niyānaṃ*)—like a moving line
- प्रति ददृश्रे (*prati dadṛśre*)—are seen

### Printed p. 935

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, when you go forward, burning with your many flames like arms the tall trees of the earth and levelling them, those many flames of yours shine like lines of an army, with many chariots going in a row, one beside another.

##### English translation
His lines (of flame) are visible, like one array of many chariots, when clearing away (the forests) with your arms (of flame) you march, Agni, over the prostrate earth.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उत्ते॒ शुष्मा॑ जिहता॒मुत्ते॑ अ॒र्चिरुत्ते॑ अग्ने शशमा॒नस्य॒  ॑
> वाजाः ।  
> उच्छ्वं॑चस्व॒ नि न॑म॒ वर्ध॑मान॒ आ त्वा॒द्य विश्वे॒ वस॑वः सदंतु ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । ते । शुष्माः । जिहतां । उत् । ते । अर्चिः । उत् । ते । अग्ने । शशमानस्य ।

### Printed p. 936

> उत् । श्वंचस्त्व । नि । नम । वर्धमानः । आ । त्वा । अद्य । विश्वे । वसवः । सदंतु ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने ते तव शुष्मा शोषका ज्वाला उज्जिहतां । उद्दच्छंतु । तथा ते
> तवार्चिर्दिप्तिश्चोद्गच्छतु । शशमानस्य स्तूयमानस्य । यद्वा ॥ शश प्लुतगतौ ।
> अस्मात्ताच्छिलिकश्चानश् । तस्य सार्वधातुकत्वे सति लसार्वधातुकत्वाभावाच्चित इत्यंतोदात्तत्वमेव शिष्यते ॥ शशमानस्य सर्वं वनमभिक्रम्य शीघ्रं गच्छतः । तव वाजा
> वेगा हे अग्ने उज्जिहतां । स त्वं वर्धमानः सन्नुच्छंचस्व । वन उद्दच्छस्व । श्वचि
> गतौ भौवादिकः । इदित्वान्नुम् ॥ तथा नि नम । प्रह्वीभव । उन्नतं वृक्षा दिकं
> प्राप्योच्छ्रितो भव । अवनतं गुल्मादिकं प्राद्यावनतो भवेत्यर्थः । ईदृशं त्वा
> त्वामद्यास्मिन्काले विश्वे सर्वॆ वसवो वासयितारो रश्मयो देवा ना सदंतु ।
> आसीदंतु । प्राप्नुवंतु ॥ सदेर्व्यत्ययेन सीदादेशाभावः । शपि प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेनाब्वा कर्तव्यः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, let your withering (शुष्मा (*śuṣmā*)) flames rise up (उज्जिहतां (*ujjihatāṃ*) = let them go up); and let your light also rise. शशमानस्य (*śaśamānasya*) means "of one who is praised". Or else: the root शश (*śaśa*) is in the sense of leaping motion, and from it comes the participle; of you who go quickly, advancing over the whole forest, let your speeds (वाजा (*vājā*) = swift movements) rise, O Agni. Growing thus, rise up (उच्छ्वंचस्व (*ucchvaṃcasva*)): go upward in the forest (the root श्वचि (*śvaci*) is in the sense of going, of the first class). Likewise नि नम (*ni nama*): bend low; that is, on reaching a high tree and the like, be raised up; on reaching low shrubs and the like, be lowered. Such as you are, today let all the Vasus, the rays or gods that cause (everything) to dwell, sit down by you, that is, attend you. The remaining remarks are on grammar.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- ते (*te*)—your
- शुष्माः (*śuṣmāḥ*)—burning flames
- उत् जिहतां (*ut jihatāṃ*)—let them rise up and shine
- ते (*te*)—your
- अर्चिः (*arciḥ*)—let your radiance also increase
- ते (*te*)—your
- शशमानस्य (*śaśamānasya*)—praiseworthy, or advancing after burning the forest
- वाजाः (*vājāḥ*)—let the praiseworthy, or swift, movements also increase (you who are such)
- वर्धमानः (*vardhamānaḥ*)—growing
- उत् श्वंचस्व (*ut śvaṃcasva*)—burn the tall trees in the forest
- नि नम (*ni nama*)—burn the small creepers and the like
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अद्य (*adya*)—now
- विश्वे (*viśve*)—all
- वसवः (*vasavaḥ*)—rays or gods
- आ सदंतु (*ā sadaṃtu*)—let them attend upon (you)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, let your burning flames rise higher and higher. Let your radiance also increase and spread. Let your praiseworthy course go forward. Growing, burn the tall trees and the creepers and the like, and move about, spreading sometimes on high and sometimes below. O Agni, may all the rays, or all the gods, now attend upon you.

##### English translation
May your withering flames, Agni, arise; may your light (arise), and the swift movements of you when you are praised; rise up: stoop down, increasing in might; may all the Vasus this day attend upon you.
