#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒पामि॒दं न्यय॑नं समु॒द्रस्य॑ नि॒वेश॑नं ।  
> अ॒न्यं कृ॑णुष्टे॒तः पंथां॒ तेन॑ याहि॒ वशा॒ अनु॑ ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अपां । इदं । निऽयनं । समुद्रस्य । निऽवेशनं ।  
> अन्यं । कृणुष्व । इतः । पंथां । तेन । याहि । वशान् । अनु ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इत्थं खांडववनस्य दाहे प्रवृत्तमग्निं जरितृप्रभृतयः स्वात्मनो रक्षणकामास्तुष्टुवुः । इदानीं च स्तंबमित्रः स्वनिवासभूमेर्दहनाभावायाग्नेरन्यत्र
> गमनं प्रार्थयते । इदमस्मदीयं निवासस्थानमपामुदकानां न्ययनं । नियंति
> नितरां गच्छंत्यस्मिन्निति न्ययनं ह्रदः । तथा समुद्रस्योदधेश्च निवेशनं गृहं । यथा
> ह्रदः समुद्रस्य स्थानं च यथा दग्धुं न शक्यते तथा दाहयोग्यं न भवत्वित्यर्थः ।
> इतोऽस्मादस्मदीयात्स्थानादन्यं पंथां पंथानं मार्गं हे अग्ने कृणुष्ट! कुरुष्व।
> तेन पथा वशाननु यथाकामं याहि । गच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In this way Jaritṛ and the others, wishing to protect themselves, praised Agni as he set about burning the Khāṇḍava forest. Now Stambamitra prays that Agni go elsewhere, so that the land where he lives may not be burned. "This dwelling-place of ours is the न्ययनं (*nyayanaṃ*) of the waters": न्ययनं (*nyayanaṃ*) is a lake, for into it (the waters) go down. Likewise it is the dwelling (निवेशनं (*niveśanaṃ*)), the house, of the ocean. The meaning is that, as a lake and the ocean's place cannot be burned, so let it not be fit for burning. O Agni, make (कृणुष्ट (*kṛṇuṣṭa*) = do) a path other than this, away from this place of ours. Go by that path as you please (वशाननु (*vaśānanu*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Agni) इदं (*idaṃ*)—this dwelling-place of ours
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—of the waters
- न्ययनं (*nyayanaṃ*)—the place of their meeting
- समुद्रस्य (*samudrasya*)—of the ocean
- निवेशनं (*niveśanaṃ*)—the house (your abode is, like the ocean, a mass of water, not fit to be burned; therefore)
- इतः (*itaḥ*)—(far) from our dwelling-place
- अन्यं पंथां (*anyaṃ paṃthāṃ*)—another path (on the path)
- कृणुष्व (*kṛṇuṣva*)—move about
- तेन (*tena*)—by that other path
- वशान् अनु (*vaśān anu*)—as you please
- याहि (*yāhi*)—go

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, this, that is our dwelling-place (house), is a meeting-place of waters, like the ocean; as it is not possible to burn the ocean, so do not burn our house. Therefore leave our dwelling-place and go as you please by another path, far away.

### Printed p. 938

##### English translation
This is the abode of the waters, the dwelling of the ocean ; pursue, Agni, a different path from this ; go by this (path) according to your pleasure.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Up to here, that is, in the six Ṛks of this sūkta, the seers Jaritṛ, Droṇa and Sārisṛkva have praised the forest fire in many ways. Now the seer Stambamitra, the seer of this Ṛk and of the next, prays that although Agni burns in other regions, he should not burn their own dwelling-place, but should leave it and go by another path. Although Agni burns all the kinds of trees and the like growing on the earth, he cannot burn the ocean, which is full of water. Therefore, as Agni leaves the ocean unburned and goes elsewhere, so the seer, giving the example of the ocean for his own house, prays Agni that he may go as he pleases by another path, leaving their house unburnt.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आय॑ने ते प॒राय॑णे॒ दूर्वा॑ रोहंतु पु॒ष्पिणीः॑ ।  
> प्र॒दाश्च॑ पुं॒डरी॑काणि समु॒द्रस्य॑ गृ॒हा इ॒मे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आऽअयने । ते । पराऽअयने । दूर्वाः । रोहंतु । पुष्टिणीः ।  
> ह्रदा । च । पुंडरीकाणि । समुद्रस्य । गृहाः । इमे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनयापि स्वनिवासस्य दाहानर्हता प्रतिपाद्यते । हे अग्ने ते तवायन
> आगमने परायणे परागमने वा सत्यस्यां निवासभूम् पुष्टिणीः पुष्पवत्यो
> दूर्वा रोहंतु । प्ररोहंतु । तथा ह्रदा अशोष्योदका जलाशयाश्च भवंतु ।
> पुंडरीकाणि पद्मानि च तेषु ह्रदेषु जायंतां । किं बहुना । समुद्रस्य जलधेरिमेऽस्मिन्निवासप्रदेशे गृहा आश्रयभूता भवंतु । यथा समुद्रावासभूमिः कदाचिदपि न दह्यते एवं कदाचिदप्यस्मत्स्थानं न दह्यतामित्यर्थः । एतदुक्तं भवति । दूर्वा-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By this Ṛk too the unfitness of his dwelling for burning is set forth. O Agni, at your coming (आयने (*āyane*)) or at your going away (परायणे (*parāyaṇe*)), on this dwelling-land let flowering durvā grasses grow. Likewise let there be lakes (ह्रदा (*hradā*)) whose water cannot dry up, and let lotuses (पुंडरीकाणि (*puṃḍarīkāṇi*)) be born in those lakes. What more? Let the houses on this dwelling-ground be shelters of the ocean (the sea). The meaning is: as the ocean's land of dwelling is never burned, so let our place never be burned. What is said is this: ...

### Printed p. 939

> कांडप्ररोहणप्रार्थनेन स्वाश्रयस्य शीतलत्वं ह्रदप्रार्थनेन तृष्णोपशमनकारणस्य
> जलस्य सत्त्वं पुंडरीकसद्भावप्रार्थनेनोपभोग्यस्य फलादेः सत्ता समुद्रगृहत्वप्रार्थनेन दाहानर्हता चेत्येतत्सर्वं प्रतिपाद्यत इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

... by praying for the growth of durvā shoots, coolness of his own shelter is set forth; by praying for lakes, the presence of water that quenches thirst; by praying for the existence of lotuses, the presence of fruits and other things to be enjoyed; by praying that the houses be the ocean's, unfitness for burning. All this is set forth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Agni) ते (*te*)—your
- आयने (*āyane*)—at the time of coming
- परायणे (*parāyaṇe*)—at the time of departure (going back), in our dwelling-places
- दूर्वाः (*dūrvāḥ*)—grass and other plants
- पुष्पिणीः (*puṣpiṇīḥ*)—putting forth flowers
- रोहंतु (*rohaṃtu*)—let them grow. Likewise
- ह्रदाः च (*hradāḥ ca*)—let the reservoirs (tanks, ponds) be full of water
- पुंडरीकाणि (*puṃḍarīkāṇi*)—(and in them) let lotuses grow
- इमे गृहाः (*ime gṛhāḥ*)—these houses of ours
- समुद्रस्य (*samudrasya*)—like the ocean, let them not be burned

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, both at your coming and at your going, let no kind of trouble befall our houses. Let grass and other plants grow luxuriantly, putting forth flowers. Let the reservoirs be full of water and shine with lotus flowers. As the ocean has no fear of fire, so let our houses also be safe, without fear of fire.

##### English translation
Both at your arrival, Agni, and at your departure. may the flowering durva grasses spring up; may lakes (be formed) and lotuses (therein); may these be the dwellings of the ocean.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The seer prays that although the forest fire burns the whole forest, it should not burn their dwelling-places. He expresses the assurance that, both while the forest fire burns the forests in the regions around their houses and afterwards, no fear of fire should come to them; that in the regions around the house grass, plants and the like should grow as they please and bear fruits and flowers; that the reservoirs should not dry up but be rich in water and shine with lotuses; and that, as the ocean has no fear of fire, so their houses too should be without fear of fire.

The supplementary mantras to be recited at the end of this sūkta:

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हिमस्य त्वा जरायुणा शाले परिव्ययामसि ।  
> उत ह्रदो हि नो धियोऽग्निर्ददातु भेषजं  
> ॥ ० ॥

### Printed p. 940
The supplementary mantras to be recited at the end of this sūkta (continued):

शीतप्रदो हि नो धियोऽग्निर्ददातु भेषजं । (*śītaprado hi no dhiyo 'gnirdadātu bheṣajaṃ |*) अंतिकामग्निमजनय दूर्वादः शशहागमत् ॥ २ ॥ (*aṃtikāmagnimajanaya dūrvādaḥ śaśahāgamat ‖ 2 ‖*)

अजातपुत्रपक्षाया हृदयं मम दूयते । (*ajātaputrapakṣāyā hṛdayaṃ mama dūyate |*) विपुलं वनं बह्वाकाशं चर जातवेदः कामाय ॥ ३ ॥ (*vipulaṃ vanaṃ bahvākāśaṃ cara jātavedaḥ kāmāya ‖ 3 ‖*)

मां च रक्ष पुत्रांश्च शरणमभूत्तव । (*māṃ ca rakṣa putrāṃśca śaraṇamabhūttava |*) पिंगाक्ष लोहितग्रीव कृष्णवर्ण नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ ४ ॥ (*piṃgākṣa lohitagrīva kṛṣṇavarṇa namo 'stu te ‖ 4 ‖*)

अस्मान्निबर्हरस्यॆनां सागरस्योर्मयो यथा । (*asmānnibarharasyènāṃ sāgarasyormayo yathā |*) इंद्रः क्षत्रं ददातु वरुणमभि षिंचतु ॥ ५ ॥ (*iṃdraḥ kṣatraṃ dadātu varuṇamabhi ṣiṃcatu ‖ 5 ‖*)

शत्रवो निधनं यांतु जय त्वं ब्रह्मतेजसा । ॥ ६ ॥ (*śatravo nidhanaṃ yāṃtu jaya tvaṃ brahmatejasā | ‖ 6 ‖*)

कपिलजटीं सर्वभक्षं चाग्निं प्रत्यक्षदैवतं ॥ ७ ॥ (*kapilajaṭīṃ sarvabhakṣaṃ cāgniṃ pratyakṣadaivataṃ ‖ 7 ‖*)

वरुणं च वशाम्यग्रे मम पुत्रांश्च रक्षतु । (*varuṇaṃ ca vaśāmyagre mama putrāṃśca rakṣatu |*) मम पुत्रांश्च रक्षत्वों नमः ॥ ८ ॥ (*mama putrāṃśca rakṣatvoṃ namaḥ ‖ 8 ‖*)

साग्रं वर्षशतं जीव पिब खाद च मोद च ॥ (*sāgraṃ varṣaśataṃ jīva piba khāda ca moda ca ‖*)

दुःखितांश्च द्विजांश्चैव प्रजां च पशु पालय ॥ १० ॥ (*duḥkhitāṃśca dvijāṃścaiva prajāṃ ca paśu pālaya ‖ 10 ‖*)

यावदादित्यस्तपति यावद्भाजति चंद्रमाः । (*yāvadādityastapati yāvadbhājati caṃdramāḥ |*) यावद्वायुः प्लवायति तावज्जीव जया जय ॥ ११ ॥ (*yāvadvāyuḥ plavāyati tāvajjīva jayā jaya ‖ 11 ‖*)

येन केन प्रकारेण को हि नाम नु जीवति । (*yena kena prakāreṇa ko hi nāma nu jīvati |*) परेषामुपकारार्थं यज्जिवति स जीवति । (*pareṣāmupakārārthaṃ yajjivati sa jīvati |*) एतां वैश्वानरीं सर्वदेवान्नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ १२ ॥ (*etāṃ vaiśvānarīṃ sarvadevānnamo 'stu te ‖ 12 ‖*)

न चोरभयं न च सर्पभयं न च व्याघ्रभयं न च मृत्युभयं । (*na corabhayaṃ na ca sarpabhayaṃ na ca vyāghrabhayaṃ na ca mṛtyubhayaṃ |*) यस्यापमृत्युर्न च मृत्युः सर्वं लभते सर्वं जयते ॥ (*yasyāpamṛtyurna ca mṛtyuḥ sarvaṃ labhate sarvaṃ jayate ‖*)

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan |*) पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*)

जाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकवर्गमार्गप्रवर्तक श्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्रापुरंधरेण सायणाचार्यॆण विचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाश (*jādhirājaparameśvaravaidikavargamārgapravartaka śrīvīrabukkabhūpālasāmrāpuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryèṇa vicite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśa*)
ऋक्संहिताभाष्येऽष्टमाष्टके सप्तमोध्यायः समाप्तः (*ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye 'ṣṭamāṣṭake saptamodhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ*)

Here ends the seventh adhyāya in the eighth aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, with Śrī Sāyaṇa's commentary and Kannada translation.

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्रुहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । (*yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātruhīnaṃ tu yadbhavet |*) शत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तुते ॥ (*śatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stute ‖*)

॥ श्रीः ॥ (*‖ śrīḥ ‖*) ॥ श्री गणाधिपतये नमः ॥ (*‖ śrī gaṇādhipataye namaḥ ‖*)

वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । (*vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame |*) यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥ (*yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖*)

यस्य निश्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । (*yasya niśvasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat |*) निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वं ॥ (*nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaṃ ‖*)

वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदध्याया सदाशिवः । (*vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedadhyāyā sadāśivaḥ |*) तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत्॥ (*tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet‖*)

सप्तमं श्रुतितत्त्वज्ञः ह्यष्टमस्याष्टकस्य च । (*saptamaṃ śrutitattvajñaḥ hyaṣṭamasyāṣṭakasya ca |*) व्याख्याय सायणामात्यो ह्यष्टकं व्याचिकीर्षति ॥ (*vyākhyāya sāyaṇāmātyo hyaṣṭakaṃ vyācikīrṣati ‖*)

Sāyaṇabhāṣya-sahitā Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Part 30.

॥ अथाष्टमाष्टकेऽष्टमोऽध्यायः ॥ (*‖ athāṣṭamāṣṭake 'ṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ ‖*) The eighth adhyāya in the eighth aṣṭaka.

## Sūkta 143 (Maṇḍala 10)
The one hundred and forty-third sūkta in the tenth maṇḍala.

**Introduction**

In this sūkta the seer Atri praises the Aśvin deities. We have already described in many places the various kinds of help and favour that the Aśvins have done for men and animals. In the present sūkta there is a description of the help given to the seer Atri and to a king named Bhujyu. There are many histories showing that they help people in times of distress; these have been explained at length in their own contexts. Even so, we explain here only a few of the principal ones.
**NOTE**

### Printed p. 942
जुजुरुषो नासत्योत वन्रिं प्रामुंचतं द्रापिमिव च्यवानात् । (*jujuruṣo nāsatyota vanriṃ prāmuṃcataṃ drāpimiva cyavānāt |*) प्रातिरतं जहितस्यायुर्दस्रादित्पतिमकृणुतं कनीनां ॥ (*prātirataṃ jahitasyāyurdasrāditpatimakṛṇutaṃ kanīnāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-10)

When the seer named Cyavana had become very old, his body decayed and without strength, his people abandoned him. When this seer prayed to the Aśvins, they came, removed his decayed body, made him a youth, made him dear to his wife, and increased his span of life; so it is said. Besides this—

युवं च्यवानमश्विना जरंतं पुनर्युवानं चक्रथुः शचीभिः । (*yuvaṃ cyavānamaśvinā jaraṃtaṃ punaryuvānaṃ cakrathuḥ śacībhiḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-13)

निष्पौग्र्यं पारयथः समुद्रात्पु नश्चवानं चक्रथयुर्युवानं । (*niṣpaugryaṃ pārayathaḥ samudrātpu naścavānaṃ cakrathayuryuvānaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-118-6)

प्र च्यवानाज्जु जुरुषो वन्त्रिमत्कं न मुंचथः । (*pra cyavānājju juruṣo vantrimatkaṃ na muṃcathaḥ |*) युवा यदी कृथः पुनरा काममृण्वे वध्वः ॥ (*yuvā yadī kṛthaḥ punarā kāmamṛṇve vadhvaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-74-5)

उत त्यद्वां जुरते अश्विना भूच्च्यवानाय प्रतीत्यं हविर्दे । (*uta tyadvāṃ jurate aśvinā bhūccyavānāya pratītyaṃ havirde |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-68-6)

युवं च्यवानं जरसोऽमुमुक्तं नि पेदव ऊहथुराशुमश्वं । (*yuvaṃ cyavānaṃ jaraso 'mumuktaṃ ni pedava ūhathurāśumaśvaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-71-5)

युवं च्यवानं सनयं यथा रथं पुनयुर्वानं चरथाय तक्षथुः ॥ (*yuvaṃ cyavānaṃ sanayaṃ yathā rathaṃ punayurvānaṃ carathāya takṣathuḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-39-4)

In these Ṛks too there is a description of how the aged seer Cyavana was made a youth. The Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa also has a long history on this subject. Likewise,

युवं विप्रस्य जरणामुपेयुषः पुनः कलेरकृणुतं युवद्वयः (*yuvaṃ viprasya jaraṇāmupeyuṣaḥ punaḥ kalerakṛṇutaṃ yuvadvayaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-39-8)

in this Ṛk there is mention of how the old age of one named Kali was removed and he was made a youth again.

याभिर्वम्रं विपिपानमुपस्तुतं कलिं याभिर्वित्तजानिं दुवस्यथः ॥ (*yābhirvamraṃ vipipānamupastutaṃ kaliṃ yābhirvittajāniṃ duvasyathaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-15)

### Printed p. 943
In this Ṛk it is said that when the Kali mentioned above took a wife and married, they gave him their aid and helped him in many ways.

And for the young women who were the wives of Vimada they granted a chariot (1-112-9), or else a wife for him (1-117-1). She appears to have been the daughter of Purumitra (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-20; 10-39-7), and her name was Kamadhyu (10-65-12).

To Viśvaka, the son of Kṛṣṇa, they brought back and restored his lost son (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-16-23; 10-65-12). And in Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-75-1, 2, 3 the names of Viśvaka and Viṣṇāpu are indicated.

The story of Bhujyu is told again and again. Bhujyu was the son of a king named Tugra. While he was voyaging on the sea and sinking, he floated holding on to a piece of wood amid the waves. Then he took refuge with the Aśvins. They came there, seated him in a ship with a hundred oars on the boundless great ocean, and took him to his home. In another place the matter is described thus: they seated Bhujyu in a ship without any cracks that seemed to fly in the sky, or in four winged boats, or in three flying chariots with a hundred feet and six horses, or in their own chariot swift as thought, speeding with the help of their horses, and so brought him and reached his house. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-3, 4, 5; 1-117-14, 15; 1-182-5, 6, 7; 7-68-7; 1-112-6, 20; 1-118-6; 1-119-4; 1-158-3; 7-62-6; 7-69-7; 8-5-22; 10-39-4; 10-47-7; 10-65-12; 10-153-5)

When the leg of a woman named Viśpalā was cut off in battle and she prayed to the Aśvins, they came, provided her with an iron leg and saved her; this is said in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-10; 1-116-15; 1-117-11; 1-118-8; 10-39-8.

When the Aśvins' mount, the ass (rāsabha), was in the form of a wolf, one named Ṛjrāśva cut up a hundred sheep from the flock he was guarding and gave them to that wolf as food. His father was angered at this and had Ṛjrāśva's eyes torn out, making him blind. Then the wolf praised the Aśvins; they were pleased and gave eyes to Ṛjrāśva (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-16; 1-117-17, 18). In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-17 there is mention of this Ṛjrāśva praising Indra.

One named Pārāvṛja was blind and lame, and he was not admitted into his caste. The Aśvins gave him sight to see and strength to walk; that is, they favoured him by giving him eyes

### Printed p. 944
and legs (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-8). When Indra is the subject, the name of Pārāvṛja is indicated in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-13-12; 2-15-7.

The seer named Rebha had been bound hand and foot by wicked men and thrown into a ruined well. For nine days and ten nights he lay there, near death. The Aśvins lifted him out of the well, as Soma juice is lifted with a ladle, and gave him life (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-5; 1-116-24; 1-117-12; 1-117-4; 7-118-6; 1-119-6; 10-39-9).

One named Vandana, likewise carried off by wicked men and thrown into a dark place (a pit), was rescued from the danger by the Aśvins and brought into the light (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-5; 1-16-11; 1-1 7-1; 1-118-6; 10-39-5; 1-119-6, 6).
**NOTE**

To Kakṣīvān of the line of Pajra they gave boons in plenty, and from a horse's hoof they poured out hundreds of jars full of liquor or honey, as if pouring through a sieve (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-7; 1-117-6).

The seer Atri was thrown by the Asuras, out of hatred and envy, into a great gorge covered in darkness and blazing with fire. When he was in distress there and prayed to the Aśvins, they came, quenched the fire with frost, gave him food and so on, comforted him, and rescued him from that state. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-7; 1-116-8; 1-117-3; 1-118-7; 1-119-6; 5-78-4, 5, 6; 7-71-5; 8-62-3, 7, 8, 9; 10-39-9) In Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-3 it is said that he protected Atri.

A woman named Vadhrimatī, being childless and barren, prayed to the Aśvins, and they granted her a son named Hiraṇyahasta. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-13; 1-117-24; 6-62-7; 10-39-7)

A woman named Ghoṣā, afflicted with leprosy, remained unmarried in her father's house. At her prayer the Aśvins granted her a suitable husband. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-7; 0-39-3, 6; 10-4-5). In the commentary on Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-7 Sāyaṇa says that this woman Ghoṣā was suffering from leprosy and that the Aśvins came and cured that disease. In the tenth maṇḍala there are two sūktas seen by this woman Ghoṣā (sūktas 39 and 40).
**NOTE**

When the cow of one named Śayu was old and bore no calf, the Aśvins made her able to give milk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-22; 1-117-20; 1-118-8; 1-119-7; 10-39-13)

### Printed p. 945
It is said that the Aśvins gave to the king Pedu a white horse as mighty as Indra, and that with it he conquered his enemies and obtained abundant goods, vehicles and so on. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-6; 1-117-9; 1-118-9; 1-119-10; 7-21-5; 10-39-10)

Besides, it is said that these Aśvins helped many men and also benefited animals, birds and the like. In this connection, when a wolf was carrying off a quail in its mouth, they freed it from the wolf's mouth at the quail's prayer and saved it; this is said in many Ṛks (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-14; 1-117-16; 1-118-8; 10-39-13). Besides these there are many other matters concerning the Aśvins; they have been explained in their own contexts.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दशमे मंडल एकादशेऽनुवाके चतुर्दश सूक्तानि व्याकृतानि । त्यं चिदिति
> षडृचं पंचदशं सूक्तं संख्यॆपुत्रस्यात्रेरार्षमानुष्टुभमश्विदेवताकं । तथा
> चानुक्रांतं । त्यं षट् सांख्योऽत्रिराश्विनमिति ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोरानुष्टुभे छंदसीदं सूक्तं । सूत्र्यते हि । आ नो विश्वाभिस्तं चिदत्रिमित्यानुष्टुभं ।
> आ. ४-१५ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the tenth maṇḍala, in the eleventh anuvāka, fourteen sūktas have been explained. The fifteenth sūkta, त्यं चित् (*tyaṃ cit*), has six Ṛks; its seer is Atri, son of Saṃkhyā, its deity the Aśvins, its metre Anuṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says त्यं षट् सांख्योऽत्रिराश्विनमिति (*tyaṃ ṣaṭ sāṃkhyo 'trirāśvinamiti*). The sūkta is used in the Prātaranuvāka and in the Aśvina-śastra in the Anuṣṭubh metre; the sūtra reads आ नो विश्वाभिस्तं चिदत्रिमित्यानुष्टुभं (*ā no viśvābhistaṃ cidatrimityānuṣṭubhaṃ*) (Āśvalāyana, 4-15).

##### Anuvāda

In the eleventh anuvāka of the tenth maṇḍala the first fourteen sūktas were explained in the previous adhyāya. In this adhyāya the explanation goes on from the fifteenth sūkta. This sūkta, beginning त्यं चित् (*tyaṃ cit*), is the fifteenth in the eleventh anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Its seer is Atri, son of Saṃkhyā; its deity the Aśvins; its metre Anuṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says त्यं षट् सांख्योऽत्रिराश्विनं (*tyaṃ ṣaṭ sāṃkhyo 'trirāśvinaṃ*). In reciting the Prātaranuvāka and the Aśvina-śastra mantras, the sūkta is used for the Ṛks in Anuṣṭubh metre, as the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra shows by the sūtra आ नो विश्वाभिस्त्यं चिदत्रि मित्यानुष्टभं (*ā no viśvābhistyaṃ cidatri mityānuṣṭabhaṃ*) (Ā. 4-15).

Sūkta 143. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 143. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 1. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6. Seer: Atri, son of Saṃkhyā. Deity: the Aśvins. Metre: Anuṣṭubh.

### Printed p. 946
#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्यं चि॒दत्रि॑मृत॒जुर॒मर्थ॒मश्वं॒ न यात॑वे ।  
> क॒क्षीवं॑तं॒ यदी॒ पुना॒ रथं॒ न कृ॑णु॒थो नवं॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्यं । चित् । अत्रिं । ऋतजुरं । अर्थं । अश्वं । न । यातवे ।  
> कक्षीवंतं । यदि । पुनरिति । रथं । न । कृणुधः । नवं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विन् शतद्वारे पीडायंत्रगृहेऽसुरैः प्रक्षिप्तो बद्धांगो योऽत्रिरस्ति
> त्यं चित्तमप्यत्रिमृतजुरं ! ऋतं स्तोत्रं यज्ञो ना । तेन जीर्यंतं । सर्वदा
> युवयोः परिचरणशीलमित्यर्थः ॥ जीर्यतेः क्विपि बहुलं छंदसीत्युत्वं ॥ यद्वा।
> ऋतेन प्राप्तेनासुरकृतोपद्रवेण ज्वरितं रुग्णं ॥ ज्वर रोगे । ज्वरत्वरेत्यादिना
> वकारस्योपधायाश्च स्थान ऊट् । जूरी हिंसागत्योरित्यस्माद्वा क्विप् । अनयोः
> पक्षयोश्चांदसो ह्रस्वः ॥ ईदृशं तमत्रिमर्थमर्थनीयं प्राप्तव्यं यातने गंतुं
> युवां कृतवंतौ । तत्र दृष्टांतः । अश्वं न । यथाश्वो बंधनाद्विमुक्तः सन् शीघ्रं
> गच्छति एवमयमपि युवयोः प्रसादादसुरकृतादुपद्रवजाताद्विमुच्यमानो
> यथास्थानमगच्छदित्यर्थः ॥ या प्रापण इत्यस्मात्तुमर्थे सेसेनिति तवेन्प्रत्ययः ॥
> यदि । अपि चेत्यर्थः । कक्षीवंतं । कक्ष्या रज्जुरश्वस्य । तद्वंतं ॥ आसंदीवदष्टिवदित्यादौ निपातनात्संप्रसारणं ॥ दीर्घतमसः पुत्रमुशिक्प्रसूतनृषिं मंदबुद्धिं
> संतं युवां पुनर्नवं पुनरभिनवप्रज्ञं कृणुथः । अकृणुतं । अकुरुतं । रथं न ।
> यथा कश्चिच्छिल्वी जीर्णं रथं पुनरभिनवं करोति तद्वत् ॥ कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च ।
> इदित्वान्नुम् । लजिर्थॆ व्यत्ययेन लट् । धिन्विकृण्ज्योरच्चेत्युप्रत्ययः । तत्संनियोगेनाकारांतादेशश्च । तस्यातो लोपे सति स्थानिवद्भावाल्लघूपधगुणाभावः । सति
> शिष्टोऽपि विकरणस्वरो लसार्वधातुकस्वरं न बाधते । म. ६-१-१५८-११ । इति वचनात्तिज एव स्वरः शिष्यते । निपातैर्यद्यदिहंतेति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, that Atri who was thrown by the Asuras into a torture-house with a hundred doors, his limbs bound, त्यं चित् (*tyaṃ cit*) that same Atri is ऋतजुरं (*ṛtajuraṃ*): ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*) is praise or sacrifice, by which he grows old; that is, he is always given to serving you. Or else ऋतजुरं (*ṛtajuraṃ*) means one made feverish and sick by the affliction caused by the Asuras. You have made him अर्थं (*arthaṃ*), one to be sought, fit to go (यातवे (*yātave*)). The example: अश्वं न (*aśvaṃ na*); as a horse freed from its bonds goes swiftly, so he too, released by your grace from the troubles made by the Asuras, went to his proper place. यदि (*yadi*) means "even if". कक्षीवंतं (*kakṣīvaṃtaṃ*): कक्ष्या (*kakṣyā*) is a horse's rope; one possessing it. He is the son of Dīrghatamas, born of Uśij, a seer who was dull of mind; you make him again new, newly wise, as a craftsman makes an old chariot new again. (The remainder of the block is grammar.)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतजुरं (*ṛtajuraṃ*)—(O Aśvins) one grown old in body while praising you
- त्यंचित् (*tyaṃcit*)—the well-known
- अत्रिं (*atriṃ*)—the seer Atri, the seer of this sūkta
- अश्वं न (*aśvaṃ na*)—like a horse that was tied up

### Printed p. 947
(The Pratipadārtha continues from the previous page.) As a horse that has been untied runs off, so, to go to the place where he should go, you freed him from the Asuras. And as a craftsman repairs a broken chariot, you made Kakṣīvān, the dull-witted ṛṣi, new again, that is, a newly wise man.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a horse whose rope is loosed goes where it will, you always praised only your own selves; you freed the famous Atri, grown old in body, from the bondage of the Asuras and made him go to his own place. As a craftsman repairs a worn-out chariot and makes it new, you made Kakṣīvān, the dull-witted ṛṣi, a wise, new ṛṣi.

##### English translation
You made this Atri, ever diligent in worship, (swift) to run to the goal like a horse, and you renewed Kakshivat as (a wheelwright renews) a car.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The Asuras' troubling of the ṛṣi Atri is told in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-7; 1-116-8, 1-117-3, 1-118-7, 1-119-6, 5-78-4, 5, 6; 7-71-5, 8-62-3, 7, 8, 9; 10-39-9, and others. But who is this Atri? Opinions differ on whether he is the ṛṣi Atri Bhauma, the seer of the 5th Maṇḍala, or the Atri son of the ṛṣi Sāṃkhya who is the seer of the present sūkta. In the 5th Maṇḍala the ṛṣi Atri nowhere says this of himself. Only the ṛṣi Saptavadhri of the Atri family describes this matter, in Ṛks 4, 5, 6 of Sūkta 78 of the 5th Maṇḍala. In other places there are many descriptions of it, but in all of them only "the ṛṣi Atri" is said, so it is not clear which Atri is meant. Still, since the ṛṣi of the present sūkta, Atri Sāṃkhya, himself tells the matter, one may guess that this ṛṣi is the one meant here.

In this Ṛk the matter is set forth through one illustration in the first half and one in the second. As a horse tied with a rope runs off freely as soon as it is untied, so the ṛṣi Atri, bound with ropes, thrown into a house of torture and suffering many kinds of cruel torment from the Asuras, was set free by the Aśvin deities, who came to him. Thereby the ṛṣi Atri became free from bondage and had the opportunity to go to any place he wished.

### Printed p. 948
The second half mentions the ṛṣi Kakṣīvān. This ṛṣi was a son of the famous ṛṣi Dīrghatamas. He was dull-witted. As a craftsman repairs a broken chariot and makes it new, so the Aśvin deities made the ṛṣi Kakṣīvān, who was devoid of understanding, that is, of little intelligence, a man of wisdom (intelligent).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्यं चि॒दश्वं॒ न वा॒जिन॑मरे॒णवो॒ यमत्न॑त ।  
> दृ॒ढं ग्रं॒थिं न वि ष्य॑त॒मत्रिं॒ यवि॑ष्ठ॒मा रजः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्यं । चित् । अश्वं । न । वाजिनं । अरेणवः । यं । अत्यत ।  
> दृढं । ग्रंथिं । न । वि । स्यतं । अत्रिं । युविष्ठं । आ । रजः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अरेणवोऽहिंस्यमानाः प्रबला असुरा वाजिनं वेगवंतमश्वं नाश्वमिव
> यमत्रिमत्नत अतन्वत बद्धमकृषत ॥ तनोतेर्लुजि तनिपत्योश्चंदसीत्युपधालोपः॥
> त्यं चित्तं चात्रिं यविष्ठं युवतमं स्तुतेर्मिश्रयितृतमं वा रजः ॥ रजंत्यस्मिञ्चना
> इति रजो भूलोकः ॥ रज इमं लोकमाभि हे अश्विन् वि ष्यतं । व्यमुंचतं ।
> दृढं स्थिरतरं ग्रंथिं न ग्रंथिमिव । यथा कश्चित्ताद्यशं ग्रंथिमयत्नेन विमुंचति तथा
> युवां तम्मषिमसुरकृताद्बंधनान्नोचितवंतावित्यर्थः ॥ स्यतमिति षोऽंतकर्मणीत्यस्माल्लजि श्यन्योतः श्यनीत्योकारलोपे रूपं । छांदसोऽडभावः ॥ यद्वा ।
> अत्रिं मां बंदाद्वि ष्यतं विमुंचतमित्यृषिरसुरैर्बद्धः सन्नश्विनौ प्रार्थयते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The unharmed, that is, mighty Asuras bound the Atri whom they had bound, as one binds a swift, speedy horse; अतन्वत (*atanvata*) means "they stretched out", that is, made him bound. That same Atri, the youngest or most youthful, or the one who mingles most closely with praise, to this world (rajas). The word अरेणवः (*areṇavaḥ*) and the "rajas" are explained: रजंत्यस्मिञ्चना इति (*rajaṃtyasmiñcanā iti*), so rajas is the earthly world. O Aśvins, you loosed him; दृढं ग्रंथिं न (*dṛḍhaṃ graṃthiṃ na*): as someone looses a knot of such a kind, firm and fixed, without effort, so you two released that ṛṣi from the bondage made by the Asuras. Or else: the ṛṣi, bound by the Asuras, begs the Aśvins, "Release me, Atri, from the bond."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—swift-going
- अश्वं न (*aśvaṃ na*)—as one ties a horse with a rope
- अरेणवः (*areṇavaḥ*)—the mighty Asuras
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Atri ṛṣi
- अत्यत (*atyata*)—they had bound with ropes
- त्यं चित् (*tyaṃ cit*)—the famous, and
- यविष्ठं (*yaviṣṭhaṃ*)—the very young
- अत्रिं (*atriṃ*)—Atri
- आ रजः (*ā rajaḥ*)—as moving freely over the earth
- दृढं (*dṛḍhaṃ*)—firmly tied
- ग्रंथिं न (*graṃthiṃ na*)—as one unties a knot
- भविष्यत (*bhaviṣyata*)—you released **NOTE**

### Printed p. 949

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, as one ties a swift horse with a rope so that it does not run away, so the mighty Asuras had bound the youthful ṛṣi Atri with ropes. O Aśvin deities, you loosed the strong knots of the rope that bound that ṛṣi Atri and made him free of bondage.

##### English translation
This Atri, whom the irresistible (Asuras) dragged bound like a swift horse, you unloosed like a strong knot, (setting him) the youngest born upon the earth.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नरा॒ दंसि॑ष्ठा॒ पत्र॑ये॒ शुभ्रा॒ सिषा॑सतं॒ धियः॑ ।  
> अथा॒ हि वां॑ दि॒वो न॑रा॒ पुनः॒ स्तोमो॒ न वि॒शसे॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नरा । दंसिष्ठा । अत्रये । शुभ्रा । सिसासतं । धियः ।  
> अथ । हि । वां । धिवः । नरा । पुनरिति । स्तोमः । न । विशसे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे नरा नर नेतारौ हे दंसिष्टौ दर्शनीयतमौ शुभ्रा शोभमानौ ईदृशौ
> हे अश्विन् आत्रय ऋषये मह्यं धियः कर्माणि बुद्धीर्वा सिषासतं । दातुमिच्छतं ॥
> षणु दाने ॥ यद्वा। आत्रय इति षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी । अत्रेर्मम धियः स्तुतीः
> कर्माणि वा सिषासतं । संभक्तुमिच्छतं । सेवेथामित्यर्थः ॥ वन षण संभक्तौ ।
> अस्मात्सनतेः सनोतेर्वा सनि सनीवंतर्धोति विकल्पनादिडभावे जनसनखनामित्यात्वं ।
> शुभ्रेत्यस्यामंत्रितस्यामंत्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवदित्यविद्यमानवत्वेन पदादपरत्वेन पादादित्वात्तिज्ञतिज इति निघाताभावः । अदुपदेशालसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे
> सनो नित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ अथा ह्यनंतरमेव दिवः । दीव्यतीति स्तूतीति द्यौः
> स्तोता । तस्य मम स्तोमो न । नशब्दश्चार्थे । स्तोत्रं च हे नरा नेतारावश्विनौ
> वां युवां पुनर्विशसे । पुनरेवाद्यापि विशेषेण शंसितुं प्रभवतीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O leaders, most beautiful and radiant ones, such as you are, O Aśvins, you desired to give me, the ṛṣi Ātreya, धियः (*dhiyaḥ*), that is, rites or understandings; सिषासतं (*siṣāsataṃ*) means "wish to give", from the root षणु दाने (*ṣaṇu dāne*). Or else: आत्रय (*ātraya*) is a dative in the sense of a genitive; you wished to share in, that is, to attend to, the praises or rites of me, Atri; the root is वन षण संभक्तौ (*vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau*). Then, immediately after, दिवः (*divaḥ*): one who praises is द्यौः (*dyauḥ*), the praiser; of that me, the praise too, O leader Aśvins, is able to praise you again, in particular, even now; "is able" is to be supplied.

### Printed p. 950

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नरा (*narā*)—leaders of rites
- दंसिष्ठौ (*daṃsiṣṭhau*)—of attractive form
- शुभ्रा (*śubhrā*)—shining with pure radiance; O Aśvin deities, you
- अत्रये (*atraye*)—to me, named Atri
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—understandings (salutary counsels)
- सिषासतं (*siṣāsataṃ*)—wished to give [or: अत्रेः (*atreḥ*)—of me, Atri; धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—praises or rites; सिषासतं (*siṣāsataṃ*)—wished to attend to]
- अथ हि (*atha hi*)—afterwards
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of me who am praising
- स्तोमः न (*stomaḥ na*)—the praise too
- नरा (*narā*)—you who are leaders
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- विशसे (*viśase*)—praises

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, leaders of rites, of attractive form, shining with divine radiance, you wished to give me, the ṛṣi Atri, counsels, that is, discernment; or you wished to listen to my praises. Afterwards my praise, as I praise you, also praises you, the leaders.

##### English translation
Leaders (of rites), of goodly aspect and radiant, deign to accept Atri's praises, and so the praise of your worshipper (is) to be sung again to you leaders (of rites).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> चि॒ते तद्वां॑ सुराधसा रा॒तिः सु॑म॒तिर॑श्विना ।  
> आ यन्नः॒ सद॑ने पृ॒थौ सम॑ने॒ पर्ष॑थो नरा ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> चिते । तत् । नां । सुराधसा । रातिः । सुमतिः । अश्विना ।  
> चि । यत् नः । सदने । पृथौ । समने । पर्षथः । नरा ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सुराधसा शोभनदानावश्विना हे अश्विन् सुमतिः शोभना स्तुतिरस्मदीया
> रातिर्हनिर्दानं च तत्तस्मात्कारणाद्दां युवयोश्चित्ते ज्ञानाय भवति ॥ चिती

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, givers of good gifts, our good praise and our offering and gift are, for that reason, for your चिते (*cite*), that is, for knowledge; the word चिती (*citī*) is explained on the next page.

### Printed p. 951

> संज्ञाने । अस्मात्संपदादिलक्षणो भावे क्विप् । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥
> यद्यस्मात्कारणात्सदने यज्ञगृहे पृथौ विस्तीर्णे समने यज्ञे नोऽस्मान् हे
> नरा नेतारावा पर्षथः आपूरयथः अभितो रक्षथो वा तस्माद्युवामस्मदीयं
> परिचरणं ज्ञातवंतावित्यनुमीमहे ॥ पृ पालनपूरणयोरित्यस्माल्लेटि सिब्बहुलमिति.
> सिप् । ततः शप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

चिती संज्ञाने (*citī saṃjñāne*): from this root, kvip in the sense of the action. Because, O leader Aśvins, you fill up or protect us in the broad sacrificial house and at the sacrifice, therefore we infer that you have taken note of our service.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुराधसा (*surādhasā*)—givers of excellent wealth
- नरा (*narā*)—leaders
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- यत् (*yat*)—for which reason
- पृथौ (*pṛthau*)—spacious
- सदने (*sadane*)—in the sacrificial house
- समने (*samane*)—in the sacrifice being performed there
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- आ पर्षथः (*ā parṣathaḥ*)—you protect
- तत् (*tat*)—for that reason
- वां (*vāṃ*)—to you
- चिते (*cite*)—there is understanding in our matter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, givers of excellent wealth and leaders of rites, you have understanding (or a mind of favour) in our matter. For in our spacious sacrificial house and in the sacrificial rites you protect us so that no hindrance befalls us.

##### English translation
Munificent Ashwins, my offering and praise (is) for your recognition because, leaders (of rites), you protect us at the sacrifice in the spacious sacrificial hall.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यु॒वं भु॒ज्यं स॑मु॒द्र आ रज॑सः पा॒र ईं॑खि॒तं ।  
> या॒तमच्छा॑ पत॒त्रिभि॒र्नास॑त्या सा॒तये॑ कृतं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> युवं । भुज्यं । समुद्रे । आ । रजसः । पारे । ईंखितं ।  
> यातं । अच्च । पतत्रिभिः । नासत्या । सातये । कृतं ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 952

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ युवं युवां समुद्र उदधौ निमग्नं रजस उदकस्य पारे
> प्रांते तरंगसमूह ईंखितं डोलायितं एवंभूतं भुज्युं तुग्रपुत्रमच्छाभि
> पतत्रिभिः पक्षोपेतैर्नौर्विशेषैः सहा यातं । आगतवंतौ स्थः । अगत्य च हे नासत्या
> सत्यस्य नेतारौ सत्यस्वभावौ वा हे अश्विनौ सातये युवयोः संभजनाय समर्थं
> कृतं । पुनर्युवानं कुरुतं ॥ करोतेर्लजि छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक्! अडभावश्च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, you came to Bhujyu, son of Tugra, who was sunk in the ocean, at the edge (end) of the water, tossed in the mass of waves, with winged ships, that is, special boats with wings; having come, O Nāsatyas, leaders of truth or of true nature, you made him fit for your service, you made him young again. For कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*) Sāyaṇa notes a Vedic form of the root *karoti* in the lṛṭ-substitute लजि (*laji*) with dropping of the vikaraṇa and absence of aṭ.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- युवं (*yuvaṃ*)—you
- समुद्रे (*samudre*)—in the sea
- रजसः पारे (*rajasaḥ pāre*)—at the edge of the waters, that is, fallen amid the waves
- ईंखितं (*īṃkhitaṃ*)—struggling
- भुज्युं (*bhujyuṃ*)—Bhujyu, son of Tugra
- अच्छ (*accha*)—coming to face him
- पतत्रिभिः (*patatribhiḥ*)—by your boats that are like wings
- आ यातं (*ā yātaṃ*)—you brought him; then
- नासत्या (*nāsatyā*)—O Aśvin deities, of true nature
- सातये (*sātaye*)—so that he be able to praise you
- कृतं (*kṛtaṃ*)—you made that Bhujyu

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, Bhujyu, son of Tugra, had fallen amid the waves in the sea and was struggling; with the help of your boats that are like wings you rescued him and brought him from there, and you made that Bhujyu able to praise you.

##### English translation
You came with winged (steeds) to Bhujyu (immersed) in the ocean, at the world's end, perturbed ; and, leaders of truth, you restored him to your worship.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The matter of the Aśvin deities saving Bhujyu from the middle of the sea we have explained in the introduction to this sūkta and in other places. This matter is also told in the following Ṛks: Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-3, 4, 5; 1-117-14, 15; 1-182-5, 6, 7; 7-68-7; 1-112-6, 20; 1-118-6; 1-119-4; 1-158-3; 6-62-6; 7-69-7; 8-5-22; 10-39-4; 10-47-7; 10-65-12; 10-143-5.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ वां॑ सु॒मैः शं॒यू इ॑व॒ मंहि॑ष्ठा॒ विश्व॑वेदसा ।

### Printed p. 953

> समस्मै भूषतं नरोत्सं न पिप्युषीरिषः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । वां । सुम्मैः । शंयूऽइवेति शंयूऽइव । मंहिष्ठा । विश्ववेदसा ।  
> सं । अस्मे इति । भूषतं । नरा । उत्सॆं । न । पिप्युषीः । इषः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे विश्ववेदसा सर्वज्ञौ सर्वधन् वा हे नरा नेतारौ वां युवां शंयू
> इव सुखयुक्तौ राजानाविव मुंहिष्ठा दातृतमावतिशयेन पूज्यौ ना संतौ सुम्मैरस्मभ्यं दातवैः सुखैः सार्धमा । उपसर्गश्रुतेर्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः । आगच्छतं।
> यद्वा । उपसर्गस्य भूषतमित्यनेन संबंधः । मुंहिष्ठेत्यपि संबोधनं । हे
> मुंहिष्ठा दातृतमावुक्तगुणावश्विन् वां युवां सुम्मैः सार्ध० शंयू इवास्मे
> अस्मान् सम्यगा भूषतं । अभिप्राप्णुतं ॥ भू प्राप्तौ । अस्माल्लोटि व्यत्ययेन
> सिप्युषौ ॥ भूष अलंकारे ॥ आ समंतात्सम्यग्भूषतं । अलंकुरुतं ! पिप्युषीः प्रवृद्धानीष इष्यमाणानि पयांस्युत्सं न । गोरूध इव । यथा बहुभिः पयोभिरूधोऽलंकृतं सद्दृश्यते अस्मानप्येवं बहुभिर्धनैरलंकुरुतमित्यर्थः ॥ पिप्युषीरिति
> प्यायतेर्लिटः क्वसुः । लिड्यजोश्चेति पीभावः । जसि वा छंदसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः॥
> यद्वा ! उत्सः प्रवाहो यथा पिप्युषीर्वृद्धानीषोऽन्नान्यलंकरोति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O all-knowing (or all-wealthy) leaders (नरा (*narā*)), you two, like kings endowed with happiness, are most generous (मंहिष्ठा (*maṃhiṣṭhā*)), exceedingly worthy of honour. Come with the comforts that are to be given to us. The prefix आ (*ā*) requires a suitable verb to be supplied, आगच्छतं (*āgacchataṃ*) ("come"). Or else the prefix is construed with भूषतं (*bhūṣataṃ*), and मंहिष्ठा (*maṃhiṣṭhā*) is again a vocative: O most generous Aśvins of the stated qualities, along with your comforts, like the two kings of happiness, come to us on all sides, reach us (root भू (*bhū*) in the sense of obtaining; the Lot form arises by irregularity). Or, from the root भूष (*bhūṣa*) in the sense of adorning: adorn us. "Abundant, desired milk" (पिप्युषीः (*pipyuṣīḥ*) = swollen, इषः (*iṣaḥ*) = desired milks) is like a spring (उत्सं न (*utsaṃ na*)), like a cow's udder: as an udder is seen adorned with much milk, so adorn us too with much wealth. Or else: as a stream (उत्सः (*utsaḥ*)) adorns with abundant swollen foods, so you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्ववेदसा (*viśvavedasā*)—you who are all-knowing, or endowed with all wealth
- नरा (*narā*)—leaders of the rite
- शंयू इव (*śaṃyū iva*)—like kings endowed with happiness
- मंहिष्ठा (*maṃhiṣṭhā*)—worthy of honour, or most generous; O Aśvin deities
- वां (*vāṃ*)—you
- पिप्युषीः (*pipyuṣīḥ*)—abundant
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—milks
- उत्संन (*utsaṃna*)—as they adorn a cow's udder
- सुम्मैः (*summaiḥ*)—with the comforts and riches to be given to us
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- आ भूषतं (*ā bhūṣataṃ*)—adorn; that is, come to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, all-knowing or possessed of all wealth, leaders of the rite, worthy of honour like kings endowed with happiness, or most generous: as an udder is filled with abundant milk and adorned, so adorn us also with many kinds of comforts and riches; that is, graciously come to us in order to give us comforts and riches.

### Printed p. 954

##### English translation
Prosperous, most adorable, all-knowing, come to us and decorate us with blessings, as a (cow's) udder is adorned with abundant food.

## Sūkta 144 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Introduction. The seer of this sūkta is said to be Suparṇa, son of Tārkṣya. For sūkta 128 of this same maṇḍala Tārkṣya is said to be the deity, and his son named Ariṣṭanemi the seer of that sūkta. Therefore a detailed account of Tārkṣya, Suparṇa and Ariṣṭanemi is necessary here.
Yāska in his Nirukta explains the derivation of the word Tārkṣya thus: तार्क्ष्यस्त्वष्टा व्याख्यातः । तीर्णे अंतरिक्षे क्षियति । तूर्णमर्थं रक्षति, अश्नो तेर्वा ॥ (*tārkṣyastvaṣṭā vyākhyātaḥ | tīrṇe aṃtarikṣe kṣiyati | tūrṇamarthaṃ rakṣati, aśno tervā ‖*) (Ni. 10-27).
The word Tārkṣya has been explained earlier, that is, when the word Tvaṣṭā was explained: त्वष्टा तूर्णमश्नुत इति नैरुक्ताः । त्विषेर्वा स्याद्दीप्तिकर्मणस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात् करोटिकर्मणः (*tvaṣṭā tūrṇamaśnuta iti nairuktāḥ | tviṣervā syāddīptikarmaṇastvakṣatervā syāt karoṭikarmaṇaḥ*) (Ni. 8-14). The explanation of the word Tvaṣṭā applies to the word Tārkṣya. The Nairuktas say that the name Tvaṣṭā exists because he pervades quickly; or the word Tvaṣṭā may be derived from the word त्वषि (*tvaṣi*), meaning "shine", or from the root त्वक्षति (*tvakṣati*), meaning "make".
The meaning of the word Tārkṣya is similar. Because the deity called Tārkṣya dwells in the vast atmosphere, he is called Tārkṣya; or the name has come because he protects water in the atmosphere, or because he pervades the atmosphere. In the Bṛhaddevatā: स्त्रीर्णेऽन्तरिक्षे क्षियति यद्वा तूर्णं क्षरत्यस् । अरिस्ट्पनेमिस्तार्क्ष्यर्षिस्तार्क्ष्यं तेनैवमुक्तवान् ॥ (*strīrṇe 'ntarikṣe kṣiyati yadvā tūrṇaṃ kṣaratyas | arisṭpanemistārkṣyarṣistārkṣyaṃ tenaivamuktavān ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 2-58).

### Printed p. 955
The seer named Ariṣṭanemi Tārkṣya has said that this deity has the name Tārkṣya because he dwells in the vast region of the atmosphere, or moves swiftly, or sprinkles water. Moreover it may be noted that the words सुपर्ण (*suparṇa*), तार्क्ष्य (*tārkṣya*), दधिक्राः (*dadhikrāḥ*) are read among the names of the horse (Ni. 2-22).
Explanation of the word Suparṇa. The word सुपर्ण (*suparṇa*) is read both among the names of rays (Ni. 2-15) and among the names of the horse (Ni.2-27) **NOTE**. And सुपर्णः सुपतना आदित्यरश्मयः (*suparṇaḥ supatanā ādityaraśmayaḥ*) (Ni. 4-3) and (Ni. 3-12): it is explained as the rays of the sun, which pervade quickly.
Explanation of the word Ariṣṭanemi. रथचक्रस्य धारा नेमिः । अरिष्टो ऽ हिंसतो नेमिर्यस्य । यत्संबंधिनो रथस्य नेमिर्न हिंस्यते सो ऽरिष्टनेमिः ॥ (*rathacakrasya dhārā nemiḥ | ariṣṭo ' hiṃsato nemiryasya | yatsaṃbaṃdhino rathasya nemirna hiṃsyate so 'riṣṭanemiḥ ‖*). Nemi means the chariot wheel. Ariṣṭanemi means one whose chariot wheels are unharmed, that is, unobstructed, of irresistible motion; this is the meaning. Skandasvāmin has explained the word nemi as the thunderbolt weapon. Ariṣṭanemi is the name of a seer, a son of Tṛkṣa. This seer, under the name Ariṣṭanemi Tārkṣya, is the seer of sūkta 178 of the 18th maṇḍala **NOTE**. Since the seer of the present sūkta is said to be Suparṇa Tārkṣya, it may be said that Suparṇa and Ariṣṭanemi are both sons of Tṛkṣa.
Tārkṣya means the son of Tṛkṣa. The commentator has given the meaning Garutmān, Garuḍa. This word indicates Āditya himself. Some say that Tṛkṣa means Kaśyapa; since Āditya is his son, Āditya himself is called Tārkṣya. Some hold that Tārkṣya is the horse of the world of the gods (दधिक्राः (*dadhikrāḥ*)), and that the sun himself is praised in this form. Others say he is the son of Tṛkṣi, a descendant of Trasadasyu. In the Khila mantras (2-4-1) and in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 10-7) the meaning "the best of birds", "a particular bird", is indicated for the word Tārkṣya. The meaning of this word remains doubtful. For Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-178 Tārkṣya himself is the deity.
On the word Suparṇa, we may see the explanation we wrote earlier in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 12, p. 421, and on the deity Tārkṣya the explanation in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 5, p. 681.

### Printed p. 956

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं हीति षडृचं षोडशं सूक्तं तार्क्ष्यपुत्रस्य सुपर्णस्यार्षं यमगोत्रस्योर्ध्वकृशनस्य वा ! आद्या गायत्रि द्वितीया बृहती तृतीयाचतुर्थ्यौ
> गायत्र्यौ पंचमी सतोबृहती षष्ठि विष्टारपंक्तिरष्टकद्विर्द्वादशाष्टकवती ।
> अनादेशपरिभाषयेंद्रो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । अयं हि तार्क्ष्यपुत्रः
> सुपर्णो यामायनो वोर्क्ष्यकृशनो गायत्रि बृहती गायत्र्यौ सतोबृहती
> विष्टारपंक्तिरिति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning अयं हि (*ayaṃ hi*) has six Ṛks and is the sixteenth sūkta. Its seer is Suparṇa, son of Tārkṣya, of the Yama lineage, or Ūrdhvakṛśana. The first Ṛk is Gāyatrī, the second Bṛhatī, the third and fourth Gāyatrī, the fifth Satobṛhatī, the sixth Viṣṭārapaṅkti, having eight, twelve, twelve and eight syllables. The deity is Indra, by the rule that applies where none is stated. He quotes the Anukramaṇī to this effect: अयं हि तार्क्ष्यपुत्रः सुपर्णो यामायनो वोर्क्ष्यकृशनो गायत्रि बृहती गायत्र्यौ सतोबृहती विष्टारपंक्तिरिति ॥ (*ayaṃ hi tārkṣyaputraḥ suparṇo yāmāyano vorkṣyakṛśano gāyatri bṛhatī gāyatryau satobṛhatī viṣṭārapaṃktiriti ‖*). The viniyoga has been given.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning अयं हि (*ayaṃ hi*) is the sixteenth sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Suparṇa, son of Tārkṣya, or Ūrdhvakṛśana of the Yama lineage. Since the Anukramaṇī does not name the deity, Indra can be said to be the deity of this sūkta. The first, third and fourth Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Gāyatrī metre; the second Ṛk is in Bṛhatī; the fifth in Satobṛhatī; the sixth in the metre called Viṣṭārapaṅkti. A Ṛk of this metre has four pādas, of which the first and last have eight syllables each and the second and third twelve syllables each. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: अयं हि तार्क्ष्यपुत्रः सुपर्णो यामायनो वोर्थ्वकृशानो गायत्रि बृहती गायत्र्या सतोबृहती विष्टारपंक्तिः (*ayaṃ hi tārkṣyaputraḥ suparṇo yāmāyano vorthvakṛśāno gāyatri bṛhatī gāyatryā satobṛhatī viṣṭārapaṃktiḥ*). The viniyoga has been stated earlier.
Sūkta 144. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 144. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 2. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6. Seer: Suparṇa, son of Tārkṣya, or Ūrdhvakṛśāna, of the Yāmāyana line. Deity: Indra. Metre: 1, 3, 4 Gāyatrī; 2 Bṛhatī; 5 Satobṛhatī; 6 Viṣṭārapaṅkti.
#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं हि ते॒ अम॑र्त्य॒ इंदु॒रत्यो॒ न पत्य॑ते ।  
> दक्षो॑ वि॒श्वायु॑र्वे॒धसे॑ ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 957

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । हि । ते । अमत्यर्त्यः । इंदुः । अत्यः । न । पत्यते ।  
> दक्षः । विश्वआयुः । वेधसे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वेधसे विधात्रे ते तुभ्यं त्वदर्थममर्त्यो मरणरहितोऽमृतत्वप्रापकोऽयं ह्ययं खल्विंदुः सोमोऽत्यो न सततगाम्यश्व इव पत्यते । गच्छति ।
> यद्वा। पत्यतिरैश्वर्यकर्मा । तव स्वभूतोऽयं सोमो वेधसे विधानाय मदस्य
> करणायेष्टे । कीदृश इंदुः । दक्षः प्रवृद्धो बलहेतुर्वा विश्वायुर्विश्वैः सर्वैरेतव्यः प्राप्तव्यः । यद्वा । विश्वेषामायुर्जीवनहेतुः । अथवा । आयुरित्यन्ननाम ।
> सर्वैश्चरुपुरोडाशादिभिरन्नॆर्हविर्भिरुपेतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, for you, the creator (वेधसे (*vedhase*)), this Soma (इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*)), immortal, conferring immortality, goes (पत्यते (*patyate*)) like a swift horse that runs continually. Or else: पत्यति (*patyati*) is a root meaning lordship; this Soma, your own, is desired for the creation (विधानाय (*vidhānāya*)), for the making of intoxication. What kind of Soma? दक्षः (*dakṣaḥ*): grown strong, or the cause of strength; विश्वायुः (*viśvāyuḥ*): to be approached by all; or, the cause of life for all; or else आयुः (*āyuḥ*) is a name for food, so: provided with all oblations of food, such as cooked cakes and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) अमूर्त्यः (*amūrtyaḥ*)—deathless, and one who bestows the state called immortality
- दक्षः (*dakṣaḥ*)—giver of strength
- विश्वायुः (*viśvāyuḥ*)—desired by all, or the giver of food that is the cause of life for all
- इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*)—Soma
- ते (*te*)—for you
- वेधसे (*vedhase*)—to the creator of the world
- अत्यः न (*atyaḥ na*)—like a swiftly moving horse
- पत्यते (*patyate*)—goes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, Soma, deathless, bestower of immortality on others, giver of nourishment, desired by all or the giver of food that is the cause of life for all, goes for you to Prajāpati, the creator of the world, like a swiftly moving horse.

##### English translation
This immortal Soma, the giver of strength, the giver of long life to all, hastens like a swift horse to you (Indra), the creator.
#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यम॒स्मासु॒ काव्य॑ ऋ॒भुर्वज्रो॒ दास्व॑ते ।  
> अ॒यं बि॑भत्र्मू॒र्ध्वकृ॑शनं॒ मद॑मृ॒भुर्न कृत्व्यं॒ मदं॑ ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 958

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । अस्मासु । काव्यः । ऋभुः । वज्रः । दास्वते ।  
> अयं । बिभर्ति । ऊर्ध्वकृशनं । मदं । ऋभुः । न । कृत्त्वं । मदं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्मासु स्तोतृषु काव्यः स्तुत्योऽयमिंद्रः ऋभुर्दिप्तः सन्दास्वते दानयुक्ताय यजमानाय वज्रः शत्रूणां वर्जको भवति । यद्वा । दास्वत इति

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Among us the praisers, this Indra, worthy of praise (काव्यः (*kāvyaḥ*)), shining (ऋभुः (*ṛbhuḥ*)), becomes the thunderbolt (वज्रः (*vajraḥ*)), the destroyer of enemies, for the sacrificer who gives (दास्वते (*dāsvate*)). Or else, as to दास्वते (*dāsvate*), the sentence continues in the next block.

> षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी । अस्मासु दास्वते दानवत इंद्रस्य वज्रः कुलिश ऋभुरुरु
> भासमानो भवति । अपि चायमूर्ध्वकृसनमुद्धततैक्ष्ममेतत्संज्ञं वा यामायनमृषिं मदं स्तोतारं बिभर्ति । पोषयति । तथर्भुर्न सौधन्वनः । पुत्राणामाद्य
> ऋभुः । स इव कृत्वं कर्मणां कर्तारं अत एव मदं मोदयि:कारं यजमानं
> बिभर्ति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Or else दास्वते (*dāsvate*) is a dative used in the sense of the genitive: among us, of the generous Indra, the thunderbolt (कुलिश (*kuliśa*)) becomes greatly shining. Moreover this Indra bears, that is, nourishes, the seer called Ūrdhvakṛśana, of exalted sharpness, or of that name, of the Yāmāyana line, the praiser (मदं (*madaṃ*)). Like Ṛbhu, son of Sudhanvan, who is the first of the sons, he bears the sacrificer, the doer of rites (कृत्वं (*kṛtvaṃ*)), and therefore the one who gives delight (मदं (*madaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्मासु (*asmāsu*)—among us who praise
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this Indra
- काव्यः (*kāvyaḥ*)—worthy of praise
- दास्वते (*dāsvate*)—of Indra, the giver of what is wished
- वज्रः (*vajraḥ*)—the thunderbolt
- ऋभुः (*ṛbhuḥ*)—shines brightly; [or: अस्मासु (*asmāsu*)—among the praisers; काव्यः (*kāvyaḥ*)—praised; अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this Indra; ऋभुः (*ṛbhuḥ*)—shining brightly; दास्वते (*dāsvate*)—for the sacrificer who offers oblation; वज्रः (*vajraḥ*)—becomes a destroyer of enemies like the thunderbolt]
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this Indra
- मदं (*madaṃ*)—the praiser
- ऊर्ध्वकृशनं (*ūrdhvakṛśanaṃ*)—the seer named Ūrdhvakṛśana, son of Yama (me)
- बिभर्ति (*bibharti*)—bears and nourishes (and)
- ऋभुः न (*ṛbhuḥ na*)—like Ṛbhu, son of Sudhanvan
- कृत्वं (*kṛtvaṃ*)—the performer of rites (therefore)
- मदं (*madaṃ*)—he nourishes the sacrificer who gives you delight

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Among us who praise, this Indra is worthy of praise. The thunderbolt of this Indra shines brightly. Or else this Indra, praised and shining brightly among the praisers, becomes for the sacrificer who offers oblation a destroyer of enemies like the thunderbolt. This Indra bears and nourishes the seer called Ūrdhvakṛśana, the praiser, son of Yama, and also the sacrificer who, like Ṛbhu, son of Sudhanvan, gives delight to Indra by performing rites.

### Printed p. 959

##### English translation
This (Indra), adorable among us and brilliant, is a thunderbolt for
the donor (of the oblation against his foes); he cherishes the exhilarating
(worshipper) Urdhwakrishana, as Ribhu (cherishes) the exhilarating celebra-
tor of holy rites.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> घृषुः॑ श्ये॒नाय॒ कृत्व॑न आ॒सु स्वासु॒ वंस॑गः ।  
> अव॑ दीधेदही॒शुवः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> घृषुः । श्वेनाय । कृत्वने । आसु । स्वासु । वंसगः ।  
> अव । दिधेत् । अहीशुवः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> फृषुर्घर्षयिता दीप्तो वा स्वासु स्वकीयास्वासु यजमानलक्षणासु प्रजासु
> वंसगो वननीयगतिः एवंभूत इंद्रः कृत्वने कर्मणां कर्त्रॆ ॥ करोतेरन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यंत इति क्वनिप् ॥ श्येनाय सुपर्णाय तार्क्ष्यपुत्राय मह्यमृषयेऽहीशुवोऽहीनव्यापनानहीनवृद्धीन्वास्मदीयान्पुत्रादीनव दीधेत् । दीपयतु ॥
> दीधीज् दीप्ति देवनयोः । अस्माच्छांदसे लिजि व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं ॥ यद्वा । हे
> इंद्र त्वदीयः सोमो फृष्ट्यादिगुणयुक्तः सन् दीप्यत इति योज्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

फृषुः (*phṛṣuḥ*) means one who harasses (the foe), or one who is brilliant. स्वासु (*svāsu*) means "among his own" subjects, who take the form of the sacrificers. वंसगः (*vaṃsagaḥ*) means one whose going is lovely. Such an Indra is meant. कृत्वने (*kṛtvane*) means "to the doer of rites" (the form ends in kvanip, since such forms are seen with other roots too). श्येनाय (*śyenāya*) means to Suparṇa, the son of Tārkṣya, that is, to me, the seer. अहीशुवः (*ahīśuvaḥ*) means those pervading without decline, or increasing without decline, that is, our sons and the like. May Indra make them shine (अव दीधेत् (*ava dīdhet*) = "let him illumine"). The root is दीधीज् (*dīdhīj*), "to shine, to play"; the parasmaipada form comes from this root by Vedic interchange in the perfect. Or else: O Indra, your Soma, endowed with such qualities as *phṛṣṭi*, shines; so it should be construed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- फृषुः (*phṛṣuḥ*)—the brilliant one
- स्वासु (*svāsu*)—among his own
- आसु (*āsu*)—among these subjects, beginning with the sacrificers
- वंसगः (*vaṃsagaḥ*)—Indra, who is a benefactor
- कृत्वने (*kṛtvane*)—to the doer of sacrifice and other rites
- श्वेनाय (*śvenāya*)—to me, the son of Tārkṣya, called Suparṇa
- अहीशुवः (*ahīśuvaḥ*)—undiminishing wealth, or the line of sons and the like
- अव दीधेत् (*ava dīdhet*)—may he give and make shine

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, who is brilliant and a benefactor to his own people, the sacrificers and others, give me, the son of Tārkṣya, the doer of sacrifices and other rites, called Suparṇa, undiminishing wealth or the line of sons and the like, and make it shine

### Printed p. 960
and flourish.

##### English translation
May the brilliant (Indra), who is a benefactor amongst these his own
(people), for the sake of Suparna, the offerer of the oblation, bestow light
upon our prgeny.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यं सु॑प॒र्णः प॑रा॒वतः॑ श्ये॒नस्य॑ पु॒त्र आभ॑रत् ।  
> श॒तच॑क्रं॒ यो॒३॒॑ ३ हो॑ ९ वर्त॒निः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यं । सुपर्णः । परावतः । श्येनस्य । पुत्रः । आ । अभरत् ।  
> शत्चक्रं । यः । अह्यः । वर्तनिः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शैनस्य तार्क्ष्यस्य पुत्रस्तनयः सुपर्णो यं सोमं परावतः परागताद्दूराद्दुलोकादाधॆरत् आहरत् । कीदृशं । शतचक्रं । शतमिति बहुनाम । बहुधनस्य
> कर्तारं ॥ मूलनिभुजादित्वात्कप्रत्पयः । पा. ३-२-५-२ ॥ यद्वा । शतकरणसाधनं ।
> बहुयागनिष्पादनमित्यर्थः ॥ घञार्थे कविधानम् । पा. ३-३-५८-४ । इति कप्रत्ययः ।
> कृञादीनां के । का. ६-१-१२-१ । इति द्विर्वचनं । यः सोमोऽहोऽहेर्वृत्रस्य
> वर्तनिर्वर्तयिता प्रेरयिता । यद्वा ॥ अह गतौ ॥ अह्यो गंतव्यो वर्तनिर्मार्गभूतः । एना वय इति वक्ष्यमाणेनैकवाक्यता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Suparṇa, the son of Śyena (Tārkṣya), brought that Soma from far away, from the heavenly world. Of what sort? शतचक्रं (*śatacakraṃ*): *śataṃ* is a word for "many"; the maker of much wealth (the affix ka). Or else: the instrument of doing a hundred, that is, the accomplisher of many sacrifices (the affix ka in the sense of ghañ; reduplication). The Soma that is the वर्तनिः (*vartaniḥ*), the impeller, the one who sets going, of अही (*ahī*), that is Vṛtra. Or else (root अह (*aha*), "to go"): अह्यः (*ahyaḥ*) is "to be gone to", and वर्तनिः (*vartaniḥ*) is that which is the road; it is to be construed together with the following एना वयः (*enā vayaḥ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- श्येनस्य (*śyenasya*)—of Tārkṣya
- पुत्रः (*putraḥ*)—the son
- सुपर्णः (*suparṇaḥ*)—Suparṇa
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Soma
- परावतः (*parāvataḥ*)—from heaven, situated in a distant region
- आभरत् (*ābharat*)—he carried off and brought
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Soma
- अह्यः (*ahyaḥ*)—of Vṛtra
- वर्तनिः (*vartaniḥ*)—the impeller (construed with the next Ṛk)

### Printed p. 961

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma that Suparṇa, the son of Tārkṣya, brought from the distant region, heaven, and the Soma that is the impeller of Vṛtra,

##### English translation
The Soma whom Suparna, the son of the falcon, brought from afar,
the bestower of many boons, who is the stimulator of Ahi.—

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यं ते॑ श्ये॒नश्चारु॑मवृ॒कं प॒दाभ॑रदरु॒णं मा॒नमंध॑सः ।  
> ए॒ना वयो॒ वि ता॒र्यायु॑र्जी॒वस॑ ए॒ना जा॑गार बं॒धुता॑ ॥५॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यं । ते । श्येनः । चारुं । अवृकं । पदा । आ । अभरत् । अरुणं । मानं । अंधसः ।  
> एना । वयः । वि । तारि । आयुः । जीवसे । एना । जागार । बंधुता ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं श्येनः सुपर्णः पक्षिराड्यं सोमं पदा । वचन
> व्यत्ययः । पद्भामाभरत् द्युलोकादाहरत् । दिवं सुपर्णो गत्वाय सोमं
> वज्रिण आभरत् । ऋ. ८-१००-८ । इति निगमांतरं । कीदृशं । चारुं शोभनं अवृकं
> बाधकरहितं अरुणमरोचमानमरुणवर्णं ना अंधसोऽन्नस्य मानं यागद्वारा
> निर्मातारं । एनैतेनानेन सोमेन तुभ्यं दीयमानेन वयोऽन्नं जीवसे
> जीवनायायुर्जीवितं च वि तारि । प्रादायि । तथैनैतेनैव सोमेन बंधुता बंधुसमूहो जागार । जाग्रत्प्रबुद्धः सन्वर्तते ॥ जागतेर्लिट छंदसि वेति वक्तव्यं ।
> पा. ६-१-८-१ । इति द्विर्वचनाभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, for you Śyena, that is Suparṇa, the king of birds, brought from the heavenly world that Soma "with the feet" (पदा (*padā*) is an interchange of number for "with the two feet"). Another Vedic passage, Ṛ. 8-100-8, says: दिवं सुपर्णो गत्वाय सोमं वज्रिण आभरत् । (*divaṃ suparṇo gatvāya somaṃ vajriṇa ābharat |*). Of what sort is the Soma? चारुं (*cāruṃ*), beautiful; अवृकं (*avṛkaṃ*), free of harm; अरुणं (*aruṇaṃ*), shining, ruddy in colour; मानं अंधसः (*mānaṃ aṃdhasaḥ*), the one who through the sacrifice constructs the food. By this Soma, being given to you, food (वयः (*vayaḥ*)) and life-span (आयुः (*āyuḥ*)) were bestowed (वि तारि (*vi tāri*)) for living. And likewise by this same Soma the circle of kinsmen is awake (जागार (*jāgāra*)), is alert. The absence of reduplication here follows the rule that the perfect of *jāgṛ* may be left unreduplicated in the Veda.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) ते (*te*)—for you
- श्येनः (*śyenaḥ*)—Suparṇa, the best of birds
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Soma
- पदा (*padā*)—holding it with his feet
- आ अभरत् (*ā abharat*)—brought from the heavenly world; such a Soma as is
- चारुं (*cāruṃ*)—beautiful
- अवृकं (*avṛkaṃ*)—free of harm
- अरुणं (*aruṇaṃ*)—of an aruṇa (dull red)

### Printed p. 962
colour
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—of the food in the form of the sacrificial oblation, that is, of the Soma juice
- मानं (*mānaṃ*)—the constructor
- एना (*enā*)—by which Soma juice offered for you
- जीवसे (*jīvase*)—for living
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—food
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—and life-span (the time of living)
- वि तारि (*vi tāri*)—was given by you
- एना (*enā*)—by such a Soma
- बंधुता (*baṃdhutā*)—the mutual kinship between Indra and the worshippers, as praised and praiser
- जागार (*jāgāra*)—grows, awakened

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the Soma that Suparṇa, the best of birds, brought for you from heaven, holding it with the claws of his feet, beautiful, free of harm, of ruddy colour, used in the sacrifice as the oblation: because this Soma juice is offered to you, you are satisfied and give us food so that we may live long. And because such Soma is offered to you, the mutual kinship between Indra and the worshippers, the relation of the praised and the praiser, grows.

##### English translation
Whom the falcon brought to you (Indra) with his claw, beautiful,
unassilable, purple-tinted, the measurer of food—by it, food and old age was
prolonged for living, by it affinity was awaked.

> क्रत्वा॒ वयो॒ वि ता॒र्यायुः॑ सुक्रतो॒ क्रत्वा॒यम॒स्मदा सु॒तः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । तत् । इंद्रः । इंदुना । देवेषु । चित् । धारयाते । महि । त्यजः ।  
> क्रत्वा । वयः । वि । तारि । आयुः । सुक्रतो इति सुक्रतो । कृत्वा । अयं । अस्मत् ।  
> आ । सुतः ॥ ६ ॥

> चिद्देवेष्टस्मासु च महि महत्यजस्तेजो दुःखस्य वर्जयित्कृ रक्षणं ना धारयाते ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

एव (*eva*) means in the manner just stated. Indra, being satisfied by that Soma (इंदुना (*iṃdunā*)), bears (धारयाते (*dhārayāte*)) among the gods and also among us great (महि (*mahi*)) *ajaḥ*, that is, brilliance, or protection that averts sorrow.

### Printed p. 963

> धारयति । शिष्टः प्रत्यक्षकृतः । हे सुक्रतो शोभनकर्मन्निंद्र क्रत्वा क्रतुनास्माभिरनुष्ठितेन कर्मणा प्रीतेन त्वया वयोऽन्नमायुर्जीवनं च वि तारि । अस्मभ्यं
> प्रादायि । योऽयमिंदुः क्रत्वा कर्मणा प्रज्ञानेन वास्मदस्माभिरा सुतोऽभिषुतः ।
> यद्वा । अस्मदस्मत्तस्त्वदाभिमुख्येन सुतः प्रेरितः तेनेंदुनेत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

धारयति (*dhārayati*), he bears. **NOTE**. O Sukratu, doer of good deeds, Indra, by the rite (क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)) performed by us you are pleased, and food (वयः (*vayaḥ*)) and life-span (आयुः (*āyuḥ*)) were bestowed (वि तारि (*vi tāri*)) on us. This Indu has been pressed out (आ सुतः (*ā sutaḥ*)) by us, by the rite or by knowledge. Or else: अस्मत् (*asmat*), from us, it has been pressed, sent forward in your direction; the construction is "by that Indu".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एव (*eva*)—in this manner
- (यः (*yaḥ*)) अयं (*ayaṃ*)—which Soma juice
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—together with the sacrificial rites, or by the knowledge enjoined
- अस्मत् (*asmat*)—by us
- आ सुतः (*ā sutaḥ*)—was pressed; such
- तत् इंदुना (*tat iṃdunā*)—satisfied by that Soma
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- देवेषु चित् (*deveṣu cit*)—among the gods and among us, the worshippers
- महि (*mahi*)—great
- त्यजः (*tyajaḥ*)—protection that destroys sorrow
- धारयते (*dhārayate*)—he provides
- सुक्रतो (*sukrato*)—O Indra, the doer of excellent deeds
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—by you, pleased by the rite we perform
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—food and the like
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—and increase of life
- वि तारि (*vi tāri*)—let them be given

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, satisfied by drinking the Soma juice pressed and offered by us together with the performance of the sacrifice, provides protection that removes sorrow both for the gods and for us, the worshippers. O Indra, doer of excellent deeds, pleased by the rite we perform, favour us by giving food and the like and also long life.

##### English translation
So then by Indu Indra obtains among the gods great brilliancy; by our sacrifice, O doer of good deeds, food and old age is prolonged, by our sacrifice, this (Soma) is poured out by us.

## Sūkta 145 (Maṇḍala 10)
In this sūkta Indrāṇī, the seer of the sūkta, in order to remove the affliction caused by her co-wife (सपत्नी (*sapatnī*)), a rival wife, and in order that her husband's love, turned away from the rival, may be directed toward herself, describes the method of digging up and using a kind of herb called pāṭhā, and praises that herb. This is a kind of abhicāra rite. In the work called Ṛgvidhāna it is said as follows.

### Printed p. 964

> इमामिति तु सूक्तेन शतकृत्तो दशावरं ।
> सपत्नीं बाधते तेन पतिश्चातीव मन्यते ॥ ६४ ॥
> पतिस्तु परिजप्यैनां पाठामेतेन वै पिबेत् ।
> पयसा सप्तरात्रं तु सपत्नान्प्रतिभाधते ॥ ६५ ॥
> मूलमंत्रजपैरन्यॆर्या पतिं जेतुमिच्छति ।
> अलोका यमलोकस्था मज्जते नरके हि सा ॥ ६६ ॥
> अन्यथा वोपनीतानि चूर्णमूलौषधान्यपि ।
> विनाशयेयुः पुरुषं तस्मान्नान्यं समाचरेत् ॥ ६७ ॥
> प्रियवंदा भर्तरि या भर्ता यस्याः परायणं ।
> वाक् चैव मधुरा यस्याः पत्युः संवननं महत् ॥ ६८ ॥
> प्रियं भर्तारमासाद्य पिबेदेवौषधीमिमां ।
> प्रियंवदां धर्मपरां धर्मपत्निमनिंदितां ॥ ६९ ॥
> अवमन्येत यो मोहात्तमाहुः पुरुषाधमं ॥

(Ṛgvidhāna, Chapter 4, verses 64-69)
By repeating this sūkta "इमां खनामि (*imāṃ khanāmi*)" a hundred times, the rival wife's harassment ceases and one's husband becomes attached to oneself. If the husband too repeats this sūkta and drinks for seven nights milk mixed with the herb called pāṭhā, all his enemies will be destroyed. The woman who, leaving aside the mantras of this sūkta, wishes to win her husband with other mantras will meet misfortune and will sink in suffering in the hell located in Yama's world. Even if herbs other than the pāṭhā mentioned here, powders and other medicines are used, those powders and other medicines will destroy that woman's husband. Therefore the mantra and the herb stated here should be used, and no other mantra or herb should be used. The woman who speaks pleasing words to her husband, whose husband is attached to his wife, and who always speaks sweet and good words with her husband: her husband will be attached to her and affectionate. The woman who desires her husband's love should drink this medicine in her husband's presence. The man who out of delusion despises and insults a lawful wife who speaks pleasing words, is devoted to dharma and is blameless, is called the lowest of men.

### Printed p. 965
The Bṛhaddevatā says thus:

इमां खनामिति सूक्तमिंद्राणी यत्त्वयं जगौ ॥ ५५ ॥ तदौपनिषदं षट्कं भाववृत्तं प्रचक्षते ॥ उत्तानपर्णां पाठां तु स्तोति सूक्ते महौषधिं ॥ ५६ ॥ पतिसंवननी त्वंत्यान्याः सपत्न्यपनोदिकाः ॥ (*imāṃ khanāmiti sūktamiṃdrāṇī yattvayaṃ jagau ‖ 55 ‖ tadaupaniṣadaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ bhāvavṛttaṃ pracakṣate ‖ uttānaparṇāṃ pāṭhāṃ tu stoti sūkte mahauṣadhiṃ ‖ 56 ‖ patisaṃvananī tvaṃtyānyāḥ sapatnyapanodikāḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 8-55, 56)

Indrāṇī (the wife of Indra) herself recited and praised this sūkta beginning "इमां खनामि (*imāṃ khanāmi*)". This sūkta is called an Upaniṣad bhāvavṛtta sūkta of six Ṛks. In this sūkta the seer (a woman) praises, describing them, the long and spreading leaves and stems of the creepers that are great medicinal plants, and their power. In the last Ṛk of this sūkta it is said that the husband's love is obtained for the wife. In the remaining Ṛks there is a description of the matter of warding off the harassment of the co-wife (rival wife). What the sage Āpastamba and the commentator have said regarding this sūkta is given in the Anuvāda of the viniyoga of this sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमामिति षडृचं सप्तदशं सूक्तमिंद्राण्या आर्षं। षष्ठी पंक्तिः शिष्टा अनु
> ष्टुभः । अनेन सूक्तेन सपत्न्या बाधनं प्रतिपाद्यते । अत एव सूक्तजपादिना सपत्न्याविनाशो भवति । अतस्तद्देवताकमिदं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । इमामिंद्राण्युपनिषत्सपत्नीबाधनमानुष्टुभं तु पंक्त्यंतमिति ॥ अस्य सूक्तस्य विनियोगो भगवतापस्तंबेन कस्मिंश्चित्सपत्नीघ्नप्रयोगविशेषे दर्शितः । त्रिः सप्तैर्यवैः पाठां परिकिरति यदि
> वारुण्यसि वरुणात्वा निष्कीर्णामि यदि सौम्यसि सोमात्वा निष्कीर्णामीति ।
> श्वोभूत उत्तरयोत्थाप्योत्तराभिस्तिसृभिरभिमंत्रोत्तरया प्रतिच्छन्नां हस्तयोराबध्य शय्याकाले बाहुभ्यां भर्तारं परिगृह्णीयादुपधानलिंगया । वश्यो
> भवति । सपत्नीबाधनं च । आप- गृ. ९-५ रिंद ८ । इति । आयमर्थः । आद्यया पाठा
> नामौषधिः खातव्या । ततस्ति सृभिरोषधेरभिमंत्रणं । षष्ठ्याबद्धा सौषधिर्यथा
> भर्तारं स्पृशति तथा तस्य भर्तुरालिंगनमिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This sūkta of six Ṛks, the seventeenth in the anuvāka, has Indrāṇī as seer. The sixth Ṛk is in Paṅkti metre, the rest in Anuṣṭubh. By this sūkta the harassment of the co-wife is set forth; hence by reciting it and the like the co-wife is destroyed, and so it has that deity. He quotes the Anukramaṇī: इमामिंद्राण्युपनिषत्सपत्नीबाधनमानुष्टुभं तु पंक्त्यंतमिति (*imāmiṃdrāṇyupaniṣatsapatnībādhanamānuṣṭubhaṃ tu paṃktyaṃtamiti*). The viniyoga was shown by the venerable Āpastamba in a particular co-wife-destroying rite: she scatters the pāṭhā plant around with three times seven barley grains, saying यदि वारुण्यसि वरुणात्वा निष्कीर्णामि यदि सौम्यसि सोमात्वा निष्कीर्णामीति (*yadi vāruṇyasi varuṇātvā niṣkīrṇāmi yadi saumyasi somātvā niṣkīrṇāmīti*). On the morrow she raises it with the next Ṛk, consecrates it with the next three Ṛks, and with the next Ṛk, binding it covered in her hands, at bedtime she should embrace her husband with her arms, using the plant as a pillow-like contact. He becomes subject to her, and the co-wife is warded off (Āpa. Gṛ. 9-5 to 8). The meaning: with the first Ṛk the plant called pāṭhā is dug up; then it is consecrated with three Ṛks; the plant bound with the sixth touches the husband, so that he is embraced.

**Anuvāda:** This sūkta "इमां (*imāṃ*)" is the seventeenth sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Indrāṇī is its seer; its sixth Ṛk is in Paṅkti metre, the other Ṛks in Anuṣṭubh. The matter set forth in this sūkta is that the harassment of the co-wife be removed. By reciting this sūkta the co-wife is destroyed. Therefore the deity of this sūkta is the removal of the co-wife's harassment. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: इमामिंद्राण्युपनिषत्सपत्नीबाधनमानुष्टुभं तु पंक्त्यंतमिति ॥ अस्य सूक्तस्य विनियोगो भगवतापस्तंबेन कस्मिंश्चित्सपत्नीघ्नप्रयोगविशेषे दर्शितः । त्रिः सप्तैर्यवैः पाठां परिकिरति यदि वारुण्यसि वरुणात्वा निष्कीर्णामि यदि सौम्यसि सोमात्वा निष्कीर्णामीति । श्वोभूत उत्तरयोत्थाप्योत्तराभिस्तिसृभिरभिमंत्रोत्तरया प्रतिच्छन्नां हस्तयोराबध्य शय्याकाले बाहुभ्यां भर्तारं परिगृह्णीयादुपधानलिंगया । वश्यो भवति । सपत्नीबाधनं च । आप- गृ. ९-५ रिंद ८ । इति । आयमर्थः । आद्यया पाठा नामौषधिः खातव्या । ततस्ति सृभिरोषधेरभिमंत्रणं । षष्ठ्याबद्धा सौषधिर्यथा भर्तारं स्पृशति तथा तस्य भर्तुरालिंगनमिति ॥ अनुवादवु—इमां ऎंब ई सूक्तवु हन्नॊंदनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि हदिनेळनॆय सूक्तवु. इदरल्लि आरु ऋक्कुगळिरुवुवु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ इंद्राणियु ऋषिकॆयु ; ई सूक्तद आरनॆय ऋक्कु पंक्तिश्चंदवु; उळिद ऋक्कुगळु अनुष्टुप् छंदस्कवु. ई सूक्तदल्लि सपत्निय (सवतिय) बाधॆयु परिहारवागबेकॆंब विषयवु प्रतिपादितवागिदॆ. ई सूक्तजपदिंद सवतिय विनाशवु आगुवुदु. आद्दरिंद ई सूक्तक्कॆ सपत्नीबाधनवे देवतॆयु. अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि—इमामिंद्राण्युपनिषत्स- पत्नीबाधनमानुष्टुभं तु पंक्त्यंतं (*imāmiṃdrāṇyupaniṣatsapatnībādhanamānuṣṭubhaṃ tu paṃktyaṃtamiti ‖ asya sūktasya viniyogo bhagavatāpastaṃbena kasmiṃścitsapatnīghnaprayogaviśeṣe darśitaḥ | triḥ saptairyavaiḥ pāṭhāṃ parikirati yadi vāruṇyasi varuṇātvā niṣkīrṇāmi yadi saumyasi somātvā niṣkīrṇāmīti | śvobhūta uttarayotthāpyottarābhistisṛbhirabhimaṃtrottarayā praticchannāṃ hastayorābadhya śayyākāle bāhubhyāṃ bhartāraṃ parigṛhṇīyādupadhānaliṃgayā | vaśyo bhavati | sapatnībādhanaṃ ca | āpa- gṛ. 9-5 riṃda 8 | iti | āyamarthaḥ | ādyayā pāṭhā nāmauṣadhiḥ khātavyā | tatasti sṛbhiroṣadherabhimaṃtraṇaṃ | ṣaṣṭhyābaddhā sauṣadhiryathā bhartāraṃ spṛśati tathā tasya bharturāliṃganamiti ‖ anuvādavu—imāṃ èṃba ī sūktavu hannòṃdanèya anuvākadalli hadineḷanèya sūktavu. idaralli āru ṛkkugaḷiruvuvu. ī sūktakkè iṃdrāṇiyu ṛṣikèyu ; ī sūktada āranèya ṛkku paṃktiścaṃdavu; uḷida ṛkkugaḷu anuṣṭup chaṃdaskavu. ī sūktadalli sapatniya (savatiya) bādhèyu parihāravāgabekèṃba viṣayavu pratipāditavāgidè. ī sūktajapadiṃda savatiya vināśavu āguvudu. āddariṃda ī sūktakkè sapatnībādhanave devatèyu. anukramaṇikèyalli—imāmiṃdrāṇyupaniṣatsa- patnībādhanamānuṣṭubhaṃ tu paṃktyaṃtaṃ*).

### Printed p. 966
Regarding the viniyoga of this sūkta, the sage Āpastamba has said as follows in the rite connected with removing a co-wife: a woman who wishes that the co-wife's trouble be removed and that her husband become subject to her should scatter around the powder of the herb called pāṭhā together with twenty-one barley grains, reciting the mantra "yadi vāruṇyasi varuṇāttā niṣkrīṇāmi yadi saumyasi somātvā niṣkrīṇāmi". Rising next morning, she should consecrate it with three Ṛks of this sūkta, and with the following Ṛk, holding the herb covered in her hand, at bedtime if she embraces her husband with her arms, the husband becomes subject to her and the co-wife's torment ceases. The chief point is: reciting the first Ṛk of this sūkta, the herb pāṭhā is to be dug out of the earth. Then with the next three Ṛks (2-4) the herb is to be consecrated. With the sixth Ṛk, binding the herb on the arm and embracing the husband so that the herb touches his body, the husband becomes subject to her.

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 145; Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 3. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6. Seer: Indrāṇī. Deity: Upaniṣat, removal of the co-wife's harassment. Metre: 1–5 Anuṣṭubh; 6 Paṅkti.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मां ख॑ना॒म्योष॑धिं वी॒रुधं॒ बल॑वत्तमां ।  
> यया॑ स॒पत्नीं॒ बाध॑ते॒ यया॑ संविं॒दते॒ पतिं॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमां । खनामि । ओषधिं । वीरुधं । बलवत्कतमां ।  
> यया । सपत्नीं । बाधते । यया । संविंदते । पतिं ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 967

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमानोषधिं पाठाख्यां वीरुधं लतारूपां बलवत्तमां स्वकार्यकरणेऽतिशयेन बलवतीं खनामि । उन्मूलयामि । ययौषध्या सपत्नीं । समान एकः
> पतिर्यस्याः सा सपत्नी । तामेषा वधूर्बाधते हिनस्ति । यया च पतिं भर्तारं
> संविंदते सम्यगसाधारण्येन लभते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I dig up this plant called pāṭhā, a creeper, exceedingly strong in doing its work; I uproot it. By which plant the co-wife — she whose husband is the same, one — this bride harasses, injures; and by which she wins her husband fully, without sharing.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यया (*yayā*)—by which plant (herb)
- सपत्नीं (*sapatnīṃ*)—the co-wife
- बाधते (*bādhate*)—is harassed (is destroyed)
- यया (*yayā*)—by the help of which plant
- पतिं (*patiṃ*)—her husband
- संविंदते (*saṃviṃdate*)—is obtained; of such a kind
- वीरुधं (*vīrudhaṃ*)—existing in the form of a creeper
- बलवत्तमां (*balavattamāṃ*)—possessing exceeding power in accomplishing the work
- इमां ओषधिं (*imāṃ oṣadhiṃ*)—this herb called pāṭhā
- खनामि (*khanāmi*)—I dig out of the earth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

By the help of which plant (herb) the co-wife can be destroyed, by the help of which plant one can obtain her husband (and his love) — such a herb called pāṭhā, in the form of a creeper and of exceeding power, I dig out of the earth.

##### English translation
I dig up this most potent medicinal creeper, by which (a wife) destroys a rival wife, by which she secures to herself her husband.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उत्ता॑नपर्णे॒ सुभ॑गे॒ देव॑जूते॒ सह॑स्वति ।  
> स॒पत्नीं॑ मे॒ परा॑ धम॒ पतिं॑ मे॒ केव॑लं कुरु ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत्तानपर्णे । सुभगे । देवजूते । सहस्वति ।  
> सप्तीं । मे । परा । धम । पतिं । मे । केवलं । कुरु ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 968

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उत्तानपर्णे । उत्तानान्यूर्द्ध्वमुखानि पर्णानि पत्राणि यस्याः तादृशि हे
> सुभगे सौभाग्यहेतुभूते हे देवजूते देवेन स्रष्टा प्रेरिते हे सहस्वत्यभिभवनवति ईदृशे हे पाठे मे मम सपत्नीं स्त्रियं परा धम । परागमय । धमतिर्गतिकर्मा । पतिं च मे ममैव केवलमसाधारणं कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O pāṭhā, you whose leaves (parṇa) are uttāna, upturned, facing upward; auspicious, cause of good fortune; sent forth by the god, the creator; सहस्वति (*sahasvati*), possessed of overpowering — drive away (परा धम (*parā dhama*), make go away; the root dham has the sense of motion) my co-wife, and make my husband mine alone, not shared.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत्तानपर्णे (*uttānaparṇe*)—O one furnished with leaves grown upward
- सुभगे (*subhage*)—bestower of good fortune
- देवजूते (*devajūte*)—impelled by the Creator
- सहस्वति (*sahasvati*)—overcomer of the enemy, O herb called pāṭhā
- मे (*me*)—my
- सपत्नीं (*sapatnīṃ*)—co-wife
- परा धम (*parā dhama*)—drive away
- पतिं च (*patiṃ ca*)—and my husband
- मे केवलं (*me kevalaṃ*)—so that he be mine only
- कुरु (*kuru*)—make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O herb called pāṭhā, furnished with upward-grown leaves, a cause of good fortune, overcomer of the enemy co-wife: drive my co-wife far from the vicinity of my husband, and make my husband mine alone — that is, not attached to another woman but loving me only.

##### English translation
O (plant) with up-turned leaves, auspicious, sent by the gods, powerful, remove my rival and make my husband mine alone.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उत्त॑रा॒हमु॑त्तर॒ उत्त॒रेदुत्त॑राभ्यः ।  
> अथा॑ स॒पत्नी॒ या मनाध॑रा॒ साध॑राभ्यः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत्तरा । अहं । उत्तरे । उत्तरा । इत् । उत्तराभ्यः ।  
> अथ । सप्तत्नि । या । मम । अधरा । सा । अधराभ्यः ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 969

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उत्तर उत्कृष्टतरे पाठे अहमुत्तरोत्कृष्टतरा भूयासं । उत्तराभ्यो
> लोके या उत्कृष्टतराः संति ताभ्योऽप्यहमुत्तरोत्कृष्टतरैव त्वत्पसादाद्भवेयं।
> अथानंतरं मम या सपत्नि साधराभ्यो निकृष्टाभ्योऽप्यधरा निकृष्टतरा भवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O superior, more excellent pāṭhā, may I become superior, more excellent; may I, by your favour, be more excellent even than those in the world who are more excellent. Thereafter, may my co-wife be lower, more inferior, even than those who are inferior.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत्तरे (*uttare*)—O excellent herb called pāṭhā
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- उत्तरा (*uttarā*)—may be more excellent than all
- उत्तराभ्यः (*uttarābhyaḥ*)—than those who are most excellent in the world, I
- उत्तरा इत् (*uttarā it*)—may be excellent
- अथ (*atha*)—afterwards
- मम (*mama*)—my
- या सपत्नि (*yā sapatni*)—whatever co-wife there is
- सा (*sā*)—she
- अधराभ्यः (*adharābhyaḥ*)—than inferior (low) people
- अधरा (*adharā*)—may be most inferior

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O excellent (superior) herb called pāṭhā, may I be more excellent than all. May I be more excellent than those who are reckoned most excellent in the world. Thereafter, may she who is my co-wife be more inferior even than the people who are inferior in the world.

##### English translation
Exallent (plant), may I too be excellent, excellent among the excellent and may she who is my rival be vile amongst the vile.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न॒ह्य॑स्या॒ नाम॑ गृ॒भ्णामि॒ नो अ॒स्मिन्॑मते॒ जने॑ ।  
> परा॑मे॒व प॑रा॒वतं॑ स॒पत्नीं॑ गमयामसि ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नहि । अस्याः । नाम । गृभ्णामि । नो इति । अस्मिन् । रमते । जने ।  
> परां । एव । परावतं । सपत्नीं । गमयामसि ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 970

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्याः सपत्न्या नाम संज्ञामपि नहि गृह्णामि । नैव गृह्णामि । उच्चारयामि॥
> नो खलु काचिदस्मिज्जने सपत्न्याख्ये रमते । क्रीडति । अपि च तां सपत्नीं परां,
> परावतमेवातिशयेन दूरदेशमेव गमयामसि । प्रापयामः । अतिशयेन भर्त्रावियोजयाम इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I do not take even the name of this co-wife; I do not utter it. No one at all takes delight (रमते (*ramate*), plays) in this person called co-wife. And we send that co-wife far away, to a distant place indeed; we cause her to reach there; that is, we utterly separate her from her husband.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्याः (*asyāḥ*)—of this co-wife
- नाम (*nāma*)—the name also
- नहि गृभ्नामि (*nahi gṛbhnāmi*)—I do not utter even with the mouth
- आस्मिन् जने (*āsmin jane*)—in the matter of this co-wife
- नो रमते (*no ramate*)—no one has delight (tolerance)
- परां (*parāṃ*)—other than myself
- सपत्नीं (*sapatnīṃ*)—the co-wife
- परावतं एव (*parāvataṃ eva*)—to a very distant place (so as to be away from the husband)
- गमयामसि (*gamayāmasi*)—let us drive away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I do not utter even the name of this co-wife. No one is pleased in the matter of this co-wife. Let us drive this co-wife, other than myself, to a very distant place (so that she is far from the husband).

##### English translation
I will not even utter her name, no (woman) takes pleasure in that person ; may we remove the other rival wife to a distance.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒हम॑स्मि॒ सह॑मा॒नाथ॒ त्वम॑सि सास॒हिः ।  
> उ॒भे सह॑स्वती भू॒त्वी स॒पत्नीं॑ मे सहावहै ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अहं । अस्मि । सहमाना । अथ । त्वं । असि । ससहिः ।  
> उभे इति । सहस्वती इति । भूत्वी । सपत्नीं । मे । सहावहै ॥ ५ ॥
