##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ओषधि अहं त्वत्प्रसादात्सहमानास्मि । सपत्न्या अभिभवित्री भवामि । अथापि च
> त्वमपि सासहिरसि । तस्या अभिभवित्री भवसि । आवामुभे अपि सहस्वती अभिभवित्र्यौ भूत्वी
> भूत्वा मे मम सपत्नीं सहावहै । अभिभवाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the herb: "By your grace I am triumphant, I overcome my co-wife; you too are a conqueror, you overcome her. Both of us, having become victorious, shall overcome my co-wife."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I (by your favour)
- सहमाना अस्मि (*sahamānā asmi*)—I overcome the co-wife
- अथ (*atha*)—and
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you also
- सासहिः असि (*sāsahiḥ asi*)—you overcome that co-wife
- उभे (*ubhe*)—we both
- सहस्वती भूत्वी (*sahasvatī bhūtvī*)—having become powerful
- मे (*me*)—my
- सपत्नीं (*sapatnīṃ*)—co-wife
- सहावहै (*sahāvahai*)—let us overcome

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O herb, by your grace I shall overcome my co-wife; and you too will overcome her. Let us both together, by our strength and power, overcome that co-wife of mine.

##### English translation
I am triumphing, you are triumphant; we two being powerfull will triumph over my rival.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उप॑ तेऽधां॒ सह॑मानाम॒भि त्वा॑धां॒ सही॑यसा ।  
> मामनु॒ प्र ते॒ मनो॑ व॒त्सं गौरि॑व धावतु प॒था वारि॑व  
> धावतु ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उप । ते । अधां । सहमानां । अभि । त्वा । अधां । सहीयसा ।  
> मां । अनु । प्र । ते । मनः । वत्सं । गौः इव । धावतु । पथा । नाः इव । धावतु ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पते ते तव सहमानां सपत्न्या अभिभवित्रीमिमामोषधिमुपाधां । शिरस
> उपाधानं करोमि । सहीयसाभिभवितृतरेण तेनोपधानेन त्वामभ्यधां । अभितो

### Printed p. 972

> धारयामि। ते तव भर्तुर्मनो मामनुलक्ष्य प्र धावतु। प्रकर्षण शीघ्रं गच्छतु ।
> तत्र निदर्शनद्वयमुच्यते । गौरिव यथा गौर्वत्वं शीघ्रं गच्छति पथा निम्मेन
> मार्गेण वारिव वारुदकं यथा स्वभावतो गच्छति तद्वत् । अनेन निदर्शनद्वयेन्त्सुक्यातिशयः स्वाभाविकत्वं च प्रतिपाद्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O husband, I place on my head this herb of yours, which overcomes the co-wife; with that more overcoming pillow I surround you on every side. Let your, the husband's, mind, looking to me, run swiftly forward." Two illustrations are given: as a cow runs swiftly to her calf, and as water naturally flows along a low path. By these two illustrations eagerness in the highest degree and naturalness are conveyed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते (*te*)—your
- सहमानां (*sahamānāṃ*)—the herb that overcomes the co-wife (the power)
- उप अधां (*upa adhāṃ*)—I place on the head
- सहीयसा (*sahīyasā*)—with that capacity of overcoming the co-wife
- अभि आधां (*abhi ādhāṃ*)—I hold you well
- ते (*te*)—of you (my husband)
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—mind
- मां (*māṃ*)—to me
- गौरिव (*gauriva*)—like a cow
- वत्सं (*vatsaṃ*)—running to her calf
- पथा (*pathā*)—on low ground
- वारिव (*vāriva*)—like flowing water
- प्र धावतु (*pra dhāvatu*)—let it come running

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O herb, I place on my head this herb that has the power to overcome the co-wife, and I also hold you, who have that power, on other parts of my body. O my husband, as a cow runs to her calf and as water flowing down a slope runs swiftly, so let your mind run to me.

##### English translation
I make you the triumphant (herb) my pillow, I support you with that more triumphant (pillow); let your mind hasten to me as a cow to her calf, let it speed on its way like water.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the first half of this Ṛk the herb is praised. In the second half the husband is addressed, and it is prayed that his mind come very quickly to her, that is, that her husband's love be directed towards her.

## Sūkta 146 (Maṇḍala 10)
The 146th sūkta is Jīrike [cumin]. In this sūkta the deity Araṇyānī is praised. Araṇyānī is the wife of the deity presiding over the forest (araṇya). Yāska:
### Printed p. 973
अरण्यानी ऎंब देवतॆयन्नु स्तुतिसलागिदॆ. अरण्यानी ऎंबुवुदु अरण्याभि मानिदेवतॆय (अरण्यद) पत्नियु. यास्करु— अरण्यानी । अरण्यान्यरण्यस्य पत्नि । अरण्यमपार्णं ग्रामादरमणं भवतीति वा ॥ (*araṇyānī èṃba devatèyannu stutisalāgidè. araṇyānī èṃbuvudu araṇyābhi mānidevatèya (araṇyada) patniyu. yāskaru— araṇyānī | araṇyānyaraṇyasya patni | araṇyamapārṇaṃ grāmādaramaṇaṃ bhavatīti vā ‖*) (Ni. 9-29)
Araṇyānī is the wife of Araṇya. Araṇya is a region far from village, city and town; or a deserted region where, unlike the village, there is no kind of entertainment and which causes boredom, is called araṇya. In the Ṛgvidhāna:
अरण्यानीत्यरण्येषु जपेत्सूक्तमनेकशः। अरण्यानीं नमस्कृत्वा सोऽरण्यात्पतिमुच्यते ॥ (*araṇyānītyaraṇyeṣu japetsūktamanekaśaḥ| araṇyānīṃ namaskṛtvā so 'raṇyātpatimucyate ‖*) (Ṛgvidhāna 4-70)
If one loses the way while wandering in a forest, and recites this sūkta "अरण्यानी (*araṇyānī*)" many times and bows in the mind to the deity Araṇyānī, one finds the right path and comes out of the forest. In this sūkta the seer describes the scenes he sees, through illustrations that touch the heart.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अरण्यानीति षडृचमष्टादशं सूक्तमिरंमदपुत्रस्य देवमुनेरार्षं । महदरण्यमरण्यानी । तद्देवताकं । आनुष्टुभं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । अरण्यानैरंमदो
> देवमुनिररण्यानीं तुष्टावेति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta अरण्यानी (*araṇyānī*) has six Ṛks, is the eighteenth, and is the vision of the divine sage Airaṃmada, son of Irammada. A great forest is araṇyānī; she is its deity. The metre is Anuṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says: Airaṃmada, the divine sage, praised Araṇyānī. The viniyoga has been stated.

The Kannada Anuvāda: this sūkta Araṇyānī is the eighteenth sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka and has six Ṛks. Its seer is Devamuni, son of Irammada; the deity is Araṇyānī; the metre is Anuṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says that Devamuni Airaṃmada praised Araṇyānī. The viniyoga was stated earlier.

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 146; Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 4. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6. Seer: Devamuni Airaṃmada. Deity: Araṇyānī. Metre: Anuṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अर॑ण्या॒न्यर॑ण्यान्य॒सौ या प्रेव॒ नश्य॑सि ।  
> क॒था ग्रामं॒ न पृ॑च्छसि॒ न त्वा॒ भीरि॑व विंदती ३ ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 974

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अरण्यानि । अरण्यानि । आसौ । या । प्रइव । नश्यसि ।  
> कथा । ग्रामं । न । पृच्छसि । न । त्वा । भीः इव । विंदती ३ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अरण्यानि । अरण्यस्य पालयित्री काचिदधिदेवतारण्यानीति नैरुक्ताः । वैयाकरणास्तु हिमारण्ययोर्महत्वे । पा- ४-१-४९-१ । इत्यरण्यस्य महत्वे जीषं
> स्मरंति । अरण्याधिदेवते अरण्यानि कांताराणि प्रति यासौ त्वं प्रेव नश्यसि । इवः
> संप्रत्यर्थे । नशतिः प्राप्तिकर्मा ॥ अत्र व्यत्ययेन श्यन् ॥ संप्रति रक्षणाय प्राप्नोषि।
> यद्वा निजने देशे वर्तमानत्वान्नष्टेव प्रतीयसे । सा त्वं कथा कथं ग्रामं न
> पृच्छसि । निर्जनेऽरण्ये कथं रमसे । नूनं त्वा त्वां भीर्भयं न निंदति । न लभते
> किं । वितर्के प्लुतः । इवः संप्रत्यर्थे परिभयार्थे वा । अत्र निरुक्तं । अरण्यान्यरण्यस्य पत्न्यरण्यमपार्णं भवति ग्रामादरमणं भवतीति वा । अरण्यानीत्येनामामंत्रयते । यासावरण्यानि वनानि पराजीव नश्यसि कथं ग्रामं न पृच्छसि न त्वा भीर्विंदतीवेतीवः परिभयार्थे वा । नि. ९-३० । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Araṇyāni": according to the Nairuktas she is some deity guarding the forest, Araṇyānī; the grammarians, citing Pā. Sū. 4-1-49-1 हिमारण्ययोर्महत्वे (*himāraṇyayormahatve*), prescribe the affix jīṣ for araṇya in the sense of greatness. Deity of the forest, you who now seem to vanish towards the forests, to reach them for protection; or, dwelling in a solitary place, you seem as if lost. How is it that you do not ask about the village? How do you delight in the lonely forest? Does fear not take hold of you? The question is asked in doubt (the pluta); इवः (*ivaḥ*) is in the sense of "now" or of "fear". The Nirukta is cited: अरण्यान्यरण्यस्य पत्न्यरण्यमपार्णं भवति ग्रामादरमणं भवतीति वा । अरण्यानीत्येनामामंत्रयते । यासावरण्यानि वनानि पराजीव नश्यसि कथं ग्रामं न पृच्छसि न त्वा भीर्विंदतीवेतीवः परिभयार्थे वा । (*araṇyānyaraṇyasya patnyaraṇyamapārṇaṃ bhavati grāmādaramaṇaṃ bhavatīti vā | araṇyānītyenāmāmaṃtrayate | yāsāvaraṇyāni vanāni parājīva naśyasi kathaṃ grāmaṃ na pṛcchasi na tvā bhīrviṃdatīvetīvaḥ paribhayārthe vā |*) Ni. 9-30.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अरण्यानि (*araṇyāni*)—O deity of the forest, guardian of the forest
- अरण्यानि (*araṇyāni*)—I ask you, the presiding deity of the forest
- या असौ (*yā asau*)—you
- प्रेव (*preva*)—now
- नश्यसि (*naśyasi*)—you are not seen, or you do not come here for protection
- कथा (*kathā*)—why
- ग्रामं (*grāmaṃ*)—where the village is
- न पृच्छिसि (*na pṛcchisi*)—do you not ask?
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- भीःइव (*bhīḥiva*)—fear
- न विंदति (*na viṃdati*)—does it not seize?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deity of the forest, guardian of the forest, you are now seen nowhere. Why do you not ask anyone where the village is? Do you not feel fear?

##### English translation
Aranyani, Aranyani, who are, as it were, perishing there, why do you not inquire of the village? does not fear assail you ?

### Printed p. 975

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Explaining the word Araṇyānī, Yāska gives the Nirukta on this Ṛk:
अरण्यानीत्येनामामंत्रये यासावरण्यानि वनानि पराजीव नश्यसि कथं ग्रामं न पृच्छसि न त्वा भिर्विंदतीवेतीवः परिभयार्थे वा ॥ (*araṇyānītyenāmāmaṃtraye yāsāvaraṇyāni vanāni parājīva naśyasi kathaṃ grāmaṃ na pṛcchasi na tvā bhirviṃdatīvetīvaḥ paribhayārthe vā ‖*) (Ni. 9-30)
Here there is a repetition, araṇyāni araṇyāni. Of these two words, by the first the seer addresses the deity presiding over the forest. The second is the accusative plural of the word araṇya; that is, araṇyāni means forests. The seer Devamuni, a mantra-seer, wandering alone in the forest, seeing that solitary wild, became very afraid and questions the presiding deity thus: O deity of the forest, do you not feel fear? In these forests you remain hidden, seen nowhere. Do you not ask anyone where the village is? It seems you feel no fear at all. Yet perhaps you feel a little fear: the words वा इवः (*vā ivaḥ*) indicate the sense that at least a little fear is felt. Here the pluta (the length-mark 3) is used to express vitarka, that is, doubt.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृ॒षा॒र॒वाय॒ वद॑ते॒ यदु॒पाव॑ति चिच्चि॒कः ।  
> आ॒घा॒टिभि॑रिव धा॒वय॑न्न रण्या॒निर्म॑हीयते ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृषरवाय । वदते । यत् । उपअवति । चिच्चिकः ।  
> आघाटिभिः इव । धावयन् । अरण्यानिः । महीयते ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषारवाय । वृषा सेचनसमर्थो रवः शब्दो यस्य सूक्ष्मजंतुविशेषस्य
> झिल्याख्यस्य स तथोक्तः । कटुकशब्दवानित्यर्थः । तस्मै वृषारवाख्याय वदते चीचीशब्दं कुर्वते चिच्चिकश्चिचीशब्दं कुर्वन्नन्यो जंतुर्यद्यदोपावति वृषारवाय
> स्वशब्दस्य प्रत्युत्तररूपेण चीचीशब्दकरेणोपगच्छति । उपेत्य पालयति वा । तत्र

### Printed p. 976

> दृष्टांतः । आघाटिभिरिव । आघाटयो घाटलिकाः कांडवीणाः । ताभिर्धावयन्निषादादिसप्तस्वराणि शोधयन्गायक इव । तदारण्यानिः सारण्यानी महीयते ।
> पूज्यते ॥ इंद्रवरुणेत्यादिना जेष् । पा. ४-१-४९ । तत्संनियोगेनानुगागमः ।
> छांदसो ह्रस्वः । अत एव हल्ज्यादिसुलोपाभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वृषारवाय (*vṛṣāravāya*): the small creature called Jhillī whose sound (rava) is vṛṣā, able to shower, that is, shrill. When that creature cries "chī chī", another creature, the chiccika, making the sound chī chī, comes up in reply to its own sound and protects it or approaches it. An illustration: आघाटिभिरिव (*āghāṭibhiriva*): the āghāṭis are ghāṭalikās, reed lutes; as a singer who tunes the seven notes beginning with niṣāda on them. Then Araṇyāni, that is, Araṇyānī, is honoured, worshipped.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वदते (*vadate*)—who makes the harsh sound chī chī (in the forest)
- वृषारवाय (*vṛṣāravāya*)—in reply to the sound of the small creature vṛṣārava
- चिच्चिकः (*ciccikaḥ*)—another small creature
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- उपावति (*upāvati*)—it also makes the sound chī chī
- अरण्यानिः (*araṇyāniḥ*)—the deity presiding over the forest
- आघाटिभिः (*āghāṭibhiḥ*)—with lutes furnished with large gourds
- धावयन् (*dhāvayan*)—like singers playing the seven notes beginning with niṣāda
- महीयते (*mahīyate*)—shines

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(The seer describes in another way the cries of animals heard in the forest, comparing them to singers playing lutes.) In one region the small creature vṛṣārava makes the harsh, ear-grating cry chī chī. As if in reply, another small creature, the chiccika, answers in the same way with chī chī. The sound so heard seems like singers playing the seven notes beginning with niṣāda on lutes fitted with large gourds (pots). With such various sounds heard in the forest, the forest shines.

##### English translation
When the chichchika replies to the crying vrisharava, Aranyani is exalted, resonant, as with cymbals.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च गाव इव गवयाद्या मृगा अस्यामरण्यान्यामदंति । तृणादिकं
> भक्षयंति । उतापि च लतागुल्मादिकं वेश्मेव गृहमिव दृश्यते । उतो अपि चारण्यानिरियमरण्यानी सायं सायंकाले । इवः संप्रत्यर्थे । संप्रति शकटीः शकटान्
> दार्वाद्याहरणायागतान्सर्जति । विसर्जयति । यद्वा । शकटीः सर्जतीव दृश्यते ।
> अहनि महदरण्यं शकटीभिः प्राप्य सर्वे जना अरण्ये क्षतं काष्ठादिकं शकटीस्वध्यारोप्य सायंकाले तस्मान्निर्गच्छंति । तदभिप्रायेणेदं वचनं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa says that wild animals such as the gavaya (wild ox) graze in this forest like cows, eating grass and the like. Creepers and thickets look like a house. At evening this forest, as it were, looks like one that "lets loose" the carts that have come to fetch timber and the like. Or else: it looks as if it were unyoking carts. During the day all people reach the great forest with their carts, load the wood and other things they have cut onto the carts, and leave it at evening. This statement is made with that in view. He glosses इवः (*ivaḥ*) as having the sense "just now" (sampratyartha).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- गाव इव (*gāva iva*)—like gentle animals such as cows (the wild beasts in the forest)
- अदंति (*adaṃti*)—graze
- उत (*uta*)—and (creepers, thickets and the like)
- वेश्मेव (*veśmeva*)—like a house
- दृश्यते (*dṛśyate*)—appears
- उतो (*uto*)—and moreover
- अरण्यानिः (*araṇyāniḥ*)—this forest
- सायं (*sāyaṃ*)—in the evening
- शकटीरिव (*śakaṭīriva*)—the carts loaded with wood and the like from the forest
- सर्जति (*sarjati*)—appears as if it has unyoked and let them go

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(In this Ṛk the seer describes the forest by comparing it to a village.) When one sees wild beasts such as deer grazing in the forest, it looks as if cows, horses and other gentle animals were grazing in the village pastures; and thickets dense with small plants and creepers look like houses. At evening, when carts loaded with wood and the like leave the forest, this forest looks like a village in which people have unyoked the oxen of the carts that brought their loads and set them standing before their houses.

##### English translation
It is as if cows were grazing, and it looks like a dwelling, and Arayani at eventide, as it were, dismissed the waggons.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> गामं॒गैष आ ह्व॑यति॒ दार्वं॒गैषो अपा॑वधीत् ।  
> 62  
> वस॑न्न रण्या॒न्यां सा॒युमक्रु॑क्ष॒दिति॑ मन्यते ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गां । अंग । एषः । आ । ह्वयति । दारु । अंग । एषः । अप । अवधीत् ।  
> वसन् । अरण्यान्यां । सायं । अक्रुक्षत् । इति । मन्यते ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अंग हे अरण्यानि एष त्वदधिष्ठिते महारण्ये संप्रति वर्तमानो गामा ह्वयति ।
> एष चान्यो दारु काष्ठमपावधीत् । अपहंति । तथा सायं सायंकाले रात्रावरण्यान्यां महारण्ये निवसन्मनुष्यो नानाविधं पक्षिमृगादिकं शब्दं शृण्वन् अक्रुक्षत्
> कश्चित्तस्करादिराक्रोशतीति भीतः सन्मन्यते । बुध्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Dear Araṇyāni, in this great forest under your care, one man now calls his cow, and another cuts timber (kāṣṭha)." Likewise at evening, that is at night, a man dwelling in the great forest hears the various sounds of birds, beasts and the like. Being afraid, he thinks "some thief or other is shouting" (अक्रुक्षत् (*akrukṣat*)); मन्यते (*manyate*) is glossed "he understands".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अंग (*aṃga*)—O deity presiding over the forest
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—a man in this forest
- गां (*gāṃ*)—his cow (grazing far away)
- आ ह्वयति (*ā hvayati*)—calls out to her to come to him
- अंग (*aṃga*)—O deity
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—another man
- दारु (*dāru*)—a tree, for firewood and the like
- अप अवधीत् (*apa avadhīt*)—cuts down. Likewise
- सायं (*sāyaṃ*)—in the evening, that is at night
- अरण्यान्यां (*araṇyānyāṃ*)—in this great forest
- वसन् (*vasan*)—the man who dwells (hearing there the fearful sounds of the wild beasts)
- अक्रुक्षत् इति (*akrukṣat iti*)—that a thief is shouting
- मन्यते (*manyate*)—thinks

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deity presiding over the forest, people in this forest are engaged in all kinds of work. One loudly calls his cow, grazing far off, to drive her home. Another cuts a tree for firewood. In the evening, after dark, if anyone staying in this great forest hears wicked beasts roaring, he is deluded into thinking a thief is shouting to frighten travellers.

##### English translation
This man calls his cow, another cuts down the timber; tarrying in the forest at eventide, one thinks there is a cry.

> न वा अ॑रण्या॒निर्हं॑त्य॒न्यश्चेन्नाभि॒गच्छ॑ति ।  
> स्वा॒दोः फल॑स्य ज॒ग्त्वा॑ यथा॒कामं॒ नि प॑द्यते ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । वै । अरण्यानिः । हंति । अन्यः । च । इत् । न । अभिगच्छति ।  
> स्वादोः । फलस्य । जग्ध्वाय । यथाकामं । नि । पद्यते ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> न वै न खल्वरण्यानिररण्यानी हंति । तत्र निवसंतं हिनस्ति । यद्यन्नो व्याघ्रचौरादिर्नाभिगच्छति । तर्हि स्वादो रसवत आम्रादेः फलस्य ॥ द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठी । फलं
> जग्द्वाय भक्षयित्वा तत्र निवसन्पुरुषो यथाकामं यथेच्छं नि पद्यते । निगच्छति ।
> वर्तते ॥ क्त्वाप्रत्ययेऽदो जग्धिल्यप्ति किति । पा. २-४-३६ । इति जग्धादेशः । क्वो
> यत् । पा. ७-१-४७ । इति । यक् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The forest does not injure; it does not harm the one who dwells there. If no tiger, thief or the like approaches, then the man dwelling there, having eaten the sweet, juicy fruit of the mango and the like (the genitive फलस्य (*phalasya*) stands for the accusative), "settles" (नि पद्यते (*ni padyate*): goes, lives) as he wishes. The substitution जग्ध (*jagdha*) before the kvā affix and the form जग्ध्वाय (*jagdhvāya*) are noted with sūtra references (Pā. Sū. 2-4-36 and 7-1-47).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अरण्यानिः (*araṇyāniḥ*)—the forest
- न वै हंति (*na vai haṃti*)—harms no one
- अन्यः च (*anyaḥ ca*)—whether a wicked creature such as a tiger, or a thief
- न अभिगच्चंति इत् (*na abhigaccaṃti it*)—does not come near him (the man there); that man
- स्वादोः (*svādoḥ*)—tasty
- फलस्य (*phalasya*)—the fruit on the forest trees
- जग्ध्वाय (*jagdhvāya*)—eating
- यथाकामं (*yathākāmaṃ*)—as he pleases
- नि पद्यते (*ni padyate*)—goes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This great forest harms no one and troubles no one; no wicked beast such as a tiger, and no thief, comes near the man there. Not only that, but eating the tasty fruits of this forest's trees, that man can go wherever he likes, as he pleases.

##### English translation
But Aryanyani injures no one unless some other assail him; feeding upon the sweet fruit, he penetrates at will.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आंजनगंधिं । अंजनस्येदमांजनं कस्तूर्यादि । तस्य गंध इव गंधो
> यस्यास्तादृशी ॥ उपमानाच्च । पा. ५-४-१३७ । इति गंधस्येदंतादेशः ॥ अत एव
> सुरभिं सौरभ्योपेतां बह्वन्नां बहुभिरन्नॆरदनीयैः फलमूलादिभिरुपेतामकृषीवलां । कृषिरेषामस्तीति कृषीवलाः कर्षकाः ॥ रजः कृषीत्यादिना । पा.
> ५-२-११२ । वलच् । वले । पा. ६-३-११८ । इति दीर्घः ॥ तैर्वियुक्तां तादृशीं
> मृगाणां मातरं जनयित्रिमरण्यानिमरण्यानीमहं प्राशंसिषं । उक्तेन प्रकारेण
> स्तुतवानस्मि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

आंजनगंधिं (*āṃjanagaṃdhiṃ*): *āṃjanaṃ* is what belongs to अंजन (*aṃjana*), musk and the like; she whose scent is like its scent is such. By Pā. Sū. 5-4-137 गंध (*gaṃdha*) takes the substitute इ (*i*) at its end, after a standard of comparison. For this very reason she is सुरभिं (*surabhiṃ*), endowed with fragrance. बह्वन्नां (*bahvannāṃ*): endowed with much food, that is edible fruits, roots and the like. अकृषीवलां (*akṛṣīvalāṃ*): those who have कृषि (*kṛṣi*) (tillage) are कृषीवलाः (*kṛṣīvalāḥ*), farmers; the affix वलच् (*valac*) comes by Pā. Sū. 5-2-112 and the long vowel by Pā. Sū. 6-3-118. She is without them. Such is the mother of the beasts, their begetter; "I have praised Araṇyāni" in the manner stated.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आंजनगंधिं (*āṃjanagaṃdhiṃ*)—that which gives off a fragrance of musk and other perfumes
- सुरभिं (*surabhiṃ*)—that which is redolent with the fragrance of flowers
- अकृषीवलां (*akṛṣīvalāṃ*)—that which, though without cultivation such as ploughing by a farmer
- बह्वन्नां (*bahvannāṃ*)—is full of many kinds of edible fruits, roots and the like
- मृगाणां (*mṛgāṇāṃ*)—for the wild beasts
- मातरं (*mātaraṃ*)—that is like a mother
- अरण्यानिं (*araṇyāniṃ*)—this great forest (the deity presiding over the forest)
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- प्र अशंसिषं (*pra aśaṃsiṣaṃ*)—am praising

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I praise this great forest: it is endowed with the divine scent of musk and the like, redolent with the fragrance of flowers, free of farming work, full of many kinds of edible fruits and roots, and like a mother to the wild beasts.

## Sūkta 147 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> श्रत्त इति पंचर्चमेकोनविंशं सूक्तं शिरीषपुत्रस्य सुवेदस आर्षं पंचमी
> त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टा जगत्यः । इंद्रो देवता । अनुक्रम्यते हि । श्रत्ते पंच सुवेदाः
> शैरीषिस्त्रिष्टुबंतमिति ॥ तृतीये रात्रिपर्याये प्रशास्तुः शस्त्र इदं सूक्तं । सूत्रितं
> च । श्रत्ते दधामिदं त्यत्पात्रमिंद्रपानमिति याज्या । आ. ६-४ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the nineteenth sūkta, of five Ṛks, of Suvedas, son of Śirīṣa. Its fifth verse is Triṣṭubh, the rest Jagatī; the deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇī says: श्रत्ते पंच सुवेदाः शैरीषिस्त्रिष्टुबंतं (*śratte paṃca suvedāḥ śairīṣistriṣṭubaṃtaṃ*). The sūkta is used in the Śastra of the Praśāstṛ in the third night-round. It is prescribed in the sūtra श्रत्ते दधामिदं त्यत्पात्रमिंद्रपानमिति याज्या (*śratte dadhāmidaṃ tyatpātramiṃdrapānamiti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-4).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning श्रत्ते (*śratte*) is the nineteenth sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Its seer is Suvedas, son of Śirīṣa; the deity is Indra; the fifth Ṛk is in the Triṣṭubh metre and the remaining Ṛks in Jagatī. The Anukramaṇī says: श्रत्ते पंच सुवेदाः शैरीषिस्त्रिष्टुबंतं (*śratte paṃca suvedāḥ śairīṣistriṣṭubaṃtaṃ*). The sūkta is used for the Śastra mantras to be recited by the priest called Praśāstṛ in the third night-round of the sacrifice, as set out in Āśvalāyana's Śrauta Sūtra, श्रत्ते दधामिदं त्यत्पात्रमिंद्रपानमिति याज्या (*śratte dadhāmidaṃ tyatpātramiṃdrapānamiti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-4).

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 147. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 5. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Suvedas Śairīṣa. Deity: Indra. Metre: 1–4 Jagatī; 5 Triṣṭubh.
#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श्रत्ते॑ दधामि प्रथ॒माय॑ म॒न्यवेऽह॒न्यद्वृ॒त्रं नर्यं॑ वि॒वेर॒पः।  
> उ॒भे यत्त्वा॒ भव॑तो॒ रोद॑सी॒ अनु॒ रेज॑ते॒ शुष्मा॑त्पृथि॒वी  ॑
> चिदद्रिवः ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 982

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> श्रत् । ते । दधामि । प्रथमाय । मन्यवे । अहन् । यत् । वृत्रं । नर्यं । विवेः ।  
> अपः ।  
> उभे इति । यत् । त्वा । भवतः । रोदसी इति । अनु । रेजते । शुष्मात् । पृथवी ।  
> चित् । अद्रिवः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तव मन्यवे कोपाय तेजसे ना प्रथमाय मुख्याय श्रद्धधामि । श्रद्धा नामादरातिशयः । तद्विषयं करोमि । यद्येन मन्युना त्वं वृत्रमावरकमसुरं मेघं वा नर्यं नेतव्यमहन् अवधीः । हत्वा च तेनावृता अप उदकानि
> च विवेः इमं लोकं प्रत्यागमयः । तस्मै मन्यव इत्यन्वयः । यद्यदोभे
> रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ त्वा त्वामनुसृत्य भवतः वर्तेते । त्वदधीने अभूतामित्यर्थः ।
> तदानीं पृथिवी चित् । पृथिवीत्यंतरिक्षनाम । प्रथितं विस्तीर्णमंतरिक्षमपि हे अद्रिवो
> वज्रवन्निंद्र शुष्मात्त्वदीयाद्बलाद्रेजते । कंपते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, I hold श्रत् (*śrat*) (faith) towards your foremost, principal मन्यु (*manyu*), wrath or splendour." Faith (śraddhā) means excess of reverence; I direct it at that. It is the wrath with which you slew Vṛtra, the enveloping asura or the cloud, the one नर्य (*narya*) (to be led), and having slain him you brought back to this world the waters he had enclosed; so construe it with that wrath. When both heaven and earth follow you and exist, that is, became dependent on you, then even पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*), which here is a name of the atmosphere (the broad, extended space), O thunderbolt-bearer (अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)) Indra, trembles from your might शुष्म (*śuṣma*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—by which wrath of yours you (O Indra)
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—the cloud, or Vṛtra who had enveloped the cloud
- नर्यं (*naryaṃ*)—to do good to men
- अहन् (*ahan*)—destroyed, and afterwards
- अप (*apa*)—the waters he had enclosed
- विवेः (*viveḥ*)—made to fall upon the earth, that
- प्रथमाय (*prathamāya*)—principal
- ते (*te*)—your
- मन्यवे (*manyave*)—for the wrath (with regard to the wrath)
- श्रत् (*śrat*)—faith, that is respect
- दधामि (*dadhāmi*)—I hold
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—heaven and earth, both
- त्वा (*tvā*)—following you
- भवतः (*bhavataḥ*)—exist, then
- अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt
- पृथिवी चित् (*pṛthivī cit*)—even the broad atmosphere
- शुष्मात् (*śuṣmāt*)—for your might (seeing your might)
- रेजते (*rejate*)—trembles

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the matter of the wrath you showed when, to do good to men, you slew Vṛtra, who had enveloped the cloud, and made the waters he had held back fall upon the earth, I show above all excess of reverence; that is, I have great reverence for your wrath. O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, when heaven and earth are both under your sway, even the broad atmosphere trembles on seeing your unfathomable might.

### Printed p. 983

##### English translation
I have faith, Indra, in your first wrath, whereby :you slew
Vritra, and undertook a work friendly to man; when both heaven and
earth were inferior to you, the firmament trembled at your might, O wielder
of the thunderbolt.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं मा॒याभि॑रनवद्य मा॒यिनं॑ श्रवस्य॒ता मन॑सा वृ॒त्रम॑र्दयः।  
> त्वामिन्नरो॑ वृणते॒ गवि॑ष्टिषु॒ त्वां विश्वा॑सि॒ हव्या॒स्विष्टि॑षु ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । मायाभिः । अनवद्य । मायिनं । श्रवस्यता । मनसा । वृत्रं । अर्दयः ।  
> त्वां । इत् । नरः । वृणते । गोऽइष्टिषु । त्वां । विश्वासु । हव्यासु । इष्टिषु ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अनवद्यावद्यरहित प्रशस्येंद्र त्वं मायिनं मायाविनं वृत्रं मायाभिर्वंचनाभिर्बुद्धिविशेषैर्वा श्रवस्यता श्रवः श्रवणीयं यशोऽन्नं वेच्छता मनसार्दयः । अहिंसीः । अपि च नरो नेतारोऽंगिरसस्त्वामित्तामेव गविष्टिषु गवां
> पणिभिरपहृतानामेषणेषु प्रापणेषु विषयभूतेषु वृणते । संभजंते । तथा
> विश्वासु सर्वासु हव्यास्वाह्वातव्यासु प्रार्थनीयास्विष्टिषु यागक्रियासु त्वामेव
> वृणते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O faultless, praiseworthy Indra, you have slain Vṛtra, the deceiver (मायिनं (*māyinaṃ*)), by deceptions (मायाभिः (*māyābhiḥ*)), that is, by tricks or special devices of intelligence, with a mind (मनसा (*manasā*)) that desires श्रवः (*śravaḥ*), that is, glorious fame, or food. अर्दयः (*ardayaḥ*) means "you killed". Moreover the leaders (नरः (*naraḥ*)), the Aṅgirases, choose you alone in the गविष्टिषु (*gaviṣṭiṣu*), the searches for and recoveries of the cows carried off by the Paṇis; they resort to you. Likewise in all (विश्वासु (*viśvāsu*)) the invocable, desirable इष्टिषु (*iṣṭiṣu*), the sacrificial rites, they choose you alone.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अनवद्य (*anavadya*)—O Indra, free from fault
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- मायिनं (*māyinaṃ*)—the deceitful
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—Vṛtra
- मायाभिः (*māyābhiḥ*)—by means of deceptions alone
- श्रवस्यता (*śravasyatā*)—desiring food and the like
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with a mind
- अर्दयः (*ardayaḥ*)—you have slain (and)
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—the Aṅgirasa seers, leaders in the performance of sacrifice
- गविष्टिषु (*gaviṣṭiṣu*)—in the work of searching for the cows carried off by the Paṇis
- विश्वासु (*viśvāsu*)—all
- हव्यासु (*havyāsu*)—invoked by praying to the gods
- इष्टिषु (*iṣṭiṣu*)—also in the sacrificial rites
- त्वामित् (*tvāmit*)—you alone (for help)
- वृणते (*vṛṇate*)—they desire

### Printed p. 984

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O faultless (venerable) Indra, with the mind that you must bring about rain that yields food, you have slain the deceitful Vṛtra by deceptive means alone. The Aṅgirasa seers, leaders of sacrificial rites, seek you alone (your help alone), both in the search for the cows carried off by the Paṇis and in the sacrificial acts in which the gods are prayed to and invoked.

##### English translation
Irreproachable Indra, with mind intent on glory, you have by your deceptions slain the deceptive Vritra. The worshipper chooses you when he seeks for his (stolen) cattle, and in all sacrifices accompanied with invocations.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऐषु॑ चाकंधि पुरुहूत सू॒रिषु॑ वृ॒धासो॒ ये म॑घवन्नान॒शुर्म॒घं ।  
> अर्चं॑ति तो॒के तन॑ये॒ परि॑ष्टिषु मे॒धसा॑ता वा॒जिन॒मह्र॑ये॒  ॑
> धने ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । एषु । चाकंधि । पुरुहूत । सूरिषु । वृधासः । ये । मघवन् । आनशुः ।  
> मघं ।  
> अर्चंति । तोके । तनये । परिष्टिषु । मेधसाता । वाजिनं । अह्रये । धने ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पुरुहूतेंद्र एषु सूरिष्वा चाकंधि । अत्यर्थमभिदीप्यस्व। अभिकामयस्व॥
> कनी दीप्ति कांतिगतिषु । अस्माच्चर्करीतमेतत् ॥ हे मघवन्थनवन्निंद्र ये सूरयो
> वृधानस्त्वत्पसादाद्वर्धमानाः संतो मघं धनमानशुः प्राप्नु वंति । अपि च मेधसाता मेधसात् यज्ञे वाजिनं बलवंतमन्नवंतं वेजनवंतं ना त्वां येऽर्चंति

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, invoked by many, shine forth greatly (चाकंधि (*cākaṃdhi*)), take great delight, with regard to these सूरिषु (*sūriṣu*) (the praisers). The root is कनी दीप्ति कांतिगतिषु (*kanī dīpti kāṃtigatiṣu*), and this form is its intensive. O wealthy Indra, those praisers who, growing by your favour (वृधासः (*vṛdhāsaḥ*)), obtain wealth (मघं (*maghaṃ*)); and who, in the sacrifice (मेधसाता (*medhasātā*)), honour you, the powerful, food-possessing (वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)) one…

### Printed p. 985
*Gist (continued):* …they honour you, for the sake of a son (तोके (*toke*)), a grandson (तनये (*tanaye*)), other desired fruits on every side (परिष्टिषु (*pariṣṭiṣu*)), and shameless (अह्रये (*ahraye*)) wealth, that is, wealth honestly obtained. When these are the occasions, they honour you alone with praises and the like. This is the meaning.

> पूजयंति तोके पुत्रे तनये तत्पुत्रे परिष्टिषु परित इष्यमाणेष्वन्येष्वपि
> फलेष्वह्रयेऽलज्जाकरे धने च । एतेषु निमित्तेषु सत्सु त्वामेव स्तुश्चा दिभिः
> पूजयंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)—O Indra, worthy of invocation by many
- एषु सूरिषु (*eṣu sūriṣu*)—with regard to these praisers
- आ चाकंधि (*ā cākaṃdhi*)—be greatly well-disposed
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- ये (*ye*)—those praisers
- वृधासः (*vṛdhāsaḥ*)—growing by your favour
- मघं (*maghaṃ*)—wealth
- आनशुः (*ānaśuḥ*)—obtain; and
- मेधसाता (*medhasātā*)—in the sacrifice
- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—you, who are endowed with strength or with food
- अर्चंति (*arcaṃti*)—those who honour (you)
- तोके (*toke*)—in obtaining a son
- तनये (*tanaye*)—also in obtaining a grandson
- परिष्टिषु (*pariṣṭiṣu*)—in the accomplishment of other desired fruits
- अह्रये (*ahraye*)—shameless, that is, honestly acquired
- धने (*dhane*)—also in obtaining wealth
- अर्चंति (*arcaṃti*)—those praisers honour you alone

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, invoked and called by many, be well-disposed toward the people who praise you. O wealthy Indra, those praisers, growing by your favour, obtain wealth. The people who honour you, who give strength or food, in the sacrifices, honour you alone, both when they have obtained children, grandchildren, desired objects and honestly acquired wealth, and in order to obtain them.

##### English translation
Indra the invoked of many, be gracious to these Suris, who thereby
prospering attain, O Maghavan, to opulence; (who) adore the powerful one
at the sacrifice (for the sake of obtaining) a son. a grand son, the fulfilment
of their desires, and honourable wealth.

> चिकेतति ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । इत् । नु । रायः । सुभृतस्य । चाकनत् । मदं । यः । अस्य । रंह्यं । चिकेतति।  
> त्वावृधः । मघवन् । दाशुअध्वरः । मक्षु । सः । वाजं । भरते । धना । नृभिः ॥४॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स इत् स एव स्तोता सुभृतस्य सुष्टु संपादितस्य रायो धनस्य । द्वितीयार्थे
> षष्ठी । ईदृशं धनं नु क्षिप्रं चाकनत्। कामयते । लभत इत्यर्थः । रंह्यं । रंहो
> वेगः । तदर्शमस्येंद्रस्य मदं सोमपानजन्यं हर्षं यः स्तोता चिकॆ तति
> स्तुतिपदैर्जानाति । हे मघवन् त्वावृधस्त्वया वर्धितो दाश्वध्वरो दत्तयज्ञो
> यजमानो नृभिर्नेतृभिर्युत्विग्भिर्भृत्यैर्वा धना धनानि वाजमन्नं च मक्षु शीघ्रं
> भरते । संपादयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That very praiser (स इत् (*sa it*)) quickly desires (चाकनत् (*cākanat*)), that is, obtains, such well-procured (सुभृतस्य (*subhṛtasya*)) wealth (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)); the genitive is used in the sense of the accusative. रंह्यं (*raṃhyaṃ*): *raṃhaḥ* is speed; for that purpose, the exhilaration (मदं (*madaṃ*)) of this Indra born of the drinking of Soma, which the praiser (यः (*yaḥ*)) knows (चिकेतति (*ciketati*)) through words of praise. O Maghavan, the sacrificer who is increased by you (त्वावृधः (*tvāvṛdhaḥ*)) and has given the sacrifice (दाश्वध्वरः (*dāśvadhvaraḥ*)), with the leaders (नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)), that is, priests or servants, quickly (मक्षु (*makṣu*)) brings (भरते (*bharate*)), that is, procures, riches (धना (*dhanā*)) and food (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra
- रंह्यं (*raṃhyaṃ*)—quickly arising
- मदं (*madaṃ*)—the exhilaration arising from drinking Soma
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the man who
- चिकेतति (*ciketati*)—knows
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- त्वावृधः (*tvāvṛdhaḥ*)—he who is increased by you
- दाश्वध्वरः (*dāśvadhvaraḥ*)—and has obtained the fruit of performing the sacrifice, that sacrificer
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—together with the priests, the leaders of the rite
- धना (*dhanā*)—riches
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- मक्षु (*makṣu*)—quickly
- भरते (*bharate*)—procures

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, the sacrificer who knows the exhilaration that quickly arises in you from the drinking of Soma, and who, increased by you, has obtained the fruit of performing the sacrifice, quickly obtains riches and food together with his own people, the priests who lead the rites and others.

##### English translation
He obtains well-procured riches, who studies to promote Indra's rapid
exhilaration. Exalted by (your favour), O Maghavan, (the worshipper),
celebrating the sacrifice, speedily obtains through the officiating priests, food
and wealth.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं शर्धा॑य महि॒ना गृ॑णा॒न उ॒रु कृ॑धि मघवङ्॒ग्धि रा॒यः ।

> हे इंद्र त्वं महिना महता स्तोत्रेण गृणानः स्तूयमानः सञ्छार्थाय
> शर्धं बलमुरु कृधि । विस्तीर्णं कुरु । हे मघवन् रायो धनानि च शग्नि । अस्मभ्यं
> प्रयच्छ । हे दस्म दर्शनीयेंद्र विभक्ता विशेषेण धनानां भाजयिता त्वं मित्रो
> वरुणो न मित्रवद्वरुणवच्च माया प्रज्ञायुक्तः सन्नोऽस्मभ्यं । नः संप्रत्यर्थे ।
> संप्रति पित्वोऽन्नानि दयसे । प्रयच्छसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, praised (गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)) with a great (महिना (*mahinā*)) hymn, make strength (शर्धं (*śardhaṃ*)) wide (उरु कृधि (*uru kṛdhi*)), that is, increase it. O Maghavan, give (शग्नि (*śagni*)) us riches (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)) as well. O beautiful (दस्म (*dasma*)) Indra, you the distributor (विभक्ता (*vibhaktā*)), who especially apportion riches, being endowed with wisdom (माया (*māyā*)) like Mitra and Varuṇa (मित्रो वरुणो न (*mitro varuṇo na*)), give (दयसे (*dayase*)) us food (पित्वः (*pitvaḥ*)). नः (*naḥ*) here is in the sense of "now" (संप्रति (*saṃprati*)).

- शग्नि (*śagni*)—give us
- दस्म (*dasma*)—O Indra of attractive form
- विभक्ता (*vibhaktā*)—who especially distribute wealth to the praisers
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- मित्रः न (*mitraḥ na*)—like Mitra
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—and like Varuṇa
- माया (*māyā*)—endowed with wisdom
- स्तो (*sto*)—(not printed)
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us

- पित्वः (*pitvaḥ*)—food
- दयसे (*dayase*)—you give

**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, praised with great hymns, increase our strength. O wealthy Indra, give us riches as well. O Indra of beautiful form, you who distribute riches among the praisers, endowed with discernment and wisdom like Mitra and Varuṇa, now provide us with food and other nourishment.

## Sūkta 148 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुष्वाहास इति पंचर्चं विंशं सूक्तं वेनपुत्रस्य पृथोरार्षं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । अनुक्रांतं च । सुष्वाहासः पृथुर्वैन्य इति । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning सुष्वाहास (*suṣvāhāsa*), of five Ṛks, is the twentieth sūkta; its seer is Pṛthu, son of Vena; its metre is Triṣṭubh and its deity Indra. The Anukramaṇī says सुष्वाहासः पृथुर्वैन्य (*suṣvāhāsaḥ pṛthurvainya*). The viniyoga has been stated before.

**NOTE**

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning सुष्वाणासः (*suṣvāṇāsaḥ*) is the twentieth sūkta in the eleventh Anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Pṛthu, son of Vena; the deity is Indra; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said सुष्वाणासः पृथुर्वैश्यः (*suṣvāṇāsaḥ pṛthurvaiśyaḥ*); the viniyoga has been stated before.

Sūkta 148. Maṇḍala 10. Anuvāka 11. Sūkta 148. Aṣṭaka 8. Adhyāya 8. Varga 6. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Pṛthu Vainya. Deity: Indra. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒ष्वा॒णास॑ इंद्र स्तु॒मसि॑ त्वा सस॒वांस॑श्च तुविनृम्न॒ वाजं॑ ।  
> आ नो॑ भर सुवि॒तं यस्य॑ चा॒कन्मना॒ तना॑ सनुयाम॒ त्वोताः॑॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुस्वानासः । इंद्र । स्तुमसि । त्वा । सस्यावांसः । च । तुविनृम्म । वाजं ।  
> आ । नः । भर । सुवितं । यस्य । चाकन् । त्मना । तना । सनुयाम । त्वाऊताः ॥१॥

### Printed p. 989

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र सुष्वाणासः सोममभिषुतवंतो वयं त्वां स्तुमसि । स्तुमः । हे
> तुविन्नृम्म बहुलधन वाजं चरुपुरोडाशादिलक्षणमन्नं ससवांसः संभक्तवंतश्च
> वयं त्वां स्तुमः । यत एवमतो हेतोर्नोऽस्मभ्यं सुवितं सुष्टु प्राप्तव्यं
> शोभनं धनमा भर ! आहर्त्व! प्रयच्छ! यद्वा! यस्य यद्धनमतिप्रियत्वेन चाकन्
> त्वं कामयसे तद्धनमा भरेत्यर्थः । वयं च त्वोतास्त्वया रक्षिताः संतस्तना ।
> धननामैतत् । विस्त्रतानि धनानि त्मनात्मना स्वयमेवान्यनैरपेक्ष्येणैव सनुयाम ।
> तव प्रसादाल्लभेमहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, we who have pressed the Soma praise you. O Indra of abundant wealth (तुविन्नृम्म (*tuvinnṛmma*)), we who have also obtained food (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)), in the form of cooked offerings, cakes and the like, praise you. Therefore bring us (आ भर (*ā bhara*)) good, well-obtainable wealth (सुवितं (*suvitaṃ*))." Alternatively: bring that wealth which you, in your great love, desire (चाकन् (*cākan*)). Protected by you, may we obtain by ourselves (त्मना (*tmanā*)), without depending on others, the widespread riches (तना (*tanā*), a name for wealth); may we gain them by your grace.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सुष्वाणासः (*suṣvāṇāsaḥ*)—we who are pressing the Soma juice
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- स्तुमसि (*stumasi*)—we praise
- तुविनृम्म (*tuvinṛmma*)—O Indra, possessed of abundant strength or wealth
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- ससवांसः च (*sasavāṃsaḥ ca*)—and also, desiring to obtain it, we praise you
- यस्य (*yasya*)—which wealth
- चाकन् (*cākan*)—you wish to give us
- सुवितं (*suvitaṃ*)—such wealth as is to be obtained by us
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—bring (we also)
- तोताः (*totāḥ*)—protected by you
- तना (*tanā*)—abundant wealth
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—through you yourself
- सनुयाम (*sanuyāma*)—may we obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, we who are pressing the Soma juice praise you. O Indra, possessed of great strength or wealth, desiring to obtain food, we also praise you. Bring us precisely that wealth which you wish to give us. Protected by you, may we obtain wealth through you yourself.

##### English translation
Having poured out the libation, we praise you, Indra; having presented the sacrificial food, we (praise you), granter of abundant wealth ; bring us the wealth which one longs for; protected by you may we acquire riches through yourself alone.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋ॒ष्वस्त्वमिं॑द्र शूर जा॒तो दासी॒र्विशः॒ सूर्ये॑ण सह्याः ।  

### Printed p. 990

> गुहा॑ हि॒तं गुह्यं॑ गू॒ळम॒प्पु जि॑भ्र॒मसि॑ प्र॒स्रव॑णे॒ न सोमं॑॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऋष्वः । त्वं । इंद्र । शूर । जातः । दासीः । विशः । सूर्येण । सह्याः ।  
> गुहा । हितं । गुह्यं । गूळ्हं । अप्सु । बिभ्रमसि । प्रस्रवणे । न । सोमं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शूर शौर्यवन्निंद्र ऋष्टो महान्दर्शनीयो ना त्वं जातो जातमात्र
> एव दासीः । उपक्षयकारिणो दासा असुराः । तत्संबंधिनीर्विशः प्रजाः सूर्येण
> सूर्यात्मना सह्याः । अभ्यभवः । तथा गुहा गुहायां हितं निहितं अत एव गुह्यमदृश्यं वलाख्यमसुरमप्पूदकेषु गूढं निगूढं कुयवाख्यं त्वमभिभूतवानसि । वयमपि प्रस्रवणे प्रवर्षणे सति। नः संप्रत्यर्थे । संप्रति सोमं बिभ्रमसि ।
> त्वदर्थं बिभ्रमः । धारयामः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O hero Indra, you who are mighty (ऋष्वः (*ṛṣvaḥ*), great and beautiful to behold), as soon as you were born you overcame with the sun's form the Dāsa tribes, the Asuras who cause destruction (दासीः (*dāsīḥ*)), that is, their people. You also overcame the invisible Asura named Vala, hidden in a cave, and the Asura named Kuyava, hidden in the waters. And we too, now that the Soma is flowing in a stream (प्रस्रवणे (*prasravaṇe*)), hold it (बिभ्रमसि (*bibhramasi*)) for you; न (*na*) here has the sense "now".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शूर (*śūra*)—valiant
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ऋष्वः (*ṛṣvaḥ*)—of great form or of attractive form
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- जातः (*jātaḥ*)—as soon as you were born
- दासीः (*dāsīḥ*)—belonging to the Dāsa race
- विशः (*viśaḥ*)—the subjects, that is, the people
- सूर्येण (*sūryeṇa*)—in the form of the sun
- सह्याः (*sahyāḥ*)—you have overcome; likewise
- गुहा (*guhā*)—in a secret place
- हितं (*hitaṃ*)—hidden
- गुह्यं (*guhyaṃ*)—the Asura named Vala, who was seen by no one
- अप्सु (*apsu*)—in the waters
- गूढं (*gūḍhaṃ*)—the Asura named Kuyava, hidden in concealment, you have also overcome. We too
- न (*na*)—now
- प्रस्रवणे (*prasravaṇe*)—while the pressed juice flows in a stream
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—that Soma juice
- बिभ्रमसि (*bibhramasi*)—we stand holding for you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O valiant Indra, you of beautiful form, as soon as you were born you overcame in the form of the sun the Dasyu peoples; likewise you defeated the Asura named Vala, hidden in a secret place unseen by anyone, and the Asura named Kuyava, secretly hidden in the waters. While the Soma juice, pressed, flows in stream after stream, we stand holding it in our hands to offer it to you.

### Printed p. 991

##### English translation
Hero Indra, you are mighty, may you as soon as you are born you overcome with Surya the races of the Dasas, and the fugitive (Vala) lurking in secrecy, hidden in the waters; we now present to you the Soma in a copious stream.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒र्यो वा॒ गिरो॑ अ॒भ्य॑र्च वि॒द्वान्ऋषी॑णां॒ विप्रः॑ सुम॒तिं  ॒॑
> चकानः ।  
> ते स्या॑म॒ ये र॒णयं॑त॒ सोमै॑रे॒नोत तुभ्यं॑ रथोळ्ह  ॒
> भक्षैः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अर्यः । वा । गिरः । अभि । अर्च । विद्वान् । ऋषीणां । विप्रः । सुमतिं । चकानः ।  
> ते । स्याम । ये । रणयंत । सोमैः । एना । उत । तुभ्यं । रथओळ्ह । भक्षैः ॥३॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विप्रो मेधाव्यृषीणां मंत्रदर्शिनां सुमतिं सुष्टुतिं चकानः कामयमानो विद्वाञ्ज्ञानन्नर्यो वा स्वामीा च भवन् हे इंद्र ईदृशस्त्वं गिरः स्तोत्यान् स्तुतीर्वाभ्यर्च । सम्यक्सुतमित्यभिपूजय । अपि च ते वयं स्याम भवेम
> ये सोमैस्त्वां रणयंत रमयंति । उतापि च हे रथोळ्ह रथैरभ्युह्यमान ॥ आ
> ऊढ ओढः । रथेन ओढो रथोढः । ओमाजोश्च । पा. ६-१-९५ । इति पररूपं ॥
> ईदृशेंद्र भक्षैर्भक्षणीयैश्चरुपुरोडाशादिभिः सार्धमेनेमानि स्तोत्राणि तुभ्यं
> त्वदर्थं क्रियंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The wise man (विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)), desiring the good praise of the seers, the mantra-seers, being knowing and a lord (अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)), that is, you, O Indra, being such, honour the praises of the singers (गिरः (*giraḥ*)): "do honour (अभ्यर्च (*abhyarca*))" means honour them as well pressed. And may we be among those who gratify you with Soma. And, O car-borne one (रथोळ्ह (*rathoḷha*)), one carried by chariots, these praises are made for you together with edible offerings, the cooked offerings, cakes and the like. (The remainder of the block is a grammatical note on रथोळ्ह (*rathoḷha*), with Pā. Sū. 6-1-95.)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—the wise one
- ऋषीणां (*ṛṣīṇāṃ*)—of the mantra-seers
- सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)—good praise
- चकानः (*cakānaḥ*)—one who desires
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—one who has knowledge
- अर्यो वा (*aryo vā*)—and the lord of all, O Indra, you being such
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—the praises made by the singers

### Printed p. 992

- अभ्यर्च (*abhyarca*)—approve
- ये (*ye*)—those who
- सोमैः (*somaiḥ*)—with Soma juices
- रणयंत (*raṇayaṃta*)—delight you
- ते (*te*)—we, such persons
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we be worthy of your favour
- उत (*uta*)—and
- रथोळ्ह (*rathoḷha*)—O Indra, borne by a chariot
- भक्षैः (*bhakṣaiḥ*)—together with edible offerings such as cooked offerings and cakes
- एना (*enā*)—these praises
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you
- are offered

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you are wise, desirous of the good praises made by the seers, discerning, lord of all. Being such, approve and welcome the praises made by the singers. May we, who gladden you with Soma juices, be worthy of your favour; and, O Indra, borne by a chariot, these edible offerings, the cooked offerings, cakes and the rest, and these praises have been prepared for you alone.

##### English translation
Do you, who are the lord, who are wise, a sage desirous of the good opinion of the Rishis, do honour to your praisers; may we be of those who gratify (you) with soma libations; to you, O car-borne Indra, these (praises are offered) with sacrificial viands.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मा ब्रह्में॑द्र॒ तुभ्यं॑ शंसि॒ दा नृभ्यो॑ नृ॒णां शू॑र॒ शवः॑ ।  
> तेभि॑र्भव॒ सक्र॑तु॒र्येषु॑ चा॒कन्नु॒त त्रा॑यस्व गृण॒त उ॒त  
> स्तीन् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमा । ब्रह्म । इंद्र । तुभ्यं । शंसि । दाः । नृभ्यः । नृणां । शूर । शवः ।  
> तेभिः । भव । सक्रतुः । येषु । चाकन् । उत । त्रायस्व । गृणतः । उत । स्तीन् ॥४॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वदर्थमिमेमानि पुरोवर्तीनि ब्रह्म ब्रह्माणि परिवृढानि स्तोत्राणि
> शंसि । अशंसिषत । शस्यंते ॥ शंसेश्चांदसे कर्मणि लुजि व्यत्ययेनैकवचनं ॥ हे

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, for you these present great praises (ब्रह्म (*brahma*), "swollen" hymns) have been recited (शंसि (*śaṃsi*), the passive aorist of शंस (*śaṃsa*), with the singular used irregularly for the plural). The continuation is on the next page.

### Printed p. 993

> शूर शौर्यवन्निंद्र त्वं नृणां मनुष्याणां मध्यॆ नृभ्यः स्तुत्यादेर्नेतृभ्यः शवो
> बलं दाः । देहि । अपि च तेभिस्तैः सक्रतुः समानकर्मा समानप्रज्ञो वा भव येषु
> स्तोतृषु चाकन् हविरादि कामयसे ॥ कन दीप्ति कांतिगतिषु । अस्माद्यज्लुगंताच्छांदसे लजि सिपि रूपमेतत् । कमर्वा पूर्ववत् । सिपि मो नो धातोरिति
> नत्वं ॥ उतापि च गृणतः स्तोत्यंस्त्रायस्व । पालय । उतापि च स्तीन् ॥ स्त्यायतेरेतद्रूपं ॥ संघीभूय स्थितान्यजमानानपि त्रायस्व ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O hero Indra, among men give strength (शवः (*śavaḥ*)) to the leaders (नृभ्यः (*nṛbhyaḥ*)), those who lead in praise and the like (दाः (*dāḥ*) = give). Be of one deed or one mind (सक्रतुः (*sakratuḥ*)) with those singers among whom you desire (चाकन् (*cākan*)) the oblation and the rest. Protect the singers who praise, and also the स्तीन् (*stīn*), the sacrificers who stand together in a group. (Grammatical notes on चाकन् (*cākan*) from कन (*kana*) and on स्तीन् (*stīn*) from *styāyati* are omitted here.)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you
- इमा ब्रह्म (*imā brahma*)—these praises
- शंसि (*śaṃsi*)—are recited
- शूर (*śūra*)—O Indra, the hero, you
- नृणां (*nṛṇāṃ*)—among men
- नृभ्यः (*nṛbhyaḥ*)—to the chief praisers
- शवः (*śavaḥ*)—strength
- दाः (*dāḥ*)—give (and)
- येषु (*yeṣu*)—among whichever singers
- चाकन् (*cākan*)—you wish to receive oblations and the like
- तेभिः (*tebhiḥ*)—by those singers
- सुक्रतुः (*sukratuḥ*)—worshipful through good ritual performance
- भव (*bhava*)—be
- उत (*uta*)—and
- गृणतः (*gṛṇataḥ*)—the people who praise
- उत (*uta*)—and
- स्तीन् (*stīn*)—the sacrificers
- त्रायस्व (*trāyasva*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, it is for your satisfaction that these great praises are recited. O hero, give strength to those among men who praise you especially. Be worshipful in the rites of those singers in whose sacrifices you desire to receive the oblation. And protect the singers who praise you, and the sacrificers.

##### English translation
To you, Indra, have these prayers been addressed; grant, O hero, strength to the leaders of men; be of one mind with those in whome you delighted, and protect those who praise you, and the worshippers who stand round about.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श्रु॒धी हव॑मिंद्र शूर॒ पृथ्या॑ उ॒त स्त॑वसे वे॒न्यस्या॒र्कैः ।  
> आ यस्ते॒ योनिं॑ घृ॒तवं॑त॒मस्वा॑रू॒र्मिन् निम्मैर्द्र॑वयंत॒  ॑
> वक्वाः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

### Printed p. 994

> श्रुधि । हवं । इंद्र । शूर । पृथ्याः । उत । स्तवसे । वेन्यस्य । अर्कैः ।  
> आ । यः । ते । योनिं । धृतवंतं । अस्वाः । ऊर्मिः । न । निम्मैः । द्रवयंत ।  
> वक्त्वा ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शूरेंद्र पृथ्याः पृथोर्ऋषेर्मम हवमाह्वानं श्रुधि । शृणु । उतापि
> च वेन्यस्य वेनपुत्रस्य ममार्कैर्मंत्रैः स्तवसे । स्तूयसे ॥ यकि प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेन
> शप् ॥ यः स्तोता धृतवंतमुदकवंतं ते तव योनिं निवासभूमिमास्वाः अभ्यस्वार्षित् अभ्यष्टौत् ॥ स्व शब्दोपतायोः । अस्माल्लुजि शिपि बहुलं छंदसीतीडभावे
> हल् ज्यादिलोपे च रात्सस्यॆति सलोपः ॥ यद्वा । धृतवंतमाज्यादिना हविषोपेतं
> योनिं । गृहनामैतत् । यज्ञगृहं प्राप्य ते त्वां योऽभिष्ति तस्य वेन्यस्यार्कैरित्यन्वयः । अपि च वक्वा वक्वानः ॥ वचेरन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यंत इति वनिप् । अंत्यविकारश्चांदसः । जसि पृषोदरादित्वाद्वर्णलोपः ॥ अन्येऽपि सर्वॆ स्तोतारो निम्मैः
> प्रवणैर्मार्गैरूर्मिनोदकसंघ इव द्रवयंत । स्तुतिभिस्तामेवाभिद्रवंति ।
> अभिगच्छंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O hero Indra, hear the call (हवं (*havaṃ*)) of me, Pṛthu the seer (पृथ्याः (*pṛthyāḥ*)). You are praised (स्तवसे (*stavase*)) with the mantras (अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*)) of me, the son of Vena (वेन्यस्य (*venyasya*)). The worshipper who praises (आस्वाः (*āsvāḥ*)) your abode (योनिं (*yoniṃ*)), full of water (धृतवंतं (*dhṛtavaṃtaṃ*))—or else: who, having come to the sacrificial house provided with oblations such as ghee, praises you—of him, the son of Vena, with whose mantras you are praised. And the other singers (वक्वा (*vakvā*)) too all rush (द्रवयंत (*dravayaṃta*)) with praises towards you alone, like a flood of water (ऊर्मिः (*ūrmiḥ*)) along sloping (निम्मैः (*nimmaiḥ*)) channels. (Grammatical notes omitted.)

- हवं (*havaṃ*)—the call
- श्रुधि (*śrudhi*)—hear
- उत (*uta*)—and
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the worshipper who

- आ स्वाः (*ā svāḥ*)—praises [or: धृतवंतं (*dhṛtavaṃtaṃ*)—provided with oblations such as ghee; योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—having come to the sacrificial house; ते (*te*)—you; आ स्वाः (*ā svāḥ*)—praises] such a one
- वेन्यस्य (*venyasya*)—of me, the son of Vena

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O valiant Indra, hear the call of me, named Pṛthu. The one who praises your abode filled with water, or who, having come to the sacrificial house full of oblations such as ghee, praises you there—of me, the son of Vena, with whose mantras you are praised.

### Printed p. 995
…he is praised by the mantras of me, the son of Vena, who praise your dwelling-place filled with water, or who go to the sacrificial house filled with oblations such as ghee and praise you there. Other praisers also approach you quickly with praises, like swiftly flowing water on a sloping, low-lying ground.

##### English translation
Hear, hero Indra, the invocation of Prithu; you are glorified by the praises of the son of Vena, who celebrated your hall of sacrifice, full of ghi; your praisers rush to you like a torrent through precipitous banks.

## Sūkta 149 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सविता यंत्रैरिति पंचर्चमेकविंशं सूक्तं हिरण्यस्तूपपुत्रस्यार्चत आर्षं
> त्रैष्टुभं सवितृदेवत्यं । अनुक्रांतं च । सवितार्चन्हैरण्यस्तूपः सावित्रमिति । गतो
> विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta सविता यंत्रैः (*savitā yaṃtraiḥ*) has five Ṛks and is the twenty-first sūkta. Its seer is Arcan, son of Hiraṇyastūpa; the deity is Savitṛ; the metre is Triṣṭubh. He cites the Anukramaṇī: सवितार्चन्हैरण्यस्तूपः सावित्रमिति (*savitārcanhairaṇyastūpaḥ sāvitramiti*). The viniyoga has already been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, सविता यंत्रैः (*savitā yaṃtraiḥ*), is the twenty-first sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Its seer is Arcan, son of the sage Hiraṇyastūpa; the deity is Savitṛ; the metre is Triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says: सवितार्चन् हैरण्यस्तूपः सावित्रं (*savitārcan hairaṇyastūpaḥ sāvitraṃ*). The viniyoga was stated earlier.

Sūkta 149; Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Aṣṭaka 8, Adhyāya 8, Varga 7. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Arcan Hairaṇyastūpa. Deity: Savitā. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒वि॒ता यं॒त्रैः पृ॑थि॒वीम॑रण्णादस्कंभ॒ने स॑वि॒ता द्याम॑दृंहत् ।  
> अश्व॑मिवाधुक्ष॒द्दु नि॑मं॒तरि॑क्षम॒तूर्ते॑ ब॒द्धं स॑वि॒ता स॑मु॒द्रं॥१॥

> अश्वं इव । अधुक्षत् । धुनिं । अंतरिक्षं । अतूर्ते । बद्धं । सविता । समुद्रं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सविता सर्वस्य प्रसविता प्रेरको मध्यमस्थानो देवः सोऽयं यंत्रैर्यमनसाधनैर्वृष्टिप्रदानादिभिरुपाय्कॆ र्वायवीय्यैः पाशैर्वा पृथिवीं प्रथितां
> भूमिमरम्मात् । अरमयत् । सुखेनावस्थापयति । तथा स एव सवितास्कंभने ।
> पतनप्रतिबंधकमालंबनं स्कंभनं । तद्रहिते स्थले द्यां द्युलोकमप्यदृंहत् ।
> दृढीकृतवान् । यथाधो न पतति तथात्मीयैरेवोपाय्कॆ रवस्थापितवानित्यर्थः ।
> अश्वमिव धुनिं कंपयितव्यं कंपयितारं वांतरिक्षमंतरा क्षांतं मध्यमस्थानगतमतूर्ते केनाप्यहिंसितेऽत्वरमाणे ना नभसि वायवीय्यैः पाशैर्बद्धं समुद्रं
> मेघमयमेव सविताधुक्षत् । उदकानि दोग्धि । यद्वा । अंतरिक्षमिति सप्तम्यर्थे
> प्रथमा । अतूर्तेऽंतरिक्षे बद्धं समुदितारं धुनिं कंपनीयं मेघमश्वमिनाधुक्षत् । सविता क्लेशयति ॥ धुक्ष संदीपनक्लेशनजीवनेषु ॥ यथा शिक्षकोऽश्वं क्लेशयत्येवं वर्षणाय मेघं क्लेशयतीत्यर्थः । अथ निरुक्तं । सविता यंत्रैः पृथिवीमरमयदनारंभणेऽंतरिक्षे सविता द्यामद्यंहदश्वमिनाधुक्षद्दु निमंतरिक्षे मेघं
> बद्धमतूर्ते बद्धमतूर्ण इति वात्वरमाण इति वा सविता समुदितारं । नि. १०-३२ ।
> इति !!

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Savitṛ, the impeller of all, the god of the middle region, has established the broad earth comfortably by his means of restraint (यंत्रैः (*yaṃtraiḥ*)), namely the bestowal of rain and the like, or the bonds that belong to the winds. In the same way he made the heaven firm in a place without support (अस्कंभने (*askaṃbhane*), where there is no prop to prevent falling), so that it does not fall downward; he set it up by his own means. Like a horse, he milked (अधुक्षत् (*adhukṣat*)) the shaking cloud (धुनिं (*dhuniṃ*)), bound by the winds' bonds in the unobstructed sky and unhurrying, the cloud called समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*), that is, he draws out its waters. Alternatively, अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*) is nominative in the sense of the locative: he milked the trembling cloud bound in the unobstructed firmament as a trainer troubles a horse; that is, he troubles the cloud to make it rain. (The root धुक्ष (*dhukṣa*) is taken in the senses of kindling, troubling, living.) He then quotes the Nirukta, सविता यंत्रैः पृथिवीमरमयत् (*savitā yaṃtraiḥ pṛthivīmaramayat*) and the rest, with the glosses of अतूर्ते (*atūrte*) as bound, "unhurried" or "hurrying" (Ni. 10-32).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सविता (*savitā*)—this god Savitṛ, who produces all things or impels all, a god of the middle region
- यंत्रैः (*yaṃtraiḥ*)—by means such as the bestowal of rain, or by the bonds called winds
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—this broad earth
- अरम्यात् (*aramyāt*)—has firmly established
- सविता (*savitā*)—that same Savitṛ
- अस्कंभने (*askaṃbhane*)—in the supportless firmament
- *dhyāṃ*—the world of Dyu (heaven)
- अदृंहत् (*adṛṃhat*)—has made firm so that it does not fall down
- धुनिं (*dhuniṃ*)—trembling
- अश्वमिव (*aśvamiva*)—like a horse
- अतूर्ते (*atūrte*)—unobstructed
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—in the firmament
- बद्धं (*baddhaṃ*)—bound by the rope that is the wind
- समुद्रं (*samudraṃ*)—the cloud (from the cloud)
- सविता (*savitā*)—this god Savitṛ
- अधुक्षत् (*adhukṣat*)—milked out the waters (as one milks)

### Printed p. 997

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This god Savitṛ, who impels or produces all beings, has bound this broad earth firmly with the bonds called winds (or with means such as the bestowal of rain) and established it so that it does not shake. In the firmament, which has no support at all, he has made the world of heaven stand so that it does not fall. From the cloud, which stands in the unobstructed sky, bound by the rope of the wind, without any support, like a trembling horse, this god Savitṛ milks the rain-water so that it falls on the earth.

##### English translation
Savitri has fixed the earth with fetters; Savitri has made the heaven firm in a place where there was no support; Savitri has milked the cloud of the firmament bound to the indestructible (ether) like a trembling horse.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Giving the derivation of the word Savitṛ, Yāska has given an explanation of this Ṛk: सविता । सविता सर्वस्य प्रसविता ॥ (*savitā | savitā sarvasya prasavitā ‖*) (Ni. 10-31). Savitā means the god who produces everything, or who is the cause of the production of all beings.
तस्यैषा भवति ॥ सविता यंत्रैः पृथिवीमरमयदनारंभणेऽन्तरीक्षे सविता द्यामदृंहदश्वमिनादुक्षद्दुनिमंतरिक्षे मेघं बद्धमतूर्ते बद्धमत्तूर्ण इति वात्वरमाण इति ना सविता समुदितारमिति ॥ (*tasyaiṣā bhavati ‖ savitā yaṃtraiḥ pṛthivīmaramayadanāraṃbhaṇe 'ntarīkṣe savitā dyāmadṛṃhadaśvaminādukṣaddunimaṃtarikṣe meghaṃ baddhamatūrte baddhamattūrṇa iti vātvaramāṇa iti nā savitā samuditāramiti ‖*) (Ni. 10-32)
The present Ṛk सविता यंत्रैः (*savitā yaṃtraiḥ*) praises this deity Savitṛ. Here the word यंत्र (*yaṃtra*) is formed from the root यम् (*yam*), which means to regulate, to keep under control. यंत्र (*yaṃtra*) means regulation, control, subjection.
सविता यंत्रैः पृथिवीं अरम्णात्-सविता यंत्रैः पृथिवीमरमयत् । (*savitā yaṃtraiḥ pṛthivīṃ aramṇāt-savitā yaṃtraiḥ pṛthivīmaramayat |*) This deity Savitṛ keeps this earth under his control by certain means and has established it firmly. What are the means? The bestowal of rain, illumination and so on. Without light and rain the beings on earth cannot live. Since the work of rain is subject to the rays of the sun, the earth, which depends on rain, also came under Savitṛ's control. That Savitṛ himself has made such an earth stand unshaking, that is, steady.

### Printed p. 998
अनारंभणेऽन्तरिक्षे सविताद्यामद्यंहत् (*anāraṃbhaṇe 'ntarikṣe savitādyāmadyaṃhat*)—This Savitṛ established the world of heaven firmly in the sky, which has no support. Nothing can be placed in the sky: if a blade of grass is thrown into the sky it does not stay there but falls at once. That being so, this Savitṛ has established so great a heaven firmly in the sky, without any support, so that it does not fall.
अश्वमिवाधुक्षद्दुनिमंतरिक्षे मेघं बद्धमतूर्ते बद्धमतूर्ण इति वात्वरमाण इति ना सविता समुदितारमिति (*aśvamivādhukṣaddunimaṃtarikṣe meghaṃ baddhamatūrte baddhamatūrṇa iti vātvaramāṇa iti nā savitā samuditāramiti*)—आतूर्ते (*ātūrte*) means unharmed, in an unobstructed place. In the sky anything may move without obstruction; nothing there stops it. When an animal moves on earth, mountains, trees, rivers and the like met across its path can block its going; but when birds and the like move in the sky, nothing there blocks them. Therefore आतूर्ते (*ātūrte*) means unharmed, unobstructed, without hindrance. In such a sky Savitṛ milks, in the form of rain, the water in the clouds bound by the wind. An illustration is given here: अश्वमिव (*aśvamiva*), like a horse. A horse makes the dust on its body fall down by shaking (shaking its body). In the same way Savitṛ makes the waters in the clouds fall on the earth as raindrops; this is the intention.
कमन्यं मध्यमादेवमवक्ष्यत् । आदित्योऽपि सवितोच्यते । तथा च हैरण्यस्तूपे स्तुतोर्चन् हिरण्यस्तूपऋषिरिदं सूक्तं प्रोवाच ॥ (*kamanyaṃ madhyamādevamavakṣyat | ādityo 'pi savitocyate | tathā ca hairaṇyastūpe stutorcan hiraṇyastūpaṛṣiridaṃ sūktaṃ provāca ‖*) (Ni. 10-32)
Whom else but this Savitṛ, a deity of the middle region, could the seer have praised in this sūkta? The Āditya too is called Savitṛ. The seer Hiraṇyastūpa, praising the god Savitṛ, said just what is in this sūkta. The matter is touched upon in the next Ṛk (the 5th Ṛk of this sūkta).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यत्र यस्मिन्नंतरिक्षे समुद्रः समुंदनशीलो मेघः स्कभितः स्तंभितो
> वायुपाशैर्बद्धः सन् व्यौनत् विशेषेण भूमिमुनत्ति उदकैः क्लेदयति ॥ उंदी
> क्वेदने । अस्माच्छांदसे लज् रूपमेतत् ॥ हे अपां नपान्मध्यमस्थान वैद्युताग्ने
> तव संबंधी सविता प्रेरको देवस्तस्य तत्स्थानं वेद । वेत्ति । जानाति । अतोऽस्मादेव
> सवितुर्भूर्भूमिरासीत् । आत एवोत्तितमूर्ध्वमेव स्थितं रजोऽंतरिक्षमाः ।
> आसीत् । अजायत ॥ अस्त्रेLर्लुजि बहुलं छंदसीतीडभावः । हल् ज्याब्ब इति लोपः ॥
> अतोऽस्मादेव सवितुर्द्व्यानापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यावप्रथेतां । विस्तीर्णे अप्यभूतां॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Where, in which firmament, the cloud called समुद्रः (*samudraḥ*) (that which wets), held fast and bound by the bonds of the wind, व्यौनत् (*vyaunat*), wets the earth specially with waters. (The root उंदी (*uṃdī*) is in the sense of wetting; this is a Vedic लज् (*laj*) form.) O अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*), Vaidyuta Agni of the middle region, your related Savitṛ, the impelling god, knows (वेद (*veda*) = वेत्ति (*vetti*), जानाति (*jānāti*)) that place. From this same Savitṛ the earth came to be (भूः (*bhūḥ*)); from him too the raised, upward-standing रजः (*rajaḥ*), the firmament, was born (आः (*āḥ*) = आसीत् (*āsīt*), अजायत (*ajāyata*)). From him too heaven and earth became extended (अप्रथेतां (*aprathetāṃ*)), that is, became wide.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अपां नपात् (*apāṃ napāt*)—O Agni, god of the middle region, your relative
- सविता (*savitā*)—Savitṛ, the impeller of all
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which firmament
- समुद्रः (*samudraḥ*)—the cloud
- स्कभितः (*skabhitaḥ*)—standing firm on the support of the wind
- व्यौनत् (*vyaunat*)—wets (the earth with rain)
- तस्य (*tasya*)—such a (firmament) place
- वेद (*veda*)—can know
- अतः (*ataḥ*)—from that Savitṛ
- भूः (*bhūḥ*)—the earth came into being
- अतः (*ataḥ*)—from this Savitṛ
- उत्तितं (*uttitaṃ*)—lofty
- रजः (*rajaḥ*)—the world of the firmament
- आः (*āḥ*)—came about
- अतः (*ataḥ*)—from this Savitṛ
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth (the worlds of heaven and earth)
- अप्रथेतां (*aprathetāṃ*)—(having come into being) spread out widely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, god of the middle region, your relative Savitṛ knows the nature of that firmament in which the cloud, held there by the help of the wind, wets the earth with rain. Savitṛ is also the cause of the origin of these widely spread heaven and earth.

##### English translation
Where the cloud thus arrested shed moisture (on the earth) Savitri, O grandson of the waters, knew that (place); from thence proceeded the

### Printed p. 1000
earth, thence arose the firmament, thence the heaven and earth were spread out.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

How is Savitṛ related to the Agni of the middle region? As stated in आदित्योऽपि सवितोच्यते (*ādityo 'pi savitocyate*) (Ni. 10-32), this Savitṛ is Āditya. There is not much difference between Āditya and Savitṛ. The rising Āditya is called Savitṛ. Agni is known in three forms: on earth as Agni (terrestrial fire), in the firmament as Vaidyuta Agni (lightning), in heaven as Āditya. Therefore Āditya, or Savitṛ, is here said to be related to Agni. That the earth and the other worlds are said here to have originated from the sun accords with modern science.

> अंग स्तोतः सुपर्णः शोभनपतनो गरुत्मान्नोमस्यापहर्तार् ताक्ष्यः सवितुः प्रेर-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This other deity, different from Savitṛ, पश्चा (*paścā*) (afterwards; पश्च पश्चा च छंदसि (*paśca paścā ca chaṃdasi*), Pā. 5-3-33, is the sūtra for this formation), became worthy of worship only after Savitṛ's impulsion. By what means? By भूना (*bhūnā*), that is, by Soma, which has come to be and arisen in heaven, the world called heaven that belongs to the deathless world. Alternatively: this other deity, belonging to the deathless world, became worthy of worship endowed with भूना (*bhūnā*), that is, plenitude. Why? He answers: O अंग (*aṃga*), praiser, the सुपर्णः (*suparṇaḥ*), the beautifully flying गरुत्मान् (*garutmān*), Tārkṣya, the carrier-off of Soma, of Savitṛ the impeller….

### Printed p. 1001

> कादस्माद्देवात्पूर्वः प्रथमभावी सञ्चातः । अतो हेतोः सुपर्णो गरुत्मानस्य
> सवितुर्धर्म धारणमनुसृत्य वर्तते । सवितृप्रेरणाधीनत्वात्सर्वगतीनां सोमाहरणमपि तदधीनमिति सवितृप्रेरणानंतरमेव सर्वे सोमयागाः प्रवर्तंत इत्यर्थः ।
> उ इति पूरकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues his explanation of the verse. The deity (Soma) is "prior", that is, first-born, in relation to Savitṛ. For this reason Suparṇa, that is Garutmān, follows this Savitṛ's dharma, his upholding. All movements depend on Savitṛ's impulsion, so the bringing of Soma depends on it too. Hence all Soma sacrifices proceed only after Savitṛ's impulsion. The particle उ (*u*) is a filler.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अन्यत् (*anyat*)—other than Savitṛ
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—this other deity
- पश्चा (*paścā*)—afterwards
- अमर्त्यस्य (*amartyasya*)—of the deathless
- भुवनस्य (*bhuvanasya*)—of the world of heaven
- भूना (*bhūnā*)—connected with it, that is, with the Soma born in heaven
- यजत्रं (*yajatraṃ*)—worthy of sacrifice
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—became
- अंग (*aṃga*)—O worshipper
- सुपर्णः (*suparṇaḥ*)—of swift flight
- गरुत्मान् (*garutmān*)—Tārkṣya (the Śyena bird), who brought Soma from heaven
- सवितुः (*savituḥ*)—by the impulsion of this Savitṛ
- पूर्वः (*pūrvaḥ*)—first
- जातः (*jātaḥ*)—was born; therefore
- सः (*saḥ*)—this Tārkṣya
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Savitṛ
- धर्म अनु (*dharma anu*)—follows his upholding
- उ (*u*)—certainly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma is a deity other than Savitṛ. Since it was in heaven, where the deathless dwell, Tārkṣya (the Śyena bird) brought it to the earth by Savitṛ's impulsion. This Tārkṣya, born from Savitṛ, brought Soma from heaven only by his impulsion. For this reason Soma became worthy of sacrifice, and Tārkṣya too remains subject to Savitṛ and follows him.

##### English translation
Afterwards arose this other adorable (deity), together with the host of the immortal world, the bright-winged Garutmat, born before Savitri obeyed his law.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Everything is born by the impulsion of Savitṛ, and all activity goes on by his impulsion only. Therefore Tārkṣya, who brought Soma from heaven to the earth, was born from Savitṛ himself, and he brought Soma from heaven to the earth by Savitṛ's impulsion alone. Soma, brought in this way, became worthy of worship in sacrifices and the like; that is, it gained an honoured place and a claim to praise in sacrifices. The chief purport is that the performance of Soma sacrifices continues only by the impulsion of the god Savitṛ.

> गावःइव । ग्रामं । युयुधिःइव । अश्वान् । वाश्राइव । वत्सं । सुमनाः ।  
> दुहाना ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गाव इव यथारण्ये संचरंतो गावो ग्रामं शीघ्रमभिगच्छंति । युयुधिरिव यथा च युद्धार्थमश्वानभिगच्छति ॥ युध संप्रहारे । आद्यगमहनजनेत्यत्रोत्सर्गश्चंदसि । पा. ३-२-१७१-२ । इति वचनात्किन्मत्तयः । छांदसं सांहितिकमभ्यासदीर्घत्वं ॥ सुमनाः शोभनमनस्का दुहाना दोग्री बहुपयस्का वाश्रेव हंभारवात्मकं शब्दं कुर्वती गौर्यथात्मीयं वत्समभिगच्छति । पतिरिव यथा भर्ता जायां
> स्वभार्यां शीघ्रमभिगच्छति एवमेव सविता नोऽस्मान्नभ्येतु । नितरामभिगच्छतु ।
> कीदृशः । दिवो द्युलोकस्य धर्ता धारयितावस्थापयिता ना अत एव विश्वावारः
> सर्वैवर्णनीयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Like cows": as cows roaming in the forest go quickly to the village. "Like a Yuyudhi": as a warrior goes to his horses for battle. Sāyaṇa derives the word from the root युध (*yudha*) "to fight". The reduplicative lengthening is Vedic and belongs to the Saṃhitā. सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*) means good-minded, दुहाना (*duhānā*) a good milker with much milk, वाश्रेव (*vāśreva*) a cow uttering the sound *hambhā* (lowing). As such a cow goes to her own calf, and as a husband goes quickly to his wife, so may Savitṛ come to us and approach us closely. He is the upholder of the sky (दिवः (*divaḥ*), the world of heaven), the sustainer, the establisher; therefore he is विश्ववारः (*viśvavāraḥ*), to be chosen by all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गावइव (*gāvaiva*)—as cows that went to graze in the forest
- ग्रामं (*grāmaṃ*)—return to the village
- युयुधिरिव (*yuyudhiriva*)—as a warrior who has set out for battle
- अश्वान् (*aśvān*)—goes to his horses
- सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*)—well-disposed
- दुहाना (*duhānā*)—giving much milk
- वाश्रेव (*vāśreva*)—and lowing, the cow
- वत्सं (*vatsaṃ*)—as she goes lowing to her calf
- पतिरिव (*patiriva*)—as the husband
- जायां (*jāyāṃ*)—goes quickly to his wife
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the sky-world
- धर्ता (*dhartā*)—the upholder
- विश्ववारः (*viśvavāraḥ*)—therefore desired by all
- सविता (*savitā*)—this god Savitṛ
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- नि अभि एतु (*ni abhi etu*)—(with great regard) draw near

### Printed p. 1003

#### Ṛk 4 (continued)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As cows that went to graze in the forest return quickly to the village in the evening; as a warrior who has set out for battle goes to his horses; as a cow that is well-disposed, gives much milk and lows eagerly for her calf goes eagerly to her calf; as a man goes lovingly to his dear wife: so may this god Savitṛ, the upholder (nourisher) of the sky and desired by all, come to us quickly, or in order to show favour.

##### English translation
As cattle hasten to the village, as the warrior to his horses, as affectionate milk-giving cows to the calf, as a husband to his wife, so may Savitri, the upholder of the sky, the desired of all. hasten to us
