> अहं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सवितः प्रेरक त्वा त्वामांगिरसोऽंगिरसः पुत्रो हिरण्यस्तूपो मम
> पितास्मिन्वाजेऽन्ने निमित्तभूते सति यथा जुह्वे आहूतवान् एवैवमर्चन्नेतत्संज्योऽहं त्वा त्वामवसेऽवनाय रक्षणार्थं वंदमानः स्तुवन् आह्वयामीति शेषः।
> आहूय च सोमस्येवांशुं यथा सोमलतां प्रति यजमाना जाग्रति यागपर्यंतं तद्रक्षणे प्रबुद्धा वर्तंते तथाहं त्वत्परिचर्यां प्रति जागर । जागर्मि ॥
> जागर्तीर्णल्युत्तमैकवचने रूपं ॥ अत्र निरुक्तं । हिरण्यस्तूपो हिरण्यमयस्टोपो

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Savitṛ, impeller: as Hiraṇyastūpa, son of Aṅgiras, my father, called you to this food (वाजे (*vāje*), the occasion being food), so I, named Arcan, praising you for protection, call you." The verb "I call" is to be supplied. Having called, "as sacrificers keep watch over the Soma plant until the sacrifice is complete and stay awake to guard it, so I stay awake in attendance on you." जागर (*jāgara*) stands for the first person singular, "I wake". Here the Nirukta says: हिरण्यस्तूपो हिरण्यमयस्टोपो (*hiraṇyastūpo hiraṇyamayasṭopo*) …

### Printed p. 1004

> हिरण्यमयः स्तूपोऽस्येति वा । स्तूपः स्त्यायतेः संघातः । सवितर्यथा त्वांगिरसो
> जुह्वे वाजेऽन्नेऽस्मिन्नेवं त्वार्चन्नवनाय वंदमानः सोमस्यॆवांशुं प्रतिजागर्म्यहं । नि. १०-३३ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Nirukta continues: *hiraṇyamayaḥ stūpo 'syeti vā* **NOTE** "or he has a golden stūpa". स्तूपः (*stūpaḥ*) is a mass, from the root स्त्यायतेः (*styāyateḥ*). The verse is then paraphrased in the order of the words: "As Hiraṇyastūpa the Aṅgirasa called you to this food, so I, Arcan, praising you for help, keep watch like one before the filament of Soma." The reference is Ni. 10-33.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सवितः (*savitaḥ*)—O Savitṛ, impeller of all
- आंगिरसः (*āṃgirasaḥ*)—the son of the sage Aṅgiras
- हिरण्यस्तूपः (*hiraṇyastūpaḥ*)—my father named Hiraṇyastūpa
- अस्मिन् वाजे (*asmin vāje*)—for the sake of food and the like
- यथा (*yathā*)—as
- त्वां (*tvāṃ*)—you
- जुह्वे (*juhve*)—he prayed to and called
- एव (*eva*)—in the same way
- अर्चन् (*arcan*)—I, known by the name Arcan
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अवसे (*avase*)—for protection
- वंदमानः (*vaṃdamānaḥ*)—praising you, I call you (after the call)
- सोमस्येव अंशुं (*somasyeva aṃśuṃ*)—as sacrificers carefully look after the Soma plants needed in the sacrifice, so
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- प्रति (*prati*)—in regard to service to you
- जागर (*jāgara*)—I remain watchful

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Savitṛ, impeller of all, as my father Hiraṇyastūpa, son of the sage Aṅgiras, prayed to you and called you for the sake of food and the like, so I too pray to you and call you for my protection. As sacrificers guard the Soma plants in the sacrifice with great vigilance, so I too remain very watchful in regard to your service (praise).

##### English translation
As Hiranyastupa, the Angirasa, Summoned you to this food, so I, praising you for your protection, watch before you as (worshippers) watch before the filament of the Soma.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The sage Arcan, seer of this sūkta, is the son of the sage Hiraṇyastūpa, himself the son of the well-known sage Aṅgiras; that is, Arcan is the grandson of Aṅgiras. In the present Ṛk this sage mentions that his father, the sage Hiraṇyastūpa, praised the deity Savitṛ in the 35th sūkta of the 1st maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā. The family of the sage Aṅgiras is very large and famous. There are 44 members of his line who are seers of sūktas in the Ṛgveda. Hiraṇyastūpa, father of Arcan, seer of the present sūkta, is one of them. The sūktas seen by the sage Hiraṇyastūpa are: in the 1st maṇḍala sūktas 31-35 (71 ṛks); in the 9th maṇḍala the 4th sūkta (10 ṛks) and the 69th sūkta (10 ṛks); in all 7 sūktas (91 ṛks) in total. The only sūkta seen by the sage Arcan is this one, that is, the 149th sūkta of the 10th maṇḍala, of 5 ṛks.

### Printed p. 1005

For this Ṛk Yāska gives a Nirukta: हिरण्यस्तूपो हिरण्मयस्तूपो हिरण्मयः स्तूपॊस्ये ति वा। स्तूपः स्त्यायतेः संघातः । सवितर्यथा त्वांगिरसो जुह्वे वाजे अस्मिन्नेवं त्वार्चन्नवनाय वंदमानः सोमस्येवांशुं प्रति जागर्म्यहं ॥ (*hiraṇyastūpo hiraṇmayastūpo hiraṇmayaḥ stūpòsye ti vā| stūpaḥ styāyateḥ saṃghātaḥ | savitaryathā tvāṃgiraso juhve vāje asminnevaṃ tvārcannavanāya vaṃdamānaḥ somasyevāṃśuṃ prati jāgarmyahaṃ ‖*) (Ni. 10-33). *Hiraṇya* means golden, or shining like gold; *stūpa* means a mass of hair, a topknot. The word *stūpa* is formed from the root *stā* meaning "to gather into one". The hair on the head gathered together and tied in a knot is called a topknot; *stūpa* means topknot. Because the topknot of this sage was shining like gold, he got this name. "O Savitṛ, now I pray to you and call you to accept the oblation prepared in this sacrifice. When performing a sacrifice, the sacrificers look after the Soma plants with great care. Likewise I am very watchful in praying to you and praising you for protection." So the sage says here.

## Sūkta 150 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> समिद्ध इति पंचर्चं द्वाविंशं सूक्तं वसिष्ठपुत्रस्य मृळीकस्यार्षमाग्नेयं ।
> चतुर्थीपंचम्यावुपरिष्टाज्योतिषी त्रिद्वादशाष्टकवत्यौ । अक्षरव्यूहेन चतुर्थी
> जगती वा । शिष्टा बृहत्यः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । समिद्धो मृळीको वासिष्ठ आग्नेयं
> बार्हतमंत्ये उपरिष्टाज्योतिषी जगत्युपांत्या वेति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta समिद्ध (*samiddha*) is of five ṛks, the twenty-second sūkta, composed by Mṛḷīka, son of Vasiṣṭha. Its deity is Agni. The fourth and fifth ṛks are उपरिष्टाज्योतिषी (*upariṣṭājyotiṣī*), with twelve syllables in the first three pādas and eight in the last (त्रिद्वादशाष्टकवत्यौ (*tridvādaśāṣṭakavatyau*)). By the arrangement of syllables the fourth is either Jagatī or उपरिष्टाज्योतिः (*upariṣṭājyotiḥ*); the remaining ṛks are Bṛhatīs. He cites the Anukramaṇī: समिद्धो मृळीको वासिष्ठ आग्नेयं बार्हतमंत्ये उपरिष्टाज्योतिषी जगत्युपांत्या वेति ॥ (*samiddho mṛḷīko vāsiṣṭha āgneyaṃ bārhatamaṃtye upariṣṭājyotiṣī jagatyupāṃtyā veti ‖*) The use in ritual has been given already.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*) is the twenty-second sūkta in the eleventh anuvāka, and it contains five ṛks. Its seer is Mṛḷīka, son of the sage Vasiṣṭha; its deity is Agni. The fourth and fifth ṛks of this sūkta are in the metre called Upariṣṭājjyotis. In the ṛks of this metre there are four pādas; the first three have twelve syllables each and the last has eight. By the count of syllables the fourth ṛk of this sūkta may also be in the Jagatī metre; the other ṛks are in the Bṛhatī metre. The Anukramaṇikā says

### Printed p. 1006

समिद्धो मृळीको वसिष्ठ आग्नेयं बार्हतमंत्ये उपरिष्टाज्योतिषी जगत्युपांत्या (*samiddho mṛḷīko vasiṣṭha āgneyaṃ bārhatamaṃtye upariṣṭājyotiṣī jagatyupāṃtyā*) and so on. The use in ritual has been given earlier.

Sūkta 150. Maṇḍala 10. Anuvāka 11. Sūkta 150. Aṣṭaka 8. Adhyāya 8. Varga 8. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 5.
Seer: Mṛḷīka Vāsiṣṭha. Deity: Agni. Metre: 1-3 Bṛhatī; 4 Upariṣṭājjyotir-Jagatī or; 5 Upariṣṭājjyotis.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> समि॑द्धश्चि॒त्समि॑ध्यसे दे॒वेभ्यो॑ हव्यवाहन ।  
> आ॒दि॒त्यै रु॒द्रैवसु॑भिर्न॒ आ ग॑हि मृळी॒काय॑ न॒ आ ग॑हि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> संइद्धः । चित् । सं । इध्यसे । देवेभ्यः । हव्यवाहन ।  
> आदित्यैः । रुद्रैः । वसुभिः । नः । आ । गहि । मृळीकाय । नः । आ । गहि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे हव्यवाहन हव्यानां हविषां वोढरग्ने समिद्धश्चित् संदीप्तोऽपि
> देवेभ्यो यागार्थं समिध्यसे । पुनरपृत्विग्भिः समिद्धिः संदीप्यसे । स त्वमादित्यैरादित्यादिभिस्त्रिभिर्गणैः सार्धं नोऽस्माना गहि । आगच्छ । तथा नोऽस्माकं मृळीकाय
> सुखाय तदर्थमप्या गहि । यद्वा । मृळीकाय्तत्संज्ञाय नो मह्यमृषये
> श्रेयांसि कर्तुमागच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, bearer of oblations (हव्यवाहन (*havyavāhana*)), although you are already kindled, you are kindled again for the gods, for the sacrifice, by the officiating priests with their fuel-sticks. Come to us with the three groups, the Ādityas and the rest, and also come for our Mṛḷīka, that is, for happiness, for that purpose. Or else: मृळीकाय (*mṛḷīkāya*) means for me, the sage of that name, come to do good things.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हव्यवाहन (*havyavāhana*)—O Agni, who carry the oblation to the gods
- समिद्धः चित् (*samiddhaḥ cit*)—although you are well kindled
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—for the benefit of the gods in the sacrifice
- सं इध्यसे (*saṃ idhyase*)—you are kindled again by the priests; such as you
- आदित्यैः (*ādityaiḥ*)—the twelve Ādityas

### Printed p. 1007

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गळिंदलू (*gaḷiṃdalū*)—(continuing) by the twelve Ādityas
- रुद्रैः (*rudraiḥ*)—by the eleven Rudras
- वसुभिः (*vasubhiḥ*)—by the eight Vasus
- नः (*naḥ*)—to our presence
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—deign to come
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- मृळीकाय (*mṛḷīkāya*)—for happiness, or for the favour of me, who am named Mṛḷīka
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—deign to come to my presence

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, bearer of oblations to the gods! Although you have been well kindled and are blazing, you have now been kindled again in this sacrifice by the priests, to blaze brightly for the gods' delight. Such as you are, come to us for the sacrifice together with the gods, who belong to the three groups called Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas, and come to us also to bring us happiness, or to show favour to me, who am named Mṛḷīka.

##### English translation
Berrer of oblations, being kindled you burn for the gods; come to us with the Adityas, the Rudras, the Vasus; come for our felicity.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मं य॒ज्ञमि॒दं वचो॑ जुजुषा॒ण उ॒पाग॑हि ।  
> मर्तासस्त्वा सविधान हवामहे मृळीकाय हवामहे ॥२॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमं । यज्ञं । इदं । वचः । जुजुषाणः । उपआगहि ।  
> मर्तासः । त्वा । संइधान । हवामहे । मृळीकाय । हवामहे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने इममस्माभिः क्रियमाणं पुरोवर्तिनं यज्ञमिदं वचः स्तोत्रं
> च जुजुषाणः सेवमान उपागहि । उपागच्छ । हे समिधान समिध्यमान मर्तासो
> मार्ता मनुष्यास्त्वा त्वां हवामहे । आह्वयामहे । मृळीकाय सुखाय्तत्संज्ञाय वर्षये त्वामेवाह्वयामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, come to this sacrifice, performed by us and set before you, enjoying (जुजुषाणः (*jujuṣāṇaḥ*)) it and this praise (वचः (*vacaḥ*)). O kindled (समिधान (*samidhāna*)) Agni, we mortals, that is human beings, invoke you. We call you alone for मृळीकाय (*mṛḷīkāya*), that is for happiness, or for the seer who bears that name.

### Printed p. 1008

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इमं (*imaṃ*)—this (sacrifice) that we are performing
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—this sacrifice
- इदं वचः (*idaṃ vacaḥ*)—this praise
- जुजुषाणः (*jujuṣāṇaḥ*)—enjoying (accepting)
- उपागहि (*upāgahi*)—deign to come near us
- सॆमिधान (*sèmidhāna*)—O kindled Agni
- मर्ताशः (*martāśaḥ*)—we who are human
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we call with prayer
- मृळीकाय (*mṛḷīkāya*)—for happiness, or to bring happiness to me, who am Mṛḷīka
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we call with prayer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, come to us, wishing to enjoy the sacrifice that we are now performing. O kindled Agni, we, who are human, call you with prayer. We call you with prayer to bring happiness to me, who am named Mṛḷīka.

##### English translation
Being gratified by this sacrifice, this praise, approach; we mortals invoke you, blazing (Agni), we invoke you for felicity.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वामु जातवेदसं विश्ववारं गृणे धिया ।  
> अग्ने देवा आ वह नः प्रियव्रतान्नृळीकाय प्रियव्रतान्॥३॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वां । ऊं इति । जातवेदसं । विश्ववारं । गृणे । धिया ।  
> अग्ने । देवान् । आ । वह । नः । प्रियव्रतान् । मृळीकाय । प्रियव्रतान् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने विश्ववारं विश्वैः सर्वैर्वर्णीयं जातवेदसं जातानां वेदितारं
> जातप्रज्ञं जातधनं ना त्वामु त्वामेव धिया स्तुत्या गृणे । सौमि ॥ गृ शब्दे ।
> क्रैयादिकः । प्वादित्वाद्ध्रस्वः ॥ प्रियव्रतान् प्रियाणि व्रतानि कर्माणि येषां
> तादृशान्देवान्नोऽस्मदर्थमा वह । आनय । अस्मद्यज्ञं प्रापय । मृळीकाय
> सुखार्थमेतत्संज्ञाय ना मह्यं प्रियव्रतांस्तानेवावह ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you are chosen by all (विश्ववारं (*viśvavāraṃ*)) and are जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*): the knower of all that is born, one whose wisdom or wealth has arisen. You alone I praise with my hymn. Bring to us the gods whose acts (व्रतानि (*vratāni*)) are dear (प्रियव्रतान् (*priyavratān*)), that is, bring them to our sacrifice. For मृळीकाय (*mṛḷīkāya*), that is for happiness, or for the seer of that name, bring to me those same gods of dear acts.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- विश्ववारं (*viśvavāraṃ*)—you who are desired by all
- जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*)—who know everything that has arisen, or who possess wealth
- त्वां उ (*tvāṃ u*)—you alone
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—with praise
- गृणे (*gṛṇe*)—I praise
- प्रियव्रतान् (*priyavratān*)—who perform deeds beneficial to men
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- आ वह (*ā vaha*)—bring here
- मृळीकाय (*mṛḷīkāya*)—for our happiness
- प्रियव्रतान् (*priyavratān*)—bring the gods who are beneficial to us

### Printed p. 1009

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you are wanted by all, and you have excellent wisdom, or know everything. You alone I praise with a hymn. Bring to this sacrificial ground of ours, for our sake, the gods who perform deeds beneficial to men. Bring them here also in order to give us happiness.

##### English translation
I glorify with my praise you, Jatavedas, desired by all; bring hither, Agni, to us the gods who are gratified by offerings, (bring) those gratified by offerings for our felicity.

> अग्निर्देवो देवानामभवत्पुरोहितोऽग्निं मनुष्या ३-

### Printed p. 1010

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवो दानादिगुणयुक्तोऽग्निर्देवानामन्येषां पुरोहितः पुरस्ताद्धृतोऽभवत् । यद्वा । पुरोहितवद्धितकार्यभवत् । यत एवमतः कारणात्तमेवाग्निमृषयोऽतींद्रियार्थदर्शिनो मनुष्या मानवा यजमानाः समाधिरे । संदीपयंति । अपि च तमग्निं महो महतो धनसात् धनस्य संभजने निमित्तभूतेऽहं
> हुवे । आह्वये ॥ विशेषणसापेक्षस्यापि धनशब्दस्य छांदसः समासः ॥ यद्वा । महतो
> यागस्य कर्तारमग्निमित्यर्थः । धनस्य सातॆये धनलाभार्थं मृळीकं सुखमेतत्संज्ञं
> ना मां सोऽग्निः करोत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the god endowed with qualities such as generosity, became the purohita of the other gods, that is, one placed in front. Or else: he became beneficial like a purohita. Because this is so, the ṛṣis (seers of what is beyond the senses), who are men, that is, the human sacrificers, kindle that same Agni. And I invoke that Agni महतो धनसात् (*mahato dhanasāt*), as the cause of sharing in great wealth; the compound with धन (*dhana*) is Vedic. Or else: the meaning is that Agni is the performer of the great sacrifice. For the gaining of wealth (धनसातये (*dhanasātaye*)) may he make me happy, मृळीकं (*mṛḷīkaṃ*), that is, may that Agni bring me happiness.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the shining one, or the one endowed with qualities such as generosity
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—than the other gods
- पुरोहितः (*purohitaḥ*)—established in front
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—is, or becomes beneficial to the gods like a purohita
- and
- ऋषयः (*ṛṣayaḥ*)—the ṛṣis, seers of what is beyond the senses
- मनुष्याः (*manuṣyāḥ*)—the human sacrificers
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—this Agni
- सं ईधिरे (*saṃ īdhire*)—kindle and make blaze
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—such an Agni
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great
- धनसात् (*dhanasāt*)—for the obtaining of wealth
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- हुवे (*huve*)—call with prayer
- धनसातये (*dhanasātaye*)—for the gaining of wealth, (me)
- मृळीकं (*mṛḷīkaṃ*)—may Agni make (me) happy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who is endowed with qualities such as generosity, is established before all the gods, or in front of everyone. The ṛṣis, who know what is beyond the senses, and the human sacrificers also kindle this Agni so that he blazes well. Such an Agni I call with prayer for the gaining of wealth. I call him also so that happiness may come to me through the gain of wealth.

##### English translation
The divine Agni, was the purohita of the gods; the Rishis, the descendents of Manu, kindled Agni. I invoke Agni for the acquisition of abundant wealth, (may he make me) happy for the acquisition of wealth.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्निगत्रिं भरद्वाजं गविष्ठिरं प्रावन्नः कण्णं त्रसदस्युमाहवे ।

### Printed p. 1011

> अग्निं वसिष्ठो हवते पुरोहितो मृळीकाय पुरोहितः॥५॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्निः । अत्रिं । भरत् ऽवाजं । गविष्ठिरं । प्र । आवत् । नः । कण्वं । त्रसदस्युं । आहवे।  
> अग्निं । वसिष्ठः । हवते । पुरःहितः । मृळीकाय । पुरःहितः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्रिं भरद्वाजं गविष्ठिरं कण्वं त्रसदस्युं च नोऽस्मानाहवे संग्रामेऽयमग्निः प्रावत् । प्ररक्षतु । पुरोहितः पुरोहितवद्धितकारी मम पिता वसिष्ठ ऋषिरग्निं
> हवते । स्तुतिभिराह्वयति । स चाहूतो मृळीकाय सुखार्थमेतत्संज्ञाय वा
> मह्यं पुरोहितः पुरोधा देवानां पुरः स्थापयिता भवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May this Agni protect in battle (आहवे (*āhave*)) Atri, Bharadvāja, Gaviṣṭhira, Kaṇva and Trasadasyu, and us. My father, the ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha, who is beneficial like a purohita, calls Agni with praises. And may Agni, so called, be a purohita for me, for मृळीकाय (*mṛḷīkāya*), that is for happiness, or for the seer of that name; that is, one who sets the gods before him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—this Agni
- अत्रिं (*atriṃ*)—the ṛṣi Atri
- भरद्वाजं (*bharadvājaṃ*)—the ṛṣi Bharadvāja
- गविष्ठिरं (*gaviṣṭhiraṃ*)—the ṛṣi named Gaviṣṭhira
- कण्वं (*kaṇvaṃ*)—the ṛṣi Kaṇva
- त्रसदस्युं (*trasadasyuṃ*)—Trasadasyu
- नः (*naḥ*)—and us
- आहवे (*āhave*)—in battle
- प्र आवत् (*pra āvat*)—may he protect
- पुरोहितः (*purohitaḥ*)—beneficial like a purohita
- वसिष्ठः (*vasiṣṭhaḥ*)—the ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha, my father
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- हवते (*havate*)—praises and invokes with hymns
- मृळीकाय (*mṛḷīkāya*)—for happiness, or to show favour to me, who am named Mṛḷīka
- पुरोहितः (*purohitaḥ*)—may this Agni be established in front of the gods

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May this Agni protect in battle Atri, Bharadvāja, Gaviṣṭhira, Kaṇva and Trasadasyu, and us. My father, the ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha, who is beneficial like a purohita, praises and invokes Agni with hymns. For my happiness may this Agni be established in front of the gods.

##### English translation
May Agni protect in war Atri, Bharadwaja, Gavishthira, ourselves, Kanwa and Trasadasyu; Vasishtha as the Purohita invokes Agni. the purohitha for our felicity.

### Printed p. 1012
## Sūkta 151 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The deity of this sūkta is Śraddhā. Śraddhā means the great regard that one shows when performing an act. This attitude itself is regarded as the deity and is praised in this sūkta. There are many sūktas in the Ṛgveda praising such deities of attitude. We have explained this matter at length in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 29, pp. 310-319. The introduction written for the 83rd sūkta of this maṇḍala applies to this sūkta also. Regarding the use (viniyoga) of this sūkta, the work called Ṛgvidhāna says as follows:

श्रद्धासूक्तं जपेन्नित्यं श्रद्धाकामः समाहितः ॥ ७१ ॥ सर्वत्र लभते श्रद्धां मेधासूक्तं तथैव च । ब्राह्मीमासाद्य सूक्ते द्वे जपेत नियतव्रतः ॥ ७२ ॥ तां पिबेत्तु यथाशक्त्या त्र्यहात्सिद्दिं नियच्छति । शंखपुष्पीं तु पयसा ब्राह्मीपुष्पाणि सर्पिषा ॥ ७३ ॥ शतावरीं तु पयसा वचामद्भिर्घृतेन च । सूक्ताभ्यामनुमंत्राभ्यामेकैकां तु त्र्यहं पिबेत् ॥ ७४ ॥ श्रद्धां मेधां स्मृतिं पुष्टिं बलं लक्ष्मीं च विंदति । सिद्धिं प्राप्नोति च परां दीर्घं चायुः समश्नुते ॥ ७५ ।' अथवा मनसा ध्यायेत्तूक्ते सिद्धिं नियच्छति । (*śraddhāsūktaṃ japennityaṃ śraddhākāmaḥ samāhitaḥ ‖ 71 ‖ sarvatra labhate śraddhāṃ medhāsūktaṃ tathaiva ca | brāhmīmāsādya sūkte dve japeta niyatavrataḥ ‖ 72 ‖ tāṃ pibettu yathāśaktyā tryahātsiddiṃ niyacchati | śaṃkhapuṣpīṃ tu payasā brāhmīpuṣpāṇi sarpiṣā ‖ 73 ‖ śatāvarīṃ tu payasā vacāmadbhirghṛtena ca | sūktābhyāmanumaṃtrābhyāmekaikāṃ tu tryahaṃ pibet ‖ 74 ‖ śraddhāṃ medhāṃ smṛtiṃ puṣṭiṃ balaṃ lakṣmīṃ ca viṃdati | siddhiṃ prāpnoti ca parāṃ dīrghaṃ cāyuḥ samaśnute ‖ 75 | ' athavā manasā dhyāyettūkte siddhiṃ niyacchati |*) (Ṛgvidhāna, Adhyāya 4, Ślo. 71-75)

A man who desires the favour of the deity Śraddhā should recite this Śraddhā-sūkta every day with self-control, and likewise the Medhā-sūkta (the khila-sūkta beginning मेधां मह्यमंगिरसः (*medhāṃ mahyamaṃgirasaḥ*)). If he does so, that man attains success in all undertakings. Moreover, if he brings the flower of the herb called Brāhmī, mixes it in water, consecrates it by reciting these two sūktas, and drinks it, then the work he has taken up will be accomplished within three days. Furthermore, if he mixes the śaṅkhapuṣpa in milk, the Brāhmī flower in ghee, the śatāvarī in milk, and the vacā in water or ghee, consecrates each with the recitation of these two sūktas, and drinks each for three days, that man obtains Śraddhā (interest in all undertakings), Medhā (intelligence), Smṛti (memory

### Printed p. 1013
*Kannada prose continuing from the previous page:* …strength of memory), nourishment, strength and wealth. He also obtains success in all undertakings and long life, and lives happily. Or, merely by reciting this sūkta silently in the mind, the desired work is accomplished.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> श्रद्धयेति पंचर्चं त्रयोविंशं सूक्तमानुष्टुभं श्रद्धादेवत्यं । कामगोत्रजा श्रद्धा नामर्षिका । तथा चानुक्रम्यते । श्रद्धया श्रद्धा कामायनी
> श्राद्धमानुष्टुभं त्विति ॥ लैंगिको विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta श्रद्धया (*śraddhayā*) has five Ṛks, is the twenty-third sūkta in this anuvāka, is in the Anuṣṭubh metre, and has Śraddhā as deity. The seer is the woman Śraddhā of the Kāmagotra. He cites the Anukramaṇī: श्रद्धया श्रद्धा कामायनी श्राद्धमानुष्टुभं तु (*śraddhayā śraddhā kāmāyanī śrāddhamānuṣṭubhaṃ tu*). The use (viniyoga) is *Laiṅgika* (according to the indication of the text).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta श्रद्धया (*śraddhayā*) is the twenty-third sūkta of the eleventh anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Its ṛṣikā is the woman Śraddhā of the Kāma lineage; the deity is Śraddhā; the metre is Anuṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: श्रद्धया श्रद्धा कामायनी श्राद्धमानुष्टुभं तु (*śraddhayā śraddhā kāmāyanī śrāddhamānuṣṭubhaṃ tu*). The use is Laiṅgika.

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 11; Sūkta 151. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 9. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Ṛṣi: Śraddhā Kāmāyanī. Deity: Śraddhā. Metre: Anuṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श्र॒द्धया॒ग्निः समि॑ध्यते श्र॒द्धया॑ हूयते ह॒विः ।  
> श्र॒द्धां भग॑स्य मू॒र्धनि॒ वच॒सा वे॑दयामसि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> श्रद्धया । अग्निः । सं । इध्यते । श्रद्धया । हूयते । हविः ।  
> श्रद्धां । भगस्य । मूर्धनि । वचसा । आ । वेदयामसि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुरुषगतोऽभिलाषविशेषः श्रद्धा । तया श्रद्धयाग्निर्गार्हपत्यादिः समिध्यते ।
> संदीप्यते । यदा हि पुरुषे श्रद्धाग्निगोचर आदरातिशयो जायते तदैष पुरु-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Śraddhā is a particular longing present in a person. By it the fire, the Gārhapatya and others, is kindled: when a person has great regard for the fire, then he kindles it, not otherwise.

### Printed p. 1014

> षोऽग्निन्प्रज्वालयति नान्यदा । श्रद्धयैव हविः पुरोडाशादिहविश्च हूयते । आहवनीये प्रक्षिप्यते । यद्वा । आ सूक्तस्य द्रष्टा श्रद्धाख्ययाग्निः समिध्यते । श्रद्धामुक्तलक्षणायाः श्रद्धाया अभिमानिदेवतां भगस्य भजनीयस्य धनस्य मूर्धनि प्रधानभूते स्थानेऽवस्थितां वचसा वचनेन स्तोत्रेणा वेदयामसि । अभितः प्रख्यापयामः ॥ इदंतो मसिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By faith alone the oblation (puroḍāśa and the like) is offered, cast into the Āhavanīya. Or else: the seer of the sūkta, called Śraddhā, is kindled as fire. We proclaim Śraddhā, the presiding deity of the faith described, who stands at the head, the foremost place, of Bhaga, the wealth to be enjoyed, by speech, i.e. by praise. इदंतो मसिः (*idaṃto masiḥ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- श्रद्धया (*śraddhayā*)—by faith (by great devotion)
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—the fire, Gārhapatya etc.
- सं इध्यते (*saṃ idhyate*)—is kindled
- श्रद्धया (*śraddhayā*)—by faith
- हविः (*haviḥ*)—the oblation, puroḍāśa etc.
- हूयते (*hūyate*)—is offered
- [Or श्रद्धया (*śraddhayā*)—by the ṛṣikā called Śraddhā, seer of this sūkta; अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—the fire; सं इध्यते (*saṃ idhyate*)—is kindled; श्रद्धया (*śraddhayā*)—by the ṛṣikā Śraddhā; हविः (*haviḥ*)—the oblation; हूयते (*hūyate*)—is offered in the fire]
- भगस्य (*bhagasya*)—of the wealth to be obtained
- मूर्धनि (*mūrdhani*)—at the chief place
- श्रद्धां (*śraddhāṃ*)—the deity presiding over faith
- वचसा (*vacasā*)—by words in the form of praise
- आ वेदयामसि (*ā vedayāmasi*)—we praise well

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Only by faith (devotion) is the fire kindled. Only by faith is the oblation offered in the fire; or, by the ṛṣikā Śraddhā, seer of this sūkta, the fire is kindled and oblations are offered in it. Let us praise well, with words of praise, this deity of faith, the chief means of obtaining wealth and the like.

##### English translation
Agni is kindled by Shraddha, by Shradda is the oblation offered; with our praise we glorify Shraddha, (who is seated) on Bhaga's head.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Explaining the derivation of the word Śraddhā, Yāska says: श्रद्धा । श्रद्धा श्रद्धानात् । तस्यैषा भवति ॥ (*śraddhā | śraddhā śraddhānāt | tasyaiṣā bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 9-30). In the word Śraddhā, the word श्रत् (*śrat*) means truth. श्रत् अस्यां धीयत इति श्रद्धा (*śrat asyāṃ dhīyata iti śraddhā*). Because truth is in it, it is called Śraddhā. The conviction that arises in dharma, artha, kāma and mokṣa is called faith: trust, great regard, longing. When doing an act one must trust that it is true, and must do it wholeheartedly and with regard; this attitude is called Śraddhā. For example the following Ṛk containing this word is given:

### Printed p. 1015
श्रद्धयाग्निः साधु समिध्यते श्रद्धया हविः साधु हूयते श्रद्धां भगस्य भागधेयस्य मूर्धनि प्रधानांगे वचनेनावेदयामः ॥ (*śraddhayāgniḥ sādhu samidhyate śraddhayā haviḥ sādhu hūyate śraddhāṃ bhagasya bhāgadheyasya mūrdhani pradhānāṃge vacanenāvedayāmaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 9-31)
Fire is kindled well by faith: if there is faith, i.e. trust and regard, when kindling the fire, the fire blazes well. Likewise an offering made with faith is well offered. Whatever work is done with faith is done well. In our effort to earn wealth faith is the chief thing: only if there is faith in the work can wealth be earned. The same holds in performing rites; only a rite done with faith gives full fruit. The main idea is: let us praise such a deity of faith with words of praise.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रि॒यं श्र॑द्धे॒ दद॑तः प्रि॒यं श्र॑द्धॆ॒ दिदा॑सतः ।  
> प्रि॒यं भो॒जेषु॒ यज्ज॑स्वि॒दं म॑ उदि॒तं कृ॑धि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रियं । श्रद्धे । ददतः । प्रियं । श्रद्धे । दिदासतः ।  
> प्रियं । भोजेषु । यज्वसु । इदं । मे । उदितं । कृधि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे श्रद्धे ददतश्चरुपुरोडाशादीनि प्रयच्छतो यजमानस्य प्रियमभीष्टफलं कुरु । दिदासतो दातुमिच्छतश्च हे श्रद्धे प्रियं कुरु । मे मम संबंधिषु
> भोजेषु भोक्तृषु भोगार्थिषु यज्जसु कृतयज्ञेषु जनेषु चेदमुदितमुक्तं
> प्रियं कृधि । कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Śraddhā, make agreeable, i.e. give the desired fruit to, the sacrificer who gives (cooked rice, puroḍāśa and the like). O Śraddhā, make agreeable also for him who wishes to give. Make this word that has been spoken agreeable among those connected with me who are enjoyers, seekers of enjoyment, and among those who have performed sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- श्रद्धे (*śraddhe*)—O deity presiding over faith
- ददतः (*dadataḥ*)—to the sacrificer who offers caru, puroḍāśa etc.
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—give the desired fruit
- श्रद्धे (*śraddhe*)—O deity Śraddhā
- दिदासतः (*didāsataḥ*)—

### Printed p. 1016
- दिदासतः (*didāsataḥ*) (continued)—to him who wishes to give
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—bring about benefit
- मे (*me*)—my
- भोजेषु (*bhojeṣu*)—among those seeking enjoyment
- यज्वसु (*yajvasu*)—among people who have performed sacrifice
- इदं उदितं (*idaṃ uditaṃ*)—this word just spoken
- प्रियं कृधि (*priyaṃ kṛdhi*)—make beneficial

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deity presiding over faith, bring benefit to the sacrificer who offers caru, puroḍāśa and the like, and to him who wishes to offer them. Among my kin, bring benefit as said above to those who seek enjoyment and to those who have performed sacrifice.

##### English translation
O Shraddha, grant the desire of the donor (of the oblation), grant O Shraddha, the desire of him who wishes to give, grant this boon which I have mentioned to my sacrificers who solicit happiness.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यथा॑ दे॒वा असु॑रेषु श्र॒द्धामु॒ग्रेषु॑ चक्रि॒रे ।  
> ए॒वं भो॒जेषु॒ यज्व॑स्व॒स्माक॑मुदि॒तं कृ॑धि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यथा । देवाः । असुरेषु । श्रद्धां । उग्रेषु । चक्रिरे ।  
> एवं । भोजेषु । यज्वसु । अस्माकं । उदितं । कृधि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवा इंद्रादयोऽसुरेषूद्गूर्णबलेषु यथा श्रद्धां चक्रिरे अवश्यमिमे
> हंतव्या इत्यादरातिशयं कृतवंतः एवं श्रद्धावत्सु भोजेषु भोक्तृषु भोगार्थिषु
> यज्जसु यष्टृष्टस्माकमस्मत्संबंधिषु तेषूदितं तैरुक्तं प्रार्थितं फलजातं
> कृधि । कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As the gods, Indra and others, had faith in regard to the Asuras of swollen strength, showing great regard, "these must surely be slain", so, among the enjoyers, seekers of enjoyment, sacrificers, who have faith and are connected with us, make the fruit that they have spoken and prayed for come true.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods, Indra and others
- असुरेषु (*asureṣu*)—in the matter of conquering (the gods')
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- श्रद्धां (*śraddhāṃ*)—faith (firm trust)
- चक्रिरे (*cakrire*)—they manifested

### Printed p. 1017
- एवं (*evaṃ*)—in that manner
- भोजेषु (*bhojeṣu*)—among people seeking enjoyment
- यज्वसु (*yajvasu*)—among people who perform sacrifice
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—in our case
- उदितं (*uditaṃ*)—the fruit each desires
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—cause to be accomplished

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As Indra and the other gods manifested firm trust in conquering the Asuras and accomplished the work, so accomplish whatever our kin who show faith, those seeking enjoyment, those performing sacrifice, and we ourselves desire.

##### English translation
As the gods had faith in (their fight with) the Asuras so grant the boon which has been asked for to our sacrificers who solicit happiness.

> श्रद्धां । हृदय्य या । आकूत्या । श्रद्धया । विंदते । वसु ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवा यजमाना मनुष्याश्च वायुगोपा वायुर्गोपा रक्षिता येषां
> ते तादृशाः संतः श्रद्धां देवीमुपासते । प्रार्थयंते । हृदय्यया । हृदये
> भवा हृदय्या । तथाविधयाकूत्या संकल्परूपया क्रियया श्रद्धामेव परिचरंति
> सर्वे जनाः । कुत इत्यत आह । यतः कारणाच्छ्रद्धया हेतुभूतया वसु धनं
> विंदते लभते श्रद्धावाज्ञानः । तत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods and the human sacrificers, having Vāyu as their protector, worship, i.e. pray to, the goddess Śraddhā. हृदय्यया (*hṛdayyayā*) means born in the heart. With such an intention, an act in the form of resolve, all people serve Śraddhā alone. Why? Because by faith, as the cause, a man having faith obtains wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- यजमानाः (*yajamānāḥ*)—sacrificers who perform sacrifice
- वायुगोपाः (*vāyugopāḥ*)—protected by the deity Vāyu
- श्रद्धां (*śraddhāṃ*)—the deity presiding over faith
- उपासते (*upāsate*)—pray (and people)

### Printed p. 1018
- हृदय्यया (*hṛdayyayā*)—born in the mind, i.e. done wholeheartedly
- आकूत्या (*ākūtyā*)—by an act in the form of resolve
- श्रद्धां (*śraddhāṃ*)—they worship this deity Śraddhā
- श्रद्धया (*śraddhayā*)—by that act done with faith
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth
- विंदते (*viṃdate*)—they obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods protected by Vāyu, and the sacrificers who perform sacrifice, pray to this deity Śraddhā. And all people worship this deity by an act done with faith and joined with the resolve to act with faith; that is, to attain their desired ends people pray to Śraddhā with wholehearted trust and firm confidence. Through faith so shown, that is, through work done with faith, people obtain wealth.

##### English translation
Gods, worshippers, and those who are protected by Vayu, Solicit Shraddha, (they cheshish) Shradaha with heartfelt desire, through Shraddha a man aquires wealth.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श्र॒द्धां प्रा॒तर्ह॑वामहे श्र॒द्धां म॒ध्यंदि॑नं॒ सरि॑ ।  
> श्र॒द्धां सूर्य॑स्य नि॒म्रुचि॒ श्रद्धे॒ श्रद्धा॑पये॒ह नः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> श्रद्धां । प्रातः । हवामहे । श्रद्धां । मध्यंदिनं । परि ।  
> श्रद्धां । सूर्यस्य । निम्रुचि । श्रद्धे । श्रत् । धापय । इह । नः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> श्रद्धां देवीं प्रातः पूर्वाह्ने हवामहे । तथा मध्यंदिनं परि ॥ लक्षणे
> परेः कर्मप्रवचनीयत्वं ॥ मध्यंदिनं परिलक्ष्य । मध्यंदिन इत्यर्थः । मध्याह्नेऽपि
> तां श्रद्धामाह्वयामहे । सूर्यस्य सर्वस्य प्रेरकस्यादित्यस्य निम्रुच्यस्तमयवे-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We invoke the goddess Śraddhā in the morning, the forenoon. Likewise मध्यंदिनं परि (*madhyaṃdinaṃ pari*): the word परि (*pari*) in the sense of a mark has the status of a karmapravacanīya; परि (*pari*) with मध्यंदिनं (*madhyaṃdinaṃ*) means "at midday": at midday too we call that Śraddhā. At the setting of the sun, the impeller of all….

### Printed p. 1019

> लायां सायंसमयेऽपि तामेव श्रद्धामाह्वयामहे । ईदृग्रूपे हे श्रद्धे
> नोऽस्मानिह लोके कर्मणि वा श्रद्धापय । श्रद्धावतः कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes the gloss of the verse. We call upon the goddess Śraddhā in the morning (forenoon). Likewise we call upon her at midday, the word परि (*pari*) being a karmapravacanīya in the sense of "marking" (lakṣaṇa), so मध्यंदिनं परि (*madhyaṃdinaṃ pari*) means "at midday". At sunset, the time when the sun, the impeller of all, goes down, that is, in the evening, we call upon that same Śraddhā. "O Śraddhā, make us here, in this world or in this rite, full of faith."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- श्रद्धां (*śraddhāṃ*)—this deity Śraddhā
- प्रातः (*prātaḥ*)—in the morning (forenoon)
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we pray and call, and likewise
- मध्यंदिनं परि (*madhyaṃdinaṃ pari*)—at midday too
- श्रद्धां (*śraddhāṃ*)—we pray and call the presiding deity of faith (and)
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of the sun, who impels all
- निम्रुचि (*nimruci*)—at the time of setting
- श्रद्धां (*śraddhāṃ*)—we pray and call that same deity Śraddhā
- श्रद्धे (*śraddhe*)—O deity Śraddhā
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- इह (*iha*)—in this world or in this rite
- श्रत् धापय (*śrat dhāpaya*)—make us full of faith

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We pray to and call this presiding deity of faith in the morning, at midday, and at the sun's setting, that is, in the evening. O deity Śraddhā, make us full of faith in this world, or in this work that we are doing.

##### English translation
We invoke Shraddha at dawn, and again at midday, and also at the setting of the sun ; inspire us in this world, Shraddha, with faith.

## Sūkta 152 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
Concerning this sūkta it is said in the Ṛgvidhāna:
शास इत्था सपत्नघ्नं संग्रामं विजिगीषतः ॥ ७६ ॥ (*śāsa itthā sapatnaghnaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ vijigīṣataḥ ‖ 76 ‖*)
प्रयोक्तव्यं तु शुचिना जुहुयात्तत्र सिद्धये अथवा जप्यमेव स्यात्संग्राममभिगच्छतः ॥ ७७ ॥ (*prayoktavyaṃ tu śucinā juhuyāttatra siddhaye athavā japyameva syātsaṃgrāmamabhigacchataḥ ‖ 77 ‖*)
शास इत्थेति यो हंतुं शत्रून्सर्वान्निवारयेत् ॥ (*śāsa ittheti yo haṃtuṃ śatrūnsarvānnivārayet ‖*)
(Ṛgvidhāna, Adhyāya 4, verses 76–77)
A man who desires victory in battle should, having become pure, recite this sūkta beginning शास इत्था (*śāsa itthā*). It destroys enemies. If one makes an offering with the mantras of this sūkta in the consecrated fire, the desired ends, such as the subduing of enemies, are attained. Or, if a man setting out for battle mutters this sūkta, he becomes able to destroy his enemies in battle.

### Printed p. 1021

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्वादशेऽनुवाके चत्वारिंशत्सूक्तानि । तत्र शास इत्थेति पंचर्चं प्रथमं
> सूक्तं शासनाम्न आर्षमानुष्टभमैंद्रं । अनुक्रांतं च । शासः शासो भारद्वाज
> इति ॥ युद्धाय संनद्धं राजानमनेनेक्षेत । तथा च सूत्रितं । अथैनमन्वीक्षेताप्रतिरथशाससौपर्णैः । आ. गृ. ३-१२-१३ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the twelfth anuvāka there are forty sūktas. Of these the first is the five-verse sūkta शास इत्था (*śāsa itthā*); its seer is Śāsa, its metre Anuṣṭubh, its deity Indra. The Anukramaṇī says: शासः शासो भारद्वाज इति (*śāsaḥ śāso bhāradvāja iti*). With it one should look upon a king girded for battle. So it is prescribed in the sūtra: अथैनमन्वीक्षेताप्रतिरथशाससौपर्णैः (*athainamanvīkṣetāpratirathaśāsasauparṇaiḥ*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-12-13).

##### Anuvāda

In the twelfth anuvāka of the tenth maṇḍala there are forty sūktas. Of them this sūkta beginning शास इत्था (*śāsa itthā*) is the first; it has five ṛks. Its seer is Śāsa, son of the seer Bharadvāja; the deity is Indra; the metre is Anuṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī says शासः शासो भारद्वाजः (*śāsaḥ śāso bhāradvājaḥ*). That, with the recitation of this sūkta, the king who has set out equipped for battle is to be looked upon is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra अथैनमन्वीक्षेताप्रतिरथशाससौपर्णॆः (*athainamanvīkṣetāpratirathaśāsasauparṇèḥ*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-12-13).

Sūkta 152. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 152. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 10. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Śāsa Bhāradvāja. Deity: Indra. Metre: Anuṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शा॒स इ॒त्था म॒हान् अ॑स्यमित्रखा॒दो अद्भु॑तः ।  
> न यस्य॑ ह॒न्यते॒ सखा॒ न जीय॑ते॒ कदा॑ च॒न ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शासः । इत्था । महान् । असि । अमित्रखादः । अद्भुतः ।  
> न । यस्य । हन्यते । सखा । न । जीयते । कदा । चन ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शासस्तत्संज्ञोऽहमित्तमनेन वक्ष्यमाणप्रकारेणेंद्रं सौमाति शेषः । हे
> इंद्र त्वं महा असि । सर्वेभ्योऽधिको भवसि । अमित्रखादोऽमित्राणां शत्रुणां

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I, Śāsa, so named, praise Indra in the manner to be stated (the verb "praises" is understood). O Indra, you are great, greater than all; you are the devourer of enemies, and so you are wonderful, a marvel.

### Printed p. 1022

> खादिता विनाशयिता अत एवाद्भुत आश्चर्यभूतश्च भवसीति' यस्येंद्रस्य सखा मित्रभूतः
> पुरुषः कदा चन कदाचिदपि न हन्यते न हिंस्यते न जीयते न च शत्रुभिः पराजितो
> भवति स त्वं महा असीत्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(continuing) He is a destroyer of foes, and therefore wonderful. The friend of Indra, a man who is his ally, is never at any time killed, harmed, or defeated by enemies. The construction is: you, such as this, are great.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शासः (*śāsaḥ*)—I, famed by the name Śāsa
- इत्था (*itthā*)—thus I praise Indra. O Indra,
- यस्यॆ (*yasyè*)—whose
- सखा (*sakhā*)—friend, a man who is your ally,
- कदा चन (*kadā cana*)—at any time
- न हन्यते (*na hanyate*)—is not harmed
- न जीयते (*na jīyate*)—is not conquered by enemies; such an Indra, you
- महान् असि (*mahān asi*)—are greater than all
- अमित्रखादः (*amitrakhādaḥ*)—the destroyer of enemies
- अद्भुतः (*adbhutaḥ*)—and of wondrous glory

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, the seer of this sūkta, named Śāsa, praise Indra in this way. The man who is Indra's friend is never harmed by anyone and is not defeated by enemies. O Indra of such glory, you are greater than all, and your glory is wonderful.

##### English translation
(I) Shasa thus (praise Indra); you are mighty, the destroyer of foes
the wonderful, (he) whose friend is not killed nor ever overpowered.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्व॒स्ति॒दा वि॒शस्वति॑र्वृत्र॒हा वि॑मृ॒धो व॒शी ।  
> वृषेंद्रः॑ पु॒र ए॑तु नः सोम॒पा अ॑भयंक॒रः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्वस्तिदाः । विशः । पतिः । वृत्रहा । विमृधः । वशी ।  
> वृषा । इंद्रः । पुरः । एतु । नः । सोमपाः । अभयंकरः ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 1023

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्वस्तिदाः स्वस्तेरविनाशस्य दाता विशस्पतिः सर्वस्याः प्रजायाः पालयिता वृत्रहा
> वृत्राणां शत्रूणां हंता विमृधः संग्रामकारी वशी वशीकर्ता वृषा वर्षिता
> कामानां सोमपाः सोमस्य पाता विवंविध इंद्रोऽभयंकरोऽभयस्य भयराहित्यस्य कर्ता सन्नोऽस्माकं पुर एतु । पुरतो गच्छतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is the giver of well-being (स्वस्ति (*svasti*), freedom from destruction), the lord of all the people, slayer of Vṛtras (enemies), the warrior, the subduer, the showerer of desires, the drinker of Soma, the maker of fearlessness. Being such, let him go before us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वस्तिदाः (*svastidāḥ*)—he who produces welfare
- विशः पतिः (*viśaḥ patiḥ*)—the lord or protector of all the people
- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—slayer of enemies
- विमृधः (*vimṛdhaḥ*)—the fighter
- वशी (*vaśī*)—he who brings enemies under his sway
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—bestower of desired things
- सोमपाः (*somapāḥ*)—the drinker of Soma juice
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अभयंकरः (*abhayaṃkaraḥ*)—granting us fearlessness (protection)
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- पुरः (*puraḥ*)—in front
- एतु (*etu*)—let him go forth as our leader

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, protector of all people and maker of their welfare, slayer of enemies, skilled in battle, subduer of enemies, showerer of desired things, and drinker of Soma, granting us fearlessness, let him go forth (to battle) in front of us as leader.

##### English translation
May Indra, the granter of prosperity, the lord of men, the slayer of
Vritra, the warrior, the subduer, the showerer. the drinker of the Soma, the
assurer of safety, come to our presence.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि रक्षो॒ वि मृधो॑ जहि॒ वि वृ॒त्रस्य॒ हनू॑ रुज ।  
> वि म॒न्यमिं॑द्र वृत्रहन्न॒ मित्र॑स्याभि॒दास॑तः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । रक्षः । वि । मृधः । जहि । वि । वृत्रस्य । हनू इति । रुज ।  
> वि । मन्युं । इंद्र । वृत्रहन् । अमित्रस्य । अभिदासतः ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 1024

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र रक्षो राक्षसजातं वि जहि । विनाशय । मृधः संग्रामकारिणः शत्रुंश्च
> वि जहि । वृत्रस्यावरकस्यासुरस्य हनू कपोलप्रांतौ वि रुज । विशेषेण भग्नौ कुरु ।
> हे वृत्रहन्निंद्र अभिदासतोऽस्मानुपक्षयतो मित्रस्य शत्रुर्मन्युं क्रोधमपि
> विनाशय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, destroy the host of rākṣasas. Destroy also the enemies who make war. Break the jaws (the sides of the cheeks) of Vṛtra, the enveloping asura. O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, destroy also the wrath (मन्युं (*manyuṃ*)) of the enemy who seeks to destroy us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*)—the host of rākṣasas
- वि जहि (*vi jahi*)—destroy
- मृधः (*mṛdhaḥ*)—the fighting enemies
- वि जहि (*vi jahi*)—defeat
- वृत्रस्य (*vṛtrasya*)—of the enveloping asura
- हनू (*hanū*)—the cheeks
- वि रुज (*vi ruja*)—strike and wound
- वृत्रहन् (*vṛtrahan*)—slayer of enemies
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अभिदासतः (*abhidāsataḥ*)—who seeks to destroy us
- अमित्रस्य (*amitrasya*)—of the enemy
- मन्युं (*manyuṃ*)—destroy the anger

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, destroy the host of rākṣasas. Defeat these enemies who are fighting. Strike and wound the cheeks of this enveloping asura. O Indra, slayer of enemies, destroy the anger of this enemy who is bent on destroying us.

##### English translation
Destroy, Indra, the Rakshasas, the enemies; fracture the jaws of
Vritra; baffle, Indra, slayer of Vritra, the wrath of (our) menacing foe.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विन॑ इंद्र॒ मृधो॑ जहि नी॒चा य॑च्छ पृतन्य॒तः ।  
> यो अ॒स्मा अ॑भि॒दास॒त्यध॑रं गमया॒ तमः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । नः । इंद्र । मृधः । जहि । नीचा । यज्ञ । पृतन्यतः ।  
> यः । अस्मान् । अभिदासति । अधरं । गमय । तमः ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 1025

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वि न इंद्रेति वैमृधस्य हविषोऽनुवाक्या । सूत्ति तं च । वि न इंद्र मृधो
> जहि मृगो न भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्ठाः । आ. २-१० । इति ॥
> हे इंद्र नोऽस्माकं मृधः संग्रामकारिणः शत्रून्वि जहि । विनाशय । तथा
> पृतन्यतः पृतनाः सेना आत्मन इच्छतो युयुत्समानानपि नीचा यच्छ । नीचीनमवाङ्मुखं यच्छ! गमय । यः शत्रुरस्मानभिदासति अभित उपक्षपयति तमधरं निकृष्टं
> तमोऽंधकारं मरणलक्षणं गमय । प्रापय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The verse वि न इंद्र (*vi na iṃdra*) is the anuvākyā (invitatory verse) for the Vaimṛdha oblation. The sūtra says so: वि न इंद्र मृधो जहि मृगो न भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्ठाः (*vi na iṃdra mṛdho jahi mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ*) (Ā. 2-10). Sāyaṇa explains: O Indra, destroy our enemies who make war on us. Bring down (नीचा यच्छ (*nīcā yaccha*)) as well those who wish to fight and who look for armies of their own, turning them face downward. Whatever enemy harasses us on every side, send him to the lower darkness, that is, the darkness of death.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—O Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—our (with us)
- मृधः (*mṛdhaḥ*)—the enemies who make war
- वि जहि (*vi jahi*)—destroy (and likewise)
- पृतन्यतः (*pṛtanyataḥ*)—these enemies who fight facing us in the enemy army
- नीचा यच्छ (*nīcā yaccha*)—make them fall down
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whichever enemy of ours
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- अभिदासति (*abhidāsati*)—who wants to surround and kill us, him
- अधरं (*adharaṃ*)—lower
- तमः (*tamaḥ*)—death, in the form of darkness
- गमय (*gamaya*)—cause to reach (make him fall down and die)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, destroy the enemies who are fighting with us. Likewise make the enemies who are fighting facing us in the enemy army fall down. Make whatever enemy wishes to surround us and destroy us fall down and become a victim of death, which is like darkness.

##### English translation
Destroy, Indra, our enemies; hunt down those who are in array against us; consign to lower darkness him who seeks to harm us.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk, वि न इंद्र (*vi na iṃdra*), is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra while the oblation is offered in the Vaimṛdha oblation (iṣṭi). This is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra वि न इंद्र मृधो जहि मृगो न भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्ठाः (*vi na iṃdra mṛdho jahi mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ*) (Ā. 2-10).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अपें॑द्र द्विष॒तो मनोप॒ जिज्या॑सतो व॒धं ।  
> वि म॒न्योः शर्म॑ यच्छ॒ वरी॑यो यवया व॒धं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अप । इंद्र । द्विषतः । मनः । अप । जिज्यासतः । वधं ।  
> वि । मन्योः । शर्म । यच्छ । वरीयः । यवय । वधं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र द्विषतो द्वेष्टुः शत्रोर्मनोऽप जहि । जिज्यासतोऽस्माकं
> वयोहानिमिच्छतश्च वधं हननसाधनवायुधं चाप जहि । मन्योः शत्रुसंबंधिनः
> क्रोधाच्चास्मान्रक्ष । वरीय उरुतरं शर्म सुखं विशेषेण यच्छ । देहि । वधं
> शत्र्युकृतं हननं च यवय । अस्मत्तः पृथक्कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, strike away (अप (*apa*)) the mind of the hating enemy. Strike away also the weapon (वधं (*vadhaṃ*)), the instrument of killing, of the one who wishes to bring about our loss of life. Protect us from the wrath of the enemy. Give us in particular broader (वरीयः (*varīyaḥ*)) happiness (शर्म (*śarma*)). Remove from us the killing done by the enemy.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- द्विषतः (*dviṣataḥ*)—of the enemy who hates us
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—the mind (the intellect, or the power of discernment)
- अप (*apa*)—spoil
- जिज्यासतः (*jijyāsataḥ*)—of the enemy who wishes to make an end of us
- वधं (*vadhaṃ*)—the weapon that is the instrument of killing
- अप (*apa*)—make useless
- मन्योः (*manyoḥ*)—protect us from the enemy's anger
- वरीयः (*varīyaḥ*)—abundant
- शर्म (*śarma*)—happiness
- वि यच्छ (*vi yaccha*)—give specially
- वधं (*vadhaṃ*)—the enemy's intention to kill us
- यवय (*yavaya*)—prevent from happening

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, spoil the mind, that is, the power of discernment, of the enemy who hates us. Make useless the weapon of the enemy who wishes to end our life. Protect us from the anger of the enemy. Give us abundant happiness and prevent the enemy from killing us.

##### English translation
Frustrate the purpose of him who hates us, (baffle) the weapon of him who seeks to overpower us; grant us entire security from his warth, ward off (his) weapon.

## Sūkta 153 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ईंखयंतीरिति पंचर्चं गायत्रमैंद्रं द्वितीयं सूक्तं । देवानां
> स्वसृभूता इंद्रमातरो नामर्षिकाः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । ईंखयंतीर्देवजामय
> इंद्रमातरो गायत्रमिति ॥ द्वितीये पर्याये प्रशास्तुः शस्त्र इदं सूक्तं ।
> सूत्रितं च । ईंखयंतीरहं दां पाता सुतं । आ. ६-४ । इति ॥ महाव्रतेऽपि प्रातःसवनिके ब्रह्मशस्त्र एतत्तूक्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta ईंखयंतीः (*īṃkhayaṃtīḥ*) has five Ṛks, is in the Gāyatra metre and is addressed to Indra; it is the second sūkta. Its seers (ṛṣikā) are the Indramātaraḥ, who are sisters of the gods. The Anukramaṇī says: ईंखयंतीर्देवजामय इंद्रमातरो गायत्रं (*īṃkhayaṃtīrdevajāmaya iṃdramātaro gāyatraṃ*). In the second paryāya this sūkta is the śastra of the Praśāstṛ. The sūtra says: ईंखयंतीरहं दां पाता सुतं (*īṃkhayaṃtīrahaṃ dāṃ pātā sutaṃ*) (Ā. 6-4). In the Mahāvrata too this sūkta belongs to the Brahma-śastra at the morning pressing.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, ईंखयंतीः (*īṃkhayaṃtīḥ*), is the second sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. The seers of this sūkta are the women called Indramātaraḥ, who are sisters of the gods. The deity is Indra; the metre is Gāyatrī. The Anukramaṇī says: ईंखयंतीर्देवजामय इंद्रमातरो गायत्रं (*īṃkhayaṃtīrdevajāmaya iṃdramātaro gāyatraṃ*). In the second paryāya, this sūkta is applied to the śastra mantras to be recited by the priest called the Praśāstṛ; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra ईंखयंतीरहं दां पाता सुतं (*īṃkhayaṃtīrahaṃ dāṃ pātā sutaṃ*) (Ā. 6-4).

##### Particulars

Sūkta 153. Maṇḍala 10. Anuvāka 12. Sūkta 153. Aṣṭaka 8. Adhyāya 8. Varga 11. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Ṛṣi: the Indramātaraḥ, the Devajāmayaḥ. Deity: Indra. Metre: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ईं॒खयं॑तीरप॒स्युव॒ इंद्रं॑ जा॒तमुपा॑सते ।  
> भे॒जा॒नासः॑ सु॒वीर्यं॑ ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 1028

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ईंखयंतीः । अपसुवः । इंद्रं । जातं । उप । आसते ।  
> भेजानासः । सुवीर्यं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ईंखयंतीर्गच्छंत्यः स्तुत्यादिभिरिंद्रं प्राप्नुवत्योऽपस्युवोऽपः कर्मात्मन इच्छंत्य इंद्रमातरोऽस्य सूक्तस्य द्रष्टोऽ जातं प्रादुर्भूतमिंद्रमुपासते । परिचरंति । सुवीर्यं शोभनवीयोर्पेतं धनं च भेजानासः । तस्मादिंद्रात्संभक्तवत्यो भवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Indramātaraḥ, the seers of this sūkta, are going (ईंखयंतीः (*īṃkhayaṃtīḥ*)) and reaching Indra with praises and the like. They desire (अपस्युवः (*apasyuvaḥ*)) work (*apaḥ*) for themselves. They attend upon (उपासते (*upāsate*)) Indra, who has newly appeared (जातं (*jātaṃ*)), and they share (भेजानासः (*bhejānāsaḥ*)) in wealth endowed with good heroic strength (सुवीर्यं (*suvīryaṃ*)). Thus they become devoted to Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ईंखयंतीः (*īṃkhayaṃtīḥ*)—the Indramātaraḥ, seers of this sūkta, who go to Indra's presence with praises and the like
- अपस्युवः (*apasyuvaḥ*)—who wish to perform work
- जातं (*jātaṃ*)—born
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- उपासते (*upāsate*)—they attend upon
- सुवीर्यं (*suvīryaṃ*)—excellent wealth
- भेजानासः (*bhejānāsaḥ*)—they obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Indramātaraḥ, the seers of this sūkta, who wish to perform work and who approach Indra with praises and the like in order to praise him, attend upon and serve Indra, who has just been born. And they obtain excellent wealth.

##### English translation
Desirous of fulfilling their functions (the mothers of Indra) approaching, worship him as soon as born, and enjoy (affluence) together with male progeny.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वमिं॑द्र॒ बला॒दधि॒ सह॑सो जा॒त ओज॑सः ।  
> त्वं वृ॑ष॒न्वृषेद॑सि ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 1029

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । इंद्र । बलात् । अधि । सहसः । जातः । ओजसः ।  
> त्वं । वृषन् । वृषा । इत् । असि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं सहसः परेषामभिभावुकाद्बलादधि जातोऽसि । अधिः पंचम्यर्थानुवादकः । वृत्रा तिवधहेतुभूता द्बलाद्धेतोस्त्वं प्रख्यातो भवसीत्यर्थः । अपि
> चौजसः । ओजो नाम बलहेतु हृदयगतं धैर्यं । तस्मादपि त्वं जातोऽसि ।
> हे वृषन्वर्षितः त्वं वृषेदसि । कामानां वर्षितैव भवसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you were born (जातः (*jātaḥ*)) from strength (बलात् (*balāt*)) that overpowers (सहसः (*sahasaḥ*)) others; the word अधि (*adhi*) only repeats the sense of the ablative. The meaning is that you become famous from the strength that is the cause of the killing of Vṛtra and the like. You were born also from vigour (ओजसः (*ojasaḥ*)): *ojaḥ* is the courage lodged in the heart that is the cause of strength. O showerer, you are indeed (इत् (*it*)) a showerer; you are the one who showers desires.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- सहसः (*sahasaḥ*)—possessing the power to defeat others
- बलात् (*balāt*)—from strength
- अधि जाता (*adhi jātā*)—you were born
- ओजसः (*ojasaḥ*)—from courage too you were born
- वृषन् (*vṛṣan*)—O Indra, giver of what is desired
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- वृषा इत् (*vṛṣā it*)—as one who showers desired objects
- असि (*asi*)—you are

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, at your very birth you were born with the power of subduing enemies, needed for the slaying of Vṛtra and the like, and endowed with boundless courage of mind. O Indra, giver of desires, you are also one who showers desired objects.

##### English translation
You, Indra, were born from overpowering strength and energy ; yon, O showerer, are indeed a showerer (of blessings).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वमिं॑द्रासि वृत्र॒हा व्य१॒ं॑ग्यतरि॑क्षमतिरः ।  
> उद्धाम॑स्तभ्ना॒ ओज॑सा ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 1030

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । इंद्र । असि । वृत्रहा । वि । अंतरिक्षं । अतिरः ।  
> उत् । द्यां । अस्तभ्नाः । ओजसा ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं वृत्रहासि । शत्रूणां हंता भवसि । अंतरिक्षं मध्यमस्थानं च
> व्यतिरः । आवारकापनोदनेन प्रावर्धयः । द्यां द्युलोकं चौजसा बलेनोदस्तभ्नाः । ऊर्ध्वमस्तंभीः । यथाधो न पतति तथोपर्यवस्थापितवानित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you are the slayer of Vṛtra, the killer of enemies. You made the firmament (अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)), the middle region, grow (व्यतिरः (*vyatiraḥ*)) by removing what obstructed it. By your strength (ओजसा (*ojasā*)) you propped up (*udastabhnāḥ*) the heaven (द्यां (*dyāṃ*)), the world of heaven, upward. The meaning is that you set it up above so that it does not fall down.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—as slayer of enemies
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the firmament, the middle region
- वि अतिरः (*vi atiraḥ*)—you have opened out
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—by your strength
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the world of heaven
- उत् अस्तभ्नाः (*ut astabhnāḥ*)—you have set it up so that it does not fall down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you are the destroyer of enemies. You have opened out the firmament. By your strength you have set the world of heaven up in a high region so that it does not fall down.

##### English translation
You, Indra, are the slayer of Vritra, you have spread out the firmament; you have unheld the heaven by your power.

O Indra, you hold in your hands, for the slaying of enemies, your thunderbolt, dear to you and praiseworthy, having rubbed it hard and sharpened it.

## Sūkta 154 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सोम इति पंचर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तमानुष्टुभं । विवस्वतो दुहिता
> यम्यृषिः । म्रियमाणानां यजमानादीनां वर्तनमत्र प्रतिपाद्यते । अतस्तद्देवताकमिदं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । सोमो यमी भाववृत्तमानुष्टुभं त्विति ॥
> प्रेतोपस्थान एतत्तूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । सोम एकेभ्य उरूणसावसुतृपा उदुंबल् । आ. ६-१० । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the third sūkta, of five Ṛks, in Anuṣṭubh metre. The seer is Yamī, daughter of Vivasvat. The conduct (state) of dying sacrificers and others is set forth here, so that is its deity. The Anukramaṇī says: सोमो यमी भाववृत्तमानुष्टुभं त्विति॥ (*somo yamī bhāvavṛttamānuṣṭubhaṃ tviti‖*) The sūkta is used at the approach to the departed (preta-upasthāna), as stated in the sūtra सोम एकेभ्य उरूणसावसुतृपा उदुंबल् (*soma ekebhya urūṇasāvasutṛpā uduṃbal*) (Ā. 6-10).

##### Anuvāda

The sūkta "Soma…" is the third sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks, in Anuṣṭubh metre. Its seer is the woman Yamī, daughter of Vivasvān. The nature of sacrificers and others who die is set forth in this sūkta; therefore that conduct is its deity. The Anukramaṇī statement सोमो यमी भाववृत्तमानुष्टुभं तु (*somo yamī bhāvavṛttamānuṣṭubhaṃ tu*) and the use of this sūkta for the approach to the departed are explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, सोम एकेभ्य उरूणसावसुतृपा उदुंबल् (*soma ekebhya urūṇasāvasutṛpā uduṃbal*) (Ā. 6-10).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सोम॒ एके॑भ्यः पवते घृ॒तमेक॒ उपा॑सते ।  
> येभ्यो॒ मधु॑ प्र॒धाव॑ति॒ तांश्चि॑दे॒वापि॑ गच्छतात् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सोमः । एकेभ्यः । पवते । धृतं । एके । उप । आसते ।  
> येभ्यः । मधु । प्रधावति । तान् । चित् । एव । अपि । गच्छतात् । १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एकेभ्यः केभ्यश्चित्पितृभ्यः सोमः पवते । उपभोगाय कुल्यारूपेण प्रवहति । एषां गोत्रजाः सामानि ब्रह्मयज्ञसमयेऽधीयते । श्रूयते हि । यत्सामानि सोम एभ्यः पवत इति । एकेऽन्ये पितरो धृतमाज्यमुपासते । उपगच्छंति ।
> उपभुंजत इत्यर्थः । एषां पुत्रादयो यजूंषि ब्रह्मयज्ञकालेऽधीयते ।
> श्रुतिश्च भवति । यद्यजूंषि धृतस्य कुल्या इति । येभ्यः पितृभ्यः । तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी ।
> उपभोगार्थं मधु क्षौद्रं प्रधानति प्रवाहरूपेण शीघ्रं गच्छति । य आथर्वणान्मंत्रान्ब्रह्मयज्ञार्थमधीयते तेषां पित्यन्मधुकुल्या प्रवहति । तथा चाम्नायते । यदाथर्वणांगिरसो मधोः कुल्या इति । तांश्चिदेव तान्पूर्वोक्तान्सर्वानेव हे प्रेत त्वं प्रत्यपि गच्छतात् । अपिगच्छ । प्राप्नुहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

For some Pitṛs Soma flows; it runs as a stream for their enjoyment. Those born in their lineage recite Sāmans at the time of the Brahmayajña. For it is heard: यत्सामानि सोम एभ्यः पवत (*yatsāmāni soma ebhyaḥ pavata*). Others, other Pitṛs, partake of ghee (ājya), that is, enjoy it; their sons and others recite Yajus at the Brahmayajña, and the Śruti says: यद्यजूंषि धृतस्य कुल्या (*yadyajūṃṣi dhṛtasya kulyā*). येभ्यः (*yebhyaḥ*) ("for whom"): the dative is in the sense of purpose. For their enjoyment honey (kṣaudra) runs swiftly as a stream. For those who recite Atharvan mantras for the Brahmayajña, a stream of honey flows to the Pitṛs; so it is declared: यदाथर्वणांगिरसो मधोः कुल्या (*yadātharvaṇāṃgiraso madhoḥ kulyā*). "To those very ones" mentioned above, O departed one, go to all of them; गच्छतात् (*gacchatāt*) means go, reach.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एकेभ्यः (*ekebhyaḥ*)—for the enjoyment of some Pitṛs
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma juice
- पवते (*pavate*)—flows as a stream
- एके (*eke*)—some others, Pitṛs
- धृतं (*dhṛtaṃ*)—ghee
- उपासते (*upāsate*)—

### Printed p. 1034
desire or enjoy
- येभ्यः (*yebhyaḥ*)—for the enjoyment of still other Pitṛs
- मधु (*madhu*)—honey
- प्रधावति (*pradhāvati*)—runs swiftly as a stream (O departed one)
- तान् चित् एव (*tān cit eva*)—to the deities mentioned above (you)
- अपि गच्छतात् (*api gacchatāt*)—go

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the enjoyment of some Pitṛs the Soma juice flows as a stream. Some other Pitṛs partake of ghee. For the enjoyment of still others honey runs swiftly as a stream. O departed one, go to all these kinds of Pitṛs and join them.

##### English translation
Soma is filtered for some (of the Pitris), others accept clarified butter; go (O dead one) to those to whom the honey flows.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

What does it mean that Soma and other juices flow for the enjoyment of the Pitṛs, and why do they flow? This is stated in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka, in the account of the Brahmayajña rite:
यत्स्वाध्यायमधीयितैकामप्यृचं यजुः साम ना तद्ब्रह्मयज्ञः संतिष्ठते । (*yatsvādhyāyamadhīyitaikāmapyṛcaṃ yajuḥ sāma nā tadbrahmayajñaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate |*) (Tai. Ā. 2-10)
The Brahmayajña is a rite a Brāhmaṇa must perform every day. It chiefly consists of svādhyāya, that is, the practice of reciting the Veda.
पंच वा एते महायज्ञाः सतति प्रतायंते सतति संतिष्ठंते देवयज्ञः पितृयज्ञो भूतयज्ञो मनुष्ययज्ञो ब्रह्मयज्ञ इति ॥ (*paṃca vā ete mahāyajñāḥ satati pratāyaṃte satati saṃtiṣṭhaṃte devayajñaḥ pitṛyajño bhūtayajño manuṣyayajño brahmayajña iti ‖*) (Tai. Ā. 2-18)
The Brahmayajña is one of the five great sacrifices. These five must be performed every day, begun and finished on the same day. What is the nature of these five, and how are they performed?
(1) Deva-yajña: यदग्नौ जुहोत्यपि समिधं तद्देवयज्ञः संतिष्ठते । (*yadagnau juhotyapi samidhaṃ taddevayajñaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate |*) If oblations such as puroḍāśa are not possible, then if even a single piece of fuel (samidh) is offered in the fire to the deities, it counts as the deva-yajña. It is completed by this one offering.

### Printed p. 1035
(2) Pitṛ-yajña: यत्पितृभ्यः स्वधा करोत्यप्यपस्तत्पितृयज्ञः संतिष्ठते ॥ (*yatpitṛbhyaḥ svadhā karotyapyapastatpitṛyajñaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate ‖*) If balls (piṇḍa) and the like cannot be given to the Pitṛs, then offering libation of water alone, saying पितृभ्यः स्वधास्तु (*pitṛbhyaḥ svadhāstu*), counts as the pitṛ-yajña.
(3) Bhūta-yajña: यद्भूतेभ्यो बलिग्ं हरति तद्भूतयज्ञः संतिष्ठते ॥ (*yadbhūtebhyo baligṃ harati tadbhūtayajñaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate ‖*) After the Vaiśvadeva rite, at midday, putting a bali, that is a little food, for crows and other creatures counts as the bhūta-yajña.
(4) Manuṣya-yajña: यद्ब्राह्मणेभ्योऽन्नं ददाति तन्ननुष्ययज्ञः संतिष्ठते ॥ (*yadbrāhmaṇebhyo 'nnaṃ dadāti tannanuṣyayajñaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate ‖*) After the Vaiśvadeva rite, giving food to a guest, such as a Brāhmaṇa, that is, feeding him, counts as the manuṣya-yajña.
(5) Brahma-yajña: यत्साध्यायमधीयातैकामष्यचं यजुः साम वा तदृह्मयज्ञः संतिष्ठते ॥ (*yatsādhyāyamadhīyātaikāmaṣyacaṃ yajuḥ sāma vā tadṛhmayajñaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate ‖*) Svādhyāya is the study of the Veda received by tradition from elders such as father and grandfather. If one recites without fail every day at least a little of this, that is, one Ṛk of the Ṛgveda, one sentence of the Yajurveda, one mantra of the Sāmaveda, it counts as the brahma-yajña. These five great sacrifices must be observed every day.
The fruit produced by such study is described here more fully:
यदृचोऽधीते पयसः कूल्या अस्य पित्यन्तस्विधा अभिवहंति, यद्यजूग्ंषि घृतस्य कूल्या, यत्सामानि सोम एभ्यः पवते, यदथर्वांगिरसो मधोः कूल्या, यद्ब्राह्मणानीः हासान्पुराणानि कल्पान्गाथा नाराशग्‌ंसीर्मेदसः कूल्या अस्य पित्यन्तस्विधा अभिवहंति (*yadṛco 'dhīte payasaḥ kūlyā asya pityantasvidhā abhivahaṃti, yadyajūgṃṣi ghṛtasya kūlyā, yatsāmāni soma ebhyaḥ pavate, yadatharvāṃgiraso madhoḥ kūlyā, yadbrāhmaṇānīḥ hāsānpurāṇāni kalpāngāthā nārāśagṃsīrmedasaḥ kūlyā asya pityantasvidhā abhivahaṃti*) (Tai. Ā. 2-10)
If a man studies the Ṛgveda with discipline, a river of milk flows as a stream to his Pitṛs in the world of the Pitṛs and satisfies them. By study of the Yajurveda, ghee flows as a river and satisfies the Pitṛs. By study of the Sāmaveda, Soma juice flows as a stream and satisfies the Pitṛs. By study of the Atharvaveda, honey flows as a stream and gives the Pitṛs delight. By study of the Brāhmaṇas, Itihāsa and Purāṇas, Kalpa sūtras, Gāthās and Nārāśaṃsī mantras, a stream together with flesh (meat) arises and satisfies the Pitṛs.

### Printed p. 1036
यदृचोऽधीते पय आहुतिभिरेव तद्देवाग्स्तरपयति, यद्यजूग्ंषि धृता हुतिभिर्यत्सामानि सोमाहुतिभिर्यदथर्वांगिरसो मध्वाहुतिभिर्यद्भा ह्मणानीतिहासान्पुराणानि कल्पान्गाधा नाराशग्‌ंसीर्मेदाहुतिभिरेव तद्दे वाग्‌स्तर्पयति त एनं तृप्ता आयुषा तेजसा वर्चसा श्रिया यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनान्नाद्येन च तर्पयंति ॥ (*yadṛco 'dhīte paya āhutibhireva taddevāgstarapayati, yadyajūgṃṣi dhṛtā hutibhiryatsāmāni somāhutibhiryadatharvāṃgiraso madhvāhutibhiryadbhā hmaṇānītihāsānpurāṇāni kalpāngādhā nārāśagṃsīrmedāhutibhireva tadde vāgstarpayati ta enaṃ tṛptā āyuṣā tejasā varcasā śriyā yaśasā brahmavarcasenānnādyena ca tarpayaṃti ‖*) (Tai. Ā. 2-10)
Study of the Ṛgveda satisfies the deities like an offering of milk. Likewise study of the Yajurveda is like an offering of ghee, of the Sāmaveda like an offering of Soma, of the Atharvaveda like an offering of honey, and study of the Brāhmaṇas and the rest like offerings of fat (meat). By such offerings the deities are satisfied and favour the men who have studied, granting them long life, brilliance, vigour, wealth, fame, Brahmanical radiance and food and the like; this is the meaning.
In the present Ṛk only the offerings of Soma, ghee and honey are mentioned; the milk offering is not spoken of. Even so it must be supplied here by ellipsis.
In this Ṛk and in the following ones the jīva that is in the body of the departed is addressed as "O departed one". After death, when the earthly body is gone, the jīva, assuming a subtle form, must go to heavenly and other worlds to experience the fruit of its deeds. It cannot go to those worlds immediately after death; for some time it must remain in a subtle body. A being in such a state is customarily called preta. The jīva that has come out of the earthly body after death may be called preta.

> तपः । ये । चक्रिरे । महः । तान् । चित् । एव । अपि । गच्छतात् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये जनास्तपसा कृच्छ्रचांद्रायणादिना युक्ताः संतोऽनादृष्याः पापैरप्रधृष्ट्या भवंति । ये च तपसा यागादिरूपेण साधनेन स्वर्ययुः स्वर्गं यांति
> प्राप्नुवंति । ये च महो महत्तपोऽन्यैर्दुष्करं राजसूयाश्वमेधादिकं
> हिरण्यगर्भाद्युपासनं वा चक्रिरे कुर्वंति एतेषु प्रवर्तंते तेषु लोकेषु । तांश्चित्तानेव तपस्विनो हे प्रेत अपिगच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those people who, endowed with penance such as the kṛcchra and cāndrāyaṇa observances, are unassailable by sins; those who by penance in the form of sacrifice and the like have gone to heaven; and those who have performed great penance (mahaḥ tapaḥ) hard for others to perform, such as the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha, or the worship of Hiraṇyagarbha and the like, and who are engaged in these in those worlds: to those very ascetics, O departed one, go.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O departed one), ये (*ye*)—who
- तपसा (*tapasā*)—by austerity accompanied by kṛcchra, cāndrāyaṇa and the like
- अनाध्यष्याः (*anādhyaṣyāḥ*)—those untouchable by sin
- ये (*ye*)—who
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—the world of heaven
- ययुः (*yayuḥ*)—who have attained
- ये (*ye*)—who
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great
- तपः (*tapaḥ*)—penance, not easy for others to accomplish, in the form of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices, or in the form of worship of Hiraṇyagarbha and the like
- चक्रिरे (*cakrire*)—who are performing
- तान् चित् एव (*tān cit eva*)—to such ascetic Pitṛs
- अपि गच्छतात् (*api gacchatāt*)—go

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O departed one, go to those Pitṛs: those men who, while in this world, became free of sin through austerity and attained an excellent world; who through penance in the form of sacrifices have obtained heaven and dwell happily; who, having performed great penance difficult for others, are devoted to the worship of Brahman.

##### English translation
Those who through penance are unassailable (by sin), to those who through penance have gone to heaven, to those who have performed abundant penance, do you (O dead one) repair.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Pradhanas" are battles, in which wealth is scattered. Those heroes who fight in them, destroying enemies; those who abandon their bodies there; and those who are *thousand-dakṣiṇā*, having performed sacrifices with a thousand dakṣiṇās: go to all of these. The meaning is: attain the excellent world in which they dwell.

- (O departed one), ये (*ye*)—who
- प्रधनेषु (*pradhaneṣu*)—in battles

- युध्यंते (*yudhyaṃte*)—who fight and destroy enemies
- ये (*ye*)—who
- तनूत्यजः (*tanūtyajaḥ*)—who give up the body in that battle (die)
- ये वा (*ye vā*)—or who
- सहस्रदक्षिणाः (*sahasradakṣiṇāḥ*)—who have performed sacrifices giving gifts such as dakṣiṇā in thousands
- तान् चित् एव (*tān cit eva*)—to such Pitṛs
- अपि गच्छतात् (*api gacchatāt*)—go and join

O departed one, go to those Pitṛs: those who fought valiantly in battles, died, and dwell in the heroes' heaven; those who gave dakṣiṇā in thousands, performed sacrificial rites, and dwell in excellent worlds.

##### English translation
To those who engage in battles, heroes who have given up their lives, or who have presented thousands of offerings, to them (O dead one) repair.

- ये चित् (*ye cit*)—which
- पूर्वे (*pūrve*)—ancestors
- ऋतसापः (*ṛtasāpaḥ*)—who practise truth or sacrifice
- ऋतावानः (*ṛtāvānaḥ*)—who are therefore truthful
- ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*)—who, devoted to the performance of true acts, increase them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

##### English translation
Repair, Yama, to those ascetic Pitris who are ancient observers of truth, speakers of truth, and augmenters of truth.

## Sūkta 155 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
In this sūkta Alakṣmī is praised. Alakṣmī (Aśrī) is the deity presiding over poverty, bodily sloth, sorrow, calamity, lack of food or famine, and similar misfortunes.

### Printed p. 1041
Since nobody desires these, here this deity is bidden to depart. Concerning this sūkta, the work called Ṛgvidhāna says:

अलक्ष्मीनाशनार्थं तु जपेन्नित्यं शिरिंबिरं ॥ ७८ ॥ अपामार्गमयिां शाखां सदर्भां सहवीरणां । गृहीत्वात्मानं पावयेदधश्चोर्ध्वं च नित्यशः ॥ ७९ ॥ आज्यं चानेन जुहुयात्सहस्रं दशतीर्दश । त्रैहेण नुदते देहादलक्ष्मीं शतवार्षिकीं ॥ (*alakṣmīnāśanārthaṃ tu japennityaṃ śiriṃbiraṃ ‖ 78 ‖ apāmārgamayiāṃ śākhāṃ sadarbhāṃ sahavīraṇāṃ | gṛhītvātmānaṃ pāvayedadhaścordhvaṃ ca nityaśaḥ ‖ 79 ‖ ājyaṃ cānena juhuyātsahasraṃ daśatīrdaśa | traiheṇa nudate dehādalakṣmīṃ śatavārṣikīṃ ‖*) and चांद्रायणं चरन्नेतत्तूक्तं सिद्धिकरं जपेत् । अलक्ष्मीं नुदते देहादपि वर्षसहस्रिकीं ॥ (*cāṃdrāyaṇaṃ carannetattūktaṃ siddhikaraṃ japet | alakṣmīṃ nudate dehādapi varṣasahasrikīṃ ‖*) (Ṛgvidhāna, Adhyāya 4, verses 78-81).

For the destruction of Alakṣmī, this sūkta beginning "अरायि काणे (*arāyi kāṇe*)" is to be muttered every day. One should bring twigs of the apāmārga tree and darbha grass, and with them offer ten thousand oblations with ghee in the fire. If this is done, poverty, disease and the like, which have followed for hundreds of years, will be removed within three days. If this sūkta is muttered with the vow and observances of cāndrāyaṇa, all diseases that have come down for thousands of years will be destroyed, and poverty too will be destroyed.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अरायीति पंचर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं भरद्वाजपुत्रस्य शिरिंबिरस्यार्षमानुष्टुभं । जपहोमादिभिरिदं सूक्तमश्रीनाशकरं । तत्राद्योपांत्ययोस्तादृशोऽर्थ
> एव देवता । द्वितीयातृतीये ब्राह्मणस्पत्ये । पंचमी वैश्वदेवी । अनुक्रम्यते हि ।
> अरायि शिरिंबिरो भारद्वाजोऽलक्ष्मीघ्नं द्वितीयातृतीये ब्राह्मणस्पत्ये अंत्या
> वैश्वदेवीति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta "अरायि (*arāyi*)", of five ṛcs, the fourth sūkta, has Śirimbiṭha (Śirimbira), son of Bharadvāja, as seer, and the Anuṣṭubh metre. By muttering, oblation and the like, this sūkta destroys Alakṣmī. Its deity in the first and the last-but-one verse (the fourth) is that very meaning (Alakṣmī); the second and third are addressed to Brahmaṇaspati; the fifth to the Viśvedevas. The Anuktamaṇī says: अरायि शिरिंबिरो भारद्वाजोऽलक्ष्मीघ्नं द्वितीयातृतीये ब्राह्मणस्पत्ये अंत्या वैश्वदेवीति (*arāyi śiriṃbiro bhāradvājo 'lakṣmīghnaṃ dvitīyātṛtīye brāhmaṇaspatye aṃtyā vaiśvadevīti*). The viniyoga has been given.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta "अरायि (*arāyi*)" is the fourth sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has five ṛcs. Its seer is Śirimbiṭha, son of the sage Bharadvāja; the metre is Anuṣṭup. Since it is said that by muttering, oblations and the like of this sūkta Alakṣmī is destroyed, the destruction of Alakṣmī is the deity of the first and fourth ṛcs; Brahmaṇaspati is the deity of the second and third; the fifth ṛc is addressed to the Viśvedevas. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: अरायि शिरिंबिरो भारद्वाजोऽलक्ष्मीघ्नं द्वितीयातृतीये ब्राह्मणस्पत्ये अंत्या वैश्वदेवी (*arāyi śiriṃbiro bhāradvājo 'lakṣmīghnaṃ dvitīyātṛtīye brāhmaṇaspatye aṃtyā vaiśvadevī*). The viniyoga has been stated earlier.
