#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अरा॑यि॒ काणे॒ विक॑टे गि॒रिं ग॑च्छ सदान्वे ।  
> ति॒रिंबि॑रस्य॒ सत्व॑भि॒स्तेभि॑ष्ट्वा चातयामसि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अरायि । काणे । विकटे । गिरिं । गच्छ । सदान्वे ।  
> शिरिंबिठस्य । सत्त्वभिः । तेभिः । त्वा । चातयामसि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अराय्यदायिनि दानविरोधिनि हे काणे कुत्सितशब्द कारिणि कुत्सितदर्शने वा
> हे विकटे विकृतगमने विकृतांगे ना हे सदान्वे सदानोनुवे सर्वदाक्रोशकारिणि
> दुर्भिक्षादिदेवते गिरिं पर्वतं निर्जनदेशं गच्छ । अस्मान्मा बाधिष्ठाः । शिरिंबिरस्य ।
> बिठमंतरिक्षं । शीर्यते बिठेऽंतरिक्ष इति शिरिंबिरो मेघः । तस्य सत्वभिरंतर्वर्तमानैरुदकैस्तेभिस्तैस्त्वा त्वां चातयामसि । चातयामः । विनाशयामः । यद्वा ।
> शिरिंबरस्यॆतत्संज्ञकस्य भरद्वाजपुत्रस्य तेभिस्तरनुष्ठितैः सत्वभिः कर्मभिर्हे अलक्षि
> त्वां विनाशयामः । इतस्त्वमेव शीघ्रं गिरिं गच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O arāyi (non-giver, hostile to giving), O kāṇā (one who makes vile sounds, or of vile sight), O vikaṭā (of distorted gait or distorted limbs), O sadānvā (ever wailing), deity of famine and the like: go to the mountain, a desolate region; do not afflict us. *Biṭha* is the atmosphere; Śirimbiṭha, "he who is shattered in the atmosphere", is the cloud. With those waters within it we drive you away (cātayāmasi, we destroy). Or else: with the deeds performed by Śirimbiṭha, the son of Bharadvāja so named, O Alakṣmī, we destroy you; so go quickly to the mountain from here.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अरायि (*arāyi*)—O hostile to giving
- काणे (*kāṇe*)—one called by a vile word, or one who walks in a distorted way
- विकटॆ (*vikaṭè*)—one of distorted limbs, or who walks in a distorted way
- सदान्वे (*sadānve*)—one who is always weeping, O deity of famine
- गिरिं (*giriṃ*)—to the mountain, a desolate region
- गच्छ (*gaccha*)—depart (do not trouble us)
- शिरिंबिठस्य (*śiriṃbiṭhasya*)—of the cloud
- सत्वभिः तैः (*satvabhiḥ taiḥ*)—with those essential **NOTE**

### Printed p. 1043
#### Ṛk 1 (continued)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- …(with those) waters that are the essence, those in the cloud
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- चातयामसि (*cātayāmasi*)—we destroy
- [Or: शिरिंबिठस्य (*śiriṃbiṭhasya*)—of the seer Śirimbiṭha, son of Bharadvāja
- तैः सत्वभिः (*taiḥ satvabhiḥ*)—by good ritual acts
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you, Alakṣmī
- चातयामसि (*cātayāmasi*)—we destroy (therefore go quickly to deserted mountains and the like).]

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess of famine (drought), you are the enemy of giving; you are called by a vile name, or you are ill-formed; you have crippled limbs, or a distorted gait. You are one who is always weeping. Such as you, go away to the deserted mountain region. Do not trouble us. With the waters that are in the cloud we destroy your fierceness; or, by the good rites performed by the seer Śirimbiṭha, we destroy you, Alakṣmī.

##### English translation
Miserable, ill-favoured, deformed, ever-railing (goddess) go to the mountain ; with these exploits of Shirimbitha we scare you away.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the goddess of famine (drought) is described. In time of famine people have no food to eat, so there is no mind to give to another; even if there is the mind, it cannot be done. Therefore this goddess of famine is called the enemy of giving. Because there is no food, people curse this famine with bad words; people go about emaciated, crippled, without strength to walk, and weeping for food. Therefore the goddess is described here by the words काणे (*kāṇe*), विकटे (*vikaṭe*), सदान्वे (*sadānve*). And since villages and towns filled with people suffer from this famine, she is bidden to go away to the deserted mountain strongholds. And for famine to be removed there must be abundant rain. Therefore the seer says that we shall destroy famine, by means of rain, with the essential waters that are in the cloud; or else it is wished that famine be removed by the sacrificial and other rites of Śirimbiṭha, the seer of the hymn. On this Ṛk Yāska has given a Nirukta and explained the principal words:
सदान्वे । शिरिंबिठः ॥ आरायि काणे विकटे गिरिं गच्छ सदान्वे । शिरिंबिरस्य सत्वभिस्तेभिष्टा चातयामसि ॥ आदायिनि काणे विकटे । काणोऽविक्रांतदर्शन इत्यौपमन्यवः । कणतीर्वा स्यादणूभावकर्मणः । कणतिः शब्दाणूभावे (*sadānve | śiriṃbiṭhaḥ ‖ ārāyi kāṇe vikaṭe giriṃ gaccha sadānve | śiriṃbirasya satvabhistebhiṣṭā cātayāmasi ‖ ādāyini kāṇe vikaṭe | kāṇo 'vikrāṃtadarśana ityaupamanyavaḥ | kaṇatīrvā syādaṇūbhāvakarmaṇaḥ | kaṇatiḥ śabdāṇūbhāve*)

### Printed p. 1044
भाष्यतेऽनु कणतीति। मात्राणूभावात्कणो दर्शनाणूभावात्काणः ॥ विकटो विक्रांतगतिरित्यापमन्यवः । कटतीर्वास्याद्विपरीतस्य विकुटितो भवति । गिरिं गच्छ सदानोनुवे शब्दकारिके । शिरिंबिठस्य सत्वभिः । शिरिंबिठो मेघः । शीर्यते बिठे । बिठमंतरिक्षं बिठं बीरिठेन व्याख्यातं ॥ तस्य सत्वैरुदकैरिति स्यात्तैष्वा चातयामः, अपि वा शिरिंबिठो भारद्वाजः । काळकर्णोपेतोS लक्ष्मीर्निर्णाशयांचकार तस्य सत्त्वैः कर्मभिरितिस्यात्तैष्वा चातयामः ॥ चातयतिर्नाशने ॥ (*bhāṣyate 'nu kaṇatīti| mātrāṇūbhāvātkaṇo darśanāṇūbhāvātkāṇaḥ ‖ vikaṭo vikrāṃtagatirityāpamanyavaḥ | kaṭatīrvāsyādviparītasya vikuṭito bhavati | giriṃ gaccha sadānonuve śabdakārike | śiriṃbiṭhasya satvabhiḥ | śiriṃbiṭho meghaḥ | śīryate biṭhe | biṭhamaṃtarikṣaṃ biṭhaṃ bīriṭhena vyākhyātaṃ ‖ tasya satvairudakairiti syāttaiṣvā cātayāmaḥ, api vā śiriṃbiṭho bhāradvājaḥ | kāḷakarṇopetoS lakṣmīrnirṇāśayāṃcakāra tasya sattvaiḥ karmabhiritisyāttaiṣvā cātayāmaḥ ‖ cātayatirnāśane ‖*) (Ni. 6-30)

In this Ṛk Alakṣmī, or the goddess of famine, is described. सदान्वे (*sadānve*) means सदानोनुवे (*sadānonuve*)—one who weeps from hunger.

अरायि (*arāyi*)—आदायिनि (*ādāyini*): one who does not give. In time of famine there is no mind to give to one another; having nothing themselves, what can they give to others? The same holds for the Alakṣmī, those afflicted by poverty: having nothing themselves, the poor cannot give to others.

काणे (*kāṇe*). काणोऽविक्रांतदर्शन इत्यौपमन्यवः (*kāṇo 'vikrāṃtadarśana ityaupamanyavaḥ*). काण (*kāṇa*) means blind, one who cannot see; in famine, from lack of food, dimness of sight is natural. So too with the poor. This is the opinion of the teacher called Aupamanyava. कणतीर्वा स्यादणूभावकर्मणः । कणतिः शब्दाणूभावे (*kaṇatīrvā syādaṇūbhāvakarmaṇaḥ | kaṇatiḥ śabdāṇūbhāve*): the root कण् (*kaṇ*) indicates a very small, that is a very soft, sound; or it may indicate "not heard at all". A man of very small form is called कण (*kaṇa*). काण (*kāṇa*) means one who cannot see, or a man who has only one eye.

कट (*kaṭa*): विकटो विक्रांतगतिरित्यौपमन्यवः (*vikaṭo vikrāṃtagatirityaupamanyavaḥ*). विकट (*vikaṭa*) means one with deformed limbs—a crooked arm, a lame leg and so on; or one with a deformed gait in walking; this is Aupamanyava's opinion. The word विकट (*vikaṭa*) is derived from the root कुट् (*kuṭ*) meaning "to be crooked"; or the letters of the word विकुटितः (*vikuṭitaḥ*) may have been transposed to give विकट (*vikaṭa*). It means very crooked.

गिरिं गच्छ सदानोनुवे शब्द कारिके (*giriṃ gaccha sadānonuve śabda kārike*): O goddess of famine, who are ever weeping, screaming and making noise, go away to the deserted hill.

### Printed p. 1045
शिरिंबिठस्य सत्वभिः (*śiriṃbiṭhasya satvabhiḥ*). शिरिंबित (*śiriṃbita*) is the cloud. The cloud is split, that is scattered, in the बिर (*bira*), the atmosphere; hence the cloud is called शिरिंबिठ (*śiriṃbiṭha*). The explanation of the word बिठं (*biṭhaṃ*) was given earlier, when the word बीरिड (*bīriḍa*) was explained (Ni. 5-28). "We destroy you with the essential waters of such a cloud" means: by the fall of rain we destroy famine.

अपि ना शिरिंबिरो भारद्वाजः । काळकर्णोपेतोऽलक्ष्मीर्निर्णाशयांचकार तस्य सत्त्वैः कर्मभिरिति स्यात्तैष्टा चातयामः । चातॆयतिर्नाशने ॥ (*api nā śiriṃbiro bhāradvājaḥ | kāḷakarṇopeto 'lakṣmīrnirṇāśayāṃcakāra tasya sattvaiḥ karmabhiriti syāttaiṣṭā cātayāmaḥ | cātèyatirnāśane ‖*). Or शिरिंबिठ (*śiriṃbiṭha*) means the son of the seer Bharadvāja. With his black ears, deformed in form, he destroyed Alakṣmī, the goddess of poverty—that is, he frightened her and drove her away. By the acts of that seer too we destroy, that is drive away, this goddess of famine. The root चातियति (*cātiyati*) has the sense of destroying, frightening and driving away.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> च॒त्तो इ॒तिश्च॒त्तामुतः॒ सर्वा॑ भ्रू॒णान्या॒रुषी॑ ।  
> अ॒रा॒य्यं॑ ब्रह्मणस्पते॒ तीक्ष्ण॑शृंगोदृ॒षन्नि॑हि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> चत्तो इति । इतः । चत्ता । अमुतः । सर्वा । भ्रूणानि । आरुषी ।  
> अराय्यं । ब्रह्मणः । पते । तीक्ष्णशृंग । उत्ऋषन् । इहि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सालक्ष्मीरितोऽस्माल्लोकाच्चत्तो चत्तैवास्माभिर्नाशितैवामुतोऽमुष्मादपि
> लोकाच्चत्ता हिंसिता भवतु । यालक्ष्मीः सर्वा सर्वाणि भ्रूणानि गर्भजातानि सर्वासामोषधीनामंकुराणि या दुर्भिक्षाधिदेवतारुष्याहंत्री भवति आराय्यं दानविरोधिनीं तां हे ब्रह्मणस्पते मंत्रपालयितरदेव हे तीक्ष्ण शृंग तीक्ष्ण तेजस्क उदृषन्नस्मात्स्थानादुद्धमयन्निहि । गच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Alakṣmī: from this world, चत्तो (*catto*)—let her be destroyed by us; from yonder world also let her be struck down (चत्ता (*cattā*)). The Alakṣmī, the presiding deity of famine, who is the destroyer of all embryos—everything born in wombs, and the sprouts of all plants—and who is आराय्यं (*ārāyyaṃ*), opposed to giving: her, O Brahmaṇaspati, protector of mantras, O sharp-horned one, of sharp radiance, driving her out from this place, go (इहि (*ihi*)).

- (the goddess of famine) who

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May this goddess of famine be struck down and driven away from this world and from the heavenly world. O Brahmaṇaspati, shining with sharp radiance, come to us, driving away this goddess of famine, enemy of giving, who destroys all unborn children and the seed-sprouts of trees.

##### English translation
May she be scared away from this (world), scared away from the next (world), the desructress of a embryos; sharp-horned Brihaspati, approach, driving away Distress.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अदः (*adaḥ*): that which is in a distant place, अपूरुषं (*apūruṣaṃ*), devoid of a maker, a man—the wood, a wooden body of the deity named Puruṣottama—floats on the shore of the sea, upon the water. O दुर्हणो (*durhaṇo*), hard to be slain, who cannot be slain by anyone, O worshipper, take hold of that wood (the explanation continues in the next block).

### Printed p. 1047

> स्तोतः आ रभस्व । आलंबस्व । उपास्स्वेत्यर्थः । तेन दारुमयेण देवेनोपास्यमानेन परस्तरमतिशयेन तरणीयमुत्कृष्टं वैष्णवं लोकं गच्छ ॥ अपर अह । हे
> दुर्हणो दुःखेन हननीये दुष्टहनुयुक्ते वा हे आलक्ष्मि सिंधोः पारे
> समुद्रतीरप्रांतेऽपूरुषं पुरुषैर्जनैर्वियुक्तमदोऽस्मत्तो दूरे देशे
> वर्तमानं यद्दारु दारुमयिा नौः प्लवते तद्दार्वा रभस्व । परिगृहाण । गृहीत्वा च
> तेन दारुणा परस्तरमतिशयेन तरणीयं ब्रह्मणस्पतिना प्रेरिता सती द्वीपांतरं
> गच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

आ रभस्व (*ā rabhasva*) means: lay hold of, worship. With that wooden deity, who is being worshipped, go to the Viṣṇu-world, the excellent one that is to be crossed most (परस्तरं (*parastaraṃ*)). Another says: O दुर्हणो (*durhaṇo*), hard to be slain, or having a bad jaw, O Alakṣmī: on the shore of the sea, devoid of men, in a place far from us, a boat made of wood floats; seize that wood; having seized it, urged by Brahmaṇaspati, go with that wood to the far side, to another island.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Spiritual (adhyātmic) sense:
- अदः (*adaḥ*)—in a distant place
- अपूरुषं (*apūruṣaṃ*)—not made by man
- यत् दारु (*yat dāru*)—which wooden body of a deity
- सिंधोः पारे (*siṃdhoḥ pāre*)—on the sea-shore
- प्लवते (*plavate*)—floats
- तत् (*tat*)—that wood
- दुर्हनो (*durhano*)—O worshipper who cannot be killed
- आ रभस्व (*ā rabhasva*)—take refuge in it (worship)
- तेन (*tena*)—worshipped by that wooden deity
- परस्तरं (*parastaraṃ*)—the excellent Viṣṇu-world
- गच्छ (*gaccha*)—go and reach it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O soul, or self, you (the self) cannot be killed. Such as you, taking refuge in the body of a deity, go and reach the most excellent Viṣṇu-world established in the middle of the sea.

Sense with reference to the goddess of famine:
- दुर्हणो (*durhaṇo*)—O goddess of famine, or Alakṣmī, who die in great suffering, or have a deformed jaw
- सिंधोः पारे (*siṃdhoḥ pāre*)—in the region of the sea-shore
- अपूरुषं (*apūruṣaṃ*)—without people
- अदः (*adaḥ*)—very far from here
- यत् दारु (*yat dāru*)—which boat made of wood
- प्लवते (*plavate*)—floats
- तत् (*tat*)—that boat
- आ रभस्व (*ā rabhasva*)—take refuge in it, that is, climb in and sit
- तेन (*tena*)—with the help of that boat (urged by Brahmaṇaspati)
- परस्तरं (*parastaraṃ*)—to another island on the far shore of the sea, which has to be crossed
- गच्छ (*gaccha*)—go away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess of famine, or Alakṣmī, who die of great suffering: take refuge in the boat floating on the water at the sea-shore, very far from here, sit in it, and go away to the other island near the far shore of the sea.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> षष्ठेऽहनि तृतीयसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिशस्त्रे यद्ध प्राचीरित्येषा । सूत्रितं
> च । कपृन्नरो यद्ध प्राचीरजगंतेति चैते । आ. ८-३ । इति ॥
> हे मंडूरधाणिकीर्मंडूरवत्कुत्सितशब्द कारिण्यो मंदनस्य धनस्य धारयित्यो वालक्ष्य उरः ॥ उर्वि हिंसार्थः । अस्मात्कपि राल्लोप इति वलोपः ।
> ततो जसि रूपमेतत् ॥ हिंसित्यो यूयं प्राचीः प्रकर्षीणांचंत्यः प्रकृष्टगमनाः सत्यो यद्ध यदा खल्वजगंत अगच्छत॥ गमर्लजि मध्यमबहुवचने छांदसः
> शपः श्लुः । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति तस्यॆ तनबादेशः । अत एव जित्वाभावादनुनासिकलोपो
> न भवति ॥ तदानीमेव सर्व इंद्रस्य शत्रवो बुद्भुदयाशवः ॥ यांति गच्छंतीति याः ।
> अश्नुवत इत्याशवः । याश्च त आशवश्च याशवः । बुद्भुदवद्यातारो व्यापनशीलाश्च
> संतो हता नष्टा आसन् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the sixth day, at the third pressing, in the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's śastra, this Ṛk *yaddha prācīḥ* is used. It is also stated in the Sūtra: कपृन्नरो यद्ध प्राचीरजगंतेति चैते (*kapṛnnaro yaddha prācīrajagaṃteti caite*) (Ā. Sū. 8-3). O मंडूरधाणिकीः (*maṃḍūradhāṇikīḥ*)—you who, like frogs, make vile sounds; or who hold joyous wealth; or Alakṣmīs; उरः (*uraḥ*)—from the root उर्वि (*urvi*) in the sense of harming: injurers. When you, going forward (प्राचीः (*prācīḥ*), moving swiftly), came (अजगंत (*ajagaṃta*)), at that very time all the enemies of Indra, बुद्भुदयाशवः (*budbhudayāśavaḥ*)—those who go (याः (*yāḥ*)) and are swift (*āśavaḥ*), moving like bubbles and pervasive—were slain, destroyed.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उरः (*uraḥ*)—those who injure people
- मंडूरधाणिकीः (*maṃḍūradhāṇikīḥ*)—those who scream with a distorted voice, the goddesses called famine or Alakṣmī
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- प्राचीः (*prācīḥ*)—walking very swiftly
- अजगंत ह (*ajagaṃta ha*)—they go away, then
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- सर्वे (*sarve*)—all
- शत्रवः (*śatravaḥ*)—enemies
- बुद्भुदयाशवः (*budbhudayāśavaḥ*)—like bubbles on the water
- हताः (*hatāḥ*)—are destroyed

### Printed p. 1049

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When these famine-deities (or deities of poverty), who torment the people and screech with distorted voices, move swiftly forward and depart, all the enemies of Indra (that is, of the people) perish like bubbles on water. The intention is that when famine has gone and plenty has arrived, the people's hardships will be removed.

##### English translation
Utterers of discordant sounds, when swiftly moving you departed, all
the enemies of Indra were slain, disappearing like bubbles.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the sixth day of the sacrifice, in the third pressing, among the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Brahman, this Ṛk beginning यद्ध प्राचीः (*yaddha prācīḥ*) is to be recited. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra कपृन्नरो यद प्राचीरजगंतेति चैते (*kapṛnnaro yada prācīrajagaṃteti caite*) (Ā. 8-3).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परी॒मे गाम॑नेषत॒ पर्य॒ग्नि म॑हृषत ।  
> दे॒वेष्व॑क्रत॒ श्रवः॒ क इ॒मा आ द॑धर्षति ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । इमे । गां । अनेषत । परि । अग्निं । अहृषत ।  
> देवेषु । अक्रत । श्रवः । कः । इमान् । आ । दधर्षति ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमे विश्वे देवा गां । जात्यभिप्रायमेकवचनं । पणिभिरपहृताः सर्वा
> देवगवीः पर्यनेषत । पर्यनयन् । यष्ट्यानंगिरसः परिप्रापयन् । ततोऽग्निं च
> पर्यहृषत । परितो व्यहरन् । यागार्थं तत्र तत्र गार्हपत्यादिरूपेण स्थापितवंत इत्यर्थः । एवं कृत्वा देवेषु यष्टव्यॆष्टिद्रादिसु श्रवोऽन्नमक्रत । अकृषत ।
> कः शत्रुरसुरादिरिमान्विश्वानेवाना दधर्षति । अभिभवितुं शक्नोति । न कश्चिदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These Viśvedevas brought back गां (*gāṃ*) (the singular is used with a view to the class): all the cows of the gods that had been carried off by the Paṇis. They conducted them and handed them over to the Aṅgirases, the sacrificers. Then they also set up the fire all around, that is, they established it here and there for the sacrifice in the form of the Gārhapatya and the others. Having done so, they prepared श्रवः (*śravaḥ*), food, among the gods who are to be worshipped with the iṣṭis and the like. What enemy, an Asura or any other, can overcome all these? None can.

### Printed p. 1050

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इमे (*ime*)—these Viśvedevas
- गां (*gāṃ*)—the herd of cows carried off by the Paṇis
- परि अनेषत (*pari aneṣata*)—brought back and placed in the power of the Aṅgirasa sages
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—the fires beginning with the Gārhapatya
- परि अहृषत (*pari ahṛṣata*)—established here and there (afterwards)
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods Indra and the rest, who are worthy of sacrifice
- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—food in the form of oblation (to offer)
- अक्रत (*akrata*)—prepared
- इमान् (*imān*)—these Viśvedevas
- कः (*kaḥ*)—what enemy or Asura
- आ दधर्षति (*ā dadharṣati*)—can resist?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

These Viśvedevas brought back the cows carried off by the Paṇis and placed them in the power of the Aṅgirasa sages. They established the Gārhapatya and other fires on the sacrificial altar. They prepared food, in the form of oblation, for Indra and the other gods who are to be worshipped in the sacrifice. Can any enemy or Asura resist such Viśvedevas?

##### English translation
These (Vishwadevas) have brought back the (stolen) cattle ; they have built up the fire ; they have provided food for the gods. Who will overcome them ?

## Sūkta 156 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निं हिन्वंतु न इति पंचर्चं पंचमं सूक्तमग्निपुत्रस्य केतुनाम्न आर्षं
> गायत्रमाग्नेयं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । अग्निं केतुराग्नेय आग्नेयं गायत्रमिति ॥
> प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्गायत्रे छंदसीदं शस्यं । सूत्रितं च । अग्निं हिन्वंतु नः
> प्राग्नये वाचमिति सूक्ते । आ. ४-१३ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta अग्निं हिन्वंतु नः (*agniṃ hinvaṃtu naḥ*) has five Ṛks and is the fifth sūkta. Its seer is Ketu, son of Agni; the deity is Agni; the metre is Gāyatrī. The Anukramaṇī says: अग्निं केतुराग्नेय आग्नेयं गायत्रं (*agniṃ keturāgneya āgneyaṃ gāyatraṃ*). In the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra this sūkta is to be recited for the Ṛks in the Gāyatrī metre. The sūtra says: अग्निं हिन्वंतु नः प्राग्नये वाचमिति सूक्ते (*agniṃ hinvaṃtu naḥ prāgnaye vācamiti sūkte*) (Ā. 4-13).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta अग्निं हिन्वंतु (*agniṃ hinvaṃtu*) is the fifth sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It contains five Ṛks. Its seer is Ketu, son of Agni; the deity is Agni; the metre is Gāyatrī. The Anukramaṇī says अग्निं केतुराग्नेय आग्नेयं गायत्रं (*agniṃ keturāgneya āgneyaṃ gāyatraṃ*). The sūkta is applied to Gāyatrī-metre Ṛks at the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra mantras. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the sūtra अग्निं हिन्वंतु नः प्राग्नये वाचमिति सूक्ते (*agniṃ hinvaṃtu naḥ prāgnaye vācamiti sūkte*) (Ā. 4-13).

### Printed p. 1051
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 156; Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 14. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Ketu Āgneya. Deity: Agni. Metre: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ग्निं हि॑न्वंतु नो॒ धियः॒ सप्ति॑मा॒शुमि॑वा॒जिषु॑ ।  
> तेन॑ जेष्म॒ धनं॑धनं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्निं । हिन्वंतु । नः । धियः । सप्तिं । आशुंइव । आजिषु ।  
> तेन । जेष्म । धनंधनं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नोऽस्माकं धियः कर्माणि स्तुतयो वाग्निं हिन्वंतु । प्रेरयंतु । यागार्थमुद्योजयंतु वर्धयंतु ना ॥ हि गतौ वृद्धौ च ॥ तत्र दृष्टांतः । आजिषु
> संग्रामेष्वशुमिव यथाशुं शीघ्रगामिनं सप्तिं सर्पणशीलमश्वं योद्धारः
> प्रेरयंति तद्वत् । तेनाग्नि ना धनंधनं सर्वं धनं जेष्म । वयं जयेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May our धियः (*dhiyaḥ*), our rites or praises, urge on Agni, that is, rouse him for the sacrifice and make him grow (the root हि (*hi*) means going and increase). The illustration: as warriors in battles urge on a swift horse, the सप्ति (*sapti*), the one given to moving along, so may our rites urge Agni. Through that Agni may we win all wealth, धनंधनं (*dhanaṃdhanaṃ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आजिषु (*ājiṣu*)—in battles
- आशुमिव (*āśumiva*)—like one of swift motion
- सप्तिं (*saptiṃ*)—as warriors urge on a horse
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—rites such as sacrifices, or praises
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- हिन्वंतु (*hinvaṃtu*)—may they urge on for the sacrifice
- तेन (*tena*)—through that Agni
- धनंधनं (*dhanaṃdhanaṃ*)—all kinds of wealth
- जेष्म (*jeṣma*)—may we win

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As soldiers in battles urge on a swift horse, may our rites or praises urge Agni on for the sacrifice. With the help of that Agni may we win all wealth.

### Printed p. 1052

##### English translation
May our rites bring Agni hither like a swift charger in battle, may we through him acquire all wealth.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यया॒ गा आ॒करा॑महे॒ सेन॑याग्ने॒ तवो॒त्या ।  
> तां नो॑ हिन्व म॒घत्त॑ये ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यया । गाः । आकरामहे । सेनया । अग्ने । तव । ऊत्या ।  
> तां । नः । हिन्व । मघत्तये ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने सेनयेनेन सह वर्तमानया सेनारूपया ना यया तवोत्या
> रक्षया गा आकरामहे अभिमुख्येन कुर्महे । लभामह इत्यर्थः । तामूतिं
> नोऽस्मान्हिन्व । गमय । किमर्थ० । मघत्तये । धनस्य दानार्थ० । अस्माकं धनलाभायेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, by that protection of yours, which is in the form of an army, सेनया (*senayā*) (that is, accompanied by *ina*), we make cows our own, that is, we obtain them. Send us, हिन्व (*hinva*), make go to us that protection, for मघत्तये (*maghattaye*), the giving of wealth, that is, so that we may gain wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- तव (*tava*)—your
- यया (*yayā*)—by which
- सेनया (*senayā*)—army-like
- ऊत्या (*ūtyā*)—by protection
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—cows
- आकरामहे (*ākarāmahe*)—we obtain
- तां (*tāṃ*)—such protection
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- मघत्तये (*maghattaye*)—for wealth
- हिन्व (*hinva*)—provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, provide us, for the gaining of wealth also, that protection of yours, in the form of an army, by which we obtain cows.

##### English translation
Send us, Agni, for the acquisition of wealth, that army with which
we may acquire cattle through your protection.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आग्ने॑ स्थू॒रं र॒यिं भ॑र पृ॒थुं गोमं॑तम॒श्विनं॑ ।  
> अं॒ग्धि खं व॒र्तया॑ प॒णिं ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । अग्ने । स्थूरं । रयिं । भर । पृथुं । गोऽमंतं । अश्विनं ।  
> अंग्धि । खं । वर्तय । पणिं ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अभिप्लविकेषूक्ष्येषु प्रशास्तुः शस्त्र आग्ने स्थूरमिति तृचो वैकल्पिकोऽनुरूपः । सूत्रितं च । आ ते वत्सो मनो यमदाग्ने स्थूरं रयिं भर । आ. ७-८। इति ॥
> हे अग्ने स्तूरं स्थूलं वृद्धं पृथुं विस्तीर्णं गोमंतं गोभिर्युक्तमश्विनमश्वोपेतं रयिं धनमा भर । अस्मभ्यमाहर । प्रयच्छ । खमंतरिक्षमंग्धि ।
> वृष्ट्युदकैः सिंच । यद्वा । आत्मीयैस्तेजोभिव्यंजय । प्रकाशय । पणिं वणिजमदातारमसुरं वा वर्तय । इतो निर्गमय । यद्वा । दाने प्रवर्तय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Abhiplava ukthya days, the three Ṛks beginning आग्ने स्थूरं (*āgne sthūraṃ*) are an optional anurūpa triplet in the Praśāstṛ's śastra. The sūtra says: आ ते वत्सो मनो यमदाग्ने स्थूरं रयिं भर (*ā te vatso mano yamadāgne sthūraṃ rayiṃ bhara*) (Ā. 7-8).
O Agni, bring रयिं (*rayiṃ*), wealth, that is स्थूरं (*sthūraṃ*), bulky and abundant, पृथुं (*pṛthuṃ*), extensive, गोमंतं (*gomaṃtaṃ*), endowed with cows, and अश्विनं (*aśvinaṃ*), with horses; bring it to us and give it. अंग्धि खं (*aṃgdhi khaṃ*): sprinkle the sky with rain-water; or else, make it manifest, illumine it, with your own splendours. वर्तय पणिं (*vartaya paṇiṃ*): send the Paṇi, the merchant or the miserly one who gives nothing, or an Asura, out of here; or else, set him to giving.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- स्थूरं (*sthūraṃ*)—abundant
- पृथुं (*pṛthuṃ*)—extensive
- गोमंतं (*gomaṃtaṃ*)—together with cows
- अश्विनं (*aśvinaṃ*)—together with horses
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—bring to us
- खं (*khaṃ*)—the sky
- अंगिः (*aṃgiḥ*)—drench with rain-water, or fill with your radiance **NOTE**
- पणिं (*paṇiṃ*)—the miserly Asura
- वर्तय (*vartaya*)—send out of here

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, bring us abundant and excessive wealth, cows and horses. Fill the sky with clouds or with your radiance. Send the miser out of here, or else prompt his mind to make gifts.

##### English translation
Bring us, Agni, substantial and extensive wealth, consistlng of cattle
and horses, sprinkle the sky (with rain), expel Pani.

### Printed p. 1054

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the ukthya sacrifices connected with the Abhiplava, among the śastra mantras to be recited by the priest called Praśāstṛ, the three Ṛks beginning आग्ने स्फूरं (*āgne sphūraṃ*) (Ṛks 3–5) are to be recited optionally as the anurūpa triplet. This is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the passage आ ते वत्सो मनो यमदाग्ने स्फूरं रयिं भर (*ā te vatso mano yamadāgne sphūraṃ rayiṃ bhara*) (Ā. 7-8).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॒ नक्ष॑त्रम॒जर॒मा सूर्यं॑ रोहयो दि॒वि ।  
> दध॒ज्जोऽति॒र्जने॑भ्यः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । नक्षत्रं । अजरं । आ । सूर्यं । रोहयः । दिवि ।  
> दधत् । ज्योतिः । जनेभ्यः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने नक्षत्रं । नक्षति सततं गच्छतीति नक्षत्रः ॥ नक्षि गत् । अमिनक्षीत्यादिनात्रन्प्रत्ययः ॥ सततं गंतारमजरं जरारहितं सूर्यं सर्वस्य प्रेरकमादित्यं
> दिव्यंतरिक्ष आ रोहयः । उपर्यवस्थितवानसि । यद्वा । नक्षत्रं कृत्तिकादिकं सूर्यं
> च दिव्यारोहयः । किं कुर्वन् । जनेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः प्राणिभ्यो व्यवहारार्थं ज्योतिः
> प्रकाशं दधद्विदधत् कुर्वन् । यथा सर्वेषां प्रकाशो भवति तथोन्नते देशे
> सूर्यमगमय इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, नक्षत्रं (*nakṣatraṃ*) is the one who constantly goes (the root नक्षि (*nakṣi*), to go). You have set on high in the sky the sun, who is the constant mover, ageless, the impeller of all. Or else: you have set in the sky the constellations such as Kṛttikā, and the sun. Doing what? Providing light, ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*), for the people, for all creatures, for their activity. The meaning is: so that there may be light for all, you made the sun go to a lofty region.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- जनेभ्यः (*janebhyaḥ*)—for all people and creatures, for their activity
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—light
- दधत् (*dadhat*)—in order to produce
- नक्षत्रं (*nakṣatraṃ*)—the constant mover
- अजरं (*ajaraṃ*)—the ageless, that is, the one who always remains the same, without increase or decrease
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the sun, who impels all
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the sky
- आ रोहयः (*ā rohayaḥ*)—you have established on high [or: नक्षत्रं (*nakṣatraṃ*)—the host of constellations beginning with Kṛttikā; आ रोहयः (*ā rohayaḥ*)—you have established]

### Printed p. 1055

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, so that all creatures may be able to go about their own affairs, you have set the Sun in the upper region of the firmament to make light everywhere. The Sun is ever on the move, shines evenly without waxing or waning, and impels all. Or else you have set the constellations beginning with Kṛttikā there as well.

##### English translation
You, Agni. have elevated the imperishable planet, the Sun, in the firmament, giving light to the people.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॑ के॒तुर्वि॒शाम॑सि॒ प्रेष्ठः॒ श्रेष्ठ॑ उपस्थ॒सत् ।  
> बोधा॑ स्तो॒त्रे वयो॒ दध॑त् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्ने । केतुः । विशां । असि । प्रेष्ठः । श्रेष्ठः । उपस्थसत् ।  
> बोध । स्तोत्रे । वयः । दधत् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने विशां प्रजानां यजमानानां केतुः केतयितासि । ज्ञापयिता
> भवसि । अत एव प्रेष्ठः प्रियतमः श्रेष्ठः प्रशस्यतमश्च भवसि । स त्वमुपस्थसदुपस्थाने
> यज्ञगृहे निषीदन्नोध । अस्मदीयं स्तोत्रमवगच्छ । किं कुर्वन् । स्तोत्रे स्तुवते
> जनाय वयोऽन्नं दधद्विदधत् कुर्वन् प्रयच्छन् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, you are the *ketu* of the people, that is, of the sacrificers: you cause them to know, you make them aware. For that very reason you are the dearest and the most praiseworthy. Such as you are, seated at the place of sacrifice (*upastha*), the sacrificial house, attend to our praise. What are you to do? Giving food to the one who praises you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni, you
- विशां (*viśāṃ*)—to the people, the sacrificers and others
- केतुः (*ketuḥ*)—a banner-like one, or one who makes known
- असि (*asi*)—you are (therefore)
- श्रेष्ठः (*śreṣṭhaḥ*)—worthy of love and regard **NOTE**
- श्रेष्ठः (*śreṣṭhaḥ*)—most praiseworthy (such as you are)
- उपस्थसत् (*upasthasat*)—seated in the sacrificial house
- स्तोत्रे (*stotre*)—to the person who praises you
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—food
- दधत् (*dadhat*)—providing
- बोध (*bodha*)—understand (hear) the praise we make

### Printed p. 1056

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you are a banner-like one, or one who makes known, to all the people, the sacrificer and the rest. You are also praiseworthy and worthy of love and regard. Seated in the sacrificial house, providing food and the like to the people who praise you, hear and understand the praises we make.

##### English translation
You, Agni, are the best beloved and most excellent benner of the people; understand (our praise) giving food to the praiser.

## Sūkta 157 (Maṇḍala 10)
The hundred and fifty-seventh sūkta

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमा नु कमिति पंचर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तमप्त्यपुत्रस्य भुवनस्यार्षं भुवनपुत्रस्य साधनसंज्ञस्य वा वैश्वदेवं । सर्वा द्विपदास्त्रिष्टुभः । तथा चानुक्रांतं ।
> इमा नु भुवन आप्त्यः साधनो ना भौवनो वैश्वदेवं दैपदं त्रैष्टुभमिति ॥
> दशरात्रस्य द्वितीये छंदोमे वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे वैश्वदेवान्नि विद्धानात्पूर्वमिदं
> शंसनीयं । सूत्रितं च । आ याहि वनसेमा नु कं बभ्रुरेक इति द्विपदासूक्तानि ।
> आ. ८-७ । इति ॥ षष्ठेऽहनि तृतीये सवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन उक्ष्यशस्त्र आद्यस्तृचः
> स्तोत्रियः । ततो द्वे अनुरूपार्थे । सूत्रितं च । ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन इमा नु कं
> भुवना सीषधामेति पंच । आ. ८-३ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta इमा नु कं (*imā nu kaṃ*) is the sixth sūkta, of five ṛks. Its seer is Bhuvana, son of Āptya, or else Sādhana by name, son of Bhuvana. Its deity is the Viśvedevas; all the ṛks are *dvipadā triṣṭubh*. The Anukramaṇī is quoted accordingly: इमा नु भुवन आप्त्यः साधनो ना भौवनो वैश्वदेवं दैपदं त्रैष्टुभमिति ॥ (*imā nu bhuvana āptyaḥ sādhano nā bhauvano vaiśvadevaṃ daipadaṃ traiṣṭubhamiti ‖*). Use: in the Vaiśvadeva śastra of the second Chandoma of the Daśarāta, this sūkta is to be recited before the insertion of the nivid. It is given in the sūtra आ याहि वनसेमा नु कं बभ्रुरेक इति द्विपदासूक्तानि (*ā yāhi vanasemā nu kaṃ babhrureka iti dvipadāsūktāni*) (Ā. 8-7). On the sixth day, at the third savana, in the Ukthya śastra of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the first three ṛks serve as the Stotriya Tṛca, and the next two are the Anurūpa verses. It is given in the sūtra ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन इमा नु कं भुवना सीषधामेति पंच (*brāhmaṇācchaṃsina imā nu kaṃ bhuvanā sīṣadhāmeti paṃca*) (Ā. 8-3).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta इमा नु कं (*imā nu kaṃ*) is the sixth sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has five ṛks. Its seer is Bhuvana, son of Āptya, or else Sādhana, son of Bhuvana. The deities are the Viśvedevas. All the ṛks of this sūkta are in the metre *dvipadā triṣṭubh*. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: इमा नु कं भुवन आप्तः साधनो वा भौवनो वैश्वदेवं दैपदं त्रैष्टुभं (*imā nu kaṃ bhuvana āptaḥ sādhano vā bhauvano vaiśvadevaṃ daipadaṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ*). This sūkta is to be recited, in the second Chandoma of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, before the nivid-sūkta that is inserted among the mantras of the Vaiśvadeva śastra when they are recited; this is expounded in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra आ याहि वनसेमा नु कं बभ्रुरेक इति द्विपदासूक्तानि (*ā yāhi vanasemā nu kaṃ babhrureka iti dvipadāsūktāni*) (Ā. 8-7). On the sixth day of the sacrifice, at the time of the third savana, among the Ukthya-śastra mantras to be recited by the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin,

### Printed p. 1057

the first three ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited as the Stotriya Tṛca and the next two (ṛks 4–5) as Anurūpa ṛks; this is expounded in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन इमा नु कंभुवना सीषधामेति पंच (*brāhmaṇācchaṃsina imā nu kaṃbhuvanā sīṣadhāmeti paṃca*) (Ā. 8-3).

##### Particulars

- Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 157
- Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 15
- Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 5
- Ṛṣi: भुवन आप्त्यः साधनो वा भावनः (*bhuvana āptyaḥ sādhano vā bhāvanaḥ*)
- Deity: विश्वेदेवाः (*viśvedevāḥ*)
- Metre: द्विपदा त्रिष्टुप् (*dvipadā triṣṭup*)

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मा नु कं॒ भुव॑ना सीषधा॒मेंद्र॑श्च॒ विश्वे॑ च दे॒वाः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमा । नु । कं । भुवना । सीसधाम । इंद्रः । च । विश्वे । च । देवाः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इमेमानि प्रदृश्यमानानि धुवना भुवनानि नु क्षिप्रं सीषधाम । साधयामः ।
> वशीकुर्मः । कमिति पूरकः । यद्वा । इमानि सर्वाणि भूतजातान्यस्मभ्यं कं सुखं
> सीषधाम । साधयंतु ॥ पुरुषव्यत्ययः ॥ इंद्रश्च विश्वे सर्वॆऽन्ये देवाश्च स्तुत्या
> प्रीता इममर्थं साधयंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These visible worlds we shall quickly accomplish, bring under our control; कं (*kaṃ*) is a filler. Or else: may all these beings accomplish happiness for us (a change of person). And may Indra and all the other gods, pleased by praise, accomplish this aim.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इमा (*imā*)—these (worlds) that we see
- भुवना (*bhuvanā*)—the worlds
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- सीषधाम (*sīṣadhāma*)—let us bring under control
- [Or इमा (*imā*)—these; भुवना (*bhuvanā*)—all the classes of beings (for us); नु (*nu*)—quickly; कं (*kaṃ*)—happiness; सीसधाम (*sīsadhāma*)—may they accomplish]
- इंद्रः च (*iṃdraḥ ca*)—and Indra
- विश्वे च देवाः (*viśve ca devāḥ*)—and all the other gods, pleased by our praise, may they approve this

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let us quickly bring under our control all these worlds that we see. Or else, may all these classes of beings (living creatures)

### Printed p. 1058

quickly accomplish happiness for us. May Indra and all the other gods accomplish this wish of ours.

##### English translation
May we, along with Indra and the universal gods, possess all these worlds.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य॒ज्ञं च॑ नस्त॒न्वं॑ च प्र॒जां चा॑दि॒त्यैरिंद्रः॑ स॒ह ची॑क्लपाति ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यज्ञं । च । नः । तन्वं । च । प्रजां । च । आदित्यैः । इंद्रः । सह । चीक्लृपाति ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नोऽस्माकं यज्ञं ज्योतिष्टोमादिकं यागं तन्नं शरीरं च प्रजां।
> पुत्रादिकां चादित्यैरदितिपुत्रैरन्यैर्देवैः सह वर्तमान इंद्रश्चीक्ष्लपाति । कल्पयतु।
> यज्ञादिकं स्वव्यापारसमर्थं करोतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May Indra, accompanied by the Ādityas, the sons of Aditi, and by the other gods, put in order (*kalpayatu*) our sacrifice, the Jyotiṣṭoma and the rest, our body, and our offspring, sons and so on. May he make the sacrifice and the rest capable of their own functions.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- आदित्यैः (*ādityaiḥ*)—with the other gods, the sons of Aditi
- सह (*saha*)—together
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the sacrifice, the Jyotiṣṭoma and the rest
- तन्वं च (*tanvaṃ ca*)—and the body
- प्रजां च (*prajāṃ ca*)—and the offspring, sons and so on
- चीक्लृपाति (*cīklṛpāti*)—may he make capable in their own functions

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, together with the other gods, the sons of Aditi, make our sacrifice, our body and our offspring capable in their own functions (may he make them prosper).

##### English translation
May Indra with the Adityas perfect our sacrifice and our bodies and our offspring.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒दि॒त्यैरिंद्रः॒ सग॑णो म॒रुद्भि॑र॒स्माकं॑ भूत्ववि॒ता त॒नूनां॑ ॥३॥

> आदित्यैरदितिपुत्रैर्मित्रादिभिर्मरुद्भिश्च सगणः सहित इंद्रोऽस्माकं तनूनां
> शरीराणां तनयानां नाविता भूतु । रक्षिता भवतु ॥

May Indra, together with his host (*sagaṇa*), accompanied by the Ādityas, the sons of Aditi, Mitra and the rest, and by the Maruts, be the protector of our bodies, that is, of our sons.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आदित्यैः (*ādityaiḥ*)—and by the gods Mitra and the rest, the sons of Aditi
- मरुद्भिः सगणः (*marudbhiḥ sagaṇaḥ*)—accompanied by the hosts of the Maruts
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—our
- तनूनां (*tanūnāṃ*)—of the bodies or of the sons
- अविता (*avitā*)—as protector
- भूतु (*bhūtu*)—let him be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, accompanied by the gods Mitra and the rest, the sons of Aditi, and by the hosts of the Maruts **NOTE**, be the protector of our bodies or of our sons.

##### English translation
May Indra with the Adityas, and attended by the Maruts be the protector of our bodies.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ह॒त्वा य॑ दे॒वा असु॑रा॒न्यदाय॑न्दे॒वा दे॑व॒त्वम॑भि॒रक्ष॑माणाः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हत्वाय । देवाः । असुरान् । यत् । आयन् । देवाः । देवत्वं । अभिरक्षमाणाः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवा इंद्रादयोऽसुरान् क्षेप्त्वान्वृत्रादीन्हत्वाय हत्वा विनाश्य यद्यदायन् आगच्छन् स्वकीयं स्थानं प्राप्नुवन् तदानीं ते देवा देवत्वमात्मीयममृतत्वमभिरक्षमाणा अभितः सर्वतो रक्षंतोऽभूवन् । बाधकाभावात्सर्वत्र प्रख्यापितवंत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods, Indra and the others, having cast down and slain the asuras, Vṛtra and the rest, when they came, that is, reached their own place, then those gods, guarding on every side their own divinity, their immortality, were established. Because there was no obstructor, the meaning is that they became famous everywhere.

### Printed p. 1060

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods, Indra and the others
- असुरान् (*asurān*)—the asuras, Vṛtra and the rest
- हत्वाय (*hatvāya*)—having destroyed
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- आयन् (*āyan*)—they came to their own places, then
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—those gods
- देवत्वं (*devatvaṃ*)—the deathless divine station (having obtained it)
- अभिरक्षमाणाः (*abhirakṣamāṇāḥ*)—became ones who guard it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the gods, Indra and the others, destroyed the asuras, Vṛtra and the rest, and returned to their own places, those gods made their deathless divine station secure and became famous. Being without enemies, they also became able to protect their station.

##### English translation
When the gods returned (home), after slaying the Asuras. (then were) the deities protecting their divinity.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When the gods had destroyed the asuras and left themselves without any enemy, the name "gods" became meaningful for them. Being without enemies, they had no fear at all, and they became deathless. The meaning is that they went on guarding this divine station in the future too, that is, kept it.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र॒त्यंच॑म॒र्कम॑नय॒ञ्छ ची॑भि॒रादित्स्व॒धामि॑षि॒रां पर्य॑पश्यन् ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रत्यंचं । अर्कं । अनयन् । शचीभिः । आत् । इत् । स्वधां । इषिरां । परि । अपश्यन्॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शचीभिः कर्मभिः परिचरणात्मकैः सार्धमर्कमर्चनसाधनं स्तोत्रं प्रत्यंचमिंद्रादीन्प्रत्यंचदनयन् । स्तोतारः प्रापयन् । यदैवं आदिदनंतरमेवेषिरां
> गमनशीलं स्वधां वृष्ट्युदकं पर्यपश्यन् । सर्वे जनाः परितः पश्यंति । यद्वा ।
> इषिरामेषणीयां स्वधां! अन्ननामैतत्। हविर्लक्षणमन्नं सर्वे देवाः परिपश्यंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Together with the *śacī*s, the acts of service, the singers brought the *arka*, the praise that is the instrument of worship, toward (*pratyañc*) Indra and the others. When this is so, immediately after, all people look around at the swift-moving *svadhā*, the rain-water. Or else: *iṣirā* means desirable; *svadhā* is a name for food, and all the gods look at the food in the form of the oblation.

### Printed p. 1061

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—accompanied by acts of service
- अर्कं (*arkaṃ*)—the praise
- प्रत्यंचं (*pratyaṃcaṃ*)—so as to reach Indra and the other gods
- अनयन् (*anayan*)—when the singers conveyed (made) it
- आश् इत् (*āś it*) **NOTE**—then, that is, afterwards (all the people)
- इषिरां (*iṣirāṃ*)—falling
- स्वधां (*svadhāṃ*)—the rain-water
- परि अपश्यन् (*pari apaśyan*)—looked around
- [Or इषिरां (*iṣirāṃ*)—desired; स्वधां (*svadhāṃ*)—the food in the form of the oblation; परि अपश्यन् (*pari apaśyan*)—the gods looked]

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

After the singers made their praise, accompanied by service, reach the gods Indra and the others, they (as the result of it) saw the streams of rain pouring down all around. Or else the gods looked at the food, oblations and the like, that the singers offer.

##### English translation
When (the worshippers) with their pious acts offered praise in honour (of the gods) then (men) beheld around them the swift descending rain.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

After people offered Indra and the other gods service of various kinds, rain fell as its fruit, and the people saw it. Or else the main idea is that the gods saw people offering them oblations and other food together with praise and the like.

## Sūkta 158 (Maṇḍala 10)
The hundred and fifty-eighth sūkta

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूर्य इति पंचर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तं सूर्यपुत्रस्य चक्षुःसंज्ञस्यार्षं
> सूर्यदेवत्यं गायत्रं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । सूर्यो नश्चक्षुः सौर्यः सौर्यं
> गायत्रमिति ॥ आश्विनशस्त्रे सूर्योदयादुत्तरकाले सौर्यकांड इदं सूक्तं ।
> सूत्रितं च । सूर्यो नो दिव उदु त्यं जातवेदसमिति नव । आ. ६-५ । इति ॥ दर्शपूर्णमासयोः स्सुगादापनात्तूर्वभाविनि जपे सूर्यो न इत्येषा । सूत्रितं च ।
> सूर्यो नो दिवस्पातु नमो महद्यो नमो अर्भकेभ्यः । आ. १-४ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta सूर्य (*sūrya*) is the seventh sūkta, of five ṛks. Its seer is Cakṣus, son of Sūrya; its deity is Sūrya; its metre is Gāyatrī. The Anukramaṇī is quoted: सूर्यो नश्चक्षुः सौर्यः सौर्यं गायत्रमिति (*sūryo naścakṣuḥ sauryaḥ sauryaṃ gāyatramiti*). Use: in the Āśvina śastra, after sunrise, in the Saurya section, this sūkta is used. It is given in the sūtra सूर्यो नो दिव उदु त्यं जातवेदसमिति नव (*sūryo no diva udu tyaṃ jātavedasamiti nava*) (Ā. 6-5). In the Darśapūrṇamāsa, in the *japa* **NOTE** the ṛk सूर्यो न (*sūryo na*) is used. It is given in the sūtra सूर्यो नो दिवस्पातु नमो महद्यो नमो अर्भकेभ्यः (*sūryo no divaspātu namo mahadyo namo arbhakebhyaḥ*) (Ā. 1-4).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*) is the seventh sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has five ṛks. Its seer is Cakṣus, son of Sūrya; Sūrya is

### Printed p. 1062

The deity is Sūrya, the son of the Sun; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: सूर्यो नश्चक्षुः सौर्यः सौर्यं गायत्रं (*sūryo naścakṣuḥ sauryaḥ sauryaṃ gāyatraṃ*). The Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra सूर्यो नो दिव उदु त्यं जातवेदसमिति नव (*sūryo no diva udu tyaṃ jātavedasamiti nava*) (Ā. 6-5), explains that this sūkta is used for the Saurya-kāṇḍa mantras, which are recited after sunrise when the mantras of the Āśvina-śastra are recited. Further, the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra सूर्यो नो दिवस्पातु नमो महद्यो नमो अभर्केभ्यः (*sūryo no divaspātu namo mahadyo namo abharkebhyaḥ*) (Ā. 1-4), explains that in the japa performed before the taking up of the sruc in the Darśa-pūrṇamāsa oblations, the first Ṛk of this sūkta, सूर्यो नः (*sūryo naḥ*), is to be recited.

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 158. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 16. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5.
Ṛṣi: Cakṣus Saurya. Deity: Sūrya. Metre: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सूर्यो॑ नो दि॒वस्पा॑तु॒ वातो॑ अं॒तरि॑क्षात् ।  
> अ॒ग्निर्नः॒ पार्थि॑वेभ्यः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सूर्यः । नः । दिवः । पातु । वातः । अंतरिक्षात् ।  
> अग्निः । नः । पार्थिवेभ्यः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूर्यः सर्वस्य प्रेरकः शोभनीयो वा देवो दिवो द्युलोकाद्दुलोकवर्तिनो जदान्नोऽस्मान्नातु । रक्षतु । वातो वायुश्चांतरिक्षान्मध्यमस्थानगताद्बाधकादस्मान्नक्षतु । तथा पृथिवीस्थानोऽग्निश्च पार्थिवेभ्यः पृथिव्यां वर्तमानेभ्यः
> शत्रुभ्यो नोऽस्मान्नक्षतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sūrya, the impeller of all, or the radiant god, is asked to protect us from (enemies) of the heaven-world, who dwell in heaven. Vāta, the wind, is asked to protect us from the harmful ones belonging to the middle region, the atmosphere. Likewise Agni, whose station is the earth, is asked to protect us from earthly foes, those who live on the earth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—Sūrya, who impels all
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the enemy folk who are in the heaven-world
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- पातु (*pātu*)—may he protect
- वातः (*vātaḥ*)—the wind
- अंतरिक्षात् (*aṃtarikṣāt*)—from the enemies who may be in the atmosphere, the middle region; (continued on the next page)

### Printed p. 1063

(…) may he protect us from them; and
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—the earthly Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- पार्थिवेभ्यः (*pārthivebhyaḥ*)—may he protect from the enemies who are on the earth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Sūrya, who impels all, protect us so that no harm comes to us from the dwellers of the heaven-world. Likewise may the wind protect us from the enemies in the atmosphere, the middle region, and the earthly Agni from the enemies on the earth.

##### English translation
May Surya protect us from (foes dwelling in) heaven, Vayu from (those dwelling in) the firmament, and Agni from those upon earth.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> जोषा॑ सवित॒र्यस्य॑ ते॒ हरः॑ श॒तं स॒वा अर्ह॑ति ।  
> पा॒हि नो॑ दि॒द्युतः॒ पतं॑त्याः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> जोष । सवितः ] यस्य । ते । हरः । शतं । सवान् । अर्हति ।  
> पाहि । नः । दिद्युतः । पतंत्याः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सवितः सर्वस्य प्रेरक सूर्य जोष । अस्मत्सुत्यादिकं सेवस्व । यस्य ते
> तव हरो रसहरणशीलं तेजः शतं सवान्बहून्यज्ञान्रत्यर्हति योग्यं भवति । यद्वा ।
> प्रकाशनादिद्वारा पूजयति । स त्वं नोऽस्मान्पतंत्या निपतंत्याः शत्रुभिरस्मासु क्षिप्यमाणाया दिद्युतः । वज्रनामैतत् । द्योतमानायाः शक्तेरायुधात्पाहि । रक्ष ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Savitṛ, impeller of all, Sūrya: accept (जोष (*joṣa*)) our soma-pressing and the like. Your radiance, which has the nature of drawing up the sap (हरः (*haraḥ*)), is worthy of a hundred sacrifices, that is, many; or else, it honours (them) by illuminating and so on. Such as you are, protect us from the दिद्युतः (*didyutaḥ*) that falls on us, hurled by enemies; this is a name of the thunderbolt; protect us from the shining weapon of power.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सवितः (*savitaḥ*)—O Sūrya, impeller of all
- जोष (*joṣa*)—accept our praises
- यस्य ते (*yasya te*)—you, whose
- हरः (*haraḥ*)—radiance, which draws up the sap
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—many
- सवान् अर्हति (*savān arhati*)—is worthy of praise in the sacrifices; such as you are
- पतंत्याः (*pataṃtyāḥ*)—which is hurled at us by enemies
- दिद्युतः (*didyutaḥ*)—from shining weapons
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—protect

### Printed p. 1064

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Sūrya, impeller of all, accept our praises, that is, receive them. Your abundant and sharp radiance, which has the nature of drawing up the sap (liquid), is praised in the sacrifices; such as you are, protect us from the shining weapons that enemies hurl (cause to fall) upon us.

##### English translation
Savitri, whose radiance merits a hundred acknowledgments, be propitiated (by our praises); protect us from the falling bolts (of uur enemies.)

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> चक्षु॑र्नो दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता चक्षु॑र्न उ॒त पर्व॑तः ।  
> चक्षु॑र्धा॒ता द॑धातु नः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> चक्षुः । नः । देवः ॥ सविता । चक्षुः । नः । उत । पर्वतः ।  
> चक्षुः । धाता । दधातु । नः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सविता प्रेरको देवो नोऽस्माकं चक्षुः प्रकाशकमिंद्रियमिंद्रियानुग्राहकं तेजो ना दधातु । उतापि च पर्वत इंद्रसहचरः पर्वताख्योऽपि देवो
> नोऽस्माकं चक्षुर्दधातु । धाता सर्वस्य विधातादित्यानामन्यतमश्च नोऽस्माकं
> चक्षुर्विदधातु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May the impelling god Savitṛ grant us चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*), the illuminating faculty, the radiance that favours the sense-organ. And also (उत (*uta*)) may the god named Parvata, the companion of Indra, grant us sight. And may Dhātṛ, the disposer of all, one of the Ādityas, grant us sight.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सविता देवः (*savitā devaḥ*)—this god Sūrya, impeller of all
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—the eye, sight, or the power to see
- दधातु (*dadhātu*)—may he give
- उत (*uta*)—and
- पर्वतः (*parvataḥ*)—the god named Parvata, the companion (friend) of Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—may he favour us with sight
- धाता (*dhātā*)—the creator
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—sight
- दधातु (*dadhātu*)—may he give

### Printed p. 1065

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May this god Sūrya, impeller of all, the god called Parvata, companion of Indra, and Dhātṛ, the creator, grant us the eye, that is, the capacity to see.

##### English translation
May the divine Savitri grant us sight, may Parvata (grant) us sight; may Dhatri (grant) us sight.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> चक्पु॑र्नो धेहि॒ चक्पु॑षे॒ चक्पु॑र्वि॒ख्यै त॒नूभ्यः॑ ।  
> सं चे॒दं वि च॑ पश्येम ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> चक्षुः । नः । धेहि । चक्षुषे । चक्षुः । विख्या । तनूभ्यः ।  
> सं । च । इदं । वि । च । पश्येम ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नोऽस्माकं चक्षुषे रूपोपलब्धिकारणायेंद्रियाय चक्षुः प्रकाशकं
> तदानुग्राहकं तेजो हे सूर्य धेहि । विधेहि । कुरु । यद्वा ॥ न इति व्यत्ययेन
> बहुवचनं ॥ चक्षुषे चक्षुःसंज्ञाय नो मह्यं चक्षुरिंद्रियं ना तेजो वा हे
> सूर्य धेहि । प्रयच्छ । तनूभ्योऽस्माकं शरीरेभ्यस्तनयेभ्यो वा विख्यॆ विख्यानाय प्रकाशनाय चक्षुस्त्वदीयं प्रकाशं विधेहि । यत एवं तस्मात्कारणात्त्वदीयेन तेजसा वयं चेदं सर्वं जगत्सं पश्येम । सम्यग्द्रष्टारो भवेम । वि
> पश्येम च । विविधं च सविशेषं द्रष्टारो भवेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Sūrya, grant (धेहि (*dhehi*), make) for our eye, the organ that is the cause of perceiving form, चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*), the illuminating radiance that favours it. Or else: नः (*naḥ*) is a plural put for the singular by exchange (व्यत्यय (*vyatyaya*)); to me, named Cakṣus, give the eye-organ or radiance, O Sūrya. For our bodies, or our offspring, for विख्यै (*vikhyai*), for illumination, spread your own light. Since it is so, by your radiance may we see this whole world well, becoming right seers; and may we see (वि पश्येम (*vi paśyema*)) in various ways, with particulars, becoming seers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Sūrya) नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- चक्षुषे (*cakṣuṣe*)—for the eye, which is the means of seeing the forms of things
- चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—light or sight
- धेहि (*dhehi*)—produce. [Or: चक्षुषे (*cakṣuṣe*)—named Cakṣus; नः (*naḥ*)—to me; चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—sight or radiance; धेहि (*dhehi*)—give]
- तनूभ्यः (*tanūbhyaḥ*)—for the protection of our bodies
- विख्यॆ (*vikhyè*)—and for illumination
- चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—your

### Printed p. 1066

light spread all around; by it we
- इदं च (*idaṃ ca*)—this whole world
- सं पश्येम (*saṃ paśyema*)—may we see well
- वि पश्येम (*vi paśyema*)—may we see things of various kinds

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Sūrya, give us the eye-organ, the means of seeing the forms of things, and produce your light so that it helps us to see them. Or else: to me, who am named Cakṣus, the seer of this sūkta, give your radiance and sight. For the protection of our bodies and for seeing, spread your radiance all around. By it may we see well the various things in this whole world.

##### English translation
Give sight, Surya, to our eyes, (bestow) sight for the illumination of our bodies, so that we may look upon and into this (world).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒सं॒दृशं॑ त्वा व॒यं प्रति॑ पश्येम सूर्य ।  
> वि प॑श्येम नृ॒चक्ष॑सः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुसंदृशं । त्वा । वयं । प्रति । पश्येम । सूर्य ।  
> वि । पश्येम । नृचक्षसः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सूर्य सुसंदृशं सुष्टु संदृष्टारं त्वा त्वां वयं प्रति पश्येम । प्रत्येकं
> द्रष्टारो भूयास्म । तथा नृचक्षसो नृभिर्मनुष्यैरस्माभिर्दृष्टव्यान्पदार्थान्वि
> पश्येम । विद्रष्टारो भवेम । यद्वा । नृचक्षसो नृणां शत्रुमनुष्याणां हिंसकाः
> संतो वयं विशिष्टज्ञाना भवेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Sūrya, you who see all well (सुसंदृशं (*susaṃdṛśaṃ*)), may we look at you, each one of us becoming a beholder. Likewise नृचक्षसः (*nṛcakṣasaḥ*): may we look into (वि पश्येम (*vi paśyema*)), becoming discerning seers of, the things to be seen by men, by us humans. Or else: नृचक्षसः (*nṛcakṣasaḥ*), being destroyers of hostile men, may we become possessed of distinguished knowledge.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूर्य (*sūrya*)—O Sūrya
- सुसंदृशं (*susaṃdṛśaṃ*)—you who can see everything well
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- प्रति पश्येम (*prati paśyema*)—may we see individually; and
- नृचक्षसः (*nṛcakṣasaḥ*)—by men

### Printed p. 1067

all the things that can be seen
- वि पश्येम (*vi paśyema*)—may we see in particular. [Or: नृचक्षसः (*nṛcakṣasaḥ*)—we, causing harm to enemy folk; विपश्येम (*vipaśyema*)—let us become possessed of distinguished knowledge.]

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Sūrya, may we see individually you who see all. May we see all the things that can be seen by men; or else, may we, harming enemy folk, be endowed with special knowledge.

##### English translation
May we look upon you, Surya, the bright beholder (of all), may we look into the things which are visible to mankind.

## Sūkta 159 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उदसाविति षडृचमष्टमं सूक्तमानुष्टुभं । पुलोमतनया शची स्वात्मानमनेनास्त् । अतः सैवर्षिः सैव देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । उदसौ षट्
> पौलोमी शच्यात्मानं तुष्टावानुष्टुभमिति ॥ विनियोगो लिंगादवगंतव्यः ॥ आपस्तंबस्तु सपत्नीनाशने सूर्योपस्थान इदं सूक्तं विनियुक्तवान् । सूत्र्यते हि ।
> एतेनैव कामेनोत्तरेणानुवाकेन सदादित्यमुपतिष्ठते । आप. गृ ९-९ । इति ।
> अत्रैतेनेति प्रकृतं सपत्निबाधनं परामृश्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

उदसौ (*udasau*) is the eighth sūkta, of six Ṛks, in the Anuṣṭubh metre. Śacī, the daughter of Pulomā, praised herself with it; hence she is both ṛṣi and deity. So the Anukramaṇikā says: उदसौ षट् पौलोमी शच्यात्मानं तुष्टावानुष्टुभमिति (*udasau ṣaṭ paulomī śacyātmānaṃ tuṣṭāvānuṣṭubhamiti*). The use is to be understood from the indication (लिंग (*liṃga*)) of the text. But Āpastamba applied this sūkta in the worship of Sūrya for the destruction of a co-wife; for it is stated in a sūtra: एतेनैव कामेनोत्तरेणानुवाकेन सदादित्यमुपतिष्ठते (*etenaiva kāmenottareṇānuvākena sadādityamupatiṣṭhate*) (Āpa. Gṛ. 9-9). Here एतेन (*etena*) refers back to the harming of a co-wife, which is the matter under discussion.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta उदसौ (*udasau*) is the eighth sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. In this sūkta the woman Śacī, daughter of Pulomā, has praised herself. Therefore Śacī Paulomī is both ṛṣi and deity of this sūkta. The metre is Anuṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: उदसौ षट् पौलोमी शच्यात्मानं तुष्टावानुष्टुभं (*udasau ṣaṭ paulomī śacyātmānaṃ tuṣṭāvānuṣṭubhaṃ*). The use is to be understood from the matters stated in the sūkta. The great ṛṣi Āpastamba, in the Āpastamba Gṛhya Sūtra, (explains that) this sūkta is used for the upasthāna mantras in the rite performed for removing the affliction caused by a sapatnī (co-wife), in the sūtra एतेन्वॆव कामे (*etenvèva kāme*)

### Printed p. 1068
by the sūtra नोत्तरेणानुवाकेन सदादित्यमुपतिष्ठते (*nottareṇānuvākena sadādityamupatiṣṭhate*) (Āpa. Gṛ. 9-9). From this it may be understood that the removal of co-wives is set forth in this sūkta.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उद॒सौ सूर्यो॑ अगा॒दुद॒यं मा॑म॒को भगः॑ ।  
> अ॒हं तद्वि॑द्व॒ला पति॑म॒भ्य॑साक्षि विषास॒हिः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । आसौ । सूर्यः । अगात् । उत् । आयं । मामकः । भगः ।  
> अहं । तत् । विद्वला । पतिं । अभि । असाक्षि । विससहिः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> असौ द्युलोकस्थः सूर्य उदगात् । उदयं प्राप्तवान् । मामको
> मदीयो भगो भजनीयोऽयमिंद्रश्च सूर्यात्मनोदगात् । यद्वा । मामको
> भगो मदीयमिदं सौभाग्यमुदगात् । तदुद्यतं सूर्यस्य तेजो विद्वला ज्ञातवती यद्वा पतिं भर्तारं विद्वला लब्धवत्यहं विषासहिर्विशेषेणाभिभवित्रि सत्यभ्यसाक्षि । अभ्यभूवं । सपत्नीरिति शेषः ॥ सहतेरभिभवार्थस्य लुज्येतद्रूपं ॥ यद्वा ।
> विषासहिः सपत्नीनामभिभवित्रि सती पतिमभ्यसाक्षि । भर्तारमप्यभूवं । यथा
> मय्येव वशीकृतश्चिरं वर्तते तथाकार्षमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This sun in the heavens has risen. "Mine" (मामको (*māmako*)) means "my own"; the "bhaga", the adorable Indra, has risen in the form of the sun. Or else: this good fortune of mine has risen. Having known the risen splendour of the sun, or having obtained my husband, I, the specially overpowering one (विषासहिः (*viṣāsahiḥ*)), have overcome (*abhyasākṣi*) — "the co-wives" is to be supplied. The form is a luṅ of the root meaning "to overcome". Or else: being the overcomer of the co-wives, I have also overcome my husband, that is, I have so acted that he remains long subject to me alone.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- असौ (*asau*)—this one shining in the sky
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—the sun
- उत् अगात् (*ut agāt*)—has risen

### Printed p. 1069
- मामकः (*māmakaḥ*)—related to me
- भगः (*bhagaḥ*)—venerable to me
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this Indra of the sun's nature has risen. [Or मामको भगः (*māmako bhagaḥ*)—my good fortune; उत् अगात् (*ut agāt*)—has risen, that is, has been obtained]
- तत् (*tat*)—the splendour of the risen sun, or my husband
- विद्वला (*vidvalā*)—having obtained
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- विषासहिः (*viṣāsahiḥ*)—specially defeating
- अभि असाक्षि (*abhi asākṣi*)—I have vanquished my co-wives

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Now the sun has risen in the sky. My good fortune too has risen. Having obtained my husband, I have vanquished my co-wives.
Or: Indra, my husband, has himself risen in this form of the sun. I have known his splendour. Having obtained my husband, I have defeated my co-wives.

##### English translation
The sun has risen; my good fortune has dawned; I, knowing this, have obtained my husband triumphing (over my rivals).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒हं के॒तुर॒हं मू॒र्धाहमु॒ग्रा वि॒वाच॑नी ।  
> ममेदनु॒ क्रतुं॒ पतिः॑ सेहा॒नाया॑ उ॒पाच॑रेत् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अहं । केतुः । अहं । मूर्धा । अहं । उग्रा । विवाचनी ।  
> मम । इत् । अनु । क्रतुं । पतिः । सेहानायाः । उपआचरेत् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अहं केतुः केतयित्री सर्वस्य ज्ञात्रि भवामि । अहं मूर्धा सर्वेष्टवयवेषु शिर इव प्रधानभूता च भवामि । अहमुग्रोद्धूर्णा सती विवाचनी विशेषेण
> पतिं वाचयित्री भवामि । क्रोधाविष्टमपि पतिं मयि सर्वदा प्रियवचनयुक्तं
> करोमीत्यर्थः । सेहानायाः सपत्नीनामभिभवित्र्या ममेन्ममैव क्रतुं कर्म बुद्धिं
> वानुलक्ष्य पतिः पालयिता भर्तोपाचरेत् । उपागच्छेत् । नान्यासां पत्निीनां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I am the "ketu", the one who makes known, the knower of all. I am the head, chief like the head among all the limbs. I am "उग्रा (*ugrā*)" (fierce, exalted), and a "विवाचनी (*vivācanī*)", one who specially makes her husband speak: even a husband filled with anger I make full of affectionate speech to me. The husband, the protector, following the will or intelligence (क्रतुं (*kratuṃ*)) of me, the overcomer (सेहानायाः (*sehānāyāḥ*)) of the co-wives, should come to me — not to the other wives.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- केतुः (*ketuḥ*)—I am one who knows everything
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- मूर्धा (*mūrdhā*)—I am chief like the head
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- उग्रा (*ugrā*)—am bold
- विवाचनी (*vivācanī*)—and one who soothes my husband
- सेहानायाः (*sehānāyāḥ*)—of me who overcomes the co-wives
- मम इत् (*mama it*)—my

- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—my husband

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I know everything. I am chief like the head. By my boldness I have soothed my husband and made him speak affectionate words concerning me. Following the mind of me who have defeated my co-wives, that is, devoted to me alone and not going to the co-wives, let him come to me alone.

##### English translation
I am the banner, I am the head, I am exalted, soothing (my lord); my husband must conform to my will, as I am victorious over my rivals.

> उत । अहं । अस्मि । संजया । पत्यौ । मे । श्लोकः । उत्तमः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ममैव पुत्रास्तनयाः शत्रुहणः शत्रूणां सपत्नानां हंतारो भवंति । अथो

> मे मम श्लोक उपश्लोकनीयं यश उत्तम उद्गततममतिशयेनोत्कृष्टं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

My sons are slayers of enemies, that is, of the co-wives' side. Moreover my daughter is a "विराट् (*virāṭ*)", shining specially. And I am a "संजया (*saṃjayā*)", a complete conqueror of the co-wives; I overcome them. For this reason, in my husband Indra, my "श्लोक (*śloka*)", my praiseworthy renown, is highest, exceedingly excellent.

> द्युम्नं द्योतमानं यशोऽन्नं वा । तद्वानुत्तम उत्कृष्टतमश्च येन हविषा
> भवति । हे देवाः स्तोतार ऋत्विजः तदिदं हविरक्रि । अकारि । जयाथिर्भर्भिवद्धिः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By which oblation Indra, my husband, becomes "कृत्वी (*kṛtvī*)", a doer of deeds; and "dyumna" means shining fame, or food; by which oblation he becomes possessed of it and "uttama", most excellent: that oblation has been made (अक्रि (*akri*) stands for अकारि (*akāri*)). O gods — the praisers, the priests — let it be made by you. Or else: O gods who are to be worshipped, I too have made this oblation. For this very reason I have become "असपत्ना (*asapatnā*)", truly free from enemies (अभुवं (*abhuvaṃ*) for अभूवं (*abhūvaṃ*)).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒स॒प॒त्ना स॑सत्न॒घ्नी जयं॑त्यभि॒भूव॑री ।  
> आवृ॑क्षम॒न्यासां॒ वर्चो॒ राधो॒ अस्थे॑यसामिव ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> असॆपत्ना । सपत्नघ्नी । जयंती । अभिभूवरी ।  
> आ । अवृक्षं । अन्यासां । वर्चः । राधः । अस्थेयसांइव ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> असपत्नाशत्रुका भवामि । कुत इत्यत आह । सपत्नघ्नी शत्रूणां हंत्री अत
> एव जयंती जयं प्राप्नुवत्यभिभूवर्यभिभवित्रि ॥ भवतेरन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यंत इति
> क्वनिप् । वनो र चेति जीब्रेफौ ॥ ईदृश्यहमन्यासां सपत्नीनां वर्चस्तेजो राधो
> धनं चावृक्षं । आ समंतादवृक्षं । अवृश्चिषं । अच्छिदं ॥ व्रश्चेर्लुज्युदित्त्वादिदभावे

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I become without rival. Why? She says: I am "सपत्नघ्नी (*sapatnaghnī*)", slayer of enemies, and therefore *jayantī*, winning victory, "अभिभूवरी (*abhibhūvarī*)", overpowering. Being such, I have cut off (अवृक्षं (*avṛkṣaṃ*), completely cut off) the splendour and wealth of the other co-wives.

### Printed p. 1073

> संयोगादिलोपे छांदसं संप्रसारणं ॥ तत्र दृष्टांतः । अस्थेयसामिवास्थिरतराणां शत्रूणां यथा धनमप्रयत्नेन वृश्चते तथेत्यर्थः ॥ स्थिरशब्दादीयसुनि
> प्रियस्थिरेत्यादिना स्थादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The illustration: as the wealth of enemies who are less steady (अस्थेयसामिव (*astheyasāmiva*)) is cut off without effort, so is it here.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (I) सपत्नघ्नी (*sapatnaghnī*)—have destroyed my co-wives, the enemies
- जयंती (*jayaṃtī*)—am victorious
- अभिभूवरी (*abhibhūvarī*)—have defeated those co-wives. And therefore
- असपत्ना (*asapatnā*)—I take pride that I am without enemies, or without the torment of co-wives. Being such, I
- अन्यासां (*anyāsāṃ*)—of my other co-wives
- वर्चः (*varcaḥ*)—the splendour
- राधः (*rādhaḥ*)—and the wealth
- अस्थेयसामिव (*astheyasāmiva*)—as the wealth of enemies who cannot stand firm is carried off
- अवृक्षं (*avṛkṣaṃ*)—have cut off (destroyed)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Having destroyed my co-wives, the enemies, I am victorious. I have defeated them in many ways. Therefore I am free from the torment of my co-wives who were enemies. Being such, I have cut off, that is, destroyed, the splendour and wealth of my other co-wives, as the wealth of enemies who cannot stand firm in battle is destroyed.

##### English translation
Free from rivals, the destructress of rivals, victorious, triumphant, I cut up the brilliance and wealth of the other (wives of Indra) as if it were the wealth of (enemies) who do not endure long.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सम॑जैषमि॒मा अ॒हं स॒पत्नी॑रभि॒भूव॑री ।  
> यथा॒हम॒स्य वी॒रस्य॑ वि॒राजा॑नि॒ जन॑स्य च ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सं । अजैषं । इमाः । अहं । सपत्नीः । अभिभूवरी ।  
> यथा । अहं । अस्य । वीरस्य । विराजानि । जनस्य । च ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 1074

> अभिभूवर्यभिभवित्र्यहमिमाः सपत्निः समजैषं । सम्यगभ्यभूवं । यथा
> येन प्रकारेणाहमस्य वीरस्येंद्रस्य तदीयपरिजनस्य च विराजानि विशेषेण
> राजमाना भवानि । तथा समजैषमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The abhibhūvarī is "she who overcomes" (*abhibhavitrī*). "I have completely conquered these co-wives, thoroughly overpowering them. In the way that I may shine in distinction (विराजानि (*virājāni*)) over this hero Indra and his retinue, so I have conquered": this is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- वीरस्य (*vīrasya*)—of the hero Indra
- च (*ca*)—and
- जनस्य (*janasya*)—of his retinue
- विराजानि (*virājāni*)—in such a way that I shine, becoming worthy of their trust and regard
- अभिभूवरी (*abhibhūvarī*)—having the nature of defeating
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- इमाः सपत्नीः (*imāḥ sapatnīḥ*)—these my co-wives
- सं अजैषं (*saṃ ajaiṣaṃ*)—have thoroughly defeated

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, who am skilled in the work of defeating co-wives, have thoroughly defeated these my co-wives. Thereby, free from obstruction, I shine, having become worthy of the love and regard of my husband, the hero Indra, and of his retinue.

##### English translation
Triumphant, I conquered these my rivals, so that I might rule this hero and his people.

## Sūkta 160 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तीव्रस्येति पंचर्चं नवमं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रस्य पूरणस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । तीव्रस्य पंच पूरणो वैश्वामित्र इति ॥ तीव्रसोमाख्य
> एकाह इदं निष्केवल्यनिविद्वानं । सूत्रितं च । क्वस्य वीरस्तीव्रस्याभिवयस इति मध्यंदिनः । आ. ९-७ । इति ॥ महाव्रतेऽपि माध्यंदिने सवने ब्रह्मशस्त्रेऽप्येतत्तूक्तं । तथैव
> पंचमारण्यके सूत्रितं । तीव्रस्याभिवयसो अस्य पाहीति माध्यंदिने । ऐ. आ. ४-१-१।
> इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning तीव्रस्य (*tīvrasya*) has five Ṛks and is the ninth sūkta. Its seer is Pūraṇa, of the Viśvāmitra line; its deity is Indra; its metre is Triṣṭubh. So the Anukramaṇī says: तीव्रस्य पंच पूरणो वैश्वामित्र इति (*tīvrasya paṃca pūraṇo vaiśvāmitra iti*). It is used in the one-day rite called Tīvrasoma, as the nivid-dhāna (the hymn to be inserted) of the niṣkevalya recitation. This is stated in the sūtra क्वस्य वीरस्तीव्रस्याभिवयस इति मध्यंदिनः (*kvasya vīrastīvrasyābhivayasa iti madhyaṃdinaḥ*) (Ā. 9-7). In the Mahāvrata too, in the midday pressing, this hymn is used in the Brahma-śastra. So the fifth Āraṇyaka states: तीव्रस्याभिवयसो अस्य पाहीति माध्यंदिने (*tīvrasyābhivayaso asya pāhīti mādhyaṃdine*) (Ai. Ā. 4-1-1). **NOTE**

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning "तीव्रस्य (*tīvrasya*)" is the ninth sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Pūraṇa of the Viśvāmitra gotra; the deity is Indra; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: "Tīvrasya, five (Ṛks), Pūrṇa Vaiśvāmitra". **NOTE**

### Printed p. 1075

(The sentence continues:) It is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra sūtra "Kva sya vīras tīvrasyābhivayasa iti mādhyandinaḥ" (Ā. 9-7) that this sūkta is used, in the one-day rite called Tīvrasoma, for the nivid-dhāna sūkta which is to be recited inserted among the mantras of the niṣkevalya śastra. It is pointed out by the sentence "Tīvrasyābhivayaso asya pāhīti mādhyandine" (Ai. Ā. 5-1-1) in the fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka that this sūkta is used for the śastra mantras recited by the priest called Brahman at the midday pressing of the Mahāvrata rite.

##### Particulars of the Sūkta

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 160. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 8. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Pūraṇa Vaiśvāmitra. Deity: Indra. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ती॒व्रस्या॒भिव॑यसो अ॒स्य पा॑हि सर्वर॒था वि हरी॑ इ॒ह मुं॑च ।  
> इंद्र॒ मा त्वा॒ यज॑मानासो अ॒न्ये नि री॑रम॒नुभ्य॑मि॒मे  ॒॑
> सुतासः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तीव्रस्य । अभिवयसः । अस्य । पाहि । सर्व९रथा । वि । हरी इति । इह । मुंच ।  
> इंद्र । मा । त्वा । यजमानासः । अन्ये । नि । रीरमन् । तुभ्यं । इमे । सुतासः ॥१॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तीव्रस्य तीक्ष्णस्य क्षिप्रंमदकरस्याभिवयसः । वय इत्यन्ननाम । अभिगतं
> चरुपुरोडाशाद्यन्नं यस्यॆ तादृशस्यास्य सोमस्य॥ क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः
> संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थ्यर्थे षष्ठी ॥ ईदृशं सोमं हे इंद्र पाहि । पिब ॥ पिबतेश्लांदसः शपो लुक् ॥ तदर्थं सर्वरथा सरणशीलरथौ हरी अश्वाविहास्मिन्यज्ञगृहे वि
> मुंच । रथाद्विस्पृज । हे इंद्र अस्मत्तोऽन्ये यजमानासो यजमानास्त्वा त्वां

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"तीव्र (*tīvra*)" means sharp, that is, quickly intoxicating. "Abhivayas": "vayas" is a name for food; the Soma is such that cooked food such as caru and puroḍāśa has come to it. Of this Soma (the genitive stands for the dative, because the act of taking is to be made, and the thing offered is the recipient): "O Indra, drink such Soma." The verb "पाहि (*pāhi*)" means "drink". For that purpose, "unyoke here, in this sacrificial house, your two bay horses, yoked to the swift-going chariot; release them from the chariot." "O Indra, let other sacrificers than us (अस्मत्तोऽन्ये यजमानासो (*asmatto 'nye yajamānāso*)) not detain you (त्वां मा नि रीरमन् (*tvāṃ mā ni rīraman*))…"

### Printed p. 1076

> मा नि रीरमन् । नितरां मा रमयंतु । वयमेव रमयाम इत्यर्थः । ततस्तुभ्यं
> त्वदर्थमेव सुतासः सुता अभिषुता इमे प्रत्यक्षेणोपलभ्यमानाः सोमा वर्तंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(continuing) "…let them not at all make you rest, delight you; we ourselves shall delight you": this is the meaning. "Therefore, for you alone, these pressed Soma juices, which are perceived directly, are present."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) तीव्रस्य (*tīvrasya*)—of the sharp, that is, quickly intoxicating
- अभिवयसः (*abhivayasaḥ*)—accompanied by caru, puroḍāśa and other food
- अस्य (*asya*)—this Soma juice
- पाहिं (*pāhiṃ*)—drink (for that)
- सर्वरथा (*sarvarathā*)—yoked to your swiftly travelling chariot
- हरी (*harī*)—the horses
- इह (*iha*)—near this sacrificial house
- वि मुंचॆ (*vi muṃcè*)—unyoke from the chariot
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अन्ये (*anye*)—other (than us)
- यजमानासः (*yajamānāsaḥ*)—sacrificers who perform sacrifice
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- मा नि रीरमन् (*mā ni rīraman*)—let them not delight
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you alone
- इमे (*ime*)—these Soma juices
- सुतासः (*sutāsaḥ*)—have been pressed and made ready

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, drink this Soma juice, which is sharp, that is, quickly intoxicating, and accompanied by caru and puroḍāśa food. For that, unyoke the horses of your swift-going chariot right here near this sacrificial house. O Indra, may other sacrificers not stop you on the way and give you delight; that is, do not stop anywhere but come quickly to us. For you alone these Soma juices are ready.

##### English translation
Drink, Indra, of this sharp (Soma-juice, wich is) combined with sacrificial food, unyoke here your bay steeds yoked to your swift chariot; let no other worshippers detain you, Indra ; these libations are for you.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When Soma juice is drunk, to make it tasty, the āśira substances milk, curd and flour are mixed into it. Soma juice mixed with milk is called gavāśira, Soma juice mixed with curd is called dadhyāśira, and Soma juice mixed with flour is called yavāśira. Soma juice that remains as it is, with nothing mixed in, is very powerful and quickly intoxicates, so it is called by names such as tīvra and tīkṣṇa.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तुभ्यं॑ सु॒तास्तुभ्य॑मु॒ सोत्वा॑स॒स्त्वां गिरः॒ श्वात्रा॒ आ ह्व॑यंति ।

### Printed p. 1077

> इंद्रेदमद्य सवनं जुषाणो विश्वस्य विद्वा इह पाहि सोमं॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तुभ्यं । सुताः । तुभ्यं । ऊं इति । सोत्वासः । त्वां । गिरः । श्वात्राः । आ । ह्वयंति ।  
> इंद्र । इदं । अद्य । सवनं । जुषाणः । विश्वस्य । विद्वान् । इह । पाहि । सोमं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र तुभ्यं त्वदर्थमेव सुता अभिषुताः सर्वे सोमाः सोत्वास इतः
> परमभिषोतव्याश्च तुभ्यमु त्वदर्थमेव ॥ सुनोतेः कृत्यार्थे तवैकेनिति त्वन्प्रत्ययः॥
> श्वात्राः श्व आशु शीघ्रमतंत्यः प्रवर्तमाना गिरः स्तुतिरूपा वाचश्च त्वामेवा
> ह्वयंति। आक्रोशयंति। हे इंद्र अद्यास्मिन्काल इदं सवनं प्रातःसवनादिकं जुषाणः
> सेवमानो विश्वस्य सर्वस्य विद्वाञ्ञाता त्वमिहास्मिन्यज्ञे सोमं पाहि । पिब ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, for you alone all the Somas have been pressed (सुता (*sutā*)), and those that are to be pressed hereafter (सोत्वासः (*sotvāsaḥ*)) are likewise for you alone." The affix tvan is used with the root सुनोति (*sunoti*) in the sense of what is to be done. "The praises (गिरः (*giraḥ*)), the words in the form of hymns, which proceed quickly and swiftly (श्वात्राः (*śvātrāḥ*)), call you alone, summon you. O Indra, today, at this time, taking pleasure in this savana, the morning pressing and the rest, you, who know everything, drink the Soma here, in this sacrifice."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you
- सुताः (*sutāḥ*)—the Soma juices that have now been pressed are here
- सोत्वासः (*sotvāsaḥ*)—and the Soma juices that are still to be pressed
- तुभ्यं उ (*tubhyaṃ u*)—for you alone
- श्वात्राः (*śvātrāḥ*)—recited very quickly
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—these words in the form of praise
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you alone
- आ ह्वयंति (*ā hvayaṃti*)—call
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अद्य (*adya*)—now
- इदं सवनं (*idaṃ savanaṃ*)—this rite of the morning pressing and the rest
- जुषाणि (*juṣāṇi*)—enjoying
- विश्वस्य विद्वान् (*viśvasya vidvān*)—you who know everything
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, for you alone these Soma juices have been pressed and made ready. The Soma juices that will be pressed hereafter, and these words in the form of praise, recited quickly for you alone, call you alone. O Indra, enjoying this morning-pressing rite, you who know everything, drink the Soma in this sacrifice.

##### English translation
For you are the libations that have been poured out, for you are those which are to be poured out; you do our quickly uttered praises invoke;

### Printed p. 1078

Indra, you are cognizant of all things, taking pleasure in this present sacrifice, drink the Soma here.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य उ॑श॒ता मन॑सा॒ सोम॑मस्मै सर्वहृ॒दा दे॒वका॑मः  ॒॑
> सु॒नोति॑ ।  
> न गा इंद्र॒स्तस्य॒ परा॑ ददाति प्रश॒स्तमिच्चारु॑मस्मै कृणोति ॥३॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । उशता । मनसा । सोमं । अस्मै । सर्वहृदा । देवकामः । सुनोति ।  
> न । गाः । इंद्रः । तस्य । परा । ददाति । प्रशस्तं । इत् । चारुं । अस्मै । कृणोति॥३॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> य उशता कामयमानेन सर्वहृदा । सर्वमविकलं हृदयं यस्य । यद्वा।
> सर्वेषामृत्विजां हृदयेन । सामर्थ्यान्मत्वर्थो लक्ष्यते । हृदयवता मनसास्मा
> इंद्राय देवकानो देवमिंद्रं कामयमानो यजमान सोमं सुनोति अभिषुणोति । इंद्रस्तस्य यजमानस्य गा न परा ददाति । परादानं विनाशः । नि विनाशयति । अस्मै यजमानाय चारुं शोभनं अत एव प्रसक्तं । इदित्यवधारणे । प्रशंसनीयमेव धनं कृणोति । करोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

*Ushatā* means "desiring". "सर्वहृदा (*sarvahṛdā*)": he whose heart is whole and undivided; or else, "with the heart of all the priests". By implication the possessive sense is understood: with a mind that has a heart. "देवकामः (*devakāmaḥ*)": the sacrificer who desires the god Indra presses (सुनोति (*sunoti*)) Soma for this Indra. Indra does not "give away" (परा ददाति (*parā dadāti*)) the cattle of that sacrificer; *parādāna* means destruction, so he does not destroy them. For this sacrificer he makes (कृणोति (*kṛṇoti*)) beautiful, and therefore excellent, wealth; इत् (*it*) is in the sense of emphasis: he makes only praiseworthy wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवकामः (*devakāmaḥ*)—desiring to worship Indra
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the sacrificer who
- उशता (*uśatā*)—having the wish to offer Soma
- सर्वहृदा (*sarvahṛdā*)—wholehearted
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with the mind
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—for this Indra
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma juice
- सुनोति (*sunoti*)—presses
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of that sacrificer
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cattle
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- न परा ददाति (*na parā dadāti*)—does not destroy; moreover
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—to that sacrificer
- चारुं (*cāruṃ*)—beautiful and
- प्रशस्तं इत् (*praśastaṃ it*)—only excellent wealth
- कृणोति (*kṛṇoti*)—provides

### Printed p. 1079

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra does not destroy the cattle of the sacrificer who, desiring to worship Indra, presses Soma juice for Indra with his wholehearted longing and with his mind; and he provides that sacrificer with excellent and beautiful wealth alone.

##### English translation
He who devoted to the deity with a willing mind offers the Soma to him with all his heart, Indra does not destroy his cattle, but gives him beautiful excellent (wealth).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अनु॑स्पष्टो भवत्ये॒षो अ॑स्य॒ यो अ॑स्मै रे॒वान्न सु॒नोति॒  ॑
> सोमं ।  
> निर॑र॒त्ना म॒घवा॒ तं द॑धाति ब्रह्म॒द्विषो॑ हं॒त्यना॑नुदिष्टः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> निः । अरत्ना । मघवा । तं । दधाति । ब्रह्मद्विषः । हंति । अननुदिष्टः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्य यजमानस्यैष इंद्रोऽनुस्पष्टो दृष्टिगोचरो भवति यो रेवान्धनवानस्मा इंद्राय सोमं सुनोति अभिषुणोति । मघवा धनोपेत इंद्रस्तं यजमानमरत्ना हस्ते निर्दधाति भयान्निकृष्ण धारयति रक्षिता सन् धृत्वा चाननुदिष्टस्तेनानुक्तोऽप्रार्थित एव सन्ब्रह्मद्विषो ब्राह्मणद्वेष्ट्वञ्त्यत्रून्हंति । हिनस्ति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Indra becomes *anuspaṣṭa*, visible to the eye, to that sacrificer who, being wealthy (रेवान् (*revān*)), presses Soma for this Indra. Maghavan, Indra the possessor of wealth, holds that sacrificer in his hand (अरत्ना (*aratnā*), निर्दधाति (*nirdadhāti*)), as his protector; and, unasked, unprayed to (अननुदिष्टः (*ananudiṣṭaḥ*)), he slays (हंति (*haṃti*)) the enemies, the haters of Brahmins (ब्रह्मद्विषः (*brahmadviṣaḥ*)). **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra becomes visible to that wealthy yajamāna who presses and offers Soma-juice to him; that is, he shows him favour. That wealthy Indra removes the fear of such a yajamāna and, with trust, holds him in his hand; that is, he protects and nourishes him with attachment, and destroys his enemies who hate Brahmins.

He is mindful of him who, as a rich man, offers Soma to him; possessed of riches (Indra) holds him in his hand, and unsolicited destroys (his enemies) who hate the Brahmin.

> याज्या । सूत्रितं च । अश्वायंतो गव्यंतो वाजयंतः शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिंद्रं । आ. २-२० । इति ॥

> गव्यंतो गा आत्मन इच्छंतः ॥ वांतो यि प्रत्यय इत्यवादेशः ॥ वाजयंतोs
> ग्नीन्वाजनेन शूर्पादिना प्रज्वलयंतः ॥ ना गतिगंधनयोः । णिचि वो विधूनने ।
