> इच्छंत इति । तदानीमवग्रहाभावस्वर् छांदसौ द्रष्टव्यौ । एवंभूता वयं हे
> इंद्र त्वामुपगंतवा उपगंतुं प्राप्तुं हवामहे । आह्वयामहे ॥ गमेस्तुमर्थे सेसेनिति तवैप्रत्ययः । गतिसमासे तवै चांतश्च युगपदिति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वमुत्तरपदस्यांतोदात्तत्वं ॥ उ इति पूरकः । हे इंद्र ते तव नवायामभिनवायां
> प्रशस्तायां सुमतौ शोभनबुद्धावाभूषंत आ समंताद्भवंतो वर्तमानाः ।
> यद्वा । आ समंताद्भूषयंतोऽलंकुर्वंतस्तवानुग्रहबुद्धौ वर्तमाना वयं
> शुनं सुखकरं त्वां हुवेम । आह्वयेम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the Śunāsīrīya parvan, the twelve-potsherd cake offered to Indra Śunāsīra has this verse, अश्वायंत (*aśvāyaṃta*), as its yājyā. For the optional offering as well (इंद्रो देवा शुन (*iṃdro devā śuna*)) this very verse is the yājyā. It is also taught in the sūtra: अश्वायंतो गव्यंतो वाजयंतः शुनं हुवेम मघवानमिंद्रं (*aśvāyaṃto gavyaṃto vājayaṃtaḥ śunaṃ huvema maghavānamiṃdraṃ*) (Ā. 2-20).
अश्वायंतः (*aśvāyaṃtaḥ*) means those who desire horses. गव्यंतः (*gavyaṃtaḥ*) means those who desire cows for themselves. ग्नीन्वाजनेन (*gnīnvājanena*) he explains वाजयंतः (*vājayaṃtaḥ*) as those kindling the fires by fanning them with a winnowing-basket and the like. Another (explainer) says it means those who desire food (वाज (*vāja*)) for themselves. Such as we, O Indra, call you, to come to us (उपगंतवै (*upagaṃtavai*), an infinitive); उ (*u*) is an expletive. O Indra, being in your new, excellent, gracious mind (सुमतौ (*sumatau*)), आभूषंतः (*ābhūṣaṃtaḥ*) means abiding there; or else adorning ourselves, abiding in your favourable thought, we invoke you, the giver of happiness.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्वायंतः (*aśvāyaṃtaḥ*)—those who desire horses
- गव्यंतः (*gavyaṃtaḥ*)—those who desire cows
- वाजयंतः (*vājayaṃtaḥ*)—we who desire food, or who make the sacrificial fire blaze by fanning it
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- उपगंतवै उ (*upagaṃtavai u*)—so that you may come near us
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we call, praying
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—your
- नवायां (*navāyāṃ*)—excellent
- सुमतौ (*sumatau*)—in the good, or gracious, mind
- आभूषंतः (*ābhūṣaṃtaḥ*)—being (as if adorned)
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—you, the giver of happiness
- हुवेम (*huvema*)—we call, praying

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, we who desire horses, cows and food pray to you and call you to come near us. O Indra, we are as if adorned in your excellent, gracious mind; that is, we have become worthy of your favour. We pray to you, the giver of happiness, and call you.

##### English translation
Wishing for horses, for cattle, for food, we invoke you, Indra, that you may come; abiding within your new favour we invoke you, Indra, the giver of happiness.

### Printed p. 1082

## Sūkta 161 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
In this hymn a prayer is made to destroy the heart-disease called rājayakṣma, or consumption (Consumption). It is said that this disease is allayed by japa, homa and the like with this hymn. The Ṛgvidhāna also states the application of this hymn thus:
मुंचामि त्वा हविषेति यक्ष्या णमपकर्षति ॥ ८२ ॥ (*muṃcāmi tvā haviṣeti yakṣyā ṇamapakarṣati ‖ 82 ‖*)
समिद्दमग्निं जुहुयादाज्येनैव यथाविधि । संपातमाज्ये निनयेत्संपातैश्च पयः पिबेत् ॥ (*samiddamagniṃ juhuyādājyenaiva yathāvidhi | saṃpātamājye ninayetsaṃpātaiśca payaḥ pibet ‖*)
संपातभाजने सर्पिश्चूर्णं तत्र निधापयेत् । तत्रास्य भोजनीयं स्यात्पानीयं चानुमंत्रितं ॥ (*saṃpātabhājane sarpiścūrṇaṃ tatra nidhāpayet | tatrāsya bhojanīyaṃ syātpānīyaṃ cānumaṃtritaṃ ‖*)
बादिराणि तु काष्ठानि चूर्णं कृत्वा सहांबुभिः । खादिराणि तु काष्ठानि चूर्णं कृत्वा सहांबुभिः । साधयीत रसं चैषां मध्वाज्याभ्यां पिबेत्सह ॥ (*bādirāṇi tu kāṣṭhāni cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā sahāṃbubhiḥ | khādirāṇi tu kāṣṭhāni cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā sahāṃbubhiḥ | sādhayīta rasaṃ caiṣāṃ madhvājyābhyāṃ pibetsaha ‖*)
मुंचामि त्वा हविषेति तत्र तत्र प्रयोजयेत् । यक्ष्माणमपकर्षति शरीरात्तेन कर्मणा ॥ (*muṃcāmi tvā haviṣeti tatra tatra prayojayet | yakṣmāṇamapakarṣati śarīrāttena karmaṇā ‖*)
(Ṛgvidhāna, Adhyāya 4, Śloka 82-86)
If one offers homa in the fire, in the prescribed manner, with this hymn beginning मुंचामि त्वा हविषा (*muṃcāmi tvā haviṣā*), together with samit and ājya, the yakṣa-disease (consumption) is cured. One should mix milk with the ājya remaining from the homa and drink it. One should put ghee-powder into the vessel holding the ājya remaining from the homa, mix water with it, consecrate it with the mantras of this hymn and drink it. And one should bring splinters of the khadira tree, grind them in water, mix that juice with honey and ājya, and drink it preceded by the mantra beginning मुंचामि त्वा हविषा (*muṃcāmi tvā haviṣā*). If this is done, the yakṣa-disease that has taken root in the body is destroyed. The 63rd hymn of this same Maṇḍala, beginning अक्षीभ्यां ते (*akṣībhyāṃ te*), likewise removes the yakṣa-disease, as this hymn does.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मुंचामीति पंचर्चं दशमं सूक्तं प्रजापतिपुत्रस्य यक्षनाशनाख्यस्यार्षं।
> अंत्यानुष्टुप् शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः । अनादेशे त्विंद्रो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं ।
> मुंचामि प्राजापत्यो यक्षनाशनो राजयक्षघ्नमंत्यानुष्टुबिति ॥ हृदयरोग-

### Printed p. 1083

> प्रमुखस्य व्याधिजातसोपशमनार्थमनेन सूक्तेन होतव्यं । सूत्र्यते हि ।
> व्याधितस्यातुरस्य यक्ष्मगृहीतस्य ना षळाहुतिश्चरुर्मुंचामि त्वा हविषा जीवनाय
> कमित्येतेन । आ. गृ- ३-६-४ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(introduction, concluding) This hymn is to be offered in homa to allay the group of diseases beginning with heart-disease. It is taught in the sūtra: व्याधितस्यातुरस्य यक्ष्मगृहीतस्य ना षळाहुतिश्चरुर्मुंचामि त्वा हविषा जीवनाय कमित्येतेन । (*vyādhitasyāturasya yakṣmagṛhītasya nā ṣaḷāhutiścarurmuṃcāmi tvā haviṣā jīvanāya kamityetena |*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-6-4).
*Gist (of the whole introduction, b4 and b5):* The hymn मुंचामि (*muṃcāmi*) has five Ṛks and is the tenth hymn. Its seer is Yakṣanāśana, son of Prajāpati. The last Ṛk is anuṣṭubh, the rest triṣṭubh; where no deity is assigned, Indra is the deity. So the Anukramaṇī: मुंचामि प्राजापत्यो यक्षनाशनो राजयक्षघ्नमंत्यानुष्टुबिति (*muṃcāmi prājāpatyo yakṣanāśano rājayakṣaghnamaṃtyānuṣṭubiti*).

##### Anuvāda

This hymn मुंचामि (*muṃcāmi*) is the tenth hymn in the twelfth anuvāka. It contains five Ṛks. Its seer is Yakṣanāśana, son of Prajāpati; since the Anukramaṇī names no deity, Indra may be taken as the deity. The last Ṛk of the hymn is in anuṣṭubh metre; the other Ṛks are in triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇī's statement मुंचामि प्राजापत्यो यक्षनाशनो राजयक्षघ्नमंत्यानुष्टुप् (*muṃcāmi prājāpatyo yakṣanāśano rājayakṣaghnamaṃtyānuṣṭup*) is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra, व्याधितस्यातुरस्य यक्षगृहीतस्य वा षळाहुतिश्चरुर्मुंचामि त्वा हविषा जीवनाय कमित्येतेन (*vyādhitasyāturasya yakṣagṛhītasya vā ṣaḷāhutiścarurmuṃcāmi tvā haviṣā jīvanāya kamityetena*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-6-4, 5), which says that for the relief of a man afflicted with heart-disease, homa is to be offered with the mantras of this hymn.

##### Particulars

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मुं॒चामि॑ त्वा ह॒विषा॒ जीव॑नाय॒ कम॑ज्ञातय॒क्ष्मादु॒त रा॑जय॒क्ष्मात् ।  
> ग्राहि॑र्ज॒ग्राह॒ यदि॑ वै॒तदे॑नं॒ तस्या॑ इंद्राग्नी॒ प्र मु॑मुकमेनं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मुंचामि । त्वा । हविषा । जीवनाय । कं । अज्ञातयक्ष्मात् । उत । राजयक्ष्मात् ।

### Printed p. 1084

> ग्राहिः । जग्राह । यदि । वा । एतत् । एनं । तस्याः । इंद्राग्नी इति । प्र । मुमुक्तं ।  
> एनं ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे यक्ष्माभिभूत हविषानेन चरुणा साधनेन होमेन त्वा त्वामज्ञातयक्ष्मात् । अयमेतत्संज्ञ इत्यप्रज्ञातः शरीरगतो रोगोऽज्ञातयक्ष्मः । तादृशाद्रोगान्मुंचामि । विश्लेषयामि । किमर्थं । जीवनाय कं जीवनार्थं । इह
> लोके चिरकालावस्थानार्थमित्यर्थः । कमिति पूरकः । उतापि च राजयक्ष्मात् ।
> यक्ष्माणां राजा यक्षरोगो राजयक्ष्मः ॥ राजदंतादित्वादुपसर्जनस्य परनिपातः ।
> पा. २-२-३१ ॥ तस्मादपि त्वां मुंचामि । यदि वा । यदि चैतदेतस्मिन्समय एनं
> व्याधितं पुरुषं ग्राहिर्गृहणशीला ग्रहरूपा देवता जग्राह गृहीतवती तस्या देवतायाः सकाशाद्भे इंद्राग्नी एनं प्र मुमुक्तं । प्रमोचयतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O you who are overcome by yakṣma, I free you from अज्ञातयक्ष्मात् (*ajñātayakṣmāt*) with this oblation, the caru, as the means of homa. अज्ञातयक्ष्म (*ajñātayakṣma*) is the disease in the body that is not recognised, of which it is not known "this is it". I release you from such a disease. For what purpose? जीवनाय कं (*jīvanāya kaṃ*), for living; that is, to remain long in this world; कं (*kaṃ*) is an expletive. उत (*uta*), and also from राजयक्ष्मात् (*rājayakṣmāt*): the king of yakṣmas, the yakṣa-disease called rājayakṣma; I free you from that too. Or else: if at this time the seizer (ग्राहिः (*grāhiḥ*)), a deity of seizing nature in the form of a seizure, has seized this afflicted man, then, O Indra and Agni, free him from that deity.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—by the homa made with the oblation-materials such as caru
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- जीवनाय कं (*jīvanāya kaṃ*)—in order to live long in happiness
- अज्ञातयक्ष्मात् (*ajñātayakṣmāt*)—from the yakṣa-disease (consumption) that has not yet spread much in the body
- मुंचामि (*muṃcāmi*)—I make free (I rescue)
- उत (*uta*)—and
- राजयक्ष्मात् (*rājayakṣmāt*)—I rescue also from the severe yakṣa-disease
- यदि वा (*yadi vā*)—if perchance
- एतत् (*etat*)—at this time
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—this man afflicted with the disease
- ग्राहिः (*grāhiḥ*)—this disease-deity, of seizing nature
- जग्राह (*jagrāha*)—has seized firmly
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—O Indra and Agni
- तस्याः (*tasyāḥ*)—from the grip of that disease
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—this man
- प्र मुमुक्तं (*pra mumuktaṃ*)—may you release

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O you afflicted with the yakṣa (consumptive) disease, in order that you may live long in happiness, I make you free of disease by offering homa in the fire with this oblation, so as to free you from the yakṣa-disease that has not yet spread much in your body, or, though spread, is not seen, and from the more severe disease called rājayakṣma. If the disease is strong, then may Indra and Agni release this man from the grip of that disease.

### Printed p. 1085

##### English translation
By means of the oblation I set you free to live safe from undeveloped cnsumption and from royal consumption; and if the seizer have already seized him, then do you, Indra and Agni, set him free.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अज्ञातयक्ष्मात् (*ajñātayakṣmāt*)—When consumption has spread through the body, it is not known at once. Gradually, when the disease becomes aggravated, it becomes known. Therefore, since it is not known in the early stages of the disease, it is here designated अज्ञातयक्ष (*ajñātayakṣa*) for the beginning period of this disease. In such early stages it can be cured easily. When the disease has grown strong and reached the aggravated state, curing it is hard to accomplish; in some cases it is not cured at all. Since the disease of a man in such a grave condition lies beyond human efforts, Indra and Agni are here prayed to remove it by their favour. It is noteworthy that a proper modern medical treatment for this consumption has not yet been discovered.
राजयक्ष्मात् (*rājayakṣmāt*)—Extremely terrible consumption; that is, the stage in which the disease, having passed the early stages, has spread well in the body and become acute. Or else, there are various kinds of yakṣa-disease, and one particular kind of them is called rājayakṣma. Since this yakṣa-disease is mentioned in many places in the Ṛgveda and the Yajurveda, it may be inferred that the ravage of this disease was especially great in that age.

### Printed p. 1086

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यदि स रोगग्रस्तः क्षितायुः क्षीणायुर्भवति यदि वा परेतोऽस्माल्लोकात्परागतो भवति यदि च मृत्योर्नैवस्वतस्यांतिकं निकटं नीतो नितरां प्राप्त एव
> भवति एवंभूतमपि तं पुरुषं निर्ऋतेः पापदेवताया आयुषः क्षयकारिण्या
> उपस्थादुपस्थानादा हरामि । अनाययामि । आवर्तयामि । आह्ृत्य चैनं शतशारदाय शतसंवत्सरजीवनार्थमस्पार्षं । प्रबलं करोमि ॥ स्पृ प्रीतिबलनयोः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

If that man seized by disease has become क्षितायुः (*kṣitāyuḥ*), one of wasted life; or if he has gone away from this world (परेतः (*paretaḥ*)); or if he has been brought near to Death, Vaivasvata, and has reached him fully — even such a man I bring back from the lap (उपस्थात् (*upasthāt*)) of Nirṛti, the evil deity who causes the waning of life; आ हरामि (*ā harāmi*) means I bring, I turn back. Having brought him back, I make him strong, अस्पार्षं (*aspārṣaṃ*), for a hundred autumns (शतशारदाय (*śataśāradāya*)), that is, to live a hundred years. The root स्पृ (*spṛ*) is in the sense of pleasing and strength.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यदि (*yadi*)—if (that man afflicted by disease)
- क्षितायुः (*kṣitāyuḥ*)—even though in the state of dying, wasted**NOTE**
- यदि वा (*yadi vā*)—or
- परेतः (*paretaḥ*)—even though dead and gone from this world
- यदि च (*yadi ca*)—or
- मृत्योः (*mṛtyoḥ*)—of Death
- अंतिकं (*aṃtikaṃ*)—to the vicinity
- नीतः एव (*nītaḥ eva*)—even though carried
- तं (*taṃ*)—such a man
- निर्ऋतेः (*nirṛteḥ*)—of the evil deity called nirṛti**NOTE**, who wastes the life
- उपस्थात् (*upasthāt*)—from the vicinity (the lap)
- आ हरामि (*ā harāmi*)—I bring back (and thereafter)
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—that man seized by disease
- शतशारदाय (*śataśāradāya*)—in order to live for a hundred years
- अस्पार्षं (*aspārṣaṃ*)—I make strong

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Even if the life of that man afflicted with consumption has been wasting away and, his body emaciated, he is in a dying state, or has died and gone away from this world, or has come near to Death, I bring such a man back from the lap of Nirṛti, the evil deity who causes the waning of life, and I make that man strong so that he lives for a hundred years.

##### English translation
If he be of wasted life, or already dead, or be come to the verge of death, I bring him back from the lap of Nirriti; I have made him strong enough to live for a hundred years.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

निर्ऋतेः उपस्थात् (*nirṛteḥ upasthāt*)—Nirṛti means the evil deity. This deity has a close connection with Death; "the lap of Nirṛti" means the deathbed. The mention of this Nirṛti in the 59th hymn of this Maṇḍala may be seen in the Special Topics of that hymn. And for an explanation of the meaning of the word nirṛti, see Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 3, page 272.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒ह॒स्रा॒क्षेण॑ श॒तशा॑रदेन श॒तायु॑षा ह॒विषाहा॑र्षमेनं ।  
> श॒तं यथे॒मं श॒रदो॒ नया॒तींद्रो॒ विश्व॑स्य दुरि॒तस्य॑ पा॒रं ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सहस्रअक्षेण । शतशारदेन । शतआयुषा । हविषा । आ । अहार्षं । एनं ।  
> शतं । यथा । इमं । शरदः । नयाति । इंद्रः । विश्वस्य । दुःइतस्य । पारं ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सहस्रमिति बहुनाम । सहस्रमक्षीणि चक्षूंषि यस्य हविषः फलत्वेन विद्यंते
> तत्सहस्राक्षं ॥ बहुव्रीहौ सत्यक्षोरिति षट् समासांतः ॥ शरदः संबंधी शारदः
> संवत्सरः । शतं शारदा यस्य तत्तथोक्तं ॥ बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ अत
> एव शतायुषा शतसंवत्सरपरिमितमायुर्जीवनं फलभूतं यस्य तादृशेन हविषा ।
> यद्वा । सहस्राक्ष इंद्रः । तेन शतशारदेन शरदां संवत्सराणां शतस्य दातृत्वेन
> संबंधिना कर्त्रा शतायुषा हविषा करणभूतेन एनं यक्ष्मगृहीतमाहार्षं ।
> रोगादनैषं । यथा येन प्रकारेणेमं पुरुषं शतं शरदः संवत्सरान् ॥ अत्यंतसंयोगे द्वितीया ॥ एतावंतं कालमिंद्रो विश्वस्य सर्वस्य दुरितस्य दुःखस्य
> पारमवसानं दुःखराहित्यं नयाति नयेत् तथाहार्षमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa takes सहस्र (*sahasra*) to be a word for "many". An oblation whose fruits are a thousand imperishable "eyes" is सहस्राक्षं (*sahasrākṣaṃ*) (a bahuvrīhi, with the samāsānta ṣac). शारदः (*śāradaḥ*) is that which belongs to the autumn, that is, the year. That which has a hundred autumns is *śataśāradaṃ*, and its accent is that of the first member of the compound. For the same reason शतायुषा (*śatāyuṣā*) means an oblation whose fruit is life, living, measured as a hundred years.

Alternatively: सहस्राक्ष (*sahasrākṣa*) is Indra. By him, the giver of a hundred autumns (years), as the agent, and by the oblation of a hundred years of life as the instrument, "I have brought back" (आहार्षं (*āhārṣaṃ*)) this man seized by yakṣma, that is, I have wished him away from the disease. यथा (*yathā*) means "in the manner in which". शतं शरदः (*śataṃ śaradaḥ*) means a hundred years (the accusative expresses continuous duration). For so long may Indra lead (नयाति (*nayāti*) = नयेत् (*nayet*)) this man to the far end, the termination, the freedom from sorrow, of all (विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)) sorrow (दुरितस्य (*duritasya*)); so I have brought him back. That is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यथा (*yathā*)—in whatever manner
- इमं (*imaṃ*)—this man seized by disease
- शरदः शतं (*śaradaḥ śataṃ*)—for a hundred years
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*)—of all
- दुरितस्य (*duritasya*)—of sorrow
- पारं (*pāraṃ*)—to the end, that is, finally
- नयाति (*nayāti*)—may lead; in that manner
- सहस्राक्षेण (*sahasrākṣeṇa*)—by Indra (by Indra's favour); or, having thousands of fruits called eyes
- शतशारदेन (*śataśāradena*)—having a span of a hundred years
- शतायुषा (*śatāyuṣā*)—having a life-span of a hundred years
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—by this oblation
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—this man afflicted with the yakṣma (consumption) disease
- आहार्षं (*āhārṣaṃ*)—I have made free from the disease

### Printed p. 1088

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In the manner in which Indra makes the afflicted man free from sorrow for a hundred years, in that manner, with this oblation, which can give thousands of kinds of fruits such as health, can keep him free from disease, that is, healthy, for a hundred years, and can increase his life-span to a hundred years, I have made this man, afflicted by the yakṣma disease, free from disease.

##### English translation
I have rescued him with an oblation having a thousand eyes, conferring a hundred years, giving life for a century, so that Indra may condnct him beyond all harm for a hundred years.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सहस्राक्षेण (*sahasrākṣeṇa*)—Here सहस्र (*sahasra*) means many, unlimited; अक्षि (*akṣi*) means eyes. "Eyes" means excellent fruits. An oblation with thousands of eyes means that by offering this oblation thousands of excellent fruits are obtained. And,

शतशारदेन (*śataśāradena*), शतायुषा (*śatāyuṣā*)—these two words indicate one and the same meaning. The intention is that this oblation has the power to increase the life-span to a hundred years. शरत् (*śarat*) means the autumn season or the cold season. Since the autumn comes only once in a year, there is a custom in many contexts of using the word शरत् (*śarat*) itself to denote the meaning "year". Therefore शरदः शतं (*śaradaḥ śataṃ*) means a hundred years.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श॒तं जी॑व श॒रदो॒ वर्ध॑मानः श॒तं हे॑मं॒ताञ्चि॒तमु॑ वसं॒तान् ।  
> श॒तमिं॑द्रा॒ग्नी स॑वि॒ता बृह॒स्पतिः॑ श॒तायु॑षा ह॒विषे॒मं पुन॑र्दुः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शतं । जीव । शरदः । वर्धमानः । शतं । हेमंतान् । शतं । ऊं इति । वसंतान् ।  
> शतं । इंद्राग्नी इति । सविता । बृहस्पतिः । शतआयुषा । हविषा । इमं । पुनः । दुः ॥

### Printed p. 1089

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे यक्ष्माद्विमुक्त वर्धमानोऽहरहरभिवृद्धिं प्राप्नुवंस्त्वं शतं शरदः
> शतसंख्याकाञ्यरदृतूञ्जीव । प्राणान्धारय ॥ पूर्ववदत्यंतसंयोगे द्वितीया ॥
> शतं हेमंतान् हेमंतर्तूंश्च जीव शतं वसंतांश्च । उशब्दः समुच्चये । अपि
> चेंद्राग्नी इंद्रश्चाग्निश्च सविता प्रेरको देवश्च बृहस्पतिर्बृहतां देवानां पालयिता देवश्च शतायुषा शतसंवत्सरपरिमितस्यायुषो हेतुभूतेन हविषा तर्प्यमाणाः संत इमं जनं पुनर्दुः । पुनरस्सभ्यं प्रादुः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O you who are freed from yakṣma, growing (वर्धमानः (*vardhamānaḥ*)) from day to day, attaining increase, live (जीव (*jīva*), bear the breaths) a hundred autumns, that is, a hundred autumn seasons" (as before, the accusative expresses continuous duration). "Live a hundred winters (हेमंतान् (*hemaṃtān*)), the winter seasons, and a hundred springs (वसंतान् (*vasaṃtān*))." The word उ (*u*) is in the sense of "and" (samuccaya). Moreover Indra and Agni, Savitṛ, the impelling god, and Bṛhaspati, the god who protects the great gods, being gratified by the oblation (हविषा (*haviṣā*)) that is the cause of a life-span measured as a hundred years (शतायुषा (*śatāyuṣā*)), "gave this man back" (पुनर्दुः (*punarduḥ*)): they gave him again to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(O man freed from the consumption disease, you) 
- वर्धमानः (*vardhamānaḥ*)—growing from day to day, that is, gradually regaining health of body
- शतं शरदः (*śataṃ śaradaḥ*)—for a hundred autumn seasons (a hundred years)
- जीव (*jīva*)—live
- शतं हेमंतान् (*śataṃ hemaṃtān*)—live until a hundred winter seasons have passed
- शतं वसंतान् (*śataṃ vasaṃtān*)—live until a hundred spring seasons have passed (and)
- इंद्राग्नी (*iṃdrāgnī*)—Indra and Agni
- सविता (*savitā*)—the god Savitṛ, the impeller of all
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Bṛhaspati also
- शतायुषा (*śatāyuṣā*)—having the power to increase the life-span so that one lives a hundred years
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—gratified by this oblation
- इमं (*imaṃ*)—this man just now freed from the consumption disease
- पुनर्दुः (*punarduḥ*)—gave back to us, that is, granted that he live in our midst

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O man freed from the consumption disease, growing from day to day, that is, gradually regaining health of body, live until a hundred autumn seasons have passed, that is, for a hundred years. In the same way live until a hundred winter seasons and a hundred spring seasons have passed, that is, for a hundred years. And Indra, Agni, Savitṛ and Bṛhaspati, all these gods, gratified by this oblation, which has the power to increase the life-span so that one lives a hundred years, have granted that this man, who had fallen ill and has recovered from it, live again in our midst.

##### English translation
Regaining your strength, live for a hundred autumns, a hundred winters, a hundred springs; may Indra, Agni, Savitri, and Brihaspati, (propitiated) by this century-yielding oblation, give this man back (to us) for a hundred years.

### Printed p. 1090

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the span of time is stated as शतं शरदः (*śataṃ śaradaḥ*), शतं हेमंतान् (*śataṃ hemaṃtān*), शतं वसंतान् (*śataṃ vasaṃtān*). Since in one year the autumn, the winter or the spring season comes only once, there is a custom of saying "the time in which a hundred autumn seasons pass" in order to denote the span of years; and the words शरदः शतं (*śaradaḥ śataṃ*) are used in this sense in many places in the Ṛgveda. But in this Ṛk, along with the words शरदः शतं (*śaradaḥ śataṃ*), the expressions शतं हेमंतान् (*śataṃ hemaṃtān*) and शतं वसंतान् (*śataṃ vasaṃtān*) are also used. The meaning stated for the words शरदः शतं (*śaradaḥ śataṃ*) applies to these words too. The span of a man's life is reckoned as a hundred years, and that is regarded as the full life; so in all contexts where one wishes to live to the full life, it is natural to pray for a hundred years of life. In the present Ṛk the words शरदः शतं (*śaradaḥ śataṃ*) alone already indicate this meaning, so that much would have sufficed. Nevertheless, with the intention of stressing here the span of a hundred years, the seer has described it by adducing two more expressions, शतं हेमांतान् (*śataṃ hemāṃtān*) and शतं वसंतान् (*śataṃ vasaṃtān*).

For this reasoning an explanation is given in the Nirukta Pariśiṣṭa as follows—

शतं जीव शरदो वर्धमानः शतं हेमंतान् शतमु वसंतान् । (*śataṃ jīva śarado vardhamānaḥ śataṃ hemaṃtān śatamu vasaṃtān |*)
शतमिंद्राग्नी सविता बृहस्पतिः शतायुषा हविषेमं पुनर्दुः ॥ (*śatamiṃdrāgnī savitā bṛhaspatiḥ śatāyuṣā haviṣemaṃ punarduḥ ‖*)
शतं जीव शरदो वर्धमान इत्यपि निगमो भवति शतमिति शतं दीर्घमायुर्मरुत एना वर्धयंति शतमेनमेव शतात्मानं भवति शतमनंतं भवति शत मैश्वर्यं भवति शतमिति शतं दीर्घमायुः ॥ (*śataṃ jīva śarado vardhamāna ityapi nigamo bhavati śatamiti śataṃ dīrghamāyurmaruta enā vardhayaṃti śatamenameva śatātmānaṃ bhavati śatamanaṃtaṃ bhavati śata maiśvaryaṃ bhavati śatamiti śataṃ dīrghamāyuḥ ‖*)
(Nirukta Pariśiṣṭa 14-36)

Here the word शतं (*śataṃ*) has many meanings. Among them "long life" is the chief one. मरुत एना वर्धयंति (*maruta enā vardhayaṃti*)—those who increase are the Maruts. As long as men or animals live, inhalation and exhalation must go on without interruption. Wind (air) is necessary for these. Therefore the Maruts (the winds), helping these inhalations and exhalations, thereby increase life. शतं (*śataṃ*) means "in many ways": to the man afflicted by disease, शतमात्मानं (*śatamātmānaṃ*)—nourishment of the body or health of the body; अनंतं (*anaṃtaṃ*)—other unlimited advantages; शत ऐश्वर्यं (*śata aiśvaryaṃ*)—unlimited wealth; शतमिति शतं दीर्घमायुः (*śatamiti śataṃ dīrghamāyuḥ*)—above all, long life—may the gods grant these. That is the chief intention of the explanation.

> सर्वऽअंग । सर्वं । ते । चक्षुः । सर्वं । आयुः । च । ते । अविदं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे व्याधिगृहीत त्वा त्वामाहार्षं । मृत्योः सकाशादाहृतवानस्मि । अत एव
> त्वा त्वामविदं । अलप्सि । हे पुनर्नव पुनरभिनव पुनरागाः । पुनरस्मत्समीपमागच्छ । हे
> सर्वांग सर्वैरविकलैरंगैरुपेत ते तव सर्वं चक्षुः । उपलक्षणमेतत् । इंद्रियवर्गं सकलमविदं । लब्धवानस्मि । ते तवायुर्जीवनं च सर्वं संपूर्णमविदं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O you seized by disease, I have brought you back (आहार्षं (*āhārṣaṃ*)): I have fetched you from the presence of death. For that very reason I have found (अविदं (*avidaṃ*), अलप्सि (*alapsi*)) you. O you who are young again (पुनर्नव (*punarnava*), newly renewed), come again (पुनरागाः (*punarāgāḥ*)), come to us once more. O you who are furnished with all limbs (सर्वांग (*sarvāṃga*)), with no limb deficient, I have found all your eye." This is an indication (upalakṣaṇa): the whole group of senses, I have obtained. "And your life, your living, I have found entire."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(O man afflicted by disease)
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- आहार्षं (*āhārṣaṃ*)—I have fetched, freeing you from death (therefore)
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अविदं (*avidaṃ*)—I have obtained again
- पुनर्नव (*punarnava*)—O man, who, having recovered from the disease, are like a new man
- पुनः अगाः (*punaḥ agāḥ*)—come again into our presence
- सर्वांग (*sarvāṃga*)—O man, who are strong in all limbs, with no defective limb
- ते (*te*)—your
- सर्वं चक्षुः (*sarvaṃ cakṣuḥ*)—all the senses beginning with the eye
- अविदं (*avidaṃ*)—I have obtained
- ते (*te*)—your
- आयुः च (*āyuḥ ca*)—life-time, or life-span
- सर्वं (*sarvaṃ*)—that which is entire
- अविदं (*avidaṃ*)—I have obtained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O man afflicted by disease, I have fetched you out of the mouth of death. Therefore it is as if you were born again. Having recovered from the disease, come to us as a new man, that is, strong with health. I have made you sound and strong in all limbs without deficiency, with no defect or fault in all the senses beginning with the eye, and with your life-span complete.

I have rescued you, I have found you; come back again, you who are young again ; sound in body, I have obtained for you all your senses, your whole life.

ऊर्ध्वरेखा प्र दहंते विष्णुरिममिंद्राग्नी अमृतं जुषेथां । (*ūrdhvarekhā pra dahaṃte viṣṇurimamiṃdrāgnī amṛtaṃ juṣethāṃ |*)
मह्यं दधाना उप दीर्घमायुरस्मे धत्तं पुरुभुजा पुरंधिः ॥ १५ ॥ (*mahyaṃ dadhānā upa dīrghamāyurasme dhattaṃ purubhujā puraṃdhiḥ ‖ 15 ‖*)

## Sūkta 162 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
In this sūkta the gods are prayed to that there be no miscarriage (abortion) before the time of birth. As an expiation to prevent miscarriage, certain rites such as an oblation in the fire are to be performed, as stated in some works such as the Ṛgvidhāna—

यस्याः गर्भः प्रमायेत तत्राग्नौ जुहुयाद्भविः । (*yasyāḥ garbhaḥ pramāyeta tatrāgnau juhuyādbhaviḥ |*)
ब्रह्मणाग्निः संविदान इत्याज्येन यथाविधि ॥ ८७ ॥ (*brahmaṇāgniḥ saṃvidāna ityājyena yathāvidhi ‖ 87 ‖*)
आज्यशेषेण चाभ्यज्य गर्भिणी प्रसवेत्ततः । (*ājyaśeṣeṇa cābhyajya garbhiṇī prasavettataḥ |*)
पिबेदेवाज्यशेषं तु जीवंस्तस्याः प्रजायते ॥ ८८ ॥ (*pibedevājyaśeṣaṃ tu jīvaṃstasyāḥ prajāyate ‖ 88 ‖*)
जातानि चेत्प्रमायेरन्नाज्यं कृत्वानुमंत्रितं । (*jātāni cetpramāyerannājyaṃ kṛtvānumaṃtritaṃ |*)
ब्रह्मणाग्निरिति हुत्वा संपातान्निनयेन्मण् ॥ ८९ ॥ (*brahmaṇāgniriti hutvā saṃpātānninayenmaṇ ‖ 89 ‖*)
मणिं तु त्रिवृति सूत्रे वासयेद्वाससा सह । (*maṇiṃ tu trivṛti sūtre vāsayedvāsasā saha |*)
न्यग्रोधशुंगया तत्र शुक्ललोहितनेष्टितं ॥ ९० ॥ (*nyagrodhaśuṃgayā tatra śuklalohitaneṣṭitaṃ ‖ 90 ‖*)
तं सावित्र्ययुतेनाथ अनुमंत्र्य यथाविधि । (*taṃ sāvitryayutenātha anumaṃtrya yathāvidhi |*)
संपातैरयुतेनैव ब्रह्मणेति च संस्तुतं ॥ ९१ ॥ (*saṃpātairayutenaiva brahmaṇeti ca saṃstutaṃ ‖ 91 ‖*)
उपरिष्टाच्च सावित्रा तावदेनानुमंत्रणं । (*upariṣṭācca sāvitrā tāvadenānumaṃtraṇaṃ |*)
सर्वॆः स्वस्त्ययनैश्च तज्जपेदभिहुतं मणिं ॥ ९२ ॥ (*sarvèḥ svastyayanaiśca tajjapedabhihutaṃ maṇiṃ ‖ 92 ‖*)
शिरसा धारयेन्नारी प्रयता गर्भिणी सती । (*śirasā dhārayennārī prayatā garbhiṇī satī |*)
तृतीये गर्भमासे तु मणिमेतं समासजेत् ॥ ९३ ॥ (*tṛtīye garbhamāse tu maṇimetaṃ samāsajet ‖ 93 ‖*)
पुष्प्यंती शरदं नारी गौः सवत्सा वसेद्यथा । (*puṣpyaṃtī śaradaṃ nārī gauḥ savatsā vasedyathā |*)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When a woman is known to be pregnant, it is good to perform certain expiatory and similar rites so that the embryo may not miscarry and so that it may be protected. On such an occasion one should offer an oblation of ghee in the fire with recitation of the mantras of this sūkta beginning ब्रह्मणाग्निः (*brahmaṇāgniḥ*). The pregnant woman should drink the ghee left over from the oblation and anoint her body with it. If this is done, the child to be born will be born alive. For the protection of the embryo the following procedure may also be followed. After offering the oblation with the mantras of this sūkta, a jewel (or ornament) should be placed in the ghee remaining from the oblation, and the jewel should be bound with a thread of three strands. Along with the jewel a tender fruit of the banyan tree is wrapped in cloth; both that and the jewel are consecrated with the mantras of this sūkta and with ten thousand recitations of the Gāyatrī. The jewel, purified by Brāhmaṇas with svastivācana, japa, homa and so on, is to be worn on her head by the pregnant woman. This is to be done in the third month of pregnancy. If it is done, the woman will bear a male child. The newborn child is to be anointed with the remaining ghee. After the year is complete, japa, homa and the rest are to be performed as before by Brāhmaṇas, preceded by svastivācana. Before the child is given the breast, the Śraddhā-sūkta श्रद्धयाग्निः समिध्यते (*śraddhayāgniḥ samidhyate*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-151) is to be recited and then the child is nursed. And with the recitation of the Medhā-sūkta मेभां मह्यं (*mebhāṃ mahyaṃ*) (a khila sūkta), flour or cooked rice mixed with honey is to be fed to the child. By so doing the child grows well and later becomes very medhāvin, that is, very intelligent; and he is full-lived: he does not die before the hundred years are complete. This is the main purport.

### Printed p. 1094

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ब्रह्मणाग्निरिति षडृचमेकादशं सूक्तमानुष्टुभं । ब्रह्मपुत्रो रक्षोहा
> नामर्षिः । अपप्रसवसमाधानरूपस्य गर्भरक्षणस्य प्रतिपाद्यत्वात्तद्देवताकमिदं ।
> अनुक्रांतं च । ब्रह्मणा षट् ब्राह्मो रक्षोहा गर्भसंस्रावे प्रायश्चित्तमानुष्टुभं
> हीति ॥ विनियोगो लिंगादवगंतव्यः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This sūkta ब्रह्मणाग्निः (*brahmaṇāgniḥ*) has six Ṛks, is the eleventh sūkta of its anuvāka, and is in the Anuṣṭubh metre. The seer is Rakṣohā, son of Brahmā. Since the sūkta teaches the protection of the embryo, in the form of preventing miscarriage, that is its deity. The Anukramaṇī is quoted: ब्रह्मणा षट् ब्राह्मो रक्षोहा गर्भसंस्रावे प्रायश्चित्तमानुष्टुभं हीति (*brahmaṇā ṣaṭ brāhmo rakṣohā garbhasaṃsrāve prāyaścittamānuṣṭubhaṃ hīti*). The viniyoga is to be understood from the indication of the mantras themselves.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning ब्रह्मणाग्निः (*brahmaṇāgniḥ*) is the eleventh sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Its seer is Rakṣohā, a son of Brahmā. Because the means of protecting the embryo so that there is no miscarriage is set forth in this sūkta, that subject is its deity. The metre is Anuṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: ब्रह्मणा षड् ब्राह्मो रक्षोहा गर्भ संस्रावे प्रायश्चित्तमानुष्टुभं (*brahmaṇā ṣaḍ brāhmo rakṣohā garbha saṃsrāve prāyaścittamānuṣṭubhaṃ*). The viniyoga is to be understood according to the meaning of the mantras.

Maṇḍala 10, Anuvāka 12, Sūkta 162. Aṣṭaka 8, Adhyāya 8, Varga 20.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6.
Ṛṣi: Rakṣohā Brāhma. Devatā: expiation in miscarriage. Chandas: Anuṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ब्रह्म॑णा॒ग्निः सं॑विदा॒नो र॑क्षो॒हा बा॑धतामि॒तः ।  
> अमी॑वा॒ यस्ते॒ गर्भं॑ दु॒र्णामा॒ योनि॑मा॒शये॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ब्रह्मणा । अग्निः । संविदानः । रक्षःहा । बाधतां । इतः ।  
> अमीनावा । यः । ते । गर्भं । दुःनामा । योनिं । आशये ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ब्रह्मणा मंत्रेण सह संविदान ऐकमत्यं प्राप्तो रक्षोहा रक्षसां हंताग्नि
> रितोऽस्मात्स्थानाद्राक्षसादिकं बाधतां । हिनस्तु । यो राक्षसोऽमीवा रोगरूपः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the slayer of Rakṣases, having come to agreement (संविदान (*saṃvidāna*)) with the mantra (ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*)), is asked to drive away from this place the Rākṣasa and the like. The Rākṣasa who, in the form of disease (अमीवा (*amīvā*)), ... (continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 1095

> संस्थे तव गर्भमाशये आशेते ॥ लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्टिति तलोपः ॥ हंतुं
> प्राप्नोति । दुर्नामार्श अख्यो रोगः । तद्रूपः सन् यश्च ते तव योनिं रेतस
> आधानं गर्भस्थानमाशेते तं बाधतामित्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

... lies in your womb (आशये (*āśaye*) = आशेते (*āśete*), with loss of the ending ta) and tries to destroy it; and who, taking the form of the disease named दुर्नामार्श (*durnāmārśa*), lies in your yoni, the receptacle of semen and the place of the embryo: him let Agni drive away. Such is the construction.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Rākṣasa (O woman)
- अमीवा (*amīvā*)—being in the form of disease
- ते (*te*)—your
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—in the womb
- आशये (*āśaye*)—has settled; and
- दुर्नामा (*durnāmā*)—in the form of the disease called arśas
- योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—dwells in your yoni: that Rākṣasa or disease
- ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*)—by the mantra
- संविदानः (*saṃvidānaḥ*)—having come to agreement
- रक्षोहा अग्निः (*rakṣohā agniḥ*)—Agni the destroyer of Rākṣasas
- इतः (*itaḥ*)—from this place
- बाधतां (*bādhatāṃ*)—let him smite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O woman, whatever Rākṣasa in the form of disease, or whatever disease, has settled in the womb, or whatever disease called arśas has enveloped your yoni, all that disease let Agni the Rakṣohan, joined with the mantra, smite and drive away from here.

##### English translation
May Agni, the destroyer of the Rakshasas, consenting to our prayer. drive hence (the evil spirit) who (in the form of) sickness assails your embryo, who. as the disease durnaman, assaults your womb.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The first half-verse has already been explained. That flesh-eater (क्रव्यादं (*kravyādaṃ*)), the Rākṣasa or the like, Agni together with the mantra (ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*)) has destroyed utterly (अनीनशत् (*anīnaśat*)); let him destroy.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—in the womb
- आशये (*āśaye*)—has settled (and)
- दुर्णामा (*durṇāmā*)—the disease called arśas
- योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—has enveloped the region of your yoni
- क्रव्यादं (*kravyādaṃ*)—eating the flesh (of the body)
- तं (*taṃ*)—that disease or Rākṣasa
- ब्रह्मणा सह (*brahmaṇā saha*)—joined with the mantra
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni Rakṣohan
- निः अनीनशत् (*niḥ anīnaśat*)—let him destroy completely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

##### English translation
May Agni, concurring in our prayer, destroy the cannibal who, as sickness, assails your embryo, who, as the disease durnaman, assaults your womb.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska gives an etymology to explain the words अमीना (*amīnā*) and दुर्णामा (*durṇāmā*) in this Ṛk:
अमीना । यस्ते गर्भममीना दुर्णामा योनिमाशये । अमीनाभ्यमनेन व्याख्यातः । दुर्णामा क्रिमिर्भवति पापनामा । कृमिः क्रव्ये मेद्यति क्रमतेर्वा स्यात्सरणकर्मणः क्रामतेर्वा ॥ (*amīnā | yaste garbhamamīnā durṇāmā yonimāśaye | amīnābhyamanena vyākhyātaḥ | durṇāmā krimirbhavati pāpanāmā | kṛmiḥ kravye medyati kramatervā syātsaraṇakarmaṇaḥ krāmatervā ‖*) (Ni. 6-12)
अमीवा (*amīvā*) means अमवान् (*amavān*), अभ्यमनवान् (*abhyamanavān*), that is परेभ्यो भयदाता यायात् (*parebhyo bhayadātā yāyāt*): that which causes fear to others, i.e. disease. दुर्णामा (*durṇāmā*) means a kind of worm (germ) named "evil". A कृमि (*kṛmi*) is, according to क्रव्ये मेद्यति (*kravye medyati*), a worm that lives in flesh and grows by eating it. Or the word क्रिमि (*krimi*) may be derived from the root क्रम् (*kram*) meaning "to move slowly", or from the root क्रम् (*kram*) meaning "to crawl".

## Sūkta 163 (Maṇḍala 1)

**Introduction**
As stated in sūkta 161, which begins मुंचामि त्वा (*muṃcāmi tvā*), in this sūkta also the means of removing the disease yakṣma (consumption) is set forth. In the Ṛgvidhāna it is as follows:

आज्यं संस्कृत्य जुहुयादक्षीभ्यां त इति द्विजः ॥ ९९ ॥ (*ājyaṃ saṃskṛtya juhuyādakṣībhyāṃ ta iti dvijaḥ ‖ 99 ‖*)
पाणिना तु घृताक्तेन मूर्धानं संस्पृशेत्ततः ॥ (*pāṇinā tu ghṛtāktena mūrdhānaṃ saṃspṛśettataḥ ‖*)
कर्ण् नेत्रे च छुबुकं नासिके चैव संस्पृशेत् ॥ १०० ॥ (*karṇ netre ca chubukaṃ nāsike caiva saṃspṛśet ‖ 100 ‖*)
एतदेव जपेन्नित्यं यक्ष्मणो विप्रमुच्यते । (*etadeva japennityaṃ yakṣmaṇo vipramucyate |*)
पूर्वोक्तेनैव कल्पेन यक्षनाशनमाचरेत् ॥ १०१ ॥ (*pūrvoktenaiva kalpena yakṣanāśanamācaret ‖ 101 ‖*)
होमेन च जपैश्चैव यक्षनाशनमाचरेत् ॥ (*homena ca japaiścaiva yakṣanāśanamācaret ‖*)
(Ṛgvidhāna, Adhyāya 4, verses 99–101)

To remove yakṣma or consumption, a twice-born man should prepare ghee according to rule and make an offering in the fire with the mantras of this sūkta beginning अक्षीभ्यां (*akṣībhyāṃ*). Then, wiping his hands with the ghee left over from the offering, he should touch with it the head, ears, eyes, chin, nose and other limbs of the man afflicted by the disease. If this is done every day, that man becomes free of the disease. The disease is to be destroyed by the same rites of recitation and offering that were prescribed earlier for the destruction of yakṣma.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अक्षीभ्यामिति षडृचं द्वादशं सूक्तमानुष्टुभं । कश्यपगोत्रोत्पन्नो
> निवृहा नामर्षिः । यक्ष्मनाशनप्रतिपाद्यत्वात्तद्देवताकं कृत्स्नं सूक्तं । अनुक्रांतं
> च । अक्षीभ्यां निवृहा काश्यपो यक्ष्मघ्नमिति ॥ लैंगिको विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta अक्षीभ्यां (*akṣībhyāṃ*) has six Ṛks, is the twelfth sūkta, and is in the Anuṣṭubh metre. Its seer is Nivṛhā by name, born in the Kaśyapa gotra.**NOTE**  Because the sūkta teaches the destruction of yakṣma, the whole sūkta has that as its deity. The Anukramaṇī says: अक्षीभ्यां निवृहा काश्यपो यक्ष्मघ्नमिति॥ (*akṣībhyāṃ nivṛhā kāśyapo yakṣmaghnamiti‖*) The viniyoga is लैंगिको (*laiṃgiko*) (by the indication of the text).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning अक्षीभ्यां (*akṣībhyāṃ*) is the twelfth sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is one named Vivṛhā, of the Kaśyapa gotra. This

### Printed p. 1102

sūkta teaches how to destroy the disease yakṣma, so the destruction of yakṣma is the deity of this sūkta; the metre is Anuṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: अक्षीभ्यां विवृहा काश्यपो यक्षघ्नं (*akṣībhyāṃ vivṛhā kāśyapo yakṣaghnaṃ*). The viniyoga is by indication (लैंगिक (*laiṃgika*)).

Sūkta 163
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 163;
Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 21;
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6
Ṛṣi: Vivṛhā Kāśyapa
Deity: Yakṣaghna (destroyer of yakṣma)
Metre: Anuṣṭup

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒क्षीभ्यां॑ ते॒ नासि॑काभ्यां॒ कर्णा॑भ्यां॒ छुबु॑का॒दधि॑ ।  
> यक्ष्मं॑ शीर्ष॒ण्यं॑ म॒स्तिष्का॑ज्जि॒ह्वाया॒ वि वृ॑हामि ते ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अक्षीभ्यां । ते । नासिकाभ्यां । कर्णाभ्यां । छुबुकात् । अधि ।  
> यक्ष्मं । शीर्षण्यं । मस्तिष्कात् । जिह्वायाः । वि । वृहामि । ते ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे यक्षगृहीत ते तवाक्षीभ्यां चक्षुर्भ्यां यक्षरोगं वि वृहामि । उद्धरयामि । विश्लेषयामित्यर्थः ॥ ई च द्विवचन इत्यक्षिशब्दस्यॆकारांतादेशः । स
> चोदात्तः ॥ तथा नासिकाभ्यां फ्राणेंद्रियाच्च कर्णाभ्यां शोत्राभ्यां च छुबुकाच्चुबुकादोष्यस्याधःप्रदेशाच्च । अधिरनर्थकः । अपि च शीर्षण्यं । शिरसि भवो रोगः
> शीर्षण्यः ॥ भवे छंदसीति यत् । ये च तद्धिते । पा. ६-१-६१ । इति शिरसः शीर्षन्नादेशः । ये चाभावकर्मणोरिति प्रकृतिभावः ॥ ईदृशं यक्षं रोगं ते तव
> मस्तिष्कात् । शिरसोऽंतरवस्थितो मांसविशेषो मस्तिष्कः । तस्माज्जिह्वाया
> रसनायाश्च सकाशाद्भि वृहामि । उद्धारयामि । पृथक्करोमीत्यर्थः ॥ वृहू उद्यमन इति धातुः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O one seized by yakṣma, I वि वृहामि (*vi vṛhāmi*) pull out, draw out, that is, separate, the yakṣma disease from your eyes; likewise from your nostrils, the organ of smell, and from your ears, the organs of hearing, and from the chin, the region below the lower lip. The word अधि (*adhi*) has no meaning of its own. Further, शीर्षण्यं (*śīrṣaṇyaṃ*) is the disease that arises in the head. Such yakṣma, the disease, I pull out and separate from your मस्तिष्कात् (*mastiṣkāt*), the particular flesh lying within the head, and from the tongue, the organ of taste." The root is वृहू उद्यमन (*vṛhū udyamana*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O one gripped by consumption) ते (*te*)—your
- अक्षीभ्यां (*akṣībhyāṃ*)—from the eyes
- यक्ष्मं (*yakṣmaṃ*)—the yakṣma disease
- वि वृहामि (*vi vṛhāmi*)—I pull out (and likewise)
- नासिकाभ्यां (*nāsikābhyāṃ*)—from the organs of smell
- कर्णाभ्यां (*karṇābhyāṃ*)—from the organs of hearing
- छुबुकात् (*chubukāt*)—from the region of the chin I pull out the yakṣma disease
- शीर्षण्यं (*śīrṣaṇyaṃ*)—the yakṣma disease that is in the head
- ते (*te*)—your
- मस्तिष्कात् (*mastiṣkāt*)—from the brain
- जिह्वायाः (*jihvāyāḥ*)—from the tongue I pull it out

### Printed p. 1103

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O one afflicted by yakṣma, from your eyes, your nose, your ears, your chin, the brain in your head, and your tongue, I pull out this yakṣma disease that has spread through those parts of the body.

##### English translation
I banish disease from your eyes, from your nose, from your ears, from your chin, from your head, from your brain, from your tongue.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ग्री॒वाभ्य॑स्त उ॒ष्णिहा॑भ्यः॒ कीक॑साभ्यो अनू॒क्या॑त् ।  
> यक्ष्मं॑ दोष॒ण्य१॒॑१ मंसा॑भ्यां बा॒हुभ्यां॒ वि वृ॑हामि ते ॥२॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ग्रीवाभ्यः । ते । उष्णिहाभ्यः । कीकसाभ्यः । अनूक्यात् ।  
> यक्ष्मं । दोषण्यं । अंसाभ्यां । बाहुभ्यां । वि । वृहामि । ते ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यो व्याधिगृहीत उष्णिहाभ्य ऊर्ध्वाभिमुखं स्निग्धाभ्य उत्स्नाताभ्यो वा
> स्नायुभ्यो ग्रीवाभ्यो गलगताभ्यो धमतीभ्यस्ते तव यक्ष्मं वि वृहामि । तथा
> कीकसाभ्योऽस्थिभ्योऽनूक्यादस्थिसंधेश्च यक्ष्मं वि वृहामि ॥ उच समवाये ।
> अनूच्यते समवेयत इत्यस्थः संधिरनूक्यः । ऋहलोर्ण्यत् । चजोः कु घिण्य-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O one seized by disease, from the उष्णिहाभ्य (*uṣṇihābhya*), the sinews that are upward-directed, or oily or bathed, from the ग्रीवाभ्य (*grīvābhya*), those at the neck, the channels (धमतीभ्य (*dhamatībhya*)), I pull out your yakṣma. Likewise I pull out yakṣma from the कीकसाभ्य (*kīkasābhya*), the bones, and from the अनूक्यात् (*anūkyāt*), the joint of the bones." The explanation of अनूक्य (*anūkya*) is from the root उच समवाये (*uca samavāye*): the bone-joint is that which is joined together. (The bhāṣya continues on the next page.)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O one gripped by yakṣma) ते (*te*)—your
- ग्रीवाभ्यः (*grīvābhyaḥ*)—from the blood-vessels in the neck
- उष्णिहाभ्यः (*uṣṇihābhyaḥ*)—from the sinews (nerves)
- कीकसाभ्यः (*kīkasābhyaḥ*)—from the bones
- अनूक्यात् (*anūkyāt*)—from the bone-joint, that is, the joints
- अंसाभ्यां (*aṃsābhyāṃ*)—from the shoulders
- बाहुभ्यां (*bāhubhyāṃ*)—from the arms
- ते (*te*)—your
- दोषण्यं (*doṣaṇyaṃ*)—that is in the roots of the arms
- यक्षं (*yakṣaṃ*)—the yakṣma disease
- वि वृहामि (*vi vṛhāmi*)—I pull out

### Printed p. 1104

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(continued): He adds that दोषण्यं (*doṣaṇyaṃ*) means what arises in the two arms; that disease also, the yakṣma, I pull out from your अंसाभ्यां (*aṃsābhyāṃ*) and बाहुभ्यां (*bāhubhyāṃ*). The upper parts of the two arms are *aṃsau*, the lower parts are बाहू (*bāhū*).

> तोरिति कुत्वं । तित्स्वरितः ॥ अपि च दोष्णोर्भवं दोषण्यं ॥ पूर्ववद्यति पद्दन्नित्यादिना दोःशब्दस्य दोषाणादेशः । पूर्ववत्पकृतिभावः ॥ तमपि यक्ष्मं रोगं
> ते तवांसाभ्यां बाहुभ्यां च वि वृहामि । हस्तयोरूर्ध्वभागावंसावधोभागौ
> बाहू ॥

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O one afflicted by consumption, from the blood-vessels in your neck, from the nerves, from the bones, from their joints, from the shoulders, from the arms, I separate and pull out the yakṣma disease that lies in the roots of your arms.

##### English translation
I banish disease from your neck, from your sinews, from your bones, from your joints, from your upper arms, from your shoulders, and from your fore arms.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आं॒त्रेभ्य॑स्ते॒ गुदा॑भ्यो वनि॒ष्ठोहृद॑या॒दधि॑ ।  
> यक्ष्मं॒ मत॑स्नाभ्यां य॒क्षः प्ला॒शिभ्यो॒ वि वृ॑हामि ते ॥३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आंत्रेभ्यः । ते । गुदाभ्यः । वनिष्ठोः । हृदयात् । अधि ।  
> यक्ष्मं । मतस्नाभ्यां । यक्षः । प्लाशिभ्यः । वि । वृहामि । ते ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे यक्ष्माभिभूत ते तवांत्रेभ्यः । आंत्रं पुरीतदन्नपानयोराधानभूतं ।
> तत्संबंधिभ्यः स्नायुभ्यो गुदाभ्यः याभिर्नाडीभिरन्नरसः समानवायुना धातुषु

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O one overcome by yakṣma, from your आंत्रेभ्यः (*āṃtrebhyaḥ*): आंत्रं (*āṃtraṃ*) is the receptacle of excrement, food and drink; from the sinews connected with it, from the गुदाभ्यः (*gudābhyaḥ*), the channels by which the juice of food, with the samāna wind, …" (the sentence is cut off at the end of this page; the next window continues it).

### Printed p. 1105

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नीयते ताभ्यो नाडीभ्यश्च सॆकाशाद्यक्षं वि वृहामि । तथा वनिष्ठोः स्थविरांत्राद्धृदयादधि हृत्पुंडरीकाच्च यक्षं वि वृहामि । अपि च ते तव मतस्नाभ्यां ।
> मतस्य पार्श्वयोर्वर्तमानानाम्रफलाकृती वृक्त् । ताभ्यां यक्षः । हृदयसमीपे
> वर्तमानः कालमांसविशेषो यकृत् । तस्माच्च ॥ पद्दन्नित्यादिना यकृच्छब्दस्य
> यकन्नादेशः ॥ प्लाशिभ्योऽन्येभ्योऽपि क्लोमप्लीहादिसंज्ञेभ्यश्च मांसेभ्यश्च
> यक्षं रोगं वि वृहामि । उत् क्षिपामि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues his gloss of Ṛk 3. *āṃtraṃ* is the receptacle of the food and drink in the intestines. "From the sinews connected with it, from the गुदाभ्यः (*gudābhyaḥ*) (the channels through which the essence of food is carried by the samāna wind into the bodily tissues), and from those channels, I tear out the यक्षं (*yakṣaṃ*)." Likewise from वनिष्ठोः (*vaniṣṭhoḥ*), the thick intestine, and from the heart, the heart-lotus, I tear it out. Further, मतस्नाभ्यां (*matasnābhyāṃ*) are the two kidneys, shaped like mango fruits and lying at the two sides of the मतस्य (*matasya*). यक्षः (*yakṣaḥ*) is the liver (यकृत् (*yakṛt*)), the black flesh lying near the heart. प्लाशिभ्यः (*plāśibhyaḥ*) means from the other fleshy parts also, called kloma, plīhā and so on. From all these I tear out the disease, that is, I cast it out.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O afflicted one)
- ते (*te*)—your
- आंत्रेभ्यः (*āṃtrebhyaḥ*)—from the entrails
- गुदाभ्यः (*gudābhyaḥ*)—from the channels of the anal region (anus)
- वनिष्ठोः (*vaniṣṭhoḥ*)—from the side regions of the abdomen
- हृदयात् अधि (*hṛdayāt adhi*)—from the heart
- ते (*te*)—your
- मतस्नाभ्यां (*matasnābhyāṃ*)—from the urine-producing organs (kidneys)
- यक्षः (*yakṣaḥ*)—from the bile-producing organ (liver)
- प्लाशिभ्यः (*plāśibhyaḥ*)—from the other fleshy parts
- यक्ष्मं (*yakṣmaṃ*)—the disease called yakṣma
- वि वृहामि (*vi vṛhāmi*)—I separate and tear out

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O afflicted one, from your entrails, anal region, sides of the abdomen, heart, kidneys, gall-bladder and other fleshy parts, and from the blood-vessels and nerves spread through them, I separate and tear out the yakṣma disease that pervades them all.

##### English translation
I banish disease from your entrails, from your anus, from your abdomen, and from your heart, from your kidneys, from your liver, from your (other) viscera.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऊ॒रुभ्यां॑ ते अष्टी॒वद्भ्यां॒ पार्ष्णि॑भ्यां॒ प्रप॑दाभ्यां ।  
> यक्ष्मं॒ श्रोणि॑भ्यां॒ भास॑दा॒द्भंस॑सो॒ वि वृ॑हामि ते ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऊरुभ्यां । ते । अष्टीवत्भ्यां । पार्ष्णिभ्यां । प्रपदाभ्यां ।  
> 70

### Printed p. 1106

> यक्ष्यं । श्रोणिभ्यां । भासदात् । भंससः । वि । वृहामि । ते ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे रुग्ण ते तवोरुभ्यामष्ठीवद्भ्यां जानुभ्यां च यक्ष्यं वि वृहामि । तथा
> पार्ष्टिभ्यां पादस्यापरभागाभ्यां प्रपदाभ्यां पादाग्राभ्यां च यक्ष्यं वि वृहामि ।
> अपि च श्रोणिभ्यां जंघनाभ्यां च यक्ष्यं वि वृहामि । तथा भासदात् । भसत्कटिप्रदेशः । तत्संबंधाद्भसंसो भासमानात्पायोस्ते तव यक्ष्यं वि वृहामि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O sick one, from your two thighs, from the अष्टीवद्भ्यां (*aṣṭīvadbhyāṃ*) (the knees), I tear out the yakṣma. Likewise from the पार्ष्टिभ्यां (*pārṣṭibhyāṃ*), the hinder parts of the feet, and from the प्रपदाभ्यां (*prapadābhyāṃ*), the fore-parts of the feet. Further, from the श्रोणिभ्यां (*śroṇibhyāṃ*), the hips, I tear it out. Likewise from भासदात् (*bhāsadāt*), the shining loin region; and by connection with it, from the shining anal part (*pāyoḥ*) of you, I tear out the yakṣma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O afflicted one)
- ते (*te*)—your
- ऊरुभ्यां (*ūrubhyāṃ*)—from the two thighs
- अष्टीवद्भ्यां (*aṣṭīvadbhyāṃ*)—from the knee regions
- पार्षिभ्यां (*pārṣibhyāṃ*)—from the heels
- प्रपदाभ्यां (*prapadābhyāṃ*)—from the great toes of the feet
- श्रोणिभ्यां (*śroṇibhyāṃ*)—from the hip regions
- भासदात् (*bhāsadāt*)—from the loins
- ते (*te*)—your
- भंससः (*bhaṃsasaḥ*)—from the anal region
- यक्ष्मं (*yakṣmaṃ*)—the yakṣma disease
- वि वृहामि (*vi vṛhāmi*)—I separate and tear out

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O afflicted one, from the regions of your two thighs, knees, heels, great toes of the feet, hips, loins and anus, I separate and tear out the yakṣma disease that pervades them.

##### English translation
I banish disease from your thighs. from your knees, from your heels! from your toes, from your loins, from your buttocks, from your private parts.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मेह॑नाद्वनं॒कर॑णा॒ल्लोम॑भ्यस्ते न॒खेभ्यः॑ ।  
> यक्ष्मं॒ सर्व॑स्मादा॒त्मन॒स्तमि॒दं वि वृ॑हामि ते ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मेहनात् । वनंकरणात् । लोमभ्यः । ते । नखेभ्यः ।  
> यक्ष्यं । सर्वस्मात् । आत्मनः । तं । इदं । वि । वृहामि । ते ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वनंकरणात् । वनमुदकं शारीरं । तत्क्रियते विसृज्यते येन तद्वनंकरणं ॥
> तस्मान्मेहनान्नेढ्रात्ते तव लोमभ्यो नखेभ्यश्च यक्ष्मं वि वृहामि । किं बहुना ।
> इदमिदानीं तं यक्ष्मं सर्वस्मादात्मनः कृत्सादेव ते तव शरीराद्वि वृहामि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वनं (*vanaṃ*) is the water of the body; that by which it is made, that is, discharged, is the वनंकरणं (*vanaṃkaraṇaṃ*). From that, from the मेहनात् (*mehanāt*), the male organ, from your hairs and from your nails, I tear out the yakṣma. Why say more? I tear out this yakṣma now from your whole self, from your entire body.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O one afflicted by yakṣma)
- ते (*te*)—your
- वनंकरणात् (*vanaṃkaraṇāt*)—from the urinary receptacle (bladder)
- मेहनात् (*mehanāt*)—from the organ of urination (urethra)
- लोमभ्यः (*lomabhyaḥ*)—from the hairs
- नखेभ्यः (*nakhebhyaḥ*)—from the nails
- ते (*te*)—your
- सर्वस्मात् आत्मनः (*sarvasmāt ātmanaḥ*)—from all the parts of the body
- तं इदं यक्षं (*taṃ idaṃ yakṣaṃ*)—this yakṣma disease
- वि वृहामि (*vi vṛhāmi*)—I separate and tear out

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O one afflicted by yakṣma, from your bladder, urinary organ, hair and nails, and from all the other regions of your body, I separate and tear out this yakṣma disease.

##### English translation
I banish disease from your urethra, from your bladder. from your hair, from your nails, from your whole person.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अंगा॑दंगा॒ल्लोम्नो॑लोम्नो जा॒तं पर्व॑णि पर्वणि ।  
> यक्ष्यं॒ सर्व॑स्मादा॒त्मन॒स्तमि॒दं वि वृ॑हामि ते ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अंगात् अंगात् । लोम्नः लोम्नः । जातं । पर्वणिपर्वणि ।  
> यक्ष्यं । सर्वस्मात् । आत्मनः । तं । इदं । वि । वृहामि । ते ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अंगादंगात् सर्वेभ्योऽंगेभ्यो लोम्मो लोम्नः सर्वेभ्यो लोमभ्यश्च पर्वणि पर्वण्यवयवानां संधौ जातमुत्पन्नं यक्ष्मं वि वृहामि । अन्यद्धतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

From every limb, from all the limbs, and from every hair, from all the hairs, and from every पर्वणि (*parvaṇi*), the junctions of the parts of the body, I tear out the yakṣma that has arisen. The rest is as already said.**NOTE**

O afflicted one, this yakṣma disease that has arisen in, or pervades, all your limbs, all the pores of your hairs, and all your joints, I separate and tear out from all the parts of your body.

## Sūkta 164 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

The hundred and sixty-fourth sūkta

> अपेहीति पंचर्चं त्रयोदशं सूक्तं । अंगिरसस्य प्रचेतस आर्षं । तृतीया
> त्रिष्टुप् । पंचमी पंक्तिः । दुःस्वप्ननाशनं देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । अपेहि पंच
> प्रचेता दुःस्वप्नघ्नं पंक्त्यंतं त्रिष्टुम्मध्यमिति ॥ लैंगिको विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The thirteenth sūkta, beginning अपेहि (*apehi*), has five ṛks. Its seer is Pracetas of the Aṅgiras line. The third ṛk is Triṣṭubh and the fifth is Paṅkti. The deity is the destruction of bad dreams. The Anukramaṇī says the same: five ṛks, seer Pracetas, deity the slayer of bad dreams, ending in Paṅkti with Triṣṭubh in the middle. The use (viniyoga) is laiṅgika.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, अपेहि (*apehi*), is the thirteenth sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has five ṛks. Its seer is Pracetas of the Aṅgirasa gotra; its deity is the destruction of bad dreams. Its third ṛk is in the Triṣṭubh metre and its fifth ṛk in the Paṅkti metre. The Anukramaṇī says: five ṛks, seer Pracetas, deity the slayer of bad dreams, ending in Paṅkti, with Triṣṭubh in the middle. The use is laiṅgika.

### Printed p. 1109
Sūkta 164. Maṇḍala 10, Anuvāka 12, Sūkta 164. Aṣṭaka 8, Adhyāya 8, Varga 22. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Pracetas. Deity: the slayer of bad dreams. Metre: 1, 2, 4 Anuṣṭubh; 3 Triṣṭubh; 5 Paṅkti.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अपे॑हि मनसस्प॒तेऽप॑ क्राम प॒रश्च॑र ।  
> प॒रो निर्यु॑त्या॒ आ च॑क्ष्व बहु॒धा जीव॑तो॒ मनः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अप । इहि । मनसः । पते । अप । क्राम । परः । चर ।  
> परः । निःऋत्यै । आ । चक्ष्व । बहुधा । जीवतः । मनः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> परः । निःऋत्यै । आ । चक्ष्व । बहुधा । जीवतः । मनः ॥ १ ॥

**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मनसस्पते स्वप्नावस्थस्य मनसः स्वामिन् दुःस्वप्नाधिदेव अपेहि । अपगच्छ!
> स्वप्नावस्थावतो मत्तो निर्गच्छ । निर्गत्य चाप क्राम । देशांतरं गंतुं पादौ विक्षिप ।
> दूरदेशं गच्छेत्यर्थः । अपक्रम्य च परः परस्ताद्विप्रकृष्टे देशे चर । यथेच्छं
> वर्तस्व । अपि च निर्यत्यै पापदेवताय्कॆ परः परस्ताद्वर्तमानाया आ चक्ष्व । वयं
> न बाधनीया इति प्रब्रूहि । जीवतो मम मनो बहुधा बहुप्रकारं भवति ।
> भोक्तव्येषु बहुषु विषयेषूत्सुकं सद्वर्तते । अतस्तद्विनाशकं दुःस्वप्नदर्शनं
> नश्यत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O lord of the mind, that is, O presiding deity of bad dreams, lord of the mind in the dream state: अपेहि (*apehi*), go away, depart from me who am in the dream state. Having departed, अप क्राम (*apa krāma*): move your feet to go to another place; that is, go to a distant place. Having stepped away, चर (*cara*), move about at will, far off in a remote place. Further, आ चक्ष्व (*ā cakṣva*): tell Nirṛti, the deity of sin, who stays far off, "We are not to be harassed." The mind of me, who am alive, is बहुधा (*bahudhā*), of many kinds; it is eager for the many objects to be enjoyed. Therefore may the vision of bad dreams, which destroys it, perish.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मनसः पते (*manasaḥ pate*)—O deity of bad dreams, lord of the mind in the dream state
- अपेहि (*apehi*)—go away from my side, as I am in the dream state
- अप क्राम (*apa krāma*)—go away elsewhere
- परः (*paraḥ*)—from there, still farther
- चर (*cara*)—go as you please
- निर्यत्यै (*niryatyai*)—to the deity of sin called Nirṛti
- आ चक्ष्व (*ā cakṣva*)—tell her that we are not to be harassed
- जीवितः (*jīvitaḥ*)—of me, who am living
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—the mind
- बहुधा (*bahudhā*)—in many ways, that is, it is attached to many objects

### Printed p. 1110

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deity of bad dreams, leave me who am in the dream state and go far away. Go to a distant place wherever you please. Tell Nirṛti, the deity of sin, that she should not harass us. The mind of me, who am alive, is attached to many objects and the like.

##### English translation
Lord of the mind, begone, depart, proceed to a distance: look at Nirriti far off ; the mind of a living being is manifold.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भ॒द्रं वै वरं॑ वृणते भ॒द्रं युं॑जंति॒ दक्षि॑णं ।  
> भ॒द्रं वै॑वस्व॒ते चक्षु॑र्बहु॒त्रा जीव॑तो॒ मनः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भद्रं । वै । वरं । वृणते । भद्रं । युंजंति । दक्षिणं ।  
> भद्रं । वैवस्वते । चक्षुः । बहुत्रा । जीवतः । मनः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> भद्रं वै शोभनमेव वरं वरणीयं दुःस्वप्नविनाशरूपं फलं वृणते ।
> सर्वे जनाः प्रार्थयंते । दक्षिणं प्रवृद्धं भद्रं शोभनं तत्पलं युंजंति ।
> प्राप्नुवंति च । नैवस्वते विवस्वतः पुत्रे यमे विषये भद्रं शोभनमेव चक्षुर्दर्शनमहं प्रार्थये । दुःस्वप्नाधिदेवो नैवस्वतोऽस्मान्मा बाधतां । भद्रमेव
> दर्शनमिह लोकेऽवस्थानलक्षणं करोत्वित्यर्थः । बहुत्रा बहुषु हि विषयेषु
> जीवतो मम मनो वर्तते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

भद्रं वै (*bhadraṃ vai*): the auspicious वरं (*varaṃ*), the desirable fruit, which consists in the destruction of bad dreams, all people pray for. दक्षिणं (*dakṣiṇaṃ*), the grown, auspicious fruit, they युंजंति (*yuṃjaṃti*), that is, they obtain. In regard to वैवस्वते (*vaivasvate*), Yama, the son of Vivasvat, I pray for an auspicious चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*), a good sight. Let Vaivasvata, the presiding deity of bad dreams, not trouble us; let him make a good sight alone, characterised by staying in this world. For the mind of me, who am alive, is engaged बहुत्रा (*bahutrā*), in many objects.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- भद्रं वै (*bhadraṃ vai*)—auspicious
- वरं (*varaṃ*)—the fruit that all need, consisting in the destruction of bad dreams
- वृणते (*vṛṇate*)—all people desire
- दक्षिणं (*dakṣiṇaṃ*)—abundant
- भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)—that auspiciousness
- युंजंति (*yuṃjaṃti*)—all obtain
- वैवस्वते (*vaivasvate*)—in regard to Yama, the son of Vivasvat
- भद्रं (*bhadraṃ*)—auspicious
- चक्षुः (*cakṣuḥ*)—sight I desire
- जीवतः (*jīvataḥ*)—of me, who am living
- मनः (*manaḥ*)—the mind
- बहुत्रा (*bahutrā*)—engages in many objects

### Printed p. 1111

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Everyone desires the auspicious fruit, which takes the form of the destruction of bad dreams, and everyone obtains that excellent auspiciousness. In regard to Yama, the son of Vivasvān, I desire an auspicious sight. The mind of me, who am alive, moves among many kinds of objects.

##### English translation
Men solicit the boon of good fortune, they acquire abundant good fortune, (I desire) the auspicious sight of Vaivaswat; the mind of a living is variously (directed).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदा॒शसा॑ निः॒शसा॑भि॒शसो॑पारि॒म जाग्र॑तो॒ यत्स्व॒पंतः॑ ।  
> अ॒ग्निर्विश्वा॒न प॑ दुष्कृ॒तान्यजु॑ष्टान्या॒रे अ॒स्मद्द॑धातु ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । आशसा । निःशसा । अभिशसा । उपआरिम । जाग्रतः । यत् । स्वसंतः ।  
> अग्निः । विश्वानि । अप । दुःकृतानि । अजुष्टानि । आरे । अस्मत् । दधातु ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यद्दुष्कृतमाशसाशंसनेनाभिलाषेण जाग्रतो जागरणावस्थायां वर्तमाना
> वयमुपारिम उपगतवंतः स्म यच्च स्वपंतः स्वप्नावस्थां प्राप्ता उपगतवंतः स्म ।
> तथा नि सशा निःशंसनेन निर्गताभिलाषेणाभिशसाभिगताभिलाषेण च कारणेनावस्थाद्वये
> यद्दुष्कृतमुपागच्छेम । तानि विश्वानि सर्वाण्यजुष्टान्यसेव्यान्यप्रियाणि ना दुष्कृतानि दुष्कर्माण्यग्निरस्मदारेऽस्मत्तो दूरदेशेऽप दधातु । अपकृष्य स्थापयतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Whatever wrong we have committed, while in the waking state, through "आशसा (*āśasā*)", that is, through wishing or desire, and whatever wrong we have committed while asleep, in the state of dream; and likewise through "निःशसा (*niḥśasā*)", that is, through desire that has departed, and through "अभिशसा (*abhiśasā*)", that is, through desire directed towards something — whatever wrong we may have incurred in the two states because of these causes: all those wrongs, which are unwelcome, not to be served, disagreeable, may Agni set far away from us. May he draw them off and place them at a distance.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जाग्रतः (*jāgrataḥ*)—while in the waking state, or
- स्वपंतः (*svapaṃtaḥ*)—while we are in the dream state
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever sin
- आशसा (*āśasā*)—by speaking with others
- उपारिम (*upārima*)—we have incurred
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever sin
- अभिशसा (*abhiśasā*)—we incur by speaking in opposition to others; whatever sin we have incurred by both these ways
### Printed p. 1112
- अजुष्टानि (*ajuṣṭāni*)—disagreeable
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- दुष्कृतानि (*duṣkṛtāni*)—those evil deeds (sins)
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- अस्मत् अति (*asmat ati*)—far from us
- अप दधातु (*apa dadhātu*)—may he carry away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Whatever sin we gain in the waking state and in the dream state by speaking with other people, by speaking against others, and by these two kinds of ways, all those disagreeable sins or evil deeds, may Agni carry away to a place far from us.

##### English translation
Whatever sin we have committed by speaking to (others), speaking against (others), speaking (evil) about (others), whether waking or sleeping, may Agni remove all such hateful sins for from us.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदिं॑द्र ब्रह्मणस्पतेभिद्रो॒हं चरा॑मसि ।  
> प्रचे॑ता न आंगिर॒सो द्वि॑ष॒तां पा॒त्वंह॑सः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । इंद्र । ब्रह्मणः । पते । अभिद्रोहं । चरामसि ।  
> प्रचेताः । नः । अंगिरसः । द्विषतां । पातु । अंहसः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र हे ब्रह्मणस्पते युवयोर्विषये यदभिद्रोहमभितो द्रोहं
> पापं दुःस्वप्नकारणं चरामसि आचरामः कुर्मः तस्मादभिद्रोहादस्मान्रक्षतमिति
> शेषः । अपि चांगिरसोऽंगिरोऽभिः स्तोतृभिः सबांधवः प्रचेताः प्रकृष्टज्ञानो
> वरुणश्च द्विषतां द्वेष्टणामंहसस्तत्कर्तृकादस्मद्विषयात्पापान्नोऽस्मान्पातु ।
> रक्षतु ॥ यद्वा ॥ विभक्तिव्यत्ययः ॥ अंगिरसमंगिरोगोत्रं प्रचेतसमृषिं नः ॥
> वचनव्यत्ययः ॥ मां द्विषतामंहसः पातु । प्रकृतत्वादिंद्र इति गम्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, O Brahmaṇaspati, whatever "abhidroha" — harm directed at all sides, a sin that is the cause of bad dreams — we commit in respect of you two, protect us from that harm; this is the supplied remainder. Moreover, Varuṇa, *prachetās*, of excellent knowledge, praised by the Aṅgirases, the singers, together with his kinsmen, shall protect us from the sin of the haters, that is, the sin committed by them and directed towards us. Alternatively, there is an interchange of case endings: *aṅgirasam* is the Aṅgiras lineage, and "prachetasam" is the seer, and "नः (*naḥ*)" is an interchange of number: may it protect me from the sin of haters. Since Indra is the subject in hand, it is understood that Indra is the protector.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ब्रह्मणः पते (*brahmaṇaḥ pate*)—O Brahmaṇaspati
- अभिद्रोहं (*abhidrohaṃ*)—the harm that wrongs others
- यत् (*yat*)—whatever sin, the cause of bad dreams
- चरामसि (*carāmasi*)—we commit; protect us from such harm. And
- अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*)—Varuṇa, praised by the singers
- प्रचेताः (*pracetāḥ*)—endowed with excellent knowledge
- द्विषतां (*dviṣatāṃ*)—of the enemies who hate us
- अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)—from the sin
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- पातु (*pātu*)—may he protect. [Or: अंगिरसः (*aṃgirasaḥ*) of the Aṅgiras lineage; प्रचेताः (*pracetāḥ*) me, the seer of this sūkta named Prachetas; द्विषतां अंहसः (*dviṣatāṃ aṃhasaḥ*) from the sin in the form of hatred; पातु (*pātu*) may he protect.]

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, O Brahmaṇaspati, protect us from the sin of wronging others that we may commit. May Varuṇa, praised by the singers and endowed with excellent knowledge, protect us from the enemies we hate, or from sin. Or else, may Indra protect me, the seer of this sūkta of the Aṅgiras lineage named Prachetas, from the sin in the form of hatred towards an enemy.

##### English translation
O Indra, O Brahmanaspati, whatever sin we run into, (save us therefrom), and may the Prachetas of the Angirasas protect us from the malignity of our enemies.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अद्यास्मिन्कालेऽजैष्म । जेतव्यानि सर्वाणि जितवंतोऽभूम दुःस्वप्नस्य नष्टत्वात् । तदनंतरमसनाम च संभक्तव्यानि च समभजाम । तथा वयमनागसोऽनपराधाश्चाभूम । जाग्रत्स्वप्नावस्थयोः संबंधी पापः पापफलरूपः स संकल्पो
> दुःस्वप्नाध्यवसायो यं शत्रुं वयं द्विष्मः तम्मृच्छतु । प्राप्पोतु । यश्च
> नोऽस्मान्वेष्टि तम्मृच्छतु । प्राप्पोतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Today, at this time, we have conquered: we have won everything that was to be won, since the bad dream has been destroyed. After that we have also obtained, that is, shared in, what is to be enjoyed. Likewise we have become free of fault, without offence. The sinful *saṅkalpa* connected with the waking and dream states, having the nature of the fruit of sin, that is, the resolve that gives rise to the bad dream — may it reach the enemy whom we hate. And may it reach him who hates us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- अद्य (*adya*)—now
- अजैष्म (*ajaiṣma*)—have conquered everything by the destruction of the bad dream
- असनाम च (*asanāma ca*)—have obtained all that was to be obtained
- अनागसः (*anāgasaḥ*)—free of sin (free of offence)
- अभूम (*abhūma*)—have become
- जाग्रत्स्वस्थः (*jāgratsvasthaḥ*)—connected with the waking and dream states
- पापः (*pāpaḥ*)—our sin
- सः संकल्पः (*saḥ saṃkalpaḥ*)—and also the evil desire to commit sin
- यं (*yaṃ*)—whichever person
- द्विष्मः (*dviṣmaḥ*)—we hate
- सः (*saḥ*)—that person
- तं (*taṃ*)—that fruit of sin
- ऋच्छतु (*ṛcchatu*)—may he obtain; and
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whichever person
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- द्वेष्टि (*dveṣṭi*)—hates
- तं (*taṃ*)—him
- ऋच्छतु (*ṛcchatu*)—may that fruit of sin go and reach.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Now, by the destruction of the bad dream, it is as though we have conquered everything. We have obtained all that was to be obtained. We have become free of sin, or without offence. May the sin we may have committed in the waking and dream states, and also the evil intent to wrong others, go and reach the enemy whom we hate and who hates us.

##### English translation
We have triumphed to day, we have won, we have become free from guilt; may evil designs formed in waking or sleep be transferred to him whom we hate, be transferred to him who hates us

## Sūkta 165 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In Vedic history birds also have a part. Soma is in many places compared to a bird and even called a bird. In particular Agni is compared to birds or called a bird. The sun too has the name of bird, and in two contexts the name Garutmān. The chief work of a bird in the Veda is (the Gāyatrī metre, in the form of a falcon) to bring to earth the soma plants that were in heaven. According to the Kāṭhaka Upaniṣad it is said that Indra himself, in the form of a falcon, brought soma or amṛta.
### Printed p. 1115
Besides this, other birds too are indicated here and there. Omen-birds and certain animals are sent by the gods. The owl and the pigeon are Yama's messengers. In the Sūtra literature the owl is said to be the messenger of evil deities and a blood-stained bird of prey, and vultures are said to be Yama's messengers. The pigeon mentioned in the present sūkta is well known as the messenger of Nirṛti, the deity of sin, or of Yama, the deity of death. For that reason the coming of a pigeon is said to be an evil omen and a sign of death. In the last sūkta of the second maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda, prayer is made to the omen-bird that it indicate only good omens. Regarding this sūkta, in the Bṛhaddevatā:
आसीदृषिर्दिीर्घतपाः कपोतो नाम नैऋत्यः ॥ ६६ ॥ अकरोत्कपोतस्तस्याष्टामग्निधाने पदं किल । स तदात्महितैर्वाक्यैः कपोतं स्तुतवानृषिः ॥ ६७ ॥ देवा इति तु सूक्तेन प्रायश्चित्तार्थमुच्यते । (*āsīdṛṣirdiīrghatapāḥ kapoto nāma naiṛtyaḥ ‖ 66 ‖ akarotkapotastasyāṣṭāmagnidhāne padaṃ kila | sa tadātmahitairvākyaiḥ kapotaṃ stutavānṛṣiḥ ‖ 67 ‖ devā iti tu sūktena prāyaścittārthamucyate |*)
(Bṛ. De. 8-66, 67)
Formerly there was a seer named Kapota Nairṛtya. He practised austerities for a long time. Once a kapota (a pigeon) set its foot in the fire-pit of this seer, in the forest where he lived. The seer, knowing that the coming of a pigeon is a sign of an evil omen, praised this kapota with words beneficial to himself. It is said that the 165th sūkta, "देवाः कपोत (*devāḥ kapota*)", is to be recited as an expiation, for the removal of the faults he had committed. And in the Ṛgvidhāna:
देवाः कपोत इति तु कपोतस्योपवेशने । सूक्तेन जुहुयादाज्यं यमदूतं हि तं विदुः ॥ (*devāḥ kapota iti tu kapotasyopaveśane | sūktena juhuyādājyaṃ yamadūtaṃ hi taṃ viduḥ ‖*) १०३ (*103*)
(Ṛgvidhāna, adhyāya 4, verse 103)
The pigeon is regarded as the messenger of Yama, that is, of death. If this bird enters a house, there is a likelihood that misfortunes such as death will befall that house. Therefore, as expiation for this fault of an evil omen, it is said that a homa with ghee is to be performed in the consecrated fire with the mantras of this sūkta "देवाः कपोत (*devāḥ kapota*)".
### Printed p. 1116

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवा इति पंचर्चं चतुर्दशं सूक्तं निर्ऋतिपुत्रस्य कपोताख्यस्यार्षं
> त्रैष्टुभं वैश्वदेवं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । देवा नैऋतः कपोतः कपोतोपहतौ
> प्रायश्चित्तमिदं वैश्वदेवमिति ॥ कपोतो यदि गृहं प्रविशेत् तदानेन सूक्तेन
> होतव्यं । सूत्र्यते हि । कपोतश्चेदगारमुपहन्यादनुपतेद्वा देवाः कपोत इति
> प्रत्यृचं जुहुयाज्जपेद्वा । आ. गृ. ३-७-७ i इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta "देवाः (*devāḥ*)", of five Ṛks, the fourteenth, has as its seer Kapota, the son of Nirṛti; its metre is Triṣṭubh and its deity the Viśvedevas. So it is stated in the Anukramaṇī: देवा नैऋतः कपोतः कपोतोपहतौ प्रायश्चित्तमिदं वैश्वदेवमिति ॥ (*devā naiṛtaḥ kapotaḥ kapotopahatau prāyaścittamidaṃ vaiśvadevamiti ‖*) If a pigeon enters a house, a homa is to be made with this sūkta. For it is taught in the sūtra: कपोतश्चेदगारमुपहन्यादनुपतेद्वा देवाः कपोत इति प्रत्यृचं जुहुयाज्जपेद्वा । (*kapotaścedagāramupahanyādanupatedvā devāḥ kapota iti pratyṛcaṃ juhuyājjapedvā |*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-7-7).

Anuvāda: This sūkta "देवाः (*devāḥ*)" is the fourteenth sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka; it has five Ṛks. Its seer is Kapota, its deity the Viśvedevas, its metre Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: "devā nairṛtyaḥ kapotaḥ kapotopahatau prāyaścittaṃ vaiśvadevam". That a homa is to be made in the fire with the mantras of this sūkta when a kapota (pigeon) enters a house is made clear by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra: "kapotaś cedagāram upahanyād anupated vā devāḥ kapota iti pratyṛcaṃ juhuyāj japed vā" (Ā. Gṛ. 3-7-7). **NOTE**

Sūkta 165

Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 23
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5
Seer: Kapota Nairṛta
Deity: Kapotopahatā prāyaścittaṃ Vaiśvadevam
Metre: Triṣṭubh

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> देवाः॑ क॒पोत॑ इषि॒तो यदि॒च्छन्नू॒तो निर्ऋ॑त्या इ॒दमा॑ज॒गाम॑ ।  
> तस्मा॑ अर्चाम कृ॒णवा॑म॒ निष्कृ॑तिं॒ शं नो॑ अस्तु द्वि॒पदे॒ शं  ॑
> चतुष्पदे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> देवाः । कपोतः । इषितः । यत् । इच्छन् । दूतः । निःयत्याः । इदं । आजगाम ।

### Printed p. 1117

> तस्मै । अर्चाम । कृणवाम । निःकृतिं । शं । नः । अस्तु । द्विपदे । शं । चतुःपदे॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवाः इषितः प्राप्तो निर्ऋत्याः पापदेवताया दूतोऽनुचरः कपोतो
> यद्बाधनमिच्छन्नभिलषन्निदमस्मदीयं गृहमाजगाम प्राप्नोत् तस्मै बाधनाय
> तद्बाधननिवृत्त्यर्थमर्चाम । युष्मान्हविषा पूजयाम । ततो निष्कृतिं कपोतप्रवेशजन्यस्य दोषस्य परिहृतिं कृणवाम । अनेन हविर्दानेन करवाम । अतो
> नोऽस्माकं द्विपदे पुत्राय शं सुखमस्तु चतुष्पदे गवाश्वप्रभृतये च शं
> सुखमस्तु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the gods. The pigeon (कपोतः (*kapotaḥ*)) has been sent (इषितः (*iṣitaḥ*), "arrived") as the messenger, the attendant, of Nirṛti, the goddess of evil. Wishing to afflict us, it has come to this house of ours. To remove that affliction we worship you with the oblation. Then we shall perform the expiation (निष्कृतिं (*niṣkṛtiṃ*)), the removal of the fault arising from the pigeon's entry, by this offering of the oblation. Therefore let there be well-being (शं (*śaṃ*)) for our biped (द्विपदे (*dvipade*)), that is, for our son, and well-being for our quadruped (चतुष्पदे (*catuṣpade*)), that is, for cows, horses and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods
- इषितः (*iṣitaḥ*)—who has come here
- निर्यत्याः (*niryatyāḥ*)—of Nirṛti, the goddess of evil (of death)
- दूतः (*dūtaḥ*)—who is the attendant
- कपोतः (*kapotaḥ*)—this pigeon
- यत् (*yat*)—what affliction to us
- इच्छॆन् (*icchèn*)—wishing to cause
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—to our house
- आजगाम (*ājagāma*)—has come
- तस्मै (*tasmai*)—for the removal of that affliction
- अर्चाम (*arcāma*)—we worship you with the oblation (afterwards)
- निष्कृतिं (*niṣkṛtiṃ*)—the expiation, for the removal of the fault arising from the pigeon's entry
- कृणवाम (*kṛṇavāma*)—let us perform it by oblations and the like (by that)
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- द्विपदे (*dvipade*)—for sons and the like
- शं अस्तु (*śaṃ astu*)—let there be happiness
- चतुष्पदे (*catuṣpade*)—for the four-footed beasts, cows and the rest
- शं (*śaṃ*)—let there be happiness

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, this pigeon, the messenger of Nirṛti, the goddess of evil, has now come here, wishing to cause us some affliction, and has come even to our house. To be rid of that affliction we worship you with oblations and the like. Further, to remove the fault arising from the pigeon's entry, we shall also perform an expiation with oblations and the like. Thereby may no harm befall our sons and the rest, nor our cows, horses and other animals, but may there be happiness.

##### English translation
O gods, let us worship for that, desiring which the pigeon sent as Nirriti's messenger, has come to this (ceremony); let us make atonement, may prosperity be given to our bipeds and quadrupeds.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवाः नोऽस्माकं गृहेष्टिषितः कपोताख्यः शकुनः पक्षी शिवः सुखकरोऽनागा अपापहेतुश्चास्तु । हि यस्माद्विप्रो मेधाव्यग्निर्नोऽस्माकं हविर्युष्मभ्यं
> परिकल्पितं जुषतां जुषते अतो युष्मत्प्रसादात्पक्षिणी पक्षोपेता हेतिर्हननहेतुः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O gods, may the bird called the pigeon (कपोताख्यः शकुनः (*kapotākhyaḥ śakunaḥ*)), which has come into our houses, be auspicious (शिवः (*śivaḥ*)), a bringer of happiness, and be faultless (अनागाः (*anāgāḥ*)), a cause of no sin. Since the wise Agni (विप्रः (*vipraḥ*), *medhāvī*) accepts our oblation prepared for you, therefore by your favour let the winged weapon (हेतिः (*hetiḥ*), the cause of killing), the pigeon, avoid us (परि वृणक्तु (*pari vṛṇaktu*)): let it leave us, that is, not trouble us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- गृहेषु (*gṛheṣu*)—in the houses
- इषितः (*iṣitaḥ*)—which has come and settled
- कपोतः शकुनः (*kapotaḥ śakunaḥ*)—this bird called the pigeon
- शिवः अस्तु (*śivaḥ astu*)—let it be auspicious (let it bring only good) and
- अनागाः (*anāgāḥ*)—let it be not a cause of sin
- हि (*hi*)—therefore
- विप्र (*vipra*)—the wise
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- हविः (*haviḥ*)—oblation
- जुषतां (*juṣatāṃ*)—let him enjoy (and by your grace)
- पक्षिणी (*pakṣiṇī*)—winged
- हेति (*heti*)—this pigeon, which has come to kill us
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- परि वृणक्तु (*pari vṛṇaktu*)—let it abandon and go away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, may this pigeon that has come and settled in our houses do us no ill but only good. May it also cause no sin to befall us. Therefore may the wise Agni enjoy the oblation we offer. May this wicked winged pigeon, which has come to kill us, leave us and go away.

May the bird sent to our dwellings, the pigeon, be ausqicious, O gods and void of offence, so that the wise Agni may approve of our oblation, and the winged weapon (of mischief) depart from us.

#### Ṛk 3

> शं नो॒ गोभ्य॑श्च॒ पुरु॑षेभ्यश्चास्तु॒ मा नो॑ हिंसीदि॒ह दे॑वाः  ॒॑
> कपोतः ॥ ३ ॥

> कपोतः ॥ ३ ॥

> पदं स्थानं कृणुते । करोति ! तत्रैव प्रदेशे निवसत्वित्यर्थः। यद्वा! अश्नंत्यस्मिन्नित्याष्ट्री
> पचनशाला ! तस्यां। अग्निधाने यत्र पचनाग्निर्निधीयते तस्मिन्द्रदेशे पदं पादनिधानं
> कृणुते। करोति । तद्देतुको बाधो नोऽस्माकं न भवत्वित्यर्थः । अपि च नोऽस्माकं
> गोभ्यश्च पुरुषेभ्यश्च शं सुखं शंसनीयानां दोषाणां शांतिर्वास्तु । भवतु । हे
> देवाः इहास्मिन्गृहे कपोतो नोऽस्मान्मा हिंसीत् । युद्धदनुग्रहान्मा बाधतां ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The winged weapon (हेतिः (*hetiḥ*), the cause of killing), the pigeon, must not harm (न दभाति (*na dabhāti*)) us. In the आष्ट्यां (*āṣṭyāṃ*), the pervaded, another forest-region, at the अग्निधाने (*agnidhāne*), the place where Agni is deposited (that is, a place with fire), it sets its foot (पदं कृणुते (*padaṃ kṛṇute*)); the meaning is that it should dwell in that very spot. Or else: *āṣṭrī* is the cooking-hall, where people eat; at the अग्निधाने (*agnidhāne*) in it, where the cooking-fire is deposited, in that place it sets its foot. May no affliction arising from that come upon us. Moreover, let there be well-being (शं (*śaṃ*)) for our cattle and our people, or else the quieting of the blameworthy faults. O gods, here in this house let the pigeon not harm us; by your favour let it not afflict us.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्य । दूतः । प्रहितः । एषः । एतत् । तस्मै । यमाय । नमः । अस्तु । मृत्यवे ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उलूको घूकसंज्ञः पक्षी यदशोभनं वदति ब्रवीति आत्मीयेन शब्देन
> सूचयति एतन्मोघं निष्पलमस्तु । कपोतश्चाग्नावग्निमति गृहमध्यॆ यत्पदं कृणोति
> करोति एतदपि मोघं निर्वीर्यमस्तु । प्रहितः प्रेषितः एष कपोतो यस्य
> स्वामिनो दूतोऽनुचरो भवति तस्मै नाम मृत्यवे मारयित्रे यमाय्कॆतन्नमः
> प्रणामोऽस्तु । भवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

What the owl (उलूकः (*ulūkaḥ*), the bird called घूक (*ghūka*)) utters, the inauspicious thing it says, announcing it by its own cry, let that be in vain (मोघं (*moghaṃ*)), fruitless. And that the pigeon sets its foot in the fire, in the midst of a house that has a fire, let that too be in vain, powerless. This pigeon has been sent (प्रहितः (*prahitaḥ*)) as the messenger, the attendant, of a certain master; to him, to Yama, to Death (मृत्यवे (*mṛtyave*)), the killer, let this homage (नमः (*namaḥ*)) be offered.

May the owl's hooting with its evil cry, as an ill omen, be in vain. Likewise may it be in vain that this pigeon sets its foot in the fire-pit to do harm. To Yama, the god of death, whose messenger this pigeon sent here is, let this homage be accepted (be offered).

May that which the owl shrieks be in vain, (and may it be in vain) that the pigeon takes his place upon the fire; may this reverence be paid to Yama, (the god of) Death, as whose messenger he is sent.
