#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं त्यमिं॑द्र॒ सूर्यं॑ प॒श्चा संतं॑ पु॒रस्कृ॑धि ।  
> दे॒वानां॑ चित्ति॒रो वशं॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वं । त्यं । इंद्र । सूर्यं । पश्चा । संतं । पुरः । कृधि ।  
> देवानां । चित् । तिरः । वशं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं त्यं सूर्यमस्तसमये पश्चा पश्चात्संतं भवंतं पुरः परेद्युरुदयकाले पुरस्तात्कृधि । करोषि ॥ लकारव्यत्ययः ॥ कीदृशं । देवानां
> चिद्देवानामपि तिरस्तिरोहितं तैरपि क्व गत इति दुर्विज्ञातं वशं कांतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you make that Sūrya, who at the time of setting is पश्चा (*paścā*) (behind, in the west), stand पुरः (*puraḥ*) (in front, in the east) on the next day, at the time of rising; कृधि (*kṛdhi*) means "you make" (a change of the person-ending). What kind of Sūrya? One who is तिरः (*tiraḥ*), hidden even from the gods, so that where he has gone is hard to know; and वशं (*vaśaṃ*), beloved.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- त्यं (*tyaṃ*)—the well-known
- देवानां चित् (*devānāṃ cit*)—even to the gods (where he is during the night)
- तिरः (*tiraḥ*)—who is unseen
- वशं (*vaśaṃ*)—the shining
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—Sūrya (in the evening)
- पश्चा (*paścā*)—in the western quarter
- संतं (*saṃtaṃ*)—being
- पुरः (*puraḥ*)—(on the next morning) as being in the eastern quarter
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—you make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you make the well-known and shining Sūrya, whose whereabouts in the night even the gods do not know, be in the western quarter in the evening and in the eastern quarter in the morning of the next day.

##### English translation
Bring forward that Surya, Indra, who is lingering behind, the beloved of the gods, (awhile) concealed from them.

## Sūkta 172 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आ याहीति चतुर्यचमेकविंशं सूक्तमांगिरसस्य संवर्तस्यार्षमुषोदेवताकं । चतस्रोऽपि विंशतिका द्विपदा विराजः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । आ याहि
> संवर्त उषस्यं दैपदमिति ॥ प्रथमे छंदोमे वैश्वदेवसूक्तात्पूर्वमिदं
> सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । आ याहि वनसेमा नु कं बभ्रुरेक इति द्विपदासूक्तानि ।
> आ. ८-७ । इति ॥ वाहाव्रतेऽपि निष्केवल्य एतत् । तथैव पंचमारण्यके सूत्रितं ॥
> ऐ. आ. ५-२-२ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn beginning आ याहि (*ā yāhi*), of four Ṛks, is the twenty-first hymn (of the anuvāka). Its seer is Saṃvarta of the Āṅgirasa line; its deity is Uṣas. All four Ṛks are dvipadā virāj of twenty syllables. So the Anukramaṇī says: आ याहि संवर्त उषस्यं दैपदमिति (*ā yāhi saṃvarta uṣasyaṃ daipadamiti*). In the first chandoma this hymn comes before the Vaiśvadeva hymn; it is so prescribed in the sūtra: आ याहि वनसेमा नु कं बभ्रुरेक इति द्विपदासूक्तानि (*ā yāhi vanasemā nu kaṃ babhrureka iti dvipadāsūktāni*) (Ā. 8-7). In the Mahāvrata too it is used in the niṣkevalya; it is likewise prescribed in the fifth Āraṇyaka (Ai. Ā. 5-2-2).

##### Anuvāda

This hymn आ याहि (*ā yāhi*) is the twenty-first hymn in the twelfth anuvāka. It has four Ṛks. Its seer is Saṃvarta of the Aṅgirasa gotra; its deity is Uṣas; the four Ṛks are in the metre dvipadā virāj of twenty syllables. The Anukramaṇī says: "आ याहि संवर्त उषस्यं दैपदं (*ā yāhi saṃvarta uṣasyaṃ daipadaṃ*)". That this hymn is to be recited before the Vaiśvadeva hymn in the first chandoma is explained by the sūtra "Ā yāhi vanasemā nu kaṃ babhrurekā iti dvipadāsūktāni" (Ā. 8-7). That it is employed in the Mahāvrata sacrifice for the niṣkevalya śastra mantras is stated in the fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka by the sentence "आ याहि वनसा सहेति नव समाम्नाताः (*ā yāhi vanasā saheti nava samāmnātāḥ*)" (Ai. Ā. 5-2-2).

##### Particulars

Sūkta 122**NOTE**; Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 172; Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 30. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 4. Seer: Saṃvarta. Deity: Uṣas. Metre: Dvipadā.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ या॑हि॒ वन॑सा स॒ह गावः॑ सचंत वर्त॒निं यदूध॑भिः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । याहि । वनसा । सह । गावः । सचंत । वर्तनिं । यत् । ऊध्भिः ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 1165

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उषः वनसा वननीयेन तेजसा धनेन सार्धमा याहि । आगच्छ । गाव
> उषसो वाहनभूता वर्तनिं रथं सचंत । सेवंते । अतस्तेन रथेनायाहीत्यर्थः ।
> यद्या गाव ऊधभिरुपलक्षिताः प्रभूताः । पीना इत्यर्थः । ता गाव इति संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Uṣas, come together with धनेन (*dhanena*) wealth, which is the desirable brilliance (वनसा (*vanasā*)). The cows, which are Uṣas's draught animals, सचंत (*sacaṃta*) (serve) the वर्तनिं (*vartaniṃ*), the chariot; the meaning is "therefore come by that chariot". Or else: the cows, distinguished by their udders, are abundant, that is, plump; the connection is "those cows".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Uṣas) यत् गावः (*yat gāvaḥ*)—the cows that are Uṣas's draught animals
- ऊधभिः (*ūdhabhiḥ*)—with udders full of milk
- वर्तनिं (*vartaniṃ*)—your chariot
- सचंत (*sacaṃta*)—when they serve, that is, draw it
- वनसा (*vanasā*)—with the radiance (light) that all desire, or with wealth
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—be pleased to come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Uṣas, when your cows, your draught animals, serve, that is, draw your chariot, be pleased to come here with the radiance, or the wealth, that all desire.

##### English translation
Come, (Ushas), with the desirabie (radiance); let the cows who are of full udders accompany your chariot.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ या॑हि॒ वस्वा॑ धि॒या मंहि॑ष्ठो जार॒यन्म॑खः सु॒दानु॑भिः ॥२॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । याहि । वॆस्वा । धिया । मंहिष्ठः । जारयत्ऽमखिः । सुदानुभिः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उषः वस्वा प्रशस्तया धियानुग्रहबुद्धा कर्मणा स्तुत्या वा सार्धमा
> याहि । आगच्छ । स चोषःकालः सुदानुभिः शोभनदानैर्दातृभिः पुरुषैर्मंहिष्ठो
> धनानां दातृतमः अत एव जारयन्मखः समापयद्यज्ञश्च भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Uṣas, come together with वस्वा (*vasvā*) excellent धिया (*dhiyā*), which is a gracious intention, or an act, or praise. And that time of Uṣas is, through the men who are good givers (सुदानुभिः (*sudānubhiḥ*)), the greatest giver of riches (मंहिष्ठः (*maṃhiṣṭhaḥ*)), and therefore it is also what brings the sacrifice to completion (जारयन्मखः (*jārayanmakhaḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Uṣas) वस्वा (*vasvā*)—excellent
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—together with your gracious intention, or praised with acts and hymns
- आ याहि (*ā yāhi*)—be pleased to come
- (that time of Uṣas) सुदानुभिः (*sudānubhiḥ*)—by good givers, men

### Printed p. 1166

- मंहिष्ठः (*maṃhiṣṭhaḥ*)—is venerable
- जारयन्मखः (*jārayanmakhaḥ*)—and brings the sacrifice to completion

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Uṣas, come here with your gracious intention. Or come here praised with act or hymn. The dawn-time that is reached through your coming is a time honoured by generous givers and one that brings the sacrifice to completion.

##### English translation
Come (Ushas), with kindly thoughts; (it is the season) most honoured by the generous, and which bring the sacrifice to completion.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पि॒तु॒भृतो॒ न तंतु॒मित्सु॒दान॑वः॒ प्रति॑ दध्मो॒ यजा॑मसि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पित्रुभ्यतः । न । तंतुं । इत् । सुदानवः । प्रति । दध्मः । यजामसि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पितृभृतो नान्नस्य भर्तार इव सुदानवः शोभनदाना वयं तंतुमित्तंतुं
> विस्तीर्णमेव प्रति दध्मः । उषसं प्रत्युपायनरूपेण धारयामः । तेन च यज्ञेन
> तामुषसं यजामसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Like bearers of food for their fathers (पितृभृतो न (*pitṛbhṛto na*)), we, good givers (सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*)), प्रति दध्मः (*prati dadhmaḥ*) the तंतुमित्— (*taṃtumit—*), that is, a spread-out offering: we hold it ready as an offering to Uṣas. And with that sacrifice we worship that Uṣas (यजामसि (*yajāmasi*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Uṣas) पितुभृतः न (*pitubhṛtaḥ na*)—like those who stand holding the food in the form of oblation, in order to offer it to you
- सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*)—we, who are endowed with good gifts
- तंतुमित् (*taṃtumit*)—abundantly (in large measure)
- प्रति दध्मः (*prati dadhmaḥ*)—we stand holding oblations and the like in order to offer them
- यजामसि (*yajāmasi*)—with those oblations we worship Uṣas by way of sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Uṣas, we who stand holding food in the form of oblation just in order to offer it to you, being endowed with good gifts, hold in our hands abundant oblations and the like to offer; and with them we worship Uṣas by way of sacrifice.

### Printed p. 1167
*Printed English*
Like bearers of food, liberal in our gifts, we spread the thread (of sacrifice before the dawn), and worship (her.)

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒षा अप॒ स्वसु॒स्तमः॒ सं व॑र्तयति वर्त॒निं सु॑जा॒तता॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उषाः । अप । स्वसुः । तमः । सं । वर्तॆयति । वर्तनिं । सुजातता ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दशमेऽहनि प्रातरनुवाक उषस्ये क्रतावुषो भद्रेभिरित्यस्याः स्थान उषा अप
> स्वसुरित्येषा । सूत्रितं च । उषा अप स्वसुस्तम इति पच्छो द्विपदां त्रिरुषस्ये ।
> आ. ८-१२ । इति ॥
> इयमुषाः स्वसुर्भगिन्या रात्रेः संबंधि तमोऽंधकारमप सं वर्तयति ।
> आत्मीयेन तेजसापगमयति । सुजातता सुजातत्वमात्मनः सुप्रजातत्वं च वर्तनिं
> रथं प्रापयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the tenth day, in the morning litany (prātaranuvāka), this verse is used in the Uṣas hymn, in the place of the verse *kratāvuṣo bhadrebhiḥ*. The sūtra says: उषा अप स्वसुस्तम इति पच्छो द्विपदां त्रिरुषस्ये (*uṣā apa svasustama iti paccho dvipadāṃ triruṣasye*) (Ā. Sū. 8-12). Sāyaṇa explains: this Uṣas drives away the darkness belonging to her sister, the night, by her own radiance. Her good birth, that is, her own fair birth and fair offspring, brings the chariot (vartani) to her.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उषाः (*uṣāḥ*)—this goddess Uṣas
- स्वसुः (*svasuḥ*)—of her sister, the night
- तमः (*tamaḥ*)—the darkness
- अप सं वर्तयति (*apa saṃ vartayati*)—drives away with her radiance
- सुजातता (*sujātatā*)—her own excellent birth (manifestation)
- वर्तनिं (*vartaniṃ*)—provides her chariot to her

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This goddess Uṣas scatters and drives away, with her radiance, the darkness of the night, who is like her sister. Her own excellent manifestation makes ready the chariot for her.

##### English translation
Ushas drives away the darkness of her sister (night); her generative benevolence (harnesses) her chariot.

### Printed p. 1168
## Sūkta 173 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
In this hymn and the next, the king is consecrated in the kingdom, and when he sets out for battle the priest instructs him for his good, blesses him and sends him off. The Ṛgvidhāna speaks of this matter thus:

राजानमभिषिच्येत तिष्येण श्रवणेन वा । पौष्ट्षा सावित्रसौम्याश्विरोहिणीषूत्तरासु च ॥ १०७ ॥ (*rājānamabhiṣicyeta tiṣyeṇa śravaṇena vā | pauṣṭṣā sāvitrasaumyāśvirohiṇīṣūttarāsu ca ‖ 107 ‖*) हुत्वाग्निं राजलिंगाभिः सावित्र्या प्रयतः शुचिः । महाव्याहृतिभिश्चैव संपाताभिहुतो भवेत् ॥ १०८ ॥ (*hutvāgniṃ rājaliṃgābhiḥ sāvitryā prayataḥ śuciḥ | mahāvyāhṛtibhiścaiva saṃpātābhihuto bhavet ‖ 108 ‖*) सर्वौषधिरसैः श्लक्ष्म्यर्नदीनां सलिलेन च । व्याघ्रचर्मण्यथासीनमासंध्यामभिषिच्य तं ॥ १०९ ॥ (*sarvauṣadhirasaiḥ ślakṣmyarnadīnāṃ salilena ca | vyāghracarmaṇyathāsīnamāsaṃdhyāmabhiṣicya taṃ ‖ 109 ‖*) तिष्ठन्प्रत्यज्मुखो ब्रूयाज्जय त्वं पृथिवीमिमां । धर्मस्ते निखिलो राजन् वर्धतां पालय प्रजाः ॥ ११० ॥ (*tiṣṭhanpratyajmukho brūyājjaya tvaṃ pṛthivīmimāṃ | dharmaste nikhilo rājan vardhatāṃ pālaya prajāḥ ‖ 110 ‖*) वर्धस्व त्वं श्रियै पुष्टै जयायाभ्युदयाय च । राजानः संतु ते गोत्रे ततोऽप्रतिरथं जपेत् ॥ १११ ॥ (*vardhasva tvaṃ śriyai puṣṭai jayāyābhyudayāya ca | rājānaḥ saṃtu te gotre tato 'pratirathaṃ japet ‖ 111 ‖*) वैयाघ्रं तु भवेच्चर्म समिदौ दुंबरी भवेत् । त्रिरेनमभिषिच्यैवं दुंदुभीनभिमंत्रयेत् ॥ ११२ ॥ (*vaiyāghraṃ tu bhaveccarma samidau duṃbarī bhavet | trirenamabhiṣicyaivaṃ duṃdubhīnabhimaṃtrayet ‖ 112 ‖*) प्राच्यां त्वा दिशि वसवो अभिषिंचंतु तेजसे । दक्षिणस्यां त्वा दिशि रुद्रा अभिषिंचंतु वृद्धये ॥ ११३ ॥ (*prācyāṃ tvā diśi vasavo abhiṣiṃcaṃtu tejase | dakṣiṇasyāṃ tvā diśi rudrā abhiṣiṃcaṃtu vṛddhaye ‖ 113 ‖*) प्रतीच्यां त्वा दिश्यादित्या अभिषिंचंतु पुष्टये । विश्वेदेवा उदीच्यां तु अभिषिंचंतु श्रेयसे ॥ ११४ ॥ (*pratīcyāṃ tvā diśyādityā abhiṣiṃcaṃtu puṣṭaye | viśvedevā udīcyāṃ tu abhiṣiṃcaṃtu śreyase ‖ 114 ‖*) अभिषिच्य च राजानमाशीर्भिरभिनंद्य च । आ त्वाहार्षमंतरेधीत्यथैनमभिमंत्रयेत् ॥ ११५ ॥ (*abhiṣicya ca rājānamāśīrbhirabhinaṃdya ca | ā tvāhārṣamaṃtaredhītyathainamabhimaṃtrayet ‖ 115 ‖*) (Ṛgvidhāna, adhyāya 4, verses 107-115)

The Kannada explains: Disciple, the king should be given the royal consecration on an auspicious day with a favourable lunar mansion, such as Śravaṇa. The king to be consecrated, purified, self-controlled and equipped with the royal insignia, should offer an oblation of ghee into the fire according to rule. Then the priest should seat the king on a seat made of tiger skin

### Printed p. 1169
and consecrate him with all the juices of herbs and with the water of the best rivers. Then, standing before that king, he should say: "O king, conquer this whole earth. May dharma increase in your country. Protect the subjects with dharma. May your lineage prosper." Having said this, he should recite silently the Apratiratha hymn आशुः शिशानः (*āśuḥ śiśānaḥ*) (10-103). A tiger-skin seat is best for the king to sit on, and fuel sticks of udumbara wood for the fire offering. After consecrating the king three times, he should consecrate the war-drum with mantras. Then: "O king, may the eight Vasus in the eastern quarter consecrate you for your splendour; likewise may the eleven Rudras in the southern quarter consecrate you for your growth; may the twelve Ādityas in the western quarter consecrate you for your nourishment; may the Viśvedevas in the northern quarter consecrate you for your welfare." With these mantras recited, he should consecrate him. Afterwards he should bless the king and congratulate him. Then, the king having set out for battle, he should consecrate him with the present hymn आ त्वाहार्षमंतरेधि (*ā tvāhārṣamaṃtaredhi*). So it is said.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आ त्वेति षडृचं द्वाविंशं सूक्तमांगिरसस्य ध्रुवस्यार्षमानुष्टुभं । अभिषिक्तस्य राज्यः स्तुतिरूपोऽर्थो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । अ त्वा षट् ध्रुवो
> राज्यः स्तुतिस्तानुष्टुभं त्विति ॥ राज्यो युद्धाय संनहनेऽनेन सूक्तेनाभिमंत्रणं पुरोधसा कर्तव्यं । सूत्रितं च । आ त्वाहार्षमंतरेधीति पश्चाद्रथस्यावस्थाय । अ. गृ. ३-१२-२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This hymn आ त्वा (*ā tvā*) has six verses and is the twenty-second hymn. Its seer is Dhruva Āṅgirasa; its metre is Anuṣṭubh. Its deity is the subject-matter, the praise of the consecrated king. The Anukramaṇī says: अ त्वा षट् ध्रुवो राज्यः स्तुतिस्तानुष्टुभं त्विति (*a tvā ṣaṭ dhruvo rājyaḥ stutistānuṣṭubhaṃ tviti*). When the king sets out to battle, the priest should consecrate him with this hymn. The sūtra says: आ त्वाहार्षमंतरेधीति पश्चाद्रथस्यावस्थाय (*ā tvāhārṣamaṃtaredhīti paścādrathasyāvasthāya*) (Aś. Gṛ. 3-12-2).

Anuvāda: This hymn आ त्वा (*ā tvā*) is the twenty-second hymn in the twelfth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Its seer is Dhruva, a son of Aṅgiras; the metre is Anuṣṭup. Since in this hymn the king consecrated to the kingdom is praised, that meaning of praise is itself the deity of the hymn; the Anukramaṇī says: आ त्वा षट् ध्रुवो राज्ञः स्तुतिस्त्वानुष्टुभं तु (*ā tvā ṣaṭ dhruvo rājñaḥ stutistvānuṣṭubhaṃ tu*). That the priest should consecrate the king with this hymn and bless him when the king sets out for battle is explained by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtra aphorism आ त्वाहार्षमंतरेधीति पश्चाद्रथस्यावस्थाय (*ā tvāhārṣamaṃtaredhīti paścādrathasyāvasthāya*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-12-2).

Sūkta 173. Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 13. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 31. Number of Ṛks in the hymn: 6. Seer: Dhruva. Deity: praise of the king. Metre: Anuṣṭup.

> आ त्वा॑हार्षमं॒तरे॑धि ध्रु॒वस्ति॒ष्ठा वि॑चाचलिः ।

> विशः । त्वा । सर्वाः । वांछंतु । मा । त्वत् । राष्ट्रं । अधि । भ्रशत् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे राजन् त्वा त्वामाहार्षं । अस्मद्राष्ट्रस्य स्वामित्वेनानैषं । स त्वमंतरस्मासु मध्य विधि । स्वामी भव । ध्रुवो नित्यः सन्नविचाचलिरतिशयेन चलनरहित एव
> संस्तिष्ठ । राष्ट्रमधितिष्ठ । सर्वाश्च विशः प्रजास्तां वांछंतु । अयमेवास्माकं
> राजास्त्विति कामयंतु ॥ वाभि इच्छायां ॥ त्वत् त्वत्तः सकाशाद्राष्ट्रं राज्यं माधि
> भ्रशत् । मा भ्रश्यतु । मा वियुक्तं भवतु ॥ भन्यु अधःपतने ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O king, I have brought you", that is, led you here to be master of our kingdom. Be master amid us. Remaining ध्रुवः (*dhruvaḥ*), constant, and अविचाचलिः (*avicācaliḥ*), utterly free of wavering, stand firm; stand over the kingdom. May all the subjects desire you, wishing "Let this man alone be our king" (root वाभि (*vābhi*), to wish). May the kingdom not fall from you, that is, not be separated from you (root भन्यु (*bhanyu*), falling down).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- आ अहार्षं (*ā ahārṣaṃ*)—I have brought you, making you lord of this kingdom; such as you are
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—in our midst
- विधि (*vidhi*)—be master over us
- ध्रुवः (*dhruvaḥ*)—firm-minded
- अविचाचलिः (*avicācaliḥ*)—unwavering (that is, not harmed by anyone)
- तिष्ठ (*tiṣṭha*)—stand firm in the kingdom
- सर्वाः विशः (*sarvāḥ viśaḥ*)—all the subjects
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- वांछंतु (*vāṃchaṃtu*)—desire (that you be our king)
- त्वत् (*tvat*)—from you
- राष्ट्रं (*rāṣṭraṃ*)—the kingdom
- मा अधि भ्रशत् (*mā adhi bhraśat*)—may it not slip away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O king, I have brought you, consecrated, as lord of this kingdom. Be our master in our midst. Firm-minded, unharmed by enemies, not fallen from your station, remain steady in this kingdom itself and protect us. May all the subjects desire you alone, that you be our king. May this kingdom not slip from you.

### Printed p. 1171

##### English translation
I have consecrated you, (Raja); come amongst us, be steady and unvacillating; may all your subjects desire you (for their king), may the kingdom never fall from you.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This hymn is uttered by the king's priest in the form of a blessing, and counsel for the king's good is given. The rites and mantras for consecrating a king in the kingdom are stated in the 37th chapter of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O king, be here, in this very kingdom": always remain as master. Do not fall away; do not depart. As a mountain stands in immovability, so be अविचाचलिः (*avicācaliḥ*), free of wavering. ##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ध्रुवा । द्यौः । ध्रुवा । पृथिवी । ध्रुवासः । पर्वताः । इमे ।  
> ध्रुवं । विश्वं । इदं । जगत् । ध्रुवः । राजा । विशां । अयं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्यौर्ध्रुवा स्थिरा भवति । पृथिवी च ध्रुवा स्थिरा भवति । इमे दृश्यमानाः
> पर्वता महीधराश्च ध्रुवासः स्थिराः । इदं विश्वं सर्वं जगद्भुवं स्थिरं भवति ।
> एवमेवायं विशां प्रजानां राजा स्वामी सन् ध्रुवः स्थिरो भवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Heaven is firm, that is, steadfast; the earth too is firm. These visible mountains, the earth-bearers, are firm. This whole world, all that moves, is firm. In the same way let this king, being lord of the विशां (*viśāṃ*) (the people), be firm and steadfast.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—the heavenly world
- ध्रुवा (*dhruvā*)—is firm
- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—this earth
- ध्रुवा (*dhruvā*)—is firm indeed
- इमे पर्वताः (*ime parvatāḥ*)—these mountains before us
- ध्रुवासः (*dhruvāsaḥ*)—are firm
- विश्वं (*viśvaṃ*)—entire
- इदं जगत् (*idaṃ jagat*)—this world
- ध्रुवं (*dhruvaṃ*)—is firm (in this very manner)
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this king
- विशां (*viśāṃ*)—to the subjects
- राजा (*rājā*)—as lord
- ध्रुवः (*dhruvaḥ*)—let him be firm

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This heaven, the earth, these mountains, this whole world are firm. Likewise let this king, the protector of his subjects, be firm.

### Printed p. 1174

##### English translation
Firm is the heaven, firm is the earth, firm are these mountains, firm is this entire world, so may this king of men be firm.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ध्रु॒वं ते॒ राजा॒ वरु॑णो ध्रु॒वं दे॒वो बृह॒स्पतिः॑ ।  
> ध्रु॒वं त॒ इंद्र॑श्चा॒ग्निश्च॑ रा॒ष्ट्रं धा॑रयतां ध्रु॒वं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ध्रुवं । ते । राजा । वरुणः । ध्रुवं । देवः । बृहस्पतिः ।  
> ध्रुवं । ते । इंद्रः । च । अग्निः । च । राष्ट्रं । धारयतां । ध्रुवं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे राजन् ते तव राष्ट्रं राजा राजमानो वरुणो ध्रुवं स्थिरं धारयतु ।
> देवो दानादिगुणयुक्तो बृहस्पतिर्ध्रुवं धारयतु । इंद्रश्चाग्निश्चोभावपि ते तव
> राष्ट्रं ध्रुवं स्थिरं धारयतां । इंद्राग्नोरुभयोरपेक्षया ध्रुवशब्दस्य द्विः
> प्रयोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O king, let Varuṇa, the shining king, hold your kingdom firm. Let the divine Bṛhaspati, endowed with the qualities of generosity and the like, hold it firm. Let Indra and Agni, both of them, hold your kingdom firm. The word ध्रुव (*dhruva*) is used twice with regard to the two, Indra and Agni.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O king) ते (*te*)—your
- राष्ट्रं (*rāṣṭraṃ*)—kingdom
- राजा (*rājā*)—the shining
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- ध्रुवं (*dhruvaṃ*)—let him hold so that it be firm
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—endowed with generosity and other qualities
- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Bṛhaspati
- ध्रुवं (*dhruvaṃ*)—let him make firm
- इंद्रः च (*iṃdraḥ ca*)—Indra
- अग्निः च (*agniḥ ca*)—and Agni, both
- ते राष्ट्रं (*te rāṣṭraṃ*)—your kingdom
- ध्रुवं (*dhruvaṃ*)—so that it be firm
- धारयतां (*dhārayatāṃ*)—let them hold

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(O king) may the shining Varuṇa, Bṛhaspati endowed with generosity and other qualities, and Indra and Agni hold and protect your kingdom so that it remains firm.

##### English translation
May the royal Varuna, the divine Brihaspati, may Indra and Agni ever give stability to your kingddom.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ध्रु॒वं ध्रु॒वेण॑ ह॒विषा॒भि सोमं॑ मृशामसि ।  
> अथो॑ त॒ इंद्रः॒ केव॑ली॒र्विशो॑ बलि॒हृत॑स्करत् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ध्रुवं । ध्रुवेण । हविषा । अभि । सोमं । मृशामसि ।  
> अथो इति । ते । इंद्रः । केवलीः । विशः । बलिहृतः । करत् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ध्रुवेण स्थिरेण हविषा पुरोडाशादिना युक्तं ध्रुवं स्थिरं सोममभि
> मृशामसि । अभिमृशामः । देवतामभिलक्ष्य यागार्थं वयमृत्विजः संस्पृशामः ।
> अथो अथानंतरमेवेंद्रो विशः प्रजास्ते तनैव केवलीरसाधारणाः सतीर्बलिहृतः
> करस्य प्रदात्रीः करत् । करोतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We touch the firm Soma, accompanied by a firm oblation such as the puroḍāśa. Having the deity in view, we priests touch it for the sacrifice. Then Indra makes your subjects wholly yours, not shared with others, payers of the tax (बलिहृतः (*balihṛtaḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ध्रुवेण (*dhruveṇa*)—that which is firm
- हविषा (*haviṣā*)—that which is accompanied by an oblation such as the puroḍāśa
- ध्रुवं (*dhruvaṃ*)—and firm
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- अभि मृशामसि (*abhi mṛśāmasi*)—we touch
- अथो (*atho*)—afterwards
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विशः (*viśaḥ*)—the subjects
- ते केवलीः (*te kevalīḥ*)—devoted to you alone
- बलिहृतः (*balihṛtaḥ*)—giving you taxes and the like (revenue)
- करत् (*karat*)—let him make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We priests touch, for the sacrifice, the firm Soma that is accompanied by a firm oblation such as the puroḍāśa. Afterwards may Indra grant that the subjects offer you loyalty to the king and tributes such as taxes.

##### English translation
With a constant oblation we handle the constant Soma ; therefore may Indra render your subject people payers of (their) taxes.

## Sūkta 174 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अभीवर्तेनेति पंचर्चं त्रयोविंशं सूक्तमांगिरसस्याभीवर्ताख्यस्यार्षमानुष्टुभं । पूर्ववद्राजस्तुतिर्देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । अभीवर्तेन पंचाभीवर्त इति ॥ पुरोहित इदं सूक्तं राजानं युद्धाय कृतसंनाहं वाचयीत ।
> सूत्रते हि । अथैनं सारयमाणमुपारुह्याभीवर्तं वाचयति । आ. गृ. ३-१२-१२ ।
> इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta अभीवर्तेन (*abhīvartena*) has five Ṛks and is the twenty-third sūkta. Its seer is Abhīvarta of the Āṅgirasa line; its metre is Anuṣṭubh; as before, the praise of the king is the deity. The Anukramaṇī says: अभीवर्तेन पंचाभीवर्त इति॥ (*abhīvartena paṃcābhīvarta iti‖*). The purohita should have the king, equipped for battle, recite this sūkta. For it is prescribed: अथैनं सारयमाणमुपारुह्याभीवर्तं वाचयति (*athainaṃ sārayamāṇamupāruhyābhīvartaṃ vācayati*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-12-12).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta अभीवर्तेन (*abhīvartena*) is the twenty-third sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. Its seer is Abhīvarta of the Aṅgirasa gotra; as in the previous sūkta, its deity is the praise of the king; its metre is Anuṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: Abhīvarta, with अभिवर्तेन (*abhivartena*), five. When the king sets out ready for battle, the purohita should have him recite this sūkta. This is set out in the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya sūtra अथैनं सारयमाणमुपारुह्याभीवर्तं वाचयति (*athainaṃ sārayamāṇamupāruhyābhīvartaṃ vācayati*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-12-12).

Sūkta 174
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 174.
Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 32.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5.
Ṛṣi: Abhīvarta.
Devatā: praise of the king.
Chandas: Anuṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भी॒व॒र्तेन॑ ह॒विषा॒ यॆनेंद्रो॑ अभिवावृ॒ते ।  
> तेना॒स्मान्ब्र॑ह्मणस्पते॒ऽभि रा॒ष्ट्राय॑ वर्तय ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभिवर्तेन । हविषा । येन । इंद्रः । अभिववृते ।  
> तेन । अस्मान् । ब्रह्मणः । पते । अभि । राष्ट्राय । वर्तय ।

### Printed p. 1177

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अभीवर्तेन अभिगच्छत्यनेनेत्यभीवर्तः ॥ करणे घञ् । थाथादिस्वरेणोत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं । उपसर्गस्य घञ्यामनुष्ये बहुलं । पा. ६-३-१२२ । इति दीर्घः ॥
> ईदृशेन येन हविषा साधनेनेंद्रोऽभिववृते सर्वमभिजगाम तेन हविषेष्टवतोऽस्मान् हे ब्रह्मणसस्पते राष्ट्राय राज्यं प्राप्तमभि वर्तय । अभिगमय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अभीवर्त (*abhīvarta*) is that by which one goes toward (an object). By such an oblation, as the means by which Indra went over everything, do you, O Brahmaṇaspati, bring us, who have sacrificed with that oblation, to the kingdom, that is, to sovereignty obtained; make us approach it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अभीवर्तेन (*abhīvartena*)—called Abhīvarta, or offered by me, Abhīvarta
- येन हविषा (*yena haviṣā*)—by which oblation
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अभिववृते (*abhivavṛte*)—conquered everything
- तेन (*tena*)—offering with that oblation
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- ब्रह्मणस्पते (*brahmaṇaspate*)—O Brahmaṇaspati
- राष्ट्राय (*rāṣṭrāya*)—for the attainment of kingship
- अभि वर्तय (*abhi vartaya*)—impel

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Brahmaṇaspati, by that oblation called Abhīvarta, through which Indra became able to conquer the entire world, make us who offer with that oblation eager to exert ourselves for the attainment of the kingdom.

##### English translation
By the abhivarta oblation, whereby Indra has conquered (everything) do you, O Brahmanaspati, bring us to sovereign rule.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि॒वृत्य॑ स॒पत्ना॑ न॒भि या नो॒ अरा॑तयः ।  
> अ॒भि पृ॑त॒न्यंतं॑ तिष्ठा॒भि यो न॑ इर॒स्यति॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभिवृत्य । सपत्नान् । अभि । याः । नः । अरातयः ।  
> अभि । पृतन्यंतं । तिष्ठ । अभि । यः । नः । इरस्यति ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 1178

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे राजन् सपत्नान् शत्रून् अभिवृत्य अभितो गमयित्वा नः अस्माकं याः
> अरातयः अदानशीलाः प्रजाः संति ता अपि अभि तिष्ठ अभिभव । पृतन्यंतं पृतनाः सेना
> आत्मन इच्छंतं युयुत्तुं च अभि तिष्ठ ॥ पृतनाशब्दात् क्यचि कव्यध्वरपृतनस्य इत्यंतलोपः ॥ यः च नः अस्मभ्यं इरस्यति ईर्ष्यति । इरस् तिरस् ईर्षायां कंड्वादिः ।
> तमपि अभि तिष्ठ । यद्वा । प्रकृतो ब्रह्मणस्पतिरेवात्रापि संबोध्यः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O king, having brought rivals and enemies near, overcome also those of our subjects who are अरातयः (*arātayaḥ*), not given to giving. Overcome too him who wishes armies for himself and desires to fight. And overcome him who is envious of us (इरस्यति (*irasyati*)). Or else, Brahmaṇaspati, the subject of the preceding verse, is to be addressed here also.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O king) सपत्नान् (*sapatnān*)—enemies
- अभिवृत्य (*abhivṛtya*)—besieging on all sides
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- याः अरातॆयः (*yāḥ arātèyaḥ*)—those subjects (or enemies) who give nothing
- अभितिष्ठ (*abhitiṣṭha*)—defeat them also
- पृतन्यंतं (*pṛtanyaṃtaṃ*)—the enemy who fights with an army
- अभि तिष्ठ (*abhi tiṣṭha*)—defeat
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whoever
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- इरस्यति (*irasyati*)—disparages with base words
- अभि (*abhi*)—defeat him too

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O king, besiege the enemies and defeat them. Defeat also enemies of other kinds; defeat the enemy who fights with an army; defeat him too who disparages us with contemptuous speech.

##### English translation
Having overcome our rivals, and those who are our enemies, do you, attack him who assaults us, and him who behaves insolently towards us.

> अ॒भि त्वा॒ विश्वा॑ भू॒तान्य॑भीव॒र्तो यथास॑सि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । त्वा । विश्वा । भूतानि । अभिवर्तः । यथा । अससि ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 1179

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे राजन् देवो दानादिगुणयुक्तः सविता त्वा त्वामभ्यवीवृतत् । अभिवर्तयतु । अभिगमयतु राष्ट्रं । सोमश्चाभिवर्तयतु । विश्वा विश्वानि सर्वाण्यपि
> भूतानि पृथिव्यादीनि त्वामभि वर्तयंतु । यथा येन प्रकारेण त्वमभीवर्तोऽसि ।
> अभितः सर्वत्र वर्तमानो भवसि ॥ अस्तेश्चांदसः शपो लुगभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O king, may the divine Savitṛ, endowed with the quality of generosity and the like, turn toward you and bring the kingdom to you; and may Soma turn it toward you. May all beings, earth and the rest, turn toward you, in the manner in which you are अभिवर्तः (*abhivartaḥ*), one who exists everywhere on all sides.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे राजन् (*he rājan*)—O king
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—endowed with generosity and the like, or shining
- सविता (*savitā*)—the god Savitṛ
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अभि अवीवृतत् (*abhi avīvṛtat*)—may he establish firmly in the kingdom
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma too
- अभि (*abhi*)—may he establish
- यथा (*yathā*)—in the manner in which you
- अभिवर्तः अससि (*abhivartaḥ asasi*)—are established everywhere
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- भूतानि (*bhūtāni*)—beings, earth and the rest
- अभि (*abhi*)—may they establish you in the kingdom

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O king, may the god Savitṛ, endowed with generosity and the like or shining, and Soma, establish you firmly in the kingdom. As you exist everywhere possessed of authority, so may all beings, earth and the rest, establish you in the kingdom so that you remain there permanently.

##### English translation
May the divine Savitri, may Soma establish you, (raja); may all beings establish you, so that you may be supreme.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> येनेंद्रो हविषा कृत्त्व भवद्दु न्मुत्यमः ।  
> इ॒दं तद॑क्रि देवा असप॒त्नः किला॑भुवं ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> येन । इंद्रः । हविषा । कृत्वी । अभवत् । द्युम्ना । उत्तमः ।  
> इदं । तत् । अक्रि । देवाः । असपत्नः । किल । अभुवं ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 1180

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> येन हविषास्माभिर्दत्तेन माद्यन्निंद्रः कृत्वी वृत्रवधादेः कर्मणः कर्ताभवत् द्युम्ना । द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो वान्नं ना । तद्वान् अत एवोत्तम
> उत्कृष्टतमश्चाभवत् तदिदं हविर्हे देवाः अक्रि । अकारि । यद्वा । अहमकार्षं ।
> अत एवाहमसपत्नः किलाभुवं । शत्रुरहितोऽप्यभवं खलु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By the oblation given by us, delighting in which Indra became the doer of deeds such as the slaying of Vṛtra, and being द्युम्ना (*dyumnā*) (द्युम्नं (*dyumnaṃ*) from *dyotateḥ*: glory, or food), possessed of it and therefore the most excellent, that same oblation, O gods, has been made (अक्रि (*akri*) = अकारि (*akāri*)). Or else: "I have made it." Therefore I have indeed become without rivals, free of enemies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- येन हविषा (*yena haviṣā*)—by which oblation offered by us, delighted
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- कृत्वी (*kṛtvī*)—capable of doing bold deeds such as slaying Vṛtra
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—became
- द्युम्ना (*dyumnā*)—became possessed of fame
- उत्तमः (*uttamaḥ*)—excellent
- तत् इदं (*tat idaṃ*)—this oblation
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods
- अक्रि (*akri*)—I have offered to you (therefore I)
- असपत्नः किल (*asapatnaḥ kila*)—without enemies
- अभुवं (*abhuvaṃ*)—have become

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This excellent oblation, by which, being satisfied, Indra became capable of bold deeds such as slaying Vṛtra and became renowned, I have offered to you, O gods. Therefore I have become free of enemies.

##### English translation
The oblation whereby Indra became heroic, renowned and eminent, I have offered, O gods, (to you), may I become freed from my rivals.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सपत्नहा सपत्नानां शत्रूणां हंता अत एवासपत्नः शत्रुरहितोऽहमभूवं ।
> अभिराष्ट्रोऽभिगतराष्ट्रः प्राप्तराज्यः सन् विषासहिः शत्रूणां विशेषेणाभिभविता
> चाभूवं । यथा येन प्रकारेणाहमेषां दृश्यमानानां सर्वेषां भूतानां
> प्राणिनां जनस्य च सेवकस्यामात्यादेश्च विराजानि यथेश्वरो भवानि तथा सपत्नहा
> विषासहिश्चा भूवमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सपत्नहा (*sapatnahā*) is the slayer of rivals, enemies; therefore I have become असपत्नः (*asapatnaḥ*), free of enemies. अभिराष्ट्रः (*abhirāṣṭraḥ*) is one who has attained the kingdom; being so, I have become विषासहिः (*viṣāsahiḥ*), one who especially overcomes enemies. In the manner in which I may reign (विराजानि (*virājāni*)), be lord, over all these visible beings, living creatures, and over the people, that is servants, ministers and so on, so have I become the slayer of rivals and the vanquisher. Such is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यथा (*yathā*)—in the manner in which
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—of those before us
- भूतानां (*bhūtānāṃ*)—of all living beings
- जनस्य च (*janasya ca*)—and of the people also
- विराजानि (*virājāni*)—may become lord, in that manner
- सपत्नहा (*sapatnahā*)—the slayer of enemies
- असपत्नः (*asapatnaḥ*)—without rival
- अभिराष्ट्रः (*abhirāṣṭraḥ*)—one who holds the kingdom in his power
- विषासहिः (*viṣāsahiḥ*)—one who defeats enemies; I have become

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I, slayer of enemies, without rival, holding the kingdom in my power and defeating enemies, shine as lord over all these living beings before us and over all people, servants, ministers and the rest.

##### English translation
May I become without a rival, the destroyer of my rivals, obtaining the sovereignty, overcoming (my foes) so that I may reign over these beings and over my people.

### Printed p. 1182
## Sūkta 175 (Maṇḍala 10)
**Introduction**
In this sūkta the stones called ग्रावाणः (*grāvāṇaḥ*), which crush the Soma plants, are praised. Although these deities are praised in many Ṛks, the sūktas praising them separately are only three in the Ṛgveda, all in the tenth maṇḍala: Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-76; 10-94; and 10-175. A detailed account of these ग्राव (*grāva*) or अद्रि (*adri*) has been given in the introductions to those sūktas, that is, in Ṛ. Saṃ. part 29, pp. 115-119 and pp. 1003-1005 of the same part.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र व इति चतुर्ऋचं चतुर्विंशं सूक्तं गायत्रं । अर्बुदस्य सर्पर्षेः पुत्र
> ऊर्ध्वग्रावा नामर्षिः । सोमाभिषवार्था ग्रावाणो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं ।
> प्र वश्चतुष्कमूर्ध्वग्रावार्बुदिग्र्राव्नोऽस्त्याद्यायत्रमिति ॥ ग्रावस्तोत्र एतत्तूक्तं ।
> सूत्रितं च । आ व ऋंजसे प्र वो ग्रावाण इति सूक्तयोः । आ. ५-१२ । इति ।
> यद्वा । इदमेकमेव सूक्तं ग्रावस्तोत्रं । सूत्र्यते हि ।-प्र वो ग्रावाण इत्येक
> उक्तं सर्पणं । आ. ५-१२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta प्र व (*pra va*), of four Ṛks, is the twenty-fourth sūkta, in Gāyatra metre. The seer is Ūrdhvagrāvan, son of the serpent-seer Arbuda; the deity is the ग्रावाणः (*grāvāṇaḥ*) used for pressing Soma. So the Anukramaṇī says: प्र वश्चतुष्कमूर्ध्वग्रावार्बुदिग्र्राव्नोऽस्त्याद्यायत्रमिति॥ (*pra vaścatuṣkamūrdhvagrāvārbudigrrāvno 'styādyāyatramiti‖*) This sūkta is a praise of the pressing stones. It is prescribed in the sūtra आ व ऋंजसे प्र वो ग्रावाण इति सूक्तयोः (*ā va ṛṃjase pra vo grāvāṇa iti sūktayoḥ*) (Ā. 5-12). Or else, this one sūkta alone is the praise of the stones; for it is prescribed: प्र वो ग्रावाण इत्येक उक्तं सर्पणं (*pra vo grāvāṇa ityeka uktaṃ sarpaṇaṃ*) (Ā. 5-12).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta प्र वः (*pra vaḥ*) is the twenty-fourth sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has four Ṛks. Its seer is Ūrdhvagrāvan, son of Arbuda; its deity is the stones called ग्रावाणः (*grāvāṇaḥ*) used for pressing Soma; the metre is Gāyatrī. The Anukramaṇī says: प्र वश्चतुष्कमूर्ध्वग्रावार्बुदिर्ग्रावोऽस्तौद्गायत्रं (*pra vaścatuṣkamūrdhvagrāvārbudirgrāvo 'staudgāyatraṃ*). In this sūkta the stone is praised. In the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, in the sūtra आ व ऋंजसे प्र वो ग्रावाण इति सूक्तयोः (*ā va ṛṃjase pra vo grāvāṇa iti sūktayoḥ*) (Ā. 5-12), this matter is set forth. Or the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra प्र वो ग्रावाण इत्येक उक्तं सर्पणं (*pra vo grāvāṇa ityeka uktaṃ sarpaṇaṃ*) (Ā. 5-12) indicates that this one sūkta alone is the praise of the stones.

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 175; Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 33; number of Ṛks in the sūkta 4; Seer: Ūrdhvagrāvā Arbudi; Deity: ग्राणः (*grāṇaḥ*); Metre: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र वो॑ ग्रावाणः सवि॒ता दे॒वः सु॑वतु॒ धर्म॑णा ।  
> धू॒र्षु यु॑ज्यध्वं सुनु॒त ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । वः । ग्रावाणः । सविता । देवः । सुवतु । धर्मणा ।  
> धूःऽसु । युज्यध्वं । सुनुत ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 1183

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ग्रावाणः सोमाभिषवार्थाः पाषाणाः वो युष्मान्सविता प्रेरको
> देवो धर्मणात्मीयेन धारणेन कर्मणा प्र सुवतु । अभिषवार्थं प्रेरयतु ॥
> षू प्रेरणे । तौदादिकः ॥ यूयं च धूर्ष्टभिषवस्थानेषु प्राच्यादिमहादिक्षु
> युज्यध्वं । युक्ता भवत । अनंतरं सुनुत । अभिषुणुत सोमं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O pressing stones, may the impelling god Savitṛ urge you, by his own sustaining action, to the pressing. (The root षू (*ṣū*) is in the sense of impelling, of the Tudādi class.) And you, yoke yourselves in the धूर्षु (*dhūrṣu*), the pressing places, in the great quarters such as the east; then press out (सुनुत (*sunuta*)) the Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ग्रावाणः (*grāvāṇaḥ*)—O stones used for pressing Soma
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you
- सविता देवः (*savitā devaḥ*)—the god Savitṛ, impeller of all
- धर्मणा (*dharmaṇā*)—by his own action
- प्रसुवतु (*prasuvatu*)—may he urge to the pressing (you also)
- धूर्षु (*dhūrṣu*)—in the quarters, east and the rest, where the Soma plants are crushed
- युज्यध्वं (*yujyadhvaṃ*)—be appointed, and
- सुनुत (*sunuta*)—crush the Soma plants

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O stones used for crushing the Soma plants, may the god Savitṛ, impeller of all, urge you to the pressing by his action of sustaining. You also, appointed in the regions such as the east, crush the Soma plants.

##### English translation
May the divine Savitri urge you stones, by his sustaining (action), be yoked to the chariot-poles, express (the juiee).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this sūkta the stones called ग्रावाणः (*grāvāṇaḥ*), inanimate things, are praised as if they were conscious deities. Sūktas of this kind are many in the Ṛgveda. The sacrificial altar, the sacred grass seat, the forest tree, or the wooden post to which the sacrificial animal is bound, mountains, plants and creepers, and so on, are all praised as if conscious deities, or as the presiding deities of those things. Since the impeller of all actions is Sūrya or Savitṛ (Sun is the Source of all energy), Savitṛ is prayed to impel the crushing of the Soma plants. The word धूर्षु (*dhūrṣu*) is in the locative plural; its meaning is "in the yokes". Oxen or horses are yoked to the yokes of a cart in order to draw it. In the same way, it is prayed here that these stones be yoked or appointed in this action of crushing Soma plants and the Soma juice be pressed out.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ग्रावा॑णो॒ अप॑ दु॒च्चुना॒मप॑ सेधत दुर्म॒तिं ।  
> उ॒स्राः क॑र्तन भेष॒जं ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ग्रावाणः । अप । दुच्चुनां । अप । सेधत । दुःमतिं ।  
> उस्राः । कर्तन । भेषजं ॥ २ ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ग्रावाणः दुच्चुनां दुःखकारिणीं शत्रुभूतां प्रजामप सेधत । आस्मत्तोऽपगमयत ॥ षिधु गत्यां ॥ तथा दुर्मतिं दुष्टाभिसंधिं चाप सेधत । भेषजं
> सुखमस्माकं यथा भवति तथोस्रा गाः कर्तन । कुरुत ॥ करोतेश्छांदसो विकरणस्य
> लुक् । तप्तनप्तनथनास्थेति तनबादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O stones, drive away (अप सेधत (*apa sedhata*), make go away from us; root षिधु (*ṣidhu*) in the sense of going) the दुच्चुनां (*duccunāṃ*), the hostile folk who cause suffering; and likewise drive away the दुर्मतिं (*durmatiṃ*), the evil intention. Make (कर्तन (*kartana*), कुरुत (*kuruta*)) the उस्रा (*usrā*), the cows, so that there is भेषजं (*bheṣajaṃ*), comfort, for us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ग्रावाणः (*grāvāṇaḥ*)—O stones
- दुच्चुनां (*duccunāṃ*)—the hostile folk who cause suffering or harm to the Soma-pressing rite
- अप सेधत (*apa sedhata*)—drive away from here
- दुर्मतिं (*durmatiṃ*)—the evil mind or bad intention in people
- अप (*apa*)—drive away (remove)
- भेषजं (*bheṣajaṃ*)—so as to bring us comfort
- उस्राः (*usrāḥ*)—the cows
- कर्तन (*kartana*)—make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O stones, drive away the hostile folk who cause suffering or harm in the Soma-pressing rite, and their evil mind or bad intention. Make the cows bring us comfort by giving milk and the like.

##### English translation
Drive away, stones, the malevolent (folk), drive away evil intention, make our cattle a remedy (against distress).

### Printed p. 1185

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ग्रावा॑ण॒ उप॑रे॒ष्वा म॑ही॒यंते॑ स॒जोष॑सः ।  
> वृष्णे॒ दध॑तो॒ वृष्ण्यं॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ग्रावाणः । उपरेषु । आ । महीयंते । सजोषसः ।  
> वृष्णे । दधतः । वृष्णं ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ग्रावाणो दिक्षवस्थिताः पाषाणाः सजोषसः सह प्रीयमाणाः संगताः
> संतो वोपरेषु । उपरो नामाभिषवाय चतुर्णां ग्रावाणं मध्ये स्थापितो
> विस्तृतः पाषाणः । प्रदेशापेक्षं बहुवचनं । उपरस्य प्रांतेषु महीयंते ।
> प्रकाशंते । आकारः पूरणः । किं कुर्वंतः । वृष्णे वर्षित्रे सोमाय वृष्णं
> वीर्यं दधतः प्रयच्छंतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The pressing-stones (grāvāṇaḥ) are those set in the quarters, in agreement and delighted (sajoṣasaḥ), together with the उपरेषु (*upareṣu*). The upara is the broad stone placed in the middle of the four pressing-stones for the pressing. The plural is used with regard to its regions: they shine (mahīyante) at the edges of the upara; the ā is a filler. What are they doing? They bestow manly strength (vṛṣṇyam) on the showering Soma (vṛṣṇe).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ग्रावाणः (*grāvāṇaḥ*)—the stones set in the quarters for pressing the Soma
- सजोषसः (*sajoṣasaḥ*)—co-operating with delight
- वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*)—to the Soma juice trickling from the crushed creepers
- वृष्ट्यं (*vṛṣṭyaṃ*)—the potent (intoxicating) power
- दधतः (*dadhataḥ*)—producing
- उपरेषु (*upareṣu*)—on the stone in the middle
- महीयंतॆ (*mahīyaṃtè*)—shine

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The stones used for pressing Soma, co-operating happily with one another, crush the Soma creepers on the central stone, give intoxicating power to the juices flowing out of them, and are honoured by people.

##### English translation
The stones consentient with the central pivot are honoured, giving energy to the sprinkling (juice).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Four stones are used when crushing the Soma creepers. Of them, the creepers are placed on the broad slab lying on the ground, and are crushed with other stones that are long, like a round stone and convenient to hold in the hands (continued on the next page).

### Printed p. 1186
Special Topics (continued): The slab in the middle is what is called उपरेषु (*upareṣu*) here. In its middle there is a slight hollow so that the juice may stand. The statement that the stones give strength to the Soma juice, which trickles and flows after being crushed with the stones, is only an exaggeration made to praise the stones; merely by being crushed with stones the juice does not gain more strength.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ग्रावा॑णः सवि॒ता नु वो॑ दे॒वः सु॑वतु॒ धर्म॑णा ।  
> यज॑मानाय सुन्व॒ते ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ग्रावाणः । सविता । नु । वः । देवः । सुवतु । धर्मणा ।  
> यजमानाय । सुन्वते ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवो दानादिगुणयुक्तः सविता हे ग्रावाणो वो युष्मान्धर्मणात्मीयेन
> धारणेन नु क्षिप्रं प्र सुवतु । अभिषवे प्रेरयतु । किमर्थ० । सुन्वते सोमाभिषवं
> कुर्वते याजमानाय यजमानार्थ० । तस्य यागनिष्पत्तय इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O pressing-stones, may the god Savitṛ, endowed with qualities such as generosity, quickly impel you (suvatu) by his own sustaining power (dharmaṇā) to the pressing. For what purpose? For the sake of the sacrificer who presses Soma, that is, for the accomplishment of his sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ग्रावाणः (*grāvāṇaḥ*)—O stones
- सुन्वते (*sunvate*)—who presses the Soma juice
- यजमानाय (*yajamānāya*)—for the benefit of the sacrificer
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—endowed with qualities such as generosity
- सविता (*savitā*)—the god Savitṛ
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you
- धर्मणा (*dharmaṇā*)—by his sustaining power
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- सुवतु (*suvatu*)—may he impel in the pressing rite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O stones, for the sake of the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice and presses Soma, may the god Savitṛ, endowed with generosity and other qualities, by his sustaining (impelling) power quickly urge you to engage in the Soma pressing.

##### English translation
May the divine Savitri quickly urge you, stones, by his sustaining (action) for the sake of the worshipper, who makes the libation.

### Printed p. 1187
## Sūkta 176 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र सूनव इति चतुर्ऋचं पंचविंशं सूक्तं । ऋभुपुत्रः सूनुर्नामर्षीः ।
> द्वितीया गायत्री शिष्टास्तिस्रोऽनुष्टुभः । आद्यर्भुदेवत्या शिष्टा आग्नेय्यः । तथा
> चानुक्रांतं । प्र सूनवः सूनुरार्भव आग्नेयमानुष्टुभं द्वितीयं गायत्र्याद्यार्भवीति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta प्र सूनव (*pra sūnava*) has four Ṛks and is the twenty-fifth. The seer is Sūnu, son of Ṛbhu. The second verse is Gāyatrī, the other three Anuṣṭubh. The first is addressed to the Ṛbhus, the rest to Agni. So the Anukramaṇī: प्र सूनवः सूनुरार्भव आग्नेयमानुष्टुभं द्वितीयं गायत्र्याद्यार्भवीति॥ (*pra sūnavaḥ sūnurārbhava āgneyamānuṣṭubhaṃ dvitīyaṃ gāyatryādyārbhavīti‖*) The application (viniyoga) has been stated already.

Anuvāda: This sūkta प्र सूनवः (*pra sūnavaḥ*) is the seventy-fifth sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. **NOTE** It has four Ṛks. Its seer is Sūnu, son of Ṛbhu. The first Ṛk is addressed to the Ṛbhus, the remaining Ṛks to Agni. The second Ṛk is in Gāyatrī metre, the rest in Anuṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: प्र सूनवः सूनुरार्भव आग्नेयमानुष्टुभं द्वितीया गायत्र्याद्यार्भवी (*pra sūnavaḥ sūnurārbhava āgneyamānuṣṭubhaṃ dvitīyā gāyatryādyārbhavī*). The viniyoga has been stated earlier.

Particulars: Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 176; Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 34. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 4. Ṛṣi: Sūnu Ārbhava. Devatā: 1. Ṛbhus; 2–4. Agni. Metre: 1, 3, 4. Anuṣṭubh; 2. Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र सू॒नव॑ ऋभू॒णां बृ॒हन्न॑वंत वृ॒जना॑ ।  
> क्षामा॒ ये वि॒श्वधा॑य॒सोऽश्न॑स्थे॒नुं न मा॒तरं॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । सूनवः । ऋभूणां । बृहत् । नवंत । वृजना ।  
> क्षाम । ये । विश्वधायसः । अश्नन् । धेनुं । न । मातरं ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 1188

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूनव एतत्संज्ञा ऋभूणां । ऋभुर्विभ्वा वाज इति त्रयाणामपि प्रथमेन
> व्यपदेशः । तेषां पुत्रा बृहत्प्रभूतं वृजना । संग्रामनामैतत् । वृजनं संग्रामं
> प्र नवंत । नवतिर्गतिकर्मा । प्रगच्छंति । प्रकर्षेण गच्छंति । प्रकृष्टगमनेन जयो
> लक्ष्यते । तत्र शत्रूज्जयंतीत्यर्थः । सूनुर्नामर्षीरात्मानमेव परोक्षेण निरदिशत् । एकस्मिन्नपि पूजार्थं बहुवचनं ' य ऋभवो विश्वधायसो विश्वस्य धारकाः
> क्षाम भूमिमश्नन् व्याप्नुवन् ॥ अशू व्याप्तौ । व्यत्ययेन श्ना ॥ धेनुं न । धेनुः
> प्रीणयित्रि गौः । तामिव तेषामृभूणामित्यन्वयः । यद्वा । सूर्यरश्मयोऽप्यभव उच्यंते । य उरु भासमानाः सूर्यरश्मयो विश्वधायसो विश्वं सर्व० रसं
> धयंतः पिबंतः । यद्वा! वृष्टादिप्रदानेन सर्वस्य धारकाः। एवंभूताः संतः क्षाम
> भूमिमश्नन् अभुंजत तदीयं सर्व० रसमपिबन् । तत्र दृष्टांतः । मातरं
> जननीं धेनुं पयस्विनीं गां यथा वत्सः पिबति तथा । य ऋभवोऽश्नंति तेषामृभूणामित्यन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Sūnus are the sons of the Ṛbhus; "Ṛbhu, Vibhvan, Vāja"—the three are designated by the first name. Their sons advance (pra navanta) to great (bṛhat) battle (vṛjanā, a name for battle); navati is a verb of motion; going forward means victory is indicated, i.e. they conquer enemies there. The seer named Sūnu indicates himself indirectly; the plural is for honour though he is one. The Ṛbhus who are sustainers of all (viśvadhāyasaḥ) have pervaded (aśnan) the earth (kṣāma); aśū is in the sense of pervading. "Like a milch cow (dhenum na)": a cow that gratifies; as a calf the mother, the construction is with those Ṛbhus. Alternatively, the Ṛbhus are the rays of the sun: the shining rays that drink all (viśva) the sap, or that sustain all by giving rain and so on; being so, they enjoyed the earth, drank all its sap, as a calf drinks its mother, the milch cow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—which Ṛbhus
- विश्वधायसः (*viśvadhāyasaḥ*)—sustaining and nourishing all
- मातरं (*mātaraṃ*)—the mother
- धेनुंन (*dhenuṃna*)—as a calf approaches the cow
- क्षाम (*kṣāma*)—the earth
- अश्नन् (*aśnan*)—pervade
- ऋभूणां (*ṛbhūṇāṃ*)—of the three Ṛbhu deities, Ṛbhu, Vibhu and Vāja
- सूनवः (*sūnavaḥ*)—the sons, called Sūnus
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—great
- वृजना (*vṛjanā*)—for battle
- प्र नवंत (*pra navaṃta*)—go eagerly
- Alternatively: मातरं (*mātaraṃ*)—its mother; धेनुं न (*dhenuṃ na*)—as a calf drinks the cow's milk; ये ऋभूणां सूनवः (*ye ṛbhūṇāṃ sūnavaḥ*)—the shining sun-rays that drink all sap, i.e. water, or that sustain and nourish all by giving rain etc.; क्षाम (*kṣāma*)—the water on the earth; अश्नन् (*aśnan*)—drink, i.e. draw up and suck; such sons of the Ṛbhus, the Sūnus, go to battle.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a calf approaches its mother cow, the Ṛbhus, who sustain and nourish all, pervade the earth everywhere. Or, as a calf drinks the milk of its mother cow, the shining rays of the sun, sustaining and nourishing the whole world by giving rain and so on, draw up and drink all the watery sap on the earth. The sons of such Ṛbhus, called Sūnus, set out eagerly to the battlefield for battle.

### Printed p. 1189

##### English translation
The Sunus, (the sons) of the Ribhus, advance boldly to battle ; supporters of all, they have spread over the earth as (a calf) over the mother cow.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र दे॒वं दे॒व्या धि॒या भर॑ता जा॒तवे॑दसं ।  
> ह॒व्या नो॑ वक्षदानु॒षक् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । देवं । देव्या । धिया । भरत । जातवेदसं ।  
> हव्या । नः । वक्षत् । आनुषक् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निप्रणयने प्र देवमिति तृचोऽनुवक्तव्यः । सूत्रितं च । प्रेषितोऽग्निप्रणयनीयाः प्रतिपद्यते प्र देवं देव्या धियेति तिस्रः । आ. २-१७ । इति ॥
> हे ऋत्विग्यजमानाः देवं दानादिगुणयुक्तं जातवेदसं जातानां वेदितारं
> जातप्रज्ञं जातधनं वेममग्निं प्र भरत । प्रकर्षेण हरत । यद्वा! प्रांचं नयत ।
> केन साधनेनेति तदाह । देव्या दीप्तया धिया प्रज्ञया कर्मणा वा । यद्वा! एषा
> सहयोगे तृतीया । देव्या धिया युक्तं । किं प्रयोजनमिति चेत् । नोऽस्माकं
> हव्या हव्यानि हवींष्ट्रानुषगानुपूर्व्यानुद्रमेण वक्षत् । अयमग्निर्वहेत् ।
> देवान्प्रापयेत् ॥ वहेर्लॆटि सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Agni-carrying rite (agnipraṇayana) the triplet प्र देवं (*pra devaṃ*) is to be recited; it is stated in the sūtra: प्रेषितोऽग्निप्रणयनीयाः प्रतिपद्यते प्र देवं देव्या धियेति तिस्रः । आ. २-१७ । (*preṣito 'gnipraṇayanīyāḥ pratipadyate pra devaṃ devyā dhiyeti tisraḥ | ā. 2-17 |*) [Ā. Sū. 2-17]. O priests and sacrificers, bring forth (pra bharata) the god Agni, endowed with generosity and the like, Jātavedas, knower of what is born, possessed of wisdom and wealth; or lead him forward. By what means? By divine (shining) wisdom (dhiyā) or rite; or the instrumental is in the sense of accompaniment: accompanied by divine wisdom. For what purpose? May he carry (vakṣat) our oblations in order, in succession, and convey them to the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O priests and sacrificers)
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—endowed with generosity etc., or shining
- जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*)—this omniscient Agni
- देव्या (*devyā*)—shining
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—by the rite of agnipraṇayana etc. or by wisdom (that is, with praise)
- प्र भरत (*pra bharata*)—carry and bring to the northern altar
- (this Agni) नः (*naḥ*)—our
- हव्या (*havyā*)—oblations
- आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)—in order
- वक्षत् (*vakṣat*)—may he carry to the gods

### Printed p. 1190

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests and sacrificers, bring this Agni, who has generosity and other qualities or is shining, who knows all or possesses all wealth, to the northern altar by the rite of agnipraṇayana or with praise. May this Agni carry the oblations we offer to the deities intended.

##### English translation
Bring forward the divine Jatavedas by means of divine wisdom ; may he bear our oblations (to the gods) in succession.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That the three Ṛks beginning प्र देवः (*pra devaḥ*) are to be recited in the agnipraṇayana rite is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: प्रेषितोऽग्निप्रणयनीयाः प्रतिपद्यते प्र देवं देव्या धियेति तिस्रः (*preṣito 'gnipraṇayanīyāḥ pratipadyate pra devaṃ devyā dhiyeti tisraḥ*) (Ā. 2-17).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यमु॒ष्य प्र दे॑व॒युर्होता॑ य॒ज्ञाय॑ नीयते ।  
> रथो॒ न योर॒भीवृ॑तो॒ घृणी॑नाइच्छीतति॒ त्मना॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । ऊं इति । स्यः । प्र । देवयुः । होता । यज्ञाय । नीयते ।  
> रथः । न । योः । अभिवृतः । फृणिवान् । चेतति । त्मना ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमु अयमेव स्य सोग्निर्देवयुर्देवान्यष्टुमिच्छन्भवति ॥ देवशब्दात्क्यचि न छंदस्य पुत्रेतीत्वदीर्घयोः प्रतिषेधः ॥ अयमेव होता देवानामाह्वाता। अयमेव यज्ञाय यागार्थं प्रणीयते । आहवनीयदेशं प्रति प्रकर्षण
> नीयते । अपि च रथो रंहणशीलः सूर्यो रथवान्वा ॥ छांदसो मत्वर्थीयस्य
> लोपः ।' स यधा घृणीनान्वीप्तिमान् तद्वद्दीपो योर्मिश्रयिता हविषां देवैः
> संगमयिता ॥ यौतेरन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यंत इति विच् ॥ अभीवृत ऋत्विग्यजमानैरा-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अयमु (*ayamu*): this very Agni, स्य (*sya*), is devayu, wishing to sacrifice to the gods. This very one is the hotṛ, the caller of the gods; he is led forward (nīyate) for the sacrifice, to the Āhavanīya place. Further, रथः (*rathaḥ*) is the swift sun, or one who has a chariot. Like him, Agni is ghṛṇīvān, radiant; योः (*yoḥ*) the mixer, who brings the oblations together with the gods. अभीवृत (*abhīvṛta*) ….

### Printed p. 1191

> वेष्टितः ॥ वृणोतेः कर्मण्यन्येषामपीति पूर्वपदस्य दीर्घः । गतिरनंतर इति
> गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ एवंभूतोऽग्निस्त्मनात्मना । स्वयमेव चेतति । सम्यग्देवान्यष्टुं जानाति ॥ मंत्रेष्वाज्यादेरात्मन इत्याकारलोपः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa continues his gloss of *abhīvṛtaḥ*. The fire is surrounded by the priests and the sacrificers. The word comes from the root वृणोतेः (*vṛṇoteḥ*), and he gives the lengthening of the earlier member and the retention of the original accent of the prefix-like first member. Such an Agni, "by himself" (त्मना (*tmanā*), that is, of his own accord), "knows" (चेतति (*cetati*)): he knows rightly how to worship the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्यः (*syaḥ*)—the well-known
- अयं उ (*ayaṃ u*)—this very Agni
- देवयुः (*devayuḥ*)—desires to worship the gods (this very Agni)
- होता (*hotā*)—is also the one who invites the gods to the sacrificial ground (this very Agni)
- यज्ञाय (*yajñāya*)—for the sake of the sacrifice
- प्र नीयते (*pra nīyate*)—is carried from near the two kindling-sticks, the place of his birth, to the Āhavanīya fire on the northern altar
- रथः न (*rathaḥ na*)—like the Sun, who is swift-moving or who travels in a chariot
- फृणीवान् (*phṛṇīvān*)—shining radiantly
- योः (*yoḥ*)—and distributing the oblations to the gods
- अभिवृतः (*abhivṛtaḥ*)—and surrounded by the priests and the sacrificer, this Agni
- त्मना (*tmanā*)—by himself (without the prompting of others)
- चेतति (*cetati*)—knows the manner of worshipping the gods in the sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This well-known Agni himself desires to worship the gods. This Agni himself invites the gods to the sacrificial ground. This Agni is carried to the Āhavanīya place for the sacrifice. This Agni, who shines like the Sun that travels in a chariot, who distributes the oblations to the gods, and who is surrounded by his attendants such as the priests and the sacrificer, knows of himself, without anyone's prompting, in what way the gods are to be worshipped in the sacrifice.

##### English translation
This ministrant priest devoted to the gods is brought (hither) for the sacrifice ; radiant as the swift-moving sun, uniting (the oblation and the gods) surrounded (by the priests, Agni) knows of himself (how to worship the gods).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यम॒ग्नि रु॑रुष्यत्य॒मृता॑दिव॒ जन्म॑नः ।  
> सह॑सश्चि॒त्सही॑यान्दे॒वो जी॒वात॑वे कृ॒तः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । अग्निः । उरुष्यति । अमृतात् इव । जन्मनः ।  
> सहसः । चित् । सहीयान् । देवः । जीवातवे । कृतः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमग्निरमृतादमरणाद्भावनिमित्ताद्भयादिव जन्मनो जायमानान्मनुष्यनिमित्ताद्भयादप्युरुष्यति । तस्माद्रक्षति । उरुष्यती रक्षाकर्मेति यास्कः । नि. ५-२३ ॥
> भाववाचिनोऽमृतशब्दस्य नञा बहुव्रीहौ नञो जरमरमित्रमृता इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । भीत्रार्थानां । पा. १-४-२५ । इत्यपादानसंज्ञा ॥ अपि चायं देवः
> सहसश्चित् ॥ सह इति बलनाम । तस्मादुत्तरस्य मत्त्वर्थीयस्य बहुलं छंदसीति लुक् ॥
> चिच्छब्धोऽप्यर्थः । सहस्वतो बलवतोऽपि सहीयान् बलवत्तरः ॥ सहस्विशब्दादीयसुनि विन्मत्तोरिति विनो लुक् । टेरिति टिलोपः ॥ एवंभूतो देवो जीवातवे
> जीवनहेतने यागाय कृतः । ब्रह्मणा सृष्टः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Agni protects (उरुष्यति (*uruṣyati*)) from fear as if from the immortal, that is, from fear arising from the state of being (the deathless); and also from the fear that comes from born beings, that is, from men. Yāska: उरुष्यती रक्षाकर्मेति (*uruṣyatī rakṣākarmeti*) (Ni. 5-23). He notes the accent of अमृत (*amṛta*), and that in the sense of fear the source of fear gets the name apādāna (Pā. 1-4-25). Further, this god is सहसश्चित् (*sahasaścit*): सह (*saha*) is a name for strength, and the particle चित् (*cit*) has the sense "even"; he is stronger (सहीयान् (*sahīyān*)) even than the strong. Such a god has been made (कृतः (*kṛtaḥ*)) for the sake of the sacrifice, the means of life (जीवातवे (*jīvātave*)): he was created by Brahmā.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अयं अग्निः (*ayaṃ agniḥ*)—this Agni
- अमृतात् इव (*amṛtāt iva*)—as he protects from the fear that may arise from the deathless gods
- जन्मनः (*janmanaḥ*)—so also from the fear arising from men, who have birth
- उरुष्यति (*uruṣyati*)—protects
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—this shining Agni
- सहसः चित् (*sahasaḥ cit*)—than even the exceedingly strong
- सहीयान् (*sahīyān*)—stronger (such an Agni)
- जीवातवे (*jīvātave*)—for the sacrifice that is the support of life
- कृतः (*kṛtaḥ*)—has been created by Brahmā

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Agni protects us from the fear arising from men just as he protects from the fear arising from the gods. This shining Agni is more powerful than even the exceedingly powerful. Such an Agni has been created by Brahmā for the sacrifice, which is the cause of life for men.

##### English translation
This Agni saves from peril caused by man as (well as) from peril caused by the immortals, a god stronger than strength, created for life-producing (sacrifice)

## Sūkta 177 (Maṇḍala 10)
Introduction.
In this sūkta the deity called Māyābheda is praised. Sāyaṇa has explained this sūkta in two ways, as referring to a deity and as referring to the self (adhyātma). The last Ṛk, beginning अपश्यं (*apaśyaṃ*), has an extensive explanation in the Nirukta-pariśiṣṭa. In the Bṛhaddevatā, a work proclaimed by Śaunaka, it is said of this sūkta:
ऋषिर्जग् पतंगस्तु पतंगमिति यत्परं । तत्सौर्यमेके मन्यंते मायाभेदं तथापरे ॥ ७५ ॥ (*ṛṣirjag pataṃgastu pataṃgamiti yatparaṃ | tatsauryameke manyaṃte māyābhedaṃ tathāpare ‖ 75 ‖*)
मायाभेदे द्वितीयायां वाक् स्तुतेत्याह शौनकः । देवीं बिभर्ति मनसा या वाचं विदितां सतीं ॥ ७६ ॥ (*māyābhede dvitīyāyāṃ vāk stutetyāha śaunakaḥ | devīṃ bibharti manasā yā vācaṃ viditāṃ satīṃ ‖ 76 ‖*)
The sage named Pataṅga is the seer of the sūkta beginning पतंगमक्तं (*pataṃgamaktaṃ*). Some say that the Sun is praised in this sūkta; others say that it speaks of the Māyābheda, that is, the counteraction of hostile rites such as sorcery. Śaunaka says that, in the context of the Māyābheda praise spoken of in this sūkta, Vāk (the goddess of speech) is praised in the second Ṛk. This goddess of speech bears in her mind the speech (the word, the language) that is known to all, that is, well known; that is, dwelling in the mind of everyone, she prompts the words each one speaks. Śaunaka's opinion is that this goddess of speech is praised in the second Ṛk.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पतंगमिति तृचं षड्विंशं सूक्तं प्रजापतिपुत्रस्य पतंगस्यार्षं । आद्या जगती
> ततस्त्रिष्टुभौ । मायाभेदस्य प्रतिपाद्यत्वात्तद्देवत्यमिदं सूक्तं । अनुक्रांतं च ।
> पतंगं तृचं पतंगः प्राजापत्यो मायाभेदं जगत्यादीति ॥ प्रवर्गैऽभिष्टव आद्ये
> ऋचौ । सूत्रितं च । पतंगमक्तमसुरस्य मायया यो नः सनुत्यः । आ. ४-७। इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning पतंगं (*pataṃgaṃ*), of three Ṛks, is the twenty-sixth sūkta of the anuvāka; its seer is Pataṅga, son of Prajāpati. The first Ṛk is in Jagatī, the next two in Triṣṭubh. Because Māyābheda is what is expounded, this sūkta has that as its deity. The Anukramaṇī says: पतंगं तृचं पतंगः प्राजापत्यो मायाभेदं जगत्यादीति (*pataṃgaṃ tṛcaṃ pataṃgaḥ prājāpatyo māyābhedaṃ jagatyādīti*). In the Pravargya rite the first two Ṛks are used in the Abhiṣṭava. It is also stated in the Sūtra: पतंगमक्तमसुरस्य मायया यो नः सनुत्यः (*pataṃgamaktamasurasya māyayā yo naḥ sanutyaḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 4-7).

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning पतंगं (*pataṃgaṃ*) is the twenty-sixth sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has three Ṛks. Its seer is Pataṅga, son of Prajāpati; because it expounds the Māyābheda, Māyābheda is its deity; its first Ṛk is in the Jagatī metre, and the next two Ṛks in the Triṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated thus: पतंगं तृचं पतंगः प्राजापत्यो मायाभेदं जगत्यादि (*pataṃgaṃ tṛcaṃ pataṃgaḥ prājāpatyo māyābhedaṃ jagatyādi*).

### Printed p. 1194
It is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, पतंगमक्तमसुरस्य मायया यो नः सनुत्यः (*pataṃgamaktamasurasya māyayā yo naḥ sanutyaḥ*) (Ā. 4-7), that the first two Ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited in the Abhiṣṭava of the rite called Pravargya.

Sūkta 177, Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Aṣṭaka 8, Adhyāya 8, Varga 35. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 3. Seer: Pataṅga Prājāpatya. Deity: Māyābheda. Metre: 1. Jagatī; 2, 3. Triṣṭubh.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

असुर (*asura*) is the Supreme Brahman, skilled in sitting (or "ruling"), free of all limiting adjuncts. By his Māyā, made of the three guṇas, the अक्तं (*aktaṃ*) is "manifest". Or else: माया (*māyā*) is a name for wisdom (प्रज्ञा (*prajñā*)); the all-knowing Pataṅga is bound to wisdom. पतति गच्छतीति पतंगः सूर्यः (*patati gacchatīti pataṃgaḥ sūryaḥ*): Pataṅga is the Sun, who goes. The wise (विपश्चितः (*vipaścitaḥ*)) see, that is, know, him with the mind restrained in the heart (हृदा (*hṛdā*) meaning "abiding in the heart"). The seers (कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)), who see beyond, look into the "ocean" (समुद्रे (*samudre*)): since the rays flow from it, the ocean is the orb of the Sun; within it, in the middle, they look; the meaning is that they know also the golden Person who dwells within the orb. Those ordainers (वेधसः (*vedhasaḥ*)), who thus perform worship of the Sun, desire the abode (पदं (*padaṃ*)) of the rays (मरीचीनां (*marīcīnāṃ*)), the Sun's orb; the meaning is that by worship they attain it.

> सच्चित्सुखात्मकं यत्परं ब्रह्म तदेवेच्छंति । तद्भावप्राप्तिमेव कामयंते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Alternatively: the wise, versed in the Vedānta, see with the inward-turned mind abiding in the heart the Self manifested by Māyā in the form of the individual soul (जीव (*jīva*)); Pataṅga is the Supreme Self, since he pervades (पतति व्याप्नोतीति (*patati vyāpnotīti*)). They see him; that is, by laying aside the limiting adjuncts they realize directly the identity of the individual soul with the Supreme Self. Further, those seers, versed in the Vedānta, "in the ocean": the ocean is the Supreme Self, since beings flow from him; in him, as the substratum, in the middle, they behold all that is seen as superimposed. Therefore, since everything apart from the seer is unreal, the ordainers desire that Supreme Brahman, of the nature of being, consciousness and bliss, which is the substratum of the rays, that is, of the modes of knowledge (वृत्तिज्ञानानां (*vṛttijñānānāṃ*)); they long only for the attainment of that state.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- असुरस्य (*asurasya*)—belonging to the Supreme Brahman, who is free of all limiting adjuncts
- मायया (*māyayā*)—by the Māyā made of the three guṇas, or by wisdom
- अक्तं (*aktaṃ*)—manifested
- पतंगं (*pataṃgaṃ*)—the Sun
- विपश्चितः (*vipaścitaḥ*)—the learned
- हृदा (*hṛdā*)—of the heart, with the restraint of the mental modes
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with the concentrated mind
- पश्यंति (*paśyaṃti*)—know
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—they, who see beyond
- समुद्रे अंतः (*samudre aṃtaḥ*)—in the middle of the Sun's orb, the source of the rays
- वि चक्षते (*vi cakṣate*)—look at and know the golden Person within the orb, that is, Brahman
- वेधसः (*vedhasaḥ*)—those who thus also perform worship of the Sun
- मरीचीनां (*marīcīnāṃ*)—of the rays
- पदं (*padaṃ*)—the abode, the Sun's orb (the world of the Sun)
- इच्छंति (*icchaṃti*)—desire, that is, obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wise know, with concentration of mind, the Sun, manifested by the three-guṇa Māyā of the Supreme Brahman, who is free of all limiting adjuncts. Those who see beyond know the golden Person abiding within the middle of the Sun's orb, the source of the rays, as the Supreme Brahman. Those who thus perform worship of the Sun obtain the world of the Sun, the abode of the rays, that is, the highest state.

##### English translation
The wice behold with their mind (seated) in their heart the Sun made manifeast by the illusion of the Asura ; the sages look into the solar orb, the ordainers (of solar worship) desire the region of his rays.

### Printed p. 1196

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पतंगं अक्तं असुरस्य मायया (*pataṃgaṃ aktaṃ asurasya māyayā*)—Here the word असुरस्य (*asurasya*) has been explained as the Supreme Brahman free of all limiting adjuncts. "Free of all limiting adjuncts" means the Supreme Brahman in the unmanifest state. मायया (*māyayā*) of this Brahman means by the Māyā made of the three guṇas, the forms sattva, rajas and tamas, or by wisdom in the form of resolve. In Brahman in the unmanifest state the three kinds of guṇas, sattva, rajas and tamas, remain in a state of equality; then none of the world and the rest exists. All is calm and Brahman alone remains. This may be called the state of dissolution. By the resolve of the Supreme Self, that is, by the wish to create, vibration arises in the guṇas sattva, rajas and tamas, which lie in equilibrium in this unmanifest state, and they come into a state of disequilibrium; that is, the three guṇas are no longer all in the same proportions but change, becoming greater and lesser. Then the unmanifest turns into the manifest form. This is what is called creation. Now, in explaining the words पतंगं अक्तं (*pataṃgaṃ aktaṃ*), for the word पतंग (*pataṃga*) he says पतति गच्छतीति पतंगः सूर्यः (*patati gacchatīti pataṃgaḥ sūryaḥ*): because he moves always, Pataṅga means the Sun; अक्तं (*aktaṃ*) means manifested, visible to the eye. In the unmanifest state only Brahman exists and there are no things endowed with name and form, so the Sun too does not exist then. When that unmanifest comes to the manifest state, the world and the rest, and the Sun, become manifest so as to be visible to the eye. This is what is here called the manifested Sun. All this creation of the world and the rest proceeds from the Māyā-power of the Supreme Brahman, that is, from his wisdom.

हृदा पश्यंति मनसा विपश्चितः (*hṛdā paśyaṃti manasā vipaścitaḥ*)—Here the words हृदा (*hṛdā*) and मनसा (*manasā*) have a special meaning. In worldly dealings, if we wish to know the nature of a thing, we know it by the eye or with the help of a sense organ. To know the nature of a thing through the sense organs of knowledge such as the eye, the help of the mind is also necessary. Nothing can be known without the help of the mind. Even if our mind is elsewhere while the eyes look at a thing, the nature of the thing is not known. This is a matter within everyone's experience. When one examines or meditates on a thing, there should be no room in the mind for modes other than that one object; that is, there must be concentration of mind. This concentration of mind is also called yoga. According to the Yoga-sūtra योगश्चित्तवृत्तिनिरोधः (*yogaścittavṛttinirodhaḥ*), yoga is to check the other activities in the mind (attention to other matters) and make that mind rest steadily in one place. This can be called, broadly, concentration of mind. Ascetics and yogins, when they meditate on the Supreme Self, meditate with this kind of concentration of mind. By this they attain direct realization of the object they meditate on, that is, of Brahman or of another deity. This is what is here विपश्चितः (*vipaścitaḥ*), that is, the knowers or

### Printed p. 1197

Scholars, with undivided minds, that is, with one-pointed concentration, fix the mind on Parabrahman alone and meditate on it continuously. By this they realise the golden Puruṣa, the inner controller in this sun-disc, that is, Parabrahman. One should understand that the Supreme Self abides as inner controller in all things created by Parabrahman, and that for this reason He is present also inside this sun-disc. On this point—

असावादित्यो ब्रह्मेति ब्रह्मैव सन्ब्रह्माप्येति य एवं वेद ॥ (*asāvādityo brahmeti brahmaiva sanbrahmāpyeti ya evaṃ veda ‖*) (Kṛ. Ā. 2-2)**NOTE**

It is said that this Āditya (the Sun), whom we now see with our eyes, is Parabrahman; one who worships this Brahman becomes Brahman itself and is united with Brahman. And further—

आदित्यो ना एष एतन्मंडलं तपति तत्र ता ऋचस्तदृचा मंडलग्० स ऋचां लोकोऽथ य एष एतस्मिन्मंडलेऽर्चिर्दिर्प्यते तानि सामानि स साम्यां लोकोऽथ य एष एतस्मिन्मंडलेऽर्चिषि पुरुषस्तानि यजूग्०षि स यजुषा मंडलग्० स यजुषां लोकस्यॆषा त्रय्येव विद्या तपति य एषोऽन्तरादित्ये हिरण्मयः पुरुषः ॥ (*ādityo nā eṣa etanmaṃḍalaṃ tapati tatra tā ṛcastadṛcā maṃḍalag0 sa ṛcāṃ loko 'tha ya eṣa etasminmaṃḍale 'rcirdirpyate tāni sāmāni sa sāmyāṃ loko 'tha ya eṣa etasminmaṃḍale 'rciṣi puruṣastāni yajūg0ṣi sa yajuṣā maṃḍalag0 sa yajuṣāṃ lokasyèṣā trayyeva vidyā tapati ya eṣo 'ntarāditye hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣaḥ ‖*) (Kṛ. U. 4-14)**NOTE**

In this Taittirīya Upaniṣad passage it is said that the golden Puruṣa in the middle of this sun-disc, that is, Brahman itself, shines in the form of the Sun.

समुद्रे अंतः कवयो वि चक्षते (*samudre aṃtaḥ kavayo vi cakṣate*)—here the word समुद्र (*samudra*) is explained thus: समुद्रवंत्यस्माद्रश्मय इति समुद्रं सूर्यमंडलं । तस्मिन् अंतः मध्यॆ (*samudravaṃtyasmādraśmaya iti samudraṃ sūryamaṃḍalaṃ | tasmin aṃtaḥ madhyè*). Since the rays go out from the sun-disc, it is called समुद्र (*samudra*); that is the meaning given. समुद्र (*samudra*) means the sun-disc. The seers (क्रांतदर्शि (*krāṃtadarśi*)), that is, the wise who know through inner vision everything that happens in past, future and present, realise the golden Puruṣa, Parabrahman, who shines within it, in its middle. This is the intention.

मरीचीनां पदं इच्छंति वेधसः (*marīcīnāṃ padaṃ icchaṃti vedhasaḥ*)—मरीचीनां पदं (*marīcīnāṃ padaṃ*) means the sun-disc, the source of the rays, or the world of the Sun, the highest abode, that is, Parabrahman. Here it is said that those who worship Parabrahman present within the sun-disc become that very Parabrahman, are united with it and attain liberation. The Śruti passage quoted above—

उद्यंतमस्तंयंतमादित्यमभिध्यायन् कुर्वन् ब्राह्मणो विद्वान् सकलं भद्रमश्नुतेऽसावादित्यो ब्रह्मेति ब्रह्मैव सन्ब्रह्माप्येति ॥ (*udyaṃtamastaṃyaṃtamādityamabhidhyāyan kurvan brāhmaṇo vidvān sakalaṃ bhadramaśnute 'sāvādityo brahmeti brahmaiva sanbrahmāpyeti ‖*) (Śrī. Ā. 2-2)**NOTE**

### Printed p. 1198

—supports this. That is: the learned brāhmaṇa who meditates on and worships Āditya alone at sunrise and sunset not only obtains all welfare but, becoming this very Brahman that has the form of Āditya, is united with Him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Meaning with reference to the Self (adhyātma)
- असुरस्य (*asurasya*)—of Parabrahman
- मायया (*māyayā*)—by māyā
- अक्तं (*aktaṃ*)—the Self (the jīva) manifested in the form of the jīva
- विपश्चितः (*vipaścitaḥ*)—the knowers of Vedānta
- हृदा मनसा (*hṛdā manasā*)—by inward-turned insight or by the mind
- पतंगं (*pataṃgaṃ*)—as the all-pervading Supreme Self
- पश्यंति (*paśyaṃti*)—they understand (and)
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—the Vedāntins, the far-seeing
- समुद्रे अंतः (*samudre aṃtaḥ*)—that all this world and the rest exist in the Supreme Self, the cause of all beings
- विचक्षते (*vicakṣate*)—they know by seeing (meditating)
- वेधसः (*vedhasaḥ*)—these Vedāntins, who know that all this world and the rest is unreal
- मरीचीनां (*marīcīnāṃ*)—of the cognitions of activity
- पदं (*padaṃ*)—the Parabrahman which is their substratum, of the nature of being, consciousness and bliss, and eternal; that is, union with Parabrahman
- इच्छंति (*icchaṃti*)—they wish to attain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In this world created by the māyā of the Supreme Self, they understand that the Self in all beings and the Supreme Self are one. These Vedāntins, by their inward-turned insight, or by mature intellect, understand that there is no difference between the individual self and the Supreme Self; the two are one; the Supreme Self Himself, as inner controller in the bodies of the various beings, is spoken of by the name "individual self". Therefore there is no difference at all between the individual self and the Supreme Self: the individual self is the Supreme Self, and the Supreme Self is the individual self. These Vedāntins understand this identity of the individual self and the Supreme Self, that He is all-pervading. And they understand that while the Supreme Self is in the unmanifest state, all beings, the world and the rest are all contained in that Supreme Self in seed form or subtle form; in the manifest state, or at the time of creation, the world and the rest all become manifest, that is, visible. Moreover, since all this world, visible to the eye, is not eternal, that is, since at the time of dissolution it merges in the Supreme Self, these Vedāntins wish to attain only the Parabrahman, which is always imperishable and eternal; and by worship of Brahman they attain the very attainment of Brahman.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

असुरस्य मायया अक्तं विपश्चितः हृदा मनसा पतंगं पश्यंति (*asurasya māyayā aktaṃ vipaścitaḥ hṛdā manasā pataṃgaṃ paśyaṃti*)—Before creation Parabrahman, the Supreme Self, alone existed. Because He was in the unmanifest state, none of this world and the rest existed. Then the Supreme Self, by His māyā, that is, by His power or intelligence or resolve, desired to create the world and the rest—

### Printed p. 1199

सोऽकामयत । बहु स्यां प्रजायेयेति । स तपोऽतप्यत । स तपस्तप्ता । इदग्० सर्वमसृजत । यदिदं किंच । तत्सृष्ट्वा । तदेवानु प्राविशत् । (*so 'kāmayata | bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti | sa tapo 'tapyata | sa tapastaptā | idag0 sarvamasṛjata | yadidaṃ kiṃca | tatsṛṣṭvā | tadevānu prāviśat |*) (Kṛ. U. 2-6)**NOTE**

The Supreme Self, who before creation was in the unmanifest state, desired to create, that is, desired to become manifest Himself in many forms (बहु स्यां प्रजायेय (*bahu syāṃ prajāyeya*)), and performed tapas. Here tapas means meditation. In ordinary practice, if one is to make a thing, a maker (an agent), a material and a means of making are needed; but with the Supreme Self it is not so. By mere meditation, that is, by meditating "let it be thus", or by resolve (decision), everything comes into being; that is, the Supreme Self Himself appears in manifest form. Therefore there is no difference between the Supreme Self in the unmanifest state and the Supreme Self who has become manifest and transformed into the world and the rest. That is, there is no distinction or difference between the Supreme Self in the unmanifest state and the individual self in the manifest state. The Vedāntins understand this principle by an intellect matured through study of the Veda, study of the śāstras, reflection, meditation and the like. Here पतंगं (*pataṃgaṃ*) means पतति व्याप्नोतीति पतंगः (*patati vyāpnotīti pataṃgaḥ*): the Supreme Self who pervades all things, that is, who is present in them as inner controller. Since the Supreme Self is in all beings and impels their movements—अंतः प्रविष्टः शास्त्रा जनानान् सर्वात्मा (*aṃtaḥ praviṣṭaḥ śāstrā janānān sarvātmā*) (Tai. Ā. 3)—there is no difference between the individual self and the Supreme Self. The individual self is manifest, that is, visible to the eye; the Supreme Self, being in unmanifest form, is beyond the senses. All this is understood by those who know the truth of Vedānta. This is the intention.

समुद्रे अंतः कवयो वि चक्षते (*samudre aṃtaḥ kavayo vi cakṣate*)—here समुद्र (*samudra*) is explained as समुद्ध्रवंत्यस्माद्भूतानीति समुद्रः परमात्मा (*samuddhravaṃtyasmādbhūtānīti samudraḥ paramātmā*). Since all classes of beings go forth from this Supreme Self, flow out from Him, that is, since the Supreme Self is the cause of their origin, समुद्र (*samudra*) means the Supreme Self. The Vedāntins understand that the world and the rest lie hidden in such a Supreme Self, that is, in the Supreme Self in the unmanifest state, and that at the time of creation they flow out from that very Supreme Self and become manifest. कवयः (*kavayaḥ*) means the far-seeing: those who, by their divine vision or knowledge, can know everything that happened, will happen and is happening in the past, future and present. Such Vedāntin knowers understand all this.

मरीचीनां पदं इच्छंति वेधसः (*marīcīnāṃ padaṃ icchaṃti vedhasaḥ*)—here the word मरीचीनां (*marīcīnāṃ*) is explained as वृत्तिज्ञानानां (*vṛttijñānānāṃ*). वृत्ति (*vṛtti*) is engagement in the various kinds of action, the doing of actions; ज्ञान (*jñāna*) is understanding. Since the original source of all these is Brahman alone, मरीचीनां पदं (*marīcīnāṃ padaṃ*) means Parabrahman, the original cause of the paths of engagement and withdrawal. This Brahman has no destruction; the world and the rest that are created have destruction. But Brahman has no destruction and is eternal. Therefore the Vedāntin knowers wish to worship this Brahman, attain the eternal Brahman itself and be united with it.

### Printed p. 1200

This union with Brahman, the attainment of the highest abode, is liberation. This is what they desire. This is the intention.

> प॒तं॒गो वाचं॒ मन॑सा बिभर्ति॒ तां गं॑ध॒र्वो॑ऽवद॒द्गर्भे॑  ॒

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)
