Sūkta 181
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 181; Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 39.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 3.
Ṛṣi: 1. Pratha Vāsiṣṭha; 2. Saprathas Bhāradvāja; 7. Gharma Saurya **NOTE**.
Deity: Viśve Devāḥ.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रथ॑श्च॒ यस्य॑ स॒प्रथ॑श्च॒ नामानु॑ष्टुभस्य ह॒विषो॑ ह॒विर्यत् ।  
> धा॒तुद्युर्त्या॑नात्सवि॒तुश्च॒ विष्णो॑ रथंत॒रमा ज॑भारा॒ वसि॑ष्ठः ॥१॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रथः । च । यस्य । सप्रथः । च । नाम । आनुस्तुभस्य । हविषः । हविः । यत् ।  
> धातुः । द्युतानात् । सवितुः । च । विष्णोः । रथंतरं । आ । जभार । वसिष्ठः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यस्य वसिष्ठस्य प्रथो नाम पुत्रो यस्य भरद्वाजस्य सप्रथो नाम पुत्रः तयोर्मध्ये वसिष्ठ आनुष्टुभस्यानुष्टुप्पंदसा युक्तस्य हविषो घर्माख्यस्य यद्धनिर्हविष्ट्वापादाकं रथंतरं । रथरंहःसाधनं साम तद्रथंतरं । धातुर्धातृसंज्ञाद्देवाद्दुतानाद्योतमानात्सवितुश्च विष्णोश्चा जभार । अजहार । हृतवान् ॥
> हृग्रहोर्भ इति भत्वं । रथशब्दोपपदात्तरतेः संज्ञायां भृत्यवृजीति खच् ।
> अरुर्द्विषदजंतस्यॆति मुमागमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Vasiṣṭha, whose son is called Pratha, and Bharadvāja, whose son is called Saprathas: among them, Vasiṣṭha carried off (आ जभार (*ā jabhāra*), अजहार (*ajahāra*), "took away") the रथंतरं (*rathaṃtaraṃ*) of the oblation called Gharma, which is joined to the Anuṣṭubh metre **NOTE**. The Rathantara is the sāman that is the means of the speed (*raṃhas*) of the chariot (*ratha*). He carried it off from the god named Dhātṛ, from the radiant Savitṛ, and from Viṣṇu.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which Vasiṣṭha-ṛṣi
- प्रथः नाम (*prathaḥ nāma*)—the one who has a son named Pratha, he
- सप्रथः (*saprathaḥ*)—and the one named Saprathas, son of Bharadvāja
- अदन्नु (*adannu*)—
- वसिष्ठः (*vasiṣṭhaḥ*)—and also the ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha
- आनुष्टुभस्य (*ānuṣṭubhasya*)—joined to the Anuṣṭubh metre
- हविषः (*haviṣaḥ*)—of the oblation called Gharma
- रथंतरं (*rathaṃtaraṃ*)—known by the name Rathantara
- यत् हविः (*yat haviḥ*)—whatever portion of the oblation there is, that
- धातुः (*dhātuḥ*)—from the god Dhātṛ
- द्युतानात् (*dyutānāt*)—radiant
- सवितुः च (*savituḥ ca*)—and from the god Savitṛ
- विष्णोः (*viṣṇoḥ*)—from Viṣṇu
- आ जभार (*ā jabhāra*)—they obtained and brought

### Printed p. 1231

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Pratha, son of Vasiṣṭha, Saprathas, son of Bharadvāja, and the ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha as well, obtained and brought that portion of the oblation which is joined to the Anuṣṭubh metre and known by the name Rathantara, from the god named Dhātṛ, from the radiant god Savitṛ, and from Viṣṇu.

##### English translation
Vasishtha, whose (son) is Pratha by name, and whose (son) is Sapratha, has (with them) borne away from Dhatri, and from the radiant Savitri, and from Vishnu, the rathanatara portion of the oblation which if offered with the Anushatubh verse.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अविं॑द॒न्ने अति॑हितं॒ यदासी॑द्य॒ज्ञस्य॒ धाम॑ पर॒मं गुहा॒ यत् ।  
> धा॒तुर्द्युता॑नात्सवि॒तुश्च॒ विष्णो॑र्भ॒रद्वा॑जो बृ॒हदा च॑क्रे  ॒
> अग्नेः ॥ २ ॥

> अविंदन् । ते । अतिहितं । यत् । आसीत् । यज्ञस्य । धाम । परमं । गुहा । यत् ।  
> धातुः । द्युतानात् । सवितुः । च । विष्णोः । भरत् ऽवाजः । बृहत् । आ । चक्रे । अग्नेः॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे धात्रादयस्तदविंदन् अलभंत यद्बृहत्सामाख्यं घर्मस्य हविषः
> संस्कारकमतिहितं तिरोहितमासीत् । यच्च बृहत्साम यज्ञस्य ज्योतिष्टोमादेः
> परममुत्कृष्टं धाम धारकं शरीरभूतं वा गुहा गुहायामस्मदादिविषये
> निहितमासीत् तत्ते धात्रादयोऽलभंत । तेभोग्योऽश्च सकाशात्तद्बृहत्साम भरद्वाज
> ऋषिरा चक्रे । अभिमुख्येन कृतवान् । आहृतवानित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Dhātṛ and the rest, you found (अविंदन् (*aviṃdan*), "obtained") that sāman called Bṛhat, the refiner of the oblation Gharma, which had been hidden (अतिहितं (*atihitaṃ*), "concealed"). And the Bṛhat sāman which is the supreme (excellent) धाम (*dhāma*) of the sacrifice, the Jyotiṣṭoma and the rest—either its supporter or its body—which had been placed in the cave (गुहा (*guhā*)), in the realm of us and others: that Dhātṛ and the rest obtained. From them the seer Bharadvāja brought (आ चक्रे (*ā cakre*), "made it come towards him"), that is, he fetched that Bṛhat sāman.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The portion of the Gharma oblation called Bṛhat sāman, which supports sacrifices such as the Jyotiṣṭoma and is quite indispensable, had been hidden in a secret place so that no one knew it. The gods Dhātṛ and the rest found it. Afterwards the seer Bharadvāja took that portion of the oblation, the Bṛhat sāman, which was with Dhātṛ, the radiant Savitṛ, Viṣṇu and Agni, and brought it from them.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते॑ऽविंद॒न्मन॑सा॒ दीध्या॑ना॒ यजुः॑ ष्क॒न्नं प्र॑थ॒मं दे॑व॒यानं॑ ।  
> धा॒तुर्द्युता॑नात्सवि॒तुश्च॒ विष्णो॒रा सूर्या॑दभरन्घ॒र्ममे॒ते ॥

> धातुः । द्युतानात् । सवितुः । च । विष्णोः । आ । सूर्यात् । अभरन् । घर्मं । एते॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ते धात्रादयो दीध्याना दीप्यमानाः संतो मनसा बुद्ध्याविंदन् ।
> अलभंत । किं तत् । यजुर्यागसाधनं स्कन्नं स्कंदनीयमासेचनीयं प्रवृंजनसाधनं प्रथमं मुख्यं देवयानं देवानां प्ताप्ति साधनं घर्मं । एवं
> धात्रादिभिः प्रथममुपलब्धं तं घर्मं धातुद्र्योतमानात्सवितुर्विष्णोः सूर्याच्चैत ऋत्विज आभरन् । आहरन् । आनीतवंत इत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those, Dhātṛ and the rest, shining (दीध्यानाः (*dīdhyānāḥ*), "blazing"), found (अविंदन् (*aviṃdan*), "obtained") with the mind (मनसा (*manasā*)), that is, with the intellect. What was it? The यजुः (*yajuḥ*), the means of the sacrifice; स्कन्नं (*skannaṃ*), what is to be poured out, the means of the *pravṛñjana*; प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*), the principal; देवयानं (*devayānaṃ*), the means of reaching the gods: the Gharma. Thus the Gharma, first obtained by Dhātṛ and the rest, these priests brought (आभरन् (*ābharan*), "fetched") from Dhātṛ, the radiant Savitṛ, Viṣṇu and Sūrya.

## Sūkta 182 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बृहस्पतिरिति तृचमेकत्रिंशं सूक्तं बृहस्पतिदेवत्यं त्रैष्टुभं । बृहस्पतिपुत्रस्तपुर्मूर्धा नामर्षिः । तथाचानुक्रांतं । बृहस्पतिस्तपुर्मूर्धा बार्हस्पत्यो
> बार्हस्पत्यमिति ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta बृहस्पतिरिति (*bṛhaspatiriti*) is a *tṛca* (three Ṛks), the thirty-first sūkta, addressed to Bṛhaspati, in the Triṣṭubh metre. The seer is named Tapurmūrdhā, son of Bṛhaspati. So the Anukramaṇī says: बृहस्पतिस्तपुर्मूर्धा बार्हस्पत्यो बार्हस्पत्यमिति ॥ (*bṛhaspatistapurmūrdhā bārhaspatyo bārhaspatyamiti ‖*). The viniyoga has been given.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*), is the thirty-first sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has three Ṛks. For this sūkta the seer is Tapurmūrdhā, son of Bṛhaspati; Bṛhaspati is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: Bṛhaspati, Tapurmūrdhā Bārhaspatya, Bārhaspatya **NOTE**. The viniyoga has already been stated earlier.

### Printed p. 1234

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> बृह॒स्पति॑र्नयतु दु॒र्गहा॑ ति॒रः पुन॑र्नॆषद॒घशं॑साय॒ मन्म॑ ।  
> क्षि॒पदश॑स्ति॒मप॑ दुर्म॒तिं ह॒न्नथा॑ कर॒द्यज॑मानाय॒ शं योः॥१॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बृहस्पतिः । नयतु । दुःगहा । तिरः । पुनः । नेषत् । अघशंसाय । मन्म ।  
> क्षिपत् । अशस्तिं । अप । दुःमतिं । हन् । अथ । करत् । यजमानाय । शं । योः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बृहस्पतिर्बृहतां देवानां पतिः पालयिता ॥ तद्बृहतोः करपत्योश्चोरदेवतयोः सुट् तलोपश्च । म. ६-१-१५७ । इति सुडागमस्तलोपश्च । उभे
> वनस्पत्यादिश्विति पूर्वोत्तरपदयोर्युगपत्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ दुर्गहा दुर्गमनानां
> हंता स देवस्तिरो नयतु । तिरस्कर्तव्यानि पापान्यपसारयतु । अघशंसायास्माकमनर्थमाशंसमानाय पुरुषाय मन्म । मन्यतेर्दिप्तिकर्मणो मन्म । दीप्तमायुधं पुनर्नॆषत् । नयतु ॥ नयतेर्लेट्यडागमः । सिब्बहुलमिति सिप् ॥ अपि
> चाशस्तिमयशस्विनं शत्रुं क्षिपतु । आस्मत्तः प्रेरयतु । दुर्मतिं दुर्बुद्धिं चाप
> हन् । अपहंतु । आथानंतरं शं रोगाणां शमनं योर्भयानां यावनं च
> करत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Bṛhaspati is the lord and protector of the great gods. He who is the destroyer of what is hard to get through, that god, is asked to put aside, i.e. drive away, the sins that are to be set aside. For the man who wishes us harm (अघशंसाय (*aghaśaṃsāya*)) let him bring again the shining weapon, मन्म (*manma*), from the root मन्यते (*manyate*) in the sense of shining. Further, let him cast away the inglorious enemy, driving him from us, and destroy the evil mind. Then let him bring शं (*śaṃ*), the calming of diseases, and योः (*yoḥ*), the warding off of fears.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- बृहस्पतिः (*bṛhaspatiḥ*)—Bṛhaspati, the protector of the great gods
- दुर्गहा (*durgahā*)—the remover of difficulties; that god
- तिरः नयतु (*tiraḥ nayatu*)—may he ward off the sins
- अघशंसाय (*aghaśaṃsāya*)—for the man who speaks harmful or sinful words concerning us
- मन्म (*manma*)—the shining

- पुनः नेषत् (*punaḥ neṣat*)—may he bring again; and

- क्षिपत् (*kṣipat*)—may he drive him away from our presence
- दुर्मतिं (*durmatiṃ*)—the evil mind
- अप हन् (*apa han*)—may he destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Bṛhaspati, protector of the gods, removes difficulties. May that god ward off our sins. To punish the man who speaks evil of us, may he bear and bring a shining weapon. May he drive the wicked enemy away from our neighbourhood. May he destroy the evil mind, and bring about the calming of disease and the warding off of fear.

##### English translation
Let Brihaspati, the overcomer of difficulties, put aside (all sins), let him thrust aside the weapon of the calumniator; may he hurl down the inglorious (enemy), may he baffle the malevolent, and bestow upon the sacrificer health and prosperity.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Among the five Prayāja offerings the second Prayāja has Narāśaṃsa as its deity. Narāśaṃsa, the Agni who is to be praised by men and is the deity of that Prayāja, is asked to protect us. At the invocations (हवेषु (*haveṣu*)), when there are Anuyājas: there are three Anuyājas, and the second Anuyāja is Narāśaṃsa.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तपुर्मूर्धा तापकशिरस्को बृहस्पती रक्षसो ये ब्रह्मद्विषो ब्राह्मणद्वेष्टारो राक्षसाः तान्राक्षसांस्तपतु । तापयतु । दहत्वित्यर्थः । किमर्थं । शरवे शरुं
> हिंसकं रक्षसामधिपतिं हंतवै हंतुं । अनुचरान्पूर्वं नाशयतु पश्चादेनमपि
> नाशयत्वित्यर्थः ॥ शृ हिंसायामित्यस्माच्छास्वस्निहीत्यादिनोप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेराद्युदात्तत्वं । क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थी ।
> हंतेस्तुमर्थे सेसेनिति तनैप्रत्ययः । अंतश्च तनै युगपदित्याद्यंतयोर्युगपदुदात्तत्वं । उशब्दः पूरकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Tapurmūrdhā, "he whose head burns", is Bṛhaspati. Those Rākṣasas who hate the Brahmins (ब्रह्मद्विषः (*brahmadviṣaḥ*)), let him burn, i.e. consume with heat. Why? To slay (हंतवै (*haṃtavai*)) the शरवे (*śarave*), the harmful lord of the Rākṣasas. The sense is: let him first destroy the followers, and afterwards destroy him also. The word उ (*u*) is a filler. The remaining half (क्षिपत् (*kṣipat*) and so on) is as before.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तपुमूर्धा (*tapumūrdhā*)—Bṛhaspati, the father of the ṛṣi named Tapumūrdhā
- ब्रह्मद्विषः (*brahmadviṣaḥ*)—haters of the Brahmins
- ये रक्षसः (*ye rakṣasaḥ*)—those Rākṣasas who exist, them
- तपतु (*tapatu*)—may he burn (consume and destroy)
- शरवे उ (*śarave u*)—also the harmful chief of the Rākṣasas
- हंतवै (*haṃtavai*)—in order to slay (may he burn him)
- अशस्तिं (*aśastiṃ*)—the wicked enemy
- क्षिपत् (*kṣipat*)—may he drive him away from our presence
- दुर्मतिं (*durmatiṃ*)—the evil mind
- अप हन् (*apa han*)—may he destroy
- अथ (*atha*)—afterwards
- शं (*śaṃ*)—calming of disease
- योः (*yoḥ*)—warding off of fear
- करत् (*karat*)—may he bring about

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Bṛhaspati, father of the ṛṣi Tapumūrdhā, burn and destroy the Rākṣasas who hate the Brahmins, and their harmful leader. May he drive the wicked enemy away from our neighbourhood, destroy the evil mind, and bring about the calming of disease and the warding off of fear.

##### English translation
May Tapurmurdhan consume the Rakshasas, who are the enemies of the Brahmanas, (and then proceed) to slay (their) malignant (chief); may be baffle the malevolent, and bestow upon the sacrificer health and prosperity. 

### Printed p. 1238
## Sūkta 183 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अपश्यमिति तृचं द्वात्रिंशं सूक्तं त्रैष्टुभं । प्रजापतिपुत्रः प्रजावान्नामर्षिः।
> ऋचः क्रमेण यजमानपत्निहोतृणामाशिषः प्रतिपादिकाः । अतस्तद्देवताकाः ।
> तथा चानुक्रांतं । अपश्यं प्रजावान्प्राजापत्योऽन्वृचं यजमानपत्निहोत्राशिष
> इति ॥ प्रवर्ग्येऽभिष्टव एतत्तूक्तं । सूत्र्यते हि । अपश्यं त्वेत्येतस्याद्यया यजमानमीक्षते द्वितीयया पत्निं तृतीययात्मानं ॥ अ. ४-६ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The thirty-second sūkta, अपश्यं (*apaśyaṃ*), is a triplet in Triṣṭubh metre. The ṛṣi is Prajāvān, son of Prajāpati. The Ṛks in order set forth the blessings of the sacrificer, the wife and the Hotṛ, and so have them as deities. So the Anukramaṇī says: अपश्यं प्रजावान्प्राजापत्योऽन्वृचं यजमानपत्निहोत्राशिष इति॥ (*apaśyaṃ prajāvānprājāpatyo 'nvṛcaṃ yajamānapatnihotrāśiṣa iti‖*) This sūkta is recited at the Abhiṣṭava in the Pravargya; for the sūtra says: अपश्यं त्वेत्येतस्याद्यया यजमानमीक्षते द्वितीयया पत्निं तृतीययात्मानं॥ (*apaśyaṃ tvetyetasyādyayā yajamānamīkṣate dvitīyayā patniṃ tṛtīyayātmānaṃ‖*) (Ā. 4-6).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta, अपश्यं (*apaśyaṃ*), is the thirty-second sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has three Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Prajāvān, son of Prajāpati. In its three Ṛks the sacrificer, his wife and the Hotṛ priest are addressed in order; therefore these are the deities of the respective Ṛks. The metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated: अपश्यं प्रजावान् प्राजापत्योऽन्वचं यजमानपत्निहोत्राशिषः (*apaśyaṃ prajāvān prājāpatyo 'nvacaṃ yajamānapatnihotrāśiṣaḥ*). That this sūkta is to be recited at the Abhiṣṭava of the ceremony called Pravargya is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: अपश्यं तैत्येतस्याद्यया यजमानमीक्षते द्वितीयया पत्नीं तृतीययात्मानं (*apaśyaṃ taityetasyādyayā yajamānamīkṣate dvitīyayā patnīṃ tṛtīyayātmānaṃ*) (Ā. 4-6).

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 183; Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 41. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 3. Ṛṣi: Prajāvān Prājāpatya. Deity: the sacrificer, the wife and the Hotṛ's blessings, Ṛk by Ṛk. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अप॑श्यं त्वा॒ मन॑सा॒ चेकि॑तानं॒ तप॑सो जा॒तं तप॑सो॒ विभू॑तं ।  
> इ॒ह प्र॒जामि॒ह र॒यिं ररा॑णः॒ प्र जा॑यस्व प्र॒जया॑ पुत्रकाम॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अपश्यं । त्वा । मनसा । चेकितानं । तपसः । जातु । तपसः । विभूतं ।  
> इह । प्रजां । इह । रयिं । रराणः । प्र । जायस्व । प्रजया । पुत्रकाम ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 1239

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे यजमान त्वा त्वां मनसा बुद्ध्यापश्यं । अदर्शं । कीदृशं । चेकितानं
> कर्माणि भृशं जानंतं तपसो दीक्षारूपाद्वृताज्ञातं पुनरुत्पन्नं यद्वा
> जन्मांतरानुष्ठितात्सुकृतादुत्पन्नं तपसोऽनुष्ठीयमानाद्यज्ञाद्देतोर्विभूते
> व्याप्तं सर्वत्र प्रख्यातं । हे पुत्रकाम पुत्रान्कामयमान स त्वमिहास्मिल्लोके
> प्रजां पुत्रपौत्रादिरूपां रराणो रमयन् रयिं धनमिहास्मिल्लोके रमयन्
> प्रजया प्रजनेन प्र जायस्व । पुत्रादिरूपेणोत्पद्यस्व । प्रजा उत्पादयेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O sacrificer, I saw you with the mind, with the understanding." What kind? चेकितानं (*cekitānaṃ*): one who knows the rites well; तपसो जातं (*tapaso jātaṃ*): born again from the austerity in the form of the dīkṣā vow; or, alternatively, born of good deeds performed in another birth; तपसो विभूतं (*tapaso vibhūtaṃ*): pervading, famed everywhere through the sacrifice being performed. "O you who desire sons (पुत्रकाम (*putrakāma*)), you here in this world, delighting in offspring in the form of sons, grandsons and so on, and delighting in wealth here in this world, be born through offspring, i.e. arise in the form of a son; the meaning is: beget offspring."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (The wife's speech to the sacrificer. O sacrificer)
- चेकितानं (*cekitānaṃ*)—one who knows well the rites such as the sacrifice
- तपसः (*tapasaḥ*)—by the rite in the form of the dīkṣā
- जातं (*jātaṃ*)—one born again, or one born of good deeds done in another birth
- तपसः (*tapasaḥ*)—by the austerity of the sacrifice and the like which you perform
- विभूतं (*vibhūtaṃ*)—and renowned everywhere
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- मनसा (*manasā*)—with the understanding
- अपश्यं (*apaśyaṃ*)—I saw and knew
- पुत्रकाम (*putrakāma*)—O sacrificer who desire sons, you
- इह (*iha*)—in this world
- प्रजां (*prajāṃ*)—the line of sons, grandsons and so on
- रराणः (*rarāṇaḥ*)—(obtaining) and enjoying
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—and obtaining wealth also
- इह (*iha*)—in this world
- प्रजया (*prajayā*)—in the form of a son (you yourself)
- प्र जायस्व (*pra jāyasva*)—be born (beget sons and the rest)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(The wife's speech addressed to the sacrificer.) O sacrificer, you who know well the rites such as the sacrifice, who are regarded as born again through the rite of the dīkṣā, or who are born of the special good deeds of another birth, and who have become famed through performing sacrifices and other rites: I saw and knew you with the understanding. O sacrificer who desire sons, obtaining in this world the line of sons, grandsons and so on, and wealth, be born yourself in this world in the form of a son; that is, beget sons.

##### English translation
(The wife speaks :) I beheld you in my mind conversant (with sacred rites), born of penance, renowned for penance; enjoying in this world progeny and riches, do you who are desirous of offspring beget offspring.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

As the Śruti sentence आत्मा वै पुत्रनामासि (*ātmā vai putranāmāsi*) says, the father himself is born as a son from his own part. Since sons are born from the father's seed, it is said that the father himself is born as the son.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अप॑श्यं त्वा॒ मन॑सा॒ दीध्या॑नां॒ स्वायां॑ त॒नू ऋत्वे॒ नाध॑मानां ।  
> उप॒ मामु॒च्चा यु॑व॒तिर्ब॑र्भूयाः॒ प्र जा॑यस्व प्र॒जया॑  
> पुत्रकामे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अपश्यं । त्वा । मनसा । दीध्यानां । स्वायां । तनू इति । ऋत्वे । नाधमानां ।  
> उप । मां । उच्चा । युवतिः । बभूयाः । प्र । जायस्व । प्रजया । पुत्रकामे ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पत्नि दीध्यानां दीप्यमानां स्वायामात्मीयायां तनू तन्वां शरीर
> ऋत्वे । ऋतुकाले भवं गर्भधारणरूपं कर्मत्वियं । तस्मिन्निमित्तभूते नाधमानां भर्तुरुपगमनं याचमानां त्वा त्वां मनसापश्यं । आद्राक्षं । हे पुत्रकामे पुत्रान्कामयमाने मामुप मत्समीपं प्राप्य सा त्वमुच्चोच्चैर्भृशं
> युवतिस्तरुणी बभूयाः । भूयाः ॥ छंदस्युभयथेत्याशीर्लिजः सार्वधातुकत्वाच्छप् । तस्य छांदसः श्लुः । अलिट्यपि व्यत्ययेन भवतेरः । पा. ७-४-२३ । इत्यभ्यासस्यात्वं ॥ युवतिर्भूत्वा च प्रजया प्रजनेन प्र जायस्व । पुत्रान्प्रसूष्व ॥ जनी
> प्रादुर्भावे । श्यनि ज्ञाजनोर्जॆति जादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O wife, I have seen you with my mind, shining in your own body at the Ṛtu-time (the act of conception that belongs to the fertile season), and begging for your husband's approach." Sāyaṇa glosses दीध्यानां (*dīdhyānāṃ*) as "shining" and स्वायां (*svāyāṃ*) as "one's own". He glosses ऋत्वे (*ṛtve*) as "belonging to the season of fertility, having the form of conception". He glosses नाधमानां (*nādhamānāṃ*) as "requesting the husband's approach", this being the occasion for it. "O you who desire sons, having come near me, be exceedingly youthful (युवतिः (*yuvatiḥ*) = young woman). Having become youthful, bring forth sons by procreation." प्र जायस्व (*pra jāyasva*) is explained as "bear sons", from the root meaning "to come into being". (The grammatical remarks are omitted.)

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वायां (*svāyāṃ*)—your
- तनू (*tanū*)—body
- ऋत्वे (*ṛtve*)—when, after the bath following the period, it is ready for union with the husband
- नाधमानां (*nādhamānāṃ*)—longing for the company of the husband
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- मनसा (*manasā*)—having known with the mind
- अपश्यं (*apaśyaṃ*)—I saw
- पुत्रकामे (*putrakāme*)—O wife who desire to have sons
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- उप (*upa*)—you who have come near
- उच्चा युवतिः (*uccā yuvatiḥ*)—having become exceedingly young (a youthful woman)
- बभूयाः (*babhūyāḥ*)—you are (therefore)
- प्रजया (*prajayā*)—by procreation (by childbirth)
- प्र जायस्व (*pra jāyasva*)—bear sons

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(The yajamāna's words:) O wife, this body of yours, shining with youth, longs for the company of the husband after the bath following the period. I have seen you, such as you are, having known it with my mind. O wife, desiring to have sons: you who have approached me wishing for sons are exceedingly young and shine with youthfulness. Therefore bring forth sons (bear them).

##### English translation
(The yajamana speaks:) I beheld you in my mind radiant (with beauty), beseeching (your husband's approach) to your body at due season ; may you, who are youthful, come up to me; bear offspring, you who are desirous of offspring.

> यागेन सर्वस्योत्पत्तेरहं सर्वजनहेतुर्भवामीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Hotṛ says: "I place the embryo in the herbs, in rice and the like, for the sake of fruit. In all the other worlds, among all born beings, I alone place the embryo. So too on the earth I beget the progeny, all human beings. I beget sons in the women other than the wives." The meaning is that, since everything comes into being through the sacrifice that I accomplish, I am the cause of all birth.

- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I, the Hotṛ-priest

- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—the embryo
- अदधां (*adadhāṃ*)—I cause it to be borne

- विश्वेषु (*viśveṣu*)—in all
- भुवनेषु अंतः (*bhuvaneṣu aṃtaḥ*)—in the bodies of living beings also
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I myself cause the bearing of the embryo (and so)
- पृथिव्यां (*pṛthivyāṃ*)—on the earth
- प्रजाः (*prajāḥ*)—all human beings
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- अजनयं (*ajanayaṃ*)—I cause them to come into being
- जनिभ्यः (*janibhyaḥ*)—apart from the wives
- अपरीषु (*aparīṣu*)—in other women also
- पुत्रान् (*putrān*)—sons
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I beget

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

(The Hotṛ's words:) I, the priest called Hotṛ, cause the herbs and other plants (creepers, trees and so on) to bear the embryo, so that they may bear fruit. In the bodies of all living beings too, I myself cause the embryo to be borne. On the earth I cause all human beings to come into being. In women other than wives also I cause sons to be born.

##### English translation
(The hotri speaks :) I implant the seed in vegetables, the germ in all living beings ; I engender progeny upon the earth ; I beget children on other women.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The priest called Hotṛ speaks thus: By the power of my mantra I cause the plants and trees to bear fruit. I cause the embryo to be borne in the bodies of all living beings. In order that human beings may come into being on the earth, I cause the embryo to be borne both in wives and in women other than wives.
## Sūkta 184 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विष्णुरिति तृचं त्रयस्त्रिंशं सूक्तमानुष्टुभं । गर्भाणां त्वष्टा नामर्षिः
> प्रजापतिपुत्रो विष्णुर्वा । लिंगोक्ता विष्णुत्वष्टृप्रजापतिसिनीवालीसरस्वत्यश्विन इति
> देवताः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । विष्णुस्तृष्टा गर्भकर्ता विष्णुर्वा प्राजापत्यो गर्भार्थाशीर्लिंगोक्तदैवतमानुष्टुभमिति ॥ लैंगिको विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*) is a group of three Ṛks, the thirty-third sūkta, in the Anuṣṭubh metre. Its seer is Tvaṣṭṛ, called Garbhakartṛ ("maker of embryos"), or else Viṣṇu, son of Prajāpati. Its deities are those named in the Ṛks themselves: Viṣṇu, Tvaṣṭṛ, Prajāpati, Sinīvālī, Sarasvatī and the Aśvins. Sāyaṇa cites the Anukramaṇī to the same effect: the seer is Viṣṇu or Tvaṣṭṛ the maker of the embryo, or else a Prajāpati's son; the sūkta is a blessing for an embryo, its deities are those named in the verses, and its metre is Anuṣṭubh. The application is Laiṅgika (by the indication of the verse itself).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Translation: This sūkta beginning विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*) is the thirty-third sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has three Ṛks. The deity Tvaṣṭṛ, maker of embryos, is the seer of this sūkta, or else Viṣṇu, son of Prajāpati, is the seer. The deities named in the Ṛks, that is, Viṣṇu, Tvaṣṭṛ, Prajāpati, Sinīvālī, Sarasvatī and the Aśvins, are the deities. The metre is Anuṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: विष्णुस्त्वष्टा गर्भकर्ता विष्णुर्वा प्राजापत्यो गर्भार्थाशीर्लिंगोक्तदैवतमानुष्टुभं (*viṣṇustvaṣṭā garbhakartā viṣṇurvā prājāpatyo garbhārthāśīrliṃgoktadaivatamānuṣṭubhaṃ*). The application is Laiṅgika. Sūkta 184.

### Printed p. 1243
Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 184. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 42. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 3. Seer: Tvaṣṭṛ the maker of embryos, or Viṣṇu, son of Prajāpati. Deity: the deities named in the verses (Viṣṇu, Tvaṣṭṛ, Prajāpati, Sinīvālī, Sarasvatī, the Aśvins); a blessing for an embryo. Metre: Anuṣṭubh.
#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विष्णु॒र्योनिं॑ कल्पयतु॒ त्वष्टा॑ रू॒पाणि॑ पिंशतु ।  
> आ सिं॑चतु प्र॒जाप॑तिर्धा॒ता गर्भं॑ दधातु ते ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विष्णुः । योनिं । कल्पयतु । त्वष्टा । रूपाणि । पिंशतु ।  
> आ । सिंचतु । प्रजापतिः । धाता । गर्भं । दधातु । ते ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विष्णुर्व्यापको देवो योनिं गर्भाधानस्थानं कल्पयतु । करोतु । त्वष्टा
> तनुकर्तैतत्संज्ञको देवश्च रूपाणि निरूपकाणि स्त्रीत्वपुंस्त्वाभिव्यंजकानि चिह्नानि
> पिंशतु । अवयवीकरोतु ॥ पिश अवयवे । मुचादित्वान्नुम् ॥ एवं प्रक्लप्तायां
> योन्यां प्रजापती रेत आ सिंचतु । निषिंचतु । सृजत्वित्यर्थः । धाता धारको देवो
> हे जाये ते तव गर्भं गर्भरूपेण परिणतं तद्रेतो दधातु । तत्रैव धारयतु ।
> गर्भपातापप्रसवा मा भूवन्नित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May Viṣṇu, the all-pervading god, make the womb, the place where the embryo is laid. May Tvaṣṭṛ, the shaper of bodies, a god of that name, carve out the forms, that is, the marks that show female or male state; "may he give them limbs". When the womb has been so prepared, may Prajāpati sprinkle the seed into it ("pour it in, emit it"). May Dhātṛ, the god who supports, place there the seed of you, O wife, which has turned into an embryo, that is, make it stay there; the meaning is that there should be no miscarriage, fall, or untimely birth. (The grammatical remarks on the root पिश (*piśa*) are omitted.)

### Printed p. 1244

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*)—the god Viṣṇu, who pervades everywhere
- योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—the womb (the female part), the place where the embryo is laid
- कल्पयतु (*kalpayatu*)—let him make (construct)
- त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*)—the god Tvaṣṭṛ
- रूपाणि (*rūpāṇi*)—the marks that show female and male form
- पिंशतु (*piṃśatu*)—let him show them with the respective limbs; in such a womb
- प्रजापतिः (*prajāpatiḥ*)—the god Prajāpati (the creator)
- आ सिंचतु (*ā siṃcatu*)—let him sprinkle the seed (semen)
- धाता (*dhātā*)—the god Dhātṛ, who supports and nourishes all (O wife)
- ते (*te*)—your
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—that seed which has turned into an embryo
- दधातु (*dadhātu*)—let him make it remain there

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Viṣṇu, the all-pervading, make the womb, the place where the embryo is laid. May the god Tvaṣṭṛ make the forms furnished with marks suitable to woman and man, that is, the limbs of woman and man. May Prajāpati pour the seed into that womb. O wife, may the god Dhātṛ, who supports and nourishes all, make that seed, which has turned into your embryo, stay there (bear it).

##### English translation
May Vishnu construct the womb, may Twastri fabricate the members, may Prajapati sprinkle (the seed), may Dratri cherish your embryo.
#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> गर्भं॑ धेहि सिनीवालि॒ गर्भं॑ धेहि सरस्वति ।  
> गर्भं॑ ते अ॒श्विनौ॑ दे॒वावा ध॑त्तां॒ पुष्क॑रस्रजा ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गर्भं । धेहि । सिनीवालि । गर्भं । धेहि । सरस्वति ।  
> गर्भं । ते । अश्विन् । देवौ । आ । धत्तां । पुष्करस्रजा ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सिनीवाल्येतत्संज्ञॆ देवि गर्भं धेहि । निषिक्तं गर्भं धारय । हे सरस्वति
> त्वं च निषिक्तं गर्भं धारय । हे जाये पुष्करस्रजा पुष्करमालिनौ स्वर्णकमलाभरणावश्विन् देवौ ते तव गर्भमा धत्तां । प्रक्षिपतां । कुरुतामित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Sinīvālī, goddess of that name, hold the embryo that has been poured in. O Sarasvatī, you also hold the poured-in embryo. O wife, may the two Aśvin gods, garlanded with lotuses (पुष्करस्रजा (*puṣkarasrajā*), adorned with golden lotuses), place your embryo; the meaning of आ धत्तां (*ā dhattāṃ*) is "let them put it in, let them make it".

### Printed p. 1245

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सिनीवालि (*sinīvāli*)—O goddess called Sinīvālī
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—the embryo in the womb
- धेहि (*dhehi*)—hold; that is, so that the woman's embryo does not fall through discharge or the like, make the embryo remain growing in the woman's womb
- सरस्वति (*sarasvati*)—O Sarasvatī, you also
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—the woman's embryo
- धेहि (*dhehi*)—make it be borne (O wife)
- पुष्करस्रजा (*puṣkarasrajā*)—adorned with garlands of golden lotuses
- अश्विन् देवौ (*aśvin devau*)—the Aśvin deities
- ते (*te*)—your
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—embryo
- आ धत्तां (*ā dhattāṃ*)—let them make it be borne (let them protect the embryo)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Sinīvālī, O Sarasvatī, make this woman bear the embryo and protect it. O wife, may the Aśvin deities also, adorned with garlands of golden lotuses, bear and protect your embryo.

##### English translation
Sustain the embryo, Sinivali, sustain the embryo, Saraswati, may the divine Aswins, garlanded with lotuses, sustain your embryo.
#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हि॒र॒ण्यया॑ अ॒रणी॒ यं नि॒र्मंथ॑तो अ॒श्विना॑ ।  
> तं ते॒ गर्भं॑ हवामहे दश॒मे मा॒सि सूत॑वे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हिरण्यया इति । अरणी इति । यं । निःमंथतः । अश्विना ।  
> तं । ते । गर्भं । हवामहे । दशमे । मासि । सूतवे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हिरण्यया हिरण्मय्यावरणी यं गर्भमुद्दिश्याश्विनाश्विन् देवौ निर्मंथतः
> निर्मथितवंतौ हे जाये ते तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं तं गर्भं हनामहे । आह्वयामहे !
> दशमे मासि सूतवे प्रसोतुं ॥ पद्दन्नित्यादिना मासशब्दस्य मास्भावः । सूतेस्तुमर्थे सेसेनिति तवेन्प्रत्ययः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With reference to the embryo which the two Aśvin gods churned out with two golden fire-sticks (अरणी (*araṇī*)), O wife, for you, that is, on your behalf, we invoke that embryo in order that it may be born in the tenth month. (Remarks on मासि (*māsi*) and the ending of सूतवे (*sūtave*) are omitted.)

### Printed p. 1246

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—the Aśvin deities (O woman)
- हिरण्यया (*hiraṇyayā*)—golden
- अरणी (*araṇī*)—the fire-sticks
- यं (*yaṃ*)—with reference to which embryo
- निर्मंथतः (*nirmaṃthataḥ*)—they churned
- तं (*taṃ*)—such
- ते (*te*)—your
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—embryo
- दशमे मासि (*daśame māsi*)—in the tenth month
- सूतवे (*sūtave*)—for the purpose of birth
- हवामहे (*havāmahe*)—we desire and invoke

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O woman, that embryo of yours, for which the Aśvin deities churned the golden fire-sticks, we desire and call, that it may be born in the tenth month.

##### English translation
We invoke your embryo which the Ashwins have churned with the golden pieces of touchwood, that you may bring it forth in the tenth month.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The Khila mantras to be recited at the end of this sūkta:
त्वष्टा रूपकर्ता । विष्णुः । अनुष्टुप् ॥ (*tvaṣṭā rūpakartā | viṣṇuḥ | anuṣṭup ‖*)
नेजमेष पराशकॆ सुपुत्रः पुनरा पॆत । अस्यै मे पुत्रकामाय्कॆ गर्भमा धेहि यः पुमान् ॥ (*nejameṣa parāśakè suputraḥ punarā pèta | asyai me putrakāmāykè garbhamā dhehi yaḥ pumān ‖*)
यथेयं पृथिवी महुत्ताना गर्भमादधे । एवं तं गर्भमा धेहि दशमे मासि सूतवे ॥ (*yatheyaṃ pṛthivī mahuttānā garbhamādadhe | evaṃ taṃ garbhamā dhehi daśame māsi sūtave ‖*)
विष्णोः श्रेष्ठेन रूपेणास्यां नार्यां गवीन्यां । पुमांसं पुत्राना धेहि दशमे मासि सूतवे ॥ (*viṣṇoḥ śreṣṭhena rūpeṇāsyāṃ nāryāṃ gavīnyāṃ | pumāṃsaṃ putrānā dhehi daśame māsi sūtave ‖*)**NOTE**
## Sūkta 185 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महीति तृचं चतुस्त्रिंशं सूक्तं वरुणपुत्रस्य सत्यधृतेरार्षं गायत्रमादित्यदेवताकं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । महि सत्यधृतिर्वारुणिरादित्यं स्वस्त्ययनं गायत्रं
> वा इति ॥ धनलिप्सया प्रवसंतं शिष्यमाचार्योऽनेन सूक्तेनाभिमंत्रयते ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning मही (*mahī*) is a group of three Ṛks, the thirty-fourth sūkta. It is the work (seer) of Satyadhṛti, son of Varuṇa, in the Gāyatrī metre, and its deity is Āditya. Sāyaṇa cites the Anukramaṇī: महि (*mahi*), seer Satyadhṛti Vāruṇi, deity Āditya, a prayer for welfare, Gāyatrī (or else the metre is different). The teacher recites this sūkta over a pupil who is going abroad out of desire for wealth.

### Printed p. 1247

> सूत्र्यते हि । महि त्रीणामित्यनुमंत्रैवमतिसृष्टस्य न कुतश्चिद्धयं भवतीति विज्ञायते । आ. गृ. १०-७-८ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa states the ritual use: it is prescribed in the Sūtra. "महि त्रीणां (*mahi trīṇāṃ*)" — having addressed him with this mantra, the pupil who has been so released (sent forth) has no fear from any quarter, so it is understood. He cites Ā. Gṛ. 10-7-8.

##### Anuvāda (Kannada)

This sūkta beginning "mahi" is the thirty-fourth sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has three ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Satyadhṛti, son of Varuṇa; the deity is Āditya; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated: महि सत्यधृतिर्वारुणिरादिश्यं स्वस्त्ययनं गायत्रं वा (*mahi satyadhṛtirvāruṇirādiśyaṃ svastyayanaṃ gāyatraṃ vā*). For the welfare of a pupil who is desirous of wealth, the teacher should consecrate the pupil with this sūkta; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra, महि त्रीणामित्र नुमंत्र्यॆवमतिसृष्टस्य न कुतश्चिद्धयं भवतीति विज्ञायते (*mahi trīṇāmitra numaṃtryèvamatisṛṣṭasya na kutaściddhayaṃ bhavatīti vijñāyate*) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-10-7, 8).

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 185. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 43. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 3. Ṛṣi: Satyadhṛti Vāruṇi. Deity: Āditya (Svastyayana). Metre: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> महि॑ त्री॒णामवो॑ऽस्तु द्यु॒क्षं मि॒त्रस्या॑र्य॒म्णः ।  
> दु॒रा॒धर्षं॒ वरु॑णस्य ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> महि । त्रीणां । अवः । अस्तु । द्युक्षं । मित्रस्य । अर्यम्नः ।  
> दुःआधर्षं । वरुणस्य ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्रीणां त्रयाणां मित्रस्यार्यन्नो वरुणस्य च द्युक्षं दीपं अत एव दुराधर्षमन्यैर्धर्षितुं बाधितुमशक्यं महि महदवो रक्षणमस्माकमस्तु । त्रीणामित्यपि
> छंदसि दृश्यत इति वचनात् । का. ७-१-५३-१ । त्रयादेशाभावः । नामन्यतरस्यामिति
> नाम उदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of the three, Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa, may there be for us a great protection, bright (द्युक्षं (*dyukṣaṃ*) = shining) and therefore unassailable, which others cannot overcome or obstruct. त्रीणां (*trīṇāṃ*) is "of three"; the form त्रीणां (*trīṇāṃ*) is seen in the Veda, so the substitute त्रय (*traya*) does not occur. The accent of the noun is udātta.

### Printed p. 1248

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रस्य (*mitrasya*)—of Mitra
- अर्यम्मः (*aryammaḥ*)—of the god called Aryaman
- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—of Varuṇa
- श्रीणां (*śrīṇāṃ*)—of these three deities **NOTE**
- द्युक्षं (*dyukṣaṃ*)—shining
- दुराधर्षं (*durādharṣaṃ*)—impossible to be harassed by others
- महि (*mahi*)—great
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—protection
- अस्तु (*astu*)—let it be ours

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the shining, great protection of these three deities, Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa, which others cannot injure, be ours.

##### English translation
May the great, brilliant, unassailable protection of the three (deities), Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuna, be (granted to me).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न॒हि तेषा॑म॒मा च॒न नाध्व॑सु वार॒णेषु॑ ।  
> ईशे॑ रि॒पुर॒घशं॑सः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नहि । तेषां । अमा । चन । न । अध्वसु । वारणेषु ।  
> ईशे । रिपुः । अघशंसः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अमेति गृहनाम । अमा चन गृहेष्टपि तेषां वरुणमित्रार्यम्मां तदनुगृहीतानां स्तोत्थाणां वाघशंसोऽघमनर्थमाशंसमानो रिपुः शत्रुर्न हीशे । न
> खलु हिंसितुमीष्टे ॥ लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्टिति तलोपः । अनुदात्तेत्वाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ॥ तथाध्वसु मार्गेषु वारणेषु यत्र पुरुषा
> निवार्यंते तेषु च स्थानेषु शत्रुर्निवारयितुं नेष्टे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

अमा (*amā*) is a name for house. Even in houses, no enemy who wishes harm (अघशंसः (*aghaśaṃsaḥ*), one who announces evil) has power over them, Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman, or over their worshippers whom they favour; he is not able to harm. Likewise in roads (अध्वसु (*adhvasu*)) and in वारणेषु (*vāraṇeṣu*), places where men are held back, the enemy is not able to restrain them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अमा चन (*amā cana*)—in our houses also
- तेषां (*teṣāṃ*)—of those Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman, or of their worshippers
- अघशंसः (*aghaśaṃsaḥ*)—one who boasts of his own evil deed
- रिपुः (*ripuḥ*)—the enemy
- नहि ईशे (*nahi īśe*)—let him not be able to harm us
- वारणेषु (*vāraṇeṣu*)—narrow
- अध्वसु (*adhvasu*)—in roads also
- न (*na*)—let him not harm us

### Printed p. 1249

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the treacherous enemy of Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman, or of the people who praise them, not trouble us in our houses. May he not harm us on narrow roads either.

##### English translation
Let not their malignant enemy have power over dwellings, or roads or enclosures.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्मै॑ पु॒त्रासो॒ अदि॑तेः॒ प्र जी॒वसे॒ मर्त्या॑य ।  
> ज्योति॒र्यच्छं॒त्यज॑स्रं ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यस्मै । पुत्रासः । अदितेः । प्र । जीवसे । मर्त्याय ।  
> ज्योतिः । यच्छंति । अजस्रं ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अदितेरदीनाया देवमातुः पुत्रासः पुत्रा मित्रादयो यस्मै मर्त्याय
> मनुष्याय स्तोत्रेजस्रमविच्छिन्नं ज्योतिस्तेजो जीवसे जीवितुं प्रयच्छंति तस्य

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sons of Aditi, the undiminished mother of the gods, Mitra and the rest, bestow on whatever mortal, a man who praises them, unbroken light, splendour, that he may live; over him the enemy is not master. This is the meaning.

- अदितेः (*aditeḥ*)—of Aditi, mother of the gods
- पुत्रासः (*putrāsaḥ*)—the sons, Mitra and the others
- यस्मै (*yasmai*)—for whichever

- अजस्रं (*ajasraṃ*)—unbroken
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—splendour (strength)
- जीवसे (*jīvase*)—for living
- प्रयच्छंति (*prayacchaṃti*)—give; let the enemy not harm such a man

For whatever praising man the sons of the goddess Aditi, the undiminished mother of the gods, Mitra and the other deities, bestow unbroken splendour, that is, strength, may the enemy not harm such a man.

## Sūkta 186 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वात इति तृचं पंचत्रिंशं सूक्तं वातगोत्रस्कोलस्यार्षं गायत्रं वायुदेवताकं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । वातो वातायन उलो वायव्यमिति ॥ गतो
> विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta वात (*vāta*), a tṛca, the thirty-fifth sūkta, has as ṛṣi Ula of the Vāta family; the metre is Gāyatrī; the deity is Vāyu. So the Anukramaṇikā: वातो वातायन उलो वायव्यमिति (*vāto vātāyana ulo vāyavyamiti*). The viniyoga has already been given.

##### Anuvāda (Kannada)

This sūkta beginning "वातः (*vātaḥ*)" is the thirty-fifth sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has three ṛks. Its ṛṣi is Ula of the Vāta family; the deity is Vāyu; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated वातो वातायन उलो वायव्यं (*vāto vātāyana ulo vāyavyaṃ*). The viniyoga was stated earlier.

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 12; Sūkta 186. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 8; Varga 44. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 3. Ṛṣi: Ula Vātāyana. Deity: Vāyu. Metre: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वात॒ आ वा॑तु भेष॒जं शं॒भु म॑यो॒भु नो॑ हृ॒दे ।  
> प्र ण॒ आयूं॑षि तारिषत् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वातः । आ । वातु । भेषजं । शंभु । मयःभु । नः । हृदे ।  
> प्र । नः । आयूंषि । तारिषत् ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 1251

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वातो वायुर्नोऽस्माकं हृदे हृदयाय भेषजमौषधमुदकं ना वातु ।
> आगमयतु । कीदृग्भूतं । शंभु रोगशमनस्य भावयितृ मयोभु सुखस्य च
> भावयितृ । अपि च नोऽस्माकमायुंषि प्र तारिषत् । प्रवर्धयतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May Vāta, the wind, blow to our heart a remedy, a medicine, water. Of what kind? शंभु (*śaṃbhu*), that which brings about the calming of disease, and मयोभु (*mayobhu*), that which brings about happiness. And may he carry our lives forward, increase them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वातः (*vātaḥ*)—the wind
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- हृदे (*hṛde*)—for the heart (mind), to produce happiness
- शंभु (*śaṃbhu*)—that which calms disease
- मयोभु (*mayobhu*)—that which is beneficial to the mind
- भेषजं (*bheṣajaṃ*)—beneficial medicine
- आ वातु (*ā vātu*)—let him come blowing
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- आयूंषि (*āyūṃṣi*)—the measure of life, that is, spans of life
- प्र तारिषत् (*pra tāriṣat*)—let him increase

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the joy of our minds, may the wind come blowing to us a beneficial medicine that calms disease and gives the mind happiness, and may that wind increase our life, that is, make us live long.

##### English translation
May Vata breathe into our hearts a healing balm, bringing happiness; may he prolong our lives.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has given the Nirukta for this: वात आ वातु भैषज्यानि शंभु मयोभु च नो हृदयाय प्रवर्धयतु च न आयुः (*vāta ā vātu bhaiṣajyāni śaṃbhu mayobhu ca no hṛdayāya pravardhayatu ca na āyuḥ*) (Ni. 10-35). शंभु (*śaṃbhu*) means that which produces happiness for the body, that is, the remover of disease. मयोभु (*mayobhu*) means that which produces benefit for the mind, that is, joy. May the wind come blowing to us these two kinds of medicine, that is, means of happiness, for the joy of our minds, that is, blow them to us. And may he increase the span of our life.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त वा॑त पि॒तासि॑ न उ॒त भ्रातो॒त नः॒ सखा॑ ।  
> स नो॑ जी॒वात॑वे कृधि ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 1252

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । पात । पिता । असि । नः । उत । भ्राता । उत । नः । सखा ।  
> सः । नः । जीवातवे । कृधि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च हे वात त्वं नोऽस्माकं पितासि । उत्पादको भवसि । उतापि च
> भ्राता भवसि । उतापि च नोऽस्माकं सखा समानख्यानो पितृभूतश्च भवसि । स त्वं
> नोऽस्माइज्वातवे जीवनहेतवे यागाय कृधि । कुरु ॥ करोतेश्चांदसो
> विकरणस्य लुक् । श्रुशृणुप्यकृवृभ्य इति हेर्धिः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vāta, you are our father, our begetter; you are also our brother; and you are our friend, of like renown and like a father. Such as you, make us, कृधि (*kṛdhi*) (do), for living, that is, for sacrifice as the cause of life.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- वात (*vāta*)—O Vāyu, you
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- पिता असि (*pitā asi*)—are a begetting father
- उत (*uta*)—also
- भ्राता (*bhrātā*)—are a brother
- उत (*uta*)—and
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- सखा (*sakhā*)—are a friend too
- सः (*saḥ*)—such you
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- जीवातवे (*jīvātave*)—for living (long)
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make (fit)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

And, O Vāyu, you are a father to us, that is, as beneficial as a begetting father. You are also brother and friend. Such as you, grant that we may live long.

##### English translation
You, Vata, are both our father and our brother and our friend; cause us to live.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यद॒दो वा॑त ते गृ॒हे॒३॒॑ ३ मृत॑स्य नि॒धिर्हि॒तः ।  
> ततो॑ नो देहि जी॒वसे॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । अदः । वात । ते । गृहे । अमृतस्य । निधिः । हितः ।

### Printed p. 1253

> ततः । नः । देहि । जीवसे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वात वायो ते तव गृहे स्थाने यददो योऽसावमृतस्यामरणस्य
> निधिर्निक्षेपो हितः स्थापितो वर्तते ततस्तस्मान्निधेराहृत्यामृतत्वं जीवसे नोऽस्माकं
> जीवनाय देहि । प्रयच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vāta, in your house, in your abode, there is placed a store of ambrosia (the deathless); from that store bring it and give it to us for our living, that is, bestow it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वात (*vāta*)—O Vāyu
- ते (*te*)—your
- गृहे (*gṛhe*)—in the dwelling-place
- यत् आदः (*yat ādaḥ*)—which this
- अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—of ambrosia (that which prevents death)
- निधिः (*nidhiḥ*)—the store
- हितः (*hitaḥ*)—is placed
- ततः (*tataḥ*)—from that store of ambrosia, bringing a little portion
- जीवसे (*jīvase*)—in order to live for a long time
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- देहि (*dehi*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vāyu, in whatever store of ambrosia is in your house, that is, in the heavenly world that is your dwelling-place, bring a little portion of that ambrosia and give it to us, so that we may live for a long time.

##### English translation
That store of ambrosia, Vata, which is placed in your house, give us of it that we may live.

## Sūkta 187 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्राग्नय इति पंचर्चं षट्त्रिंशं सूक्तं । अग्नेः पुत्रस्य वत्सस्यार्षं गायत्रमाग्नेयं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । प्राग्नये पंचाग्नेयो वत्स आग्नेयं त्विति ॥
> प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोगायत्रे छंदसीदमादिके द्वे सूक्ते । सूत्र्यते हि ।
> प्राग्नये वाचमिति सूक्ते इमां मे अग्ने समिधं । आ. ४-१३ । इति ॥ दशरात्रस्य
> नवमेऽहन्याग्निमारुत इदं जातवेदसं निविद्वानं । सूत्रितं च । मरुतो यस्य हि
> प्राग्नये वाचमित्याग्निमारुतं । आ. ८-११ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn beginning प्राग्नये (*prāgnaye*) is the thirty-sixth sūkta, of five Ṛks. Its seer is Vatsa, son of Agni; the metre is Gāyatrī; the deity is Agni. As the Anukramaṇī says: प्राग्नये पंचाग्नेयो वत्स आग्नेयं त्विति॥ (*prāgnaye paṃcāgneyo vatsa āgneyaṃ tviti‖*). Use: in the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra, this and the next sūkta are used for the Gāyatrī-metre portion; it is stated in the sūtra प्राग्नये वाचमिति सूक्ते इमां मे अग्ने समिधं (*prāgnaye vācamiti sūkte imāṃ me agne samidhaṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 4-13). On the ninth day of the Daśarātra, in the Āgnimāruta (śastra), it is the Nivid-hymn: मरुतो यस्य हि प्राग्नये वाचमित्याग्निमारुतं (*maruto yasya hi prāgnaye vācamityāgnimārutaṃ*) (Ā. Sū. 8-11).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The Kannada Anuvāda says: this hymn प्राग्नये (*prāgnaye*) is the thirty-sixth sūkta in the twelfth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. The seer is Vatsa, son of Agni; the deity is Agni; the metre is Gāyatrī. The Anukramaṇī says: प्राग्नये पंचाग्नेयो वत्स आग्नेयं (*prāgnaye paṃcāgneyo vatsa āgneyaṃ*).

### Printed p. 1254
(The Anuvāda continues:) At the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra mantras, this hymn and the one after it are applied to the Gāyatrī-metre mantras, as explained by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra प्राग्नये वाचमिति सूक्त इमां मे अग्ने समिधं (*prāgnaye vācamiti sūkta imāṃ me agne samidhaṃ*) (Ā. 4-13). On the ninth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, in the middle of the Āgnimāruta śastra mantras, this hymn is to be inserted and recited as the Nivid-hymn praising Jātavedas Agni, as explained by the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra मरुतो यस्य हि प्राग्नये वाचमित्याग्निमारुतं (*maruto yasya hi prāgnaye vācamityāgnimārutaṃ*) (Ā. 8-11).

Maṇḍala 10, Anuvāka 12, Sūkta 187; Aṣṭaka 8, Adhyāya 8, Varga 45. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Vatsa Āgneya. Deity: Agni. Metre: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्राग्नये॒ वाच॑मीरय वृष॒भाय॑ क्षिती॒नां ।  
> स नः॑ पर्ष॒दति॒ द्विषः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । अग्नये । वाचं । ईरय । वृषभाय । क्षितीनां ।  
> सः । नः । पर्षत् । अति । द्विषः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे स्तोतः अग्नये स्तुतिरूपां वाचं प्रेरय । उच्चारय । कथंभूताय ।
> क्षितीनां मनुष्याणां यजमानानां वृषभाय कामानां वर्षित्रे । किं प्रयोजनमिति चेत् । सोऽग्निर्नोऽस्मान्द्विषो द्वेष्टानति पर्षत् । अतिपारयेत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praiser, send forth, that is, utter, a speech in the form of praise to Agni, who is the showerer of desires for the kṣitis, that is, men, the sacrificers. If asked what the purpose is: may that Agni carry us across those who hate us, that is, our enemies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O praiser) क्षितीनां (*kṣitīnāṃ*)—to the human sacrificers
- वृषभायॆ (*vṛṣabhāyè*)—who showers desired objects
- अग्नये (*agnaye*)—addressing Agni
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—speech in the form of praise
- प्र ईरय (*pra īraya*)—utter

### Printed p. 1255
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—from our enemies (or from the affliction of our enemies)
- अति पर्षत् (*ati parṣat*)—may he carry across

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, utter a speech in the form of praise for Agni, the granter of desires to human sacrificers. May that Agni carry us across our enemies and protect us.

##### English translation
Raise the hymn to Agni, the benefactor of mankind; may he bear us (safe) beyond (the reach of) those who hate us.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यः पर॑स्याः परा॒वत॑स्ति॒रो धन्वा॑ति॒रोच॑ते ।  
> स नः॑ पर्ष॒दति॒ द्विषः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । परस्याः । परावतः । तिरः । धन्व । अतिरोचते ।  
> सः। नः । पर्षत् । अति । द्विषः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> योऽग्निः परस्याः परावतोऽतिशयिताद्दूरदेशात्तिरः । प्राप्तनामैतत् ।
> प्राप्तसंबंधं धन्व मरुभूमिं जलवर्जितं देशमतिरोचते अतिक्रम्य प्रज्वलति ।
> यद्वा । धन्वांतरिक्षं । धन्वांतरिक्षं तिरस्तिर्यगतिरोचते भृशं प्रकाशयते ।
> गतमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Agni who from the farthest, most distant region shines beyond the dhanva, the desert, a waterless country, which he has reached (तिरः (*tiraḥ*) here is a word meaning "reached", connected with what is reached). Or else: धन्वांतरिक्षं (*dhanvāṃtarikṣaṃ*), dhanva is the atmosphere; तिरः (*tiraḥ*) means "across", and he shines exceedingly. The rest is as already explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Agni
- परस्याः परावतः (*parasyāḥ parāvataḥ*)—from the very distant region
- तिरः (*tiraḥ*)—spread out
- धन्व (*dhanva*)—the desert region
- अतिरोचते (*atirocate*)—shines, passing beyond [or धन्व (*dhanva*)—in the atmospheric region; तिरः (*tiraḥ*)—pervading; अतिरोचते (*atirocate*)—shines exceedingly]
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—from the side of enemies
- अति पर्षत् (*ati parṣat*)—may he carry across

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Agni who shines pervading the desert spread over the very distant region, or the atmospheric region—may that Agni deliver us from the side of our enemies.

### Printed p. 1256

##### English translation
May (Agni), who from a great distance shines fiercely upon the desert tract that he has attained, bear us (safe) beyond (the reach of) those who hate us.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The word dhanva also has the name "atmosphere". Yāska says: धन्वांतरिक्षं धन्वंत्यस्मादापः । तिरो धन्वानि रोचते इत्यपि निगमो भवति । (*dhanvāṃtarikṣaṃ dhanvaṃtyasmādāpaḥ | tiro dhanvāni rocate ityapi nigamo bhavati |*) (Ni. 5-3). Because the waters flow from the atmosphere toward the earth in the form of rain, the word dhanva has the meaning atmosphere. In this matter the Vedic text तिरो धन्वानि रोचते (*tiro dhanvāni rocate*) is the example.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो रक्षां॑सि नि॒जूर्व॑ति॒ वृषा॑ शु॒क्रेण॑ शो॒चिषा॑ ।  
> स नः॑ पर्ष॒दति॒ द्विषः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । रक्षांसि । निजूर्वति । वृषा । शुक्रेण । शोचिषा ।  
> सः । नः । पर्षत् । अति । द्विषः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषा वर्षिता योऽग्निः शुक्रेण निर्मलेन शुभ्रवर्णेन वा शोचिषा तेजसा
> रक्षांसि यज्ञस्य हंतृणि निजूर्वति निहिनस्ति । जुर्वी हिंसार्थः । गतमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Agni who is the showerer, with his pure or white-coloured radiance, that is, brilliance, destroys the Rakṣases, the slayers of the sacrifice; निजूर्वति (*nijūrvati*) means "strikes down"; the root जुर्वी (*jurvī*) has the sense of injury. The rest is as already explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—the granter of desires
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Agni
- शुक्रेण (*śukreṇa*)—of white colour
- शोचिषा (*śociṣā*)—with brilliance
- रक्षांसि (*rakṣāṃsi*)—the demons who are obstructers of the sacrifice
- निजूर्वति (*nijūrvati*)—injures
- सः (*saḥ*)—such Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—from the power of our enemies
- अति पर्षत् (*ati parṣat*)—may he deliver

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Agni, granter of desires, who with his pure brilliance injures the demons who obstruct the sacrifice—may such an Agni deliver us from our enemies.

### Printed p. 1257

##### English translation
May (Agni), the showerer of benefits, who, with his pure radiance destroys the Rakshsas, bear us (safe) beyond (the reach of) those who hate us.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो विश्वा॒भि वि॒पश्य॑ति॒ भुव॑ना॒ सं च॒ पश्य॑ति ।  
> स नः॑ पर्ष॒दति॒ द्विषः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । विश्वा । अभि । विपश्यति । भुवना । सं । च । पश्यति ।  
> सः । नः । पर्षत् । अति । द्विषः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> योऽग्निः सूर्यरूपेण विश्वा विश्वानि सर्वाणि भूतजातान्यभिमुखं विपश्यति
> विशेषेण तेजसा प्रेक्षते । प्रकाशयतीत्यर्थः । भुवना भुवनानि भूतजातानि सं पश्यति
> च सम्यग्ज्ञानाति च । अन्यत्सिद्धं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Agni who, in the form of the sun, looks upon all beings (विश्वा (*viśvā*) = all) face to face, sees them distinctively with his brilliance, that is, illumines them; and who sees the bhuvanas, the beings, well, that is, knows them rightly. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Agni (in the form of the sun)
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all beings (living creatures), with his light
- अभि (*abhi*)—face to face
- विपश्यति (*vipaśyati*)—sees, that is, illumines
- भुवना (*bhuvanā*)—the living creatures
- सं पश्यति च (*saṃ paśyati ca*)—and knows well
- सः (*saḥ*)—such Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—from enemies who hate
- अति पर्षत् (*ati parṣat*)—may he deliver

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Agni who, in the form of the sun, can see and know all beings, that is, living creatures—may such an Agni deliver us from our enemies.

##### English translation
That Agni who in the form of sun sees directly i.e. shines brightly and understands all the living beings bears us (safe) beyond (the reach of) those who hate us.

### Printed p. 1258

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

It was explained earlier that Agni is renowned in three forms: as terrestrial fire on earth, as lightning (vaidyuta fire) in the atmosphere, and as the sun in heaven. In the first three Ṛks of this sūkta terrestrial Agni is praised, in this Ṛk the Āditya, and in the next Ṛk the lightning-fire.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो अ॒स्य पा॒रे रज॑सः शु॒क्रो अ॒ग्निरजा॑यत ।  
> स नः॑ पर्ष॒दति॒ द्विषः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । अस्य । पारे । रजसः । शुक्रः । अग्निः । अजायत ।  
> सः । नः । पर्षत् । अति । द्विषः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्य रजसो लोकस्यांतरिक्षस्य पार उपरिदेशे शुक्रः शुभ्रवर्णो योऽग्निर्विद्युदात्मना सूर्यात्मना वाजायत प्रादुर्भवति स नोऽस्मान्द्विषो द्वेष्टानति
> पर्षत् । अतिपारयतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the farther side, in the upper region, of this rajas, this world, the atmosphere, the white-coloured Agni is born, that is, appears, as lightning or as the sun; may he carry us across those who hate us, our enemies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्य रजसः (*asya rajasaḥ*)—of this atmospheric world
- पारे (*pāre*)—in the very high region
- शुक्रः (*śukraḥ*)—white-coloured
- यः अग्निः (*yaḥ agniḥ*)—which lightning-fire
- अजायत (*ajāyata*)—is born
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- द्विषः (*dviṣaḥ*)—from the side of enemies
- अति पर्षत् (*ati parṣat*)—may he deliver

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The lightning-fire that appears with white colour in the very high region of this atmospheric world—may that Agni deliver us from our enemies.

##### English translation
That Agni who in the form of sun or lightening rises brightly in the far-off regions bears us (safe) beyond (the reach of) those who hate us.
